english: Yes, once the rains return, cocoa trees can shoot fresh leaves and new buds, provided their roots survived the dry period and the land receives adequate water again.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ baanyɛ ajie baai heei kɛ ŋmeii heei. Kɛji akɛ eshishifãi lɛ hi shi yɛ hɔmɔ bei amli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know when the land is ready for a good cocoa year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha kookoo afi kpakpa?

english: When the major rainy season settles in and the soil retains moisture without waterlogging, the land is in good condition to support flowering and high pod yields.
ga: Beni nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ baashɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shihilɛ kpakpa mli ni baanyɛ aye abua fɔfɔi kɛ pod ni fa babaoo.

english: Why does my farm yield plenty of cocoa pods in some years but very few in others?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ kookoo ŋmeii babaoo yɛ afii komɛi amli ni ekrokomɛi fioo pɛ woɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa yields naturally fluctuate depending on annual rainfall patterns, soil nutrient recovery, and how well the farm was weeded and maintained in the previous season.
ga: Cocoa feemɔ tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa afi lɛ naa. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛ bɔ ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli.

english: Is it harmful to leave diseased cocoa pods lying on the ground under my trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ mashi kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi?

english: Yes, leaving infected or rotten pods under cocoa trees allows fungal diseases like Black Pod to stay active in the soil, which can easily spread back up to healthy pods during rains.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni efite lɛ yɛ cacao tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ahe helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli. ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ekoŋŋ kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: Why shouldn't I harvest or bruise green, immature cocoa pods on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikpaa loo mifoɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛko ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Handling or harvesting immature pods damages the skin and seeds inside, creating open wounds that attract pests and cause early pod rot before the beans develop.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni edako lɛ tsu nii loo okpa lɛ, ebaafite hewolo kɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa pilamɔi ni agbele naa ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baa. ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ oya dani ŋmeii lɛ baa.

english: Why do I hear strange rustling noises in my cocoa farm early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minuɔ gbeei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni tswaa lɛ? Yɛ mi kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi?

english: Pests such as squirrels, rats, or monkeys often visit cocoa farms during quiet hours to chew on ripe pods, leaving damaged pods behind that rot quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yaa kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ bei ni yɔɔ dioo mli koni amɛyaye ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ. Shiɔ ŋmeii ni efite ni fiteɔ oya lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if rodents are damaging my cocoa pods before I see them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miifite mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ dani mana amɛ?

english: Look for small chew marks on the pod husk or empty pod shells lying on the ground under the trees, which indicate animal pests are actively feeding on your farm.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmɔlɔ he okadii bibii. yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ loo ŋmeii ni kã shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei ashishi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii miihi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: What basic maintenance work must I do regularly to protect my cocoa yield?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee saamɔ ehe miihia ni mafee daa koni mabu mi-kookoo ni mifeɔ lɛ he?

english: Regular weeding, pruning shade branches, removing sick pods, and keeping farm boundaries clear ensure your trees get enough air and sunlight to produce heavy pods.
ga: Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ jwɛi amli daa Nibii ni afoɔ kɛhaa hulutsoo Nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli husui ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: What is the best way to prevent cocoa theft on my farm during harvest time?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ kookoo juu naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Harvesting ripe pods promptly, clearing undergrowth so visitors can be seen easily, and monitoring your farm regularly during the peak season help deter unauthorized picking.
ga: Nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni oookpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ Ojie tsei lɛ ashishi koni saralɔi ana lɛ oya Ni kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ fa babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akakpa tsei ni ahaaa hegbɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or good compost early in the season helps keep the leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ kpakpa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa wo mli yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni ebaaha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees need taller plantain trees planted next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni adu dumɔwui kakadaji yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture around young cocoa plants until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔleɔ Cocoa tsei lɛ ahe lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa kwraa.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot under the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot primarily when excess water collects in heavy or poorly drained soil, allowing destructive soil fungi to attack and break down the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ titri kɛji nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during strong rainstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that cannot hold tight in wet soil, especially when carrying heavy bunches of fruit or if root-damaging pests like nematodes have weakened them.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ amɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ ootere aduawai babaoo loo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi, tamɔ nematodes lɛ eha amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips sucking the plant's sap, or by viruses carried into the field by these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmɔji amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomatoes get black, sunken spots on the bottom of the fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni ebote shishi lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit during development, often brought on by uneven watering patterns.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are my harvested yams growing small and twisted instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ji bibii ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams require loose, deep soil mounds to expand properly; hard or stony soil restricts tuber development, causing the yams to become stunted or distorted.
ga: Sweet potatoes biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni enyɛ egbɛ eshwa jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa. Enɛ haa sweet potato lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo etsɔɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why are flowers falling off my cocoa branches without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience water stress during dry spells, or when there are not enough beneficial midges in the area to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛna nu he haomɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollin yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the soil. Drooping is a self-defense mechanism to reduce leaf area exposed to the sun and conserve moisture.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Defoliation ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛba baa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Weeds are native plants adapted over centuries to thrive in local conditions, allowing them to absorb nutrients, water, and sunlight faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni atsake amɛ yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛshwere yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛ nuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni amɛ duɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine I buy at the market is genuine and effective?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Always purchase inputs from registered agrochemical dealers, check for official regulator seals like the EPA tag, inspect the bottle for expiration dates, and avoid buying unlabelled or extremely cheap chemicals.
ga: Hemɔ nibii kɛjɛ agrochemical jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ mlai ahe okadi, tamɔ EPA tag lɛ. Kwɛmɔ tɔ lɛ mli koni ona gbi ni ekɛbaatsu nii. Ni tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni aŋmalako nɔ ko loo ni jara waaa kwraa lɛ hemɔ he.

english: Market sellers always claim all their crop sprays are good, so how do I choose the right one?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ kɛɔ akɛ tsofai ni amɛkɛshwieɔ amɛŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ fɛɛ hi. No hewɔ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsofa ni sa?

english: Sellers focus on making sales, so you should check the active ingredients on the label or consult an extension officer to match the exact pest, weed, or disease affecting your crop rather than relying only on vendor recommendations.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa nihɔɔmɔ nɔ No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo obi o-extension agent lɛ koni ona tsɛŋemɔ helai, jwɛi, loo helai ni miigba oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ ohe aaafɔ̃ nihɔɔlɔ lɛ ŋaawoo pɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do some cheap farm chemicals fail to clear weeds or pests from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai komɛi ni jara waaa lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie jwɛi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛjɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Cheap products are often diluted or counterfeit, containing very little of the active ingredient needed to kill pests. Using fake products ends up costing more money because you have to buy and spray multiple times without success.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ nibii ni jara waaa lɛ woɔ nu mli loo amalei. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nibii ni tsuɔ nii ni he hiaa koni akɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faaa kwraa. Kɛ́ okɛ amale nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ofite shika babaoo ejaakɛ esa akɛ ohe ni okɛwo mli shii abɔ ni oyeee omanye.

english: Why is the pest medicine I have used for many years suddenly no longer killing the insects on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛtsuɔ nii afii babaoo lɛ egbeee kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When you use the exact same chemical season after season, the surviving insects build up resistance to it. Switching to a medicine with a different active ingredient breaks this resistance and controls the pests.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsu nii daa be lɛ, kooloi ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee tsofa ko ni mli nibii ni tsuɔ nii kroko yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaakumɔ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ mli ni eye tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ.

english: If I spray my crop medicine and it does not work, does it mean the product is bad?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ ni etsuuu nii. Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ nibii ni afee lɛ efite?

english: Not always. Bad timing, using dirty water to mix, spraying right before rain, or applying the wrong dosage can make a good chemical fail even if it is authentic.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be, be lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni mli ewo muji ni akɛfutu mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ dani nugbɔ anɔ Aloo bɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai kpakpai akatsu nii kɛji tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ji amɛ po.

english: Should I keep buying the same reliable crop spray every season if it worked well last year?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ ni ji nɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli? Kɛji etsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli

english: It is better to rotate between different families of chemicals each season. Using the same spray repeatedly encourages pests and fungi to adapt and become immune over time.
ga: Esa akɛ atsake tsofai srɔtoi. Be fɛɛ be hi fe no. Spray kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ Ebaawo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛtsake amɛhe ni amɛná hewalɛ ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Does farm medicine lose its strength if I keep it stored in my shed for a long time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli tsofa lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli kɛji mikɛto mi shĩa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, exposure to high heat, sunlight, moisture, or storing chemical containers past their expiration date causes the active chemicals to break down and lose their killing power.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli wa, hulu la, hulutsoo be, loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he ni eho be ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ he lɛ baaha tsofai ni tsuɔ nii lɛ afite ni amɛhewalɛ ni amɛkɛgbeɔ mɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: Why do my crop leaves keep turning yellow even after I spray them with pest medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are often a sign of nutrient deficiency or soil issues rather than insect damage. Spraying pest medicine will not solve a soil issue; your crops likely need fertilizer or organic manure instead.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ naagbai ahe okadi moŋ fe nɔ ni kooloi fiteɔ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛŋ atsu shikpɔŋ nɔ naagbai ahe nii. Ekolɛ onibii lɛ baabi ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli moŋ.

english: Why are my crops failing to yield well even though I spray them regularly against pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Pest control is only one part of crop growth. Crops also require proper plant nutrition, correct planting distance, sufficient water, and healthy soil to yield well.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nitsumɔ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fã kome pɛ. Tsei hu he miihia tsei amli niyenii ni sa. dumɔ he ni jɛkɛmɔ ni ja Nu ni fa kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa kɛha yibii kpakpai

english: How can I plan my farm budget so I don't run out of money for crop medicine mid-season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ mli shika he gbɛjianɔ koni shika akafite mi koni mikɛhe tsei ahe tsofa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Calculate your field size and required chemical quantities before planting begins. Purchasing your inputs upfront or joining a local farmer group to buy in bulk can lower costs and protect your budget.
ga: Buu he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dalɛ kɛ tsofai babaoo ni he hiaa lɛ he akɔntaa dani obɔi dumɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni ooohe kɛtsɔ hiɛ loo okɛ ohe awo okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ mli koni oyahe babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha shika ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ aba shi ni ebu oshika he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ he.

english: Can I just plant corn kernels taken from the maize I bought at the local market to eat?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ mli koni maye?

english: Market maize is usually intended for cooking and may not produce a strong crop. Selecting properly dried, high-quality seeds that were intentionally harvested and stored for cultivation ensures better sprouting, healthier plants, and higher yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji ŋmãa ni akɛhooɔ nii ni ekolɛ ekɛ ŋmãa ni hi baaa. Dumɔwui ni egbi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ akɛ abaakpa ni akɛto koni adu lɛ ni ahala jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa, ni amɛná yibii babaoo.

english: What is the difference between crops grown for daily eating and crops selected specifically for seeds?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ koni aye daa gbi kɛ tsei ni ahala pɔtɛɛ kɛha dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ?

english: Crops grown for eating are harvested for quick food consumption. Crops selected for seeds are carefully picked from the healthiest, strongest plants, fully matured, and dried properly so they can survive storage and sprout successfully when planted next season.
ga: Akpaa tsei ni aduɔ koni aye lɛ oya koni aye. Ahalaa tsei ni ahala kɛha dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ amli. ni amɛdara kwraa ni amɛgbi amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekwɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: How should I safely store my dry corn seeds so insects don't destroy them before planting time?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani dumɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Store thoroughly dried seeds in clean, airtight containers or specialized bags, keeping them off the damp floor in a cool, dark room to protect them from moisture, mold, and pest damage.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ awo tsinsii ni he tse, ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku pɔtɛɛ ko mli. Ha dumɔwui lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Koni abu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe.

english: Why should I leave slashed green leaves and weeds on my farmland instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai eŋɔli ni afolɔ kɛ jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ?

english: Green leaves and plants decay into organic matter, which feeds the soil, keeps the ground moist during dry hot days, and protects topsoil from washing away during heavy rains.
ga: Baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni ebuɔ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he koni nugbɔ akashwie nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: How can I use the bush plants and grass on my farm to help my corn grow better?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni eye ebua mi-ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Chopping up local green grass and bush leaves to cover the soil around your crops creates a natural blanket called mulch. This traps moisture in the soil and breaks down into natural food for your growing corn.
ga: Kɛ́ ofolɔ jwɛi eŋɔli kɛ ŋmɔ mli baai ni okɛwo onibii ahe lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Enɛ baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ebaagbala mli ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha o-abele ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How do I properly prepare my soil before putting my maize seeds in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani madu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: Clear invasive weeds, loosen hard soil with a hoe so young roots can spread easily, and mix in natural organic plant material to give your seeds a soft, nutrient-rich bed to sprout in.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Okɛ ŋmei ajie shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ koni shishifãi bibii lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei ahe nibii futuɔ mli koni eha odumɔwui lɛ aná he ko ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to start planting my corn seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi?

english: Wait until the main rainy season has truly established in your area. Planting after just one early rain can cause seeds to sprout and then wither if dry weather returns immediately after.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ abashɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ no sɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my corn seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were damaged during storage, planted too deep in the dirt, lacked soil moisture to awaken them, or were eaten by ants and rodents underground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji amɛfite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ Fɛ̃i ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛteɔ shi loo ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: How can I tell if my young corn plants are getting enough nutrition from the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Healthy corn plants have thick stems and vibrant, deep green leaves. If the leaves turn pale green or yellow, the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen and needs soil enrichment.
ga: Abele tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ tsei ni mli wa kɛ baai ni kpɛɔ, eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ nitrogen ni ehe miihia ni akɛ shikpɔŋ awo mli.

english: Can I grow food crops like beans or groundnuts together in the same field with my corn?
ga: Mibaanyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ani abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmãa afata he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting legumes like beans alongside corn is very beneficial. Beans shade the soil to stop weed growth and naturally trap nitrogen from the air into the soil, which helps feed the corn.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akpa shweremɔ ni ekɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ awoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni baaye abua ni akwɛ ŋmãa

english: Why are my tomatoes growing so small instead of getting big and heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miidara bibii moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni etsii lɛ?

english: Tomatoes stay small when the plant lacks enough water during fruit growth or lacks potassium in the soil. Planting seedlings too close together or leaving too many fruit clusters on one branch also starves individual tomatoes of nutrients.
ga: Tomato bafeɔ bibioo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ loo potassium bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo ashiɔ aduawai akui babaoo yɛ tso nine kome nɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha niyenii aŋkroaŋkroi lɛ akaná niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden water stress. Using too much nitrogen fertilizer can also make the plant focus only on growing leaves, causing it to shed its flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu he haomɔ trukaa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama baai ni miida lɛ pɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium in the fruit. It usually happens when watering is irregular, which prevents the roots from carrying soil calcium up to the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ calcium ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya tomatoi ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my green tomatoes crack open on the sides right before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ mli gbalaa yɛ afãi dani etsɔɔ tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when there is a sudden increase in water, such as heavy rainfall after a long dry period. The inside of the tomato expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing it to split.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nu lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. Tomato lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. kɛ mligbalamɔ baa

english: Why do extension officers advise tying tomato plants to wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nitsumɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ tomato tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Staking keeps leaves and fruits off wet soil, which prevents soil-borne fungal rots and insect damage. It also exposes the plant to more sunlight and fresh air, leading to healthier growth and easier harvesting.
ga: Staking baaha baai kɛ aduawai akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ naa. Ehaa tsei naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ, ni ekpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo.

english: How far apart should I plant my tomato seedlings when transferring them to the field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ miiwo ŋmɔ mli?

english: Spacing tomato plants about 2 feet apart within rows and 3 feet between rows ensures each plant gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients. Good spacing also allows air to flow through the crop, reducing leaf diseases.
ga: Okɛ tomato tsei lɛ afee ŋwɛi aaafee ninetalɔi 2 yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli kɛ ninetalɔi 3 yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ teŋ koni tomato tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa helai baa shi

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my tomato crop to get the best harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tomato tsei lɛ amli koni amɛwo yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: Apply a nitrogen-rich starter fertilizer about two weeks after transplanting to build strong stems and leaves. Switch to a potassium-rich fertilizer once flowering begins to encourage big, firm fruits.
ga: Okɛ shishijee ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛma ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai ni wa. Tsakemɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ kɛji fɔfɔi je shishi koni eha aduawai lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my tomato plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or early fungal blight starting from humid soil. Removing affected lower leaves improves airflow and helps stop fungal diseases from spreading upward.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni ji fungal blight lɛ shishijee fãi, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni ena hela lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Why do tomatoes spoil and rot much faster on the farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli tomatoi fiteɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: High air humidity and splashing rain create ideal conditions for fungal diseases like blight to spread rapidly. Raindrops bounce fungal spores from the soil onto the lower leaves and fruits, causing quick decay.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ late blight ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa baai kɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. ha efite oya

english: Why do white, papery patches appear on the skin of my ripening tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ woji yɛŋ he okadii yɛ mi-tomato ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is sunscald, which happens when ripening fruits are exposed to direct, intense sunlight without leaf cover. Protecting the plant's leafy canopy keeps fruits shaded and prevents sunburn spots.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ wo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni baa ko bɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ abu tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa aduawai lɛ náa hulutsoo ni ehaa hulu lɛ shãa amɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and yellow when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Spacing maize properly lets each plant get enough nutrients to grow thick stalks and big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Abɛi tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrients out of the earth, while leguminous plants like groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally refreshing the land for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha jɛmɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn yellow before the fruits are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil, which it needs to stay green. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer early on keeps the leaves green so the plant can feed its developing tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni esa akɛ ehi shi eŋɔli Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aye abua tomato ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning pale yellow in spots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Curling leaves with yellow spots are a sign of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny flies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems recommended by extension officers keeps your field healthy.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji yucca mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Yucca tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ jɛmɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni eha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the pods on my mature cocoa trees turn black and rot during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, heavy shade and wet weather. Pruning overgrown tree branches and removing affected pods quickly helps prevent the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei niji ni eda fe nine lɛ amli ni ojie ŋmeii ni ena hela lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my okra flowers drop off the plant without forming any okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee okra ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Okra flowers fall off when the plant gets stressed by drought during very hot weather or flooded soil from heavy rain. Regular, moderate watering during dry spells keeps the flowers attached so they turn into pods.
ga: Roselle fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ haoɔ tso lɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves when I see small white butterflies around my farm?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi kaabaji baa lɛ nɔ be ko lɛ mina ŋmei bibioo ko yɛŋ. yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ he

english: Those butterflies lay eggs on the leaves that hatch into hungry caterpillars, which eat holes in the leaves. Checking under the leaves regularly and spraying natural neem solutions can protect your cabbage.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ni ji neem lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu okabe lɛ he.

english: Why do wild weeds grow much faster and taller than my crops even without fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkwɔ fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii po fataaa he lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, meaning they steal light, water, and soil food much faster than farm crops can. Clearing weeds early in the season gives your main crop a fair chance to grow well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛjuɔ la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ehaa otsei titrii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn soft and rot inside my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni egbo yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots inside storage if it is put away while still holding water inside the grains. Spreading your maize in the sun to dry completely until the grains are hard prevents mold and rot during storage.
ga: Abɛi baafite yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ kɛji ajie kɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lolo lɛ. Abɛi ni agbiɔ yɛ hulu mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: NPK fertilizer contains three main plant foods: Nitrogen for green leaves, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for healthy fruit and disease resistance. It gives your crops balanced nutrition to grow well.
ga: NPK ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ tsei amli niyenii titrii etɛ: Nitrogen kɛha baai eŋɔli. Fosfɔs kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Ehaa otsei lɛ náa niyenii ni sa ni sa koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the difference between Urea and NPK fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ urea ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ?

english: Urea provides a quick, concentrated boost of Nitrogen to help plants grow tall and bushy, while NPK is a complete food mix that supports overall plant health from roots to harvest.
ga: Urea haa nitrogen ni mli wa oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji, yɛ be mli ni NPK ji niyenii ni yeɔ emuu ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli.

english: Where exactly should I place solid fertilizer around my crop stem?
ga: Nɛgbɛ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa awo mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: You should place fertilizer in a small circle or band about a hand-width (5 cm) away from the main stem, not touching it directly, so the roots can reach the food safely without burning the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli yɛ kooyigbɛ bibii loo kooyigbɛ ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee nine kome (5 cm) kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he, ni okɛ ohe akataa he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa niyenii shweshweeshwe ni amɛshãaa tso lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants bending and looking weak after I put Urea right at the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbɔjɔ beni mikɛ urea efata shishi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Urea is very strong. When placed directly against the stem, it chemically burns the base of the plant, causing the tissue to break down and the stalk to grow crooked or fall over.
ga: Urea lɛ mli wa waa. Kɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ Ebaashã tso lɛ shishi kɛ tsofai. Enɛ haa fãji lɛ fiteɔ ni tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shwieɔ shi loo egbeeɔ shi.

english: What happens if I accidentally spill a large heap of fertilizer in one place on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shwie he kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ oshara mli?

english: Spilling too much fertilizer in one spot over-concentrates chemical salts, which burns the soil and kills the crop roots in that area, while also wasting expensive materials.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli ŋmeii babaoo aba mli fe nine. Enɛ baashã shikpɔŋ lɛ ni efite tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ nakai he lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ nibii ni jara wa.

english: Should I put strong fertilizer in the soil on the very day I plant my seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ baadu lɛ nɔ?

english: No, it is best to wait until seeds sprout and develop young roots. Applying strong fertilizer too early can scorch delicate seedlings before they establish themselves.
ga: Dabi, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná shishifãi bibii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ amli oya lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ dani amɛma shi.

english: How do I know when it is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain and when the crops are actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting, so the roots can easily drink up the nutrients.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida Bei pii lɛ Enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ mlɛo.

english: My neighbor applies fertilizer as soon as the rains start, should I just copy what he does?
ga: Akutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ. Ani esa akɛ makase nɔ ni efee lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. Different crops, planting dates, and soil types require different schedules, so copying others without understanding your own crops' timing can lead to wasted fertilizer or crop damage.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi, gbii ni aduɔ, kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi biɔ gbɛjianɔtoo srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi fee nɔ ko ni onuuu be ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Why are my young crops growing out crooked instead of standing up straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daa ni amɛbɔleɔ amɛhe moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Crooked growth often happens when roots or stem bases are damaged on one side—frequently by misplaced strong fertilizers—forcing the plant to lean or bend as it tries to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi loo tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ fite yɛ efã kome. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni akɛwoɔ he ni esaaa lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tso lɛ atsi ehe loo ekoto ehe beni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehi shi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if I have given my crops too much fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine?

english: Signs of over-fertilization include leaf tips turning brown and dry as if burned, stems twisting or curling sideways, and plants wilting even when the soil is wet.
ga: Nɔ ni fata okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔmɔ ewo mli fe nine lɛ ahe ji baai lɛ ashishifãi ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã. Akɛ tso lɛ shishi loo abɔle ehe kɛtee afã. ni tsei gboɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-decomposed animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the strength they need to turn dark green and produce big, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni efite jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛtsɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ nii waa ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I avoid burning dry weeds on my field before clearing the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛshãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he dani majie he ni mikɛbaadu nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys natural plant nutrients and good organisms in the topsoil that help your crops grow. Allowing cut weeds to rot on the ground turns them into natural fertilizer and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli niyenii kɛ nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa onibii ni okwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ jwɛi ni afo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: What is causing small caterpillars to eat holes through the leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli?

english: This is likely the Fall Armyworm, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on young corn leaves. You can protect your crop by regularly checking the center leaves and applying safe pest control measures as soon as you spot them.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu onibii ahe kɛtsɔ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni oookwɛ daa lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛbaagbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa kɛji ona amɛ pɛ.

english: Why are my sweet pepper fruits turning black and rotten at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ shishigbɛ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This rot happens when pepper plants cannot get enough calcium or face irregular watering while fruiting. Watering your plants regularly and adding wood ash or lime to the soil prevents this damage.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛkɛ nu ni ejaaa kpeɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ. Nu ni oooha tso lɛ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant cassava and maize together in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is ready to harvest in a few months, while cassava grows slowly underneath. Planting them together makes good use of your land, gives you two different food crops, and protects the soil from drying out.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni eshɛɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Beni ŋmei lɛ daa fiofio yɛ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fee ekome lɛ, ebaaha okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Ha tsei lɛ niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi

english: When maize seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin stalks that break easily and produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni fãa oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ baa. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Can I save seeds from my hybrid maize harvest to plant during the next farming season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ ŋmãa ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving and replanting seeds from hybrid maize will give you much smaller yields and weaker plants in the next season. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each season to get strong plants and heavy yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli lɛ ni oootoo ni okwɛ lɛ baaha oná yibii fioo kwraa ni tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves of my tomato plants curl upwards during hot afternoon weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl to reduce water loss and protect themselves from high heat. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass (mulching) helps retain soil moisture and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Akɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ni tsiɔ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ naa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving only a cluster of leaves at the top. You can carefully dig up one side of the root system to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Baai akuu ko pɛ eshwɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu shishifã lɛ fã kome he nii koni okwɛ kɛji shishifã lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to direct heat and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains next to them creates living shade and keeps the soil moist, giving the young cocoa trees the shelter they need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ, ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa hulutsoo ni wala yɔɔ mli baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa cacao tsei bibii lɛ naa he ko ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb instead of letting them creep on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo tsei kɛha sweet potato wain tsei koni makwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the tuber underground. Lifting the vines on stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight while keeping them off wet soil, which prevents rot and leaves you with bigger tubers.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni awoɔ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnáa hulu la ni fe fɛɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baatsi fitemɔ naa ni eha oná bulbs wuji.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I leave many young shoots around the main tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa beni mishiɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The main plantain tree shares water and nutrients with every young shoot growing around its base. Leaving too many shoots starves the main plant, so pruning extra suckers allows all the soil energy to go into making one large, heavy plantain bunch.
ga: Dumɔwui titrii lɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ jaa nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo mli fe nine lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye ŋmeii titrii lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baahe hewalɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni ekɛfee ŋmeii akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. When nitrogen is low, the plant steals nutrients from its older bottom leaves to keep the new leaves at the top growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni baai heei akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without forming any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms, making it impossible for fruit to form. When temperatures drop or plants get light shade, the flowers will start setting fruit again.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa yibii aba. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi loo tso lɛ ná hulutsoo lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baabɔi yibiiwoo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of lush green leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen-rich manure makes pepper plants focus entirely on growing leaves instead of fruit. Adding nutrients like phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to stop growing foliage and start producing peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa chili tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛbaafata he Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akpa baai lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔtɔ feemɔ.

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that capture nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This natural fertilizer stays in the ground and feeds neighbouring crops like maize.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and soft when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a water-loving fungus that spreads in cold, damp weather. Rain droplets bounce the fungal spores onto wet pods, where they enter and destroy the beans inside.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Hydrophilic fungus ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ fɛ̃i, fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores lɛ nɔ kɛyaa pods ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. ni amɛbaafite kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cassava roots spoil and turn brown inside just a few days after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, harvested cassava roots do not have a tough outer skin to protect them from air. As soon as cassava is dug up, exposure to air causes rapid internal chemical changes that spoil the root within two to three days unless it is processed.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni akpa lɛ bɛ kponɔgbɛ nɔ ko ni wa ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahe. Kɛji atsa ŋmei lɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ oya. Enɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. ja atsu he nii

english: Why do my fresh tomatoes rot so quickly when packed in deep wooden crates for transport to town?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hee lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ awo tso adekai ni mli kwɔ amli koni akɛya maŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy pressure in deep crates crushes the soft tomatoes at the bottom, opening tiny wounds where decay bacteria grow rapidly. Heat built up inside tightly stacked crates speeds up this rotting process during transport.
ga: Nɔnyɛɛ ni tsii ni yɔɔ adeka ni mli kwɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwie tomato bibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. ni ekɛ pilamɔi bibii baa he ni helatsɛmɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ daa oya Dɔlɛ ni buaa ehe naa yɛ adekai ni ato amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ amli lɛ haa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa oya yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed to make food and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains make the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha niyenii feemɔ kɛ shweremɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why should I apply fertilizer when the ground is moist instead of when it is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ fe be mli ni egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat dry fertilizer. Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into liquid form so the roots can drink it up. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can also burn your crop's roots.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nu koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily in harsh sunlight. Large shade trees act like umbrellas that protect the young cocoa from direct sun, keep the air humid, and protect the soil from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela ni buɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi

english: How can my cassava crop survive and stay green during the dry season when there is no rain?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi ni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava is naturally built for dry weather. It stores water and starch in its underground tubers and can shed its leaves to stop water loss, staying alive until the rains return.
ga: Abɔ cassava kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi. Ekɛ nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ toɔ tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai afɔ shi koni ekɛkpa nu ni elaaje lɛ ni ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba

english: What happens to my maize if I plant the seeds too close together in the same row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmãa kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stems and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii loo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start growing shoots in the barn even before I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ bɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu amɛ po lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally track time and temperature. As the dry season ends, warm weather signals to the tuber that it is time to break its resting period and use its stored energy to push out sprouts.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ nyiɛɔ be kɛ latsaa sɛɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ kɛje kpo.

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is sudden water stress. When stressed, the plant tries to save its own life by dropping flowers instead of trying to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu he haomɔ ba trukaa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehere ehe kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni eeeŋmɛɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding under the leaves, or by a viral sickness carried by those pests that damages the leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ hela ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ baa lɛ shweremɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ mli

english: Why do fall armyworms seem to appear overnight and chew up my young maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni fall armyworms lɛ jeɔ kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli ni amɛyeɔ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths fly into farms at night and lay hundreds of eggs under leaves. When the tiny caterpillars hatch, they eat quickly and hide inside the central leaves of the maize where rain and spray cannot reach them easily.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛboteɔ ŋmɔji amli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai ashishi. Kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii lɛ fɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ nii oya ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. ni nugbɔ kɛ nu afua nyɛŋ ashɛ he mlɛo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my planted cassava and vegetables after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei kɛ aduawai yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that are naturally adapted to local soil conditions. Their seeds can sit in the dirt for years and are always ready to sprout faster and drink water quicker than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ ahi sũ lɛ mli afii babaoo. ni efee klalo akɛ ebaakwɛ̃ oya ni enu nu oya fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. Plants need nitrogen to make green leaves, and when there isn't enough, the plant pulls nutrients from its older leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen he miihia tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Ni kɛ́ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ Tsei lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains the soil of the specific nutrients that crop needs and allows pests and diseases that feed on it to multiply in the ground.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tsei lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mifolɔ tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong direct sunlight. They need shade trees to act as living umbrellas to protect them from harsh heat and keep moisture in the soil while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my seeds after the first rain falls?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adũ dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become regular and wet the soil deep down, because a single early rain is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry out and kill newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni amɛmɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shikome pɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni mli egbi lɛ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long or when fungi spread in wet conditions. Soil that drains water easily prevents roots from suffocating and rotting.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ loo kɛji ŋmeii lɛ gbɛ eshwa shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛkafite.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off before any pepper fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper yibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients, causing the plant to shed its flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall down easily whenever a strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy bunches of fruit, making them top-heavy. Supporting them with strong wooden poles helps keep them standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛwoɔ aduawai babaoo, ni no haa amɛfeɔ tsiimɔ. Tso tsei ni wa fiɔ esɛɛ koni eye ebua ni edamɔ shi kɛyashi nikpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up high into the sunlight so they can catch enough light to manufacture food, which goes down to swell the yam tuber underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni amɛná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛfee niyenii. ni baagbee shi ni eha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi

english: Why do weeds make my crops stay small and weak even when I plant them well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like greedy neighbours; their roots steal water and food from the soil, and their tall leaves block sunlight from reaching your crops.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akutsoŋbii ni hiɛ kɔ̃ɔ mɔ nɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Ni amɛbaai kakadaji lɛ tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ onibii ahe.

english: Why are there small worms hiding inside the leaves of my young maize plants eating holes in them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai ni miiye bu yɛ amɛmli lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hatch from moth eggs and hide inside the central leaves of maize plants to feed on the tender leaf tissues.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni jɛɔ ŋmeii akui amli ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ amli fãji.

english: Why does the local factory reject my cassava harvest even though the roots are large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ mli nitsumɔhei lɛ kpooɔ mi-cassava ni mikpaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi lɛ dara moŋ?

english: Factories look for specific starch content and freshness, not just root size. Certain cassava varieties have low starch or spoil rapidly within 24 to 48 hours after harvest, making them unsuitable for factory processing.
ga: Nitsumɔhei lɛ taoɔ ashikishaŋ abɔ pɔtɛɛ kɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ ehee. Jeee shishifã lɛ dalɛ pɛ he ewieɔ. Cassava henɔi komɛi amli ŋmɔtɔ faaa loo amɛfiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli beni akpa amɛ. ni no haa esaaa akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhei

english: Why are my maize crops failing while my neighbor who planted a different seed variety gets a heavy harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miikpa shi yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo ni duɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ naa ŋmaa babaoo lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties are bred for specific soil types, rainfall levels, and pest resistance. Improved seed varieties perform much better during unpredictable weather than older or uncertified seed types.
ga: Akwɛɔ tsei srɔtoi yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ bɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ mli. moŋ fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ loo ni bɛ he odaseyeli.

english: How can I know if a crop variety will sell well before I invest money to plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso ko baahɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ dani mikɛ mishika awo mli?

english: Markets prefer crops with high buyer demand, long shelf life, and proper processing qualities. Checking with local extension officers or crop buyers helps you select high-demand varieties that will not go to waste.
ga: Jarayelihe lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ babaoo lɛ. Shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛ nitsumɔ mli nibii ni sa Kɛ́ okɛ omaŋbii ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ loo mɛi ni heɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni ataoɔ waa ni sɛɛ efooo.

english: Why do my tomatoes rot so fast before I can even transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ fiteɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes spoil quickly if harvested fully ripe or packed tightly in hot, unventilated sacks. Harvesting them when they just start changing color and using ventilated wooden crates delays decay during transport.
ga: Tomato fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa lɛ ni egbɔ kwraa loo akɛwo kotokui ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote mli lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ. Nikpamɔ be mli ni amɛjeɔ amɛhe su tsakemɔ shishi kɛkɛ kɛ tso adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha fitemɔ asɛɛ afo yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantains turn soft and black so quickly when I stack them inside a transport truck?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ feɔ blɛoo oya ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛto tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains release a natural gas called ethylene as they ripen, and heavy stacking causes heat build-up and physical bruising. This trapped heat and pressure causes the entire load to ripen and decay rapidly.
ga: Dares jieɔ adebɔɔ mli la ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii wuji baaha dɔlɛ aba ni gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli agbɔjɔ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ kɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa jatsu muu lɛ fɛɛ shãa oya ni efiteɔ.

english: How can I prevent my dried cocoa beans from turning moldy while waiting for transport?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-kookoo ni egbi lɛ naa koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni akɛmaje lɛ?

english: Cocoa beans trap moisture easily. If they are not fully dried to 7% moisture level and stored in clean, raised bags away from damp floors and walls, mold will grow and ruin their quality.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli oya. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, ha egbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi hulutsoo be ni ji 7% ni okɛto kotoku ni mli tse mli ni awo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ gbogboi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ ahe. Mold baakwɛ̃ ni ebaafite su lɛ.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny pests like whiteflies or thrips transmitting a plant virus. The virus weakens the plant, preventing it from producing healthy peppers and leading to severe yield loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Virus haa tsei gbɔjɔɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ afeemɔ naa ni ehaa yibiiwoo lɛ fiteɔ waa.

english: Why do my yam tubers rot underground in the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Underground yam rot is caused by poor soil drainage combined with attacks from soil fungi or nematodes. Standing water around the roots smothers the tubers and allows rot organisms to destroy the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sweet potato fitemɔ baa ji shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo nematodes ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. nu ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa bulb lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my orange trees dropping their young fruits before they are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Premature fruit drop occurs when citrus trees face water stress, nutrient shortages, or attacks from fruit flies. Consistent watering and fruit fly control prevent the tree from shedding immature fruit.
ga: Yibii ni shwieɔ shi oya lɛ baa kɛji akɛ citrus tsei lɛ na nu he haomɔ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo aduawai amli ŋmeii ni tutuaa lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ aduawai amli ŋmeii ni akudɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii ni eshɛko lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay small and loose instead of forming hard balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee nɔ ko ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages require high nitrogen and constant moisture to build dense heads. High temperatures and poor soil nutrients cause the leaves to grow open instead of wrapping tightly into a firm head.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ he miihia Cabbage koni ekɛfee yitsei ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ waa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ haa baai lɛ gbeleɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee bulbs ni mli wa.

english: Why do some trees need to be left standing on my farm when I am clearing land for new crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi eshwɛɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijieɔ he ko kɛhaa tsei heei lɛ?

english: Certain tall shade trees protect young crops like cocoa from direct heat and heavy winds, holding moisture in the soil and preventing delicate plants from drying out.
ga: Tsei kakadaji komɛi ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii tamɔ kookoo he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaaa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbi.

english: What will happen to my crop yield if I do not clear weeds and bush thoroughly before planting?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mijieee jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani midu?

english: Weeds compete directly with young crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, which stunts crop growth and leads to much smaller harvests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kpaa amɛkwɛ̃mɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: How does cutting down all big trees on my farm affect soil moisture during the dry season?
ga: Te tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Without shade trees to block direct sunlight, water in the soil evaporates much faster, leaving the ground dry and causing crops to wilt quickly.
ga: Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho oya kwraa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii hu gbɔjɔɔ oya.

english: Can I use the same machine to clear land and also sow my crop seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsɔne nɛɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛjie shikpɔŋ ni mikɛdu dumɔwui?

english: Yes, multipurpose farm machinery can handle different jobs by changing implements—using heavy blades or cutters for clearing land and seed-drill attachments for planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsɔnei ni tsuɔ nibii babaoo he nii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nitsumɔi srɔtoi. kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni akɛtsakeɔ tsɔne loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛjieɔ he lɛ kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ dumɔwui ni akɛduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does plowing deep into the soil change the way my crop roots grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsuɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Deep plowing breaks up hard soil, allowing roots to grow deeper down to reach underground water and nutrients, making the plants stronger against drought.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ baagbala shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli. Ha shishifãi lɛ ada kɛya shɔŋŋ koni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Ehaa tsei he waɔ kɛshiɔ hɔmɔ.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is missing essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or that waterlogging around the roots is preventing the crop from feeding properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no haa tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce big leaves and tall stems but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava plants to push all their energy into leafy growth above ground rather than storing starch in the roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ starch ato shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do crops growing under large mango trees seem to develop much slower than crops in open light?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni aduɔ yɛ mango tsei wuji ashishi lɛ daraa blɛoo kwraa fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kpo nɔ lɛ?

english: Dense tree canopies block the sunlight crops need to produce food, while the tree's large roots absorb most of the water and fertilizer from the soil.
ga: Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná niyenii lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nii babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli.

english: How does heavy rainfall right after planting affect my seeds in the soil?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa beni adu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ saa midumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Excessive rain can wash seeds away, cause them to rot in waterlogged soil, or compact the ground surface so tightly that young shoots cannot sprout through.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baanyɛ ahoo dumɔwui lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Aloo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ abɔ he waa bɔni afee ni ŋmeii bibii lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Why is it important to dry my harvested crops in the sun before processing or storing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mikpamɔ lɛ agbi dani mikɛtsu nii loo mikɛto lɛ?

english: Sun-drying removes moisture from harvested grains and roots, which stops mold from growing and prevents insects from spoiling the crop during storage.
ga: Gbimɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui kɛ shishifãi ni akpa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ, ni ehaaa ŋmeii afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the dry heat drains moisture from their roots; planting shade crops like plantains around them keeps the soil moist and protects them until they mature.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni la ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, dark environments; removing infected pods and pruning thick branches lets sunlight in and helps prevent the fungus from spreading to healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Fɔ̃ɔ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ofolɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli waa koni hulu la lɛ abote mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii akagbɛ ashwã kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce many flowers that just fall off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges to carry pollen between them; if the farm is too dry or sprayed with harsh chemicals at the wrong time, these insects die off and unpollinated flowers drop to the ground.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Atsɛɔ amɛ midges koni amɛkɛ pollen awo amɛteŋ. Kɛji ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo akɛ tsofai ni mli wa shwie nɔ yɛ be ni esaaa mli Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gboiɔ ni fɔfɔi ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why should I avoid picking green coffee berries along with the red ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ kɔfi ŋmɔji ni akɛfataa ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Coffee berries ripen at different speeds on the same branch, and harvesting green berries reduces the quality and taste of the coffee beans, leading to lower sale prices.
ga: Kɔfi yibii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ oyaiyeli srɔtoi amli yɛ tso nine kome nɔ. Ni tsei ayibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe fɛo kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ lɛ baa shi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, jara ni akɛhɔ̃ɔ lɛ ba shi.

english: How do I know if my land is suitable for growing coffee bushes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ sa kɛha kɔfi tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Coffee grows best in deep, fertile soil that drains water easily and in areas that receive moderate rainfall with partial shade to shield the bushes from excessive sun heat.
ga: Kɔfi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni nu hoɔ oya lɛ nɔ. kɛ hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ fã ko hu yɔɔ lɛ koni akɛbu tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why do shea trees take so many years before they start producing their first fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani shea tso ko jeɔ shishi ewoɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Shea trees grow naturally in dry climates and spend their early years developing very deep root systems underground to survive long droughts before they can store enough energy to yield nuts.
ga: Shea tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli egbi. ni ekɛ shishijee afii lɛ tsu nii Koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yaa shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ waa koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli dani enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii aba lɛ ato.

english: Is it better to pick shea fruits directly from the tree or gather them from the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookpa shea tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: It is best to gather shea fruits after they naturally fall to the ground because dropped fruits are fully ripe and yield higher quality oil for making shea butter.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa chia aduawai lɛ beni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ egbɔ kwraa, ni ejieɔ mu ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfeɔ shea butter.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches from my crop trees if the branches look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ mitso lɛ mli kɛji akɛ niji lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary foliage so the tree can focus its water and nutrients on growing bigger, healthier fruit rather than feeding extra leaves.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ahe tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ moŋ fe ni eeekɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli baa lɛ aha.

english: Why does heavy rain during the flowering season cause my crop trees to yield less fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ haa mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall can knock delicate blossoms off the branches and prevent pollinating insects from flying, resulting in fewer flowers successfully turning into fruit.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ agbee shi kɛjɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ ni eha fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ akafo. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi fioo komɛi ni bafeɔ aduawai.

english: How does clearing weeds around the base of my trees help my farm yield a better harvest?
