ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle mi lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal vital water, fertilizers, and soil nutrients meant for your trees, so removing them ensures your main crop gets all the nourishment it needs to produce a strong yield.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ amli lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ooojie lɛ haa onibii titri lɛ naa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Young cocoa plants require shade to protect them from direct, intense sunlight and high heat, which scorch their young leaves. Planting food crops like plantain alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the cocoa seedlings, retain soil moisture, and create a cooler climate until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã. Niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains ni akɛ kookoo duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ofee kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellowing of lower maize leaves usually indicates a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential food for plants to stay green and grow leaves, so when the soil runs out of it, the plant pulls whatever nitrogen is left from its older lower leaves up to its newer growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei ahi shi eŋɔli ni eye ebua amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ etee Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei heei ni daraa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I get very small maize cobs if I plant three or four seeds in every single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii waa nɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ bu fɛɛ bu mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one hole, the plants are forced to crowd each other and fight for the same water, sunlight, and plant food in that small spot. Spacing seeds out evenly allows every single stalk to get enough nutrients to build full, heavy ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, anyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa ni amɛwu amɛtao nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei niyenii yɛ nakai he bibioo lɛ. Kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli gbalamɔ nɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekɛfee ŋmei toi ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves with tiny green or brown caterpillars hiding inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli lɛ Amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Akɛtee teŋgbɛ baa lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a pest that feeds aggressively on the central growing tip (the whorl) of maize plants. Checking crops early in the morning and applying recommended natural or chemical sprays directly into the center funnel of the plant stops them before they destroy the entire yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm caterpillar, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ashishifãi (rings) lɛ waa. Kwɛmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli leebi ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ awo tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa nakai tsei lɛ kpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Does it matter which way up I bury my cassava stem cuttings when planting?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, nɛgbɛ esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji lɛ yɛ?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If buried upside down, the plant has to bend energy around to push new shoots upward and roots downward, resulting in weak growth and significantly lower tuber yields.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ afu lɛ ŋwɛi Esa akɛ tso lɛ abɔle ehewalɛ he. Koni akɛtsi tsei heei kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ shishifãi kɛba shi. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ baa ni tuber yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa.

english: Why does burning my bush to clear the land make the soil poor after just two harvest seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa koni akɛjie shikpɔŋ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ kpamɔ bei enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning land destroys organic matter—like dried leaves and decaying wood—that naturally feeds the soil and retains water. While fire gives a quick burst of ash nutrients in the first season, it bakes the soil and kills off friendly soil organisms, causing the land to dry out faster and lose fertility quickly.
ga: He ni shãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ baai ni egboi kɛ tsei ni egboi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ la haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ tswaa oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli moŋ, shi la shãa sũ lɛ ni efiteɔ sũ mli wala ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans on my land help my next crop grow better without buying chemical fertilizer?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni mahe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans have tiny beneficial bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the crop is harvested, those nitrogen stores are left behind in the earth to naturally fertilize the next crop planted in that field.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ helai bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Ashiɔ nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni adu yɛ nakai ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves upward toward the sun to catch maximum light for making food. Staking keeps the leaves dry and off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and allowing the plant to pump more energy down into growing larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã hulu lɛ nɔ koni amɛná he ko ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi fungal helai anaa Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ babaoo woɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Extreme heat causes tomato flowers to dry out and fail to pollinate properly, prompting the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy. Keeping soil evenly watered and providing partial shade during the hottest periods helps protect the blossoms so they can develop into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ̃ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ hulutsoo fã ko ha yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough moisture to start sowing my seeds at the beginning of the rainy season?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ oje dumɔwui adumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Sowing seeds into topsoil that feels wet on the surface but is dry underneath will cause the seeds to sprout and then wither when the rain pauses. Squeeze a handful of soil from a hand-depth deep; if it holds together in a ball without breaking easily, the ground has absorbed enough steady rainwater for planting.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni nuɔ he akɛ edɔ yɛ nɔ shi egbi yɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbo kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa. Mimɔ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo kɛjɛ onine mli. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he ni efee bɔɔlu ni efoŋ mlɛo Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nugbɔ nu ni yaa nɔ daa ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce large leaves that provide living shade and keep the ground moist, protecting the cocoa plants during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly in dark, overly wet, and humid conditions. Clearing farm weeds and pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm and reduce the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ fɛ̃i ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow instead of remaining deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually shows that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. It often happens when heavy rains wash away soil nutrients or when the soil lacks organic matter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Bei pii lɛ ebaa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stalks that produce very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei ni kɛlɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if the soil is too dry, if they are buried too deep, or if underground insects eat them before they germinate. Planting when the soil is damp and using clean, treated seed stock helps ensure strong sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ Aloo kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni atsa amɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole crop?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is usually mature when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, leaving bare woody stems. You can carefully dig around the base of one sample plant to check if the tubers are thick enough before harvesting the entire farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ eda kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Shi tso lɛ ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ. Obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli. Adu tso kome ni akɛfee nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ koni ana kɛji ŋmeii lɛ mli eyi obɔ bɔ ni sa dani akpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food required to build large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground where they catch more light and stay safe from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená la babaoo ni eha ehe akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as intense heat, irregular watering, or a lack of flowering nutrients like phosphorus in the soil.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ he amanehulu. aloo niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ni bɛ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by viral infections spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Covering young beds and watering consistently around the roots helps protect the plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ Saji bibii ni afee kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ he lɛ Shishifãi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Why does my farmland produce smaller harvests every year even though I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth each time they grow. Harvesting repeatedly without adding manure or fertilizer, or without letting the land rest, starves the soil and causes crop yields to decline.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa shii abɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ahaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why does my harvested rice have so many small stones and dirt mixed in it, and how does that affect what buyers pay me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ hiɛ tɛi bibii lɛ? kɛ muji babaoo ni efutu mli Ni te enɛ saa shika ni hɔlɔ lɛ woɔ mi lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dirt and stones get mixed into rice during traditional ground threshing and open drying. Clean, sieved grain fetches a higher market price because buyers and millers do not have to spend extra time and effort sorting out debris before processing or cooking.
ga: Muji kɛ tɛi futuɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ kusum naa ŋmãa ŋmɔmɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni agbiɔ yɛ faŋŋ mli lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni atsuu he ni atsɔ mli lɛ haa jara wa waa yɛ jara nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ ŋmɔji lɛ afite be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ kroko yɛ jwɛi mligbalamɔ mli dani amɛtsu he nii loo amɛhoo nii.

english: Why does my harvested grain spoil and grow mold so quickly after I put it into bags for storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya beni mikɛwo kotoku mli koni mikɛto lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil inside bags when they are bagged before being thoroughly dried. Freshly harvested crops still contain high internal moisture, which causes heat and humidity to build up inside the bag, creating the perfect conditions for mold and pests to ruin the harvest.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baafite kɛ́ awo kotoku lɛ mli dani egbi kwraa. Tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ mligbɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa lolo. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i buaa amɛhe naa yɛ kotoku lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmaa lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen in the soil or struggling with waterlogged roots. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and maintain strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli loo shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ miipiŋ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee baai eŋɔli ni amɛha amɛdara waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I cut down all the large trees on my farm land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifoɔ tsei ni eda ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight because their root systems are shallow and delicate. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as living umbrellas, shielding the tender cocoa leaves from intense heat until the trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava tubers are fully grown and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ edara kwraa ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava shows it is mature when its lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack or bulge from the expanding tubers hidden beneath the ground.
ga: Yucca tsɔɔ akɛ eda beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ loo ejɛɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmei ni eda ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why does swamp rice thrive in flooded fields while my maize rots and dies under the same wet conditions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ fiteɔ ni egboɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special air channels inside their stems and roots that allow oxygen to travel underwater, whereas maize roots do not have these channels and suffocate when buried under standing water for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui nɛɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause tomato plants to enter a survival mode. When temperatures get too high, the plant deliberately drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water rather than trying to support growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ tomato tsei ba shihilɛ mli. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛjieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oye obua aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ

english: Why do the maize seeds I saved from my previous harvest produce smaller cobs than new seeds bought from an extension dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni mijie kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa bibii fe ŋmãa heei ni mihe kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Improved commercial hybrid seeds lose their high-yielding traits after the first harvest. Replanting saved seeds results in weaker offspring with smaller cobs and uneven growth compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛfee jarayeli nibii ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ laajeɔ amɛsu ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa seshibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ kome nɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my farm soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni madu lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts team up with tiny soil organisms to catch nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in root nodules. When the plant roots rot back into the earth, that stored food stays in the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What causes my maize stalks to snap easily and show tiny holes filled with yellowish powder?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya ni amɛfeɔ buji bibii? Eyi kɛ powda ŋmɔŋ?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that tunnel into the core of the maize stalk. By eating the internal stem tissues, they strip the plant of structural support and stop water and food from reaching the top, causing the stalk to collapse.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers ni boteɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ tso lɛ mli fãji ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ Amɛgbalaa tsei ni fiɔ shishitoo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ nu kɛ niyenii naa koni ekashɛ ŋwɛi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gbeeɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong, direct sunlight and harsh wind. Scorched leaves mean the plants need shade trees, such as plantains or leguminous shade trees, grown alongside them to shield them while they are still fragile.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Baai ni shã lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo beans. Dumɔ amɛ yɛ he kome koni obu amɛhe be mli ni amɛhe waaa lolo lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves have tiny ragged holes in them while the crop is still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni etse amɛhe be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are a key sign of fall armyworm feeding on the growing leaves inside the leaf whorl. Detecting this early allows you to treat the crop before the pest destroys the center growing point of the plant.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ abɛi bibii amli lɛ ji okadi ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ asraafoi ni egbee shi lɛ yeɔ baa ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ. mra mli ni anaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ohereɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ yiwala dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni edaa yɛ lɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, leaving a bare stem, typically between 9 to 12 months after planting depending on the specific variety.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli Bei pii lɛ Enɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, nu ni bɛ, loo sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛ́ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni aha tso lɛ niyenii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I need to make high dirt mounds before planting my yam seed tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni matswa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand downwards into smooth, large tubers. Mounds also keep water from pooling around the roots, which prevents the yam seed from rotting in wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni no yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize help my soil and crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When grown near maize, they naturally feed the soil with nitrogen, which helps the maize grow stronger without needing as much added fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nitrogen lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni awo lɛ ŋmãa babaoo tamɔ nɛkɛ.

english: Why does covering the ground with dry grass around my vegetable plants help them during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi aha shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua kɛ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, blocks the sun from evaporating moisture out of the earth. It keeps the soil cool and moist so the plant roots have steady access to water.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni etsĩ hulu la lɛ naa, ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ aná nu be fɛɛ be.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the suckers keep growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mihaa ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow causes them to steal water and food from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers and keeping only one or two leaves all the plant's energy focused on producing a heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ahiɛ baa kome loo enyɔ pɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ atsu plantains babaoo ni ebaawo lɛ he nii.

english: Why should I avoid applying dry fertilizer to my crops when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer must dissolve in water before plant roots can suck it up. Applying dry fertilizer to dry soil can burn the plant roots and waste the nutrients because they sit uselessly on top of the ground.
ga: Esa akɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo nu mli dani tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei shishifãi lɛ ashã ni niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ afite ejaakɛ amɛhe ehiaaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my tomato plants turn black and die after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain splashes dirt containing fungal spores onto the lower leaves, causing fungal diseases like blight. Tying up the tomato plants to wooden stakes keeps the leaves off the ground and dry, preventing disease spread.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa muji ni ŋmeii yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli tsɛŋemɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tomato tsei fĩ tsei ahe lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shikpɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Koni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct, harsh sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil too fast. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside them protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebaabu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, an essential food for green growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it, so adding compost or fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay small even when the plants grow very tall leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyɛ baai ni kɛlɛ waa moŋ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and lacks other key nutrients like potassium, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy tops instead of expanding its underground roots. Balancing soil nutrients helps tubers grow thick.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo ni niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium bɛ mli lɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, the seeds will sprout but then dry up and die before the main, reliable rainy season truly begins.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do my pepper flowers keep falling off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or dry soil. Watering regularly during hot weather keeps the soil moist and encourages the plant to hold onto its flowers until peppers form.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baafee.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and destroy my maize leaves so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ miitutua mi ŋmãa baai lɛ oya nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths lay hundreds of hidden eggs on young leaves at night. When the caterpillars hatch, they eat non-stop to grow, making it seem like an attack happened overnight. Inspecting leaf folds early helps catch them before they multiply.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ yɛ baai bibii anɔ gbɛkɛ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛbaaye nii ni amɛkpaaa koni amɛdara. Enɛ ha efee tamɔ nɔ ni tutuamɔ lɛ ba nyɔɔŋ kome mli. Baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛfɔ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are crowded together, the young plants fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each seed proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough resources to yield big crops.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baawuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fioo. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa kã dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than the crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally survive in harsh conditions and absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the food your crops need to grow big.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa onibii koni amɛdara lɛ.

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to grow deep and wide easily. Building high mounds loosens the soil and prevents water from pooling around the tuber, which stops it from rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse koni amɛdara oya ni amɛmli alɛɛ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha nu akabɔle bulb lɛ he, ni no baaye abua ni amɛkafite.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot quickly when I store it in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Maize rots if it is stored while still carrying moisture from the farm. Sun-drying the maize cob until the grains are completely hard and dry prevents dampness, mold, and rot during storage.
ga: Abele baagbo kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Abele ŋmeii ni agbiɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees planted near them to protect their soft leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ. Enɛ ji koni baa bibii lɛ akashã, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to more light while protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃mɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni awo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Na la babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why is my maize growing thin and turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong stalks, deep green leaves, and big ears.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ adara waa. Baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ kɛ toi wuji

english: Why do farmers say that planting cowpeas or beans helps improve the soil for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpea and bean plants have helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes whatever crop you plant in that spot next.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ cowpea kɛ bean tsei amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa tso fɛɛ tso adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ he ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I spread dry fertilizer on my maize field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi shwieɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔ nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and cause the nutrients to evaporate into the air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if a cassava stem cutting is healthy enough to plant in my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: A healthy cassava cutting should leak a clear or milky sap when you slightly scratch the bark, and the small growth buds along the stem should look firm and fresh rather than dry or brown.
ga: Esa akɛ yucca tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná nu ni mli tse loo ni tamɔ mliki ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛji okɛ ŋmɔlɔ shwie shi fioo, ni esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ he lɛ afee nɔ ni wa ni efee ehee. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbi loo efee ŋmɔtɔ

english: Covering the soil with dried leaves or grass, known as mulching, prevents the hot sun from drying out the soil, stops weeds from taking over, and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaha nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do the stems of my pepper plants start to rot when there is too much rain on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants suffer in standing water because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air and allows harmful soil fungi to multiply and attack the roots and stems.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ yeɔ pepper tsei anɔ amanehulu ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni eha shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛtutua shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to save its energy instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hao lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly when weeds are growing closely around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ be mli ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight, essentially starving your crops until the weeds are removed.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ hulu la, ni amɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my crops droop during the hot afternoon sun but stand up straight again in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi shidaamɔ tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ?

english: During strong sunshine, crops lose water quickly through their leaves to stay cool, causing them to wilt slightly. When the evening arrives and temperatures cool down, the plant stops losing water so fast and restores its strength.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbɔjɔ fioo. Kɛ gbɛkɛ shɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ oya ni ebaaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Does direct sunlight help my crops grow, or can too much sun hurt them?
ga: Ani hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃? Aloo ani hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aye ŋmɔshi nibii awui?

english: Crops need sunlight to produce their food, but intense heat combined with dry soil can stress them. A balance of warm sunny days and cool evenings allows plants to grow steadily without drying out.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛna niyenii. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Gbii ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa kɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ egbɔ lɛ haa tsei yaa nɔ amɛdaraa ni amɛgbiɛɛ.

english: Why is it better to water or spray my crops early in the morning or in the evening rather than at noon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu loo mashwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: Cooler temperatures in the morning and evening prevent water and crop chemicals from evaporating too fast in the sun, giving the plants enough time to absorb what they need.
ga: He ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ lɛ haaa nu kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ yɛ hulu la mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛnu nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to apply fertilizer while my crops are growing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when crops are actively growing and the soil is moist. Applying it when the soil is wet allows the roots to easily drink up the nutrients.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni tsei miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ okɛwo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ mlɛo.

english: Should I pour fertilizer directly on the stem of my crop or put it nearby?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛma he ko ni bɛŋkɛ?

english: Always place fertilizer a few inches away from the plant's stem. Placing chemical fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant tissue and cause damage.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ fãji ni efite.

english: Is it good to apply fertilizer when the ground is dry and the sun is very bright?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni hulu lɛ miitso waa?

english: No, applying fertilizer on dry soil under hot sun can burn your crops' roots. It is best to apply fertilizer after a good rain when the ground holds enough moisture.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are crop chemicals important if I already clear my land and plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he hiaa kɛji akɛ mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni midu dumɔwui kpakpai lɛ?

english: Seeds and land clearance give crops a good start, but pests and weeds will compete with your crops for food. Chemicals protect your plants so they can reach their full harvest potential.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Shi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii. Tsofai buɔ otsei lɛ ahe koni amɛshɛ amɛkpamɔ hegbɛi lɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How do weedicides and crop sprays reduce the heavy work on my farm?
ga: Te tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nitsumɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Using recommended chemicals controls weeds and pests quickly, saving you long days of manual weeding and allowing your crops to grow without competition.
ga: Tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye jwɛi kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ oya. Ehaa onáa be babaoo yɛ jwɛi ni okɛ onine jieɔ lɛ mli. ni oye obua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Why do crops that receive extra care and input look much greener than those left alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ shihilɛ he jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni ashiɔ amɛ pɛ lɛ?

english: Crops given proper fertilizers and pest protection receive all the nutrition and health defense they need, allowing them to produce deep green leaves and strong stems.
ga: Tsei ni nine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahebuu nɔ lɛ naa niyenii kɛ hewalɛnamɔ hebuu ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai ni tsuɔ waa kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How do I make sure that the chemicals I buy will actually help my crops yield well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tsofai ni miheɔ lɛ baaye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Buy your farm chemicals from certified dealers, apply the exact right dosage recommended for your crop type, and apply them at the correct growth stage.
ga: Hemɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai kɛjɛ jarayelɔi ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Kɛ yibɔ ni sa lɛ atsu nii taakɛ atsɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct heat and harsh winds. Without enough shade trees or plantains around them, the direct sunlight scorches the foliage and dries out the soil, causing leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ he lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why is my young oil palm tree producing flowers but no actual palm fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso bibioo lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi shi ebɛ tso yibii diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Young oil palm trees produce male and female flowers separately. In early growth stages or during periods of water stress, the tree naturally produces mostly male flowers, which pollinate but do not form fruit bunches until the tree matures and receives sufficient nutrients.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. yɛ shishijee dalɛ mli loo yɛ nu mli haomɔ bei amli Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ji hii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ afee pollination shi efeŋ aduawai akui kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara jogbaŋŋ ni ená niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the ground before I get to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in waterlogged soil with poor drainage, especially after heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: Yam vines climb naturally to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Staking allows the leaves to catch light efficiently, giving the plant the energy it needs to build larger, healthier tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Staking yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ la jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains lɛ ashishi lɛ

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) forces them to compete with the main plant for water and soil food. Pruning excess suckers and leaving only two or three ensures the main plant gets enough energy to yield heavy, large bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ amɛná ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo lɛ, no haa amɛkɛ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii he. Kɛ́ afo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni tsii.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer can shock tomato plants, causing flower drop. Consistent watering and balanced nutrients help flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ ahe afee shoo, ni eha fɔfɔi lɛ agbo. Nu ni akɛhaa fɔfɔi lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap beneath the leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling pests early prevents the leaves from twisting and distorting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛjɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Early Pest Control Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkatsake.

english: Why is my maize crop turning a pale yellow color instead of a dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize turns light green or yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which the plant needs to build strong, green leaves. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizers or animal manure helps restore the natural green color and boosts growth.
ga: Abɛi feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in small bumps on their roots. When these plants die and break down in the ground, that stored nitrogen is released, acting as natural food for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛfite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Nitrogen ni ato lɛ jeɔ kpo. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my main crops grow so much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tso titri lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients directly out of the soil before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your main crops get full access to food and light.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ dani ŋmɔshi nibii shɛɔ amɛhe. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei ni yɔɔ ohe lɛ naa niyenii kɛ la babaoo.

english: Leaves turn yellow mostly when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or when heavy rains soak the ground and choke the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK, and ensuring good soil drainage, helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ bei pii kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo NPK atsu nii ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the heat gets too intense, when there is not enough water in the soil, or when the plant has too much nitrogen. Watering regularly at the base of the plant during dry spells helps the flowers stay attached and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the center shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli lɛ? Akɛtee teŋgbɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Those caterpillars are fall armyworms, a common pest that eats crop leaves rapidly during early growth. Checking your fields early and spraying recommended neem extracts or insecticides directly into the plant funnel can protect your crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ cutworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ tsei ahe baai oya yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ. Nibii ni odu lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni oooshwie nɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nibii ni oduɔ lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ abu onibii ahe.

english: How do weeds actually prevent my cassava from growing big tubers underground?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmei naa koni ekakwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Weeds compete with your cassava for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. When weeds surround young cassava plants, the crop spends its energy struggling for light rather than storing food down in its tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi bɔleɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtao la yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛyitsei amli.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my maize seeds very close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for air, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This causes the plants to grow thin and weak, resulting in very small cobs or stalks that produce no grain at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji tso loo tso bibioo ko ni dumɔwui ko kwraa bɛ mli.

english: How deep into the ground should I bury my seeds when I start planting after the rain?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ maje dumɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ Te esa akɛ mafu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ha tɛŋŋ?

english: Burying seeds too deep starves them of air and makes it hard for shoots to reach the surface, while planting too shallow leaves seeds for birds to eat. A safe general rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its size.
ga: Kɛ́ ofu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ akafee lɛ, ni ebaaha ewa aha ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛakwɛ̃. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha efee mlɛo aha okpoi akɛ amɛye. Mla ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advice me to plant plantains beside my newly planted cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ emasɛi lɛ? Kookoo tsei ni adu ehee

english: Young cocoa plants are fragile and get easily burnt by strong, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural shade umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and moist during its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya kɛji hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like cowpeas or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and naturally breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku adebɔɔ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up and look droopy during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl and droop in the hot afternoon sun to conserve internal moisture and prevent water loss. As long as the leaves bounce back and stand straight by evening or early morning, it is just the plant protecting itself from heat.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni hulutsoo ahi mli ni nu akafite. Shii abɔ ni baai lɛ baaku amɛsɛɛ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ gbɛkɛ loo leebi maŋkpa lɛ, Eji tso ko kɛkɛ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before it is time to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers rot when excess rainwater sits in heavy soil without draining, causing the roots to suffocate and decay. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps water flow away from the roots, keeping the tubers dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ehaa yitso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli.

english: If I only give my maize crop nitrogen fertilizer, will that be enough to produce a big harvest?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ nitrogen wo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli kɛkɛ lɛ, ani no baashɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo yibii babaoo?

english: No, crops need a variety of nutrients just like humans need a balanced diet. Nitrogen helps leaves grow green and broad, but crops also need phosphorus for strong roots and potassium to form heavy seeds and resist dry weather.
ga: Dabi, niyenii srɔtoi he miihia tsei tamɔ bɔ ni niyenii ni ja he hiaa adesai lɛ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ shwiili. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia phosphorus koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ, kɛ potassium hu koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ni tsii ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my tomato plants turning yellow while the top leaves stay bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older lower leaves up to the young top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa baai bibii amli koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every season when I plant maize on the exact same patch of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa be mli beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year. Rotating maize with beans, cowpeas, or groundnuts helps restore nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii, tsina ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and tall with tiny ears when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛkwɔ kɛ toi bibii beni midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete for sunlight, air, and nutrients. They stretch upward trying to reach the sun instead of putting energy into growing strong stems and full cobs.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fa tsɔ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafite amɛhewalɛ yɛ tsei ni wa kɛ tsei ni eda lɛ ahe.

english: Will leaving grass and weeds around my pepper plants affect them if I water them regularly?
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he Ani mi-pepper tsei lɛ baaná amɛnɔ hewalɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo amɛnɔ daa?

english: Yes, weeds steal water, light, and soil nutrients right from your pepper roots. Even with regular watering, weeds act like thief plants that slow down crop growth.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, jwɛi juɔ nu, la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ o-pepper lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ afɔ lɛ nu daa po lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ hu feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei julɔi ni haa tsei lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: My cassava leaves dried up and dropped off during the dry spell, but new leaves are coming now—will it recover?
ga: Mi-cassava baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ baai heei miiba. Ani ebaahe ewa lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava drops its leaves during droughts to preserve moisture. Once the rains return, it uses energy stored in its stems and roots to grow fresh leaves and continue swelling its tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ashwieɔ cassava baai yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akahi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Ebaakɛ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi amli lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai heei ni eha eshishifãi lɛ aya nɔ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants wilting in the hot sun even though the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in wet soil often means root damage or root rot caused by stagnant water or fungal disease, which prevents the roots from pumping water up to cool the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni fiteɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ ni nu ni damɔ shi loo tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛbaa. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu nɔ amɛwo ŋwɛi koni amɛha baai lɛ mli ajɔɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without forming any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when plants experience extreme heat stress, inadequate soil water, or poor air circulation, preventing the flower from setting fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Enɛ haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ nyɛɛɛ awo yibii.

english: Why should I cut away extra suckers growing around my plantain tree instead of letting them all grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain baai lɛ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mahã amɛ fɛɛ amɛdara

english: Multiple suckers compete with the main tree for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves one strong shoot to produce a large, healthy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers babaoo kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ afee plantains akuu agbo ko ni mli wa.

english: How does spreading dry grass over my yam mounds help the crop grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, protecting the soil from hot sunlight, reducing water loss, and keeping the mound cool so the yam tubers can grow large and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Buu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ nu ni laajeɔ lɛ shi ni oha gɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Koni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees slowly turning yellow and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miida fiofio lɛ? Ani obaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ogbo?

english: Cocoa trees often turn yellow and die due to viral diseases like Swollen Shoot or fungal infections. These diseases attack the tree's internal water and nutrient transport system, causing the leaves to wither and the tree to eventually die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu loo ŋmeii ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ahewɔ. Helai nɛɛ tutuaa nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Can a sick cocoa tree recover on its own if I give it extra fertilizer and water?
ga: Ani cacao tso ni hela mɔ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fata he?

english: No, serious viral diseases like Swollen Shoot cannot be cured with fertilizer or water. Fertilizer only nourishes healthy plants; applying it to an infected tree will not eliminate the virus or stop the tree from dying.
ga: Dabi, anyɛɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nu atsa helai ni mli wa ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ fãji ni efuu lɛ. Okɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ awo mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ejieee hela lɛ kɛjɛɛɛ tso lɛ mli loo ekpaaa tso lɛ gbele naa.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut down cocoa trees that are sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ bo akɛ ofolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Cutting down infected cocoa trees is the only effective way to stop viral diseases from spreading to healthy parts of your farm. Because there is no chemical cure for the virus, removing the infected host plant destroys the source of the disease.
ga: Cacao tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ anaa koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ tsofa ko bɛ ni baanyɛ atsa hela lɛ. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ fiteɔ he ni hela lɛ jɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why would I need to cut down a healthy-looking cocoa tree next to a sick one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ kookoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ emasɛi lɛ? Tso ni hela mɔ lɛ

english: Diseases often spread to neighboring trees through insects before visible signs like swollen stems or leaf yellowing appear. Removing nearby contact trees creates a safe boundary that prevents invisible infections from spreading across the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ tsɔɔ kooloi bibii anɔ egbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ. dani okadii ni anaa tamɔ tsei ni efu loo baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baaje kpo. Shikpɔŋ ahe mfoniri ni bɛŋkɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa koni helai ni anaaa lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if a cocoa tree needs to be cut down or if it just needs chemical spraying?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni mafo kookoo tso lɛ loo mikɛ tsofai afɔ nɔ kɛkɛ?

english: If a tree shows swollen stems, red leaf veins, or stunted pods, it likely has Swollen Shoot disease and must be cut down. If leaves have small holes or insect damage, it is usually caused by pests like capsids, which can be treated with approved insecticides without cutting the tree.
ga: Kɛji tso lɛ shishifãi efuu, baai lɛ ahe fãji tsuru, loo eshishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ, ekolɛ eyɛ ŋmeii ni efuu ni esa akɛ afo. Kɛji baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii loo kooloi efite lɛ Bei pii lɛ, kooloi tamɔ capsids ji nɔ ni kɛbaa, ni abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu he nii ni afooo tso lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to burn or clear diseased cocoa branches after cutting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashã loo ahoo kookoo niji ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ahe beni afo amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like mealybugs carry the virus and live in the cut branches. If left on the ground, these insects can crawl back onto remaining healthy trees; burning or clearing the wood destroys the pests and completely eliminates the risk.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs hiɛɔ hela nɛɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei niji ni afo lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baanyɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ ni ashãa loo ajieɔ lɛ kpataaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahiɛ, ni ehaa oshara ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: If my neighbor has sick cocoa trees on his farm, can the disease cross over to my farm?
ga: Kɛji mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ yɛ eŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani hela nɛɛ baanyɛ afo mli kɛba miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, diseases can spread across farm borders through crawling insects like mealybugs, shared pruning tools, or close tree canopy contact. Working with neighboring farmers to control disease on all adjacent lands helps protect everyone's yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ amli kɛtsɔ kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ tamɔ mealybugs, nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ni ajaa nɔ. loo ni akɛ tsei akutsei ni agbe naa lɛ aaabɔ Okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ahe nitsumɔ koni akɛkudɔ helai yɛ hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Does cutting down diseased cocoa trees ruin the soil for future planting?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni akɛbaadu wɔsɛɛ lɛ?

english: No, viruses like Swollen Shoot affect the living plant tissues, not the soil. Once the infected trees and root systems are cleared, the soil remains fertile and safe for planting new crops or seedlings.
ga: Dabi, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ tamɔ Swollen Shoot lɛ saa tsei ni hiɛ ka lɛ ahe, shi jeee shikpɔŋ lɛ, kɛji ajie tsei kɛ amɛshishifãi ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ pɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei heei loo dumɔwui akwɛmɔ.

english: How soon can I plant new crops on land where sick cocoa trees were cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ madu tsei heei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ oya?

english: You can plant temporary shade crops like plantains or food crops immediately after clearing the land. Once the old roots are dead and shade is established, you can plant new, disease-resistant cocoa seedlings.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains loo niyenii tsei kɛji ogbe he ni oyɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji shishifãi momo lɛ gboi ni amɛhe ejɔ amɛ lɛ, Obaanyɛ okwɛ kookoo tsei heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: Are there new cocoa tree varieties that are stronger against diseases?
ga: Ani cacao tsei srɔtoi heei ni he wa fe helai yɛ?

english: Yes, agricultural research centers in Ghana have bred improved hybrid cocoa varieties that grow faster, produce high pod yields, and show greater resistance to common pests and diseases than older traditional varieties.
ga: Hɛɛ, Okwaafoi Ahe Nibii Amli Taomɔ He ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ efee kookoo henɔi ni akɛ tsofa ebɔ he ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni baakwɛ̃ oya High pod yibiiwoo ni ejieɔ hewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛteɔ shi ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ kpo fe kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn dark green and grow faster when I put dried chicken manure around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi wo he lɛ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and other key nutrients that act as direct food for plants, helping them build strong stems and healthy green leaves quickly.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii tɛ̃ɛ kɛhaa tsei Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ oya.

english: Why does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas have beneficial bacteria in their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, providing natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites feeding on the plant's sap, or by viruses spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni yeɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do white spots appear on my cucumber leaves after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔ nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ kukumba baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: High humidity and wet conditions create the perfect environment for fungal diseases like powdery mildew to grow on plant leaves.
ga: Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ powdery mildew, ni baakwɛ̃ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from getting ruined by insects while waiting to sell to buyers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ he koni kooloi akafite lɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni ahɔ̃ɔ aha mɛi ni heɔ lɛ?

english: Drying your maize completely until the kernels are hard and storing them in hermetic (airtight) bags prevents insects like weevils from surviving and multiplying.
ga: Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii akahi shi ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when planted in direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that dry out easily; they require shade from temporary crops like plantains to protect them from heat while their roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ maa lɛ.

english: If I plant my cassava sticks very close together, will I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he waa Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too close forces the cassava plants to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, which results in thin plants with small, low-weight tubers.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmei tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛyitsei bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing fruits during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔ̃ɔ ni ewooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat combined with low moisture causes stress that prevents the flowers from successfully pollinating, causing the blossoms to fall off.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni baa shi lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni tsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkaye omanye yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ baa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does removing extra side branches from my tomato plant make the remaining tomatoes bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji niji krokomɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ haa tomato ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ wuji lɛ?

english: Pruning redirects the plant's energy and nutrients away from growing unnecessary stem leaves and focuses that energy into developing larger, healthier fruits.
ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jeɔ tso lɛ yibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe. ni okɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ awo aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ooona lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I save and plant seeds from this year's harvest of hybrid maize for next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ afi nɛɛ hybrid ŋmãa dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ toɔ ni miduɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their special yield-boosting traits after the first generation, so replanting saved seeds results in weaker plants and lower yields.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ amɛ sui ni haa yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ekoŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why is it important for me to clear and loosen my soil before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie ni majie sũ lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil before the rain allows the earth to absorb rainwater easily and lets crop roots grow deep without struggling against hard ground.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ sũ lɛ mli dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaaha efee mlɛo kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ akɛ eeemɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ. ni ehaa tsei shishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ.

english: What does it mean when an officer says good land preparation makes the soil work well?
ga: Kɛ́ onukpai kɛɛ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, mɛni ji nɔ ni amɛtsɔɔ?

english: Good preparation breaks up hard ground, buries dead weeds, and creates a soft home where crop roots can easily breathe and drink water.
ga: Hesaamɔ kpakpa baatsɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ. Fuu jwɛi ni egboi lɛ ni ofee shia ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ amu ni amɛnu nu mlɛo.

english: Why should I clear unwanted bushes and weeds from my farmland before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii kɛ jwɛi ni ataooo kɛjɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani midu nii lɛ?

english: Clearing weeds ensures that when it rains, the water and soil nutrients nourish your crops instead of feeding unwanted plants that steal their food.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, Nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ. Mohu ɔ, e haa tsehi nɛ a sume nɛ a juɔ e niye ní ɔ.

english: How do ridges or mounds help my land when the rain falls?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋshɔkei loo gɔji yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges collect fertile topsoil into soft heaps that protect crop roots from being flooded while letting excess water flow away safely.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii buaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ naa amɛfeɔ gɔŋji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni buɔ tsei shishifãi ahe kɛjɛɔ nu afua he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does heavy rain affect my farmland if I do not prepare the ground properly?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ kɛji misaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Without proper land preparation like ridges or channels, heavy rain will wash away your soft topsoil and seeds, leaving behind hard, unproductive ground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ asaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ ŋshɔkei loo ŋshɔkei lɛ, Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kɛ odumɔwui ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ. Eshiɔ he ko ni wa ni wooo yibii yɛ esɛɛ.

english: Since I cannot control when the rain falls, how do I know when it is safe to plant my crops?
ga: Ejaakɛ minyɛɛɛ makudɔ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehi akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should plant after the first steady rains have soaked deep into the ground, ensuring the soil stays moist enough for your seeds to germinate.
ga: Esa akɛ odu beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ sɛɛ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops rot when rainwater sits on my farm for too many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu hi miŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns crop roots by cutting off air in the soil, which causes the roots to rot and prevents the plant from taking in nutrients.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa niyenii.

english: How can I prevent the rain from washing away the valuable nutrients in my farm's soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ naa koni ekajie niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting across slopes or leaving cover crops reduces the speed of rainwater, allowing the water to soak into the soil while keeping the rich nutrients on your land.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ gɔji lɛ anɔ loo ashi shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu lɛ oyaiyeli lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, yɛ be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ hiɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to dead leaves and plant remains left on my land when it rains?
ga: Mɛni baa baai kɛ tsei ni egboi ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ?

english: If managed properly, dead leaves protect the soil surface from heavy raindrops and gradually decompose into natural fertilizer that enriches your land.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, baai ni egboi lɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa sɛɛnamɔ baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it good for me to apply fertilizer right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa?

english: No, heavy rainfall right after application will sweep the fertilizer away into streams before your crop roots can absorb it, wasting your money.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ baawo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛya faa lɛ mli dani otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ehaa ofiteɔ oshika.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is low in nitrogen, which plants need to build strong green leaves. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plants the food they need to stay green and produce bigger cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Why does my farmland yield smaller harvests every year if I keep planting the same crop in the same spot?
