ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ hei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pests that feed on that crop multiply. Rotating your crop with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni efo ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits stagnant around them because the soil loses oxygen. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots can breathe and remain healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ be mli ni nu lɛ ŋmɛɔ amɛhe kɛbɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, soil moisture, and food. Spacing your seeds properly ensures each plant gets enough resources to grow strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ baawu koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii fioo Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains near young cocoa provides living shade umbrellas that protect them until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: Weeds steal the valuable soil nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to thrive. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow fast and strong.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛshwere. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa tsei ni okwɛɔ amɛ lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛhe wa lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ewooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when intense heat or dry soil stresses the plant, preventing proper pollination. Watering consistently and providing light shade during extremely hot periods keeps the flowers healthy so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, ni ekɛ haomɔ baa tso lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ pollination ni sa naa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why should I pinch off the small extra side shoots growing on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Extra side shoots consume nutrients that the plant could otherwise use to grow big fruits. Pruning unnecessary branches directs the plant's energy toward producing larger, higher-quality peppers.
ga: Lateral shoots lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ ekɛtsu nii ni ekɛwo aduawai wuji. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baakudɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put all my fertilizer into the soil at the same time I sow my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kome too mli ni miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Young seeds do not have developed roots to soak up large amounts of fertilizer right away, causing rain to wash most of it away. Applying fertilizer in split stages as the crop grows ensures nutrients are available when the plant needs them most.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo shikome. Ha nugbɔ anɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo ashwie. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ miida lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa be mli ni tsei lɛ he hiaa amɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest grow weaker plants than the certified hybrid seeds I buy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔ fe dumɔwui ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni awo he odaseyeli ni mihe lɛ?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specially bred for strong growth and high yields in their first generation. Replanting saved seeds causes the crop to lose those special high-yielding traits, resulting in smaller plants and lower production.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni awo he odase lɛ mli krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amɛ su ni haa amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ bibii, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: When is the right time to start applying fertilizer to my young maize seedlings?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi mi-bibii ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fɔmɔ?

english: Young maize seedlings need about 10 to 14 days after germinating to establish basic root systems before they can safely absorb nutrients without burning.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abifabii abele dumɔwui lɛ aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 yɛ amɛkwɛ̃mɔ sɛɛ koni amɛto shishijee shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo ko shishi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni amɛshãaa lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I know if my tomato seedlings are ready to be transplanted into my main farm field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaawo miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Tomato seedlings are ready to be moved when they have grown 3 to 4 true leaves and a sturdy stem, which usually occurs 3 to 4 weeks after sowing in the seedbed.
ga: Tomato dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaadu amɛ kɛji amɛyɛ baai diɛŋtsɛ 3 kɛyashi 4 kɛ ŋmeii ni wa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa yɛ otsii 3 kɛyashi 4 sɛɛ beni adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, protecting them until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa diɛŋtsɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛ cocoa tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Buu nakai tsei lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava plants naturally drop or curl their leaves during dry periods to reduce water loss and protect themselves from heat, allowing the crop to survive until rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ nɛɔ.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from high temperatures, excessive drought, or poor soil nutrients, as they cannot support fruit development under stress.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ ji akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛha aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ shishi.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly into tubes on hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll inward as a self-defense mechanism to minimize the leaf area exposed to the sun, which conserves moisture inside the plant during hot hours.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants fall over so easily during heavy wind and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and top-heavy fruit bunches, making them unstable in strong winds unless they are supported with wooden props or protected by windbreaks.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni ŋmeii ni tsii yɔɔ mli. Enɛ haaa amɛhi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. ja akɛ tso fiɔ amɛsɛɛ loo abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seeds after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to germinate aggressively with very little water, whereas farm crops take longer to absorb water and wake up from their dormant state.
ga: Afee jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛmuɔ nu ni amɛteɔ shi kɛjɛɔ amɛshihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds away while my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ yɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops have delicate roots and cannot compete with weeds, which quickly steal essential sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients needed for early crop growth.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi abɔ akaŋ. Enɛ juɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cowpea plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young leguminous crops like cowpea usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or overwatering, which prevents roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu ewo mli fe nine. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Yam tubers grow crooked when the soil is too hard or stony for them to push through easily. Building big, soft soil mounds or ridges gives the tubers space to stretch out and grow large.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi yɛ mli tsɔ ni enyɛŋ ebote mli mlɛo. Gɔji loo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni afeɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛshwereɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow from the tip towards the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ kɛyashiɔ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the leaf tip indicate that your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Applying NPK or urea fertilizer near the base helps the plant stay green and grow strong ears.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ he miihia o-ŋmã lɛ. NPK loo urea ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhaa amɛtoi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn black and rot before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ ashishigbɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Dark spots at the bottom of peppers are caused by a lack of calcium or inconsistent watering while the fruit is forming. Keeping the soil evenly moist and adding compost or agricultural lime helps prevent this.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni faaa loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fũu daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why does my rice crop fall flat on the ground right before it is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Rice stalks fall over when they grow too tall and top-heavy, often from receiving too much nitrogen fertilizer early on. Using balanced fertilizer and planting varieties with stronger stalks keeps the crop standing upright.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ amɛkwɔ tsɔ ni amɛtsii. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni anáa mra. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja kɛ tsei sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ shishifãi ni wa tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by hot dry weather, poor nutrients, or damage from sap-sucking insects like mirids. Protecting the trees from harsh weather and controlling pests helps the flowers develop into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. niyenii ni ehiii loo nɔ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mirids lɛ fiteɔ. Tso lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai ahe kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds in well-drained soil prevents waterlogging and rot during heavy rains.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by a soil disease like bacterial wilt that blocks water from moving up inside the stem. Rotating your tomato crop to a new plot each season keeps this disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ hela ko, tamɔ bacteria wilt, ni haa nu nyɛɛɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛya tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ shwieɔ shi trukaa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ otsake tomato ni oduɔ lɛ daa afi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Tiny holes on leaves are caused by small caterpillars like the diamondback moth feeding on the plant. Spraying with neem leaf extract or approved pest controls protects the leaves so the cabbage can form a tight head.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛ ŋmeii bibii, tamɔ diamondback ŋmei, ni yeɔ tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni kaabe lɛ aná yitsei ni mli wa.

english: Why are my garden egg leaves curling up and sticky to the touch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he kɛji mɔ ko ta he lɛ?

english: Curled, sticky leaves are caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and leaving a sugary waste. Spraying soapy water or neem oil on the underside of the leaves washes away these pests.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle, ni wa baa. Ekɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee loo neem fɔ shwie baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ atsu nii.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is lacking nitrogen, which gives plants green energy and strength. This often happens when the soil is worn out or when heavy rains wash away nutrients from the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni ji eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ elaaje kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my crops growing so small and weak even though I planted them right when the rains started?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ kɛji nugbɔ je shishi pɛ kɛkɛ?

english: When crops stay stunted, the soil is often hungry and lacks essential nutrients, or it has become too hard for the roots to spread. Adding cow dung, poultry manure, or compost feeds the soil so roots can grow deep and strong.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ yeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmei, kooloi ŋmei, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants keep dropping off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from intense sun heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. When the plant feels stressed, it drops flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi ashwie shi koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to each other to try to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛfee nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete like crowded people sharing one small bowl of food. They fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin plants that produce very little yield.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tamɔ gbɔmɛi babaoo ni miija niyenii tsɛnsii bibii lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do people tell me not to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ mikadu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same food from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground. Alternating with beans, groundnuts, or cowpeas restores nitrogen naturally into your soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo tsina ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I plant plantains next to my young tree crops on a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu plantains yɛ tsei bibii ahe yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight like small babies. Plantains grow fast and have giant leaves that provide natural umbrella shade and keep the soil moist while your main tree crop gets established.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi tamɔ gbekɛbii bibii. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni oduɔ otso titri lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves roll up and droop in the afternoon even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ moŋ?

english: Leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water during peak sun heat. If your soil lacks organic material like decayed leaves or manure, it cannot hold water for long, causing crops to dry out quickly between rains.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu akaje mli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛŋ ahi nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Why do my crops turn yellow and rot when water stays on the farm for a few days after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ beni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When excess water sits on the field with nowhere to drain, the roots drown, rot, and can no longer pull up nutrients to feed the rest of the plant.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ta ŋmɔ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛgbala niyenii ni haa tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ sɛɛ dɔŋŋ.

english: What causes holes in my crop leaves and why is it making my whole farm perform poorly?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bulɛ baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ amli? Ni mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Holes are caused by insect pests like caterpillars feeding on the leaves. Leaves act as the engine that makes food for the plant using sunlight; when insects destroy them, the plant starves and cannot produce good yields.
ga: Buji jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli. Baai tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ afeɔ niyenii ahaa tsei kɛtsɔ hulu la nɔ. Kɛ́ kooloi bibii kpata amɛhiɛ Tso lɛ hɔmɔ baaye lɛ ni enyɛŋ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: How can I test if the leftover seeds I saved from last year's harvest will grow well before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji dumɔwui ni eshwɛ ni mikɛto kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ dani adu?

english: Wrap ten seeds in a wet cloth and keep it in a warm place for five days. If eight or more sprout, your seeds are strong and good to plant; if only a few sprout, the seed batch is weak and will fail in the field.
ga: Okɛ mama ni mli efɔ abɔ dumɔwui nyɔŋma he ni okɛto he ko ni mli edɔ gbii enumɔ. Kɛji ŋmeii kpaanyɔ loo nɔ ni fe nakai Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ odumɔwui lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛmiida jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji dumɔwui fioo komɛi pɛ kwɛ̃ Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaafite yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the plants fight each other for sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. This results in weak, thin stalks and small cob yields instead of healthy crops.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii feɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Curling yellow leaves on cassava usually indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease reduces the plant's ability to make food and severely shrinks root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii lɛ baa shi, ni efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ waa.

english: Insects called maize weevils burrow inside dry grains to feed and lay eggs. They destroy the inside of the kernel and leave behind dust unless the grain is properly dried, treated, or stored in airtight bags.
ga: Kplukai ni atsɛɔ amɛ corn weevils lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii ni amɛwo amɛwui. Efiteɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli ni eshiɔ sũ yɛ sɛɛ. ja agbi ŋmaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ, atsu he nii loo akɛto vacuum kotoku mli.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on my plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, naturally restoring soil fertility for heavy-feeding crops like maize in the next season.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛo aha niyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli.

english: If your previous harvest was very small, or if plants on that land grow slowly with pale green or yellow leaves, the soil is low on nutrients and needs compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ faaa kwraa loo tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without growing any peppers when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes heat stress in pepper plants, making them shed their flowers to save water and survival energy rather than spending resources on producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa pepper tsei amli. Ha amɛshwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii koni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why should I cut off the lower leaves and suckers from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli baai kɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Removing low leaves prevents soil-borne fungal diseases from splashing onto the plant during rains and directs the plant's energy into growing larger fruits instead of extra leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akashwie tsei lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛwo aduawai wuji moŋ fe ni okɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with deep root systems that absorb rainwater and soil food instantly, allowing them to outgrow cultivated crop seedlings unless cleared early.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni wa ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni ŋmɛɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe tsei amli dumɔwui ja ajie amɛ oya.

english: Why do some of the seeds I bought fail to sprout after I plant and water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛɛɛ beni adu ni awo nɔ nu lɛ?

english: Seeds may fail to germinate if they are old, damaged by insects during storage, kept in hot conditions, or planted too deep in the soil where oxygen cannot reach them.
ga: Ekolɛ dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. Kplukai fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Okɛto he ko ni mli edɔ. aloo adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ tsɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ mli

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. When nutrients are scarce in the soil, the plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences environmental stress, such as extremely hot daytime temperatures, prolonged dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ kɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ kpe. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi be kakadaŋŋ. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe aduawai.

english: Why does my groundnut plant bend its flowers down into the soil after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally perform a process called 'pegging.' After the flower is pollinated above ground, the stem grows downwards into the soil so that the actual peanut pods can safely grow and mature underground.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ tsɔɔ gbɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ‘fixation’ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ajie fɔfɔi lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Tsoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do small green cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before growing into big pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji Kɛyashi ebaagbo ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani eda ni etsɔ ŋmeii agbo lɛ?

english: This is often caused by 'cherelle wilt,' a natural self-thinning process where the cocoa tree drops excess pods it cannot feed. However, severe dry weather or insect attacks can also trigger this extra pod loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ‘cherelle wilt’ ni ji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kakao tso lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ he ni enyɛŋ eye nii yɛ lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi waa loo kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ hu baanyɛ aha nɛkɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi nɛɛ afite.

english: Why are my plantain stalks snapping and falling over near the root even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ fãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees collapse easily when underground pests like root nematodes or stem borer weevils burrow inside the stem base and roots, destroying the plant's structural foundation.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ root nematodes loo stem borers lɛ bote tso lɛ shishi kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. ni fiteɔ tsei lɛ ashishitoo mlai lɛ

english: Why are there big holes in my cabbage leaves and white butterflies flying around my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kaabeji baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ miiho kɛmiibɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ bu agbo ko.

english: The white butterflies lay eggs on the leaves, which hatch into small green caterpillars. These caterpillars eat large holes in the cabbage leaves, preventing the cabbage from forming a solid, healthy head.
ga: Kpɔŋɔi yɛŋ fɔɔ amɛwui yɛ baai anɔ. Kɛkɛ ni efɔ ni etsɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ bu agboi ni yɔɔ kaabe baa mli lɛ. Enɛ haaa cabbage lɛ aná yitso ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn brown and dry up at the leaf edges in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ baai lɛ ahe yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots that cannot pump water fast enough under full sun. They need shade crops like plantains overhead to protect them from intense sunlight and retain moisture around them.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ ajie nu oya bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ he miihia amɛ. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb instead of spreading on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso kakadaŋŋ ni ekɛkwɔ moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Extra sunlight helps the leaves manufacture more energy, resulting in larger yam tubers under the ground.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la babaoo aná bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la ni fa fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are mature enough to harvest without digging up the farm?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei lɛ shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa ni akuuu mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the leaves near the bottom turn yellow and drop off, the leaf stems turn dark, and visible cracks appear in the soil surface around the main stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni bɛŋkɛ shishi lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Baai lɛ ahe tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle tso lɛ tso wulu lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants roll up tightly into tubes during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Corn plants curl their leaves as a protective mechanism during hot hours. Rolling reduces the surface area exposed to direct sunlight, helping the crop conserve internal water during hot periods.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ akɛ hebuu gbɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be mli. Rolling haa hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he yɛ amɛmli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut trees turning yellow and dropping off before the fruits are ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛyibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often signal early stages of lethal yellowing disease or severe nutrient deficiencies. When trees lose leaves prematurely, they lose their ability to produce energy, which eventually causes the tree to dry up and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ hela ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ shishijee mli loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa. Kɛ tso ko baai lɛ fite mra lɛ Ebaafee nɔ ni nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbiɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egboɔ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are just wilted from heat or actually infected with a sickness?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo kɛkɛ kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ mli loo hela emɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Heat-wilted crops usually droop during the hottest part of the day and recover in the cool evening or after watering. Sick plants will show spots, stem discoloration, or rotting that do not go away regardless of water or temperature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli waa lɛ mli. Ni ebaahe ejɔ lɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo yɛ nu ni awo lɛ sɛɛ. Tso ni hela mɔ lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kpo. tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ loo efiteɔ ni eyaaa ekɔɔɔ he eko nu loo latsaa.

english: How does a crop disease move from an infected tree to a healthy one far away on my farm?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni tsei ahe helai jɛɔ tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni kɛ miŋmɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Diseases travel through wind-borne fungal spores, splashing rainwater, contaminated soil on farm boots, or sap-feeding insects like beetles and leafhoppers that fly between plants.
ga: Helai tsɔɔ ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa lɛ amli. nugbɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi Shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tokotai anɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ nu tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni foɔ yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ.

english: Can using my cutlass on a sick crop spread the sickness to my healthy plants?
ga: Ani mi-dagger ni mikɛtsu nii yɛ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã mitsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, farm tools like cutlasses and pruning shears transfer infected sap directly into the open wounds of healthy plants. Cleaning tools with soapy water or bleach between trees stops this spread.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔ mli nibii tamɔ dade kɛ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ tsuɔ nu ni hela emɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ apilamɔi ni agbele naa lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛ saamɔ nu loo bleach tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei ateŋ lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why did my mature tree suddenly dry up and die within just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni eda lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigboi yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rapid tree death usually happens when a root rot disease or stem borer pest attacks the internal water-transport system, cutting off water and food supply from the roots to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso gbele oya baa kɛ́ shishifãi ni egbo loo kooloi ni boteɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tutua nu ni akɛyaa mli lɛ. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni afoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do diseases seem to kill older trees on my farm while young ones stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni hela gbeɔ tsei ni edara yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be mli ni tso bibioo lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: Older trees often have weaker immune systems and accumulated root damage over the years, making them less able to fight off deep trunk or root infections compared to energetic young saplings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ ahewalɛ ni gbeɔ helai lɛ egbɔjɔ, ni amɛshishifãi ni efite lɛ ebua amɛhe naa yɛ afii babaoo mli. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛwu amɛshi helai ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi loo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops get sick more often during the rainy season than during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: High humidity, moist soil, and wet leaf surfaces during the rainy season create the ideal environment for fungal spores and bacteria to multiply and infect plant leaves.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ baai ni mli efɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal kɛ bacteria spores ni baafa ni amɛye tsei baai lɛ anɔ hela.

english: Why does a crop sickness suddenly destroy my farm this year when I haven't seen it for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso hela ko kpata miŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ trukaa afi nɛɛ be mli ni minako lɛ afii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Disease pathogens can survive quietly in soil or wild weeds for years until specific weather conditions, like prolonged rainfall or unusual humidity, trigger a massive outbreak.
ga: Muawai baanyɛ ahi shi dioo. yɛ shikpɔŋ loo jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli afii babaoo Kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi komɛi tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ loo hulutsoo ni ejaaa baaha hela wulu ko aba.

english: If my cassava plants die from root sickness, can I plant new cassava in that exact spot right away?
ga: Kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ gboi yɛ shishifã hela hewɔ Ani manyɛ madu cassava hee yɛ nakai he lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, because disease organisms remain active in the soil long after the plant dies. Replanting the same crop immediately exposes new roots to the same disease; rotating to a different crop like maize gives the soil time to clean itself.
ga: Dabi, ejaakɛ helai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yaa nɔ amɛtsuɔ nii yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ tso lɛ gbele sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi heei lɛ aná hela kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ atsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛtsuuɔ ehe.

english: Will applying fertilizer cure my crops once they start showing signs of rotting?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ehere miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala kɛji amɛje shishi amɛjie fitemɔ he okadii akpo?

english: Fertilizer feeds the plant but does not kill the disease causing the rot. In fact, adding too much nitrogen fertilizer to a sick plant can make its tissues softer and more vulnerable to further decay.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii shi egbeee helai ni haa tsei fiteɔ lɛ. Yɛ anɔkwale mli lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo fata tso ni hela mɔ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha efãji lɛ afee blɛoo ni ebaanyɛ egbo oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my plantain suckers turning yellow and drying up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require a lot of water to keep their large leaves healthy. During the harmattan or dry season, intense sun and water stress cause the outer leaves to dry up as the plant conserves moisture for its main stem and growing central leaf.
ga: Nu babaoo he miihia plantains koni ekwɛ̃ baai wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ harmattan loo hulutsoo be mli lɛ Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nu mli baa lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ buɔ ŋmɔtɔ he kɛhaa eshishifã titri lɛ kɛ baai ni miida yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen all at once so quickly after I cut the bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Once a plantain bunch is cut from the stem, it naturally releases ethylene gas, which triggers rapid ripening. If bunches are kept in a warm area or tightly packed together, heat and gas build up, causing the whole batch to ripen simultaneously.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo plantains kuu ko kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ Ejieɔ ethylene gas yɛ ebɔɔ su mli, ni no haa ekwɛɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ akɛ kuu lɛ to he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo akɛto he kome lɛ, Dɔlɛ kɛ gas baabua amɛhe naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii muu lɛ fɛɛ shwereɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Leaving too many suckers causes them to compete with the mother plant for soil nutrients and water. Removing extra suckers leaves just one or two strong stems, allowing the main tree to produce a much bigger and heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛkɛ tso nyɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii ni dara ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my cassava stems produce very big roots while others only give me thin roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi wuji waa lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsei komɛi woɔ shishifãi bibii pɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots swell large when planted in loose, well-drained soil with plenty of space. If the soil is hard and compacted, or if plants are squeezed too close together, the roots struggle to expand and remain thin.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛji adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbɛ fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni ebɔle ehe loo kɛji akɛ atswa tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni ebaawa akɛ aaakwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting roots and shoots even when I keep them inside my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shishifãi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers are living plant stems in a resting phase. As the season changes, natural internal signals tell the tuber it is time to grow, causing sprouts to emerge even without water or soil.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii ji tso ni hiɛ ka lɛ shishifãi yɛ wɔɔhe be mli. Beni bei lɛ tsakeɔ Adebɔɔ mli okadii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ kɛji nu loo sũ bɛ po.

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm. The parent moths lay eggs on the plant, and the hatching caterpillars feed on the soft green leaf tissue, particularly inside the central leaf funnel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei yoo ni woɔ ewui yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa. Ni ŋmeii ni fɔɔ lɛ yeɔ baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot. It happens when tomato plants do not get enough calcium or when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, preventing the plant from sending necessary minerals to the tip of the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Etsĩɔ tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekatsu nibii ni he hiaa waa lɛ kɛya aduawai ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before producing small cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwo cacao ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience environmental stress such as hot dry spells, insufficient shade, or poor pollination. Maintaining shade trees and soil moisture helps flowers stay attached to form healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ kpe. Shade ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ahi shade mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: How can I tell if my soil is missing nutrients without paying for a lab test?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni miwooo laboratori mli kaai ahe nyɔmɔ?

english: You can read the leaves of your crops. Stunted growth, pale yellow leaves (nitrogen deficiency), or purplish leaf edges (phosphorus deficiency) are clear signs that the soil lacks key nutrients needed for crop development.
ga: Obaanyɛ okane oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai. Dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, baai ŋmɔŋ (nitrogen bɛ) loo baa lɛ naa purple. Fosforo ni faaa (fosforo ni bɛ) ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants naturally adapted to local soils and tough weather conditions. They have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔji kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛyɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe bɔ ni tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee.

english: Young cocoa plants are very delicate and cannot handle direct sunlight. Big shade trees act like umbrellas to protect cocoa leaves from scorching heat and retain moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa kwraa, ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni eda ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food and grow big tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛhoo ni amɛkwɛ bulbs wuji. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo aba ni ekɛtsi baa helai ni shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ kɛbaa lɛ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to make green leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will restore their green color and help them grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on the same field make my maize grow better afterwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the bean family, which has the natural ability to pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This enriches the ground with natural fertilizer for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni amɛyɛ adebɔɔ mli nyɛmɔ ni amɛkɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ.

english: Why should I avoid putting chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei ahe lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fertilizers are concentrated salts. If placed directly against the plant stem or leaves, they burn the plant tissue and pull moisture out of the root system, which can stunt or kill the crop.
ga: Fertilizer ji ŋmei ni mli eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛwo tso shishifãi loo baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Tso lɛ mli fãji lɛ shãa ni egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground if I don't harvest them before heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ akpaaa amɛ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with water for days, air cannot reach the cassava roots. Starved of oxygen in waterlogged soil, the roots rot quickly due to soil fungi.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu yiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. Yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: When heat is too intense or water is scarce, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and energy. Without healthy flowers remaining on the plant, fruits cannot form.
ga: Kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nu faaa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛji fɔfɔi ni hi jogbaŋŋ eshwɛɛɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ Yibii nyɛŋ afee.

english: Why do I see ragged holes in my young maize leaves and soft brown powder in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe baai kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls inside the rolled leaves at the center of the plant to feed where it is safe from sun and predators, leaving behind damaged leaves and waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ. Ekɛ ehe shwieɔ baai ni abɔle ehe ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni eyatao niyenii yɛ he ko ni hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ nyɛŋ abote lɛ. Eshiɔ baai ni efite kɛ jwɛi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and turning small and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny pests like aphids or thrips sucking the juice from under the leaves, or transmitting a virus that distorts how the leaf grows.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ. loo egbɛɔ helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ eshwaa.

english: Why do wild weeds grow faster and stronger than my planted crops even when planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ani adu yɛ be kome mli?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive hard conditions. Their roots spread faster to steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight before your crops get a chance to establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya koni amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛtswa amɛhe shi.

english: If I cut or tap into my cocoa tree trunk, does it weaken the tree or drain its water?
ga: Kɛ mifo loo mitswa kookoo tso lɛ Ani ebaagbɔjɔ loo ebaaha nu atsɔ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cutting or tapping into a cocoa tree trunk creates open wounds that cause the tree to lose water and essential nutrients. It stresses the plant, leaves it vulnerable to pests and diseases, and reduces its strength to produce healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo loo atswa kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ehaa pilamɔ ni mli tse ni haa tso lɛ náaa nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ haoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ lɛ oya ni ehaa hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛbaafee tsɛŋemɔ helai ni mli wa lɛ baa shi

english: Does trimming extra branches help my crop produce more yield?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ baaye abua ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, pruning unnecessary or dead branches allows the tree to direct its energy, water, and soil nutrients into flowering and growing healthy pods rather than wasting energy on extra leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni egboi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛhaa fɔfɔi kɛ pod ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: How do cocoa trees behave when the dry Harmattan season arrives?
ga: Te kookoo tsei feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: During dry weather, cocoa trees lose moisture rapidly through their leaves. To protect themselves, they may shed older leaves to save water, which is why keeping soil covered with dry leaves or mulch helps store moisture around the roots.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Cacao tsei lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. koni obu ohe he Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie baai ni egbɔ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Why do I need to keep shade trees over my young cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ he hiaa mi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight without getting burned. Shade trees act like giant umbrellas, keeping the air cool and humid while protecting young seedlings from losing too much water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛshãaa amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela wuji. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ ni edɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ fe nine lɛ he.

english: When trees are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, and their canopy blocks sunlight. This competition makes all the plants weaker and reduces your overall harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tso shishifãi wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ haa hulu lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my crop plants look weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crops to stay strong. Plants need essential nutrients from healthy soil to grow, so if the soil is worn out or poor, the crops will stay weak despite getting plenty of water.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii ahi shi shiŋŋ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ efite loo ehiii Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ kɛji amɛná nu babaoo po.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has lost its strength?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ?

english: If your crops grow slowly, leaves become pale or yellow, and your yield drops year after year despite good weather, the soil has likely run out of essential nutrients and needs organic manure or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Ni onibii ni ofeɔ lɛ baa shi afi fɛɛ afi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hi po. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hu bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni ehe hiaa humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: How should I prepare the ground before planting new seedlings?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Preparing good soil involves clearing weeds without burning them off completely, loosening compacted earth so roots can spread easily, and adding organic compost to help the ground hold onto water and nutrients.
ga: Nɔ ni fata shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ ni ashãaa amɛ fɛɛ. Gbalamɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo. Ni okɛ organic compost afata he koni eye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of my young cocoa pods shrivel up and die before growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: When a tree lacks enough water, shade, or nutrients, it cannot support all its growing pods. It naturally drops small pods—a process called cherelle wilt—to save its strength for the remaining crop.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu, hulutsoo, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ po nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. Ejieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni ji nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherry wilt lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: What causes crop leaves to turn yellow and fall off early?
ga: Mɛni haa tso baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a problem with root health, nutrient shortages in the soil, or attacks by sap-sucking insects that drain the sap and water directly from the plant's leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ naagbai ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ ahewalɛ he. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni nuɔ nu ni shwieɔ nu kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tutuamɔ.

english: Those are likely fall armyworms, a common pest that feeds on young maize leaves. Checking your farm early and applying recommended treatments or neem extracts when the plants are small protects the crop before major damage happens.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji cutworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii beni tsei lɛ darako lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani nɔ ko ni naa wa aba.

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems from trusted suppliers stops the sickness from spreading across your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ lɛ. Kɛ okɛ cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ baatsu nii Ebaatsi hela ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ naa.

english: Maize uses up specific nutrients from the soil very fast. Changing crops every season—like planting beans or groundnuts after maize—helps the soil regain its strength and breaks pest cycles naturally.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii oya. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa be, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil lacks the food my crops need to grow well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops grow very slowly, have pale green or yellow leaves, or produce small fruits despite getting enough rain, your soil is low on nutrients and needs compost, manure, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo waa Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ aduawai bibii Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Yam plants need their leaves high in the sunlight to make energy. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet ground to prevent fungal diseases and helps the plant produce bigger tubers below the soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia baai ni hulu la babaoo shɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the main plantain tree for soil food and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree grows strong and bears large bunches of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwui titrii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada waa ni ewo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle full, harsh sunshine. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains near young cocoa shelters them from direct sun heat and keeps moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa kwraa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ he. ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Why do my tomato plants rot and die during heavy rain even though crops need water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia tsei lɛ moŋ?

english: Too much standing water around tomato roots chokes them and encourages root diseases. Planting tomatoes on raised soil beds allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: nu ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tomato shishifãi babaoo tsɔ baatsi amɛnaa ni ewo shishifã hela he hewalɛ. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do my pepper seeds fail to grow when I plant them directly in my main farm field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds are small and delicate, so heavy rain or hard soil easily destroys them. Starting them in a protected nursery bed gives them soft soil and care until they are strong seedlings ready for the main farm.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ daraaa ni amɛhe waaa. No hewɔ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo shikpɔŋ ni wa fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ oya. Aje tsei ashishi yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni abuɔ he kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui ni he wa ni asaa amɛhe kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants have healthy green leaves but very few nuts under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants need loose, soft soil so their flower stems can easily push underground to form pods. If the soil is too hard or packed tightly, the stems cannot penetrate it to grow nuts.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia ŋmei tsei bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi oya koni amɛfee ŋmeii. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ Tso lɛ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli ni ekɛdu ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize lacks nitrogen, which is a vital nutrient plants use to make food and grow strong. It can also happen if the field is flooded and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains all the specific nutrients maize needs from the soil and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the ground.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa abɛi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale or yellowish leaves, or gave very small harvests despite good rain, your soil is likely low in nutrients and needs manure or commercial fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo lɛ Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔŋ loo ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ babaoo nɛɔ moŋ Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ hu nɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ faaa ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large trees provide gentle shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until its roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo be blɛoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ mli baawo wu bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I wait for the main rainy season before transplanting my pepper seedlings into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ amɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ dani adu pepper dumɔwui awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Young pepper seedlings have fragile roots that dry out easily. Planting them at the start of the rainy season ensures they get reliable water to establish roots without dying from heat stress.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni egbiɔ oya. Dumɔ ni aduɔ mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ haa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni hulutsoo be mli haomɔ gbooo.

english: How long does a new plantain sucker take to give me a full bunch of fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani plantain sucker hee ko woɔ aduawai babaoo?

english: A plantain sucker typically takes about 9 to 12 months to produce a flower, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to fully mature for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain suckers lɛ heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes in the middle leaves of my corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the central leaf whorl of maize to feed on tender growth, which can severely reduce your yield if left untreated.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmãa ni dalɛ yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha onibii lɛ aba shi waa kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava root rot is caused by fungal diseases that thrive in poorly drained, waterlogged soil, or when pests cut the underground roots and let infection in.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni amɛhaa amɛhe tsɛŋeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that are naturally adapted to quickly grab water and soil nutrients faster than domestic crops, which take more time to build root systems.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛjie nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe shia tsei. ni heɔ be babaoo dani atswaa shishifãi lɛ

english: Tomato flowers drop off when daytime temperatures get too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks essential nutrients needed to hold and form fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhe akpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make green food. Adding compost, manure, or a small amount of NPK fertilizer around the base restores their green color and boosts growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee niyenii ni ji eŋɔli Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo NPK ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko baafata he Shishitoo lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Growing cassava continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating cassava with legumes like groundnuts refills the soil's nutrients naturally.
ga: Cassava ni aduɔ lɛ yaa nɔ ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Cassava ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛtsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does planting cowpeas help make my farm's soil richer for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cowpea roots trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop finishes growing, that trapped food stays in the soil to help whatever you plant next grow strong.
ga: Cowpea shishifãi mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ eda kwraa Niyenii ni ekpɛtɛ he lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eye ebua nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ ni ehiɛ wa.

english: Crowding seeds forces crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in weak plants with tiny harvests. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow big and yield heavily.
ga: Dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Young crops are fragile and easily choked out by fast-growing weeds that steal sunlight, space, and water. Clearing weeds early gives young plants the head start they need to outgrow competitors.
ga: Nibii bibii ni aduɔ lɛ waaa ni jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni juɔ hulu la, ŋwɛi kɛ nu lɛ haa amɛhe oya. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ fe akaŋshilɔi lɛ.

english: Why am I advised to pinch off the small side branches growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ

english: Removing these extra shoots, called suckers, directs the plant's energy away from useless leaf growth and forces it to produce bigger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmeii lɛ ajiemɔ Enɛ baajie tso lɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ adalɛ mli. ni enyɛ tomato nɔ koni ewo tomato ŋmɔshi nibii ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a plant's natural way of saving water during extreme heat. Spreading dry grass or straw around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist, reducing heat stress on the pepper plants.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni baa pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: What causes small ragged holes in my maize leaves with sawdust-like dirt inside the growing top?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: This damage comes from Fall Armyworms that eat the soft center of young maize plants. Checking crops early and applying recommended treatments like neem extract or biopesticides protects your yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ jɛɔ Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ hei ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli lɛ amli. Nibii ni akwɛɔ mli mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baaye abua ni abu onibii ahe.

english: Should I apply chemical fertilizer right when I put the seed in the hole or wait?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ awo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ́ miidu dumɔwui yɛ bu lɛ mli loo esa akɛ mamɛ?

english: Seeds already hold enough energy to sprout, and putting strong fertilizer directly on a seed can burn tender young roots. It is best to wait a few weeks after germination when green leaves appear and roots are ready.
ga: Dumɔwu lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli edɔ wo dumɔwui lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi bibii lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ otsii fioo komɛi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ beni baai eŋɔlii lɛ jeɔ kpo ni shishifãi lɛ efee klalo lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get tiny holes and turn to powder after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni etsɔɔ powda beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: Grains stored with hidden moisture attract insects like weevils that eat the inside of the grain. Sun-drying grains until they are completely hard and dry before storing them in airtight bags keeps pests out.
ga: Nibii ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni yeɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa dani okɛwo vacuum kotokui amli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why does my land stop producing good yields after I use strong chemical weedkillers for many years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ekpa ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai awomɔ beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa tsu nii afii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: While weedkillers quickly destroy unwanted plants, overuse can also harm the tiny living organisms in the soil that break down organic matter and feed your crops, eventually leaving the soil weak and barren.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ oya. Shi kɛ akɛtsu nii fe nine lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye bɔɔ nii bibii awui. yɛ shikpɔŋ ni fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ amli ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbiɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow even after I apply chemical fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? He ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ewo ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant roots cannot absorb nutrients. This can happen if the soil is too dry, if the soil is too acidic, or if heavy rain washed the fertilizer away before the roots could take it in.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ shishifãi nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aba mli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ acid tsɔ Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: How can I tell if my farmland soil is healthy and rich before I start planting my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, feels soft and crumbly when you squeeze it, holds moisture without staying waterlogged, and naturally contains earthworms and decaying leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe ke a ngɔ lɛ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ehiɛɛɛ mli. Ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ hu yɛ.

english: Why does leaving my land to rest for a season without planting anything make the next harvest better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni ashiɔ yɛ be kome mli ni aduuu nɔ ko lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving land fallow allows wild plants and grass to grow, fall over, and decay. This natural process recharges the soil with organic matter and essential nutrients that crops removed in previous seasons.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ haa koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ, amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni amɛgboiɔ. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyiɔ kɛ nibii ni he hiaa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ jie lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and droop during the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ko po.

english: During intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it from the ground. The plant wilts to shrink its leaf area and slow down water loss until the weather cools down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ baagboi koni amɛha baai lɛ afee bibioo ni amɛha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ asɛɛ afo kɛyashi kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why do my young crop seedlings die a few days after sprouting even though it rained recently?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ moŋ?

english: Young sprouts have very short roots that stay near the surface. If the top layer of soil bakes under strong sunshine, it dries out fast, causing tender stems to dry up before their roots can reach deeper soil moisture.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji waa ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi oya. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ gbɛ́ɔ dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava tubers to stay thin and woody instead of swelling into big roots?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ tso yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛfuu kɛ shishifãi wuji?

english: Cassava roots need loose, uncompacted soil to expand easily, along with nutrients like potassium. If the soil is too hard or packed down, the tubers struggle to grow wide and remain small and fibrous.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Kɛfata niyenii mli nibii tamɔ potassium he Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Ewa akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɔ shi bibii ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds come back so much faster and stronger than my crops after I clear and till the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mitsu he nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds can lie dormant deep underground for years. Tilling flips the earth over and brings those seeds up to the top layer where sunlight and fresh air trigger them to sprout instantly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ aya wɔɔ. shikpɔŋ shishi afii babaoo Tilling tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ baa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ. Hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant crops like cowpea or groundnuts together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas can grab nitrogen gas directly from the air and store it in their roots. When grown alongside maize, they share this free natural fertilizer, helping the maize grow stronger.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ ŋmãa Amɛjaraa nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ. Koni eye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa

english: How do chemical sprays protect my farm crops from insect damage?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni kooloi akafite amɛ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Insecticide sprays work either by coating the leaves so insects get poisoned when they chew on them, or by direct contact with the pests to disrupt their breathing and feeding.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ baai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo mli kɛ́ amɛmiiye nii loo kɛtsɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛ kpeɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛtsi amɛmumɔ kɛ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ naa lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are very sensitive to strong sunlight and can easily dry out. Plantain trees grow fast and have wide leaves that act like natural umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa from intense heat while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbi oya. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing lots of tall green leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaŋŋ agboi babaoo shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?
