english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients, or if the plant gets too much shade, it spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of tubers. Pruning excess foliage and ensuring full sunlight encourages the plant to store energy in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo fe nitrogen kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi ahe. aloo kɛji tso lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ feɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ bulbs najiaŋ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni okwɛ koni hulu la babaoo aba lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato eshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves that form a V-shape starting from the leaf tip indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient maize needs to build green leaves; applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps restore healthy green growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ V su ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni eha baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. When temperatures get too hot or soil dries out, the plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy. Keeping soil consistently moist and providing light shade helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa la kpɛɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a virus spread by whiteflies. Spraying natural neem oil solution or organic insecticidal soap helps control these pests before they cause severe damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni ŋmeii egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem mu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite nii waa.

english: Why must I put tall wooden stakes next to my yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yam is a vine crop that needs to climb off the wet ground toward sunlight to manufacture food for its roots. Staking prevents the leaves from rotting on damp soil and ensures maximum light exposure so the underground tubers grow large.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la mli koni amɛná niyenii kɛha amɛshishifãi lɛ. Staking baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni enine shɛɔ la babaoo nɔ koni eha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother plant. Cutting away small suckers and leaving only one strong replacement shoot ensures the main plantain tree receives enough energy to yield a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. ŋmeii bibii ni afoɔ lɛ Jiemɔ ni oshi ŋmeii kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni dumɔwu titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: How do groundnut plants grow their nuts under the ground after flowering above the soil?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ko akwɛ̃ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni ewo fɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: After the yellow groundnut flowers are pollinated above ground, they drop their petals and send down long stems called pegs directly into the dirt. Once these pegs penetrate loose soil, their tips swell to form the groundnut pods underground.
ga: Beni afee ŋmɔtɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Ebaajie efɔfɔi lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kakadaji ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ amaje shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ bote shikpɔŋ ni etse lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei lɛ naagbee lɛ fũuɔ aahu kɛyashiɔ ebafeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei ŋmei.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers suddenly turn brown and fall off before making pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbee shi dani amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop rapidly when attacked by tiny insects called flower thrips that feed inside the buds. Spraying targeted organic or recommended bio-pesticides right as flower buds begin to open protects the blooms so healthy pods can form.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji kooloi bibii ŋmɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ tutuaa, ni eyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa lɛ shwie nɔ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does swamp rice require standing water in the field during its early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni peat rice lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni edara lɛ?

english: Standing water suppresses competing weeds that would otherwise choke young rice plants, while keeping soil temperatures stable. The water layer acts as a natural weed barrier and creates the warm, wet environment rice roots need to establish quickly.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ anaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ mlihiɛmɔ. Nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ jwɛi anaa. ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa shishifãi afee oya lɛ baa.

english: Why do Fall Armyworms attack and destroy my young maize leaves so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ tutuaa mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ amɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fall Armyworm caterpillars target the tender inner leaves inside the central funnel of young maize plants. Because they multiply rapidly and feed hidden inside the crop's growing point, they can destroy foliage rapidly if not detected and managed early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshwereɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni akɛtee hei ni tsei lɛ daraa yɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ amɛbaanyɛ amɛfite baai oya kɛji akɛ anaaa amɛ ni atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: What causes my pepper leaves to curl up and become twisted?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap from the leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Managing pest insects with neem oil or appropriate sprays prevents the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsu kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of soil nutrients like calcium. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and protecting plants during intense afternoon heat helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ calcium. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ tsei ahe ni abuɔ yɛ shwane mli ni edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellowing leaves on maize typically signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for leafy vegetative growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted compost early in the growing cycle restores leaf greenness and crop vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ amɛdalɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil through their root nodules. Intercropping them with maize enriches the soil naturally, helping the maize grow better while improving overall field yield.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, reduces water evaporation under the sun, keeps crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from competing with your crops for water and nutrients.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ yɛ hulu la shishi lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekɛ otsei lɛ akatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when exposed to full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves and shallow root systems that lose moisture quickly under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shwieɔ nu oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi. Enɛ baaha hulutsoo lɛ abu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Does the direction I point cassava stem cuttings in the soil affect how they grow?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ saa amɛdalɛ he?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds or nodes pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting stem cuttings upside down forces the new shoots to turn around underground, which delays growth and leads to lower tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ, ebaaha tsei heei lɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ fioo ni ebaaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why should I cut away extra shoots from around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛjɛ he ni mi-plantain tso titri lɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Excess shoots, or suckers, compete with the main mother stem for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Pruning away secondary suckers leaves the main stem with maximum resources to produce larger, heavier bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsoi ni fa fe nine loo tsei kɛ nu he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la kɛ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ yibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ mli nibii lɛ yeɔ ehe koni ekɛ plantains wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Excess water fills up soil pore spaces and prevents air from reaching the roots. When roots remain submerged in waterlogged soil for too long, they suffocate and fungal rot sets in, destroying the cassava tubers before harvest.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ ayashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, Enɛ baaha mɔ agbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ dani akpa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which acts as food for the plant. When the crop doesn't get enough food from the soil, it pulls nutrients from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni haa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Egbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Groundnuts put good nutrients back into the soil naturally through their roots. Planting them after maize helps restore the soil's strength so your next crops can grow big without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abele ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Yams need loose, soft soil so their roots can expand smoothly into large tubers. Big mounds capture rainwater better and give the yam room to grow without pushing against hard, packed dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni amɛshishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji wuji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛhiɛɔ nugbɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ ni eŋmɛɛɛ muji ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ he.

english: Does it matter which direction I push my cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni adu ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, planting cassava stems upside down forces the new buds to grow downward first before curving up toward the sun. This wastes the plant's energy and results in weak stems and very small tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni akwɛ̃ɔ ni tsɔɔ shishi lɛ nyɛɔ ŋmeii heei anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛya shi dani amɛku amɛsɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ bulbs bibii waa.

english: Why should I clear young shoots from around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie ŋmeii bibii kɛjɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, act like extra mouths to feed. They steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree, causing it to produce smaller bunches of fruit.
ga: Suckers loo shoots ni fa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ daaŋ krokomɛi ni akɛyeɔ nii. Amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ plantain tsei titrii lɛ amli. Ha ewo yibii yɛ kui bibii amli.

english: Why do my young crops grow so slowly when I delay weeding my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo nɛkɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ be sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and drink up the soil's water and fertilizer before your crops can reach them. Removing weeds early gives your main crop full access to light and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii. ni onu nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayashɛ jɛmɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa tsei ni okwɛɔ amɛ lɛ naa la kɛ niyenii kpakpai babaoo.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees keep falling off before forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the tree is stressed by drought or when there are no tiny insects, like midges, around to pollinate them. Without pollination, the tree sheds the unfertilized flowers.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ, tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni ewooo mli lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny, invisible pests like whiteflies or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves. They can also pass along viruses that make the leaves wrinkle and stunt the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii yɛji loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛha helai ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛhaa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ hu.

english: Why do my small green tomatoes drop off the plant before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop their young fruit when the weather becomes too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet too quickly. This stress causes the plant to drop fruit to save its own life.
ga: Tomato shwieɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ yibii koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Small insects called weevils lay eggs inside dry maize kernels. When the eggs hatch, the tiny worms eat the inside of the grain and leave behind dust and empty shells.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ weevils lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni egbi mli. Kɛji wɔji lɛ fɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ sũ kɛ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why does cutting off healthy-looking branches from my cocoa trees actually help them produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ aniji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Removing extra branches opens up the canopy so sunlight and fresh air can reach the main stem, while preventing the tree from wasting valuable food and energy on useless leaves instead of pods.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tso lɛ tso titri lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii ni jara wa kɛ hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmeii najiaŋ.

english: Why are my cocoa trees growing very tall with lots of green leaves but producing very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi eshishifãi fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees get too much shade or nitrogen without enough sunlight and pruning, they spend all their strength growing tall and leafy instead of producing flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo loo nitrogen babaoo ni hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ tsei ni afoɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ, kookoo tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ɔ ni ekɛ baai shwereɔ.

english: If young cocoa trees are exposed to full sun without shade crops like plantains, their leaves will burn, turn yellow, or dry up at the edges because their stems are too young to handle harsh heat.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa ko shɛ kookoo tso bibioo ko nɔ ni tsei tamɔ plantains ni haaa ehiɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, ebaai lɛ baashã. tsɔ ŋmɔŋ Loo egbi yɛ eshishigbɛi lɛ ahe ejaakɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ darako tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees curl up and droop during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane latsaa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to seal in moisture and stop water from evaporating too fast during intense heat, which is the tree's natural defense mechanism to keep itself alive during dry weather.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Enɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: People say my low cocoa yield is caused by spiritual bad luck, but what physical farm problems actually stop a tree from bearing pods?
ga: Mɛi babaoo kɛɔ akɛ mi-kookoo ni miwoɔ lɛ faaa lɛ toɔ mumɔŋ haomɔ he, shi mɛɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okwaayeli he saji miitsi tsei lɛ anaa diɛŋtsɛ koni amɛkawo ŋmeii?

english: Low yield is usually caused by lack of soil nutrients, overgrown branches blocking light, pest damage, or aging trees, which can all be corrected through proper pruning, weeding, and farm maintenance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni haa yibiiwoo baa shi. Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ tsiɔ la lɛ naa. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tso momo Abaanyɛ asaa enɛ kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli saamɔ nɔ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving all the plants weak and producing smaller, poorer yields overall.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi ni ehiii kwraa.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn black and rot before they are ready for harvesting?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa?

english: Black pod is a waterborne fungus that thrives in dark, crowded, and wet farms; letting sunlight into the farm through pruning and weeding helps keep pods dry and free from rot.
ga: Black pod ji nu mli ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ, ni mɛi eyi mli obɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni hulu la bote ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa trees dry up and fall off before developing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is under stress from dry weather, insect attacks, or lack of proper soil nutrients needed to nourish the new pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa ni he hiaa koni akɛha ŋmeii heei lɛ niyenii lɛ mli.

english: How do weeds growing around my crops actually reduce my final cocoa harvest?
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Te feɔ tɛŋŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa mi naagbee kookoo kpamɔ lɛ shi?

english: Weeds act as hidden thieves beneath the soil, drinking up the water and eating the nutrients that your cocoa trees need to produce big, healthy pods.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi ni kɛ amɛhe ewo shikpɔŋ shishi. Nuu nu ni oye niyenii ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa.

english: Should I rake away and burn all the dry leaves under my cocoa trees or leave them on the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã baai ni egbi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi loo mashi yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Leaving clean fallen leaves on the ground forms a natural protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, holds in water, and decays into free fertilizer for your trees.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi ni he tse lɛ ni ajieɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, efeɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up into tight tubes during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up to protect themselves and save water when the heat is too intense. Covering the soil around the crops with dry grass (mulching) keeps the soil cool and moist so the leaves stay open.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛbu nu he kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Mulching abɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ jwɛi (mulch) koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ ahi shi ni amɛgbele.

english: Can I grow vegetables like tomatoes continuously through both the dry and rainy seasons?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu aduawai tamɔ tomato be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be fɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, you can grow tomatoes year-round if you have access to a small water source like a borehole or stream during the dry months, and use raised soil beds during the rainy season to prevent waterlogging.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu tomato afi muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛji oyɛ nu jɛɛhe bibioo ko, tamɔ nubu loo faa ko yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ atsu nii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni nu afua akaho.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before they can grow into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani etsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience extreme heat stress, lack sufficient soil moisture, or lack nutrients like phosphorus. Watering regularly and applying well-rotted manure helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa kɛ ŋmeii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava naturally sheds its lower leaves to conserve water and nutrients during dry spells, or it may signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost will nourish the soil and reduce leaf loss.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ eshishi baai lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Aloo ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni ebaaha baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first planting. Saving and replanting those harvested seeds results in weak plants, smaller cobs, and a much lower yield in the second generation.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ amɛdumɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds sprout and grow so much faster than my crop seeds right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are extremely tough and lie hidden in the soil waiting for moisture. When the first rain falls, weeds absorb water faster than planted crops, so clearing them early gives your main crop room to grow.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Beni nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ Jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do farmers in my community plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ mi akutso lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Intercropping maize and cassava maximizes your land. Maize grows fast and is harvested early within four months, giving you quick food and income while the slower cassava takes its time to mature over the year.
ga: Abɛi kɛ ŋmei ni ooodu lɛ haa ohegbɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ nyɔji ejwɛ pɛ. Na niyenii kɛ shika oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ heɔ be dani edaa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need plantain trees grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ aná dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under strong direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that provide living umbrella shade and keep the air humid for the young cocoa trees.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛhaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ.

english: How do I know my field maize is completely ready to harvest for long-term storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa koni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Maize is ready for dry storage when the outer husks turn dry and brown, the stalks turn yellow, and the individual kernels become hard enough that you cannot dent them with your thumbnail.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo kɛha nibii ni egbi ni akɛtoɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mli wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ nineshi ŋmei bibioo ko akafo.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from going soft and rotting while I wait for a buyer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafee blɛoo ni efite be mli ni mimɛɔ mɛi ni baahe lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly when exposed to direct heat, moisture, or touching the bare damp ground. Storing them in a well-ventilated, shaded barn off the ground allows air to circulate and keeps them fresh for months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo dɔlɛ, fɛ̃i, loo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ kpe tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya nɔ abɔle amɛhe ni amɛhi shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. High heat causes extreme stress and breaks down the green pigment in leaves, which is why planting shade trees or plantains alongside them protects their leaves while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo lateral plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: What causes the tiny holes in my maize leaves and why are the leaves rolling up?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai amli lɛ baa, ni mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Tiny holes and rolled leaves in maize are typically caused by pests like stem borers or fall armyworms. They burrow into the central funnel of the plant to feed on tender young leaves before they fully open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ stem borers loo cutworms ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛfoɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli koni amɛye baai bibii dani amɛgbele amɛhe kwraa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids. As they suck sap from the underside of tender leaves, the damaged tissue twists, curls, and stops growing normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baa ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ, fãji ni efite lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe, amɛfoɔ amɛhe, ni amɛkpaa dalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when soil holds too much water due to poor drainage. Fungi and bacteria grow rapidly in waterlogged soil, attacking the roots and causing them to decay before harvest time.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Fungi kɛ bacteria daa oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Etutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ dani kpamɔ be shɛɔ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme heat, drought, or erratic watering. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its blossoms to conserve energy and water rather than supporting fruit growth.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔ̃ɔ kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ ni ejaaa hao amɛ. Kɛ tsei nu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. moŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. If you allow too many sucker shoots to grow around the main stem, they compete for root anchor space and weaken the main tree against wind.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Kɛji oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe lɛ, tso titri lɛ fa tsɔ Ekɛ shishifãi ahe he akaŋ ni ehaa tso titri lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa kɔɔyɔɔ waa.

english: Why do the tips of my crop leaves turn brown and dry after I put fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Brown and scorched leaf tips usually mean fertilizer burn. Applying chemical fertilizer too close to the plant stems or roots concentrates salts in the soil, which pulls water out of the roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi ni tsuɔ ni edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashã. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ wo tso lɛ shishifãi loo eshishifãi lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei babaoo aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ fe ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why does my farmland soil become hard like concrete after heavy rain dries up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okwaayeli shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Soil crusts and hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost or manure. Raindrops break down bare soil particles, and without organic material to keep the soil loose, the hot sun bakes the surface into a hard layer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ mli. Nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ gbálaa sũ mli nibii bibii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ amli. Ni kɛji akɛ nɔ ko bɛ ni baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my young maize plants turning pale yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves on young maize indicate a shortage of nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the key nutrient plants use to build healthy green leaves and grow rapidly during their early stage.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛwo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ shishijee dalɛ oya.

english: How do weeds actually stop my crops from growing big even when I apply fertilizer?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli po?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for root space, soil nutrients, and sunlight. Because weeds grow aggressively, they steal the water and fertilizer meant for your crops before the crop roots can absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow even though I put fertilizer on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ ŋmãa woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are starving for nitrogen, or the soil is too dry for the roots to soak up the medicine you gave it. Fertilizer needs moisture in the soil to dissolve and feed the plant properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ tsofa ni okɛhaa lɛ lɛ. Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afee fɛ̃i koni etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why does speargrass keep coming back on my land even after I clear it completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi yaa nɔ ekuɔ esɛɛ ebaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Kɛji mijie fɛɛ po?

english: Speargrass has deep underground roots that store food and hide from your hoe. When you cut the top, the roots under the ground simply sprout new leaves, so you have to dig up the roots or use the right weed chemical to kill it.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni kɛ niyenii toɔ ni ekɛ ehe woɔ ŋmei lɛ mli. Kɛji ofo ŋwɛigbɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ baai heei. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni otsa shishifãi lɛ loo okɛ tsofai ni sa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛgbe amɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees shed all their leaves when the dry Harmattan wind starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ fɛɛ kɛji Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during dry spells to protect themselves from losing water through their leaves. Planting tall shade trees like plantains around young cocoa helps keep the farm cool and moist so they stay green.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ he. tsei kakadaji ni aduɔ Haa hulutsoo be ni ebɔle he lɛ Kookoo bibioo lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahi shi akɛ ŋmɔji.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains keep changing every year?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa? Be ni nugbɔ lɛ tsakeɔ daa afi?

english: Instead of planting after the very first shower, wait until the rain falls steadily for a few days and wets the soil deep down. This prevents the seeds from germinating and then drying up if the rain stops for weeks.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ be fɛɛ be gbii fioo komɛi ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afee shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo.

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny white flies that bite the leaves. You can stop this by planting disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension officers.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Fɛ̃i bibii yɛŋ ni ŋmɔɔ baai lɛ woɔ enɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my plantain leaves to dry up and turn brown from the bottom before the fruit is mature?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi plantain baai lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ shishi dani yibii lɛ baa?

english: This is caused by a common leaf disease that spreads through air and water drops on the leaves. Cutting off and burning the affected dry leaves early keeps the disease from spreading to the rest of your plantain farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji baa hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu mli nu ni hoɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli. Kpɔ̃ɔ ni oshã baai ni egbi ni ena hela lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa hei krokomɛi. ni yɔɔ o-plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers without giving me any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant doesn't get enough water. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the roots and giving them light shade during high afternoon heat helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo tomato nɔ yɛ shishigbɛ daa, ni okɛ hulutsoo be ha yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves but no pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ lɛ? Ani oyɛ baai babaoo shi obɛ pods?

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen fertilizer or grow under deep shade, they spend all their energy making leaves instead of food. They need full sunlight and less nitrogen to start producing pods.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo eda yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai yɛ niyenii najiaŋ. Hulu ni fa kɛ nitrogen fioo he miihia amɛ koni amɛje pods feemɔ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very thin when I plant them close together with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Crops compete for sunlight, water, and food in the ground just like animals at a feeding trough. If cassava and maize are too close, the maize steals the light and food, leaving the cassava roots weak and small.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ tamɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ niyenii atoohe lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa lɛ baaju kane kɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvest to replant hybrid maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to give a high yield only for the first planting. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven growth if you plant them again.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ dalɛ ni ejaaa baa kɛji odu ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up tightly when the afternoon sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves curl inward during hot afternoons as a natural defense mechanism to save water. By rolling up, the plant reduces the leaf surface area exposed to heat and sun, preventing excess moisture loss.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ mli yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Tsei haa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ he ni dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni amɛfoɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam plants yield bigger tubers when I give the vines wooden sticks to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ naa bulbs wuji beni miha wain tso lɛ nine lɛ kwɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy for the plant. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sun exposure, which creates more food to feed and expand the underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ aha tso lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa niyenii babaoo baa ni eha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking sap from the leaves, or by viral diseases spread by these insects. Keeping the field weed-free and spraying neem oil helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ jɛmɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ kooloi nɛɛ anaa.

english: Why do young cocoa pods on my trees turn black and shrivel up before they grow fully?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is commonly caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches lets air and sunlight in, which dries out the pods and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la boteɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, making pollination fail. Giving the plants consistent water and shade during peak heat helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tsei lɛ hao. ni haa pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛhaa tsei yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai lɛ ni amɛtoɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my orange trees drop so many small green fruits shortly after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Amɛteŋ mɛi babaoo yɛ fɔfɔii ni amɛwo lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Citrus trees naturally drop extra fruits they cannot support if they lack enough water or nutrients. Regular watering and applying compost or fertilizer during flowering helps the tree hold onto more fruit.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ kɛji nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛsu naa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ aduawai babaoo mli.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and watery if I leave them in wet ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need well-drained soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the tubers to suffocate, rot, and turn watery.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi, egboɔ ni etsɔɔ nu.

english: Why are the leaves of my hibiscus (sobolo) plants turning pale yellow instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi hibiscus tso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the plant is getting too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or compost restores nitrogen so the leaves can turn dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo tso lɛ miiná nu babaoo tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ waa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during rainstorms once they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni ebɔi yibiiwoo lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. When rain softens the soil and wind pushes the tree, the heavy top pulls the shallow roots out of the ground. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop prevents this.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa tsei lɛ. Tsoi ni tsii lɛ gbalaa shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ tso ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When the crop season ends, that natural fertilizer remains behind to nourish the maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ dumɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baakã he ahi shi koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: What is the main benefit of planting a crop variety that matures in just three months?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ he?

english: Fast-maturing three-month crops allow you to harvest quickly before dry spells hit, earn income faster, and potentially plant and harvest multiple times within a single rainy season.
ga: Nyɔji etɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa onine shɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ oya dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ. Na shika oya ni abaanyɛ adu ni akpa shii abɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli.

english: How do short-duration crops help me deal with unpredictable rains in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ ye ebua mi ni minyɛ midamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ naa?

english: Because short-duration crops need less total time in the ground, they can complete their growth cycle and give you a full harvest even if the rainy season turns out to be shorter than usual.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli lɛ biɔ be fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ be lɛ yeɔ emuu ni ehaa yibiiwoo ni fa eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ faaa fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ moŋ.

english: What happens if I leave a fast-maturing crop in the soil past its three-month harvest period?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji akɛ mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaving mature crops in the field too long exposes them to insect pest damage, field rot, and reduced crop quality, so it is best to harvest them as soon as they reach maturity.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edara lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai afite amɛ. jɛmɛ fitemɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu baa shi No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa kɛji tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ.

english: How do I know the right time to harvest my crops after planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ beni midu nii sɛɛ?

english: Every crop variety has a specific maturity window, such as three months. You can tell it is time to harvest by tracking the weeks since planting and looking for physical signs like leaf yellowing or firm seed pods.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni ekɛbaa, tamɔ nyɔji etɛ. Obaanyɛ ole be ni esa akɛ akpa nii kɛtsɔ otsii ni eho kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ nɔ, ni otao gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ baai ni efee ŋmɔŋ loo dumɔwui ni mli wa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I buy new crop varieties from the market instead of re-using seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tsei heei kɛjɛ jara nɔ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Newly released crop varieties are specifically bred to grow faster, produce higher yields, and resist local pests better than older seeds that lose their strength over time.
ga: Akwɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara oya. Ha yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni enyɛɔ eshiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fe dumɔwui momo ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ.

english: When I go to buying seeds, I see different varieties of the same crop. How do I choose the right one for my farm?
ga: Kɛ mitee koni miyahe dumɔwui lɛ mina tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ henɔi srɔtoi babaoo. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala nɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Different varieties are created for different needs. Look at how long each variety takes to mature, how much water it needs, and whether buyers in your local market prefer its taste or size.
ga: Afee henɔi srɔtoi koni akɛtsu hiamɔ nii srɔtoi ahe nii. Taomɔ be ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko heɔ dani ekwɛɔ. Nu enyiɛ he hiaa? Ni ani mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ sumɔɔ nibii ni ŋɔɔ loo amɛdalɛi srɔtoi?

english: If a seed variety was newly brought to the market this year, is it safe for me to plant on my farm?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie dumɔwui srɔtoi awo jara nɔ afi nɛɛ Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ makwɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, certified seeds released onto the market undergo official testing. However, it is good practice to test a small portion on your field first to see how well it grows in your specific soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, akaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ajie amɛ kpo kɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ akwɛɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ, shi kɛlɛ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaaka fã bibioo ko akwɛ. yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni edaa jogbaŋŋ yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do seed producers offer multiple varieties of the same crop group at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ tso kuu kome mli dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo haa shikome lɛ?

english: Having multiple varieties gives farmers choices suited to different conditions—some varieties mature faster, others resist drought better, and some are suited for specific soil types.
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi lɛ yɛ srɔtoi babaoo lɛ, amɛhalaa nibii ni sa kɛha shihilɛi srɔtoi. Henɔi komɛi shwereɔ oya. Henɔi komɛi nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ fe tsutsu lɛ. Ni henɔi komɛi hi kɛha shikpɔŋ henɔi komɛi.

english: Why are some new seed varieties difficult to find in my local village market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaana dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi yɛ mi akrowa lɛ jarayelihe lɛ?

english: When new seed varieties enter the market, it takes time for supply chains to distribute them from central agricultural hubs to small, local agro-dealer shops in rural areas.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi heei bote jara nɔ lɛ, mɛi ni kɛ nibii baa lɛ heɔ be dani amɛnáa amɛ kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli hei ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa maŋ lɛ mli okwaayeli jarayelɔi bibii ni yɔɔ akrowai amli lɛ anɔ.

english: How does growing a fast-maturing crop help me get better market prices?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni miduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Harvesting early allows you to bring your produce to market before the main harvest season starts, when demand is high and overall supply is low, enabling you to sell at better prices.
ga: ŋmaakpamɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyaa jara nɔ dani ŋmaakpamɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi. Beni nibii ni ataoɔ lɛ fa ni nibii fɛɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ faaa lɛ Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohɔ̃ɔ yɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Is it really necessary to build a permanent structure with a roof for my crop nursery instead of just using wooden poles and palm fronds?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni ama tsũ ko ni baahi shi daa ni ŋwɛitsu yɔɔ nɔ kɛha mi-greenhouse lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsei kɛ ŋmei baai pɛ baatsu nii?

english: A permanent structure gives you full control over light, heavy rain, and strong winds year after year without rotting. It protects high-value seeds and nursery beds from being washed away or damaged by unexpected heavy downpours.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ daa lɛ haa onyɛɔ oyeɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo, ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa nɔ kwraa afi fɛɛ afi ni efiteee. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ni jara wa waa kɛ ŋmɔ mli tsei ahe koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni akpaaa gbɛ lɛ akafite loo efite.

english: Why should I cover my seed nursery with fine netting material?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋshɔŋloo kpakpa aha mi-greenhouse lɛ he lɛ?

english: Fine netting acts as a physical barrier that keeps tiny flying insects like aphids and whiteflies away from fragile seedlings, preventing them from spreading destructive plant viruses while still letting light and air through.
ga: Mesh kpakpa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ gbɛtsii nii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi bibii ni foɔ tamɔ aphids kɛ whiteflies lɛ akaboteɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe. Enɛ haaa amɛgbɛ tso mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwã. yɛ be mli ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ lolo kɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some commercial seedling producers build concrete floors in their nursery rooms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi komɛi ni feɔ dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ jarayeli he nii lɛ maa kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ yɛ amɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhei lɛ?

english: Concrete floors prevent wild weeds from growing up into nursery bags, stop soil-borne pests from creeping in from the ground below, and make it easy to wash and disinfect the entire space between planting cycles.
ga: Kɔnkrit shikpɔŋ lɛ tsiɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kotokui. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkajɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nɔ amɛbote mli. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaafɔ he fɛɛ he ni agbe helai yɛ dumɔwui ashishijee bei lɛ ateŋ lɛ.

english: What is this cocoa peat media I keep hearing about, and can I use it to grow my seedlings instead of regular garden soil?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ kookoo peat medium ni minu he nɛɛ? Ni ani manyɛ mikɛtsu nii kɛdu dumɔwui yɛ abɔɔ mli sũ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Cocoa peat is a natural material made from processed coconut husks. It holds water extremely well while staying loose so young roots can breathe, making it ideal for starting seeds without introducing natural soil diseases.
ga: Coco peat ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni akɛ ŋmei ŋmeii ni atsu he nii lɛ feɔ. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ amu. Enɛ haa ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni ekɛ hela baaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do seedling roots seem to spread faster in cocoa peat media compared to my regular farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ coco peat media mli kɛ akɛto mi daa ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa peat is soft and lightweight, which allows delicate young roots to push through and expand easily without fighting hard, packed dirt, while still holding enough moisture to keep the seedling fed.
ga: Coco peat lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni ehiɛ waaa. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ boteɔ mli oya ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ muji ni egbɔjɔ lɛ akpee. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua dumɔwui lɛ yɛ lolo lɛ.

english: If cocoa peat media does not contain natural soil nutrients, how do my nursery plants get food to grow?
ga: Kɛji akɛ coco peat media lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ Te mi dumɔwui lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Cocoa peat acts like a sponge that holds onto liquid food. You nourish the plants by mixing water-soluble plant nutrients or liquid fertilizers directly into the water you use to hydrate the media.
ga: Peat cocoa tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni ŋmɛɔ niyenii ni ji nu lɛ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ. Ohaa otsei lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ tsei amli niyenii ni haa nu mli shwieɔ shi loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni okɛfutuɔ nu ni okɛtsuɔ nii kɛhaa amɛhe nu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some agricultural experts recommend heating or sterilizing soil before planting seeds in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nilelɔi komɛi kɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ akɛ la awo sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ helai awo mli dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Sterilizing soil with heat or steam kills hidden weed seeds, harmful bacteria, fungi, and tiny worms called nematodes. This gives your sprouted seeds a clean, disease-free environment during their most vulnerable stage.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ la loo lasu tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaagbe jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Muawai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes Enɛ baaha odumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ aná he ko ni he tse, ni hela bɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhe waaa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why is it important to wash my shoes and hands before stepping inside a seedling preparation building?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ofɔ oniji kɛ okotokui ahe dani obote dumɔwui ahe saamɔ tsu ko mli lɛ?

english: Dirt stuck to your boots or hands can easily carry microscopic plant diseases into the clean nursery area, which can spread fast and destroy thousands of young seedlings at once.
ga: Muji ni kpɛtɛɔ okotokui loo oniji ahe lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ tsei ahe helai bibii ni anaaa lɛ kɛya hei ni akwɛɔ tsei yɛ ni he tse lɛ. Ebaanyɛ egbɛ eshwa oya ni egbe tsei bibii akpei abɔ shikome.

english: Will putting dark shade netting over my young cocoa seedlings slow down their growth?
ga: Ani ŋshɔŋlooi ni tsuɔ diŋ ni mikɛbaafata mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha amɛdalɛ aba shi?

english: No, young cocoa plants actually grow better under shade netting because direct, intense tropical sun can burn their tender leaves and dry out their small root systems before they are strong enough to handle full light.
ga: Dabi, cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ashishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai bibii lɛ ni efite shishifãi bibii lɛ. Egbiɔ dani ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ la ni fa babaoo lɛ baatsu nii.

english: What causes my young nursery seedlings to suddenly rot and fall over right at the soil level?
ga: Mɛni ha mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ fite trukaa ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by a fungal infection commonly called 'damping-off', which thrives in wet, unsterilized soil. Using clean, sterilized media or cocoa peat prevents these soil fungi from attacking fragile seedling stems.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ lɛ tsɛmɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela. ‘Damping’, ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ nibii ni he tse, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli loo coco peat tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni waaa lɛ.

english: How big is one hectare compared to an acre, and how does knowing this help my farm?
ga: Te hectare kome dalɛ ji ha tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto acre kome he? Ni te enɛ ni mile lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔ lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: One hectare is equal to about two and a half acres. Knowing your exact land size helps you buy the right amount of seeds, fertilizer, and chemical sprays so you do not waste money or under-feed your crops.
ga: Hectare kome kɛ aaafee acre enyɔ kɛ fã yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ da ha pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ohé dumɔwui, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ayibɔ ni sa. Enɛ ji koni okafite shika loo okaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and tiny cobs. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to grow strong and yield big, full ears.
ga: Dumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ atswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do extension officers advise planting plantains inside a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu plantains yɛ kookoo ŋmɔji heei amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade umbrellas and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to endure the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ edamɔ dɔlɛ naa lɛ,.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow from the middle during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ teŋgbɛ yɛ be mli ni edara lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient for green growth. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer early in the growth stage will restore the green color and improve yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers during hot dry spells instead of making fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil place heavy stress on tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to protect themselves from dying. Mulching around the roots and watering early in the morning keeps the plant cool enough to produce fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tomato tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ wo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe ni awo amɛ nu leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ amli jɔɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping naturally, indicating the roots beneath are dense, starchy, and ready for harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaayɔse akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shishifãi lɛ amli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni amɛhe esa kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific crop diseases to build up. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts naturally rebuilds soil fertility.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsei ahe helai pɔtɛɛ aba. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Ebaatswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ama shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dark powder inside the plant heart?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ powda ni tsuɔ yɛ tso lɛ tsui mli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the central leaves. Checking your farm early and applying safe insecticides or neem extracts directly into the funnel stops them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ awoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: How do weeds damage my crops if they are not directly touching or eating the crop leaves?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ afite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ ni etaaa tsei ahe baai ahe tɛ̃ɛ loo eyeee amɛ?

english: Weeds steal essential water, fertilizer, and sunlight from under the ground before your crop roots can reach them, which starves your main crop and lowers your total harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu ni he hiaa, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dani tsei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii titrii lɛ anɔ ni ehaa nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Applying fertilizer when the soil is damp—not bone dry and not during heavy downpours—allows the roots to absorb it immediately. Putting top-dressing fertilizer on when the plants are knee-high gives them energy when they need it most.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ—jeee wui ni egbi ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ—baaha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ni akɛwoɔ ŋwɛi lɛ fata he beni tso lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa lɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I nurse my cocoa seeds in plastic nursery bags first instead of planting them directly into my main farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu kookoo ŋmeii yɛ plastic kotoku mli dani madu? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu shikpɔŋ titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ

english: Nursery bags allow you to protect fragile young seedlings from harsh weather, pests, and strong winds while controlling soil moisture. This gives the seeds a safe environment to build strong root systems before being exposed to the harsh conditions of the main field.
ga: Grow bags haa onyɛɔ obuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he yɛ be mli ni okwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa shihilɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛyaje shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow when I leave the nursery bags in full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ mishi grow bag lɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings are delicate and cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. The heat burns their soft leaves and dries out the limited soil in the small nursery bag faster than the roots can drink, causing the leaves to scorch and turn yellow.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkpe hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ fioo ni yɔɔ grow bag bibioo lɛ mli lɛ agbi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Must I remove the plastic nursery bag completely before putting the seedling into the farm ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni majie plastic grow bags lɛ fɛɛ dani mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, you must remove the bag completely. The plastic will not decay in the soil, so leaving it on will trap the roots inside, preventing them from spreading out to find food and water, which eventually starves and kills the plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie kotoku muu lɛ fɛɛ. Plastic lɛ fiteŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ ashi lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaamɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Tsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛyatao niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni egbo yɛ naagbee.

english: How can I tell if I am watering my nursery bag seedlings too much?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ nu miiwo midumɔwui lɛ amli fe nine?

english: If you water too much, the roots drown from a lack of air in the soil. The leaves will begin to turn yellow, feel limp, or rot at the stem base, and the soil inside the bag will remain muddy and sour-smelling rather than light and damp.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli babaoo Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ. Baai lɛ baaje shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Henumɔ ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe loo egbɔjɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi Ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baakã he afee muji ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee mlɛo ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do cocoa pods grow straight out of the thick trunk of the tree instead of on the thin green branches like other fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei akutsei ni mli tse lɛ amli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ tsei aniji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Tamɔ aduawai krokomɛi?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers and pods directly on their thick trunks and main limbs because cocoa pods are heavy. The strong, woody trunk provides the heavy support needed to hold the weight of mature pods without breaking.
ga: Kookoo tsei woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii yɛ tso lɛ shishi ni mli wa lɛ kɛ amɛniji wuji lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ ejaakɛ kokoo ŋmeii lɛ tsii. Tso ni mli wa ni tamɔ tso lɛ haa yelikɛbuamɔ ni he hiaa koni ekɛfi ŋmeii ni eda lɛ agbɔjɔmɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni efoŋ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods grow from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Trees shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as dry spells, low soil nutrients, or excessive heat. Dropping flowers is the tree's way of conserving energy and water so it can survive harsh weather conditions.
ga: Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛi, tamɔ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ. loo dɔlɛ babaoo Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu he koni amɛhi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings grow much better when I plant plantains right next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Plantains grow quickly and produce large leaves that act like natural umbrellas. They shade young cocoa trees from intense heat, keep the surrounding soil cool and moist, and shield the young plants from drying winds.
ga: Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛbuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. and protect young plants from drying winds

english: This rot is caused by a fungal disease known as Black Pod, which spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and high-humidity weather. Excess moisture on the pods allows fungal spores to germinate and penetrate the pod skin.
ga: Hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Black Pod, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛboteɔ tso lɛ hewolo lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches from my healthy cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and fresh air to flow through, which dries out damp leaves and prevents fungal diseases. It also directs the tree's energy into making bigger pods instead of useless extra leaves.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai ni mli efɔ lɛ agbi ni ebaatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa. Ekɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi ni he ehiaaa lɛ baatsu nii.

english: Why do I need to clear all weeds from around my young cocoa trees before the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients that your young cocoa plants need to grow. Clearing weeds removes competition and destroys hiding places for pests that damage young leaves and shoots.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa o-cacao tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa, ni efiteɔ hei ni kooloi ni fiteɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wither and die so quickly as soon as the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya kɛji hɔmɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: During the dry season, extreme heat evaporates moisture from both the soil and plant leaves faster than roots can draw it up. Without proper soil cover or drought-tolerant crop choices, plants dehydrate rapidly.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tso lɛ baai fɛɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie lɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ ahalaaa lɛ, Tsei lɛ amli nu faaa oya.

english: Is there a simple way I can keep moisture in my farm soil so my crops do not dry out?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni matsɔ nɔ mahiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii akagbi?

english: You can cover the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or crop stalks—a practice called mulching. Mulching blocks direct sunlight, keeps the soil cool, and dramatically slows down water evaporation.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo tsei ashishifãi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni ebɔle onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching tsiɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi waa.

english: How can I store water on my farm to water my vegetables when the streams dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato nu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha aduawai nu beni faa lɛ mli egbi lɛ?

english: You can harvest rainwater by digging simple earth ponds lined with plastic, using water storage drums, or digging shallow contour trenches that trap rainwater runoff during the wet season for later use.
ga: Obaanyɛ okpa nugbɔ nu kɛtsɔ sũ bu ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛ plastic ehà nɔ lɛ ni oootsu lɛ nɔ. Nu ŋtayaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ŋtayaa ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni aaafo Koni akɛmɔ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ koni akɛtsu nii sɛɛ mli.

english: What type of crops can I plant in Northern Ghana where water becomes very scarce during the long dry months?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ Ghana Kooyigbɛ? Nu faaa yɛ nyɔji kakadaŋŋ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: In dry northern areas, crops like sorghum, millet, cowpeas, and groundnuts grow best because they have deep root systems or short life cycles that require very little water compared to crops like maize or rice.
ga: Yɛ kooyigbɛ kpokpai ni egbi lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ loo wala be kuku ni biɔ nu fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he.

english: Why do crops seem to grow much easier in the middle belt of Ghana compared to the far north?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo kwraa yɛ Ghana teŋgbɛ kɛ akɛto kooyigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: The middle belt, or transitional zone, receives a better balance of rainfall and has soil that retains moisture longer, creating a less harsh climate for a wider variety of crops year-round.
ga: Teŋgbɛ bɛlt loo tsakemɔ he lɛ baaná nugbɔshiimɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa waa lɛ baa shi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do farmers in Southern Ghana have different planting times than farmers in Northern Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ duɔ nii yɛ srɔto yɛ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Southern Ghana gets two distinct rainy seasons each year (major and minor), allowing for two crop harvests, whereas Northern Ghana has only one single rainy season followed by a long dry period.
ga: Ghana wuoyigbɛ yɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ bei sɔrɔtoi enyɔ daa afi. (Primary kɛ Secondary be) lɛ haa anyɛɔ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ. yɛ be mli ni Ghana Kooyigbɛ lɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ yɔɔ. Nɔ ni nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ ji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Which crops can I grow to feed my livestock during the dry season when green grass disappears?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei manyɛ madu koni mikɛye kooloi niyenii yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni jwɛi eŋɔli lɛ efo mli lɛ?

english: You can grow drought-tolerant forage crops like Pigeon Pea, Lablab, or Napier grass during the rains, which can be harvested and dried into hay or kept alive to feed farm animals throughout the dry season.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu niyenii ni haa hɔmɔ yeɔ egbɔ tamɔ Pigeon Pea, Lablab loo Napier jwɛi yɛ nugbɔ be mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ abaanyɛ akpa ni agbi akɛ jwɛi loo akwɛ akɛ niyenii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from the sun's heat or if they just need plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ hewɔ loo tsei niyenii kɛkɛ he miihia lɛ?

english: Heat-stressed crops will curl their leaves, look droopy during the hot afternoon, and dry out at the leaf tips, whereas crops lacking nutrients usually turn pale yellow even when the soil has plenty of water.
ga: Tsei ni dɔlɛ haa amɛhaoɔ lɛ baa baa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ehiɛ egbo yɛ shwane ni edɔ waa mli. kɛ baai ni egbi lɛ ashishifãi Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ni niyenii eshɛɛɛ amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Do I need expensive pumps to irrigate my crops in the dry season, or are there low-cost options?
ga: Ani pɔmp ni jara wa he miihia mi koni mikɛfɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli? Aloo gbɛi krokomɛi ni jara waaa yɛ?

english: You do not need expensive machines; low-cost options like bucket-drip systems, hand-dug shallow wells, or simple watering cans can keep small crop plots healthy throughout the dry season.
ga: Tsɔnei ni jara wa he ehiaaa bo. Nibii ni jara waaa, tamɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tanki mli lɛ Bu ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii Aloo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ mlɛo baanyɛ aye abua ni ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What are cover crops, and how do they protect my land when nothing else is growing?
ga: Mɛni ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mishikpɔŋ lɛ he be mli ni aduko nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Cover crops are fast-growing plants like cowpeas or velvet beans planted to cover bare soil. They protect the ground from burning in the hot sun, prevent wind erosion, and add nutrients back into the soil for your next main crop.
ga: Cover crops ji tsei ni daa oya, tamɔ cowpeas loo velvet beans, ni aduɔ koni akɛha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashã. Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?
