english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build healthy green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its strength and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every year and allows soil pests and diseases to build up. Rotating your maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the soil and breaks the pest cycle.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and burn up when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshãa beni mijieɔ hulutsoo tsei wuji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight when they are small. Leaving shade trees or planting fast-growing plantains nearby protects young cocoa leaves from scorching and helps the soil stay moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ beni amɛdarako lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo odu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ, ebaabu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems curling up and looking sticky during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Curled and sticky leaves are caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like mealybugs or aphids that gather under the leaves. Spraying them with a mild soap-and-water solution or neem extract helps wash them off and protects your harvest.
ga: Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ mealybugs loo aphids ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni wa lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem mli nu lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efɔ he ni ebu onibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ ahe.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my corn leaves with small dark crumbs in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes and dark droppings in the central shoot are clear signs of the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. Checking your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem spray directly into the leaf funnel stops them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Buji ni etse kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji Fall Armyworm he okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ nibii ni odu lɛ amli mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem spray ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ awo baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Tsi amɛ gbɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves up high to catch maximum sunlight, which provides energy to grow large tubers underground. Unstaked yam vines stay on the hot ground, leading to leaf diseases and smaller yams.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. ni ji hewalɛ ni akɛbaakwɛ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Sweet potato wain tsei ni shishifãi bɛ amɛhe lɛ baahi hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ. Ekɛ hela baa baai kɛ sweet potato bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Allowing too many shoots (suckers) to grow around one mother plant creates competition for nutrients and water. Removing excess suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones ensures you get large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) akwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso nyɛ kome he lɛ fa tsɔ. Enɛ baaha akaŋshii aba kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha oná plantain tso agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my pepper plants with dry grass or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating in the heat, suppresses weeds, and breaks down into rich soil food over time.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent throughout the growing period prevents this issue.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa yɛ be fɛɛ mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the dirt when I sow them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall often heats up dry soil and is usually followed by several hot days without rain, causing seeds to bake or decay. Waiting until the rainy season fully sets in ensures continuous moisture for healthy germination.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ. Ni gbii babaoo ni mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shãa loo amɛgboɔ. Ni aaamɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fɛɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ aya nɔ aná koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if I clear all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji fɛɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, strong sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out. Tall shade trees or leafy crops like plantains act as living shields, protecting young cocoa plants from heat while keeping moisture in the soil until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ tsɔne ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ amɛmligbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient that gives leaves their deep green color. When there is not enough nitrogen in the ground, the plant steals it from older lower leaves to keep new upper leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas in my field helps my next crop of maize grow better without added fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni mikɛ ŋmãa wooo mli lɛ?

english: Cowpea plants have a quiet partnership with helpful bacteria living on their roots. These bacteria pull nitrogen food out of the air and fix it into the soil, leaving behind rich nutrients that feed whatever crop you plant in that field next.
ga: Cowpea tsei lɛ yɛ wekukpaa ni yɔɔ dioo kɛ amɛhe. kɛ helai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni hiɔ shi yɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ Helai nɛɛ gbalaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji nitrogen lɛ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛshiɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa babaoo koni amɛkɛye ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaadu yɛ ŋmɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to spend energy putting sticks in the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite mihewalɛ ni mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso ko akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to lift their leaves into full sunlight where they make food for the plant. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also protects the foliage from soil-borne rot and diseases, leading to much larger tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo ni amɛkɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ feɔ wuji babaoo.

english: Small shoots (suckers) suck water and food away from the mother plantain tree. Removing most extra shoots leaves only one or two strong stems, ensuring all nutrients go toward producing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tsobii bibii (shoots) lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ateŋ babaoo lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni eha niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ aya ni ekɛ plantains agboi ni tsii aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling, turning yellow with light green patches, and shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe lɛ? Etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ni egbɔjɔɔ?

english: Twisted and mosaic-patterned leaves are caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies that feed on sap. The virus stops the leaves from making food properly, which severely reduces the size of your cassava roots.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsake ni yɔɔ mosaic he mfoniri lɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ tsofa lɛ mli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ haaa baai lɛ anyɛ ahoo nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aba shi waa.

english: Why are the top leaves of my pepper plants curling tightly downward and stopping new growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyaa shishi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ hee lɛ?

english: Curled pepper leaves are often caused by tiny insects like mites or aphids sucking sap from the underside of leaves. Their feeding injects toxins or spreads viruses that stunt leaf growth and prevent flowers from forming.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Amɛ niyenii lɛ kɛ tsofai fɔji woɔ amɛmli loo egbɛɔ helai ni haa baa lɛ daa ni ehaaa fɔfɔi afee lɛ eshwaa amɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and humidity is low, the pollen inside tomato flowers becomes sticky or sterile and cannot fertilize the bloom. The plant then drops the unfertilized flowers to save its water and energy.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ hu faaa lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. ni enyɛŋ ekɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo fɔ No sɛɛ lɛ tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni awoko fɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he.

english: Why does my oil palm tree produce plenty of flowers but no fruit bunches in some seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Oil palms carry separate male and female flowers on the same tree. During dry or stressful periods, the tree mostly produces male flowers, or tiny pollinating beetles are absent, leaving female flowers unpollinated so no fruit sets.
ga: Mu tsei yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ tso kome nɔ. during periods of drought or stress Most plants produce male flowers. Or the small beetles disappear, resulting in the female flowers not being pollinated and therefore not producing fruit.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn tough and woody if I leave them in the soil for too long before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa ni amɛfeɔ tsei kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots are storage organs for starch; as the plant gets older, it starts converting soft starch into hard wood fiber to support its tall stem above ground, making the root tough and poor for eating.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji nibii ni akɛ starch toɔ. When the plant gets older It will begin to convert soft starch into hardwood fibers to support the trunk high above the ground. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni amɛyeee nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize curling up during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up during extreme heat to trap moisture and prevent water from escaping into the dry air. If the leaves stay rolled up into the cool evening, it is a clear signal that the crop urgently needs water.
ga: Abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛtsi nu naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ Eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii oya.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop in the afternoon even when the ground feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When sunlight is intense, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it up from the soil. This causes temporary wilting during peak sun hours, but the leaves usually recover as the heat dies down.
ga: Kɛ hulu la lɛ tsoɔ waa Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Shi bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛji latsaa lɛ ba shi.

english: Why do my pawpaw trees produce plenty of flowers but never bear any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants have separate sexes. Male pawpaw trees only produce pollen to fertilize female flowers and will never grow fruit themselves, so you need to cut down excess male trees and keep female or hermaphrodite ones.
ga: Pawpaw tsei lɛ yɛ hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Pawpaw tsei hii lɛ woɔ pollen pɛ ni amɛkɛ fɔfɔi yei feɔ ekome. ni ewoŋ yibii yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɔkɔɔkɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ofolɔ tsei ni ji hii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ yei loo tsei ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before any fruit starts to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: High daytime temperatures and dry heat prevent proper pollination in tomato flowers. When the plant gets too hot and stressed, it drops its unpollinated flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa kɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa ni baa tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ naa. Kɛ tsei lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni amɛhao lɛ Ejieɔ fɔfɔi ni bɛ pollen lɛ koni ekɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves but giving me tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to direct all its food energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kudɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmeii kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ, moŋ fe ni eeekɛ ŋmei ato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I clear all the surrounding big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They require temporary shade from trees or food crops like plantains to keep them cool while their root systems develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei loo niyenii tsei, tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni amɛhe ajɔɔ amɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: How can I reduce the money I spend on chemical fertilizers without harming my maize yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo shika ni mifiteɔ yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ shi ni enaaa mi-ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: You can mix organic compost or poultry manure into the soil and place small, precise amounts of chemical fertilizer directly at the base of each plant instead of scattering it across the whole farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ organic compost loo kooloi ashishifãi afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okɛ tsofa fioo ko ni sa pɛpɛɛpɛ awo tso fɛɛ tso shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeegbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: Why do my crops grow thin and pale when I plant maize and cowpeas too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ midu ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overcrowding forces crops to fight for the same sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients, leaving both plants starved and unable to develop fully.
ga: Mɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛná hulu la. shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni no haa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that multiplies in wet, cool, and shady environments. Pruning excess farm branches lets in sunlight and air to dry the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni fɔɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: Why is my maize crop turning yellow and dying in small patches across my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbo yɛ hei srɔtoi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: This localized damage is often caused by Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches itself underground to maize roots, stealing nutrients and water before the weed even shows above ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu dani jwɛi lɛ po jeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their tender leaves burn easily in full sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains nearby, direct sun overheats the leaves, causing them to dry up and fall off to conserve water.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu la ni kpɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha baai lɛ adɔ fe nine. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi koni amɛbu nu he.

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes on the stem where leaves used to grow. These buds must point upwards toward the sky so the shoot can grow straight up out of the ground easily.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo nodes bibii Yɛ tso lɛ nɔ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of a maize plant mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant steals nitrogen from its old lower leaves to feed new upper leaves, causing the bottom ones to turn yellow.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why are my tomato blossoms falling off the plant before turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or erratic watering. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ejaaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites hiding under the leaves. They suck the plant juice, causing new growth to warp and twist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ tsei amli nu, ni no haa tsei heei ni eda lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Ajie mi plantain lɛ shishitoo lɛ.

english: If too many shoots grow around the main plantain tree, they all compete for the same food and water. Removing extra shoots leaves one strong plant that can produce a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ dara kɛbɔle Dumɔwui titrii babaoo tsɔ Tsobii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli kɛha niyenii kɛ nu kome. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome ni wa ni baanyɛ awo ŋmeii akui wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food and grow large tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up off the damp ground where they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ, ni amɛhe bɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: When maize plants are too crowded, their roots fight over water and fertilizer while their leaves fight for sunlight. This competition leaves you with thin, weak stalks and very small cobs.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ kɛ nu kɛ ŋmãa baabɔ mɔdɛŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ hulu la lɛ baawu. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei bibii waa.

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a free, natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Muawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii amli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry leaves help them during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi woɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves acts like a blanket that shades the soil from the hot sun, keeping the soil cool and trapping water so roots stay moist longer.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ atade, ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: If I see yellow leaves on my crops, should I wait to see if they turn green again on their own?
ga: Kɛji mina baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni mana kɛji ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your crops are starving for soil nutrients or being attacked by a disease. Waiting usually makes the problem worse because diseases spread quickly to healthy plants; it is better to identify and treat the issue immediately.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni oduɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo helai miitutua amɛ. Bei pii lɛ, mɛmɔ haa naagba lɛ mli woɔ wu ejaakɛ hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona naagbai ni yɔɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni osaa amɛ.

english: Can a crop disease spread to my field just by talking about it with other farmers?
ga: Ani tsei ahe helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔji amli kɛtsɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni mikɛ amɛ aaagba sane kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: Diseases do not spread by talking or looking; they spread through physical contact, contaminated tools, infected seeds, insects, wind, or rain. Sharing photos or describing symptoms to extension officers actually helps you find the cure faster.
ga: Jeee wiemɔ loo hiŋmɛi nɔ atsɔɔ hela gbɛɔ eshwaa. Gbalamɔ kɛtsɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nifeemɔ nɔ Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni mli ewo muji, dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ, kooloi bibii, kɔɔyɔɔ, loo nugbɔ Mfoniri loo okadii ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ yelikɛbuamɔ nitsulɔi lɛ jaa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ana tsabaa oya.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct, intense sunlight. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava planted next to them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi cacao tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the pods on my cocoa trees turning black and shriveling up before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal infection called Black Pod disease, which thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning unnecessary tree branches lets sunlight and air in to dry the pods and stop the fungus.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela kɛ kookoo diji baa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa.

english: Why is my farm soil getting harder and less productive even though I work on it every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni ewooo yibii babaoo eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crops every year drains the essential nutrients out of the soil and weakens its structure. Adding organic manure or compost softens hard soil and restores the natural plant food needed for strong crops.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ afee blɛoo ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my crops are hungry and need plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni maná tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Stunted growth, pale green leaves, thin stems, and poor flowering are signs that plants lack food. Feeding the soil with fertilizer early in the season gives crops the energy to produce bigger harvests.
ga: stunted growth Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, kɛ fɔfɔi ni ehiii ji okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpa. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: How do insect pests move so fast from my neighbor's field onto my crops?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ aya oya kɛjɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Insects fly or crawl across farm borders looking for fresh food, especially when neighboring crops are harvested or sprayed. Keeping farm borders weed-free and inspecting crop edges daily helps catch invading pests early.
ga: Kplukai fɔ̃ɔ loo amɛfoɔ ŋmɔ husui amli kɛtaoɔ niyenii hee. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ loo ashɛreɔ tsofa. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ ŋmɔ mli husui lɛ anɔ, ni akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe daa gbi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni anyɛ amɔmɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ mra.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after clearing the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds are naturally tough and lie hidden in the soil for years waiting for rain to sprout. Removing weeds while they are still small prevents them from stealing water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afii babaoo ni amɛmiimɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds saved from my last harvest produce less food than new seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo fe dumɔwui heei lɛ?

english: Seeds saved over many years lose their strength and resistance to pests and dry weather. Certified seeds are specially selected to give higher yields and protect against local plant diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto afii babaoo lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ baa shi. Ahala dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛ yibiiwoo babaoo aba ni ebu he kɛjɛ tsei ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe helai ahe.

english: Is it good for my crops if I plant beans and maize together in the same plot?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize helps both crops. Beans pull natural nitrogen out of the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow tall and strong without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ewaa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Applying poultry manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help the plants recover their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmɔŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon heat even when the soil is still moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, pepper leaves lose water faster through evaporation than the roots can suck it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to protect itself from drying out, and it usually recovers by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ebu ehe koni ekagbi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Cassava drops its leaves during dry periods to save water and energy. It enters a resting phase so it does not dry out, and as soon as the rains return, it will grow fresh green leaves.
ga: Akɛ cassava baai shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa koni akɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Ni eboteɔ wɔɔhe be lɛ mli, shi jeee ni egbi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai lɛ baafee eŋɔli.

english: Why do my seeds sprout after the very first rain, but die a few days later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi egbo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: The first rain triggers the seeds to germinate, but if a short dry spell follows, the weak young roots cannot reach deeper moisture in the soil, causing the seedlings to dry up and die.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ be kuku ko ni mli egbi nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. Ehaa dumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when daytime temperatures are extremely high, when there is too little water, or when insects like bees are not visiting to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa waa. Be mli ni nu faaa tsɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii eyaaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push stalks down into the dirt after they flower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ eshishifã lɛ ewoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts produce their fruit underground. After the flowers above ground are pollinated, small stalks called pegs grow downward into the soil where the nuts will safely form and mature.
ga: Peanut nibii ni anáa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afee ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot every season drains the exact same soil nutrients and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like beans or groundnuts restores the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaajie niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tamɔ nakai pɛpɛɛpɛ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the earth. If the soil is hard, compacted, or rocky, the tubers cannot push downward easily, resulting in small and misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shi oya. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii ni efite.

english: Even short weeds take away hidden water, sunlight, and fertilizer from the soil that your taller crops need, which will reduce the size and quality of your harvest.
ga: Jwɛi kukuji po jieɔ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa otsei kakadaji lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha okpamɔ lɛ dalɛ kɛ bɔ ni ehi ha lɛ nɔ aba shi.

english: Why are tiny green insects curling the leaves of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Curling baa yɛ mi cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Those insects are likely aphids that suck juice from the underside of cowpea leaves, causing the leaves to curl up and weaken the plant. Spraying approved neem water or recommended insecticides will control them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsina ŋmeii ashishi lɛ mli nu lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ neem nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from harsh sunlight. Without larger plants like plantains or temporary shade trees planted above them, direct sunlight burns their leaves and dries out the topsoil, causing the cocoa leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛji tsei wuji bɛ lɛ, abaanyɛ adu tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the maize the food it needs to grow strong and turn dark green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni amɛhe awa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with lots of leaves but give me very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or the plants are shaded, the cassava puts all its energy into growing top leaves and stems instead of storing food underground. Choosing the right cassava variety and avoiding excess nitrogen fertilizer helps energy go into tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ ehiɛ hulutsoo. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ baai kɛ tsei. Yɛ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmei henɔ ni sa ni ooohala ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni akɛ hewalɛ awo ŋmei shishifãi ni miida lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds as close together as possible so I can get more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from each other. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow big, heavy cobs instead of many small, weak ones.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii. Yɛ cob bibioo ko najiaŋ lɛ, mɛi babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ

english: How does leaving weeds in my farm hurt my crops even if the weeds are small?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mashi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui, kɛji jwɛi lɛ faaa po?

english: Weeds act as thieves in your field. They drink the ground water and absorb the plant food meant for your crops, while also providing a hiding place for harmful insect pests that feed on your crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ julɔi yɛ nyɛŋmɔji amli. Amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni amɛmuɔ tsei aniyenii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni yeɔ onibii lɛ náa he ko ni amɛhiɔ amɛhe.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating cassava with crops like beans or maize helps the soil recover.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa ehe feɔ fɛo.

english: Why do small caterpillars curl up inside the funnels of my young corn plants and eat the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ?

english: These are young caterpillars, commonly Fall Armyworms, which hide in the central funnel of maize where the leaves are tender. Inspecting fields early allows you to crush them or apply targeted biopesticides before they damage the growing tip.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii bibii, ni bei pii lɛ amɛji Fall Armyworms, ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli he ni baai lɛ ji bibii lɛ. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo okɛwoɔ mli dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot spells without enough water in the soil, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Regular watering and mulching help keep the plant calm so flowers become fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ, tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa trukaa ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ feɔ dioo. Fɔfɔi lɛ batsɔ aduawai.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly a few days after heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast when exposed directly to the hot sun and wind. Covering the bare soil around crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps rainwater in the ground longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni aduɔ nibii ni akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) tsuɔ nii tamɔ blanket ni haa nugbɔ nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land has good soil for growing vegetables before I spend money on fertilizer?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni abaanyɛ adu aduawai yɛ mli dani ofite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: Good soil is usually dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, and holds moisture well. If native weeds grow thick, dark green, and tall on uncultivated ground, it is a good sign that the soil is rich in natural plant nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ oya yɛ oniji amli ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Kɛji akɛ jwɛi ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ dara babaoo Eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ. kɛ nɔ ni nɔ kwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nɔ nii nɔ lɛ nɔ Eji okadi kpakpa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsei amli niyenii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Is it good for me to spray chemical medicine on my crops early in the morning when there is heavy dew on the leaves?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ leebi be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy dew can dilute the spray medicine or cause it to drip off the leaves before the plant can absorb it. It is best to wait until the dew dries slightly so the medicine sticks properly to the crop and gives full protection.
ga: Afua ni naa wa baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ afee mlɛo loo eha ejɛ baai lɛ anɔ dani tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ agbi fioo koni tsofa lɛ akpɛtɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ ni ebu he kwraa.

english: Will rain wash away the medicine I just sprayed on my crops?
ga: Ani nugbɔ lɛ baatsumɔ tsofa ni mikɛshwie miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ amrɔ nɛɛ?

english: Yes, if heavy rain falls shortly after spraying, it washes the medicine off the leaves before it can work. Try to spray when you expect a few hours of dry weather so the crop has time to soak up the chemical.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ etsɛɛɛ lɛ Tsofa lɛ baaho baai lɛ ahe dani ebɔi nitsumɔ. Bɔɔmɔdɛŋ ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ beni okpaa gbɛ akɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi baahi shi lɛ koni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná tsofai lɛ.

english: Which direction should I turn my cassava stems when planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ akwɛ kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should always be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the plant wastes energy trying to turn its shoots around, resulting in weak growth and smaller roots.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji okɛ tsei shwie shi lɛ Tso lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ ato najiaŋ. Enɛ haa dalɛ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi bibii baa.

english: What will happen if I plant my crop seeds too deep down in the dirt?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ?

english: If seeds are buried too deep, they exhaust all their stored energy trying to push up through the soil and may die before reaching the light. Planting at the recommended shallow depth helps seeds sprout faster.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Akɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋwɛi ni ebaanyɛ egbo dani eshɛ la lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni aaadu yɛ he ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Seed yams rot when cut surfaces are not properly dried before planting or when planted in overly wet soil. Protecting the exposed cut area allows a hard skin to form, keeping soil rot from entering the inside.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ agbiko he ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu loo kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ nɔ. He ni afo lɛ he ni abuɔ lɛ haa hewolo ni wa baa. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekafite yɛ mli.

english: How do small insect eggs on my crop leaves cause damage inside the fruits later?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite aduawai lɛ amli?

english: When insect eggs hatch, the tiny worms burrow directly into the fruit or pod to feed. Once inside, they are protected from rain and chemical sprays, causing the harvest to rot from the inside out.
ga: Kɛ́ kooloi akui lɛ fɔ lɛ, kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ tso lɛ yibii loo tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛye nii. Kɛ́ obote mli lɛ, abaabu ohe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot inside even when I don't see any insects around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ mli be mli ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by tiny fungi that spread through water drops and high moisture, not just insects. Damp weather allows the fungus to penetrate the pod skin and destroy the beans inside.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu mli ni eyɛ fɛ̃i babaoo Jeee kooloi bibii pɛ Shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ pod lɛ hewolo lɛ mli ni efiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do young crop seedlings wilt even when the ground has some moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ fioo moŋ lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air as well as moisture. If the soil is too packed or waterlogged, the roots drown and cannot send water up to the stem, causing the upper leaves to droop and wither.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu nu kɛya tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my harvested vegetables spoil so fast when I carry them around in the sun after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo hulu lɛ mli beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested crops remain alive and produce heat. Leaving them under hot sun or handling them roughly causes hidden bruises on the inside, which quickens decay and allows rot to set in rapidly.
ga: Nibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛmiiwo dɔlɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi lɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo okɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Ebaaha ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aba. Enɛ baaha egbo oya ni ebaaha egbo oya.

english: Why do insects still destroy my dried grains after I tie them up inside storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ lolo beni mikɛ amɛ ewo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insect eggs are often already hidden on the grains before bagging. If the grains are not treated or stored in hermetic (airtight) bags, the eggs hatch inside and the pests feed on the grain undisturbed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ kooloi bibii afɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ dani akɛwoɔ kotoku mli. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu dumɔwui lɛ ahe nii loo akɛtooo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (vacuum) mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafɔ yɛ mli ni ŋmeii lɛ baaye dumɔwui lɛ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko gbaaa amɛnaa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and shallow roots that dry out quickly under direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or cassava grown nearby to block harsh sun rays and keep the soil cool and moist until the cocoa plants grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo yucca ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni naa wa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara waa.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal nutrients, water, and light from the main mother plant. Removing extra shoots and leaving only two or three healthy ones ensures the main plant grows big and produces large bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ plantain kome he lɛ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ la kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii 2-3 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ekɛ ŋmeii babaoo aba.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn dark green and grow healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What are these tiny caterpillars eating the inside leaves of my maize, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ yeɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛ naa?

english: These pests are Fall Armyworms, which feed on the fresh leaves inside the maize stalk. You can manage them by spraying recommended safe insecticides early in the morning or late evening, or by dropping a mixture of neem powder and sand directly into the center of the plants.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni yeɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei amli lɛ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ amɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ neem powda kɛ ŋã ni akɛfutu mli ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from the hybrid maize I bought to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid corn ni mihe lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: It is not recommended to plant saved seeds from hybrid maize. Hybrid seeds are specially produced to yield heavily only in the first season; seeds saved from that harvest will grow into weak plants with very low yields in the next season.
ga: Akɛ ŋaawoo haaa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni ahere kɛjɛ ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil and cannot drain away quickly. Planting your cassava stems on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to run off, keeping the roots dry enough to grow healthy tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli oya. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ agbi bɔ ni sa koni bulbs ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very good for your soil. Groundnuts capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the dirt, which naturally feeds the surrounding maize plants and improves crop yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ hi waa kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ. Akpɔlɔi mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves (called mulching) stops the hot sun from drying out the dirt, prevents weeds from sprouting, and decays over time into rich natural fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baaha Enɛ (ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching) lɛ baaye abua ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfite yɛ be ni sa mli koni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa kɛha onibii.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants curling up and falling off before making peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off pepper plants mainly due to extreme heat, dry soil, or attacks from tiny insects like thrips. Watering your plants consistently and using safe insect sprays or soap water helps keep the flowers healthy so they turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ pepper tsei anɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni oooha otsei lɛ daa ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ loo samla ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning small and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe wa lɛ?

english: Curling leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies spreading a virus, or from severe heat stress. Controlling these insects early and keeping the soil moist helps protect your plants from leaf curl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Haomɔ ni naa wa nɛɛ nɔyeli mra Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu otsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and drop off during the Harmattan dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dry Harmattan winds strip moisture rapidly from young cocoa plants. Shade trees and mulching around the roots help keep the soil humid and protect delicate leaves from scorching.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ amli oya. Shade trees kɛ mulching ni bɔleɔ he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Having too many shoots forces the main plant to share limited water and nutrients. Pruning extra shoots leaves only one or two strong suckers, which produces much larger plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ tso lɛ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso titri lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii fioo pɛ aha. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ amli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ, ni no baaha plantain tso lɛ afee nɔ ni da kwraa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars hiding inside the central stalk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii Mine lɛ yɛ bu ni etse. Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that feeds on tender leaf growth. Spraying early when the caterpillars are small prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa fe fɛɛ ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ baai bibii ni daraa lɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shishijee Beni ŋmeii lɛ ji gbekɛbii lɛ enɛ haaa amɛfite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why does lowland swamp rice thrive in standing water while my maize crop dies if the field floods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ marsh ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu shwie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal structures that allow oxygen to travel down to roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot without oxygen from dry soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ mligbɛ gbɛjianɔtoo krɛdɛɛ ko ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shi kɛyaa amɛshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to mount tall sticks for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makɛ tsei kakadaji ama shi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground spreads out leaves to capture maximum sunlight, which provides the energy needed to grow big, heavy tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaagbɛ efoji lɛ eshwa koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Cassava roots cannot survive in waterlogged soil because excess moisture encourages fungal diseases. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ he hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or calcium deficiency causes severe stress, making the tomato plant drop its flowers to conserve energy instead of forming fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be Loo calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and growing small and crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee bibii ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies transmitting plant viruses, or by intense heat stress. Managing pests early prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai lɛ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa Mra be mli ni akwɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei ahe tsei lɛ ahe fitemɔ naa.

english: Why do agricultural officers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds nutrient-hungry crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei ni he hiaa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ abele niyenii.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crops with dry grass or maize leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Vegetables with hay or corn leaves?

english: Covering the soil (mulching) blocks hot sunlight, retains soil moisture longer during dry stretches, and suppresses weeds from growing around crop roots.
ga: Mulching (mulching) baatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni ekpaa jwɛi ni shwereɔ yɛ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ naa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains come late in my area?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ enɛɔ fioo yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the first heavy, soaking rain ensures seeds absorb moisture right away to germinate fast, which is critical when the remaining wet period is short.
ga: Kɛ́ adu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. Enɛ he miihia beni hulutsoo be ni eshwɛ lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: What should I do if the rainy season is going to be very short this year?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ afi nɛɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ faaa kwraa hu?

english: You should switch to short-duration or early-maturing seed varieties that need less time to flower and fruit before the dry weather sets in.
ga: Esa akɛ otsake kɛya dumɔwui ni yeɔ be kukuoo loo ni shwereɔ mra, ni biɔ be fioo dani amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai dani hulutsoo be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why does my harvest drop so much if I plant during the minor rainy season instead of the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi waa kɛji midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli moŋ fe nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ?

english: The minor rainy season provides less total rainfall and shorter wet periods, giving plants less time and water to build up food for large grains or tubers.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni baa shi lɛ haa nugbɔshiimɔ baa shi kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei kukuji. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náaa be kɛ nu babaoo ni ekɛbaafee niyenii kɛha dumɔwui loo bulb agboi.

english: Why do my crops wither so quickly if I plant them even a few weeks late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛji midu amɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi po sɛɛ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Late-planted crops do not have enough time to grow deep root systems before the sun dries out the topsoil, causing them to dry up as soon as rains slow down.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ bɛ be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ dani hulu lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ pɛ kɛkɛ ni sũ lɛ gbiɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets very dry and hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa ni edɔ waa lɛ?

english: High heat and lack of water cause pepper plants extreme stress, so they drop their blossoms to save water and keep the rest of the plant alive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ babaoo baa pepper tsei anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Is it better for me to clear my farm land long before planting or right when I am ready to plant?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ dani madu nii loo kɛ́ mifee klalo akɛ madu nii pɛ?

english: Clearing land early helps destroy weed roots, but tilling right before planting keeps the soil soft and ready to catch moisture when the first rains arrive.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni efiteɔ jwɛi shishifãi Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ dani aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni efee klalo akɛ ebaaná ŋmɔtɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba.

english: Why are my cassava stems taking so long to sprout leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ebaakwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need moist soil and warm conditions to break out of dormancy; if planted in dry soil, growth pauses until water becomes available.
ga: Yucca tso lɛ mli tsei ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ koni enyɛ ejɛ wɔɔhe mli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, aŋmɛɔ dalɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nu ni fa bɔ ni sa baa.

english: How deep should I bury my bean seeds so they sprout quickly before the soil dries up?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafu mi-beans lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya dani shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi?

english: Beans should be planted about 2 to 3 centimeters deep—shallow enough to sprout fast into the sunlight, but deep enough to stay protected from direct heat.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii aaafee sɛntimita 2 kɛyashi 3, ni mli ekɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ oya kɛya hulu la lɛ mli. shi eyɛ mli bɔ ni sa ni baabu he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Should I plant all my vegetable seeds on the same day or spread the planting across different weeks?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ loo magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã otsi lɛ mli?

english: Spreading your planting over several weeks reduces risk, ensuring that a sudden dry week will not ruin your entire crop at once.
ga: Kɛ́ atsake he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mli otsii babaoo lɛ, oshara ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa otsi ni nu hɔmɔ baa trukaa lɛ efiteee onibii fɛɛ shikome.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist and crops are growing actively, but avoid applying right before expected heavy downpours that can wash the nutrients off the field.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida lɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa, ni baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: How can I stop free-roaming farm animals like sheep and goats from destroying my young maize shoots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yɔɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe, tamɔ tooi kɛ tooi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmãa bibii lɛ?

english: Young maize shoots are tender, sweet, and rich in nutrients, making them a favorite food for free-roaming livestock. Protecting your plot with living fences, such as Jatropha or thorny hedges, creates a natural barrier that deters animals while your crops establish.
ga: Abele bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe ŋɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ sumɔɔ waa. Bu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka tamɔ jatropha loo ŋmeii. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi anaa yɛ be mli ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why do domestic chickens scratch around my seedbeds, and how can I protect my newly planted seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shia kooloi miiho yɛ mibii akwɛmɔhe lɛ he lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui heei lɛ ahe?

english: Chickens dig in freshly tilled soil to search for worms, insects, and easy seeds to eat. Covering your planted seedbeds with light mulch, palm fronds, or netting hides the seeds and prevents poultry from disturbing the soil until the seeds sprout.
ga: Kooloi tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ehee lɛ mli koni amɛtao ŋmeii, kooloi bibii kɛ dumɔwui ni ayeɔ oya. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmei tsei, loo ŋshɔŋlooi ha dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato ni ebaatsi kooloi anaa koni amɛkagba shikpɔŋ lɛ naa kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to reduce water loss. The plant is not dead; it goes into a dormant state to conserve moisture until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Ebabote shihilɛ ni yɔɔ kpoo mli koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during intense midday sun to reduce leaf surface area exposed to heat, which minimizes water evaporation. It is the plant's natural self-defense reaction to stress from heat and sunlight.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛba baa lɛ hiɛ ni dɔlɛ baa lɛ shi. ni haa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi Eji tso ko adebɔɔ mli hetoo ni ekɛbuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la mli baa lɛ he.

english: Why are my young maize leaves turning purple after a long period of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ purple yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on maize often mean wet, cold soil is temporarily stopping the roots from absorbing phosphorus. Once the soil dries out and warms up, the roots recover and the new leaves grow green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni mli ejɔ lɛ miitsi shishifãi lɛ anaa be kukuoo ko koni amɛkaŋɔ fɔsfɔs. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ ni edɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni baai heei lɛ baafee eŋɔli.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme heat or drought stresses the plant, preventing successful pollination. Providing adequate watering and light shade during extremely hot periods helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ ha tso lɛ hao. Enɛ haaa anyɛ afee pollination yɛ omanyeyeli mli. Nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why is my yam crop growing very lush, long vines but producing small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ wain tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa lɛ? Shi eyɛ yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages yams to put all their energy into leafy vine growth above ground instead of tuber development. Adding potassium-rich fertilizers helps redirect energy to growing bigger tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ awo wain tsei ni baai yɔɔ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaafee ŋmeii. Potassium ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aya bulbs wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and dry up while still on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods turn black due to black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cool, humid, and heavily shaded conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches opens the canopy to sunlight and airflow, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ black pod hela lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni shwereɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Kookoo niji ni fa fe nine ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Ehaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cowpeas produce excessive leaves and fewer pods when planted in soil rich in nitrogen or when they receive heavy rainfall during flowering. Moderate water and balanced soil prompt the plant to shift energy into flowering and pod production.
ga: Cowpea woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nitrogen eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ja baaha tso lɛ atsake ehewalɛ lɛ ni etsɔ fɔfɔi ni woɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that stay near the surface, making them prone to falling under heavy bunches and strong winds. Staking trees with sturdy wooden poles or planting them in windbreaks keeps them upright.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbeeɔ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa shishi. Tso lɛ ni akɛ tso ni wa duɔ loo aduɔ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, a major nutrient needed for growth. Applying an appropriate fertilizer like NPK or Urea, or adding well-rotted animal manure, helps restore their green color and boosts healthy development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo urea tsuɔ nii loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha hiɛyaa kpakpa aya hiɛ.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my cassava so it does not spoil in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei? Koni ekafite yɛ sũ lɛ mli?

english: Most cassava varieties in Ghana mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, when the bottom leaves turn yellow and begin to drop. Leaving mature cassava roots in the soil for too long can cause them to become woody, tough, and lose starch content.
ga: Cassava henɔi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo shɛɔ shweremɔ he yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ. Beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbɔi gbee shi lɛ Kɛ́ ashiɔ ŋmei shishifãi ni eda lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛtsɔ tsei, amɛhe wa ni amɛmli ŋmei lɛ akafee nɔ ni yɔɔ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is risky to plant after just one rain because early rains are often followed by long dry spells that scorch germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become consistent and the soil stays moist before planting.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara. Enɛ ji akɛ, bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani odu.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark dust inside the center shoot?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ ni eshiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ yɛ amaga lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a widespread crop pest. Checking your field early, crushing caterpillars by hand on small farms, or applying approved sprays into the heart of the plant in early morning or evening can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. Ni akɛ niji shwieɔ ŋmeii anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli Aloo, kɛ akɛ tsofa ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon even if the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Vegetable leaves curl up during the hottest part of the day to reduce water loss from intense sunlight. As long as the soil has moisture and the leaves uncurl when the sun goes down, this is a natural self-defense response to heat.
ga: Aduawai ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Koni nu ni hulu la ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni baai lɛ shwieee shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ, Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ ohe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he.

english: Will I harvest more food if I plant my crop seeds very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Ani makpa niyenii babaoo kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛhi mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close together actually lowers your harvest because crops will compete heavily for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant to grow stronger and produce bigger, healthier fruits or tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aba shi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulu la he akaŋ waa. Gbɛ ni sa, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii loo bulbs ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young crops have small root systems and are easily overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds that steal sunlight, water, and fertilizer. Clearing weeds during the first three to four weeks gives your young plants the best environment to establish strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni jwɛi ni daa oya ni juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ oya. Kɛ́ okwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aná shihilɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why should I avoid growing maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously on one piece of land drains specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts rebuilds soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: Can I save seeds from my current hybrid maize harvest to plant during the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ hybrid ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crop varieties usually results in weak plants and significantly lower yields in the next season. It is best to buy fresh certified hybrid seeds each season, or only save seeds from traditional open-pollinated plant varieties.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi waa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ daa afi. Aloo buaa dumɔwui pɛ anaa kɛjɛɔ blema tsei ni agbeleɔ amɛnaa lɛ amli.

english: How deep into the soil should I push my seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ matsi dumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: As a simple guide, plant seeds at a depth equal to two or three times their size. Planting too deep prevents the shoot from reaching the surface before running out of energy, while planting too shallow leaves seeds exposed to birds and drying sun.
ga: Nyiɛmɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo sɛɛ Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛ́ adu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛhewalɛ lɛ afite. Yɛ be mli ni oduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, ha dumɔwui lɛ ata okpoi lɛ ahe ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants need protection from direct sunlight. If they do not have shade trees or plantains planted nearby, the strong sun scorches their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. If there are no shade trees or seedlings planted nearby, the strong sunlight will scorch the young leaves and dry out the soil moisture.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Placing seeds too close together forces plants to compete for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to develop thick stems and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tso lɛ mli tsei ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and humid conditions. Pruning excess tree branches and clearing weeds allows air to flow through the farm and reduces dampness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa hulutsoo baa shi.
