english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the central leaves (the whorl) to feed, so applying early control measures directly into the center of the plant helps protect the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ atsu gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ he nii mra. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baaye abua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: It is usually better to wait for steady rainfall. The first rain is often followed by a dry spell, which can heat up the soil and ruin newly planted seeds before the main rainy season starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ daa. Bei pii lɛ, ahum ni mli egbi nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adɔ ni efite dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting, when lower leaves begin to turn yellow and fall off. You can also dig up one plant to check if the roots have reached a good size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa tso ko hu koni okwɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ dalɛ sa.

english: Why should I cut away the small shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots (suckers) forces the main tree to share its food and water. Keeping only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant produces larger and healthier plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ajara niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo plantain tso ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my crops look pale green even though I clear weeds from my farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ?

english: Pale green or yellowish leaves often mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient for healthy leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can give the plants the food they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ.

english: Flowers often drop when plants experience heat stress or a lack of water during flowering. Watering regularly and keeping mulch around the base of the plant helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Nu ni oooha amɛ daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: How can I stop small insects from destroying my stored dried maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii ni mifite ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ naa?

english: Insects thrive in damp environments. Ensuring your maize is completely sun-dried before storage and keeping it in clean, sealed bags or hermetic containers stops insects from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni o-corn lɛ agbi kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ mli dani okɛto. ni okɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli. Ebaaye ebua ni kooloi bibii akafee babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to direct heat and sunlight. They require shade trees or fast-growing nurse crops like plantain to shield their young leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist around their roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛkɛbu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ shãa he. kɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe

english: Why is cocoa farming so much more labor-intensive throughout the year compared to grain crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo dumɔ heɔ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli kɛ akɛto ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ abele dumɔ he lɛ?

english: Cocoa is a perennial tree crop that needs continuous care, including year-round weed clearing, regular pruning of dead branches, shade management, pest control, and multi-step manual processing like pod splitting, fermenting, and drying.
ga: Cocoa ji tso ni yeɔ daa ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ nɔ daa. Nɔ ni fata he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Niji ni egboi lɛ ahe ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa Shade nɔkwɛmɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ nibii babaoo ni akɛ niji tsuɔ he nii tamɔ pod mligbalamɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the branch before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, humid conditions with excessive shade. Pruning your tree branches lets sunlight and air pass through, which helps prevent the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Niji ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What causes green bushy plants with small sticky berries to grow directly on my cocoa tree branches, and will they harm my crop?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei feɔ jwɛi eŋɔli ni yibii bibii ni shwieɔ shi yɔɔ mli? Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-kookoo nine lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ni ani amɛbaaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: That plant is mistletoe, a parasite spread by bird droppings. It burrows into the branches to steal food and water from your cocoa tree, which slows crop growth and can eventually kill the tree if you do not cut it off.
ga: Nakai tso lɛ ji mistletoe. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni okpoi afɔfɔi gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Efoɔ tsei aniji amli koni eju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ cacao tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ dalɛ baa shi ni yɛ naagbee lɛ ebaanyɛ egbe tso lɛ kɛji ofooo lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants curl up tightly during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yucca tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in intense afternoon heat is a natural reaction to conserve water. The plant closes up its leaf area to slow down water loss through evaporation during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni akɛbuɔ nu he. Tsei lɛ ŋaa amɛbaai lɛ ahe koni nu lɛ akafite fiofio yɛ la ni hoɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow so well in forest regions like Ashanti, but struggle in dryer areas of Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni kooi yɔɔ tamɔ Ashanti shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ Ghana hei ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Forest regions like Ashanti have deep, rich soil that retains moisture and high rainfall spread across two wet seasons, which matches the natural tropical environment cocoa trees need to thrive.
ga: Kooi amli hei tamɔ Ashanti yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo ni gbɛɔ eshwaa nugbɔ bei enyɔ mli. Enɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ni mli edɔ waa ni he hiaa cacao tsei koni amɛshwere lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are turning light green because of poor soil or because of lack of rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ?

english: When plants lack rain, their leaves wilt and droop, but they bounce back quickly after watering. If the leaves remain pale green or yellow even when the soil is wet, the soil lacks nutrients and needs fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ tsei bɛ nugbɔ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shi. Shi nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba oya. Kɛji baai lɛ tee nɔ efee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my cocoa tree produce plenty of flowers, but only a few of them turn into actual pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ anɔkwa ŋmeii.

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many flowers if they experience water stress, lack essential soil nutrients, or lack small pollinating insects like midges to fertilize the blossoms.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei baajie fɔfɔi babaoo kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges ni baaha kookoo tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛ.

english: Weeds are wild local plants adapted to quickly absorb water and surface nutrients before cultivated crops can. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital plant food from your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju tsei niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ otsei titrii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small and thin even though the leaves look healthy and bushy above ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ waa lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfee jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi

english: If soil has too much nitrogen or if plants are grown too close together, the cassava focuses energy on growing tall leaves instead of storing starches in the roots underground.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ baai kakadaji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ ahe nii moŋ fe ni ekɛ starch baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why did my cassava tubers rot in the ground after I sprayed weed medicine on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If weed medicine (herbicide) is sprayed too close to cassava plants or mixed too strong, the chemical soaks through the leaves and stem down into the roots. This destroys the plant's internal food storage, causing the tubers to spoil and rot before harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi (herbicide) lɛ shwieɔ ŋmei tso lɛ he tsɔ loo akɛfutuɔ waa tsɔ Tsofai lɛ hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii ni atoɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: What happens to my maize if I mix more farm chemical with water than the bottle instructions say?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofai futu nu babaoo fe bɔ ni aŋma yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using more chemical than instructed makes the solution too strong, which causes 'chemical burn.' Instead of just killing weeds or pests, the harsh mixture damages the leaves of your maize, turning them brown and dry as if they were scorched by fire.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. ni kɛ ‘Chemical burns’ baa yɛ jwɛi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ agbemɔ najiaŋ Nibii ni mli wa baafite o-corn baai lɛ. Etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egbiɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ashã.

english: Can spraying weed killer on my land damage my neighbor's nearby plantain trees?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbe mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ?

english: Yes, fine mist from weed killer can drift in the wind to nearby crops like plantains. Even small amounts of herbicide landing on plantain leaves can cause severe leaf burning, deformed growth, or plant death.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, afua kpakpa ni jɛɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ anɔ. Tsofa fioo ko po ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni baagbee plantain baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha baai lɛ ashã waa. shweremɔ ni efite loo tso lɛ baanyɛ agbo

english: My parents taught me to plant maize seeds very close together, so why are you advising me to leave bigger gaps?
ga: Mifɔlɔi tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ okɛɔ akɛ mashi gbɛ agbo ko?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving proper space allows each maize plant to grow strong roots, thick stalks, and larger, fuller cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi he ni sa lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa tso náa shishifãi ni wa, ŋmeii ni mli wa, kɛ ŋmãa wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less harvest every year when I keep planting cassava on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls specific nutrients out of the soil to grow its heavy tubers. Planting cassava on the same spot every year depletes those vital nutrients, leaving the soil exhausted unless you rotate with other crops like beans or let the land rest.
ga: Cassava jieɔ niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa nakai niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa shi, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ baa shi ja okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmeii, loo oha shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning light green and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that the corn plant is starving for nutrients, particularly nitrogen. When soil lacks organic matter or nutrients, crops cannot produce the green color needed to catch sunlight and make food.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli. titri lɛ nitrogen Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ Dumɔwui nyɛŋ ajie su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa koni akɛmɔ hulu la ni akɛfee niyenii lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa saplings burn and die when I clear away all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tso lɛ shã ni egbo beni mijie tsei wuji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants naturally require shade to survive. Removing all canopy trees exposes tender cocoa leaves to harsh direct sunlight and heat, which dries out the soil and scorches the young plants.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ ajie kookoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ baa kookoo baai bibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni eshã tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly into tiny balls during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu bibioo ko yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a self-defense reaction. The pepper plant rolls its leaves to shrink the surface area exposed to direct sun, preventing precious water from evaporating out of the plant during peak heat.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji nɔ ko ni afeɔ koni akɛbu he. Pepper tsei shwieɔ amɛ baai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ afee bibioo. Enɛ ji koni nu ni jara wa lɛ akajɛ tsei lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to spray pest medicine on my bean crops while they are in full bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ oookɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛmiikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Spraying during flowering kills beneficial insects like bees that visit flowers to pollinate them. Without pollination, bean flowers fall off without forming crop pods, leading to a poor harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni saraa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Pea fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛfeee pods. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji kpamɔ ni ehiii.

english: Why do armyworm caterpillars suddenly appear in large numbers right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo jeɔ kpo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Armyworm moths fly in with rain clouds and lay thousands of eggs on fresh green sprouts. When the rains arrive, these eggs hatch all at once, leading to sudden caterpillar swarms that feed on young crops.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nugbɔ atatui fɔ̃ɔ kɛbaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii akpei abɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, wɔji lɛ feɔ ekome kɛfɔ̃ɔ. Amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ekɛ ŋmeii akui ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and turn brown when the sun gets too hot during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have weak root systems and delicate leaves that cannot handle intense, direct sunlight. Establishing temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from scorching, keeps the soil cool, and helps them retain moisture while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shãa naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without turning into fruit during the hot months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ nyɔji ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high and water is low, plants drop their flowers to save energy and survive heat stress. Providing regular water directly to the soil and using light shade netting can keep the soil cool enough for flowers to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni nu lɛ hu faaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ daa kɛ shade netting ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa ni fɔfɔii lɛ baawo yibii.

english: Why are my old cocoa trees producing fewer pods now than they did ten years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei momo lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo fe afii nyɔŋma ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: As crop trees age, the soil around them loses vital nutrients, and old branches become inefficient at bearing fruit. Pruning dead branches, replenishing soil nutrients, and replacing very old trees with fresh seedlings restores total farm yield over time.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ da lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baafite niyenii ni he hiaa ni niji momo lɛ wooo yibii. tsei niji ni egboi lɛ akwɛmɔ Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ tsei ni egbɔ waa lɛ ni akɛ dumɔwui heei yeɔ najiaŋ. Ebaaye ebua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why should I trim off healthy branches from my fruit trees when they look so big and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni jɛ mi-aduawai tsei lɛ amli lɛ be mli ni amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Trimming branches allows sunlight and fresh air to reach the center of the tree, which stops fungal diseases from breeding and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger pods and fruits instead of extra leaves.
ga: Tso lɛ mlifomɔ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa shɛɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ akagbɛ ashwã. ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji kɛ aduawai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛ baai baafata he.

english: What causes the pods on my cocoa trees to turn dark brown and dry up before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ dani akpaa?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp, and overly shady conditions. Clearing excess weeds, trimming overgrown tree branches to let light in, and removing infected pods quickly keeps the healthy pods safe.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, edɔ, kɛ shade tsɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ Niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ koni la abote mli Ni ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ahiɔ shi shweshweeshwe.

english: How do fall armyworms destroy my maize farm so fast, and where do they come from?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii kpata mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ hiɛ oya? Ni nɛgbɛ amɛjɛɔ?

english: Armyworm moths fly into farms at night and lay hundreds of eggs on young leaves. Once the caterpillars hatch, they eat the central leaves of the maize plant where growth happens, so catching them very early is critical to saving the crop.
ga: Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ fãa kɛboteɔ ŋmɔji amli gbɛkɛ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai ni yɔɔ he ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɔmɔ amɛ mra. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia waa akɛ abu ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us not to plant cassava too close to young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkadu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava plants are heavy feeders that aggressively steal water and nutrients from the soil, and their underground tubers spread widely, which chokes the weak roots of young cocoa seedlings.
ga: Cassava tso lɛ ji niyenii ni tsii ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ egbɛ eshwã he fɛɛ he. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: How does leaving dry leaves on the ground around my crops help them during dry weather?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ amɛbuaa amɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry leaves act as mulch, forming a protective cover over the soil that stops sunlight from evaporating groundwater, keeping the root area cool and moist for much longer.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Etsuɔ nii koni ekɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la akajɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ tsɔne ko yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants roll their leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which prevents moisture from evaporating out of the plant leaves during hot, dry days.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do my mature cassava roots become soft and rot in the ground when heavy rains last too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When rain saturates the soil for too long, water displaces the air in the dirt, suffocating the roots and creating perfect conditions for rot-causing soil organisms to destroy the cassava tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni miifite lɛ mli lɛ akpãtã ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my crops and soil when I plant on a hill?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ midumɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu nii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When rain falls on a slope, water moves quickly downhill and carries rich topsoil and plants with it. Planting along contour lines across the slope slows down the water so it sinks into the soil to nourish your crops instead of washing them away.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Nu lɛ yaa oya kɛyaa shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ yaa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaha nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. No hewɔ lɛ nu lɛ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha onibii lɛ niyenii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeshwie amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers ask us to mark contour lines when preparing farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni wɔkadi husui beni wɔsaa ŋmɔji ahe lɛ?

english: Contour lines follow the natural height level of your land. Making ridges or planting along these lines acts like a series of small dams, stopping heavy rainwater from rushing downhill and destroying your crops.
ga: Kontu linei nyiɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔyaa sɛɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi nɛɛ anɔ ŋshɔkei ni ooofee loo dumɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋshɔkei bibii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ, ni etsĩɔ nugbɔ nu ni naa wa ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ naa ni efiteɔ onibii.

english: What is the purpose of digging ditches across my farm land?
ga: Mɛni ji yiŋtoo ni yɔɔ nubui ni mifoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Ditches help control excess rainwater by directing floodwater safely away from crop roots so they do not rot, while also catching rich soil that washes down during heavy downpours.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ nu afua lɛ ni etsɔɔ gbɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi ahe lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akafite Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni kulɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ baaho kɛya lɛ toɔ.

english: Why do my crops at the bottom of the slope grow differently from those at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ramp lɛ shishi lɛ daa lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Water and washed-away soil nutrients naturally collect at the bottom of a slope, making that area wetter and richer, while the top of the hill dries out faster and loses nutrients easily.
ga: Nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa ni nu lɛ hoɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ gɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa jɛmɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehaa jɛmɛ feɔ nii babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, gɔji lɛ anɔ yitsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi oya.

english: Is it a good idea to plant my crops directly inside low areas where rainwater collects?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Most crops like maize and cocoa will rot if their roots stay soaked in standing water for too long. Low areas need proper drainage ditches to channel water away before you can safely plant crops there.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ kookoo lɛ ateŋ babaoo baafite kɛji akɛ akɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu ni damɔ shi mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Esa akɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ aná nu tsɔne ni sa ni baaha nu lɛ atsɔ mli dani abaanyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ jɛmɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: How does building a farm shed or structure affect water flow to my crops?
ga: Te tsũ loo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni ama lɛ saa nu ni hoɔ kɛyaa miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Putting up a building or heavy foundation changes how water naturally runs across the land. This can accidentally block water from reaching your crops or redirect dangerous floodwater straight into your planted field.
ga: Tsu loo shishitoo ni tsii ni akɛma shi lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni nu tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ nu naa koni ekashɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ loo ekɛ nu afua ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ aya he ni okwɛɔ nii yɛ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I level out the natural ditches and mounds along my farm boundary?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifeɔ adebɔɔ mli nubui kɛ gɔji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ he lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Natural ditches and boundary mounds serve as protective barriers. They slow down heavy runoff coming from neighboring land and prevent your fertile topsoil from washing off your farm.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli nubui kɛ gɔji tsuɔ nii akɛ hebuu. Amɛhaa nu ni hoɔ babaoo ni jɛɔ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi. ni otsi osũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ naa koni ekafɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does fertilizer wash away from my crops even when I bury it in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛfutuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: If water flows too fast across your land during heavy rains, underground water streams carry nutrients away past the root zone before plants can absorb them. Ridge barriers help hold water and fertilizer in place.
ga: Kɛji nu hoɔ oya tsɔ kɛtsɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni hoɔ lɛ woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ ahe dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hiɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ.

english: How do I stop heavy water runoff from a neighboring farm from damaging my young crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi muji ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli lɛ naa koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ?

english: You can dig a diversion ditch along your farm border to safely catch incoming floodwater and guide it around your planted field rather than allowing it to rush through your crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ husu lɛ naa koni nu ni baa lɛ ahi mli shweshweeshwe. ni otsɔ gbɛ kɛbɔle ŋmɔji ni odu lɛ ahe Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha etsɔ onibii amli.

english: Why do crops wilt faster in sandy parts of my farm compared to clay parts after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii gboiɔ oya yɛ hei ni ŋã yɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ fã ni yɔɔ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Sandy soil has loose particles that allow water to drain away very fast beyond the reach of crop roots, while clay soil holds onto water longer like a sponge, keeping crops hydrated during dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii ni haa nu hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni akɛ shikpɔŋ fee lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore their green color and boosts grain growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmaa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during wet and damp weather. Clearing weeds around the base and pruning excess shade branches improves airflow and keeps the pods dry, preventing the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛkpamɔ baaha kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ koni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying neem oil or appropriate protective sprays early on keeps these pests away so the plant can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. Neem fɔ loo tsofa ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings suddenly fall over and die right after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This is called damping-off, caused by fungi in overly wet soil that attack tender young stems. Planting seeds in well-drained soil and avoiding overwatering protects fragile seedlings in their first few days.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ damping off, ni ŋmei ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fe nine ni tutuaa tsei bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ baaye abua ni abu dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ gbii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small even when the leaves on top grow big and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbɔjɔ lolo ni amɛhe efee bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ dara ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is packed too hard, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing top leaves instead of expanding underground roots. Loosening the soil gives the roots space to swell into fat tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeegbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ amli shwereɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ fɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests to build up. Alternating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and starves crop-specific pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ehaa niyenii ni baa tso lɛ mli kooloi pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why is it wasteful for me to apply fertilizer right before heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji fitemɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the root zone into gutters before the plant can drink it, wasting your money. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist—not soaked—allows the roots to absorb the nutrients properly.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli kɛyaa nubui lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ nuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite oshika. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli beni sũ lɛ mli edɔ—jeee ni edɔ—eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kpakpai lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants drop off without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady with mulching and planting heat-tolerant varieties helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ adumɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested yams grow crooked and split instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɛ eshwa moŋ fe ni eeefee kakadaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams bend and split when their growing tips hit hard rocks or compacted clay underground. Creating deep, soft soil mounds cleared of stones allows the yam to expand straight and smooth.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efoɔ kɛ́ eshishigbɛ ni miida lɛ tswa tɛ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni tɛi bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during strong winds right when the fruit bunch gets heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli beni aduawai akutsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛtsiimɔ pɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and carry heavy weight at the top, making them easy targets for strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy wooden prop gives the tree structural support until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Ehaa efeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which plants need to build healthy green leaves. Rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil where young roots cannot reach it, or the soil may simply need manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. Nugbɔ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi bibii nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Aloo ekolɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen awo mli.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume plants decay, they release this free plant food into the ground for the next crop to use.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ Amɛjieɔ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsu nii.

english: Harmattan brings dry, dusty winds that pull moisture out of plant leaves faster than roots can absorb it from the dry soil. Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves, so they need shade trees and mulching around their bases to keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ baa. Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛbaai lɛ hu yɛ bɔdɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and watery if I harvest them right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛji mikpa amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rain falls after a dry spell, the cassava plant quickly drinks up large amounts of water and stores it in its tubers. This temporary surge of water dilutes the solid starch inside, making the tuber soft and watery until the excess water settles.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmei tso lɛ nuɔ nu babaoo oya ni ekɛtoɔ ŋmei lɛ mli. Nu ni yaa hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli nɛɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ. Ha bulb lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ kɛ nu kɛyashi nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaho.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when there is too much fertilizer causing leaf growth instead of fruit growth. It can also happen if insects are not visiting the farm to shake pollen inside the flowers to fertilize them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo mli lɛ haa baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii eyaaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛyawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo amɛ fɔ.

english: Why do so many tiny blossoms on my cocoa trunk drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo fɔfɔi bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ kookoo babaoo ni yɔɔ mi kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support. The tree voluntarily sheds most blossoms so it can focus its limited water and nutrients on growing a healthy smaller number of full-sized pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ fe bɔ ni fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baafɔ fɔfɔi babaoo kɛjɛ etsuiŋ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama nu fioo kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni dalɛ yeɔ emuu lɛ anɔ fioo.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, or by a virus carried by whiteflies. These pests suck the plant juices, causing leaves to grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, baai lɛ yɛ su ko ni ejaaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily once the bunch starts growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ tsei lɛ aniji je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms in the soil (nematodes) or banana weevils often chew into the root base, weakening the plant's grip on the soil. When the fruit bunch gets heavy, the weakened root system can no longer hold the stem upright.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii bibii (nematodes) loo banana ŋmeii shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa bɔ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baa shi. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ mli tsii lɛ, shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ shi dɔŋŋ.

english: Why does my yam vine start yellowing and drying up long before I dig up the yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani mifoɔ sweet potato lɛ?

english: When a yam plant finishes building its tuber under the ground, it naturally stops sending energy to its leaves. The vine drying up is a normal signal that all the energy has moved into the tuber and the yam is mature for harvesting.
ga: Kɛ sweet potato tso lɛ gbe eshishifãi lɛ akwɛmɔ naa lɛ, Ebaakpa hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa baa lɛ baa lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Wein tsei ni egbi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ etee ŋmeii lɛ amli ni ŋmeii lɛ edara kɛha kpamɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks snap in half easily when a small storm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa enyɔ oya yɛ ahum bibii amli lɛ?

english: Maize stems become weak and hollow if planted too close together, as plants compete for light and grow thin. Lack of potassium in the soil also weakens the outer stem wall, making the plant snap under wind pressure.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la he akaŋ ni amɛdaraa bibii. Potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hu haa tso lɛ kponɔgbɛ gbogboi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa tsei fãa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa amɛ.

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a short dry spell. Planting too early means seeds might sprout and then dry up under the scorching sun before steady rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku nyiɛɔ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do certified seeds from the agricultural officer give a better yield than the seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ema nɔ mi lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specifically bred for strong root systems, high yield, and resistance to local pests and heat, whereas saved seeds lose these strong traits over successive generations.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa, amɛwo yibii babaoo, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli dɔlɛ. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does planting my maize too close together result in smaller cobs instead of a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa fioo pɛ baa shi moŋ ni ebaawo ŋmãa babaoo lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, their roots fight each other for limited water and soil nutrients, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching neighboring plants, leaving all of them weak.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ahe. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛ fɛɛ amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why does my cassava grow very tall with bushy leaves but leave me with very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai bibii shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or plants are shaded, the cassava focuses all its energy on growing tall towards the sun instead of storing food in the tubers below ground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo tsei lɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ koni ekwɛ hulu lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii amli lɛ,.

english: Why do the leaves of my young maize turn light yellow when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil smothers plant roots, preventing them from taking up air and nitrogen. Once the soil drains and gets sunshine, the roots can feed properly again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nitrogen. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ho ni hulu la lɛ shɛ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ana niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground exposes them to maximum sunlight so they can feed the tuber, while also keeping the leaves dry to prevent fungal diseases from the damp soil.
ga: Kɛ́ owó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛ bulbs lɛ akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ agbi koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akajɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my green tomatoes turning black and soft before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This issue is blossom end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular dry and wet spells in the ground.
ga: Naagba nɛɛ ji fɔfɔi tip ni fiteɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji shikpɔŋ ni egbi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for my soil if I plant groundnuts or cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts capture natural nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, which enriches the soil and naturally feeds heavy-eating crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ, ni eji niyenii kɛha tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli amɛyeɔ nii babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops right after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mitso titri lɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that absorb water and fertilizer much faster than young crops. Clearing weeds right before fertilizing ensures your main crop gets the food.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei bibii. Jwɛi ni ooogbe dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ baaha onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii.

english: Why should I pinch off some of the small side branches on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Pruning unnecessary side branches allows the plant to redirect its water and food supply straight into growing larger, healthier pepper fruits instead of extra stem leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ tsakeɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ gbɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ pepper yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ akwɛ̃ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai krokomɛi baatsu nii.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks too close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛɔ he tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for water and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread out and produce large, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshwaa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do I need to clear big trees or plant shade crops next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei wuji loo madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full, harsh sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees provides living shade and moisture that protects young cocoa until it matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo canopy tsei lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for leaf growth. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Planting maize in the same spot repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to multiply. Rotating your crop with legumes like beans or groundnuts helps rebuild soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Ebaafite niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ ayiɔ babaoo. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot and die after a few days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato roots cannot survive when submerged in standing water because they lose the ability to breathe. Planting your tomatoes on raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Tomato shishifãi nyɛŋ ahi shi kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Tomato ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cowpea flowers fall off without forming pods during very hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant, forcing it to drop its blossoms to conserve water and survive. Planting early in the rainy season ensures the crop flowers when temperatures are cooler and soil moisture is adequate.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. ni enyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ baaha tso lɛ awo fɔfɔi be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ hu yɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upwards and stunted in growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛdaraaa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from young leaves and spreading plant viruses. Using natural sprays like neem oil helps remove these insects before they damage the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofai tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ onibii.

english: Weeds grow faster than cultivated crops and aggressively steal sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the planting season ensures your crops get all the resources they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai waa. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: How can I tell when my groundnuts are ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-peanuts lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are ready for harvest when the leaves start turning yellow and drying up. You can pull up one test plant; if the inside of the pods has turned dark brown or black, the crop is mature.
ga: No mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ ogbala kaa nitsumɔhe kome kɛya ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ pod lɛ mli batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eshɛ.

english: Why do seeds I saved from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mihere kɛjɛ naagbee nikpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu lɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in damp or hot places lose their internal energy or become infected by tiny pests. Keeping saved seeds completely dry, clean, and stored in sealed containers protects their ability to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ loo hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ baafite amɛmli hewalɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii baamɔ amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ egbi kwraa, amɛhe tse, ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ naa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ he.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and dying after I water them with water from the local river where galamsey happens?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mikɛ nu ni jɛ maŋ lɛ mli galamsey faa lɛ mli lɛ fɔ amɛnɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: River water contaminated by illegal mining (galamsey) often contains toxic heavy metals and harsh chemicals. When you use this water, the toxins damage the crop's root system, preventing the plant from taking up food and water, which turns the leaves yellow and kills the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ tsofai ni mli wa yɛ faa mli nu ni shika tsuru ni ajieɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ (galamsey) mli efite lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nu nɛɛ tsu nii lɛ, tsofai fɔji lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetables grow so slowly when I irrigate them with muddy water from the stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ko mli lɛ shwie amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Thick, muddy water carries heavy silt that settles on the plant's roots and the top layer of dirt. This seals the soil, cutting off oxygen to the roots and making it difficult for the plant to absorb nutrients needed for fast growth.
ga: Nu ni mli edɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ yɛ sũ ni tsii ni ebɔle tsei shishifãi kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ahe. Enɛ baatsi shikpɔŋ lɛ naa. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli Ni enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya lɛ.

english: Why are my vegetable seedlings wilting even when the soil around them is freshly watered?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables dumɔwui lɛ miiho eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu kpakpa moŋ lɛ?

english: If your irrigation water contains high levels of chemicals or pollution from land runoff, it causes chemical stress. Instead of roots absorbing the water, toxic or salty water actually pulls moisture out of the roots, making the plant wilt despite being in wet soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofai babaoo yɛ o-irrigation nu lɛ mli loo nu ni hoɔ lɛ efite lɛ. Ebaaha tsofafeemɔ mli haomɔ aba. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ, nu ni yɔɔ gbeyei loo nu ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli diɛŋtsɛ. Enɛ haa tsei gboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ po nɔ.

english: Why does the soil around my cocoa seedlings turn into a hard crust after I water them from the river?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-kookoo tso lɛ he lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa beni mikɛ nu shwie nɔ kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: River water polluted with heavy sediment and fine clay deposits leaves behind a thick layer of mud every time you water. When the sun dries this mud, it bakes into a hard crust that prevents air from reaching the roots and stops future water from soaking in properly.
ga: Faa mli nu ni ŋmeii ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ sũ ewo mli lɛ shĩɔ sũ ni mli edɔ yɛ sɛɛ be fɛɛ be ni abaawo mli nu. Kɛ́ hulu lɛ gĩ sũ nɛɛ Ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni ehaaa nu abote mli jogbaŋŋ wɔsɛɛ.

english: Why won't my cassava tubers grow big on land that was previously dug up for mining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ atsa koni akɛtao shika tsuru lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mining strips away the rich topsoil where crops find food and organic matter. It leaves behind hard, nutrient-poor subsoil or toxic tailings where roots cannot spread easily, resulting in small or stunted cassava tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni ŋmɔshi nibii naa niyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ mlifomɔ. Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi sũ ni wa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ bɛ mli loo tsitsii ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraaa loo amɛgbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my overall crop yields dropping year after year even though I fetch water for them every dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ miiba shi afi fɛɛ afi lɛ? Kɛji akɛ mijie nu miha amɛ daa be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ po?

english: If your main water source is polluted by chemical runoff or heavy silt, using it over long periods gradually builds up toxins and salt in your soil. This damages soil fertility over time, leading to lower crop yields each season.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onu jɛɛhe titri lɛ mli ewo muji kɛjɛ tsofai ni hoɔ loo sũ ni tsii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baaha tsofai fɔji kɛ ŋmeii abua shikpɔŋ lɛ naa fiofio. Enɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni baa lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops along the riverbank wash away whenever a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: When trees and bushes near water bodies are cleared for settlements or mining, the soil loses the root structures that hold it together. Heavy rains then easily erode the banks, washing topsoil and crops straight into the river.
ga: Beni ajieɔ tsei kɛ tsei bibii ni bɛŋkɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ koni akɛhi shi loo ajie shika tsuru. Shikpɔŋ lɛ shishifãi ni fiɔ lɛ lɛ laajeɔ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ faai lɛ anaa oya. Enɛ haa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hoɔ kɛboteɔ faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How can I prepare land that was damaged by dirty water runoff so crops will grow on it again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa shikpɔŋ ni nu ni mli ewo muji ni hoɔ lɛ efite lɛ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore damaged land by adding heavy amounts of compost or animal manure to rebuild soil life, and planting cover crops like cowpeas. These cover crops help break up hardened ground, trap clean nutrients, and clean out mild soil toxins.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aku sɛɛ aba kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni okɛbaafata he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala lɛ nɔ. ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni egbɛɔ hei ni wa lɛ. Emɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he tse ni ejieɔ tsofai fɔji ni jeee basabasafeemɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Is it safe for me to use water from my fishpond to water my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ loo ŋshɔ mli lɛ baawo mi-aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: Yes, clean fishpond water is rich in natural nutrients from fish waste. When applied to vegetables, it acts like a natural liquid fertilizer that helps crops grow greener and stronger without needing extra chemical fertilizers.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni mli tse ni yɔɔ loo ŋshɔi amli lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ loo sũ mli. Kɛ́ akɛwo aduawai anɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nu ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: How does having multiple fishponds near my farm affect the ground where my crops grow?
ga: Te loo ŋshɔi babaoo ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi lɛ saa shikpɔŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fishponds help raise the water level in the nearby ground, keeping surrounding crop soil moist during dry periods. However, if the pond water is polluted or untreated, that dirty water can seep underground and damage the roots of nearby crops.
ga: Loo ŋshɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ha tso shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji akɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji loo atsuuu he nii lɛ, Nakai nu ni mli ewo muji lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ashishifãi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and burning under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot handle intense sun exposure. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa provides a protective cover, keeping the air moist and shielding the young plants from sunburn until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains yɛ Light cocoa masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he. shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my maize leaves curl up tightly into rolls during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural reaction to conserve water during extreme heat. By rolling their leaves, the plants reduce the surface area exposed to the sun to limit evaporation. If they uncurl when the sun goes down, the crop is managing stress normally.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni haa nu hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ haa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi koni ekɛtsi la ni hoɔ lɛ naa. Kɛji amɛjie amɛhe beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ atsu nɔnyɛɛ he nii bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to stress such as dry soil, excessive heat, or a lack of phosphorus in the soil. Consistent watering during flowering and applying fertilizers rich in phosphorus will help the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo la ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ he. loo fɔsfɔs ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa yɛ fɔfɔii ashishi kɛ fɔsfɔs ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my tomato plants have many green leaves but are not producing fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they focus all their energy on growing leaves and stems instead of setting flowers and fruits. Using balanced fertilizers that contain phosphorus and potassium encourages tomato plants to flower and fruit.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai adumɔ najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-tomato tsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ mli lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This results in tall, thin stems above ground and small, thin tubers underground because the roots lack room and energy to swell.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ bɛ he ko ni amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaafutu.

english: Why do weeds cause my young crops to stay small and turn pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miifee bibii ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal vital soil nutrients, moisture, and sunlight away from your crops. When weeds crowd your crops, the crops cannot feed properly, causing their growth to stall and leaves to lose their deep green color.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Anyɛɛɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni baai lɛ hu bɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cowpea plants sticky and covered with small black insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ mli wa ni ŋmeii bibii diji ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: The sticky substance is honeydew produced by aphids, which are small sap-sucking insects. Aphids weaken the plant by drinking its juices, but spraying the crop early with organic solutions like diluted neem oil or appropriate insecticides can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kpɛtɛɔ he lɛ ji wuo ni aphids, ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ feɔ lɛ. Aphids haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛtsɔ amɛmli nu lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem fɔ ni atsɔ mli loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaanyɛ akudɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my yam tubers rotting in the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ shishi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam tuber rot underground is usually caused by waterlogged soil and fungal infections. When water accumulates around the roots without draining, fungi attack the tubers. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato tuber fitemɔ baa. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my groundnut seeds fail to sprout if I plant immediately after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain of the season often wet only the surface layer of the dry soil. If no rain follows immediately, the heat bakes the seeds underground before they can fully germinate. It is safer to wait until the rains become regular before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni egbi lɛ pɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ enɛɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shãa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kwraa. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba dani odu.

english: Will cutting off the lower leaves of my tomato plants harm their growth?
ga: Ani tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ baaye edalɛ awui?

english: Removing the lower leaves that touch the soil actually helps tomato plants. It improves airflow around the base of the plant, prevents soil-borne diseases from splashing onto the foliage, and directs energy toward developing healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpaa gbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tomato tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ yaa hiɛ, ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ. kɛ hewalɛ ni yaa tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ

english: Why should I leave some big trees on my farm instead of clearing all of them before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni majie amɛ fɛɛ dani madu?

english: Big trees act as natural shields. They protect your crops from harsh heat during the day, keep moisture in the soil, and prevent strong winds and heavy rains from washing away your topsoil.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu. Amɛbuɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni otsi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I cut down all the trees on my land, how will it affect my crops during the dry season?
ga: Kɛji mifo tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Te enɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ eha tɛŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Without shade trees, the intense sun bakes the bare ground, causing soil water to evaporate rapidly. This makes your crops dry out and wither much faster during dry spells.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baashã hei ni agbele naa lɛ. Ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya. Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi oya kwraa yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do crops planted right under a big tree grow slower than crops planted a small distance away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ daraa fioo fe tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Large trees have extensive root systems that draw away water and nutrients from the soil, competing directly with your smaller crops for food and sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ yɛ shishifãi babaoo ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ aka akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii kɛ hulu la.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops fold up or droop during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the hottest hours of the day, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. They droop or roll their leaves to reduce exposure to the sun and conserve moisture until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfoɔ amɛhe koni hulu la lɛ aba shi ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is rich and good for farming before I pay for it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse ni ehi kɛha okwaayeli dani mawo nyɔmɔ?

english: Good agricultural land usually has dark, crumbly soil rich in rotted leaves, retains moisture without staying waterlogged, and naturally supports lush green vegetation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, okwaayeli hei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni baai ni egboi eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu bɛ mli. ni efiɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ asɛɛ

english: My land has very rich soil, but why am I still getting small harvests?
ga: Mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa. Shi mɛni hewɔ ni minine shɛɔ nibii fioo pɛ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Good land alone is not enough. Without proper field management—such as correct seed spacing, timely weeding, and protecting the land from water erosion—the soil cannot produce its full potential.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛji akɛ he ko he gbɛjianɔtoo ni sa bɛ, tamɔ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja, jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be naa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ejie ehewalɛ fɛɛ kpo.

english: Is it better to clear my land by burning the bush or by cutting it down with a cutlass?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafolɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ jwɛi lɛ ashãmɔ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning kills beneficial organisms in the soil and destroys natural organic matter. Cutting down bushes without burning allows the plant material to decay naturally into free fertilizer for your soil.
ga: Shãa gbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ni efiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei bibii ni ashãaa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ mli nibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oshikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know if renting a machine to clear my farm is worth the money?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsɔnei ni mikɛbaatsu nii kɛjieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia shika lɛ?

english: Machine clearing is worth it if you are working on a large area of land where manual labor would take too long or cost more. For small plots, the high rental cost of heavy machines may reduce your overall profit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ootsu nii yɛ he ko ni da lɛ, tsɔne ni akɛjieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he ehiaaa shika babaoo. Nine nitsumɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ahe be babaoo loo ebaahe shika babaoo. Kɛha shikpɔji bibii Nibii ni tsii ni akɛhaa lɛ he nyɔmɔwoo ni fa babaoo lɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔi fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Can using heavy machinery on my farm hurt the soil for future crops?
ga: Ani tsɔnei ni tsii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye shikpɔŋ lɛ awui kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, heavy machines compress the ground, packing the soil too tightly. This makes it difficult for crop roots to spread out and prevents rainwater from sinking into the ground properly.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei ni tsii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa tsɔ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛha tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni ehaaa nugbɔ nu lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to organize and manage my farmland properly instead of just planting anywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ ni makwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he ko kɛkɛ?

english: Proper farm management helps you track inputs, plant crops in orderly rows for easier weeding and harvesting, and rotate crops to prevent pests and soil weakness over time.
ga: Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Dumɔ tsei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo koni eha jwɛi shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ afee mlɛo. ni atsake ŋmɔshi nibii koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkwɛɛɛ moŋ lɛ? He ni esa akɛ afɔse nu yɛ daa?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for the crop. Even with plenty of water, the plant starves without proper nutrients, so adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help restore its healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛji nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ moŋ, shi tsei po baanyɛ aye hɔmɔ kɛji amɛnáaa niyenii ni sa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yams every year even though I plant in the exact same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ

english: Yams take heavy nutrients out of the soil during every harvest season. If you do not replace those stolen nutrients using compost, animal manure, or fertilizer, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot feed new crops.
ga: Sweet potatoes jieɔ niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa kpamɔɔ be. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aju lɛ tsakeee ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei anɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava field has a disease before the roots rot under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ mi-cassava ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani shishifãi lɛ agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava diseases usually show warning signs on the leaves first, such as yellow patches, curling, or brown spots. Inspecting the top leaves weekly allows you to spot contamination early before it spreads down into the tubers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca helai jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii akpo yɛ baai lɛ anɔ klɛŋklɛŋ, tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Otsi fɛɛ otsi ni oookwɛ baa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona muji mra. dani egbɛ eshwa yitso lɛ nɔ

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in cool, wet weather. Removing and burying infected pods immediately stops the fungus from contaminating the rest of your healthy cocoa harvest.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ waa mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni afuɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afite kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do I see holes in my young maize leaves even when I don't see any insects during the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa bu yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli be mli ni minaaa kooloi bibii komɛi lɛ? Yɛ gbi lɛ mli?

english: Pests like Fall Armyworms hide inside the center funnel of the maize plant during the hot day to deceive predators, coming out only at night to eat. Opening the top leaves to check for hidden caterpillars helps you catch them before they destroy the stalk.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworms lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛlaka kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii gbɛkɛ pɛ. Kɛ́ ogbele baai lɛ anɔ koni okwɛ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ yɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛfite tso lɛ yitso lɛ.

english: What will happen to my crops if I plant my pepper seeds very close together to save space?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu pepper dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni mikɛha he ko akafee nɔ ko?

english: Planting peppers too close creates an overcrowded jam where crops fight for light, air, and soil nutrients. This overcrowding makes stems weak and traps moisture, which leads to early fungal contamination and low yield.
ga: Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ kɛ naagba ni ji gbɔmɛi ni eyi obɔ lɛ baa. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ agbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa mra ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: How do I know if the fertilizer I bought from the market is genuine and safe for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Genuine fertilizer has uniform grains, dissolves evenly in water, and comes in sealed bags from certified dealers. Fake or adulterated fertilizer often contains sand or salt that can burn crop roots instead of feeding them.
ga: Fertilizer diɛŋtsɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni yaa nɔ daa. Ekɛ ehe woɔ nu mli pɛpɛɛpɛ, ni ebaa yɛ kotokui ni akɛwo mli lɛ amli kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni jaa ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋã loo ŋmei ni baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi lɛ yɛ amalei loo nibii ni akɛfee lɛ amli yɛ ŋmei mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha amɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and roll inward during the hottest part of the afternoon?
