ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in the afternoon heat is a normal defensive behavior where the tomato plant reduces its exposed leaf surface to hold onto moisture. If the leaves relax again in the evening, the crop is simply protecting itself from sun stress.
ga: Baai ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ ji subaŋ ni afɔɔ feemɔ kɛha hebuu. Tomato tsei lɛ baa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ shi koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ miibu amɛhe kɛmiijɛ hulu la ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers droop and lose leaves right after I transplant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo he kroko lɛ?

english: Transplanted plantain suckers suffer from root shock because their main water supply was disturbed during digging. Trimming off the larger outer leaves before planting helps the sucker conserve water until new roots grow.
ga: Plantain suckers ni adu lɛ lɛ naa shishifãi ni tswaa lɛ he amanehulu ejaakɛ nu jɛɛhe titri lɛ mli gbala yɛ be mli ni atsaa lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ kponɔgbɛ baai wuji lɛ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli kɛyashiɔ shishifãi heei baakwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize grain get moldy and bad during storage even after sun drying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ shwie shi ni efite yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli beni mikɛwo hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Maize gets moldy when hidden moisture remains inside the core of the grain or when storage rooms lack fresh airflow. Drying grains until they crack cleanly between your teeth prevents fungal contamination during long storage.
ga: Abɛi feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ tee ŋmãa lɛ mli loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ni ooogbi kɛyashi amɛbaagbala yɛ onyanyɔji ateŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii akabote mli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is lacking nitrogen fertilizer or water. Nitrogen is essential for maize to build strong, green leaves, so applying fertilizer like NPK or Urea at the right stage restores their healthy color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen ŋmãa loo nu. Nitrogen he hiaa koni ŋmãa afee baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How do I know the right distance to leave between my maize seeds when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male gbɛ ni sa ni kã ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ beni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak stalks and small ears. Giving about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between seeds ensures each stalk gets enough space and food to produce big cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ toi bibii. Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni miihe ashɛ sɛntimitai 75 kɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni miihe ashɛ sɛntimitai 40 haa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it good for me to stop planting maize and switch to another crop like cassava on the same field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makpa ŋmãa dumɔ ni matsake kɛya ŋmãa kroko nɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, changing the type of crop you plant—known as crop rotation—stops soil pests from building up and prevents the land from losing all its nutrients. Cassava uses different soil nutrients than maize and handles dry periods better, making it a good choice after maize.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ Ale lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsakemɔ. Ehaa sũ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nibii fɛɛ ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Cassava kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmãa ni etsuɔ ​​be ni nu hɔmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, eji nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa najiaŋ.

english: Why did my crop fail to grow well even though my neighbor harvested a lot from his farm nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ yɛ ŋmaa babaoo kɛjɛ eŋmɔ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Crop growth depends heavily on the specific seed quality, planting depth, and soil preparation. Even neighboring farms can have different soil fertility, water retention, or seed varieties that affect harvest outcome.
ga: Tso dalɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hi ha lɛ nɔ. dumɔ mlibotemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ babaoo Ekolɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ po bɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ. nu ni ahiɔ mli loo dumɔwui srɔtoi ni saa ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ he lɛ

english: Can I plant my crops on land near old building sites or community grounds, or will it harm the plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ tsu momo ko loo akutso lɛ mli he ko? Aloo ebaaye tsei awui loo ebaayeee amɛ awui?

english: Land near old settlements can be very fertile if organic materials broke down there over time. However, you must clear buried concrete, stones, or compacted soil that could block root growth and prevent water from sinking in.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ hei momoi lɛ baanyɛ afee shikpɔŋ ni baa nii waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ fite yɛ be ni sa mli. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ojie kɔnkrit, tɛi, loo sũ ni mli edɔ fɛɛ ni baanyɛ atsĩ shishifãi lɛ adalɛ naa ni eha nu akabote mli lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly when I plant them on sloping land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sloping land allows rainwater to wash away quickly down the hill before it can soak into the root area, taking valuable topsoil with it. Planting along contour lines or making ridges helps trap water and topsoil for your crops.
ga: Hei ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ shishi dani enyɛɔ eboteɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ekɛ ŋwɛi shikpɔŋ ni jara wa yaa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ line loo ŋmeii ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu hiɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very tall and leafy but failing to produce cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewooo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen relative to other nutrients like phosphorus, or when they don't get enough sunlight, they put all their energy into growing leaves and stems instead of flowering and developing cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná nitrogen babaoo fe nine kɛ akɛto niyenii krokomɛi tamɔ fɔsfɔs he, loo kɛ́ amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ

english: How can I tell if my crop field is healthy just by looking at it from a distance?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ shɔŋŋ kɛkɛ?

english: A healthy field has a uniform deep green color, consistent plant height, and thick stalks without bare or stunted patches. Even height across the field shows that all plants are getting equal nutrients and water.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ji unifɔm, eŋɔli ni tsuɔ. tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tamɔ amɛhe ni eyɛ tso ni mli tse ni plɛtei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo nɔ ni etse ehe lɛ bɛ mli. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei fɛɛ miiná niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like tubes during hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation during extreme heat. Once the temperature drops in the evening or rain falls, the leaves unroll back to normal.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni ekɛbaa nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi gbɛkɛ loo nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Baai lɛ baagbala amɛhe ekoŋŋ kɛya bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Holes in the central funnel of young maize plants are typically caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaves. Catching and treating this early protects the growing point so the plant can still produce cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ amɔmɔ amɛ mra ni atsa amɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua. Ebuɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ he koni tso lɛ anyɛ awo cob lolo.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my topsoil, and how does that hurt my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni te no saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain washes away the top layer of soil, which contains the most plant food and organic matter. Without this rich topsoil, crop roots cannot find enough nutrients to grow strong, leading to weak plants and poor yields.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ, ni tsei aniyenii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii bɛ lɛ Tso shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How can I stop my newly planted seeds from being carried away during heavy downpours?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ anaa koni akaŋɔ amɛ kɛya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Planting across the slope of your land using contour ridges or planting grass barriers slows down rushing rainwater. This keeps the soil in place and prevents your seeds from being washed away.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii anɔ loo jwɛi gbɛtsii nii ni adu lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni ebaatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaho.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow when water stays on my farm for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni nu eba miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need air to breathe just like people do. When water covers the soil for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the plant to choke, stop taking in nutrients, and turn yellow.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. ŋmɔ tso lɛ Kpa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ

english: Which food crops can survive in soil that stays wet and muddy after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii tsei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ muji nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Crops like rice and taro (cocoyam) thrive in wet, muddy soils, while crops like maize, cassava, and tomatoes need well-drained soil and will rot if kept in standing water.
ga: Dumɔwui tamɔ omɔ kɛ taro (kookoo) kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛ muji nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ tomato biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ akɛto nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why does my clay farm soil turn into hard, cracked ground after being flooded and dried by the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa beni hulu lɛ efo mli ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clay soil expands when wet and shrinks as it dries out. When heavy rain leaves the field and the sun cooks the wet clay, the soil particles pull tightly together, creating hard ground with deep cracks.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ kɛji edɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛji egbi. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shi ŋmɔji lɛ amli ni hulu lɛ shã shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii lɛ gbalaa amɛhe waa. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmeii ni mli kwɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tall maize plants fall over flat on the ground after a strong rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain softens the soil around the base of the plant, weakening its grip. When strong winds push against tall maize plants, the soft, wet ground cannot support the roots, causing the stalks to blow over.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ehaa nɔ ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ he lɛ baa shi Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswa ŋmãa tsei kakadaji lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ha tso lɛ fã kɛya

english: How does rain splashing mud onto vegetable leaves cause diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ muji ni nɛɔ yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ lɛ kɛ hela baa?

english: Soil naturally contains tiny disease germs (fungi and bacteria). When heavy rain strikes bare soil, it splashes muddy water onto the lower leaves, allowing these germs to enter and rot the plant.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ helai bibii (fungi kɛ bacteria) yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Nu ni mli ewo muji baashwie baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa muawai nɛɛ boteɔ tso lɛ mli ni ehaa tso lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when we get too much continuous rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ wɔná nugbɔ babaoo ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Excessive water creates airless soil conditions where harmful fungal diseases thrive. These fungi attack wet cassava roots underground, turning them soft, watery, and rotten before you can harvest them.
ga: Nu babaoo haa shikpɔŋ nɔ shihilɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baa. he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ oshara baanyɛ ada yɛ Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ tutuaa ŋmei shishifãi ni efɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Ha amɛfee bɔdɔɔ, amɛfee nu, ni amɛfite dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast on my cocoa farm during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The fungus that causes black pod disease loves cool, damp weather. Raindrops splash fungal spores from diseased pods and soil onto healthy cocoa pods, spreading the infection quickly across the farm.
ga: Fuŋ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ sumɔɔ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ kɛyaa kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: If rain falls heavily once and then disappears for two weeks, will my planted seeds die?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa shikome ni no sɛɛ lɛ elaaje otsii enyɔ Ani dumɔwui ni adu lɛ baagboi?

english: The first rain tells the seed to absorb water and start sprouting. If the rain stops before the young root goes deep enough to find moisture, the tender seedling will dry up and die under the hot sun.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ kɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛmɔmɔ nu ni amɛbɔi kwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa dani shishifãi bibii lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛna ŋmɔtɔ lɛ, Tender dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm for days without draining, it drowns the roots and causes them to rot before you can harvest them.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ ŋmɔ ko mli gbii babaoo ni ajieee lɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha amɛgboi dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: It is best to water early in the morning. If you water in the hot afternoon, the sun causes most of the water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi. Kɛji okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Hulu la haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nuɔ.

english: Why does my maize turn light green and stop growing when water collects and stays on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ekpaa dalɛ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water washes away plant food like nitrogen from the soil and starves the roots of air, which turns the leaves pale and stops the maize from growing tall.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hoɔ tsei amli niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa ŋmãa lɛ adara.

english: No, planting too close together causes crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This leaves all the plants weak and small, giving you a smaller overall harvest.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ bibioo. Enɛ haa okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and create clean paths between my crop rows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ ni mafee gbɛi ni he tse yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing paths stops weeds from competing with your crops and allows air to flow freely, preventing plant diseases.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Gbɛjegbɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaye akaŋ. ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ Tsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up like tubes during the middle of the day when it is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from the intense sun. By curling up, the plant loses less water through its leaves during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Kɛtsɔ curling nɔ lɛ, tso lɛ fiteɔ nu fioo kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without turning into fruits when the heat is too strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the pepper plant and dries out the pollen inside the flowers. When flowers are not fertilized due to heat, the plant drops them to save its strength.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ egbiɔ. Kɛji fɔfɔii lɛ ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ latsaa hewɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhiɛ amɛhewalɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas that protect young cocoa from sunburn and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my garden eggs plant turning yellow and falling to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the plant lacks water or nitrogen food in the soil. The plant sacrifice its older bottom leaves to keep the young leaves at the top alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tso lɛ kɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ shaa afɔle bɔni afee ni baai bibii lɛ ahi nɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry up and burn if I apply fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs soil water to dissolve properly. On dry soil, strong fertilizer sucks the remaining moisture directly out of the plant roots, causing the leaves to dry up and burn.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ shikpɔji ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa.

english: Yellow leaves starting at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer early in the season helps keep the leaves healthy and green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my beans and cowpeas grow so well in poor soil where my maize fails to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans kɛ cowpeas lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni mi-corn lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas belong to a plant family called legumes that can make their own plant food from the air through tiny bumps on their roots. Maize cannot do this and relies entirely on nutrients already in the soil.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas fata tsei akuu ko ni atsɛɔ amɛ legumes lɛ he, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee amɛ niyenii kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni amɛfeɔ yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi nyɛŋ afee enɛ ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ kwraa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under hot direct sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa trees establish themselves.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ maa amɛhe shi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high off the ground to catch as much sunlight as possible. Lifting the leaves helps the plant make food to grow big tubers underground and protects the leaves from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ awo tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni efeɔ niyenii kɛhaa bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground when we receive heavy rain for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi beni nugbɔ enɛ waa gbii babaoo nɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in flooded soil for too long, it pushes all the air out, causing the roots to drown and rot under the surface.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛje kpo. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ yɛ nu lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants during the hot dry season without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii shwieɔ tomato tsei anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: When the weather gets extremely hot and dry, tomato plants get stressed and cannot pollinate their flowers properly. The plant drops its flowers to save energy and water.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or thrips hiding under the leaves, or by a plant virus spread by these insects as they feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow so slowly if I wait to clear weeds until the weeds are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo nɛkɛ kɛji mimɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi lɛ atsu nii kɛyashi jwɛi lɛ shwere momo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal water, sunlight, and soil food away from young crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to nutrients when they need them most.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii amli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ waa lɛ.

english: If too many sucker shoots grow from one plantain root, they all fight for the same water and nutrients. Removing extra shoots leaves only one or two main stems to grow large, healthy bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii babaoo miikwɛ̃ kɛjɛ plantain shishifã kome mli lɛ, Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋshii mli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ ŋmeii titrii kome loo enyɔ pɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛhe awa.

english: Why does my tall maize fall over so easily when strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Maize falls over when its root system is shallow or weak, often because the soil is too loose or planted too shallow. Moulding soil around the base of the stem gives the roots extra support to withstand wind.
ga: Abɛi baagbee baai lɛ kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo ebɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse tsɔ loo dumɔ nii lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni abɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ babaoo koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ.

english: How can I tell if the crop seeds I buy will actually grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good seeds are clean, unbroken, full-sized, and free from insect holes. Certified seeds from reliable suppliers are tested to ensure almost all of them will sprout into healthy, high-yielding crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi, ni he tse, ni ekumɔko, ni amɛdalɛ fa, ni kooloi akutsei bɛ mli. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ amli ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are old, buried too deep, planted in dry soil, or eaten by insects. Seeds need the right depth, warm soil, and balanced moisture to wake up and start growing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji amɛgbɔ, afu amɛ tsɔ, loo adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. loo kooloi yeɔ lɛ Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant is starving for nutrients like nitrogen or is suffering from poor water drainage. Dark green leaves mean the plant has enough food to make energy and produce good yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii, tamɔ nitrogen, loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ miipiŋ lɛ. Baai eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ená hewalɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpa aba.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and weak without producing large fruits or grains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii loo dumɔwui wuji lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they stretch upward to compete for light, using all their energy to grow tall stems instead of building heavy fruits or thick grains.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baagbala amɛhe koni amɛye la he akaŋ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei kakadaji moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii ni tsii loo dumɔwui ni mli tse.

english: Why do my young crops wilt during the hot afternoon sun even if the soil is damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water faster than young roots can drink it up, making the plant droop to protect itself. If roots are healthy, the plant will recover as the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi bibii baanyɛ anu. Ha tsei agbi koni amɛbu amɛhe Kɛji shishifãi lɛ wa Tso lɛ he baajɔ lɛ kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my soil is soft and rich enough for root crops like cassava to expand?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni eyɛ nii babaoo bɔ ni sa ni tsei ni woɔ shishifãi tamɔ yucca lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã?

english: Good soil for root crops feels loose in your hands, crumbles easily, and lets water sink in without pooling. Hard, compacted soil squeezes roots and stops tubers from expanding.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni akɛduɔ bulbs lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nine mli, efoɔ oya, ni ehaa nu boteɔ mli ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa ni ehaaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why is it better to plant my crops in straight, measured rows instead of spreading seeds everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni asusu he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets its own fair share of sunlight, air, and soil food. It also makes weeding, inspecting for diseases, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Row planting haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni sa. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, helai akamɔ, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: How exactly do weeds slow down the growth of my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive thieves that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your plants. When weeds surround your crops, your crops starve and stay small.
ga: Jwɛi ji julɔi ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Beni jwɛi ebɔle oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛbaafee bibii.

english: Why does my land produce a smaller harvest when I plant the same crop on the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests to build up in the ground, lowering your overall harvest.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: What basic steps can I take to help my farm thrive and get higher crop yields?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi titrii manyɛ matsɔ nɔ maye mabua miŋmɔ lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ ni ená ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo?

english: To get good yields, start with high-quality certified seeds, give plants proper spacing, clear weeds early, and nourish the soil with manure or fertilizer to keep crops healthy.
ga: bɔni afee ni aná nibii kpakpai Je shishi kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli. Shi he ko ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs if I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Kɛji midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. The plant spends all its energy growing tall to reach the sun instead of putting energy into making big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛshɛ hulu lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee cob bɔɔlu agboi lɛ

english: Why do extension officers always tell us to plant beans or cowpeas in the same field with our cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ be fɛɛ be akɛ wɔdu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ wɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special crops that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it back into the ground. Planting them alongside cassava or maize feeds the soil naturally, helping your main crop yield more without needing as much expensive fertilizer.
ga: Peas kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua onibii titrii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my plantain and cocoa leaves turn yellow and dry up when there is no rain for just a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain kɛ cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow and dry up during dry spells because plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the hot soil. The plant intentionally drops leaves to save water and keep its main stem alive.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsɔɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my young crops with dry grass or cocoa husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo kookoo ŋmeii aha he ni tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dried grass or plant husks acts like an umbrella that keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground too fast. It keeps the soil cool and wet for longer, stops weeds from growing, and eventually rots into good food for your soil.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi loo tsei ahe tsɔi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni tsiɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ egbo ji niyenii kpakpa kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking green branches from my cocoa tree when it is growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ cacao tso niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ amli beni eedara lɛ?

english: Cutting off extra branches allows fresh air and light into the middle of the tree, which prevents damp diseases like black pod from building up. It also forces the tree to direct its energy into producing pods rather than growing unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ofo tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ahe lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛ la abote tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni mli edɔ tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ akakwɛ̃. Enyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ hu koni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakwɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ.

english: Why do young flowers and small pods fall off my trees before they get a chance to grow into big fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ hu daraaa lɛ? Ni mikɛ mitso lɛ agbee shi dani ená hegbɛ ni eda ni etsɔ aduawai agbo?

english: Flowers and small pods fall off when the plant feels too much stress from heat, lack of water, or insect attacks. It can also happen if the plant realizes it doesn't have enough food in the soil to support all the fruits it started making.
ga: fɔfɔi bibii kɛ ŋmeii Amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ nu haomɔ babaoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa, loo kooloi ni tutuaa lɛ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba mli hu kɛji tso lɛ yɔse akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai fɛɛ ni ebɔi feemɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer on my farm right when a heavy rainstorm is falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away into gutters or pushes it too deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach it. Fertilizer works best when applied to damp soil on a calm day so roots can drink it up immediately.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa nubui amli loo ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ yɛ gbii ni yɔɔ kpoo lɛ anɔ. koni anyɛ anu shishifãi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ

english: Growing the same crop in the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until the land becomes weak. It also allows insects and soil diseases that love maize to multiply in that spot, so rotating with other crops starves those pests out.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni sũ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni sumɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ hu ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ nakai he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ tsei krokomɛi tsake lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ akashɛ ohe.

english: How do weeds actually reduce my harvest if there seems to be enough space on the land for all of us?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aha mikpamɔ lɛ aba shi? Be mli ni etamɔ nɔ ni gbɛ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha wɔ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive roots that steal water and fertilizer away from your crops before your crops get a chance to eat. They also hide harmful bugs and block air from moving through your crops, which encourages diseases to spread.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛyeɔ amɛ. Ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hu teeɔ shi, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ onibii amli. ni kanyaa helai srɔtoi

english: Why do seeds I buy from the agricultural office grow much better than seeds I save from my own harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miheɔ kɛjɛɔ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe dumɔwui ni mikɛtoɔ kɛjɛɔ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ?

english: Saved seeds often lose their vigor if they get warm or damp during storage, or if they were infected by insects you couldn't see. Certified seeds are specially bred, treated against diseases, and stored in controlled conditions so that almost every seed sprouts strong.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ fɔɔ hewalɛ ni baa shi kɛji akɛ adɔ amɛ loo edɔ amɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii emɔ amɛ lɛ onyɛɛɛ ona. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ, atsuɔ he nii, ni akɛtoɔ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli bɔni afee ni nɔ ni miihe ashɛ dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains produce large leaves that provide immediate shade and keep the soil cool and moist, acting as protective umbrellas for the cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ Etsu nii akɛ he ko ni Cocoa baanyɛ ahi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central funnel of the maize plant during the daytime and feed on the fresh leaves, weakening the plant if not controlled early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ akudɔɔɔ lɛ mra.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with thick leaves but produce small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil contains too much nitrogen or plants are spaced too closely together, the cassava puts most of its energy into growing stems and leaves above ground instead of storing food in the underground roots.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ niyenii baato shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi amli lɛ

english: Why shouldn't I pour chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tomato tsei lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer directly on or against the plant stem can scorch and burn the delicate skin and upper roots due to high salt content. Fertilizer should be placed in a ring a few inches away from the stem where feeder roots can safely drink it in.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi loo emasɛi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã hewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ yɛ ŋmei ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋwɛi ŋta ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ. ni feeder shishifãi lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni anuɔ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without forming peppers when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni efeee pepper be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes stress to the flower, which prevents successful pollination. When the flower cannot be pollinated properly, the plant naturally drops it to conserve its water and energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa fɔfɔi anɔ. ni tsiɔ pollination ni yeɔ omanye lɛ naa. Kɛ fɔfɔii nyɛɛɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet conditions and high humidity. Excess rainfall and poor air flow allow fungal spores to travel quickly from pod to pod across your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Fungi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni hoɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii amli tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ yaa oya kɛjɛɔ pod mli kɛyaa pod mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my main crops help my soil grow better plants?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural food inside the soil. This enriches the soil with free fertilizer that nearby crops can use to grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ehaa efeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do the leaves of my maize plants roll up tightly into tubes during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ tsɔji yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival mechanism. By curling its leaves inward, the maize plant reduces the amount of surface area exposed to the hot sun and dry wind, which prevents water from evaporating out of the plant.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ awo mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni nu akajɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why must I stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them spread across the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa he ni agbele lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the vine leaves high off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight to make food for growing large tubers. It also keeps leaves off damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and rotting.
ga: Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: Why do weeds make my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds actively steal vital soil nutrients like nitrogen away from your crops. Without enough nitrogen, crops cannot maintain their healthy green color, causing leaves to turn yellow and growth to slow down.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdaraa fioo.

english: Why do weeds and bush take over my farm so quickly when I am away for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ oya kɛ́ mibɛ jɛmɛ otsii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: When a farm is left unworked, sunlight reaches the bare soil and wild weed seeds sprout rapidly. Regular clearing and active presence keep crops dominant and prevent weeds from stealing water and nutrients.
ga: Beni ŋmɔ lɛ bɛ nitsumɔ ko ni etsuɔ ​​lɛ Hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei lɛ daa kɛ bɔ ni amɛfeɔ amɛnii amɛhaa lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ srɔto, ni ehaaa jwɛi lɛ aju nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why should I clear a clean boundary around my crop field before the dry Harmattan starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo husu ni mli tse ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he dani Harmattan ni egbi lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Dry grass and brush at the edges of farms burn easily in the dry season. Clearing a wide border, or firebreak, prevents stray bushfires from entering your farm and destroying your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ojie he ko ni ebɔle ohe loo la he lɛ, ebaatsi koo mli la gbɛ koni ekagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo ni efite onibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and cannot survive strong direct sunlight. Shade crops like plantains or shade trees act like natural umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist until the young cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛŋmɛɛɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei tamɔ tsei bibii loo shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ

english: When maize is planted too close, the leaves block sunlight from each other, causing the stalks to stretch thin for light instead of developing strong roots and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Ha tso lɛ shishi lɛ afee bibioo koni enyɛ emɔ la. Mohu ɔ, e peeɔ sisifãhi nɛ a he wa kɛ ngmɔkɔ nguahi.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil is low in nitrogen and other essential nutrients. Adding well-rotted manure or compost returns nutrients to the soil so the plant can grow healthy green leaves and big roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen kɛ niyenii krokomɛi ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ faaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi wuji.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil every season and lets soil pests build up. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. kɛ gbɛ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni tsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How does inspecting my crops every few days help stop diseases from ruining my whole harvest?
ga: Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko mlikwɛmɔ Te gbii fioo komɛi baanyɛ atsĩ hela naa koni ekafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Walking through your field regularly allows you to spot yellowing leaves or pest damage early on a few plants. Removing or treating those infected plants immediately prevents the disease from spreading to the rest of the farm.
ga: Kɛ́ onyiɛ ŋmɔji amli daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ona baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ tsei komɛi mra. Kɛ́ ajie nakai tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ oya loo atsa amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli hei krokomɛi.

english: Why do black spots spread faster on my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe kookoo ŋmeii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Fungal diseases thrive in cool, damp conditions with low airflow. Trimming excess canopy leaves lets sunlight and wind inside the tree, keeping pods dry and reducing disease spread.
ga: Fungal helai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Afolɔ tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers spoil quickly if I leave them on damp ground in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moisture on harvested skin attracts soil bacteria and fungi that cause tubers to rot. Storing tubers off the ground in a cool, shaded, well-ventilated barn keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ hewolo ni akpa lɛ nɔ lɛ gbalaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ. Too bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni yitso lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored grains get eaten by tiny insects even when I put them in closed bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yeɔ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛtoɔ kotokui ni aŋã mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Insects or their invisible eggs often come from the field inside the grain. Drying your grain thoroughly under the sun before bagging lowers the moisture level so insect eggs cannot hatch and multiply.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi loo ŋmeii ni anaaa lɛ jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulu mli dani awo amɛ kotoku mli lɛ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baa shi. Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akafɔ ni amɛkafee babaoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die when I clear all the big trees away from the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie cacao tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that get burnt easily by strong sunlight. Keeping bigger shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a cool environment that protects the young crop until it grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa oya. Ha tsei wuji lɛ afee shade loo dumɔ tsei bibii yɛ amɛmasɛi. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is the pepper plant's natural defense against heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun to trap moisture inside and prevent itself from drying out.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ pepper tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Tsei haa he ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ amɛbaai lɛ ni amɛfoɔ mli koni amɛmɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or inconsistent watering. When it is too hot, the pollen inside the flower dries out, preventing fruit from forming.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Beni edɔ tsɔ lɛ Pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni ekafee

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas or beans alongside my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas are special plants that pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. Planting them with maize feeds the soil naturally, helping the maize grow greener and stronger without needing as much chemical fertilizer.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: Yam vines naturally search for height so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight to make food. Lifting the leaves off the damp ground also prevents soil-borne diseases from ruining the leaves and reducing tuber size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. Baai ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ akafite baai lɛ, ni ehaa tuber lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: Weeds are wild native plants that are adapted to survive in poor soil with very little water. Domesticated crops need specific nutrients and care, while weeds quickly snatch up sunlight and soil moisture before your crops can.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kɛ nu fioo ko pɛ nɔ. Shia tsei biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kɛ kwɛmɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi lɛ baatswa hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ oya dani otsei lɛ baanyɛ afee nakai.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the maize plant moves its remaining nutrients up to protect new growing leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ Abele lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ebu baai heei ni miida lɛ ahe. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants yield smaller bunches when there are many small stems growing around the main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: The small stems, called suckers, drink water and food from the main mother plant. Leaving too many suckers causes them to steal nutrients away from the main plant, resulting in smaller, lighter plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii, ni atsɛɔ amɛ shoots lɛ, nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ tso titri lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, plantain tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start to rot if heavy rain floods the farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Roots need air underground to breathe just like humans do above ground. When water sits on the soil for too long, it cuts off air to the cassava tubers, causing them to drown and rot in the mud.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛmu tamɔ bɔ ni adesai feɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaafo kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei shishifã lɛ mli lɛ. Nu mli gbee kɛ fitemɔ yɛ muji mli

english: How do I know that my cassava underground tubers are ready for harvesting without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifã ko efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni okɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: As cassava tubers mature under the ground, the leaves at the base of the plant naturally turn yellow and drop off, and cracks may begin to form in the soil directly around the base of the stem.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ dara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Ni ŋmeii baanyɛ aje shishi afee yɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients out of the soil or leaves the roots sitting in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo eha shishifãi lɛ ebote nu mli tsɔ.

english: Is it helpful to plant cowpeas together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ ko yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ duɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas alongside maize is very beneficial. Cowpeas naturally take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which acts as a natural fertilizer to feed your maize crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Cowpeas lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce tiny roots when I plant them close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When cassava plants are crowded together, their roots fight over the same soil nutrients, space, and water. Giving each plant enough space allows the roots to expand freely and form big tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ feɔ ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ, he kome, kɛ nu kome mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are my sweet potato plants growing lots of leaves on top but almost no potatoes under the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo yɛ nɔ shi ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or manure, the sweet potato plant spends all its energy growing big branches and leaves instead of storing energy in the roots to make potatoes.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo niji kɛ baai wuji. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ toɔ shishifãi lɛ amli koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crop is fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is typically ready when the lower leaves of the plant naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts cracking open as the tubers swell underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ feɔ klalo kɛ́ tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep falling off before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or lack of water. Without enough water and steady temperatures, the plant drops its flowers to save its own life.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ bɛ Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: How do I know if my young cocoa trees are getting too much sunlight during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Young cocoa leaves will start turning brown, curling at the tips, or dropping off entirely. Cocoa trees need partial shade when young because full direct sun dries them out faster than their roots can take up water.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ baabɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Curls yɛ naagbee lɛ loo egbeeɔ shi kwraa. Cocoa tsei biɔ hulutsoo fioo kɛji amɛdara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa cacao tso lɛ gĩɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu.

english: Weed seeds are very tough and lie hidden in the soil waiting for moisture. Once the rain hits, they wake up immediately and start absorbing food and light faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa waa ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛmɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, amɛteɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni amɛjeɔ niyenii kɛ la shishi oya fe tsei dumɔwui.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves and sucking out the sap, or by a virus these insects spread from plant to plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewoɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my maize crop dry up prematurely before the cobs full out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani ŋmãa lɛ eyi lɛ?

english: Early drying usually happens if drought hits right when the maize is flowering, or if pests like the Fall Armyworm destroy the leaves so the plant can no longer create energy to fill out the cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ hɔmɔ ba be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ aahu akɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni ekɛwo ŋmei lɛ mli ekoŋŋ dɔŋŋ.

english: If I buy fertilizer for my corn farm, how do I know the right amount to apply so I do not waste my money?
ga: Kɛji ohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛduɔ ŋmãa lɛ Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole bɔ ni sa? No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee shika?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn your corn crops, while too little will not produce good yields. It is best to follow recommended local guidelines for your soil—such as applying NPK fertilizer at planting and urea a few weeks later—so your plants get only the nutrients they actually need.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashã. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ ni akɛhaa lɛ haaa yibii kpakpai aba lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooonyiɛ maŋ lɛ mli ŋaawoi ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee kɛha oshikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ, tamɔ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛbaafata he yɛ dumɔ mli kɛ urea yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Enɛ haa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ pɛ.

english: What should I do if my maize crops start showing strange spots and signs of disease on their leaves?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mi-abɛi tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmeii kɛ helai okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ namɔ?

english: Strange spots are usually signs of crop diseases like leaf blight or rust. You should act quickly by removing badly affected plants, showing leaf samples to an extension officer, and applying recommended treatments or switching to disease-resistant seed varieties to protect the rest of your field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hei ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ji tso helai, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei he okadi. Esa akɛ otsu he nii oya kɛtsɔ tsei ni ena naagbai waa lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ wolo lɛ he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ otsɔɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ hiɛyaa nɔ lɛ. Ni okɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ atsu nii loo otsake kɛya dumɔwui srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ anɔ koni obu ohe ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: How does growing only one type of crop like corn make my farm more open to disease outbreaks?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome ni miduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ haa helai baa miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When you grow only one crop continuously, pests and plant diseases that attack that specific crop can build up in the soil and spread rapidly because they have an unlimited supply of their favorite food. Rotating crops or intercropping helps break this disease cycle.
ga: Kɛji okwɛ tso henɔ kome pɛ daa lɛ Tsɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai ni tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ niyenii ni amɛsumɔɔ waa lɛ ni husu bɛ he lɛ hewɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, loo nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: How do fall armyworms affect my corn plants, and how can I keep them away?
ga: Te fall cutworms lɛ saa mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi amɛnaa?

english: Fall armyworms are destructive caterpillars that eat the leaves and central shoots of young corn, preventing the plant from growing healthy ears. You can control them by checking your farm early and often, applying safe approved insecticides, or using resistant seed varieties.
ga: Autumn cutworm ji ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛteŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Tsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaná toi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ shii abɔ nɔ, ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii. loo okɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ atsu nii

english: Why do my harvested crops spoil so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya dani anyɛɔ akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops spoil easily after harvest if they are exposed to moisture, heat, or poor storage conditions. Proper drying techniques and using improved storage containers, like hermetic bags or ventilated sheds, protect your crops from moisture and pests until transport arrives.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ kɛji akɛ ewo fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ loo shihilɛ ni ehiii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli. Gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbiɔ nii kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ vacuum bags loo greenhouses ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nibii ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baashɛ.

english: How can better community roads and storage facilities help me make more profit from my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ akutso lɛ mli gbɛjegbɛi ni hi kɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Good roads allow buyers and trucks to reach your farm easily without damaging produce during transport, while proper storage lets you hold onto your harvested crops safely until market prices rise, helping you get a better income.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi kpakpai haa mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛ lɔlei shɛɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli oya ni amɛfiteee nibii ni adu lɛ yɛ gbɛfaa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nibii ni okɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaye abua bo ni okɛ onibii ni okpa lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe kɛyashi jara nɔ jara baaya hiɛ. ni yeɔ ebua bo ni onáa shika kpakpa

english: What do bank managers usually look for before approving a farm loan for a smallholder farmer?
ga: Mɛni shikatoohe nɔkwɛlɔi fɔɔ taomɔ dani amɛkpɛlɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nyɔmɔwoo nɔ amɛhaa okwaafoi bibii?

english: Bank managers look for signs that your crop yields will be safe and profitable. They want to see that you have a plan to protect crops from diseases, access to good markets, and basic records showing your farm's income and production history.
ga: Sikatoohe nɔkwɛlɔi taoɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni obaawo lɛ baafee shweshweeshwe ni sɛɛnamɔ hu baajɛ mli aba. Amɛmiisumɔ ni amɛna akɛ oyɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni okɛbaabu onibii ahe kɛjɛ helai ahe. jarayeli he gbɛ kpakpa kɛ shishijee woji ni tsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ shika ni onáa kɛ nibii ni ofeɔ lɛ ahe yinɔsane.

english: How can government agricultural programs help protect my farm from complete failure during a disease outbreak?
ga: Te maŋ nɔyeli okwaayeli he gbɛjianɔtoo ko baanyɛ abu miŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛ shigbeemɔ kwraa yɛ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mɛi lɛ mli lɛ he aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Government programs often assist farmers by offering subsidized disease-control chemicals, training extension officers to guide you, introducing high-yield resistant seed varieties, and providing crop insurance support to recover losses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi kɛtsɔ tsofai ni akɛyeɔ abuaa helai ni akɛyeɔ abuaa amɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsɔsemɔ nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ koni amɛkudɔ bo. Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni woɔ yibii babaoo ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo. ni ekɛ yelikɛbuamɔ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ahe inshuɔrans koni akɛná nibii ni elaaje lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What modern tools or technologies can help a small farmer like me prevent crop losses?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii loo ŋaalee baanyɛ aye abua okwaafoi bibii tamɔ mi koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Modern farming technologies include high-quality disease-resistant seeds, mobile phone apps that help identify plant diseases early from leaf photographs, and specialized sprayers that apply protective treatments efficiently.
ga: Nɔ ni fata ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he ŋaalee he ji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ. Mobile app ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ayɔseɔ tsei ahe helai mra kɛjɛɔ baai amli mfonirii amli kɛ tsɔne krɛdɛɛ ko ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ ni buɔ mɔ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to use improved, disease-resistant seeds instead of saved seeds from my previous corn harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i he kɛ je ye ngma nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ tsu ní.

english: Improved seeds are specifically bred in laboratories to withstand common local pests, severe drought, and major diseases, whereas seeds saved from past harvests lose their strength over time and are much easier for diseases to attack.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yɛ laboratori ko mli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛye tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. hɔmɔ ni naa wa kɛ helai ni he hiaa Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli, ni helai tutuaa amɛ oya kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps bring back the healthy green color and boosts crop yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why should I clear my field without burning the bush before planting cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ ni mishãaa jwɛi lɛ dani midu ŋmei?

english: Burning destroys organic matter and beneficial soil organisms that keep soil fertile and moist. Clearing without burning leaves organic material to rot into natural fertilizer, keeping the soil cool and healthy for your cassava.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Enɛ haa sũ lɛ baa nii ni ehaa enɔ fũuɔ. Kɛ́ ajie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ni ashãaa lɛ, ebaaha nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afite ni etsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ feɔ fɛo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa trees until they are mature enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe Kɛyashi tso lɛ da bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the plot where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni midu ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nitrogen, leaving the ground tired. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, restoring land fertility naturally for your next crop.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shãa. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni okɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my cabbage leaves, and how can I protect them?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ naa?

english: Small holes are usually caused by caterpillars or insect larvae eating the leaves. Checking under the leaves early in the morning and applying recommended organic sprays like neem leaf extract helps control these pests safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai lɛ kɛ bu bibii baa. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ leebi ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsofa mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa tamɔ neem baa lɛ mli nu lɛ atsu nii. Ye obua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop dark, rotten spots on the bottom as they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi kɛji ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition, called blossom end rot, happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium or face irregular watering. Mulching your soil and keeping moisture levels consistent helps the roots absorb nutrients properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa beni tomato tsei lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛkɛ nu ni ejaaa kpeɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli ni okwɛ koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛná niyenii mli hewalɛ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and bushy but not producing flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji shi ewooo fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer causes pepper plants to produce leaves instead of flowers. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to set flowers and produce plenty of peppers.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha pepper tso lɛ awo baai yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses the plant and prevents proper flower pollination. Covering the soil around the base with dried grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and helps the blossoms stay on the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some of the saved maize seeds from my last harvest fail to sprout when I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds fail to germinate if they were stored with too much moisture or damaged by hidden insects like weevils. Drying seeds properly until they are hard and storing them in airtight containers protects their ability to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɔɔ mli loo kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ ŋmeii efite amɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaadara lɛ he.

english: Harvested yams are living roots that need cool air circulating around them to prevent heat buildup and sweating. Storing them in a shaded, well-ventilated yam barn keeps them dry and prevents rotting.
ga: Atomɔ ni akpa lɛ ji shishifãi ni hiɛ ka ni he hiaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ koni ebɔle amɛhe. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo kɛ latsaa akafee nɔ ko. Okɛ amɛ ato sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni yɔɔ hulutsoo, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ehi shi ni eha ehiɛ akafite.

english: Can I plant cocoyam under the shade of my plantain trees on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo yɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ ashishi?

english: Yes, cocoyam naturally prefers partial shade and moist soil. Plantain trees provide large leaves that shelter young cocoyams from harsh sunlight while keeping the ground cool and damp.
ga: Hɛɛ, kookoo sumɔɔ shade fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ. Tsei bibii lɛ ji baai agboi ni buɔ ŋmei tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Is it good to plant short-term food crops like corn between my coconut trees while they are young?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaadu niyenii ni heɔ be kukuoo, tamɔ ŋmãa, yɛ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ kɛjɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, because coconut trees take several years to mature and need wide spacing, planting fast-growing crops like corn or cocoyam between them makes good use of the empty land and provides early harvests.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmei tsei heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛdaraa, ni amɛbiɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe babaoo. Nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei enyɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa akɛ he ni yɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa yibiiwoo baa oya.

english: Will growing different crops like plantain, cocoyam, and corn on the same land ruin my soil faster?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tamɔ plantain, cocoa, kɛ ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ baafite mishikpɔŋ lɛ oya?

english: Not if spaced properly. Different crops feed at different soil depths and require different amounts of light, which helps protect the soil from erosion and keeps it balanced.
ga: Dabi kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ sa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi yeɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ srɔtoi ni amɛbiɔ la babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do plantain stalks hold so much water even during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ banana tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi po lɛ?

english: The stem of a plantain is made of tightly wrapped leaf sheaths designed by nature to store large reserves of water and nutrients, allowing the plant to withstand brief dry spells.
ga: Akɛ baai ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ ni adebɔɔ fee koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo ahi mli lɛ feɔ plantain tsei lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛŋmɛɔ hulutsoo be kukuoo naa.

english: Why do my cocoyams dry up faster during heat spells than my plantain plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli fe midumɔwui lɛ?

english: Cocoyam roots stay close to the soil surface where moisture evaporates quickly, whereas plantains store water inside their thick stems and have deeper root structures.
ga: Cocoyam shishifãi lɛ bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ he ni nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya lɛ. Shi plantains lɛ, ekɛ nu toɔ tsei ni mli tse amli, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my plantain plant turn brown and hang down as the plant gets bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: This is normal crop behavior; as plantains grow, they shed older outer leaves to send water and energy upward to nurture new leaves and growing fruit bunches.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ subaŋ. Beni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ, amɛshwieɔ kponɔgbɛ baai momo lɛ koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ aya ŋwɛi koni amɛha baai heei kɛ aduawai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why does my corn yield get smaller when I plant it in the exact same spot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele yibiiwoo lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu yɛ he kome daa be lɛ?

english: Corn is a heavy feeder that quickly uses up nitrogen in the soil. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil nutrients unless you rotate crops or add organic manure.
