ga: Abɛi ji niyenii ni tsii ni yeɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ afite. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he.

english: What can I do with leftover plantain stems and crop waste after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni mifeɔ kɛ plantain tsei ni eshwɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashwieɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Chop them up and leave them on the soil. As crop stems decay, they return vital nutrients like potassium to the ground and act as mulch to keep the soil moist.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ lɛ ni oshi yɛ shikpɔŋ. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite lɛ Nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does spreading fallen dry coconut leaves around my plants help them grow?
ga: Akɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ he Te mi tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa tɛŋŋ?

english: Laying dry coconut fronds between your crops acts as a natural blanket that blocks weeds, lowers soil temperature, and traps moisture in the ground during hot days.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei baai ni egbi wo tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ aba shi ni emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli

english: How can I tell if my farm soil has enough nutrients to grow heavy crops like corn and plantain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Healthy, fertile soil is usually dark, feels soft and crumbly, holds water well without becoming muddy, and contains living organisms like earthworms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. E nuɔ he kaa e ngɛ bɔdɔɔ nɛ e ngɛ tsɔe. Ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ni etsɔɔɔ muji. ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli tamɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hu yɛ

english: How can I tell if my maize leaves turning yellow means the plant is sick or just needs water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela mɔ tso lɛ loo nu kɛkɛ he miihia lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can mean either, but the pattern tells the story: uniform yellowing starting at the tip of lower leaves usually means a lack of nitrogen or water, while patchy, spotted, or streaked yellowing points to a disease or insect attack.
ga: Kaadi ŋmɔŋ baanyɛ atsɔɔ ekome loo ekroko. Shi nɛkɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ nɛɛ gbaa sane ko: Bei pii lɛ, su ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ekome ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ anaagbee lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii, ŋmeii loo mfonirii kɛ hela loo kooloi tutuamɔ baa.

english: If I see one cassava plant with twisted and spotty leaves, should I remove it immediately from my farm?
ga: Kɛ mina ŋmei tso ko ni baai etsake ni egbɔjɔ lɛ, ani esa akɛ majie kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, twisted and spotted leaves often indicate Cassava Mosaic Disease, which spreads quickly to healthy plants through whiteflies. Uprooting and destroying infected plants early prevents the sickness from spreading across your entire field.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsake ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii yɛji anɔ lɛ. Tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ashishijee mra kɛ amɛhiɛkpatamɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni hela akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and dry up when there are no tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without shade trees to filter the sun and maintain humidity, the high heat burns the leaves and causes the crop to dry out and stunt.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji tsei bɛ ni baaha hulutsoo aba ni amɛha hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni egbɔjɔɔ lɛ baa.

english: High heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination. When temperature levels get too high or dry winds blow, the plant drops its flowers to conserve energy and water instead of producing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni etsĩɔ pollination ni sa naa. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi tswaa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival behavior where plantain plants reduce their surface area exposed to the sun. This helps the plant trap moisture inside and prevent water loss during the hottest parts of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yibiiwoo su ko ni dumɔwui lɛ haa hulu la ni shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni emɔɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with small ears when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛtoi bibii yɔɔ mli beni adu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, they compete aggressively for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. The plants spend all their energy growing tall to reach light instead of producing large, heavy ears.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛ́ amɛmiida yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛshɛ la he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee toi wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow slowly when weeds are left growing around their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ́ jwɛi ebɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Weeds have strong root systems that steal water, fertilizer, and soil nutrients directly from your pepper plants. Keeping the base of your pepper plants weed-free ensures your crop gets full nourishment to produce healthy yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ jwɛi bɛ o-pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods are typically caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungal infection triggered by excess water, low air circulation, and shade that is too dense. Pruning trees to let in light helps keep pods healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ he lɛ baa. Fungal hela ni jɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa shi kɛ hulutsoo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli baa. Tsei ni afolɔ koni amɛha la lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I leave diseased cocoa pods on the ground after harvesting, will it harm next season's crop?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Ani ebaaye be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, leaving infected pods on the ground keeps fungal spores alive in the soil over the dry season. When the rains return, wind and splashing water carry these spores back onto your new crop, restarting the sickness.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba Kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ baaŋɔ nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ aku sɛɛ kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ amli. Koni hela lɛ aje shishi ekoŋŋ

english: How can I tell if my soil has enough nutrients to support a good harvest of yam?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba?

english: Healthy, nutrient-rich soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to touch, and holds moisture without staying soggy. If your previous crops grew slowly or had pale leaves, your soil likely needs manure or compost before planting yam.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ fɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ ota he ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa efee ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji akɛ onibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ da blɛoo loo eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ Ekolɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ he baahia oshikpɔŋ lɛ dani odu ŋmɔtɔ.

english: What causes small holes in my young maize leaves, and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Small holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the leaves. You can manage this by checking your farm early, picking off caterpillars by hand, or applying recommended organic or chemical sprays into the leaf whorls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. Nine ni akɛbuaa ŋmeii anaa Aloo akɛ organic sprays loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee lɛ awo baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots rot underground mainly due to waterlogged soil and fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots dry and healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ kɛ ŋmeii helai ji nɔ titri ni kɛ ŋmeii shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛhe wa

english: Your soil likely lacks nutrients if previous crops produced small yields, grew very slowly, or had pale yellow leaves. You can also look at weeds; if even weeds grow weakly on the land, the soil needs organic manure or chemical fertilizer.
ga: Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji tsei ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo, amɛdaraa blɛoo waa, loo amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Obaanyɛ ona jwɛi lɛ lolo. Eyɛ mli akɛ jwɛi lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ, shi Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ lolo.

english: Why should I not plant maize on the same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize continuously in the same place drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with crops like beans or peanuts restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa helai lɛ asɛɛkuu.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for future crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in small nodules on their roots. When the crop dies, that stored nitrogen remains in the soil as free, natural fertilizer for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboi. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and become very top-heavy when carrying bunches. Supporting the main stem with a sturdy forked wooden pole (propping) and building up soil around the base helps keep them upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ amɛmiiwo panicles lɛ. Akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwo mli (fiɔ sɛɛ) fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ ni amaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ he lɛ. Shishitoo lɛ haa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes in the ground to support my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei awo shikpɔŋ koni mikɛfi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and grow large underground tubers. Staking also keeps the foliage off the damp soil, preventing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛha hulu la ni fa babaoo. Akɛ tsei lɛ hoɔ nii ni akɛduɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni fungal leaf helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa leaves turn yellow and drop during the dry season because the tree is trying to save water in hot, low-humidity weather. Planting shade crops like plantains and placing dry grass mulch around the tree bases keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cocoa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu nu he yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛ sũ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What is the best time of day for me to water my pepper plants so they stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mawo mi-pepper tso lɛ nu koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: The best time to water pepper plants is early in the morning. This lets the roots absorb moisture before the afternoon heat and gives wet leaves time to dry quickly in the sun, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ pepper tsei anɔ nu ji leebi maŋkpa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛheɔ nu dani shwane mli latsaa lɛ baa, ni ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ naa be ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la mli. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal light, root space, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing weeds during the first few weeks after planting gives your crops the best chance to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ la, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ waa. Kɛ́ otsi jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha onibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ waa.

english: How do I know if the crop seed I am buying will actually sprout and grow well on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni miheɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Certified seeds undergo testing in specialized laboratories to check their purity, health, and germination strength before they reach the market. Choosing seeds with an official certification label ensures you are planting clean, healthy seeds that are proven to grow well.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo amɛ he odase lɛ amli yɛ laboratorii krɛdɛɛi komɛi amli koni ana bɔ ni amɛhe tse, bɔ ni amɛhe wa ha, kɛ bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amɛhaa dani amɛyashɛ jara nɔ. Dumɔwui ni amralo lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ akɛ oohala lɛ haa onaa nɔmimaa akɛ oodu dumɔwui ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the green leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛyitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tips usually show that the plant is starving for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and build strong stems. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure will help restore their green color and speed up growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛma tsei ashishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my crops seem to get weaker and produce less every time I plant the same crop on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be ni madu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same soil every year continuously drains specific nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground. Rotating different crop types, such as switching between corn and beans, restores soil nutrients and stops pest build-up.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛi hoɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ tsakemɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaabuamɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes to appear on the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai amli lɛ baa?

english: Small holes and chewed leaf edges on young corn are typically caused by destructive caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the inner leaves. Checking your fields early and applying targeted treatments into the plant leaves helps protect the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ Fall Armyworm ni yeɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii kɛ baai ni ashɛreɔ yɛ ŋmeii bibii anɔ lɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe lɛ baaye abua ni abu hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do black spots appear on my tomato leaves and cause them to wither up from the bottom of the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ tomato baai anɔ ni ehaa amɛgboɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Black spots that cause leaves to dry up are usually fungal diseases that splash up from the wet soil when it rains. Removing the lower leaves near the ground and avoiding watering directly onto the leaves keeps the plant dry and reduces disease spread.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii diji ni haa baai lɛ gbiɔ lɛ ji ŋmeii hela ko ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ. Jiemɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbi ni helai gbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when excessive water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage, suffocating the roots and allowing fungi to attack. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu babaoo hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa amɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves dry up and turn brown during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ mli egbi ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ Harmattan nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the dry Harmattan season, hot dry winds pull water out of cocoa leaves faster than the root system can suck up water from the soil. Keeping permanent shade trees on your farm and mulching around the roots helps hold moisture in the soil and protects young cocoa trees.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ daa lɛ akwɛmɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ haa sũ lɛ mli nu shwieɔ shi ni ebuɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, inadequate water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing it to drop flowers to survive. Keeping the soil evenly moist and giving plants balanced plant food keeps the flowers attached so they can grow into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo bɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni oha tsei lɛ tsei niyenii ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantain suckers very close to each other on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ plantain dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in thin stems and small bunches. Proper spacing ensures each plantain tree gets enough sunlight and soil nutrients to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni no haa tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii feɔ ŋmeii. Gbɛ ni sa ni ato lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni plantain fɛɛ plantain naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my farm right after I clear the land for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daa oya nɛkɛ beni mijie he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Clearing the field exposes hidden weed seeds buried in the topsoil to direct sunlight and water, which signals them to germinate all at once. Planting fast-growing cover crops like cowpeas helps shade the ground and naturally chokes out weeds.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jɛmɛ lɛ, jwɛi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni afu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ hulu la kɛ nu mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ baakwɛ̃ shikome. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why should I change the number of seeds I plant on my farm depending on whether it is the dry season or the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsake dumɔwui ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ayibɔ? Edamɔ kɛji hɔmɔ be loo nugbɔshiimɔ be ji lɛ nɔ?

english: In the rainy season, abundant water allows more crops to grow closely together without starving, so you can plant a high density (up to 120,000 plants). In the dry season, water is limited, so you must reduce the number of plants (around 60,000) so they do not compete for moisture.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ, nu babaoo ni yɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ. Obaanyɛ odu yɛ hei ni tsei babaoo yɔɔ (kɛyashi tsei 120,000). Yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ, nu faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ tsei lɛ ayibɔ aba shi (aaafee tsei 60,000) koni okɛ akaŋ awo ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ.

english: Is it possible to double the amount of crops I plant on my field during the rainy season?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ he toi enyɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, abundant rainfall provides enough soil moisture to support twice as many plants—increasing your population from a dry season rate of around 60,000 plants up to 120,000 plants on the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tsei ni fa fe nakai lɛ shii enyɔ—ni ehaa oyibɔ yaa hiɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei aaafee 60,000 ni yɔɔ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ nɔ kɛyaa 120,000 yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: Which season in Ghana is best if I want to plant the highest possible number of seeds per acre?
ga: Mɛɛ be hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana kɛji miisumɔ ni madu dumɔwui babaoo fe fɛɛ yɛ acre kome mli?

english: The main rainy season is best for high-density planting because the continuous water supply can feed a heavy population of crops without causing them to dry out.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ ji be ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha dumɔwui ni fa babaoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu ni yaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo aye nii ni ehaaa tsei lɛ agbi.

english: Why do extension officers recommend different seed counts for the major rainy season compared to the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ akwɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi kɛha nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ kɛ akɛto nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he lɛ?

english: The two seasons have very different soil moisture levels; rainy seasons support heavy plant populations (up to 120,000), while dry seasons require lower populations (around 60,000) to keep plants from dying of thirst.
ga: Bei enyɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ srɔto kwraa. Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei babaoo (ni shɛɔ 120,000), yɛ be mli ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ biɔ tsei fioo (aaafee 60,000) koni tsei akagboi yɛ kumai hewɔ.

english: How does water availability affect how close together I can plant my crops?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When water is plentiful, crops can be planted very close together because every plant gets enough drink. When water is scarce, you must space them further apart so each plant has enough soil water to survive.
ga: Beni nu fa bɔ ni sa lɛ Abaanyɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Beni nu faaa lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ gbɛ abɔ he koni tso fɛɛ tso aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die if I plant too many seeds together during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season, soil moisture is low. If too many seeds are planted close together, their roots fight over the little water available, causing all the plants to stress, wither, and fail.
ga: Yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ faaa. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ yɛ nɔ ni nu fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ haoɔ, amɛgbiɔ, ni amɛgbeeɔ shi.

english: How do I decide how much space to leave between my crops based on the water condition of my land?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ he ni esa akɛ mashi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ he yɛ nu shihilɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa?

english: If your land has plenty of water or regular rain, you can reduce spacing to fit more plants. If the land is dry or rain is low, leave wider spaces between plants so each crop gets enough water to grow strong.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa loo nugbɔ nɛɔ daa. Obaanyɛ otsi gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ nɔ koni anyɛ adu tsei babaoo. Kɛji he lɛ mli egbi loo nugbɔ fioo pɛ enɛɔ lɛ Shi gbɛ ni da yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: If the rain is not as strong as expected this season, how many plants should I target for my land?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ waaa tamɔ bɔ ni esa akɛ enɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ Tsei enyiɛ esa akɛ mafee miyiŋ akɛ madu kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: If water conditions are poor or moderate, you should aim for an intermediate planting density—around 100,000 plants—so your crops don't suffer from water shortages.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ shihilɛ lɛ ehiii loo eshɛɛɛ he lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ ohiɛ afɔ̃ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ, ni miihe ashɛ tsei 100,000 nɔ, koni nu ni faaa lɛ akapiŋ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What happens to my harvest if I plant a very high number of crops when rainfall is poor?
ga: Mɛni baaba minikpamɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Planting too many crops under low rainfall leads to weak, stunted plants and poor yields because the crops waste energy competing for scarce water instead of producing healthy fruit.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ shishi lɛ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni egbɔjɔ kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi baa ejaakɛ nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛmiitswa nu ni faaa lɛ he akaŋ. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ yiblii nɛ ngɛ he wami.

english: If my farm relies on poor or uncertain water supply, should I plant fewer seeds than normal?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ miŋmɔ lɛ kɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ nu jɛɛhe ni ehiii loo ni bɛ shiŋŋ nɔ hu? Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui fioo fe bɔ ni esa akɛ madu?

english: Yes, when water supply is poor, reducing your plant count (to around 60,000 to 100,000 plants) ensures that the crops you do plant have enough moisture to reach harvest maturity.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ nu lɛ ehiii Otsei lɛ ayibɔ ni oooba shi (kɛyashɛ aaafee tsei 60,000 kɛyashi 100,000) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmaa ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or is getting too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure gives the crops the food they need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing water in intense heat. If the leaves stay curled up in the evening or morning, it means the soil is too dry and the plant needs water.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Kɛji baai lɛ shwie shi gbɛkɛ loo leebi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ ni tso lɛ he miihia nu.

english: Why do I need to clear away extra young shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi tsɔne titri lɛ eje kpo.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water, light, and soil nutrients from the main plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to direct all its energy into growing a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ nu, la kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ dumɔwui babaoo.

english: Why do I have to put tall wooden sticks in the ground for my yams to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei lɛ awo ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ nɛkɛ? Shikpɔŋ nɔ koni mi sweet potato lɛ akwɔ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can reach full sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp soil, protecting them from diseases and helping the plant produce bigger tubers underground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛbaji lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers keep dropping off without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree experiences stress from extreme heat, dry weather, or insect attacks. Giving young trees enough shade and managing pests helps the flowers successfully turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, loo kooloi ni baatutua lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa ha tsei bibii kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii yɛ omanyeyeli mli.

english: This soft black bottom is blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the dry soil. Watering your tomato plants regularly keeps the soil evenly moist so calcium can reach the growing fruits.
ga: Nɛkɛ shishigbɛ diŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɛɛ miipiŋ kɛjɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ he. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ daa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bɔni afee ni calcium lɛ ashɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to the local soil, so they absorb rainwater and plant food faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from starving your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kpãa gbee yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni aduɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni hɔmɔ akaye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ.

english: Why is it good for my farm to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. This feeds the soil naturally, making it richer and helping neighboring maize plants grow better without extra fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ewoɔ yibii babaoo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa kroko awo mli.

english: Cassava is typically ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower stem leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn powdery and full of small insects in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ etsɔ ashikishaŋ kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Maize rots and attracts weevils if it is stored while still holding moisture. Drying the maize cobs thoroughly in the sun until the grains are hard prevents insect damage during storage.
ga: Abele baagbo ni ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛba kɛji akɛ akɛto he ni edɔ lolo. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kooloi fiteɔ nii yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed leaves during dry weather to save water and protect themselves from drying out. Providing shade trees and placing mulch around the base of the cocoa trees helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How long does it take for a newly planted cocoa seedling to start bearing pods?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Modern hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas traditional cocoa varieties can take between 4 and 5 years to yield their first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni blema kookoo henɔi lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛfee amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This blackening is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions. Pruning excess tree branches to allow sunlight and airflow, along with removing infected pods, helps control it.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ duŋ nɛɛ baa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ niji lɛ.

english: Why are tiny holes appearing in my cocoa leaves and young shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-kookoo baai kɛ mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Tiny holes on young cocoa trees are usually caused by mirids (capsids), small insects that suck sap from leaves and young shoots. Spraying recommended insecticides during peak pest seasons helps protect the trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, myrids (capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii amli lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe nu ni jɛɔ baai kɛ tsei bibii amli lɛ Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: What causes my cocoa tree to produce small pods instead of large, healthy ones?
ga: Mɛni haa mi cacao tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii? Mohu ɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ɔmɛ agbo nɛ a ngɛ he wami.

english: Small pods usually mean the tree lacks sufficient nutrients or water during the fruit development stage. Applying proper fertilizers and pruning unneeded branches ensures the tree sends full energy to the developing pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli ni afolɔ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do cassava plants produce big root tubers in some farms but only thin roots in mine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei woɔ shishifãi wuji yɛ ŋmɔji komɛi amli lɛ? Shi shishifãi komɛi yɛ minɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava needs soft, well-drained soil to expand its tubers. Packed or hard soil prevents the roots from swelling, even if the plant leaves above look healthy and green.
ga: Yucca biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛdu ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo ni wa lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafuu. Kɛji tso lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ eŋɔli po lɛ,.

english: Why should I plant shade trees in my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Shade trees protect young cocoa trees from intense direct sunlight, lower field temperatures, and shed leaves that decay into natural manure for your crops.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. lower temperature Ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha onibii.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds away from the base of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Clearing them ensures your main crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha otsei titrii lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli dani aduawai lɛ shwereɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and top-heavy fruit bunches. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo fork prevents the plant from bending or breaking under heavy wind and fruit weight.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii. Kɛ́ okɛ tso loo ŋmei ni wa fĩ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafo loo efo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ tso lɛ yibii lɛ amli tsiimɔ hewɔ.

english: How do I know when my maize crop is fully ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-ŋma lɛ eshɛ kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the kernels become hard with a visible dark mark forming at the point where each kernel connects to the cob.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni ŋmeii lɛ wa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni anaa yɛ hei ni ŋmeii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kpaa gbee yɛ lɛ.

english: Can I use pig manure on my farm crops, and how does it help them grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa?

english: Yes, properly composted pig manure is rich in key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus. When mixed into the ground, it enriches the soil structure, helps hold moisture, and supplies essential food to help crops grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. Kɛ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ shishitoo lɛ afee nɔ ni hi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi Ni eji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: Why do my crops yield less when I plant the exact same crop in the same field every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests that like that plant to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops keeps the soil balanced and naturally reduces pest problems.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsei buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii srɔtoi ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai baa shi.

english: Why is it necessary to clear and break up my soil properly before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie sũ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni akumɔ mli dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil removes competing weeds, allows young roots to easily spread deep into the earth, and helps rainwater and air soak down to where the plant feeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ajie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa nugbɔ nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni eboteɔ he ni tsei yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when left under full direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that lose water rapidly under intense sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a shaded canopy that retains soil moisture and protects the cocoa until its roots are established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nu fiteɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ehaa hulutsoo baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their tiny green pods before they ever turn into mature pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani ebaatsɔ pod ni eda kwraa?

english: Small cocoa pods often drop when the tree lacks enough water or nutrients to feed them, or when insects attack. Ensuring the farm gets adequate nutrients and keeping pests under control helps the tree keep its fruit to maturity.
ga: cocoa pods bibii Bei pii lɛ, amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua lɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa amɛ Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why should I cut off unnecessary branches and suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji kɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ?

english: Pruning removes useless branches so the tree can focus its water and food on growing bigger pods. It also opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and fresh air, which prevents fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afolɔ mli lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ koni tso lɛ anyɛ ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii anɔ yɛ tsei wuji lɛ anɔ. Egbeleɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ hu koni enine ashɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa nɔ. ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa

english: Why do crop leaves curl up or droop during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl or droop to reduce the surface area exposed to direct heat, which helps the plant reduce evaporation and conserve its internal water until temperatures drop.
ga: Ha ni ebɔle ehe loo efolɔ ehe koni ekɛba ŋwɛi he ni la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhaa nu ni hoɔ lɛ baa shi, ni amɛbuɔ nu ni yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my crops turning yellow means the soil is starving?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii ni miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves—especially starting from older, lower leaves—usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Adding compost or fertilizer restores this missing nutrient and turns the foliage green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, titri lɛ kɛjɛ baai bibii amli Bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What happens if I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops into my plot?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Overcrowding forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stems and tiny fruits rather than a larger, healthy harvest.
ga: Nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ aduawai bibii baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds seem to grow much faster than the food crops I carefully planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally hardy and adapted to quickly soak up sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. Removing them early ensures they do not steal vital food and water from your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛ onibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or crop residue helps restore the green color so the plant can make food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdara waa. Nitrogen ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii.

english: What makes my crops produce so many leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa midumɔ nii lɛ woɔ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ?

english: When crops get too much nitrogen without enough phosphorus or potassium, they use all their energy to grow leaves and stems. Plants need balanced soil nutrients to transition from growing leafy branches to producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ ni phosphorus loo potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai kɛ ŋmeii. Niyenii ni sa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛtsake kɛjɛ niji ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Flowers fall off when the tree is stressed by extreme heat, drought, or lack of pollination by tiny insects. Providing moderate shade and keeping moisture in the soil helps the tree retain its flowers so they can develop into full pods.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo kooloi bibii ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔfɔi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha tso lɛ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ hi shi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdara kwraa ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Mulching around the plant helps keep soil moisture steady so roots can continuously absorb the calcium needed for healthy fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Mulching ni akɛbɔleɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ yaa nɔ daa. Enɛ ji koni shishifãi lɛ aya nɔ aŋɔ calcium ni he hiaa kɛha aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cassava roots are mature and ready for harvesting underground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: As cassava matures—usually around 9 to 12 months after planting—the lower leaves turn yellow and drop naturally. You can also test harvest by gently digging up the soil around one plant to check the size and firmness of the tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ daa (bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ), shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Obaanyɛ oka okpamɔ lɛ hu okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ooofo kɛbɔle ohe lɛ nɔ. Tso ni mli tse Koni akɛkwɛ bɔ ni yitso lɛ da ha kɛ bɔ ni eyɛ mlɛo ha

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves roll up tightly during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in high heat is a crop's self-defense trick to prevent water loss. By curling, the leaves hide from direct sunlight so less moisture evaporates from them during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ŋaa ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni nu akafite. kɛ curl Akɛ baai lɛ ewo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Fɛ̃i fioo pɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I space my crops far apart instead of planting as many as possible close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ato he ko ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ? Mohu ɔ, mo du mɛ kɛ su a he bɔ nɛ o ma nyɛ.

english: Crops planted too close compete with each other for water, soil nutrients, and sunlight, leading to thin and weak plants. Giving each crop enough space ensures it gets the full resources needed to yield large, healthy fruits.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baatswa nu he akaŋ. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Kɛ́ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ, ehaa enáa nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni ewo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry out quickly during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya yɛ harmatta be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose water rapidly in dry winds. Covering the soil around the base with dried leaves or grass helps trap moisture in the soil to keep the roots alive.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ, ni nu lɛ laajeɔ oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why does clearing weeds from my farm make my crops grow much faster?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya lɛ?

english: Weeds act as competitors that steal water, fertilizer, and light meant for your main crops. Removing them leaves all the soil nutrients exclusively for your plants to feed on and grow without stress.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha onibii titrii lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi koni otsei lɛ aye ni amɛdara ni haomɔ ko bɛ he.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to save hybrid maize seeds from my harvest to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo kɛha mi akɛ mahere ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛjɛ kpamɔɔ ko mli koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for high performance in their first generation only. Saving seeds from that harvest results in weaker offspring plants that yield far less and mature unevenly.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nitsumɔ ni nɔ kwɔ aba yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa ni amɛdaraaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Why does my rice field need so much standing water compared to my maize field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he hiaa nu ni damɔ shi babaoo kɛ akɛto mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Rice plants thrive in wet conditions because standing water keeps the soil constantly moist, suppresses weed growth, and helps the plant absorb essential nutrients more efficiently than dry-land crops.
ga: Omɔ tsei yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ.

english: What is the benefit of planting modern improved rice seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ adumɔ he yɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ tsutsu ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛaato he lɛ najiaŋ?

english: Improved rice varieties are bred to grow faster, withstand common local diseases better, and produce larger yields compared to older seeds saved season after season.
ga: Omɔ henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ daa oya. Helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ. ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui momo ni ato kɛha be lɛ he.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crops in neat rows rather than broadcasting seeds randomly across the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni yɔɔ fɛo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu dumɔwui trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ?

english: Row planting ensures every crop gets equal access to sunlight and soil nutrients, while making it much easier for you to weed, apply fertilizer, and move around your field.
ga: Row planting haa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli, ni okɛyaa he fɛɛ he. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ waaa kwraa.

english: Why do extension officers recommend starting rice seeds in a nursery bed before moving them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ ŋmãa shikpɔji anɔ dani adu amɛ awo ŋmãa wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: A nursery protects young, delicate shoots from heavy rains, bright sun, and pests, allowing only the strongest seedlings to be transplanted into your main farm.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔhe lɛ buɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe, ni ehaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my rice plants turning yellow before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a cry for help indicating that your soil is low in nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ amɛ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ ni amɛdu niyenii.

english: Why should I split my fertilizer application into two or three steps instead of putting it all in the ground at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majara mi-fertilizing lɛ mli enyɔ loo etɛ moŋ fe ni makɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ awo mli shikome?

english: Crops consume food in stages as they grow; giving fertilizer in split doses prevents rain from washing it away before the plant roots are ready to use it.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ niyenii yɛ be kɛ bei amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi wo mli lɛ, ehaaa nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ amɛkɛbaatsu nii.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds once the rainy season starts?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: You should wait until the rains are steady and the ground stays wet, because planting during early erratic rainfall can cause seeds to germinate and then dry out and die.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ ba shi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei ni bɛ faŋŋ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛgbi ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops, and how does that reduce my harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Ni te no baaha minikpamɔ lɛ aba shi eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops, leaving your farm plants weak and unable to produce full grains.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are insect pests attacking my crop leaves early in the morning and late in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ leebi kɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Insects hide during the hottest daylight hours to save energy and feed when temperatures cool down, making early mornings and evenings the best times to inspect and treat your field.
ga: Kplukai kɛ amɛhe teeɔ amɛhe yɛ hulutsoo be mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛna niyenii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ. Ha leebi maŋkpa kɛ gbɛkɛ afee be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okwɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why must I thoroughly dry my harvested rice before putting it into storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ agbi kwraa dani mikɛwo kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Damp grains cause mold to grow and attract insects that will destroy your harvest inside the bag, whereas fully dried grains can stay safe to eat or sell for many months.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa kooloi bibii ni baafite onibii ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa ni egbi kwraa lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe ni aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why are there so many ants crawling all over my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo miiho yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Ants are often attracted to cocoa trees because they farm smaller insects like mealybugs, which produce a sweet liquid. In cocoa farms, ants can protect these harmful insects and help spread diseases like Black Pod and Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus across your farm.
ga: Kookoo tsei sumɔɔ ŋmeii ejaakɛ amɛkwɛɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs, ni haa nu ni ŋɔɔ baa lɛ. Yɛ kookoo ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ ahe ni amɛye amɛbua ni amɛgbɛ helai tamɔ black pod kɛ kookoo bud virus amɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: How do ants actually harm my cocoa pods and stems?
ga: Te ŋmeii yeɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji kɛ mishishifãi lɛ awui amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While ants may not eat the pods directly, they build mud tents over other destructive insects to protect them. These protected insects suck the sap from your cocoa stems and pods, causing the pods to dry up or grow weak.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeee ŋmeii lɛ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ, shi moŋ, amɛmaa sũ buu yɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anɔ. koni ebu amɛhe Nɛkɛ kooloi ni abuɔ amɛhe nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe waaa.

english: What is the best way for me to get rid of ants disturbing my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie ŋmeii ni fiteɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: You can manage ants by pruning low-hanging cocoa branches so they do not touch the ground, clearing weeds regularly to break their pathways, and applying approved bio-pesticides or recommended insecticides to the trunks.
ga: Obaanyɛ okudɔ ŋmeii kɛtsɔ kookoo niji ni shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ ni ooofo koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa koni okpata amɛgbɛ lɛ hiɛ. ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ awo tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do ants build mud shelters on my cocoa stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitswa sũ shĩai yɛ mikoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Certain species of ants build mud structures to shelter scale insects and mealybugs from rain and predators. Removing these mud tents manually or spraying them helps expose the pests underneath so they cannot damage your trees.
ga: Akpɔlɔi komɛi maa sũ mli tsũi koni amɛkɛbu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ onine jieɔ sũ buu nɛɛ loo okɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akahi amɛshishi. bɔni afee ni akafite tso lɛ

english: Why are some of the shade trees on my farm causing my cocoa trees to get sick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ miiha kookoo tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Certain large forest trees act as natural host trees for pests and viruses like Swollen Shoot. If these shade trees carry the disease, insects can easily carry it down to your nearby cocoa trees.
ga: Koo mli tsei wuji komɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ, tamɔ akɔɔblei ni efuu lɛ baanyɛ ahi mli. Kɛji akɛ nɛkɛ shade tsei nɛɛ hiɛ helai lɛ, Kooloi baanyɛ ashɛ kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ oya.

english: How do I know if a non-cocoa tree on my farm needs to be cut down?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ehe miihia ni mafolɔ tsei ni jeee kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: If a non-cocoa tree creates too much thick shade, harbors severe pest nests, or belongs to a species known to host cocoa viruses (like the Baobab or Silk Cotton tree), it should be pruned or cut down to protect your crop.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni jeee kookoo tsei lɛ feɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ, Ayɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli. loo efata tso ko ni ale akɛ ehiɛ kookoo hela (tamɔ baobab loo cotton silk tsei) lɛ he, esa akɛ afolɔ loo ajie koni akɛbu onibii ahe.

english: How much shade do my mature cocoa trees need to stay healthy?
ga: Mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ he hulutsoo be enyiɛ he hiaa koni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Mature cocoa trees need light shade that lets in balanced sunlight. Too much shade traps excess moisture and attracts ants and fungal diseases, while too little shade leaves the trees vulnerable to drought and heat stress.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulutsoo be ni sa. Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo fioo ko pɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ hɔmɔ kɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ.

english: Should I abandon an old cocoa farm that is heavily infested with pests?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashi mi-kookoo ŋmɔ momo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: You do not necessarily need to abandon it immediately. If the trees are reasonably young, aggressive pruning, weeding, and proper pest control can restore them. However, if the trees are very old and diseased, clearing and replanting with hybrid cocoa is usually better.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni okpa amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛji tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo lɛ Tso lɛ he tsemɔ ni sa, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha nakai tsei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ekoŋŋ. Shi, kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ egbɔ waa ni helai emɔ amɛ lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie tsei lɛ ni akɛ hybrid cocoa awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Will clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help reduce pest problems?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ Ani kookoo tsei lɛ baaye abua ni eba tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, keeping the ground around your trees clear creates a barrier that makes it difficult for ants, bush crickets, and other crawling pests to climb up into your cocoa canopy.
ga: Hɛɛ, he ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ Tsei lɛ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni gbalaa ŋmeii baa. bush cricket kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui Kookoo ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ kwɔɔ wa.

english: Why do pests attack some cocoa trees on my farm while leaving the trees next to them untouched?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi, ni amɛshiɔ tsei ni yɔɔ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Ashɛko he?

english: Pests usually attack trees that are already weak due to poor soil, lack of nutrients, or direct exposure to harsh sun. Strong, well-nourished cocoa trees produce natural compounds that make them harder for pests to infest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa tsei ni egbɔjɔ momo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ, loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ hewɔ lɛ. Cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni haa ewaa kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and die when I remove all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving taller shade trees protects them while they are growing and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. Kɛ́ oshi tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: When cocoa trees are planted too close together, their roots fight for food and water in the soil, and their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. This causes the trees to grow tall and thin with very few pods.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kookoo yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni ebaai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my older cocoa trees produce fewer and smaller pods every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo ni amɛfeɔ bibii daa afi lɛ?

english: As cocoa trees grow older, their roots become less efficient at absorbing nutrients from the soil, and their branches become more vulnerable to disease. Pruning them back or replacing very old trees helps restore high yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tso lɛ eda lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni eniji lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai oya. Tsei momoi ni afolɔ loo amɛtsakeɔ Ebaaye ebua ni yibiiwoo lɛ aku sɛɛ aba he ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why is it bad for my crop yield if I let tall weeds grow around my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii kɛji miŋmɛ gbɛ ni jwɛi kakadaji kwɛ̃ yɛ mikoo tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Tall weeds steal nutrients and water from the soil that your cocoa trees need to make pods. They also trap moisture around the tree trunk, creating a damp environment where fungal diseases can easily breed.
ga: Jwɛi ni kɛlɛ lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ sũ ni he hiaa cacao tso lɛ koni ekɛfee eshishifãi lɛ amli. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ hu. tso shishi Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ yɛ mli mlɛo.

english: Why should I prune off dead branches and small suckers from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni egboi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Pruning removes useless branches that waste the tree's energy. Opening up the branch canopy allows sunlight and breeze to dry off the leaves, preventing diseases from developing and helping the tree focus its energy on growing healthy pods.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa ni fiteɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Kɛ́ agbele ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa lɛ, hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa baai lɛ agbiɔ. Tsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and rot on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly through rain droplets and high humidity. Removing infected pods right away stops the fungal spores from spreading to healthy pods on neighboring trees.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi kɛ hulutsoo be ni fa babaoo nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli lɛ anaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops fail to grow properly on land that was previously used for illegal gold digging?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsutsu lɛ akɛ shika tsuru tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Digging for gold strips away the fertile topsoil where crop roots feed. It leaves behind compacted subsoil and toxic heavy metals that prevent plants from getting nutrients and water.
ga: Shika tsuru ni ataoɔ lɛ jieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii ni haa tsei shishifãi lɛ niyenii lɛ. Eshiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ dade ni tsii ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii kɛ nu.

english: Why does muddy water from nearby river digging ruin my crops when I use it for watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo nu lɛ?

english: Water polluted by land digging carries toxic chemicals and heavy sediments that coat plant roots and poison the soil. This prevents the roots from taking in air and clean water, causing the plants to turn yellow and die.
ga: Tsofai ni yɔɔ gbeyei kɛ sũ ni tsii ni haa tsei ashishifãi ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni atsa lɛ mli lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ akamu kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli tse kɛ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ.

english: Why do the tiny flowers on my cocoa tree fall off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? Yɛ mi koko tso lɛ nɔ koni egbee shi ni etsɔko pod?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off if the tree lacks nutrients, suffers from dry soil, or is not pollinated by tiny beneficial insects like midges. Keeping the soil healthy and avoiding harsh chemical sprays helps preserve these pollinators.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi yeɔ amanehulu loo kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ midges lɛ haaa ená pollen. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oookwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni mli wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do young cocoa leaves look scorched and crumpled even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by sap-sucking pests like capsids. As they feed on young shoots, they inject poisonous saliva into the plant, making the leaves look burnt and weakening overall pod production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ capsids, kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa, ejaakɛ amɛyeɔ ŋmeii bibii. Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei awoɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni ehaa pod ni afeɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds too close to the trunks of big trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tso agbo ko ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi tsɔ?

english: Big trees have large roots that soak up most of the water and nutrients in the soil, and their thick canopy blocks sunlight. Maize planted too close will grow thin, pale, and yield very small ears.
ga: Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji ni gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo. ni ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa Abele ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baafee bibioo, ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaawo toi bibii waa.

english: Why do my crops grow bent and weak when I plant the seeds too close to each other in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the young plants compete aggressively for light and air. They stretch upward and sideways to reach sunlight, making their stems thin, weak, and easily broken by wind.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he akaŋ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe kɛyaa ŋwɛi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa afã koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ fiteɔ lɛ oya.

english: How do I know when my land is getting tired from growing the same crop every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ miigbɔjɔ kɛjɛ tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ daa afi lɛ mli?

english: Tired soil speaks through your crops: leaves turn yellow early, stalks stay short, pests attack more easily, and your harvest drops every year even when the rains are good.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ tsɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ oya, tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ kukuji, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa amɛ oya. Ni onikpamɔ lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but very small tubers when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi eshishifãi bibii waa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or green foliage fertilizer, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in roots underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my crops right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to harsh conditions, so they absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing them early protects your crop's drinking water and food.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaabu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe nu kɛ niyenii ni onuɔ lɛ he.

english: Can I grow light-loving crops like tomatoes directly under the deep shade of big farm trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei ni sumɔɔ la, tamɔ tomato, yɛ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, tomatoes need direct sunlight for at least 6 hours a day to produce flowers and fruit. Heavy shade causes flower drop and small, sour tomatoes.
ga: Dabi, kɛ hoo lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ he hiaa tomato ŋmɛlɛtswai 6 daa gbi koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Shade ni tsii haa fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ tomato bibii ni mli edɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural self-defense against heat. By rolling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface exposed to the hot sun to conserve moisture.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ baa shi yɛ he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers keep dropping off the tree branches without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when stressed by severe dryness, lack of shade, or pest attacks like mirids (capsids). Keeping proper shade and soil moisture helps flowers stay and turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ capsids lɛ tutua amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ ha lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are some of the seeds I planted sprouting quickly while others right next to them have not come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ mi lɛ kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ? Ekwɛko lolo?

english: Seeds sprout unevenly if buried too deep, placed in dry soil pockets, or damaged by soil insects. Planting at a uniform shallow depth in moist soil gives even sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui baakwɛ̃ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ. Okɛwo bu ko mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ efite lɛ Kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ, ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaawo dumɔwui lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why does my pepper crop give a smaller harvest in its second year compared to its first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ná ŋmaa bibioo yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Pepper plants consume heavy nutrients during their first harvest and grow older, weaker roots that struggle to feed the plant in the second year without fresh manure or soil feeding.
ga: Pepper tsei yeɔ niyenii ni tsii yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli. Ni shishifãi ni edara ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii yɛ afi ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli ni ŋmei hee loo shikpɔŋ niyenii he ehiaaa.

english: How do I know if my land is good enough to support cocoa trees for many years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo tsei afii babaoo?

english: Good cocoa land needs deep, dark, well-drained soil rich in organic matter. Soil that holds too much water or dries out completely during dry spells will cause cocoa roots to rot or wither, leading to tree death.
ga: Cocoa shikpɔŋ kpakpa biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni hiɛɔ nu babaoo loo egbiɔ kwraa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ baaha kookoo shishifãi lɛ agbo loo amɛgboi. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji tso lɛ gbele.

english: What can I do to improve my farm soil if my crops are struggling to grow?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛji akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃?

english: You can strengthen weak soil by applying recommended cocoa fertilizers, adding organic compost, and leaving clearings of leaves as mulch around the base of trees to lock in nutrients and moisture.
ga: Obaanyɛ owo shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ hewalɛ kɛtsɔ kookoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. add organic compost Ni oshi baai lɛ akɛ mulch yɛ tso lɛ shishi koni niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Why would cocoa trees that started producing pods suddenly die off until none are left?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni eje shishi amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ gboiɔ trukaa ni nɔ ko nɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden total loss of cocoa trees is usually caused by destructive diseases like Swollen Shoot virus, heavy capsid insect attacks, extreme dry seasons without shade, or severely depleted soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni fiteɔ nii tamɔ bud swollen virus kɛ kooloi babaoo ni yeɔ capsid lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cacao tsei ni fiteɔ trukaa lɛ baa. Be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli loo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa kwraa

english: What are the early signs that my cocoa trees are getting sick before I lose the whole farm?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ baaje midɛŋ?

english: Early warning signs include yellowing or drooping leaves, swollen branches, black patches on pods, or sudden leaf loss. Identifying these early allows you to spray or remove infected trees before sickness spreads.
ga: Nɔ ni fata kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii ni tsɔɔ mra lɛ ahe ji baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ni miigbee shi, tsei niji ni efuu, ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ, loo baai ni elaaje trukaa. Nibii nɛɛ ni oooyɔse mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsofa shwieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ loo ojieɔ amɛ dani hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.
