english: If all the cocoa trees on my farm have died, can I plant new cocoa directly on the same land right away?
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboi Ani manyɛ madu kookoo hee yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: It is best not to plant immediately. You should first remove all dead roots to clear hidden diseases, let the soil rest or grow cover crops like plantains, and treat the land before planting new cocoa seedlings.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ ojie shishifãi ni egboi lɛ fɛɛ koni ojie helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe loo odu ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ plantains, ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ dani odu kookoo dumɔwui heei.

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically start bearing pods in 2 to 3 years under good management, while older traditional varieties usually take 4 to 5 years to begin yielding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli yɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa shishi. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, kusum mli kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: How many years can a healthy cocoa tree continue to produce pods once it starts yielding?
ga: Afii enyiɛ cacao tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo ŋmeii kɛji ebɔi yibii womɔ pɛ?

english: With good maintenance like regular pruning, weed control, pest spraying, and proper shade management, a cocoa tree can produce good yields for 25 to 30 years or more.
ga: Kɛtsɔ saamɔ kpakpa tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ daa lɛ nɔ. jwɛi nɔkwɛmɔ Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be ni sa Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai afii 25 kɛyashi 30 loo nɔ ni fe nakai.

english: Do my cocoa trees need shade trees planted around them, or do they grow better in full sun?
ga: Mi koko tso lɛ he miihia tsei ni haa hulutsoo baabɔle ehe. Aloo ebaada jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ enine shɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo nɔ?

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to protect their tender leaves from burning. While mature cocoa produces well in sunshine, keep some permanent shade trees to protect the soil from drying out during long dry seasons.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ la he. Eyɛ mli akɛ kookoo ni eda lɛ woɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la mli moŋ, shi esa akɛ akwɛ tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo daa lɛ anɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akagbi yɛ hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: How does a long dry season affect my cocoa trees, and how can I protect them from heat?
ga: Te hulutsoo be kakadaŋŋ lɛ saa mi-kookoo tsei lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he?

english: Extended dry weather makes trees shed leaves and drop young pods to survive. You can protect them by leaving dried leaves on the soil around the tree bases to keep the ground cool and moist.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii koni amɛhi shi. Obaanyɛ obu amɛhe kɛtsɔ baai ni egbi ni oooshi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: What routine work must I do every month to keep my cocoa farm healthy and yielding well?
ga: Mɛɛ nifeemɔ esa akɛ mafee daa nyɔŋ nɔ koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ aya nɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii?

english: Essential monthly care includes clearing weeds, cutting off dead or diseased branches (pruning), removing unwanted shoots (suckers), and inspecting trees for pest insects or pod diseases.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nyɔji amli kwɛmɔ ni he hiaa lɛ he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ. Niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ (Pruning) Ajieɔ tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni ataooo (shoots) kɛ tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛji amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo pod helai.

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over food in the soil and their leaves block sunlight from one another. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough nutrients, water, and light to produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛ amɛhe Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa niyenii, nu, kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry periods to conserve water. By dropping leaves, the plant reduces moisture loss through transpiration and protects its underground tubers until the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli baa lɛ baa shi. ni ebu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Maize takes a lot of nitrogen out of the soil, but legumes like cowpeas can take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground. Rotating them naturally restores soil fertility for your next planting.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Adebɔɔ mli tsakemɔ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha odumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to produce smaller harvests even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal fertilizer, water, and sunlight directly from your crops. If weeds surround your plants, your crops will starve and produce small, weak harvests.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi ebɔle otso lɛ he Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures or inconsistent watering. If the soil completely dries out and then gets flooded, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ no lɛ nu afua baaho. Tsei baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Excess moisture and low sunlight during heavy rains create damp conditions where fungi thrive and spread black pod disease. Pruning extra shade tree branches lets sunlight and air dry out the moisture, preventing pod rot.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine kɛ hulu la fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli lɛ haa fɛ̃i shihilɛ baa. he ni ŋmei lɛ daa ni egbɛɔ black pod hela lɛ eshwaa lɛ Niji ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni mli edɔ baa. Etsiɔ pods lɛ anaa koni ekafite

english: Why do I need to cut away the small sucker shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Multiple sucker shoots compete with the main plantain stem for nutrients. Removing excess shoots leaves only one strong follower, allowing the main plant to put all its energy into growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei bibii babaoo kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai. Nibii ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ haa sɛɛnyiɛlɔ kome pɛ ni he wa shwɛɔ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites sucking sap from the undersides of leaves, or by viruses carried by these pests. Managing these insects early stops the leaves from crumpling and stunting the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni ji nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akwɛmɔ nɔ mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbo ni amɛkafee tso lɛ shwiemɔ.

english: Why is it beneficial to cover the ground around my vegetables with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle aduawai ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It keeps the root zone cool and damp while also blocking weeds from sprouting.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, yɛ be mli ni ehaaa jwɛi hu akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when I leave them out in the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Heat accelerates water loss and causes harvested crops to rot quickly. Keeping freshly harvested vegetables in a cool, shaded place slows down breakdown and maintains their market quality much longer.
ga: Dɔlɛ haa nu fiteɔ oya ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa lɛ oya. Aduawai ni akpa ehee lɛ ni akɛtoɔ Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha fitemɔ aba shi ni ebaaha jarayeli mli nibii ahi shi be babaoo.

english: Why do my freshly harvested cocoa beans need to get warm under banana leaves before I dry them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atswa kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ awo banana baai ashishi dani amɛgbi lɛ?

english: The heat generated under the leaves triggers fermentation, which breaks down the bitter pulp and allows the cocoa beans to develop their rich chocolate color and flavor.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ akumɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛnáa tsokolate lɛ su ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my growing maize crop turning yellow instead of remaining dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency or waterlogged soil. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores the green color and helps the plant produce strong ears of maize.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu eyi mli obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my harvested cassava roots turn dark blue and spoil within two days if I do not cook or process them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ feɔ bluu ni mli edɔ ni efiteɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ mli kɛji mihooo loo mitsuuu he nii lɛ?

english: Cassava roots undergo rapid natural decay once dug up from the ground. Processing them into gari or flour within 24 to 48 hours stops this damage and preserves the food.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji atsa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afee lɛ gari loo ashikishaŋ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 24 kɛyashi 48 mli lɛ, ehaa nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ kpaa, ni ehaa niyenii lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I buy certified stem cuttings from the extension office instead of taking stems from any random farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe ŋmeii ni Extension Office lɛ etsɔɔ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohe ŋmɔshi nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli.

english: Planting material from an unverified source can carry hidden diseases like the cassava mosaic virus. Certified stems come from clean, strong parent stock that guarantees higher yields.
ga: Tse mli nibii ni jɛ hei ni akwɛɛɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ tamɔ cassava mosaic virus. Tsofai ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi akwɛlɔi ni he tse, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli, ni no haa yibiiwoo babaoo baa.

english: Why do my pepper seeds fail to sprout when the soil temperature gets too hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ latsaa lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Pepper seeds require cool moisture and mild warmth to germinate. Excessive soil heat burns and dries out the fragile seed embryos before they can sprout.
ga: Pepper dumɔwui lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ latsaa fioo koni amɛkwɛ̃. Dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ baashã ni eha dumɔwui bibii ni waaa lɛ agbi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my stored maize bags feel warm inside and end up infested with insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kotoku ni mikɛ ŋmãa eto lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ hela emɔ emli lɛ?

english: Grain stored with too much moisture traps heat and creates a perfect home for insects and mold. Sun-drying your maize until it is completely dry before bagging prevents heat buildup and pests.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ dumɔwui amli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ ni ehaa shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi egbi kwraa dani awo lɛ kotoku mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa dɔlɛ ni baa kɛ kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akabote mli.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up on the trunk during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ Mɛni hewɔ minɔ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease caused by excess moisture and shade. Pruning overhead tree branches allows sunlight in to warm and dry the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo. Tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la boteɔ mli ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaa egbiɔ. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my plantains before they turn soft and yellow on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa plantains dani tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse?

english: Harvest plantains while they are still green, as soon as the sharp edges on the fruit become plump and rounded. Waiting until they yellow on the plant makes them soft and hard to transport without damage.
ga: Kpaa plantains be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛ kɛkɛ, Tsei lɛ ni ooomɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baaha amɛfee blɛoo ni ewa akɛ abaaŋɔ amɛ kɛya he kroko ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee amɛ.

english: Does the size and quality of the seed yam tuber I plant really affect the size of the yam I harvest later?
ga: Ani bɔ ni ŋmeii ni miduɔ lɛ daraa kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha lɛ saa ŋmeii ni mikpaa yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Yes, the seed tuber provides the initial food supply and genetic potential for the vine. Using a healthy, thick seed tuber from a high-yielding origin ensures a large, healthy yam harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei ji shishijee niyenii kɛ fɔmɔ nii ni yɔɔ wain tso lɛ mli lɛ. Dumɔwui ayitsei ni mli wa ni jɛ hei ni yibiiwoo babaoo yɔɔ lɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni anáa sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and dig into the dirt after they bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut pods grow underground rather than on top of the stem. After the flowers are pollinated, the stems naturally extend downwards into the soil so the nuts can safely form and mature beneath the ground.
ga: Peanut pods lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi moŋ fe ni eeekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ. Beni afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over so easily when the fruit bundle grows big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni eyɛ aduawai akui wuji lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not hold deep in the ground. Supporting the trunk with a sturdy Y-shaped wooden pole helps carry the heavy weight of the fruit bunch until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Akɛ tsei ni wa ni tamɔ Y fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛfi tso yibii akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ kɛyashi be mli ni abaakpa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants leave the soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ shĩɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii babaoo kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas belong to the legume family, which can capture nitrogen directly from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant decomposes, this natural fertilizer stays in the soil for future crops.
ga: Cowpeas yɛ legume weku lɛ mli, ni baanyɛ amɔmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛto amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni tsei fiteɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and build leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer will supply what the plant needs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛwo baai. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baafee nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ ahiamɔ nii aba mli.

english: Why is it important for me to heap soil into mounds before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ naa mawo gɔŋ mli dani madu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand underground. Mounding gathers rich topsoil together and makes it easy for the yam tuber to grow long and thick without pushing against hard dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ he miihia sweet potato koni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔji buaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ anaa. ni ehaa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ oya ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ waa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, dark, and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets in sunlight and airflow, which helps keep the cocoa pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, duŋ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ agbi ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes curling up and getting yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whitefly insects. Using disease-free stem cuttings for planting prevents this problem from starting.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Niji ni hela bɛ mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ́ adu lɛ baatsi naagba nɛɛ naa koni ekaje shishi.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms keep falling off instead of turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and covering the base with dried leaves keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ baai ni egbi aha shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing new leaves during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ baai heei kwɛ̃mɔ yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants slow down their growth when water is scarce to conserve energy and avoid drying out completely. Providing regular irrigation or watering helps them stay active and keep producing.
ga: Pepper tsei haa amɛdalɛ baa shi kɛ́ nu faaa koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato ni ekɛtsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa. Kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu loo afɔ amɛ nu daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why does my lowland rice field need to hold shallow standing water while the plants are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahi nu ni mli ekɔɔɔ mli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Shallow water prevents weeds from growing and taking over the field, while ensuring the young rice roots always have the moisture they need to absorb food from the soil.
ga: Nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ haaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ ni amɛkaye ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ koni ŋmãa shishifãi bibii lɛ aná nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Sir, why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong leaves, or your ground is holding too much rain water around the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa. Aloo ani oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nugbɔ nu babaoo ni ebɔle oshishifãi lɛ ahe?

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, allowing tiny damp fungi to attack and break down the cassava tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Shi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ fioo. Amɛbaa koni amɛbatutua ni amɛfite ŋmei shishifãi lɛ.

english: Sir, why does my land produce less food when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo be mli ni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific crop pests make a permanent home in your soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni ooodu lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa kooloi komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ feɔ shiai ni hiɔ shi daa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily even when the wind is not very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa po lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and when microscopic worms called nematodes eat the root tips underground, the plant loses its grip on the soil and falls under the weight of its own fruit.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ ye shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ ni egbeeɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ eyibii lɛ ashishi.

english: What makes the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and stop growing big?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that inject viruses into the plant while feeding, or by the plant trying to protect itself during very hot, dry days.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tso lɛ mli be mli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Sir, why do tiny worms keep eating big holes in my cabbage leaves during the night?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni misumɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ ji buji wuji. Yɛ mi kaabaji baai lɛ anɔ gbɛkɛ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Moths lay tiny eggs underneath the cabbage leaves, and when these eggs hatch into caterpillars at night, they chew through the leaves to feed themselves.
ga: Moths woɔ wɔji bibii. Kaabeji baai lɛ ashishi Ni kɛ́ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ fɔ ni amɛfee ŋmeii gbɛkɛ lɛ Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ koni amɛna amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii.

english: Sir, why do my cocoa trees drop all their fresh flowers before any small pods can grow?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi heei lɛ fɛɛ dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by intense heat, long dry spells, or when sucking insects damage the delicate stems that hold the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. Be ni hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ekome lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their tiny fruits before the peppers get a chance to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho aduawai bibii dani pepper lɛ ená hegbɛ ni edara lɛ?

english: Peppers drop young fruit when the weather changes too suddenly between very hot days and cold nights, or when the plant does not get a steady supply of water.
ga: Peppers shwieɔ amɛyibii lɛ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsake trukaa tsɔ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ kɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ ateŋ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa

english: Sir, why do I need to guide my yam vines onto wooden stakes instead of letting them grow across the soil?
ga: Nuŋtsɔ, mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha eda yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes helps the leaves catch direct sunlight to make food for the tubers underground while keeping the leaves away from wet soil that causes rot.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ shɛɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ he.

english: How can I tell if the first rain of the season is enough for me to start planting my seeds safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: You should wait until the rain wets the soil deep enough that it stays moist for several days, so a sudden hot spell will not dry out and kill your young seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ gbii babaoo. Enɛ ji koni hulutsoo ni naa wa ni baa trukaa lɛ akagbi ni egbe odumɔwui bibii lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to grow green leaves. Adding decomposed animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their healthy green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni efite fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa trees scorch and turn brown in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn under full sunlight because they cannot absorb water fast enough. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from harsh sun rays until they grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada waa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience heat stress or sudden soil dryness. Keeping the soil consistently moist using mulch—like dry grass around the roots—helps the plant hold onto its flowers and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi trukaa lɛ kpe. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni okɛbaatsu nii yɛ jwɛi lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔii amli ni ewo yibii.

english: Why are some of the kernels missing on my maize cobs after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi elaaje yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Missing kernels happen when pollen fails to reach every silk during flowering, often caused by drought or planting maize in long single rows. Planting maize in blocks helps the wind spread pollen evenly.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ siliki lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli. Bei pii lɛ, hɔmɔ loo ŋmãa kakadaŋŋ adumɔ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Abele ni aduɔ yɛ blɔkii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ni ejaraa pollen lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why is my plantain tree taking so long to produce a bunch compared to my neighbor's?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmeii kɛ akɛtoɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow slowly when too many young suckers grow around the main trunk, stealing food and water. Cutting off excess suckers leaves more energy for the main plant to produce fruit faster.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ daraa blɛoo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii babaoo miida yɛ amɛhe. main trunk koni eju niyenii kɛ nu Kpojiemɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso titri lɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ yibii oya.

english: Why are my tomato leaves curling upward and stopping the plant from growing big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekadara lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies that transmit a virus to the plant. Spraying the leaves with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap deters these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai kɛyaa tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahe.

english: Yam tubers rot when rain accumulates in flat soil without proper drainage, allowing harmful fungi to multiply. Planting yams on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the tubers.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thin stems and tiny tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni eshishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ eyitsei bibii lɛ?

english: Cassava grows thin stems and small tubers when planted too close together, forcing the plants to fight for sunlight. Giving each cassava stem about one meter of space allows the leaves to catch light and food to travel down into big tubers.
ga: Cassava baaná tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei awuu koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa baai lɛ naa la kɛ niyenii ni baa shi kɛyaa ŋmei agbo lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and loose instead of forming hard, solid balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo lolo ni eyɛ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages remain loose if they suffer from irregular watering or lack phosphorus during the head-forming stage. Consistent watering and adding wood ash or phosphorus fertilizer helps them form tight, firm heads.
ga: Kaabage baanyɛ ahi shi ni efee mlɛo kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee nɔ loo ebɛ fɔsfɔs yɛ be mli ni eyitso lɛ feɔ lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tso sũ loo fɔsfɔs ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛfeɔ bulbs ni mli wa ni ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil get dry and hard just two days after heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter, which works like a sponge to trap rainwater underground. Adding compost or dry crop leftovers into the soil helps it retain moisture much longer after rainfall.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa oya kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji, ni mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi ni eshwɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make food and keep leaves green. Applying manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛha amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts like a free natural fertilizer for crops planted there next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa tsei ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller crop yields every time I plant on the same patch of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni madu nii yɛ he kome ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground as they grow. If you plant the same spot repeatedly without adding manure, organic matter, or letting the soil rest, the nutrients get used up and the plants starve.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji odu he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he loo ohaaa sũ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. Niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baafite ni hɔmɔ baaye tsei.

english: Why do my cassava plants stay green and alive during the dry season when other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli ni ehiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni tsei krokomɛi gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava has very deep root systems that reach water far underground, and it can shed leaves or slow its growth during severe dry weather to save energy and survive.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ waa ni shɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ he. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛshwie amɛbaai lɛ loo amɛha amɛdalɛ aba shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden poles next to my yam plants after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko fɔ̃ɔ sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that needs to reach sunlight. Training the vines up wooden poles helps the leaves catch maximum sunlight to make food, which makes the tubers underground grow bigger.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la. Wein tsei lɛ ni atsɔseɔ amɛ yɛ tsei ahe lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ kɛha nihoomɔ. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees burst into heavy flowering right after the rain begins following a dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi enɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees use a short dry spell to rest, and the sudden arrival of rain signals to the tree that conditions are safe to bloom and grow fruits.
ga: Cocoa tsei kɛ be kuku ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛjɔɔ amɛhe, ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa lɛ haa tsei lɛ leɔ akɛ shihilɛi lɛ yɛ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛdara shweshweeshwe.

english: Too many young shoots compete with the mother plantain tree for water and soil nutrients, which reduces yield. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsobii bibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ fɔlɔ dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha nibii ni afee lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the weather gets too hot, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no beneficial insects around to shake the flowers and help them produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ mli ejɔɔɔ loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he lɛ, Hosomɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ni oye obua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses, which stops the leaves from opening fully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbele kwraa.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars hiding and eating inside the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ miitee amɛhe ni amɛmiiye nii yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, pests that hide in the growing center of the plant where leaves are softest. Early treatment with recommended control methods protects the plant from major damage.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni teɔ shi yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ teŋgbɛ he ni baai ni mli tse fe fɛɛ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Mra be mli tsamɔ Kɛtsɔ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baabu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa he.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is missing nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to stay green and grow leaves. It can also happen when heavy rain washes away nutrients or leaves soil too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ amɛ eŋɔli kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they feel stressed, especially from sudden heat spikes, too little water, or too much water. The plant drops flowers to save its own strength when conditions aren't right.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛnu he akɛ amɛmiifee basaa. Titri lɛ kɛjɛ latsaa ni yaa hiɛ trukaa lɛ mli. nu fioo tsɔ loo nu babaoo yɛ Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhewalɛ he kɛji shihilɛi lɛ bafee nɔ ni ehiii.

english: How do caterpillars like Fall Armyworm find my maize crop so fast?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ na mi ŋmãa lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Parent moths fly long distances at night and use smell to locate soft, young green maize leaves. They lay hundreds of eggs on the leaves, which quickly hatch into hungry caterpillars.
ga: Nyɛ lɛ foɔ kɛyaa he ko shɔŋŋ gbɛkɛ ni ekɛ eŋɔli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtaoɔ abele bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ohai abɔ yɛ baai anɔ. ni shwere oya ni etsɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: Why does black pod disease spread so fast on my cocoa tree during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ black pod hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is caused by a small fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather. Splashing rain drops and dirty farm tools easily carry the fungus from infected pods or soil onto healthy pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pods diji baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela bibioo ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ, ni efɔ lɛ. Nugbɔshiimɔi ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni he tseee lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii loo shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli oya.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller when I plant it on the same land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ adu yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots suck specific nutrients out of the soil to grow big tubers. Planting cassava repeatedly without resting the soil or adding manure drains those nutrients, leaving less food for the next crop.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni eha ŋmei agbo lɛ akwɛ̃. Kasava ni aduɔ shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ aŋmɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ atsɔ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, niyenii ni baashwɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ beni nugbɔ ebɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit naturally in the soil and are adapted to wake up and absorb water instantly. Their roots grow faster than crop roots, allowing them to steal food, water, and sunlight early.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛte shi ni amɛŋɔ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ashishifãi. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la oya.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die if I plant them in an open field with no shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli tse ni hulutsoo be bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have soft leaves and shallow roots that dry out and burn under full heat. Taller shade plants act like an umbrella, keeping the air cool and the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ́ akɛwo la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ ni amɛshãa. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I cut off extra branches growing from the base of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo niji ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Extra branches steal plant food and water away from the main stem. Removing them forces the plant to send its energy directly into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of more leaves.
ga: Niji ni fa lɛ juɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he. Tomato ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni etsɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tomato ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ baai babaoo baafata he.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to produce one strong, high-yielding harvest. Seeds collected from that harvest lose their special traits, producing weaker plants with smaller yields next season.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ futuɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛná tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot quickly when stored in a warm room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that breathe and release moisture. Warm, closed spaces trap humidity and heat, creating the perfect environment for fungi and bacteria to enter small scratches and rot the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni muɔ ni amɛjieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kpo. He ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ. Ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ baanyɛ abote ŋmeii bibii amli. ni eha yitso lɛ agbo

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight during their early stage. They need fast-growing shade plants like plantains planted next to them to act as living umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and protecting the cocoa leaves from burning.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛshishijee fãi lɛ amli. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛha wala, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu kookoo baai ahe koni amɛkashã.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tips usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong, so adding manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer will help restore its health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does putting animal manure in my soil help my crops grow better during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmei ni mikɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Animal manure and compost act like sponges in the soil. They help the ground hold onto rainwater longer, while slowly feeding nutrients to the plant roots so crops do not dry out quickly during hot weather.
ga: Manɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. kɛfata he fiofio Ha niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛduɔ shishifãi Enɛ ji koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: No, planting cassava stems too close together causes them to compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. The plants will grow tall and leafy, but the tubers underground will remain very small and thin.
ga: Dabi, ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛyeɔ akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee baai. Shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibii ni amɛhe afee bibioo waa.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal nutrients and water from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them and leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main tree to concentrate its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tsoi loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo ni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ yeɔ ehe koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama tso agbo ko ni tsii ni ekwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground with stakes allows them to catch maximum sunlight, which the plant uses to make food and swell its underground tubers. It also keeps leaves away from wet soil pests and diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tso wo sweet potato baai anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ Ebuɔ baai lɛ hu ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curl on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the juices of young leaves. Spraying early with recommended treatments stops these pests from stunting the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Mra mli shwiemɔ Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ nɔ lɛ, abaatsi nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkatsi tso lɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of balanced nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing proper nutrition helps the flowers set healthy fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i daa ni akɛ niyenii ni sa haa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same land drains the same specific nutrients from the soil year after year and causes maize-specific pests to build up. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans helps restore soil health.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ ekoŋŋ

english: How can I tell the exact right time to harvest my maize so it doesn't spoil in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa koni ekafite yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn completely dry and brown, and the grains feel hard to the touch. Harvesting too early leaves high moisture that causes mold, while waiting too long exposes the ears to insects in the field.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi kwraa. ni ewa akɛ abaata dumɔwui lɛ ahe Nikpamɔ mra tsɔ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa ni no haa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha otoi lɛ amɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are growing as strongly as they should be?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa?

english: Healthy maize plants should have broad, deep green leaves and thick, sturdy stalks. If the leaves turn pale yellow or the stems look thin and floppy, your crop is likely missing key nutrients like nitrogen or is not getting enough water.
ga: Esa akɛ abɛi tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ aná baai ni mli kwɔlɔ, eŋɔli ni tsuɔ kɛ tsei ni mli tse, ni wa. Kɛji baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbee shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli loo amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: How do I check my field for insect pests before they destroy my harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli dani amɛfite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Walk through your field at least twice a week and inspect under the leaves and inside young shoots. Looking for small holes, leaf curling, sticky spots, or tiny eggs allows you to catch pests early before they spread to the whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, nyiɛmɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Ni okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli. taoɔ bu bibii Baai ni ebɔle ehe, he ni etse, loo ŋmeii bibii baanyɛ aye abua bo ni omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra. dani egbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and wither under bright sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate intense direct sunlight because their roots and leaves are delicate. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them creates a canopy that protects them from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ waaa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains lɛ, abɔle amɛhe lɛ, ehaa amɛfeɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How can I check if the soil on my farm has enough moisture for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Dig down about a hand's length into the dirt and squeeze a handful of soil. If it holds together in a soft ball, there is good moisture, but if it crumbles into dry powder, your crops need watering or rain soon.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ aaafee ŋmei tso kome kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ ni okɛ shikpɔŋ ni fa fioo ko ajie mli. Kɛ́ amɛfee ekome ni amɛfee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, amɛbaaná ŋmɔtɔ kpakpa. Shi kɛji akɛ akumɔ mli afee powda ni egbi lɛ, etsɛŋ ni Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he baahia ni awo amɛ nu loo nugbɔ.

english: When crops are planted too tightly together, their roots fight over soil nutrients and their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing them properly ensures every plant gets enough light, air, and food to yield big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni baai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava leaves turn yellow when the soil is drained of nutrients or during dry spells as the plant tries to save water. Adding compost or poultry manure to the soil helps restore nitrogen and keeps the plant leafy and strong.
ga: Cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo yɛ hɔmɔ be mli beni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo baai ni amɛhi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why is it necessary to clear weeds from around my crops when they are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and aggressively steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from them. Clearing weeds early ensures all the goodness in your soil goes directly into feeding your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ koni kpakpai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ aya tɛ̃ɛ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: What causes the cocoa pods on my tree to turn black and rot?
ga: Mɛni miiha kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbo?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in wet, dark conditions. You can prevent it by pruning extra branches to let sunlight reach the tree trunk and removing any infected pods immediately so the fungus does not spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ, ni mli ewo duŋ mli. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni ooofo koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ. Ni jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ koni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Maize is ready to harvest for dry grain when the outer leaves turn completely brown and papery, the stalks dry out, and the kernels inside are hard enough that you cannot dent them with your thumbnail.
ga: Abɛi efee klalo akɛ abaakpa akɛ ŋmeii ni egbi beni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmeii kwraa ni efee tamɔ woji, ŋmeii lɛ egbi, ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni onyɛŋ okɛ oshishifa lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why should I add animal manure or compost to my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔji amli dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Manure feeds the helpful small organisms in the dirt and improves the soil's ability to hold onto water during hot days, giving your seeds a rich environment to germinate and grow rapidly.
ga: Manure yeɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ niyenii. No he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct, intense sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains around them creates a canopy that protects tender cocoa leaves from sun scorch and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai ni mli tse lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to produce energy. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into full sunlight, which helps the plant manufacture the food required to grow large tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ aya ŋwɛi kɛyashi amɛbaaná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni enáa niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing maize plant turning yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually indicate that the soil is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient maize needs to stay green and healthy. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps restore leaf color and grain yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ ahe su kɛ dumɔwui lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm make the ground better for next season's maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their root nodules. When these plants die and decay, they release that nitrogen into the soil, feeding the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛgbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tsei nɛɛ gboi ni amɛgboi lɛ Amɛjieɔ nakai nitrogen lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do the leaves on my tomato plants curl up tightly and turn small and yellowish?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe waa ni amɛji bibii ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is commonly caused by a plant virus spread by tiny whitefly insects. Controlling the whiteflies early prevents them from transmitting the virus between plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso mli hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Whitefly Nɔkwɛmɔ Mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amɛshwã tsei ateŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the central leaf funnels of my maize plants with dark droppings inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ yɛ bu ni etse yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ emli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of the plant to feed on young leaves. Identifying it early allows for targeted treatment before the caterpillar destroys the growing tip.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. mra be mli ni ayɔseɔ Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii jogbaŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Cassava roots require aerated soil to breathe. When soil stays flooded or waterlogged for long periods, roots suffocate and become vulnerable to rotting fungi in the wet soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: Heavy rainfall washes granular fertilizer away off the soil surface or leaches it deep into the ground past the root zone, wasting your fertilizer before the crop can absorb it.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ dani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Crowding plants causes them to compete aggressively for soil nutrients, water, and sunlight, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or empty ears of corn.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli lɛ, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ bibii kɛ ŋmeii bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off instead of turning into actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop prematurely when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, insufficient water, or a lack of essential nutrients like potassium needed for fruit development.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ potassium ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ mli.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly during heavy rain. You can prevent it by plucking off infected pods early, clearing weeds, and pruning extra tree branches so sunlight and air can dry out the farm.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ooojie mra, jwɛi ni oookpa, kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni oookpa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa tree flowers drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop when the trees do not get enough water, when there is too much hot sun, or when tiny pests like mirids (capsids) damage them. Providing shade trees and spraying recommended insecticides at the right time helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ. Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ Aloo, kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ mirids (capsids) fite tsei lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ amɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nutrients, especially nitrogen, or that the field is waterlogged. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or Urea, or adding well-rotted animal manure, will turn the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. titri lɛ nitrogen loo hei ni nu damɔ shi Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ.

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize when the rain season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bashɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives steady, deep rainfall for two or three consecutive days so the ground stays moist. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to germinate and then dry up if the rain pauses.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa be kukuoo ko.

english: Why are my cassava roots very thin and hard instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo waa ni amɛhe wa yɛ agboi ni yɔɔ blɛoo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots remain thin if the soil is too hard and compact, or if you plant them in poor soil without nutrients. Loosening the soil into mounds or ridges before planting gives the tubers room to expand and grow thick.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ baakã he ahi shi bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Aloo kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ ni niyenii kpakpai bɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii dani adu lɛ, ebaaha tuber he lɛ mli alɛɛ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my yam tubers split open inside the mound before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ mli gbalaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii dani mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers crack when there is a sudden heavy rain after a long dry period. The quick water intake makes the inside of the yam expand faster than the skin. Keeping soil covered with organic mulch helps maintain steady moisture.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa trukaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Nu ni anuɔ oya lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe hewolo lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ organic mulch baakwɛ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi daa.

english: Why do the bottom parts of my tomato fruits turn black and rotten before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is called Blossom End Rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium or when the soil goes from very dry to very wet repeatedly. Regular, even watering and adding lime or organic matter to the soil stops it.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ Blosom Naagbee Rot. Ebaa kɛ́ tsei lɛ bɛ calcium loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ shii abɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli ni akɛ lime loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ akpa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies that suck plant juices and spread viruses. Spraying neem oil solution or recommended extension-approved pesticides early keeps these pests away.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ. Neem fɔ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ taakɛ atsɔɔ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Is it better for me to burn the bush after clearing my farm land or leave the weeds to rot?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi lɛ beni mijie nibii ni adu lɛ sɛɛ loo maha jwɛi lɛ agbo?

english: It is better to let the cleared weeds rot into the soil. Burning kills good soil organisms and burns away plant food, while letting weeds rot turns them into free compost that keeps the soil moist and fertile.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha jwɛi ni ajie lɛ lɛ agbo kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ni ehaa tsei aniyenii tsakeɔ. Yɛ be mli ni jwɛi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ haa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii baa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops dry up quickly even when rain fell just two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Your soil may be low in organic matter or too sandy, which prevents it from holding water. Adding compost, leaves, or animal manure increases the soil's ability to act like a sponge and trap moisture for your crops.
ga: Ekolɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa loo ŋã yɔɔ mli tsɔ. Enɛ baaha anyɛɛɛ akɛ nu ato. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, baai, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛhaa onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their leaves when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kooko tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai babaoo kɛji harmattan fɛ̃i be lɛ je shishi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during the Harmattan dry season as a self-defense mechanism to conserve water. Reducing leaf surface area prevents the tree from losing vital moisture through evaporation, helping it survive until the rainy season returns.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ mli nu ni he hiaa lɛ afite kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: The first rain of the year is often followed by a long dry spell. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout but quickly dry up and die before the main rainy season fully settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ afi lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaagbi oya ni amɛbaagboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aba.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build green leaves. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller yields every year when I keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients out of the soil every year. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen to the soil and restores its fertility.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni ji ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eha ŋmãa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: How does spreading animal manure on my farm help my crops grow better than using plain soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛshwãa miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Animal manure feeds the soil with natural nutrients that release slowly over time. It also improves soil structure, helping the earth hold more moisture during dry periods so crop roots stay hydrated.
ga: Koolooi amli ŋmeii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ fiofio lɛ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hu feɔ fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Koni tso shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why does rainwater sit on top of my field for days after a heavy downpour instead of sinking into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ moŋ fe ni eeebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Water stays on top when the soil is heavily compacted or contains high clay content without enough air spaces. Adding organic matter like compost breaks up hard soil so water can sink in and reach plant roots.
ga: Nu taa nɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli bɔni afee ni nu anyɛ abote mli kɛyaduɔ shishifãi.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge leafy stems above ground but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing tall stems and leafy leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers. Plant spacing that is too tight can also cause this.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ, tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni mli wa hu baanyɛ aha enɛ aba.

english: This is often cherelle wilt, which happens when the tree cannot support all the young pods it produces and naturally sheds the extra ones, or when high humidity allows black pod fungal disease to infect young pods during heavy rains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji Cherel tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ŋmeii bibii ni ewoɔ lɛ fɛɛ anɔ. ni ejieɔ wala yibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Aloo kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ haa black pod fungus lɛ yeɔ pod bibii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers struggle to grow when I plant them in direct sunlight without shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni hulutsoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers lose water very fast under hot, direct sunlight before their roots are fully developed. Providing temporary shade and mulching around the base keeps the soil moist and cool for healthy root growth.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi dani shishifãi lɛ daraa kwraa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if damaged spots on my pepper leaves are caused by insects or by a crop disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ahe helai ji nɔ ni kɛ hei ni efite yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ lɛ ba?

english: Insects typically leave visible bite holes, chewed edges, or visible pests on the leaves. Crop diseases usually show up as discolored spots, powdery patches, or sudden wilting without direct chewed holes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi shĩɔ ŋmeii ni anaa, ŋmeii ni amɛyeɔ, loo ŋmeii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai jieɔ amɛhe kpo akɛ ŋmeii ni amɛhe su etsake. Eji he ko ni tamɔ powda. aloo egboɔ trukaa ni ŋmeii ni akɛyeɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ bɛ mli

english: Cocoa thrives in deep, rich, well-drained soil that holds moisture without getting waterlogged, in areas that receive good rainfall and have warm temperatures year-round.
ga: Cocoa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni nu ehiɛɛɛ mli Yɛ he ko ni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔɔ yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Can I plant cashew trees on the same plot of land where I grow cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cashew tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni aduɔ kookoo yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is usually best to keep them separate because cashew trees prefer sunny, drier conditions, whereas cocoa trees need shade and high moisture to thrive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oootsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ cashew tsei sumɔɔ hulu la ni mli egbi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo babaoo he miihia kookoo tsei koni amɛdara.

english: How many years does a new cocoa tree take before it starts bearing fruit?
ga: Afii enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso hee ko jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Traditional cocoa trees usually take between 3 to 5 years to bear fruit, but improved hybrid varieties can start producing pods in about 2 to 3 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii, shi tsei ni afee amɛ srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaje shishi amɛwo yibii yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli.

english: Why would my mature cocoa trees suddenly dry up and die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso ni eda lɛ gĩ trukaa ni egbo lɛ?

english: Sudden dying of cocoa trees can be caused by severe drought stress, root damage from pests, or diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, which prevents the tree from taking up nutrients and water.
ga: Hɔmɔ ni naa wa ni baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei agboi trukaa lɛ baanyɛ aba. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo helai tamɔ cocoa bud virus lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aŋɔ niyenii kɛ nu.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads rapidly during heavy rains when the farm has too much shade and poor air flow.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni ŋmɔji amli hulutsoo be babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cashew trees turning white and curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miifee futafuta ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is typically powdery mildew, a common fungal disease that attacks young cashew leaves and flowers during humid weather conditions.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji powder mildew. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni tutuaa cashew baai bibii kɛ fɔfɔi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need plantains or big trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu plantains loo tsei wuji yɛ kookoo tso bibioo ko masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight, so fast-growing plants like plantains act as living umbrellas to provide shade and hold soil moisture while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo tsei koni amɛha hulutsoo ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my cashew trees drop their flowers before any fruit forms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Cashews drop their flowers mainly due to insect attacks on the blooms or extreme heat and lack of water during the flowering stage.
ga: Cashew ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kooloi ni tutuaa fɔfɔi lɛ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose a lot of leaves right at the start of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai babaoo miifite yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a cocoa tree's natural response to protect itself; shedding foliage reduces the amount of water the tree loses through its leaves during dry periods.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji bɔ ni cacao tso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa kɛbuɔ ehe he. Baai ni gbeeɔ shi lɛ haa nu ni tso lɛ laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ ebaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What makes my cocoa pods stay small and empty instead of developing seeds?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee dumɔwui?

english: Small or flat pods usually happen when the flowers are not fully pollinated by tiny insects or when the tree lacks necessary soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii eshɛɛɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: I have just cleared my piece of land; how do I go about converting it into a new cocoa farm?
ga: Mijie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsake lɛ mafee kookoo ŋmɔ hee?

english: To convert cleared land to cocoa, start by planting shade crops like plantains first. Once shade is established, you can transplant young cocoa seedlings into the field during the onset of the rainy season so their roots can settle.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni otsɔ he ni agbele lɛ nɔ otsɔ kookoo Je shishi kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains lɛ adumɔ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Kɛji akɛ amɛhe ejɔ amɛ lɛ, Obaanyɛ okɛ kookoo dumɔwui bibii awo saatso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli koni amɛshishifãi lɛ ama shi.

english: Can I replace my old food crop fields directly with young forest trees and cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsake mi niyenii ŋmɔji momo lɛ tɛ̃ɛ mafee dumɔwui kɛ kookoo?

english: Yes, you can transition food crop land into cocoa and tree plantations. It is best to clear out old plant residue, improve soil fertility with organic manure, and plant temporary shade trees before introducing the cocoa and timber seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ otsɔ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ otsɔ kookoo kɛ tsei aŋmɔji. Gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ji ni ajie tsei momo ni efite lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. ni amɛdu tsei koni amɛha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko dani amɛdu kookoo kɛ tsei ahe dumɔwui.

english: How long does it take for cocoa seeds to sprout after I plant them in the nursery?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cocoa ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmeii akwɛmɔhe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Cocoa seeds usually begin to sprout within 7 to 14 days after planting in fertile, moist soil. You will see small green shoots emerging above the soil surface shortly before the first leaves unfold.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ŋmeii jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 mli beni adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fioo dani klɛŋklɛŋ baai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: My young cocoa plants seem to be growing very slowly in their first year; is this normal?
ga: Etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ daaa blɛoo waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli. Ani enɛ ji nɔ ni ja?

english: Yes, this is completely normal. In their first year, cocoa plants focus most of their energy on developing deep root systems under the ground to reach water and nutrients before growing rapidly above ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kwraa. Yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ, cacao tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ koni ená nu kɛ niyenii. dani eda oya kɛho shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why do farmers in the northern region of Ghana use different farming methods compared to us in the south?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ kɛ okwaayeli gbɛi srɔtoi tsuɔ nii fe wɔ ni yɔɔ kooyigbɛ lɛ?
