english: The northern region has a shorter rainy season and drier climate, so farmers there use specialized moisture-conserving methods like mulching, water harvesting, and drought-tolerant crop varieties adapted to their weather.
ga: Kooyigbɛ kpokpaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi. No hewɔ lɛ okwaafoi kɛ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔtɔ he tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛ nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii. kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ amɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli.

english: How does changing the method of land preparation affect how well my crops will sprout?
ga: Te gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakemɔ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃mɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Proper land preparation improves soil aeration and water retention. Using methods that keep soil moist and protected helps seeds sprout faster and prevents young root systems from drying out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni asaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛi ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya, ni ebaatsi shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi.

english: What are the benefits of establishing a tree plantation on my farm instead of planting only seasonal crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ he?

english: Tree plantations provide long-term financial security through timber or tree crops, improve soil fertility, protect against wind erosion, and require less daily labor once the trees mature.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ shika he shweshweeshwefeemɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baa kɛtsɔ tsei loo tsei anɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ Etsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Ni daa gbi nitsumɔ fioo pɛ he hiaa be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Which types of shade trees are best to plant alongside my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ hulutsoo tsei hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ mi-kookoo tso lɛ masɛi?

english: Indigenous forest trees like Terminalia ivorensis (Emire) and Milicia excelsa (Odum) are ideal because they form a high canopy, provide good shade, enrich the soil with leaf litter, and do not compete heavily for nutrients.
ga: Koo mli tsei tamɔ Terminalia ivorensis (Emire) kɛ Milicia excelsa (Odum) lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛ ŋwɛi tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ ahewɔ. Ehaa hulutsoo kpakpa Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa baai babaoo. Ni amɛyeee akaŋ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo he.

english: How does planting tree crops help restore land that has lost its fertility from years of farming?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni efite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ afii babaoo ni akɛtsu nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ?

english: Tree roots grow deep into the soil to pull up nutrients to the surface. As their leaves fall and decay, they add organic matter back into the soil, rebuilding soil structure and fertility over time.
ga: Tso shishifãi daa kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛgbala niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi ni amɛgboi lɛ Amɛbaaku sɛɛ amɛkɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etswaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to wait several years for tree plantations and cocoa to mature before harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ afii babaoo dani tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni kookoo lɛ akwɛ̃ dani akpa?

english: Tree crops require time to build strong trunks, deep roots, and healthy branches capable of supporting heavy yields. The early years are an investment in the plant's permanent structure for long-term production.
ga: Tso tsei taoɔ be koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli wa, shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ niji ni wa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Shishijee afii lɛ ji shika ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni hiɔ shi daa lɛ mli kɛha nitsumɔ ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves stay wet and start to rot during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When leaves stay water-soaked for too long without enough airflow or sunlight to dry them, fungal diseases like Black Pod thrive. Trimming excess canopy branches helps air flow through the farm and dries out the leaves faster.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akɛ baai wo nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛgbi lɛ bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji baanyɛ adara. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya.

english: Can diseases spread from old, rotten cocoa pods on the ground to my healthy standing trees?
ga: Ani helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ kookoo tsei momo ni egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, fungi and pests live in bad pods left on the farm floor. Rain drops bounce off diseased pods and splash fungal spores onto healthy low-hanging pods and stems, spreading infection across your farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui hiɔ ŋmeii gbohii ni ashi yɛ ŋmɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli. Nugbɔ nɛɔ kɛjɛɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ. ni okɛ fungal spores lɛ afɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ hela lɛ mli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: What causes my crops to get fungal infections after rain falls on them?
ga: Mɛni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ?

english: Fungi spores need trapped moisture to grow. When water sits on leaves and stems without drying quickly, spore seeds germinate and penetrate the plant skin, causing dark spots and decay.
ga: Mold spores lɛ he miihia ŋmɔtɔ ni amɔmɔ amɛ koni amɛdara. Beni nu kpɛtɛɔ baai kɛ tsei lɛ ahe ni ehaaa amɛgbi oya. Dumɔwui amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛ boteɔ tso lɛ hewolo mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Should I keep sick or damaged cocoa pods away from the healthy ones when harvesting?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni hela mɔ amɛ loo efite lɛ akabɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe beni mikpaa nii lɛ?

english: Yes, always keep bad or infested pods separate. Mixing infected pods with healthy ones allows fungus and rot to spread to good beans during storage and fermentation, lowering your total crop quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii ni ehiii loo ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ futu mli lɛ, ebaagbɛ ŋmeii ashwã ni ebaafite ŋmeii kpakpai lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ Enɛ haa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ baa shi.

english: How can I easily tell when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be picked?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Ripe cocoa pods change color distinctly—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting only fully ripe pods ensures the beans inside have proper sugars for good fermentation.
ga: Kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su yɛ faŋŋ mli. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji loo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ pɛ lɛ, ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ náa sugar ni sa koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I mix unripe cocoa pods with ripe ones when breaking pods for fermentation?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni eshɛko lɛ futuɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ mli beni mifoɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Unripe beans lack natural sugars needed for proper fermentation, resulting in slatey, bitter beans. Mixing them reduces the overall flavor and grade of your final dried cocoa bag.
ga: Beans ni ahoo lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli sugar ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kɛji akɛ okɛfutu lɛ, ebaaha osɛɛkpee kookoo kotoku ni egbi lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ kɛ sɛɛnamɔ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: How do buyers measure the weight and grade of my cocoa beans when I take them to the shed?
ga: Te mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ amɛsusu mi-kookoo lɛ mli tsiimɔ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he kɛ́ mikɛba he ni mikɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers weigh your dry beans in standard scale pounds or kilograms and take small samples to check moisture levels, size, and bean quality to determine the final payout.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ susuɔ ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ ahe yɛ pound loo kilogram ni sa mli. No sɛɛ lɛ, ŋɔɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ bibioo ko Koni okwɛ bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ mli nu lɛ fa ha, amɛdalɛ kɛ bɔ ni amɛhi ha. koni akɛtsɔɔ naagbee nyɔmɔwoo

english: How should I store harvested cocoa pods before breaking them open so they do not spoil?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-kokoo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ ato dani mifo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Keep harvested pods off the bare, wet ground in a dry, shady area, and do not pile wet or diseased pods on top of clean ones. Break pods within 2 to 5 days of harvesting to prevent beans from germinating inside.
ga: Too pods ni akpa kɛjɛ he ni nɔ ko bɛ, ni efɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni egbi, ni shade yɔɔ. Ni kaabua ŋmeii ni efɔ loo hela emɔ ŋmeii ni he tse lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ gbii 2 kɛyashi enumɔ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni akpa ŋmeii lɛ koni ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃ yɛ mli.

english: Why is it important for me to regularly inspect every part of my cocoa farm myself?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ miniji akwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã mli daa lɛ?

english: Walking through your farm regularly helps you catch early signs of diseases, pest attacks, or shade issues before they spread, allowing you to treat problems early and protect your cocoa yields.
ga: Kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona helai, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo hulutsoo naagbai ahe okadii mra dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Ehaa onyɛɔ otsuɔ naagbai ahe nii mra. ni obu o-cocoa ni ofeɔ lɛ he

english: Why does removing shade tree branches help my cocoa trees yield more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shade tso niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cocoa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Too much shade keeps moisture trapped around cocoa trees and starves them of light. Pruning shade trees allows balanced sunlight to stimulate flowering while letting wind blow through to dry excess leaf moisture.
ga: Shade babaoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. cocoa tsei lɛ ni ekɛ la ni bɛ baa Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ni afolɔ mli lɛ haa hulu la ni sa lɛ haa fɔfɔii lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mli koni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ agbi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear away all the big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade from larger canopy trees or temporary shade crops like plantains, the intense heat burns their delicate leaves and dries out the topsoil before their root systems can fully develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni tsei wuji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛitsu nɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko tamɔ plantains haa lɛ bɛ lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning light yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. The disease prevents the leaves from capturing sunlight effectively, which reduces the plant's ability to make food and grow large tubers.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ amɔmɔ hulu la lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nyɛmɔ ni tso lɛ yɔɔ ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni ekɛ bulbs wuji baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the edges of my young maize leaves turn purple during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ purple yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on maize are a common sign of phosphorus deficiency in the soil. Phosphorus helps roots grow strong and fuels plant energy; without enough of it, the crop becomes stunted and exhibits reddish-purple stress coloring.
ga: Baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni ehaa tsei lɛ tsofa. Kɛji akɛ eshɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry spells. High daytime temperatures make pollen sterile, preventing fertilization, which causes the plant to shed the flower because it cannot develop into a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa. Gbi mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa pollen lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ kotoku. Etsiɔ fɔmɔ naa Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ etsɔ aduawai.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a much bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting too closely forces crops to compete aggressively with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. This competition results in weak, thin stems and small or unfilled cobs, ultimately lowering your total harvest compared to proper spacing.
ga: Amɛdumɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ tsei bibii loo ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa. Yɛ naagbee lɛ, Okpamɔ fɛɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds rot underground instead of sprouting after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need oxygen in the soil to germinate. Waterlogged soil fills up all the tiny air pockets, effectively suffocating the seeds and giving soil fungi the wet environment they need to decay the seeds before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ naa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛgboi dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds slow down my crop growth even when there is plenty of rain for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds often have faster-growing root systems that steal fertilizers and natural soil nutrients before your crop's roots can reach them. Even with rain, your crops suffer because they are starving for essential soil food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa amanehulu ejaakɛ hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why am I getting huge, bushy leaves on my sweet potatoes but only tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ baai agboi anɔ yɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Applying too much nitrogen fertilizer encourages the sweet potato plant to spend all its energy growing heavy vines and foliage above ground instead of sending starches downward to expand the edible roots below.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ woɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkɛkwɛɔ wain tsei kɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ atsu nii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu starch kɛya shi koni amɛkwɛ shishifãi ni ayeɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves roll up tightly like tubes during the middle of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ paipii yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense mechanism against heat. By exposing less leaf surface to the direct sun, the plantain reduces water loss through evaporation and protects itself from drying out during the hottest hours of the day.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi ji tso adebɔɔ hebuu gbɛ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Plantains haa nu ni laajeɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ, ni ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ he yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli kɛtsɔ baa lɛ nɔ ni ekɛwoɔ hulu la ni shɛɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are completely mature and ready to dig up?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ o-sweet potato tubers lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ atsa?

english: Yams indicate maturity when their green vines and leaves naturally yellow and dry out at the end of the rainy season. This shows that the plant has stopped above-ground growth and transferred all its stored energy down into the tuber.
ga: Atomɔ tsɔɔ akɛ eshɛ beni wain tsei kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee shishi kɛtee ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in very wet soil because water helps control weeds and keeps the soil consistently moist for their shallow root systems, which cannot reach deep underground for hidden water.
ga: Omɔ tsei kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekwɛɔ jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ eshishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ lɛ ahewɔ, ni enyɛɛɛ eshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ nu lɛ ato.

english: How does having a constant water channel help my crops grow better during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: When crops get steady water year-round, they can continuously absorb nutrients from the soil without wilting or stopping their growth during dry weather.
ga: Kɛ tsei ná nu daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛya nɔ amɛjie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛgbooo loo amɛkpaaa amɛdalɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: What happens to my rice crop if the field dries up while the grains are forming?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji ŋmɔji lɛ gĩ be mli ni ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ miifee lɛ?

english: If rice plants lack water during grain formation, the seeds become empty, lightweight, or cracked, which drastically reduces your final harvest weight.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baafee efolo, amɛhe baajɔ loo amɛmli etse, ni no baaha onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli tsiimɔ aba shi waa.

english: Why is it better for me to invest in a shared irrigation system rather than waiting for rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mishika awo nu ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ yɛ mli lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ?

english: Shared irrigation systems provide reliable water even when rains fail, allowing you to plant and harvest crops multiple times a year instead of waiting for natural rainy seasons.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni akɛhaa lɛ haa nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ po. Ehaa oduɔ ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ yɛ afi mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni amɛmɛ kɛyashi adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ

english: Can I plant and harvest rice twice in a single year if I have access to guaranteed irrigation?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ni makpa ŋmãa shii enyɔ yɛ afi kome mli kɛji miná nu ni akɛwoɔ nu mli ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ?

english: Yes, guaranteed irrigation removes your dependence on seasonal rain, allowing you to plant a second crop immediately after harvesting the first as long as the soil has enough nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni anáa nɔmimaa lɛ jieɔ naagba ni ji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ nɔ hiɛnɔkamɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ tso ni ji enyɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji okpa klɛŋklɛŋ tso lɛ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow when the soil gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: Plants use water to carry food and nutrients from the roots up to their leaves; without enough water, the plant cannot feed itself and its green leaves begin to fade and turn yellow.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛ yaa niyenii kɛ hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi kɛyaa baai amli. Kɛji nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ amɛhe. Ni baai eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ shishi efoɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does putting fertilizer on dry soil burn my crops instead of helping them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shãa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ moŋ fe ni eeeye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so roots can safely drink them; without water, concentrated fertilizer salts draw moisture out of the roots, causing the plant to burn and dry up.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anu amɛ shweshweeshwe. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baajie ŋmeii kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: How does keeping water standing in my rice field prevent weeds from choking my crop?
ga: Te nu ni mikɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha jwɛi akafite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Most common farm weeds cannot sprout or breathe under standing water, so keeping the field flooded naturally prevents weed growth while allowing rice to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ loo amɛmu yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ nu shwie ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do some of my crops dry up faster than others during a short spell of dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi gbɛ́ɔ oya fe ekrokomɛi yɛ be kukuoo mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops with shallow root systems run out of moisture quickly when topsoil dries out, whereas crops with deep taproots can pull water stored far underground.
ga: Tsei ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ mli nu faaa oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛteŋ lɛ mli egbi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: How does improving water supply to my fields lead to better market prices for my harvest?
ga: Te nu ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha miŋmɔji lɛ ahe jara aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Crops that receive regular water grow larger, heavier, and healthier seeds and fruits, which attract buyers and fetch higher prices per bag at the market.
ga: Tsei ni naa nu daa lɛ baawo dumɔwui kɛ aduawai ni dara, ni wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ gbalaa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ ni ehaa kotoku kome jara yaa hiɛ yɛ jara nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with broad leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa the shade and moisture it needs to survive its first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to grow large, heavy ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛtoi agboi ni tsii baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and wilt during the afternoon even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: In hot afternoon heat, leaves lose water faster than roots can draw it from the ground. The plant temporarily wilts to close its leaf pores and save moisture, usually bouncing back once the evening cool returns.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛŋa baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ be kukuoo ko ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ejieɔ ehe kpo ekoŋŋ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers need heat within a safe range and wind or insects to move pollen inside the flower. Extreme heat or a lack of natural movement prevents fruit formation, causing the unpollinated flowers to drop.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia dɔlɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe. ni kɔɔyɔɔ loo kooloi bibii yɛ ni baatsi pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ mli Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo adebɔɔ mli tsiimɔ ni bɛ lɛ tsiɔ yibiiwoo naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ pollen lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves are a clear sign that plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient required for leafy growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa kɛha baa lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔji kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop on the same ground repeatedly drains specific plant foods from the soil. Rotating yams with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome shii abɔ Enɛ baaha tso niyenii komɛi aje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii atsake ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are my garden egg plants remaining tiny and short weeks after transplanting them into the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi abɔɔ mli ŋmeii lɛ eshwɛ otsii fioo pɛ beni ajie amɛ awo mli lɛ?

english: Stunted growth usually happens when soil is too compacted for roots to spread out or lacks key nutrients. Digging loose soil around the base and mixing in organic matter encourages strong root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã loo niyenii ni he hiaa waa bɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni aaatsi kɛbɔle A shishi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛfutu mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ waa.

english: Why do the roots of my cassava plants start to rot when rainwater sits on my field for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nu ta miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Crop roots need oxygen from the air inside the soil to breathe. Standing water fills all air spaces, effectively suffocating the roots and allowing rot-causing fungi to multiply.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni yɔɔ lolo lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ feɔ babaoo.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster and taller than my crops even though I planted at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya ni amɛkwɔ fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants adapted to suck up water, light, and nutrients quickly. Clearing weeds early stops them from stealing the resources your crop needs to establish itself.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛnu nu, la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛfee amɛ lɛ.

english: Why are small holes appearing all over the leaves of my cabbage plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cabbage tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Small holes in leaves are caused by chewing pests like caterpillars or beetles using the plant for food. Catching them early or applying natural sprays like neem oil protects the leaves from further damage.
ga: Buji bibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ tso lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Aloo okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ, tamɔ neem fɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I plant them in an open field without taller trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei kakadaji bɛ he lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle full direct sunlight. They need shade from taller plants like plantains or shade trees to protect their delicate leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist while their roots grow.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Bɔni afee ni abu baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ shãa he, ni koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: How do I make sure I am planting cassava stem cuttings the right side up in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at the small leaf buds or nodes along the stem cutting. These buds should always point upwards toward the sky so the leaves can sprout properly above the ground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo nodes bibii Nyiɛmɔ line ni akɛfoɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be bɔni afee ni baai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to support my yam vines with tall wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji afi mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ asɛɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground, giving them full sunlight and protecting them from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulb agbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Ha hulu lɛ fɛɛ ni otsi helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and produce tiny cobs when I plant many seeds very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the roots and leaves compete fiercely with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no extra energy for the plant to build large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi kɛ baai kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni tsei lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape down the middle of the leaf?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni V su yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means your crop is hungry for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth and green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni he hiaa koni baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ adalɛ.

english: Why does my soil give me smaller harvests every time I plant maize on the same plot without resting the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni abaadu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season, leaving the soil tired and exhausted unless you rotate crops or add fertilizer.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ ni egbɔjɔ. Ja otsake ŋmɔshi nibii loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm help make the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni jara wa kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have helpful organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen directly from the air and store it in the soil, acts as a natural soil fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa mli yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why should I cut off some of the young suckers growing at the base of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ midumɔwui titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ ekomɛi?

english: Too many young shoots steal water and nutrients from the main parent tree. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei bibii babaoo juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ tso wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the blossoms on my pepper plants falling off the stems without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extremely hot weather, too little water, or poor soil fertility, causing the plant to save its energy rather than produce fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa kɛ nu fioo tsɔ. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Enɛ haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Is it better to water my tomato crop early in the morning or during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oooha tomato tsei lɛ nu leebi loo shwane?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the roots absorb water before the heat of the day. Watering in the hot sun causes water to evaporate too quickly and can scorch leaves or cause fungal diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ dani kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli adɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã loo ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my rice field so the grains don't fall off or spoil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmaa lɛ shwieee shi loo egbooo?

english: You should harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the rice grains on the panicle turn a golden-yellow color. If you wait too long, the grains become dry and drop onto the ground (shattering), but if you harvest too early, the grains are soft, chalky, and spoil easily during storage.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa be mli ni ŋmaa ni yɔɔ toi lɛ nɔ lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 etsɔ shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ. Kɛji omɛ be kakadaŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagbee shikpɔŋ (shatter), shi kɛji okpa amɛ mra tsɔ lɛ amɛbaafee bɔdɔɔ, amɛbaafee chalky ni amɛbaafite oya yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better to wait for a combine harvester machine to arrive in my village or just hire labor to cut my rice by hand?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mamɛ nikpalɔi lɛ abashɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli loo mahe nitsulɔi ni amɛkɛ amɛdɛŋ akpɛ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: If your rice is fully golden and ready, but heavy rains or birds threaten the crop, it is better to harvest manually with sickles rather than wait weeks for a machine. While machines save time and labor costs, delaying harvest too long causes grain loss and stem lodging that costs you more than manual labor.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-rice lɛ ji shika tsuru ni yeɔ emuu ni efee klalo. Shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo okpoi woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbeyei. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ onine baakpa nii kɛtsɔ ŋmei nɔ moŋ fe ni ooomɛ otsii babaoo ni okɛ tsɔnei atsu nii. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsɔnei haa be kɛ nitsumɔ he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi moŋ, Shi ŋmaakpamɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ laajeɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni no jara wa fe adesa nitsumɔ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested grain thoroughly on a tarp before packing it into sacks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ yɛ tarp nɔ dani mikɛwoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested grain contains hidden moisture that creates a wet, warm environment inside sealed sacks. This causes destructive molds, fungi (like aflatoxin), and grain-weevils to multiply rapidly, ruining the quality and safety of your crop.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ yɛ kotoku ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tsɛŋemɔ helai (tamɔ aflatoxin) kɛ dumɔwui amli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo yaa hiɛ oya. Efiteɔ onibii ni okwɛɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal that your maize lacks nitrogen, which acts as the essential building block for leaf greenness and growth. It can also happen when heavy rain waterlogs the soil, preventing the plant roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ tsumaa nɔ ko ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ baai adalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo nu. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛhe niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do crops grow much taller and healthier on land where livestock used to sleep, but look weak on the rest of my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii shwereɔ babaoo ni amɛnáa hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni be ko ni eho lɛ kooloi wɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Animal manure and urine contain concentrated natural nitrogen, phosphorus, and organic matter. This naturally enriches the soil, giving plants the quick nutrients and soil moisture retention needed to grow strong stems and broad leaves.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ amɛfɔmɔ kotoku mli nibii ni ji adebɔɔ mli nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya, ni ehiɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni wa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops very close together so I can fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots fight underground for water and soil food, while their leaves block sunlight from reaching each other. This competition leaves you with thin, weak plants that produce tiny fruits or grains instead of a rich yield.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa onáa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo dumɔwui yɛ ŋmaa babaoo najiaŋ.

english: The first rain often moistens only the top layer of dry, hot soil without deeply soaking the ground. If a dry spell follows that first rain, your seeds will germinate, quickly run out of water in the heat, and wither underground before full rains return.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋwɛi fã lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ Kɛji hɔmɔ ba sɛɛ mli Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃. Nu ni hoɔ yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli oya yɛ latsaa be mli ni egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani nugbɔ lɛ fɛɛ nɛɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more during the first few weeks after planting than later in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni mikɛduɔ lɛ sɛɛ fe sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crop seedlings are small and weak, making them easily overwhelmed by fast-growing weeds competing for light and water. Once the crops grow taller and build a broad leaf canopy, they naturally shade out smaller weeds and can tolerate minor competition.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Enɛ haa jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ nu he akaŋ lɛ yeɔ enɔ oya. Kɛ tso lɛ da ni efee ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli kwɔ lɛ, Amɛbaafee jwɛi bibii lɛ ahe hulutsoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ akaŋshii fioo ko gbɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant groundnuts and cassava together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the soil, which feeds nearby heavy-feeding crops like cassava. Additionally, low-growing groundnut leaves cover the bare soil to reduce weed growth and retain moisture while the taller cassava matures slowly.
ga: Akpɔlɔi gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii kɛha tsei ni tsii ni yeɔ kooloi niyenii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmei. Peanut baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ fioo lɛ hu haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi, yɛ be mli ni cassava ni kɛlɛ lɛ daa blɛoo.

english: Why do caterpillars and worms suddenly attack my crop leaves right after a light rain follows a dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ trukaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ fioo pɛ? Yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The combination of warmth and new moisture creates the ideal environment for pest eggs laid on the soil or leaves to hatch simultaneously. The soft, tender green leaves that sprout immediately after a rain give these young insects ideal food to eat.
ga: Nɔ hee ni ji hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni akɛfee ekome lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔfɔi yɛ shikpɔŋ loo baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli. Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ feɔ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary living umbrellas that protect the young cocoa from heat and retain moisture until the trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo he lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko ni buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow starting from the bottom, it usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new top leaves, showing that the farm needs organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishigbɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii. Etsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he miihia organic ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when heavy rains start late in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood clay soil or flat land, standing water starves the tubers of oxygen, causing soil fungus to rot the roots before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi shikpɔŋ loo hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha yitso lɛ aná oxygen. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ dani akpaa.

english: Why do my yam plants need wooden stakes to climb on to give me bigger tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ koni ená ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce tubers by using sunlight to make food in their leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get full sunlight exposure, which generates more energy to feed and expand the underground tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni amɛkɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ amli. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la lɛ fɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa hewalɛ babaoo baa koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why does my plantain plant take longer to produce fruit if I leave all the suckers growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii kɛji mishi ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Nakai plantain tso lɛ

english: Multiple suckers growing around one plantain stem fight for the same soil food and water. Cutting back extra shoots leaves only one main stem and one small replacement sucker, concentrating the energy to grow larger fruit bunches faster.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain tso kome he lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa shikpɔŋ kome nɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, eshiɔ tso titri kome pɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii kome ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Ekɛ hewalɛ maa bɔ ni afeɔ aduawai akuu lɛ agboɔ oya lɛ nɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat or inconsistent watering. If the plant feels stressed by dry soil during flowering, it drops its blossoms to save its own energy to survive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Kɛji tso lɛ nuɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ Tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea farm mostly when the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli babaoo beni tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and bright petals that attract pests like pod borers and thrips. Protecting the plants right at the flowering stage stops insects from damaging the newly forming pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu mli nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ pod borers kɛ thrips. Kɛ́ abu tsei ahe kɛjɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ fɔfɔi heei lɛ anaa.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck the sap out of new leaves and transmit leaf-curl viruses. Sprays made from neem oil or soap water help control these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Enɛ shwieɔ baai heei amli nu lɛ ni ekɛ hela ko ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Nibii ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ saamɔ fee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni eyeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I get very small maize cobs when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii waa nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize stalks to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room for its roots and leaves to nourish a full, large cob.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha eshishifãi kɛ baai lɛ koni ekɛha tso agbo lɛ niyenii.

english: Why are my cabbage plants growing big leaves but failing to form a hard, solid head?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi enyɛɛɛ efee yitsei ni wa ni wa lɛ?

english: Cabbages fail to form solid heads if they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer or if temperatures get too hot during growth. High nitrogen causes leaves to spread outward rather than folding tightly into a dense center head.
ga: Cabbage nyɛŋ afee yitsei ni wa kɛji akɛ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ be mli ni edaa lɛ. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa baai lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔle amɛhe shi ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries up the soil moisture around their roots. Planting shade crops like plantains protects them until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa sũ mli nu ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Will planting cassava too close to my maize affect how well my maize grows?
ga: Ani ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsɔ lɛ baaná ŋmãa dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Cassava takes up a lot of space and draws heavy nutrients from the soil as its roots grow deep and wide. If planted too close to maize, both crops will fight for water and sunlight, which reduces maize yield.
ga: Cassava heɔ he babaoo ni egbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni eshishifãi lɛ daraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa tsɔ Tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha ŋmãa ni anáa lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees grow tall and thin without producing many pods when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo ŋmeii babaoo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When trees are planted too close, they compete for sunlight and stretch upward instead of growing thick branches. The tree spends its energy reaching for light rather than producing flowers and cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ baaná niji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ, ekɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ ni ehaa ehe feɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtao la yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni amɛbaafee lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my crops turning yellow while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an important nutrient for growth. The plant naturally moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛha baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the soil. They temporarily wilt to conserve moisture and usually bounce back when temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛbaagboi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop extra flowers if they lack sufficient nutrients, water, or insect pollination. Stress from high temperatures or pest attacks can also cause the tree to shed flowers to save energy.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi kɛji akɛ amɛbɛ niyenii, nu, loo nibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa loo kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ amli baa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afɔlɔ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: How long does it take for young hybrid cocoa trees to start flowering after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tsei bibii ni ji hybrid lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi shishi beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties typically start flowering within two to three years after planting if they receive proper shade, water, and fertilizer, unlike traditional varieties that take longer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi yɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ kɛji amɛná hulutsoo, nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ blema kookoo henɔi ni heɔ be babaoo lɛ ahe.

english: Continuous rain creates high humidity, which helps a fungal disease called Black Pod spread quickly. Excessive shade and poor air circulation around the trees also trap moisture and worsen the pod rot.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod disease lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya. Shade ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni ebɔle Tso lɛ he lɛ hu hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaa pod lɛ fiteɔ waa.

english: Why does cutting off extra branches help my cocoa tree produce more pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni afolɔ ashwie shi krokomɛi lɛ baaye abua mi-cacao tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pruning removes dead or overcrowded branches so the tree stops wasting nutrients on them. It lets sunlight and air into the canopy, reducing diseases and helping the tree focus energy on pod growth.
ga: Niji ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo ni ebɔle amɛhe fe nine lɛ. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ akafite niyenii ni jɛɔ nakai niji lɛ amli lɛ. Ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ tso lɛ mli, ni ehaa helai baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ maa pod lɛ dalɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young crops grow so much slower?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi dumɔwui lɛ miida blɛoo nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from young crops. Clearing weeds regularly leaves all those essential resources for your main crop to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli ni hulu la lɛ laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baaha nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni onibii titri lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together instead of giving them space?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mikɛ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ duɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni maha amɛ gbɛ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sun from one another. Proper spacing gives each crop room to grow strong and produce larger yields.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ amɛhe lɛ haa tsũ fɛɛ tsũ ni daa lɛ daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my yam vines try to climb up any nearby tree or stick instead of growing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɔ tsei loo tsei aniji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally grow upwards to catch maximum sunlight. When you stake them with sticks, their leaves get full access to the sun, allowing the plant to make more food and produce larger tubers under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Kɛ okɛ tso nine fĩ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ baaná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tso lɛ woɔ niyenii babaoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when I plant them alone under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mikome too midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under intense heat. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains alongside them provides necessary shade and keeps the soil moist while the young cocoa gets established.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Nurse tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ akwɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ ni he hiaa ni eye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwereɔ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cassava and beans together in the same field, or will they spoil each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo amɛbaafite?

english: They actually help each other. Beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and put it into the soil, which enriches the ground and feeds the heavy-eating cassava plants while protecting the soil from washing away in heavy rain.
ga: Amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa amɛhe diɛŋtsɛ. Beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa hiɛ ni ehaa ŋmei tsei ni yeɔ nii babaoo lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ sũ lɛ he koni nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa lɛ akahole lɛ.

english: Leaf curling is the plant's defense response to extreme heat. By rolling its leaves inward, the plant reduces the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun to stop moisture from evaporating too quickly.
ga: Baai ni etsilɛ ji tso hebuu hetoo kɛha dɔlɛ ni naa wa. Kɛ́ tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ baa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ lɛ nɔ koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo oya tsɔ.

english: How do I know if my newly transplanted vegetable seedlings are getting enough water to survive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-aduawai dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ miiná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛhi shi?

english: If seedlings stand upright with firm leaves early in the morning, they have enough water. If their stems look limp or droop before the sun even comes up, their roots are thirsty and need immediate watering.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ damɔ shi jaŋŋ ni amɛyɛ baai ni wa leebi lɛ Tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Kɛji tso lɛ tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbo dani hulu lɛ te shi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye amɛshishifãi lɛ ni ehe miihia ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the bush without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ jwɛi lɛ mli ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when stressed by severe heat, erratic watering, or a lack of visiting insects like bees to pollinate the blooms. Without pollination or consistent water, the plant drops flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa hao amɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baahã fɔfɔii lɛ afee pollin lɛ ni bɛ Kɛji pollination loo nu ni baa daa bɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baajie fɔfɔii koni ehiɛ ehewalɛ mli.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain plant turn yellow and die off as the plant gets bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, the plant naturally sheds its older bottom leaves so it can redirect water and energy to the new leaves at the top and feed the growing bunch of fruit.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aya baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ ni ekɛ niyenii aha aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my main crops right after the rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants with widespread root systems that absorb rainwater and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni shishifãi egbɛ eshwã he fɛɛ he ni shwieɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning pale yellow while the stems stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni shishifã lɛ kã he efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Pale yellow leaves indicate that the plant has run out of key soil nutrients like nitrogen or cannot absorb them due to dry soil. Adding compost or manure around the base restores nitrogen and turns the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo enyɛɛɛ ejie amɛ yɛ sũ ni egbi lɛ hewɔ. Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baafata he ni akɛbaabɔle Cones lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni ekɛ nitrogen aku sɛɛ aba ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: What kind of plants can I grow around the border of my farm to stop wandering animals from entering?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei srɔtoi manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ naa koni kooloi ni elaaje lɛ akabote mli?

english: Dense, thorny plants like Jatropha, prickly pear, or closely planted citrus trees act as natural living fences. Animals avoid the thorns and bitter sap, which helps keep them away from your main crops.
ga: Tsei ni ŋmeii ebɔle amɛhe, tamɔ jatropha kɛ prickly pear. Aloo, citrus tsei ni adu amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbogbo, he ni kooloi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni mli edɔ lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ akakwɛ̃.

english: Are there specific crops I can plant around my field edges that animals naturally refuse to eat?
ga: Nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ ni manyɛ makwɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Miŋmɔ lɛ naa he ni kooloi Bei pii lɛ amɛkpooɔ niyenii?

english: Strong-smelling or spicy plants like hot chili peppers, lemongrass, and ginger are usually avoided by livestock. Planting a thick border of chili peppers can discourage animals from pushing into your main field.
ga: Tsei ni ŋmɔlɔ waa loo ŋmɔlɔ yɔɔ mli, tamɔ chili, lemongrass, kɛ ginger lɛ, bei pii lɛ, kooloi tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ he. Kɛ́ oodu ŋmeii ni mli tse husu lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha kooloi anijiaŋ aje wui koni amɛkabote oŋmɔ titri lɛ mli.

english: If cattle step on my young maize plants and crush them, will the plants be able to grow back?
ga: Kɛ́ tsina ko nyiɛ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ anɔ ni efolɔ amɛ lɛ, Ani abele tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ?

english: If the growing point near the base of the stem isn't snapped, young maize can recover and push out new leaves. However, if the stem is broken off at ground level, the plant will not regrow and should be replaced.
ga: Kɛji akɛ he ni tso lɛ daa yɛ ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ efoŋ lɛ, Young corn baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni ekɛ baai heei aba. Shi, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ fã yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tso lɛ shwereŋ shweremɔ hee ni esa akɛ atsake.

english: Can my cassava plants survive if livestock eat all the leaves off the stems?
ga: Ani mi-cassava tso lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji kooloi ye baai fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava is very tough. As long as the underground roots remain healthy, the plant will use its stored energy to sprout fresh leaves within a couple of weeks after losing its foliage.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei wa waa. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ baahi shi shiŋŋ lɛ, Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛwo baai heei yɛ otsii fioo komɛi amli kɛjɛ be mli ni amɛlaaje lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods rot faster when the tree branches get broken by roaming animals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ fiteɔ oya fe be mli ni kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ fiteɔ tsei aniji lɛ?

english: Broken branches leave open wounds on the cocoa tree. These wounds allow fungal spores and insects to enter easily, which speeds up the spread of diseases like black pod rot.
ga: Niji ni ekumɔ lɛ shiɔ ŋmeii yɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ pilamɔi nɛɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii boteɔ mli mlɛo. Enɛ baaha helai tamɔ black pod rot lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly in areas where cattle frequently walk across my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni tsinai fɔɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ foɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy animals compact the soil, crushing out the essential air spaces. Hard, compacted soil prevents plant roots from expanding and stops rainwater from soaking down to feed the roots.
ga: Koolooi ni tsii baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni he hiaa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã, ni ehaaa nugbɔ nu lɛ abote mli koni ekɛha shishifãi lɛ niyenii.

english: What should I do to the soil after animals have trampled my farm plot before I plant new crops?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee shikpɔŋ lɛ beni kooloi etsɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ dani midu tsei heei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should turn and loosen the hard, trampled topsoil with a hoe to let air and water back in. Mixing in organic compost while loosening helps restore soil structure for healthy seed germination.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei atsake ni okɛ ŋmei ajie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni wa ni atsɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu aku sɛɛ aba mli.

english: Is fresh cow manure left on my field by roaming animals good for my crops right away?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hee ni kooloi ni nyiɛɔ kɛyaa kɛbaa lɛ shiɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: No, fresh manure is very high in ammonia and heat, which can burn delicate plant roots. Manure needs to dry out and decompose for a few weeks before it becomes safe, useful fertilizer.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii heei amli ammonia kɛ dɔlɛ fa babaoo waa. ni baanyɛ ashã tsei ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii agbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi dani ebatsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Why do animals prefer eating my sweet potato leaves over my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛye ŋmɔtɔ baai fe mi ŋmɔtɔ wein tsei lɛ?

english: Sweet potato vines have soft, succulent leaves that are easy for livestock to digest, whereas yam vines are often tougher, hairier, or spiky, making them much less appealing to animals.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ ni kooloi baanyɛ aye amɛ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ fɔɔ kaa, amɛhe yɔɔ yitsɔi, loo amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii. Enɛ haaa kooloi aŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my main crops after a field is eaten down by livestock?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ beni kooloi eye shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie dormant in large numbers in the soil. When livestock clear your crop leaves, full sunlight reaches the bare ground, which triggers weed seeds to germinate and grow rapidly before your crops can recover.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ baakã shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ babaoo nɔ Kɛji kooloi jie onibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ Hulu la ni shɛɔ he ni agbele lɛ Enɛ haa jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea around the base of the plant will help it recover its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei, tamɔ urea, fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eku esɛɛ eba eŋɔli su lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni eda waa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of water. Watering your tomatoes regularly at the base early in the morning helps the plant stay cool and hold onto its flowers so they can form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa yɛ shishigbɛ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo tomato.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaf. Spraying the plants with a natural neem seed extract or appropriate crop spray kills these insects and stops the leaves from curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem dumɔwui ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ni ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my young maize stalks have small holes in the leaves and sawdust-like dirt inside the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bu bibii yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars or armyworms that hatch from eggs laid by moths. Treating the central funnel of the plant with an approved pest control method early in the season stops the worms before they eat through the stem.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers loo asraafoi awui ni fɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ gbɛ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nii lɛ atsu tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ he nii yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ kpaa dani amɛyeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why do my crops grow tall, thin, and weak when I plant seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kɛlɛ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe kpaakpa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops end up fighting each other for sunshine, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows its roots and stems enough room to grow thick, strong, and produce a bigger yield.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ ni amɛná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara, amɛwa, ni amɛha nibii babaoo aba.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds when the main rainy season starts?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should wait until the rain has soaked the ground deep enough that if you dig a hand's depth, the soil easily forms a ball in your fist without crumbling. Planting in shallow moisture right after the first light rain can cause seeds to dry up if the rain takes a break.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni kɛji okɛ oniji tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ kokroo. yɛ o-fist mli ni efoŋ Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be lɛ faaa yɛ Nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa.

english: Why does adding dried cow dung or decomposed leaves to my farm land help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei ni egbi loo baai ni egboi ni mikɛfataa nibii ni miduɔ lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Decomposed animal dung and leaf matter act as natural plant food that enriches the soil. They improve the soil's ability to hold moisture during dry days and loosen hard dirt so crop roots can easily spread and feed.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi kɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shi Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛye nii oya.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees around my newly planted cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ he lɛ? Kookoo dumɔwui ni adu ehee

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under the harsh, direct sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants, keeping the soil cool and moist until the cocoa is strong enough to survive on its own.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when heavy rainwater sits in the soil for too long without draining away. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges helps excess water flow off so the roots remain dry enough to stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejeee kpo. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during heavy rains even when the fruits are not ripe yet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛyibii lɛ eshɛko lolo moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and the heavy fruit bunch makes the tree top-heavy during strong winds and rain. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy branched bamboo or wooden pole supports the weight and keeps the plant standing until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ni haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni ji ŋmei loo tso ni niji ni mli wa yɔɔ mli lɛ to tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni tsii lɛ ni eye ebua ni edamɔ shi kɛyashi kpamɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when planted in low-lying ground or heavy clay soils that hold too much water. Cassava roots need well-draining soil to breathe; excess standing water suffocates the roots and encourages fungal diseases that cause rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ he ni nu babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu. Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɛ ŋmeii baa lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Yam tubers grow straight down into the earth and need soft, deep soil to expand properly. If you plant yams in hard, compacted ground or shallow soil without making high mounds, the growing tuber hits hard soil and is forced to bend.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛbiɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ odu sweet potato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni mli edɔ loo ni mli ekwɔɔɔ nɔ ni okɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ efeee lɛ, Planted bulbs lɛ tswaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni enyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle ehe.

english: Young cocoa trees are sensitive to strong, direct heat and direct sunlight. Taller companion plants like plantains provide living shade, keeping the air moist and protecting the young cocoa leaves from scorching while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni hiɔ shi yɛ he kome yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ, tamɔ plantain lɛ haa hulutsoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fũɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting beans together with my maize helps the maize grow stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ mli wa lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans have tiny organisms on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. When grown next to maize, the beans share this natural fertilizer, helping the maize build strong stalks and healthy leaves.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmãa lɛ, Peas baajara adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa nɛɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni enáa tsei ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow big cobs, whereas overcrowding leads to many thin, weak plants with small or empty ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo ko akwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baaha amɛtoi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow even after I apply fertilizer from the bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Fertilizer kɛjɛ kotoku lɛ mli momo?

english: Fertilizer must be placed at the right distance from the plant and at the right time. If applied too close to the stalk, it can burn the roots, and if applied right before heavy rains, the nutrients wash away before the plant can drink them in.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ, ni yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛwo tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashã. ni kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ Akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ dani tsei lɛ nuɔ amɛ.

english: Why did half of the maize seeds I saved in a rubber bag fail to sprout when I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɔndom mli lɛ fã ekwɛɛɛ beni adu lɛ?

english: Seeds stored in airtight rubber bags or warm places can trap dampness, causing the seeds to rot or lose their energy before planting. Storing seeds in a cool, dry, and breathable container keeps the embryo inside healthy until planting season.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kɔndom ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo he ko ni mli edɔ lɛ baanyɛ ahi ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ loo amɛhewalɛ baa shi dani aduɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni mumɔ baanyɛ ashɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔmɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or irregular watering. When a plant feels extreme heat or dry soil, it drops its flowers to save water and survival energy instead of spending energy on growing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛ tso lɛ nu latsaa ni naa wa he loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and stopping new fruit from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiikpa aduawai heei lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves. This damages the leaf tissue and can spread plant viruses, preventing the plant from making energy to produce peppers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ fiteɔ baa fãji ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tso lɛ hela lɛ eshwã. Enɛ haa tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crops and choke them early on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii ni miitsi amɛnaa mra lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants adapted to take up water, fertilizer, and light much faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crop plants a chance to grow tall enough to shade the soil and stop new weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhe nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hegbɛ ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛtsi jwɛi heei ni baaye nɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Tomato plants have weak stems that bend under the weight of heavy fruit. Tying them to wooden sticks keeps the leaves and fruits off the wet ground, which prevents fruit rot, keeps soil pests away, and helps the plant get more sunlight.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni tsii ni tsii lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛfi tso he lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akafite. Eshwieɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo

english: Why is it important for me to measure and leave specific spaces between my cassava stems when planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni masusu ni mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ kɛ́ midu lɛ?
