english: Cassava roots need enough room underground to swell into large tubers. If you plant them too close together, their roots fight for nutrients and moisture, resulting in small, thin roots instead of big, heavy yields.
ga: Esa akɛ cassava shishifãi lɛ aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii agbo ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving the cocoa trees the shade and cool soil moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Planting maize continuously drains the same nutrients, especially nitrogen, out of the soil and allows maize pests to multiply in the ground. Rotating your crop with beans or groundnuts restores natural nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii lɛ nɔŋŋ. titri lɛ nitrogen ni yaa nɔ eshiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ, ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to cut down on water loss when it gets too hot and dry. However, severe curling and yellowing usually means the plant is thirsty or that tiny insects like aphids are sucking the sap out of the leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛ́ amɛdɔ tsɔ ni amɛgbi. Shi kɛlɛ, bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye tso lɛ. Aloo kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids miinu nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my bean plants fall off without producing any pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-bean tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Bean flowers drop when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or attacks from flower-eating insects. If the soil is too dry while flowering, the plant sheds flowers to preserve its own life.
ga: Pea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni yeɔ fɔfɔii lɛ tutua tsei lɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: Why should I cut off the lower branches and extra leafy suckers from my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni baai ni fa fe nine yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Removing lower leaves stops rain from splashing soil-borne fungal diseases onto your crops. Pruning extra leafy branches also forces the plant to send its water and food energy directly into making larger fruits instead of unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ojie baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, nugbɔ lɛ haaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ashwie onibii anɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ baai krokomɛi ni afoɔ lɛ hu nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ awo aduawai wuji amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa ni ekɛbaatsu nii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why did many of the seeds I planted fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they were planted too deep, if the soil was too dry, or if insects and heavy rains damaged them. Buying clean, certified seeds and planting them at the right depth ensures high germination.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. aloo kooloi bibii kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni he tse ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni aheɔ ni aduɔ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yams are ready for harvest when the green leaves and vines above ground naturally turn yellow and completely dry up. This signals that the plant has stopped growing and stored all its energy into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ miito ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast across my cocoa pods during the heavy rain season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that loves moisture and cold weather. Raindrops splash the fungal spores from dirty soil and infected pods onto healthy ones, so keeping the farm weeded and pruned stops the wet environment the disease needs.
ga: Black pods ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fɛ̃i. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji kɛ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ tsei ni afoɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni hela lɛ biɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do extension officers advise me not to burn my farmland after clearing the bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akashã ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ beni ajie jwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the good living organisms in the soil and burns away natural organic nutrients. Leaving cut vegetation to decompose naturally acts as mulch, keeping the soil moist and feeding your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ni eshãa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni afo lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ, ebaatsu nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: How do I know if my land is ready for me to start planting maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Your land is ready when the soil has been loosened, cleared of large weeds or roots, and is moist from the first steady major rains, usually around April or May depending on your region.
ga: Oshikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwie shi. Jiemɔ jwɛi wuji loo shishifãi lɛ. ni eyaa nɔ ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛjɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ, aaafee April loo May. Edamɔ kpokpaa ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants naturally drop or yellow their leaves during dry spells to conserve water and protect their underground roots. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ loo amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Koni akɛbu nu he ni abu shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ahe Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tsei lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants are getting too little water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ miiná nu fioo tsɔ?

english: When maize plants suffer from water drought, their leaves roll up tightly into thin tubes during the hot daytime to stop moisture from evaporating.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he naagbai kpe lɛ, akɛ ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni efeɔ ŋmãa bibioo ko. Yɛ gbi ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akafo.

english: Pepper flowers often fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil lacks water, or when pollinators like bees are missing from the field.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni feɔ pollen, tamɔ ŋmeii, laajeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji amli.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate tender leaves and short roots that dry out fast in full sun. They need shade crops like plantains to act as natural umbrellas during their early years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ mli egbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains koni amɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients, leading to tall, weak stems and small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tsei kakadaji ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo baa shi

english: What causes small round holes to appear on my tomato leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo jeɔ kpo yɛ mi tomato baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Small holes are typically caused by leaf-eating insects like caterpillars or beetles, which feed on the leaves and weaken the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ baai tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii kɛ bu bibii baa. ni yeɔ baai ni ehaa tsei adalɛ baa shi

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating with beans or cowpeas returns vital nitrogen back into the earth.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsake amɛhe lɛ, ehaa nitrogen ni he hiaa waa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I save seeds from my previous hybrid harvest to plant in the next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ hybrid kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops usually produce weaker plants with lower yields in the second generation. It is best to get fresh certified seeds from approved seed suppliers each season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ woɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni woɔ yibii fioo yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooona dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛjɛ dumɔwui ahe nihɔɔlɔ ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ dɛŋ yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your maize is hungry for nitrogen. When the soil runs out of nitrogen, the plant steals it from its older lower leaves to keep its newer top leaves growing.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ba naagbee Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛ ŋwɛi baai heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my field make my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua mi ŋmei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which has tiny bacteria on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, creating natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he ni eyɛ helai bibii ni yɔɔ eshishifãi ni heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do we need to build raised mounds to plant yams instead of just putting them in flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ wɔmaa gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni wɔkɛbaawo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth so the tubers can expand deep and wide without fighting hard ground. Mounds also keep water from gathering around the tuber and rotting it.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potatoes bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛshwere ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawu. Gɔŋ lɛ hu tsiɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle bulb lɛ he ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: How do I know which end of a cassava stick should face up when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmei ŋmei lɛ fã ni esa akɛ makwɛ hiɛ kɛ́ midu?

english: Look at the small buds or leaf scars on the stem stick. They should point upward like small hooks facing the sky so the leaves grow up into the sun and roots sprout downward.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo baai ahe tsɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ Esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi tamɔ ŋmei bibioo ko, ni ekwɛ ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni baai lɛ adara koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛba shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot take direct, full sunlight. Big trees act as natural umbrellas that cool the air and protect the young leaves from scorching until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he sɛɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers off without forming any pepper fruit during the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ yibii ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When the day temperatures get too hot, pepper plants drop their blossoms to save water and energy. Once the air cools down or gets shade, the flowers will stay and form fruits.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ loo eyɛ hulutsoo Fɔfɔi lɛ baahi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves turn black and rot in the middle of the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ, kaabe baa lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Too much rain sitting in the cabbage leaves creates a wet environment for bacterial rot and fungi to grow. Good spacing helps air flow through and dry the plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ewo fɔ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ anyɛ ada. He ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce very tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil, leaving them with too little energy to build big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why should I cut off the extra leafy branches from my tomato plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Removing small side shoots allows the plant to send its food and water directly into making bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: ŋmeii bibii ni ajieɔ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu baa tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small even when I water the farm well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ bibioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Weeds have strong roots that steal the fertilizer and water out of the dirt before your crop roots can drink them up.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni he wa ni juɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yeɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them in an open field without big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni tsei ni eda bɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to harsh direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees alongside cocoa creates a cooler canopy that protects young cocoa leaves from burning until the trees are established.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ maa shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the maize plant lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf greenness and growth. Adding compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves and big ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni ekwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔji wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it helpful for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my land after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nutrients from the soil, but legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. Rotating these crops naturally refills your soil nutrients for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Nibii nɛɛ ni oootsake lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I spread dry grass or leaves around the roots of my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ magbɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ashwã he lɛ? pepper tso shishifãi

english: Spreading dry organic matter—known as mulching—keeps direct sunshine off the soil. It traps moisture in the ground for a longer time, keeps crop roots cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your plot.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ baaye abua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi anaa koni amɛkaye he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers through their leaves catching sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground using stakes allows leaves to capture maximum sunlight while preventing damp earth from causing leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ feɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ kɛtsɔɔ baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ náa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ kɛ tso helai baa.

english: If you leave too many suckers, they fight with the main tree for soil water and food. Removing all but one or two strong suckers concentrates the plant's energy into producing large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ekɛ tsei ni ji gbɔi lɛ baawu koni amɛná nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ niyenii. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee plantain tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the stem without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the crop experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Maintaining steady soil moisture helps the plant retain flowers long enough to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava cuttings need to be planted at a slant or buried sideways in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ koŋ nɔ loo afu lɛ yɛ esɛɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko mli lɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings horizontally or at an angle encourages roots to sprout evenly along the stem, creating a wider root footprint that produces more tubers and anchors the crop securely against rain and wind.
ga: Kasava niji ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛi loo yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi. ni haa shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ Enɛ haa ŋmeii babaoo baa ni ehaa tso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in my young maize leaves with tiny worms inside the shoot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmeii bibii yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworms eating through the leaves while hidden inside the plant funnel. Spotting them early allows you to clean out the funnels or apply appropriate pest controls before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsumɔ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ anɔ loo okɛ tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsuɔ nii dani amɛfiteɔ hei ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding under the leaves, or by viral infections spread by those insects. Keeping the crop clear of sap-sucking bugs keeps the foliage flat and active.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kɛ́ tsei lɛ akafee nɔ ni kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow on farmland where all the big trees have been cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ ni afo tsei wuji yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Big trees act as a shield for the land. When they are removed, the hot sun bakes the soil and heavy rains wash away topsoil nutrients, leaving the land dry and weak like a wasteland where crops struggle to find food and moisture.
ga: Tsei wuji buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Beni ajieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ gbiŋ ni egbɔjɔ, tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛna niyenii kɛ nu ni mli edɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland turn into hard, cracked dirt during the dry season when there are no plants or trees on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni tsei loo tsei bɛ jɛmɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water very fast because there is no leaf cover to shade it from direct sunlight. Without plant roots holding moisture underground, the top layer bakes hard and cracks under extreme heat.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nu fiteɔ oya waa ejaakɛ baai bɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Kɛji tso shishifãi ni akɛbaato ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ bɛ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baashã waa ni ebaagbala yɛ la ni naa wa lɛ shishi.

english: Will planting trees alongside my food crops steal water and food from my main plants?
ga: Ani tsei ni mikɛduɔ yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ mi tsei titrii lɛ amli?

english: If chosen correctly, trees actually help your crops. Certain trees pull water and nutrients from deep underground where regular crop roots cannot reach, bringing moisture up and shedding leaves that rot into rich natural fertilizer for your food crops.
ga: Kɛji ahala jogbaŋŋ lɛ Tsei baaye abua onibii diɛŋtsɛ. Tsei komɛi gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ daa lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ ni ejieɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ, ni ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa oniyenii tsei lɛ.

english: How do farm trees help protect my food crops during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ he yɛ hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Trees lower the temperature around your farm by providing shade and trapping cool moisture in the air. This protects your crops from burning up under intense sunlight and reduces how much water they lose each day.
ga: Tsei haa hulutsoo ni ebɔle ohe lɛ baa shi. oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ hulutsoo ni oooha kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni ooomɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baabu onibii ahe koni ekashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni eha nu ni tsei fiteɔ daa gbi lɛ aba shi

english: Is it true that dry leaves falling from trees on my field actually feed my crops?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ baai ni egboi ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ atsu nii diɛŋtsɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, as fallen leaves decay on the soil surface, they break down into rich organic matter called humus. This acts like natural manure, enriching the soil and keeping it moist so your crops can grow stronger.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kɛ́ baai ni egbee shi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Amɛgbalaa amɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ humus. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara waa.

english: Can I successfully grow crops on land that has become dry and degraded like a wasteland?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni efite tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji nɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli?

english: Yes, but it takes time and effort. You must first rebuild the soil by planting shade plants or fast-growing trees, which loosen the hard earth and restore nutrients before sensitive food crops can thrive.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi ebiɔ be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ. Esa akɛ otswa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ klɛŋklɛŋ kɛtsɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni daa oya lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ dani niyenii tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crops dry out faster when I burn all the bushes and plants on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛ́ mishã tsei bibii kɛ tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the plant material that normally sits on top of the earth to keep it cool. Without that natural ground cover, the heat directly hits the bare soil, causing water to evaporate rapidly and leaving your crops thirsty.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ tsei ahe nibii ni bei pii lɛ amɛtaraa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha edɔ lɛ. Kɛji adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ bɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaná shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya ni ehaa kumai yeɔ onibii.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops on newly cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ mishikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants designed to quickly cover bare, hot soil exposed to direct sunlight. Without tree shade or early ground cover from your crops, weeds will sprout fast to grab the open sunlight and water.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni afee koni amɛha shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ tsei loo shikpɔŋ nɔ hulutsoo bɛ mra mli lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya koni amɛŋɔ hulu la kɛ nu.

english: Why does growing food crops on newly cleared forest land take so much more physical labor in the first year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ hee ni agbele naa lɛ nɔ lɛ biɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ nitsumɔ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cleared forest land requires heavy work to manage strong weed invasion, clear leftover roots, and prepare hard soil. Once your crops and young trees establish a canopy, the shade will control the weeds and lighten your workload.
ga: Kooi amli hei ni ajie lɛ biɔ nitsumɔ ni wa koni akɛtsu jwɛi ni baa shi lɛ ahe nii. Jiemɔ shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ fɛɛ. ni osaa shikpɔŋ ni wa Be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei bibii Abɔ O-canopy. Shade lɛ baaye jwɛi lɛ anɔ ni ebaaha onitsumɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my crop seeds take longer to sprout on land that was recently cleared of all trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ajie kɛjɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ mli etsɛko lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly exposed soil gets extremely hot and dry near the surface. Seed roots need cool, moist dirt to push out easily, so high soil temperatures on bare ground can slow down or stop germination.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Dumɔwui shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ, ni mli efɔ koni amɛtsi amɛhe oya. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ loo ekpa.

english: How do I know if my maize plants are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye mi-abele tsei lɛ ni amɛmiitao ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Maize plants show hunger through their leaves; when they lack essential nutrients like nitrogen, the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern starting from the tip, signaling that the soil needs more fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi tsei jieɔ amɛ hɔmɔ lɛ kpo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ naagbee. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Should I keep fertilizing my cassava plants as they grow older, or when should I stop?
ga: Ani esa akɛ maya nɔ mawo mi-cassava lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii be mli ni edaa lɛ loo mɛɛ be esa akɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava needs fertilizer during its first three months to build strong roots, but you should stop fertilizing as it matures because too much nitrogen later on causes the plant to produce thick leafy stems instead of big tubers.
ga: Cassava he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 3 lɛ mli koni etswa shishifãi ni wa. Shi esa akɛ okpa fɔmɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛji edara. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, sɛɛ mli lɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná ŋmeii kɛ baai ni mli tse yɛ ŋmeii wuji najiaŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close, they crowd each other out and fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak, thin stalks that yield tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei lɛ ahe tseee ni amɛhe waaa, ni no haa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do I need to pull out some of my young seedling sprouts after they germinate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui bibii komɛi kɛjɛ mli beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Thinning out crowded seedlings leaves space for the strongest plants to spread their roots, absorb enough water, and grow into large, high-yielding crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa gbɛ ahaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛshishifãi akwɛ̃. Eŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni woɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava plants drop leaves during hot dry spells to conserve internal moisture and survive drought, naturally sprouting fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ lɛ koni amɛbu amɛmli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ he ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli. Taakɛ eji lɛ, ebaakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers without growing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi ni eduuu pepper ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or soil nutrient shortages, as a self-defense mechanism to preserve energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ mɔ he koni akɛbu hewalɛ he

english: Why do my tomato plants grow so many extra side shoots, and should I cut them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii babaoo nɛkɛ? Ni ani esa akɛ mafo mli?

english: Tomato plants produce many extra sucker branches that consume food and moisture; removing these side shoots directs the plant's food supply toward producing bigger, healthier fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei woɔ sucker niji krɛdɛɛi babaoo ni yeɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ ŋmeii lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ niyenii lɛ yaa yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do fall armyworms prefer to attack young maize plants instead of older maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua ŋmãa tsei bibii moŋ fe ŋmãa momo lɛ?

english: Young maize plants have soft, tender leaves that are easy for young worms to chew and digest, whereas older plants develop tough leaves and thick stalks that pests find harder to eat.
ga: Abɛi tsei bibii yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii baanyɛ aye ni amɛye. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ baai ni wa kɛ tsei ni mli wa ni ewa kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ.

english: Can I grow specific crops on my land just to feed farm animals during dry periods?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii pɛ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛha ŋmɔ mli kooloi niyenii yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛkɛ?

english: Yes, planting dedicated forage crops like Elephant grass or legume bushes provides nutritious green feed for livestock, especially when pasture grass dries up during the dry season.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni akɛyeɔ niyenii krɛdɛɛi tamɔ shwuɔ jwɛi loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa kooloi lɛ náa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ ji anɔkwale, titri lɛ kɛ́ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ gbi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first planting; seeds saved from that harvest lose their special strength, resulting in uneven plant growth and poor yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daraaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: How can I get my mango trees to produce a huge bumper harvest every season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi mango tso lɛ awo yibii babaoo daa afi?

english: To get a large bumper harvest, mango trees need regular pruning to let in sunlight, balanced fertilizer to nourish the soil, and early protection against pests before the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: bɔni afee ni aná nibii babaoo lɛ, ehe miihia ni afolɔ Mango tsei lɛ amli daa koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ. ni otsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa mra Dani fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii

english: Why do my citrus fruits drop off the tree before they are big and ready to pick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-citrus yibii lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara ni amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Citrus trees drop premature fruit mainly when they don't get enough water during dry spells, or when they lack key nutrients in the soil. Consistent watering and feeding keep the fruit firmly on the tree.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛyibii lɛ oya titri lɛ, kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni niyenii titrii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my fruit trees produce plenty of flowers, but very few of them turn into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Flowers fail to set fruit if insects don't pollinate them, or if the tree experiences water stress and nutrient shortages right when the flowers are forming.
ga: Fɔfɔi nyɛŋ awo yibii kɛji kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. aloo kɛji tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa beni fɔfɔii lɛ ebɔi feemɔ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ.

english: How many years must I wait after planting before my young orange or mango trees start giving fruits?
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko du lɛ, afii enyiɛ esa akɛ emɛ dani ŋmei loo mango tso lɛ aje yibiiwoo shishi?

english: Grafted mango and citrus trees generally start producing fruit within two to three years, though full production increases as the trees grow bigger over the following years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango kɛ ŋmei tsei ni akɛwo amɛhe lɛ jeɔ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii enyɔ loo etɛ mli. Eyɛ mli akɛ yibiiwoo lɛ baaya hiɛ kwraa beni tso lɛ daa yɛ afii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli lɛ moŋ.

english: What basic inputs do I need to support my crops so they don't fail?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee nibii he hiaa mi koni manyɛ maye mabua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni amɛkafite?

english: Essential crop inputs include high-quality seeds or grafted seedlings, fertilizers to feed the plant, and proper crop protection products to prevent insect pests and diseases from damaging your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni he hiaa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ekomɛi ji dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli niyenii kɛ nibii ni sa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai akafite okpamɔ lɛ.

english: How do government extension projects help farmers get inputs and manage their farms?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ hiɛyaa gbɛjianɔtoi yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛnáa nibii ni amɛkɛbaatsu nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛɔ amɛŋmɔji lɛ anɔ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Extension projects often work in phases by first supplying farmers with subsidized inputs like seeds and fertilizers, and then assisting with technical advice and market access in later phases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, atsuɔ shweremɔ nitsumɔi lɛ ahe nii yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli kɛtsɔ nibii ni akɛyeɔ abuaa kɛjɛɔ okwaafoi adɛŋ, tamɔ dumɔwui kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua kɛ ŋaawoo ni kɔɔ ŋaa he kɛ jarayeli hegbɛ yɛ fã ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do crop prices drop so low as soon as harvest season begins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ahe jara baa shi nɛkɛ kɛji kpamɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: When all farmers in a region harvest crops like mangoes or citrus at the same time, the market becomes flooded with produce. This high supply allows buyers to lower their buying prices.
ga: Beni okwaafoi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ kpokpaa ko nɔ lɛ kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ mango loo ŋmei yɛ be kome mli. Jarayelihe lɛ eyi kɛ nibii ni aduɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni fa babaoo nɛɛ haa mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ baa amɛnibii ahe jara shi.

english: How can I protect my farm investment so I don't lose money after spending so much on inputs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mishika ni mikɛwo ŋmɔ mli lɛ he? Bɔni afee ni mikafite shika beni mifite shika babaoo yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can protect your money by joining farmer groups to sell produce in bulk, securing agreements with buyers before harvesting, or staggering your planting so you don't harvest all at once.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oshika he kɛtsɔ okwaafoi akui ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ amɛnibii babaoo lɛ nɔ. Okɛ hɔlɔlɔ lɛ akpa kpaŋmɔ dani okpa ŋmaa lɛ. Aloo, shwiemɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni okakpa fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why do my fresh fruits spoil so fast after I pick them from the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii heei lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikpa amɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested fruits continue to breathe and heat up. Leaving them in the sun, handling them roughly, or packing them tightly in hot sacks speeds up rotting and spoilage.
ga: Yibii ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ emuɔ ni edɔɔ. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli ni akɛtsu nii waa loo akɛwo kotokui ni mli edɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha fitemɔ kɛ fitemɔ aya hiɛ oya.

english: Is it possible to make my crops produce fruit slightly off-season when prices are higher?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ aha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo yibii fioo yɛ be ni sa mli beni jara wa lɛ?

english: Yes, by using irrigation during dry periods and applying specific plant nutrients at deliberate times, you can trigger flowering earlier or later than normal to hit higher market prices.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛ tsei amli niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ bei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ owo fɔfɔii ni baa mra loo sɛɛ mli lɛ he hewalɛ koni onine ashɛ jara ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields after I farm on it year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni midu nɔ afi fɛɛ afi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Every time crops grow and are harvested, they take essential food and minerals out of the ground. Over time, the soil becomes depleted of these nutrients and needs help to regain its strength so future crops can grow well.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni akpa amɛkpamɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ shika tsuru ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ efo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe miihia ni aye abua lɛ koni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ bɔni afee ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are struggling because the soil has lost its nutrients?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ miiho?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops show clear signs such as stunted growth, pale or yellowing leaves, weak stems, and producing very small fruits or grains.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baajie okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tamɔ amɛdalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ kpo. Baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ, tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ, kɛ aduawai loo dumɔwui bibii waa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant again without letting the soil recover its nutrients?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu ekoŋŋ ni mikɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ eko eko eko eko eko ehãaa?

english: Planting in exhausted soil leads to weak plants that struggle to survive, yield very little food, and are easily damaged by pests and diseases because they lack proper nutrition.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi lɛ ashiɔ. Ekɛ nibii fioo ko pɛ haa. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ oya yɛ niyenii kpakpa ni anáaa lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are there different types of fertilizer, and why can't I just use the same one for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Different fertilizers supply different nutrients, like nitrogen for leaves or phosphorus for roots. Using the right fertilizer ensures you are giving the soil the specific nutrients it has lost for that crop's needs.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ eko fɛɛ eko haa niyenii srɔtoi, tamɔ nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ loo phosphorus kɛha shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii ni elaajeɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he hiaa lɛ pɛ.

english: Will my crops react differently if I change to a new type of fertilizer this season?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee tsake amɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Yes, crops respond differently depending on the nutrients provided. A new fertilizer tailored to your soil's missing nutrients will help crops grow stronger stems, greener leaves, or bigger fruits compared to old ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛnáa lɛ naa. Nibii heei ni akɛwoɔ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ Aloo aduawai lɛ da kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii momo lɛ ahe.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so my crops absorb the nutrients properly?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛwo mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil has some moisture, such as early in the morning or after light rain, so the plant roots can dissolve and soak up the food easily.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ, tamɔ leebi maŋkpa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ fioo sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ atsɔ mli oya ni amɛŋɔ niyenii.

english: How does the dry season around Christmas affect the way my crops behave?
ga: Te Blonya hɔmɔ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ajeŋba he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: During the end-of-year dry period, hot weather and dry winds make crops lose water fast, causing leaves to wilt, growth to slow down, and plants to focus on survival rather than rapid growth.
ga: Yɛ fɛ̃i be mli yɛ afi lɛ naagbee lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraa blɛoo Ni tsei maa wala ni amɛaahi shi lɛ nɔ mi moŋ fe ni amɛaadara oya.

english: How can I protect my crops from losing moisture when the weather gets hot and dry towards the end of the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ afi lɛ naagbee?

english: Covering the soil around your crops with dry leaves or straw (mulching) acts like a blanket, keeping the sun from drying out the soil and trapping moisture near the roots.
ga: Mulching ni akɛbaa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi (mulch) koni etsu nii tamɔ blanket. Etsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni emɔɔ nu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why should I prepare my land early before the new year rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ wɔsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa dani Afi Hee nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Preparing land early allows the soil to loosen up and absorb the very first rains, giving seeds the best start to absorb newly released soil nutrients right away.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eŋɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii heei ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow even when there is plenty of sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ hulu la babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for food, not light. It often means the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the nutrient responsible for keeping leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji niyenii he bolɔmɔ, shi jeee la. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa

english: How can I tell if my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When cocoa pods mature properly, their skin color changes from green or dark red to a bright yellow or orange color, showing that the seeds inside have developed correctly.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Ehewolo nɔ su tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ.

english: What happens if I harvest my cocoa pods before they mature properly?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Harvesting cocoa before it fully matures leads to flat, underdeveloped beans that produce poor flavor and yield very low market quality.
ga: Kookoo ni akpaa dani egbɔ lɛ haa anáa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɛɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni jara waaa kwraa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods taking longer than usual to turn yellow on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni sa dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cold weather, excessive shade, or lack of proper nutrients in the soil can slow down the natural ripening and maturation process of cocoa pods.
ga: cold weather Shade babaoo Aloo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ adebɔɔ mli shweremɔ kɛ shweremɔ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ asɛɛ afo.

english: How many days should I leave my cocoa beans to ferment under banana leaves?
ga: Gbii enyiɛ esa akɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛho yɛ banana baai ashishi?

english: Cocoa beans typically need at least 5 to 6 days of fermentation under banana leaves to kill the bean germ and develop good flavor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ hoo lɛ, ehe hiaa ni cocoa ŋmeii lɛ aná gbii 5 kɛyashi 6 dani amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ banana baai ashishi koni amɛgbe helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni amɛná ŋmɔlɔ kpakpa.

english: Why do my cocoa beans look flat and purple inside instead of dark brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii lɛ amli feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple and flat beans mean the cocoa was harvested while still unripened or was not given enough days to ferment properly.
ga: Purple beans kɛ flat beans tsɔɔ akɛ akpa cocoa lɛ be mli ni eshɛko lolo loo enáaa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why is it wrong to stop drying my cocoa beans after only a few days when they still feel soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaakpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ agbimɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni amɛyɛ bɔdɔɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Stopping the drying process early leaves too much moisture inside the beans, which causes mould to grow and ruins the crop quality.
ga: Ni oookpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ mra Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmeii daa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa trees drop their young pods before they can grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Trees often drop young pods during periods of severe dry weather or heavy pest attacks because the plant lacks the energy and water to mature them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛbii bibii lɛ ashwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi waa loo be mli ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa amɛ waa lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei bɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni amɛkɛbaadara.

english: Will heavy continuous rainfall close to harvest time affect my crop quality?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Excessive rain during harvest makes it hard to dry cocoa properly, increasing the risk of pod diseases and mouldy beans.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ haa ewaa akɛ aaagbi kookoo jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa pod kɛ bean mold hela lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How does trimming shade trees help my cocoa pods mature better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni ooofo lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Trimming extra shade branches allows more sunlight to reach the trees, which warms the cocoa canopy and helps pods mature evenly.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la babaoo shɛɔ tso lɛ he. Enɛ haa kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli dɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛdaraa pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave harvested cocoa pods on the wet ground for many days before breaking them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ gbii babaoo dani mifoɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving harvested pods on damp ground allows fungus and rot to enter through the pod shell and ruin the beans inside before you process them.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ dani abaanyɛ atsu he nii.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmei ni yɔɔ nitrogen tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my plot after harvesting my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen food from the air and trap it in the soil. Planting them after maize naturally refills the soil with food for the next season without buying expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen nibii ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ abɛi sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot inside the ground when heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in heavy soil around them for too long, drowning the roots. Planting your cassava cuttings on raised soil mounds or ridges lets excess rainwater drain away safely so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bote shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ shweshweeshwe. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why is it good for me to cover the ground around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, called mulching, acts like an umbrella for the soil. It keeps the ground cool, prevents water from drying out quickly in the hot sun, and stops stubborn weeds from sprouting and stealing food.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekagbi oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni amɛtsi jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛkaju niyenii.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop many of their small flowers before turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi enyiɛ dani etsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or insufficient shade. Keeping shade trees alive nearby and applying dried organic mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and preserves the flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi ni ji organic mulch lɛ aha amɛhe. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ekwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Plantain plants fall because tiny underground pests eat their roots, making the plant weak, or because heavy winds push down top-heavy stems. Propping the stems up with sturdy bamboo poles and keeping the base clear of pests helps them stand until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yeɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ, ni no haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Aloo akɛni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa tsei ni tsii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni wa damɔ tsei lɛ anɔ, ni aha shishitoo lɛ nɔ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, small, and bent instead of long and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, bibii, ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛja lɛ?

english: Yams grow crooked or short when the soil beneath them is too hard, stony, or compacted for the tuber to push through easily. Digging deep, loose planting mounds gives the yam soft earth to stretch downwards cleanly.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo kukuji kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ, tɛi yɔɔ mli, loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ aahu akɛ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli mlɛo. Kɛ́ atsa sũ ni akɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato lɛ sũ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die suddenly even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by tiny disease organisms living in the dirt that block the water tubes inside the plant stem. Rotating tomatoes with non-related crops like corn breaks this disease cycle in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela bibioo ko ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. No hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ naa lɛ mli. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛ amɛhe bɛ tsakpaa, tamɔ ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa hela nɛɛ sɛɛkuu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpaa.

english: Why are my garden eggs and peppers getting dark holes and rotting before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmeii diji ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛhooɔ lɛ?

english: Dark holes and rotting fruit are caused by fruit flies laying eggs inside young fruits or fungal rot thriving in crowded leaves. Pruning extra leaves so air can blow through the plant keeps the fruits dry and protected.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ buji diji kɛ aduawai ni fiteɔ baa ji aduawai amli ŋmeii ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ aduawai bibii amli lɛ. loo ŋmeii ni egbo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ anɔ. Baai ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli Ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ebuɔ he.

english: When is the best time for me to clear my farmland before the main rainy season begins?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie midumɔi lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi?

english: Clearing land is best done towards the end of the dry season, around late February or March. This gives weeds time to dry out and be cleared so your land is clean and ready as soon as the first major rains drop in April.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa naagbee, yɛ February loo March naagbee gbɛ. Enɛ baaha jwɛi lɛ aná be ni amɛgbi ni ajie amɛ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atse ni efee klalo kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ba yɛ April mli pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build healthy green leaves and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay tiny even when the stems and leaves grow very big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii eyɛ mli akɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ekwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: When soil is packed too hard or has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing big leaves above ground instead of expanding its tubers underneath.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ eshishi lɛ.

english: Why do my cowpea crops produce mostly leaves and very few beans when I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai babaoo ni ewoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen food from the air. Adding extra nitrogen fertilizer tricks the plant into growing bushy leaves instead of flowering and making pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tso lɛ akwɛ̃ baai bibii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni efee ŋmeii.

english: How does muddy water from nearby galamsey sites affect the crops I plant on my farm?
ga: muddy water from Te Ramsey ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ saa ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Water polluted with heavy mud and chemical waste coats root systems and hardens soil, preventing crops from absorbing clean water and nutrients, which causes them to stunt or die.
ga: Nu ni sũ ni tsii kɛ tsofai fɔji ewo mli lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli waa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ loo amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees grow better when I plant plantains next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have big leaves that shield young cocoa trees from heat and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ latsaa he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is stressed by intense heat and dry soil, or when there are not enough tiny insects around to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ ha tso lɛ hao. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee bɔɔlu ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap and spreading viruses, or by the plant trying to protect itself from harsh sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ tsei ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black rotten patches on the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by a shortage of calcium in the growing fruit, which happens when dry spells and irregular watering stop roots from drawing up soil minerals properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkajie shika tsuru kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain plants take so much longer to produce fruit when I let many shoots grow around one stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni mihaa ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ yɛ tso kome he lɛ?

english: When too many shoots grow around one main plant, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, taking away energy needed for the main plant to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ tso wulu kome he lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni tso titri lɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo lɛ baa.

english: Why do my yam vines start drying up and turning yellow at the end of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ miije shishi egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ tamɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally wither when the underground tuber has finished growing and storing food, which is the plant's way of showing that the yam is mature and ready to harvest.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji agbe ŋmeii lɛ adumɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ naa pɛ. Enɛ ji gbɛ ni tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ etsɔɔ akɛ sweet potatoes lɛ eda ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn quickly in intense heat. They require partial shade from crops like plantains and regular mulching around the roots to trap moisture and survive the dry Harmattan months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ko kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ plantains kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe daa lɛ amli. shishifãi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ Harmattan nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa flowers need tiny insects called midges for pollination. High temperatures, dry weather, or spraying strong insecticides during the flowering stage can kill these beneficial midges or cause the tree to shed flowers to conserve water.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ he miihia kooloi bibii. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ yɛ pollination, hulutsoo ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi. Aloo, tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ babaoo yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ agbe kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ loo eha tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni akɛbu nu he.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves and delicate root systems that cannot handle strong, direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted beside them to shield them from high heat and retain soil moisture during their early growth stage.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ dɔlɛ ni fe nine naa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ shishijee bei ni shwereɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it really necessary for me to put tall wooden stakes next to my yam vines?
ga: Ehe bahia waa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi. Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ?

english: Yes, yam vines naturally climb. Staking elevates the leaves off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight for photosynthesis, which direct energy into growing larger tubers underground while preventing leaf diseases from wet soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha fotosintɛsis. ni kudɔɔ hewalɛ koni ekɛ bulb agboi akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tso helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa.

english: Look closely at the small buds or nodes along the stem where leaves used to grow. These buds should point upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down causes the sprouts to bend backwards, wasting energy and reducing tuber yield.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. loo nodes bibii Ebɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi he ni tsutsu lɛ baai lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ hiɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwu lɛ atsɔ sɛɛ. Efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa tuber yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Maize seeds need steady moisture to germinate and establish roots. If you plant in dry soil before rainy season fully begins, high soil temperatures can burn the seeds, or heat and insects can destroy them before they sprout.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni yɔɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi. Kɛji odu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Aloo dɔlɛ kɛ kooloi bibii baanyɛ afite dumɔwui dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the leaf tips in a V-pattern indicate that the soil lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for green leaf growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted animal manure will help solve this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ V su mli, ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai eŋɔli lɛ adalɛ Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant harvest is done, those roots decompose and release natural fertilizer into the soil for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛji akpa tsei lɛ pɛ. Nakai shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛjieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating with different crops keeps the soil balanced and breaks pest lifecycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers cover the ground around their crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi haa he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass is called mulching. It acts like a blanket to keep the soil cool, stop soil moisture from evaporating in hot weather, and prevent weeds from getting light to sprout.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ naa koni ekaho yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ kɛtsɔ la nɔ

english: Why do I see ragged holes and small black droppings inside the leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni ekpɔtɔ kɛ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the growing center of the plant. Checking your field early and applying neem seed extract or recommended insecticides into the leaf funnel will stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ mli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ neem dumɔwui amli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo baai lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni akpa amɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress, such as sudden hot dry spells, insufficient water, or nutrient imbalances in the soil. Consistent watering and protecting soil with mulch help keep the plant stable enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei kɛ haomɔi, tamɔ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ kpe. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ejaaa Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ buɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and weak roots that burn easily under full sunlight. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the air cool and preserving soil moisture so the young plants can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do I need to heap the soil into big mounds before planting my seed yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ okɛ muji agbo ko ato dani odu ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Yam tubers grow deep under the ground and need soft, loose earth to expand fully. Mounding loosens the soil so the tuber can grow large without struggling against hard dirt, and it prevents water from soaking the root and rotting it.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli edɔ koni egbɛ eshwa kwraa. Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni bulbs lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawuu. ni etsĩ nu naa koni ekatsɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni efite

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Maize needs a lot of nitrogen to grow strong, so planting them together naturally feeds your soil and gives your maize better yield.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsina ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni enyɛ eda waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni adu yɛ he kome yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni ebaaha ŋmãa yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when many small shoots grow around the main trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ daa bibioo nɛkɛ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso wulu lɛ he.

english: The small shoots (suckers) drink the same water and eat the same soil nutrients as the main tree. Cutting away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, allowing the main tree to keep all its strength for a large bunch.
ga: Tso bibii lɛ (tso lɛ) nuɔ nu kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni amɛyeɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ tamɔ tso titri lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ahi shi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni no baaha tso titri lɛ ahiɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ mli akɛ kuu agbo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much water. When stressed, the plant saves its energy to stay alive rather than making fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔ ni jɛ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nu babaoo mli lɛ he. Kɛ́ haomɔ ba Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tsei baawo yibii lɛ, amɛbuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants turn yellow and curl up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and curling can be caused by cassava mosaic disease spread by tiny insects, or simply drought stress. The plant sheds leaves to save water, but severe curling usually means insects are damaging the crop.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ loo hɔmɔ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ aba. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni naa wa tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii miifite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: What causes the small holes and powdery dirt inside my maize stalks and leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ powda ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch on the leaves and tunnel into the stalk to feed. They weaken the plant from the inside, preventing ears of corn from growing properly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji stem borers ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛboteɔ stem lɛ mli koni amɛye nii. Amɛhaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ emli. Etsiɔ ŋmãa toi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This condition is called blossom end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is forming, often caused by irregular watering or dry soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot ni ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ ewo fɔfɔi lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ enɛ baa.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my maize seed after the first rains fall?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the ground. Planting after the very first light rain is risky because the soil can dry out quickly, causing young seeds to sprout and die.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yɛ oshara ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya, ni no haa dumɔwui bibii kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and quickly steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nourishment.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip in a V-pattern usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an important food for green growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or rich farmyard compost to the soil will help turn the leaves green again.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi yɛ V su mli yɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ fɔɔ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans on the same land where I grow maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches your soil, reducing the amount of chemical fertilizer you need for your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni he hiaa bo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why should I place fertilizer a few inches away from my crop stem instead of touching it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi 2-3 moŋ fe ni mata he?

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn and damage the plant tissue. Putting it a short distance away in the soil allows the roots to safely absorb the nutrients without harming the main stem.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ shãa aba ni efite tso lɛ fãji. Kɛ́ okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kukuoo ko Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ shweshweeshwe ni eyeee tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ awui.

english: Cassava roots rot mainly when water collects around them in heavy or poorly drained soil. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots remain dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ babaoo kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ hiɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl upward and stop growing thick foliage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa baai ni mli tse lɛ shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by small insects like whiteflies spreading a plant virus, or by extreme heat and dry conditions. Keeping the soil damp with mulch and controlling insects early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni gbɛɔ tsei amli helai eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kooloi bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ mra lɛ he miihia waa. Ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ mli awa.

english: Why do my yam leaves develop dark spots and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which thrives in damp conditions. Staking yam vines off the wet ground keeps leaves dry and lowers the chance of disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ Kɛ́ ajie sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ agbi ni ebaaha helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed small pods—known as cherelle wilt—when the tree lacks enough nutrients, shade, or water, or when attacked by bugs like capsids. Proper shade management and feeding the soil helps save more pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ jieɔ ŋmeii bibii. Ale lɛ hu akɛ cherry wilt. Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii, hulutsoo, loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids tutua amɛ lɛ, hulutsoo nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ baanyɛ ahere pods babaoo ayiwala.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, irregular watering, or lack of soil nutrients. Consistent watering at the roots and adding organic manure stops flower drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni afɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli woɔ mli lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep, and heavy fruit bunches make the plant top-heavy. Supporting the plants with wooden Y-props and planting windbreak trees around your farm protects them from falling.
