ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Ni aduawai akutsei ni tsii baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. Tsei ni akɛ nibii ni tamɔ Y fiɔ sɛɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are my sweet orange trees bearing fruits that taste sour instead of sweet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso ni ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni mli edɔ moŋ fe ni ŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Oranges need plenty of sunlight, adequate potassium in the soil, and proper water while ripening to build sugars. Poor soil nutrition or picking the fruit too early before full maturity leads to a sour taste.
ga: Hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa he hiaa ŋmeii. Potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni nu ni sa he miihia lɛ be mli ni ekwɛ koni efee sugar. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii loo aduawai lɛ ni ajieɔ oya tsɔ dani ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ baa.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them directly under the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides living shade and keeps the soil cool and moist while the cocoa grows.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, yɛ Emasɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do extension workers tell me to cut off the extra small shoots growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? Surplus ni miida yɛ Mi dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ eje kpo.

english: The extra small shoots (suckers) steal food, water, and sunlight from the main plantain tree. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough energy to produce large bunches.
ga: Tsoi bibii krokomɛi (tsoi) juɔ niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu wulu lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ashishifãi 1 loo 2 pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo niji wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are usually a sign that the maize plant is hungry for nitrogen, an essential plant food. Adding a small amount of urea fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure near the stem helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tso lɛ. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ urea fioo loo kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer a short distance away from the plant stem instead of dumping it right on top of it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Placing fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's skin and delicate roots. Placing it a few inches away allows the spreading roots to safely absorb the nutrients from the wet soil.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ shishifãi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ amɛ to he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the central leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai amli kɛ muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant where it is dark and moist, so applying recommended natural or chemical sprays directly into that funnel early in the morning helps get rid of them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli ewo duŋ ni edɔ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofa loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ shwie tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie amɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when there is plenty of water in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigboi trukaa ni amɛmiigbi eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil disease that blocks water from traveling up inside the stem. Once infected, the plant cannot recover, so it is best to remove it and avoid planting tomatoes or peppers in that spot next season.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji shikpɔŋ hela ko ni haaa nu akabote tso lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ hela lɛ emɔ tso lɛ pɛ lɛ, enyɛŋ ehiɛ ahi ehe nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie lɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ tomato loo ŋmɔtɔ ni ooodu yɛ nakai he lɛ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds away from my young crops as soon as they start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ mitsei bibii lɛ amli kɛji amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your plants. Clearing them early gives your crops the space and nutrients they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni sũ lɛ yɔɔ kɛha otsei lɛ waa. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by severe heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch during hot spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers and make fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ha tsei lɛ miihao. Kɛ́ akɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli fũu pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when heavy rains fall for a long time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field without draining, the roots drown and rot, which is why planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water run away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains get destroyed by tiny black insects while stored in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji kpata mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ ahiɛ beni akɛtoɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Those insects are grain weevils that multiply rapidly if the corn is stored while still damp. Drying your maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are very hard before storing them in sealed bags keeps the weevils away.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ ji ŋmaa ŋmeii ni faa oya kɛji akɛ ajie ŋmãa be mli ni edɔ lolo lɛ. Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa dani okɛwo kotokui ni atsĩ naa mli koni ŋmãa lɛ akabote mli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from older lower leaves up to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops grow better when I leave dry grass on top of the soil instead of burning my farm clearing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mishi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashã he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving dry grass on the soil creates a natural blanket called mulch. This blanket keeps the soil cool, holds water during dry spells, and decomposes into natural manure, whereas burning destroys nutrients and kills helpful soil organisms.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulch baa. Nɛkɛ tsɔne nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Too nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ be mli ni shãa fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni egbeɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: What makes the leaves on my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni haa baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids feeding under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Spraying neem leaf extract or mild soapy water helps control these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛji kɛbaa lɛ anɔ. Neem tso lɛ mli nu loo samla ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants wilting in the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ?

english: Tomatoes wilt in hot afternoon heat when the leaves lose water faster than the roots can absorb it, or if a soil disease is blocking water movement inside the stem. Mulching around the base keeps root zones cool and reduces water stress.
ga: Tomato baagbo yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli. Beni baai lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. aloo kɛji hela ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu he haomɔ baa shi.

english: Why are my cocoa flowers dropping off the tree branches without forming young cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei aniji anɔ ni efeee kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees shed their flowers if the weather gets too dry or if tiny insects called midges are missing to transfer pollen between flowers. Planting shade trees keeps moisture in the farm and provides a safe habitat for these helpful pollinators.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ midge lɛ laajeɔ koni ekɛ pollen aya fɔfɔi ateŋ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ehaa nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ nɛɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do some of my maize plants produce big cobs while others planted right next to them stay small and stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiwo ŋmeii wuji lɛ? yɛ be mli ni tsei krokomɛi ni adu yɛ Ani amɛji bibii ni amɛhe ejɔ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds out properly ensures every plant gets enough food to develop full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa haa tsei fɛɛ náa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot in the ground when heavy rains fall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy, but heavy rains on flat land cause standing water that drowns the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to run off so the tubers stay firm and dry.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shi nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ kplanaa lɛ nɔ, ni eha nu lɛ damɔ shi aahu kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mii nu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛgbi.

english: Why is my flooded lowland rice turning a rusty reddish-brown color and growing slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni edaaa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Reddish-brown leaves in flooded rice fields usually mean there is too much iron dissolved in the stagnant water, which damages the roots. Draining the field for a few days lets air back into the soil so the rice can recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dade ni mli edɔ babaoo yɛ nu ni damɔ shi lɛ mli. Enɛ baafite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eha ŋmãa lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over so easily during small windstorms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa fioo mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily because they have shallow roots, especially if microscopic worms or root borers have weakened the underground base. Staking fruiting plants with wood poles and planting pest-free suckers keeps them firmly rooted.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii bibii loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ eha shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo lɛ egbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni akɛwoɔ yibii amli lɛ wo tso mli, ni adu tsei ni tsɛŋemɔ helai bɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored seed yams start sprouting inside the barn months before the rainy season arrives?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Yams wake up from dormancy and sprout early when storage spaces become warm and stuffy. Storing seed yams in a cool, well-ventilated barn shielded from direct sunlight keeps them resting until planting time.
ga: Sweet potatoes teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ wɔɔhe mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ́ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ sweet potato dumɔwui ato tsũ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli mli. Kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he ni abuɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashiɔ dumɔ be mli.

english: Why is my pawpaw tree flowering heavily but never bearing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tso fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Pawpaw plants can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male pawpaw trees produce many flowers on long stems to shed pollen, but they cannot produce fruits themselves. You need female or hermaphrodite trees on your farm, with at least one male nearby for pollination, to get fruit.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Pawpaw tsei hii woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ tsei kakadaji ni jieɔ pollen kpo lɛ anɔ. shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii kɛjɛ ehe Esa akɛ oná yei loo hermaphrodite tsei yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ hoo lɛ, nuu kome ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni ekɛ pollination baawo yibii.

english: What are the soft brown threads hanging out of my corn cobs, and why are they important?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai kpãa ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fĩ mi ŋmãa lɛ he lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa lɛ?

english: Those threads are called silk, and each thread is attached to a single potential kernel of corn. The silks catch pollen carried by the wind from the top of the corn plant (the tassel). Every silk that gets pollinated will form one full grain of corn on the cob.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai kpãai lɛ akɛ siliki. Ni akɛ kpãa lɛ eko fɛɛ eko fĩɔ ŋmãa dumɔwu kome ni baanyɛ afee ŋmãa lɛ he. Siliki lɛ mɔ̃ɔ pollen ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tso (tassel) lɛ yiteŋ lɛ. Siliki fɛɛ siliki ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa kome ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my watermelon vines produce flowers that fall off without making any watermelons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon tso lɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ watermelon ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Watermelon plants grow two distinct types of flowers: male flowers and female flowers. The male flowers bloom first just to provide pollen and naturally drop off. Only the female flowers—which have a small round green miniature fruit at their base—will turn into full watermelons after bees transfer pollen to them.
ga: Watermelon tsei woɔ fɔfɔi srɔtoi enyɔ: fɔfɔi hii kɛ fɔfɔi yei. Fɔfɔi hii fɔɔ klɛŋklɛŋ koni amɛŋmɛ gbɛ ni pollen lɛ agbo yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Fɔfɔi yei lɛ pɛ yɛ aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shishitoo lɛ pɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ watermelon ni eyi obɔ beni ŋmeii kɛ pollen eha lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my sweet pepper flowers drop off during the peak heat season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress and deliberately drop their flowers to save energy and water. Providing partial shade or ensuring adequate soil moisture during hot periods helps the plant keep its blossoms and set fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ni amɛjɛɔ amɛyiŋ amɛshwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo fã ko ha loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai amli.

english: Yellowing along the main central vein of older lower leaves is a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency. The maize plant is moving available nitrogen from its older leaves up to feed the newer top growth, indicating your soil needs nitrogen fertilizer or organic compost.
ga: Yellow ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Abele tsei miitsi nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛmiijɛ baai momoi lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling upward and looking crinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ nɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites living on the underside of the leaf, or by a virus transmitted by whiteflies. As these insects feed on the leaf juices, they cause the leaf to distort and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ. Amɛhaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why is my cassava plant flowering above ground when I only want roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ miifɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be mli ni nɔ pɛ ni he hiaa mi ji shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi?

english: Flowering is a natural phase in the growth cycle of a mature cassava plant and does not harm tuber growth. The plant continues to store food energy in its underground roots while flowering, so you do not need to cut the flowers off.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko yɛ ŋmei ni eda lɛ dalɛ mli. ni eyeee ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ awui Tsei yaa nɔ amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe ehiaaa ni ofolɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense sunlight and struggle to survive extreme heat. Fast-growing plantain plants provide broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, supplying the shade and moisture young cocoa seedlings need during their first two years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa shishi, ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hɔɔŋ. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small shoots growing at the base of my plantain stand?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantain lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: The main plantain stem shares nutrients and water with all the young shoots (suckers) growing around its base. Removing extra suckers leaves only one or two strong ones, ensuring the main plant gets maximum energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ tso titri lɛ jaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛ ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ baashwɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves out in full sunlight to create food through photosynthesis. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground where they might rot, allowing the plant to collect maximum sunlight and send energy down to grow larger yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ ashwã kɛyashɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgboi yɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ buaa hulu la babaoo naa bɔ ni eeenyɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my maize seeds fail to grow even after I buy good seeds from the town market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mihe dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ? Ani ojɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ momo?

english: Seeds need proper moisture and soil warmth to wake up. Even good quality seeds will fail to sprout if planted in bone-dry soil, buried too deeply, or stored in hot places before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ dɔlɛ ni sa koni amɛte shi. Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ po nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ sũ ni mli egbi tamɔ wui amli, afu amɛ tsɔ, loo akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ dani adu.

english: How do I know if the seeds I saved from my last oil palm harvest are good enough to plant again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmei fɔ ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ekoŋŋ?

english: Seeds from harvested crops often lose their strength or produce weaker plants. Buying certified seeds from agricultural officers ensures higher yields and resistance to diseases compared to re-using old seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi loo ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Dumɔwui ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi ema nɔ mi lɛ ni ooohe lɛ baaha oná yibii babaoo ni helai nyɛŋ ashi bo jogbaŋŋ fe beni okɛ dumɔwui momo tsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants burning and falling off during the bright sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that cannot endure harsh direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantain beside them provides temporary shade to protect them until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ Emasɛi lɛ baaha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko aba koni ebu tso lɛ he kɛyashi ebaada.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems. If underground pests damage their roots or if the soil is too loose, the heavy weight of the fruit bunch easily pulls the entire tree out of the ground.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite eshishifãi lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse tsɔ. Yibii ni tsii ni abua naa lɛ baajie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop harvests every year even though I plant at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi lɛ? Nɛgbɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil every season. Without adding animal manure, compost, or fertilizer, or rotating crops like beans to replenish the soil, the ground gets tired and hungry.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he, loo atsake ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii koni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Etɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni hɔmɔ hu baaye lɛ.

english: How does leaving dried grass around the base of my crops help them grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mishiɔ yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dried leaves or grass keeps the ground cool, prevents moisture from drying up in the heat, and stops weeds from competing with your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekagbi yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekɛ oŋmɔshi nibii akaye akaŋ.

english: Why is burning my farm weeds before planting bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the living earthworms and helpful organic matter that make topsoil rich. Slashing weeds and letting them decay into the soil naturally builds food for future plants.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahiɛ. Jwɛi ni afoɔ ni aŋmɛɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛgboi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa niyenii baa wɔsɛɛ tsei anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with bushy leaves but give me small underground tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ baai shi ehaa mi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil or too much shade causes cassava plants to spend all their energy growing leaves and stems above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo babaoo haa ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni jɛɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or poor nutrients in the soil during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Yellow maize leaves are usually a sign that the plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaves to produce plant food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baa ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni he hia koni baai lɛ afee tsei niyenii.

english: What is the main advantage of growing my tomatoes inside a greenhouse instead of directly on open land?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi titrii ni yɔɔ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: A greenhouse protects your tomatoes from heavy rain, harsh sun, and insect pests, creating a controlled environment so your crops can grow healthier and produce better yields.
ga: Greenhouse buɔ o-tomato lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe. Bɔɔ shihilɛ ko ni akudɔɔ koni onibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Does placing a shade net over my vegetable bed really help protect my crops from diseases?
ga: Ani shade netting ni mikɛwoɔ mi-vegetables tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ahe diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, shade nets block harmful insect pests from reaching your plants and spreading viral diseases, while also protecting delicate leaves from severe sunlight and beating rain.
ga: Hɛɛ, shade netting yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akashɛ otsei lɛ ahe ni amɛkagbɛ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli baa lɛ ashwã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: How often do I need to water tomato plants grown inside a greenhouse compared to those outside?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo tomato tsei ni adu yɛ greenhouse mli lɛ nu kɛ akɛto tsei ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ ahe?

english: Greenhouse tomatoes do not get natural rainfall, so they need consistent watering at the root level every 1 to 2 days, whereas outdoor crops depend on rainfall and natural soil moisture.
ga: Tomatoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ náaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni awo tomato nu yɛ shishifã lɛ he daa gbi 1 kɛyashi 2, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ damɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my young seedlings look weak and wilted right after I move them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings experience transplant shock when moved. Their roots need a few days to settle into the new soil and absorb water properly before the plant brightens up and grows strong.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ baanu shoofeemɔ he kɛji akɛ adu amɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni amɛmu nu jogbaŋŋ dani tsei lɛ akpɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of leaves but producing very few flowers and fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes plants to spend all their energy making big green leaves instead of fruits. Using a balanced fertilizer with phosphorus and potassium encourages flowering and fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii, ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants start falling over once they get tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbee shi kɛji amɛdara pɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally weak and cannot hold up the heavy weight of their own branches and fruits. Tying them to wooden stakes keeps them upright and prevents diseases from ground contact.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛniji kɛ amɛyibii ni tsii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akpɛtɛ tso he lɛ, ehaa edamɔ shi jaŋŋ, ni ehaaa helai ashɛ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do some crops struggle when they are first planted but then start growing well on their own later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ waa kɛ́ adu amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ? Shi no sɛɛ lɛ, ebɔi dalɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe sɛɛ mli?

english: As plants grow older, their root systems go deeper into the soil to find water and nutrients on their own, making them tougher and more resilient to harsh conditions.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda Amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtao nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Enɛ haa amɛhe waa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and dries up their pollen, causing the flowers to drop off. Giving plants adequate water and partial shade during hot spells helps preserve the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from too much water or from a pest attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu babaoo loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko miigbe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Overwatering causes leaves to turn soft, yellow, and droopy while the soil remains wet. Pest damage usually leaves visible holes, spotted leaves, or insects under the foliage.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nu wo mli fe nine lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ afee blɛoo, amɛfee ŋmɔŋ, ni amɛbaagbee shi be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa bu, baai ni yɔɔ srɔtoi, loo kooloi bibii baa baa lɛ ashishi.

english: Will my land get better at growing tomatoes if I keep planting them on the same plot every season?
ga: Ani mishikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛji midu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: No, planting tomatoes in the same spot continuously exhausts specific soil nutrients and builds up soil diseases. Rotating tomatoes with legumes or maize keeps the soil healthy and reduces pests.
ga: Dabi, tomato ni adu yɛ he kome lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ afite be fɛɛ be, ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai baaba. Tomato ni akɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen, which maize needs a lot of to stay green and grow. It can also happen when the field stays waterlogged for too long, preventing the roots from breathing and taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi he miihia lɛ babaoo koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ ŋmɔji amli nu eyi mli obɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu ni amɛye niyenii.

english: Why does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my farm make my maize crop grow better in the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the dirt. When the crop is harvested, that extra natural fertilizer stays in the ground to feed the maize that comes after it.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear away all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that cannot handle full sunlight and hot winds. Leaving taller trees provides shade and keeps the air moist, protecting the young plants until they are strong enough to handle more sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni oooshi lɛ baaha hulutsoo aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo.

english: Does tying my yam vines up on tall wooden stakes really help produce bigger tubers under the ground?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni akɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa diɛŋtsɛ ni afeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yes, lifting the vines onto stakes helps the leaves spread out to catch direct sunlight. Leaves use sunlight to make food for the plant, and that extra food is sent down to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, wain tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii kɛha tso lɛ. Ni akɛ nakai niyenii krɛdɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground if I leave them after the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When heavy rains fill the soil with water for too long, air cannot reach the cassava roots. Starved of air in wet mud, the roots easily catch fungal diseases that cause them to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ ashɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe. yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ muji ni mli efɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa amɛgboiɔ oya.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. The stress makes the plant abandon its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa lɛ nɔ kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ trukaa lɛ nɔ. Haomɔ haa tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato kɛha wala.

english: Why shouldn't I let all the small shoots grow around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii bibii shwereɔ yɛ mi plantains titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: If you leave too many suckers, they fight with the main plantain tree for water, soil nutrients, and light. Cutting them back so only one or two remain lets the main tree produce a bigger, heavier bunch.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo Ekɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ baawu koni ená nu. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la. Kɛ́ afo mli koni ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ feɔ ŋmei ni da ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ.

english: What happens to my maize harvest if I plant seeds very close together to fit more into my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ bɔni afee ni ekɛ miŋmɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting too close forces the maize stalks to compete fiercely for light and water. Instead of getting more corn, you will end up with tall, thin stalks that fall easily and yield small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmãa babaoo Obaagbe naa kɛ ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbeeɔ shi oya ni ewoɔ dumɔwui bibii loo ŋmãa ni nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do caterpillars attack and eat the heart of my young maize leaves right after the first rains arrive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baa koni amɛbaye mi-abɛi bibii lɛ atsui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Warm weather followed by early rain creates the perfect conditions for Fall Armyworm moths to lay eggs. The hatching caterpillars hide inside the tender funnel of the leaves where it is cool and soft to chew.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha fɛ̃i be mli ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui. Kplukai ni efɔ lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ baai lɛ amli gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee blɛoo kɛji akɛ ashɛre.

english: Weeds are wild plants built to survive harsh conditions, dry weather, and poor soil with deep roots and fast seeds. Because they are naturally tougher, they will quickly steal all the water and plant food unless you clear them early.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni abɔ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛhe wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ oya. Ja ojie amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: Yellow leaves are a clear sign that your crop is missing essential nutrients in the soil, usually nitrogen, or suffering from flooded roots. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer feeds the soil and helps the leaves regain their healthy green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni oduɔ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji nitrogen. aloo shishifãi eyi mli obɔ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná hewalɛ ni eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater stays trapped in the soil without draining, which suffocates the tubers and allows fungal rot to develop. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water flow away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ bote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu bɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What is eating small holes into the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-bibii ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ yeli?

english: Small ragged holes in corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm that feed on young plant shoots. Checking your fields early in the morning lets you catch them before they multiply and damage your entire harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ fall armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔji lɛ amli leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ amɛ dani amɛshwere ni amɛfite oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings fall over and die right at the ground level soon after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This happens due to a fungal issue called damping-off, which grows rapidly in overly wet, crowded nursery beds. Giving seedlings proper spacing and avoiding overwatering keeps the stems dry and strong.
ga: Enɛ baa mli yɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ damping off, ni daa oya yɛ tsɛji akwɛmɔhei ni efɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ amli lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ he ko ni sa ni okpa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets pest populations grow in the ground. Rotating maize with crops like groundnuts or beans naturally restores nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ yaa hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abele tsakemɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: How can I test if my soil is healthy enough to grow vegetables before planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu aduawai dani madu?

english: Healthy soil is dark, crumbly, holds water well without pooling, and contains earthworms. You can also bring a soil sample to your local agricultural extension office to test for missing nutrients before spending money on seeds.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ su yɛ ediŋ, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ehiɛɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ ehe kpaaa gbee. ni eyɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ hu aya okwaayeli he nitsumɔhe ni yɔɔ okpokpaa lɛ nɔ lɛ koni oyakwɛ kɛji niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ yɔɔ mli dani okɛ shika awo dumɔwui ahe.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crop rows very close together to fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ ooodu tsei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni tsei babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded together, they compete for sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients, resulting in tall, weak plants with small yields. Giving crops the recommended spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and air to produce heavy yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ ni amɛhe waaa shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa. Kɛ́ aha tsei lɛ he ni esa akɛ amɛhi shi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn under full direct sunlight, and their shallow roots dry out quickly. Keeping big shade trees or planting plantains alongside cocoa provides a living canopy that keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Ni shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ baagbi oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up and droop during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl during hot afternoons to protect themselves and conserve internal moisture. Covering the surrounding soil with dried grass or mulch prevents water from evaporating quickly out of the hot ground.
ga: Shi lɛ ni ebɔle ehe yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli koni ebu ehe ni eha hulutsoo ahi emli. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekajɛ he ni edɔ lɛ oya.

english: Why do tiny insects bore holes into my stored cowpeas inside my storage room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwieɔ tsina ŋmeii ni ato yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weevil insects lay microscopic eggs on pea pods while still in the field, which hatch inside your storage bags and eat the seeds. Drying your harvest completely under the sun and storing grains in sealed hermetic bags starves insects of air and preserves your yield.
ga: Weevil lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni anaaa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ. Enɛ baafo yɛ onitoo kotoku lɛ mli ni eye dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩ kwraa yɛ hulu lɛ shishi ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hɔmɔ aye kooloi ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because direct sunlight scorches their soft leaves and dries out the soil. Planting plantains or leaving larger shade trees protects the young cocoa until its roots grow deep enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ loo tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ ni ashiɔ lɛ buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts together on the same land as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that can pull nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. This acts as a natural fertilizer that helps your maize grow greener and stronger without buying extra artificial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa oŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohe ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfee.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning dark purple instead of green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on young maize are usually a sign that the soil lacks phosphorus. Phosphorus is a vital soil nutrient that helps crops build strong root systems and absorb water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosfɔs ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtswaa shishifãi ni wa ni amɛmɔɔ nu.

english: Why does my yam crop grow huge green leaves above ground but produces very small tubers under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: When crops receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, they put all their energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Using a balanced fertilizer with more potassium helps the yam grow big tubers.
ga: Kɛ tsei nine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-sweet potato lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Curled and yellowing leaves on cassava are typically caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this virus from destroying your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ yucca baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ hela nɛɛ akafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to suddenly turn black and rot on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ trukaa ni amɛgboi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during wet, rainy seasons when sunlight cannot reach the trees. Pruning shade trees and removing rotten pods stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ ni aaafolɔ ashwie shi ni ajie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do I see small worms hiding in the leaves of my maize plants and eating holes through them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa tsei ahe baai amli ni amɛyeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: These worms are Fall Armyworms, a pest that attacks the growing tips of maize. Early spraying with recommended insecticides or applying clean neem leaf extract kills the caterpillars before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni tutuaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra Aloo, kɛ akɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu ni he tse tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over whenever a small wind blows on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ baatswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be destroyed by microscopic worms called nematodes or by poor drainage. Planting suckers deeper and mulching around the stem strengthens the roots against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii lɛ amli shɔŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmeii awo tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaawaje shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot or when the soil gets too dry. Keeping the soil moist and providing partial shade prevents the flowers from drying out before they form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo lɛ, ebaatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my pineapples stay small and sour even after spending many months on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pineapple lɛ ji bibioo ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Pineapples require proper spacing and plenty of potassium in the soil to grow sweet and large. Planting them too close together forces them to compete for sunlight and nutrients, making the fruits small.
ga: Pineapple he miihia ni ekɛ he ni sa kɛ potassium babaoo awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee agbo. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, yibii lɛ faaa.

english: What are crop hormones, and how do they actually help my plants grow?
ga: Mɛni ji tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɛkɛ tsofai nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa?

english: Crop hormones are natural signals inside plants that tell them when to grow roots, shoot out new leaves, or produce fruits. When you apply extra hormones, it gives weak or slow-growing crops a boost to grow faster and yield more.
ga: Tso mli tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadii ni yɔɔ tsei amli ni tsɔɔ amɛ be ni esa akɛ amɛkwɛ̃, amɛwo baai heei, loo amɛwo yibii. Kɛ okɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, Ebaaha tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni edaa blɛoo lɛ aná hewalɛ ni amɛdara oya ni amɛwo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I use growth boosters on all my crops like maize, cassava, and cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nibii ni haa shweremɔ yaa hiɛ lɛ atsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ kookoo nɔ?

english: Yes, growth boosters work on almost all crops, but the way you apply them and the amount you use will depend on whether it is a vegetable, a grain, or a tree crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ nibii ni haa tsei daa lɛ atsu nii yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ tsei fɛɛ anɔ. Shi bɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii ohaa kɛ bɔ ni okɛtsuɔ nii ohaa lɛ damɔ kɛji eji aduawai, dumɔwui, loo tso nɔ.

english: Why do some farm medicines come as powder while others come as liquid?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofai komɛi baa yɛ powda mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni tsofai komɛi baa yɛ nu mli lɛ?

english: Powders are often easier to store for a long time without spoiling, while liquids dissolve very quickly in water. Both perform the same work as long as they are mixed correctly.
ga: Akɛ powder toɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee oya. Yɛ be mli ni nu lɛ shwieɔ nu mli oya waa lɛ. Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ kome, kɛji akɛ akɛfutu amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the right way to mix powder medicine with water so it doesn't form lumps?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ tsofa powda afutu nu mli koni ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko?

english: First, mix the powder with a small amount of clean water in a small container to form a smooth mixture, then pour that mixture into your big sprayer tank filled with water.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, okɛ powda lɛ afutu nu ni mli tse fioo ko yɛ tsɛnsi bibioo ko mli koni efee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ nakai tsofa ni okɛfutu lɛ awo baagi agbo ko ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together in the same sprayer?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ henɔi enyɔ baafutu yɛ tsɔne kome mli?

english: Not always. Some medicines react badly when mixed together, which can spoil the medicine or burn your crop leaves. Always ask an officer before mixing two different chemicals.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Tsofai komɛi kɛ amɛhe futu mli lɛ ehiii kwraa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa lɛ afite loo eshã tso lɛ baai. Bi nɔyeli lɛ mli onukpai lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ tsofai srɔtoi enyɔ afutu.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray liquid medicine on my crop leaves?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni ji nu afɔ mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Early morning or cool late afternoon is best because the leaves absorb the medicine easily when the sun is not hot, preventing the liquid from drying up too fast.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo shwane mli ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ tsofa lɛ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ, ni no haaa nu lɛ agbi oya tsɔ.

english: What should I do if heavy rain falls right after I finish spraying my farm?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa beni migbe miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ tsofa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: If it rains within two hours of spraying, the rain will wash the medicine off before the leaves absorb it, and you will likely need to spray again once the leaves dry.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai enyɔ mli beni afɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ Nugbɔ baaho tsofa lɛ he dani baai lɛ aŋɔ. Ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ ekoŋŋ kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi.

english: Will adding more medicine than instructed make my crops grow twice as fast?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo ni mikɛfataa he fe bɔ ni ajieɔ yi lɛ baaha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ada oya shii enyɔ?

english: No, using too much medicine can burn your crop leaves and damage the plant. Plants need just the right amount, similar to how taking too much human medicine makes a person sick.
ga: Dabi, tsofa babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã baai lɛ ni efite tso lɛ. Tsei he miihia bɔ ni sa. Etamɔ bɔ ni tsofai babaoo ni ayeɔ yɛ adesai amli lɛ baanyɛ aha gbɔmɛi aná hela.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning yellow even after I give them fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo mli po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the plant lacks specific minor nutrients or hormones, or that waterlogging or root disease is stopping the plant from taking up the fertilizer you applied.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii loo tsofai ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli fioo, loo akɛ nu ni hoɔ loo shishifã hela miitsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwo mli lɛ.

english: How do I tell if my crop needs a growth booster or a disease medicine?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ nɔ ko ni haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa loo tsofa he miihia amɛ?

english: If your plants look healthy but are growing slowly, they need a growth booster. If you see spots, holes, rotting, or insects on the leaves, they need disease or pest medicine.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ shi eedara blɛoo Ehe miihia ni oná nibii ni haa edara. Kɛji ona ŋmeii, bu, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo ŋmeii ahe tsofa he miihia.

english: Oil palm seedlings should be planted about 29 feet (9 meters) apart, usually in a triangular pattern. Proper spacing ensures each palm gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients to grow strong and produce plenty of fresh fruit bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ adu oil palm dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 9, bei pii lɛ, amɛfeɔ tamɔ koŋ etɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko naa hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo aduawai heei babaoo.

english: What is the recommended distance to leave between coconut seedlings during planting?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ahi ŋmei tsei ateŋ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut seedlings are typically planted about 25 to 30 feet (7.5 to 9 meters) apart. Leaving this space allows their roots to spread and their large canopies to receive enough sunlight without competing with neighboring trees.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduɔ akooshi dumɔwui aaafee ninetalɔi 25 kɛyashi 30 (mitai 7.5 kɛyashi 9) kɛjɛ amɛhe. He nɛɛ ni amɛshiɔ lɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Ni ŋwɛitsu agbo lɛ naa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Why is it important to measure the distance between seedlings instead of just planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu gbɛ ni kã dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, which results in weak trees and poor yields. Proper spacing ensures every plant has room to thrive and give a big harvest.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli, ni no haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How do I make sure my seedlings are planted in straight, evenly spaced rows?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ adu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji ekome?

english: You can use long measuring ropes, pegs, and lining techniques before digging your planting holes. Marking out straight rows makes it much easier to walk through, weed, fertilize, and harvest your farm later.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ kpãa ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe, ŋtayaai, kɛ ŋtayaai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ atsu nii dani okɛ dumɔ bu lɛ atsu nii. Kɛ́ okadi ŋwɛi ŋta ni ja lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ oootsɔ mli, okɛ jwɛi awo mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni obaakpa oŋmɔ lɛ mli nii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to trim or prune the fronds of my palm trees as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mi-palm tso lɛ mli be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Cutting off dry or lower fronds helps the tree direct its energy toward growing new leaves and fruit bunches. Pruning also keeps the farm tidy, prevents pests from hiding in dead leaves, and makes harvesting easier.
ga: Baai ni egboi loo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa baai kɛ aduawai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni afoɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli feɔ fɛo. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe yɛ baai ni egboi amli. ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ feɔ mlɛo

english: How does pruning tree branches help me create clear paths through my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mafee gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: By trimming away low-hanging or overgrown fronds that stick out into the rows, you clear open walkways between your trees. This allows you to carry tools, transport fertilizer, and haul harvested produce without getting blocked.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi loo baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni jeɔ kpo yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ afolɔmɔ. Enɛ baaha gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ aba otsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otereɔ nitsumɔ dadei, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ yaa ni nɔ ko tsiii bo gbɛ.

english: How do I safely prune fronds from my growing coconut or palm trees without damaging them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tso ni miida lɛ baai shweshweeshwe ni mifiteee amɛ?

english: Use a sharp cutlass or pruning chisel to make clean cuts close to the trunk without gouging the stem. Only cut away dry, diseased, or lower fronds that hang beneath the fruit, leaving the healthy green fronds above.
ga: Kɛ tsɔne ni mli wa loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfolɔ tso lɛ he ni he tse ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ he ni ogbalaaa tso lɛ mli. Kpãa baai ni egbi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shwieɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ pɛ. Shi baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do with the branches and fronds that I cut off during pruning?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee tsei niji kɛ baai ni mifo yɛ be mli ni mifoɔ tsei lɛ?

english: Instead of burning them, line the cut fronds neatly between your tree rows. As they rot, they act as mulch that traps soil moisture, stops weed growth, and returns valuable organic food back into the soil.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã lɛ, ŋmɛ baai ni afo lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ otsei lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ amɛgboi lɛ Ebaatsu nii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni jara wa ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Why should I follow the specific planting measurements taught by agricultural extension officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni makwɛ gbɛ pɔtɛɛ ni mi-agricultural extension officer lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Agricultural extension officers share field-tested spacing methods designed for local soils and crop varieties. Following their guidance helps you get the highest possible yield from your land without wasting space or resources.
ga: Agricultural Extension nitsulɔi lɛ jaa gbɛi ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ tsei srɔtoi lɛ. Kɛ́ onyiɛ ŋaawoi nɛɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni oná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni okɛ he loo nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ efiteee.

english: Can I plant quick food crops in the open spaces between my young palm seedlings?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ niyenii ni ayeɔ oya yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ yɛ tsei tsei ateŋ?

english: Yes, while your palm seedlings are still small and haven't shaded the area, you can plant temporary crops like maize, legumes, or vegetables in between the rows to provide food and income while keeping weeds down.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ji bibii ni amɛhaaa he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ hulutsoo po. Obaanyɛ odu be kukuoo mli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa. loo aduawai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ ateŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ shika yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I keep my young crop seedlings under a shaded nursery canopy instead of leaving them out in the open sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahã dumɔwui bibii ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ

english: Young seedlings are very delicate and burn easily in direct sunlight. Keeping them in a protected, shaded nursery keeps the soil moist and shields the tender leaves from high heat until they are strong enough for the main field.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ waaa waa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo he ko ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni abuɔ he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaabu tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: How can I stop stray animals and people from walking through and damaging my young vegetable farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi kɛ gbɔmɛi ni elaaje lɛ anaa koni amɛkaho ni amɛkafite mi-aduawai ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: You can protect your crop field by planting a live hedge of dense shrubs around the boundary or constructing a simple wooden or net fence. Shielding the plot prevents physical damage and keeps your plants safe.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ tsei ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ooodu yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo loo trellis ni oootswa lɛ nɔ. Saa hebuu baatsi gbɔmɔtsoŋ fitemɔ naa ni ebaaha otsei lɛ ahi shi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees need protection from intense, open sunlight to survive. Keeping taller shade trees or planting temporary shelter crops like plantains creates a cool environment that prevents the cocoa leaves from scorching.
ga: Ehe miihia ni abu kakao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he koni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo be kukuoo mli tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni haaa kookoo baai lɛ ashã.

english: What is the best way to store my harvested maize so that insects do not get inside and eat it?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ toɔ? Koni kooloi bibii akaye lɛ?

english: Store thoroughly dried maize inside sealed, airtight bags or metal drums in a covered room. Protecting the grain from open air prevents weevils and pests from entering and destroying your harvest.
ga: Kɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ awo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo dade baagi ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ tsu ko ni aha nɔ mli. Kɛ́ obu odumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote onibii amli ni amɛfite.

english: Why should I cover my planted seeds with mulch or light soil right after sowing them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo shikpɔŋ ni mli tse aha dumɔwui ni adu lɛ anɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu lɛ?

english: Covering seeds protects them from direct heat, keeps the soil moist, and prevents birds or heavy rains from washing them away before they can take root in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ nɔ ko ha dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa okpoi loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛwoɔ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does using a net house benefit my tomato crops compared to planting them in an open field?
ga: Te trellis greenhouse ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-tomato tsei lɛ amɛhaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto amɛdumɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse mli lɛ he?

english: A net house encloses the plants, shielding them from strong winds, scorching sun, and insect pests. This protected space allows tomatoes to grow healthier without getting damaged by outside threats.
ga: Latishi shia lɛ ebɔle tsei lɛ ahe. Buu tsei ahe kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he. hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui He nɛɛ haa tomatoi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ni woɔ mɔ he gbeyei lɛ efiteee lɛ.

english: If I put many crop nursery trays together in one small area, will the seedlings stay safe?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tratii babaoo to he bibioo kome lɛ, ani dumɔwui lɛ baahi shi shweshweeshwe lolo?

english: Grouping nursery trays closely inside a protected enclosure creates a moist micro-environment that keeps seedlings from drying out, as long as they get enough air and are transplanted once they grow larger.
ga: Nibii ni akɛkwɛɔ gbekɛbii lɛ akui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋtayaa ni abuɔ he lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ baa. Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi. Shii abɔ ni amɛyɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ amɛ atsake be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How do windbreak trees help prevent my plantain trees from snapping during heavy rains?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔnei tsiɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting tall, sturdy trees around the border of your farm breaks the power of strong winds, protecting delicate stems and heavy fruit bunches from blowing over during storms.
ga: Tsei kakadaŋŋ agboi ni he wa ni ooodu yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baafite kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ hewalɛ. Ebuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii ahe koni kɔɔyɔɔ akatswa amɛ yɛ ahum be mli.

english: Why should I heap soil over the exposed roots of my cassava plants as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo sũ yɛ ŋmei shishifãi ni jeɔ kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding soil over growing tubers protects them from direct heat and pests like root-boring insects, allowing the tubers to stay safe and expand safely beneath the ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akɛtoɔ bulbs ni miida lɛ nɔ lɛ baabu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ kooloi ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I dry my harvested cocoa beans open on the ground near public walkways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ migbiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ maŋ gbɛjegbɛ ko nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying crops on the open ground leaves them exposed to dust, foot traffic, and animals. Using raised wooden mats or covered raised beds keeps the produce safe and clean.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ lɛ haa sũ, tsɔnei kɛ kooloi baa amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔji ni awo nɔ loo saatsoi ni awo nɔ ni akɛ tsɔji ewo nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii ni anáa lɛ feɔ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhe tseɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to grow, and when the soil does not have enough, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ faaa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct sunlight. They need shade trees or companion crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas, keeping them cool and moist during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground when the rainy season lasts longer than usual?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Excess rain creates waterlogged soil, which cuts off air to the roots. Without oxygen, cassava tubers choke and become vulnerable to fungal infections that rot them underground.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ atsɔ nu. ni ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ, Cassava shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaafee oshara akɛ amɛbaaná tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing any tomatoes during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni aduuu tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and low humidity stress tomato plants. When temperatures get too high, the plant drops its flowers to save energy and water rather than attempting to grow fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei ni mli edɔ waa ni hulutsoo be faaa. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni odu aduawai

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce small bunches when I leave many shoots growing around its base?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain titri lɛ shwereɔ bibii bibii lɛ? Beni ashiɔ ŋmeii babaoo yɛ tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, compete with the main plant for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Pruning all but one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to focus its energy on growing a large bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ tso ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ fɛɛ mli, ja tso lɛ yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ yibii babaoo ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller maize harvests every year if I plant it on the same piece of land without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil over and over. Rotating crops like maize with beans or cowpeas helps put nutrients like nitrogen back into the dirt naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen, kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do fall armyworms feed on my maize leaves mostly at night or early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms yeɔ mi-corn baai lɛ babaoo gbɛkɛ loo leebi lɛ?

english: Armyworms hide inside the center whorl of the plant during the hot afternoon to protect themselves from the sun. They come out to feed when cooler temperatures return at night and dawn.
ga: Asraafoi amli ŋmeii lɛ teɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu lɛ he. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye nii kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba gbɛkɛ kɛ leebi maŋkpa.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves towards sunlight to make food for growing large tubers underground. Staking also lifts leaves off damp ground, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛná niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi

english: Why does chicken manure take longer to make my vegetables grow compared to chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmei heɔ be babaoo dani ehaa aduawai shwereɔ fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizer dissolves quickly in water for plants to drink immediately. Animal manure must first be broken down by tiny organisms in the soil before its nutrients are unlocked for plant roots.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu mli oya koni tsei lɛ anu amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Esa akɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ akumɔ kooloi ashishifã lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ dani enyɛ ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and turning thick and tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the sap and passing along leaf curl viruses that twist plant leaves and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ ahe hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni tsɔɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni ehaa amɛdalɛ mli aka shi faŋŋ

english: What basic conditions do I need to provide if I want to start growing mushrooms on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ shihilɛi titri he hiaa mi kɛji miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Mushrooms require three essential conditions to grow successfully: complete darkness, plenty of water or moisture, and good air circulation.
ga: Shihilɛi etɛ ni he hiaa he miihia ŋmeii koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ: duŋ ni yeɔ emuu kɛ nu loo hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa. kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ

english: How is growing mushrooms different from growing green crops like maize or vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esoro ŋmeii adumɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo aduawai adumɔ he?

english: Unlike green crops that need direct sunlight to make food, mushrooms grow best in dark environments and rely heavily on high humidity and proper airflow instead of light.
ga: Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ tsei eŋɔli ni he hiaa hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛhoo nii lɛ ahe. Mushrooms daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ. ni ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe la.

english: Can I use an air conditioner in my mushroom room to keep the temperature cool?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kɔɔyɔŋ mli tsɔne ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsu lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ?

english: While an air conditioner will cool the room, it will also draw the essential water and moisture directly out of your mushrooms, causing them to dry out and spoil.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔŋ tsɔne lɛ haa tsu lɛ mli jɔɔ moŋ. Shi egbalaa nu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa lɛ hu kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Will letting direct sunlight into my mushroom house affect how they grow?
ga: Ani hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔtɔ shĩa lɛ mli lɛ baaná edalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, direct sunlight heat up the room and dries out the moisture that mushrooms need to survive. Mushrooms thrive best in dark, shaded environments.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tsu lɛ mli adɔ ni ebaaha nu ni he hiaa ŋmeii lɛ koni amɛhi shi lɛ agbi. Mushrooms daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ.

english: Why do my mushrooms need fresh air if they are supposed to grow in dark, enclosed spaces?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he hiaa mi ŋmɔji lɛ? Beni edaa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni aŋã?

english: Mushrooms need good airflow because fresh air provides oxygen and prevents stagnant, stale conditions that can ruin the crop, even while kept in the dark.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa he miihia ŋmeii. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa, ni etsĩɔ shihilɛi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa. Kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ po.

english: Why are my growing mushrooms shrinking and losing their firmness?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Mushrooms lose moisture very easily when the surrounding air is dry or when artificial cooling units pull water out of them. They must stay in a moist environment to remain healthy.
ga: Muji lɛ fiteɔ nu oya waa kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi loo kɛ́ nibii ni akɛfee ni haa hulutsoo lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ mli. Esa akɛ akɛ amɛ ato he ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best way to keep my mushroom house moist without ruining the crop?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi-mushroom shĩa lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni mifiteee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: The best way is to maintain steady water moisture in the room while ensuring there is gentle natural airflow to keep the air humid without letting water become stagnant.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu lɛ mli ahi tsu lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, kwɛmɔ ni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya mli blɛoo. Koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni ahaaa nu lɛ ahi shi.

english: How does dry air affect mushrooms compared to other farm crops?
ga: Te kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ saa ŋmeii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ahe?

english: Dry air quickly sucks the moisture straight out of mushrooms because of their sensitive skin, whereas regular farm crops can handle dry air much better if their roots have water.
