ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛhewolo ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ hewɔ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ atsu kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi he nii jogbaŋŋ kɛji ŋmeii shishifãi yɛ nu lɛ,

english: What kind of place on my farm is ideal for setting up a mushroom growing shed?
ga: Mɛɛ he ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni sa akɛ ato ŋmeii akwɛmɔ shĩa?

english: An ideal location is a dark, well-shaded area that allows good natural breeze to flow through while keeping moisture trapped inside.
ga: He ni hi jogbaŋŋ ji he ko ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ jogbaŋŋ koni adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ emli lɛ.

english: How can I cool my mushroom structure naturally without using electricity or machines?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafee mi-mushroom lɛ mli fɛ̃i yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni mikɛ srawa hewalɛ loo tsɔnei tsuuu nii?

english: You can build a shaded, well-ventilated structure using local materials that block sunlight while allowing natural air movement, keeping the space moist and dark without machines that dry out the mushrooms.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa yɛ be mli ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ mli lɛ afee tsũ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ha he ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee duŋ ni okɛ tsɔnei ni haa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ lɛ akatsu nii.

english: Can I mix different types of fertilizers together before applying them to my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi afutu? Ani abaanyɛ afutu amɛ dani akɛ ŋmãa atsu nii?

english: No, mixing wrong fertilizers together can damage your crops or waste your money because different crop stages require specific nutrients; for example, NPK helps root and shoot growth early on, while Urea supplies nitrogen for leaf growth later.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite onibii loo efite shika. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ biɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, NPK haa shishifãi kɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ mra. yɛ be mli ni urea haa nitrogen koni sɛɛ mli lɛ baai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Can I use the same chemical I use for killing weeds to spray insects on my pepper plants?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ jwɛi lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛshwie ŋmeii yɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: No, weedkillers are designed to destroy plants and will kill your pepper crop, whereas insecticides are specifically made to kill insect pests without harming the plant.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ koni efite o-pepper tsei lɛ ni egbe amɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ji nɔ ni afee koni akɛgbe kooloi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni eyeee tsei lɛ awui lɛ.

english: Is it good to burn all the dry weeds on my land before I start planting?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashã jwɛi ni egbi yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani mabɔi dumɔ?

english: While burning clears the field quickly, it burns away beneficial soil nutrients and kills good organisms; clearing and letting weeds decay naturally enriches the soil and keeps it moist.
ga: yɛ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ lɛ jieɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ oya. Eshãa sũ mli niyenii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni efiteɔ nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ ni aŋmɛ amɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows fast and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly and takes over the field after the maize is harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ daa blɛoo ni eyeɔ jɛmɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces the young plants to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food, resulting in thin stalks and tiny corn ears.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei bibii lɛ abɔi nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii toi bibii baa.

english: Why do some of my cassava cuttings rot in the soil instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot if they are planted upside down, placed in waterlogged soil without good drainage, or cut from weak, diseased parent stems.
ga: Kasava tsei ni afo lɛ baafite kɛji akɛ adu amɛyitso. Okɛwo shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ nɔ. loo afolɔ kɛjɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli

english: Leaf curling and yellowing are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the sap and spreading viruses, or by severe heat and lack of soil moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ baa. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomatoes stretch tall and thin when they do not get enough direct sunlight, spending all their energy reaching for light instead of making flowers and fruits.
ga: Tomatoi baakpã kɛya shɔŋŋ ni ebaafee bibioo kɛji amɛnáaa hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa tɛ̃ɛ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛyaa la nɔ moŋ fe ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai.

english: How do I know if Fall Armyworms are attacking my maize crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ Fall Armyworms miitutua mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: You will notice ragged holes eaten through the young leaves and dark, sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel of the plant where the caterpillars hide.
ga: Obaana buji ni egbɛ eshwa ni aye kɛtsɔ baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he ni ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does heavy rain during flowering cause my maize to produce cobs with missing kernels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ haa ŋmãa feɔ ŋmãa ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall during flowering washes away the pollen from the tassels at the top before it can reach the silks on the cob to form full corn grains.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ hoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe dani eshɛɔ siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ he koni ebatsɔ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yellowing that starts at the leaf tip and moves down the central vein usually means your maize is short on nitrogen. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ anaagbɛ ni etsɔɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves twisting up and getting yellow and pale patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ etsɔ ŋwɛi ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf twisting is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. The disease damages the leaves, preventing the plant from making enough energy to grow big roots.
ga: Yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii yɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Hela nɛɛ fiteɔ baai lɛ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do my cowpea leaves look brown and dry around the edges after a few very hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ gbii babaoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and strong sun make crops lose moisture faster than their roots can draw water from the soil. The leaf edges dry out first because they are the thinnest parts of the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la haa ŋmɔshi nibii amli nu lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ baagbi klɛŋklɛŋ ejaakɛ amɛji tso lɛ fã ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and drop off without forming pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop flowers when they experience water stress or high heat to save energy and protect themselves. Without enough soil moisture or shade, the tree refuses to carry young pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ amɛbote nu mli haomɔ loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛhe. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ loo hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ eŋmɛŋ gbɛ ni ŋmɔtɔ bibii aba.

english: Why are my groundnut shells empty inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔji lɛ amli efee efolo kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods happen when the soil lacks calcium during the pod development stage. Groundnut pegs take up calcium directly from the damp soil to build the seed inside the shell.
ga: Peanut pods ni bɛ nɔ ko lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ pod lɛ shweremɔ be mli. Peanut pins lɛ jieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn soft, dark, and rotten as they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai ashishi feɔ bɔdɔɔ, ediŋŋ, ni egboɔ kɛ́ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It occurs when tomato plants do not get a steady supply of water, which stops calcium from moving evenly into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu nɔ daa. Enɛ haaa calcium lɛ aya tso yibii ni miida lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing plenty of leaves but dropping all their flowers before setting fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai babaoo shi fɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer or very high nighttime temperatures can cause pepper plants to put all their energy into leafy foliage while dropping flowers instead of fruiting.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa waa lɛ baanyɛ aha pepper tso lɛ atsu ehewalɛ fɛɛ he nii yɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ yɛ be kome mli. Ni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily even when the wind is not strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees easily fall over when underground pests like root nematodes or stem weevils eat away their root system, leaving the heavy plant without a firm anchor in the dirt.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ root nematodes loo stem weevils ye amɛshishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni tsii lɛ bɛ ŋwɛi ŋta yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yams begin to rot inside the soil before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani manyɛ makpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Yam rot in the field is usually caused by waterlogged soil that lacks good drainage. Excess water cuts off oxygen to the tubers, allowing soil fungi and bacteria to enter and decompose the yams.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ ni nu kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ kɛyaa tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa sũ mli ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi boteɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why is my maize crop producing tassels and flowering while the stalks are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ fɔfɔi shi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo lɛ?

english: When young maize faces severe water stress or drought, it panics and speeds up its growth cycle to produce seeds early before the plant dries up and dies.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa bibii kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ kpe Ebaafee gbeyei ni eha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ oya koni ekɛ dumɔwui aba mra. Dani tso lɛ agbi ni egbo

english: Why do grasscutters and other rodents keep destroying my young cassava and sugarcane plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi shwieɔ jwɛi kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi lɛ? Mɛni hewɔ amɛfiteɔ mi-cassava tsei kɛ mi-sugar cane lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Grasscutters are attracted to soft, sweet, and starchy crops like cassava roots and sugarcane stalks because they offer easy food and hydration. Fencing your farm plot or clearing dense bush around the borders removes their hiding places and deters them from entering.
ga: Mɛi ni shwieɔ jwɛi lɛ sumɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni ŋɔɔ, ni starch yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmei shishifãi kɛ ŋmei tsei. Ejaakɛ niyenii ni amɛyeɔ lɛ waaa, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hu baa. Fɔ̃ɔ oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he gbogbo loo ojie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ. Husu lɛ baajie amɛteemɔ hei lɛ, ni ebaatsĩ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkabote mli.

english: What causes large holes and tunnels under my crop beds, and will it kill my plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji wuji kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ midumɔi lɛ ashishi lɛ baa? Ni ani ebaakpãtã mitsei lɛ ahiɛ?

english: Underground tunnels are usually created by burrowing pests like grasscutters or field mice searching for roots and shelter. These pathways disrupt root systems, preventing plants from absorbing water and nutrients, which causes crops to wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, tamɔ jwɛi fɔlɔi loo ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii, ni taoɔ shishifãi kɛ wɔɔhe lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi gbɛjegbɛi. Kukuji nɛɛ gbaa shishifã gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ naa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni haa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ

english: Why is it important for me to clear tall grass and weeds from around my crop field regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi kɛjɛ midumɔ mli daa lɛ?

english: Tall grass and weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Leaving tall grass uncontrolled also creates ideal hiding and breeding spots for destructive field pests.
ga: Jwɛi kakadaji kɛ jwɛi bibii kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Jwɛi kakadaŋŋ ni ashiɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akudɔ lɛ hu feɔ hei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɛɔ amɛhe kɛ hei ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii yɛ shia lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why do some farmers spread cut dry grass around the base of their crop plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shwieɔ jwɛi ni afo lɛ amɛshwãa amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Spreading dry grass around crops is called mulching. It traps moisture in the soil during hot weather, prevents weed seeds from sprouting, and slowly breaks down to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi dumɔwui anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛgbala fiofio amɛfee niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize stems bend over and fall flat on the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: Maize plants fall over (known as lodging) when their roots are shallow, when pest damage weakens the lower stem, or during heavy wind and rain. Mounding extra soil around the stem base gives plants strong support.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi Akɛ shishifãi lɛ woɔ shweshweeshwe (ni atsɛɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe) kɛji shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fite lɛ, shishigbɛ tsei lɛ ahe waaa. aloo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli Okɛ sũ krokomɛi abɔ he Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ ebuaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without producing good yield when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight for sunlight and stretch upward instead of developing strong stems and fruits. Proper spacing ensures every plant gets enough light, air, and nutrients.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ ni amɛfeɔ amɛhe shwiili moŋ fe ni amɛaawo ŋmeii kɛ aduawai ni wa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei fɛɛ naa la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Crops lacking water will show curling, limp, or wilting leaves, especially during the hottest part of the day. Watering early in the morning or late evening ensures the soil absorbs water before it evaporates.
ga: Tsei ni nu efo mli lɛ baajie baai ni ebɔle, ni egbo loo ni egbo, titri lɛ yɛ gbi lɛ mli bei ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu dani etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my vegetable crops turning pale yellow even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves can mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is waterlogged from overwatering, which suffocates the roots. Adding well-rotted manure or compost helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ atsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Which fast-growing grasses can I intentionally cultivate to feed farm animals?
ga: Mɛɛ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya manyɛ majɛ yiŋtoo mli madu koni mikɛha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ niyenii?

english: Elephant grass (Napier grass) and Guinea grass are excellent cultivated forage crops. They grow rapidly, withstand repeated cutting, and provide rich nutrition for grass-eating livestock.
ga: Shɔji jwɛi (Napier jwɛi) kɛ Guinea jwɛi ji niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Amɛdaraa oya. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni afoɔ lɛ shii abɔ ni ehaa niyenii babaoo kɛhaa kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ.

english: How do I safely store my harvested grain at home so pests do not ruin it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato shia shweshweeshwe? Koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite lɛ.

english: Harvested grain must be thoroughly dried in the sun until fully hardened before storage. Storing grain in clean, airtight bags or raised containers keeps moisture, mold, and insects out.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa kwraa dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni akɛto vacuum kotoku ni mli tse loo tsɛnsi ni awo nɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi bibii ahe.

english: Why do I need to clear and dig up the soil before planting my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mafo mli dani madu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Loosening the soil allows soft young crop roots to grow deep into the ground easily, helps rainwater sink down, and buries old plant waste so your seeds start with clean, healthy soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni ofu tsei momo ni eshwɛ lɛ koni odumɔwui lɛ aje shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Does digging deep into the soil hurt my farmland over time?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni mifoɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ saa midumɔi lɛ ahe yɛ gbɛ fɔŋ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Digging too deep or too often can break up the soil structure and expose the moist layer underneath to the hot sun, causing it to dry out quickly and lose its fertile topsoil during heavy rains.
ga: Kɛ́ akumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo shii abɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ akumɔ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ hulu lɛ shishi lɛ mli adɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya ni elaajeɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Check your plants early in the morning; if their leaves are wilting or curling before the sun gets hot, and the soil feels completely dry two inches below the surface, your crops are thirsty.
ga: Kwɛmɔ otsei lɛ amli leebi. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ gboi loo amɛbɔle amɛhe dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ba Ni kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nu he akɛ egbi kwraa aaafee 2 inches yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it better to water my crops early in the morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔ tsei anɔ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ?

english: Early morning is best because it gives the plants moisture to handle the daytime heat, whereas watering late at night leaves the foliage wet for too long, which can attract diseases.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tso lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni ekɛkpeɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni oooha amɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. ni baanyɛ agbala helai srɔtoi kɛba

english: Why is it bad to leave weeds growing around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ashi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ mi dumɔwui lɛ ji nɔ fɔŋ.

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm; they aggressively steal water, soil nutrients, and sunlight away from your main crop, causing your crops to grow weak and yield very little.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ nu mli niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni hulu la lɛ etee kwraa kɛjɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: How soon after planting should I start clearing weeds from my field?
ga: Beni adu nii sɛɛ Etsɛ tɛŋŋ esa akɛ mabɔi jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jiemɔ?

english: You should start clearing weeds within the first three to four weeks after planting, as young crops are at their weakest stage and need a clean field to establish strong roots.
ga: Esa akɛ oje jwɛi lɛ ŋmɔmɔ shishi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli yɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo, ni ehe miihia ni ená he ko ni he tse koni shishifãi ni wa aba.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce small tubers when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ náa bulbs bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, their roots fight underground for limited space and nutrients, preventing the roots from expanding into full, heavy tubers.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko ni faaa kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee bulbs ni tsii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does proper plant spacing make it easier to manage a large farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ haa ŋmɔji wuji anɔkwɛmɔ feɔ mlɛo?

english: Correct spacing leaves clean pathways between rows, making it much easier for you to walk through, remove weeds, apply fertilizer, and harvest without damaging the growing crops.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ ni ja haa gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ahe tseɔ yɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ teŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ oootsɔ mli, okɛ jwɛi awo mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa nibii ni ofiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense where the plant shrinks its surface area to stop water from escaping, while yellowing shows the plant is stressed and unable to draw nutrients from dry soil.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu nɔ ko ni tsei lɛ baa amɛhe shi koni nu akaje mli. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miihao ni enyɛɛɛ ejie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: What causes my crop seedlings to suddenly fall over and die shortly after sprouting?
ga: Mɛni haa mitso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by fungal diseases that thrive in soggy, uncleared soil; excessively wet earth suffocates delicate stems right at the ground level, causing the young plant to collapse.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni he tseee nɔ lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi

english: How should I care for new plantain suckers as soon as I receive them to plant on my farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ plantain tsei heei lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Clear the field properly, dig deep and wide planting holes, add well-rotted manure, and plant the suckers upright in moist soil to help them establish strong roots quickly.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ Tsɔɔmɔ dumɔ bu ni mli kwɔ ni elɛɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ afata he. Ni odu ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ koni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ oya.

english: How long does it usually take from planting a plantain sucker until the fruit is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ni edaa lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Plantains typically take between 12 to 15 months to produce a harvestable bunch, depending on soil fertility, water supply, and the specific variety planted.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 15 dani ewoɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli kɛ tso pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my plantain bunches coming out small, and how can I get bigger bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ ji bibii nɛkɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná jwɛi agbo ko?

english: Small bunches happen when plants lack nutrients or face heavy competition from too many side shoots. Pruning extra shoots to leave only two or three stalks per stool and applying organic manure will help grow larger bunches.
ga: Kui bibii baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ loo amɛkɛ akaŋshii ni naa wa waa ni jɛɔ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ kpeɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛyashi 2-3 stems yɛ stool kome mli kɛ organic fertilizer ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua niji lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Should I cut off the extra shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fɛɛ? Ani midumɔwu titri lɛ je kpo?

english: Yes, you should regularly remove excess sucker shoots so they do not steal water and food from the main mother plant, ensuring the main plant produces healthy fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ daa. Bɔni afee ni ekaju nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tso titri ni ji nyɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ awo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my plantain trees turn yellow and dry up during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have large leaves that lose moisture quickly. During dry weather, the tree naturally sheds its lower leaves to conserve water and protect its growing center.
ga: Plantain yɛ baai agboi ni ŋmɔtɔ fiteɔ oya. Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when strong winds blow, and how can I prevent it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa miitswa lɛ? Ni te ooofee tɛŋŋ otsĩ naa?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can be damaged by pests or soil erosion. Supporting fruiting trees with strong bamboo or wooden props prevents wind from pushing them over.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo shikpɔŋ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni wa fi yibii tsei lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ akatsɔ amɛmli.

english: Can I safely grow plantains together with young cocoa trees on the same land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains ni kookoo tsei bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shweshweeshwe?

english: Yes, plantains are excellent shade plants for young cocoa trees because their large leaves protect the young cocoa from harsh sunlight while providing early income before the cocoa starts producing.
ga: Hɛɛ, plantains ji tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii feɔ hulutsoo. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai wuji lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa anáa shika mra dani ajeɔ kookoo feemɔ shishi.

english: How can I tell the exact right time to cut down a bunch of plantains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafo plantains ŋmɔ ko?

english: Harvest plantains when the individual fruits are plump and rounded rather than sharp-edged, and before the outer skin starts turning yellow on the tree.
ga: Kpaa plantains beni aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeehiɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ Ni dani kponɔgbɛ lɛ aje shishi etsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How should I store harvested plantain bunches so they do not ripen too fast before I take them to market?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ ato koni amɛkakwɛ̃ oya dani mikɛ amɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Keep harvested plantains in a cool, well-ventilated shade away from direct sunlight, and avoid stacking bunches directly on top of each other to prevent bruising.
ga: Kɛ plantains ni akpa lɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. He ni hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ Ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ plantains akui ni okɛaawo amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ koni akafite lɛ he.

english: What type of manure or soil treatment works best to help plantain plants feed well?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ aha plantains?

english: Plantains feed heavily on soil nutrients; applying decomposed poultry manure or compost around the base of the plant provides essential nitrogen and potassium for strong growth.
ga: Plantains yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ kooloi ashishi loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ haa nitrogen kɛ potassium ni he hiaa koni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps the plant maintain healthy green leaves and produce full, heavy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi ni tsii.

english: Why does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops better over time than using chemical fertilizer alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli fe tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers feed the plant quickly, but manure improves the soil itself by helping it hold water better, improving soil structure, and keeping nutrients available in the farm for many growing seasons.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei niyenii oya. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo kɛtsɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni ekɛhaa koni ehiɛ nu mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii aya hiɛ ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahi shi yɛ be babaoo mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce huge bushy leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy building big stems and leaves above ground instead of sending nutrients down to expand its roots into large tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei agboi kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ niyenii kpakpahi kɛ yaa si konɛ e ha nɛ sisifã ɔmɛ nɛ a pee bulb nguahi.

english: If you leave too many suckers, they steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main plant grows big and produces large bunches of plantains.
ga: Kɛji oshi ŋmeii babaoo lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ adara ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which is then sent down to build large, healthy tubers under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ anɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii. No sɛɛ lɛ, atsuɔ lɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni he wa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What is causing my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛshwereɔ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in wet, dark, and humid weather. Clearing extra tree shade and harvesting mature pods quickly helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ, duŋ, kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Tso lɛ mli ŋmɔlɔ ni ajieɔ babaoo kɛ ŋmeii ni eda lɛ ni akpaa oya lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes through the leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu kɛtsɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely fall armyworms, a common insect pest that feeds on the soft growth center of maize plants. Spotting them early and applying recommended pest treatments prevents them from destroying the crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ. Ni ooona amɛ mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atsu nii lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the plants to compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and yield more food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni eda ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm as their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛduɔ ŋmei lɛ?

english: Beans and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen out of the air and fix it into the soil. Planting them alongside maize acts as a natural fertilizer, keeping the soil rich and helping the maize grow better.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ, ebaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Extreme afternoon heat causes tomato leaves to lose water faster than the roots can drink it from the soil. Covering the soil around the plants with dry grass (mulching) keeps the root zone cool and reduces stress.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato baai lɛ sɛɛ foɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa nɔnyɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves suddenly full of holes with tiny caterpillars hidden inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii trukaa lɛ? Akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide deep inside the tender central leaves of the plant to feed. Catching them early with recommended control methods prevents them from destroying the growing leaves and reducing your corn yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye niyenii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ amɛ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite baai ni miida lɛ ni ebaaha o-abele yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die within a few days even though the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ? Ani nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: This sudden wilting is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease living in the soil that enters through the roots and blocks water from moving up the stem. Because the water channels are blocked, the leaves dry out quickly even when the ground is wet.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni etsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli eboteɔ mli ni ehaaa nu aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ. Ejaakɛ atsĩ nu gbɛ lɛ naa. Baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot or when the plant lacks sufficient water and nutrients. High heat damages the pollen, causing the plant to shed the flowers because they cannot form healthy seeds.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa fiteɔ pollen. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight and dry wind. Fast-growing plantains provide living shade umbrellas that keep the soil moist and cool until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa edɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ daraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulutsoo be muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ.

english: Why are my mature cocoa trees producing fewer pods now that the big forest trees on my farm have grown very dense?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei ni eda lɛ miiwo ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko pɛ yɛ be mli ni koo ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida waa lɛ?

english: While young cocoa needs heavy shade, mature cocoa trees need moderate sunlight to form flowers and develop pods. Too much shade blocks the sunlight needed for pod growth and creates dark, damp conditions where black pod disease spreads fast.
ga: yɛ be mli ni kookoo gbekɛ lɛ he miihia hulutsoo ni mli wa. Kakao tsei ni eda lɛ biɔ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛfee fɔfɔi ni amɛfee ŋmeii. Shade babaoo baatsi hulu la ni he hiaa kɛha pod lɛ dalɛ naa. ni ekɛ shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ kɛ hulutsoo baa. Black pod hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oya.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop harvests every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Crops feed on specific nutrients in the dirt to grow. Planting the same crop on the same plot year after year drains those specific plant foods; alternating your main crops with legumes like cowpeas restores natural food back into the soil.
ga: Tsei yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ baaha tsei lɛ amli niyenii komɛi afite. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii atsake oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my newly planted cassava shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmei ni adu ehee lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to grow aggressively and grab available soil nutrients and water faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life gives the cassava time to establish leaves and shade out competing weeds naturally.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛjie niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi yɛ egbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ehaa yucca lɛ be ni ekɛbaa, ni ehaa jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out in direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Leaves lying flat on damp soil get shaded out and rot easily, leading to much smaller underground tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛjie amɛbaai lɛ akpo yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ niyenii. Baai ni kã shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe oya ni amɛgboiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the ground if I leave them buried during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excess rainwater fills all the air gaps in waterlogged soil, suffocating the tubers and allowing soil rot organisms to quickly destroy the starch inside.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ hei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ obɔ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nibii ni fiteɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ oya.

english: How do I know if the first rainfall in April is enough water to start planting my maize seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ April mli lɛ haa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛjeɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui shishi?

english: The very first rainfall after the dry season usually only wets the top layer of dirt, which can trick seeds into germinating before dying of heat. Wait until you receive two or three heavy rains so moisture settles deep into the soil to support early root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ baanyɛ alaka dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ dani dɔlɛ lɛ agbo. Mɛɛ kɛyashi obaaná nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii enyɔ loo etɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my soybean plants make the soil better for my maize when I plant them on the same field later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-soybean tso lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa lɛ beni miduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Soybeans are legumes that pull natural fertilizer called nitrogen out of the air and store it in their roots. When the soybean crop is harvested, those roots stay in the ground and decay, leaving rich, free food in the soil for your next crop like maize.
ga: Soybeans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa soybeans Nakai shishifãi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Shi niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does adding chicken manure to my field help my crops grow better than using no manure at all?
ga: Te tsina ŋmei ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ fe bɔ ni mikɛ ŋmei ko kwraa fataaa he lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Chicken manure is packed with essential plant foods like nitrogen and phosphorus that crops need to grow strong green leaves and deep roots. When mixed into the soil, it slowly releases these nutrients over time and helps the dirt hold onto rain water longer.
ga: Kooloo ŋmɔtɔ eyi kɛ tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ aná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ Kɛ́ akɛfutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafiofio Nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ jeɔ kpo yɛ be kɛ bei amli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni muji lɛ kpɛtɛɔ nugbɔ nu he be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Should I plant the exact same crop that everyone else in my village is planting this season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu tsei ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ duɔ yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: While copying your neighbors makes it easier to share tools, if everyone grows the same crop at the same time, the market gets flooded and local prices drop. Planting a different crop can get you better prices and prevents pests from easily jumping from field to field across the village.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ akutsoŋbii lɛ ahe mfonirifeemɔ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajara dɛŋdadei moŋ. Shi kɛji akɛ mɔ fɛɛ mɔ du tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be kome mli hu? Nu baaho jara lɛ nɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli nibii ajara baa shi. Nibii krokomɛi ni ooodu lɛ baaha oná jara kpakpa. ni etsĩ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaho kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli mlɛo yɛ akrowa lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I grow tomatoes on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and sicknesses that attack tomatoes build up and stay hidden in the soil after harvest. If you plant tomatoes again immediately, those pests attack early; but if you swap to a different crop like cassava or beans, the tomato pests starve and die off.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni tutuaa tomatoi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji odu tomato ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ Nakai tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baatutua bo oya. Shi kɛji otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei. Tomato kooloi lɛ baaye hɔmɔ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow when my field gets flooded with heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nu eyi ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When the soil stays full of water for too long, the roots drown, stop working, and cannot suck up food from the dirt, causing the leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ ná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛkpaa nitsumɔ, ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhe niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crop seeds right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ kwɛ̃ oya fe dumɔwui ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native to the area and naturally suited to survive on very little. Their seeds wake up instantly with the first rain, whereas farm crops need a bit more care and warm soil to start growing, which is why clearing weeds early gives your seeds a fair chance.
ga: Jwɛi ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ ji jɛmɛ jɛɛhe, ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ehiɔ shi yɛ nɔ fioo ko pɛ nɔ. Amɛdumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔ mli tsei biɔ kwɛmɔ fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni ehe hiaa ni ajie jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ. Enɛ baaha odumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni sa.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they get too stressed by extreme afternoon heat, a sudden dry spell, or too much strong fertilizer. The plant sheds its flowers to save energy so it can survive until conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛhao fe nine kɛjɛ shwane latsaa ni naa wa lɛ mli. kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa tsɔ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: When seeds are planted too tightly, the plants fight each other for sunlight above ground and water below ground. Instead of healthy cobs, you will end up with thin, tall stems that produce very small or empty maize ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui lɛ babaoo tsɔ Tsei wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooona ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ Obaagbe naa kɛ ŋmei ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmei toi bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts under cassava plants while the cassava is still short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii tsei lɛ ashishi shi ŋmeii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants grow low to the ground like a carpet, covering the soil to keep it cool and prevent weeds from taking over. Meanwhile, the tall cassava grows overhead, allowing you to harvest two different foods from the same piece of land.
ga: Peanut tsei kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ tamɔ kapɛti. Mulch koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔɔ ni jwɛi akaye nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, Tall cassava kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ yitso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii srɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome.

english: How do I know when my soybean crop is fully mature and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-soybean lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Soybeans are ready when the plant leaves turn yellow and drop to the ground, leaving behind brown, dry pods. If you shake a mature pod near your ear and hear the seeds rattling inside like small stones, it is time to harvest.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo kɛji tso lɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shikpɔŋ. Ashiɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji okpokpo ŋmɔtɔ ko ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ otoi lɛ ni onu dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso tamɔ tɛi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, no lɛ be eshɛɛ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to survive because direct sunlight burns their tender leaves and dries out the soil quickly. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides living shelter and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa plants mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ daa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for healthy leaves and stalks. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea at the right growth stage helps restore green leaves and improves crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai kɛ tsei ahewalɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba eŋɔli ni eha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Does it matter if I plant my cassava stem cuttings flat or at an angle in the soil?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni madu ŋmei ni afolɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋwɛigbɛ?

english: Yes, planting cassava cuttings at a slanting angle of about 45 degrees helps the plant grow deeper and stronger roots, leading to better tuber production compared to laying them completely flat on top of the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni afolɔ ashwie shi yɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni ji aaafee digrii 45 lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ená shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa nɔ lɛ he.

english: What is eating holes in the middle leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu ko ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso ko baa teŋgbɛ ni eshiɔ muji ni tsuɔ waa yɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a common pest that feeds on the central leaves of young corn. Early detection and applying recommended bio-pesticides or approved sprays into the leaves can control them before they destroy the whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot and happens when tomato plants cannot get enough calcium or when watering is uneven. Keeping the soil steadily moist without overwatering helps the plant absorb calcium properly and stops the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ ni nu shwieee nɔ fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ calcium lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows corn-specific pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas returns nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ agbɛjianɔtoo lɛ.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food that goes into growing large underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves high off the ground, ensuring they capture enough light and preventing leaves from rotting on damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii ni baanyɛ akwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ ana la ni fa bɔ ni sa. ni ehaa baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: It is best to sow seeds after two or three continuous, heavy rains have thoroughly soaked the soil rather than after the very first light shower, ensuring the seeds have enough moisture to germinate and survive.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu dumɔwui beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that suck sap from the plant and spread viruses. Controlling these insects early using neem oil or insecticidal soap helps keep the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ hela lɛ amɛshwãa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Neem fɔ loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I harvest more food from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: No, planting crops too close together makes them fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants and smaller yields. Giving each crop proper spacing ensures each plant grows strong and yields its full potential.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my green maize turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: When lower maize leaves yellow in a V-shape from the tip inward, it usually means the crop lacks nitrogen nutrient in the soil or the ground is soaked with water, preventing the roots from feeding.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, amɛfeɔ V su kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa kɛyaa mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana niyenii

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from larger trees or companion crops like plantains to keep the air humid and protect their soft leaves from burning.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni fata amɛhe, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni amɛtsi baai bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkashã.

english: Cassava tubers rot underground when water sits in the soil for too long without draining, or when wet soil conditions allow fungal diseases to attack the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu hoɔ. Aloo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves high up into the sunlight using stakes so they can catch enough light to build up energy and grow big tubers underneath the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants shrinking and curling up into tight shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or aphids that spread viruses to the plant, or by extreme heat stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni gbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ nɔ loo kɛjɛɔ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ mli

english: Tomatoes shed their flowers when temperatures become too high, when there is severe water shortages, or when there are no bees or wind to help move pollen within the flowers.
ga: Tomatoi lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu faaa waa Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni baaye abua ni ajie pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ mli lɛ bɛ.

english: What makes my plantain trees fall over so easily when heavy rains and wind come?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot hold heavy bunches of fruit during strong winds, especially if tiny underground worms called nematodes have damaged their roots.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ aduawai babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fite eshishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do small insects attack my cowpea crop as soon as the flowers open?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛwo fɔfɔi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce sweet nectar and soft petals that naturally attract pests like flower thrips, which come to feed and lay eggs right when the pods start forming.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu mli nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ fɔfɔi thrips lɛ. Taakɛ eji lɛ, amɛbaa koni amɛbaye nii ni amɛwo ŋmeii kɛji ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛfee pɛ.

english: Why does covering the soil around my vegetables with dry grass help them grow better in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi wo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and prevents precious water from evaporating into the sunlit air.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why does swamp rice survive in standing water while my maize crop dies if water sits on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ swamp rice hiɔ shi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ be mli ni mi-corn lɛ gboɔ kɛji nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air tubes in their stems and roots that allow them to transport oxygen from the leaves down to the roots even when submerged in water.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbɛi krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛwo nu mli po

english: Why do my crops keep getting attacked by insects even when I sweep and keep the ground on my farm clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mishwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni mihaa ehe tseɔ moŋ.

english: While sweeping clears surface debris, many crop pests live underground, fly in from neighboring bush, or hide under living leaves. Farm sanitation helps, but checking crop leaves regularly and using proper natural or chemical pest treatments is necessary.
ga: yɛ be mli ni ejieɔ sũ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kooloi babaoo hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. fã kɛjɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli kɛba. loo ni akɛteeɔ baai ni hiɛ ka lɛ ashishi Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ baanyɛ aye abua. Shi ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei ahe baai lɛ amli daa ni ehe miihia ni ana adebɔɔ mli loo tsofafeemɔ gbɛi ni sa ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe.

english: Why does planting maize on the same plot of land every single year result in smaller harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba lɛ?

english: Maize continuously drains specific nutrients, especially nitrogen, from the soil. Rotating your plot with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas restores vital nutrients to the soil naturally between maize seasons.
ga: Abele shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ komɛi be fɛɛ be. titri lɛ nitrogen, ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii atsake oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa be mli.

english: Why does spreading dry grass around the base of my pepper plants help them survive dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni No hewɔ lɛ, mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) acts as a protective blanket. It keeps the soil cool, prevents moisture from evaporating under the hot sun, and stops weeds from stealing water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ naa. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekaju nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees turn yellow and wither when I cut down all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ mifo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and burn under full, direct sunlight. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains or large trees act as living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa leaves and keeping the soil cool while roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ shade tsei ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo baai bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: When cassava plants are crowded, they compete aggressively with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This forces the plant to waste energy growing tall stems instead of swelling its roots into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛfee bulb agboi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to be trained up wooden poles to grow bigger yams underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tso atsɔse mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ sweet potatoi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need to capture maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the growing underground tuber. Staking holds leaves up toward the sun and prevents them from rotting on damp ground.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato baai lɛ amɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa hulu lɛ he ni ehaaa amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn cobs are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen. The plant moves available nitrogen to its newer upper leaves, causing older bottom leaves to fade; adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer fixes this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai heei amli. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme afternoon heat, irregular watering, or a lack of pollinating insects like bees. Maintaining consistent soil moisture and light shade helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa ha amɛ hao yɛ shwane mli. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ faaa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even during heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa po mli lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal liquid fertilizer and soil nutrients directly from crop roots. Even with plenty of rain, your crops remain undernourished if weeds are taking their food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli tɛ̃ɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baaná niyenii mli hewalɛ lolo kɛji jwɛi ye amɛ.

english: Why should I avoid putting fertilizer on bone-dry soil during the hottest part of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wu yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizer applied to hot, dry soil cannot dissolve properly for root absorption and can burn tender plant roots. Fertilizer should always be applied when the soil is moist so it dissolves gently into the root zone.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi nɔ lɛ shwieee shi jogbaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei shishifãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be fɛɛ be kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli fiofio. shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishifã lɛ he

english: Why should I leave big trees growing near the stream where I get water for my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tso agbo ko yɛ faa ko masɛi koni nu ahi jɛmɛ kɛha midumɔ nii lɛ?

english: Trees along streams keep the water cool, reduce evaporation from hot sunlight, and hold the soil together with their roots so your water source does not dry up or turn into mud.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ faa lɛ naa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli la ni hoɔ lɛ aba shi ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ atswa shishifãi lɛ ahe bɔni afee ni nu jɛɛhei lɛ akagbi loo akatsɔ muji.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast during the dry season even when a river is nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ faa ko bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: If trees around the river have been cut down, direct sunlight heats the soil and water, causing moisture to evaporate rapidly and leaving less underground water available for your crop roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ afo tsei ni bɔle Faa lɛ he lɛ. Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli adɔ. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya Ni ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa shikpɔŋ shishi nu fioo.

english: How does cutting down trees near our community dam affect the yield of my vegetables?
ga: Te tsei ni mifoɔ yɛ wɔ akutso lɛ mli faa lɛ masɛi lɛ saa mi-vegetables ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Cutting trees allows rain to wash soil directly into the dam, filling it with mud. This reduces the amount of water the dam can store, leaving less water to irrigate your crops during dry spells.
ga: Tsei ni afoɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa faa lɛ mli. ni eha eyi kɛ muji Enɛ baaha nu ni faa lɛ baanyɛ ato lɛ aba shi. Enɛ haa nu ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crops look healthier when they are planted near areas with surrounding trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa waa kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni tsei ebɔle he lɛ?

english: Trees release water vapor into the air and provide relief from extreme heat, creating a cooler environment that protects your crops from burning and helps them retain water.
ga: Tsei jieɔ nu lasu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa hejɔɔmɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ mli. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ onibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away my young crops and topsoil when there are no trees on the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ? Beni tsei bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tree roots act like nets underground that hold the soil in place, while tree leaves break the force of falling rain so it doesn't strip away your fertile topsoil and wash away small plants.
ga: Tso shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋshɔŋloo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni tsei ahe baai lɛ fiteɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ ejieee shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ ni ekɛ tsei bibii lɛ efɔɔɔ.

english: Should I clear all the trees near the stream on my land so I can have more space to plant maize?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tsei fɛɛ ni bɛŋkɛ faai ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni maná gbɛ babaoo kɛha ŋmãa?

english: Clearing trees near the stream gives you a little extra land today, but it causes the stream to dry up quickly, which will leave your maize without water to mature later.
ga: Tsei ni ooofo yɛ faai ahe lɛ baaha oná hegbɛ fioo ŋmɛnɛ. Shi ebaaha faa lɛ agbi oya. Enɛ baaha o-abele lɛ akafee nɔ ni nu bɛ mli ni ebaakwɛ̃ sɛɛ mli.

english: How do trees around my farm help keep the ground wet for my cassava during heatwaves?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei ni ebɔle miŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛ̃i yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Tree roots help rain soak deep into the earth rather than running off the surface. This underground water slowly feeds the surrounding soil, keeping your cassava roots moist during dry weather.
ga: Tso shishifãi haa nugbɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni eeejo foi kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi nu nɛɛ baabote shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ mli fiofio Ha o-cassava shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: How do leaves falling from trees near my farm benefit my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Leaves that fall and rot turn into natural manure (organic matter), which feeds nutrients to your crops and improves the soil's ability to hold onto water.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi ni miifite lɛ bafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. (organic matter) ni haa niyenii ni haa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli hewalɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants break down easily during the Harmattan season when there are no trees around?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ harmattan be mli beni tsei bɛ he lɛ?

english: Trees act as windbreaks that slow down dry, harsh Harmattan winds. Without them, strong winds directly strike tall crops like plantains, drying them out fast and blowing them over.
ga: Tsei lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni egbi lɛ baa shi. Kɛ amɛbɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ tamɔ plantains lɛ tɛ̃ɛ, ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ oya ni amɛtswaa amɛhe.

english: Why is the stream water muddy now when I use it to water my nursery bed, and will it harm my seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni yɔɔ faa lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji amrɔ nɛɛ beni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛwoɔ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe lɛ nu lɛ? Ni ani ebaaye midumɔwui lɛ awui?

english: Muddy water happens when trees along the bank are cut and rain washes loose dirt into the stream. Using this muddy water can form a hard crust on top of your seedbed, making it difficult for seeds to germinate.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji baa kɛji afo tsei ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ naa lɛ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni ekɛ muji ni etse ehe lɛ shwieɔ faa lɛ mli. Nu ni mli ewo muji nɛɛ ni akɛaatsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ ni wa aba dumɔwui lɛ anɔ. Ehaa ewaa kɛhaa dumɔwui akɛ amɛakwɛ̃

english: Why do my young cocoa plants dry up and die when I clear all the big shade trees off my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and short root systems that burn and dry out quickly under direct sunlight. Leaving taller shade trees shields the young cocoa from harsh sun, keeps the soil moist, and protects them until their roots grow deep enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi kukuji ni shãa ni egbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kakadaŋŋ ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaabu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do cocoa trees drop so many of their tiny flowers before they ever develop into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo dani amɛbatsɔ pods ni eyi obɔ?

english: A cocoa tree produces far more flowers than it can feed at one time. If the tree lacks sufficient water, soil nutrients, or insect pollinators, it naturally sheds extra flowers so it can focus its strength on forming just a few strong pods.
ga: Kakao tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni ebaanyɛ eye yɛ be kome mli. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my green cocoa pods turn black and rot away right on the tree when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads rapidly in cold, wet weather. Removing infected pods quickly and pruning excess tree branches allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni afoɔ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, turning yellow, and staying small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant stem cuttings prevents this sickness and helps the crop produce large roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ Nibii ni afolɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi wuji shwereɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees if I want a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni fata he kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ kɛji miitao yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When a tree has too many branches, it wastes its food and energy supporting extra leaves instead of growing pods. Pruning off unnecessary or weak branches directs all the plant's nutrients straight into making large, healthy pods.
ga: Kɛ tso ko yɛ niji babaoo Efiteɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ ni fiɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ sɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Niji ni he ehiaaa loo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tso lɛ mli niyenii fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe bɔni afee ni anyɛ adu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Crops planted too close together compete like people fighting for a single plate of food. Their roots steal water and soil nutrients from each other, and their leaves block sunlight, leading to weak, skinny plants with small yields.
ga: Tsei ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ tamɔ gbɔmɛi yɛ niyenii kome he. Amɛshishifãi lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa, ni yibiiwoo hu baa shi.

english: How can I tell if my soil has lost its power and needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: When soil runs out of nutrients, crops grow slowly, leaves turn pale green or yellow instead of dark green, and the fruit or grain stays small. Applying the right fertilizer restores these missing nutrients so plants can grow strong again.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ̃ fiofio. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. ni yibii loo dumɔwu lɛ baakã he ahi bibioo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni eha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than most crops. They drink up the rainfall and steal the plant food out of the ground before your crops ever get a chance to take it in.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe tsei babaoo. Amɛnuɔ nugbɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ tsei aniyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa hegbɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ mli.

english: Why do I need to cover my freshly harvested cocoa beans with plantain leaves for days before drying them in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ plantain baa haa kookoo yibii ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe gbii babaoo dani mikɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the fresh beans creates heat, causing a natural process called fermentation. Fermentation kills the seed inside, removes the bitter taste, and develops the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɔfi yibii heei ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ haa dɔlɛ baa. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ni mli wa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to make big mounds of dirt before planting my yam seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafee shikpɔŋ agbo dani madu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Yams grow deep under the ground. Making loose dirt mounds creates soft soil that allows the yam root to expand easily into a long, thick tuber without struggling against hard ground.
ga: Atomɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Loaming haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni haa sweet potato shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii kakadaji ni mli tse ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa etswaaa.

english: How can I tell if the chemical I sprayed on my caterpillars is actually working?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsu nii diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Check the insects a few hours to a day after spraying. If they fall off the leaves, stop moving, or turn dark, the chemical is working. If they are still actively eating your crop after two days, the mixture may be too weak or it is the wrong product for that pest.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai fioo komɛi kɛyashi gbi kome sɛɛ beni okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ gbee shi lɛ, amɛkpaa nyiɛmɔ. loo tsakemɔ kɛya su ni tsuɔ waa mli Tsɔɔ akɛ tsofa lɛ miitsu nii Kɛji amɛmiiye onibii lolo yɛ gbii enyɔ sɛɛ. Ekolɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ loo eji nɔ ni ejaaa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ.

english: Why are my young maize leaves wilting and turning brown just a day after I sprayed for weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ egbo ni efee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ gbi kome pɛ ni mikɛ jwɛi shwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Leaves burn quickly if weedkiller is mixed too strong or accidentally sprayed directly onto tender crop leaves during hot sunny hours. Always shield your crops or spray early in the morning.
