ga: Tso lɛ baai lɛ shãa oya kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ futu mli waa loo akɛshwie tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Buu onibii ahe be fɛɛ be loo okɛshwie nɔ leebi.

english: Why did the tips of my yam leaves turn black after I applied a new pesticide?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato baai lɛ ashishigbɛi lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ beni mikɛ tsofa hee ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Blackened leaf tips usually mean chemical burn, which happens when a spray is mixed with too little water or applied under intense afternoon sun, shocking the plant's delicate tissues.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ tsɔɔ tsofa ni shãa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ akɛ nu fioo ko pɛ futu tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ mli loo akɛwo hulu la ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa tso lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: When is the best time of day for me to spray chemical treatments on my crops so they don't get damaged?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ? Koni akafite tsei lɛ

english: Spray early in the morning between 6:00 AM and 9:00 AM, or late in the afternoon. The cooler temperatures allow the plant to absorb the treatment safely without the sun scorching wet leaves.
ga: Okɛshwie nɔ leebi ŋmɛji 6:00 AM kɛ 9:00 AM teŋ loo sɛɛ mli yɛ shwane mli. He ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ tsofa lɛ tsuɔ nii shweshweeshwe ni hulu lɛ shãaa baai lɛ ni ehaaa baai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why should I test a new fertilizer on just a small section of my farm before using it everywhere?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka ŋmɔshi nibii hee aka yɛ he bibioo ko? ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani akɛtsu nii yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: Testing on a small patch lets you observe how your soil and crops react over a few days. If the product causes damage or doesn't work well, you save the rest of your farm from potential crop loss.
ga: Kaa ni afeɔ yɛ he bibioo ko nɔ Ehaa okwɛɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli. Kɛji nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ fiteɔ nii loo etsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ Obaanyɛ ohere oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baanyɛ afite lɛ mli.

english: Why do pests return to my vegetable farm just a few days after I spray them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmeii kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Most chemical sprays kill adult bugs but do not destroy hidden insect eggs. When those eggs hatch a few days later, a new batch of pests appears, which is why a follow-up spray is often needed.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni eda shi jeee ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. Kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ fɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ, ŋmeii akuu hee ko baaje kpo. Enɛ hewɔ ni bei pii lɛ ehe hiaa ni akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ sɛɛ lɛ atsu nii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into cups during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves to reduce water loss and protect themselves from extreme heat. If the leaves uncurl when the air cools down in the evening, the plant is simply managing sun stress.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi, ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwie shi beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ miitsu haomɔ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli baa lɛ he nii kɛkɛ.

english: What causes my cassava plants to drop their lower leaves during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava plants shed their lower leaves during dry spells to save water and keep the underground tubers alive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves at the top.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishi baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants keep dying even after I apply fertilizer to help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ fɔ wo mli koni eye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ moŋ.

english: Fertilizer provides food for healthy plants, but it cannot cure root diseases or wilts caused by fungi or bacteria in the soil. If the roots are infected, adding fertilizer will not save the plant.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli Shi enyɛŋ etsa shishifã helai loo ŋmeii ni ŋmeii loo helatsɛmɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi lɛ emɔ hela lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ hereŋ tso lɛ yiwala.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees need more plant food or fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia tsei niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi?

english: Look at the leaf color and stem growth. Pale, light-yellow leaves and slow growth usually show that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, while yellow edges on older leaves signal a need for potassium.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baa lɛ su kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, yɛ be mli ni baai ni egbɔ lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ potassium he miihia.

english: Why should I leave big trees on my farm when they make clearing and planting so much harder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsemɔ kɛ dumɔwui lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa waa nakai?

english: Big trees provide crucial shade that protects young crops from scorching sun, drop leaves that break down into natural fertilizer, and help the soil hold water during dry periods.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Baai ni ekumɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli

english: Will having too many trees on my farm reduce the yield of my food crops?
ga: Ani tsei babaoo ni miyɔɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha niyenii ni miduɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, if shade trees grow too dense, they block the sunlight crops need to produce food and their roots compete for soil nutrients. Pruning tree branches allows light to filter through while keeping the soil protected.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shade lɛ dara tsɔ. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná niyenii lɛ naa, ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa la tsɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he.

english: Is it better to clear my farm land completely clean or keep some trees scattered around?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ majie miŋmɔ lɛ mli kwraa loo mashi tsei lɛ ni egbɛ eshwã he fɛɛ he?

english: Clearing all trees exposes your soil to heavy rain and direct heat, which washes away topsoil and dries out the land. Keeping selected trees protects soil health and creates a better environment for crops.
ga: Tsei fɛɛ ni ooojie lɛ baaha nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ aba oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiɔ. Tsei ni ahala lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ he ni eha shihilɛ kpakpa aba kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why shouldn't I spray chemical pesticides or weedicides on my farm around 1:00 PM or 2:00 PM in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo jwɛi shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ aaafee shwane ŋmɛji 1:00 loo 2:00 PM?

english: Spraying during the hottest part of the day causes the chemical liquid to evaporate quickly into the air before the plants or weeds can absorb it, wasting your time and money.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ haa tsofai lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tsei loo jwɛi baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji be kɛ shika fitemɔ.

english: What is the best time of the day for me to apply spray on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: The best time to spray is early in the morning before the sun gets hot or late in the evening when temperatures drop, allowing the crops to absorb the treatment properly.
ga: Be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ ji leebi dani hulu lɛ adɔ loo gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛheɔ tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why did my crop leaves turn brown and burn after I sprayed them on a sunny day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Liquid drops on crop leaves act like small magnifying glasses under intense afternoon sunlight, concentrating heat and burning the plant tissues.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibioo ko ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ekɛ dɔlɛ baa ni eshãa tso lɛ mli fãji.

english: Why do the pest sprays I buy sometimes fail to kill insects on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ ni miheɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ agbe kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Sprays often fail if applied at the wrong heat of the day, mixed with incorrect water ratios, or applied when pests are hiding under leaves away from the sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii kɛji akɛ akɛwo he ni hulutsoo be ni esaaa yɔɔ. ni akɛ nu ni ejaaa efutu mli Aloo afɔse nɔ beni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo baai ashishi yɛ he ko ni hulu la shɛɛɛ he lɛ.

english: How can government initiatives like 'Planting for Food and Jobs' help me choose the right methods for my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nɔyeli nifeemɔi tamɔ ‘Nibii ni Aduɔ Kɛha Niyenii kɛ Nitsumɔi’ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni mahala gbɛi ni sa kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Government programs provide subsidized inputs like improved seeds and guidance on modern techniques, but you should consult an extension officer to match those inputs to your specific soil and land conditions.
ga: Nɔyeli gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ saji ni akɛyeɔ abuaa tamɔ dumɔwui ni asaa kɛ ŋaawoi ni kɔɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaai ahe haa. Shi esa akɛ oyabi o-extension official lɛ koni ekɛ nakai saji lɛ ato oshikpɔŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ he.

english: Why are my crop yields still poor even though I put in so much hard physical labor every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nii waa daa gbi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hard work alone isn't enough if critical practices like correct plant spacing, proper timing of fertilizer, and sun protection are overlooked, causing effort to go to waste.
ga: Nitsumɔ ni wa pɛ faaa kɛji akɛ aku hiɛ ashwie nifeemɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ja nɔ. Be ni sa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hulutsoo hebuu mli Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ

english: Do tree roots take away all the fertilizer and water meant for my crops?
ga: Ani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Tree roots reach deep into the ground to bring up minerals, but if planted too close to shallow-rooted crops, they can compete for surface water, so proper spacing is essential.
ga: Tso shishifãi yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛjie shika tsuru. Shi kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ he eko lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ nu ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ abɔ he akaŋ No hewɔ lɛ, he ni jɛkɛmɔ ni sa he hiaa.

english: Why do my crops grow well until harvest time in December, but then no buyers want to pay a good price for them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi kpamɔɔ be mli yɛ December mli lɛ? Shi ani hɔlɔ ko bɛ ni sumɔɔ ni ewo nakai tsei lɛ ahe nyɔmɔ kpakpa?

english: When many farmers harvest the exact same crop at the end of the season, the market gets flooded, which causes prices to drop. If your crop isn't dried properly, graded by size, or produced when market demand is high, buyers will choose lower prices or buy from someone else.
ga: Kɛ́ okwaafoi babaoo kpa ŋmɔshi nii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ be lɛ naagbee lɛ, nu yiɔ jara lɛ nɔ, ni no haa nibii ajara baa shi. Kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbiko jogbaŋŋ lɛ, jaa mli yɛ elɛɛmɔ naa loo afee be mli ni jarayeli nibii babaoo biɔ lɛ. Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baahala jara ni baa shi loo ebaahe kɛjɛ mɔ kroko dɛŋ.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting in storage just a few weeks after I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ bɔi fitemɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are bruised by farm tools during harvest, left under the hot sun too long, or stored in a warm room without good airflow. Careful digging and keeping them in a cool, well-ventilated barn helps them last much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ okwaayeli nibii fite amɛ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Aloo okɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ atsa amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ babaoo.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get more maize at the end of the season?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani minine shɛŋ ŋmãa babaoo nɔ yɛ be lɛ naagbee?

english: No, planting seeds too close together makes the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper space ensures they grow strong stems and produce bigger, healthier ears of maize.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa waa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: If I keep planting cassava on the same piece of land every year, why do my yields keep getting smaller?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni hewɔ mi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ miiba shi lɛ?

english: Cassava pulls specific food out of the soil every time it grows. If you do not add fertilizer or rotate the land with crops like beans or groundnuts, the soil becomes tired and weak, leading to smaller tubers.
ga: Cassava gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ebaakwɛ̃. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii wooo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo okɛtsakeee shikpɔŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Does leaving small weeds on my farm hurt my crops if the weeds are not tall enough to hide them?
ga: jwɛi bibii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo Ani ekɛto miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaná miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo kɛji jwɛi lɛ eshɛɛɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatee?

english: Yes, even small weeds have roots under the ground that steal water and soil nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food and water they need to grow well.
ga: Hɛɛ, jwɛi bibii po Shishifãi hu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants full of small holes with stuff that looks like sawdust inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmei yɛ mli?

english: That is a sign of Fall Armyworm attack. The caterpillars hide inside the plant leaves and eat them, leaving behind droppings that look like sawdust. Spraying the right treatment early stops them before they destroy the whole farm.
ga: No ji Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he okadi. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ahe baai amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni ashiɔ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra ni sa Kpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly into tubes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miibɔle ehe kɛmiitsɔ tsɔne mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny, invisible insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the juice from the leaves, or transmitting a virus. Protecting the plants with proper sprays prevents the leaves from twisting and curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii kɛ baai lɛ shwiemɔ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ Emuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai amli loo egbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa shwieɔ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkabɔle amɛhe.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without forming any tomatoes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli woɔ la waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants and cause the pollen inside the flowers to dry up, so fruits cannot form. Giving the plants enough water and light shade during hot spells helps them hold their flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, aduawai efeee. Kɛ́ akɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tso lɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know which crop is best to plant on my land before the main rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: Different crops prefer different soil types and water levels. An agricultural extension officer can test your soil quality and advise you on which crops match your land's soil type and rain patterns.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu srɔtoi. Okwaayeli he nitsulɔi baanyɛ aka bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ amɛkwɛ ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ tsei ni kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ he.

english: Officer, why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying off?
ga: Ofisa Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Yellow leaf tips moving down the middle of the leaf usually mean your maize is lacking Nitrogen. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and make food; when it runs short, the plant drains it from older bottom leaves to feed new top leaves.
ga: Baai lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nyiɛɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛhaa niyenii. Kɛji eyɛ kuku lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is my farm giving me smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same maize on it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi lɛ? He ni miduɔ ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ jɛmɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients over and over without giving the dirt time to recover. Switching to crops like groundnuts or beans helps put good nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli shii abɔ ni amɛfiteee be ni amɛkɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ ahe tsakemɔ haa niyenii kpakpai kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my fertilizer when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can actually drink it in. Putting dry fertilizer on dry ground can burn the plant roots or just sit on top and blow away in the wind.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ ashishifãi ashã loo amɛta nɔ kɛkɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atswa amɛ.

english: If I plant my maize stalks very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest?
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba lɛ efeŋ nɔ ni da?

english: When you plant too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. Instead of getting many big cobs, you end up with tall, thin plants that produce tiny or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji odu ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo najiaŋ lɛ, eji tso kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni woɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: Why do my heavy plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch is getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that cannot support heavy weight during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a strong wooden prop or bamboo pole helps carry the weight until harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛŋ akwɛ nibii ni tsii nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei loo ŋmeii ni wa fi tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi muji lɛ sɛɛ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants wither and die when I clear all the big trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei ni edara lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that sunburn and dry out quickly under full sun. Shade trees act like umbrellas, keeping the cocoa cool and retaining soil moisture until the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu lɛ shãa amɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Shade tsei tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi kookoo lɛ shishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why do I have to spend extra time making high soil mounds before planting my yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafite be kroko kɛfee gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose soil to grow long and thick. Mounds loosen the earth, stop rainwater from drowning the roots, and make it easy for the tubers to expand underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Gɔji lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi. Etsiɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekabote shishifãi lɛ amli. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ mlɛo

english: Why do some of my cassava stem cuttings rot in the dirt instead of sprouting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ekomɛi miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings need to be planted with their growth buds pointing upwards toward the sky. Planting them upside down or in waterlogged soil chokes the stem and causes it to decay.
ga: Ehe miihia ni adu Yucca niji ni ŋmeii wuji lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. To protect itself from dying, the plant drops the flowers instead of spending energy to grow fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ gbele he Tsei baashwie fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni amɛkɛdu aduawai.

english: How do groundnut plants help make the soil better for the next crop I plant?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tso ko aha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut roots have tiny swellings that take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil as natural fertilizer, leaving behind food for whatever crop you plant next.
ga: Peanut shishifãi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii. No baajie nitrogen gas kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. ni ashiɔ niyenii kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ. Nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli

english: Why are my young cocoa leaves turning brown and dying during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight and heat. They require shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them from sun scorch and retain soil moisture until their roots grow deep.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark powder inside the central stem?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baa lɛ nɔ Ni ashi powda ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They hide inside the center whorl of the maize plant to feed, which weakens the plant and reduces your harvest if not treated early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ oya.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting right on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded conditions. Clearing bushy weeds and pruning extra branches lets sunlight and air in, keeping the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ shade yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni ofolɔ tsei krokomɛi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aba mli. Ha pods lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop all their leaves when the long dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is a natural survival response cassava uses to reduce water loss during dry weather. Once the rains return, the stems will sprout fresh leaves and continue growing the underground tubers.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni yucca tsɔɔ nɔ etsuɔ ​​adebɔɔ mli wala he nii. Akɛ enɛ tsuɔ nii koni nu ni fiteɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ aba shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ No lɛ tso lɛ tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni ebaaya nɔ ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii.

english: Tomato leaves curl inward during peak afternoon heat to protect themselves from losing water. If the leaves remain curled in the cool morning, it may indicate a virus or pest problem.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ hela ko loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ko he naagba ko eba.

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea helps the plant stay green and grow taller.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa.

english: Weed seeds rest in the soil and sprout quickly when exposed to rain and sunlight. Because weeds are wild plants adapted to the environment, they absorb water and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce smaller bunches as the farm gets older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ feɔ bibii be mli ni ŋmɔ lɛ daa lɛ?

english: When too many shoots (suckers) grow around one main plantain stem, they compete for nutrients and water. Pruning extra suckers so only two or three remain gives the main plant enough energy to grow large fruit.
ga: Beni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) lɛ daraa kɛbɔleɔ Tso titri kome lɛ fa tsɔ. Amɛyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu he akaŋ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ koni eshwɛ enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a larger harvest?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani manyɛ makpa babaoo?

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients. This produces thin, weak stalks and tiny cobs, whereas proper spacing yields bigger, healthier cobs and a higher overall harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛná ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ be mli ni gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha ŋmeii wuji aba. amɛná hewalɛ kpakpa ni ŋmaa lɛ fɛɛ fa babaoo.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce energy that builds the tuber underground. Staking keeps the vines lifted off damp soil, giving leaves maximum sunlight while preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa wain tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ehe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa ŋmeii helai aba amɛnɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants turn yellow and die when I remove all the big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight. Big trees act like living umbrellas that shield the young cocoa from burning heat and keep the soil moist while the young plants grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei wuji lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔi ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni wa yɔɔ lɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize turning yellow before the corn is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize plant usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen. The plant is moving whatever food it has left from its bottom leaves up to the top to grow the corn cob.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ miitsi niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛmiijɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛmiiya ŋwɛi koni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot underground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ babaoo?

english: When rainwater stays trapped around cassava roots for too long, the soil runs out of air. Without air in the soil, fungal rot develops and destroys the tubers before you can harvest them.
ga: Kɛ nugbɔ nu hi shi yɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Rot fungus lɛ baa ni efiteɔ bulbs lɛ dani obaanyɛ okpa amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow very thin and yield small food when I plant seeds close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee waa ni ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too close together act like too many people eating from one small bowl. They fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving every plant weak and underdeveloped.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ mɛi babaoo ni yeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ tsɛnsi bibioo kome mli. Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛdarako jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they feel too much stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or poor nutrition. Dropping flowers is the plant's way of saving energy to survive the hard conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛnu haomɔ babaoo he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni esaaa mli. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Planting maize on the same spot every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows pests and diseases that attack maize to multiply in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How does covering the soil around my vegetables with dried grass help them grow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket over the soil. It blocks the direct sun, keeps the ground cool, and stops water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Etsĩɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni otsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli

english: Why do extension officers tell me to cut off the small side branches growing near the bottom of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafo tsei niji bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tso lɛ shishigbɛ he lɛ.

english: Those extra bottom branches steal water and food away from the main stem. Removing them forces the plant to send all its energy into making larger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Nakai tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ mli. Tomatoi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I see holes chewed into my young maize leaves in the morning even when I see no insects during the hot day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii ni atsɔ mli yɛ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli leebi be mli ni minaaa ŋmeii yɛ hulutsoo be mli gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests, like armyworms, hide deep inside the soil or under leaves during the hot day to stay safe. They come out to feed on the leaves during the cool morning and evening hours.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ cutworms Hiɔ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ loo baai ashishi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli koni amɛná shweshweeshwe shihilɛ. Amɛjeɔ kpo koni amɛbaye baai lɛ yɛ leebi kɛ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam vines need tall sticks to climb up in order to produce big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa ni ekɛ tsei kakadaji akwɔ koni ekɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji aba lɛ?

english: Yam leaves make food for the plant using sunlight. Staking the vine lifts the leaves up off the ground so they can catch maximum sunlight, which creates the energy needed to swell the tuber under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tso lɛ. Nɔ ni fata wein tso lɛ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ biɔ ni ajie tso lɛ baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni enyɛ ená hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are the leaves of my young cassava plants turning yellow and falling off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during prolonged dry spells to conserve water and survive heat stress, but they naturally sprout fresh green leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Shi amɛwoɔ baai eŋɔli ni kpɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my vegetable crops wilt quickly in the afternoon even when I watered them heavily in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu babaoo haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: When the sun is extremely hot, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can take it up, but if the soil stays too soggy, excess water can also suffocate the roots and cause wilting.
ga: Kɛ hulu lɛ mli edɔ waa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ nu lɛ. Shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ lolo lɛ Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I clear all the big trees away from the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in full sun; they require shade crops like plantains to shelter them from direct heat and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo tamɔ plantains koni ebu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa tɛ̃ɛ he, ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers grow very tall and thin instead of thick and strong when planted under dense forest trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ tsei ashishi yɛ koo ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require direct light to build strong stems, so when they are overcrowded by big trees, they stretch unnaturally high to reach sunlight, making them weak and easy for wind to break.
ga: La he miihia plantains tɛ̃ɛ koni efee tsei ni wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ tsei wuji eyi amɛmli obɔ lɛ, Amɛbaashɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa koni amɛshɛ hulu la lɛ he. Enɛ haa egbɔjɔɔ ni ewaaa akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ baakumɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop is fully mature and ready to harvest so it does not spoil before I get it to market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa? No hewɔ lɛ, egbooo dani akɛwoɔ jara nɔ?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks dry out and turn completely brown, and the kernels become hard enough that pressing them with your thumbnail leaves no dent.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa. Ni dumɔwui lɛ wa bɔ ni sa ni obaanyɛ okɛ onineshi tsɔne lɛ anyɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni amɛkashi ŋmeii komɛi.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots inside the barn even when I haven't planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduuu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yam tubers are living storehouses that naturally break their internal rest period after a few months, using their stored moisture and nutrients to push out shoots in anticipation of the rainy season.
ga: Sweet potato tubers ji nitoohei ni hiɛ ka ni baafo amɛmli shihilɛ ni amɛyɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Ekɛ nu ni ato kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ koni emɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields of food crops when I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ niyenii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients like nitrogen, so growing it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients unless you rotate with nitrogen-fixing crops like cowpeas or groundnuts.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii komɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ babaoo, tamɔ nitrogen, no hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ adu shii abɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, nakai niyenii lɛ baaho aya. No ji ja okɛ tsei ni haa nitrogen hiɔ shi tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ amɛhe.

english: Why do weeds along the roadside edges of my farm grow much faster than the crops inside my main plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbɛjegbɛ lɛ he ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miida oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ titri lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Roadside edges receive undisturbed sunlight and rainwater runoff carrying rich topsoil, which creates ideal conditions for wild weed seeds to germinate and grow rapidly.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ naa hulu la ni sɛɛ efooo kɛ nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ ni hiɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni koo mli jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara oya.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers onto the ground before any peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miishwie efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani pepper lɛ baanyɛ ada lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from high temperature stress, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil minerals like calcium during the flowering stage.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa mli. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo sũ mli nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni bɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ beaŋ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often the plant's natural reaction to intense heat and dry winds to prevent water loss, though it can also be caused by viral infections spread by insects like whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ tomato mli lɛ ji bɔ ni tso lɛ feɔ enii ehaa kɛji edɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi. Bɔni afee ni nu akafite Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji hela ko ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela mli ni kooloi tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ po.

english: Leaves turn yellow mainly when the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or when heavy rain causes waterlogging around the roots. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving field drainage helps the leaves regain their green color.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ titri kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa haa nu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo aha nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes their pollen to dry out, which prevents fruit formation and makes the flowers fall off. Providing regular watering and light shade during peak hot periods helps protect the flowers.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haaa aduawai afee ni ehaa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ nu kɛ hulutsoo be mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Pepper leaves curl up in the heat to reduce their surface area and save water from evaporating too quickly. However, if the leaves stay curled all the time, it is usually a sign that tiny insects like thrips or mites are feeding on them.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ la mli koni ekɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni ekɛtsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be lɛ, Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites miiye amɛ.

english: Why does my rice crop need standing water in the field during its early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mi-ŋmãa tso lɛ aná nu ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ shishijee be mli ni edaa lɛ?

english: Standing water suppresses weeds naturally by suffocating weed seeds while keeping the soil consistently soft and moist for the rice roots, which are adapted to thrive in flooded conditions.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛtsɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaa ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ. ni atsake lɛ koni eda yɛ shihilɛi ni nu afua yɔɔ mli lɛ amli

english: Why does my traditional local rice variety give me lower yields compared to the modern seed varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi lɛ?

english: Older traditional rice varieties tend to grow very tall leaves instead of heavy grains and fall over easily in strong winds. Modern varieties are bred to stay shorter, grow faster, and direct more of their energy into producing abundant rice grains.
ga: Kusum mli ŋmãa henɔi ni etsɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ baa ni kɛlɛ waa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni tsii najiaŋ. ni egbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Afɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kooloi srɔtoi lɛ koni amɛfee kuku. shwereɔ oya ni ekɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa ni woɔ yibii

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest grow into weaker plants than fresh seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ da ni etsɔ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial seeds are specially crossed for maximum vigor in their first generation. When you save and replant those harvested seeds, they lose that combined strength, leading to uneven plant heights and smaller cobs.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ fɛɛ fiteɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ akwɔlɛ jeee ekome, ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do I get bigger cassava roots when I plant on soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmei shishifãi wuji anɔ kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers need loose, uncompacted soil to expand easily. Making mounds creates soft, well-drained soil that allows the roots to grow wide and long compared to hard, flat ground.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni mli tse he miihia cassava tsei lɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Gɔŋ ni afee lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ kakadaŋŋ kɛ akɛto shikpɔŋ ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ he.

english: What happens to my cowpea crops if I plant the seeds too close together in my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cowpea tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting cowpeas too closely forces the plants to compete for sunlight, ground water, and nutrients, resulting in thin stems and fewer pods. It also traps humidity, which encourages fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsina ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee bibii ni ŋmeii fioo pɛ aba. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hu hiɔ shi, ni no woɔ ŋmɔtɔ helai ahe hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why is it important for me to weed around my young yam vines very early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Sweet potato tsei bibii ni yɔɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Weeds grow much faster than young yam plants and quickly steal water and soil nutrients. Early weeding removes this competition so your yam vines can establish strong roots and form large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe sweet potato tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni ajie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Enɛ baaha o-sweet potato wain tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving the young cocoa trees the shade and cool moisture they need to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why are parts of my cocoa trees turning black and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ fãi komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ?

english: Blackened leaves, stems, or pods on cocoa trees are usually signs of fungal infections like Black Pod disease or damage from sap-sucking insects. These pests feed on the tree's fluids, causing the affected parts to dry up, turn dark, and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai, amɛshishifãi, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii emɔ amɛ, tamɔ ŋmeii diji hela loo ŋmeii ni nuɔ ŋmeii lɛ efite. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tsei amli nu. Enɛ haa he ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ lɛ gbiɔ, ewoɔ duŋ, ni egboɔ.

english: Can small insects really kill an entire full-grown cocoa tree?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii baanyɛ agbe kookoo tso ni eda kwraa lɛɛlɛŋ?

english: Yes. Even small insects can kill a large tree if they attack in large numbers over time. As they feed continuously on the sap, they drain the tree's energy and can also spread harmful viruses or fungi directly into the wood.
ga: Hɛɛ. Kplukai bibii po baanyɛ agbe tsei wuji kɛji amɛtutua amɛ babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli. Kɛ amɛnuɔ mliki be fɛɛ be lɛ Ejieɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ helai loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui hu eshwa tso lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to rot dark black before they are ripe?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛshwere?

english: This is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in damp, shaded environments. The fungus spreads across the pod surface, turning it black and destroying the beans inside if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Fuŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa pod lɛ hiɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ kɔfe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How do I know if an insect pest on my farm is actively destroying my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miifite mi-cacao tsei lɛ?

english: You will notice damage like dark spots on stems, wilting leaves, damaged pods, or sticky residue on branches. If insects are feeding continuously, the tree will start losing leaves and show signs of severe weakness.
ga: Obaana nibii ni efite tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe, baai ni egbo, ŋmeii ni efite, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ. Kɛji kooloi bibii tee nɔ amɛtao niyenii Tso lɛ baabɔi baai lɛ shwiemɔ ni ebaajie bɔjɔmɔ he okadii ni mli wa kpo.

english: Why do some insect pests destroy my crops heavily and then suddenly disappear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii waa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛlaaajeɔ trukaa lɛ?

english: Many crop pests go through distinct lifecycles. They feed aggressively while growing, complete their feeding stage until their energy is spent, lay eggs, and then die off or fly away to search for new food sources.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo yɛ wala shihilɛi srɔtoi. Amɛyeɔ nii waa beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Eyeɔ nii kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ehewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ, ewoɔ wɔji, kɛkɛ ni egboɔ loo efoɔ kɛyaa koni eyatao niyenii hee.

english: What makes a cocoa tree lose all its strength and stop producing pods?
ga: Mɛni haa cacao tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi ni amɛkpaa ŋmeii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree loses its strength when diseases or pests continually drain its stored nutrients. When the tree uses all its energy just trying to stay alive, it can no longer afford to produce flowers or grow pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ ahewalɛ baa shi kɛ́ helai loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ato lɛ be fɛɛ be. Beni tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ lɛ. Enyɛɛɛ ewo fɔfɔi loo ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii dɔŋŋ.

english: If my cocoa tree leaves turn black and drop off, can the tree recover on its own?
ga: Kɛji mi-kookoo baai lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ Ani tso lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baatsa ehe?

english: If only a few leaves are damaged, the tree can grow new ones once given fertilizer and proper care. However, if a disease has reached the main trunk or root system, the damage may be permanent and kill the tree.
ga: Kɛji baai fioo komɛi pɛ ni efite lɛ Tso lɛ baanyɛ adara ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ. Shi, kɛji hela lɛ shɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he lɛ Nɔ ni efite lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi daa ni eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why does cocoa disease keep returning to my farm every year even after I spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni cocoa hela lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ ebaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi beni mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwie nɔ po lɛ?

english: Disease spores and insect eggs can hide in old stems, fallen leaves, or uncollected black pods. If these sources are not cleared away, the disease will reactivate and attack new growth as soon as weather conditions are favorable.
ga: Helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ kooloi awui baanyɛ ahi tsei momo, baai ni egbee shi, loo tsei diji ni ajieee lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ajieee nɛkɛ jɛɛhei nɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, Hela lɛ baabɔi nitsumɔ ekoŋŋ ni ebaatutua shweremɔ heei amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ŋmɛɔ gbɛ.

english: Why is it bad to leave black, ruined pods hanging on my cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashi ŋmeii diji ni egboi yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Black pods act as breeding grounds for fungi and pests. Leaving them on the tree allows the infection to remain active, multiply, and spread to healthy trees nearby during rain or wind.
ga: Black pods ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ aya nɔ atsu nii, eshwere ni egbɛ eshwa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ be mli.

english: When is the best time to protect my cocoa trees from pests before they weaken the crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ abu kookoo tsei ahe kɛjɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe dani amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbɔjɔ?

english: The best time is early in the season when new shoots and young pods begin to appear. Spraying early kills pests while their population is small, stopping them before they feed enough to damage or kill the trees.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be lɛ shishijee mli beni ŋmeii heei kɛ ŋmeii bibii jeɔ shishi amɛjeɔ kpo lɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ shi koni akɛgbe kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ mra be mli ni amɛyibɔ ​​faaa Ehaa amɛkpaa dani amɛyeɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baafite loo egbe tso lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the primary food maize needs to grow green and strong. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed poultry manure around the base will help the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ bɔleɔ tso lɛ he. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense tropical sunlight. Plantain trees grow rapidly and produce wide leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa plants need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli akpɔlɔi. Ha kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungal infection that spreads fast during rainy and damp weather. Pruning heavy shade tree branches to let sunlight and wind into your farm, along with removing infected pods, helps keep the disease away.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo waa lɛ ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ hu. Ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ helai anaa.

english: What is making ragged holes in the leaves at the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni miiha baai lɛ miishi bu yɛ mi ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: Ragged holes in the central leaf funnel are a common sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars. You can control them by spraying recommended insecticides early in the morning or by placing a small pinch of clean sand or dry ash into the funnel of affected plants.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni oookɛshwie nɔ leebi lɛ nɔ. aloo kɛtsɔ ŋã ni he tse loo sũ ni egbi fioo ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ atsɔnei lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them for too long, especially in heavy soils during heavy rains. Planting your cassava stems on raised ridges or mounds allows excess water to drain away easily and protects the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Titri lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo gɔji anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya ni ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight so their leaves can produce food for the underground tuber. Keeping the vines off the wet ground also prevents leaves from catching diseases and results in much bigger tubers.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná hela, ni no haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji babaoo.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids that suck the sap and spread viruses. Spraying the plants with neem leaf extract or appropriate pest sprays kills the insects and allows healthy leaves to grow.
ga: Kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ hela lɛ eshwaa Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ ni ebaaha baai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the soil dries out completely or when weather temperatures become extremely hot. Watering your plants consistently at the root zone and applying straw mulch keeps the soil cool and helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa yɛ he ni eshishifã lɛ yɔɔ lɛ, ni okɛ jwɛi ha he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i, ni ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How do tiny beetles get inside my harvested cowpea beans and leave holes in them?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii bibii boteɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ amli ni amɛshiɔ bu yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: Cowpea weevils lay tiny, unseen eggs on the pods while they are still in the field, and the larvae burrow into the seeds during storage. Storing dry cowpeas in airtight containers or triple-layer bags suffocates the insects and prevents damage.
ga: Cowpea ŋmei lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii bibii. ni anaaa yɛ pod lɛ nɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo Ni ŋmeii lɛ baafo dumɔwui lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsina ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo kotoku ni mli fãi etɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaatsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa.

english: Standing water suppresses aggressive weeds that compete with young rice for soil nutrients and sunlight. While rice plants do not need to be completely submerged, controlled water keeps soil temperatures stable and promotes uniform growth.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ tsiɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni kɛ ŋmãa bibii yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ naa. Eyɛ mli akɛ ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ awo nu mli kwraa moŋ, shi nu ni akudɔɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli latsaa hiɔ shi daa ni ehaa amɛdaraa po.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their leaves burn easily and the dry heat drains soil moisture. They need partial shade from fast-growing plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya, ni la ni mli egbi lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli. Koni abu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure can help bring back the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi ashishifãi ni egbo jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha amɛbaai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I keep planting maize on the exact same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. Alternating your maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina loo ŋmãa baatsake ŋmãa Enɛ baaha nitrogen lɛ aku esɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes small caterpillars to eat holes in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are usually Fall Armyworms, a common pest that hides in the center of maize plants and eats the leaf tissue. Inspecting your field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or chemical treatments directly into the plant center can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ ni eyeɔ baai amli fãji. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ afee yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: How do I know when my cassava tubers are ready to be harvested from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Cassava is typically mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. A key indicator is when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, or you can carefully dig near the base of one plant to check tuber size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Nɔ ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ ji be mli ni shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsa he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso kome shishi koni ona bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ dara ha.

english: Why do some farmers cover the soil around their vegetable plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This practice is called mulching. Covering the soil traps moisture so the ground stays damp longer during dry periods, reduces weed growth, and eventually breaks down into rich organic food for the crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Mulching mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli. Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni naagbee lɛ egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ niyenii ni jara wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines and tie them to tall wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tsei anɔ ni mikɛfiɔ tsei kakadaji ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing plant that produces energy through sunlight to build large underground tubers. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which prevents leaf rot and increases your tuber size.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji tsei ni kwɔɔ ni jieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ hulu la mli koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la mli. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite ni eha bulb lɛ dalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do some of the seeds I sow fail to sprout even after good rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni miduɔ lɛ kwɛɛɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ po lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are too old, damaged by insects, planted too deeply in the soil, or submerged in standing water. Using certified, high-quality seeds and planting at the correct depth ensures better sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji amɛgbɔ tsɔ. ni kooloi bibii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ loo ni awo amɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo mli lɛ efite Kɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odase akɛ akɛtsu nii ni adu amɛ yɛ he ni sa lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping the fruits from growing well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiitsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by heavy heat stress, irregular watering, or viruses spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Maintaining regular watering and protecting young plants from sap-sucking insects helps prevent this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ he haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo helai ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa kɛ tsei bibii ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Does clearing weeds early really make a big difference in how much grain my maize will produce?
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ani eyɛ hewalɛ ni sa kadimɔ yɛ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛhaa lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, because weeds grow faster than young crops and steal soil food, water, and sunlight. Clearing weeds within the first four to six weeks of planting gives your crops all the nourishment they need to build strong stalks and large ears.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la mli. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi enumɔ ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni wa kɛ toi wuji.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth, or that heavy rain has logged the soil so roots cannot breathe. Adding a nitrogen fertilizer like urea or rich compost helps restore the green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyashiɔ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli ewo muji fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Cassava roots rot when water settles in the soil for too long during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away so the tubers stay dry and healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme sun, lack of moisture, or insect damage. Keeping enough shade trees around your cocoa and protecting them from sap-sucking pests keeps flowers healthy enough to turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hao amɛ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo kooloi bibii fiteɔ Kookoo tsei akwɛmɔ haa hulutsoo ni sa kɛ hebuu kɛjɛɔ kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ahe. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ pods.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of flowers, so why are they not producing any fruit?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛni hewɔ ekɛ yibiiwoo ko baaa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need gentle breezes or insects like bees to shake the pollen inside the flower so fruit can grow. If the weather is too hot and dry, the pollen dies before fertilizing the flower, causing it to drop off empty.
ga: Tomato he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli jɔ loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ ŋmeii, koni amɛwoso pollen ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi lɛ Pollen baagbo dani ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why does my soil dry out completely just two days after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii enyɔ pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses water fast under hot sunshine. Covering the bare ground around your crop roots with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps water in the ground for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. He ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle he lɛ nɔ ni akɛhaa Tso shishifãi ahe kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu hiɔ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines curling up and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids living under the leaves or by a plant virus. Checking under the leaves early and spraying with organic solutions like neem water can clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi loo tsei amli helai baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsofa ko ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn brown and break off easily during dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkuɔ oya yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Dry winds and lack of water weaken plantain leaf stems, making them snap. Removing dry lower leaves and keeping organic mulch around the plant base helps hold moisture during dry spells like the Harmattan.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ haa plantain baa lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ajieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbi lɛ ni akɛ organic mulch haa amɛhe. Taakɛ Harmattan ji lɛ, shishitoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping small green peppers onto the ground before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho pepper bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ? Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ekwɛ̃?

english: Pepper plants drop young fruit when watering is irregular—such as letting the soil get very dry and then suddenly flooding it—or during sudden spikes in temperature. Giving the plants consistent, steady water prevents fruit drop.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie aduawai bibii kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua ni baa trukaa lɛ ba. aloo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ trukaa lɛ Nu ni oooha tsei lɛ daa kɛ daa lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ akagbee shi.

english: Why are my groundnut plants staying short and stunted instead of spreading across the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ yɔɔ kuku ni amɛhe ejɔ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts stay small if the ground is too hard for the roots to expand or if underground pests like nematodes are damaging the roots. Loosening the soil well before planting allows the roots to spread and feed properly.
ga: Peanuts baafee bibioo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes miifite shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani adu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛyeɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do wild weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are naturally wild and tough, so they steal water, light, and nutrients from the soil faster than domestic crops can. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops get all the food they need to outgrow the weeds.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji adebɔɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shia tsei baanyɛ afee. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya fe jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees burn and die when I clear away all the large shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shã ni amɛgboi beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate foliage and sensitive root systems that burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains shields young cocoa plants, keeping the leaves cool and retaining moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize stalks stay thin and weak when I plant four or five seeds together in a single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa nɛkɛ beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted in one hole, the seedlings compete fiercely with each other underground for root space, water, and soil nutrients, causing all of them to grow weak and yield small ears.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli Dumɔwui lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná shishifãi ahe gbɛ, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ daaa fioo ni amɛwoɔ toi bibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the leaf tips are a sign of nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen gives plants their deep green color and growth energy, so adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-decomposed manure will help green up the crop.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nitrogen haa tsei lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die during the day even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial wilt diseases that clog the plant's internal water pipes, preventing moisture from reaching the leaves from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni baa trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ baa. ni tsiɔ tsei amli nu paipii lɛ anaa Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekashɛ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli.

english: What causes black spots to appear on my cocoa pods, making them dry up and turn completely black?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ baa? Ha egbi ni etsɔ ediŋŋ kwraa?

english: This damage is typically caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads during cool, wet weather, or insect pests like mirids (akate) that pierce the pod skin and allow rot to enter.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Fungal helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli ejɔ, ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (akatate) ni tsɔɔ pod lɛ hewolo mli ni ehaa egboɔ.

english: Why did the tips and edges of my leaves turn brown and scorched after I put chemical fertilizer around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibaai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛ amɛshishigbɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshã beni akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle baa lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Placing fertilizer too close to the stem or applying it in dry soil draws water out of the plant roots rather than feeding them, causing a chemical burn on the leaf edges.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishi tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeebote mli. Ehaa tsofa shãa baa lɛ naa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall stems with leafy tops, but the roots underneath stay very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kɛlɛ kɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli etsii waa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus all its energy on growing leaves and stems, leaving very little energy to form thick, starchy tuber roots underground.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ eshwɛ ni baanyɛ afee tuber shishifãi ni mli tse ni tamɔ powder lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground without sprouting after heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ sũ mli ni amɛkwɛɛɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need both water and air to germinate. When heavy rain saturates the soil without proper drainage, oxygen is pushed out, causing the buried seeds to drown and decay.
ga: Nu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fɛɛ he hiaa dumɔwui koni amɛkwɛ̃. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ nu ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ jogbaŋŋ. Akɛ oxygen lɛ shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni afu lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before forming any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when plants suffer from stress caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of balanced nutrients like calcium and boron, which plants need to hold onto blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni sa tamɔ calcium kɛ boron ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why is my maize crop producing flowers and tassels when the plants are still very short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ yɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ? Tso lɛ yɛ kuku waa lolo?

english: When crops face early drought or extreme stress, they trigger early flowering as a survival mechanism to produce seeds before dying, even if the plant stalk hasn't finished growing.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ hɔmɔ loo haomɔ ni naa wa kpe mra Amɛhaa fɔfɔi baa mra akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛwo dumɔwui dani amɛgboi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ edako kwraa lolo moŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when the sun is too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Beni hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct heat. Planting plantains or shade trees next to them provides a living umbrella that keeps the ground cool and retains soil moisture until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: When crops are planted too close to each other, they fight for the same limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to produce large, healthy ears of maize.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmãa toi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water builds up around them because the soil cannot drain. Planting your cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers, keeping them healthy.
