ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu ni ekã shi ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ amli. ha amɛhe awa

english: Why does covering the ground around my crops with dry grass and leaves help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni eha he ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ No hewɔ lɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves (mulching) blocks direct sunlight from drying out the dirt, keeping the soil cool and moist for longer. It also smothers unwanted weeds so they cannot grow.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haaa muji lɛ agbi. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be kakadaŋŋ. Ejieɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ hu koni amɛkakwɛ̃.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, pests that hide inside the central funnel of young maize plants to eat the soft leaves. Detecting them early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts protects the crop before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. mra ni anaa Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper bushes curling up and turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Curling leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap out of the leaves and spreading viruses. Spraying early with neem oil or soapy water keeps these pests away and stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo nu ni mli edɔ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe ni amɛkpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my vegetable leaves after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew, which spreads quickly in damp, humid weather. Spacing plants well to let air flow between them reduces moisture on the leaves and prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Pauda yɛŋ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei lɛ to he ko jogbaŋŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ amɛteŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ aba shi, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a signal that the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an important food for growth. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color and increases your yield.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Yam vines need to reach up to catch sunlight so the plant can make food. Staking keeps the leaves off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases while encouraging the tuber underground to grow larger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it weak. Legumes like cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, naturally restoring fertility for your next planting cycle without costly chemicals.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why do my maize grains lose so much weight after I dry them in the sun before selling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ amli shwieɔ shi babaoo beni agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: When maize is freshly harvested, the grains hold a lot of water inside. Sun-drying removes this extra water so the grains will not rot during storage, but losing that water weight makes the harvest lighter on the scale.
ga: Kɛji akpa ŋmãa hee Dumɔwui lɛ toɔ nu babaoo. Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ jieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ fiteŋ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Shi nu ni tsiimɔ baa shi lɛ baaha kpamɔ lɛ afee mlɛo yɛ sɛkɛl lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some of my harvested cocoa beans lighter in weight than others, even when they fill the same 25-kilo bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa yibii ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi yɛ mlɛo fe ekrokomɛi lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ewo kotoku ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 25 lɛ nɔŋŋ mli moŋ.

english: Cocoa beans become light or flat if the cocoa tree did not get enough water or nutrients while the pods were forming. Well-nourished trees produce fully developed, dense seeds that pack more actual weight.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ muji ni yɔɔ mligbɛ muji babaoo.

english: Why do my yams spoil quickly in the sack if I pack them right after digging them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo amɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly dug yams release moisture and warmth. If you pack them immediately into bags without letting them dry and cure in a cool, airy place, the trapped moisture causes heat and mold, which rots the tubers.
ga: Atomɔ ni atsa ehee lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ dɔlɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ okɛwo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ohaaa egbi ni okɛwo he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ. Fɛ̃i ni emɔ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa. ni baanyɛ aha yitso lɛ agbɔjɔ

english: Why do my stored cowpeas seem to shrink and weigh less after a few months in the bag?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cowpeas ni mikɛto lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsiimɔ baa shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi ni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny pests like weevils bore into stored cowpeas and eat the insides of the seeds. Even if the bag looks completely full, the hollowed-out seeds lose their inner substance and weigh much less on the scale.
ga: Nibii bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii baafo tsina ŋmeii ni ato lɛ amli ni amɛye dumɔwui lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ kotoku lɛ mli eyi obɔ moŋ, shi dumɔwui ni afo mli lɛ laajeɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ, ni amɛtsiimɔ baa shi kwraa yɛ sɛkɛl lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested soybeans are dry enough to pack into 25-kilo bags without spoiling?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi soybean ni mikpa lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo 25kg kotokui amli ni efiteee?

english: You can test soybean dryness by biting or pressing a seed with your fingernail; a properly dry seed is hard and will not dent. If it feels soft or leaves a dent, it still holds water and will rot if sealed inside a bag.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka bɔ ni soybeans lɛ egbi ha lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni oookɛ onine ashɛ nɔ loo ooonyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wa ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo loo eyɛ ŋmeii Nu baahi mli lolo ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ awo kotoku mli.

english: If I harvest my cassava early before it fully matures, will it affect how much weight I get when I sell it?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmei mra dani eda kwraa Ani enɛ baaná muji ni mináa kɛji mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, young cassava tubers contain mostly water and very little starch. As the plant grows to full maturity, it fills the roots with heavy solid starch, making mature cassava tubers denser and heavier on the scale.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu babaoo yɛ ŋmei shishifãi bibii amli kɛ ŋmei fioo ko pɛ. Kɛ tso lɛ da kɛyashɛ shweremɔ he lɛ Ebaawo shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsii ni wa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni edara lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ shwiili lɛ mli tsiimɔ.

english: How does applying fertilizer to my rice field affect the actual weight of the harvested grains?
ga: Te mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ saa ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ diɛŋtsɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Fertilizer gives rice plants the essential food needed to fill out every single grain completely. Plump, fully filled grains contain fewer empty husks, giving you more solid weight per bag at harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmãa fɛɛ ŋmãa mli ekoŋŋ. Plump grains lɛ bɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko. Enɛ haa onáa muji babaoo yɛ kotoku kome mli kɛ́ ookpa nii.

english: Why do some of my tomato plants produce large fruits while others on the same land produce tiny, light ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni waaa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants need equal access to water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Plants that are shaded, crowded, or competing with weeds cannot feed their fruits properly, resulting in smaller, lighter tomatoes.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ hia ni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli, ni eyi obɔ kɛ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ lɛ nyɛŋ aha amɛyibii lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tomato bibii ni waaa lɛ baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before the peppers can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii dani pepper lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of water, or sudden weather changes. The plant sheds its flowers to conserve its own life and energy rather than feeding new fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ mli, nu ni bɛ, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala kɛ hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaawo yibii heei.

english: Why do my plantain bunches weigh less when I plant the suckers very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ tsiimɔ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmeii lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When plantains are planted too close together, their broad leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for food in the soil. Without enough nutrients, each plant produces smaller, lighter fruit bunches.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu plantains ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaai ni mli kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulu la lɛ he tsɔi. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii yeɔ akaŋ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso fɛɛ tso baawo yibii bibii ni waaa.

english: How can I tell if my papaya plants will actually bear fruit or if they are just male plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mipapaya tso lɛ baawo yibii diɛŋtsɛ loo eji tso ko ni ji nuu kɛkɛ?

english: Papaya plants come in male, female, and hermaphrodite types. Male flowers grow on long, branching stalks and do not produce fruit, while female and hermaphrodite flowers grow close to the main trunk and can develop into fruits.
ga: Papaya tsei lɛ baa yɛ hii, yei kɛ hii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii lɛ amli. Fɔfɔi hii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji ni niji yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ ni amɛwooo yibii. yɛ be mli ni pistillate kɛ hermaphroditic fɔfɔii lɛ daa kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing on cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease. It spreads through tiny insects called whiteflies or when you use infected stems as planting material.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kooloi bibii amli. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛ́ okɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ tsu nii akɛ dumɔ nii.

english: The best time to apply the first batch of fertilizer is about 10 to 14 days after the seeds germinate. You should apply a second round when the stalks reach knee height, around 4 to 6 weeks after planting.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli ji aaafee gbii 10 kɛyashi 14 beni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ nɔ ni ji enyɔ awo nɔ beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ tsitsi nɔ, aaafee otsii 4 kɛyashi 6 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I remove all the large trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mijie tsei ni eda lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Leaving taller trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects the cocoa seedlings from scorching heat and retains soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni aaashi loo adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ kookoo plantains lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Does the color of a yam tuber mean one variety is automatically better than another?
ga: Ani sweet potato shishifã lɛ su tsɔɔ akɛ eko hi fe ekroko?

english: Color shows the difference between varieties, such as white yam or yellow yam, which differ in taste, dry matter, and cooking texture. However, skin or flesh color alone does not mean one variety is healthier or higher yielding than another.
ga: Su tsɔɔ srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ, tamɔ sweet potato yɛŋ loo ŋmɔŋ, ni esoro amɛhe yɛ bɔ ni amɛmli ŋɔɔmɔ, bɔ ni amɛgbiɔ, kɛ bɔ ni amɛhooɔ amɛhaa lɛ mli. Shi kɛlɛ, hewolonɔ su loo loo su pɛ etsɔɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ eko yɛ hewalɛ loo ewoɔ yibii babaoo fe ekroko.

english: Pepper plants usually drop flowers due to stress from extreme heat, dry soil, or over-fertilizing. When the plant gets too hot or lacks steady water, it drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo ebɛ nu ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them after maize restores nutrients naturally so your next crop grows better.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni ooodu yɛ abele sɛɛ lɛ baaha adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if fall armyworms are attacking my corn field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ fall cutworms miitutua mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Look for ragged holes eaten into the central leaves of the corn plant, along with dark, sawdust-like droppings inside the whorl. You may also see caterpillars with an inverted 'Y' shape on their heads.
ga: Taomɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ. Ayeɔ awoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli. Kɛfata ŋmeii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ he. Obaanyɛ ona ŋmei ko ni ‘Y’ ni atsake lɛ yɔɔ eyitso nɔ.

english: Cassava is generally ready 9 to 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping off, and the base of the main stem will swell slightly as tubers mature underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Ni tso lɛ shishigbɛ tso lɛ shishi baafu fioo be mli ni bulb lɛ daa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Wild weeds are naturally adapted to local soils and can absorb water and nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early gives your planted crops the sunlight and nutrition they need to grow strong.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ebaanyɛ ejie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha otsei lɛ aná hulu la kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the soil is too wet for roots to feed properly. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ aye abua lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa blossoms fall off the tree without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from dry heat stress, nutrient shortages, or insect damage like capsids. Providing proper shade trees and managing pests helps the blossoms mature into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni mli egbi lɛ hewɔ. niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii, tamɔ capsids. Shade ni sa kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛɔ dalɛ mli.

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil encourages cowpeas to produce leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally feed themselves nitrogen from the air, so they need little to no extra nitrogen fertilizer to produce heavy pod yields.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ tsina ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛwo baai moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Cowpeas yeɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbiɔ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ loo amɛhe ehiaaa kwraa koni amɛfee pod ni tsii.

english: How do I know when the rainy season has truly started so I can plant my cassava?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ nugbɔnɛmɔ be lɛ eje shishi diɛŋtsɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani manyɛ madu ŋmei?

english: Wait until the soil stays wet at least hand-deep for several consecutive days after the early rains begin. Planting during the first short rain can trick you, leaving cassava stem cuttings to dry out if dry heat returns.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, kɛ hoo lɛ, eshɛɔ onine he, gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ beni nugbɔ lɛ eje shishi lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi kukuji amli Klɛŋklɛŋ be lɛ baanyɛ alaka bo. Kɛtsɔ ŋmei niji ni oooŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛgbi kɛji latsaa lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my farm soil turn hard like a brick after rain dries up in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sũ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ brikii beni nugbɔ enɛɔ ni hulu lɛ eshɛ enɔ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost or decomposing plant material. Mixing dry leaves, crop leftovers, or animal manure into the topsoil keeps it soft, spongy, and easy for roots to grow through.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsei ni egbo lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ baai ni egbi ni akɛfutu tsei amli nibii ni etse Loo kooloi aŋmei ni akɛfata shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ ŋmeii ni eha shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ mlɛo.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of large and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, deep, and loose soil mounds to stretch out easily. Compacted soil or underground rocks stop the tuber from expanding freely, causing it to grow small, branched, or twisted.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia gɔŋ ko ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni shwieɔ shi koni ekɛgbala mli mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ tsiɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe. ni haa efeɔ bibioo, niji, loo egbɛɔ eshwaa

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die even when I water them every morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting despite moist soil is usually caused by soil-borne diseases like bacterial wilt that clog the plant's internal water channels. Rotating tomatoes with crops like maize or cassava cleans the soil of these germs over time.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa, tamɔ bacteria wilt ni tsiɔ tso lɛ mli nu gbɛi lɛ anaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli edɔ po baa trukaa. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake tomato. Enɛ baaye abua ni etsumɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛjɛ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ amli yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are there so many ants crawling up and down my vegetable stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii babaoo miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-vegetables tsei lɛ anɔ kɛmiiba shi lɛ?

english: Ants do not usually harm plants directly; they are attracted to tiny insects like aphids or mealybugs that secrete a sweet sticky liquid. Controlling those tiny sap-sucking pests will make the ants leave your plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii etutuuu tsei tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛgbalaa kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ni jieɔ nu ni mli tse ni ŋɔɔ kpo lɛ. Nibii bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ Namɛi baaha ŋmeii akaje otsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why are my plantain leaves curling up and turning brown at the edges?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Plantain leaves curl and turn brown when the plant suffers from intense heat, drought stress, or leaf spot disease. Placing a thick layer of dry grass mulch around the plant base keeps the soil moist and cool.
ga: Plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ ye hulutsoo ni naa wa waa nɔ. Hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo baai amli hela, jwɛi ni egbi ni mli tse ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my pepper fruits turn black and rot while still hanging on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot happens when the pepper plant cannot draw enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture steady prevents the fruit tips from turning black and rotting.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa kɛji akɛ pepper tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ baatsi aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛkafite.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which is essential food for the crop. Adding fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers and tiny fruits before they can mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers and tiny fruits drop when the soil dries out too quickly or when small insect pests attack the blossoms. Keeping the soil evenly moist and checking for pests helps the plants hold onto their fruit until harvest.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai bibii Amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ oya tsɔ. aloo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ aduawai amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni abaakpa.

english: How do I choose the right cassava stems from my farm to cut and plant for the next season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmei tsei ni sa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mafolɔ ni madu kɛha be ni baa lɛ?

english: Select mature, healthy stems from plants that are 8 to 12 months old with no insect holes or diseases. Cut pieces from the middle part of the stem, about as thick as a thumb, because they sprout much faster than the soft top or hard base.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12, ni kooloi bibii loo hela ko bɛ mli lɛ ashishifãi ni eda ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ mli bibii kɛjɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ. ni tamɔ tsitsi bibioo ko Ejaakɛ edaa oya kwraa fe shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo shishigbɛ ni wa lɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo ngɔ dumɔwuhi nɛ je nyagbe ngma kpami ɔ mi ɔ yi.

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to resist local diseases, withstand dry spells, and yield more grain. Seeds saved from past harvests often lose these strong qualities, resulting in smaller yields and weaker plants.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli helai. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi ni ewoɔ dumɔwui babaoo Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ sui ni mli wa nɛɛ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni tsei lɛ hu baa shi.

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady, usually after two or three good rains. Planting right after the first rain can cause your seeds to sprout and then wither if a dry stretch follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛgbi.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the soil around their vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the soil cool and holds water so you do not need to water as often. It also stops weeds from growing and turns into natural food for the soil as it rots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Ehaa jwɛi hu shwereɔ, ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ́ egbo.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young maize plants overnight and leaving holes?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome ni eshi bu?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms, which hide inside the growing leaf funnel. You can control them by inspecting your farm early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or putting clean wood ash into the leaf centers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni oookwɛ mra lɛ nɔ. ni okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii. Aloo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse awo baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when the tree suffers from heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or attacks from insects like capsids. Planting shade trees like plantains and protecting the crop from pests helps the flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi tamɔ capsids ni tutuaa mɔ lɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it good for me to plant cowpeas or beans inside the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu cowpeas loo beans yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ mi-corn lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans alongside maize is very beneficial. Beans naturally take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil for the maize, and growing both crops gives you two harvests from the same piece of land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ ŋmãa. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oná yibii enyɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my yam mounds before putting up stakes for the vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi ni ebɔle he lɛ? Ani okɛ sweet potatoes toɔ shi dani okɛwoɔ tso mli kɛha wain tsei?

english: Weeds steal water and soil nutrients that your yams need to grow big tubers. Clearing weeds early ensures the yam vines get full sunlight once they climb the stakes, leading to a much better harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa o-sweet potatoes lɛ koni bulbs wuji lɛ akwɛ̃. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ haa sweet potato wain tsei lɛ naa hulu la ni fa babaoo beni amɛkwɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa kpamɔ kpakpa kwraa.

english: If the rains start late this year, does that mean I should wait longer before planting my crops?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ lɛ je shishi fiofio afi nɛɛ Ani no tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ mamɛ be babaoo dani madu tsei?

english: Not necessarily. When the early rains are delayed, delaying your planting even further shortens the time your crops have to grow, which often leads to a smaller harvest.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ Dumɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa sɛɛ babaoo lɛ baaha be ni heɔ koni akɛdu tsei lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ haa nikpamɔ bibioo baa.

english: Why do my crops perform poorly when I delay planting after the first rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ dumɔ lɛ sɛɛ fo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Crops need a full cycle of steady water to grow strong. When you plant late, the crop may run out of rain before its seeds or fruits fully mature, resulting in weak growth and reduced yields.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii daa yɛ be fɛɛ mli koni amɛdara waa. Beni oduɔ nii yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekolɛ nugbɔ bɛ Dumɔwui lɛ amli dani dumɔwui lɛ loo aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: What should I do if the rainy season starts late but officers say the rains will last longer into the year?
ga: Ni kɛji nugbɔ be lɛ je shishi sɛɛ mli shi onukpai lɛ kɛɛ nugbɔ baanɛ kɛyashi afi hu?

english: You should prepare your land and plant as soon as the rains arrive, taking advantage of the prolonged rainy period so your crops get water throughout their whole life cycle.
ga: Esa akɛ osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Ekɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekɛ nu aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my neighbors who plant right after the first major rain usually get a bigger harvest than me when I wait?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋbii ni duɔ nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ naa yibii babaoo fe mi be fɛɛ be kɛ́ mimɛ lɛ?

english: Early planting allows seeds to catch the initial release of nutrients in the soil triggered by the first water, giving plants a head start to build strong roots before any mid-season dry spells.
ga: Dumɔwui kɛjɛ gbekɛbiiashi Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni nu tsirɛɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ klalo akɛ amɛbaatswa shishifãi ni wa dani hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ aba.

english: How do late rains affect how my maize flowers and forms grain before the dry season?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ saa ŋmãa fɔfɔii kɛ dumɔwui ahe dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baa lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: If maize is planted too late, the rains might stop right when the plant is flowering or filling its cobs with grain, leading to small cobs or empty husks due to water shortage.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ tsɔ Nugbɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa kɛji tsei lɛ fɔfɔi loo ŋmãa lɛ mli eyi kɛ dumɔwui pɛ. ni kɛ ŋmã bibioo loo ŋmãa ni bɛ nɔ ko baa yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ

english: Why is it risky to sit and wait after the first rainy days instead of clearing my farm immediately?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ ooota shi ni omɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ gbi lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni oootsi ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Waiting causes you to lose precious soil moisture from the initial rains; once that early moisture evaporates, your seeds will struggle to germinate evenly.
ga: Mɛɛmɔ baaha shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa ni jɛ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ afite bo. Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɔi shwiemɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baaná naagba ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: What type of crop seeds should I buy if the rainy season in my district starts later than expected?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui esa akɛ mahe kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ je shishi sɛɛ fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ?

english: You should choose early-maturing or drought-tolerant seed varieties because they grow and produce food quickly before the weather dries up again.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya loo ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii oya dani shihilɛi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I still get a good harvest if the weather schedule in my region changes unexpectedly?
ga: Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa lolo kɛji akɛ mikpokpaa lɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ tsake trukaa?

english: Yes, you can still get a good harvest by planting immediately when the rain starts, using quick-growing seeds, and listening to seasonal weather updates from extension officers.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ oná ŋmaa kpakpa lolo kɛtsɔ dumɔ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ. Okɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ atsu nii. ni obo be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni jɛ extension nitsulɔi adɛŋ lɛ atoi

english: Does a delayed start to the rains mean we will have a shorter rainy season overall?
ga: Ani nugbɔshiimɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baaha nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ fɛɛ afee kuku?

english: Not always. Sometimes a delayed rainy season simply shifts the calendar, meaning the rains will stay around longer into months like November instead of stopping early.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Bei komɛi lɛ, nugbɔnɛmɔ be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha kalanda lɛ atsake. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nugbɔ lɛ baaya nɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyɔji babaoo, tamɔ November mli, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ebaakpa mra.

english: How does dry, hot ground right before the late rains affect my seed germination?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni edɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ baaná dumɔwui akwɛ̃mɔ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Very hot and dry soil hardens the upper crust, so if you don't plant quickly after the first good soaking rain, the seeds may not get enough moisture to push through the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa ni egbi lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli wa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji akɛ oduuu nii oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ekolɛ Dumɔwui hu naaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow and curling cassava leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties from the extension office is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Kasava baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni Extension Office lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ aduɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches and harvesting infected pods quickly helps keep the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ fe nine. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo fe nine lɛ amli, ni akpa ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: What makes my harvested maize turn into powder with tiny holes after a few months in storage?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ tsɔɔ powda ni eyɛ bu bibii? Beni akɛto nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ

english: This destruction is caused by maize weevils that lay eggs inside the dried grain. Storing your well-dried maize in sealed, airtight hermetic bags prevents these insects from surviving and ruining your crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei ŋmeii ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmei ni egbi mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ wo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum tsiɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkahi shi ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why does my maize crop grow tall and green but produce very small ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ shi eyɛ toi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Maize plants that are planted too close together compete for soil nutrients and sunlight, leaving little energy to form large ears. Proper spacing and applying nitrogen fertilizer at the right growth stages ensure full ear development.
ga: Abɛi ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ hulu la lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ feɔ fioo aahu akɛ toi lɛ feɔ agbo. Gbɛ ni sa kɛ nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ haa toi lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm field after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally fix nitrogen from the air back into the soil. Rotating them with maize restores soil fertility for the next season without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ haa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmã tsu nii yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: When is the best time for me to clear my land and prepare the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu nii?

english: Land preparation should be done during the dry season just before the main rains begin. Clearing early allows the soil to settle so you can plant seeds immediately after the first steady rains arrive.
ga: Esa akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli, dani nugbɔ anɛ. mra be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, obaanyɛ odu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and full of rough bumps instead of smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ etsake ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Deformed yams are usually caused by microscopic worms in the soil called nematodes or by planting in hard, stony ground. Making high, soft mounds with loose topsoil and using healthy seed yams keeps the tubers growing long and smooth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potatoes ni efite lɛ baa. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ko ni kɛlɛ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni sũ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ mli etse ni akɛ sweet potatoes ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ adara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or extreme dry conditions in the soil. Mulching around the base with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my pepper plants suddenly wilting and dying even though the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni egboɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually root rot caused by excess water drowning the roots. Planting peppers on raised ridges or beds allows water to drain away easily so the roots can breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifãi ni nu ni fa fe nine ni shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa ji shishifãi ni fiteɔ trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ mli. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii loo saatsoi ni awo nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ amu.

english: How does this purple-flowered weed called Striga destroy my corn farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ko ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ Striga lɛ miifite mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Striga, or witchweed, attaches its roots directly to maize roots underground and steals the plant's food and water. You can control it by pulling it up before it flowers and rotating your corn with leguminous crops like cowpeas.
ga: Striga loo Witchweed lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmãa shishifãi ahe tɛ̃ɛ ni ejuɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu. Obaanyɛ okudɔ amɛ kɛtsɔ amɛ ni ooogbala kɛya ŋwɛi dani amɛfɔ lɛ nɔ. Ni okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii atsake o-corn lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are missing nitrogen in the soil or are getting too much or too little water. Nitrogen gives plants their healthy green color and strength to grow big.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛmiiná nu babaoo loo fioo tsɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ eŋɔli, amɛhe wa ni amɛhe wa kɛha dalɛ.

english: Why does my farm yield less harvest if I plant maize on the exact same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and attracts specific pests. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas helps put good nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake onibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii kpakpai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to the soil on the exact same day I sow my crop seeds?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ gbi ni midu dumɔwui lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the seeds sprout and form young roots, usually a week or two after planting. Placing strong fertilizer directly next to seeds can burn them before they can grow.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni shishifãi bibii eba. Bei pii lɛ, otsi kome loo enyɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo dumɔwui lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from excessive sun heat, dry soil, or insect attacks. Providing adequate shade trees keeps the farm cool and helps the flowers stay on the tree to turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la, sũ ni egbi, loo koolooi shwieɔ amɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmeii.

english: How do I know which way to insert cassava stem cuttings into the ground when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ odu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the tiny buds along the cassava stem. Point these buds upward toward the sky so the leaves can shoot up easily into the air instead of struggling underground.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Nyiɛmɔ ŋmei tso lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmeii nɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi bɔni afee ni anyɛ atswa baai lɛ kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli mlɛo. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ teemɔŋ

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food that grows large yam tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they get full sunlight and don't rot from rain moisture.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii kɛ́ amɛmiikwɛ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaye abua ni ewó tso lɛ yibii lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ koni enyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo. ni egbooo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hewɔ

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the leaves. Keeping the farm clean and spraying organic treatments like neem water helps protect the foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baai lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ aha ŋmɔ lɛ mli tse ni akɛ tsofai tamɔ neem nu shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster and stronger than the crops I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early removes this competition so your crops can thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amɛhi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baajie akaŋshii nɛɛ. koni onibii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃

english: Why are my tomatoes getting dark, rotten spots at the bottom before they even ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ hiɛ ŋmɔtɔ diji ni egboɔ yɛ shishi dani eshɛɔ po lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by uneven watering and a lack of calcium in the plant. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant absorb nutrients properly so tomatoes grow clean and smooth.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔɔ lɛ daa kɛ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni tomatoi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhe atse ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: When crops are crowded together, they fight each other for limited light, water, and plant food. Spacing them far enough apart allows each plant to grow thick stems and produce heavy harvests.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛwuɔ koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii ni faaa. Akɛni amɛteŋ jɛkɛ bɔ ni sa hewɔ lɛ, tso fɛɛ tso yɛ tso ni mli tse kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants developing small holes and looking chewed up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni ekwɛɔ akɛ eshɛre?

english: This is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed on young crop leaves. Spraying with approved biopesticides or neem extract early in the morning or late evening helps protect the plants before they get destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tsei bibii ahe baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei ahe dani amɛfite.

english: Leaf curling is often a sign of tomato leaf curl virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Controlling whiteflies early using insecticidal soaps or ash water spray keeps the insects from spreading the virus across your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tomato baa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Early Whitefly Control Kɛ okɛ samla loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young green pods before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛ ŋmɔji bibii lɛ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt, which happens when the cocoa tree lacks enough nutrients or water to support all its pods, or due to fungal infections like black pod. Proper pruning and applying balanced fertilizer helps the tree retain its healthy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ cacao tso lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua tso muu lɛ fɛɛ. aloo yɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji ahewɔ. Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afolɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava leaves turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the soil lacks key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or compost around the plant helps restore green leaves and improves root growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii titrii tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Nibii ni egbo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni eha baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha shishifãi lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is my yam producing plenty of big green leaves but very small tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes yam to spend all its energy growing leaves above ground rather than tubers below. Yam needs soil rich in potassium to help the tubers swell and grow big.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkwɛɔ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. Shikpɔŋ ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia sweet potato koni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛdara.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even when it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Clearing weeds during the first four weeks after planting allows your crops to get all the nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ lɛ mli yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast with wide leaves that shade young cocoa, protecting them from heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize seeds when the rainy season begins?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ bote mli lɛ?

english: It is safest to wait until the soil gets two or three heavy, continuous rains so moisture penetrates deep. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and then dry out if hot weather returns.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔshiimɔi ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni nugbɔ lɛ abote mli jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers during hot, dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stress causes pepper plants to drop flowers to conserve water and survive. Covering the soil with dried leaves or straw keeps the root area cool and moist so the plant can hold its flowers.
ga: Haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli baa lɛ haa chili tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ fɔfɔi.

english: Cassava tubers rot when water collects around the roots in heavy or poorly drained soils during heavy rains. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away easily and keeps tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni yitso lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ

english: How does planting my crops in neat straight rows help them yield more food than scattering seeds freely?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mitsei lɛ ni mikɛbaadu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛná niyenii babaoo fe dumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã amɛhe lɛ?

english: Straight rows give every plant enough space, air, and sunlight to grow strong without competing with neighboring plants. It also makes weeding, applying fertilizer, and harvesting much easier.
ga: Nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ. Ehaa jwɛi ni ajieɔ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ hu feɔ mlɛo kwraa.

english: Why does my field produce less harvest every year if I keep planting only maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi kɛji akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season. Rotating maize with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts puts vital nutrients back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmei tsakeɔ lɛ Haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my growing maize plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer will help fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaatsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. They need shade trees or temporary crops like plantains to act as living umbrellas until they are old enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Ehe miihia ni amɛná tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛdara bɔ ni sa ni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when the wind blows hard during the fruiting stage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa waa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the ground, and a full bunch of fruit makes the top of the tree very heavy. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy wooden fork supports the weight and prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. ni aduawai ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ feɔ tsiimɔ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ afite.

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause stress to tomato plants, forcing them to drop flowers to save energy. Watering regularly at the roots and covering the soil with mulch keeps the soil cool and preserves moisture.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi koni amɛkafite hewalɛ. Kɛ́ afɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ nu daa ni akɛ sũ awo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my young maize leaves and leaves covered in powdery waste?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni eha baai lɛ ahe lɛ baa?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the center of the young plant during the day to eat the leaves, which slows crop growth unless controlled early.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye baai lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ daa blɛoo, ja akudɔ amɛ oya.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the soil if I leave them in the ground during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excessive water trapped around the roots starves them of oxygen, causing root rot disease. Harvesting before the heavy rains peak or planting cassava on raised mounds helps drain extra water away.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ebɔle he. Oxygen bɛ shishifãi lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ shishifãi ni fiteɔ hela aba. Nibii ni akpaa dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa loo ni aduɔ ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli.

english: Why should I not spray pest chemicals on my crops in the middle of a hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Strong sunshine makes liquid chemicals evaporate into the air before they can work, and high heat mixed with chemicals can scorch your crop's leaves. It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani amɛtsuɔ nii. Ni la ni mli edɔ waa ni akɛ tsofai efutu mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai lɛ ashã. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Will driving heavy machinery or tractors over wet soil hurt my future harvests?
ga: Ani nibii ni tsii loo traktɔi ni akudɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ baaná wɔsɛɛ be mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ gbonyo?

english: Yes, heavy machinery compresses wet soil, squishing out the tiny air spaces roots need to breathe. This hardens the dirt like concrete, making it difficult for future crop roots to push through and absorb nutrients.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsɔnei ni tsii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Mimɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii lɛ amli. Ehe miihia ni shishifãi lɛ amu kɛje kpo. Enɛ baaha muji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tamɔ kɔnkrit. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tso shishifãi ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ akɛ amɛaatsɔ mli ni amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Cocoa trees take time to establish. If you care for them properly, many of the trees will begin producing pods for harvest around six years after planting.
ga: Cacao tsei he miihia be dani amɛfee. Kɛji okwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ Tsei babaoo baabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛkpaa ŋmɔshi nibii aaafee afii enumɔ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ.

english: What should I do with my young cocoa seedlings right after I put them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee yɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛji midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: After planting young cocoa trees, you generally let them grow naturally for the first few years without major heavy pruning, while making sure the farm is kept clear of weeds.
ga: Beni adu kookoo tsei bibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaanyɛ oha ekwɛ̃ yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli ni okɛ tsei ni tsii efolɔɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, esa akɛ jwɛi akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: When is the right time for me to start pruning my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi cacao tsei bibii lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: You should start looking closely at your cocoa trees to prune them one by one when they reach about three years of age.
ga: Esa akɛ oje o-cacao tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ kɛha amɛ aŋkroaŋkroi beni tsei lɛ eye aaafee afii etɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to trim the small shoots growing at the base of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa mi akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: Pruning unwanted shoots at the base of the cocoa tree helps the plant direct its energy into the main stem and upper branches so it can grow strong and bear fruit later on.
ga: Niji ni ataooo ni afolɔ yɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ yaa tso lɛ shishigbɛ titri lɛ kɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ada ni ewo yibii yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do I need to cut off extra branches from my cocoa trees instead of letting everything grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ cacao tso lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã nɔ fɛɛ nɔ akwɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes crowded and unnecessary branches, allowing air and light to circulate through the tree, which helps the cocoa tree stay healthy and produce fruit to harvest.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la tsɔɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa cacao tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛha kpamɔ.

english: How does clearing weeds around my cocoa trees help them grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ajiemɔ Te mi-cacao tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Clearing weeds regularly stops unwanted plants from competing with your cocoa trees for nutrients and water, giving your cocoa trees the strength to grow and bear fruit.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ haa tsei ni ataooo lɛ kɛ kookoo tso lɛ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Enɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni edaa ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why is it necessary for me to spray my cocoa farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu afɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ?

english: Spraying protects your cocoa trees from harmful insects and diseases that can damage the flowers and pods, ensuring you get a good harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ o-cacao tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ni baanyɛ afite fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Ehaa onáa hekɛnɔfɔɔ akɛ obaaná yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling me to keep my cocoa farm clean and tidy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ maha kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni efee fɛo lɛ?

english: Keeping the farm tidy by clearing weeds and pruning dead branches reduces pests and diseases, creating a good environment for cocoa trees to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli fee fɛo ni ehi jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ooojie kɛ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni ooofolɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai aba shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha cacao tsei lɛ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What basic routine steps do I need to follow to make sure my cocoa farm gives me a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii titrii esa akɛ mafee koni mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: To get a good harvest, you must consistently clear weeds, keep the farm clean, prune the branches properly, and spray your trees nicely against pests and diseases.
ga: bɔni afee ni oná yibiiwoo kpakpa Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ daa. Ha ŋmɔ lɛ mli atse Afolɔ tsei lɛ aniji jogbaŋŋ Ni okɛ nu afɔ tsei lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ajie amɛ.

english: How do I know when it is the right season to harvest my oil palm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei fɔ?

english: Oil palm reaches harvest time when the fruit bunches ripen to a bright reddish-orange color and a few loose fruits begin dropping naturally to the ground near the base of the palm.
ga: Mu tsei lɛ shɛɔ kpamɔ be mli beni aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ akui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni aduawai lɛ ekomɛi bɔi gbee yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when I clear all the big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi beni mijie tsei ni eda ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Shade trees act like protective umbrellas, keeping the soil cool and moist while shielding young cocoa plants until they are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seedlings as close together as possible so I can get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tsei ahe dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe bɔ ni manyɛ koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough room and food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo yibii.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer to help my crops produce well?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ efite ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crop leaves look pale green or yellow instead of deep green, or if the plants grow very slowly and produce tiny fruits despite getting enough rain, your soil is likely low in nutrients.
ga: Kɛji otso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ eŋɔli ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa ni ewoɔ yibii bibii Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it a bad idea for me to apply fertilizer on my farm right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nii dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes fertilizer away from the roots before the crops can absorb it. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but not when heavy downpours are expected to wash it away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi jeee be mli ni akpaa gbɛ akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baaho shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, humid weather. Keeping the farm weeded, pruning branches to let in air, and applying approved treatments help stop the disease.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni edɔ waa lɛ kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Afolɔ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli Kɛ tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akpa hela lɛ.

english: Why are the branches on my cocoa tree swelling up and the leaves showing red patterns?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niji ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ efu ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called mealybugs. Because the virus cannot be cured, infected trees must be removed to protect the healthy trees on your farm.
ga: Enɛ ji Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus, ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ he okadi. Atsɛɔ no akɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ ji akɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa hela lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ ajie tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ koni akɛbu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops curling up and getting covered in a sticky black film?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni akɛ sini diŋ ko ni shwieɔ shi ehà nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mealybugs sucking juices from the leaves and leaving sugary waste that grows black mold. Controlling these pests removes the black film and protects the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mealybugs ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ni amɛshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ akudɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ, ejieɔ sini diŋ lɛ ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he.

english: Pruning opens up the canopy so light and air can flow through the tree, which prevents diseases. It also stops the tree from wasting energy on extra leaves and directs that energy into producing cocoa pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli lɛ, egbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akamɔ mɔ. Etsiɔ tso lɛ hu naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ anɔ, ni ekɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before any pods start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by dry weather, poor soil nutrition, or intense heat. Providing proper shade, mulching, and balancing soil nutrients helps the tree hold onto its flowers to produce pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ hao amɛ. shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa, ni haa hulutsoo, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii ni ja lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do weeds growing around my young crops slow down their growth so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ miiha amɛdalɛ miiba shi babaoo?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crop's root zone. Clearing weeds regularly leaves all those vital resources available for your crops to grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa lɛ, ebaaha nakai nibii ni he hiaa lɛ aya koni eha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ oya.

english: Does buying bigger seed tubers make my harvested yams grow larger?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ayitsei wuji ni miheɔ lɛ baaha mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, larger seed tubers carry more stored food and energy, giving the young plant a stronger start and generally producing bigger, healthier yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ayitsei ni dara lɛ toɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ naa shishijee ni mli wa. Ni bei pii lɛ amɛwoɔ yibii wuji ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if a cassava stem is healthy enough to cut and plant in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni adu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Choose stems from mature, disease-free plants that are about as thick as a thumb, with closely spaced node buds that feel firm and full of life.
ga: Halamɔ tsei ni edara, ni hela bɛ mli ni dalɛ tamɔ tsitsi wulu lɛ ashishifãi. kɛ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni nuɔ he akɛ amɛyɛ shiŋŋ ni amɛyi obɔ kɛ wala

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight; plantains grow fast and provide broad living shade that keeps the cocoa seedlings cool and moist.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛhaa hulutsoo babaoo, ni no haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ mli jɔɔ ni amɛfeɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What is causing small caterpillar holes in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa? Yɛ mi-abɛi tso bibioo lɛ teŋgbɛ baa lɛ nɔ

english: That damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm, a pest that eats the tender inner leaves of young maize plants and needs early treatment.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii ni ehe hiaa ni atsa amɛ mra lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ baa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an important soil food that gives leaves their rich green color and strength to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe wa kɛha dalɛ.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo midumɔi lɛ amli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and plants are actively growing, avoiding dry sunny spells where it burns the plant or heavy rains that wash it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida lɛ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni egbi ni haa tsei shãa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni shwieɔ tsei lɛ ahe.

english: Weeds compete aggressively with your crops for water, sunlight, and ground nutrients, stealing the food your plants need to grow thick and strong.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ejuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why is it bad for me to plant pepper in the exact same spot on my farm every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly allows crop-specific diseases and pests to build up in the soil, reducing yields over time.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Enɛ baaha helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tso pɔtɛɛ nɔ lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off without fruiting when the air gets too hot, water is irregular, or bees and wind aren't moving pollen around enough.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee yɛ jɛmɛ. Aloo ŋmeii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsiii pollen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi amli.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves curl up and droop during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up in high heat as a defense to save water, but if they don't bounce back by morning, the soil is too dry and needs watering.
ga: Baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni nu akafite. Shi kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe wooo mli leebi lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbi tsɔ ni ehe baahia ni awo nɔ nu.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and weak when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many seeds are planted closely together, the seedlings fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing allows roots to spread and stalks to grow thick and strong.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni eshishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa.

english: What will happen to my tomato seedlings if I keep too many of them in a small nursery box?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tomato dumɔwui babaoo to ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ adeka bibioo ko mli?

english: Overcrowding in a nursery traps moisture between leaves and restricts airflow. This creates a perfect environment for fungal diseases to spread quickly and leaves seedlings too weak to survive transplanting.
ga: Kɛ́ mɔ ko eyi ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ, emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akabote mli. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya. ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ gbɔjɔɔ tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ adu amɛ.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my crops all at once or in smaller steps over the growing season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli shikome loo fiofio yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Applying fertilizer in split steps feeds the plant gradually as it grows. If you apply it all at once, heavy rains can wash the nutrients away before the plant can absorb them, or it can burn the young roots.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii fiofio. Ha tso lɛ niyenii be mli ni edaa lɛ. Kɛ okɛ fɛɛ tsu nii shikome Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Aloo ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi bibii lɛ ashã.

english: If I notice insects damaging a few leaves on my farm, should I spray the whole field immediately or treat it step by step?
ga: Kɛji mina kooloi bibii ni miifite baai fioo komɛi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Ani esa akɛ mafɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo matsa lɛ fiofio?

english: It is best to start by treating only the affected spots to save money and protect beneficial insects. However, you must inspect the farm daily so you can treat the rest of the field if the pests begin to spread.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooje shishi kɛtsɔ hei ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ koni akɛto shika he gbɛjianɔ ni abu kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ahe. Shi kɛlɛ, ehe miihia ni okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbi koni onyɛ otsa hei ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai bɔi gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up and turning yellow all of a sudden?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe trukaa ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Infected plants cannot process sunlight properly, leading to small or poor tuber yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baa ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu hulu la lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa tuber yibii bibii loo ehiii baa.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and dry up even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni egbiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by fungal root rot or bacterial wilt. Microorganisms in the soil destroy the root system, preventing the plant from taking up water despite the soil being moist.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi loo bacteria ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ mli baa. Nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná nu kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their young green pods before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ miiho eshishifãi bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Young cocoa pods drop naturally if the tree carries more fruit than its water and nutrient supply can support, or if cool, wet weather encourages black pod disease to attack the tender stems.
ga: Kokoo ŋmeii bibii lɛ baagbee shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji tso lɛ wo yibii babaoo fe nu kɛ niyenii ni tso lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ nɔ. Aloo kɛji shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ black pod hela lɛ hewalɛ koni etutua tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant lacks calcium while the fruit is forming, often triggered by irregular watering that prevents roots from absorbing minerals consistently.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji calcium bɛ tso lɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miifee lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ minerals be fɛɛ be lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over during rainstorms before the fruits are fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ be mli dani eyibii lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots and top-heavy fruit bunches. Underground pests like nematodes often weaken the root system, making it necessary to prop the stems with bamboo poles to keep them upright.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akui ni ŋmeii ni tsii yɔɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni akɛ ŋmei tsei afi tso lɛ sɛɛ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How can I tell the difference between a crop leaf that is just dry from the hot sun and one affected by a serious disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tsei ahe baai ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ egbi kɛkɛ kɛ nɔ ni hela ni naa wa yɔɔ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Sun-stressed leaves usually revive when temperatures cool down in the evening. Disease symptoms, such as dark spots with yellow rings, powdery coatings, or sticky residues, remain visible regardless of the time of day.
