ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hulu lɛ eshɛ amɛhe lɛ baa wala mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ. Hela okadii lɛ ekomɛi ji hei ni ediŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, nɔ ko ni tamɔ powda, loo hei ni kpɛtɛɔ he. Ehiɔ shi ni anaa ekɔɔɔ gbi lɛ mli be he.

english: How can I tell when my maize is fully mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, the silks turn dark brown, and the kernels are hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your thumbnail.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi. Siliki lɛ tsɔɔ blɔfo. Ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa bɔ ni sa ni okɛ onaji shwieŋ mlɛo.

english: Tomato flowers usually drop off when the heat is too intense, when water supply is irregular, or when there are no insects like bees around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii ni baawo fɔfɔii amli ŋmeii lɛ bɛ.

english: Why does my farmland produce less food after I plant crops on it for two consecutive years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa beni midu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mli afii enyɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth to grow. If you do not add compost or manure, or rotate crops like beans and groundnuts back into the field, the soil loses its strength and yields decline.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛdara. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii tsakeee. ku sɛɛ kɛya ŋmɔ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ baaje mli ni nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: How can I keep my vegetables growing green and healthy even during the dry season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi-aduawai lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po?

english: You can keep vegetables healthy during dry periods by covering the soil around them with dry grass or leaves (mulching) to trap moisture and using simple bucket drip irrigation.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha o-vegetables lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ni oookɛwo mli lɛ nɔ. kɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo baai (mulch) koni akɛmɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni akɛ baagi mli nu ni hoɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii.

english: Why is it good for me to plant groundnuts or beans in the same land where I plant maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ he ni miduɔ ŋmei yɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that feeds your maize crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ o-corn lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and shrinking before the cassava is full grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ dani yucca lɛ eda lɛ?

english: Yellow, twisted leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by small whiteflies; planting disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yucca mosaic hela, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa. Cassava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up into tight balls when the plants are still small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ bɔɔlu ni mli wa beni eji gbekɛ fioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper is caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids, which feed on the sap and spread plant viruses that stunt crop growth.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids. ni yeɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni egbɛɔ tso mli helai ni tsiɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa lɛ eshwaa

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up on the trees before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in cool, very damp, and overly shaded farms; pruning excess tree branches lets in sunlight to stop it.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli waa, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la akabote mli

english: What is causing my yam tubers to rot underneath the soil before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ?

english: Yam rot in the soil is caused by waterlogging in poorly drained soil or attacks from microscopic soil worms (nematodes) and fungi that enter damaged tubers.
ga: Nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato fitemɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baa. loo tutuamɔi ni jɛɔ sũ mli ŋmeii bibii waa (nematodes) kɛ ŋmeii ni boteɔ ŋmeii ni efite lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my farm when my crops are still very young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako kwraa lɛ?

english: Young crops need all the water, sunlight, and soil nutrients they can get; clearing weeds early stops the weeds from stealing these vital elements from your crops.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ hia nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ehaa jwɛi lɛ juɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa seedlings turning brown and crisp during the sunny dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Without shade crops like plantains or cassava growing around them to block direct light, the heat scorches the leaves and dries out the young plant.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he ni tsiɔ la tɛ̃ɛ naa lɛ bɛ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni ebaaha tsei bibii lɛ agbi.

english: How does putting dry grass on top of the soil around my tomato plants help them grow better?
ga: Akɛ jwɛi fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ nɔ Te mi tomato tsei lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops sunlight from drying out the ground, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make leaves green. The maize plant takes nitrogen from its older, bottom leaves to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni tsei lɛ afee amɛbaai lɛ eŋɔli Abɛi tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛ baa ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha baa heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil. Rotating crops, especially with beans or groundnuts, gives the soil time to rest and naturally restores nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ ni atsakeɔ, titri lɛ, ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: If I plant my cassava stems closer together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe lɛ maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ ŋmɔ bibioo ko mli. Ani minɔ ni?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for food, water, and sunlight. Instead of many large cassava tubers, overcrowded plants usually produce tiny, thin roots because none of them got enough resources.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii wuji babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ. Tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ fɔɔ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kpojiemɔ ejaakɛ amɛbɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What is causing ragged holes in my maize leaves with small dirt-like particles inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli kɛ muji bibii ni tamɔ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars. They crawl into the central funnel of the maize plant where leaves are soft, eating the growing parts and leaving behind chewed holes and droppings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛbaa, ni amɛshwereɔ kɛyaa ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli he ni baai bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ. Ye fãi ni edara lɛ, ni oshi bu kɛ ŋmeii ni ashɛre.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, shrinking, and showing yellow patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbɔjɔ, ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This leaf distortion is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny whiteflies. The virus prevents the plant from producing enough green leaf area to feed itself, which reduces tuber yield.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai lɛ ni etsake nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Virus lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee baai eŋɔli ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe. Enɛ baaha tuber yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, soil that is too dry, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. The plant drops flowers to save energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛna haomɔi, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi tsɔ. loo nitrogen fertilizer babaoo Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni haa amɛdaraa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt and droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the ground feels moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ

english: On hot days, leaves lose water to the dry air faster than roots can drink it up from the soil. The plant temporarily droops its leaves to shrink its surface area and cut down water loss until evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ laajeɔ nu koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ aya oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei lɛ feɔ amɛbaai lɛ kuku yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛha ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ aba shi ni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni fɛ̃i baa.

english: Why is it a bad idea to spread my chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ aaagbɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ashwã dani ahum ni naa wa aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash the fertilizer away into streams or deep into the soil below where roots cannot reach it. Applying fertilizer when the soil is moist, rather than during heavy downpours, ensures the crop actually drinks the nutrients.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa faai amli loo kɛyaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛbaatsu nii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii mli hewalɛ diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How long does it usually take for fresh cocoa seeds to sprout after I plant them?
ga: Be enyiɛ bei pii lɛ eheɔ dani cocoa yibii heei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Healthy cocoa seeds typically sprout within 7 to 14 days when planted in moist soil. If seeds take longer than a few weeks, it usually means the soil is too dry or the seeds were not fresh.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo yibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii 7 kɛyashi 14 mli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ eheɔ be fe otsii fioo komɛi dani dumɔwui lɛ duɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo dumɔwui lɛ ehiii.

english: Can I plant cocoa seeds directly into my main farm field right after taking them from the pod?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ beni mijie dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: While direct planting is possible, it is much safer to plant seeds in polybags in a shaded nursery first. This protects the delicate young sprouts from harsh sun and pests until they are strong enough for the main farm.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ moŋ Shi eyɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ polybags mli yɛ dumɔwui akwɛmɔhe ko ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli klɛŋklɛŋ. Enɛ baabu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need shade from plantain or palm leaves when they are small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ he hiaa ni ená hulutsoo kɛjɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmei tsei amli be mli ni eji gbekɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under direct sunlight. Overhead shade protects their leaves from scorching and helps keep moisture in the soil while their roots are still developing.
ga: Cacao bibioo lɛ mli yɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni eshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade ni yɔɔ yiteŋ lɛ buɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu lɛ ahiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to brush or clean dirty pods while they are growing on the cocoa tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ atsumɔ loo atsumɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji lɛ ahe beni akwɛɔ yɛ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Brushing off dirt, cobwebs, and debris removes tiny insects and fungal spores that cause diseases like black pod, keeping your pods healthy until harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ sũ, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmeii shwie shi lɛ, ebaajie ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni gbeɔ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are some of the green cocoa pods on my trees turning black and dying before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess branches to let air and sunlight in helps stop the fungus from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la abote mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Wait until you get consistent rains over two to three weeks rather than planting after the very first rain, so your seeds do not dry up if the rain stops unexpectedly.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ nɛ be fɛɛ be otsii fioo komɛi, moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ trukaa.

english: Should I cut down all the big shade trees on my land before planting new cocoa?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ dani madu kookoo hee?

english: No, you should keep some large trees. Cocoa grows better under light shade, as forest trees protect cocoa from excessive summer heat and help maintain soil fertility.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okɛ tsei wuji komɛi ato. Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: How can I tell when a cocoa pod on my tree is fully ripe and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: A ripe cocoa pod changes color—green pods turn bright yellow, and reddish pods turn orange-yellow. It will also make a hollow sound when you knock on it gently.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmeii tsuji lɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ ŋmeii-ŋmei. Ebaafee gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ otswa nɔ fioo.

english: What is the best tool to use when breaking open cocoa pods after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni ji dɛŋdade ni hi fe fɛɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii kɛ́ agbele kookoo ŋmɔji amli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to use a blunt wooden club or stick rather than a sharp cutlass. A sharp blade can slice the seeds inside, which damages bean quality.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ tso loo tso ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ baatsu nii moŋ fe kakla ni naa wa. Lade ni mli wa baanyɛ atsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ.

english: Why do I need to cover my fresh cocoa beans under plantain leaves right after breaking the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ cocoa yibii heei haa plantain baai ashishi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ etswa lɛ?

english: Covering fresh beans with plantain leaves starts the fermentation process. This essential step kills the seed so it stops sprouting, and it creates the rich chocolate flavor and brown color buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ plantain baai ha ŋmeii heei ahe lɛ, no jeɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishi. Nɛkɛ gbɛ ni he hiaa nɛɛ gbeɔ dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkakwɛ̃. ni ekɛ tsokolate ni mli ŋɔɔ waa kɛ su ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants use to build green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-decomposed animal manure helps restore their dark green color and strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ ni efite jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ kɛ dalɛ ni mli wa aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or mites, or a virus spread by them. Spraying the plants with neem oil or recommended organic pest treatments stops the insects and allows healthy new leaves to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛjieɔ yi akɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ tsei anɔ. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves turn brown and fall off during the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During the Harmattan, dry winds and low moisture scorch cocoa trees. Without enough shade trees or soil moisture retention, the cocoa drops its leaves to conserve water and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Yɛ Harmattan beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni kookoo tsei lɛ shãa, ni hulutsoo be lɛ faaa. Kɛji tsei komɛi bɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo loo ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa aba lɛ, Cocoa shwieɔ baai lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛtsi amɛhe gbɛ koni amɛkagbi kwraa.

english: Does it matter which way up I stick cassava stem cuttings into the soil?
ga: Ekɔɔɔ he eko gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ miduɔ ŋmei lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Yes, cassava cuttings must be planted with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to bend upward, wasting energy and producing fewer, weaker roots.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekoto kɛya ŋwɛi. Enɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ ni ehaa shishifãi fioo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds around my young crop seedlings early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Tall weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients from young crops that are still developing roots. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop seedlings get all the resources they need to establish strong growth.
ga: Jwɛi ni kwɔlɔ lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lolo lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni otso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ aná nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why do I have to build high soil mounds to plant yams instead of planting on flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaadu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, deep soil to expand into large tubers. High mounds keep the soil soft so the tubers grow easily without restriction and prevent water from pooling around the roots and causing tuber rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli tse he miihia sweet potato koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni bulbs lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ oya ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ. ni etsĩɔ nu naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas together with maize makes the soil richer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay, they release this natural nutrient into the soil, feeding surrounding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi lɛ fite Amɛjieɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii nɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ niyenii aha tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe tamɔ ŋmãa

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller when I plant the same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni miwoɔ lɛ faaa kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests and diseases specific to that crop build up in the soil. Rotating different types of crops gives the soil time to recover and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eha tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni efiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the roots of my vegetable crops help them during hot dry weather?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he fɛɛ he Te mi-vegetables shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, shades the earth from direct sunlight. This keeps the soil cool, stops moisture from evaporating quickly, and helps crops stay hydrated longer.
ga: Mulching ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ

english: Tomato blossoms often drop off due to extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping soil moisture consistent and providing light shade during peak heat prevents flower abortion so fruit can set.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ la ni ahiɛɔ mli be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ fɔfɔii ashwiemɔ naa koni aduawai anyɛ ama shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow leaves and stems. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives them back their green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil sucks out the same nutrients year after year and lets maize pests build up in the ground. Rotating with legumes like beans or cowpeas puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eha ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why are the flowers on my cocoa trees falling off before they turn into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by prolonged dry spells, harsh sunlight, or insect pests like mirids. Keeping enough shade trees on your farm and protecting the crop from pests helps flowers form into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa, loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ hulu la hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo bɔ ni sa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my plantain tree leaning over and falling down before the fruit bunch matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ aniji lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that can easily rot or get weakened by tiny soil worms called nematodes, making the heavy plant collapse in strong wind. Supporting the tree with a strong wooden prop prevents it from falling.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni baanyɛ afite oya loo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematodes ni haa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni wa fi tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekagbee shi.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up into small cups and stopping growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? ni ekpa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap and spreading viruses. Spraying neem leaf extract or appropriate insecticide keeps these insects away so leaves stay flat and open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni sa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi nɛɛ akashɛ ohe. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbeleɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become watery and soft when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ nu ni amɛhe yɔɔ blɛoo kɛ́ akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers store water instead of starch if they are harvested immediately after heavy rain or left in waterlogged soil. It is best to harvest cassava during drier periods so the tubers remain firm and starchy.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ nu yɛ ŋmei najiaŋ kɛji akɛ akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaakpa ŋmei yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ koni ŋmei lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɛ ŋmei.

english: How do I know the exact right time to dig up my yam from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmeii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yam is ready for harvest when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up completely toward the end of the rainy season, showing that the tuber under the ground has finished growing.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ momo.

english: What is eating small holes in my maize leaves and leaving dark sawdust-like dirt inside?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni mli edɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar feeding inside the growing shoot of the plant. Spraying safe bio-pesticides or recommended treatments early in the morning directly into the central shoot destroys the worms.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa ni akɛhaa akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi lɛ afɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaakpata ŋmeii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: This dark rot at the bottom is caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, often due to irregular watering. Watering your tomatoes evenly every day ensures the roots can constantly absorb calcium from the soil.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo o-tomato lɛ nɔ daa gbi lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable garden in the afternoon sun or early in the morning?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu shwane loo leebi maŋkpa?

english: It is best to water early in the morning because the ground can absorb the moisture before the strong afternoon heat evaporates it, helping the roots take up water effectively.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi maŋkpa ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ afee lɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛjieɔ nu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some farmers plant coconut trees on the same piece of land with cocoa and other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ akokoo tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni amɛduɔ kokoo kɛ nibii krokomɛi yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting coconuts alongside cocoa and food crops is called intercropping. The taller coconut trees provide shade that protects young cocoa plants from harsh direct sunlight, and combining crops allows you to harvest different foods and income from the same land throughout the year.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo kɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ akɛ intercropping. Kokoo tsei ni kɛlɛ lɛ haa hulutsoo be ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ okpa niyenii kɛ shika kɛjɛ he kome afi muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant my cassava or maize quickly right after planting young tree crops like coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa loo ŋmãa oya beni midu tsei bibii tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting food crops quickly allows them to take advantage of the open sunlight and cleared land before the young coconut trees grow large leaves that block the light. It lets you harvest food while the trees are still growing.
ga: Niyenii ni aduɔ oya lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni yɔɔ faŋŋ lɛ he sɛɛ ni amɛjieɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ feɔ baai agboi ni tsiɔ hulutsoo naa. Ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa niyenii yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my coconut trees if I want to grow cocoa and other crops between them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ abɔ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ kɛji miisumɔ ni madu kookoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi? yɛ ŋmei tsei ateŋ

english: Spacing coconut trees about 8 to 10 meters apart gives enough room between rows. This ensures that plenty of sunlight still reaches the ground so cocoa and food crops can grow well without their roots competing heavily for water and soil nutrients.
ga: Gbɛ ni kã ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji aaafee mitai 8 kɛyashi 10, ni no haa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ haa hulu la lɛ yaa nɔ eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni shishifãi lɛ abɔi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ babaoo lɛ he akaŋ.

english: What types of food crops grow best during the early years of starting a new coconut or cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee afii ni akɛjeɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ mli?

english: Fast-growing crops like plantains, cassava, maize, and beans grow best initially. Plantains provide helpful shade for young cocoa, while legumes like beans add natural nitrogen to the soil to feed the growing trees.
ga: Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains, cassava, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishijee mli. Plantains haa kookoo bibii lɛ hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekɛha tsei ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Is it better for me to have all my farm crops on one single land or spread across different smaller plots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ loo magbɛ amɛ ashwã shikpɔji bibii srɔtoi anɔ?

english: Having crops spread across different plots reduces risk. If pests, flooding, or poor soil affect one location, your crops on the other plots far away are more likely to stay safe and yield a harvest.
ga: Ni aaaha ŋmɔshi nibii agbɛ ashwã shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ Ehaa oshara baa shi kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, nu afua loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ ná he ko nɔ hewalɛ. Etamɔ nɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: If pests attack the cocoa trees on one of my farmlands, will they automatically spread to my other land nearby?
ga: Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔji lɛ eko mli lɛ, Ani amɛbaagbɛ amɛshwã mihei krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ amli amɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Pests do not automatically spread if the land pieces are physically separated. The physical distance acts as a natural barrier, giving you time to stop the pests on the affected plot before they can reach your other fields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fãi lɛ amli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ gbɛŋ amɛshwãaa amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Gbɔmɔtsoŋ he ni jɛkɛmɔ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii. Enɛ haa onáa be ni okɛkpaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ amli lɛ dani amɛyashɛ oŋmɔji krokomɛi lɛ amli.

english: How can I manage weeding and caring for my crops effectively when my land is split into different places?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ jwɛi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ be mli ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbala lɛ?

english: Creating a rotating farm schedule helps you manage split land. You can dedicate specific days of the week to focus on one plot at a time, ensuring every field gets regular weeding, spraying, and care without exhausting yourself.
ga: Okwaafoi akuu he gbɛjianɔtoo ni tsakeɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ shikpɔji sɔrɔtoi anɔ. Obaanyɛ ojɔɔ gbii pɔtɛɛ komɛi anɔ yɛ otsi lɛ mli ni okɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli. Enɛ haa ajieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli daa, afɔseɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ogbɔjɔɔɔ ohe.

english: Won't growing cocoa, coconuts, and food crops together exhaust all the nutrients in my soil quickly?
ga: Ani kookoo, ŋmei kɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ afite oya?

english: Not necessarily, because different crops feed at different depths. Coconut trees have deep roots that pull nutrients from deep underground, while food crops feed near the surface. Additionally, falling leaves from cocoa and coconut trees rot and feed the topsoil.
ga: Enɛ he ehiaaa, ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi baaye nii yɛ ŋshɔkei srɔtoi amli. Kokoo tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni niyenii tsei yeɔ nii yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ Kɛfata he lɛ, baai ni egbee shi kɛjɛɔ kookoo kɛ ŋmei tsei amli lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛyeɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do tall coconut trees affect food crops growing under them as the trees grow older?
ga: Te ŋmei tso ni kɛlɛ lɛ saa niyenii tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ eshishi lɛ ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As coconut trees grow taller, their leaves move high above the ground, allowing filtered sunlight to pass through to the crops below. While they cast some shade, many shade-tolerant crops like cocoa continue to grow well beneath them.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmei tso lɛ da lɛ Ebaai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hulu la ni atsɔ mli lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ anɔ. yɛ be mli ni amɛhaa hulutsoo Tsei babaoo ni nyɛɔ hulutsoo be mli, tamɔ kookoo lɛ, kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ amɛshishi.

english: Why do my cocoa plants need continuous care and pruning when they grow alongside other fast-growing plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni akwɛ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni afolɔ mli beni edaa yɛ tsei krokomɛi ni daa oya lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fast-growing companion plants can easily cover young cocoa and block all sunlight if left unmanaged. Regular pruning removes excess branches and weeds, letting light and air flow around the cocoa trees to prevent fungal diseases like black pod.
ga: Nɛkɛ nanemɛi tso ni daa oya nɛɛ baanyɛ aha kookoo tsei bibii ahe mlɛo ni eha hulu la fɛɛ akashɛ amɛhe kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ mli daa lɛ, ejieɔ tsei niji kɛ jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ. Enɛ haa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɔleɔ kookoo tso lɛ he koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji black pods lɛ anaa.

english: How do I know the right time to plant my maize when the rains start coming?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Wait until the rains become steady—usually after 2 or 3 heavy downpours that soak the soil deep down—so the seeds do not germinate and then dry up during a sudden dry spell.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ anɛ shiŋŋ—bei pii lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ sɛɛ—koni dumɔwui lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbi yɛ hɔmɔ ni baa trukaa lɛ mli.

english: I want to start growing ginger on my farm; what kind of soil and environment does it need to grow well?
ga: Miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmei dumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ shihilɛ he hiaa bo koni okwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Ginger grows best in loose, fertile, well-drained soil rich in compost, and it prefers light shade or moderate sunlight so its underground roots can expand easily without rotting in trapped water.
ga: Ginger kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni baa nii, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ni esumɔɔ hulutsoo be ni mli tse loo hulu la ni mli tse. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya ni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni emɔ mli lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants turning yellow even though it has been raining?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often show that your crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed away nutrients and left the soil waterlogged, preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up and develop light green patches on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli tse lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies; using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwiemɔ baa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions; clearing bush around the trees and pruning branches lets air and sunlight in to keep pods dry.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, kɛ hulutsoo. Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ ni ofolɔ mli koni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi.

english: I see small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the funnels of my maize plants; how can I protect my farm?
ga: Mina ŋmeii bibii ni miiye baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔ lɛ he?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms; you can protect your crop by applying neem leaf extract or recommended insecticides directly into the center funnel of each plant early in the morning or late evening.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms; Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ko ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni oookɛwo tso fɛɛ tso teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my stored maize and beans a few months after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi-ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils attack stored grain that still has moisture inside; drying your grain thoroughly in the sun until it is hard and storing it in airtight bags keeps these pests out.
ga: Moth lɛ tutuaa ŋmaa ni ato ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ. Okɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛto vacuum kotokui amli koni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akabote mli.

english: How can I make my soil fertile again without spending money on chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ ni afiteee shika yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ahe?

english: You can restore soil fertility by adding well-rotted animal manure or compost, and by planting cover crops like cowpeas or mucuna, which naturally add nitrogen to the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ tsina loo mucus ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ. ni baaha nitrogen afata shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Is it good for my crop if I plant groundnuts together with my maize on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji mikɛ ŋmei fata ŋmei he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting groundnuts with maize is very helpful because groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa waa.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted during the hot afternoon sun even when the ground feels slightly damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fioo po.

english: During intense afternoon heat, crop leaves lose water into the air faster than roots can pull it from the ground; covering the soil around the plants with dry leaves or straw helps keep the root zone cool and moist.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa lɛ Tso lɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: How do I know if my land has enough strength in the soil to grow a good harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai aba?

english: Checking or testing your soil reveals what nutrients are already present and what food elements are missing. Knowing your soil's strength helps you add exactly what your crops need to thrive.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo oka lɛ okwɛ lɛ, ebaana niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii ni bɛ mli. Kɛ́ ole bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni oha nɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa bo koni onibii lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my crop leaves turning pale yellow even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen. When the soil lacks full strength, crops cannot make food properly, so testing the soil helps identify what missing nutrient needs to be supplied.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ hu nyɛŋ afee niyenii jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa baaye abua ni ana niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje ni esa akɛ akɛha lɛ.

english: How can checking my soil before planting save me money on inputs?
ga: Te shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ dani aduɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha shika akafite yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Testing your soil shows you the exact nutrients your land lacks so you only buy the specific nutrients your crops need, preventing you from wasting money on unnecessary fertilizers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ pɛ oheɔ. Koni okafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni he ehiaaa lɛ ahe.

english: Why does my crop grow very tall and strong on one side of my farm, but stays small and weak on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiya hiɛ ni amɛhe wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ afã kroko lɛ nɔ.

english: Soil strength and nutrient content can vary across different parts of the same land. Checking different sections of your farm helps you identify weak spots so you can feed those specific areas properly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ baanyɛ afee srɔtoi yɛ hei srɔtoi. of the same land Fãi lɛ akwɛmɔ Yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ebaaye ebua bo ni ona hei ni egbɔjɔ koni onyɛ oha nakai hei pɔtɛɛi lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops now compared to when I first cleared the farm years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii faaa fe beni mijie miŋmɔ lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull strength and nutrients out of the ground. Over time, the soil becomes empty unless you check what is missing and replace those nutrients.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee efolo ja okwɛ niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje lɛ ni okɛ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ ato najiaŋ.

english: Are all fertilizers the same, or do different crops require different types?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ji ekome? Aloo tsofai sɔrɔtoi he miihia tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ?

english: Different fertilizers contain different types of plant nutrients. Using various types of fertilizers allows you to give specific crops the exact nutrients missing from your soil.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ tsei amli niyenii srɔtoi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei komɛi aná niyenii kpakpai ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I need to spread fertilizer on my land if weeds are already growing naturally fine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Be mli ni jwɛi lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Weeds survive on weak soil, but farm crops need balanced nutrients to produce heavy fruits or grains. Applying fertilizer provides the extra strength crops require to produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ. Shi ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa koni enyɛ ewo yibii loo ŋmaa ni tsii. Tsei ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baaha amɛná hewalɛ kroko kɛha yibiiwoo ni yeɔ emuu.

english: Can applying too much fertilizer cause harm to my crops?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui?

english: Yes, putting too much fertilizer or the wrong type can burn plant roots and damage the land. Checking your soil strength first ensures you spread only the right amount your crops need.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli fe nine loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ha lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ebaaha ona nɔmimaa akɛ oogbɛ nɔ ni sa ni he hiaa onibii lɛ pɛ oshwã.

english: How soon after spreading fertilizer on my land should I check my crops to see if it is working?
ga: Beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛɛ be esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli koni mana kɛji amɛmiitsu nii?

english: It usually takes a few days to a couple of weeks after applying fertilizer to see changes. Inspecting your land regularly helps you monitor if the crop leaves are turning darker green and growing faster.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii 2-3 kɛyashi otsii 2-3 yɛ fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ sɛɛ dani anaa tsakemɔi. Kɛ́ okwɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni okwɛ kɛji tsei ahe baai lɛ miitsɔ eŋɔli ni amɛmiida oya.

english: Should I apply fertilizer directly around the plant stem or spread it across the entire field?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ loo mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: How you apply fertilizer depends on the type of crop and fertilizer used. Spreading or placing fertilizer near the root zone allows plants to easily drink up the missing nutrients provided to the soil.
ga: Gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ awoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shwie shi loo akɛwo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nuɔ niyenii ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mlɛo.

english: How long does it usually take for a newly planted cocoa tree to start giving pods?
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be enyiɛ eheɔ dani cacao tso ni adu ehee lɛ jeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Hybrid cocoa trees usually take about 2 to 3 years of steady care before they start flowering and producing their first pods. During this early time, the plant is focusing its energy on building strong roots and branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ daa dani amɛjeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛfeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee be nɛɛ mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ shishifãi kɛ niji ni mli wa amamɔ he nii.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to grow big leaves after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ baai wuji beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When you first plant a plantain sucker, it spends its first few weeks working underground to establish strong roots. Once the root system is set up to absorb water and nutrients, the leaves above ground will start growing much faster.
ga: Beni oduɔ dumɔwui klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa Ebaahe klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dani shishifãi ni wa aba. Enɛ ji be mli ni atoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaje shishi amɛdara oya kwraa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops use to stay green and grow big. Feeding the soil with fertilizer or compost helps the crop stay green and form good corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. As long as the stems stay healthy, the plant will grow fresh leaves and continue expanding its roots once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shii abɔ ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli wa lɛ Tsei lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ̃ baai kɛ shishifãi heei kɛji nugbɔ ku esɛɛ eba.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava in soft mounds or ridges instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni yɔɔ blɛoo loo ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ amli moŋ fe hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mounds and ridges create soft, loose soil that makes it easy for cassava roots to expand into large tubers. Raised soil also allows excess rainwater to drain away so the roots do not sit in water and rot.
ga: Gɔji kɛ ŋshɔkei feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni shwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Shikpɔŋ ni awó nɔ lɛ hu haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ akabote nu mli ni amɛkagboi.

english: Why do I need to guide my yam vines up bamboo or wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu sweet potato wain tsei yɛ ŋmeii loo tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground where they can gather energy from the sun to feed and grow large yam tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Staking woɔ baai anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ koni ekɛbua hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli lɛ naa kɛha niyenii ni ekɛ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What causes my tomato flowers to fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme afternoon heat or a sudden lack of soil water. When stressed, the plant cancels fruit formation to save its energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ trukaa lɛ hao tsei lɛ. Kɛji haomɔ ba lɛ Tsei jieɔ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha wala.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing tall and thin without making many fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ daa ni efeɔ mlɛo ni ewooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants stretch upward and become tall and thin when they are planted too close together or under heavy shade. Giving each plant enough spacing and direct sunlight encourages them to grow bushy and produce flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo yɛ hulutsoo be babaoo shishi. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do my cowpea and bean crops make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea kɛ bean tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have tiny natural helpers on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the bean harvest is done, that trapped nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii bibii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ akpa ŋmeii lɛ, Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crop leaves are dying from a disease or just from lack of water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela miigbe mitso lɛ baai lɛ loo nu ni bɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Lack of water causes the entire plant to droop and wilt evenly. Disease usually shows up as brown spots, yellow patches, or strange powdery markings on specific leaves even while the ground still has moisture.
ga: Nu ni bɛ lɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ. Bei pii lɛ, hela lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ baai komɛi anɔ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo po.

english: Why do my maize plants stay thin and small when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa beni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they fight each other for soil food, water, and sunlight. Just like crowded animals, cramped plants cannot get enough nourishment to grow strong, leaving them weak and stunted.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli koni amɛná niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ, nu, kɛ hulu la mli, taakɛ koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ hu feɔ lɛ. Tso ni mli edɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ana niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: If I give my crops plenty of fertilizer, why do they still stay small when planted very close to each other?
ga: Kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ hiɔ shi bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: Fertilizer gives plants food, but crops also need physical space for their roots to spread and leaves to catch sunlight. Without enough room, plants get crowded out and cannot use the fertilizer properly.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii hu he miihia gbɔmɔtsoŋ he ko koni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛ baai lɛ koni amɛná hulu la. Kɛji he ko bɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers come out very thin and short even though the leaves look very healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo ni eyɛ kuku nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, their roots do not have enough space underground to swell into thick tubers. The plant puts its energy into competing above ground rather than developing heavy roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔi tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfu ni amɛtsɔ ŋmei ni mli edɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ yeɔ akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo shishifãi ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and weak with very few fruits when planted tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ daa ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When tomato plants are cramped, they stretch upward searching for light. Because they waste energy growing tall to escape the shade of neighboring plants, they lack the strength to produce heavy fruit.
ga: Kɛji tomato tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ Ebaakpã kɛya ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ lɛ koni amɛjo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ ashishifã lɛ naa foi. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛaawo yibii ni tsii.

english: Why should I remove some healthy young seedlings from my bed after they sprout instead of leaving them all to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ saatso lɛ nɔ beni amɛje kpo lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha fɛɛ aya hiɛ lɛ

english: Removing weaker seedlings gives the remaining ones enough space, light, and soil nutrients to grow into strong, healthy crops that yield far more harvest than a crowded farm ever could.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ hewalɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui ni eshwɛ lɛ gbɛ, la, kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔmɔ dumɔwui ni he wa, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe ŋmɔji ni eyi obɔ lɛ pɛŋ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings fall over and die easily when I scatter too many seeds in one seedbed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ migbɛ dumɔwui babaoo shwie dumɔwui akutso kome mli lɛ?

english: Overcrowded seedbeds trap moisture and stop fresh air from flowing between seedlings. This damp environment creates mold and fungal diseases that make young crop stems rot and collapse.
ga: Dumɔwui asaji ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni ebaatsi kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hoɔ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ naa. Shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii helai ni haa tsei bibii lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛkuɔ shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my crops turn yellow and decay when the farm becomes very bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ waa lɛ?

english: When crops grow too thick and overcrowded, sunlight cannot reach the lower leaves and air cannot circulate. Without sunlight and air, those trapped lower leaves turn yellow and die off.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara tsɔ ni amɛyi obɔ lɛ Hulu la lɛ shɛɛɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ahe ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ atsɔ mli. Kɛji hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Baai ni akɛkpɛtɛ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagboi.

english: How do weeds actually stop my main crops from growing well?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ mitso titri lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds overcrowd your field and steal the water, fertilizer, and light that your crops need, causing your plants to become starved and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi eyi oŋmɔji amli obɔ ni amɛjuɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ ni amɛhe feɔ shoo.

english: Why does cutting off extra leaves and small side branches help my crop produce bigger fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaafolɔ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Eyeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji.

english: Trimming unnecessary branches reduces crowding inside the plant, allowing air and light to reach every part while directing all the plant's energy into growing big fruit.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni mɛi ni eyi tso lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ la shɛɔ he fɛɛ he. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ aduawai wuji.

english: What happens to my garden crops if I plant them directly under big shade trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baaba mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ amɛ du tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Crops need open sunlight to make their food. Under large tree canopies, crops get shaded out and cramped, stopping them from growing properly or giving a full harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia hulu la ni jɛɔ kpo nɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haaa enyɛ eda jogbaŋŋ loo ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are my crops failing even though I plant at the exact same time I always do every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ be kome mli daa afi moŋ lɛ?

english: Rainfall patterns have become unpredictable due to changing weather conditions. Relying solely on traditional planting dates can cause crops to suffer if rains start late or end early, which is why using short-duration seed varieties and checking soil moisture before planting helps protect your investment.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ahewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ blema be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ apiŋ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ loo egbe naa mra. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okwɛɔ dani oduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oshika ni okɛwo mli lɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants turn yellow and stop growing whenever the rain stops for just a couple of weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ lɛ baakpa otsii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: When the soil dries out, maize roots cannot take up nitrogen from the soil, causing the leaves to turn yellow from lack of nutrients. Covering the soil around your plants with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap moisture in the ground during short dry spells.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Mulching around Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛhaa tsei ahe (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi.

english: Curling and yellowing leaves are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies or by planting infected stems. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties and removing infected plants early stops the disease from destroying your whole crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe ni efee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies loo tso tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Adumɔ tso henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Black pod is caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shady conditions during heavy rains. Pruning extra branches on cocoa trees and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the farm, preventing the fungus from ruining your yield.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata he yɛ kookoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ni ajie jwɛi lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi aya hiɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. ni otsi ŋmeii ni fiteɔ onibii lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants suddenly wilt and die when there is too much water standing on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ beni nu babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits on the farm for too long, it smothers the roots by cutting off air, causing them to rot underground. Creating raised soil beds or drainage channels allows excess rainwater to flow away so the plant roots stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni afoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ saatsoi ni awó nɔ loo nu homɔ gbɛi ni afee lɛ baaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli. Koni tso shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and healthy in one part of my land, but remain small and weak in another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛhe wa yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã kome nɔ lɛ? shi eji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ fã kroko mli

english: Soil quality is not the same across an entire farm because rain can wash away nutrients in higher or exposed areas. Adding animal manure or compost to the weak areas replenishes the nutrients needed for uniform plant growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su lɛ jeee ekome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nugbɔ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ hei ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo hei ni gbɛ yɔɔ babaoo lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata hei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa koni tsei lɛ aya hiɛ daa lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce plenty of green leaves but very few nuts underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo baai eŋɔli babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes groundnuts put all their energy into growing leaves instead of seeds, while a lack of calcium leads to empty pods. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizers and adding agricultural lime or compost helps groundnuts form full, healthy pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ dumɔwui najiaŋ. Yɛ be mli ni calcium ni faaa lɛ baaha pods lɛ afee efolo lɛ. Kɛ́ okpa nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni okɛ lime loo okwaayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua o-peanuts lɛ ni ená ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to spend time clearing weeds around my young crops if weeds are just green plants too?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maŋɔ be kɛjie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? mi tso lɛ Fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ, jwɛi ji tsei eŋɔli kɛkɛ hu.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, water, and soil food away from your young plants. Keeping the farm clean during the early stages of plant growth ensures your crops get everything they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ ekãa juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ sũ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei bibii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ oha oŋmɔ lɛ mli tse yɛ tsei lɛ adalɛ shishijee bei amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off without growing into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plants experience severe heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Giving plants steady water at the root level and planting flowering companion crops nearby helps attract insects to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa loo kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ falɛ faaa Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe kɛ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ baaye abua ni egbala kooloi kɛba fɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Why do I get smaller harvests when I replant seeds saved from my previous harvest instead of buying new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ yibii fioo nɔ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, hɔɔ dumɔwuhi ehehi nɛ a wo he odase ɔ.

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops naturally lose their vigor, uniform growth, and disease resistance in the next generation. Using fresh certified seeds ensures uniform germination, stronger growth, and maximum yields that justify your effort.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi. shweremɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni nyɛɔ eshiɔ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ daa. shweremɔ ni mli wa kɛ yibiiwoo ni fa fe fɛɛ ni maa omɔdɛŋbɔɔ lɛ nɔ mi.

english: What is plant layering, and how does it help me get new fruit trees?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei amli srɔtofeemɔ? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni maná aduawai tsei heei?

english: Layering is a method where you encourage a branch to root while it is still attached to the parent tree. Once roots form, you cut the branch off and plant it as a new tree that grows faster and fruits sooner than trees grown from seed.
ga: Layering ji gbɛ ko ni otsɔɔ nɔ owoɔ tsei aniji hewalɛ koni amɛshishifãi yɛ be mli ni amɛkãa tso ni amɛjɛ mli lɛ he. Kɛji shishifãi lɛ dara lɛ Obaafolɔ nine lɛ ni odu lɛ ni ofee tso hee ni daa oya ni ewoɔ yibii oya fe tso ni jɛ dumɔwui amli ekwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: How does layering guarantee that my new tree will be just as good as the mother plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ stratification lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ mitso hee lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi tamɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ?

english: Because layering uses a piece of the parent plant itself rather than a seed, the new plant is an exact clone. It will keep all the desirable qualities of the original tree, such as sweet fruit or dwarf height.
ga: Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, stratification lɛ kɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ fãi komɛi tsuɔ nii moŋ fe dumɔwui. No hewɔ lɛ tso hee lɛ ji nɔ ko ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Ebaahiɛ sui kpakpai ni yɔɔ shishijee tso lɛ mli lɛ amli, tamɔ tso yibii ni ŋɔɔ loo ŋwɛi ŋta ni etse ehe lɛ mli.

english: Can I make my own dwarf trees on my farm using layering, or do I have to buy them from a specialized nursery?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee mi diɛŋtsɛ mi tsei bibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ layering nɔ? Aloo esa akɛ mahe kɛjɛ he ko ni akwɛɔ gbekɛbii yɛ gbi mli?

english: You can do layering on your own farm if you have a good parent tree, but it requires practice to get high success rates. Many farmers buy them from certified nurseries to ensure the plants are healthy and properly rooted.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee stratify yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oŋmɔ mli kɛji oyɛ fɔlɔ tsei kpakpai. Shi eheɔ nifeemɔ dani anyɛ aye omanye ni nɔ kwɔ. Okwaafoi babaoo heɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ tsei akwɛmɔhei ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ tsei lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ ewo shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is a dwarf crop variety, and why should I plant it on my farm instead of tall trees?
ga: Mɛni ji tsei srɔtoi ni ji dwarf lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu yɛ ŋmɔ mli moŋ fe tso kakadaŋŋ nɔ?

english: Dwarf varieties are bred to grow shorter in height. They are easier to harvest, less likely to be knocked down by strong winds, and usually produce fruit much faster than tall, traditional varieties.
ga: Afɔ dwarf henɔi lɛ koni amɛhe afee kuku. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ abaakpa Hegbɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatswa lɛ faaa. ni bei pii lɛ ewoɔ yibii oya kwraa fe blema tsei srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ.

english: Why do dwarf trees usually produce fruits much faster than taller trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ tsei bibii woɔ yibii mra kwraa fe tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Dwarf trees put less energy into growing thick, tall trunks and heavy branches. Instead, they direct their nutrients early on into producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Tsei bibii kɛ hewalɛ fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara, amɛtso lɛ mli eyi kɛ amɛniji ni tsii. Shi amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa koni amɛfee fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai mra.

english: Why do crops of the same type have different variety names, and how do I choose the right one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kome lɛ nɔŋŋ yɔɔ gbɛi srɔtoi lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala gbɛi ni sa?

english: Varieties differ in traits like height, fruit size, maturity time, and disease resistance. You should choose a variety based on your local rainfall, soil type, and what buyers in your market prefer.
ga: Esoro henɔi lɛ yɛ sui tamɔ amɛlɛɛmɔ, amɛyibii lɛ adalɛ, amɛdalɛ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ mli. Esa akɛ ohala henɔi srɔtoi. Kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ henɔ kɛ nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ ojarayelihe lɛ taoɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I take seeds directly from a high-quality fruit I harvested, will the new plants produce the exact same good fruits?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni mikpaa lɛ mli. Ani tso hee nɛɛ baawo yibii kpakpai ni tamɔ nɛkɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ?

english: Not always. Seeds are formed through pollination and carry mixed traits from two parent flowers. Plants grown from saved seed may not turn out identical to the mother plant.
ga: Jeee be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui jɛɔ pollination mli baa ni amɛji fɔlɔi fɔfɔi enyɔ ni akɛfee ekome. Ekolɛ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso lɛ kpaaa gbee.

english: How can I tell if the seeds or seedlings I am buying from the market are truly high quality?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni miheɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: High-quality seeds are uniform in size, free from pest damage, molds, or dirt, and come from trusted, certified suppliers rather than unverified sellers.
ga: Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni dalɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Ebɛ nɔ ko ni tsɛŋemɔ helai, ŋmeii, loo muji fiteee. ni ejɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ nibii haa lɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ ni amɛná hegbɛ lɛ adɛŋ. Nɔ ni fe mɛi ni hɔ̃ɔ nii ni akwɛɛɛ amɛmli

english: Why is it often better to buy certified seeds instead of just reusing seeds from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i kɛ dumɔwuhi nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ tsu ní ekohu.

english: Certified seeds are carefully produced to ensure high germination rates, disease freedom, and uniform growth. Reusing saved seeds, especially from hybrid varieties, often leads to lower yields in the second generation.
ga: Akɛ hiɛdɔɔ feɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, hela akafee amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ Titri lɛ kɛjɛ hybrid henɔi amli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yibiiwoo ni baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grown from saved seeds produce smaller or weaker yields after repeating this for a few years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛdu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo loo fioo beni mikɛ enɛ fee afii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Reusing seeds over multiple generations causes genetic degeneration and increases susceptibility to local diseases. Refreshing your stock with clean, high-grade planting material restores high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ yɛ yinɔi amli lɛ kɛ fɔmɔ nii amli fitemɔ baa ni ehaa helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni he tse ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ wo onibii amli lɛ, ebaaha oná yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they fight each other for food?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii he?

english: They work together very well. Cowpeas pull nitrogen gas out of the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize. At the same time, cowpea vines cover the ground to shade out weeds and keep the soil damp.
ga: Amɛfeɔ ekome kɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, he ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ yeɔ nii yɛ lɛ. yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ Jwɛi wain tsei haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha jwɛi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, or heavy rain has washed the nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it. Applying fertilizer or compost rich in nitrogen will fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efɔ nitrogen lɛ ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do you advise me to leave dry cut grass on top of the soil around my vegetable beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ mashi jwɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry cut grass, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the soil quickly. It keeps the roots cool, stops weeds from taking over, and slowly rots into natural plant food.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni afo lɛ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekaye nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer heat stress, drought, or too much wet weather. Keeping the soil evenly moist and avoiding extreme dryness helps the flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ, hɔmɔ, loo shihilɛi ni mli edɔ fe nine lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni fe nine lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: What is eating tiny ragged holes inside the young funnels of my maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni miiye buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that crawl deep into the leaf funnel. Spraying neem water extract or recommended pesticides directly into the funnel early in the morning kills them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotten at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is blossom end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, usually because the soil moisture is inconsistent. Regular, steady watering helps the plant transport calcium from the soil into the developing fruit.
ga: Enɛ ji blossom end rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ bɛ shiŋŋ. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why should I leave wider gaps between my tomato plants during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ babaoo yɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ ateŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?
