english: Leaving wider space lets wind blow freely between the plants. This dries the leaves faster after rain, preventing fungal diseases and leaf rot from spreading quickly in damp weather.
ga: He ni yɔɔ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ tswaa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛgbiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ baa ni fiteɔ lɛ naa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden poles for the vines to climb, or can they just crawl on the ground?
ga: Ani mi sweet potato tso lɛ he miihia tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ diɛŋtsɛ koni wain tsei lɛ akwɔ? Aloo okɛ ohe afɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Yam vines need poles so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Staked yams make energy far faster and grow much larger tubers than yams left crawling on the ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ko koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Atomɔ ni adu lɛ haa hewalɛ baa oya ni eyɛ ŋmeii wuji babaoo fe ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava tubers are mature and ready for harvest without digging up the whole plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ tso muu lɛ fɛɛ efolɔɔɔ mli?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ bɔi fãmɔ

english: Why are my crops wilting and turning yellow even when it is not the main dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbo ni efee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ jeee nugbɔshiimɔ be titri ji no lɛ?

english: Unpredictable weather changes cause sudden high temperatures and dry spells. Extreme heat forces crops to lose moisture quickly, stressing the plant and making leaves turn yellow or drop even outside the traditional dry season.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni yaa hiɛ trukaa kɛ hɔmɔ baa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. ehaa tso lɛ he feɔ shoo ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ sɛɛ po.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from weather stress instead of an insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miipiŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ mli moŋ fe ni kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ?

english: Weather stress usually causes widespread wilting, leaf scorching, or stunted growth across a field without physical damage. Insect attacks typically leave visible bite holes, chewed edges, or sticky residue on the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa he fɛɛ he baa. baai ni eshã loo ni edaaa kwraa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ he okadii, ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛyeɔ, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni anaa ni eshwɛɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do some spots on my farm produce weak crops while plants nearby are growing strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ miida waa lɛ?

english: Soil fertility and moisture retention vary across a farm field. Patchy growth happens because specific areas may lack vital soil nutrients, suffer from poor drainage, or have harder soil that prevents roots from growing deep.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Patchy growth Enɛ baa mli ejaakɛ ekolɛ hei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Naagbai ni kɔɔ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I give extra liquid nourishment to only the weak patches of crops in my farm instead of treating the whole field?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii ni ji nu krokomɛi moŋ fe ni mahã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ niyenii?

english: Yes, spot-treating gives struggling plants extra nutrients to help them catch up with healthier crops, saving you time and money compared to treating the entire farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, spot treatments lɛ haa tsei ni miiwuu lɛ naa niyenii krokomɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ahe. Okɛ obei kɛ oshika ato ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔkwɛmɔ he.

english: Why do my crops look weaker after a sudden heavy rainfall followed by intense sunshine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Heavy rain flushes key nutrients out of the topsoil, and immediate hot sunshine causes water on the leaves to evaporate too quickly, creating severe stress for young roots.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii titrii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ. Enɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa shishifãi bibii anɔ.

english: Why is it necessary to measure liquid farm chemicals accurately instead of estimating the amount with a cup?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni asusu tsofai ni ji nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ kɔɔpoi baasusu yibɔi ahe lɛ

english: Measuring accurately ensures the exact dose needed to heal the plant; using too much liquid chemical can burn crop leaves and poison the soil, while using too little will not fix the plant's weakness.
ga: Susumɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ haa anáa yibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛtsa tso lɛ. Tsofa ni ji nu babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni efite shikpɔŋ lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni nɔ fioo pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nyɛŋ asaa tso lɛ he ni egbɔjɔ lɛ.

english: What is the advantage of using a liquid crop treatment compared to a solid powder chemical?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ nu mli tsei ahe tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛ powda ni wa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ he?

english: Liquid treatments dissolve fully in water and are absorbed much faster by crop leaves and roots, making them useful for quickly boosting weak plants that need urgent nutrition.
ga: Nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli kwraa, ni tso lɛ baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ lɛ oya kwraa. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha tsei ni egbɔjɔ ni niyenii he miihia amɛ oya lɛ ni yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why should I avoid mixing my water-based crop treatments with muddy water from the nearby stream?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛtsaa tsei ahe lɛ kɛ nu ni mli ewo muji ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ mli lɛ futumɔ he?

english: Dirty or muddy water contains soil particles and minerals that bind to the chemical, weakening its effectiveness and clogging your sprayer nozzle.
ga: Nu ni mli ewo muji loo muji lɛ ji sũ mli nibii kɛ tɛi ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he. Enɛ haa tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaa tsɔne lɛ mli nu lɛ tsiɔ ehe.

english: Is it better to spray liquid nourishment on my crops in the afternoon heat or in the cooler hours?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafɔ nu ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ nɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shwane mli loo yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli?

english: It is best to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon because intense heat causes the liquid to evaporate before the leaves can absorb it, and hot sun on wet leaves can cause scorching.
ga: Esa akɛ afɔse nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi dani baai lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmɔɔ. Ni hulu la ni tsoɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shãa.

english: Why should I consult an agricultural expert before introducing a new liquid spray on my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mabi okwaayeli he nilelɔ ko dani mikɛ nu hee ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ atsu nii?

english: An expert knows the correct dosage, safety precautions, and specific timing required for your crop type, helping you avoid costly crop damage and wasted chemical inputs.
ga: Nileelɔi le tsofa lɛ falɛ ni sa. Shweshweeshwefeemɔ he gbɛjianɔtoi kɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Eye ebua bo ni otsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa ni fiteɔ kɛ tsofai ni afiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some farmers in Ghana switch from growing food crops to long-term cash crops like rubber?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miitsake kɛmiijɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛduɔ lɛ nɔ kɛmiiya shika ŋmɔshi nibii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ tamɔ rɔba lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Food crops like maize and vegetables provide quick, short-term money after a few months, but tree crops like rubber provide steady, long-term financial security for up to 30 years once the trees mature.
ga: Niyenii nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai haa shika ni heɔ be kukuoo oya yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli tamɔ rɔbɔt tsei haa shika he shweshweeshwe shihilɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ afii 30 kɛji tsei lɛ dara pɛ.

english: How do I know if my farmland is suitable for growing rubber trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ sa kɛha rɔbɔt tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Rubber trees need deep, well-drained soil and high rainfall to grow well, making them ideal for forest zones in southern Ghana, such as the Western and Central regions.
ga: Rɔba tsei he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ, kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha kooi ni yɔɔ Ghana kooyigbɛ lɛ, tamɔ anaigbɛ kɛ teŋgbɛ kpokpai lɛ.

english: How long will I have to wait after planting rubber trees before I can start harvesting latex?
ga: Kɛ́ odu rɔbɔt tso lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ dani obɔi latɛs lɛ naabuamɔ?

english: Rubber trees generally take about 6 to 7 years of growth after planting before their trunks are thick enough to be tapped for latex.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛdaraa beni adu amɛ sɛɛ. Dani tso lɛ shishi lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afo rɔbɔt tsei

english: How can I tell when a crop on my farm is fully ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ eshɛ he kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Crops show clear physical signs when ready, such as leaves turning yellow or brown, fruit changing color, pods drying out, or stems drooping.
ga: Tsei baajie gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii ni yɔɔ faŋŋ kpo kɛ́ amɛfee klalo, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. Yibii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, loo amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Will cutting into the bark of a rubber tree to collect latex kill the tree?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt lɛ shishifã lɛ ni abaafo koni akɛbu latɛs lɛ naa lɛ baagbe lɛ?

english: No, as long as you only shave thin strips of the outer bark without cutting into the inner wood, the tree naturally heals and will keep producing latex for over 20 years.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ obaakpa kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ bibioo. ni efooo tso ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli Tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ebaaya nɔ ekɛ latɛs aba nɔ ni fe afii 20 sɔŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of the year in Ghana for me to plant new tree seedlings?
ga: Mɛni ji afi lɛ mli be ni hi fe fɛɛ yɛ Ghana ni mikɛdu tso dumɔwui heei?

english: The best time to plant is at the start of the major rainy season (around April or May), so the seedlings can use the natural rainwater to build strong roots.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ shishijee. (aaafee April loo May mli) koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ amɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ nu atsu nii ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava or plantain on the same land while my young rubber trees are growing?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu niyenii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ he kome be mli ni mi-gum tsei bibii lɛ miida lɛ?

english: Yes, you can intercrop cassava, plantain, or maize between young rubber trees for the first 2 to 3 years to earn income before the tree leaves grow wide and shade out the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu cassava, plantains loo ŋmãa yɛ gum tsei bibii ateŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 lɛ mli koni onine ashɛ shika nɔ dani tso lɛ baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are my young crops growing tall and thin instead of strong and healthy under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso bibioo lɛ miida ni efee mlɛo yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee hewalɛ ni efee hewalɛ yɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ?

english: Plants need sun to make food; when shaded by bigger trees, young crops stretch upward desperately searching for light, which makes their stems weak and thin.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛji akɛ eyɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, tsei bibii lɛ baagbala amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi, ni amɛtao la waa. ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni efeɔ mlɛo

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant the same crop in the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the specific nutrients that plant needs from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ pɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What basic care do young rubber seedlings need to survive their first year in the field?
ga: Mɛɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ he hiaa rɔbɔt tso ko koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli?

english: Young rubber seedlings need regular weeding so weeds do not steal their water and soil nutrients, protection from animals, and clearing around them to prevent wildfire damage during the dry season.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei bibii lɛ amli daa koni jwɛi lɛ akaju nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, koni abu he kɛjɛ kooloi ahe, ni ajie he ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ. Bɔni afee ni koo mli la akafite nii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: How do I know which way to stick my cassava stems into the ground when planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni esa akɛ madu mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look closely at the small bumps or nodes where leaves used to grow on the stem; these nodes should always point upwards toward the sky. If you plant cassava stems upside down, the plant will struggle to grow and will produce very few or small roots.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ nodes nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be. Kɛji odu ŋmei tso ni okɛ ohiɛ fɔ̃ shi lɛ Tso lɛ dalɛ baawa ni shishifãi fioo pɛ loo bibii baafee nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground with sticks keeps the leaves healthy, prevents rots from wet soil, and helps the yam tubers beneath the ground grow much larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei niji tsu nii koni akɛwo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ baai lɛ. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ fitemɔ naa. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ni amɛdaraa babaoo.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to grow green and full. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems will help them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes into the center leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei abifao lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the growing tip of the plant during the hot sun. Inspecting your farm early in the morning and applying neem oil or recommended treatments directly into the plant whorl helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli leebi ni okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai krokomɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my newly planted cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no big trees nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he ko lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby acts as a living umbrella, protecting the delicate seedlings from heat and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why is it better to wait for steady rains before planting my crop seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be dani odu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Seeds require continuous moisture to sprout and build strong roots. If you plant after just one isolated rain, the ground can dry out quickly during the heat, causing your seeds to dry up and die before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni wa. Kɛji odu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my plants with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves—a practice called mulching—keeps the soil cool, traps moisture so you don't lose water to the heat, and prevents unwanted weeds from growing around your crop.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ—nifeemɔ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ ŋmɛɔ bɔni afee ni nu akaje odɛŋ kɛya latsaa lɛ nɔ. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Planting maize in the exact same spot year after year drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows maize-specific pests to build up. Swapping with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the yellow blossoms on my tomato plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil becomes too dry, or if there aren't enough bees to pollinate them. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing light shade helps save the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee pollination lɛ bɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔii lɛ akafite.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny, invisible insects like aphids or mites feeding on the undersides of the leaves. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with soapy water or neem extracts helps keep these pests away.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni anyɛɛɛ ana, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem mli nu shwie baa lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ akashɛ he.

english: Is it beneficial for me to plant coconut trees right around my house?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei ni miduɔ yɛ mishia lɛ he lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ kɛha mi?

english: Yes, planting coconut trees around your compound provides natural shade, acts as a windbreak to protect your home, and gives your family easy access to nutritious food and water without taking up space on your main farmland.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he fɛɛ he. He ni oyɔɔ lɛ baafee hulutsoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni buɔ oshia lɛ he. Ni ehaa oweku lɛ náa niyenii kɛ nu ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ mlɛo ni eŋɔɔɔ he ko yɛ oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ titri lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do these new crop varieties from agricultural experts yield more fruit than my old local seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei heei ni jɛ okwaayeli he nilelɔi adɛŋ nɛɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe mimaŋ dumɔwui momo lɛ?

english: Expert-developed seeds are specially selected to resist local diseases, absorb nutrients efficiently, and focus their energy on producing higher yields of fruit and food rather than just growing tall stems.
ga: Ahala dumɔwui ni ŋaalɔi fee lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ haa aduawai kɛ niyenii ni baa babaoo lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, e daa tso nɛ gagaa kɛkɛ.

english: How long does a new dwarf coconut tree take to start giving fruits compared to the old tall ones?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmei tso hee ni ji dwarf lɛ woɔ yibii? Kɛ akɛto tsei kakadaji momo lɛ ahe?

english: Improved dwarf coconut trees usually start flowering and producing fruits in about 3 to 4 years, which is much faster than traditional tall varieties that often take 7 to 10 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo shishi yɛ aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ yaa oya kwraa fe blema ŋmeii kakadaji ni bei pii lɛ amɛheɔ afii 7 kɛyashi 10 lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young plants dry up even when there is rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: If soil drains too fast or weather gets extremely hot, intense sunlight can make leaves lose water faster than roots can drink it. Providing temporary shade or mulching around the roots helps hold moisture.
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu hoɔ oya tsɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa Hulu la ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha baai lɛ afite nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔleɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that the plant is starving for nutrients—usually nitrogen—or that water is standing around the roots for too long, preventing them from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye tso lɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. (Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen) loo nu ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni eha amɛmiigbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I leave some shade trees on my farm instead of clearing every tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni majie tso fɛɛ tso?

english: Shade trees shield tender young crops from harsh sunlight, keep soil moist during dry periods, and drop leaves that decompose into natural food for your plants.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu kpɛɔ lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa lɛ. ni okɛ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha otsei lɛ.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough soil for everything?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, which starves the crop and slows down its growth and fruit production.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehaa amɛdaramɔ kɛ yibiiwoo baa shi.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same small pocket of food and water, causing all the plants to grow thin, weak, and produce small fruits.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli yɛ kotoku bibioo kome mli, ni no haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ mlɛo, egbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii bibii.

english: Why are the blossoms on my vegetable plants falling off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-vegetable tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress—such as dry soil, excessive heat, or a lack of nutrients—causing the plant to shed its blossoms to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na nɔnyɛɛ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo dɔlɛ ni fe nine. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ afɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛhi shi.

english: How do leguminous crops like cowpeas help make my soil richer for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes have special bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into plant food, which enriches the soil naturally for crops planted after them.
ga: Legumes yɛ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ.

english: How long does a plantain sucker take from the day I plant it until the fruit is ready for harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ aduawai lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ?

english: A plantain plant usually takes between 11 to 15 months from planting to harvest, depending on the variety, water supply, and soil quality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa. Edamɔ srɔtoi lɛ anɔ, nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Look for 'sword suckers' that have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and strong base stems. Avoid suckers with broad, flat leaves because they grow slower and produce smaller yields.
ga: Taomɔ ‘Sword Bud’ ni baai lɛ mli tseee ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishigbɛ tso ni mli wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ahe ejaakɛ amɛdaraa blɛoo ni amɛwooo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I grow plantain on the same piece of land alongside crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, intercropping plantain with short-term crops like maize or cassava works well in the first few months. The secondary crops shade the soil and provide early income while the plantain grows.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni akɛ be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsakeɔ. Etsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji 2-3 lɛ amli. Tsei ni ji enyɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shika baa oya be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves turn yellow and dry up before the crop even fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani tso lɛ woɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves often indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, insufficient water during dry periods, or fungal diseases like Black Sigatoka that damage leaf tissue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ sigatoka diŋ ni fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ.

english: How does putting dried grass and leaves around the base of my plantain crop help it grow better?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai ni akɛfataa he lɛ Te midumɔwui lɛ ashishitoo baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: This practice is called mulching. It trap moisture in the soil, prevents weeds from taking over, keeps the root area cool in hot weather, and adds natural nutrients as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ mulching. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. ni yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fataa he beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: What causes strong winds to easily push over my plantain plants before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa kɛtsɔɔ mi-plantains lɛ amli dani kpamɔ be baashɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and heavy top foliage. Poor soil nutrients weaken the roots, and underground pests like nematodes eat the root system, making the plant fall easily unless supported with wooden stakes.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ ŋwɛi baai ni mli tse. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi tamɔ nematodes yeɔ shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei baagbee shi, ja tso ko fiɔ amɛsɛɛ.

english: What causes small holes in my plantain stems and roots that make the plant look weak?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mitso lɛ shishi kɛ plantain shishifãi ni haa tso lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ lɛ mli.

english: These holes are caused by plantain stem borers (weevils) or root nematodes. Cleaning suckers before planting and keeping the field clear of decaying crop waste prevents them.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishifãi (ŋmeii) loo shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ otsumɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe dani adu, ni aha he ni ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu amɛhe.

english: Why does my plantain plant produce very small bunches even though the stalk itself looks big and healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miiwo ŋmeii bibii waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmeii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛdara ni amɛhe wa moŋ lɛ?

english: A plant can grow large using excess nitrogen, but if it lacks potassium and phosphorus, it won't have enough nutrient energy to produce big, thick plantain fingers.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ adara babaoo kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ potassium kɛ phosphorus faaa lɛ Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha afee nineshi tsɔji wuji ni mli tse lɛ bɛ.

english: Does a plantain tree produce fruit continuously, or do I have to cut it down after harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui lɛ baaya nɔ awo yibii loo esa akɛ afolɔ amɛ ashwie shi beni akpa amɛ?

english: Each plantain stem fruits only once in its lifecycle and then dies. However, the root system continuously sprouts new shoots (suckers) at the base to produce the next harvest.
ga: Plantain tso fɛɛ tso woɔ yibii shikome pɛ yɛ ewala be mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ egboɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, shishifã lɛ yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii heei (ŋmeii) yɛ shishigbɛ koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: How many side shoots should I leave around my main plantain stem to get the best harvest?
ga: Esa akɛ mashi sɛɛ tsei enyiɛ mabɔle plantain tso wulu lɛ he koni maná yibii ni hi fe fɛɛ?

english: It is best to leave only 2 to 3 strong shoots around the main mother plant. Leaving too many shoots causes them to fight for soil nutrients and light, resulting in smaller fruit.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooshi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2 kɛyashi 3 pɛ yɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ he. Tsoi babaoo tsɔ baatswa shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji aduawai bibii.

english: Officer, why is it important for me to test my farm's soil before I plant my crops?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Testing your soil tells you what plant nutrients are already present and what is missing. It prevents you from wasting money on the wrong fertilizers and helps your crops grow healthy.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa baatsɔɔ bo tsei amli niyenii ni yɔɔ mli kɛ nɔ ni bɛ mli. Etsiɔ bo gbɛ koni okafite shika yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my land has lost its strength and needs help to recover?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ efo mli ni ehe miihia ni aye abua koni aku sɛɛ akɛba ekoŋŋ?

english: When land loses strength, crop yields drop, crop leaves may turn yellow early, and water drains away too quickly or pools up. Testing the soil helps identify the exact missing nutrients.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ fite lɛ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ baa shi Tso lɛ baai baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya. ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya tsɔ loo etsɔɔ mli babaoo. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa yeɔ ebuaa ni ayɔseɔ niyenii mli nibii ni elaaje lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: I hear people talking about soil being too sour for crops. What does that mean?
ga: Minu ni mɛi miiwie shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he. Mɛni no tsɔɔ?

english: Sour soil means the ground has high acidity, which stops crop roots from drinking in food and water properly. Soil testing measures acidity so you can fix it with agricultural lime.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ tsɔɔ akɛ eyɛ acid babaoo. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii kɛ nu jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa susuɔ acidity he bɔni afee ni okɛ okwaayeli lime ajaje.

english: Why are my crops still growing poorly even after I buy and apply standard fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ miheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Applying fertilizer without testing the soil is like taking medicine without knowing your sickness. If your soil lacks a specific element or is too acidic, regular fertilizer will not solve the problem.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni okaaa lɛ okwɛ lɛ, etamɔ tsofa ni oooye ni oleee akɛ hela mɔ bo. Kɛji akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nɔ pɔtɛɛ ko loo eyɛ acid tsɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ atsu naagba lɛ he nii.

english: Why do you advise that I test a new farming practice on a small piece of land first instead of my whole farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko makwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko klɛŋklɛŋ, moŋ fe miŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Testing on a small plot lets you observe how a new crop seed or practice performs on your specific land without risking your entire harvest or income if things do not go as expected.
ga: Kaa ni ooofee yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ haa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ bɔ ni dumɔwu loo nifeemɔ hee ko tsuɔ nii ehaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ ko nɔ. Ni akɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ loo shika ni anáa lɛ wooo oshara mli kɛji nibii eyaaa nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Jeee bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ lɛ

english: What is an agricultural demonstration plot, and how does it help me as a farmer?
ga: Mɛni ji okwaayeli he nɔkwɛmɔnɔ shikpɔŋ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ebaanyɛ eye ebua mi akɛ okwaafonyo?

english: A demonstration plot is a local field where extension officers show new farming methods step-by-step so you can see the real results with your own eyes before trying them on your land.
ga: Demo plots ji akutsoŋ hei ni extension nitsulɔi lɛ jieɔ okwaayeli gbɛi heei akpo fiofio koni bo diɛŋtsɛ ona nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa diɛŋtsɛ dani oka amɛ okwɛ yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I be sure that a new crop variety will actually perform well in my village?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ tso henɔ hee ko baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli?

english: You can plant a small test row of the new variety side-by-side with your traditional seed to compare their growth, pest resistance, and harvest under your local weather conditions.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa line bibioo ko. ni yɔɔ srɔtoi hee lɛ mli lɛ kɛ oshishijee dumɔwui lɛ masɛi. koni akɛ dalɛ ato Pest resistance kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ he yɛ okpokpaa lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ shihilɛi amli.

english: What kind of modern tools do extension officers use to check the condition of farmland?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nibii ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ?

english: Officers use portable digital meters, soil test kits, and mobile tools to quickly check moisture, nutrient levels, and acidity directly on your field.
ga: Amralofoi kɛ dijitaal mitai ni akɛyaa he fɛɛ he, shikpɔŋ kaa nibii kɛ mobile nibii tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ ha. Niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ acidity tɛ̃ɛ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ oya

english: How does using modern technology help me more than just following traditional farming wisdom?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaalee ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa babaoo fe blema okwaayeli he nilee ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ?

english: Modern technology removes the guesswork by giving accurate details about your soil and climate, helping you produce more crops while spending less on inputs like fertilizer.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ ŋaalee jieɔ susumɔi ni ejaaa lɛ kɛyaa kɛtsɔ oshikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he saji ni ja ni ekɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Ehaa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ofiteɔ shika fioo yɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: What steps can I take to restore land that has become completely dry and unproductive?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛi manyɛ matsɔ nɔ mafee shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni wooo yibii lɛ ekoŋŋ?

english: You can restore bad land by adding organic manure, planting cover crops like beans that add nitrogen back into the dirt, and letting small sections rest after testing the soil.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ nibii ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni oha fã bibioo ko Ajɔɔ ehe yɛ shikpɔŋ kaa sɛɛ

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of a maize stalk usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, a key food plant needs to grow green and healthy. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa ni ehe hiaa ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield every year when I keep planting on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi be mli ni miyaa nɔ miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to rest. Rotating different crops, like planting beans after maize, helps rebuild soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ kɛkɛ lɛ ŋmãa. Ebaaye ebua ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers stay very small even though the leaves and stem are growing tall and leafy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ daraaa lɛ? He ni baai kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ kɛlɛ lolo ni amɛyɛ baai?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or cassava plants are planted too close together, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen babaoo loo aduɔ ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ amli moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli.

english: Yam leaves produce food using sunlight. Staking lifts the leaves off the damp ground into the sun, which prevents leaf rot and allows the plant to produce larger, healthier tubers.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii. Staking baaye abua ni ewó baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ kɛya hulu la mli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ woɔ bulbs wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot, when water is applied irregularly, or when tiny insects attack the blossoms before pollination happens.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii tutuaa fɔfɔii dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛmli.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Shade trees act like living umbrellas, keeping the surrounding ground moist and cool until the cocoa plants mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ambrela ni hiɛ ka. Ha he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi cacao tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the juices from fresh shoots, or by a plant virus spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ ŋmeii heei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper leaf curl baa. loo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: How do I know if it is the right time to plant my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ eji be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: You should wait until the ground has received a few heavy rains that wet the soil deep down. Planting after just one light shower will cause seeds to sprout and quickly die when the soil dries out.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni naa wa fioo nɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo sɛɛ Nɔ kome pɛ ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi oya be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer right before a heavy rain falling?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo mli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes the fertilizer off the soil surface into ditches before plant roots have time to drink it up, wasting your money and labor.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyaa buji amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika kɛ nitsumɔ fɛɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than my cultivated crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild native plants with deep roots that are naturally adapted to steal water, light, and soil nutrients much faster than farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji maŋ tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛju nu, la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei.

english: Why should I buy certified seeds every year instead of saving seeds from my last maize harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase daa afi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are specially produced to give high yields and resist diseases. Saved seeds from harvested hybrid crops lose their strength in the next generation, leading to smaller cobs and much lower yields.
ga: Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛha yibii babaoo kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: How can I store my harvested seeds safely at home so that insects do not destroy them before the next planting season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ato shĩa shweshweeshwe? Bɔni afee ni kooloi akafite nii dani be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aba.

english: Seeds must be dried completely until they are hard before storage. Storing them in sealed airtight bags, like PICS bags, cuts off oxygen so insects cannot survive or damage the seeds.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi dumɔwui lɛ kwraa kɛyashi amɛhe wa dani akɛto. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli, tamɔ PICS kotokui amli lɛ, efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni kooloi bibii akahi shi loo amɛkafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Will planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger harvest from my plot of land?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni madu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and produce larger yields.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some of my seeds fail to sprout at all after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil is too dry, or if waterlogged soil rots them. Planting at the right depth in moist, well-drained soil helps them sprout successfully.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ha dumɔwui lɛ fite. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow. Applying a nitrogen fertilizer like Urea can help restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni mɔ lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or poor soil nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding compost helps the plants hold onto flowers and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni ehiii lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with green leaves but forming very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai eŋɔli shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to focus energy on growing leafy stems instead of roots. Cassava needs balanced soil rich in potassium to develop large, healthy tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi ni miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja ni potassium eyi mli obɔ lɛ he miihia cassava koni enyɛ ená ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are there ragged holes in the center leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn plant lɛ yɛ bu yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaves. Early inspection and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts can stop them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baanyɛ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii akpãtãmɔ.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil fertility and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves on growing maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is receiving too much water. Nitrogen helps plants stay green and grow strong, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or compost helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo enine shɛɔ nu babaoo nɔ. Nitrogen yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ aná su ni ji eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend that I plant groundnuts or cowpeas on the same land where I harvested maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni extension agent lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmei yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on soil nutrients and exhausts the ground. Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which restores fertility for future crops without needing expensive synthetic fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni efiteɔ sũ lɛ. Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee nibii ni jara wa atsu nii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I clear all the large trees from my farmland?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei ni eda kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and dry winds. Keeping larger shade trees or planting plantains beside them creates a canopy that protects young cocoa seedlings from heat stress while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Tsei wuji ni akɛwoɔ amɛhe shade loo tsei bibii ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ baa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling upward and looking twisted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the leaves, or by a plant virus. Spraying neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap on the leaves helps clear these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Does my yam crop really need wooden stakes to grow well, or can I leave the vines to spread on the ground?
ga: Mi sweet potatoes lɛ he miihia tso tso koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ oshi wain tsei lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ.

english: Staking yam vines on wooden poles lifts the leaves toward sunlight so they can manufacture more food for the tuber. Leaving vines on the ground exposes them to humidity and soil-borne diseases, resulting in much smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ akwɛ hulu la lɛ hiɛ koni amɛná niyenii babaoo amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo kwraa.

english: Why should I prune some of the young shoots growing around the base of my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-plantain lɛ shishi lɛ ekomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Extra shoots, known as suckers, compete with the main plantain stem for nutrients and water. Removing all but one or two healthy suckers ensures the main stem gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ yibii lɛ, kɛ plantain tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. Ajieɔ ŋmeii fɛɛ ja ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting underground during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in flat, poorly drained soil. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows heavy rainwater to drain away, keeping the root tubers healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. ni oha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why should I cover the soil around my tomato plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps soil moisture under the hot sun, keeps roots cool, prevents weeds from sprouting, and breaks down into rich organic food for your crops over time.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa niyenii ni jara wa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli kɛhaa onibii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How do I know the best time to sow my maize seeds during the major rainy season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: It is best to plant maize after two or three consecutive steady rains when the soil is thoroughly wet, rather than after the very first light rain. Planting too early in dry soil can burn the seeds before they germinate properly.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaadu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, kɛ́ odu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã dani amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture fluctuates drastically. High heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy instead of forming tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake waa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei haoɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he moŋ fe ni amɛaafee tomato.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and dropping when exposed to direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants prefer shade because their root systems are tender and cannot absorb water fast enough to cool down under harsh, direct sunlight. Providing temporary shade using crops like plantains protects them until their roots fully develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii sumɔɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ nu oya bɔ ni sa ni amɛha amɛhe ajɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei tamɔ plantains tsu nii ni akɛha hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava plants drop most of their leaves during the dry season, and is my crop dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Ni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ miigboi?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells as a survival mechanism to conserve water. The crop is not dead; underground, the roots remain alive and continue storing energy until the rains return to sprout fresh leaves.
ga: Cassava gbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli akɛ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ anáa wala koni akɛbu nu he. Nibii ni adu lɛ gboko lolo. Yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, shishifãi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtoɔ hewalɛ aahu kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ haa amɛfeɔ baai heei.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before any fruits begin to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures get too high or when moisture levels in the soil swing dramatically between wet and dry. Consistent watering and keeping soil cool with mulch helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa kɛ sũ ni akɛwoɔ sũ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are my maize plants growing thin and turning purple on the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baai lɛ miitsɔ purple lɛ?

english: Purple leaves on maize are usually a clear sign of phosphorus deficiency in the soil. Phosphorus helps roots grow strong and supports early leaf development, so applying balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the planting season fixes this issue.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ fɔsfɔs faaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Fosforo yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsu nii yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: How do cowpea crops improve the soil for other crops grown after them?
ga: Te cowpea tsei feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni aduɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas work with beneficial bacteria in their root nodules to capture nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food. When the plant residues decompose, this trapped nitrogen remains in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpea kɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ lɛ amɛfeɔ tsei aniyenii. Beni tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ fiteɔ Nitrogen ni aŋã awo mli nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam leaves need to catch maximum sunlight to produce the energy required to grow big underground tubers. Staking keeps the foliage off the damp ground, exposing leaves to light while preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni hulu la ashɛ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛkwɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛtsɔ baai lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo atsɔɔ la mli yɛ be mli ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai hu ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do flowers grow directly out of the main trunk and heavy branches of a cocoa tree instead of at the ends of thin twigs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ eniji ni tsii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ niji bibii lɛ anaagbee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce flowers directly on the thick trunk and structural branches so that the plant can support the heavy weight of mature cocoa pods without breaking slender branches.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ tsei akutsei ni mli tse kɛ tsei niji ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni kookoo tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ kookoo ŋmɔji ni edara kwraa lɛ anɔ ni efoŋ niji bibii lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain stem produce small shoots around its base, and should I leave all of them to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni bɔleɔ amɛshishi lɛ he lɛ, ni esa akɛ maha amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: Plantain plants multiply naturally by growing suckers from their base. Leaving too many suckers causes them to fight for nutrients and light, resulting in smaller fruit bunches, so it is best to remove most and leave only one or two strong ones.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii babaoo ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ, ebaaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ la. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, aduawai lɛ feɔ bibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooojie amɛteŋ babaoo ni oshi eko loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves, or by a virus carried by insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kudɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ mra Ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: What happens to my crop yield if I plant my crops very close together to fit more plants in my field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in thin stems and lower yields. Proper spacing allows each plant enough room to build strong roots and yield more produce.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi ni wa baakwɛ̃ ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ su fɛfɛo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow leaves. Heavy rains can wash this nutrient deep into the soil away from roots, or the soil may be exhausted and need compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ jeee nakai lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ awo mli.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they face stress from dry weather, intense heat, or a lack of shade trees. If the cocoa tree feels it doesn't have enough water or food to nurture pods, it drops its flowers to save its strength and survive.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo hulutsoo ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛji akɛ cacao tso lɛ nu he akɛ ebɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha pod lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, Ebaafɔ fɔfɔi koni ehiɛ hewalɛ mli ni ehi shi.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different fertilizers together before giving them to my cassava?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi enyɔ afutu mli dani okɛwo ŋmei mli?

english: Mixing certain fertilizers can trigger chemical reactions that lock up nutrients or burn crop roots. It is best to apply fertilizers separately or use an already balanced compound fertilizer recommended for cassava.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi futu mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofa ko ni tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa loo eshãa tsei shishifãi lɛ aba. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli srɔtoi loo akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛha ŋmei lɛ awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: During extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can draw it from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to shrink its surface area and protect itself, usually recovering when the sun goes down.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛha ehiɛ he lɛ afee bibioo ni ebu ehe. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛji hulu lɛ nyɔ shi.

english: Why are my yam vines growing big, leafy stems, but the yams under the ground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii kɛ baai wuji lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi yam lɛ ji bibioo?

english: When the soil contains too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, the yam plant spends all its energy producing leaves above ground instead of sending food down to swell the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium faaa lɛ Sweet potato tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is typically caused by a virus spread by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat and drought. The curling is the plant's defensive reaction to disease or severe weather stress.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Curling ji bɔ ni tso ko buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ hela loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni naa wa he.

english: You can sample your farm by pulling up just one or two plants. If the inside of the groundnut shells has turned dark brown with dark veins and the seeds are full and firm, the whole field is ready to harvest.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtsɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni ooogbala lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ hu yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa.

english: Why do plantain suckers take so long to sprout if I plant them during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers require steady soil moisture to break sleep and form new roots. In dry soil, the sucker enters a waiting phase to preserve its water, delaying stem and leaf growth until regular rains begin.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkpa wɔɔ ni amɛfee shishifãi heei. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii boteɔ mɛmɔ be mli koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. Ha tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ baaje shishi.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas on the plot where I harvested my maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmãa yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of nitrogen from the soil, but cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and deposit it back into the ground through their roots, naturally restoring soil fertility for your next crops.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi tsina ŋmeii lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my main crops right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds are adapted to lie dormant in dry soil and react instantly to the first moisture. Crop seeds usually take longer to wake up, build roots, and establish themselves than tough wild weeds.
ga: Atsakeɔ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛkã shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni amɛfee nɔ ko amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nu lɛ ba. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui heɔ be babaoo dani amɛteɔ shi, amɛwoɔ shishifãi, ni amɛmaa shi fe koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have shallow roots and tender leaves that lose water very quickly in dry winds. Without shade trees like plantains or Gliricidia to block the intense sun and wind, the seedlings dry out and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii, ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi mli. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ bɛ lɛ, Dumɔwui lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaagboi.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast across my cocoa pods when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: This is black pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in cold, wet weather. Rain droplets splash the fungal spores from the soil or infected stems onto healthy pods, spreading the disease rapidly.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ fɛ̃i kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ fungal spores kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Heavy rains can also wash this nutrient out of the reach of plant roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa abɛi koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nɛɛ he ni tso shishifãi lɛ akashɛ he.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farm make the soil better for my next crop of maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmeii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. When you harvest them, that trapped nutrient remains in the ground to feed the next crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. beni okpaa lɛ Niyenii nibii ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves but give me small tubers at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen or is planted too close together, it uses all its energy to grow leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food down in the roots to form tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ loo adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ ehe tsɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ baai kɛ tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso ɔ sisije ɔmɛ a mi konɛ e pee bulb.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to grow big tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso koni ekɛwo bulbs lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce the food that feeds the underground tuber. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all leaves catch light and stay safe from soil diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná la ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off the plant before any fruits appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ yaa nɔ amɛshwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when the weather gets extremely hot or when water is low. Heat stress prevents successful pollination, so the plant sheds flowers to save its strength.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa loo kɛ́ nu faaa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛhewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my pepper plants produce small, wrinkled fruits during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants need consistent moisture to stretch and swell their fruits. When water is scarce, the plant shrinks its fruit size and concentrates energy just to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛyibii lɛ asɛɛ atsɛ ni amɛmli alɛɛ. Beni nu faaa Tsei lɛ baa aduawai lɛ anɔ shi ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛkɛ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow around my crops reduce my final yield at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ oŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ haa minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. They steal food away from your plants, leaving the crops weak and unable to produce full yields.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛjuɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when heavy wind blows during fruiting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit bunches at the top. If the soil is loose or wet, the weight makes the tree top-heavy, so wind easily uproots it unless it is supported with wooden props.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai akuu ni tsii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse loo edɔ lɛ Muji lɛ baaha tso lɛ yiteŋ afee shwiili. No hewɔ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi amli oya. ja akɛ tso ni akɛtsuɔ nii

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate root systems and tender leaves that dry out quickly under harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantain or nursery shade trees to protect them from heat and keep moisture in the soil while they grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni akɛkwɛɔ amɛ. Enɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi ni wa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant are usually a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main nutrient plants use to build green leaves and stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛha amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put four or five seeds in one hole to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ woɔ bu kome mli koni maná yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the young crops to fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. This makes all the plants grow weak and skinny, producing smaller or fewer fruits than properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ awu yɛ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ enɛ mli baa ji yibii bibii loo bibii fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ teŋ jɛkɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvests keep getting smaller every time I plant maize on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mitsuɔ lɛ miiba shi lɛ? Be fɛɛ be lɛ, abaadu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ

english: Growing the exact same crop on the same plot every season empties the soil of the specific nutrients that plant relies on. It also gives crop-specific pests and diseases a permanent home to multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be. Bei lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tsei kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei amli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ naa shia ni amɛhiɔ shi daa hu.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot under the ground when the heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When heavy rain fills the soil with excess water that cannot drain away, it starves the plant roots of air. Without oxygen, harmless soil fungi turn destructive and cause underground roots and tubers to rot.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛya. Ebaaha tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ akaná kɔɔyɔɔ. Kɛji oxygen bɛ lɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii ni bɛ awui lɛ fiteɔ shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my maize plant leaves look ragged with large holes cut into them overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ fee tamɔ nɔ ni etse ni afo buji wuji nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ?

english: Ragged holes with brownish waste inside the center leaf funnel are typical signs of Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the plant during the day and feed aggressively on the young leaves at night.
ga: Buji ni ekumɔ kɛ jwɛi ni tsuɔ yɛ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ ahe okadii ni afɔɔ namɔ, ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ gbɛkɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant suffers from extreme heat, poor watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which causes the plant to focus on growing tall green leaves instead of holding onto its fruit flowers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. nu ni ehiii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Enɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni kɛlɛ ni ji eŋɔli ni miida lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce so little fruit even if I add fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiwo yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than domestic crops and will steal the fertilizer, soil water, and light long before your main crops have a chance to absorb them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya kwraa fe shia tsei. Ni amɛbaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ la be kakadaŋŋ dani otsei titrii lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni amɛŋɔ amɛ.

english: Why is it bad for my soil if I burn the dead weeds and dry grass on my farm before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mishã jwɛi ni egboi kɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Burning grass and crop remains kills the good living organisms in the soil and removes the organic cover that keeps the land moist and fertile. Leaving the plant remains to rot naturally builds richer soil.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashãa lɛ gbeɔ nibii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. ni ejieɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Tso ni eshwɛ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni egboɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nii babaoo.

english: Why are the bottoms of my tomato fruits turning black and rotten while still on the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato aduawai lɛ shishi miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Black, sunken spots on the bottom of tomatoes are caused by a condition called blossom-end rot, which happens when dry soil prevents the plant from taking up calcium needed to build solid fruit walls.
ga: Shihilɛ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ tsi tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná calcium ni he hiaa koni amɛfee aduawai gbogboi ni wa lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots and delicate leaves that easily burn under full sun. Planting them alongside fast-growing temporary shade crops like plantains protects them from extreme heat and helps retain soil moisture during the dry Harmattan season.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu yɛ be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ Harmattan be ni nu lɛ mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that rely on exposed leaves to capture maximum sunlight. Elevating the vines off the ground provides the energy required to grow large, healthy tubers underground and prevents ground rot.
