ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛbaai ni miiba lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ awó wein tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa mɔ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience extreme heat stress or irregular watering. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to conserve energy and water rather than spend it on developing fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni abaafite shika yɛ aduawai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ mli lɛ

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. This often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients away or when the soil lacks organic matter and fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning small instead of growing flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛji bibii moŋ fe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or a virus spread by whiteflies, which damages the leaf tissue as it grows.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni ŋmeii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni kɛ baa lɛ mli fãji fitemɔ baa be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why are my cowpea plants growing plenty of dark green leaves but very few flower pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ waa shi fɔfɔii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Excess nitrogen in the soil causes cowpea plants to focus all their energy on leafy vegetative growth rather than shifting energy into producing flowers and seed pods.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni miida lɛ ahe nii. Mohu ɔ, a jeɔ he wami ɔ kɛ yaa fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwuhi a peemi mi.

english: Cassava plants signal maturity when their lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop off, and visible cracks begin to form in the soil around the main stem as the tubers expand below.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛmiida kɛji akɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbee shi. ni ŋmeii ni anaa lɛ bɔi feemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Trunk titri lɛ beni yitso lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ.

english: If I plant fresh plantain suckers today, how long must I wait to harvest the first bunch?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɛnɛ midu dumɔwui heei Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ dani makpa mi klɛŋklɛŋ nine lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers typically take between 11 to 15 months to produce a harvestable bunch, depending on rainfall, soil fertility, and proper removal of excess side suckers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ aaafee nyɔji 11 kɛyashi 15 dani amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni abaanyɛ akpa. Edamɔ nugbɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛ sɛɛgbɛ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ajiemɔ jogbaŋŋ nɔ.

english: Why is my hybrid oil palm tree taking longer than expected to bear fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-hybrid oil palm tso lɛ heɔ be babaoo fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ koni ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palms require consistent sunlight, proper spacing, and weed clearance around the base. Heavy shading or low soil nutrients like potassium delay flowering and fruit set.
ga: Mu tsei ahe miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ daa. sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni sa ni ojie jwɛi ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Shade ni tsii loo shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa tamɔ potassium haa fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: Why do my cabbage heads stay soft and leafy instead of forming hard, tight balls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitso lɛ yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lolo ni eyɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ko ni wa ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads fail to firm up when temperatures get too high or when plants receive inconsistent watering and insufficient nutrients during the head-forming stage.
ga: Kaabaji yitsei nyɛŋ afee shiŋŋ kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni afɔɔ tsei anɔ nu be fɛɛ be ni amɛnáaa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni amɛfeɔ tuber lɛ.

english: Cocoa pods change color when ripe, usually turning from green or dark red to bright yellow or orange. You can also tap the pod gently; if it makes a hollow sound, the seeds inside have loosened from the inner wall, indicating it is ready.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, etsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ loo akutu ni mli tse. Obaanyɛ otswa pod lɛ hu fioo kɛji efee gbee ni mli ewo muji. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ejie ehe kɛjɛ mligbɛ gbogbo lɛ he. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: You should harvest every 2 to 3 weeks during peak season so that ripe pods do not over-ripen or rot on the tree, which can attract pests and ruin the quality of the beans.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa daa otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ. Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ fe nine loo amɛkafite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baanyɛ agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛba ni efite kɔfe yibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why shouldn't I cut cocoa pods off the trunk using a blunt cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsɔne ni mli tseee shwieɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Using a blunt tool can strip the bark and damage the flower cushion on the tree trunk where future pods grow. A sharp sickle or pruning knife leaves a clean cut that protects next season's harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ dɛŋdade ni bɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ejie tso lɛ yibii lɛ ni efite fɔfɔi lɛ akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi ni wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmeii lɛ baajɛ mli aba lɛ. Sickle loo tsɔne ni akɛfoɔ tsei ni yɔɔ oya lɛ baaha pilamɔ lɛ he atse koni ebu be ni baa lɛ mli kpamɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do flowers and pods grow directly on the main trunk of my cocoa tree instead of the small branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi cacao tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe niji bibii anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce flowers directly on the trunk and thick woody limbs—a trait called cauliflory. This strong structure allows the tree to hold heavy cocoa pods safely as they mature.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei kɛ amɛniji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ. ni atsɛɔ lɛ cauliflower Nɛkɛ tsɔne ni mli wa nɛɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ shweshweeshwe beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: How many years will it take for my newly planted cocoa seedlings to start producing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi-cocoa dumɔwui ni midu ehee lɛ aje shishi amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties in Ghana usually start bearing pods within 2 to 3 years after planting, whereas older traditional varieties may take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ jeɔ ŋmɔtɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, yɛ be mli ni kookoo henɔi ni etsɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ blema lɛ baanyɛ ahé afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Cocoa trees drop leaves during hot, dry spells to reduce water loss and protect themselves from drought. Plantain trees or shade trees planted nearby help shade young cocoa plants and keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ. Koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi ni obu ohe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hulutsoo baa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi.

english: Why are some of my tiny green cocoa pods turning black and shriveling up before they grow full size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ minɔ lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni egbo dani eda kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: This is often caused by a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the tree drops pods it cannot afford to feed, or by fungal infections like Black Pod disease brought on by excess rain and shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherel’s wilt lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. he ni tso lɛ shĩɔ ŋmeii ni anyɛɛɛ aye loo kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ahe helai tamɔ black pod hela ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa lɛ mli.

english: Why are mirid insects such a big danger to my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mirid kooloi yeɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ awui lɛ?

english: Mirids (capsids) suck sap from young cocoa stems and pods, leaving dark spots that dry out the branches and allow fungal infections to enter, reducing your total harvest.
ga: Mirids (capsids) lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ kookoo tsei bibii kɛ ŋmeii amli lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni haa tsei lɛ aniji lɛ gĩɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii boteɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ nɔ ni baa shi.

english: Why do I need to pile my fresh cocoa beans under plantain leaves for a few days right after pod breaking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ kookoo ŋmeii heei toɔ plantain baai ashishi gbii fioo komɛi beni ŋmeii lɛ efo lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fermenting the beans under plantain leaves heats them up naturally, developing the chocolate flavor, removing bitterness, and stopping the seeds from germinating.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii lɛ wo plantain baai lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ adɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa tsokolate mli ŋɔɔ, ejieɔ ŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why must I dry my harvested cocoa beans on raised bamboo mats instead of on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbiɔ mi-kookoo ni mikpa lɛ yɛ ŋmeii anɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Raised mats let air flow freely beneath the beans for uniform drying while keeping the cocoa clean from soil dirt, mold, and farm animals.
ga: Mat ni awo nɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ kɔfi ŋmɔji lɛ ashishi jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛha kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ po agbi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa kookoo lɛ he tseɔ kɛjɛɔ muji, ŋmeii, kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Heavy rain can wash nitrogen deep into the soil away from roots, so applying a nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nitrogen lɛ he kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, kɛjɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaf edges of my crops turn brown and look burnt after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etamɔ nɔ ni eshã yɛ be mli ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer or placing it right against the plant stem causes 'fertilizer burn' by drawing water out of the roots. Fertilizer should always be placed in a small ring a few inches away from the stem when the soil is wet.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo wo tso lɛ mli loo okɛwo tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaha eshã kɛtsɔ nu ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii bibii amli. Ha ekɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo komɛi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, wet conditions. Pruning extra shade branches and removing infected pods helps air and sunlight flow through the farm to stop the fungal spread.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli lɛ amli ni ajie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛkpa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are my heavy plantain trees snapping off at the base before the fruit is ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni tsii lɛ miifo yɛ shishigbɛ dani aduawai lɛ shwere lɛ?

english: Microscopic worms called nematodes or stem-boring weevils are likely eating the roots and underground stem, weakening the tree's anchor. Planting clean suckers and keeping the base clear of rotting debris helps protect the root system.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ahe tsei ni he tse ni aha shishitoo lɛ akafee nɔ ko ni fiteɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Your plants likely have Cassava Mosaic Disease, a viral infection spread by tiny whiteflies or carried in old stems used for planting. Switching to disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to prevent this.
ga: Ekolɛ otso lɛ yɛ yucca mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii loo tsei momo ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ amli kɛbaa. Ni aaatsake kɛya ŋmei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: How can I tell underground yams are ready to harvest without digging them up first?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni mikɛ amɛ tsuuu nii klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Yams tell you they are mature above ground when their leafy green vines stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up. This natural sign shows that the vine has finished feeding energy into the tuber below.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɔ bo akɛ etsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ beni e-wein tso ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ kpa kwɛ̃mɔ. Kɛ́ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbi lɛ, enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ bulb ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: This condition is Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or uneven watering while the fruit develops. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the plant transport calcium directly into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be be mli ni tso lɛ yibii lɛ miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa aduawai ni miida lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought stress, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Providing light shade and steady watering during very hot spells helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. hɔmɔ he haomɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo He hulutsoo ni mli tse ni akɛhaa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very few leaves when planted under tall trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ baai fioo ko pɛ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ tsei kakadaŋŋ ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food energy. When shaded by dense trees, the plant spends all its energy stretching upwards to find light instead of growing thick stems, leaves, and fruits.
ga: Tsei hia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii hewalɛ. Beni amɛyɔɔ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii koni amɛshɛ la he. Mohu ɔ, e wa nɛ e peeɔ tso tsɔwi, baa, kɛ yiblii.

english: Why should I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmãa yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the field, they naturally enrich the soil with nitrogen, which reduces the need for expensive chemical fertilizers for the next crop.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ Amɛbaahã nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa atsu nii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested maize grains turn into powder after I keep them in my storeroom for a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ powda beni mikɛto mi-nitoohe lɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Grain weevils and beetles eat the inside of stored maize and lay eggs there. Drying your maize until it is very hard and storing it in airtight hermetic bags suffocates insects and keeps your harvest fresh for a long time.
ga: Ŋmãa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ mli aahu kɛyashi ebaawa waa ni okɛwo kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni eye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers growing smaller and smaller every year I plant on the same farm plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ feɔ bibii bibii daa afi ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull food out of the ground to grow. Planting cassava on the same soil every year without resting the land or adding manure exhausts the nutrients, leaving no food for future harvests.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ ehe loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ niyenii eshwɛɛɛ kɛha wɔsɛɛ nikpamɔ lɛ.

english: Apply fertilizer when the maize plants are about knee-high and the soil is moist. This gives the roots quick access to nutrients just as the plant begins its fastest growth stage.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eshɛ aaafee tsitsi nɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ naa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya tamɔ bɔ ni tso lɛ jeɔ shishi edaa oya bɔ ni eeenyɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides shade and preserves soil moisture so the cocoa can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak when I put many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Seeds planted too closely fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough food to build strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli niyenii He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and look wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies sucking the sap from the leaves and spreading plant diseases. Protecting the plants early with natural pest controls prevents leaf damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsei ahe ni abuɔ mra Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, atsĩɔ baai ni fiteɔ lɛ naa.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or applying too much nitrogen fertilizer stresses tomato plants, causing them to shed their flowers before fruits can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baaha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo.

english: How do I know when my yams are fully ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potatoes lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the green leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up completely. This signals that the plant has stopped growing above ground and stored all its nutrients in the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ eda kɛji baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi kwraa. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ ekpa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves turn yellow and decay during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kaabe baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water sitting around cabbage roots drowns them by cutting off oxygen, leading to root rot that turns the leaves yellow. Creating raised ridges helps excess water drain away.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Cabbage shishifãi lɛ baagbe amɛ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ baafo mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Kɛ́ afee ŋwɛi ŋta ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ.

english: Why do my harvested sweet potatoes rot quickly after I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested sweet potatoes have thin skins with minor scratches that let in rot fungi. Resting them in a dry, shaded place for several days hardens the skin and heals wounds before long-term storage.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni akpa ehee lɛ yɛ hewolo ni mli tseee kɛ ŋmɔlɔ fioo ni baanyɛ aha fungal rot aba. Kɛ́ okɛwo he ko ni egbi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli gbii babaoo lɛ, ebaaha hewolo lɛ mli awa ni etsa dani akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow so tall and thin when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are crowded, they compete with each other for sunlight. They stretch upwards as fast as they can to reach the light, making them grow tall and weak instead of developing strong stems and big ears.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. Amɛkpã amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ tso nɛ he wa kɛ tue nguahi.

english: How do I know if my cassava plants need more space in the soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tso lɛ he miihia he ko babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: If cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots compete underground for nutrients and space. When space is limited, the plant puts energy into surviving rather than expanding its roots into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi he ko. Kɛji he ko bɛ lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi. Mohu ɔ, sisifã ɔmɛ lɛɛɔ nɛ a peeɔ bulb nguahi.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers on my field?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ?

english: Plantains have broad leaves and roots that spread wide. Spacing them about three meters apart allows each plant to get enough sunlight, air, and soil moisture without shading or crowding its neighbors.
ga: Plantain lɛ yɛ baai kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. He ni jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mitai 3 lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa. ni etsĩii hulu lɛ naa loo etsĩii akutsoŋbii anaa

english: Why do my crop yields get smaller every year if I plant on the same small piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Each crop draws specific nutrients from the soil. Planting the exact same crop on the same plot season after season drains those specific nutrients faster than the soil can naturally rebuild them.
ga: Tso henɔ fɛɛ henɔ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei komekomei pɛpɛɛpɛ ni akwɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crops when I clear a fresh plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ mijie he ko hee lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly grab open space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients before cultivated crops can establish themselves.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛmɔ he ko ni yɔɔ faŋŋ, hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and fall off as the plant gets bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As a pepper plant grows new branches on top, those upper leaves block sunlight from reaching the lower ones. The plant discards the shaded bottom leaves to save energy for new growth and fruit.
ga: Beni pepper tso lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ niji heei yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ahe. Tsei shwieɔ amɛ shishigbɛ baai ni yɔɔ shade lɛ shi koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛha dalɛ hee kɛ yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings burn and die when I clear all the shade trees away?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are delicate and sensitive to harsh direct sunlight and heat. They need shade from larger trees or plantains to keep the air cool and moist around them while they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛnuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ he. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi amɛhe. Ehe ejɔ ni edɔ be mli ni edaa lɛ

english: Why do my yam vines try to climb every stick or tree nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miitao ekwɔ tso nine loo tso fɛɛ tso ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines cannot stand up on their own. They naturally climb upwards on nearby objects to lift their leaves into the sunlight, which gives the plant the energy it needs to grow tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei nyɛŋ adamɔ shi amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, amɛkwɔɔ nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ anɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛ hulu la lɛ akpee. Enɛ haa tso lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my crops drop their flowers when the weather stays hot and dry for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops suffer from heat and lack of water, they drop their flowers and young fruits to conserve water and protect the main plant from dying.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ he lɛ Fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu tso titri lɛ he kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Can I plant beans together with my maize on the same plot without harming the maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miyeŋ ŋmãa lɛ awui?

english: Yes, because beans and maize help each other. Beans take nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil to feed the maize, while the maize stalks give the bean vines support to climb.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ejaakɛ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yeɔ ebuaa amɛhe. Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bean wain tso lɛ ni ekwɔɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi.

english: Is it true that every piece of land has a specific crop or palm variety that grows best on it?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmei tso pɔtɛɛ ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, different crops thrive in different soils. Some crops prefer deep, rich topsoil, while hardy crops like certain oil palms can tolerate rocky or poorer soils as long as they get sufficient rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ekomɛi sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa, tamɔ mu tsei komɛi baanyɛ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii kwraa lɛ naa, kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my food crops grow very well on one part of my land, but fail on another part?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eyeee omanye yɛ fã kroko mli?

english: Soil depth, water retention, and nutrient levels change across different parts of the same farm. Food crops like maize and vegetables need soft, nutrient-rich soil, so they will struggle wherever the soil is shallow or dry.
ga: shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ mli nu ni ahiɔ mli kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni tsakeɔ yɛ hei srɔtoi Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ aduawai biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛbaabɔ mɔdɛŋ waa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi.

english: How can I tell what type of crop will perform well on my land before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu?

english: You can look at the soil texture, depth, and how well it holds water. Soil that is deep and moist is great for food crops, while tougher or rockier land might be better suited for resilient tree crops like oil palm.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ, bɔ ni emli kwɔ ha, kɛ bɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ ehaa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha niyenii tsei. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔji ni wa loo tɛi yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni sa jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi tamɔ mu tsei.

english: Does oil palm require the same fertile land as vegetables and cassava?
ga: Ani mu tso biɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ tamɔ aduawai kɛ ŋmei?

english: No, oil palms are strong tree crops with deep root systems. While they produce best in fertile soil, they can survive and yield on tougher land where delicate food crops would burn or fail.
ga: Dabi, mu tsei ji tsei ni wa ni yeɔ afii babaoo ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ amɛwoɔ yibii fe fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ moŋ. Amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii yɛ shikpɔji ni wa fe tsutsu lɛ anɔ. he ni niyenii tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ waa lɛ baashã loo amɛbaagbee shi yɛ lɛ

english: Can I plant oil palm trees on land that has a lot of rocks?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ adu mu tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, oil palms can grow on rocky land because their roots can search deep into underground crevices for water and support, though clearing stones around the planting hole helps them establish faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, mu tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ana nu ni amɛye amɛbua yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ ajieɔ tɛi ni ebɔle lɛ lɛ moŋ Bu ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ ama shi oya.

english: Why do some trees do well on rocky soil while my vegetables die on the same ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi yeɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ shi mi-aduawai lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Vegetables have short, delicate roots that need loose, rich soil to feed. Tree crops like palms have strong, persistent root systems that can penetrate hard or stony ground to reach nutrients hidden deeper below.
ga: Aduawai lɛ yɛ shishifãi kukuji ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni baa nii koni amɛye nii. Tso tsei tamɔ ŋmei tsei yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa, ni yaa nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ebote shikpɔŋ loo tɛ ni wa mli koni enine ashɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ shɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What can I do to help crops grow better on land where I usually struggle to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni eye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bei pii lɛ mibɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni maná yibii kpakpai lɛ nɔ?

english: You can add organic compost or manure to improve soil fertility, practice mulching to keep moisture in the ground, or switch to hardier crops like palm or cassava that match that specific land type.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo humus afata he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ. Kasemɔ mulching koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko. Aloo tsakemɔ kɛya tsei ni wa tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ lɛ kpãa gbee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does my farm produce green, tall crops on one side but stunted ones on the other side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ miiwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni kɛlɛ yɛ fa kome shi egbɔjɔ yɛ fa kroko lɛ?

english: Land is rarely uniform. Underground rocks, differences in shade, slope, or past farming practices cause moisture and nutrients to sit unevenly across the farm, leading to uneven crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ ŋwɛi, tɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi, hulutsoo, ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi. Aloo, okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni eho lɛ ha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ mli eja yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: Is it a waste of money to plant tree crops like palm on land where food crops refuse to grow?
ga: Ani eji shika fitemɔ akɛ aaadu tsei, tamɔ ŋmei tsei, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii baakwɛ̃ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Not necessarily. Food crops refuse to grow when topsoil is poor or shallow, but tree crops like palms are hardier and can often thrive on land that food crops find unfavorable.
ga: Dabi, niyenii tsei kpooɔ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ehiii loo ekɔɔɔ he eko. Shi tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi amli, tamɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ, wa fe tsutsu lɛ, ni bei pii lɛ amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni niyenii tsei naa akɛ ehiii lɛ nɔ.

english: Should I separate my food crops from my oil palms based on the quality of my land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madamɔ bɔ ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ magbala niyenii ni aduɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmei mli lɛ mli?

english: Yes, that is smart farming. Reserve your deep, moist, and fertile land for shallow-rooted food crops, and use the harder or rockier parts of your land for tough tree crops like oil palm.
ga: Hɛɛ, no ji okwaayeli ni yɔɔ ŋaa. Too shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni efɔ, ni baa nii kɛha niyenii tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni okɛ hei ni wa loo tɛi lɛ atsu nii kɛha tsei ni wa tamɔ mu tso.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize are usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil or waterlogging. Nitrogen is the main food crops use to make green leaves, so when the soil lacks it or when too much water drowns the roots, the plant starves and turns yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu eyi mli obɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ sũ lɛ faaa loo nu fa tsɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Hɔmɔ baaye tso lɛ ni ebaatsɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas have tiny natural organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legume plants decay, they leave this free fertilizer behind for the next crop to feed on.
ga: Nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ tsina ŋmãa mli. Yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji ŋmeii lɛ fite lɛ Amɛshiɔ nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko nɛɛ koni tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ aye.

english: Why do I need to provide tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their broad leaves to catch sunlight and convert it into energy to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground and spreads them out so they can catch maximum sunlight without rotting from ground moisture.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛhe hulu la ni amɛtsake lɛ amɛfee hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking haa baai lɛ woɔ amɛhe nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa bɔni afee ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ ni amɛfiteee kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nu ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers fall off without growing into proper cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔji ni sa lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop off when the tree is stressed by drought, poor soil nutrients, or a lack of midges (tiny insects that pollinate the flowers). Without insect pollination or enough water, the tree drops the flowers to save its own strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hɔmɔ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni haa mɔ he waaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo midges (koolooi bibii ni haa fɔfɔii amli fɔfɔii) ni bɛ kɛji kooloi bibii ni fɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔii amli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ. Tso lɛ hu baashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die during the afternoon even when the soil has moisture?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: This sudden wilting is often caused by bacterial wilt, a soil germ that enters the plant's stems and blocks water channels. Even if water is in the soil, the plant cannot draw it up to its leaves, so it wilts rapidly under the hot afternoon sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni boteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsĩɔ nu gbɛi lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Tso lɛ nyɛŋ agbala lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baa lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, egboɔ oya yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting closely together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites, or viruses spread by sap-sucking insects. As these insects feed on the soft, fresh juice of young leaves, the leaves shrink and curl up unnaturally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni baa mɔ mli ni ŋmeii ni nuɔ nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Enɛ ji akɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ. Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaabɔle amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ.

english: What causes small ragged holes in the leaves of my young maize and tiny dirt inside the central funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The moth lays eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central shoot (funnel) of the plant to feed on fresh foliage, leaving behind droppings that look like saw dust.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmei, ni ji ŋmei ni woɔ ewui yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmei (cone) lɛ mli koni amɛye baai heei. Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmei sũ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots soft-rot under the ground during heavy continuous rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil just as much as water. When heavy rain saturates the ground without draining away, water replaces soil air, causing the roots to drown, decay, and rot under the attack of soil fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ agbɛnɛ hu nu. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Nu baaye kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli, amɛgboiɔ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atuatsemɔ shishi.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry out quickly if I do not plant them immediately after uprooting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji miduuu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni migbala amɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers store a lot of water in their soft corm (base), but when dug up and left exposed to hot sun, they lose moisture rapidly through transpiration. Planting them quickly keeps the corm hydrated so new roots can sprout.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ toɔ nu babaoo yɛ bulb bibioo lɛ mli (shishijee), shi kɛ́ atsa ni ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Efiteɔ nu oya kɛtsɔ nu ni faaa lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu oya lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi heei akwɛ̃.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to grow thin and yield very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ baa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive unwanted guests at a dinner table. They grow faster than crops and steal the soil's fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your main crops have a chance to take what they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbɔi ni ataooo amɛ ni yɔɔ basabasa yɛ gbɛkɛ niyeli okpɔlɔ lɛ nɔ. Amɛdaraa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dani oŋmɔshi nii titri lɛ baaná hegbɛ ni ená nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa lɛ,

english: How can I prepare my soil so that my crops will yield a much bigger harvest this season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ koni miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awo yibii babaoo yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: A heavy yield starts with good land preparation: clear weeds without burning off vital soil nutrients, till the soil so roots can push deep, and mix in organic compost or manure to keep the soil rich and moist throughout the growing season.
ga: Yibiiwoo wuji jeɔ shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ kpakpa: jwɛi ni ajieɔ ni ashãaa niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ashɛre kɛya shɔŋŋ. Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ afutu mli koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do crops on one part of my farm grow tall and healthy while the crops on another part remain stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ fã kome mli lɛ daa ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ fa kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ yaa nɔ egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Soil quality, shade, and water retention vary across different sections of a farm. Adding organic manure to the weaker plots helps balance out nutrients so all your crops grow evenly across every field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su, hulutsoo, kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ ateŋ. Kɛ́ okɛ organic fertilizer fata ŋmɔji ni baanyɛ afee ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ akwɛ̃ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ ŋmɔji lɛ amli.

english: Why do my maize crops grow thin and fail to produce big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli tseee ni ewooo ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to absorb what it needs to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ koni efee tso agbo ni eyi obɔ.

english: Is it good for my crop yield if I grow cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Ani ebaafee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa fee ekome yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving sunlight and soil space for the slower-growing cassava tubers to expand later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi hulutsoo kɛ sũ gbɛ kɛha ŋmei shishifãi ni daa blɛoo lɛ koni amɛmli agbɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my growing crops need fertilizer or extra plant food?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi tsei ni miida lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi loo tsei niyenii?

english: When crops are hungry for nutrients, their lower leaves often turn pale green or yellow, growth slows down, and stems become thin. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure early quickly restores their green vigor.
ga: Be mli ni tsei he hiaa niyenii Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ mlɛo Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ tsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba oya.

english: How do wild weeds hurt the growth and tuber size of my yam plants?
ga: Te koo mli jwɛi miiye mi sweet potato tsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛtuber lɛ awui amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight directly from your crop. If weeds are left unchecked around your yams, the plant loses energy fighting for survival, resulting in small, undersized tubers.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji jwɛi ko bɛ sweet potato lɛ he lɛ, tso lɛ baafite hewalɛ ni ekɛwuuɔ koni ehi shi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, sweet potato lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the afternoon sun even when I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: Strong afternoon heat causes water to evaporate from crop leaves faster than roots can draw it from the soil. Placing dry grass or leaves around the stem as mulch traps moisture in the soil and keeps root zones cool.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe baai amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbala kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛaabɔle Mulch tsei lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i.

english: What causes my pepper crops to drop their flowers before producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi chili pepper tsei lɛ miifo amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when they experience stress from hot dry spells, irregular watering, or attacks by tiny sap-sucking insects. Keeping water levels steady prevents flower fall.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ tutuamɔ Nu ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbee shi.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds saved from my last harvest produce less than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose vigor and disease resistance over time, whereas certified seeds are specifically bred for high growth strength, disease resistance, and higher fruit yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛdara babaoo, helai ni nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe, ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Does trimming lower leaves off my tomato plants help them produce bigger fruits?
ga: Ani kɛ́ afo tomato tsei lɛ ahe baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii wuji?

english: Yes, removing old lower leaves allows air and sunlight to circulate around the main stem, reduces fungal leaf diseases, and forces the crop to direct its energy into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes.
ga: Hɛɛ, baa momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ he, ni ehaa fungal leaf disease lɛ baa shi. ni enyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii koni amɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does rice need so much water compared to crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in flooded or very wet soil because their root system is adapted to absorb nutrients under submerged conditions, which also naturally prevents weeds from choking the crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛnyɛ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ amli. Enɛ tsiɔ jwɛi anaa yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekatsi ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa.

english: Rice grows best on low-lying, flat land with heavy clay soil that holds water well, ideally near a natural water source like a stream, river, or swampy valley bottom.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shikpɔŋ ni mli wa ni nu yɔɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ebɛŋkɛ adebɔɔ mli nu jɛɛhe, tamɔ faa, faa, loo jɔɔ lɛ shishi ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli.

english: Does rice need to stay covered in water all the time until harvest?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni akɛ nu aha ŋmãa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ?

english: No, while rice needs plenty of water while growing and forming grains, you must drain the water off the field a few weeks before harvest so the plants can dry out and mature properly.
ga: Dabi, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa biɔ nu babaoo yɛ be mli ni edaa ni efeɔ dumɔwui lɛ moŋ. Esa akɛ ojie nu ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ otsii fioo komɛi dani okpa ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Koni tsei lɛ agbi ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do some rice plants turn yellow and stop growing shortly after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkpaa dalɛ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing usually means the rice plants are lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, or that the field has dried up too fast and the roots cannot absorb what they need.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmã tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo ŋmɔji lɛ miigbi oya tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nɔ ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: How will using modern machines to plant or harvest help me more than doing it by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsɔnei ni akɛduɔ nii loo nikpamɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi fe bɔ ni mi diɛŋtsɛ mafee lɛ?

english: Machines allow you to prepare land and plant much faster across large areas, helping you take full advantage of the rainy season and reducing the heavy labor needed at harvest time.
ga: Tsɔnei haa onyɛɔ osaa shikpɔŋ ni oduɔ nii yɛ hei wuji oya. Eye ebua bo ni oná nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ he sɛɛ babaoo. ni eba nitsumɔ ni tsii ni he hiaa yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ shi

english: Can modern farming tools help me continue growing crops even during the dry season?
ga: Ani ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli he nibii baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maya nɔ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hɔmɔ be mli po?

english: Yes, using technology like water pumps and simple irrigation channels allows you to bring water from nearby rivers or wells directly to your crops when there is no rainfall.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɔnei tamɔ nu pɔmpii kɛ nu shwiemɔ gbɛi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsɔɔ nu ni jɛɔ faa loo nu bu ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli kɛyaa onibii amli kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ.

english: Will using heavy tractors on my land damage the soil where my crops grow?
ga: Ani trakta ni tsii ni mikɛbaatsu nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baafite shikpɔŋ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If tractors drive over very wet soil, they can press it down too tightly (compaction), which makes it hard for crop roots to push deep down and absorb air and water.
ga: Kɛji traktɔ lɛ nyiɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa nɔ Amɛbaanyɛ amɛmi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ waa (compaction), ni no haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaatsi amɛhe kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu.

english: If a modern farming method works well in another region of Ghana, will it automatically work on my farm?
ga: Kɛji ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ. Ani ebaatsu nii eha miŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Not automatically. Every region has different soil types, rainfall, and temperatures, so it is best to try the new method on a small part of your land first to see how your crops respond.
ga: not automatically Kpokpaa fɛɛ kpokpaa yɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ hulutsoo be srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooka gbɛi heei okwɛ yɛ he bibioo ko. otsei lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ koni ona bɔ ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii amɛhaa.

english: What happens to my crops if the rains stop earlier than expected in the season?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa mra fe bɔ ni akpaa gbɛ yɛ be lɛ mli?

english: Without enough water during crucial growth stages like flowering, crops get stressed, produce smaller or hollow grains, and may dry up early unless you can irrigate them.
ga: Kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ yɛ dalɛ bei titrii tamɔ fɔfɔii amli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii bafeɔ nɔ ni haoɔ. Ewoɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bibii loo ni mli ewo muji. ni ebaanyɛ egbi oya. Ja obaanyɛ okɛ nu awo mli.

english: Why is it important to level my field flat before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afee shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Leveling your field ensures that water spreads evenly across all your crops, preventing water from pooling too deep in some spots while leaving other spots dry.
ga: He ni oyɔɔ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ haa nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa onibii fɛɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haaa nu lɛ abua ehe naa tsɔ yɛ hei komɛi, yɛ be mli ni ehaa hei krokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide quick shade to shield the young cocoa plants and keep the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni shwereɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo oya koni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni eha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: When crops are crowded, they compete for sunlight, water, and nutrients. Giving maize plants proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food to build strong stems and big cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the growing stage helps keep the foliage green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛmɔ be lɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhiɛ ahi amɛhe nɔ.

english: Why does my land yield less food every year even though I work it the same way?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii faaa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mitsuɔ nitsumɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Crops remove nutrients from the soil each harvest. If you continuously plant the same crop without adding organic matter or rotating with leguminous crops like beans, the soil loses its natural fertility.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakpa. Kɛji akɛ oya nɔ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii tsakeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my yam vines growing thick green leaves while the tubers underground stay very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni eshishifãi lɛ bibii waa lolo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen makes plants put all their growth into leaves instead of roots. Yams need balanced nutrients and higher potassium levels to direct their energy into building large underground tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tsei woɔ baai yɛ shishifãi najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja kɛ potassium ni fa babaoo he miihia sweet potato koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji lɛ aba.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with dark dirt left inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi gbekɛ ŋmãa baai ni muji diŋŋ ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying approved organic extracts like neem solution early inside the leaf whorl helps manage them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ wala mli ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli tamɔ neem tsofa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Baai lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akwɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids or whiteflies that transmit plant viruses. Spraying plants with neem water or soapy solutions reduces these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem nu loo samla shwie tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when left in standing water because waterlogged soil starves the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience severe heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying dry grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ po ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ he ni ebɔle he lɛ mli lɛ mli egbi. Shishitoo lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Fertilizer works best when plants are actively growing, usually two to three weeks after sprouted leaves appear. Applying fertilizer during heavy rain washes it away, so apply it when the soil is damp but not flooded.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida waa. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ beni baai ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ eje kpo lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaafɔ ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛwo nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nu ehiɛɛɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my maize turning yellow instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients too deep into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Yams feed heavily on soil nutrients. Planting them on the same piece of land continuously drains the earth of essential food, causing the soil to become exhausted so new plants cannot build large tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. fiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ Tsei heei nyɛŋ afee bulbs wuji.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast with large leaves that create living shade, keeping the soil cool and moist so the cocoa can survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni haa hulutsoo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni kookoo lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ebatsɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience temperature stress or dry soil. When conditions get too hot or dry, the plant sheds its flowers to save water and energy just to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo egbi lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛhi wala mli kɛkɛ.

english: How do I know if my harvested ginger is good enough quality to sell for export?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ginger ni mikpa lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ kɛya maŋsɛɛ?

english: Export-quality ginger must be fully mature, firm, clean, and free from mold, insect holes, or skin scratches. Proper washing and careful drying after harvest prevent rot during shipping.
ga: Esa akɛ ginger ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ eda kwraa, efee shiŋŋ, ehe atse, ni ebɛ muji, kooloi ahewolo loo ŋmei yɛ hewolo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ he jogbaŋŋ ni agbi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akafite yɛ be mli ni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain bunches stay so small compared to other farms around me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ ji bibioo kwraa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji krokomɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Plantain bunches remain small if too many suckers are left growing around the main stalk. The suckers steal food and water from the main tree, reducing the size of the fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains baafee bibii lolo kɛji akɛ ŋmeii komɛi eshwɛ yɛ amɛhe. Tso wulu lɛ babaoo Suckers juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso wulu lɛ mli. Enɛ haa aduawai akuu lɛ dalɛ baa shi.

english: How can I tell if the ground is ready for planting cassava after the first rain falls?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakwɛ ŋmei yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until several steady rains have soaked deep into the ground. Planting after just one light rain leaves stem cuttings vulnerable to rotting or drying out if a dry spell immediately follows.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ sɛɛ shikome pɛ Niji yɛ oshara mli akɛ amɛbaafite loo amɛbaagbi kɛji akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato stems wilt in the heat of the day even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Why do tomato stems wither in hot weather? Ani nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt disease. Bacteria block the water tubes inside the stem, preventing the plant from pulling water up from the roots to the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ sũ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Muawai tsiɔ nu paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ anaa. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkagbala nu kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛyashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce high yields only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest will lose their special strength, producing uneven plants and much lower yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ amɛ hewalɛ krɛdɛɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ekome ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kwraa.

english: Why does having weeds near my cassava plants reduce the size of the roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ masɛi lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds compete aggressively with cassava for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. When weeds take those resources, the cassava plant cannot produce enough food energy to send down to swell its underground roots.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ jwɛi ye nakai nibii lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ aya koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why are insects eating the leaves of my crops, and how does this affect my harvest?
ga: Why are insects eating the leaves of my crops? Ni te enɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Insects feed on crop leaves to survive, but leaves act as the crop's factory for making food. When pests destroy the leaves, the crop starves and cannot produce fruits or pods properly, which is why applying targeted pest control like Akate drives pests away and protects your crop yields.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ tsei ahe baai koni amɛhi shi. Shi baai lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii afeemɔ he. Kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kpata baai lɛ ahiɛ lɛ Hɔmɔ baaye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni enyɛŋ ewo yibii loo ŋmeii ni sa. Nɔ ni hewɔ ni kɛ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ tamɔ Akate tsu nii lɛ, eshwieɔ ŋmeii kɛyaa he kroko ni ebuɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ.

english: What causes pests to suddenly attack my farm even when I water and care for my crops well?
ga: Mɛni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli trukaa eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli ni mikwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ moŋ?

english: Pests are naturally drawn to healthy, green crops as a source of food and shelter, especially during seasonal changes. Routine farm care keeps crops growing, but dedicated pest protection is needed to drive away insects that come to feed on them.
ga: Kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai gbalaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ akɛ niyenii kɛ wɔɔhe jɛɛhe. Titri lɛ, yɛ be mli ni be tsakeɔ lɛ. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ daa yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii daa. Shi ehe miihia ni abu kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ koni akɛshwie kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ.

english: How do pest control sprays actually work to protect my crops from insect damage?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii ehaa tɛŋŋ koni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ahe?

english: Pest control solutions work by either repelling nuisance insects or eliminating them when they attempt to feed on the plant. This keeps the environment around your crops clear so your farm work can proceed smoothly without constant pest disturbance.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni amɛshwieɔ loo amɛjieɔ amɛ kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye tsei lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shihilɛ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ Oŋmɔshi nibii amli tse. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe wooo mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Is it normal for my crop leaves to curl up and turn yellow when tiny bugs gather under them?
ga: Ani eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ baabɔle amɛhe ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔŋ yɛ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ahiɛ? abua amɛhe naa yɛ shishi

english: Yes, small insects suck the vital juices directly from the leaves, causing them to curl, turn yellow, and lose strength. Treating your farm with an effective pest control product stops these bugs from draining your crops' essential food supply.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii nuɔ nu ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. ha amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfite hewalɛ Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tsu oŋmɔ lɛ he nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite niyenii ni he hiaa ni okɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce fewer fruits when insects keep disturbing them during flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ kooloi bibii ba amɛnɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: When insects attack crops, the plants waste their energy trying to heal damage instead of forming flowers and fruits. Getting rid of the pests allows the plant to focus all its energy on producing a full, healthy harvest.
ga: Beni kooloi bibii tutuaa ŋmɔshi nibii Tsei fiteɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsa nɔ ni efite lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbaafee lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do I feel completely exhausted and lack strength every time I return home from working on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ be fɛɛ be ni majɛ ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ miba shia lɛ, etɔ mi ni etɔ mi lɛ?

english: Farm activities like weeding, carrying heavy loads, and spraying under the hot sun drain your body's energy and fluids rapidly. Taking restorative health products like 'Adom' helps replenish your missing strength so you can recover after a long day of farm labor.
ga: Okwaafoi anitsumɔi tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ Nibii ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi shwiemɔ Ehaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu lɛ hoɔ oya. Hewalɛ nibii ni ayeɔ kɛha gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ tamɔ ‘Adom’ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ baa ekoŋŋ. Koni eye ebua bo ni oná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ gbi nitsumɔ ni wa ni otsu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How does my physical tiredness affect how well I can care for my crops?
ga: Te migbɔmɔtsoŋ tɔlɛ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: When you lack bodily strength, essential farm tasks like weeding, watering, and monitoring for pests get delayed. Maintaining your personal health and energy ensures you have the physical stamina needed to complete all farm work on time.
ga: Beni obɛ gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔi ni he hiaa tamɔ jwɛi shwiemɔ, nu ni akɛhaa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ akwɛmɔ hu baahe sɛɛ. Ohewalɛ kɛ ohewalɛ ni oookwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha oná gbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni onyɛ ogbe ŋmɔ mli nitsumɔi fɛɛ anaa yɛ be naa.

english: Why does carrying heavy farm equipment cause my body and back to ache so much in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaawo okwaayeli he nibii ni tsii lɛ? Koni eha ogbɔmɔtso kɛ osɛɛ afee bo shoo waa gbɛkɛ?

english: Carrying heavy equipment like knapsack sprayers puts continuous strain on your muscles and back. Resting properly and using health tonics like 'Adom' helps soothe tired muscles and rebuild bodily strength for the next work day.
ga: Nibii ni tsii tamɔ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ ni ooohiɛ Ebaaha fãji kɛ sɛɛ mli fãji lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be. Hejɔɔmɔ ni sa kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he tsofai tamɔ ‘Adom’ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fãji ni etɔ lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni ehaa hewalɛ hee kɛha nitsumɔ gbi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What should I do when the sun makes me lose strength quickly while working in the field?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ hulu lɛ miigbɔjɔ mi oya beni mitsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Working in intense sun causes dehydration and rapid physical burn-out. Taking regular breaks in the shade, drinking plenty of water, and using strength-restoring supplements helps maintain your stamina throughout the working day.
ga: Nitsumɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa mli lɛ baanyɛ aha nu agbɔjɔ mɔ mli oya ni etɔ lɛ. Hejɔɔmɔ ni afeɔ daa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nuɔ nu babaoo Ni kɛ hewalɛwoo nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua bo ni oná hewalɛ yɛ onitsumɔ gbi lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is taking care of my physical health just as important as taking care of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ migbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ nɔkwɛmɔ he hiaa tamɔ bɔ ni migbɔmɔtsoŋ hewalɛnamɔ nɔkwɛmɔ he hiaa lɛ lɛ? With taking care of my crops?

english: Your farm relies entirely on your body's power to plant, manage pests, and harvest. If physical weakness prevents you from working, your crops suffer from neglect, making your health the most important tool on the farm.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ damɔ ogbɔmɔtso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nɔkwɛmɔ Kɛji gbɔmɔtsoŋ bɔjɔmɔ tsi bo gbɛ ni okɛtsu nii Abaaku hiɛ ashwie oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Ha ohewalɛ afee dɛŋdade ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: How many maize seeds should I drop into a single planting hole?
ga: Abele dumɔwui enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛwo dumɔ bu kome mli?

english: You should plant at most two or three seeds per hole. Putting more seeds in one spot causes overcrowding, making the plants fight for food and resulting in weak crops.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ odu dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ bu kome mli. Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ he kome lɛ haa mɛi ayiɔ obɔ fe nine. Enɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii he akaŋ ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ.

english: If I plant a large handful of maize seeds in one spot, won't I get a bigger harvest from that area?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui fioo ko yɛ he kome lɛ, Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛjɛ nakai he lɛ?

english: No, planting too many seeds in one spot creates severe overcrowding. The plants will strangle each other fighting for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving you with weak stalks and very small yield.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui babaoo ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha mɛi ayi obɔ waa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa.

english: What is the maximum number of corn seeds I should put in one hole during planting?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni fa fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mikɛwo bu kome mli yɛ dumɔ be mli?

english: The maximum is three seeds per hole. Keeping it to two or three ensures that every sprout gets enough space, soil nutrients, and water to grow strong cobs.
ga: Nɔ ni fa fe fɛɛ ji dumɔwui etɛ yɛ bu kome mli. Ha fioo komɛi ahi shi koni dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu aná he ko. niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmei lɛ adara waa.

english: Why do my crops look tall, thin, and fragile when they grow close together in a clump?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni kɛlɛ, eyɛ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ kui amli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely in one place, they overcrowd each other. They stretch upward fighting for sunlight while starving for soil nutrients below, making them thin and weak.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ he kome tsɔ lɛ Abaawo dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ. Amɛkpãa amɛhe ni amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ koni amɛná niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ

english: Is it good to save land by planting my crop seeds tightly together in fewer holes?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaato he ko he gbɛjianɔ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ jogbaŋŋ ni bu fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ?

english: No, crowding seeds into fewer holes hurts your harvest. Crops need space for their roots to spread and draw enough nourishment from the soil without competing with too many neighboring seeds.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui fioo komɛi ni oookɛwo bu lɛ mli lɛ baafite onibii lɛ. He ko he miihia tsei koni amɛshishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛgbala niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akaŋshii babaoo bɛ mli kɛha dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from overcrowding on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miihe afee shoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Overcrowded crops usually grow in dense clumps with thin, yellowish stalks that struggle to stand strong or produce heavy cobs because they lack enough nutrients.
ga: Tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ daa yɛ kui ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni ehi shi shiŋŋ loo ewo cob ni tsii yɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni bɛ hewɔ

english: Why do I need to follow a proper plan when planting seeds on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni manyiɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa sɛɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Having a clear planting plan helps you space your crops correctly, which prevents overcrowding and makes sure every plant gets its fair share of sunlight, water, and nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ oyɛ dumɔwui ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni mli ka shi faŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebua bo ni otoɔ he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa tsei lɛ ayi obɔ fe nine ni ehaa tsei fɛɛ naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa.

english: What does an extension officer mean when speaking about 'appropriate agriculture' for crop planting?
ga: Nɔyaa he nitsulɔi kɛ amɛmiiwie Mɛni ‘kwaayeli ni sa’ tsɔɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ?

english: It means following proper farming practices suited to your crop, such as measuring crop spacing correctly and putting only the recommended number of seeds per hole.
ga: Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ onyiɛ okwaayeli nifeemɔi ni sa ni sa kɛha onibii lɛ asɛɛ, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni ooosusu jogbaŋŋ. ni akɛ dumɔwui ayibɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ awo bu kome mli lɛ pɛ afata he.

english: How does keeping proper distance between crop holes help my food grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni sa ni kã dumɔ bui lɛ ateŋ lɛ baaye abua mi niyenii lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper distance prevents roots from competing with each other for ground food, allowing every crop to grow full and healthy without being choked out by nearby plants.
ga: He ni akɛtoɔ he ni sa lɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye niyenii ni atswa lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tsiii amɛ gbɛ.

english: What should I do if I accidentally dropped too many seeds into one hole while planting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo shwie bu kome mli yɛ oshara mli beni miduɔ nii lɛ?

english: Once the seeds sprout, you should carefully thin them out by removing the extra seedlings until only two or three healthy sprouts remain in that hole to prevent overcrowding.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ, esa akɛ ogbala dumɔwui lɛ blɛoo kɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ooojie lɛ nɔ. Kɛyashi dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ 2-3 pɛ eshwɛ yɛ bu lɛ mli koni dumɔwui babaoo akakwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the soil or when the soil stays waterlogged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi ni nu eyi mli obɔ.

english: Will planting cowpeas or beans in the same field as my maize steal nutrients from the maize?
ga: Ani tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, planting legumes like beans actually helps your maize. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and release it into the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer that helps maize grow better.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni ooodu tamɔ ŋmeii yeɔ ebuaa o-corn lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer so that heavy rain does not wash it away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akashwie nɔ?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a light rain, rather than right before a heavy rainstorm. Burying the fertilizer slightly near the plant roots and covering it with soil also prevents rain from washing it away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ Kɛ́ ooofu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fioo yɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nugbɔ akashwie lɛ.

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil. It is usually triggered by irregular watering or sudden dry spells during fruit development.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like mites, thrips, or aphids, or a virus transmitted by these insects. These pests feed on plant sap, causing the new leaves to grow deformed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, thrips, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ baa. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ yeɔ tsei amli nu. Enɛ haa baai heei lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ejaaa.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves during the dry season, and does it mean they are dead?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ? Ni ani no tsɔɔ akɛ egbo?

english: Your cassava plants are not dead; shedding leaves is their natural way of saving water and surviving the heat. The plants will quickly grow fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: O-cassava tso lɛ gbooo lolo. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ nu he ni ehiɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli. Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba ekoŋŋ.
