english: My cocoa trees produce plenty of flowers, but why do most of them fall off without growing into cocoa pods?
ga: Mikoo tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: It is normal for a cocoa tree to drop flowers it cannot support. However, excessive flower drop is often caused by water stress, poor shade management, or a lack of small insects needed to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Eji nɔ ni yaa nɔ akɛ cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye amɛbua lɛ anɔ. Shi, bei pii lɛ, nu mli haomɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi fe nine lɛ baa. hulutsoo be ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why do I need to spend time putting stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite be kɛwo tsei anɔ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to manufacture food, which travels down to build larger and heavier yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ bɔni afee ni amɛbaa lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Hulu la haa baai lɛ woɔ niyenii. ni fãa gbɛ kɛyaa shi koni efee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii

english: If I plant my maize seeds very deep in the soil, will it protect them from drying out when the rain delays?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ waa Ani abaatsi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ?

english: Planting too deep makes it difficult for the seedling to break through the surface, and the seed may die before reaching the light. It is best to plant about 3 to 5 centimeters deep in moist soil.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha dumɔwui lɛ akɛ amɛaabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ agbo dani amɛshɛ la lɛ he. Esa akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ aaafee sɛntimitai 3 kɛyashi 5 mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow thin and weak even when I plant good seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kpakpai moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal essential sunlight, soil water, and nutrients away from your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can a sick coconut tree be cured, or do I have to cut it down immediately?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ atsa ŋmei tso ni hela mɔ lɛ loo esa akɛ afo lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Many coconut diseases can be treated if caught early. Applying the right treatments and improving soil nutrients can help the tree recover fully without needing to cut it down.
ga: Abaanyɛ atsa ŋmei helai babaoo kɛji ana amɛ mra. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni sa tsu nii ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ aya nɔ kwraa ni ehe ehiaaa ni afo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my coconut tree turning yellow and dropping early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmeii tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves can be caused by plant diseases or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Treating the plant with proper nutrients and checking for signs of disease can help restore its green color and health.
ga: Tso hela loo niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha baai ŋmɔŋ aba. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni sa tsu tsei ahe nii, ni akwɛ kɛji hela ko yɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni amɛná su ni ji eŋɔli kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will my coconut tree produce fruits again after recovering from a disease?
ga: Ani akoko tso lɛ baaná hewalɛ kɛjɛ hela lɛ mli ni ewo yibii ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, once a coconut tree recovers from a disease and receives proper food and care, it will grow fresh leaves and resume producing healthy coconuts.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji ŋmei tso lɛ he wa kɛjɛ hela mli ni enine eshɛ niyenii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ pɛ. Kokoo tso lɛ baakwɛ baai heei ni eku esɛɛ ebawo kooko ni hi jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Are there really pests that can destroy my entire coconut farm?
ga: Ani tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ akpata mi-kokoo tso muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ lɛ yɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, severe pests like the rhinoceros beetle can cause 100% damage to a farm if left unchecked. Regular farm inspection and early control methods are essential to prevent complete loss.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hiɛdɔɔ tamɔ rhinoceros ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔ ko 100% kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Okwaafoi akwɛmɔ daa kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ mra Enɛ he miihia koni akafite kwraa.

english: How can I tell if my crop problem is caused by a pest or a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai kɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe naagbai lɛ baa?

english: Pests usually leave physical marks like chewed leaves, holes, or visible insects, whereas diseases often cause discoloration, wilting, or rotting across the plant without obvious insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, bu, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ tso lɛ su tsakeɔ, egbɔjɔɔ, loo egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli fɛɛ ni kooloi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ bɛ mli.

english: What simple step can I take to stop pests from spreading across my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo mafee koni matsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Regularly cleaning your farm, clearing away rotting logs where pests breed, and removing heavily infested plant parts will help prevent pests from moving to healthy trees.
ga: Oŋmɔ lɛ mli saamɔ daa Tsoi ni egboi ni ji he ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ lɛ ahe saamɔ kɛ tsei ni ŋmeii emɔ amɛ waa lɛ fãi komɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii lɛ akaya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ.

english: How does applying fertilizer help my crops resist pests and diseases?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi tsei lɛ ni amɛte shi amɛwo tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai?

english: Fertilizer supplies key nutrients that strengthen the plant's natural defense system, making it tougher for diseases to take hold and for pests to cause severe damage.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso mli lɛ haa niyenii titrii ni wajeɔ tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa helai akɛ amɛaahi shi, ni tsɛŋemɔ helai hu baafite nii waa.

english: Can poor soil quality make my coconut trees get sick more easily?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei tsei lɛ aná helai oya?

english: Yes, crops growing in weak soil lack essential nutrients, making them weak and vulnerable to diseases and pest attacks that healthy plants could normally survive.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi lɛ baanyɛ atswa amɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to apply fertilizer to my coconut trees?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmei tsei amli ŋmei?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer during the rainy season when the soil is wet, as moisture helps the tree roots absorb the nutrients quickly and effectively.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli, be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ yeɔ ebuaa tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Is it better to use animal manure or chemical fertilizer for my coconut trees?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmei mli lɛ baatsu nii kɛha ŋmei tsei?

english: Both are beneficial; manure improves soil structure and retains moisture, while chemical fertilizers deliver quick nutrients. Combining both often gives your crop the best protection and yield.
ga: Enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ. Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ fata he lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ buɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibiiwoo.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants keep drying up when I clear all the big trees off my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from direct, harsh sunlight. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains or forest trees keeps the soil cool and moist so the young cocoa seedlings can survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsei ni ajieɔ loo aduɔ koni ekɛha hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo koo mli tsei Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ bɔni afee ni cacao tsei bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that water is standing around the roots for too long. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plants regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eta shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: What is eating small holes inside the leaves of my corn plants early in the season?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Those holes are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Checking your corn fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract can protect your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nakai bu lɛ baa. Abɛi ŋmɔji amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods without good drainage. Planting your cassava on raised earth mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up high to catch full sunlight, which helps the crop produce larger tubers under the ground. Staking also keeps leaves off the damp soil, reducing disease.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni helai baa shi.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever strong wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baatswa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that can be weakened by microscopic soil worms called nematodes or stem borers. Supporting heavy bunches with wooden poles and using clean planting suckers prevents them from uprooting.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ, ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo stem borers lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛgbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni tsii fiɔ tsei niji ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ, ni akɛ nu ni mli tse tsuɔ nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Curling leaves are often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites that suck the plant's juices and transmit viruses. Spraying neem water or insecticidal soap early helps control these pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. ni shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni ekɛ helai baa Neem nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi amli mra Ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get extremely high or when the soil dries out completely. Consistent watering at the base of the plant and providing light shade helps the flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli tse lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why do older farmers recommend planting cowpeas or groundnuts on the same field with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni aduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil for maize and improves future harvests.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa ŋmãa ni ehaa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmãa lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: How can I stop weeds from taking over my garden without spending money on chemical sprays?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi jwɛi ni yeɔ mibɔɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ naa ni mikɛ shika tsuuu tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ ahe nii?

english: Covering the bare soil around your crops with dry grass, leaves, or cocoa pods (a method called mulching) blocks light from reaching weed seeds while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ni okɛbaabɔle ohe lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo kookoo ŋmɔtɔi (gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ mulching) ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ, ebaatsi la naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my maize crops turn yellow and look weak even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Maize plants need nutrient 'food' like nitrogen from the soil to stay green and strong. Rain provides water, but if the soil lacks nutrients, the plants cannot generate enough energy to grow properly, causing their leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Abɛi tsei he miihia ‘niyenii’ ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔŋ mli ni amɛná hewalɛ. Nugbɔ haa nu, shi kɛji akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does adding rotten manure or compost to my farm make my crops perform better over time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni egboi wo miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Compost and manure act like long-term energy reserves in the soil. They break down slowly, releasing steady food for crop roots over months while helping the soil hold onto water during dry weather.
ga: Kompost kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii akɛ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. Amɛfiteɔ fiofio. Eshiɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ kɛhaa tso shishifãi nyɔji babaoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: How does chemical fertilizer give my crops a fast boost in growth?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated plant food that dissolves quickly in soil moisture. Crop roots take it in immediately, giving the plant a sudden surge of energy to grow leaves and fruits faster.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ji tsei niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ ni shwieɔ oya yɛ sũ mli nu mli. Tso shishifãi baaŋɔ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ trukaa koni ekwɛ baai kɛ aduawai oya.

english: Why does cassava stay alive underground for a long time even when dry weather destroys other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii hiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi be kakadaŋŋ nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ gbeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi moŋ?

english: Cassava roots act like a stored energy tank deep underground. When there is a drought, the plant slows down its leaf growth and relies on the energy and water saved in its tuberous roots to survive.
ga: Cassava shishifãi tsuɔ nii tamɔ hewalɛ ni akɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ. Kɛji hɔmɔ ba lɛ Tsei haa baai lɛ daraa fioo ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ hewalɛ kɛ nu ni ato yɛ amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun and then stand up straight again in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane latsaa mli, ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, crops lose water faster than their roots can drink it. Drooping is the crop's defense trick to save energy and water; overnight, the roots catch up with water intake, restoring the leaves by morning.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Drooping ji teemɔŋ sane ko ni akɛbuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni akɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Gbi gbɛkɛ mli lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baaŋɔ nu lɛ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba leebi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees lose their leaves when all the big wild trees around them are cut down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ baai lɛ shwie shi beni afo tsei ni eda ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need shade because direct, harsh sunlight drains their moisture and energy too quickly. Without shade trees acting as a protective barrier, the heat stresses the cocoa trees, causing them to drop their leaves.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛnáa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ oya tsɔ. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, tsu nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Dɔlɛ lɛ haa kookoo tso lɛ haoɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my plants give smaller yields when I plant them too close to each other on the plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ wooo yibii fioo kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ saatso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Every crop needs its own border or space to collect sunlight and draw energy from the soil. When planted too close together, their roots fight over the same food and water, leaving all the plants weak.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ fɛɛ he miihia lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe husu loo he ko ni ekɛbua hulu la naa ni ejie hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ nu kome he akaŋshii mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei fɛɛ bɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it recommended to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of nutrient energy out of the ground. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, restoring the energy reserve for the next crop you plant.
ga: Abɛi heɔ e-nutrient hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. koni okɛ hewalɛ ni ato kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ aku sɛɛ aba

english: Why do hybrid seeds bought from agricultural suppliers grow stronger than seeds I saved from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni akɛ tsofai ebɔ he ni mihe kɛjɛ okwaayeli he nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ shwere waa fe dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Commercial hybrid seeds are specifically bred to have high vigor and fast growth energy. Saved seeds naturally lose strength over generations, resulting in weaker plants and lower yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ jarayeli dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaadara oya. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi.

english: When is the right time to give my rice crops extra fertilizer during their growth?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi aha ŋmãa tsei lɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Rice needs extra plant food right before it starts producing flower heads and grains. Adding fertilizer at this specific stage directs all the new energy straight into forming large, heavy rice grains.
ga: Omɔ he miihia tso niyenii krokomɛi dani ebɔi fɔfɔi ayitsei kɛ dumɔwui feemɔ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛ nɛkɛ be pɔtɛɛ nɛɛ mli lɛ kudɔɔ hewalɛ hee lɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋmaa agbo ni tsii lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Beni kookoo tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enyɛɔ enáa hulu la lɛ fɛɛ lɛ,.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key soil nutrient, or the soil has too much trapped water that is stopping the roots from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing center of maize plants and eat tender leaves, reducing your eventual harvest if not treated early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ baaha onibii lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ atsaaa lɛ mra.

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings have small growth buds that must point upwards toward the sky; planting them upside down forces the shoots to grow downwards first, causing weak plants and low yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii ni afo lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii. ni esa akɛ etsɔɔ ŋwɛi Dumɔ ni akɛ ŋwɛi shishi lɛ baaha ŋmeii lɛ akwɛ̃ kɛya shishi klɛŋklɛŋ. Ehaa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Why do I need to clear tall bushes and put up sticks for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei bibii ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni mato tsei aniji koni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to produce big tubers underground, and lifting the leaves off the damp ground prevents leaf diseases while maximizing sunlight exposure.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Ni kɛ́ owó baai anɔ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ, ebaatsi baa hela naa yɛ be mli ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baa.

english: Fertilizer is very strong and can burn the soft skin and roots of your crop if placed directly on the stem. Placing it a short distance away in the soil lets the roots safely drink the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli wa waa, ni ebaanyɛ eshã tsei ahewolo ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi kɛji akɛ akɛwo tsei lɛ ashishifã lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ni akɛaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kukuoo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why is it good for my land if I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on a plot after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize takes away heavy nutrients from the soil, but leguminous crops like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii ni tsii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their blossoms without giving me any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miikwɛ ni ekɛ tomato ko kwraa wooo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the heat gets too intense, when water supply goes from very wet to very dry too quickly, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like calcium to support fruit growth.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji la lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni jɛɔ pɔmpi mli lɛ tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ waa mli kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ oya tsɔ loo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ.

english: Covering soil with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating water out of the earth, keeps soil temperatures cool, and blocks weeds from growing around your plants.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ akajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i lɛ afee fɛ̃i. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ otsei lɛ ahe lɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if the ground has enough water to safely sow my seeds after the first rain of the season?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ shweshweeshwe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Squeeze a handful of topsoil into a ball; if it holds together loosely without dripping excess water and crumbles easily when poked, the soil has the right moisture for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ fioo ko ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛ he mlɛo Ekɛ nu ni fa fe nine shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sũ lɛ yɛ nu ni sa bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die whenever the harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be ni harmattan be lɛ baaje shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong sun and dry harmattan winds because their roots are shallow. Planting plantains or shade trees alongside young cocoa provides moisture and shields them from scorching dry heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ kookoo bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo aya hiɛ ni ebaabu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni mli edɔ ni shãa mɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does my cassava crop rot under the ground when there is too much rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need breathable soil; when water sits on the field without draining, the roots drown from lack of air, allowing fungus to grow and rot the tubers. Mounding soil into ridges helps excess rain drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mumɔ baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Beni nu yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ gbee shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaabɔ he ni efee ŋmeii lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: Plants are like children sharing a single plate of food; if planted too close, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow thick stems and healthy yields.
ga: Tsei tamɔ gbekɛbii. Niyenii kome ni ajaa Kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaaye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ tsei ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take longer to bear fruit if I don't cut off the extra shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii kɛji mifolɔɔɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ?

english: Extra suckers attached to the main plantain tree steal water and food from the mother plant. Removing all but one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem receives enough energy to produce heavy bunches quickly.
ga: Tsoi bibii krokomɛi ni kpɛtɛɔ dumɔwu wulu lɛ he lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Ajieɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa lɛ fɛɛ, ja ekome loo enyɔ pɛ. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tso ni tsii oya.

english: Why did my crops burn and dry up after I put fertilizer right next to their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Chemical fertilizers contain concentrated salts that draw water out of plant stems and roots if placed directly against them. Fertilizer should be applied a few inches away from the stem in a ring so the roots can safely absorb it.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli kɛji akɛ akɛwo mli tɛ̃ɛ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli inchii fioo komɛi kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key food plants use to build green leaves and grow big. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer restores the green color and helps the plant produce grain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo dumɔwui.

english: Why do weeds grow back faster than my crops even after I cleared the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds lie buried in the soil for a long time and quickly sprout as soon as clearing exposes them to rain and sun. Mulching with dry leaves or clearing weeds before they produce seeds helps slow down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji nugbɔ kɛ hulu la shɛ shikpɔŋ ni atse lɛ nɔ pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egboi wo nɔ loo jwɛi ni ajieɔ dani amɛyaa dumɔwui amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ekwɛ̃ fioo.

english: Extreme heat, lack of water, or insect damage can stress tomato plants, causing them to drop flowers to save energy. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the plant hold onto its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why don't the seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize give me as much food as the original packaged seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haaa mi niyenii babaoo tamɔ shishijee dumɔwui ni akɛwo kotoku mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields only in their first planting. The seeds saved from that harvest lose those special combined traits, leading to smaller harvests and uneven crop growth.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ dumɔwui lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ sui ni haa amɛfeɔ ekome lɛ. Enɛ haa kpamɔ bibioo kɛ tsei adalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and turning soft in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni akpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ ni efee blɛoo yɛ mi-ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams are living tubers that wake up and sprout when stored in warm, poorly ventilated spaces. Storing them on raised bamboo racks in cool, well-shaded, and airy barns keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Atomɔ ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka. ni baate shi ni ebaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Okɛwo ŋmei ŋtayaai anɔ yɛ ŋtayaa he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do I see so many insect pests on my farm during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa ŋmeii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Insect pests thrive in warm weather because heat speeds up their growth and activity, making hot places ideal environments for them to settle and feed on your crops.
ga: Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔŋ mli edɔ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, dɔlɛ haa edalɛ kɛ nitsumɔ yaa oya. Ha hei ni mli edɔ lɛ afee he ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛye oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does it seem like pest insects double in number on my tomato plants overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ayibɔ etee hiɛ shii enyɔ yɛ nyɔɔŋ kome mli lɛ?

english: Many crop pests multiply very quickly when conditions are warm, laying hundreds of eggs that hatch in just a few days and creating huge infestations in a short time.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui babaoo lɛ faa oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ. Amɛwoɔ wɔji ohai abɔ ni amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli. ni ekɛ hela babaoo baa yɛ be kukuoo mli

english: Why do my harvested grains get full of small insects when stored in a warm shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ eyi kɛ kooloi bibii lɛ? Beni akɛtoɔ tsũ ko ni mli edɔ mli?

english: Warm, closed storage spaces create an ideal home for pests like grain weevils, which quickly multiply inside bags if the grain is not treated or properly dried.
ga: He ko ni mli edɔ ni aŋã ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ feɔ shia ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmaa ŋmeii, ni amɛshwereɔ oya yɛ kotokui amli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ loo agbiee amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I stop termites and bugs from nesting in the wooden stakes I use for my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmeii kɛ kooloi krokomɛi anaa koni amɛkafee amɛ ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni mikɛfeɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ amli?

english: Insects like to settle inside warm, untreated wood. Treating the wooden stakes with approved wood preservatives or insecticides before planting prevents pests from building homes in them.
ga: Kplukai sumɔɔ ni amɛhi tso ni mli edɔ ni asaaa he lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akɛbuɔ tso he loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu tso tsei ahe nii dani adu lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kooloi ni yeɔ kooloi lɛ akafee shĩai yɛ nakai tsei lɛ amli.

english: Is there a pest medicine I can spray on my seedbed soil before planting to keep insects away?
ga: Ani tsofa ko yɛ ni manyɛ makɛshwie dumɔwui lɛ ashikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu koni mikɛshwie kooloi?

english: Yes, applying soil-drench insecticides or heat-treating nursery soil before sowing creates a protective barrier that stops pests from settling in the soil and attacking young seedlings.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ dani adu lɛ, ehaa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsiɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkabote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛtutuaa tsei bibii lɛ.

english: Why are tiny white bugs sticking tightly under my cassava leaves and not leaving?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ Kpɛtɛɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ashishi waa ni amɛlaajeŋ lɛ?

english: Insects like mealybugs seek sheltered, warm spots under leaves where they attach themselves, feed on plant sap, and build protective coatings so they are hard to shake off.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs naa wɔɔhe kɛ hulutsoo yɛ baai lɛ ashishi he ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ amɛhe yɛ lɛ, amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛfeɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ amɛhe ni haa ewaa kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛbaajie amɛhe.

english: How can I stop crop insects from constantly crawling on me while I weed my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa tsei amli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ mihe be fɛɛ be be mli ni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When weed growth gets thick, pests nest in large numbers; clearing weeds early and applying targeted sprays keeps pest populations low so they do not swarm onto you while you work.
ga: Kɛ jwɛi lɛ dara lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee shĩai babaoo. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni jwɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ akafee nɔ ni baa shi. Enɛ baaha amɛkabote ohe beni otsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do soil grubs seem to stay right around the top layer of earth where my crops grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yiteŋgbɛ he ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ?

english: The top layer of soil stays warm from sunlight and contains roots to eat, making it the preferred place for soil pests to live and multiply close to the surface.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baaha hulu lɛ adɔ ni eha shishifãi ni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ haa efeɔ he ko ni kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ waa akɛ amɛhi shi ni amɛfɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Can I treat the wooden frames of my vegetable green nursery so insects stop hiding in the corners?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso ni akɛwoɔ mi-green vegetable nursery lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii koni kooloi akatee amɛhe yɛ koŋji lɛ amli?

english: Applying an approved chemical mixture to wooden frames creates a barrier that prevents pests from making homes in the cracks and corners of your nursery structures.
ga: Tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ tso ni yɔɔ odaseyeli mli lɛ ni okɛwoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ feɔ gbɛtsii nii ko ni tsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee shĩai yɛ o-greenhouse lɛ mli ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Why do caterpillars like to hide deep inside the center of my cabbage heads?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ mi-kaaba yitso lɛ teŋgbɛ tɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: The inside of a cabbage head offers a warm, dark shelter that protects insects from heat, rain, and sprays while giving them plenty of soft leaves to eat.
ga: Kaabe yitso lɛ mli haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ, ni eyɛ duŋ. Enɛ buɔ kooloi ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ, nugbɔ, kɛ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Agbɛnɛ hu koni aye

english: Is there any real difference between how I should care for my plantain trees compared to banana trees?
ga: Ani srɔtofeemɔi diɛŋtsɛ yɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ makwɛ plantain tso nɔ kɛ banana tso he lɛ teŋ?

english: Yes, even though plantains and bananas look very similar, plantains require different pruning methods, wider field spacing, and heavier soil feeding to produce large bunches because they grow taller and take longer to mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ plantains kɛ banana tamɔ amɛhe waa moŋ, Shi plantains biɔ gbɛi srɔtoi ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ. Gbɛ ni kã ŋmɔji lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli bawo wu. kɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni yeɔ niyenii koni efee ŋmeii wuji ejaakɛ amɛbaadara ni amɛhe be babaoo dani amɛdara.

english: Why do I need to cut off the old dry leaves from my plantain stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ baai ni egbɔ ni egbi kɛjɛ mi plantain tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cutting off dead or yellowing leaves prevents plant diseases from spreading through your farm, allows air to circulate around the stem, and helps the plant direct all its food and energy into growing the fresh fruit bunch.
ga: Baai ni egboi loo ni miifee ŋmɔŋ lɛ ni oookpa lɛ baaye abua ni tsei ahe helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ eniyenii kɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai heei.

english: How do I choose which small shoots to cut away from the main plantain tree?
ga: Miiya ni mayajie ŋmeii bibii komɛi. Higbɛ esa akɛ afo kɛjɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli?

english: You should leave one or two strong 'sword suckers'—the shoots with thin, narrow leaves—because they produce heavy fruits. Cut away the 'water suckers' with broad, flat leaves since they grow weakly and produce small bunches.
ga: Esa akɛ oshi ‘klante tso’ kome loo enyɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ - tso ni baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo - ejaakɛ amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii. Kpɔ̃ɔ ‘suckers’ lɛ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ejaakɛ amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over right before the fruit is ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains lɛ miigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ baafee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Plantain stems are full of water and soft, so when the fruit bunch becomes heavy, strong winds can easily pull the plant down. You need to prop up the stem using bamboo or wooden poles to support the weight of the fruit.
ga: Nu eyi plantain tsei lɛ amli obɔ, ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ. No hewɔ lɛ kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ batsɔ tsii Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei kɛba shi mlɛo. Esa akɛ okɛ ŋmei loo tso tso ko afi tso lɛ yibii lɛ asɛɛ.

english: What is the proper way to cut down a plantain stalk during harvest so I don't ruin the next crop?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ kpakpa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ dumɔwui yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli? koni ekafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: You should cut the main stem at a slant about waist-high after taking the fruit bunch. Leave the bottom part standing for a while so the remaining nutrients flow down into the young sucker shoot that will produce your next harvest.
ga: Esa akɛ ofo tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli yɛ koŋ ni shɛɔ otsitsi nɔ beni ogbala aduawai akuu lɛ sɛɛ. Shi shishigbɛ lɛ ni ajie lɛ kpo be fioo koni niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ aba shi kɛya tso ni woɔ yibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my plantains very close together like I do with maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ plantains ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tamɔ bɔ ni miduɔ ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees grow very wide leaves that block sunlight. If you plant them too close, the leaves shade each other out, making the stems thin and weak, which results in very small fruit bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ waa ni tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Kɛji odu ni obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Baai lɛ baaha amɛhe. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi feɔ mlɛo ni egbɔjɔ Enɛ haa efeɔ ŋmeii bibii waa.

english: Should I dig out the root of a plantain tree immediately after I cut down the fruit?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mifo aduawai lɛ?

english: No, you should leave the underground root system intact because it continues to feed and support the young sucker shoots growing next to it for the next season's crop.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ oshi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ebaaya nɔ eha ŋmeii bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ emasɛi lɛ niyenii kɛ yelikɛbuamɔ. kɛha dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli

english: Why are the leaves on my banana plants turning dark spots and dying early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ banana tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ diŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by leaf spot fungal diseases like Sigatoka, which spread rapidly in warm, humid weather. You can manage it by cutting off affected leaves with a clean knife and ensuring good drainage on your farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ji fungal leaf spot, tamɔ Sigatoka, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Obaanyɛ otsu enɛ he nii kɛtsɔ baai ni hela lɛ emɔ lɛ ni okɛ tsɔne ni he tse baafo lɛ nɔ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni nu kpakpa ahi oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do plantain leaves fold down and wither so quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboɔ oya yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and giant leaves that lose water fast. During dry spells, the leaves fold down to reduce water loss, so mulching around the base with dry grass helps keep moisture in the soil.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni nu fiteɔ oya. yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi ni egbi ha shishigbɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain plants require more manure than my cassava crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fe mi-cassava tsei lɛ?

english: Cassava has deep roots that can search for nutrients in poor soils, but plantains are heavy feeders with shallow roots that need rich soil and plenty of organic manure to grow sturdy stems and produce heavy bunches.
ga: Cassava yɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baanyɛ atao niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ. Shi plantains ji tsei ni yeɔ nii waa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni biɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo koni amɛkwɛ̃ amɛshishifãi ni wa ni amɛwo ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow so poorly even when I give them enough water every day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa daa gbi moŋ?

english: Water alone is not enough for crops to grow strong. Over time, soil loses essential plant nutrients due to continuous farming or rain washing them away, meaning you need to feed the soil with manure or fertilizer to make it productive again.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ laajeɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei lɛ yɛ okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni shwieɔ amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ koni ekɛku esɛɛ eba nitsumɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I easily tell if my farm land has lost its fertility and needs attention?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ ewooo yibii dɔŋŋ ni ehe miihia ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: If your crops stay small, show pale or yellowing leaves during normal weather, or produce very small fruits, it is a clear sign that the ground lacks the natural food required for healthy crop growth.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji bibii Pale loo yellow leaves yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni sa mli loo nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ ji bibioo kwraa Eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant tomatoes on the exact same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop in the same spot continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop loves and allows ground pests that feed on that crop to build up in large numbers in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ hoɔ be fɛɛ be. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ koni amɛbua amɛhe naa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why do bugs attack my vegetables more when I plant them out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo tutuaa mi-aduawai lɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Open fields expose your crops to wind currents that easily carry insects from neighboring farms, while direct sun and weather changes can stress plants, making them easier targets for pests.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni agbele naa lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa oya ni kɛ kooloi ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli lɛ baa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Why are insects eating my seeds and crop roots from underground before they even grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye midumɔwui kɛ mishishifãi kɛmiijɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Many pests, like cutworms and white grubs, live and hide inside the dirt itself. Turning over the soil and exposing it to the sun before planting helps kill these hidden ground pests and their eggs.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui srɔtoi babaoo tamɔ cutworms kɛ white beetles Shihilɛ kɛ teemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni atsakeɔ ni agbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni agbe nɛkɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ.

english: What simple step can I take to clear pests out of my soil before I sow new seeds?
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo Te mafee tɛŋŋ majie tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu dumɔwui heei?

english: Clearing out old crop roots, weeding the farm borders, and plowing the soil to expose it to the hot sun drying effect will destroy insect nests and eggs resting in the ground.
ga: Tso shishifãi momo ni ajieɔ lɛ Jiemɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsu nii koni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ ashɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ kooloi atsũi kɛ amɛwuji ni awoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why do so many insects suddenly appear on my farm right after the early rains begin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii babaoo baa trukaa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ pɛ?

english: Rainfall and warm weather trigger dormant insect eggs in the ground to hatch quickly, while fresh young leaves give the newborn pests plenty of food to feed on.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baaha kooloi bibii ni wɔɔ shi lɛ awui aba. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni etse oya lɛ nɔ Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, baai bibii ni yɔɔ ehee lɛ baaha kooloi ni miiba lɛ niyenii babaoo ni amɛye.

english: Why do insects seem to prefer attacking my cabbage and pepper plants over my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii sumɔɔ ni amɛtutua cabbage kɛ pepper tsei fe ŋmei lɛ?

english: Vegetables have soft, juicy, and nutrient-rich leaves that are easy for insects to chew and digest, unlike cassava leaves which are tougher and contain natural bitter compounds.
ga: Aduawai yɛ baai bibii, ni nu yɔɔ mli ni niyenii babaoo yɛ mli ni koolooi baanyɛ amɛye ni amɛye mlɛo. Enɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ ŋmei baai ni wa fe fɛɛ ni nibii ni mli edɔ ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects hiding under the leaves that drink the plant's juices and sometimes spread plant diseases from farm to farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ni ekɛ ehe ewo baai lɛ ashishi ni enuɔ tso nu. Ni bei komɛi lɛ, tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli.

english: Can I use wood ash from my kitchen stove to protect my crop leaves from insects?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tso sũ ni yɔɔ mi-kitchen stof lɛ mli lɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe baai ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe?

english: Yes, dusting clean wood ash on young crop leaves creates a dry barrier that irritates crawling insects and prevents soft-bodied pests from eating the leaves.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso sũ ni he tse ni akɛshwieɔ tsei bibii ahe baai anɔ lɛ haa gbɛtsii nii ko ni egbi ni haa kooloi bibii ni shwereɔ lɛ amli fuɔ lɛ baa. ni etsĩɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye baai lɛ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to produce green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the crop the nourishment it needs to stay healthy and green.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji.

english: Why do my cassava roots start rotting in the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain leaves standing water on the field, the soil becomes waterlogged, which drowns the roots and encourages fungal rot to grow.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu lɛ ŋmɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee nu. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ewoɔ ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plant leaves curl upwards when the sun gets very hot in the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The tomato plant curls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping it conserve water and survive extreme heat stress.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nu toɔ he ni eyeɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ nɔ.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. Because the stem and fruit bunch are very heavy, a strong wind can easily pull the shallow roots out of the soft soil unless the tree is supported with wooden poles.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii akui lɛ tsii waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ nɔ oya, ja akɛ tsei ni akɛfee tso lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop many of their flowers before pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally shed flowers if the soil lacks nutrients or moisture to support pod growth. Flower drop also happens if there are not enough tiny beneficial insects, called midges, to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baawo fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii loo nu ni baaye abua ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ hu baanyɛ aba kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ midges lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why must I clear weeds away from my crops when the plants are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Young crops have small, delicate roots that cannot compete with fast-growing weeds. Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, starving your young crop and stopping it from growing strong.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛŋ amɛkɛ jwɛi ni daa oya lɛ ashi akaŋ. Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Hɔmɔ aye onibii bibii lɛ anɔ ni otsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkadara waa.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop making fresh peppers during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ pepper heei feemɔ yɛ harmatta be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The intense hot, dry air causes pepper plants to drop their flowers to save moisture. Without flowers staying on the plant, no new pepper fruits can develop until the plant receives adequate water.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji fɔfɔi bɛ tso lɛ nɔ Kɛyashi tso lɛ baaná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ŋmeii nyɛŋ awo yibii heei.

english: Why do I need to clear and loosen the soil deeply before planting yam?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ dani madu sweet potatoes lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing outward under the ground. Soft, loose soil makes it easy for the tuber to expand smoothly, while hard, packed earth prevents growth and results in small or crooked yams.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni etse ehe lɛ haa bulbs lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ dalɛ naa ni ehaa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni etse amɛhe lɛ baa.

english: Why do caterpillars like to hide and eat deep inside the middle funnel of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛtee amɛhe ni amɛye nii yɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The central funnel of the maize plant provides shelter from hot sunlight, rain, and predators, while offering the tenderest leaves for the pest to feed on safely.
ga: Abɛi tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ haa hulu ni tsoɔ waa, nugbɔ, kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ náa abobaahe, yɛ be mli ni ehaa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ lɛ hu haa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ koni amɛye shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do insects swarm onto my cowpea farm as soon as the plants start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii shwereɔ kɛboteɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji tsei lɛ bɔi fɔmɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea blossoms produce sweet nectar and bright flowers that attract insects. While some insects help pollination, harmful pests use flower time to lay eggs that grow into worms that eat the crop's pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ woɔ nu mli nu kɛ fɔfɔi ni kpɛɔ ni gbalaa kooloi. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi komɛi yeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ Shi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi be tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Leaf curling and yellowing in cassava is often caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting helps keep your crop healthy.
ga: Kasava lɛ ebɔle ehe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela kɛbaa. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii kɛdu lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without forming fruit when daytime temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly from dry to very wet. Keeping soil moisture steady with mulching helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ kɛyaa nɔ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛtsɔ mulching nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer before I plant maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmãa?

english: If your crops from the previous season were short, had yellowish leaves, or gave small yields, your soil is low on nutrients. Testing the soil or applying well-rotted manure or commercial fertilizer will help restore its strength.
ga: Kɛji akɛ onibii ni okpa yɛ nyɛsɛɛ be lɛ mli lɛ yɛ kuku, eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo ewoɔ yibii fioo Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa loo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo jarayeli ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni eha hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting seeds too close forces plants to compete with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to grow strong and yield big cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe yeɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ baawo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Is it good to plant cowpeas or beans in the same field with my maize?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is very helpful. Beans capture nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil to feed the maize, while the tall maize gives support to climbing bean vines.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Beans mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ fiɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɔɔ lɛ asɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense heat, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than roots can drink it from the soil. As long as they bounce back by evening, it is normal heat stress, but mulching the soil helps keep root zones cool.
ga: yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ Pepper tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni amɛbaaku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni yaa nɔ kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ mli. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni shishifã lɛ he afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why did many of my vegetable seeds fail to sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to germinate if they are planted too deep, if the soil dries out completely, or if heavy rain causes the soil to waterlog and rot the seeds before they can break through.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa Aloo kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ fite dani amɛbote mli.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow poorly and give small yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haaa midumɔ nii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal the water, sunlight, and soil food meant for your crops. Removing weeds early in the season lets your crops get all the nourishment they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa onibii. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛshwere.

english: Why is it important to prune some of the lower branches of my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Pruning weak or low branches allows sunlight and fresh air to pass through the tree canopy. This prevents fungal diseases like black pod and directs the tree's energy into growing healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ niji ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa abote tso lɛ yiteŋ. Bɔni afee ni atsĩ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ anaa ni akɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni akɛkwɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start rotting so quickly in the storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot quickly if they are cut or bruised during harvesting, left in direct hot sun, or stored without good airflow. Gentle handling and keeping the storage barn cool and well-ventilated helps them last much longer.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ afolɔ loo atswa yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Ashi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli loo akɛto he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛtsu nii blɛoo ni oha otsu lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu abote mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do many farmers in Ghana plant plantains in the same field as young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ duɔ plantain yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni amɛduɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide living shade to protect the young cocoa, while also giving you food to harvest early on.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa, ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa hulutsoo buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa bo niyenii ni obaakpa mra.

english: Is it safe for me to plant corn in the space between my young plantain trees?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ he ni midumɔwui bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Yes, intercropping corn with young plantains works well because corn grows and matures quickly. As long as you give both crops enough space, the corn can be harvested without taking away the soil nutrients needed by the growing plantains.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ plantains bibii duɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya. Shii abɔ ni obaaha tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. Abaanyɛ akpa ŋmãa hu ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha plantains ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Does dragon fruit need a pole or post to grow on my farm?
ga: Ani drako aduawai lɛ he miihia tsei loo tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, dragon fruit is a climbing cactus plant that cannot stand upright by itself. It needs a strong concrete or wooden post to climb so its branches can spread out and produce fruit.
ga: Hɛɛ, drako aduawai ji tso ko ni kwɔɔ ni nyɛŋ adamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe. Ebiɔ ni akɛ kɔnkrit loo tsei ni wa awo mli dani anyɛ akwɔ. No sɛɛ lɛ, tsei niji lɛ baagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How long does a pineapple crop take from planting until I can harvest the fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ ni akɛduɔ ŋmei dani abaanyɛ akpa?

english: Pineapples are slow-growing crops that typically take between 12 to 18 months to produce mature fruit, depending on the planting material used and local soil conditions.
ga: Anana ji tso ko ni daa blɛoo ni bei pii lɛ eheɔ aaafee nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 dani ewoɔ yibii. Enɛ damɔ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are some of my papaya trees flowering heavily but never bearing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mipapaya tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papaya plants can be male, female, or bisexual. Male papaya trees produce abundant flowers containing pollen, but they cannot form fruit themselves; you only need a few male trees on the farm to pollinate the fruit-bearing female trees.
ga: Papaya tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo hii kɛ yei. Papaya tsei hii woɔ fɔfɔi ni pollen babaoo yɔɔ mli. shi enyɛŋ ewo yibii kɛjɛ ehe Tsei hii fioo pɛ he miihia bo yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni okɛwo tsei yei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli pollen.

english: Can dragon fruit actually survive and produce fruit in Ghana's weather and soil?
ga: Ani drako yibii lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi diɛŋtsɛ ni ewo yibii yɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, dragon fruit grows well in warm, tropical climates like Ghana's, provided it gets full sunlight and is planted in sandy, well-drained soil so its roots do not rot in excess water.
ga: Hɛɛ, drako aduawai lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tamɔ Ghana lɛ kɛji hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa yɛ nɔ. ni adu yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ nɔ Enɛ baatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite kɛji nu fa babaoo.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my corn plants turning yellow before the cobs are ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on corn usually mean the plant lacks essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, or that the soil is overly waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer can restore healthy green leaf growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ, ni eyɛ eŋɔli ekoŋŋ.

english: What is the best material to use if I want to plant new pineapples on my farm?
ga: Kɛji miisumɔ ni makwɛ ŋmei hee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛni ji nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii?

english: You can plant pineapples using suckers (shoots from the base) or crowns (the green top of the fruit). Suckers are usually best because they grow faster and produce fruit several months earlier than crowns.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmeii (tsobii ni jɛ shishigbɛ) loo akɔɔblei (aduawai lɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ) atsu nii ni okɛdu pineapple. Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii nyɔji babaoo mra fe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I stop wandering goats from eating my young crop shoots?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi tooi ni elaaje lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye mi ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Goats naturally feed on fresh leaf shoots. Protecting young crops requires building physical wire fences, planting dense thorn hedges around the plot border, or keeping livestock tethered away from fields.
ga: Tooi yeɔ baai heei yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Bɔni afee ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe lɛ, ehe bahia ni ama ŋtayaai ni akɛ ŋmeii ebɔ he. Adu waya gbogbo ni mli wa ni akɛbɔle shikpɔŋ lɛ naa lɛ he. aloo fimɔ kooloi kɛjɛ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe

english: Why do rats attack my mature pineapples and cocoa pods right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miitutuaa mi-pineapple kɛ mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni eda lɛ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Rats are attracted to the high sugar content in ripe fruits and cocoa pods. Keeping the field clear of weeds, harvesting fruit promptly as soon as it matures, and placing traps along field borders helps suppress rat populations.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sugar ni fa babaoo ni yɔɔ aduawai ni ekwɛ̃ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii amli lɛ gbalaa ŋmeii. Gbɛjegbɛi ni jwɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ Akpaa aduawai kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ pɛ. Ni tsɔnei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ baaye abua ni ajie ŋmeii ayibɔ.

english: Why should I plant beans or cowpeas in the same field alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ ŋmei masɛi?

english: Legumes like beans and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. This naturally enriches the soil with nutrients that help your maize grow healthier, giving you a better maize yield and an extra harvest of beans.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ baaha sũ lɛ afee nɔ ni niyenii ni baaye abua o-ŋmã lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmãa babaoo.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei adu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground so they can catch direct sunlight to produce food for growing big tubers. Spreading on the ground exposes leaves to hot soil burns and diseases, leading to smaller yams.
ga: Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ gbɛfaŋnɔ kɛ baa shwiemɔ kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii.

english: Covering the soil (mulching) acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, traps rainwater so the soil stays moist longer, prevents weeds from sprouting, and turns into organic manure as it decays.
ga: Mulching (mulching) tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji efite

english: Yellow leaves on maize are usually a sign that the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the roots. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or poultry manure helps the leaves turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo kooloi aŋmɔŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking juices from under the leaves, or by a virus they spread. Treating the plants early stops the pests and protects new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ mli Tsei akwɛmɔ kɛjɛ amɛgbekɛbiiashi Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛtsi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa ni etsi baai heei ni baa lɛ anaa.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without forming any small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛfeee tomato bibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop off mainly when the plants suffer from extreme afternoon heat or irregular watering. When the plant gets too hot or thirsty, it drops its flowers to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi babaoo kɛ́ tsei lɛ naa amanehulu yɛ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ tso lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kumai miiye lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. Excessively heavy rains create waterlogged soil where roots drown and soil fungi thrive, causing the tubers to rot underground before harvest.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa fe nine lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nu. He ni shishifãi shwieɔ nu mli ni ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ daa yɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa.

english: Watering early in the morning gives roots moisture to handle the hot daytime heat while allowing wet leaves to dry quickly in the morning sun, which prevents leaf diseases from growing on wet foliage overnight.
ga: Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛkpee shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ naa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai ni efɔ lɛ agbi oya yɛ leebi hulu lɛ mli. Enɛ baatsi baa helai anaa koni ekakwɛ baa ni efɔ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: Why should I clear weeds around my young cocoa trees before the main rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Kookoo tsei bibii dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ jeɔ shishi?

english: Weeds steal water and soil nutrients away from young cocoa plants. Clearing them early ensures that when the rain comes, your cocoa trees get all the water and nutrients they need to grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ kookoo tsei bibii amli lɛ. Kookoo tsei ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ Okokoo tsei lɛ baaná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara oya.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees snap or fall over easily during windy storms when carrying heavy bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains ni eda lɛ fãa loo amɛgbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tswaa lɛ mli kɛ́ amɛmiiwo tsei niji ni tsii lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and weak stems. When a heavy fruit bunch matures, the plant becomes top-heavy, making it easy for strong winds to push it over unless you support the stem with bamboo props.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ. Beni aduawai akuu lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Tso lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii waa. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baatsɔ mli. Ja okɛ ŋmei nibii fiɔ tsɔne lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cocoa trees turn yellow and fall off when the dry Harmattan season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Harmattan brings dry, harsh winds and very low moisture. Cocoa trees drop their leaves to save water and protect themselves from drying out, though having good shade trees can reduce this leaf loss.
ga: Harmattan kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa baa. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe koni amɛkagbi. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo kpakpa ni ooona lɛ baaye abua ni baai ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi moŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin with small cob size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. Proper spacing allows each plant to get enough sunlight and nutrients to grow strong stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji akwɛ̃.

english: How do I know that my cassava is mature and ready for me to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will notice the lower leaves turning yellow and dropping, and the soil around the base of the stem starting to crack as the tubers expand.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into growing leaves instead of fruits. Switching to fertilizers rich in phosphorus and potassium will encourage your plants to flower and produce peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tsei yeɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ kɛduɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua otsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa baadu tsina loo ŋmãa?

english: Yes, leguminous crops like cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps the maize grow better. They also cover the soil surface to keep weeds away and preserve soil moisture.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. Amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu koni jwɛi akabote mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which feed inside the growing center of young maize. Checking your field early and applying neem extracts or recommended insecticides can control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ tsui mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ enɛɛmɛi.

english: The first rain after a dry season only wets the top layer of soil, which quickly dries out. If you plant immediately, a dry spell following that single rain can kill your germinating seeds. It is safer to wait until the rains become steady.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ, ni kɛji odu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, egbiɔ oya. Hɔmɔ ni baa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbe dumɔwui ni miikwɛ̃ lɛ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do I need to clear tall sticks and stake my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ ni mawo sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, allows more light exposure, and prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa la babaoo ni ekɛtsiɔ baa helai anaa

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop and curl up in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil has water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: Plants temporarily curl their leaves during the hottest part of the day to protect themselves from losing too much water into the air. If they bounce back in the evening, it is just a natural protective behavior.
ga: Tsei baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ akaje amɛdɛŋ. Kɛ amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu subaŋ kɛkɛ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the small shoots growing around the bottom of my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi lɛ he

english: If too many shoots grow around one plantain stem, they steal nutrients and water from the main tree. Leaving only two or three healthy suckers ensures your main tree produces a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ ehe Plantain kome Ebaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha otso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Why do my bean plants dry up and drop their flowers when there is no rain for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛko otsii fioo komɛi nɛ lɛ?

english: When bean plants lack water during their flowering stage, they become stressed and shed their blossoms to conserve energy, which stops them from producing pods unless you provide extra water using an irrigation system.
ga: Beni bean tso lɛ bɛ nu yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ Amɛhaoɔ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Enɛ haaa amɛfee pods. Ja okɛ nu babaoo fata he kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is watering my crops late in the afternoon better for them than watering at midday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mafɔ midumɔ nii lɛ anɔ nu shwane mli fe shwane mli lɛ?

english: The hot midday sun causes most water to evaporate into the air before the roots can drink it, whereas late afternoon watering allows the moisture to sink deep into the soil so roots can absorb it overnight.
