ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ haa nu lɛ fa ko shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnuɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwane mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ nyɔɔŋ kome.

english: What causes small insects to destroy the leaves of my crops, and how does spraying help?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii fiteɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ? Ni mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ mɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa?

english: Insects feed on plant leaves and juices, which weakens the crop and reduces harvest, but using a sprayer lets you spread protective medicine evenly over the leaves to stop pests from damaging your farm.
ga: Kplukai yeɔ tsei ahe baai kɛ aduawai amli nu. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmaakpamɔ baa shi. Shi kɛ okɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ hela nɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, onyɛɔ ojaa tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ mli pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ baai lɛ amli koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafite oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: How does using a knapsack sprayer protect my crops better than splashing water on them by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ sɛɛ mli ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ buɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe jogbaŋŋ fe nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: A knapsack sprayer turns liquid mist into tiny droplets that cover every part of the plant, including hidden leaf undersides where pests hide, giving complete protection without wasting liquid.
ga: Nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baagi nɔ lɛ haa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ feɔ nu bibii bibii. ni haa tso lɛ fã fɛɛ fã nɔ Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ. Ehaa hebuu ni yeɔ emuu ni nu ni afiteɔ bɛ mli.

english: What makes black spots appear on my crop leaves during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii diji jeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Fungal diseases spread quickly in damp, humid weather when leaves stay wet, but spraying the right protective chemical prevents the fungus from taking hold and spreading across your field.
ga: Fungal helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ be mli ni baai lɛ mli edɔ lolo lɛ. Shi tsofai ni sa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ ni oooshwie lɛ baatsi ŋmei lɛ naa koni ekakɛ ehe akabɔ he ni egbɛ eshwa oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil lacks nutrients when my crop leaves start turning light yellow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni tsei ahe baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is hungry for key nutrients like nitrogen, which slows down its growth and reduces the overall amount of produce you will be able to harvest and sell.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia niyenii titrii, tamɔ nitrogen, ni baaha edalɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni ehaa nibii fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ okpa ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are some of my bean pods full of healthy seeds while others stay small and empty?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean pods lɛ ekomɛi eyi kɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni pods komɛi ji bibii lolo ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Beans need steady water, sunlight, and good soil food while forming seeds; if the plant lacks water or suffers pest damage early on, the pods cannot develop full seeds inside.
ga: Nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpa he miihia ŋmeii be fɛɛ be be mli ni amɛfeɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite amɛ mra lɛ, The pods lɛ nyɛŋ afee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin with very little yield when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ mlɛo ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they shade each other and fight for sunlight, causing them to stretch upward instead of spending energy on making big, healthy fruits or pods.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛfee aduawai loo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do my crop roots turn soft and rot when water stays pooled on my farm land for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu bua ehe naa yɛ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Roots need air in the soil to breathe; when water sits on the field for too long, it smothers the roots and allows fungal rots to kill the plant from below.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Ekɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ gbeɔ tso lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishi.

english: Weeds have strong, wild root systems that rapidly steal water and nutrients from the rain, so you must clear them early before they starve your main crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli. Enɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni ojie amɛ mra. Dani hɔmɔ baaye oniyenii titri lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees typically take between 3 to 5 years to bear fruit, depending on the variety you plant. Modern hybrid varieties usually yield faster if given proper care, water, and shade.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo tsei heɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Edamɔ tso srɔtoi ni oduɔ lɛ nɔ. Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ hybrid henɔi lɛ fɔɔ yibiiwoo oya kɛji akɛ akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ, nu kɛ hulutsoo.

english: Why do my mango trees produce many flowers, but most of them fall off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi amɛteŋ babaoo gbeeɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Heavy flower drop in mangoes is often caused by sudden weather changes, poor soil moisture, or insect attacks like thrips and midges during the flowering stage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa trukaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ mango ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii loo kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids kɛ thrips ni tutuaa mɔ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli.

english: How do I know if my land has the right soil for growing healthy mango trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni sa kɛha mango tso ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Mango trees prefer deep, well-drained soil where water does not sit for long periods. If your soil is loose, rich in organic matter, and doesn't flood during rains, mangoes will root deeply and grow well.
ga: Mango tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu lɛ damɔɔɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ, kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ mli. ni nu afuaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli Mango baawo shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to spray pesticides on my crop field?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afɔ miŋmɔji lɛ anɔ?

english: The best times are early morning or late afternoon. Spraying when the sun is hot can burn the crop leaves and cause the chemical to evaporate before it can kill the pests.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji leebi loo shwane. Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ beni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai ni eha tsofai lɛ atsɔ la dani amɛgbe ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How do I know the correct month to start spraying chemicals against black pod disease on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔŋ ni sa ni esa akɛ mabɔi black pod hela tsofai lɛ shwiemɔ yɛ kookoo tsei anɔ?

english: Black pod disease thrives in cool, damp conditions. Spraying should begin just before the main rainy season starts, usually around May or June, to protect the young pods before moisture spreads the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Esa akɛ aje tsofa lɛ shwiemɔ shishi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ aje shishi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee May loo June. Koni abu ŋmɔtɔ bibii lɛ ahe dani ŋmɔtɔ agbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ashwã.

english: How often am I supposed to spray my farm to protect cocoa pods from capsid bugs?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mikɛ tsofa afɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ koni mikɛbu kookoo ŋmeii ahe kɛjɛ capsid kooloi ahe?

english: Capsid pests are most active between August and December. Extension guidelines generally recommend spraying twice during this peak season, spaced about four weeks apart.
ga: Capsid tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ tsuɔ nii waa yɛ August kɛ December teŋ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ sɛɛkuu he lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ be ni fa nɛɛ mli. ni amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ aaafee otsii ejwɛ

english: Can I mix fertilizer together with my pest control chemicals when spraying my trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ afutu ŋmɔshi nibii beni mikɛ tsofai fɔ̃ɔ tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: It is safer to apply them separately unless a specialist confirms they are compatible. Mixing certain chemicals can reduce their strength or cause leaves to burn.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ amɛ baatsu nii srɔtoi. ja mɔ ko ni le nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ ma nɔ mi akɛ ekɛ ehe kpãa gbee Tsofai komɛi ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai lɛ ahewalɛ aba shi loo eha baai lɛ ashã.

english: Why are the leaves on my young fruit trees turning yellow and dropping prematurely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, overwatering, or sap-sucking insects feeding under the leaves. Checking under the leaf surface helps identify if insects are the cause.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nu babaoo Aloo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu ni amɛtaoɔ niyenii yɛ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ jɛmɛ. Kɛ́ akwɛ baa lɛ hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji kooloi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn dark black and dry up while still hanging on the tree?
ga: Mɛni ha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ batsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbi beni amɛkã tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection spread by rain splashes and high humidity. Clearing weeds, pruning shade trees, and applying approved fungicides help control it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Fungal hela ko ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa. weeding Tsei ni afolɔ koni amɛha hulutsoo Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to check with other farmers in my village before applying pest chemicals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ agba sane dani mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ atsu nii?

english: Insects fly easily between neighboring fields. If you spray at the same time as your neighbors, pests cannot simply fly away to an unsprayed farm next door, making pest control far more effective for everyone.
ga: Kplukai fãa yɛ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ateŋ oya. Kɛji okɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ fee ekome kɛshwie tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Pests nyɛŋ afã kɛya ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ ni afɔko tsofa lɛ amli lɛ amli. Ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe nitsumɔ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ.

english: Why are the plantains on my farm smaller than the ones my neighbour harvested?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ daraaa fe nɔ ni mikutsoŋbii lɛ kpaa lɛ?

english: Fruit size mainly depends on the food the plant receives from the soil. If your crop gets adequate nutrients, water, and good soil, it will produce larger fruits, whereas poor soil leads to smaller harvests.
ga: Niyenii ni tso lɛ nine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ titri ji yibii lɛ adalɛ. Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa. Tso lɛ baawo yibii wuji. Yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baaha yibiiwoo fioo aba lɛ.

english: If I give my crops more compost or fertilizer, will it make the harvested fruits bigger?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ Ani ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Yes, plants use nutrients from compost and fertilizer as food to build larger and healthier produce, though giving too much can sometimes damage the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ bei komɛi lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ babaoo ha lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite shishifãi lɛ moŋ.

english: Why did my maize cobs turn out small with missing grains this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ daraaa ni amɛmli ŋmãa bɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: When maize plants do not get enough water or soil nutrients during their flowering stage, they lack the food needed to fill out all the grains on the cob.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, no lɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaná niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekɛwo ŋmãa fɛɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Does every cassava variety grow big tubers, or are some naturally small?
ga: Ani ŋmei henɔi fɛɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji loo bibii yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Different crop varieties are naturally programmed for different sizes. Some cassava varieties are bred to produce large tubers for heavy yield, while others naturally stay smaller but mature much faster.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha amɛdalɛi srɔtoi. Akwɛ ŋmei srɔtoi komɛi kɛha yitsei wuji kɛ yibiiwoo babaoo. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei henɔi komɛi ji bibii shi amɛdaraa oya kwraa lɛ.

english: If I plant seeds from an extra-large papaya, will the new tree automatically produce extra-large papayas?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ papaya ni da fe nine mli lɛ Ani tso hee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ baawo papaya ni da fe nine?

english: While seeds from a large fruit carry good genetic traits, the new tree will only produce extra-large fruit if it also receives good soil food, adequate water, and sunlight.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ aduawai wuji amli lɛ yɛ fɔmɔ nii kpakpai moŋ, Shi tsei heei baawo aduawai ni da fe nine kɛji akɛ aye amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ hulu la hu

english: Why do some tomato plants on the same land yield large tomatoes while others yield small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ he kome lɛ woɔ tomatoi wuji lɛ? Shi tsei komɛi haa gbekɛbii bibii?

english: Individual plants that get more sunlight, space, and nutrients will grow larger fruits than nearby plants that are crowded or struggling for soil food.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso ni hulu la, ŋwɛi, kɛ niyenii babaoo baawo lɛ baawo yibii wuji fe tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ ni amɛhe wa loo amɛmiitao niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods have two seeds fused together or unusually large beans inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ ekomɛi yɛ dumɔwui enyɔ ni efutu loo dumɔwui wuji ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ yɛ mli lɛ?

english: When a cocoa flower receives heavy pollination and abundant nutrients during pod formation, the plant can produce twin seeds or extra-large beans within a single pod.
ga: Enɛ ji be mli ni kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ waa ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ be mli ni afeɔ pod lɛ. Cacao tsei baanyɛ awo dumɔwui enyɔ loo ŋmeii wuji fe nine yɛ ŋmeii kome mli.

english: Why do I sometimes find double groundnuts inside one large shell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ minaa ŋmeii enyɔ yɛ ŋmeii agbo kome mli lɛ?

english: Strong plant health and extra moisture during pod development cause the groundnut plant to form multiple extra-large seeds together inside a single shell.
ga: Tso lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni yaa hiɛ yɛ pod lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei tsei lɛ woɔ dumɔwui wuji babaoo ni abua naa yɛ ŋmei kome mli.

english: Why do foreign export buyers prefer medium-sized pineapples instead of the giant ones I grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nibii ni akɛyaa maŋsɛɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmeii ni dalɛ ji mlɛo fe ŋmeii wuji ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers for export markets often prefer uniform, medium-sized produce because they fit standard shipping crates better and match the buying habits of consumers abroad.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii kɛha maŋsɛɛ jarayeli hei lɛ sumɔɔ nibii ni yaa nɔ daa, ni dalɛ yɔɔ teŋgbɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, abaanyɛ akɛwo tsɔnei ni akɛmajeɔ lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ ni ekɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ ajeŋba lɛ akpã gbee.

english: Why do my garden eggs look small and dull compared to the bright, plump ones at the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛhe ejɔɔɔ kɛ akɛto ŋmeii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Garden eggs need steady watering and rich soil nutrients like compost to reach a full size and develop a shiny, healthy outer skin before harvest.
ga: Abɔɔ mli ŋmeii biɔ ni afɔ amɛ nu daa kɛ sũ mli nibii ni fa babaoo, tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, koni amɛshɛ amɛdalɛ he ni amɛná kponɔgbɛ ni kpɛɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani akpa amɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by dry spells, lack of soil nutrients like potassium, or attacks from insects like capsids. Providing adequate shade, mulching, and applying balanced fertilizers help the tree hold onto its flowers so they can form healthy pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji hulutsoo be ko hao amɛ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ potassium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids ni baatutua lɛ, hulutsoo ni sa, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaye abua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni efee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are there tiny holes in my corn leaves and caterpillars eating inside the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi kɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ye nii yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that feeds on the young inner leaves of maize plants. Early detection and spraying recommended bio-pesticides or putting a tiny bit of clean sand or ash in the central funnel can help destroy the caterpillars.
ga: Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni fiteɔ nii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ ana mra ni afɔ amɛ nɔ. Aloo, kɛ́ akɛ ŋã loo sũ ni he tse fioo ko fata ŋã ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato and pepper plants suddenly wilt and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato kɛ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is usually caused by root diseases from fungi or bacteria living in the soil that block the plant's water pathways. Changing the crop location each season and planting disease-resistant varieties prevents these soil diseases from building up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishifã hela ni jɛɔ ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni tsiɔ tso lɛ nu gbɛ lɛ naa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Kɛ́ otsake he ni oduɔ nii yɛ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ, ni odu tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ, ebaatsi helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkaje shishi.

english: Yellow leaves are a sign that your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to build healthy green leaves. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer such as NPK or Urea at the right growth stage restores the green color and accelerates growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha eda oya.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans alongside my main crops make my soil richer?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and beans pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When these roots break down in the ground, they release natural fertilizer into the soil for neighboring crops like maize or cassava to feed on.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ beans gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli. Kɛji shishifãi nɛɛ gbá kɛtee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛye ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why is it better to bury fertilizer near my plant roots rather than scattering it across the top of the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaafu yɛ mitsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hi fe ni mikɛbaagbɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Scattering fertilizer on the surface allows heavy rains to wash it away and sunlight to evaporate its nutrients before plants can feed. Placing fertilizer in small covered holes near the root zone ensures the roots absorb maximum nourishment.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nɛɔ waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ni hulu la lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shi dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ aha amɛ niyenii. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ bu bibii amli Kɛ́ oyɛ ŋwɛitsu ni bɛŋkɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli nibii babaoo.

english: Planting crops too closely causes them to compete against each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets full sunlight and enough soil food to grow larger and healthier fruits.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la. Shikpɔŋ nɔ Niyenii kɛ Nu: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la ni fa kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛkwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take much longer to produce fruit compared to those on my neighbor's farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe nɔ ni yɔɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains require large amounts of soil nutrients and constant moisture to grow quickly. If the soil lacks organic matter or dries out during dry months, growth slows down; placing compost and organic mulch around the base speeds up fruiting.
ga: Plantains he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii babaoo kɛ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni enyɛ eda oya. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo egbi yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ewo yibii oya.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates in heavy soil and cannot drain away, suffocating the tubers. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain properly, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ ajie kɛjɛ mli. suffocate the head Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa jogbaŋŋ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ewajeɔ shishifãi lɛ

english: Why are tiny insects turning my stored maize grains into powder inside my storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tsake mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ amɛfee powda yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain insects like weevils multiply rapidly when maize is stored before it is fully dried. Drying your harvested maize thoroughly until it snaps cleanly and storing it in airtight Hermetic bags starves insects of oxygen and prevents damage.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli, tamɔ ŋmeii, feɔ babaoo oya kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa to dani egbi kwraa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha o-ŋmã ni okpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi ebaakumɔ ni okɛwo vacuum bag ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli. Ebaaha kooloo lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni hɔmɔ baaye lɛ, ni ebaatsi nɔ ni efite lɛ naa.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct, harsh sunlight because their roots are shallow and leaves burn easily. Large shade trees protect them like umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and the microclimate cool until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji haa amɛhe jɔɔ ni amɛbuɔ amɛhe tamɔ akpɔlɔi. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural protection mechanism against intense heat. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to hold onto internal moisture until the weather cools down.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛ́ tso lɛ baa lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ehaa he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi bɔni afee ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi emli kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli baajɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks very close together so I can fit more crops on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni manyɛ madu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When cassava plants are packed too tightly, their roots battle underground for soil nutrients and space. Proper spacing gives each plant room to spread out and develop bigger, heavier tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ ŋwɛi lɛ mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa ni ehaa bulbs wuji ni tsii fe tsutsu lɛ feɔ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I put four seeds in one planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ woɔ dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planted too closely, seedlings block light from each other and exhaust the nutrients in that small patch of soil. This forces the maize to grow tall and thin reaching for light instead of building a strong stalk and large cobs.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii bibii lɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni ekwɛɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛyaa la lɛ he moŋ fe ni eeefee ŋmãa ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their yellow flowers without producing fruit during hot dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water is low and temperatures are high, a tomato plant enters stress mode. It drops its blossoms to conserve water and energy for survival rather than spending resources on developing fruits.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ ba shi ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ baaya stress mode mli. Efɔ̃ɔ fɔfɔi koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni enyɛ ehi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii baatsu nii koni akɛfee aduawai lɛ

english: Why can rice plants live in standing water while my corn rots in swampy ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei baanyɛ ahi nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni mi ŋmãa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋshɔ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that transport oxygen down to their roots even underwater. Corn roots lack these channels, so standing water smothers the roots and causes rot.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni yɔɔ amɛmli ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ amɛyɔɔ nu shishi po. Abɛi shishifãi bɛ gbɛi nɛɛ. Nu ni ekã shi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbo ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Staking holds yam leaves high off the ground where they receive maximum sunshine. Leaves exposed to sunlight generate more energy through photosynthesis, which feeds and expands the yam tuber underground.
ga: Okɛ sweet potato baai lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ. Baai ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ babaoo kɛtsɔ fotosintɛsis nɔ. ni baaha sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their yellow flower stems back down into the dirt after flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ tsiɔ efɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ amli ekoŋŋ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni ewo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts flower above ground, but the actual nuts grow under the soil. After pollination, the stem naturally bends down and burrows into the dirt so the peanut pods can safely form underground.
ga: Peanuts fɔ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ, shi nuts diɛŋtsɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. after pollination Tso lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa shishi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni efoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my harvests get smaller every season if I grow maize on the exact same piece of land every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa daa afi kɛji miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil repeatedly and allows pests that attack maize to build up in the soil, leading to weaker harvests over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it better for me to try a new farming method on a small corner of my farm first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ko makwɛ yɛ mikoŋ bibioo lɛ mli lɛ? Ni ŋmɔ lɛ hu klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Testing new techniques on a small plot lets you observe how your soil and local rainfall handle the change without risking your entire season's food supply, allowing you to learn step-by-step.
ga: Gbɛi heei ni oooka yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua bo ni okwɛ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nyɛɔ etsuɔ ​​tsakemɔi ahe nii eha. ni okɛ be muu lɛ fɛɛ mli niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ wooo oshara mli Eyeɔ ebua bo ni okaseɔ nii fitsofitso.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plant turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso ko shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape pattern, it usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green and grow strong.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ, bei pii lɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ.

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is too tired to grow good crops without spending money on tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ edu ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni mikɛ shika tsuuu nii kɛkaaa mikwɛ?

english: Tired soil usually produces crops with pale yellow leaves, thin stems, and very low yields even when there is good rain, showing that the soil has run out of natural plant nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ po. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy; when heavy rains flood the soil for long periods, the roots drown, suffocate, and begin to rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛnyɛɛɛ amɛmu, ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off instead of turning into tomatoes during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ tomato yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high or the plant experiences drought stress, tomato plants drop their flowers to save water and energy to protect themselves from dying.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe Tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die if I do not plant shade trees near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji miduuu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight; shade trees protect them from harsh heat and keep moisture in the soil until their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni amɛhaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli waa.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in direct sunlight to capture light and make food, which is then sent down into the ground to build large, heavy yam tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ emɔ la ni ehoo. No sɛɛ lɛ, akɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi koni efee sweet potato ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Too many shoots compete with the main plantain tree for food and water in the soil, which leads to small bunches; removing extra shoots leaves energy for one strong stem to produce large bunches.
ga: Tsobii babaoo tsɔ kɛ dumɔwu titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni kɛ tso nine bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso kome ni he wa lɛ náa hewalɛ babaoo koni efee panicle agbo.

english: What is making holes in the middle of my young corn leaves and leaving powder behind?
ga: Mɛni haa bu ko baa mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ ni eshiɔ powda lɛ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the growing center of the corn plant during the day and chew through young leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and staying tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni efee bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves, feeding on the plant's juices and spreading diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ mites loo thrips ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ numɔ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai amɛshwãa.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if they are just growing in the spaces between them?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui? Kɛji amɛdara yɛ gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that secretly drink up the water and eat the natural fertilizer from the soil before your main crop roots can reach them.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ mɛi ni nuɔ nu yɛ teemɔŋ ni amɛyeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani otso titri lɛ shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because their roots cannot absorb enough water under direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains nearby protects young seedlings from drying out.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii biɔ hulutsoo ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye abua ni ebu tsei bibii ahe koni amɛkagbi.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and tiny caterpillars hiding inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni Akɛtee tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ anɔ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar eating the leaf whorl. Applying recommended pesticides or neem extracts early in the morning when the pest is active helps protect the crop.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai ahe ŋmeii lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛwo mli leebi be mli ni kooloi lɛ miitsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is ready to harvest without digging up all my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa ni mikɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fɛɛ tsuuu nii?

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 and 12 months after planting when the lower leaves naturally turn yellow and fall off, and small cracks begin to show in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ ŋmeii bibii Ebaabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium uptake, usually due to irregular watering. Keeping soil moisture consistent prevents the fruit tips from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ baatsi aduawai ayitsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Why shouldn't I apply fertilizer to my maize farm when the soil is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ wooo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve into a form plant roots can take in. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn crop roots and cause the nutrient investment to waste away in the sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ mli yɛ gbɛ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ hulu la mli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upwards and the plants remaining short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni tso lɛ yɛ kuku lolo lɛ?

english: Leaf curl disease is spread by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips. Controlling insect populations early and removing heavily twisted plants helps stop the disease from spreading.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips lɛ gbɛɔ leaf curl hela lɛ eshwaa. Kooloi ayibɔ ni akudɔɔ mra Ni tsei ni efite waa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Yam vines need stakes so their leaves can spread out and catch maximum sunlight to feed tuber growth. Staking also keeps leaves off damp soil, reducing fungal leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia ni atswa amɛ tsei lɛ koni amɛbaa lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni eye ebua tuber lɛ dalɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa baa helai ni jɛɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ shi.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers produce huge bunches while others produce small ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi woɔ ŋmeii wuji yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi woɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Sword suckers—which have narrow leaves and a strong, wide corm base—grow stronger and yield larger bunches than water suckers, which have broad leaves early on but weak roots.
ga: Klante tso lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ bulb shishi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa. Ebaada waa ni ebaawo aduawai akui ni dara fe nu mli ŋmeii, ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ kɛjɛ shishijee shi shishifãi lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my land before maize make my maize grow taller and greener?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ haa mi ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that pull natural nitrogen from the air into the soil through their roots. When maize is planted next, it uses this leftover nitrogen to grow faster and stronger.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Be ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ sɛɛ mli Ekɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ oya ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cabbage leaves turn yellow and rot when heavy rain pools around the stems for days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni ebɔle tso lɛ he gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Excess water drowns plant roots by cutting off oxygen, causing root rot. Creating raised ridges or drainage gutters helps excess rainwater flow away from vulnerable plant roots.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala lɛ ni efoɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔnaa ŋshɔi ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ akashɛ tsei shishifãi ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense sunlight because direct heat burns their tender leaves and dries out soil moisture quickly before their root systems can fully establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa ejaakɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gĩɔ oya dani amɛshishifãi lɛ gbeɔ naa.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is the essential plant food needed to keep leaves green and build thick stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛma ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Growing the same crop continuously exhausts specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the field.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ foɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tamɔ tsei ni buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baa

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but small, thin roots under the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi shishifãi bibii komɛi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil is packed too hard or has excessive leaf-growing nutrients, the cassava plant puts all its energy into top leaves rather than pushing heavy food reserves down into underground tubers.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo niyenii mli nibii babaoo ni adu yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ niyenii ni tsii awo ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Yam vines need to reach high into the sunlight to generate energy for tuber growth, and keeping them off the hot ground prevents leaves from rotting and getting infected.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ taoɔ hulu la ni fa babaoo koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Ni kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ akafite ni helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: What is chewing hole marks into the middle of my young maize stems and leaving small brown dirt behind?
ga: Mɛni ji nakai bu ni atsɔ mli yɛ mibi lɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni shĩɔ muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ? Sɛɛ?

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the plant during the day and chews through young leaves before they unfold.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and becoming crinkly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids that feed on plant sap and spread plant viruses that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni egbɛɔ tso mli helai ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ lɛ eshwaa

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or when air temperatures get too high for pollen to successfully fertilize the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa tsɔ bɔ ni pollen lɛ nyɛŋ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crop seeds very close together so I can fit more plants on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ? Bɔni afee ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting too close forces crops to fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in tall, weak plants that produce tiny fruits or low yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii bibii loo nɔ ni baa shi lɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much even if I add fertilizer to the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui waa nɛkɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔji amli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than domestic crops and aggressively steal the fertilizer, moisture, and sunlight meant for your plants, effectively starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe shia tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ waa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are spoiled before I dig them out of the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ egbo dani mafo amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: You can inspect the leaves and stems above ground. If the leaves turn yellow, curl up, or show dark patches, or if the main stem looks dry and swollen with cracks, it is a strong sign that the roots underground are diseased or rotting.
ga: Obaanyɛ okwɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛbɔle amɛhe, loo amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo kɛji tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni efuu ni egbɛ eshwa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ loo amɛmiifite.

english: How do I know if a mango fruit is diseased while it is still hanging on the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mango yɛ hela be mli ni eyɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Look for small dark, sunken spots, oozing sap, or whitish powdery coating on the skin of the fruit while it hangs. A healthy growing mango will have smooth, clean skin without black soft spots.
ga: Taomɔ hei bibii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ ni ebote mli, nu ni hoɔ, loo nɔ ko ni yɔɔ futafuta ni tamɔ powda yɛ aduawai lɛ anɔ be mli ni efoɔ lɛ. Mango ni eda lɛ yɛ hewolo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni he tse ni ŋmɔlɔ diji bɛ he.

english: How can I know if my maize crop is sick while it is still growing in my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmã lɛ hela mɔ lɛ be mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lolo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Check for pale yellow stripes on the leaves, reddish spots, or husks that turn dry and brown long before the cob is fully formed. Chewed leaves or rolled-up leaf centers also indicate pest infestation.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ, ŋmeii tsuji, loo ŋmeii ni egbi ni etsɔ ŋmeii be kakadaŋŋ dani ŋmeii lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kwraa. Baai ni ashɛre loo baai lɛ ateŋ ni afolɔ mli lɛ hu tsɔɔ akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko eba.

english: How do I spot black pod disease on my cocoa trees before it spreads to all my pods?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana black pod hela yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ dani egbɛ eshwa mi-pod lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: Look closely at green cocoa pods for tiny brown spots that rapidly spread until the entire pod turns dark black. During wet weather, a white powdery mold will also appear on the blackened surface.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ jogbaŋŋ. koni ana ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya aahu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ ediŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmei ni ji powdery mildew lɛ hu jeɔ kpo yɛ hei ni edɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants wilt during the afternoon even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: When a plant wilts in wet soil, it usually means disease-causing fungi or bacteria have attacked its roots. Damaged roots lose the ability to drink water, causing the leaves to droop under hot sunlight.
ga: Kɛ tsei gboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ etutua shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛnu nu dɔŋŋ. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ enɔ.

english: How can I tell if my plantain tree is sick before it produces a bunch?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji midumɔwui lɛ hela mɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃?

english: Watch the leaves at the top of the tree. If older leaves rapidly turn yellow and snap downward along the trunk while green, or if new leaves emerge small, bunched, and crumpled, the tree is suffering from a wilt or viral disease.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Kɛji akɛ baai momoi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ oya ni amɛkumɔ tso lɛ shishi be mli ni amɛji ŋmɔŋ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ baai heei lɛ ji bibii Ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ yɛ jwɛi amli ni abɔle amɛhe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye ŋmɔtɔ loo hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my green tomatoes turning black while still ripening on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishigbɛ naagbee lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ be mli ni wain tso lɛ ekwɛ̃ lolo lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom end rot. It happens when the plant cannot transport enough calcium to the developing fruit, usually caused by irregular watering during hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aya aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why do my yams look healthy when I dig them up but start rotting a few days later in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ kɛ́ mifo mli shi ebɔi fitemɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams often carry tiny invisible fungal spores or small surface cuts from harvesting tools. Once stored in a warm, dark, or poorly ventilated space, those hidden wounds quickly develop into full rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii yɛ sweet potato mli. ni anaaa loo ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ni afo yɛ nɔ kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔ nibii amli lɛ Kɛ́ akɛto he ko ni hulutsoo, duŋ, loo kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ lɛ Pilamɔi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baatsɔ oya.

english: How can I prevent my harvested fresh peppers from soft-rotting immediately after picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-peppers ni mikpa ehee lɛ naa koni ekafite amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Harvest your peppers early in the morning while it is cool, avoid harvesting wet peppers, handle them carefully to prevent skin bruises, and store them in open, well-ventilated woven baskets rather than sealed bags.
ga: Kpaa o-peppers lɛ leebi be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni efɔ lɛ ni okɛtoɔ he lɛ he. Okɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ koni hewolo lɛ akatswa. ni akɛtoɔ tsɛnsi ko ni akpɛ́ ni agbele mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli lɛ mli. Mohu ɔ, ngɔ kɛ to kotoku ko nɛ a tsi mi ɔ mi.

english: How can I tell if my stored dried corn is infected with dangerous mold?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui?

english: Check for a grayish, greenish, or white powdery dust clinging to the grains, or a strong musty smell. If the stored corn feels warm to the touch or clumped together, mold is actively growing.
ga: Kwɛmɔ kɛji sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ, eŋɔli, loo eyɛŋ ko yɛ ni ekpɛtɛ ŋmãa lɛ he loo ŋmɔtɔ ni naa wa ko yɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ nuɔ he akɛ edɔ kɛji akɛ ota he loo ebɔle ehe lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ miida oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot handle direct heat and heavy sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantain around your young cocoa creates a umbrella-like leaf cover that keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ dɔlɛ ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni ooodu yɛ O-cocoa tso bibioo lɛ he Ehaa baai ni tamɔ umbrella ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and carry heavy fruit heads, making them top-heavy. Cutting off extra suckers around the base, building soil mounds around the main trunk, or using wooden stakes for support keeps the stem stable during heavy winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ aduawai ayitsei ni tsii. cause a lot weight Afoɔ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni bɔleɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he, ni afeɔ gɔŋ ko ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ he, loo akɛ tsei ni akɛfiɔ sɛɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii. Koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli

english: How far apart should I space my maize seeds when planting so I get bigger cobs?
ga: Esa akɛ mafo ŋmãa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli kɛji midu koni manyɛ maná ŋmãa wuji.

english: Maize seeds grow best when planted about 75 centimeters between rows and 40 centimeters between hills. If you plant seeds too close together, the stems crowd each other and compete for water and nutrients, leading to tiny or incomplete cobs.
ga: Abɛi dumɔwui lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ aaafee sɛntimita 75 yɛ ŋmeii ateŋ kɛ sɛntimita 40 yɛ gɔji ateŋ. Kɛji odu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, amɛbaakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ tsei lɛ buaa amɛhe naa ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii ni eshɛɛɛ he lɛ baa.

english: Which plantain suckers are best for me to dig up and plant in a new garden?
ga: Mɛɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ mafo ni madu yɛ abɔɔ hee mli?

english: Choose 'sword suckers', which have thick bases and narrow, spear-shaped leaves. Avoid 'water suckers' with broad leaves, because sword suckers have larger underground food reserves that help the plant root quickly and produce heavy fruit bunches.
ga: Halamɔ 'sword shoot' ni yɔɔ shishi ni mli tse kɛ baai ni mli tse, ni tamɔ lance. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ ‘nu ŋmei’ ni yɔɔ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ he, ejaakɛ klante ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi niyenii jɛɛhei wuji. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii ni tsii.

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my maize plants?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ awo ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmãa?

english: Apply the first dose of NPK fertilizer about two weeks after planting when shoots emerge to build strong roots. Put a second dose of nitrogen fertilizer (Urea) when the plants reach knee height to support quick growth and healthy cob formation.
ga: Okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ awo mli aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ beni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo ni amɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa. Okɛ nitrogen fertilizer (urea) awo mli shii enyɔ nɔ beni tsei lɛ eshɛ amɛnaji ahe lɛ koni eye ebua amɛdalɛ oya kɛ cob ni mli wa lɛ feemɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds have hardy, wild roots that quickly absorb small amounts of water and surface soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early in the season prevents them from stealing vital nutrients and sunlight away from your young crop stems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni wa, adebɔɔ mli. Ekɛ nu fioo kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ mra yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ otso bibii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh leaves of my young maize stems, and how do I fix it?
ga: Buji bibii ni ayeɔ Mɛni yɔɔ mi-baby ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai heei lɛ anɔ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar hiding inside the central leaf funnel. Applying recommended extension insecticides or dropping clean wood ash into the leaf funnels early in the morning kills the caterpillars.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ tsu nii loo okɛ tso sũ ni he tse awo baai lɛ amli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the branch during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cool, dark, and damp shade. Pruning dense branch foliage and harvesting ripe cocoa pods frequently lets sunlight and dry air flow through the tree canopy to stop fungal growth.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ. Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ yibii ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ni afolɔ kɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ ni akpaa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ yiteŋ koni ekɛtsi ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why do my cassava roots get woody and tough to cook if I leave them in the soil too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ tsei ni ewaa akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch while growing, but after 12 to 18 months in the ground, the root tissue starts converting starch into tough wood fiber. Harvesting at the right maturity time ensures soft, easy-to-cook tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ hiɛɔ starch mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ, shi kɛ́ amɛye nyɔji 12 kɛyashi 18 yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ pɛ. Shishifã lɛ jeɔ shishi etsakeɔ starch efeɔ tso fibers ni wa. Kɛ́ akpa yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ ni ahomɔ hu afee mlɛo.

english: Blossoms drop when plant stems experience extreme heat stress or sudden dry soil spells. Keeping the soil consistently moist with organic mulch around the base stops the plants from dropping flowers so fruit can set.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩ trukaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni akɛ organic mulch tsuɔ nii yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ akagbee shi bɔni afee ni aduawai lɛ anyɛ ama shi.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy so quickly after I put it in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya beni mikɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize grains naturally hold internal moisture even after harvesting. If they are bagged before reaching the proper low moisture level, the trapped dampness creates a warm environment that causes mold and fungi to grow rapidly.
ga: Abele mli ŋmeii lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ po. Kɛji akɛ awo kotoku lɛ mli obɔ dani eshɛ he ni hulutsoo be ni baa shi fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ, hulutsoo ni amɔmɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ yaa hiɛ oya.

english: Why does my rice break into tiny pieces when it goes through the milling machine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ etsɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice grains become brittle if they are left to dry out too much in the sun or harvested too late. When the grain is too dry or unevenly dried, it cannot withstand the pressure of milling and cracks easily.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli tsɔ loo akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbi tsɔ loo amɛgbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ Enyɛŋ edamɔ nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli baa lɛ naa ni ebaagbala oya.

english: How do I know that my standing maize crop is fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmãa ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: When maize is fully mature, the leaves and husks turn brown and dry, and a small dark layer (black layer) forms at the tip where the kernel attaches to the cob, signaling that the grain has stopped growing.
ga: Kɛji ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ Baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ. Ni fã bibioo ko ni tsuɔ (black layer) baa yɛ naagbee he ni dumɔwui lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekpa kwɛ̃mɔ.

english: Why are insect pests still attacking my stored maize even though I dried it under the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi-ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ migbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Sun-drying reduces outer moisture, but insects can still survive if the core moisture is high or if the storage container is not airtight. Proper drying combined with clean, sealed storage prevents pests from feeding and multiplying.
ga: Hulu ni tsoɔ lɛ haa kponɔgbɛ hulutsoo baa shi. Shi kooloi bibii baanyɛ ahi shi lolo kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ fa loo kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛɛɛ abote nɔ ni akɛtoɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ agbi jogbaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ he ni he tse ni atsĩ naa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akaye nii ni amɛshwere.

english: Why do some traders reject my maize bags because of a bad smell or discoloration?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayelɔi komɛi kpooɔ mi-abele kotokui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔ gbonyo loo amɛhe su ni tsakeɔ lɛ hewɔ?

english: Discoloration and bad odor usually mean the maize was affected by aflatoxins or rot, caused by damp storage conditions. Buyers reject this because it is dangerous for human consumption and animal feed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ su ni tsakeɔ kɛ ŋmãa ni ehiii lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ aflatoxins loo ŋmãa lɛ efite. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nibii ni akɛtoɔ mli ni mli efɔ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ enɛ akɛ eji oshara kɛha adesai aniyenii kɛ kooloi aniyenii.

english: Why are buyers offering me a lower price for my harvested rice even when my bags are full?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kɛ jara ni baa shi haa kɛha mikpamɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mibaagi lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Buyers look beyond quantity; they check grain quality. If your rice has too many broken grains, husk remnants, or stones mixed in, it fails basic market standards, which lowers its market value.
ga: Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ fa ha lɛ nɔ Amɛkwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmaa lɛ hi ha. Kɛji akɛ o-rice lɛ yɛ dumɔwui ni ekumɔ, ŋmeii bibii, loo tɛi babaoo yɛ mli. ehoŋ shishijee jarayeli mlai lɛ ahe Enɛ baaha jarayeli jara lɛ aba shi.

english: Who sets the official rules for how clean and dry my maize or rice must be before selling?
ga: Namɔ woɔ mlai ni maŋ lɛ woɔ akɛ esa akɛ mi-ŋmãa loo mi-ŋmãa lɛ he atse ni egbi dani ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: In Ghana, the Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) sets the national quality and safety standards for agricultural produce like maize and rice to ensure fair trade and consumer safety.
ga: Yɛ Ghana lɛ, Ghana Standards Authority (GSA) lɛ toɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he mlai kɛha okwaayeli nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa. Enɛ ji koni jarayeli ni ja kɛ jarayelɔi ashweshweeshwefeemɔ aba.

english: What standard must my maize or rice meet if I want to produce grains that can be exported abroad?
ga: Mɛɛ shishitoo mlai esa akɛ mi ŋmãa loo mi ŋmãa lɛ ashɛ he kɛji miisumɔ ni mafee ŋmãa ni abaanyɛ akɛmaje maŋsɛɛ?

english: To sell abroad, your grains must meet international standards verified by bodies like the Ghana Standards Authority. This means maintaining very low moisture levels, zero pest contamination, and no harmful chemical or aflatoxin residues.
ga: Kɛji oosumɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ kɛya maŋsɛɛ Esa akɛ oŋmaa lɛ ashɛ majimaji ateŋ mlai ni nitsumɔhei tamɔ Ghana Standards Authority lɛ kwɛɔ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ esa akɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi waa lɛ mli. Zero pest mujiwoo Ni tsofa ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo aflatoxin ni eshwɛ bɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I just measure and sell my harvested grains using any local bucket or sack available?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ maŋ lɛ mli tsɛnsii loo kotokui ni yɔɔ lɛ susuɔ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ he ni mihɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Unstandardized containers vary in size, leading to unfair pricing for either you or the buyer. Selling by standardized weight (kilograms) based on approved measurement guidelines ensures you get the exact value for your yield.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni jeee nɔ ni sa lɛ dalɛi yɛ srɔtoi. Enɛ haa jara ni ejaaa baa bo loo mɔ ni heɔ lɛ nɔ. Nihɔɔmɔ damɔ tsiimɔ ni sa (kilogram) nɔ taakɛ susumɔ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ onine shɛɔ sɛɛnamɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ nɔ ni ojieɔ lɛ kpo lɛ nɔ.

english: How does ensuring my grains are properly cleaned and dried help me get a better price at the market?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmaa lɛ ni mikɛbaatsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni migbi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara kpakpa yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Clean, dry grains resist spoilage and meet national quality standards. Traders pay higher prices for standardized grains because they can be stored longer without loss and sold to formal markets or processors.
ga: Nibii ni he tse ni egbi lɛ teɔ shi ewoɔ fitemɔ ni eshɛɔ maŋ lɛ mli nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe. Jarayelɔi woɔ ŋmaa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ jara babaoo. Ejaakɛ abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko elaajeee. ni ahɔ̃ɔ ahaa jara nɔ loo ahaa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing of the bottom leaves is a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen. The maize plant moves available nitrogen from its older lower leaves up to support new growth at the top, showing that the crop needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Etsɔɔ kɛji tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does grass growing close to my crops slow down their growth even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ miigbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Weeds and grass have aggressive roots that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your crops, starving your plants even if moisture is present.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ moŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl upward during the hot afternoon and open back up in the evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛgbeleɔ amɛhe ekoŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves in intense heat to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, which helps them conserve internal moisture and avoid drying out.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ emli, ni ehaaa egbi.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit during very hot periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat sterilizes tomato pollen, preventing flowers from being pollinated. Unpollinated flowers drop off because the plant cannot turn them into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa gbeɔ tomato mli ŋmeii. Etsiɔ fɔfɔi anaa koni amɛkafee pollination Fɔfɔi ni pollination bɛ mli lɛ baagbee shi ejaakɛ tso lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ aduawai.

english: This pattern is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Infected leaves cannot produce energy efficiently, leading to smaller root yields.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ su nɛɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ nyɛŋ afee hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shishifãi ni ajieɔ lɛ shi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop small green pods long before they mature into full pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? be kakadaŋŋ dani etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa?

english: This is known as cherelle wilt, a natural response where the cocoa tree sheds excess pods it cannot support due to a lack of water, shade, or soil nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ cherelle wilt, ni ji adebɔɔ mli hetoo ko ni baa beni kookoo tso ko shwieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ akwɛ nɔ yɛ nu, hulutsoo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing short, twisted, and small even though the leaves above ground look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato tsei lɛ amli tsei lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛtsiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛfeɔ bibii eyɛ mli akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe wa moŋ?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when the soil underneath is too hard and compacted for roots to expand, or when tiny worms called nematodes attack the growing tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa ni ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ tutua ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why does local maize take much longer to harvest compared to the improved seeds sold at the farm shop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa heɔ be babaoo dani akpaa kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shwapoi amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Improved seed varieties are bred to grow faster and flower early so they can produce full grains quickly, helping farmers harvest successfully even during short rainy seasons.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ mra bɔni afee ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni eyi obɔ oya. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa okwaafoi ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kukuoo lɛ mli po.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have wide leaves that create shade and keep the soil cool, protecting young cocoa trees until they are strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and rotting so quickly in my storage barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ni mikpaa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ kɛ fitemɔ oya yɛ mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams rot and sprout rapidly when stored in hot, poorly ventilated places or when they suffer cuts during harvest, which allows heat and rot-causing organisms to enter the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto hei ni mli edɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa bɛ mli. aloo kɛ́ afolɔ amɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli. Enɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ nibii ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ boteɔ bulb lɛ mli.

english: How long will it take for my new plantain crops to give me a harvest after planting?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani akpa mi dumɔwui heei lɛ beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains generally take about 9 to 12 months (roughly a year) from the time you plant suckers until the fruits mature and are ready for your first harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantains heɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 (aaafee afi) kɛjɛɔ be mli ni oduɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni aduawai lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ.

english: Do I need to buy thousands of plantain suckers right at the start to have a successful farm?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mahe plantain tsei akpei abɔ kɛjɛ shishijee koni miŋmɔ lɛ aye omanye?

english: No, you do not need to start very big. You can begin with a small plot of a few hundred suckers, and as they grow, they will produce new offshoots that you can use to expand your farm for free.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni okɛfee nɔ ko wulu. Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aje shishi. kɛ ŋmeii bibii ohai fioo Ni kɛ́ eda lɛ Amɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii heei ni obaanyɛ okɛtsu nii ni okɛgbala oŋmɔ lɛ mli yaka.

english: Where will I get new plantain suckers when I want to start a second farm field?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ mana plantain tsei heei yɛ be mli ni miisumɔ ni mabɔi ŋmɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ?

english: Once your first plantain farm matures, the parent plants will naturally produce young shoots (suckers) around their bases. You can dig these up and transplant them directly into your new field.
ga: Kɛji oklɛŋklɛŋ plantain ŋmɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ Tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ baawo ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) yɛ eshishigbɛ he lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Obaanyɛ otsa enɛɛmɛi ni okɛwo oŋmɔ hee lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How many years can a single plantain farm keep producing food before I need to replant it completely?
ga: Niyenii enyiɛ plantain ŋmɔ kome baanyɛ ajie dani ehe baahia ni adu lɛ kwraa ekoŋŋ?

english: A well-managed plantain farm can remain productive for around 3 to 4 years, as new sucker shoots continuously grow up to replace the harvested main stems.
ga: Plantain ŋmɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii aaafee afii 3 kɛyashi 4 be mli ni ŋmeii heei yaa nɔ amɛdaraa koni amɛye tso titri ni akpa lɛ najiaŋ lɛ.

english: How can I make sure I am always harvesting plantains instead of waiting for everything to mature at once?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mikpa plantains be fɛɛ be moŋ fe ni mamɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni ekwɛ̃ shikome?

english: You can stagger your planting schedule across different sections of land. By planting fields at different times, one field will be maturing and yielding fruit just as you finish harvesting another.
ga: Obaanyɛ oja odumɔ he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli owo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hei srɔtoi kɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni ooodu yɛ bei srɔtoi amli lɛ nɔ. ŋmɔ kome baakwɛ ni ewo yibii tamɔ bɔ ni ogbe ŋmɔ kroko mli nikpamɔ naa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Is it very expensive to buy plantain suckers when setting up a small farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani ejara wa waa akɛ ooohe dumɔwui a-sucker beni atoɔ ŋmɔ bibioo ko shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers are relatively low-cost items, often sold for small change (pesewas) per sucker, making it affordable for new farmers to get started with a modest budget.
ga: Plantain tsei lɛ ji nɔ ko ni jara waaa kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ kɛtsakeɔ shika fioo (pesewa) yɛ tso kome mli, ni enɛ haa okwaafoi heei jeɔ shishi kɛ shika fioo ko.

english: If I plant a few hundred plantain suckers, will it be enough to feed my family and still make money?
ga: Kɛ midu plantain dumɔwui ohai fioo komɛi Ani ebaashɛ bɔ ni sa ni mikɛkwɛ weku ko ni maná shika lolo?

english: Yes, even a medium-sized plot of around 800 plantain plants can yield enough harvest to comfortably feed your household while leaving a healthy surplus to sell at the local market.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji mlɛo po ni plantain tsei aaafee 800 yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akpa nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha oweku lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ashiɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ hewalɛ koni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: What happens to a plantain tree after I cut down its bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni baa dumɔwui lɛ anɔ beni mifo ŋmeii lɛ amli sɛɛ?

english: The main plantain stem dies after bearing fruit, but it leaves behind several baby shoots (suckers) around its base that will grow up to produce the next bunches.
ga: Plantain tso titri lɛ gboɔ beni ewo yibii sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, e siɔ tso bibihi (tso) nɛ a bɔleɔ sisi ɔ nɛ wa kɛ peeɔ panicle nɛ nyɛɛ se ɔ.

english: What is the best way to expand my farming business year after year without taking big financial risks?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ maha mi okwaayeli nitsumɔ lɛ aya hiɛ afi fɛɛ afi ni mikɛ mihe wooo shika he oshara kpele mli?

english: Start with a small, manageable plot using your initial savings, harvest the crops for income, and use the free seeds or suckers generated from that first plot to establish larger fields every season.
ga: Je shishi kɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko. Abaanyɛ akɛ shika ni ato shishijee lɛ atsu nakai he nii. Kpaa ŋmɔshi nibii koni ona shika Ni okɛ dumɔwui loo ŋmeii ni aheee nɔ ko ni abɔ kɛjɛ klɛŋklɛŋ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ atsu nii ni okɛfee ŋmɔji wuji daa be.

english: How will I know when my plantain field has reached full maturity?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-plantain lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa?

english: A plantain field reaches full maturity within a year when the stalks bear full, heavy bunches of green plantains that have filled out and are ready for harvesting.
ga: Plantains ŋmɔ ko baashɛ shweremɔ he yɛ afi kome mli beni ŋmeii lɛ yɛ plantains ŋmɔji babaoo ni eyi obɔ ni esa akɛ akpa lɛ.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves usually mean your maize lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen in the soil, or it is being attacked by pests like fall armyworms. Adding organic manure or fertilizer helps restore green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ o-ŋmã lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. aloo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms tutuaa lɛ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli Humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ekoŋŋ.

english: How deep should I bury my cassava stem cuttings when planting them?
ga: Kɛ́ oodu lɛ, te esa akɛ afu ŋmei niji lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ?

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 5 to 10 centimeters deep into loose soil at an angle. Burying them too deep makes it hard for tubers to expand, while planting them too shallow causes them to dry out quickly.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse nɔ ni mli kwɔ sɛntimitai 5 kɛyashi 10 yɛ koŋ nɔ. Kɛ́ ofu mli tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha bulb lɛ akɛ ebaagbɛ eshwa. yɛ be mli ni dumɔ ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha bulb lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why does my soil produce smaller harvests every time I farm on the same plot without letting it rest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo be fɛɛ be ni matsu ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ he nii ni mihaaa ehi shi lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth as they grow. Farming the same land repeatedly without adding manure or leaving it to rest drains the soil of those nutrients, making it weak over time.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Okwaayeli ni afeɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli loo ashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, be ni be shwieɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow tall and thin without bearing good fruit when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni yibii kpakpai baaa kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space ensures it gets the food and light it needs to produce strong yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni enáa niyenii kɛ la ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed their flowers when the days get extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi beni gbii lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and prevents proper pollination. When flowers fail to pollinate, the plant drops them to conserve water and energy for survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaaa amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ. Beni fɔfɔii lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee pollination lɛ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔii koni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi shi.

english: How can I tell if my sweet potatoes are mature and ready for harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Sweet potatoes are usually ready when the vines start turning yellow and drying up. You can carefully dig up one test plant to check if the tubers have reached a good size before harvesting the whole field.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ ayeɔ kɛ́ wain tsei lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbi. Obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso kome ni akɛkaa nii lɛ he nii koni okwɛ kɛji bulb lɛ dalɛ sa dani okpa ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields in their first generation only. If you save and replant those harvested seeds, the new plants will lose their vigor, resulting in smaller yields and weaker crops.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ mli pɛ. Kɛji okɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ to ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei heei ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii hu baa shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly soak up any available water and soil food. Removing them early stops them from stealing vital nutrients and light away from your growing crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛmɔmɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya. Amɛjiemɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju niyenii ni he hiaa kɛ la kɛjɛ otsei ni miida lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my harvested grains get full of insects and rot so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni akpa lɛ amli lɛ mli eyi kɛ ŋmeii ni efiteɔ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Grains spoil quickly if they are stored before they are completely dry, or if they are kept in damp rooms. Drying your grains thoroughly in the sun before storing them in clean, airtight containers prevents mold and insect damage.
