ga: Nibii ni ŋmaa fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛto dani amɛgbi kwraa. Aloo kɛji akɛ akɛto tsu ko ni mli edɔ mli Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli dani akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi akafite amɛ.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tips of older maize plants usually means the plant lacks nitrogen. Nitrogen is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow fast, and heavy rains often wash it deeper into the soil where roots cannot reach.
ga: Yellowing ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei ni egbɔ lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ, nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara oya. Ni bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nitrogen yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me that planting cowpeas makes my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ, kɛ́ midu tsina ŋmeii lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans have small nodules on their roots that host friendly bacteria. These bacteria take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as free fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans yɛ ŋmeii bibii. yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni ji he ni helatsɛmɛi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo lɛ hiɔ Nɛkɛ helatsɛmɛi nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard, woody, and watery when I wait too long to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei ni nu yɔɔ mli beni mimɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani mikpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for the plant's survival. When the plant gets too old or when fresh rains start after a dry spell, the plant uses up its stored starch to grow new leaves, leaving behind tough fiber and water in the tuber.
ga: Cassava shishifãi toɔ starch kɛha tso lɛ wala. Kɛ́ tso lɛ egbɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be ko sɛɛ. Tso lɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai heei. Eshiɔ tsɔji ni shwieɔ shi kɛ nu yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: Why must I push wooden stakes into the ground for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ tso nɔ mawo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to spread out their leaves to catch as much sunlight as possible to build big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing rot and disease while maximizing leaf exposure to the sun.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbala amɛbaai lɛ amli koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai anaa yɛ be mli ni baai lɛ naa hulu la fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Those small shoots, called suckers, steal food, water, and sunlight from the main stem. By removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones, all the energy goes into making a larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Atsɛɔ nakai ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ ŋmeii. Koni amɛju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ tsɔne lɛ mli. Enɛ jieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni eshwɛɔ ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Akɛ nakai hewalɛ lɛ fɛɛ feɔ plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, extreme drought, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its own life rather than putting energy into growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ latsaa ni naa wa he. hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tso lɛ baashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛdu aduawai

english: This is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium while the fruit is growing rapidly. It is usually caused by irregular watering—going from very dry soil to very wet soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ aná calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa nɔ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ waa nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and drop leaves during the harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have soft leaves and shallow roots that cannot tolerate strong, direct sunlight and dry harmattan winds. They require temporary shade plants, like plantains, to shield them and trap moisture until they mature.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ kɛ Harmat kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashi amɛbaadara.

english: Why do my cabbages stay small and refuse to form tight heads when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage lɛ ji bibii ni etswaaa shi shiŋŋ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded together, their roots compete for water and nutrients in the soil while their leaves fight for sunlight. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough resources to form a full head.
ga: Kɛ́ abua ŋmɔshi nibii anaa lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la he akaŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe he ni sa lɛ ha lɛ, ebaaha ana nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛma nitsumɔhe lɛ kwraa.

english: Why do the leaves of my okra plants get full of tiny holes right after the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ eyi kɛ buji bibii beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tiny holes are caused by leaf-eating pests like flea beetles that multiply rapidly when fresh foliage grows after the first rains. Weeds around your farm often host these insects before they move onto your okra.
ga: Bui bibii lɛ jɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ baai, tamɔ ŋmeii, ni mli lɛɛɔ oya kɛji baai heei kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Bei pii lɛ, jwɛi ni bɔle oŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ hiɛɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfãa kɛyaa okra lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight and need moisture to survive. Plantains grow very fast and have wide leaves that provide immediate shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa establishes itself.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi, ni ehe miihia ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛhi shi. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know the best time to plant my maize when the rains start?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: It is best to wait until the rain falls steadily two or three times so the ground is deeply soaked. Planting after just one light rain can cause seeds to sprout and die if a dry spell follows.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Shikome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be ba.

english: Yellow and curled leaves are usually caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is carried by small insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant stem varieties prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔlɔ baa. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ helai ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same spot drains specific food from the soil and attracts corn-specific pests. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts essential nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni egbalaa abɛi pɔtɛɛ kooloi. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba sũ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes tiny holes in the leaves of my young corn plants and how can I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa?

english: This damage is often caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the center leaves. Checking your fields early allows you to spray recommended treatments or apply neem extract before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ehaa okɛ tsofa shwieɔ nɔ tamɔ bɔ ni atsɔɔ lɛ loo okɛ neem mli nu tsuɔ nii dani efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: When crops grow too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant grows strong, healthy, and yields larger fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ dara ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa, enáa hewalɛ ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: When is the right time to put fertilizer on my crops so it doesn't waste?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni amɛkafite?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a moderate rain, but not right before a heavy downpour. Wet soil helps roots absorb the nutrients, while heavy rain washes the fertilizer away from the farm.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Shi esaaa akɛ ofeɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔji amli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I stop the soil around my vegetable beds from drying out too fast during hot weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Covering the bare ground around your crop stems with dry grass or straw—known as mulching—blocks direct sun. This holds water in the soil longer and keeps the roots cool.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle otso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni eye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why do some of the seeds I saved from last year's harvest fail to sprout after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mito kɛjɛ nyɛsɛɛ afi nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekomɛi fite beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds can lose their strength if stored in warm, damp places or damaged by insects. Storing seeds in sealed containers with dry ash in a cool spot preserves their ability to germinate.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ baanyɛ afite hewalɛ kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo, amɛhe edɔ, loo kooloi fite amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni atsĩ mli ni sũ ni egbi yɔɔ mli lɛ mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛnyɛ amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it necessary to trim some of the branches off my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ tomato tso lɛ niji komɛi lɛ?

english: Removing side branches allows the plant to send its energy directly into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes instead of wasting food on extra leaves and thin stems.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ esɛɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite niyenii yɛ baai kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Something is eating holes in my cocoa leaves, but I cannot see any animals on the farm. Could this be witchcraft?
ga: Noko ye mi-kookoo baai lɛ. Shi minaaa kooloo ko yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ani enɛ baanyɛ afee majik?

english: No, it is not witchcraft. Many cocoa pests like mirids and caterpillars feed at night or hide under leaves during the day. Inspecting the undersides of leaves and spraying approved insecticides will control these hidden insects.
ga: Dabi, jeee majik ni. Kookoo mli kooloi babaoo, tamɔ mirids kɛ caterpillars, tsuɔ nii gbɛkɛ loo amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ baai ashishi yɛ shwane mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ.

english: My cocoa trees are dying, and people in my village say a relative put a spiritual curse on my farm. How can I know the real cause?
ga: Mi koko tso lɛ miigbo. Ni mɛi ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ kɛɛ akɛ miwekunyo ko elomɔ mumɔ ko yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli. Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Trees die from physical problems such as pest attacks, root diseases, or parasitic plants, not spiritual curses. An extension officer can examine the roots, trunk, and leaves to identify the exact disease or insect causing the damage.
ga: Gbɔmɔtsoŋ naagbai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, shishifãi, loo tsei ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ gbeɔ tsei, shi jeee mumɔŋ loomɔi. Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ shishifãi, tsei lɛ ashishifãi, kɛ tsei lɛ ahe baai koni amɛna hela loo kooloo ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How can I tell if insects are destroying my cocoa pods or if the pods are just rotting naturally?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miifite mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ loo kɛji akɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifite yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Insect damage leaves small puncture holes, dark spots, or sticky sap leaking from the pod. Fungal rot usually turns the entire pod brown or black and covers it with a whitish dust without any bite marks.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ mli baa ji ŋmeii bibii, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ, loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi. Nɔ ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ pod lɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ, fungal rot lɛ haa pod lɛ fɛɛ feɔ blɔfo loo ediŋŋ ni sũ yɛŋ ehà nɔ, ni ŋmɔlɔ he okadi ko bɛ he.

english: What causes the young shoots and bark of my cocoa trees to look burnt and cracked?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cacao tsei kɛ amɛhewolo lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni egbɛ eshwa?

english: This is caused by mirids (also called capsids), which are small insects that suck sap from young cocoa branches and inject a poison that burns the plant tissue. Spraying approved insecticides prevents this damage.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji mirids (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ capsids), ni ji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu kɛjɛɔ kookoo niji bibii amli ni amɛwoɔ poison ni shãa tso lɛ mli fãji. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ naa.

english: Why does my cocoa farm get so many pests when I let the bush and shade trees grow very thick?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ lɛ naa tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo nɛkɛ beni mihaa jwɛi kɛ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ daraa babaoo lɛ?

english: Overgrown trees and tall weeds create excessive shade and trap damp air, creating a dark, wet environment where insects and fungal diseases multiply rapidly. Clearing weeds and trimming excess shade keeps pests away.
ga: Tsei ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ jwɛi kakadaji haa hulutsoo fe nine baa ni amɛmɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli efɔ. Enɛ haa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ duŋ ni edɔ. he ni kooloi kɛ ŋmeii helai baagbɛ amɛshwã oya Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa.

english: Will cutting back overgrown branches on my cocoa trees reduce the number of pods I harvest?
ga: Ani niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: No, proper pruning actually increases your harvest. Removing extra branches opens the tree canopy to sunlight, which encourages fresh flowering and prevents fungal diseases from destroying your pods.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa onibii ni owoɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Kɛ́ ajie tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa hulu la baa tso lɛ nɔ. Enɛ woɔ fɔfɔi heei ahe hewalɛ ni ehaaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ akafite o-pods lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn completely black and dry up before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ kwraa ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛfeɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod Disease, a fungus that spreads in wet, overly shady conditions. Removing infected pods right away and weeding your farm improves air movement and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ tsɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ oya ni ojie jwɛi kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ aya hiɛ.

english: Is it okay to leave bad or rotten cocoa pods hanging on the tree until harvest time?
ga: Ani abaanyɛ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni efite loo efite lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛyashi kpamɔ be lɛ mli?

english: No, spoiled pods act as breeding grounds for pests and diseases that will spread to healthy pods nearby. You should pluck off spoiled pods immediately and bury them far from your cocoa trees.
ga: Dabi, ŋmeii ni egbo ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai fɔɔ yɛ. No baagbɛ eshwa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. Esa akɛ ojie ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni ofu amɛ kɛjɛ cacao tso lɛ he.

english: How often should I walk through my cocoa farm to check on my crop?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ matsɔ kookoo ŋmɔ mli koni makwɛ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: You should walk through your farm at least once a week. Regular checks allow you to catch insect attacks or diseases early before they cause severe damage to your entire crop.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, esa akɛ otsɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli. Kɛ́ okwɛ mli daa lɛ, onyɛɔ omɔ kooloi bibii loo helai fɛɛ helai. Na kɛjɛ shishijee dani ekɛ fitemɔ ni mli wa ba onibii fɛɛ nɔ.

english: What should I do first when I notice my cocoa trees are suddenly losing leaves and dropping pods?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee klɛŋklɛŋ kɛji trukaa lɛ mina akɛ Kookoo tso lɛ gbee shi ni ŋmeii lɛ gbee shi?

english: First, clear all heavy weeds and pluck off spoiled pods from the trees. Then, invite your local extension officer to inspect the farm so they can diagnose the exact pest or disease and advise you on the right remedy.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsii lɛ fɛɛ ni ojie ŋmeii ni egbo kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli. Nɔ ni tsa nɔ lɛ, fɔ̃ɔ oakutso lɛ mli nitsulɔ ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nine koni ebakwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ena tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ gbɛ ni ja ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa hela lɛ he

english: Why do my crops start wilting and drying up around December and January?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ December kɛyashi January mli lɛ?

english: During the dry season starting around Christmas and January, rainfall stops completely in many parts of Ghana. Without rain, crops lose moisture faster than they can draw it from the dry soil, causing them to wilt and struggle if you do not step in.
ga: Nuu be lɛ jeɔ shishi yɛ Blonya kɛ January beaŋ. Nugbɔ lɛ ekpa kwraa yɛ Ghana hei babaoo. Kɛ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fiteɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni abaanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ baagbi ni ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛji okɛ ohe wooo mli.

english: What happens to crops if they do not get any water during the dry months?
ga: Mɛni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji amɛnáaa nu yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli?

english: When crops go without water during hot, dry weather, their growth stalls, leaves turn yellow or crisp, and they cannot produce flowers or fruit, eventually leading to plant death.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tso lɛ baakpa dalɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni enyɛŋ ewo fɔfɔi loo aduawai Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji tso lɛ gbele yɛ naagbee.

english: Why is relying only on rain risky for my farm during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ ji oshara kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Rainfall in Ghana follows seasons, and during dry months like January, it does not rain at all. Relying only on rain means your crops will suffer severe water stress during these predictable dry gaps.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ji be kɛ bei amli. Ni yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ nɛɔ tamɔ January mli lɛ, nugbɔ enɛɛɛ kwraa. Nugbɔ pɛ tsɔɔ akɛ onibii lɛ baaná nu he haomɔ ni naa wa yɛ nɛkɛ hulutsoo bei ni atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ nɛɛ amli.

english: Can a crop recover if I start giving it water after it starts wilting from dry weather?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ kɛji mibɔi nu hamɔ beni eje shishi egbo kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, if the plant has only recently started to wilt from a lack of rain, giving it water right away helps it regain strength and continue growing successfully.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ ebɔi shwiemɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɛɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ oya lɛ baaye abua ni ená hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eya nɔ eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil dry out so quickly around the Christmas season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya yɛ Blonya beaŋ lɛ?

english: Around Christmas and January, rain stops while atmospheric heat and dry Harmattan winds increase, rapidly pulling all remaining moisture out of the topsoil.
ga: Yɛ Blonya kɛ January beaŋ Nugbɔ lɛ kpaɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya.

english: Should I give my crops water myself if the rain stops before harvest time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ nu kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa dani kpamɔ be lɛ shɛ?

english: Yes, when natural rains fail during critical growth stages, manually supplying water is necessary to keep the plants healthy until they reach maturity.
ga: Hɛɛ, beni adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa mɔ diɛŋtsɛ he miihia koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaashɛ amɛdalɛ he.

english: How do I know when my crops need me to fetch water for them instead of waiting for rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ehe baahia ni miyajie nu yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ lɛ?

english: When the topsoil feels completely dry and your crop leaves droop or look weak during dry months, it is a clear sign that natural rain will not come and you must supply water yourself.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nuɔ he akɛ egbi kwraa ni otso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi loo etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ. Eji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔ baaa ni ehe baahia ni bo diɛŋtsɛ okɛ nu aha.

english: Is it helpful to give my plants just a little water during the dry season, or does it have to be a lot?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaaha tsei nu fioo pɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ oha babaoo?

english: Even a small, consistent amount of water during dry periods keeps the soil moist around the roots, preventing the crop from drying out completely while waiting for better weather.
ga: Nu fioo po ni akɛwoɔ mli daa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi kwraa yɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa lɛ.

english: How can I keep my young plants alive during months when it never rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha mi dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ amli?

english: Young plants have shallow roots that cannot reach deep underground water, so you must help them by pouring water directly around their base during rainless months.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni oye obua tso lɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha he ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ. Yɛ tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Will my crop yield drop if the rain stops before my crops finish growing?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbe naa?

english: Yes, if the rain stops early, crops stop developing fruit or grains properly. Giving them extra water during dry spells ensures they stay healthy enough to produce a full harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa oya lɛ, Dumɔwui hu kpaɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa lɛ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ. Nu kroko ni akɛhaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa koni amɛkpa nii babaoo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain trees on the same farm as my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa shade and keeping the soil cool during its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo ŋmɔlɔ ni mli tse. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the food plants need to stay green and grow tall. Adding manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant regain its bright green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: When cassava stems are planted too close together, their roots fight each other underground for space, water, and food. Giving each plant proper distance allows the roots enough room and nutrients to swell into thick tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛ niyenii ni haa amɛshwereɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: Why do extension officers encourage me to plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ woɔ mi hewalɛ koni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas have a special ability to take nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them with maize naturally feeds the soil and helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Beans kɛ cowpeas yɛ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛjieɔ niyenii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa du ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant tomatoes on the exact same piece of land where I harvested pepper last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers are from the same plant family and share the same diseases and pests. Planting them in the same spot year after year allows pests and diseases to build up in the soil and attack your new crop.
ga: Tomato kɛ ŋmɔtɔ jɛ tso kome mli ni amɛyeɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kome. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ, ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote mli. Ebua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni etutuaa oŋmɔshi nibii heei lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry ground around my vegetable plants with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha hei ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ahe lɛ? Tsoi ni jwɛi loo baai ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, protects the ground from the hot sun so water does not evaporate quickly. It keeps the soil cool and moist for a longer time.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, nu lɛ efooo oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small stems growing out of my healthy tomato branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni jɛ mi tomato nine ni mli wa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Removing extra side branches, known as suckers, forces the tomato plant to send its food and water directly into growing bigger, healthier fruits instead of wasting energy on useless leaves.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ afã ni atsɛɔ lɛ shoo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ Enɛ baaha tomato tso lɛ amaje niyenii kɛ nu tɛ̃ɛ kɛya aduawai ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: Pepper flowers usually fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or too much fertilizer. When the plant feels stressed, it drops its flowers to save energy to stay alive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɛ tso lɛ nu he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaashwie fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi wala mli.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry stretch. If seeds sprout and the rain stops for weeks, the burning sun will dry out the soil and kill the delicate young seedlings.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa otsii babaoo. Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which love to hide inside the central funnel of young maize to feed on tender leaves. Identifying them early helps you spray or treat them before they destroy the whole plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Amɛyoomɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ okɛ tsofa afɔ amɛ nɔ loo otsa amɛ dani amɛfite tso muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does my land produce good maize for the first two years but yields very little by the third year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wo ŋmãa ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli shi ewoɔ fioo pɛ yɛ afi ni ji etɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every harvest season. Without adding manure, compost, or fertilizer back into the soil, the land becomes exhausted and cannot nourish new plants properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa kpamɔɔ be mli. Kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he ekoŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbɔjɔ ni enyɛɛɛ ekwɛ tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which acts as the main food for leaf growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant stay green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together so I can get more crops from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: If plants are overcrowded, their roots fight each other for water and soil food, while their leaves block each other from sunlight. Spacing them out gives every plant enough resources to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la he. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ baaha nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why do I see small holes in my maize leaves and sticky dirt inside the leaves at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? Muji ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ baa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ mli?

english: This is a sign of Fall Armyworm caterpillars eating your crops from the inside out. Checking your fields early and applying the right pest control before they multiply preserves your crop yield.
ga: Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ onibii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ. Odumɔi lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe gbɛjianɔtoo ni ja ni okɛaatsu nii dani amɛshwere lɛ baaye abua ni okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts together with maize helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa wo tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Legume plants like cowpeas and groundnuts have special root nodules that pull nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, feeding both themselves and nearby maize naturally.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛtsɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehe kɛ ŋmãa fɛɛ ni eyeɔ niyenii ni bɛŋkɛɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops curl up tightly during the middle of the day when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the direct sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water through evaporation.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ haaa hulu la lɛ aya nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ.

english: How do simple weeds hurt my maize crops when they are just growing nearby in the same field?
ga: Te jwɛi ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye mi ŋmãa lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ? Be ni adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ Yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, drinking water, and soil nutrients before your maize roots can reach them, leaving your main crop starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu ni anuɔ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli oya dani ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii titrii lɛ.

english: Why don't seeds saved from my last hybrid maize harvest grow as well when I plant them again next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ minaagbee ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni miduɔ amɛ ekoŋŋ yɛ afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred from two specific parent plants to produce high yields only in the first generation. Saving and replanting those seeds causes them to lose that special strength, resulting in uneven and smaller harvests.
ga: Akɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ fɔɔ tsei pɔtɛɛ enyɔ komɛi amli koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ ni akɛtoɔ ni aduɔ ekoŋŋ lɛ haa hewalɛ ni fa nɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee ni kɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni faaa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a short dry stretch before the main rains establish. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout and then dry up and die from lack of moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be kukuoo ko nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dani nugbɔ titri lɛ baa Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Odumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots start turning soft and brown quickly if I leave them in the ground too long after maturity?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ beni amɛdara lɛ?

english: Once cassava reaches full maturity, it stops growing actively. Leaving mature roots in wet soil subjects them to rots and soil insects that destroy the starch and spoil the tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ Ebaakpa shweremɔ. Kɛ́ ashi shishifãi ni edara lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛgboi ni shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: What is foundation seed, and why shouldn't I just buy that to plant directly in my commercial field?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwu shishitoo? Ni mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miheɔ nakai dumɔwu lɛ koni mikɛdu yɛ mi jarayeli ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Foundation seed is a high-purity seed produced specifically for seed growers to multiply into certified seeds. It is expensive and meant for seed production, not for growing grain to sell in the food market. Farmers should buy certified seed for regular planting.
ga: Shishijee dumɔwui ji dumɔwui ni he tse waa ni afee pɔtɛɛ aha dumɔwui akwɛlɔi koni amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli. Ejara wa ni afee kɛha dumɔwui afeemɔ. Jeee kɛha ŋmaa ni aduɔ koni ahɔ̃ɔ yɛ niyenii jarayeli hei. Esa akɛ okwaafoi ahe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli kɛha dumɔ daa.

english: Why do some of my saved maize seeds fail to grow even when I plant them immediately after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Saved seeds from previous harvests often carry hidden diseases, lack proper drying, or come from hybrid crops that lose their vigor after the first generation. Certified seeds are specially treated and tested to ensure high germination.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ yɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ. ŋmɔlɔ ni sa ni bɛ loo kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome ni hewalɛ baa shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell if seed grain bought from the local market will give me a good harvest on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ baawo yibii kpakpai yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Grains sold in general markets are usually intended for cooking, not planting, and often have low germination rates or mixed varieties. Certified seed packaged by registered seed dealers undergoes quality testing to guarantee crop health and uniform yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ jarayeli ŋmaa tsuɔ nii kɛhaa nihoomɔ, jeee kɛha shweremɔ, ni bei pii lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ loo amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe. Dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni dumɔwui jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo mli lɛ wo kotoku mli. Akwɛ bɔ ni ehi ha koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa.

english: How do I know when my crops have moved to the seed formation stage, and why does my field care need to change then?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ etee dumɔwui afeemɔ he lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni miŋmɔ mli nitsumɔ lɛ atsake lɛ?

english: Crops enter the seed formation stage when flowers, tassels, or pods appear. At this critical stage, the plant shifts its energy from growing leaves to filling seeds, making consistent water and nutrient supply essential to prevent poor grain filling.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ boteɔ dumɔwui lɛ afeemɔ mli kɛ́ fɔfɔi, ŋmeii, loo ŋmeii je kpo. Yɛ nɛkɛ be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, Tsei tsakeɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli kɛyaa dumɔwui ni woɔ mli ekoŋŋ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ehe hiaa ni aha nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yaa nɔ daa koni dumɔwui lɛ akayimɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it urgent to plant my maize right at the start of the rains instead of waiting a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni adu ŋmãa mra yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia ni amɛmɛ otsii babaoo lɛ

english: Planting immediately with the first stable rains ensures your crop makes full use of early soil nitrogen and sufficient moisture. Delayed planting leaves crops vulnerable to mid-season dry spells and heavy pest pressure.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nii kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ kpakpa lɛ ba pɛ kɛkɛ, ebaaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa aba. Dumɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ oshara yɛ be teŋgbɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni naa wa.

english: Young cocoa trees have soft, delicate leaves that burn easily under strong direct sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains next to young cocoa creates living umbrellas that protect the plants until their root systems mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe. Ehaa hulutsoo ni buɔ tso lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daa.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves but very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen in the soil causes cassava to direct all its energy into stem and leaf growth instead of root swelling. Balancing soil nutrients helps the plant transfer food down into developing tubers.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ yaa tso lɛ shishi kɛ baai lɛ amli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ yaa bulbs ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually indicate a nitrogen deficiency. The corn plant moves available nitrogen from its older lower leaves up to feed the young growing leaves and developing cobs, signaling that fertilizer is needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Abɛi tsei tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha baai bibii lɛ niyenii ni ekɛha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Why do my crop yields improve when I plant groundnut or cowpea on my land before planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani midu ŋmei yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special root nodules that absorb nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses this left-behind nitrogen as natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa.

english: Why do fall armyworms attack my young maize plants instead of older plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall cutworms lɛ miitutua mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mi tsei momo lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer the soft, tender leaf whorls of young maize plants because they are easy to eat and digest. Protecting young crops early prevents the worms from destroying the growing center of the plant.
ga: Autumn cutworms lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe waaa ni amɛyeɔ ni amɛmli shwieɔ shi. Tsei bibii ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishijee mli Ebaatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I just throw away the stalks and leaves I cut off from my crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsei kɛ baai ni mifoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ mashwieɔ lɛ?

english: Cut crop residues contain valuable nutrients and moisture. Leaving them on your soil as mulch or feeding them to animals puts those nutrients back into your farm cycle instead of wasting them.
ga: Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ oshi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ni okɛye kooloi lɛ, ehaa nakai niyenii lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa oŋmɔ mli nibii amli moŋ fe ni ooofite.

english: Is it good to trim or cut back parts of my plants during the farming season?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ mitsei lɛ ahe yɛ okwaayeli be lɛ mli?

english: Yes, trimming or pruning dead or excess parts of a plant allows the crop to focus its energy and nutrients on growing stronger stems and bigger grain cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso lɛ fãi ni egboi loo ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ loo afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui wuji ni miida lɛ tsuɔ nii.

english: Will spraying or washing my crop fodder with salty water attract goats and cows to eat it?
ga: Ani nu ni mli edɔ ni akɛshwieɔ niyenii nɔ loo ahoɔ lɛ baagbala tooi kɛ tsinai koni amɛbaye?

english: Yes, farm animals naturally crave salt. If you soak or wash crop stalks in a light salt water mixture, animals will quickly smell it and chew it up enthusiastically.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmɔ mli kooloi yɛ adebɔɔ mli hiamɔ nii kɛha ŋmei. Kɛji akɛ okɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ wo nu ni akɛ ŋmei fioo efutu mli loo ofɔ he lɛ, Kooloo lɛ baanu he oya ni ekɛ miishɛɛ baaye.

english: Why do goats and sheep keep breaking into my field to eat my corn stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ abotiai kɛ gwantɛŋi yaa nɔ amɛboteɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbaye miŋmaa tsei lɛ?

english: Corn stalks are naturally sweet and nutrient-rich, especially if livestock detect moisture or salts on them. Animals will actively seek out the field once they recognize corn as a tasty feed.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Especially if livestock detect moisture or salt on corn stalks, animals will eagerly explore the field once they perceive corn as a delicacy.

english: How do I stop farm animals from destroying my harvested crop when I leave it out in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmɔ mli kooloi anaa koni amɛkafite mikpamɔ nii lɛ beni mishiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested crops like corn attract roaming livestock by sight and smell. You must gather and store your harvest in enclosed cribs or raised structures out of reach of animals.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa kooloi ni hoɔ lɛ kɛtsɔ hiŋmɛi kɛ ŋmãa nɔ. Esa akɛ obua oŋmɔshinii lɛ anaa ni okɛto tsɔji ni afo mli loo tsũi ni awó nɔ ni kooloi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ amli.

english: Can I use leftover maize stalks as feed for my cattle and goats after harvest?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ aha tsinai kɛ tooi niyenii yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, leftover maize stalks make good farm fodder. Chopping them up and sprinkling a little salty water on them makes them easier and more appetizing for livestock to digest.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ baanyɛ afee niyenii kpakpa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afolɔ amɛ ni akɛ nu ni mli edɔ fioo shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi oya, ni kooloi hu ŋɔɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my maize crop seem to produce smaller cobs when the plants are crowded or unpruned?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-abele lɛ bɛ ŋmeii babaoo beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe loo afolɔko amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize has to compete with excess shoots or weeds, sunlight and soil nutrients get diverted away from the main cob, preventing the corn from growing to its full size.
ga: Beni ehe bahia ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa loo jwɛi ni fa fe nine lɛ abɔ akaŋ lɛ, ajieɔ Hulu la kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa wulu lɛ mli. Etsiɔ ŋmãa naa koni ekakwɛ̃ kɛyashɛ ŋmãa ni eshɛɔ ŋmãa he

english: Why do farm animals prefer eating corn stalks over normal pasture grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi sumɔɔ abele tsei fe jwɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Corn is a tall grass rich in natural carbohydrates and sugars. Animals recognize its high energy value and will always prefer it over tough, dry pasture grass.
ga: Abɛi ji jwɛi kakadaŋŋ abɔ ni carbohydrates kɛ sugars babaoo yɔɔ mli. Koolooi yɔseɔ hewalɛ ni fa babaoo ni eyɔɔ lɛ. ni amɛsumɔɔ fe prairie jwɛi ni wa ni egbi lɛ.

english: How does adding a little salt to animal water affect how much feed my livestock eat?
ga: Te ŋmei fioo ni mikɛwoɔ mikooloi lɛ anu mli lɛ saa niyenii ni mikooloi lɛ yeɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Adding a small amount of salt to water or feed stimulates an animal's appetite and thirst, encouraging them to consume more roughage like dry corn stalks.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋoo fioo ko wo nu loo niyenii mli lɛ, ehaa kooloo lɛ shweɔ ni enáa niyenii he akɔnɔ. Kɛtsɔ kooloi ni ekanyaa amɛ koni amɛye niyenii ni mli edɔ babaoo, tamɔ ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens if I leave my cut crops on the ground in a area where animals freely roam?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mishi miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ he ko ni kooloi yɔɔ? Okɛ ohe awo mli?

english: Animals will quickly spot the cut plants and eat them all up. Cut crops should be moved immediately to a safe processing or storage area if you want to keep them.
ga: Koolooi naa tsei ni afolɔ lɛ oya ni amɛyeɔ amɛ. Esa akɛ ajie tsei ni afo lɛ kɛya he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo akɛtoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ osusu akɛ obaato amɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize plants usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or improving field drainage helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ okɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he loo oha nu ni hoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What makes my cocoa flowers drop off the trees without forming any pods?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni efeee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa flowers often fall off if the tree suffers from heat stress, prolonged dry weather, or attacks from insects like mirids (capsids). Maintaining sufficient shade trees and controlling sap-sucking pests helps pods form successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji akɛ tso lɛ na hela yɛ dɔlɛ hewɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi tamɔ mirids (capsids) ni tutuaa amɛ, ni haa hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ akudɔmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni pods lɛ yeɔ omanye.

english: Cassava tubers rot in wet soil because the roots suffocate when surrounded by standing water for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji nu ni damɔ shi ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What is causing the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up and stay small?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ bibii?

english: Curling pepper leaves are typically caused by tiny pests like thrips, aphids, or mites sucking sap from the leaf undersides, or by viruses transmitted by these pests. Using targeted pest control early prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni akɛgbeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ ashishijee naa.

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the fruit, which often happens when watering is inconsistent. Keeping soil moisture steady and adding compost or lime restores fruit quality.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni akɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ afee fɛo ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do you advise me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okɛ ŋaawoo haa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mikpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, whereas legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil. Rotating maize with legumes naturally restores soil fertility and breaks insect disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ekoŋŋ, ni efoɔ ŋmeii ahelai ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the new suckers growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ ŋmeii heei ni shwieɔ shi lɛ? Mi plantain tso titri lɛ

english: Allowing too many suckers to grow at once forces them to fight for nutrients and sunlight, leading to small plantain bunches. Pruning to keep just the main mother plant and one or two follower suckers produces much larger fruits.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ ŋmeii bibii tsɔ gbɛ ni amɛdaraa shikome Enɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛwu amɛtao niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la. ni kɛ plantain tsei bibii baa Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei lɛ koni akɛto nyɛ tso titri lɛ pɛ kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi kome loo enyɔ ni nyiɛɔ esɛɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha yibii ni da fe no kwraa aba.

english: Why is it wasteful for me to scatter fertilizer right before a big rainstorm comes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he akɛ aaagbɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ashwã dani nugbɔ wulu aba lɛ?

english: Heavy rains wash away granular fertilizer before the plant roots can soak it in, wasting your investment. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after a rainfall rather than right before a downpour.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. ni kɛ shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooowo lɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ

english: Why do my crops perform poorly when I allow weeds to grow around them for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ miha jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Amɛyeɔ otsii enyɔ loo enyɔ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, sunlight, and soil moisture. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks of planting ensures your crops get all the nourishment they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ waa. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo ni okɛdu lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Yam vines dry prematurely due to fungal leaf spot diseases or root attacks by soil pests like nematodes. Rotating your yam field each season and using healthy, disease-free seed yams stops this early drying.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ fungal leaf spot hela loo shishifãi ni sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes tutuaa amɛ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ otsake o-sweet potato saatso lɛ daa afi ni okɛ sweet potato tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni hela bɛ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha nɛkɛ mra be mli ŋmɔlɔ nɛɛ akpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow and purple at the tips instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛshishigbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaahi shi ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, while a purple color shows a lack of phosphorus. Adding balanced fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps your crops regain their healthy green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni purple tsɔɔ akɛ fɔsfɔs bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara waa.

english: I noticed dark brown and black spots on my cassava leaves, what is causing this and will it destroy my farm?
ga: Miyɔse ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ baai anɔ. Mɛni amɛkɛbaa ni ani amɛbaafite miŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Those dark spots are usually caused by cassava brown streak or fungal leaf spot disease, which spread easily during rainy periods. Clearing weeds regularly to improve air movement around the plants helps prevent the disease from taking over.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei streak loo fungal leaf spot hela, ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ baa. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ daa koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ aya hiɛ. Tsei yeɔ ebuaa ni helai akaye nɔ.

english: When I harvest my cassava, why does the center inside sometimes turn reddish-brown instead of staying white?
ga: Kɛ́ mikpa ŋmei lɛ Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, ŋmei lɛ mli fã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nɔ ni eshwɛɔ yɛŋ lɛ najiaŋ?

english: A reddish-brown stem center in harvested cassava is caused by natural spoilage that happens once the root is dug up and exposed to air. To stop this, harvest only what you can sell or process within two days.
ga: Nɔ ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli fitemɔ ni baa kɛji atsa shishifãi lɛ amli ni akɛwo kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli baa ji tso lɛ shishifãi ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmei ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ. Koni akpa Nikpamɔ nɛɛ nɔ pɛ ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ loo otsu he nii yɛ gbii enyɔ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings curl up and turn brown when planted under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees act like human babies—their tender leaves burn under direct heat. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains nearby creates a natural umbrella that protects the young cocoa from harsh sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ adesai abifabii. Ebaai bibii lɛ shãa kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he.

english: How do I know the right time to pick my peppers when some are green and others are turning red on the same bush?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔtɔ? Beni ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmeii komɛi hu feɔ etsuru yɛ jwɛi kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ.

english: Green peppers are mature but unripe, while red peppers are fully ripe and naturally sweeter. You can harvest green ones to encourage the plant to grow more fruits, or wait for them to turn red for a higher market value.
ga: Chili ŋmɔji lɛ eshɛ shi kwraa shi eshɛko lolo. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, chili tsuru lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa, ni eyɛ ŋɔɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Obaanyɛ okpa tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ koni owo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Aloo mɛ ni etsɔ tsuru koni ená jara ni nɔ kwɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants droop during the hot afternoon even when the soil around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli egbi moŋ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Tomato plants shed moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can drink water during peak afternoon heat. If they stand upright again by evening, it is normal, but placing dry grass mulch around the base keeps the root soil cool.
ga: Tomato tsei jieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu yɛ shwane mli latsaa be mli. Kɛ amɛte shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ, no lɛ ehi. Shi kɛ́ okɛ sũ ni egbi wo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifã lɛ sũ lɛ mli ajɔ.

english: I have black cowpea seeds and white cowpea seeds, is there any difference in how they will grow on my land?
ga: Miyɛ tsina ŋmeii diji kɛ tsina ŋmeii yɛŋ. Ani gbɛi srɔtoi yɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ aduɔ nii yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, different seed coat colors often mean different crop varieties. Darker-seeded cowpeas usually resist wet weather and pests better, while white cowpea varieties mature quicker and are often preferred by market buyers.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ahe sui srɔtoi tsɔɔ tsei srɔtoi. Cowpeas ni dumɔwui ni tsuɔ waa lɛ nyɛɔ eshiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei henɔi ni ji white lɛ daa oya, ni bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii yɛ jara nɔ lɛ sumɔɔ.

english: Why are all the flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when plants get stressed by high heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Giving your crops steady water and avoiding heavy chemical fertilizers during flowering helps the blossoms turn into peppers.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Nu ni okɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be fɛɛ be kɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli ni tsii ni oootsi ohe kɛjɛ he yɛ fɔfɔi be mli lɛ baaye abua ni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is there a white powdery coat spreading over the leaves of my garden egg plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ yitsɔi yɛŋ ni ha ŋmei tso lɛ baai ahe yɛ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: That white coating is a fungal condition called powdery mildew, which thrives when plants are crowded in hot, humid conditions. Pruning excess leaves helps air circulate better and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Nakai nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ni kwɛ̃ɔ beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are the bottom stems of my yam vines turning black near the soil line and causing the vine to die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishigbɛ tsei lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ ni ehaa wain tso lɛ gboɔ lɛ?

english: Blackened stems near the soil are a sign of rot caused by fungal attack in waterlogged ground. Planting your yams on high ridges or mounds ensures excess water drains away, keeping the base of the vine dry and healthy.
ga: Tsoi ni etsɔ ediŋŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ loo gɔŋ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli. Ha wain tso lɛ shishi lɛ agbi ni ehi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know exactly when my cassava is ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni ŋmei lɛ eshɛ he ni abaakpa?

english: Cassava usually takes 9 to 12 months to mature depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves turn yellow and fall off, and the soil around the stem begins to crack as the roots expand beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei heɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekwɛɔ. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi, ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli lɛɛɔ yɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams rot so quickly when I store them indoors?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mikɛto shĩa lɛ?

english: Yams rot easily if they are bruised during harvest, exposed to heat, or stored in direct sunlight. Keeping undamaged yams on raised wooden racks in a cool, shaded barn with good airflow allows them to breathe and last for several months.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa amɛ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be mli, akɛwo la mli, loo akɛto hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ atomɔ ni mli ewo muji lɛ ato tso adekai ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ, ni shade yɔɔ mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa boteɔ mli. Ehaa amɛmuɔ ni ehiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is an important food source in the soil. Heavy rains often wash nitrogen deep into the ground where short roots cannot reach it.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ jɛɛhe ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Bei pii lɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi kukuji nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants keep dropping their flowers before any fruit grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ dani eyibii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by extreme heat, irregular watering, or tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips. Keeping the soil moist and managing pests helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop soft, black bottoms before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishi diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused by a shortage of calcium while the fruit is growing. It usually happens when watering is irregular, making it hard for the plant roots to absorb and transport calcium evenly.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa tsei shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛbaaŋɔ calcium ni amɛkɛya.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of big green leaves but very few bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ.

english: Cowpeas naturally create their own soil nitrogen. If you add too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant gets confused and spends all its energy producing leaves instead of setting flowers and pods.
ga: Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ nitrogen babaoo wo mli lɛ Tso lɛ futuɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii ato

english: Why is it better for me to plant several different crops on my farm instead of focusing on just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ makwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama ŋmɔshi nibii henɔ kome pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Growing multiple crops protects your family's income if weather or disease ruins one crop. It also keeps your soil healthy because different plants use and return different nutrients to the earth.
ga: Nibii babaoo ni ooodu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ oweku lɛ shika he kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ loo hela kpata nibii kome pɛ hiɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ tsei kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do young cocoa trees struggle to survive if I do not plant shade crops like plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cacao tsei bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛhi shi kɛji miduuu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very tender leaves and shallow roots that burn and dry out in full sunlight. Fast-growing plantains provide the necessary shade and moisture to protect the cocoa until it grows stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ waa kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ haa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa koni ebu kookoo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewaa.

english: Planting seeds after just one light rain can cause them to sprout and then die if the soil dries out completely. Waiting for steady rains ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow strong roots.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ Saramɔ kome pɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgboi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ daa lɛ ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How does keeping a strict distance between my planted seeds help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbɛ ni kã dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ateŋ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Proper spacing ensures that plants do not crowd each other or compete for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. It also allows wind to pass through the field easily, reducing fungal diseases.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni tsei lɛ akabɔ amɛhe loo amɛkaye akaŋ kɛha hulu la. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔji amli mlɛo, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main plant food needed for leaf growth, or that the soil is waterlogged. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted manure will help the leaves turn green and grow strong again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ adara loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making small holes in the leaves and center leaves of my growing maize crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa ni miida lɛ baai kɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Those holes are typically caused by a pest called the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that eats the young growing leaves of maize. Checking your farm early and using recommended treatments or neem extracts can stop them before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem mli nu lɛ atsu nii lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔ lɛ akpa dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off some branches from my cocoa trees when they are already growing leaves well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-kookoo niji lɛ ekomɛi? Ni kookoo tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lolo?

english: Pruning cocoa trees opens up the canopy so sunlight and air can flow through. This prevents damp conditions that cause diseases like black pod and encourages the tree to put its energy into growing cocoa pods rather than excess leaves.
ga: Kookoo tso ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ helai tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ diji baa lɛ naa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ ni ekɛwoɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ atsu nii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa trees need to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tso lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Cassava cuttings should be planted about 1 meter apart from each other. Giving them enough space ensures that the underground roots have plenty of room to expand into large tubers without competing for water and food.
ga: Esa akɛ adu tsei ni afo lɛ aaafee mita kome kɛjɛ amɛhe. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ haa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves to catch sunlight, which allows them to make food for the underground tubers. Staking also lifts the leaves off the damp ground, protecting them from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato vines must climb high to spread out their leaves to receive sunlight. Enɛ haa enyɛɔ efeɔ niyenii ehaa ŋmeii lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do experienced farmers cover the ground around crops with dry leaves and grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ baai ni egbi kɛ jwɛi haa he ni amɛduɔ nii yɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass is called mulching. It keeps the soil cool and moist during dry periods, prevents weeds from growing, and slowly rots to feed the soil with natural nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. It keeps the soil cool and moist during dry periods. It prevents weeds from growing and slowly decays to provide natural nutrients to the soil.

english: It is best to water early in the morning so the plants can take in moisture before the hot afternoon sun arrives. Watering in the hot afternoon causes water to evaporate quickly, and leaves stay wet overnight if watered too late, causing diseases.
ga: Esa akɛ afee nu leebi maŋkpa bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ ŋmɔtɔ dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ aba. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo mli yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya. Ni baai lɛ baafee ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ kome kɛji akɛ awo amɛ nu blɛoo tsɔ. Ekɛ helai srɔtoi baa

english: Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to resist common diseases and withstand dry weather better. Saved seeds lose their strength over time, leading to smaller harvests compared to certified seeds.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni afɔɔ namɔ, ni amɛŋmɛɔ amɛtsui shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ amli babaoo. Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do I need to cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mitso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: Removing excess shoots, or suckers, leaves only one or two strong stems to feed on soil nutrients. This focuses the plant's energy so it produces one very large, heavy bunch of plantains instead of many tiny bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Gbɛ nɛɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa tso lɛ hewalɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, afeɔ plantain ŋmɔ agbo kome ni tsii yɛ ŋmɔ mli bibii babaoo najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen or getting too much water around the roots. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to make green leaves, so adding manure, compost, or fertilizer helps them turn green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi eŋɔli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together so I can fit more crops on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and thin, resulting in a smaller total harvest than if you gave each plant enough space to grow.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ ni egbɔjɔ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibii fɛɛ ni abaawo lɛ baafee bibioo fe kɛji oha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛkwɛ̃.

english: How do groundnuts and beans help make my soil better for other crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha tsei krokomɛi?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans have tiny lumps on their roots that take nitrogen from the air and put it into the ground. When the crop is harvested, that nitrogen remains in the soil as free food for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ ŋmeii bibii. Yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ, ni amɛheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I grow maize on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up in the ground. Changing crops each season gives the soil time to recover and starves out pests.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni eha tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ni ekɛjie tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: Why do experienced farmers keep big trees standing inside their cocoa farms?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ kɛ tsei wuji toɔ amɛ kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need shade, especially when young, because intense sunlight and high heat stress the leaves and dry out the ground. Large trees act as natural umbrellas, keeping the farm cool, moist, and protected from harsh winds.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ hia hulutsoo. Titri lɛ kɛ́ gbekɛbii ji gbekɛbii Enɛ ji akɛ, hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ. Tsei wuji tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa, ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves stops the hot sun from drying out the soil, keeps weeds from taking over, and prevents heavy rain from splashing muddy water and diseases onto your plant leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni otsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekɛ nu ni mli ewo muji kɛ helai srɔtoi aba Okɛshwie otso lɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden sticks as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tying tomato stems to sticks keeps the heavy fruit off the wet ground where it can easily rot or get eaten by insects. It also opens up the leaves to more sunshine and airflow, keeping the plant healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ o-tomato lɛ shishifãi lɛ fĩ tsei aniji ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ akafee shwiili. ni hoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ ni baanyɛ afite oya loo kooloi baanyɛ aye lɛ nɔ Egbeleɔ baai lɛ hu koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo aba mli. ha tsei lɛ awa

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they suffer from stress, usually caused by extreme afternoon heat, too little water, or soaked soil. When stressed, the plant drops flowers to save its energy to stay alive.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔ̃ɔ kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ haomɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni baa shwane mli lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. nu fioo tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato koni amɛhi wala mli.

english: Roots need air inside the soil to breathe. When heavy rains leave standing water in the farm for too long without proper drainage, the roots suffocate in the mud and soft rot sets in.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he hiaa shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ashiɔ nu lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ bɛ. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ muji lɛ mli ni amɛgboɔ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest that loves to nest inside the hidden center fold of young maize plants where tender leaves grow. They feed there safely away from sun and rain, which damages the growing point of the plant.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni sumɔɔ ni amɛfee amɛshĩa yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni baai bibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ amli. Amɛtaoɔ niyenii yɛ jɛmɛ shweshweeshwe, ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ he. ni fiteɔ he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ

english: Why do my maize plants grow so thin and produce small cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Beni aduɔ Dumɔwui babaoo ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each stalk gets enough resources to grow strong and produce large, healthy cobs.
