ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso lɛ yitso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni he wa baa.

english: Why shouldn't I leave all the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishiɔ tsei bibii yɛ mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Too many shoots, or suckers, compete with the main mother plant for food and water. Removing extra suckers and leaving only one or two strong ones allows the main plant to produce a much larger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei loo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ kɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ashi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo ŋmeii babaoo ni dara ni tsii.

english: Yellowing and curling leaves on cassava are often caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies, or a lack of soil nutrients like nitrogen. Checking under the leaves for insects helps identify if treatment or better soil management is needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akwɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni ana kɛji ŋmeii yɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa kɛji ehe miihia ni atsu he nii loo akwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: This black rot at the base of the tomato is blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering or dry spells during fruit growth.
ga: Diŋ ni fiteɔ yɛ tomato shishi lɛ ji fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo be ni hulu enyɔ shi yɛ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling tightly and stopping new peppers from forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe waa ni etsĩɔ pepper heei ni baa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Tightly curling leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips, mites, or aphids that attack young leaves. Controlling these insects early protects the leaves and allows the plant to set fruit properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, mites, loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe waa yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baa. ni tutuaa baai bibii Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many of their flowers before small pods can grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo dani ŋmeii bibii lɛ baanyɛ adara lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of shade, poor soil nutrients, or insect pests like mirids. Maintaining reasonable shade trees and ensuring good soil care keeps flowers attached so pods can form.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ, hulutsoo ni bɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni faaa lɛ hao amɛ. loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen. Shade ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ afee.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves high up toward the sun. Exposure to sunlight allows the plant to produce energy efficiently, which then feeds and expands the tuber growing underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia tso ni akɛwoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu lɛ he. Hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni baaha bulb ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii ni egbɛ eshwa.

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops sunlight from drying out the earth too fast, keeps the soil cool, blocks weeds from growing, and decomposes over time to enrich the soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be ni sa mli koni ekɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why should I wait until my maize is knee-high before putting my second round of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni mi-ŋmei lɛ ashɛ aaafee mitsitsi nɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ awo mli lɛ?

english: Young seedlings cannot absorb large amounts of nutrients right away. Applying fertilizer when maize reaches knee height provides nutrients right when the stalk enters its fastest growing stage, preventing fertilizer waste.
ga: Tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli beni ŋmãa lɛ shɛɔ enaji ahe lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ beni ŋmãa lɛ boteɔ amɛmra be mli dalɛ mli pɛ. Tsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ naa

english: Why do small insects destroy my harvested maize cobs so quickly while they are in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ oya be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils thrive when stored maize still contains too much moisture. Drying the maize thoroughly under the sun until the grains are very hard prevents insect breeding and protects the stored crop.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii yeɔ omanye kɛji ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli efɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ ŋmãa ni baa lɛ naa, ni ebuɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ he.

english: Why does my soil dry out so fast these days, and what can I plant to keep it moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ gbiɔ oya nɛkɛ? Ni mɛni manyɛ madu koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Extreme heat and direct sunlight bake the soil, removing moisture quickly. Planting cover crops or broad-leafed crops like plantains creates shade, keeping the ground cool and holding moisture in the soil.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ashã oya ni ejie ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛ mli. Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ loo tsei ni yɔɔ baai babaoo tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers keep telling us to leave tall trees on our farms instead of cutting everything down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔshi tsei kakadaji yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni wɔbaafo nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Tall trees create a cooler local climate, protect sensitive crops from harsh sunlight, prevent heavy rain from washing away rich topsoil, and help bring rain to your area over time.
ga: Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa maŋ lɛ mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Buu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ nɔ. ni eye ebua ni nugbɔ aba he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees drying up and dying when the sun gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need temporary shade crops, like plantain, to shield them while their roots grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni ebu amɛhe yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: How many years after planting does a new cocoa tree start bearing pods?
ga: Afii enyiɛ sɛɛ beni adu cacao tso hee lɛ, ejeɔ shishi ewoɔ ŋmeii?

english: Most modern cocoa varieties in Ghana start producing pods within 2 to 3 years if they are given adequate shade when young and kept free from diseases.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ kookoo henɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛji amɛná hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa beni amɛji gbekɛbii ni hela bɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily during strong winds and rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that do not reach deep into the ground. Planting them alongside taller trees or windbreaks helps block strong winds and protects your crop.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ tsei kakadaji loo kɔɔyɔɔ he hei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa bo, ni ebaabu onibii ahe.

english: Why do my plantain suckers need so much water when I first plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa mi plantain tsei lɛ beni miduɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers rely heavily on moist soil to produce new leaves and establish roots. If the soil is too dry at the beginning, the plant's growth will stunt completely.
ga: Dumɔwui damɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ waa koni amɛna baai kɛ shishifãi heei. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ Tso lɛ dalɛ sɛɛ foɔ kwraa.

english: Can cassava survive on my farm if the hot weather lasts longer than usual?
ga: Ani ŋmei baahi shi yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ be kakadaŋŋ fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ?

english: Yes, cassava is a very tough crop that tolerates heat and dry conditions well. Its underground tubers store nutrients and water, allowing it to survive long dry spells.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmei ji tso ko ni kpɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo be naa jogbaŋŋ. Eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ toɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli

english: Why are my cassava stems growing very tall with many leaves, but the roots underneath are tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei tso lɛ kwɔ waa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ daraaa kwraa?

english: If cassava receives too much shade or too much nitrogen in the soil, the plant spends all its energy growing upper foliage instead of building thick tubers underground.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo eŋwɛi baai lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeefee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli tse.

english: How long does a rubber tree take before I can start harvesting latex from it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani rɔbɔt tso ko jeɔ latɛs ŋmɔmɔ shishi?

english: Rubber trees usually take about 6 to 7 years of growth before the trunk becomes thick enough for tapping latex safely.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, rɔbɔt tsei lɛ heɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 dani amɛtso lɛ mli shwereɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtswa nu lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Does growing rubber trees on my farm require a lot of rain?
ga: Ani rɔbɔt ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ nugbɔ babaoo?

english: Rubber trees grow best in warm areas with reliable rainfall, but once mature, their deep taproots allow them to endure seasonal dry spells.
ga: Rɔba tsei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ. Shi kɛ́ amɛdara kwraa Amɛ shishifã ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ be mli hɔmɔ naa.

english: How can I tell if my cocoa trees are sick or if they are just getting too old?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cacao tso lɛ hela mɔ lɛ loo egbɔ tsɔ?

english: Sick trees show sudden signs like rotting pods, yellowing leaves, or swollen stems, whereas aging trees slowly produce fewer pods over several years without sudden decay.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ baajie okadii ni baa trukaa, tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbo, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmeii ni efuu, yɛ be mli ni tsei ni edara lɛ baaná okadii fiofio. Ha ŋmeii lɛ afee bibioo yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli ni amɛfiteee trukaa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the tree lacks key soil nutrients, is suffering from severe drought, or is under attack by pests like capsids or viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. kɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa miikpe loo kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ capsids loo helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ cocoa bud swelling virus lɛ anɔ.

english: What should I do if spraying chemical medicine does not stop my cocoa trees from dying?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ haaa amɛgboi?

english: If spraying does not work, the problem may be a viral infection like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus (which chemicals cannot cure) or severely degraded soil, and an extension officer should inspect the farm.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii lɛ, ekolɛ naagba lɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli, tamɔ kookoo tso mli hela. (ni tsofai nyɛŋ atsa) loo shikpɔŋ ni efite waa Ha mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why am I getting so few pods from my cocoa trees this harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛ cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: A sudden drop in pods is usually caused by fungal diseases, insect damage, or exhausted soil that lacks the essential nutrients needed to support pod development.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ahela, kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ nii, loo shikpɔŋ ni efite ni niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmeii lɛ shweremɔ bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii lɛ baa shi trukaa.

english: Why do my small cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii bibii Do mine lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young pods turning black is commonly caused by Black Pod disease or severe dry conditions; pruning branches to let in sunlight and spraying approved fungicides can help.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni feɔ ediŋŋ lɛ baa ji ŋmeii diji hela loo shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la ashɛ nɔ kɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua.

english: What causes cocoa pods to rot right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ tsei anɔ dani akpaa?

english: Pod rot is caused by fungal spores that spread quickly in dark, overly shady, and wet conditions during the rainy season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ pod rot baa ji ŋmeii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ yɔɔ lɛ. hulutsoo tsɔ ni edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli

english: Why does my cocoa farm give a high yield one year and almost nothing the next?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afi kome mli ni eshɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Yields fluctuate when rainfall varies or when trees become exhausted after a heavy crop load and need additional soil fertilizer to rebuild strength.
ga: Yibiiwoo lɛ tsakeɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ tsake loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ ahe jɔ̃ amɛhe yɛ dumɔ ni mli wa sɛɛ. ni ehe miihia ni akɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he koni ekɛma hewalɛ ekoŋŋ

english: Can poor soil cause my harvest to drop even if there is no disease on my farm?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aba miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ hela ko bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Yes, tired soil lacking nutrients like potassium and nitrogen cannot nourish the tree enough to grow pods, even if no disease is present.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, shikpɔŋ ni etɔ lɛ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ potassium kɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Anyɛɛɛ aha tso lɛ niyenii bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ akwɛ̃. Kɛji hela ko bɛ po

english: Does cutting down a sick cocoa tree help protect the rest of my farm?
ga: Ani cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ ni abaafo lɛ baaye abua ni abu miŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, cutting out severely infected trees prevents viral diseases like Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus from spreading to nearby healthy trees through ants or root contact.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ waa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli tamɔ cocoa bloat virus lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii loo shishifãi ni akɛtswaa amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: How does trimming and pruning my cocoa trees prevent crop loss?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashikpamɔ kɛ amɛhe ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ atsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ anaa?

english: Trimming excess leaves and branches allows air and sunlight to reach the trunk, keeping the farm drier so harmful fungi cannot easily grow on pods.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai kɛ tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la shɛɔ tso lɛ shishi. ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli agbi babaoo Enɛ baatsi ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ mlɛo.

english: How do I know which crop will sell for a good price before I start planting on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii ni abaahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara kpakpa dani mabɔi amɛdumɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Before planting, talk to local market women, traders, and agricultural officers to find out what buyers are asking for. Planning your farm based on market demand prevents you from growing crops that no one wants to buy at harvest time.
ga: Dani obaadu lɛ, okɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayeli yei, jarayelɔi, kɛ okwaayeli he onukpai agba sane koni ona nɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ. Kɛ́ oto oŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ yɛ jarayeli hiamɔ nii ahe lɛ, ebaatsi bo gbɛ koni okadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɔ ko mɔ ko sumɔɔɔ ni eheɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli lɛ.

english: Why does the price of tomatoes drop so low when everyone in my village harvests at the same time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato jara baa shi nɛkɛ be mli ni mɔ fɛɛ mɔ ni yɔɔ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ miikpa nii yɛ be kome mli lɛ?

english: When many farmers harvest the exact same crop at the same time, the market gets flooded with more food than buyers need. This oversupply forces farmers to lower their prices just to sell before the crop spoils.
ga: Beni okwaafoi babaoo kpaɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome yɛ be kome mli lɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, niyenii babaoo baayi jara lɛ nɔ fe bɔ ni mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ taoɔ. Nɛkɛ nibii ni fa fe nine nɛɛ nyɛɔ okwaafoi anɔ koni amɛba jara shi koni amɛhɔ̃ɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How can I find buyers for my harvest before I even put seeds in the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana mɔ ko ni baahe miŋmɔshi nii lɛ dani madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can connect with buyers, schools, or food processors early to agree on supply arrangements. Joining a local farmers' group also helps you combine your yield with others to attract larger buyers who purchase in bulk.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ, skulbii loo mɛi ni feɔ niyenii lɛ abɔ mra. koni okpɛlɛ nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ Okwaafoi akuu ko ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni okɛ ohe aaawo mli lɛ hu haa okɛ onibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ feɔ ekome kɛ mɛi krokomɛi. Koni ekɛgbala jarayelɔi wuji ni heɔ nibii babaoo lɛ

english: What should I do with my extra maize if buyers do not show up at my farm during harvest?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛji mɔ ni heɔ lɛ baaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ kpamɔ be mli?

english: You can dry your maize properly and store it in airtight bags (like PICS bags) or a secure crib. Safe storage allows you to hold your crop until the market supply drops and prices go back up.
ga: Obaanyɛ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli (tamɔ PICS kotoku) loo ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe mli. Nɔ ni akɛtoɔ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ onibii lɛ toɔ kɛyashiɔ jara nɔ nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ baa shi ni jara lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: How can changing my planting date help me get better prices for my vegetables?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ gbii ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ tsakemɔ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná mi-aduawai lɛ ahe jara kpakpa?

english: Planting slightly earlier or later than most farmers shifts your harvest away from the peak season glut. Harvesting when a crop is scarce allows you to command much higher prices in the market.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu mra fioo loo sɛɛ mli fe okwaafoi babaoo lɛ baaye abua ni otsi oŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛ be mli ni okwaayeli lɛ fa babaoo lɛ mli. Nikpamɔ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii faaa lɛ haa onyɛɔ okudɔɔ jarayeli jara ni nɔ kwɔ kwraa.

english: Can I process my harvested cassava so it does not rot while I look for buyers?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsu mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ he nii koni ekafite be mli ni mitaoɔ mɔ ni baahe lɛ?

english: Yes, turning fresh cassava into gari, high-quality flour, or dried chips preserves it for months. Processing gives you extra time to find buyers without worrying about your crop rotting within a few days.
ga: Hɛɛ, ni atsakeɔ ŋmei hee ni afee lɛ gari Ashikiŋsha ni hi jogbaŋŋ Aloo, abaanyɛ akɛ ŋmei ni egbi lɛ ato nyɔji babaoo. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa onáa be kroko ni okɛtao mɔ ni baahe bo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohao yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ni baafite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli lɛ he.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my entire land with only one crop like watermelon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛ tamɔ watermelon lɛ?

english: If the market price for that single crop crashes or a disease attacks it, you risk losing all your income. Planting two or three different crops spreads your risk so you still make money if one crop fails.
ga: Kɛji akɛ jarayeli jara ni akɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome lɛ gbee shi loo hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa mɛi lɛ ba lɛ, Okɛ ohe woɔ oshara mli akɛ shika fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baaje odɛŋ. Tsei srɔtoi enyɔ loo etɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaha oshara ni oyɔɔ lɛ afee srɔtoi. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ oná shika lolo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko fite.

english: Why do my harvested leafy vegetables spoil so quickly before I can transport them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nibii ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya dani akɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh vegetables lose moisture and rot quickly when exposed to direct sunlight and heat. Harvesting during the cool early morning hours and keeping them in shaded, ventilated crates keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Aduawai ŋmɔji laajeɔ nu ni amɛfiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ amɛ shɛ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ yɛ leebi maŋkpa ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli, ni akɛto adekai ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhi shi ehee be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do I choose a crop that fits both my soil type and the local market needs?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ henɔ kɛ maŋ lɛ jarayeli he hiamɔ nii?

english: Consult an extension officer to test or evaluate your soil to see what grows well, then check nearby markets to see which of those suitable crops have consistent buyer demand before buying seeds.
ga: Kwɛmɔ extension nitsulɔ ko koni eka oshikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ loo ekwɛ mli koni ena henɔi ni kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ jarayeli hei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ koni ona ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ daa dani ohé dumɔwui.

english: Why do some of my crops produce high yields while others fail on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ekomɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu wooo yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Different crops draw different nutrients from the soil and require different amounts of water. Rotating different types of crops each season keeps the soil healthy and prevents nutrients from being completely drained.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi gbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ, ni amɛbiɔ nu babaoo. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Be fɛɛ be lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehaaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ akaje mli kwraa.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for green leaves and strong stems. Applying fertilizer like urea or adding well-rotted manure helps feed the plant and restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai eŋɔli kɛ tsei ashishifãi ni wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ niyenii ni eha efee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil in my field become hard and cracked just a few days after heavy rain stops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens quickly when it lacks organic matter like compost or dried leaves that help retain moisture. Adding rotten manure or leaving crop residues on the field improves soil structure so it stays soft and holds water longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa oya kɛji akɛ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo baai ni egboi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he loo ashi ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. No hewɔ lɛ, ehiɔ shi blɛoo ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle strong direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily and dry out quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving some tall trees gives them the cooler temperature and humidity they need to grow strong in their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛɛɛ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ, ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ loo tsei kakadaji ni ashiɔ yɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ ni mli wa yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain leaves droop and turn brown quickly during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems and large broad leaves that lose water very quickly in hot sun. Covering the ground around the base of the plantain with dry straw or leaves keeps the soil cool and locks in moisture.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai wuji ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ, nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle plantain lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why should I plant my maize seeds spaced apart instead of putting four or five seeds together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ejwɛ loo enumɔ baafata he yɛ bu kome mli?

english: Putting many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight with each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients. Giving each seed its own space allows roots to spread out and produces bigger, healthier cobs.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwu fɛɛ dumɔwu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ egbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛwoɔ dumɔwu ni da ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines produce tubers underground by catching sunlight through their leaves above ground. Staking lifts the vine off the soil so leaves catch maximum sunlight and prevents leaf diseases caused by sitting on damp ground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛnáa kɛtsɔɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tso lɛ yibii lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he, ni ekɛtsi tsei lɛ ahe helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ ni eta lɛ mli baa lɛ naa.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when temperatures are too high, when water is inconsistent, or if bees are not visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering and avoiding excessive nitrogen fertilizer helps the flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa Aloo kɛji ŋmeii ebaaa koni amɛbafee pollination. Nu ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli daa kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Cassava is typically ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves start yellowing and dropping off. Harvesting too early results in thin tubers, while waiting too long makes the tubers tough and woody.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa nikpamɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, yitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, yɛ be mli ni kɛ́ mɛ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, yitsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ tsei.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips or aphids hidden under the leaves, or by a virus carried by those insects. Sprinkling wood ash or spraying neem oil water helps control these pests before they ruin the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ nɔ Tso mli sũ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ kooloi nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually eaten by small caterpillars, such as the Diamondback moth larvae. Inspecting under the leaves regularly and using botanical sprays like neem seed extract can stop them before they destroy the cabbage head.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ diamondback ŋmei lɛ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ kaabii baa lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi daa, ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ tamɔ neem dumɔwui amli nu lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo. Abaanyɛ akpa amɛ dani amɛfite kaabe yitso lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to stay green and healthy, or that excessive rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni mɔ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ená hewalɛ. aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ efɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Covering the soil, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, holds water longer during hot days, and stops weeds from growing and stealing your crop's nutrients.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli. ni etsĩɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and shrink on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly in wet, shaded conditions where air cannot flow freely between trees.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela lɛ kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli. he ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ atsɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ oya lɛ

english: Your cassava likely has Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny whiteflies and by planting stems taken from already sick plants.
ga: Ekolɛ o-kasa lɛ yɛ kasa mosaic hela. Hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ gbɛɔ eshwaa. kɛtsɔ ŋmeii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ momo lɛ amli lɛ nɔ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when the plant does not have enough nutrients to feed developing fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni nu lɛ haaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be loo be mli ni tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tso lɛ yibii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually because the soil moisture levels keep changing too drastically.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni haa ebaa lɛ nakai ji akɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ miitsake oya tsɔ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto stakes instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miwoɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines gets the leaves up into direct sunlight so the plant can make more food, which leads to much bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulu la shɛɔ baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo niyenii babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei wuji babaoo baa.

english: Why is it bad to plant my crops very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaadu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting too closely forces your crops to fight over sunlight, water, and soil food, making them grow thin and weak while helping diseases spread faster.
ga: Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awuu kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ daraa bibii ni amɛhe waaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt in the hot afternoon even when the ground is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli be mli ni mi lɛ shwieee lɛ? Nɛgbɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can suck it up from the soil, causing the plant to temporarily droop to save moisture.
ga: Yɛ shwane gbi lɛ mli lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔɔ waa. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ tso lɛ agbo yɛ be kukuoo mli koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: Why do my plantain leaves dry up and tear during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ egbi ni egbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dry, windy Harmattan air sucks water out of broad plantain leaves very quickly, causing the leaves to split and dry up as the plant tries to save water for its stem.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ plantain baai amli oya. Enɛ haa baai lɛ mli gbalaa ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekɛ nu ato etsitsi lɛ he lɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously on the same soil wears out the specific nutrients maize needs to grow strong. It also allows pests and diseases that attack maize to build up in the soil, leading to weaker crops and lower harvests over time.
ga: Kɛ́ aya nɔ adu ŋmã yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekwɛ̃ lɛ afite. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa ŋmãa lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii baa shi ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ hu baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: How far apart should I plant my cassava cuttings so the roots can grow big?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu mi-cassava niji lɛ kɛjɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ tɛŋŋ koni shishifãi wuji aba?

english: Cassava needs about one meter of space on all sides. When planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, small tubers instead of thick ones.
ga: Cassava he miihia he ko ni miihe ashɛ mita kome yɛ efãi fɛɛ. Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ yitsei ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: Extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two healthy suckers ensures the main plantain tree gets enough energy to produce a large, heavy bunch of fruit.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi loo tsei lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa plantain titri lɛ naa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ aduawai akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants full of holes and small caterpillars?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworms. These pests hide inside the tender center leaves of the young maize plant to eat, which can stunt the plant's growth if not caught early.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai bibii lɛ amli koni amɛye nii. Enɛ baanyɛ atsĩ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa kɛji akɛ amɔmɔɔɔ amɛ oya.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck the sap out of the leaves and spread viruses, causing the foliage to twist and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli. Enɛ haa baai lɛ tsɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛkpaa dalɛ ni sa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather is extremely hot and dry, or if the soil lacks moisture. The heat damages the pollen inside the blossom, preventing it from forming a fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa ni edɔ waa. aloo kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ Dɔlɛ kpataa ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ hiɛ. ha efee nɔ ni wooo yibii

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings need to be planted next to shade crops like plantain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu kookoo tsei bibii yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct, harsh sunlight and burn easily. Fast-growing shade plants like plantains act as natural umbrellas, providing cooler temperatures and moisture while the young cocoa roots establish.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni naa wa lɛ he waa, ni amɛshãa oya. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shade. Ha dɔlɛ ni mli ejɔ kɛ latsaa be mli ni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ shwereɔ.

english: How can I tell if my yellowing crop leaves mean the plant needs fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ mitso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: When older leaves at the bottom of the plant turn pale green or yellow first while the top leaves stay green, it usually means the soil is low in nitrogen, which is a key food plants need for leafy growth.
ga: Be ni baai lɛ daa yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, amɛfeɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ klɛŋklɛŋ, yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ yaa nɔ amɛfeɔ eŋɔli. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni baai lɛ adara lɛ

english: Why do my pepper leaves look wilted in the hot afternoon even if I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgboi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the soil. As long as the soil is damp, the leaves usually recover and stand back up in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Shii abɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ he waaa ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Weeds are wild plants with deep, tough root systems that are adapted to jump into action immediately when water arrives, allowing them to quickly steal nutrients and sunlight from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. ni atsake koni etsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nu ba Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ onibii amli lɛ oya.

english: I have been growing yams on my land for years, but now my harvest is poor. Why does yam farming exhaust the soil?
ga: I have been growing sweet potatoes on my land for many years. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ, minitsumɔ lɛ ehiii kwraa. Why does cooking sweet potatoes deplete the soil?

english: Yam plants are heavy feeders that pull large amounts of nutrients out of the earth as their tubers grow deep underground. Harvesting them removes those nutrients from the field, leaving the soil tired and hungry if you do not restore it.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji niyenii ni tsii ni gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ lɛ. Nikpamɔ jieɔ nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni hɔmɔ yeɔ lɛ kɛji okɛ hewalɛ haaa lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I tell by looking at my land that the soil has lost all its goodness?
ga: Kɛ́ mikwɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ, te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ehilɛ fɛɛ elaaje?

english: When soil is exhausted, it often looks pale or dry, hardens quickly after rain, and crops planted on it grow slowly with small, yellowish leaves and produce very low yields.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ, bei pii lɛ efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo egbi. Ewaa oya yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ daa blɛoo. Eyɛ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo kwraa.

english: If my land can no longer grow good food crops like yams, can I plant cash crops like cocoa or cashew instead?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ niyenii kpakpai tamɔ ŋmeii dɔŋŋ hu? Ani manyɛ madu shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo loo cashew ŋmeii moŋ?

english: Yes, cash crops like cocoa and cashew often thrive where food crops fail because tree crops develop deep root systems that reach untapped nutrients far below the depleted topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ cashew shwereɔ yɛ he ni niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii nyɛɛɛ atsu nii yɛ lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ jwɛi mli lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni shɛɔ niyenii ni akɛtsuuu nii ni efiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he.

english: How do I know whether my land is better suited for planting cocoa or planting cashew?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kookoo loo cashew ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Cocoa trees need deeper, richer soil with plenty of moisture and shade, while cashew trees are much tougher and perform very well in dry, sun-exposed, or poorer soils.
ga: Cocoa tsei biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ nii babaoo. kɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, Cashew tsei lɛ wa babaoo ni amɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji ni egbi, ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ yɛ nɔ, loo shikpɔji ni ehiii fe nakai lɛ anɔ.

english: When I dig into my farmland, what should I look for to know if the earth is good for planting tree crops?
ga: Beni mifoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Mɛni esa akɛ makwɛ koni mana kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha tsei akwɛmɔ?

english: Look for dark, crumbly earth that is easy to dig into without hitting solid rock or hard clay close to the surface, which allows tree roots to grow long and strong.
ga: Taomɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbɛ eshwa ni abaanyɛ akumɔ mli oya ni atswaaa tɛ ni wa loo shikpɔŋ ni wa ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwaa.

english: Will clearing out old yam roots and mounds help prepare my soil for planting new tree crops?
ga: Ani sweet potato shishifãi momoi kɛ ŋmeii ni ajie lɛ baaye abua ni esaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛha dumɔwui heei?

english: Yes, leveling old yam mounds and removing dead root debris opens up the field, prevents pests from hiding, and gives new tree seedlings a flat, uniform space to grow.
ga: Hɛɛ, sweet potato momo ni ato lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ojie shishifãi ni egboi lɛ baagbele he lɛ naa. Etsiɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anaa koni amɛkatee amɛhe ni ehaa tso dumɔwui heei lɛ náa he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛdaraa po.

english: Why do cashew trees manage to stay green and produce nuts even in very dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cashew tsei lɛ hiɛɔ amɛ su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi waa po mli lɛ?

english: Cashew trees grow long taproots that dive deep into the earth to search for underground water, allowing them to survive heat and drought better than most other crops.
ga: Cashew tsei yɛ shishifãi kakadaŋŋ agboi ni boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyatao shikpɔŋ shishi nu. Enɛ haa amɛnyɛɔ amɛdamɔɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ naa jogbaŋŋ fe tsei krokomɛi.

english: Do I need to put a lot of fertilizer on my land before planting cashew trees?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu cashew tso?

english: Cashews are resilient trees that do not need rich soil to start growing, though adding a little organic compost in the planting hole helps young seedlings establish faster.
ga: Cashews ji tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi, ni ehe ehiaaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii jogbaŋŋ dani amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃. Eyɛ mli akɛ kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko fata dumɔ bu lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua dumɔwui bibii lɛ ni amɛma shi oya moŋ, shi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings struggle to grow when planted in open, sunny soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse nɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and suffer when exposed to hot, direct sunlight, so they need temporary shade from crops like plantain to protect them while they are young.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ amanehulu. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei tamɔ plantains adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe be mli ni amɛji gbekɛbii lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea to completely replace my food crops with cocoa trees all at once?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mikɛ cacao tsei baatsake miniyenii ni miduɔ lɛ shikome?

english: It is safer to transition gradually, because cocoa trees take several years to produce fruit and bring income, while food crops keep your family fed in the meantime.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni yaa nɔ fiofio lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe fe tsutsu lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, cacao tsei lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii ni amɛnáa shika. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, niyenii ni aduɔ lɛ baaha oweku lɛ aná niyenii yɛ be nɛɛ mli.

english: How does having heavy rain every day affect the growth of my crops?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa gbi lɛ saa tsei adalɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: While crops need water, daily heavy rain can drown root systems by pushing air out of the soil, causing yellow leaves, root rot, and washing away vital topsoil nutrients before the plants can use them.
ga: Yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ hia nu Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa daa gbi lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do my crops get stressed or fail to grow well when the rainy season comes late?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ haoɔ loo amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba lɛ?

english: Crops adjust their lifecycle based on predictable seasonal weather; when rains delay, the soil remains too dry and hot, which stops seeds from germinating properly and weakens growing shoots.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛ wala shihilɛi kɛyaa be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni atsɔɔ hiɛ atsɔɔ lɛ anɔ. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baakã he ahi shi ni edɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it important for me to test my farm soil before planting a new crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni maka shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ makwɛ dani madu tsei heei lɛ?

english: Soil testing reveals which nutrients your land is missing and whether it is too sour or sweet, helping you choose the right fertilizer and crop variety instead of guessing and wasting money.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kaa tsɔɔ niyenii mli nibii ni bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔlɔ tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni sa. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni aaasusu nii ahe ni afite shika

english: How do I know if a new seed variety will perform better on my land than my traditional seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji dumɔwui heei baatsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fe dumɔwui ni aduɔ daa lɛ?

english: You can plant a small test patch of the new seed right next to your usual seed under the exact same field conditions to directly compare their growth rate, yield, and resistance to disease.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu kaa ŋmɔ bibioo ko. ni ji dumɔwui heei ni bɛŋkɛ odumɔwui ni okɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli koni akɛto bɔ ni amɛdaraa, amɛwoɔ yibii, kɛ bɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa lɛ he tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Is it worth investing money to rent machinery for my land preparation instead of using manual labor?
ga: Ani ehe yɛ sɛɛnamɔ akɛ akɛ shika baawo tsɔnei ni akɛhaa koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni akɛ adesai anitsumɔ baatsu nii?

english: Using machinery saves considerable time and heavy physical effort, allowing you to clear and till larger areas quickly so you can plant at the very start of the rains for maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne tsu nii lɛ, ehaaa afite be kɛ mɔdɛŋbɔɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ nii oya ni otsuɔ nii yɛ hei wuji. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu amɛ kɛjɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli koni onine ashɛ yibii babaoo nɔ.

english: Why do some new crop varieties stand stronger against drought and pests than older seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii heei komɛi nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ hɔmɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fe dumɔwui momo lɛ?

english: Improved crop varieties are carefully bred and tested by researchers to develop deeper root systems, thicker stems, and natural defenses against common local pests and dry spells.
ga: Akɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ ekwɛ jogbaŋŋ ni niiamlitaolɔi eka amɛ amɛkwɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ, amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ, kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cocoa trees seem to produce fewer pods as they grow older?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo pɛ beni edaa lɛ?

english: As trees age, their overgrown branches create too much shade for themselves, and the soil beneath them loses nutrients over time, leaving less energy for the tree to produce fresh pods.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ eda Amɛniji ni edara fe nine lɛ feɔ hulutsoo babaoo tsɔ. Ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ baafite niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ be ni sa mli. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ aná hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii heei.

english: Why are the leaves of my crops turning yellow even though there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves during wet periods often mean nitrogen has been washed out of the soil, or the roots are too wet to absorb food, making the plant starve despite the rainfall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ajieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ edɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye tsei kɛji nugbɔ nɛ po.

english: How does clearing weeds regularly make my crops grow stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil food directly from your crops; removing them removes competition so your main crops get everything they need to grow thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa lɛ jieɔ akaŋshii kɛyaa. No hewɔ lɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baaná nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants produce flowers but then fail to form fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Vegetable flowers often drop off without fruiting if there are no insects like bees to pollinate them, or if the crop experiences extreme heat and sudden dry shocks during flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii bɛ ni baanyɛ afee pollination, Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shɛ latsaa ni naa wa he ni egbi trukaa yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: What basic steps should I take to prepare my land properly before the rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ afee koni akɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Preparing early by clearing weeds, breaking up hard soil, and creating ridges helps the land trap rain water and allows seed roots to spread easily once the first rains arrive.
ga: Hesaamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee kɛtsɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ hiɛkpatamɔ nɔ Kɛ ŋmeii ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa mlɛo kɛ́ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ba.

english: Can I grow any crops on a piece of land that has a lot of rocks and stones?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ko ni tɛi kɛ tɛi wuji babaoo yɔɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, crops with shallow roots like cowpeas, groundnuts, or cassava can survive in rocky soil better than deep-root crops, though clearing loose stones and adding compost will help them grow much better.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tamɔ cowpeas, peanuts, loo cassava baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ tɛi amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei ni shishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ tɛi ni etse amɛhe lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ moŋ.

english: Does burning dry weeds on my field before planting help or hurt my soil?
ga: Ani jwɛi ni egbi ni mishãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani miduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa loo eyeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui?

english: While burning clears land quickly, it destroys rich organic matter and beneficial insects in the soil; clearing weeds by hand or using them as mulch keeps the soil fertile and moist.
ga: Shi kɛlɛ, la ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi efiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Nine ni akɛjieɔ jwɛi loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How does removing big stones from my field help my crops yield more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tɛi wuji ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛná niyenii babaoo?

english: Removing large stones gives plant roots space to spread out and absorb water easily, while also making it simpler for you to weed, dig, and apply fertilizer.
ga: Tɛi wuji ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛmɔɔ nu oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa bo akɛ obaajie jwɛi, otsa shikpɔŋ, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your plants are hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient that helps crops grow strong, which often happens when heavy rains wash nutrients away or soil is worn out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye otso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa waa Enɛ fɔɔ baa kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa tsei lɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why is it bad to plant many seeds very close together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ewa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni akɛaawo bu kome mli ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ ehiii.

english: When seeds are crowded together, the young plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, resulting in thin, weak stalks that produce very small yields.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ fee ekome yɛ kui amli lɛ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii fioo pɛ baa.

english: Why do crops grow well on my neighbor's farm but struggle on mine even though we live close by?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli shi amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ wɔhiɔ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Soil quality can change completely within a short distance; your farm might have harder soil, less moisture, or lack nutrients that your neighbor added using manure or organic compost.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su baanyɛ atsake kwraa yɛ be kukuoo mli. Ekolɛ oŋmɔ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa fe no. hulutsoo be fioo loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ ni okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot or get destroyed by insects so quickly in the barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ miifite loo helai miibote mli oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize spoils quickly if stored while still damp or in open spaces where insects enter; drying corn thoroughly under the sun and storing it in sealed bags or raised granaries keeps pests and moisture out.
ga: Abɛi baafite oya kɛji akɛ akɛto be mli ni edɔ lolo loo yɛ he ko ni ŋmeii yɔɔ. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu shishi ni akɛto kotoku loo ŋmãa ni atsĩ naa lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmɔtɔ he.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my corn so it doesn't go to waste in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmãa? Bɔni afee ni wɔkashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔji amli?

english: Maize is ready to harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown and the grains feel hard; leaving mature corn in the field too long exposes it to wild animals, rain mold, and insect attacks.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni dumɔwui lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa Kɛ́ ashi ŋmãa ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha koo mli kooloi, ŋmeii, kɛ kooloi bibii atutua lɛ.

english: What can I do to keep my harvested corn safe from mold if it rains during harvest time?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ akafee shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe kɛji nugbɔ nɛ yɛ ŋmãa be mli?

english: Hang the corn cobs under a well-ventilated roof or place them on raised wooden drying racks off the ground so air flows around them and dries them naturally despite damp weather.
ga: Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo tsũ ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ shishi. Aloo okɛwo tso adeka ni awó nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni kɔɔyɔɔ abɔle Abɛi ŋmeii ahe ni eha amɛgbi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ.

english: Fertilizer acts like food for your crops. It provides essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil might lack, helping plants build strong stems, grow healthy leaves, and yield larger harvests.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa onibii. Ehaa niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni ekolɛ ebɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa shishifãi ni wa. ha baai lɛ awa ni ewo yibii babaoo

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist, typically early in the morning or shortly after a light rain. Avoid fertilizing right before a heavy rain, as the water will wash the nutrients away.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, leebi loo yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, tsi ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Ejaakɛ nu hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛyaa.

english: How will I know if I have put too much fertilizer on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo miiwo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: If you apply too much fertilizer, the leaf tips and edges may turn brown and look burned. The plant may also wilt suddenly or grow tall and weak without producing good fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo fata he lɛ Baai lɛ ashishigbɛ kɛ eshishigbɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã. Tsei baanyɛ agbi trukaa loo amɛdara ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai.

english: Can I use both store-bought fertilizer and animal manure on the same farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, using both together is very beneficial. Manure improves the soil's structure and helps it hold water, while store-bought fertilizer provides a quick supply of specific nutrients your crops need right away.
ga: Hɛɛ, nibii enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ekomefeemɔ mli lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Manure haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ shi. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya.

english: Is it true that chicken manure is good for my crops?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmɔtɔ hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, chicken manure is a very rich natural fertilizer. It contains high amounts of nitrogen and organic matter that help crops grow healthy leaves, build strong stems, and improve soil quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmei ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmei ni jara wa waa. Nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Bɔɔ tso ni mli wa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo

english: Can I put fresh chicken manure directly onto my crops right after cleaning the coop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmei hee awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ beni mitsumɔ tsina ŋmei lɛ mli sɛɛ?

english: No, fresh chicken manure is too hot and strong, which can burn your crop roots due to high ammonia levels. You should allow the manure to dry out and rot for a few weeks before spreading it on your farm.
ga: Dabi, tsina fɔmɔ nii hee mli edɔɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã otsei lɛ ashishifãi yɛ ammonia ni fa babaoo lɛ hewɔ. Esa akɛ oha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni egbo otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛshwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Can I use chicken manure to help my papaya trees produce better fruit?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ tsina ŋmɔtɔ aye abua mipapaya tso lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: Yes, papaya trees respond very well to chicken manure. Applying well-rotted chicken manure around the base of the papaya tree gives it a steady supply of nutrients needed to grow strong and produce large, sweet fruit.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, papaya tsei lɛ hereɔ tsina ŋmɔtɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ waa. Kɛ akɛ tsina ŋmei ni egbo ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsuɔ nii Shishitoo lɛ haa papaya tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ eda waa ni ewo yibii wuji ni ŋɔɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my papaya tree turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi papaya tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Papaya leaves usually turn yellow due to a shortage of nutrients like nitrogen, or because the soil is either waterlogged or too dry. Feeding the plant with compost or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, papaya baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ, tamɔ nitrogen ni bɛ, loo akɛni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu loo egbi tsɔ hewɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ ha otsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I spray liquid fertilizer directly on top of my crop leaves instead of putting it in the soil?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu ni ji ŋmɔshi nibii afɔ tso lɛ baai anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛbaawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, this is called foliar feeding. Leaves can absorb liquid nutrients quickly through tiny pores, giving weak or flowering crops a fast energy boost when they need quick nourishment.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ foliar niyenii. Baai lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii bibii amli aŋɔ niyenii ni ji nu lɛ oya. Ehaa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ loo tsei ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ náa hewalɛ oya kɛ́ niyenii he miihia amɛ oya.

english: Can I spray liquid fertilizer on my crops in the afternoon when the sun is very hot?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ afɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, spraying liquid fertilizer under strong afternoon sunlight can scorch the leaves because the liquid droplets act like small magnifying glasses. It is safest to spray early in the morning or late in the afternoon.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ shwie shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha baai lɛ ashã. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu mli nu ni hoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ akɛ oooshwie nɔ lɛ leebi loo shwane mli.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. They require temporary shade crops like plantains or shade trees to protect them and keep the soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off healthy branches from my cocoa tree if I want it to produce more fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso niji ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so the tree does not waste energy on leaves. It lets air and light flow through the tree, which keeps humidity down and helps flowers turn into healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. So that the tree doesn't waste energy on leaves. Allows air and light to flow through the plant. Enɛ haa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: This is usually Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and shady conditions. Clearing heavy weeds and letting sunlight into the farm helps prevent water from staying on the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, fɔ́, kɛ hulutsoo kɛbaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ babaoo kɛ hulu la ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ kɛboteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni nu akakpɛtɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do the small flowers on my cocoa trees drop off instead of turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi lɛ daraaa lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, mi-cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by drought, lack of nutrients in the soil, or attacks from pests. Feeding the soil and protecting the tree during flowering helps it retain its pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hɔmɔ hao amɛ. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuamɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛ tso lɛ he ni abuɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ etsitsii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the new shoots and leaves on my trees turning brown as if they were burned by fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai heei ni yɔɔ mitso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ nɔ ni la eshã amɛ lɛ?

english: This damage is often caused by insects called capsids or akate. They suck sap from young branches and shoot poison into the plant, which makes the leaves wither and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ capsids loo akates lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei niji bibii amli lɛ ni amɛtswaa tsofa fɔŋ amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli. ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ.

english: Can I grow food crops like cassava together with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ akwɛ niyenii tamɔ ŋmei?

english: You can grow crops like plantain to provide shade, but heavy feeders like cassava can take too much water and nutrients away from young cocoa roots if planted too close.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsei tamɔ plantains koni ekɛ hulutsoo aha. Shi niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmei baanyɛ ajie nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛ kookoo shishifãi bibii amli kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ tsɔ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil is exhausted and needs fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efo mihe ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: When soil loses its fertility, crops grow very slowly, leaves turn pale green or yellow, and the trees produce fewer or smaller fruits than usual.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli loo ŋmɔŋ. ni tso lɛ woɔ yibii fioo loo bibii fe bɔ ni efɔɔ daa lɛ

english: Why do weeds lower the yield of my crops even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii baa shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds compete with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the dirt. They also trap moisture and harbor insects that spread diseases to your plants.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Emɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ hu ni ekɛ kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ helai eshwaa otsei lɛ anɔ lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Cocoa pods are mature when their skin changes color completely from green or dark red to a clear yellow or orange. Harvesting them at this stage ensures the seeds inside are fully developed.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛji amɛhiɛ su tsake kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look sickly after a long period of heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehiii yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Too much standing water drowns crop roots by cutting off air in the soil. Without air, roots rot and cannot send food up to the leaves, making the plant turn yellow.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ shwieɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni efoɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagboi ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu niyenii kɛya ŋwɛi kɛtsɔ baai lɛ anɔ. Ha tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ

english: Why do I need to make big soil heaps for planting my yams instead of planting directly in flat land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama sũ agbo ko ni akɛdu sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow downwards and need soft, loose earth to expand easily. Hard soil blocks their growth and makes the yams small or misshapen, while high heaps gather fertile topsoil and keep the tubers well-drained.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ni ehe miihia ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɛ eshwa koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsiɔ shweremɔ naa ni ehaa sweet potatoes feɔ bibii loo amɛhe esaaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii ni nɔ kwɔlɔ buaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa lɛ naa ni amɛhaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How deep should I plant my plantain suckers when establishing a new farm?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ amli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ mima ŋmɔ hee?

english: Plantain suckers should be planted deep enough—about knee-deep—so that strong winds will not blow the heavy adult plant over when it starts carrying a big cluster of fruit.
ga: Esa akɛ adu plantain tsei lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa. (aaafee tsitsi nɔ) koni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa akatswa tso ni eda lɛ beni ebɔi aduawai akui wuji womɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil is wet enough to start planting my maize after the first rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Gather a handful of soil from your farm and squeeze it tightly. If it holds together in a ball without dripping excess water, the ground has absorbed enough moisture for your maize seeds to germinate successfully.
ga: Bua sũ ko naa kɛjɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni okɛwo mli. Kɛji akɛ ebɔle ehe ni nu babaoo shwieee shi lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves of my young maize plants being eaten from the inside out during the hot weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ayeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the warm center leaf roll of maize plants; treating them early prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni mli edɔ lɛ amli yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ atsa amɛ mra lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot on the tree when the rains become very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rains and high humidity encourage a fungal attack called Black Pod disease, which spreads through water drops landing on the pods and requires regular harvesting and proper farm clearing to control.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo woɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ black pod hela lɛ he hewalɛ. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ Ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmɔji lɛ daa ni ajie amɛ jogbaŋŋ koni akɛkudɔ.

english: Why do white powdery spots appear on my pepper leaves during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder yɛŋ jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-pepper baai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is powdery mildew, a disease that thrives when daytime weather is warm and humid but soil is dry; keeping the ground moist and giving plants enough space helps stop its spread.
ga: Powdery mildew ji hela ko ni baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ ni edɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli shi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni oha tsei lɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekpa shweremɔ.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves during dry periods to conserve water and protect their underground tubers; as soon as the rains return, the plant will shoot fresh green leaves and resume growing.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba pɛ kɛkɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaada ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem without producing any tomatoes when the weather gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat damages the pollen inside tomato blossoms so fruit cannot form, causing the plant to drop the useless flowers to save energy until temperatures cool down.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi amli lɛ. Ehaa aduawai lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shiɔ fɔfɔi ni he ehiaaa koni amɛkɛto hewalɛ he kɛyashi hulutsoo be lɛ mli baa shi.

english: Why do cowpeas grow so well on poor soil even when I do not apply chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ? No kɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fataaa he?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that trap nitrogen directly from the air through their roots, feeding themselves and leaving natural nutrients behind in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni ŋmɛɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Ha ohe niyenii ni oshi adebɔɔ mli niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the new leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli koni ekɛye baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain plants produce very small bunches when I let many stems grow together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantain lɛ woɔ panicles bibii waa kɛ́ miha tsei babaoo shwere yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When too many plantain suckers grow around one mother plant, they all compete for the same soil food and water, leaving less energy for any single plant to make big bunches.
ga: Beni plantain tsei babaoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nyɛ kome tso lɛ he lɛ Amɛ fɛɛ amɛyeɔ niyenii kɛ nu he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ. Enɛ haaa tso fɛɛ tso aná hewalɛ fioo ni ekɛfee kuu agbo.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas on my land help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei ni miduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, which naturally fertilizes the ground for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha kooloi aniyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaf funnel and chew on the emerging foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baa ni miiba lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by bacterial wilt or root rot fungus in the soil, which clogs the plant's internal tubes so water cannot reach the stem and leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ji bacteria wilt loo fungal root rot ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. ni tsiɔ tsei amli paipii lɛ anaa Nu nyɛɛɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ baai lɛ ahe.

english: Why do young cocoa trees die when I clear away all the big canopy trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii gboiɔ kɛ́ mijie ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade trees to protect them from direct heat and conserve soil moisture until their roots grow deep.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he, ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ mli baawo shɔŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant my cassava stick at a slant instead of pushing it straight down or upside down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu mi-cassava lɛ yɛ koŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni matsi lɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya shi loo matsɔ hiɛ?

english: Planting cassava cuttings at a slant allows the roots to grow horizontally near the surface where soil is rich, making it easier for large tubers to form and be harvested.
ga: Yucca niji ni aduɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daraa yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni sũ eyi mli obɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa bulb lɛ daraa ni ehaa ekpamɔ waaa.

english: Staking gets the yam leaves off the wet ground to prevent fungal rot and exposes more leaf surface to sunlight, which the plant uses to feed and expand the tuber underground.
ga: Staking baajie sweet potato lɛ kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni fungal rot akafite ni eha baa lɛ hiɛ hulu la babaoo aba. ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ ni amɛkwɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii

english: Why do my crop leaves curl up tightly during the middle of hot days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up on hot days to reduce their surface area exposed to the sun, which stops the plant from losing too much moisture into the hot air.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ anɔ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ akafite ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without producing any fruit when it gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa he lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen, causing the plant to drop its flowers naturally to save energy for survival rather than making seeds.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔii kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha wala moŋ fe ni amɛaawo dumɔwui.

english: Why are people telling me not to throw away crop waste like cocoa pods and plantain peels anymore?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi miikɛɛ mi akɛ mikashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni efite tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ plantain ŋmɔji lɛ ashwie shi dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crop waste like cocoa pods and plantain peels contains valuable plant nutrients. When allowed to decompose into compost, this waste acts as free fertilizer, restoring organic matter and moisture to your soil without needing expensive chemical inputs.
ga: Tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli tamɔ kookoo ŋmɔji kɛ plantain ŋmɔji amli. When left to decompose into compost. This waste acts as a free fertilizer. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: How does adding animal manure to my farm help my crops survive long dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kooloi ashishifãi ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Animal manure acts like a sponge inside the soil. It improves the soil's structure so it can hold water for much longer, giving your crop roots steady moisture and food even when rains are sparse.
ga: Koolooi ashishifã tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji yɛ sũ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Ehaa otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo po.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant pulls whatever nutrients it has left from its older bottom leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ gbalaa niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni eha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ adara.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tight during hot afternoons?
