ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to protect themselves from losing too much water in intense sun. However, if they stay curled all the time, it means tiny insects like mites or thrips are hiding underneath and sucking the juice out of the leaves.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe koni nu babaoo akafite yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Shi, kɛji amɛfo amɛhe be fɛɛ be lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii Ekɛ ehe teeɔ shishi ni ekɛ nu lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ amli.

english: Why does my mango tree yield plenty of fruit one year, but produces almost nothing the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango woɔ yibii babaoo afi kome shi afi ni baa lɛ, eshɛɛɛ eko kwraa lɛ?

english: Mango trees often practice what is called alternate bearing. After spending a huge amount of energy producing a heavy harvest, the tree gets exhausted and spends the following year resting and storing up food energy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mango tsei feɔ nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsakemɔ. Beni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsu nii ni ekɛkpa nii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ, no sɛɛ lɛ, egbɔjɔɔ ni ekɛ afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ebuaa niyenii hewalɛ naa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that create a living umbrella, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool soil they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni haa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa cacao tsei bibii lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why do my cassava plants produce thin, woody roots when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When cassava plants are crowded, their roots fight each other underground for limited water and plant food. Without enough room and nutrients, no single plant can store enough food energy to swell into large, thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ tsei niyenii fioo. Kɛji he ko kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso ko bɛ ni baanyɛ ato niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛda ni etsɔ ŋmei agbo ni mli edɔ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow much faster than my crops even after I apply fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with deep roots that absorb water and fertilizer faster than cultivated crops. If you apply fertilizer before clearing weeds, the weeds will drink up the food first and choke your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ mli kwɔ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo mli dani okɛ jwɛi lɛ shwie shi lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaye nii klɛŋklɛŋ ni ebaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop off the stem before producing any fruit during high heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ dani ewoɔ yibii yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Extreme sun and hot weather burn the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing fruit from forming. When heat stress gets too high, the plant cuts off the flower to save its remaining water for basic survival.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashã ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Etsiɔ aduawai anaa koni amɛkafee Kɛji dɔlɛ he haomɔ fa tsɔ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ mli kɛha shishijee wala.

english: Why does my harvested maize rot quickly inside the storehouse if I harvest on a wet day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ nitoohe lɛ mli kɛji mikpa yɛ gbi ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize harvested in wet weather traps damp moisture inside the grain cob. When stored damp in a dark, warm place, mold and small insects quickly multiply and destroy the crop.
ga: Abele ni akpaa yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ mli lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli ewo ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ewo duŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii babaoo yaa hiɛ oya ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so fast if I leave them in my hot room?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomatoes continue to breathe and age after harvest. Warm air speeds up this process and encourages mold growth, while keeping them in a cool place slows down decay and keeps them fresh much longer.
ga: Tomatoi yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛdaraa yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ yaa oya ni ewoɔ ŋmeii adalɛ he hewalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ oha amɛfee fɛ̃i lɛ, ebaaha amɛfite fioo, ni ebaaha amɛhi shi ehee be babaoo.

english: How can I make sure my fresh vegetables don't spoil when transporting them to distant markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni mi-vegetables heei lɛ akafite kɛ́ akɛmiiya jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Harvesting crops early in the morning when it is cool, keeping them shaded, and using cold storage or insulated containers prevents heat buildup that causes vegetables to wither and rot during transit.
ga: Kɛ́ akpa ŋmɔshi nibii leebi be mli ni hulu lɛ miitso, ni ehaa hulutsoo baa, ni akɛ nibii ni mli ejɔ loo nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi dɔlɛ ni haa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ yaa lɛ naa.

english: Is it better to sun-dry my peppers or keep them in a cold place to preserve them for months?
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha chili lɛ agbi loo okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ koni okɛto nyɔji babaoo.

english: Sun-drying removes moisture for long-term room-temperature storage, but cold storage preserves the original fresh texture, color, and flavor of the peppers without needing to dry them out.
ga: Gbimɔ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛtoɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ tsu mli dɔlɛ mli. Shi kɛ́ akɛto friji mli lɛ, ehaa bɔ ni chili lɛ yɔɔ tsutsu lɛ, bɔ ni eyɔɔ, kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ ha lɛ hiɔ shi, ni ehe ehiaaa ni agbi.

english: What causes my green plantains to turn yellow and go soft so quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo oya yɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Plantains naturally produce a ripening gas called ethylene as they warm up. Storing them in a cool, shaded environment reduces gas production and keeps them green and firm for a longer period.
ga: Plantains jieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ baa beni amɛdɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ oha efee fɛ̃i ni eyɛ hulutsoo lɛ, ebaaha gas ni ajieɔ lɛ aba shi. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Can I keep my dry maize seeds in a cold fridge or freezer to protect them until the next planting season?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni egbi awo friji loo friza ni mli ejɔ mli? Ani ebaanyɛ ebu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, cold temperatures put seeds into a deep sleep state and prevent pests from attacking them, but the seeds must be completely dry before freezing so ice doesn't destroy the seed inside.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ haa dumɔwui lɛ wɔɔ waa ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baatutua amɛ. Shi esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi kwraa dani amɛfee ais. Enɛ ji koni ais lɛ akafite dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Will freezing temperatures kill the weevils that eat my stored beans?
ga: Ani hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ baagbe ŋmeii ni yeɔ mi ŋmeii ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Freezing stored beans for a few days stops insect activity and destroys weevil eggs without needing chemical powders, keeping your grain safe for long-term storage.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni ato lɛ wo fɛ̃i mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akatsu nii, ni ebaafite ŋmeii lɛ ni akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii amli lɛ tsuuu nii. Enɛ haa odumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛha be kakadaŋŋ ni akɛtoɔ.

english: How long can crop seeds remain good for planting if kept in a cool, dry place?
ga: Be enyiɛ abaanyɛ akwɛ dumɔwui kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi?

english: When stored in cool, low-humidity conditions, most seeds remain healthy and capable of germinating for many months or even several years beyond their normal season.
ga: Kɛ akɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo be faaa lɛ. Dumɔwui babaoo baahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ̃ nyɔji loo afii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛfeɔ daa lɛ.

english: Why does cassava start turning dark and spoiling just two days after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei jeɔ shishi ewoɔ duŋ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii enyɔ pɛ ni akpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Once harvested, cassava roots react quickly to oxygen in the air, causing rapid rot; keeping them chilled or processing them immediately stops this chemical reaction.
ga: Kɛji akpa Cassava shishifãi lɛ tsuɔ nii oya kɛha kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa fitemɔ baa oya. Friji loo nitsumɔ haa tsofa nɛɛ tsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my yams rot or sprout quickly in the barn while others last for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ ekomɛi fiteɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni ekomɛi hiɔ shi nyɔji babaoo lɛ?

english: Yams require cool temperatures and good airflow to remain dormant. Excessive warmth triggers sprouting or fungal rot, which shortens their shelf life.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni tsɔɔ mli koni amɛhi shi ni amɛwɔ. Dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ kɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baa. Enɛ baaha be ni akɛtoɔ lɛ afee kuku.

english: Why is it dangerous to put freshly harvested maize into sealed bags before it is dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ baawo kotoku ni atsĩ naa mli dani egbi lɛ?

english: Trapped moisture in sealed bags creates high heat and humidity, causing dangerous mold and toxins to grow quickly on the grain, making it unsafe to eat or sell.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ kotokui ni atsĩ naa lɛ amli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni fa babaoo baa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Ehaa ebɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aye loo ahɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape before the corn is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: When lower leaves turn yellow starting from the tip and moving down the center vein, it means the crop is running out of nitrogen in the soil. Maize takes available nitrogen from its older, lower leaves and sends it up to nourish the new growth at the top.
ga: Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ baa lɛ naa kɛyashi shishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi heɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai bibii lɛ amli ni ekɛtsuɔ nii kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing tall with thick leafy leaves, but the roots inside the ground remain very thin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni mli tse lɛ? Shi shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ egbɔjɔ waa lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure but not enough potassium, the cassava crop puts all its strength into producing heavy foliage above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakɛ starch awo ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmei tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛfeɔ baai ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is the plant's natural shield against heat and drought. By curling its leaves tightly, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun and dry wind, preventing moisture from escaping quickly through leaf pores.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ he. Kɛ́ abɔle baai lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ he ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ baa shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekatsɔ baai lɛ amli ŋmeii lɛ amli oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die if I clear away all the tall shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have soft leaves and shallow root systems that burn easily under full sunlight. Canopy shade trees protect young cocoa from harsh heat and preserve air moisture, acting like living umbrellas while the roots mature.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kpoji lɛ ahe hulutsoo lɛ buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ kã be mli ni shishifãi lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience severe temperature changes, lack of water, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. The plant sacrifices flower development to conserve water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ tsake waa, nu bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ. Tso nɛɛ kɛ fɔfɔii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ shaa afɔle koni ekɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala.

english: Why do my ripening tomato fruits develop a dark, flattened rot on the bottom end while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ shishigbɛ ŋwɛigbɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This rot is caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil into the fruit. It is usually triggered by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets soaked.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ashishigbɛ fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ agbala calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛya aduawai lɛ amli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni afɔɔ yɛ he ni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa.

english: Why are small dark spots spreading across my tomato leaves, turning the leaves yellow and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji bibii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tomato baai lɛ fɛɛ mli nakai lɛ. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: These leaf spots are signs of fungal infection spread by moisture and rain splashing soil onto lower leaves. As microscopic fungi grow, they destroy leaf cells, preventing the leaf from producing energy for the plant.
ga: Nɛkɛ baai nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni jɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ he okadi. Kɛji ŋmeii bibii lɛ dara Ebaakpãtã baa mli wala yibii lɛ ahiɛ. Etsiɔ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee hewalɛ kɛha tso lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cowpea crop look full of tiny holes like a fishing net?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni bu bibii eyi mli obɔ lɛ? Tamɔ ŋshɔŋ wuo?

english: Leaf chewing insects like beetles or caterpillars are feeding on the leaf tissue between the hard veins. These holes reduce the leaf area capable of capturing sunlight, which slows down the plant's growth.
ga: Kplukai ni yeɔ baai, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Amɛmiiye baa lɛ mli fãji ni yɔɔ fãji ni mli wa lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Buji nɛɛ haa baa lɛ he ni baanyɛ ashɛ hulu la lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: Why do crops growing in one corner of my farm look dark green and bushy, while crops in another corner stay pale and short?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ koŋ ko nɔ lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ afã kroko lɛ nɔ lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ kuku.

english: Soil depth, water drainage, and organic matter vary across a single field. Areas where rainwater collects or topsoil has washed away create uneven nutrient levels, causing crops in the same field to behave differently.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ, nu ni hoɔ, kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ he fɛɛ he. Hei ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa loo ehoɔ kɛyaa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ feɔ ekome. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ.

english: Why do weeds make my young maize plants turn pale and slender if I do not clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi-babi corn tsei lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛji mijieee amɛ oya lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively draw up groundwater and soil nutrients before crop roots can reach them. This root competition starves the young crop of light and food during its critical early growth stage.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ sũ mli oya dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɛkɛ shishifãi ahe akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ naa la kɛ niyenii yɛ amɛdalɛ mra be mli ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and wither when I clear away all the large shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive direct, harsh sun. They need partial shade from plantains or shade trees to protect their tender leaves from drying out while their root system is still developing.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei amli koni ebu baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo lɛ.

english: Why should I remove the extra small suckers growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maŋɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? ni kwɛ̃ɔ kɛbɔleɔ Ajieɔ plantain shishitoo titri lɛ.

english: Too many suckers compete with the mother plantain stem for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Removing extra suckers ensures the main plant gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo tsɔ kɛ plantain lɛ tsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do the lower leaves of my maize plants start turning yellow in a V-shape starting from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmã tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ amɛnaa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. The plant moves nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed the young growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow lots of lush green leaves but produce very few flower pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ fɔfɔii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes leguminous plants put all their energy into leafy growth instead of flowers and seed pods. Balanced nutrients or lower nitrogen levels encourage pod formation.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui ahe ŋmeii najiaŋ. Niyenii ni ja loo nitrogen ni baa shi lɛ baawo pod feemɔ he hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits in the soil without draining away, it suffocates the roots and encourages soil fungal rot.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need full sunshine to make food. Lifting the vines on tall stakes spreads the leaves out to catch light and keeps them off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and helping roots grow large.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni fa bɔni afee ni amɛhoo. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko nɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbɛ ashwã koni emɔmɔ la lɛ ni eha ehiɛ akafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Etsiɔ baa helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants falling off without turning into any pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper aduawai lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when plants experience stress from high heat, dry winds, or poor pollination. Without proper flower fertilization during warm daytime hours, the plant sheds blossoms to save energy.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ afɔɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling upwards and looking twisted and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ bibioo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips, which spread plant viruses, or by extreme hot weather where leaves curl to prevent moisture loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ eshwaa tsei amli loo kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa mli he ni baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite lɛ.

english: Why is it beneficial for me to plant groundnuts or beans on my plot before planting maize the next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani madu ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that capture nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally enriching the land for heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and wilt in the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ?

english: On hot afternoons, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can draw it from the soil. The leaves temporarily wilt to conserve water and normally recover by evening when temperatures drop.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛhiɛ nu mli. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ beni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen or are standing in too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving soil drainage helps them regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele tsei lɛ miiye nitrogen loo amɛyɛ nu babaoo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni mli kwɔ ni amɛdara waa lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know the best time to apply fertilizer to my crops so it does not go to waste?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Bɔni afee ni akafite lɛ?

english: Fertilizer works best when crops are actively growing and the soil is damp, usually two to three weeks after germination. Applying it to dry soil or right before heavy downpours can burn the roots or wash the nutrients away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tsei miida ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli yɛ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni ŋmɔ lɛ ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ loo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaashã shishifãi lɛ loo ebaafɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground before I even get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani amɛná hegbɛ po ni amɛkpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soil for too long, causing fungal infections. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. cause fungal infection Dumɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ bulb lɛ he.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts alongside my maize will help my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii yɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and other legumes trap nitrogen from the air and trap it in their roots. When they grow beside maize, they act as a natural fertilizer, making the soil richer without you having to buy extra chemicals.
ga: Peanuts kɛ legumes krokomɛi Emɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmãa fata he lɛ Amɛbaatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe tsofai krokomɛi.

english: Curling leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that spread viruses. Spraying natural insecticidal soap or neem oil early prevents these pests from damaging new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli samla loo neem fɔ ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ baashwie nɔ mra Enɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ akafite ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Why do insects attack my cowpea plants as soon as they start bringing out flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛji amɛje fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers and young pods are sweet and rich in nutrients, which attracts sap-sucking pests like pod borers. Protecting your crop with safe organic or recommended sprays right at the start of flowering safeguards your harvest.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ŋɔɔ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Amɛgbalaa kooloi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ pod borers lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ bu onibii ahe kɛjɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu onibii ni okpa lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of moisture, or attacks by mirid pests. Keeping shade trees over young cocoa and watering during dry spells helps flowers develop into healthy pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa Tso lɛ ni oooha ehi kookoo tsei bibii anɔ kɛ nu ni awoɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: What causes my tomatoes to split open on the vine just when they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni haa tomato kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Tomatoes crack open when their water supply suddenly increases, such as heavy rain after a dry stretch. The inside of the fruit grows faster than the skin can stretch, so maintaining regular, steady watering prevents splitting.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛ́ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tee hiɛ trukaa, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ nu ni mli egbi be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ lɛ nu daa kɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaatsi enaa koni ekagbala.

english: Why do my bearing plantain trees keep falling over during heavy rains and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when carrying full bunches. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo or wooden forks gives them structural support against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ eyi obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei loo tsei ni akɛfee ŋmei tsu nii ni akɛwaje tso lɛ shishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛfi ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ koni ekɛshi kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slow and thin even when I clear the land before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida blɛoo ni efee mlɛo lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ mijie jɛmɛ dani midu nii moŋ.

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal sunlight, soil nutrients, and moisture from your crop's roots. Clearing weeds within the first four weeks of crop growth removes this competition so your crops can grow thick and healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni jɛɔ otso lɛ shishifãi amli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii ejwɛ ni tso lɛ daa lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni ejie akaŋshii nɛɛ kɛya. Bɔni afee ni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to buy certified seeds in original factory-sealed packages instead of unsealed loose seeds from the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase yɛ shishijee tsɔne ni akɛwo mli ni nitsumɔhe lɛ etswa lɛ mli lɛ? Mohu ɔ, mo he dumɔwuhi nɛ a ngma we nya ngɛ jua nɔ.

english: Factory-sealed seed packages ensure you are getting clean, disease-free seeds with high germination rates. Loose seeds sold out of open sacks may be contaminated with pests, mixed with low-quality grain, or damaged by moisture, leading to poor crop emergence.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ haa onaa dumɔwui ni he tse, ni hela bɛ mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya. Dumɔwui ni egbee shi ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ kotokui ni agbele mli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ewo mli. ni akɛ dumɔwui ni ehiii efutu mli loo ŋmɔtɔ efite lɛ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and moisture they need to survive their first couple of years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ni amɛnáa hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are flooded with water and cannot breathe. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea when the soil is moist will help turn the leaves dark green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea fata he beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Which direction should the stems point when I am burying cassava cuttings in the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ esa akɛ tso lɛ yitso lɛ atsɔɔ kɛ́ adu ŋmei nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the shoots will struggle to grow upward, resulting in weak stems and very low root yields.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni ŋmeii lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ Shoots baaná naagba yɛ shweremɔ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi lɛ hu baa shi waa.

english: Why should I bury fertilizer near the plant roots instead of broadcasting it over the top of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ tsei shishifãi ahe moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Placing fertilizer near the root zone ensures the crop gets direct access to the nutrients. If you scatter it on top, sun heat can evaporate the nutrients into the air, heavy rain can wash it away, or nearby weeds will feed on it instead.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo he ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji ogbɛ eshwa ŋwɛi Dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli lɛ baanyɛ ajie niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo lɛ kɛya. Aloo jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaye lɛ moŋ.

english: Why are small caterpillars hiding inside the central funnels of my corn plants during the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ amɛhe teeɔ mi-ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ feɔ fɛo lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that feeds on the soft growing tissues inside the maize funnel. Applying recommended biopesticides or placing clean wood ash into the funnels early in the morning helps destroy them before they ruin the crop yield.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmeii ŋmeii amli lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii loo tso mli sũ ni he tse ni akɛwoɔ hoppers lɛ amli leebi lɛ baaye abua ni efite amɛ dani efite ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: Maize draws a lot of nutrients out of the earth, leaving the soil tired. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally grab nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, refreshing the land for the next crop.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, etɔ sũ lɛ. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ afata he lɛ he kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruits during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes their pollen to dry up, making the flowers drop off before fruit can form. Providing shade nets or watering the base of the plants consistently in the early morning helps prevent flower loss.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa pollen lɛ gbɛ́ɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo. Kɛ́ okɛ shade netting ha loo okɛ nu wo tso lɛ shishi daa leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do wild weeds grow back so much faster than my crops after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that have deep, aggressive root systems adapted to local conditions, allowing them to drink water and soil nutrients instantly, whereas cultivated crops take longer to establish their roots.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni etsɔ ehe ewo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. Enɛ haa amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni adu lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛshishifãi shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize grains are dry enough to bag without rotting in storage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-corn kernel nikpamɔ lɛ mli egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mawo kotoku mli ni efiteee yɛ nitoohe lɛ?

english: You can use the simple bite test: bite a maize kernel with your teeth. If it makes a sharp, clean cracking sound, it is dry enough. If it feels soft or dents without cracking, it still holds moisture and will grow mold inside a bag.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ ŋmɔlɔ kaa ni yɔɔ mlɛo atsu nii: okɛ onyanyɔŋ ŋmɔlɔ ŋmei ŋmei. Kɛji gbee ni naa wa ko ba lɛ, no lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa. Kɛji enu he akɛ eyɛ bɔdɔɔ loo eyɛ ŋmeii ni etseee Ebaahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lolo ni ŋmɔtɔ baakwɛ̃ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees burn and dry up when I do not plant plantains around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni miduuu plantains yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are soft and sensitive to direct, intense sunlight. Plantain trees grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist while the young cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ darako ni amɛnuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo tsei bibii lɛ daraa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient the plant uses to grow green and leafy. When nitrogen in the soil is depleted or washed away by heavy rain, the plant steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai lɛ. Beni nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fite loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei heei ni eda yɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when rain sits on my farm for a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need oxygen from the soil to survive. When water collects and stays on the field, it cuts off the air supply, causing the roots to drown and rot quickly due to soil bacteria and fungi.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ nu bua ehe naa ni ehi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ebaakpa kɔɔyɔɔ ni baa lɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ahewɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop all their flowers without producing any fruits during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry conditions put stress on tomato plants. To protect themselves from losing too much water and energy, the plants drop their flowers instead of putting energy into growing fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Koni obu ohe kɛjɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ babaoo ni ofiteɔ lɛ he. No sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting tightly together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny insects like mites or thrips hiding under the leaves and sucking out their plant juices. As the damaged leaf cells continue to grow, the leaf warps and curls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii, tamɔ mites loo thrips, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. yɛ be mli ni baa mli wala yibii ni efite lɛ yaa nɔ edaa lɛ. Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over when the fruits start getting big, even without strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ aduawai lɛ bɔi kwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ko bɛ po lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when their underground root system is damaged by pests like nematodes or root borers. Without a healthy root network anchoring the plant into the soil, the tree cannot support the heavy weight of the developing fruit bunch.
ga: Plantains gbeeɔ shi kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ nematodes loo shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ fite amɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ shishifãi ni mli wa ni ŋmɛɔ tso lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ lɛ, Tso lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ aduawai akui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ amli tsiimɔ ni tsii lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high to spread their leaves open to capture as much sunlight as possible for food production. Keeping the vines off the wet ground also prevents humidity-loving fungal diseases from attacking the foliage.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ kɛha niyenii feemɔ. Wein tsei ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tutuaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ.

english: Why do some of my maize cobs come out with missing grains or empty spaces on the cob?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii lɛ ekomɛi bɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Missing grains happen when pollen from the top flower (tassel) fails to land on the silk strands of the cob during hot or windy days. Every silk strand must receive a grain of pollen for a full kernel of corn to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui ni elaaje lɛ baa kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ amli pollen (tassels) lɛ nyɛɛɛ akpɛtɛ cob lɛ siliki lɛ he yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa lɛ amli. Esa akɛ siliki kpã fɛɛ kpã aná pollen ŋmei kome koni eda ni etsɔ dumɔwu ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does planting cowpea or groundnut on my land make the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas and groundnuts have friendly bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil. When the plants finish growing, this extra nitrogen remains in the soil as natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ naanyobɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ egbe naa Nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and weak when I put many seeds closely together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa beni mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo bɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the seedlings to compete fiercely with one another for soil nutrients, groundwater, and sunlight. Giving each seed adequate space allows its roots and stem to develop fully without crowd competition.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ anɔ koni amɛye akaŋ waa koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ mli, kɛ hulu la lɛ mli hewalɛ. Kɛ́ aha dumɔwui lɛ eko fɛɛ eko gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkɛ asafo babaoo lɛ yeee akaŋ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves is usually a sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore healthy leaf color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baa lɛ su ni hi jogbaŋŋ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmei loo ŋmei yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi ŋmei lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil. This naturally enriches the soil, helping your maize grow better without needing as much expensive chemical fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ye obua o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he ehiaaa.

english: This is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stem varieties is the best way to keep your harvest safe from this disease.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmei mosaic hela. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kasava henɔi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaanyɛ otsɔ nɔ oha onibii akahi hela nɛɛ he.

english: What is making small holes in my corn leaves and leaving brown powder inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ anɔ ni mishiɔ powda ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm pest. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended treatments, like neem leaf extracts or targeted sprays, helps stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Fall Armyworm tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni ajieɔ yi tamɔ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mɔ he lɛ atsu nii. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily in direct sun. Planting plantain or banana trees next to them provides shade and holds moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui loo banana tsei ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Ha hulutsoo ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or lack of water. Giving plants regular water and protecting them from severe heat helps the flowers stay on and produce fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo nu ni faaa yɛ emli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ afɔ tsei anɔ nu daa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Lifting the vines on stakes exposes leaves to more sun and keeps them off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Wein tso lɛ ni ooowo nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ baaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe, ni ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ehe akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Koni akɛtsi baa helai anaa

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open right before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miikwɛ̃ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes split when watering is irregular, such as a long dry period followed by heavy rainfall. Keeping the moisture in the soil even and steady prevents the fruit skins from cracking.
ga: Tomatoi tswaa kɛji nu ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ baatsi aduawai ahe ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala.

english: Why should I leave specific spaces between my plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ tsei ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Giving crops proper space ensures each plant gets enough sunlight, water, and soil nutrients without fighting its neighbors. Proper spacing leads to healthier plants and bigger yields.
ga: He ni sa ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ ekutsoŋbii lɛ awuu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and grow slowly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛdaraa blɛoo lɛ?

english: Weeds act as competitors that steal food, water, and sunlight away from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your main crops full access to what they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ akaŋshilɔi ni juɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otso titri lɛ naa nɔ ni he hiaa lɛ lɛ fɛɛ koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Does rice really need to grow in standing water all the time, or can I grow it on dry land?
ga: Ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni adu ŋmãa yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Aloo abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Not all rice needs standing water. Swamp rice (lowland rice) thrives in flooded fields because water keeps weeds down and supplies moisture, but upland rice can grow on normal dry land like maize, as long as there is regular rainfall.
ga: Jeee ŋmãa henɔi fɛɛ biɔ nu ni damɔ shi. Swamp rice (lowland rice) kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli ejaakɛ nu lɛ hiɛɔ jwɛi ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Shi gɔŋ nɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ egbi tamɔ ŋmãa nɔ. Shii abɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ

english: Why do some of my rice plants produce pale, empty heads with no grains inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ayitsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty rice heads—often called 'whiteheads'—usually happen when insects like stem borers attack the plant stem from inside, or when extreme heat and lack of water hit the plant right when it is flowering.
ga: Omɔ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ‘yitsei yɛŋ’ lɛ fɔɔ baa beni kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Etutuaa tso lɛ shishifã lɛ kɛjɛɔ emli. Aloo kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni bɛ lɛ saa tso lɛ he beni fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ pɛ kɛkɛ.

english: How can I tell if a piece of land is suitable for starting a new rice farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ko sa kɛha ŋmãa ŋmɔ hee shishijee?

english: Good rice land usually has heavy soil with clay that holds water well rather than loose sandy soil. If water naturally settles on the land after rain without draining away too quickly, it is a great site for lowland rice.
ga: Omɔ shikpɔji kpakpai lɛ fɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni tsii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni sũ yɔɔ mli ni hiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ fe shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji nu gbee shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni etsɔɔɔ oya tsɔ lɛ, Eji jɛɛhe kpakpa hu kɛha ŋmãa folo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is the best way for me to clear fresh bush land before putting seeds in the soil?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ majie tsei heei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ dani mikɛ dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Clear the bush by cutting down weeds and shrubs, but avoid burning everything if possible. Leaving organic matter to decompose builds rich soil, and leveling the ground helps water spread evenly across your field.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni ooofo lɛ nɔ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni okɛshãa lɛ he kɛji ebaahi. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ gbɛ ni amɛfite lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ ni baa nii baa. Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ooofee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔji lɛ amli pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: If I harvest a good yield of rice, can I save those seeds to share with other farmers for the next season?
ga: Kɛji mikpa ŋmãa ni miná yibiiwoo kpakpa Ani manyɛ makɛ nakai dumɔwui lɛ ato koni mikɛ okwaafoi krokomɛi agba he sane yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Yes, but you must select seeds only from healthy, strong plants. Dry the seeds properly until they are hard, and store them in airtight containers so they stay healthy and germinate well when shared.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui kɛjɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ amli. Gbimɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ooja.

english: How should I store my saved crop seeds so insects do not destroy them before planting time?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ ato tɛŋŋ? Bɔni afee ni kooloi akafite lɛ dani be ni akɛduɔ nii lɛ aba.

english: Ensure seeds are thoroughly sun-dried until they crack between your teeth rather than bend. Store them in clean, sealed sacks or containers off the bare floor in a cool, dry room to keep moisture and pests away.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi amɛbaatswa ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni amɛaakumɔ. Okɛto kotoku loo tsɛnsi ko ni mli tse ni atsĩ naa mli yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi mli koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better for me to plant my crop in straight rows instead of scattering seeds all over the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ moŋ fe ni madu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each crop equal space, sun, and nutrients to grow big. It also makes it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa. kɛfata he koni amɛdara Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo hu akɛ oootsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa ŋmaa.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my young crops right after I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ beni midu amɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive anywhere, so they quickly grab sunlight, water, and nutrients before your crops can establish roots. Clearing weeds early gives your young crops a head start to grow tall.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe koni amɛhi shi yɛ he fɛɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya dani onibii lɛ shishifãi baa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ adara babaoo.

english: When is the right time for me to apply fertilizer to my rice crop?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa awo ŋmãa tsei amli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied in stages: a base application during planting to help roots grow, and a top-dressing of nitrogen (like Urea) when the rice starts tillering (producing new shoots) and before flowering.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ fãi srɔtoi amli: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa waa yɛ dumɔ be mli koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. kɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii (tamɔ urea) ni akɛwoɔ mli beni ŋmãa jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ (ŋmãa heei) kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the leaves of my young crops turning yellow even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for green, leafy growth. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli kwɛ̃ɔ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why does it take several months or years before my crops produce food after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ nyɔji loo afii babaoo dani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ niyenii beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops must first establish roots, stems, and leaves to support fruit development. Each crop has a biological growth cycle that requires time to accumulate energy before it can mature and yield food.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee shishifãi, tsei, kɛ baai ni baaye abua aduawai lɛ adalɛ. Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ wala yibii adalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni eheɔ be dani ebuaa hewalɛ naa dani enyɛɔ edaa ni ewoɔ niyenii.

english: Why do tree crops like cocoa take years to yield, while maize produces food in just a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji fioo pɛ mli.

english: Different crops have different life cycles; seasonal crops like maize mature quickly to provide fast food, while long-term tree crops spend their early years growing strong trunks and branches so they can yield high returns for many years.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ wala shihilɛi srɔtoi. Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be mli tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa oya kɛha niyenii ni ayeɔ oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ ni amɛdaraa. Koni akwɛ tsei akui kɛ tsei niji ni mli wa koni ekɛ yibii babaoo aha afii babaoo.

english: How will I know when my crops have fully matured and are ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Crops show visual signs when mature, such as leaves turning yellow, fruits changing color, stalks drying up, or tubers reaching full size under the ground.
ga: Tsei baajie okadii ni anaa kpo beni amɛdaraa lɛ, tamɔ baai ni baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ. Yibii lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ, tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gbɛ́ɔ, loo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei lɛ daa kɛyashɛɔ egbɔ.

english: Can poor rainfall or bad soil slow down the time it takes for my crops to grow and mature?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ jogbaŋŋ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ baanyɛ aha be ni heɔ koni ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛ̃ ni amɛshwere lɛ asɛɛ afo?

english: Yes, plants need consistent water and soil nutrients to grow. Without enough water or nutrients, crop growth stags, which delays maturity and reduces the overall yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei be fɛɛ be dani amɛnyɛ amɛdara. Kɛji nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tso lɛ dalɛ haa edalɛ sɛɛ foɔ ni ehaa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some crops produce flowers first before they give me any food?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi fɔɔ fɔfɔi dani mihaa amɛ niyenii lɛ?

english: Flowering is a key stage in crop growth where the plant prepares to create fruits or seeds. The flowers must be pollinated before they can turn into the food you eventually harvest.
ga: Fɔfɔi fɔmɔ ji gbɛ ni he hiaa waa yɛ tso dalɛ mli ni tso lɛ saa ehe koni ewo yibii loo dumɔwui. Esa akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ awo mli dani yɛ naagbee lɛ amɛbatsɔ niyenii ni okpaa.

english: Is crop farming really a profitable business that can support my family long-term?
ga: Ani tsei ahe nitsumɔ ji nitsumɔ ko ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he diɛŋtsɛ ni baanyɛ aye abua miweku lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli?

english: Yes, crop farming is a sustainable business because demand for food is constant. With proper land management, quality seeds, and patience until maturity, a farm can provide significant profit and long-term security.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei akwɛmɔ ji nitsumɔ ko ni yaa nɔ ejaakɛ niyenii ni ataoɔ lɛ yaa nɔ daa. Kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa nɔ lɛ, dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsuishitoo kɛyashi be mli ni Okwaafoi lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ aha sɛɛnamɔi wuji kɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli shihilɛ aba.

english: Why do I have to keep spending money on my crops long before I make any income from them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafite shika yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be kakadaŋŋ dani manyɛ maná shika kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: Farming requires upfront investment in seeds, land preparation, weed control, and fertilizer to help crops grow healthy. This initial care ensures the crops reach full maturity and generate high returns at harvest time.
ga: Okwaayeli biɔ ni akɛ shika awo dumɔwui amli, shikpɔŋ saamɔ, kɛ jwɛi akwɛmɔ. kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa Nɛkɛ shishijee kwɛmɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli.

english: How can I feed my family while waiting for my slow-growing crops to mature?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ miweku lɛ yɛ be mli ni mimɛɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: You can practice intercropping by planting fast-yielding food crops, like cassava or vegetables, between your long-term crops so you have food and quick income while waiting for the main crops to yield.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ intercropping atsu nii kɛtsɔ niyenii ni woɔ yibii oya tamɔ ŋmei loo aduawai ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ koni eha bo niyenii kɛ shika oya be mli ni omɛɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is earning income from farming different from receiving a regular monthly job salary?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika ni anáa kɛjɛɔ okwaayeli mli lɛ yɛ srɔto yɛ nyɔmɔwoo ni anáa daa lɛ he lɛ?

english: A regular job pays a fixed amount at set intervals, whereas farming rewards you with larger, bulk payouts only when crops complete their growth cycle and are sold at harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nitsumɔ ko woɔ shika ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha be pɔtɛɛ ko. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, okwaayeli woɔ bo nyɔmɔ babaoo kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii shɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara kwraa, ni ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ pɛ kɛji akpa.

english: What should I do with the money I earn after harvesting my crops to keep my farm profitable?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ shika ni minine shɛɔ nɔ beni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ koni miŋmɔ lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ?

english: After harvesting, you should reinvest a portion of your profits into farm inputs like fertilizer, improved seeds, and maintenance for the next season to guarantee continuous harvests for your family.
ga: ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Esa akɛ okɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni oná lɛ fã ko awo ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ dumɔwui ni asaa lɛ amli ekoŋŋ. kɛ saamɔ kɛha be ni baa lɛ koni eha oweku lɛ aná kpamɔ ni yaa nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, a key nutrient in the soil. Giving the crops the right fertilizer at the right time helps them grow green and produce heavy ears of corn.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ha otsei lɛ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi ni tsii.

english: Maize needs fertilizer twice: a small dose when planting or shortly after germination to help roots grow, and a second dose when the crop reaches knee-height to help the ears develop.
ga: Abɛi he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii shii enyɔ: fioo yɛ be mli ni aduɔ loo beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara. kɛ shi ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tso lɛ shɛɔ etsitsi nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua toi lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central funnel of the plant. Checking early and treating the center of the plant with safe pesticides or neem extract can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nubu lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji ni ekumɔ yɛ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Ni akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ tsuɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ he nii lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa.

english: Why do my cassava leaves look twisted with yellow patterns on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni efite ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted leaves with yellow spots are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant cassava stems from agricultural officers is the best way to prevent it.
ga: Baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Kooloi bibii eyɛŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ duɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ naa.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants burn and die when I clear all the trees from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie tsei lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn under direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains around them keeps the moisture in the soil and protects them while they are small.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ebuɔ sũ lɛ he be mli ni eyɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ.

english: Yam plants need sunlight on their leaves to make food and grow big tubers under the ground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so all leaves catch sunlight and stay free from soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la, ni helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Will planting cowpeas together with my maize spoil my crop?
ga: Ani cowpea ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ baafite miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: No, planting cowpeas or beans with maize actually helps the soil. Beans feed the soil with natural nutrients that maize needs, so both crops can do well together if spaced properly.
ga: Dabi, tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Beans haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ baanyɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛji akɛ amɛteŋ jɛkɛmɔ sa.

english: Are improved seed varieties from local researchers really better than saving seeds from my own harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui srɔtoi ni atsake kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ mli niiamlitaolɔi adɛŋ lɛ hi fe dumɔwui ni jɛ mi diɛŋtsɛ mikpamɔ mli lɛ ni mikɛbaahere?

english: Improved seeds bred by local Ghanaian scientists are tested to survive local droughts, resist common diseases, and yield much more grain than seeds saved from previous harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni Ghana jeŋ nilelɔi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kwɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ jɛmɛ hɔmɔ mli. Enyɛɔ eshiɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmaa babaoo fe ŋmaa ni aŋmala ashwie shi kɛjɛ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil is wet enough to plant my seeds after the first rain comes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain can be misleading. Squeeze a handful of soil; if it forms a soft ball that holds together without dripping water, the soil has enough moisture for planting.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ baanyɛ atsɔ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Mimɔ sũ ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden drying of tomato plants in wet soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot from wet conditions. Rotating tomatoes with corn or cassava prevents these soil organisms from attacking your crops.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ tomato tsei ni shwieɔ shi trukaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ baa ji bacteria wilt loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake tomato lɛ, ebaatsi shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkatutua oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I plant my crops in straight rows instead of just scattering them across the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja moŋ fe ni magbɛ amɛ ashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows helps you manage space efficiently, makes weeding easier, and allows each crop to get enough sunlight and soil nutrients to grow properly.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebua bo ni okwɛɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni enáa hulu la kɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How does creating specific rows on my land make my farming work easier?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii pɔtɛɛ ni mifeɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa mi okwaayeli lɛ feɔ mlɛo?

english: Using rows creates clear paths through your farm, making it simple to walk around, apply fertilizers, inspect crops for pests, and harvest without stepping on plants.
ga: Kɛ okɛ rows tsu nii lɛ, ehaa gbɛ ni yɔɔ faŋŋ tsɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooonyiɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛji tsɛŋemɔ helai yɛ mli. ni okpa ni onyiɛɛɛ tso lɛ nɔ

english: What happens if I plant my plantain suckers too close together without any order?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔ ko bɛ he?

english: When crops are crowded without proper row spacing, they fight each other for water and sunlight, resulting in weak plants and smaller yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ebɔle amɛhe ni sɛɛgbɛ ni sa bɛ amɛteŋ lɛ, ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha nu kɛ hulu la Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: How can changing the way I arrange my crops increase the amount of harvest I get?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ bɔ ni mitoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ mihaa lɛ ni matsake lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni minine shɛɔ nɔ lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Arranging crops in an organized row system allows you to maximize space so you can safely fit more plants per acre, directly increasing your total harvest.
ga: Kɛ́ oto ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onáa he ko babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii shweshweeshwe yɛ acre kome mli. Ha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aya hiɛ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do some plantain farmers get far more bunches from their farm than others with the same land size?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain okwaafoi komɛi naa ŋmeii babaoo kɛjɛɔ amɛŋmɔji amli fe okwaafoi krokomɛi ni shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ tamɔ amɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Farmers who use standardized row layouts can plant a higher density of healthy crops per plot without overcrowding them, giving them a much higher crop count at harvest.
ga: Okwaafoi ni kɛ gbɛjianɔtoo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ tsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ adu tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ni amɛhaaa tsei lɛ eyi obɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ayibɔ yaa hiɛ kɛ́ akpa.

english: How do I know if my new planting arrangement is actually giving me better results?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ midumɔ hee lɛ miiwo yibii kpakpai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You will know it is working when the total quantity of crop bunches you harvest is significantly higher than what you used to get from the same land size using old methods.
ga: Obaale akɛ eetsu nii kɛ́ ŋmeii ni okpa lɛ fɛɛ fa kwraa fe nɔ ni kulɛ obaaná kɛjɛ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ kɛtsɔ blema gbɛi anɔ lɛ.

english: What is the best way to harvest plantains directly from the field to keep them good?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akpaa plantains kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni akɛbu srɔtoi kpakpai ahe?

english: Harvesting directly from the standing plant by carefully cutting the bunch allows you to collect mature, clean fruit without damaging the rest of the crop.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa tso ko ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔ eniji lɛ ni oookpa jogbaŋŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa aduawai ni he tse ni ekwɛ̃ ni ofiteee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Does row planting help me calculate how much harvest I should expect from my farm?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mibuɔ yibii ni manyɛ makpa gbɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he akɔntaa?

english: Yes, planting in fixed rows makes it easy to count your plants accurately, allowing you to estimate your total harvest long before it is time to collect the crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ oookane otsei lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ obuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni obaaná lɛ he akɔntaa be kakadaŋŋ dani be shɛɔ ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I try new farming methods recommended by extension officers instead of sticking to my old ways?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maka okwaayeli gbɛ hee ni mi-extension agent lɛ wo he ŋaa lɛ makwɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookpɛtɛ blema gbɛi lɛ ahe lɛ

english: Adopting modern practices like row planting reduces wasted effort, improves farm organization, and helps you get a much higher yield from your land.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ nifeemɔi tamɔ dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ lɛ baa shi. Ha ŋmɔ mli gbɛjianɔtoo aya hiɛ ni eye ebua bo ni oná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it hard to switch my farm setup from traditional random planting to structured row planting?
ga: Ani ewa akɛ matsake miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo kɛjɛ kusum naa dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛya dumɔ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: It requires a bit of extra planning and land preparation at the beginning, but once the rows are set up, daily work becomes faster and your harvest increases.
ga: Ebiɔ gbɛjianɔtoo fioo kɛfata he kɛ shikpɔŋ he saamɔ yɛ shishijee mli. Shi beni ato line lɛ daa gbi nitsumɔi lɛ baafee oya ni okpamɔ lɛ baaya hiɛ.

english: Can I just bring a small bag of soil from my farm to your office to be checked, or do you have to come to my land yourself?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ sũ kotoku bibioo ko aba. Ani manyɛ maba o-ɔfis lɛ koni makwɛ mli kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ oba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You can collect soil samples yourself and bring them to the office, provided you take small scoops from several different spots across your field and mix them together so the test accurately represents your entire farm.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ ko aba bo diɛŋtsɛ ni okɛya nitsumɔhe lɛ. Kɛtsɔ skɔpu bibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ hei srɔtoi ni bɔle ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛfutuɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Bɔni afee ni kaa lɛ adamɔ shi aha oŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: How do I know if the soil on my land is good enough to grow cocoa or maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu kookoo loo ŋmãa?

english: Different crops prefer different types of soil. Soil examination measures nutrient levels and texture to show you exactly which crops will thrive or what fertilizers you need to add for a successful harvest.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ shikpɔŋ srɔtoi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa susuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ ha lɛ he koni etsɔɔ bo tsei ni baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ehe hiaa ni okɛfata he koni ŋmaa lɛ aye omanye?

english: When is it better for an extension officer to visit my farm in person rather than me coming to the office for advice?
ga: Mɛɛ be extension nitsulɔ ko baasara miŋmɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooba ɔfis lɛ koni obabi ŋaa

english: You should request a farm visit when your crops show widespread signs of disease, sudden wilting, or unusual pest damage, as seeing the field environment helps the officer diagnose full-scale field issues.
ga: Esa akɛ obi ni abasara bo yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miitsɔɔ hela he okadii ni egbɛ eshwa he fɛɛ he lɛ. ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi trukaa loo nibii ni fiteɔ nii ni jɛɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni bɛ tɛ̃ɛ mli baa Enɛ ji akɛ, shihilɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni akwɛɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa onukpai lɛ ni amɛnaa naagbai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How often should I get the soil on my farm examined by an officer?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Testing or examining your soil every two to three years is usually sufficient to monitor nutrient loss and help you make smart choices about fertilizers before planting new crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ kaa loo kwɛmɔ fɛɛ mlikwɛmɔ Bei pii lɛ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛkwɛɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni elaaje lɛ nɔ ni eyeɔ ebua bo ni ohalaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani odu tsei heei.

english: If I acquire a new piece of farmland in a different town, will my crops grow the exact same way as on my old farm?
ga: Kɛji minine shɛ shikpɔŋ hee nɔ yɛ maŋ kroko nɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ tamɔ bɔ ni mikwɛ̃ yɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Soil quality and water retention vary greatly from one location to another. Land in a new town may have different sandiness, nutrient levels, or acidity, meaning your crops may require different care.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha kɛ bɔ ni nu lɛ hiɔ mli ehaa lɛ waa yɛ he kome kɛyaa he kroko. Ekolɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ maŋ hee lɛ mli lɛ ji ŋã. Nutrient level loo acidity sɔrɔtoi Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ abi ni akwɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ srɔtoi anɔ.

english: Why do my crops dry out and wilt so quickly when I plant them in sandy soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ gĩɔ ni egboɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋã shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Sandy soil has large particles that allow rainwater to drain away very quickly instead of staying near the plant roots. Adding organic matter like compost or animal manure helps sandy soil retain moisture much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ nibii bibii wuji ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeebɛŋkɛ tsei shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does the dark or light color of my farm's soil tell me how well my crops will grow?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ loo ni mli tse lɛ tsɔɔ mi bɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ aha?

english: Yes, dark brown or black soil usually indicates rich organic matter and plenty of nutrients, while lighter or reddish soil often contains fewer nutrients and may require extra compost or fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ loo ediŋŋ tsɔɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo tsuru lɛ amli niyenii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni ekolɛ ehe baahia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: Yellow leaves often mean the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become too acidic for the plant roots to absorb food properly.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hia, tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my seeds struggle to sprout when I plant them in very hard, packed soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa waa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Hard, tightly packed soil prevents tender young roots from pushing through to find water and nutrients. Loosening the soil before planting ensures roots can spread easily and breathe.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkabote mli koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ dani adu lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo ni amɛmuɔ.

english: If the soil on my farm is poor and crops are not growing well, can it be fixed or do I have to leave the land?
ga: Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ehiii ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hu edaaa jogbaŋŋ. Ani abaanyɛ asaa loo esa akɛ mashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: You do not need to abandon poor soil. Adding compost, animal manure, or growing cover crops over time restores lost nutrients and rebuilds the soil so crops can grow well again.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa ni oshi shikpɔŋ gbonyo. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ fata he yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni etswa shikpɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my land produce less crop every year even though I clear and weed it properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ baa daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni mijieɔ jwɛi kɛjɛɔ nɔ moŋ?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the earth every time they grow. If you do not give the soil time to rest or add organic material back into it, the land becomes exhausted and cannot feed new plants.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be ni amɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛji ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he ekoŋŋ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafo ni tsei heei nyɛŋ aye abua.

english: How does leaving my land untouched for a few seasons help bring back its strength?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni mashi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko etaaa nɔ yɛ bei fioo komɛi amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ekɛ ehewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ?

english: When land rests, wild plants and grasses grow and drop leaves that rot into rich organic food. Their roots break up hard ground and pull deep nutrients back to the surface, naturally renewing the soil.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ he jɔɔ lɛ Koo mli tsei kɛ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛjɛɔ amɛbaai ni egboi lɛ amli amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbatsɔ niyenii ni jara wa, ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli. Amɛshishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa mli ni amɛgbalaa niyenii mli nibii kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shɔŋŋ. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa

english: Why does using chemical fertilizer alone make my soil hard and dry after a few harvests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa ni egbiɔ yɛ ŋmaa fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?
