english: Chemical fertilizer provides quick food directly to the plant, but it does not nourish the living organisms in the earth. Without organic matter like animal manure or compost, the soil loses its structure and water-holding ability.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ niyenii oya tɛ̃ɛ. Shi ekɛ niyenii haaa wala yɛ je lɛŋ. Kɛji nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii bɛ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ egbɛjianɔtoo kɛ nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ nu lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stunt when the field stays flooded with rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbɔjɔɔ kɛ́ nu shwie ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Plant roots need air to breathe just like humans do. When water sits on the field for too long, it chokes the roots, preventing them from soaking up the nutrients needed to keep leaves green.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tso shishifãi he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Leaf curling is a natural survival trick. The plant rolls its leaves to expose less surface area to the hot sun, preventing its precious water from evaporating into the air.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ he ŋaa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ bɔni afee ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akashɛ amɛhe fioo. Enɛ haa nu ni jara wa lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with huge leaves but leave me with small, thin tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When a plant gets too much shade or excessive nitrogen, it spends all its energy building leaves and stems above ground instead of storing food in its root tubers below.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ná hulutsoo babaoo loo nitrogen babaoo Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Why should I buy new improved seeds from the agricultural office instead of using saved seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved seeds are bred to withstand local dry spells and resist common diseases better than old seeds, helping you get a larger yield from the same plot of land.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsɔse amɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi yɛ maŋ lɛ mli hɔmɔ shihilɛi amli, ni helai ni afɔɔ namɔ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe fe dumɔwui ni etsɛ. Eyeɔ ebua bo ni onáa yibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Why do insect pests attack my crops much more heavily during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii waa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Hot, dry weather stresses plants and weakens their natural defenses. Pests multiply faster in warm temperatures and target these weak plants for easy food and moisture.
ga: Shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ ni ehaa amɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu hewalɛ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ nɛɛ anɔ koni ená niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mlɛo.

english: Why is it harmful to plant tomatoes in the exact same patch of ground every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Pests and diseases that target tomatoes stay hidden in the soil after harvest. Planting the same crop in the same spot feeds those pests year after year, allowing them to ruin future harvests.
ga: Akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ tomato nɔ lɛ teeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ. Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aaakwɛ yɛ he kome lɛ baaha nakai kooloi lɛ aye nii afi fɛɛ afi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfiteɔ wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How does planting cover crops like beans help protect my farmland from rain damage?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ, tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe koni nugbɔ akafite?

english: Cover crops spread across the ground like a carpet. Their leaves soften the impact of heavy rains so soil does not wash away, while their roots fix natural nitrogen into the earth to feed future crops.
ga: Nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tamɔ kapɛti. Amɛbaai lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baa shi. koni shikpɔŋ lɛ akaho yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akɛ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni akɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii.

english: If I start raising pigs, how can my crop farm benefit from having pigs on the land?
ga: Kɛji mibɔi tsinai akwɛmɔ Te mi ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ baaná tsinai akwɛmɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ he sɛɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Pig manure is full of natural nutrients like nitrogen and organic matter. When you dry or compost the manure and spread it on your farmland, it improves the soil so crops like maize and cassava yield better without relying heavily on expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Kplotoo mli eyi kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Beni ogbiɔ loo okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli ni okɛshwãa he ni oduɔ nii yɛ lɛ. Ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa aná yibii kpakpai ni ekɛ ehe akafɔ̃ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ anɔ.

english: What crops can I plant on my farm to feed pigs so I do not spend too much money on feed?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii manyɛ madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛha tsinai niyenii? Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ofite shika babaoo yɛ niyenii he.

english: Crops like cassava roots, sweet potatoes, maize, and green leaves can be grown to feed pigs. Growing these crops yourself keeps your feed costs low and turns leftover crops into meat you can sell.
ga: Abaanyɛ adu nibii tamɔ ŋmãa shishifãi, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni akɛye tsinai. Kɛ́ bo diɛŋtsɛ odu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ, ehaa oniyenii he nyɔmɔwoo baa shi, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ feɔ loo ni obaanyɛ ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield smaller harvests every season when I plant on the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa be mli ni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops pull nutrients out of the earth as they grow. If you plant the same crop every season without adding compost, manure, or resting the land, the soil becomes exhausted and cannot nourish new crops properly.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ odu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ejɔɔɔ mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ tsei heei jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do crops like groundnuts or cowpeas help make the soil better for my next farm crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii baanyɛ aye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that feed on air and trap nitrogen in their roots. When you harvest them and leave the stems to rot in the ground, that trapped nitrogen acts as a natural fertilizer for crops planted next.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni amɛtoɔ nitrogen yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji okpa ni oha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa tsei lɛ daraa.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing plants fight each other underground for water and soil nutrients. Their leaves also block sunlight from each other, resulting in tall, thin stalks with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai lɛ hu tsiɔ hulu la naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa baa.

english: Why do farmers plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows quickly and is ready for harvest in three to four months, while cassava grows slowly over a whole year. Planting them together lets you harvest maize early while leaving space for the cassava to spread out later.
ga: Abɛi daa oya ni efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ yɛ nyɔji 3-4 mli, yɛ be mli ni ŋmã daa blɛoo yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. Hefatalɔi adumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ mra ni ehaa gbɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop sprouts die if I plant immediately after the very first rainy day of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ gbi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rainfall is often followed by days of hot, dry weather that bakes the ground. Seeds need continuous soil moisture to develop strong roots, so waiting until the rainy season fully sets in keeps young sprouts from drying up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, gbii ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa koni shishifãi ni wa aba. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baashɛ shi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni dumɔwui lɛ akagbi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow and drop during long dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Plants use water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their leaves. During dry weather, plants drop their lower leaves to save water and keep the main stem alive until the rains return.
ga: Tsei kɛ nu tsuɔ nii kɛ woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛyaa amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ Tsei shiɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ koni ekɛbu nu he ni eha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crop gets all the food and water it needs from the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa onibii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii lɛ aná niyenii kɛ nu fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Covering bare soil with dry leaves or grass keeps the sun from drying out the ground too fast. It holds moisture near the roots, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulu lɛ akagbi shikpɔŋ lɛ oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my young maize crops turning yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa lɛ daa moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves on young plants usually mean they lack essential soil nutrients like nitrogen. Just like a growing child needs good food, young crops need early fertilizer or manure support to build strong roots and healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Taakɛ niyenii kpakpa he hiaa gbekɛbii ni miida lɛ, nakai nɔŋŋ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii hu he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii mra. koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why is my oil palm tree taking several years to produce fruit after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani ewoɔ yibii beni adu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Perennial tree crops take time to establish strong root systems and build up energy. They need extra care and nutrients during their early years before they reach the stage where they can yield heavy fruit.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ he miihia be koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa ni amɛná hewalɛ. Amɛbiɔ kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ kɛ niyenii kpakpa yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Dani ebaashɛ ŋwɛi gbɛhe ni haa yibii ni tsii lɛ nɔ

english: Why do older farmers advise me to plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo onukpa ko wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantains act as living shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa grows strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains ni shwereɔ oya lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo be ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, kookoo daa waa bɔ ni sa ni enine shɛɔ hulu la ni fa nɔ.

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to wooden stakes as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei ahe be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As tomato plants develop, the heavy fruits weigh down the branches. Staking provides physical support to keep the plant upright, preventing stems from breaking and keeping the fruit off the wet ground where it could rot.
ga: Beni tomato tso lɛ daa lɛ Yibii ni tsii lɛ yɛ muji yɛ tsei lɛ aniji anɔ. Staking haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ yelikɛbuamɔ koni tso lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ. Enɛ haaa tso lɛ tso lɛ akumɔ, ni ehaaa aduawai lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ, ni baanyɛ afite.

english: When is the best stage to feed my crops with fertilizer to get a good harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔshi nibii amli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Crops need the most support early in their growth cycle when they are developing roots, stems, and leaves. Feeding them early gives them the push they need to reach their full flowering and fruiting potential.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ he miihia yelikɛbuamɔ fe fɛɛ yɛ amɛdalɛ shishijee mli beni amɛshishifãi, amɛshishifãi, kɛ amɛbaai lɛ miiya hiɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaha amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my seeds very close together to fit more crops in my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves all the plants weak and thin, resulting in a much lower total harvest.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, nibii fɛɛ ni afee lɛ ba shi waa.

english: Removing excess leaves allows the plant to redirect its food and energy away from useless growth and into developing bigger, healthier peppers.
ga: Baai ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ yaa shɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ dalɛ ni he ehiaaa lɛ he. ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out so quickly a day after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbiɔ oya kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛ gbi kome lɛ?

english: Soil with low organic matter cannot hold onto water. Adding compost or dry mulch keeps the soil spongy and moist, ensuring young crop roots have steady water access between rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli faaa yɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa nu be fɛɛ be yɛ nugbɔ be mli.

english: Why do some cassava varieties yield in six months while others take over a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii srɔtoi komɛi woɔ yibii yɛ nyɔji 6 mli, yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu heɔ nɔ ni fe afi lɛ?

english: Different crop varieties have different growth rates built into them. Early-maturing varieties grow quickly for fast harvests, while late-maturing ones take extra time to develop larger root tubers.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ srɔtoi. Henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ daa oya kɛha ŋmaa oya. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei srɔtoi ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ baahe be kroko dani amɛná shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do insects attack the soft new leaves on my plants more than the old leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi babaoo tutuaa baai bibii ni yɔɔ mi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ fe tsei ni egbɔ lɛ?

english: Young shoots and tender leaves are soft and rich in nutrients, making them an easy target for pests. Protecting crops during this delicate early stage prevents stunted growth later on.
ga: Tsoi bibii kɛ baai lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. Kɛ́ abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe yɛ nɛkɛ shishijee be ni he hiaa waa nɛɛ mli lɛ, ebaatsi ŋmɔshi nibii ni edaaa lɛ anaa yɛ sɛɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil, or heavy rains have waterlogged the roots, preventing the plant from taking up food.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa ni haa shishifãi lɛ amli nu shwieɔ shi. Ehaa tsei nyɛɛɛ aye niyenii

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark brown and shrivel up before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads quickly during wet, humid weather when there is too much shade and poor air movement around the trees.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hu eyaaa tso lɛ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with plenty of big leaves, but yielding small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji, shi eyɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen fertilizer or rich animal manure, it spends all its energy producing leaves and stems instead of storing starch in its underground roots.
ga: Beni ŋmei nine shɛɔ nitrogen ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei babaoo nɔ. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ tsei. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How can I easily tell if my soil has enough moisture and good texture for planting tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu fa bɔ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tomato dumɔ?

english: Good soil should feel moist and soft enough to crumble easily in your fist; if it forms a hard, sticky ball, it holds too much clay, and if water sits on top without sinking in, drainage is too poor.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ efo oya yɛ otsitsi mli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni wa ni shwieɔ shi Ebaamɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Ni kɛji nu yɛ ŋwɛi ni efooo shi lɛ, Drainage lɛ ehiii tsɔ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rolling leaves is the plant's natural defense mechanism to protect itself from heat by reducing the surface area exposed to the sun and cutting down water loss.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he kɛtsɔ he ni hulu la shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ ni ebaa shi kɛ nu ni elaajeɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the bottoms of my garden eggs and tomatoes rot and turn black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ tomatoi ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ashishi miifite ni etsɔɔ ediŋŋ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This issue is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium inside the developing fruit, which often happens when soil moisture fluctuates heavily between rainy and dry periods.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei ateŋ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my yam mounds with dry grass or palm leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi loo ŋmei baai awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi sweet potato ŋtayaa lɛ he lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry vegetation keeps the ground cool, retains moisture, prevents heavy rain from washing away the mound, and protects fragile young seed tubers from baking in the hot sun.
ga: Tsei ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya nɔ Etsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ gɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ebuɔ dumɔwui ayitsei bibii ni waaa lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cowpea plants produce many flowers, but the flowers drop off without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii?

english: Flower drop is often caused by tiny insect pests like thrips that feed on the soft flowers hidden inside, damaging them before they can form bean pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni yeɔ fɔfɔi bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kpata fɔfɔi lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛfee pea pods.

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally adapted to your local soil; their seeds wake up instantly with water and absorb nutrients much faster than introduced crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ewo he ni oyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛ nu ni amɛheɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya kwraa fe dumɔwui ni ajieɔ yi lɛ.

english: How do I know that my cassava tubers are mature enough to dig up without wasting the crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsa ni yibiiwoo lɛ sɛɛ efooo?

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop, the lower stem turns thick and woody, and cracks start appearing in the soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ mli tse ni eyɛ tsei. Ni ŋmeii bɔi baa yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and heat. Leaving or planting shade trees like plantains protects them from sun scorch, keeps the soil moist, and helps them survive their early years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni ashiɔ loo aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs in large amounts to grow healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps bring back the green color and boost growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abele babaoo he miihia koni ebaakwɛ baai ni wa. Kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni eha ŋmei lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmei lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains all the specific nutrients maize needs and allows pests to build up in the field. Rotating with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni yaa nɔ aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsu nii yɛ ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight to produce energy for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the hot ground toward the sun and protects them from soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha bulb agboi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking woɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni edɔ lɛ kɛyaa hulu la mli ni ebuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Plantain trunks are made mostly of water and foliage rather than true wood, making them top-heavy. As the fruit bunch grows, wind or weight easily pushes the tree over unless it is propped up with a strong wooden pole.
ga: Nu kɛ baai ji nɔ ni akɛfeɔ plantain tsei lɛ babaoo fe tso diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa tso lɛ shishi tsiimɔ waa Kɛ́ aduawai akuu lɛ miida Kɔɔyɔɔ loo tsiimɔ baanyɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ashwie shi mlɛo. ja akɛ tso ni wa fĩ shi

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow tall and thin with very few fruits when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow thick stems and produce good yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Ragged holes inside the center of young maize plants are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars feeding on the soft leaves. Inspecting the field early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extracts controls them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ yi lɛ atsu nii ni okɛkudɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when there is heavy rain for many days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ gbii babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to remain healthy. Waterlogged soil smothers the roots, preventing them from breathing and creating perfect conditions for harmful fungi to rot the tubers underground.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haaa amɛmu ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa koni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anyɛ afite shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, too little water, or poor soil fertility. Regular watering during hot spells and adding compost helps the plant hold onto its blossoms to set fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli. nu fioo tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akpɛtɛ efɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ewo yibii.

english: Weeds are fast growers and will steal the fertilizer, water, and sunlight before your crops can reach them. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the nutrients you add to the soil.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni ebaaju ŋmɔshi nibii, nu, kɛ hulu la dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ abashɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer to the soil helps restore their bright green color and improves corn cob size.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my cassava stem cuttings rot in the dirt after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava cuttings rot when the ground holds too much water or has poor drainage. Planting your cuttings on raised mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away so the stems can sprout roots safely.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo loo nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni afo yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa jɛmɛ bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Is it helpful to plant groundnuts or beans together with my maize in the same field?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ yɛ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo ŋmei kɛ ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting beans or groundnuts with maize is very good for the soil. These legume crops trap nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps your maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa o-abele lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ waa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteee.

english: How do I know if my land is healthy enough to grow good tomatoes?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu tomato kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil feels crumbly, holds moisture without turning into sticky mud, contains earthworms, and looks dark from rich organic matter. If your dirt is hard like dry clay, mixing in dead leaves or manure will make it suitable for tomatoes.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baanu he akɛ egbɔjɔ. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni etsɔɔɔ muji, shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ebɔle ehe, ni etamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ duŋ kɛjɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo lɛ amli. Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Baai loo ŋmeii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ baaha efee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tomato.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of straight and long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni kɛlɛ lɛ?

english: Yams become small and misshapen when planted in hard, stony, or compacted ground that squeezes the roots. Clearing stones and loosening the earth into high, soft heaps allows the tubers to expand smoothly.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji bibii ni efiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu yɛ hei ni wa, tɛi yɔɔ, loo hei ni mɛi babaoo eyi mli obɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ. Tɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ajieɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛfeɔ ŋtayaa ni nɔ kwɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa bulb lɛ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in water supply. Giving your plants steady watering and light shade during hot dry spells keeps the blossoms attached so fruit can form.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakemɔi trukaa. Kɛ́ aha tso lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni egbiɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ koni amɛwo yibii.

english: What causes small round holes in my cabbage leaves and how do I stop it?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ akpa?

english: Holes in cabbage leaves are usually eaten by small caterpillars or beetles. You can protect your crop by spraying leaves with natural neem seed water or hand-picking the insects off early in the morning.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ŋmeii yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ kaaba baa mli lɛ. Obaanyɛ obu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli neem dumɔwui nu ni oookɛshwie nɔ loo kɛtsɔ onine ni okɛbaakpata amɛhiɛ leebi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still attached to the tree trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ be mli ni amɛkpɛtɛ tso lɛ shishi lolo lɛ?

english: Black cocoa pods are caused by a fungal disease called Black Pod, which spreads quickly in dark, damp shade. Pruning tall cocoa branches lets sunlight in to dry the pods, and picking off infected pods keeps the rest healthy.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ blackpod kɛ kookoo diji baa. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ duŋ ni mli edɔ mli. Kookoo niji ni kɛlɛ lɛ ni aaafolɔ Ha hulu lɛ akpɛ koni eha ŋmeii lɛ agbi. Ni ŋmeii ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amligbalamɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my okra farm produce giant green leaves but very few okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra ŋmɔ lɛ yɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi okra ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Okra produces excessive leaves when it receives too much nitrogen fertilizer or doesn't get enough direct sunlight. Okra needs full sunshine and balanced feeding to focus its energy on flowering and making pods.
ga: Okra woɔ baai babaoo tsɔ kɛ́ enine shɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ loo enine shɛɛɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Okra he miihia hulu ni fa kɛ niyenii ni ja koni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔfɔi kɛ pod feemɔ nɔ.

english: Why do my harvested plantains soften and rot so quickly before I can get them to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-plantains ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya dani mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Plantains ripen rapidly when exposed to direct sunshine, high heat, or rough handling during harvest. Storing them in a cool, shady shed and handling the bunches gently keeps them firm much longer.
ga: Plantains lɛ shwereɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ gbeyei nɔ yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ amɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Ni kɛ́ akɛtsu nii blɛoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow starting at the bottom when the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth, or when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves wilt during the afternoon sun even when I watered them early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ leebi moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot afternoon weather causes leaves to evaporate water faster than the roots can drink it, so the plant temporarily wilts to protect itself from losing too much moisture.
ga: Gbi gbɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be kukuoo mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine lɛ he.

english: Why are flowers falling off my pepper plants without turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Extreme heat, lack of moisture, or using too much nitrogen fertilizer can stress the pepper plant, causing it to drop its flowers instead of setting fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, hulutsoo ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo baanyɛ aha pepper tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ aduawai ni baa lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay small when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full direct sunlight to produce food for its underground tubers; tree shade prevents the leaves from making enough energy to grow big roots.
ga: Hulu la he miihia cassava tɛ̃ɛ koni enyɛ ená niyenii eha eshikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ. Tso lɛ shade lɛ tsiɔ ebaai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha shishifãi wuji akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my seeds sprout quickly after the first rain but then turn brown and die shortly after?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Shi etsɔɔ blɔfo ni egboɔ yɛ no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: If a dry spell follows the initial rain, the newly sprouted seeds run out of moisture in the topsoil before their roots can reach deeper water.
ga: Kɛji hɔmɔ ko nyiɛ shishijee nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ Dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ bɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and shrivel up before they are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in cold, wet conditions and high shade, destroying pods before they fully ripen.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ waa. Enɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛshwere kwraa.

english: Hard, compacted soil or rocks in the mound stop the yam root from expanding downward smoothly, forcing it to bend as it searches for soft dirt.
ga: Shikpɔŋ loo tɛi ni yɔɔ gɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ lɛ baaha sweet potato lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shi mlɛo kɛya shi. ni enyɛɔ enɔ koni ebɔle ehe beni etaoɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why does Striga weed keep appearing around my grain crops in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ Striga jwɛi lɛ miijie ehe kpo yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Midumɔwui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: Striga is a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to crops like maize and sorghum to steal water and food, especially in poor soils that lack organic matter.
ga: Striga ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni ekɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa he tɛ̃ɛ. koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow very tall and thin and fall over when I plant seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they stretch upward to compete for sunlight, which leaves them with thin, weak stalks that snap easily in strong winds.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛkpãa amɛhe koni amɛye hulu la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ, amɛkuɔ oya.

english: Why do the leaves of my groundnut plants turn yellow and begin to dry out when the pods mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally stop feeding their leaves and redirect all remaining energy down into the underground seeds when they finish maturing.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ kpaɔ foliar niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛtsakeɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi dumɔwui amli beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my plantain trees dry up and hang down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ egbi ni efo shi lɛ?

english: Plantain trees naturally shed older outer leaves to send energy to new foliage and fruit. Trimming off dead or diseased leaves with a sharp tool keeps pests away and helps the fruit bunch grow much larger.
ga: Plantains shwieɔ baai ni egbɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni ekɛ hewalɛ awo baai kɛ aduawai heei amli. Kɛ́ okɛ dɛŋdade ni mli wa shwie baai ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ anaa, ni ebaaye ebua aduawai akuu lɛ ni edara babaoo.

english: Is it safe for me to cut off extra branches and leaves from my tomato plants?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mafolɔ niji kɛ baai krokomɛi ni jɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yes, removing lower leaves and small extra shoots helps the plant direct its energy toward producing bigger tomatoes instead of excess leaf growth. It also lets air flow freely to protect against fungal diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie baai kɛ ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ ehewalɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛfee tomatoi wuji. Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ baai ɔmɛ nɛ a wa tsɔ. Ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ hu tsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa.

english: Why should I manually cut off diseased leaves from my crops instead of letting them fall off on their own?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ miniji afolɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mitsei lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha egbee shi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Diseased leaves act as a breeding ground for pests and fungi. Removing them immediately prevents the sickness from spreading across your field and destroying the rest of your harvest.
ga: Baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ojie oya lɛ, ebaatsi hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ ni efite onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or is getting flooded with too much water. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted compost will help restore green, healthy foliage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the tips of my rice leaves turning a reddish-orange color?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ yiteŋ feɔ ŋmãa-tsuru lɛ?

english: Reddish leaf tips in rice often point to iron toxicity or a lack of potassium in flooded soil. Draining the excess water from your field periodically helps air reach the roots and restores normal leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai tsuru ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dade ni yɔɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ faaa loo potassium faaa. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa baa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither when I clear all the large shade trees from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ mijie tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that dry out easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Keeping taller shade trees or planting fast-growing crops like plantains alongside them keeps the soil moist and protects them from heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose all their leaves whenever heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai fɛɛ shwieɔ shi be fɛɛ be ni nugbɔ baanɛ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper roots suffocate and rot when water sits in the soil for too long, causing the leaves to drop. Planting your peppers on raised soil beds allows extra rainwater to drain quickly so the leaves stay attached.
ga: Pepper shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ, ni no haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Pepper ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya koni eha baai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up with tiny white insects on the undersides?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛyɛ kooloi bibii yɛŋ lɛ? Shishi gbɛ?

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies sucking the plant juices. Pruning off heavily infested leaves early prevents the pest population from spreading to the rest of your cassava roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies ni nuɔ tso nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Kpɔ̃ɔ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ waa lɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ayibɔ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa o-cassava shishifãi lɛ fãi krokomɛi amli.

english: Why are dark black spots spreading across the leaves of my yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ egbɛ eshwã mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots on yam leaves are a sign of anthracnose, a common fungal disease that thrives in warm, wet weather. Removing infected vines and leaves stops the fungus from spreading and destroying the tubers underground.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ ji anthracnose hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni yaa hiɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Wein tsei kɛ baai ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haaa ŋmeii lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before any pods can develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or lack of light caused by overgrown branches. Trimming back excess foliage helps the tree save energy to turn flowers into healthy cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji dɔlɛ, nu ni faaa, loo la ni bɛ ni niji ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ kɛbaa lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ afo baai ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ hewalɛ toɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni etsɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa provides living umbrellas that shield the seedlings, maintain soil moisture, and allow strong roots to develop.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ baaha. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ shiŋŋ

english: Yellowing and curling cassava leaves are common symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whitefly insects. These pests suck nutrients from the leaves, causing the plant to weaken and produce much smaller tubers.
ga: Kasava baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ he. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ nuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why do my crops grow pale and weak even when there is plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ lɛ?

english: Water alone is not enough for plants to grow well; they also need essential nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium from the soil. When soil nutrients are depleted from continuous farming, plants become pale and stunted unless enriched with manure or fertilizer.
ga: Nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa koni tsei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam hu he hia amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ba shi kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ Tso lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ. ja akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he.

english: Why should I leave measured spaces between my maize seeds instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Spacing out maize plants gives each stem enough room to capture sunlight, collect groundwater, and absorb soil nutrients. When plants are crowded, they fight each other for resources, leading to thin stalks and small cobs.
ga: He ni ŋmãa tsei lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ ha lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni hulu la baanyɛ aná. shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni akɛtoɔ ni ekɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ shi Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛbaatswa amɛhe adafi koni amɛná nibii ni he hiaa. Enɛ haa tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii baa.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without growing into fruits during hot spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High temperatures and heat stress can destroy the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower fails to get pollinated, the plant drops it to conserve water and nutrients.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa kɛ dɔlɛ mli haomɔ baanyɛ afite pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Tsi pollination naa Beni anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollination Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants growing lots of tall green leaves but no actual peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani chili diɛŋtsɛ ko bɛ?

english: Excessive nitrogen fertilizer causes plants to put all their energy into growing leaves and stems rather than fruits. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to produce flowers and set peppers.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi ni miida lɛ ahe nii. yɛ aduawai najiaŋ Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛtoɔ ŋmeii.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a water mold fungus that thrives in damp, humid conditions. Pruning dense branches and removing infected pods helps airflow and sunlight reach the trees, drying out dampness and slowing the disease.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmei, nu mli ŋmei, ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ, ni mli edɔ mli lɛ mli baa. Niji ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la ashɛ tso lɛ he. Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa helai sɛɛ tsɛɔ.

english: How do weeds lower my crop yields if I do not clear them early?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mi yibiiwoo lɛ aba shi kɛji mijieee amɛ mra?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal soil nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your crops. They also act as hiding places for pests and diseases that attack your farm.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ, nu kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ mli. Amɛji hei hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni tutuaa oŋmɔ lɛ teɔ shi yɛ.

english: Why should I not save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn harvest lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for high yields, but their offspring do not carry the same strong traits. Planting saved hybrid seeds results in uneven growth, smaller cobs, and reduced yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Shi amɛshwiei lɛ bɛ sui ni mli wa tamɔ nɛkɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Cob lɛ ji bibioo fe no. ni yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahemɔ he.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my harvested grains so quickly while in storage bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ oya be mli ni amɛyɔɔ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Weevils and insects thrive in stored grains that still hold moisture. Drying grains thoroughly in the sun before bagging and storing them in airtight containers deprives insects of moisture and air, keeping the harvest safe.
ga: Weevils kɛ kooloi bibii yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni ato ni edɔ lolo lɛ amli. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui yɛ hulu mli dani akɛwo kotoku mli ni akɛto tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi amli lɛ akaje mli. Ha nikpamɔ lɛ afee shweshweeshwe

english: Why should I consider planting soya beans on my farm instead of stick to maize and cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu soybeans ni madu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he yɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Soya beans are valuable because they enrich your soil with nitrogen, cut down fertilizer costs for future crops, and have high market demand from animal feed and food processing factories.
ga: Soybeans he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ ejaakɛ ekɛ nitrogen haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe nyɔmɔwoo shi kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara babaoo yɛ ni jɛ kooloi aniyenii kɛ niyenii feemɔ nitsumɔhei amli

english: Can I plant soya beans alongside my tall maize crop on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu soybeans yɛ ŋmãa kakadaji ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, but you must space them correctly so the tall maize does not block sunlight from the soya, as soya plants need direct light to grow strong and produce healthy seed pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, shi esa akɛ okɛ amɛ abɔ he jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni ŋmãa ni kɛlɛ lɛ akatsi hulu lɛ naa kɛjɛ soybeans lɛ ahe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, soybean tsei lɛ he miihia la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my legume plants produce small, empty pods when there is a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-legumes lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: When crops face dry weather while flowering, they get stressed and lack enough water to fill out the seeds inside the pods, leading to light or empty pods at harvest.
ga: Kɛji tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe wo shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be mli ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ Tso lɛ haoɔ ni ebɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo dumɔwui lɛ amli. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo loo nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛji akpa.

english: Why do crops grow weaker when I plant the exact same crop on the same land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛ́ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Repeatedly planting the same crop depletes specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up, whereas rotating with legumes like soya restores soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni oookwɛ shii abɔ Ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ afite. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ soybeans ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Do soya bean crops require as much chemical fertilizer as maize does to yield well?
ga: Ani tsofai babaoo he miihia soybean tsei tamɔ ŋmãa koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai?

english: No, soya beans work with good soil bacteria to capture nitrogen directly from the air, meaning they require much less chemical fertilizer than heavy feeders like maize.
ga: Dabi, soybean kɛ sũ mli helai kpakpai tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛbiɔ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fioo kwraa fe niyenii ni tsii tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning pale yellow even though I am watering them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nutrients in the soil—especially nitrogen—or poor drainage causing root suffocation, which prevents the plant from making chlorophyll to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen loo nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ afee klorofil koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to harvest my soya beans so I do not lose my crop?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa soybeans? Bɔni afee ni miŋmɔshi nibii akafite?

english: Harvest when the plant leaves dry up and fall off and the seed pods turn brown and rattle when shaken; waiting too long causes pods to pop open and spill seeds onto the ground.
ga: Kpaa beni tso lɛ baai lɛ egbi ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ekpokpoɔ kɛji akpokpo. Kɛ́ mɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fãa ni dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ.

english: Why do market prices for crops drop so low immediately after the harvest season in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ jara baa shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ be lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ?

english: Prices drop because many farmers harvest and sell at the same time, creating a flood of supply in the markets, whereas prices rise later when produce becomes scarce.
ga: Nibii ajara ba shi ejaakɛ okwaafoi babaoo kpaa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli. ni kɛ nibii ni fa fe nine baa jara nɔ yɛ be mli ni jara lɛ baaya hiɛ yɛ sɛɛ mli beni nibii ni anáa lɛ faaa lɛ.

english: Why do major processing factories prefer to buy raw crops in large bulk quantities like 100kg bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nitsumɔhei wuji ni feɔ nibii lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛhe nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ babaoo, tamɔ kotokui ni tsiimɔ ji kilogram 100 lɛ?

english: Processing factories use big machines that require large, continuous supplies of raw grain to run efficiently, so buying in standard bulk weights reduces their transport and transaction costs.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni tsuɔ nii yɛ nibii amli lɛ kɛ tsɔnei wuji ni biɔ ŋmaa babaoo ni yaa nɔ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, nibii babaoo ni aheɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ haa shika ni akɛmajeɔ kɛ nibii ni akɛheɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Is it better for me to sell my harvested soya beans raw or try to process them first?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahɔ̃ɔ soybeans ni akpa lɛ ŋmɔŋ loo maka bɔ ni mafee lɛ makwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Selling raw soya beans provides quick cash, but basic local processing—such as making soya flour, milk, or feed—adds value and can yield higher profits if you have access to local buyers.
ga: Soybeans Raw ni Ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ Haa Shika Baa Oya Shi shishijee nibii ni afeɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ soybean ashikiŋsha, mliki loo kooloi aniyenii feemɔ, Ehaa ojara walɛ yaa hiɛ ni ehaa onáa sɛɛnamɔi babaoo kɛji onyɛ oyashɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelɔi ahe.

english: What does it mean to dress my seeds before planting, and why should I do it?
ga: Mɛni ji dumɔwui ni afolɔ dani adu lɛ tsɔɔ? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee enɛ?

english: Dressing seeds means coating them with safe protective treatments before they go into the ground. This shields the seeds from soil insects, rot, and fungi, ensuring more of your planted seeds actually sprout and grow strong.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe awo amɛhe dani amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baabu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ sũ mli ŋmeii, ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe, ni ebaaha dumɔwui ni odu lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛdara waa.

english: The best time to plant is when the soil stays consistently moist for a few days after rain, rather than right after the very first light drizzle. Planting too early in dry soil can scorch the seeds, while waiting too long wastes the best moisture of the season.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ gbii fioo komɛi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ, shi jeee yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ fioo lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ adu oya tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, mɛmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ tsɔ lɛ baafite be lɛ mli nu ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: How damp should the soil be when I am putting my seeds into the ground?
ga: Te esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tɛŋŋ beni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The soil should feel moist like a squeezed sponge—wet enough to cling together gently, but not muddy or flooded. Excessive water rots the seeds before they sprout, while completely dry soil prevents them from waking up to grow.
ga: Esa akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ anu he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ sponji ni ashɛre mli—eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ehe akpɛtɛ he blɛoo. Shi jeee muji loo nu afua eyi mli obɔ. Nu babaoo baaha dumɔwui lɛ agbo dani amɛkwɛ̃. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi kwraa lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkate shi ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Is it better for my crops if I plow the land with a tractor instead of clearing it by hand?
ga: Ani ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ trakta tsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baatsu he nii?

english: Using a tractor to plow breaks up hard, compacted soil deep down, making it much easier for young roots to spread out and absorb water. However, on sloped land, light hand clearing can be better to prevent heavy rains from washing away your topsoil.
ga: Trakta ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛtsu shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni wa he nii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa shishifãi bibii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛŋɔ nu. Shi, yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ Okɛ oniji atsu nii blɛoo Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops grow better when the soil is loosened before sowing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani adu nii lɛ?

english: Loosening hard soil creates tiny air spaces and softens the ground, allowing tender new roots to push deep easily, drink water, and absorb soil nutrients for faster growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii baa. ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ boteɔ mli oya, amɛnuɔ nu, ni amɛmɔɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli koni amɛdara oya.

english: How deep under the soil should I place my seeds when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ midumɔwui lɛ awo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: A good general rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its size. If you plant too deep, the seed runs out of energy before reaching the surface; if too shallow, sun and birds will destroy it.
ga: Mla kpakpa ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui lɛ adalɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ. Kɛji odu mli tsɔ Dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji eyɛ shishi tsɔ Hulu kɛ okpoi baafite lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my crop seeds very close to one another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops grow too close together, they fight for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin stalks and poor yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce big fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he, ni no haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ewoɔ aduawai loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: Does planting my seeds in straight lines really make a difference compared to scattering them?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔi komɛi yɛ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ he kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni aduɔ lɛ he?

english: Yes, planting in straight lines ensures every plant gets equal space and sunlight, while making it much easier for you to walk through the farm to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest without stepping on your crops.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa kɛhaa bo akɛ ooonyiɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛyajie jwɛi, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli, ni okpa nibii ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ onaji ashwie onibii anɔ.

english: Why are some of my seeds failing to sprout even after I have planted and watered them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu ni mikɛ nu wo amɛmli po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they were stored improperly, planted too deep, destroyed by underground pests, or exposed to excessive heat. Using fresh, treated seeds planted at the correct depth usually solves this issue.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ akɛto yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. adu mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ efiteɔ loo ekɛwoɔ la ni mli edɔ fe nine mli Dumɔwui heei ni atsa amɛ ni adu yɛ shɔŋŋ ni sa lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ naagba nɛɛ he nii Bei pii.

english: Why do my crops yield less food if I plant the same crop on the same plot year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ naa niyenii fioo kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating different crops restores soil strength and reduces pests naturally.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plants lack nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. This usually happens when the soil lacks fertilizer or when heavy rains wash away nutrients.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: When cassava plants are planted too close together, their roots compete for the same water and food in the soil, while their leaves block sunlight from each other, resulting in smaller tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso bibioo.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot tolerate direct sunlight and strong winds because their leaves lose water too quickly. Shade trees protect them by keeping the air cool and moist around the young plants.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ buɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛhaa efeɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛfeee pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot and dry or when the soil lacks sufficient moisture. Heat stress causes the plant to save its energy by shedding flowers instead of producing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Heat stress haa tsei lɛ buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yɛ yibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt during the hot afternoon even when the soil feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: On very hot days, tomato leaves lose water into the air faster than their roots can suck it up from the ground. They temporarily wilt to save water and usually recover in the cooler evening.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ, Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛto nu he gbɛjianɔ be kukuoo ko, ni amɛsumɔɔ ni amɛhe ajɔ amɛ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli.

english: Why do some of my crop seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in dry soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need moisture to wake up and start growing. If the soil is too dry, the seed remains dormant or dies shortly after starting to germinate before it can reach the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui he miihia amɛ koni amɛte shi ni amɛbɔi dalɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakã he ahi shi. Aloo egboɔ beni ebɔi kwɛ̃mɔ lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ dani eshɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do leaves on my yam vines get full of small holes during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ bu bibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: The rainy season brings out insects that feed on soft, fresh green leaves. The extra moisture in the air also creates ideal conditions for leaf-damaging fungi to spread.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji ni kpɛɔ lɛ baa. Kɔɔyɔɔ mli fɛ̃i ni yaa hiɛ lɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my harvested plantains ripen and spoil so quickly after I cut them from the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Once harvested, plantains release a natural ripening gas called ethylene. Storing them in warm, enclosed places traps this gas, causing them to ripen and rot faster.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akpa Plantains lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa mɔ shwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Kɛ́ amɛha amɛhe edɔ ni amɛtsi amɛhe lɛ, ebaamɔ gas nɛɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshwereɔ ni amɛgboɔ oya.

english: Why does planting beans near my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ mi ŋmãa lɛ masɛi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Beans and other legumes take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots, naturally feeding the nearby maize plants.
ga: Beans kɛ legumes krokomɛi Egbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛhaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year if I keep planting the same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi kɛji mitee nɔ midu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ hei komekomei lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows pests and diseases specific to that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ nakai tso lɛ he pɔtɛɛ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long do I need to keep fruit tree seedlings in the nursery before transplanting them to my farm?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ makɛ tso yibii ahe dumɔwui ahi ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛwo miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fruit tree seedlings typically need between four weeks to two months in the nursery to build a strong root system and sturdy stem. Transplanting them too early leaves them weak to harsh outdoor sun and rain.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai tsei ahe dumɔwui biɔ otsii ejwɛ kɛyashi nyɔji enyɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhe lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ tso lɛ shishifãi ni wa. Tsei ni aduɔ mra tsɔ lɛ haa hulu ni naa wa ni jɛɔ kpo nɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ oya.

english: How can I tell if my young tree seedling is strong enough to survive out in the open field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ midumɔwui lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: A seedling is ready for the main farm when its stem turns firm and slightly woody rather than soft green, and it has grown at least four to six healthy, mature leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ efee klalo kɛha ŋmɔ wulu lɛ beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ mli wa ni amɛbatsɔ tsei fioo lɛ. yɛ eŋɔli ni mli tse najiaŋ ni kɛ hoo lɛ, eyɛ baai 4-6 ni eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehe wa.

english: How often should I water my newly transplanted fruit trees during their first month in the ground?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mawo mi tso yibii ni midu ehee lɛ nu yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni eyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli?

english: Young fruit trees need deep watering every two to three days during their first month. This helps their roots settle into the soil before they can search for deeper underground water on their own.
ga: Ehe miihia ni awo tsei bibii lɛ nu babaoo daa gbii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnaa shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why must I wait a few weeks after clearing my land before I start planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ otsii fioo komɛi beni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nii lɛ sɛɛ dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Waiting a few weeks gives cleared vegetation time to rot into nutrient-rich organic matter and allows soil pests disturbed by clearing to clear out, giving new seeds a healthy start.
ga: Otsii fioo komɛi ni ooomɛ lɛ baaha aduawai ni ajie lɛ lɛ afite ni amɛtsɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Ni eyeɔ ebuaa koni agbala tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛtsɔ amɛhe ni ajieɔ koni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehaa dumɔwui heei jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ

english: Is it good to plant fruit trees on the same plot where I grow my food crops?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu tsei ni woɔ yibii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ niyenii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Yes, planting fruit trees alongside food crops provides beneficial shade, keeps moisture in the soil, and gives you extra fruit harvests while your main crops or long-term trees mature.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni woɔ yibii ni aduɔ yɛ niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ baaha hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ aba. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ yibii krokomɛi aha be mli ni onibii titri loo tso ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Plants curl their leaves in intense afternoon heat to reduce surface area and prevent water loss. If they bounce back by evening or morning, it is just a natural defense mechanism.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni ekɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shi ni nu akafite. Kɛji amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba gbɛkɛ loo leebi lɛ, eji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ko kɛkɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dry while the top leaves are green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tso ko shishi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ hiɔ shi eŋɔli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is running out of nitrogen in the soil or getting too much water around its roots, causing it to pull nutrients from older leaves to feed new growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ eshishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ajieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni akɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil, which prevents proper pollination.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa.

english: Why does it take up to three weeks for agricultural officers to issue quality test results for my harvested crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi otsii etɛ dani amɛjieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ ahe kaa ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ he saji kpo lɛ?

english: Officers require around 21 days to complete laboratory tests on soil and crop samples to confirm there are no harmful chemicals, pests, or diseases before certifying the yield as safe for major markets.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ gbii 21 he miihia onukpai lɛ koni amɛkɛfee laboratori mli kaai yɛ shikpɔŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Koni akɛma nɔ mi akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, loo helai komɛi bɛ jɛmɛ. dani ebaama nɔ mi akɛ nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛha jarayeli hei wuji

english: Why do buyers inspect fruit trees for disease before agreeing to purchase the farm harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kwɛɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ amli koni ana kɛji helai yɛ mli dani amɛkpɛlɛɔ nɔ akɛ amɛbaahɔɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii lɛ?

english: Inspectors check trees early to ensure the fruit will not spoil during transit, as unseen fungal or insect infections on trees can ruin an entire shipment after harvest.
ga: Mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ kwɛɔ tsei lɛ amli mra. Enɛ baaha aduawai lɛ akafite beni akɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela loo kooloi bibii ni anaaa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afite gbɛfaa fɛɛ ni akɛyaa ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to start clearing my land for planting maize in Ghana?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mabɔi shikpɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ ŋmãa yɛ Ghana lɛ shishi?

english: You should clear your land right before the major rainy season starts, usually around March in southern Ghana or April/May in the north. Clearing early allows you to prepare the soil so your seeds can catch the very first rains.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ aje shishi. Bei pii lɛ, aaafee yɛ March mli yɛ Ghana kooyigbɛ. loo April/May yɛ kooyigbɛ mra be mli ŋmɔshi nibii Ehaa osaa shikpɔŋ lɛ koni odumɔwui lɛ anyɛ ana klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ.

english: Is it better for me to plant my crops in straight rows or scatter the seeds freely across my field?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja loo magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikɛ mihe awo mli?

english: Planting in straight rows makes it much easier to weed, apply fertilizer, and harvest. It also ensures every crop gets an equal amount of space and sunlight to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ́ adu nii yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ, ehaa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie jwɛi, abaawo ŋmɔshi nibii, ni akpa. Ekwɛɔ hu koni ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ aná he ko kɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that burn and lose water very quickly in full sun. They need fast-growing shade crops like plantains planted next to them to act as natural umbrellas while their roots develop.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛhe. Amɛmiisumɔ tsei ni haa hulutsoo baa oya, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow before they produce corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani amɛwo abele lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen or that the ground is waterlogged. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps keep the leaves green so the plant can make healthy corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ obɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔji bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ awo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen if I plant my cassava cuttings too close together on my farm?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe tsɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall, thin stems with very small tubers instead of large yield roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa, ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ bulbs bibii waa yɛ shishifãi ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support a good vegetable harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua aduawai akpamɔ kpakpa?

english: Healthy soil is usually dark in color, crumbly to the touch, and stays moist without becoming waterlogged. Seeing earthworms and decaying plant matter in your soil is a great sign that it is fertile.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ su yɛ ediŋŋ. Efoɔ kɛji akɛ eta he ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa nu lɛ ahi shi Kɛ́ ona shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii kɛ tsei ni fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eji okadi kpakpa ni tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tse.

english: Why should I avoid growing pepper on the exact same piece of land year after year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni miduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ he?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows pepper-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating with crops like cowpeas restores nitrogen to your land.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni kɔɔ pepper he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina ŋmei ni oootsake lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together on the same plot with my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu tsina ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, mixing maize and cowpeas is a beneficial farming practice. Cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, while the sturdy maize stalks give the cowpea vines a place to climb.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛfutuɔ tsina ŋmãa lɛ ji okwaayeli nifeemɔ ko ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ. Cowpeas lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa tsei ni wa haa cowpea wain tsei lɛ he ko ni amɛkwɔɔ.

english: Why do leaf-eating caterpillars attack my crops more during the rainy season than the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ tutuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Insects thrive in the high humidity and rich green leaf growth brought by rains because food is plentiful and conditions are perfect for laying eggs. Regular farm monitoring helps catch them before they spread.
