ga: Kplukai yeɔ omanye yɛ hei ni hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ kɛ baa dalɛ ni nugbɔ kɛbaa. Niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ kɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi ni sa kɛha ŋmeii fɔmɔ hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔji amli kwɛmɔ daa baaye abua ni amɔmɔ amɛ dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and fall over before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ egbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally wither when the underground tuber has finished maturing. However, if they dry up too early, it means the hot soil lacks mulch to trap moisture and keep the root system cool.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baagbi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ daraa lɛ. Shi, kɛji amɛgbi oya tsɔ lɛ, Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi ni eha shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why does local perfume rice smell sweet when it grows, and can I make my regular rice smell like that too?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ he ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ waa kɛ́ adu lɛ? Ani maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ hu baanyɛ aŋɔ ŋmãa tamɔ nakai?

english: Perfume rice has natural genetic traits that produce aromatic compounds as the plant matures. You cannot turn regular rice into perfume rice by adding anything to the field; you must buy and plant certified perfume rice seeds.
ga: Omɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli su ko ni haa tsofai ni ŋɔɔ baa beni tso lɛ daa lɛ. Onyɛŋ otsɔ ŋmãa folo nɔ otsɔ ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ kɛtsɔ nɔ ko ni okɛbaafata ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Esa akɛ ohe ni odu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ŋɔɔ ni awo he odaseyeli akɛ.

english: Is local Ghanaian perfume rice suitable for growing in every part of the country?
ga: Ani Ghana maŋ lɛ mli ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ sa akɛ adu yɛ maŋ lɛ kpokpai fɛɛ anɔ?

english: Perfume rice grows best in warm areas with good soil fertility and reliable water, such as inland valleys or fields with good irrigation. Secure water access and good soil ensure the plant develops its full aroma and yield.
ga: Omɔ ni ŋɔɔ waa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ nu ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, tamɔ jɔɔ lɛ loo omɔ ŋmɔji ni nu shwieɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Nu ni hi kɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni anáa lɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Does rice always have to grow in standing water, or can I grow it on dry land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ nu ni mli ejɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo abaanyɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ?

english: While rice loves water, different varieties behave differently. Lowland rice thrives in flooded fields, but upland rice varieties are bred to grow on dry farmland with regular rainfall, just like maize.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ nu moŋ Shi ŋmãa srɔtoi yɛ subaŋ srɔtoi. Omɔ folo kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli. Shi atsɔse ŋmãa henɔi ni kɛlɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ okwaayeli hei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ. tamɔ ŋmãa nɔŋŋ

english: I planted one single rice seed, but now I see many stems growing from the bottom. Is my plant dividing correctly?
ga: Midu ŋmãa ŋmãa kome pɛ. Shi amrɔ nɛɛ minaa tsei babaoo ni miida kɛmiijɛ shishi. Ani mitso lɛ miijara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, this is a normal behavior called tillering. A healthy rice plant naturally produces multiple side shoots (tillers) from a single root, and each strong tiller will produce a cluster of rice grains.
ga: Hɛɛ, enɛ ji subaŋ ko ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ tillering. Omɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii babaoo (ŋmeii) kɛjɛɔ shishifã kome mli, ni ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko woɔ omɔ ŋmeii akui.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your rice crop lacks nitrogen fertilizer or is stressed by insufficient water. Applying nutrients like NPK or Urea at the right growth stage helps the leaves turn green and make food for grain production.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-rice tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen fertilizer loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa hewɔ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ NPK loo urea ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ atsɔ eŋɔli ni eha niyenii kɛha dumɔwui afeemɔ.

english: Why do my rice plants fall flat on the ground just when the grains start forming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ lɛ?

english: Falling over, known as lodging, happens when stems grow too weak to hold heavy grains, often caused by applying too much nitrogen fertilizer or strong winds. Choosing strong-stemmed varieties and balanced fertilizing keeps plants standing upright.
ga: Ale shigbeemɔ hu akɛ abobaahe. Ebaa kɛji tso lɛ shishi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ eye ebua dumɔwui ni tsii. Bei pii lɛ, nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ ahala tsei srɔtoi ni shishifãi lɛ wa, ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do wild grasses choke my rice farm faster than they affect my cassava farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi miifite mi ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ oya fe bɔ ni enaa mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Rice belongs to the grass family, so it competes directly for the exact same nutrients, water, and sunlight as wild grass weeds. Early weeding is crucial because young rice plants take time to cover the ground and block out weeds.
ga: Omɔ ji tso ko ni yɔɔ jwɛi weku lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii, nu kɛ hulu la tamɔ bɔ ni koo mli jwɛi jwɛi lɛ yeɔ akaŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ he hiaa ejaakɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ he miihia be ni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛha jwɛi lɛ akashɛ amɛhe.

english: How do I know when my rice crop is fully ripe and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋmã tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Your rice is ready to harvest when about 80 to 85 percent of the grains turn from green to a golden-yellow color, and the heads bend downward under the weight of the firm grains.
ga: O-rice lɛ efee klalo akɛ obaakpa beni o-rice lɛ mli aaafee oha mlijaa 80 kɛyashi 85 tsakeɔ kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa shika tsuru ŋmɔŋ mli lɛ. ni yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmaa ni mli edɔ lɛ tsiimɔ shishi.

english: Why do my rice grains break into small pieces when I take them to be milled after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ atsɔ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ agbe naa lɛ?

english: Grains crack if they are left in the sun to dry too fast or if harvested when already over-dry in the field. Drying harvested rice slowly in light sun or shade keeps the kernels strong so they stay whole during milling.
ga: Omɔ ŋmɔshi nibii baagbala kɛji akɛ agbi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli oya tsɔ. aloo kɛji akɛ akpa be mli ni egbi tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli Omɔ ni akpa lɛ ni agbiɔ blɛoo Yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni omɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ lɛ.

english: What is the difference between paddy rice fresh from my field and processed rice ready for selling?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa hee ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ ŋmãa ni afee lɛ klalo ni ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Fresh paddy rice is still wrapped in a hard outer protective shell called a husk. Processing or milling removes this outer shell and polishes the grain into clean white or brown rice ready for cooking.
ga: Akɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni atsɛɔ lɛ husk lɛ efo ŋmãa hee mli lolo. Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jieɔ nɛkɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei nɛɛ ni ekɛ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ ŋmãa yɛŋ loo ŋmãa ni he tse ni asaa he kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Officer, why should I buy improved crop varieties like MC Zonia or Emele cassava instead of using stem cuttings from my old farm?
ga: Nitsulɔi Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ, tamɔ MC Zonia loo Emele cassava, yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ tsei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Improved crop varieties like MC Zonia and Emele are specially bred by agricultural scientists to grow faster, produce higher yields, and resist common plant diseases much better than traditional farm stems.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi ji mɛi ni ekwɛ tsei srɔtoi ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ tamɔ MC Zonia kɛ Emele lɛ anɔ krɛdɛɛ. bɔni afee ni amɛdara oya Ha yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ Ni amɛteɔ shi amɛwoɔ tsei ahe helai ni afɔɔ namɔ waa fe blema ŋmɔ mli tsei lɛ.

english: How can I tell if a new crop variety will grow well in my district before I spend my money buying the seeds?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tso henɔ hee ko baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ? Dani abaafite shika kɛhe dumɔwui

english: Different crop varieties are tailored for specific ecological zones in Ghana, such as the forest zone or coastal savanna. Extension officers can advise you on which certified varieties are tested and recommended for your local soil and rainfall.
ga: Afee tsei srɔtoi kɛha shihilɛhei pɔtɛɛ komɛi yɛ Ghana, tamɔ kooi amli hei loo ŋshɔnaa savannahs. Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ awo bo ŋaa yɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni aka amɛ akwɛ ni ajie amɛyi kɛha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ shihilɛi lɛ ahe.

english: Can I bring foreign crop seeds from another country to plant directly on my farm in Ghana?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ maji krokomɛi anɔ aba ni mikɛdu yɛ miŋmɔ ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: No, importing and planting uncertified foreign seeds is strictly regulated by law because exotic plants can introduce destructive pests or foreign diseases that can wipe out local farms. All foreign seeds must pass official quarantine inspection.
ga: Dabi, mla kudɔɔ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui ni bɛ odaseyeli ni akɛbaa maŋsɛɛ kɛdumɔ waa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ amɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni fiteɔ nii loo maŋsɛɛ helai ni baanyɛ akpata maŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔji ahiɛ lɛ aba. Esa akɛ maŋsɛɛ dumɔwui fɛɛ atsɔ quarantine kwɛmɔ mli.

english: How can I plan my farm layout so that my family always has food ready to harvest throughout the year?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato miŋmɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni miweku lɛ aná niyenii ni esa akɛ amɛkpa yɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ mli?

english: You can achieve year-round food security by staggered planting—mixing quick-maturing crops like leafy vegetables and maize with long-term root crops like cassava and yams planted at different times of the rainy season.
ga: Obaanyɛ onine ashɛ niyenii ni anáa afi muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ baai kɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni shishifãi kakadaŋŋ yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli bei srɔtoi amli lɛ feɔ ekome.

english: Why do my harvested cassava tubers rot so quickly within days after I dig them up from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mifo amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava tubers deteriorate fast after harvest because exposed roots lose water quickly and react to air. To preserve them, tubers should either be processed into gari/flour immediately or kept undamaged in cool, moist conditions.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akpa amɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni ajie amɛ kpo lɛ laajeɔ nu oya ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ feɔ ekome. koni akɛto yitso he Esa akɛ afee lɛ Gari/Instant Powder loo akatoo he ko ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting and turning yellow during the growing season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe baai lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Leaf twisting and yellowing are major signs of cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by small insects called whiteflies. Planting disease-resistant varieties and removing infected plants early prevents the virus from spreading across your field.
ga: Baai lɛ ni tsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii mosaic hela lɛ yɛ. Kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Tsoi srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ajiemɔ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my harvest yield if I leave weeds growing around my young crops?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mishi jwɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he? Mi tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from young crops. If weeds are not cleared early, your crops will grow weak and produce very low yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ sũ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ tsei bibii amli. Kɛji ojieee jwɛi lɛ mra lɛ, Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaawo yibii fioo kwraa.

english: Should I plant my maize together with leguminous crops like cowpea or groundnuts on the same land?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, intercropping maize with legumes improves soil fertility because legumes capture nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil, which naturally feeds the neighboring maize plants while protecting the topsoil.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmeii duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛfataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ he.

english: Why is proper spacing so important when I am planting my crop seeds or stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɛ ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he hiaa waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui loo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Proper spacing makes sure that each plant gets enough sunlight, air, and underground room for roots to gather soil nutrients without competing against neighboring crops.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hulu la, kɔɔyɔɔ, kɛ shishigbɛ tsũ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ abua niyenii mli hewalɛ naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ akaŋ akaŋ.

english: When is the safest time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops so it does not burn them?
ga: Mɛni ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baawo mli koni shãa akafee mi?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a rain and the plants are actively growing. Place the fertilizer a few centimeters away from the plant stems to prevent direct contact chemical burns.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji sɛntimitai fioo komɛi koni tsofa akashã tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is the plant food responsible for green leafy growth. Adding a balanced fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted manure helps the plant grow strong and stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni haa tsei ahe baai lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhiɔ shi ŋmɔji amli.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the crop is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and using balanced plant food helps the flowers stay on and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ha tso lɛ hao. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa loo nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ mli babaoo Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ tso niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: What are these small caterpillars eating the leaves inside the central shoot of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni ji nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest that destroys young maize plants. You can manage them early by applying recommended crop sprays or putting a small pinch of clean dry sand or wood ash directly into the center funnel of the plant.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni fiteɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsu amɛhe nii mra. Abaanyɛ afee enɛ kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tso nɔ ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ loo kɛtsɔ ŋã ni egbi loo tso mli sũ fioo ko ni akɛshwieɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny insects called whiteflies, or by severe heat stress. Spraying with neem oil solution helps control the whiteflies and protects the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly loo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli Neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ whiteflies ni ebu tso lɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees dry out easily under direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and provide large leaves that act as living shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa seedlings during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why shouldn't I burn the bush on my farmland before planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani miduɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the good organic matter and microscopic soil organisms that natural crop food comes from. Allowing the cleared bush to decompose back into the ground keeps the soil fertile, soft, and moist.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ sũ mli nibii bibii ni haa tsei niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei bibii ni ajie lɛ lɛ fite kɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛbote sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sũ lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni efee blɛoo, ni edɔ.

english: Yam vines need to spread their leaves high up in the sunlight to produce energy for growing big underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and prevents diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ agbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni baa lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɛɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni ehaaa helai aba.

english: Why is it wrong to plant my crop seeds very close together to get a bigger harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ejaaa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni amɛwo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak and thin crops. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space to feed and produce a maximum yield.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa lɛ baa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Cassava is generally ready for harvest between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell it is ready when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, or by carefully digging up the soil around one plant to inspect the size of the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ baai lɛ efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. aloo kɛtsɔ sũ ni ebɔle tso kome he lɛ ni oootsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ dara ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my vegetable crops during the early morning or late in the evening?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ?

english: It is best to water early in the morning so plants can drink before the sun gets hot. Evening watering leaves plant leaves wet overnight, which encourages fungal diseases to grow on your crops.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha nu leebi koni tsei lɛ aná nu dani hulu lɛ adɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli gbɛkɛ lɛ haa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ nyɔɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa onibii amli lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Why do my tomato leaves roll up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves often curl and turn yellow when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or viral infections spread by small insects like whiteflies. Giving them steady water and protecting them from pests helps keep the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli. Kɛ́ aha amɛ nu daa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛbaa lɛ feɔ eŋɔli.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before the pods even start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ po jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not get enough water, when the soil lacks nutrients, or if insects like mirids attack them. Proper shade, adequate soil feeding, and pest control help the tree hold onto its flowers so they turn into pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ baafɔ̃ kɛ́ amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Be mli ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ kooloi bibii tutua amɛ. suitable shade Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my maize leaves have holes and silver stripes when the plants are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ shika tsuru ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Holes and striped patterns on young maize leaves are usually signs of insect attacks, such as the Fall Armyworm, or soil nutrient deficiencies. Catching these pests early and applying compost or fertilizer helps the maize grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, bu kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii ahe lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi bibii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ooomɔ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ mra Ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa.

english: Why does my soil turn as hard as rock after it rains, making my crop roots struggle to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ? Enɛ haa mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛdara.

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter like compost, manure, or dried leaves. Mixing organic matter into the soil keeps it loose, allowing water to sink in and roots to spread easily.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo baai ni egboi bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa nu boteɔ mli ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans in my field help my maize grow better in the next season?
ga: Te ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. This leaves behind natural fertilizer in the ground that feeds the maize planted after them.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni haa ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ niyenii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I clear small weeds around my crops even when my crops are much taller than the weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi bibii lɛ? ebɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe Miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ kwraa fe jwɛi lɛ, shi kɛlɛ.

english: Even small weeds steal hidden water, light, and soil nutrients that your crops need to produce big harvests, and they can also hide harmful insects that attack your crops.
ga: Jwɛi bibii po juɔ nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛkpa nii babaoo lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni tutuaa onibii lɛ hu ato.

english: How do I know if my cassava stems are healthy enough to cut and plant for a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ afolɔ ni adu yɛ ŋmɔ hee mli?

english: Healthy cassava stem cuttings come from mature plants that are 8 to 12 months old, free from pest holes or disease spots, and show firm, green inner bark when gently scraped.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni afolɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei ni edara ni eye nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 ni tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ahe ŋmeii bɛ mli lɛ amli. ni ejieɔ mligbɛ ŋmei ni ma shi shiŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kpo kɛji akɛ atsɔ mli blɛoo.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take so long to produce fruit after I plant them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains take longer to fruit if the soil lacks organic nutrients, if they do not receive enough water during dry spells, or if weeds compete with their shallow root systems.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baahe be babaoo dani amɛwo yibii kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛji onine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli loo kɛji jwɛi kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ miitswa akaŋ.

english: What causes my pepper plants to drop all their tiny young fruits right after flowering?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ eyibii bibii lɛ fɛɛ kɛji efɔ fɔfɔi?

english: Pepper plants shed young fruits when the weather becomes too hot, when watering is irregular, or when the soil lacks key nutrients like calcium and phosphorus required for fruit development.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baawo yibii ni yɔɔ blɛoo kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ calcium kɛ phosphorus ni he hiaa koni aduawai lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my orange trees produce sweet fruits in some years but very sour fruits in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-orange tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni ŋɔɔ yɛ afii komɛi amli shi ewoɔ yibii ni mli edɔ waa yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Citrus fruit sweetness changes based on sunlight, steady water supply while the fruit is growing, and whether the soil has enough potassium to nourish the tree.
ga: Bɔ ni citrus aduawai lɛ ŋɔɔ ha lɛ tsakeɔ kɛ hulu la. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ Ni ani shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ?

english: Why is it important to clear away dead leaves and rotten pods from under my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie baai ni egboi kɛ ŋmeii ni egboi kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Leaving dead plant material on the ground creates a breeding spot for tiny pests, fungi, and bacteria. Sweeping or clearing them away keeps crop diseases from growing and spreading to healthy trees.
ga: Tso mli nibii ni egboi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii, tsɛŋemɔ helai, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ loo ajie amɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei ahe helai akakwɛ̃ ni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Can dirty tools like my cutlass spread sickness from one crop to another?
ga: Ani dɛŋdade ko ni he tseee tamɔ mi-dagger lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ hela ashwã kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli kɛya ekroko mli?

english: Yes, crop diseases caused by invisible bacteria and fungi stick to dirty tools and pass to healthy plants when you prune or harvest them. Cleaning your tools regularly stops disease from spreading.
ga: Hɛɛ, helai ni baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni kɛ amɛhe kpɛtɛɔ nibii ni he tseee ahe lɛ amli, ni amɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli kɛ́ ofo loo okpa. Kɛ́ otsumɔ odɛŋdadei lɛ ahe daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I burn or bury plants that show heavy disease symptoms instead of leaving them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashã loo mafu tso ni jieɔ hela ni naa wa he okadi kpo lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Sick plants are full of bacteria and fungi spores that can blow in the wind or travel in water. Burning or burying them destroys the sickness so it cannot infect your healthy crops.
ga: Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ eyi kɛ helatsɛmɛi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni kɔɔyɔɔ baanyɛ atswa loo amɛfã gbɛ yɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ ashã gbonyo loo afu lɛ lɛ, ebaakpata hela lɛ hiɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, enyɛŋ ekɛ hela aba onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my harvested maize kernels turn powdery white when I store them in my barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ŋmeii ni mikpa lɛ feɔ powder yɛŋ kɛ́ mikɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Moisture causes tiny organisms called fungi or mold to grow on stored grain. Sweeping and drying your storage room well before putting maize inside stops this mold from spoiling your crop.
ga: Fɛ̃i haa nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ daraa. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ fungus loo mold lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ dumɔwui ni ato lɛ anɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsumɔ onitoohe lɛ ni oha egbi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛ ŋmãa lɛ awo mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akafite onibii.

english: Why should I clean out my crop storehouse thoroughly before bringing in a new harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsumɔ he ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii toɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani makpa ŋmɔshi nibii heei?

english: Old grains and dirt left behind carry hidden germs, fungal spores, and insects that will attack your fresh harvest immediately if the storehouse is not swept clean.
ga: Ŋmãa kɛ muji ni ashi yɛ sɛɛ lɛ haa ŋshɔkpɔ lɛ nɔ helai baa. Fungal spores kɛ kooloi bibii ni baatutua onibii heei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji atsuuu shĩa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my yam tubers start rotting quickly if I store them on the damp ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya kɛji mikɛto shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Damp ground provides the wet environment that fungi and bacteria need to grow and penetrate cuts in the yam. Storing yams off the ground on clean, dry wooden racks prevents rotting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli efɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ he hiaa koni amɛdara ni amɛbote sweet potato tsei lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ sweet potato to tso adeka ni he tse ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkafite.

english: How does keeping my harvested grain dry stop fungi from growing inside the sacks?
ga: Mi-Dumɔwui ni Akpa lɛ ni Aaaha Egbi Te Mafee tɛŋŋ akpa ŋmɔtɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ?

english: Fungi need moisture to grow and multiply. By thoroughly sun-drying your grains before sacking them, you remove the water they need to survive, keeping your stored harvest fresh.
ga: Fungi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ koni amɛdara ni amɛshwere. Kɛtsɔ ŋmaa lɛ ni egbiɔ dani ekɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ jieɔ nu ni he hiaa dumɔwui lɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛhi shi lɛ kɛyaa. ni ehaa onibii ni okɛto lɛ feɔ ehee.

english: Why can eating moldy groundnuts make my family sick with stomach aches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha miweku lɛ aná musu mli piŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Mold and fungi growing on stored crops produce harmful poisons called toxins. Eating spoiled crops can cause stomach pains and health problems, so moldy harvests must be discarded.
ga: Muji kɛ ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ jieɔ tsofai fɔji ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsofai fɔji. Nibii ni efite ni ayeɔ lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ musu mli piŋmɔ kɛ hewalɛnamɔ he naagbai aba. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ ashɛrɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ ashwie.

english: What causes my cassava roots to turn soft and smelly in the soil before harvest?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa?

english: Excess water in the soil creates a good environment for bacteria to grow and rot the roots. Keeping your farm well-drained prevents these sickness-causing germs from destroying the crop.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai ni kɛ helai baa lɛ akafite oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How do tiny germs and fungi get onto my crops when I cannot even see them?
ga: Muawai bibii kɛ ŋmeii Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ eboteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli? Be mli ni minyɛɛɛ mana po lɛ

english: Fungi and bacteria are tiny living things carried through the air by wind, splashing rain, or dirty hands. They stay invisible until they multiply in damp, uncleaned places and cause visible plant disease.
ga: Fungi kɛ muawai ji nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli. ni kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, loo niji ni mli ewo muji kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli Anaaa amɛ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfɔɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni he tseee. ni ekɛ tsei ahe helai ni anaa baa.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and curling up in the heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ latsaa be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that burn easily in direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa creates a canopy that shields them from scorching heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do my crops look weak and wilted in the afternoon even when it rained earlier in the week?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ yɛ otsi lɛ shishijee mli moŋ lɛ?

english: Hot tropical sun causes water to evaporate rapidly from both the plant's leaves and the topsoil. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture beneath the surface.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ baai kɛ sũ lɛ yiteŋ fɛɛ mli. Mulching around Kɛ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni emɔɔ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize plants need fertilizer just by looking at their leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-abele tso lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip and moving down the middle vein, showing that the crop is starving for nutrients.
ga: Kɛji akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli, ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ ni eyaa shishi kɛyaa ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Why do my vegetables grow better when I plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetables lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ midu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally feed the soil and act as a free source of plant food for neighboring crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛbaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛbaatsu nii akɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha tsei ni yeɔ naagbai.

english: Does planting my seeds very close together give me a bigger total harvest?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baaha yibii fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ?

english: No, planting seeds too close forces plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in weak, thin stems and small or missing fruits.
ga: Dabi, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛhe waaa kɛ aduawai bibii loo ni bɛ mli baa.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from sudden stress, such as extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients, because the plant shuts down flower production to save its own life.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbai lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛna haomɔi trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso lɛ kpaɔ fɔfɔii feemɔ koni ekɛhere lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ewala yiwala.

english: Is it bad if I trim off some of the leaves from my cassava or tomato plants?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mifo ŋmei loo tomato tso ko baai komɛi?

english: Removing dead, diseased, or excess lower leaves helps the crop direct its food and energy into growing big roots or fruits instead of maintaining unnecessary leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni fa fe nine lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni etsɔɔ niyenii kɛ hewalɛ gbɛ kɛyaa shishifãi loo aduawai wuji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooohiɛ baai ni he ehiaaa lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow so slowly even during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa fiofio yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli po lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that absorb water, fertilizer, and light much faster than farm crops, effectively starving your crops of what they need to mature.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ la oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper or tomato in the exact same patch of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo tomato yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting crops from the same family in the same spot every year allows soil diseases and harmful pests to build up in the ground, causing poorer yields with each new harvest.
ga: Tsei ni jɛ weku kome mli ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo baa shi yɛ kpamɔ hee fɛɛ kpamɔ hee mli.

english: Why do seeds I saved from last year's maize crop produce smaller yields than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ wooo yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength over generations and can carry hidden diseases, whereas certified seeds are specifically bred for high vigor, uniform growth, and resistance to common field pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato lɛ he waaa kɛjɛɔ yinɔ kome mli kɛyaa yinɔ kroko mli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ aba. Yɛ be mli ni akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ. shweremɔ ni yɔɔ ekomefeemɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni fɔɔ baa lɛ ahe hewalɛ

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that provide living shade to protect the cocoa trees while keeping the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo tso lɛ he yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to build green leaves. Applying organic manure or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps the leaves stay green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmei he hiaa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba Kɛ akɛ organic fertilizer loo nitrogen fertilizer tamɔ urea tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa.

english: Cowpeas gather nitrogen from the air and store it in tiny nodules on their roots. When the cowpea plant leaves decay after harvest, that natural fertilizer stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Cowpea buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi bibii amli. Beni cowpea tsei lɛ baai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ, Nakai adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when it rains too heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to survive. When heavy rain leaves water standing in the soil for too long, it cuts off air and encourages soil fungi to attack and rot the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Heat stops the flowers from pollinating, so the plant drops them instead of spending energy to make fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ mli. Dɔlɛ lɛ baatsi fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii.

english: Why do I have to lift my yam vines onto wooden poles instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ mawo tso ko nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves onto poles helps them capture more sunlight to produce larger tubers underground, while keeping leaves off the damp dirt to prevent fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛmɔɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akafee muji ni amɛhe afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my maize ears stay small when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa toi lɛ feɔ bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When maize plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to form large ears.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei lɛ eko kwraa bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ekwɛ̃ toi wuji.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking sap from the leaves, or by a leaf-curl virus spread by whiteflies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ baai ni shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii yɛji gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear weeds while my crops are still small instead of waiting until later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lɛ moŋ fe sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young crops are weak and grow slowly if weeds steal their share of water and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early lets young plants grow strong roots before the weeds take over.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ blɛoo kɛji jwɛi ju amɛgbɛfaŋnɔ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra lɛ Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei bibii ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa dani jwɛi lɛ yeɔ nɔ.

english: Why do tiny insects appear inside my dried maize bags even when the bags were sealed tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mi-ŋmãa ni egbi kotoku lɛ mli lɛ? Ni akɛ kotoku lɛ ewo mli jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weevil insects often lay microscopic eggs inside maize grains while they are still in the field. If the grain is not dried completely before storage, heat and moisture inside the bag cause those hidden eggs to hatch.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ amɛwui bibii ni anaaa lɛ woɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ afɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and intense heat. Planting them alongside taller crops like plantains or under shade trees provides a natural canopy that retains moisture and shields the young cocoa from sun damage.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ ahe loo tsei ashishi lɛ, ehaa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli lɛ baa, ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he.

english: Is it helpful for my soil if I plant cowpeas or beans together with my maize in the same farm?
ga: Ani ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji mikɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmãa wo mli lɛ du yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting beans or cowpeas alongside maize improves soil health. Legumes catch nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which naturally feeds the maize and helps both crops produce better yields.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ adu ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ahe lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ yaa hiɛ. Legumes mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Yam plants are natural climbers that need sunlight to produce big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground where diseases spread, allowing the plant to catch maximum sunlight for growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la koni amɛwo shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hela lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo kɛha amɛdalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil. It can also happen when heavy rains wash nutrients away from the root area, leaving the plant hungry.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifã lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Why should I lay dry grass and leaves around the stems of my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai abɔle he lɛ? Kpɔ̃ɔ tso?

english: Covering the ground with dry organic matter is called mulching. It acts like a protective blanket that trap moisture in the soil, prevents weeds from growing, and keeps the roots cool in hot weather.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni egbi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or poor soil fertility. When the plant feels under strain, it drops its blossoms to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii Beni tso lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ haomɔ mli lɛ Ebaafɔlɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rain sits on the field without draining, it drowns the roots and creates damp conditions where harmful fungi rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni eha shihilɛ ko ni mli edɔ aba ni ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baafite ŋmeii lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil has enough water to plant my seeds after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni mikɛbaadu midumɔwui lɛ beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eba naagbee lɛ?

english: Do not plant immediately after the very first rain because only the surface gets wet. Dig a small hole down to your wrist level; if the soil at that depth feels moist and holds together when squeezed, it is ready for planting.
ga: Kaadu amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ ejaakɛ enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ pɛ. Tsɔɔmɔ bu bibioo ko kɛyashɛ onine he. Kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ nakai ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ ni ehiɛɔ shi kɛji akɛ ashɛre lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ efee klalo akɛ ebaadu.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my maize leaves and small caterpillars inside the central leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ ŋmeii bibii amli Yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm. The caterpillars hide deep inside the central leaf funnel of the maize plant to feed on new leaves before moving to the rest of the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai heei dani amɛya nɔ amɛya ŋmãa ni eshwɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant juices, or by a virus carried by these insects. This damage weakens the plant and stops it from developing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ hiɛɔ lɛ nɔ Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaaa eda jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under intense direct sunlight. Plantain trees grow rapidly and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, which is a fungal infection that thrives in dark, wet, and humid conditions. Rainy weather helps the fungus spread quickly across pods via rain splashes and damp air.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Nugbɔshiimɔ be haa ŋmeii lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmeii lɛ amli oya kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. The plant pulls available nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the young growing leaves at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha baai bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller cassava roots each year when I plant on the same plot without resting it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmeii bibii daa afi lɛ? Adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni ajɔɔɔɔ he?

english: Crops pull food and nutrients out of the ground every season. When you plant cassava continuously without adding fertilizer, compost, or letting the land rest (fallow), the soil loses its fertility and cannot support large root growth.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Kɛ́ oya nɔ odu ŋmei ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli, loo ohaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe (egbee shi lɛ), shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi ni enyɛŋ eye ebua shishifãi wuji ni shwereɔ lɛ.

english: Why should I place fertilizer near the base of the plant in the soil instead of throwing it over the leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo tso lɛ shishigbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe baai lɛ anɔ?

english: Plants drink up nutrients through their root systems in the soil. Placing fertilizer directly on leaves can burn the plant tissue, whereas putting it near the roots allows the plant to safely soak up the food.
ga: Tsei nuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ mli fãji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ eshɛɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ he shweshweeshwe.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants must fight each other for limited sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition results in thin, weak stems and very small corn cobs.
ga: Beni adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Esa akɛ tsei ni miida lɛ awuu koni hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aná. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii waa baa.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites that feed on plant juices and spread viral infections, causing the leaves to twist and stunt growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa. ni yeɔ tso mli nu ni egbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai amli baa lɛ eshwaa Enɛ haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaaa amɛdara.

english: Why do white powdery patches cover the leaves of my garden eggs during dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ powder woji yɛŋ haa eggplant baai ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This white powder is a fungal disease called powdery mildew. It thrives during dry weather with high humidity, coating the leaves and blocking the plant from absorbing sunlight to make food.
ga: Nɛkɛ powda yɛŋ nɛɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ powdery mildew. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi kɛ hulutsoo babaoo mli. Ehaa baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ hulu la ni akɛhooɔ nii lɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off the plant without turning into tomatoes during hot afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ tomato yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and causes their pollen to become sterile. To protect itself from drying out, the plant drops its unpollinated flowers instead of spending energy turning them into fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni bɛ fɔmɔ nii. Bɔni afee ni obu ohe kɛjɛ ŋmɔlɔ he Tso lɛ baashwie fɔfɔi ni ŋmɔlɔ bɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛtsake fɔfɔii ni etsɔ aduawai lɛ,.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest yield less corn than certified seeds bought from an agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ haaa ŋmãa fioo fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Commercial certified seeds are specially bred hybrid seeds that combine strong traits for high yields. Seeds saved from a hybrid harvest lose those vigor traits in the next generation, producing smaller cobs and weaker plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛ jarayeli he odaseyeli haa lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afɔ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni kɛ sui ni mli wa feɔ ekome kɛhaa yibiiwoo babaoo. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ baafite nakai hewalɛ sui lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei bibioo kɛ tso ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why should I plant beans on the same piece of land alongside my other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ mitsei krokomɛi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Beans add natural nitrogen food into the soil through their roots. This naturally feeds nearby crops, helping them grow thicker leaves and yield more harvest without spending extra money on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni ji nitrogen lɛ fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Gbɛ nɛɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ adebɔɔ lɛ niyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa baai ni mli tse ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo ni ehe ehiaaa ni amɛfite shika yɛ tsofai krokomɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe.

english: Why is it better to nurse my cocoa seeds in nursery bags before moving them to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ grow bags amli dani mikɛ amɛ aya ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young seeds are delicate and easily eaten by pests or scorched by direct sun. Nursing them lets you give them controlled water and shade until they are strong enough to survive out on the open farm.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ amɛ oya loo hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Amɛtsɔsemɔ haa onyɛɔ ohaa amɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni agbele naa mli.

english: Should I burn all the cleared bush when preparing my new farmland?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mashã tsei ni ajie lɛ fɛɛ beni miisaa he hee ni abaadu nii yɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys valuable natural matter that feeds the soil. It is usually better to leave the cleared plants to rot on the ground as mulch, which keeps the soil cool, retains water, and turns into plant food.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni jara wa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ. Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaaŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ lɛ gbɛ ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ebafeɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei.

english: What steps should I take if I take over an old cocoa farm that is overgrown and not producing well?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ miŋɔ kookoo ŋmɔ momo ko ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine ni yibiiwoo bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Clear away choking weeds, cut off dead or diseased tree branches to let light in, and replace non-producing old trees with newly nursed seedlings to slowly bring the farm's yield back up.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi ni tsiɔ mɔ naa lɛ kɛjɛ ohe. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ koni la abote mli. ni akɛ tsei momo ni wooo yibii lɛ ato tsei heei ni akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ najiaŋ koni fiofio Akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Young cocoa plants are like human infants and cannot survive full, harsh sunlight. Leaving some taller trees gives them the cooling shade they need to grow strong root systems.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ tamɔ adesai abifabii ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ kwraa. Tsei lɛ ni oooha amɛdara lɛ Kɛ́ oshi ekomɛi lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: How can I tell if a virgin piece of land will be good for planting crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii adumɔ?

english: Look at the soil color and natural vegetation. Dark, soft soil with lots of earthworms and thick natural weed growth usually means the land is full of nutrients ready to support healthy crops.
ga: Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe su. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii babaoo kɛ jwɛi ni mli tse ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ lɛ yɔɔ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eyi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni baaye abua ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will I get more crop harvest if I pack my seeds as close together as possible?
ga: Ani maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo tsɔne mli bɔ ni manyɛ?

english: No, planting too close makes crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and small harvests. Giving each crop its proper spacing allows it to grow fully.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara kɛyashɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ he.

english: How do weeds hurt my young crops during their early growth stage?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ awui yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and steal their water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Regular weeding during the early months ensures your main crop gets all the nourishment it needs.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ daa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni onibii titri lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops turn yellow and droop during hot, dry weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing and drooping leaves are a sign that the crop is thirsty and stressed by high heat. Adding a layer of dry grass or leaves around the plant base keeps moisture in the ground for longer.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ kumai miiye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛmiihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli. Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛbaafata he lɛ baaye abua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Is it safe to plant cassava and maize together on the same land during the start of the rains?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Yes, maize grows fast and can be harvested in a few months, leaving space and time for the slower-growing cassava to expand and yield later in the season.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa daa oya, ni abaanyɛ akpa yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Enɛ haa gbɛ kɛ be haa ŋmei ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo lɛ koni egbɛ eshwa ni ewo yibii yɛ sɛɛ mli yɛ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do farmers say it is best to plant maize during the major rainy season instead of waiting for the minor season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi kɛɔ akɛ esa akɛ amɛdu ŋmãa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ mli moŋ fe ni amɛaamɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni ji enyɔ lɛ?

english: The major rainy season provides continuous and heavy rainfall, which gives maize seeds the consistent moisture they need to grow tall and produce big, full cobs compared to the shorter, less predictable minor season.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be ni he hiaa lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni yaa nɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nɛɔ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ naa nu ni he hiaa amɛ be fɛɛ be koni amɛdara ni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ. Kɛ akɛto sɛkɛndre be ni yɔɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ atsɔɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: How do orange trees know when to flower so that fruit is ready around December?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmei tsei leɔ be ni esa akɛ amɛwo fɔfɔi koni amɛyibii lɛ afee klalo yɛ December mli?

english: Orange trees respond to dry spells followed by rain, which triggers flowering; because of Ghana's weather patterns, flowers that bloom after early rains naturally take about 7 to 9 months to mature into ripe oranges just in time for Christmas.
ga: Orange tsei tsuɔ nii kɛji nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ. ni haa fɔfɔi baa Enɛ jɛ Ghana kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ ahewɔ. Fɔfɔi ni fɔɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 7 kɛyashi 9 dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛha Blonya.

english: Why does it take several years for a new oil palm tree to produce its first bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani ŋmei tso hee ko woɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm is a long-term tree crop that spends its first 3 to 4 years building a strong trunk and deep root system so it can support heavy fruit bunches for over 20 years.
ga: Mu tsei ji tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛheɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 dani amɛwoɔ amɛshishifãi ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua aduawai ni tsii fe afii 20.

english: Why do many of the small flowers on my orange tree fall off before turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi bibii babaoo ni yɔɔ mi-orange tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbee shi dani amɛbatsɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Orange trees naturally produce more flowers than they can support; if the tree lacks water or nutrients, it drops extra flowers so it can save its strength for the fruits it can successfully grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akutu tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua. Kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ Ebaajie fɔfɔi krokomɛi ashwie shi bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ hewalɛ mli koni aduawai lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: What will happen to my maize crop if I plant the seeds too close together in the row?
ga: Mɛni baa mi ŋmãa lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ sɛɛ mli?

english: If maize seeds are planted too close, the growing plants will fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ dumɔwui bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Can I plant cash crops like pepper or cassava between my young oil palm trees while they are still small?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu shika nibii tamɔ pepper loo cassava yɛ mi-oil palm tsei lɛ ateŋ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, while oil palms are small and haven't created a canopy, there is plenty of sunlight and space between rows to grow short-term crops without harming the palms.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mu tsei lɛ daraaa ni amɛfeee ŋwɛi ŋta moŋ, Shi hulu la kɛ gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋtayaai lɛ ateŋ ni abaanyɛ adu be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyeee ŋtayaai lɛ awui.

english: Yellow lower leaves are a common sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, an important food that maize needs to stay green and grow vigorously.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ namɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ko ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli ni eda waa.

english: Can I put fresh poultry manure directly on my crops as soon as I clean out the bird house?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ kooloi ashishifã hee awo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛji mitsumɔ okpoi atsu lɛ mli pɛ?

english: Fresh poultry manure is too strong and hot for plants, which can burn roots and kill young crops; it needs to dry out and decompose for a few weeks before being put on the farm.
ga: Kooloi afɔfɔi ni afee ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ waa kɛha tsei. ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi ni egbe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii Esa akɛ egbi ni egbo otsii fioo komɛi dani akɛha ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why does maize grow so well on newly cleared bushland during the first year compared to old land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ koo mli shikpɔŋ hee ni ajie lɛ nɔ yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afi lɛ mli fe shikpɔŋ momo nɔ lɛ?

english: Newly cleared forest or bushland has accumulated years of fallen leaves and organic matter, making the soil rich in natural food that feeds the first crop of maize very well.
ga: Koo loo he ko ni tsei yɔɔ ehee lɛ ebua tsei ni egbee shi kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa yɛ afii ni eho lɛ amli. Enɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ batsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa henɔi lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ waa.

english: Why do the bottom fronds of my oil palm trees turn brown and hang down as the tree grows taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi beni tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: As oil palms grow new leaves from the top, the older bottom leaves naturally die off after giving their stored energy to the tree, which is a normal part of the palm's growth cycle.
ga: Kɛji akɛ mu tso lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ, baai heei jɛɔ ŋwɛigbɛ Baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ gboiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ekɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ eha tso lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji nɔ ko ni yaa nɔ daa yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli.

english: Why do some farmers leave tall trees standing over their young cocoa crops to form a leaf cover above them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ tsei kakadaji yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛha cacao tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under full sunlight. Tall trees create a canopy above them that acts like a sunshade, keeping the delicate young cocoa cool and holding moisture in the soil so they survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛitsu ko yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛitsu. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do experienced cocoa farmers cut back the bushy upper branches of tall cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ ni duɔ kookoo lɛ shwieɔ kookoo tsei aniji kakadaji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Trimming the upper canopy lets light and air flow through the tree branches. This prevents dampness that causes black pod disease and forces the tree to direct its strength into growing cocoa pods rather than tall wood.
ga: Afolɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ yiteŋ koni la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ amli. Koni akafee ŋmɔtɔ ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ. kɛ tsei ni anyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛdu kookoo ŋmeii yɛ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why do my yam plants produce thin, string-like stems that crawl around looking for wooden sticks to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ yɛ tsei bibii ni tamɔ kpãa ni shwieɔ shi kɛbɔleɔ he lɛ? koni ana tso ni akɛkwɔ nɔ

english: Yam plants naturally grow as climbing vines. They use tall sticks as support so their leaves can reach upward to catch direct sunlight, which gives the plant energy to build big tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe tamɔ wain tsei ni kwɔɔ. Akɛ tsei niji ni kɛlɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ sɛɛfimɔ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ ashɛ ŋwɛi koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛfeɔ bulb agbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why should I tie my tomato branches off the ground onto tall stakes instead of letting them spread across the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-tomato niji lɛ akpɛtɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ko he moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting tomato plants on stakes keeps the leaves and fruits away from wet soil. This keeps the crop clean and prevents ground insects and soil diseases from rotting your tomatoes before harvest.
ga: Tomato tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akashɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe atse, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai akafite tomatoi lɛ dani akpa.

english: If I plant cassava right beneath tall plantain trees, will the leaf cover affect my cassava tuber growth?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ dumɔwui kakadaji ashishi Ani baai ni akɛhaa lɛ baaná ŋmei shishifãi lɛ adalɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, because cassava needs strong, direct sunlight to store food in its roots. Heavy shade from plantain leaves will cause the cassava to grow long and skinny without producing heavy tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ hulu la he miihia ŋmei tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shade ni jɛɔ plantain baai lɛ amli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni efee mlɛo ni ekɛ ŋmei ni tsii baaa.

english: Why do crop roots spread far out sideways under the ground instead of growing straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi yɛ afãgbɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaakwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Spreading root networks serve two main jobs: they hold the plant firmly in the ground against heavy rain and winds, and they reach out widely to grab water and nutrients from the top layer of soil.
ga: Shishifãi ni yaa hiɛ lɛ tsuɔ nitsumɔi titrii enyɔ: ekɛ tso lɛ fĩɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shi shiŋŋ koni ebu ehe kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he. ni eshɛɔ he fɛɛ he koni ejie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cashew trees produce thousands of tiny flowers, but most of them fall off without turning into nuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii akpei abɔ, shi amɛteŋ babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Trees produce far more flowers than they have energy to support. Dropping extra flowers is a natural habit that allows the tree to concentrate its water and plant food into maturing a healthy batch of nuts.
ga: Tso woɔ fɔfɔii babaoo fe bɔ ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaaye ebua lɛ. Fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli su ko ni yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuaa nu naa ni amɛduɔ niyenii koni amɛwo ŋmeii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow and shed whenever there is heavy, prolonged rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Too much water fills all the tiny air spaces in the dirt, causing roots to drown. When roots cannot breathe, they stop feeding the plant, which makes the leaves turn yellow and drop off.
ga: Nu babaoo yiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ amli, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ nu mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu lɛ ebaakpa tsei lɛ niyenii Enɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi.

english: Why do small green shoots keep sprouting out from the base of my plantain tree stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, eda kɛjɛ midumɔwu lɛ shishi?

english: These shoots are natural baby plants called suckers. The main plant produces them from its root base so that new plantain trees can grow and replace the mother tree after it fruits.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli gbekɛbii tsei ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Tso ni hereɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛshishigbɛ bɔni afee ni dumɔwui heei akwɛ̃ ni amɛye fɔlɔ tso lɛ najiaŋ beni ewo yibii sɛɛ.

english: Why does speargrass keep growing back in my field even after I cut all the leaves off at soil level?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akpɔlɔ jwɛi yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji mifo baai lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ po.

english: Speargrass has underground stems that store food beneath the soil surface. Even when you cut the leaves above, those underground stems remain alive and quickly shoot up fresh green growth.
ga: Speargrass yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei ni kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Kɛji ofolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ po. Nakai tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛfee eŋɔli ni mli tse.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in the open field without plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ni mli tse ni plantains bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them provides essential canopy cover and retains soil moisture until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ masɛi Enɛ baaha ŋwɛi ŋta ni he hiaa lɛ aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ eŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: How do I choose a crop variety that won't easily break or fall over during heavy rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni fiteŋ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: Look for certified seed varieties described as having high lodging resistance. These varieties have been bred with thicker stems and deeper root systems that anchor the plant securely against strong wind and heavy rain.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ mli akɛ amɛhe wa waa yɛ dormancy mli. Atsake nɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi nɛɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Ehiɛɔ tso lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he.

english: Why do some of the papaya trees on my farm produce flowers but never grow any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ papaya tsei komɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ lɛ?

english: Papayas have distinct male, female, and hermaphrodite plants. Male trees only produce pollen to fertilize female trees, so they will flower continuously without ever setting fruit themselves.
ga: Papaya yɛ tsei srɔtoi ni ji hii, yei kɛ tsei ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei hii feɔ pollen pɛ koni amɛkɛ tsei yei abɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛfɔɔ fɔfɔi be fɛɛ be ni amɛwooo yibii kɔkɔɔkɔ.

english: What causes the leaves of my maize plants to turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ?

english: Yellowing leaves typically indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Adding well-rotted animal manure, compost, or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore green leaf growth and improves plant vitality.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmei, loo ŋmei ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ ni eha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ.

english: Why do experienced farmers advise me to plant cowpeas in the same field as my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi ŋmãa yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas naturally fix nitrogen from the air into the soil. This process enriches the soil naturally, providing essential food for the neighboring maize crop without competing heavily for nutrients.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas lɛ saa nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɛkɛ gbɛ nɛɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ehaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni akaŋshii babaoo bɛ mli kɛha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ.

english: Will I get a bigger harvest if I plant my cassava stems very close to each other?
ga: Ani maná yibiiwoo babaoo kɛji midu ŋmei tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: No, overcrowding causes plants to compete aggressively for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving cassava stems adequate space ensures each plant gets enough energy to grow large, healthy root tubers.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni eyi obɔ lɛ haa amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa ŋmei tsei lɛ haa tsei lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli wa lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I have to erect wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mato tsei ahe tsɔi koni mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam leaves off the ground on stakes allows them to spread out and catch maximum sunlight. Better sunlight exposure increases leaf production, which fuels larger tuber growth underground.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Hulu la ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tuber tsei lɛ daa babaoo.

english: Why do caterpillars and armyworms suddenly appear in large numbers right after the first rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ asraafoi akuu mli ŋmeii jieɔ amɛhe kpo babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The onset of the rainy season brings warmer temperatures and fresh plant leaves, creating ideal environmental triggers for insect eggs dormant in soil or crop residue to hatch all at once.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee kɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ kɛ tsei ahe baai heei baa. Enɛ haa shihilɛ ni sa baa koni akɛkanya kooloi bibii ni ehiɛ edɔ lɛ afɔfɔi. Yɛ shikpɔŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli lɛ, efɔ̃ɔ fɛɛ shikome.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before turning into actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛfeɔ tomato diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flower drop usually happens due to extreme heat, uneven watering, or poor insect activity for pollination. Maintaining steady soil moisture and encouraging natural pollinators helps flowers stay on to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo ni naa wa waa hewɔ ni tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ lɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaaa daa Aloo pollinators gbohii yɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔtɔi ni woɔ fɔfɔi lɛ hewalɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛyaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Saving seeds from hybrid crops leads to poor results because the second generation loses the uniform strength and yield of the original parent seeds. Buying fresh certified seeds each season guarantees consistent performance.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ ahe lɛ kɛ yibii kpakpai baaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ laajeɔ shishijee fɔlɔ seshi lɛ hewalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli hemɔ daa be mli lɛ maa nɔ mi akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii daa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which feeds green growth, or the soil is waterlogged and suffocating the roots. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like Urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn healthy green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni no haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa. Aloo nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my cassava crop grow very tall with huge leaves, but the tubers under the ground are very small?
