ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ji bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or leaf fertilizer, the cassava plant spends all its energy growing leaves above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Using balanced soil nutrients encourages bigger tuber growth.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen loo foliar ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaa lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa ŋmeii wuji lɛ daraa.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ náa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i. Esa akɛ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in cool, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning tree branches to let sunlight and air into the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni duŋ yɔɔ. Tsei ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tsei lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly like small tubes?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tsei lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi tamɔ tsɔnei bibii?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from under the leaves, or by extreme heat. Protecting the plants from sap-sucking pests keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa mli Tsei ahe ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ nu lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my yam vines getting small dark spots and dying off early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii diji lɛ? Ni egbo yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Dark spots on yam leaves are usually caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose, which spreads through rain splashes. Clearing weeds and planting resistant yam varieties helps prevent leaf destruction.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi amli Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛduɔ sweet potato henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ baai shwiemɔ naa.

english: Why do my cowpea plants flower nicely, but the pods end up flat and empty without seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ miifɔ fɛfɛo lɛ? Shi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni dumɔwui bɛ mli?

english: Empty cowpea pods happen when small pod-sucking bugs attack the young pods early, sucking out the nutrients before the seeds inside can develop.
ga: Afeɔ cowpea ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ kɛ́ kooloi ŋmɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ. Tutua pods bibii lɛ mra. ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ shwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants before turning into small tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ dani amɛtsɔɔ tomato bibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when water is inconsistent, or when there are no insects to pollinate them. Regular watering and afternoon shade help keep the flowers on the plant.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni kooloi ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ lɛ Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa kɛ shwane mli hulutsoo be yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize stalks break and fall over easily whenever there is a mild wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ fãa oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa lɛ?

english: Maize stalks collapse when stems are weakened by stalk borer insects, when planted too closely together, or when lacking potassium in the soil to build strong stems.
ga: Abɛi tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi bibii ni boteɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ ha tsei lɛ gbɔjɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ loo kɛji akɛ potassium faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛma tsei ahe tsei ni wa.

english: Why are my young oil palm trees producing plenty of flowers but no fruit bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwu lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Oil palm trees need both male and female flowers along with pollinating insects (weevils) to transfer pollen. If the tree is very young or pollinating insects are absent, fruit bunches will not form.
ga: Mu tsei biɔ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei kɛ pollinators (ŋmeii) koni amɛkɛ pollen lɛ aya. Kɛji tso lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo loo kooloi ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ bɛ. Yibii akui efeŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees produce broad leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting young cocoa trees from sun damage and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Buu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu ni fiteɔ amɛ lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Why do I have to put wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking lifts the foliage off the hot ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing maximum sunlight reach for bigger yields.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni mli edɔ lɛ. Tsi foliar helai anaa ni oha hulu la ni fa babaoo aba koni ená yibii babaoo.

english: Why do some farmers plant groundnuts or cowpeas between rows of maize instead of growing maize alone?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii yɛ ŋmeii ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ moŋ fe ŋmeii kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans naturally capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. This acts like natural fertilizer for the maize, suppresses weeds, and gives you two crops to harvest from the same plot of land.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmãa. tsiɔ jwɛi anaa ni ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green and grow strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer around the plant will restore its green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eda jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata Tsei ahe lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes small ragged holes inside the central leaves of my growing maize plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei ni miida lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ baa?

english: This damage is typically caused by caterpillars called Fall Armyworms that hide deep inside the growing leaf funnel. Checking leaves early and applying appropriate control methods prevents them from destroying the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ amli mra Ni okɛ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafite tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot underground when the rains get very heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long because roots need air to breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ebɔle amɛhe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ he miihia kɔɔyɔɔ koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when temperatures become too high or when there is sudden heat stress, which prevents proper pollination. Providing light shade and maintaining steady soil moisture helps flowers turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ko ba trukaa. Enɛ tsiɔ pollination ni sa lɛ naa. Shade ni mli tse ni akɛhaa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl upwards and look wilted during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants curl their leaves during peak heat to reduce water loss through evaporation. If the plant unfurls and looks healthy again by evening, it is just protecting itself from the harsh sun.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni latsaa waa lɛ koni nu ni laajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Kɛji tso lɛ gbele ehe ni efee tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ gbɛkɛ lɛ Eji koni obu ohe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he kɛkɛ.

english: Why are my cassava tubers getting smaller every harvest even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni makpa amɛ lɛ? Ani eekwɛ̃ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same land continuously drains essential nutrients from the soil. Rotating crops or leaving the land to rest with soil-building legumes restores soil fertility for future harvests.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni aaatsake loo ashi he ko ni ŋmeii ni feɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmaakpamɔi.

english: How do I know the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting seeds when the early rains begin?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ maje dumɔwui ashishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Wait until rainfall soaks the soil to at least the depth of your hand, rather than planting after the very first light shower. Planting in deeply moist soil ensures seeds germinate without drying out if rain stops for a few days.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ hoo lɛ, ni eshɛ oniji ahe. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ ahum lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɛɛ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ gbii fioo komɛi.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. They need shade plants, like plantains or shade trees, to shield them from high heat while their roots develop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ miida lɛ.

english: Why do I need to clear tall weeds from around my young cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kakadaji ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Mi-cassava tso bibioo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young cassava and block sunlight from reaching the crop's leaves. When weeds shade the crop, the cassava cannot make enough food to build big root tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe yucca bibii lɛ, ni amɛtsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ ahe. Beni jwɛi haa tsei lɛ hulutsoo Cassava nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee shishifãi wuji.

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the soil is low in nitrogen. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves up to new leaves to keep growing, leaving the bottom leaves to starve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli kɛyaa baai heei amli koni baa heei akwɛ̃. Ha shishigbɛ baai lɛ aye hɔmɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves start curling up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ miije shishi amɛmiifee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is often caused by small sap-sucking pests like aphids or mites, or by hot dry winds. The leaf curls up as a stress response to protect itself from losing water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa ni mli egbi Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔnyɛɛ hetoohamɔ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ nu ni fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the stems grow thin and weak as they fight each other for sunlight and soil food. Thin stems cannot support heavy cobs or resist strong winds.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ be mli ni amɛwuɔ koni amɛná hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsoi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ anɔ loo amɛnyɛŋ amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa naa.

english: Why does my main plantain tree produce smaller fruit when there are many small shoots growing around it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso titri lɛ woɔ yibii bibii be mli ni eyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Mɛi babaoo miida yɛ he fɛɛ he.

english: The small shoots, called suckers, drink water and take fertilizer away from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers leaves more food for the mother tree to produce larger fruits.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ akɛ suckers. Abaanu nu ni ejie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ehaa tso nyɛ lɛ náa niyenii babaoo koni ewo yibii wuji.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in the air to catch as much sunlight as possible. Staking keeps the leaves off the ground and exposed to the sun, which helps the underground tubers grow bigger.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni hulu la ashɛ amɛhe bɔ ni aaanyɛ. Staking baaha ajie baai lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni hulu la lɛ aba amɛnɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get enough water. Heat stress stops the flowers from pollinating, so the plant drops them.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ tsiɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tso lɛ gbee shi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava roots are ready to harvest without digging up the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakpa ni akuuu mli?

english: When cassava is mature, the lower leaves naturally dry up and drop off, and the soil around the base of the main stem begins to crack open as the expanding tubers push upward.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mli egbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni egbeeɔ shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso titri lɛ shishi lɛ baaje shishi egbɛ eshwa be mli ni bulb ni miigbɛ eshwa lɛ tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Is it bad to water my garden vegetables under the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani nu ni oooha o-abɔɔ lɛ mli yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli lɛ ehiii?

english: Watering in high heat causes water droplets on leaves to evaporate quickly before reaching roots. It can also shock hot plants and cause water spots on leaves that invite disease.
ga: Nu ni akɛ la ni mli edɔ waa woɔ mli lɛ haa nu ni shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya dani eshɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Ebaanyɛ eha tsei lɛ hu ahe afee shoo kɛtsɔ dɔlɛ nɔ ni ekɛ nu ŋmɔtɔ aba baai lɛ anɔ ni kɛ hela baa.

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and high heat. Without larger shade trees or food crops like plantain to cover them, the sun scorches their leaves and dries out their shallow roots before they can establish.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei wuji ni baaha hulutsoo loo niyenii tsei tamɔ dumɔwui ni baaha nɔ lɛ bɛ lɛ, Hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Egbiɔ dani edaa.

english: Leaf curling and yellow patches on cassava are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava stems helps prevent this problem.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ nɔ lɛ ji ŋmɔtɔ mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa Kasava tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ he odaseyeli lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when temperatures become too hot, when water is irregular, or when there is too much nitrogen in the soil, which causes the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: How do I know if my maize crop needs nitrogen fertilizer just by looking at the leaves?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii he miihia mi-ŋmãa lɛ kɛtsɔ baai lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛkɛ nɔ?

english: When maize lacks nitrogen, the lower leaves turn pale green and then start yellowing in a 'V' shape pattern starting from the leaf tip moving down the middle vein.
ga: Kɛji nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ eŋɔli ni baaje shishi efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ ‘V’ su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa ni ebaaya shi yɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn stalks roll up into tight tubes during the sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, helping the plant save moisture and prevent water loss during heat stress.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ehaaa nu lɛ afite yɛ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why does spear grass keep growing back on my farm even after I clear it completely with a cutlass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ji spear lɛ yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛ mikɛ dade jie fɛɛ po?

english: Spear grass has deep underground stems called rhizomes that hold stored food energy. Even when you cut the leaves above ground, those underground stems remain alive and quickly shoot up new growth.
ga: Spear jwɛi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni mli kwɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ rhizomes ni kɛ niyenii hewalɛ toɔ. Kɛji ofo baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ po Nakai shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni amɛfeɔ ehee oya.

english: Why do my corn plants grow very tall and thin with tiny cobs when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. This competition forces the stalks to stretch tall for light while leaving them too weak to form full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ koni ená la. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni ekɛfee ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my harvested yams small and bent instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni egbo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep, loose soil mounds to expand easily. If the soil is hard, compacted, or stony, the growing tubers meet resistance under the ground and become stunted or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli kwɔ, ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ wa, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baaná hewalɛ ni teɔ shi woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛbaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cashew trees drop many of their leaves right before they start flowering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cashew tso lɛ baai babaoo shwieɔ shi dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ?

english: Cashew trees naturally drop older leaves during dry periods to conserve water. This leaf shedding signals the tree to shift its energy into flowering and fruiting as part of its normal seasonal cycle.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cashew tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai momo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nɛkɛ baa ni laajeɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ tso lɛ akɛ ebaatsake ehewalɛ kɛya fɔfɔii kɛ yibiiwoo nɔ akɛ eji be ni ekɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ fã.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single high-yielding generation. If you harvest and replant those saved seeds, the new plants will produce much lower yields, grow unevenly, and lack resistance to diseases.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha yinɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛji okpa dumɔwui ni ahere lɛ ni odu ekoŋŋ lɛ Tsei heei baaná yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa. dalɛ ni kɛ ehe kpaaa gbee kɛ helai ni nyɛɛɛ amɛshi amɛhe lɛ ni bɛ

english: How do I know if my soil is healthy enough to plant maize?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makwɛ ŋmãa?

english: Dark, loose soil that drains water well without getting waterlogged is best for maize. You can test it by squeezing a handful of moist soil—if it holds shape gently but crumbles easily when touched, it has good structure for planting.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni nu bɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmãa. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ ni oootsi mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛji ehiɛ egbɛhe lɛ mli blɛoo, Shi kɛ́ ata he lɛ, efoɔ oya. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo kpakpa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: Is it better to burn the cleared weeds on my farm or leave them on the ground before planting?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mashã jwɛi ni ajie yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ loo mashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ dani madu?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the ground as mulch is better than burning. Burning destroys valuable organic matter and micro-organisms in the soil, while leaving cleared weeds protects the soil from drying out under the hot sun and turns into natural food for your crops as it decays.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajie lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi fe shãa. Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ nibii bibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, jwɛi ni he tse ni ashiɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ebatsɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii beni amɛfiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crop yields drop if I keep planting cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific nutrients that crop needs from the soil and allows pests that feed on it to multiply. Rotating cassava with crops like groundnuts or beans allows the soil to rebuild its nutrients naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tso lɛ lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ tsei lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ. Kasava ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei tsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ emaa shi ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Should I plant my cassava stem cuttings flat in the ground or standing upright?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu yucca tsei aniji yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ja nɔ?

english: Planting cassava stems at an slant or upright into the soil helps the roots grow deeper and stronger. Planting them flat can cause the roots to develop too close to the surface, making them prone to rotting if the land floods.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ o-cassava tso lɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ koŋ nɔ loo ehi shi jaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛhe awa. Kɛ́ adu yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ata shi ni amɛbɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ebaagbo kɛji nu shwie nɔ.

english: What will happen if I plant my seeds very close to each other so I can fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni anyɛ adu shikpɔŋ babaoo?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow thin and weak, resulting in smaller yields than if they had enough space.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baafee bibioo fe kɛji akɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ.

english: How long should I wait after the first rain before I sow my maize seeds?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ omɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani okɛdu ŋmãa dumɔwui?

english: It is best to wait until the rains become steady rather than planting immediately after the very first rain. A early dry period after one rain can easily dry out and kill your newly sprouted seeds.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ fe ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Be ni nugbɔ nɛɔ oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi oya.

english: Why are the leaves on my young corn plants turning pale yellow instead of bright green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are a signal that your plant is lacking nitrogen, which is essential for healthy green growth, or that the roots are suffocating from waterlogged soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their green color.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ. Aloo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee eŋɔli.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or excessive nitrogen fertilizer. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shaded during hot afternoons helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ na haomɔi tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni ekɛhaaa lɛ be fɛɛ be. loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eha hulu tsoɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is a great practice. Cowpeas pull nitrogen from the air into the soil to feed the maize, while the maize provides support for the cowpeas, allowing you to harvest two crops from the same field.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ ji nifeemɔ kpakpa. Cowpeas gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa yeɔ ebuaa tsina ŋmãa lɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do I keep finding small holes eaten through the leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mina bu bibioo ko lɛ? Ani oyeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai be fɛɛ be?

english: Holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by pests like the fall armyworm caterpillar eating the soft leaves. Catching them early and applying natural neem leaf extracts or recommended treatments prevents them from destroying the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ cutworms ni yeɔ baa bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa bibii amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ omɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite hei ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green foliage and healthy growth. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plants the nutrients they need to turn dark green and grow big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa waa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni mli edɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies, that stored nitrogen stays in the soil, acting as a natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi bibii amli kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo. Nakai nitrogen ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Why are small caterpillars eating holes inside the central funnel of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are Fall Armyworms, which love to hide in the soft, tender middle leaves of young maize. Applying recommended insecticides or neem leaf spray directly into the leaf funnel early on stops them before they destroy the main growing shoot.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛhiɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ amli. Tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi loo neem baa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa baa lɛ mli mra. Koni akpa lɛ dani efite tsei titri ni miida lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my tomato plants curling up and turning yellow at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whiteflies, or by extreme heat and lack of water. Controlling whiteflies with nets or sprays and keeping the soil moist helps protect the plant from getting damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni faaa mli Whitefly Control kɛ Nets loo Sprays Ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ fitemɔ he.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy or humid weather when water stays on the pods. Removing infected pods regularly and clearing weeds allows sunlight and air to dry out the trees, stopping the disease from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ loo hulutsoo be mli kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ daa, ni ajieɔ jwɛi lɛ, ehaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ haa tsei lɛ agbiɔ. ni ekpa helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from stress caused by hot sun, dry soil, or insect attacks like capsids. Keeping enough shade trees and making sure the soil retains moisture helps flowers stay on the branches long enough to form pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ capsids lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ nɔ hulutsoo bɔ ni sa, ni shikpɔŋ lɛ hu mli edɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose all their blossoms without producing any peppers during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ efo ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa wooo yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Very hot sun and dry air make pepper blossoms dry out and fall off before they can be pollinated. Covering the soil around the base of the plant with dry grass (mulching) keeps the roots cool and helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ haa pepper fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee pollin. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi (mulch) shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: How do I know the exact time to dig up my yams after the leaves start turning brown?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafo sweet potato beni baai lɛ ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ sɛɛ?

english: When yam leaves turn yellow and die back at the end of the rainy season, it means the plant has finished sending energy underground to build the tuber. This is the natural sign that the yam is fully grown and ready to harvest.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛmajeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi koni ekɛfee ŋmeii lɛ naa. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potatoes eda ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over right when the fruit bunch gets big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni aduawai akui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and tiny worms (nematodes) or stem borers can eat through the roots and base, weakening the tree. Supporting the stem with a wooden prop and planting clean, healthy suckers prevents heavy bunches from pulling the tree down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. ni ŋmeii bibii (Nematodes) loo ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ aye nii kɛtsɔ shishifãi kɛ shishigbɛ nɔ. ni haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni akɛfiɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tsu nii ni akɛdu tsei ni he tse ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tsei niji ni tsii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbala tso lɛ shi.

english: Cassava roots rot when water accumulates around them in heavy clay soil or poorly drained fields, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows water to drain away freely and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa amɛhe naa yɛ amɛhe lɛ. amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni tsii loo ŋmɔji ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mli lɛ amli. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu lɛ hoɔ oya ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do my young maize plants die when I spray non-selective weedkillers around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-babi corn tsei lɛ gboiɔ kɛ mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ shwie amɛhe lɛ?

english: Strong non-selective weedkillers (often called 'condemn' in local markets) are designed to kill every green plant they touch, not just weeds. If the chemical splashes onto your maize leaves, it damages the leaves instantly and kills the whole plant.
ga: Afee tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni halaaa jwɛi (ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘damn’ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ) koni egbe tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛkɛkpeɔ lɛ. Jeee jwɛi pɛ Kɛji tsofai shwie ŋmãa baai anɔ lɛ Ebaafite baai lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ ni eha tso muu lɛ fɛɛ agbo.

english: Why does using strong weedkiller every season make my farm soil look dry and hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbi ni ewa lɛ?

english: Heavy chemical weedkillers kill beneficial living organisms in the soil that naturally keep it soft and moist. Exposed, bare soil also dries out quickly under the hot sun and becomes hard packed after rains.
ga: Tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni tsii waa lɛ gbeɔ sũ mli nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa sũ lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ hu gbiɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni ebaawa yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that create living umbrellas, providing the shade and moisture young cocoa needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa cocoa gbekɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ haa.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb on instead of trailing on the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight and make food for tuber growth. Lifting the leaves up on stakes lets them catch maximum sunlight and air, resulting in larger yam tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛ baai lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ hulu la ni amɛha niyenii kɛha ŋmeii lɛ adalɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tso ko nɔ lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ babaoo. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baafee wuji.

english: Cassava drops its leaves naturally during dry spells to conserve water. The plant goes into a resting state while keeping its roots alive underground, sprouting fresh leaves as soon as the rains return.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ hɔmɔ be mli koni ekɛbu nu he. Tso lɛ boteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli yɛ be mli ni ehiɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Baai heei lɛ baakwɛ̃ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts before maize make my maize crop grow greener and stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ midu ŋmei dani miwo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa mi ŋmei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ehaa ehe waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the groundnut crop is harvested, these roots rot and leave behind natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nɛkɛ shishifãi nɛɛ baagboi ni amɛbaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha dumɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting from the middle vein down the tip of lower leaves is a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency. The plant is hungry for nitrogen fertilizer to build healthy green leaves.
ga: Yellow ni jɛɔ tsitsii lɛ ateŋ kɛyaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa. Tsei he miihia nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl tightly together and stop the plant from producing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe shi shiŋŋ ni amɛtsiɔ tso lɛ naa koni ekafee pepper lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking leaf sap and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents leaves from twisting and allows flowering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni miinu baai lɛ amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Ebaatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ amɛhe ni amɛkawo fɔfɔi.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn dark brown or black and shrivel up during rainy weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in dark, damp conditions. Pruning heavy leaves lets sunlight and wind dry out the trees, preventing fungal spores from multiplying.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni efɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Kɛ́ afo tso lɛ yibii ni tsii lɛ, ebaaha hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ aha tso lɛ agbi. Etsiɔ fungal spores lɛ naa koni amɛkafee babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruits when the weather is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages their pollen, preventing flowers from fertilizing. Without fertilization, the flowers die and drop off before fruit can form.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ pollen lɛ. Ehaa fɔfɔi nyɛɛɛ awo fɔ Kɛji fɔ bɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagbee shi dani amɛwo yibii.

english: Why is it better for me to water my vegetables early in the morning rather than in the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ nu woɔ mi-aduawai lɛ amli babaoo leebi fe shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: In the early morning, the soil is cooler and plants are actively waking up to take in water. In the afternoon heat, much of the water evaporates into the air before the plant's roots can drink it up.
ga: Leebi lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni tsei lɛ teɔ shi koni amɛná nu. Yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ Nu lɛ mli babaoo shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ nuɔ nu lɛ.

english: Does gentle morning sunlight help my crops grow better than the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Ani leebi hulu ni tsoɔ blɛoo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Yes, morning sunlight allows crops to start photosynthesizing and making their food without thermal stress, whereas harsh afternoon sun causes plants to lose water rapidly and wilt.
ga: Hɛɛ, leebi hulu la yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛjeɔ fotosintɛsis kɛ nihoomɔ shishi ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ bɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tsei lɛ amli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Does morning dew on my crops help them drink, or can it cause diseases like black pod in cocoa?
ga: Ani leebi ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnuɔ nu? Aloo ebaanyɛ ekɛ helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji ni yɔɔ kookoo mli lɛ aba?

english: Morning dew provides temporary leaf hydration, but if crops stay wet under deep shade for too long, the persistent moisture creates an environment for fungal diseases like black pod to spread.
ga: Leebi ŋmɔtɔ haa baai lɛ mli fũuɔ be kukuoo ko. Shi kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli kwɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ, Fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ haa shihilɛ ko baa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why should I clear weeds from my farm when they are still tiny instead of waiting for them to grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ moŋ fe ni mamɛ ni amɛdara?

english: Tiny weeds are easy to destroy before they take root deeply. If you let them grow big and strong, they will consume the soil nutrients and water meant for your crops long before your crops can get them.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ abaakpata jwɛi bibii lɛ ahiɛ dani amɛwo shishifãi. Kɛji oha amɛdara ni amɛhe wa lɛ, Amɛbaaye niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni yɔɔ kɛha onibii lɛ dani onibii lɛ baanyɛ aná amɛ.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to apply my fertilizer early in the morning or right before the rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli leebi loo dani nugbɔ lɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Applying fertilizer early gives moisture the time to dissolve nutrients into the root zone so crops can feed on them immediately as their roots awaken during the day.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli mra Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ aná be ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ awo shishifã lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni tsei lɛ anyɛ aye nii kɛji shishifãi lɛ te shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli pɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants produce smaller cobs when I plant them too close to big, older trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii beni midu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tso agbo ni egbɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Older trees have extensive root systems already established underground. They drink up available water and nutrients early while blocking sunlight, leaving young maize plants starving.
ga: Tsei ni edara lɛ yɛ shishifãi babaoo ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ momo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Amɛnuɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mra. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ hulu la lɛ naa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii.

english: Why do I need to trim excessive plantain suckers when growing them as shade for young cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mifoɔ plantain tsei babaoo tsɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ koni mikɛha kookoo bibii lɛ aná hulutsoo lɛ?

english: If too many plantain suckers grow around young cocoa, they take over the soil nutrients and block all sunlight, starving the cocoa instead of giving it gentle shade.
ga: Kɛji akɛ plantain tsei babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe lɛ, amɛbaaye niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ najiaŋ ni amɛbaatsi hulu la lɛ fɛɛ naa. Ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ kookoo lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha hulutsoo blɛoo.

english: Why does my maize mature in just three months while my cassava takes a whole year in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ shwere yɛ nyɔji etɛ pɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-cassava lɛ yeɔ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing crop designed to quickly capture surface water and light to produce seeds early, while cassava slowly builds a deep tuber system that stores energy over a long period.
ga: Abɛi ji tso ko ni daa oya ni afee lɛ koni emɔ nu kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya koni ewo dumɔwui mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei lɛ baafee fiofio Efee shikpɔŋ shishi tuber gbɛjianɔtoo ko ni mli kwɔ ni kɛ hewalɛ toɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I prepare my land weeks before the major rainy season begins in Ghana?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ otsii komɛi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be titri ni yaa nɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ aje shishi lɛ?

english: Preparing land early loosens the soil so it can capture the very first rains, giving your seeds a head start to sprout immediately when soil moisture is at its peak.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni enyɛ emɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ. Kwɛmɔ ni odumɔwui lɛ abɔi kwɛ̃mɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ shɛɔ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ pɛ.

english: Why do my mature tree crops start producing leaves and flowers faster than young trees when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei ni eda lɛ jeɔ baai kɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ shishi mra fe tsei bibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Mature trees store reserve food energy in their thick trunks and deep roots over the dry season, allowing them to react instantly to the first rains while young trees are still struggling to build roots.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ toɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔlɔ kɛ amɛshishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei bibii lɛ miibɔ mɔdɛŋ lolo ni amɛfee shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing too much water in the hot sun. It is the plant's natural way of saving moisture, but if the leaves stay rolled up early in the morning, it means the crop urgently needs water.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni nu akafite fe nine yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eji adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa tsei feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lolo leebi lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nu he miihia tso lɛ oya.

english: When pepper plants do not get enough water or face extreme heat stress, they drop their flowers to conserve energy and survive, rather than using up precious water to produce fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ loo amɛkpe hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Amɛbaashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛhi shi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nu ni jara wa baatsu nii kɛfee nii

english: Early morning or late evening is the best time to water crops. During these cooler hours, the soil absorbs the water deeply before the sun can evaporate it away.
ga: Leebi maŋkpa loo gbɛkɛ ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ nu. Yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli ejɔ lɛ amli lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ dani hulu lɛ shwieɔ nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my tender tomato seedlings keep dying when I pour water on them using a bucket?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ gboiɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ mikɛ baagi shwie nu nɔ lɛ?

english: Heavy streams of water from a bucket wash away the soil from fragile roots and break delicate stems. Young seedlings need a light, gentle spray, like from a watering can, so they can absorb water without damage.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ waa kɛjɛɔ tanki lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ sũ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ anɔ, ni efoɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ amli. Tsei bibii lɛ he miihia ni afɔ amɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ blɛoo. Etamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu mli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ejie nu ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee.

english: Why does my crop field dry out so fast even after I water it heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ he ni miduɔ nii yɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji mikɛ nu babaoo wo nɔ po lɛ?

english: Bare soil exposes moisture directly to the strong sun, causing rapid evaporation. Placing dry grass or leaves around the bases of your plants (mulching) keeps the soil cool and traps moisture for much longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ haa hulu la ni naa wa, ni yɔɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa ŋmɔtɔ. Ekɛ la ni hoɔ oya baa Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi wo tsei lɛ ashishi (mulching) lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why should I make mounds or ridges before planting my crops instead of planting on flat soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ dani madu nii moŋ fe ni madu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Ridges and mounds keep the soil loose, allowing rainwater to soak in easily without washing away topsoil, while also preventing crops from sitting in stagnant water during heavy downpours.
ga: Ridges and mounds help loosen the soil. Ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ shwieɔ shi oya ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ efɔɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaaa ŋmɔshi nibii akabote nu ni damɔ shi mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants rot and turn yellow in the low part of my land after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miifite ni amɛmiitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water collects and stands on land for too long, it fills all the air spaces in the soil. Roots need air to live, so standing water suffocates cassava roots and causes them to decay.
ga: Beni nu buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia shishifãi koni amɛhi shi. No hewɔ lɛ, nu ni ekã shi lɛ baaha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping leaves during long periods of flooding?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei shwieɔ shi yɛ nu afua ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water around crop roots prevents them from taking up essential nutrients from the soil. When roots are choked by water, the tree drops leaves to reduce its workload and survive.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni ebɔle he lɛ Tse shishifãi tsiɔ tsei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni nu eyi shishifãi lɛ anɔ Tsei lɛ baagbee shi koni amɛnitsumɔ lɛ aba shi ni amɛhi shi.

english: Can I safely use water from a stream near a village to irrigate my garden crops?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ faa ko ni bɛŋkɛ mi akrowa lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe kɛfɔ mibɔɔ lɛ nɔ nu?

english: You can, but you must ensure the stream is free from soapy runoff, chemicals, or animal waste. Dirty or chemically polluted water can burn crop leaves, damage roots, or make harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi kwɛmɔ ni nu lɛ mli akafee samla ni hoɔ, tsofai, loo kooloi ahe jwɛi. Nu ni mli ewo muji loo tsofai baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai, efite shishifãi, loo eha niyenii ni akpa lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ.

english: How do I know if the water I am using for my crops has too much salt or chemicals in it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ nu ni mikɛtsuɔ nii kɛduɔ nii lɛ mli ŋmei loo tsofai babaoo yɛ mli?

english: If water has too much salt or chemical pollution, you will often see white crusts on top of the soil, or the edges of your crops' leaves will look scorched and burnt.
ga: Kɛji nu lɛ mli ŋmei loo tsofai babaoo yɛ mli lɛ Bei pii lɛ obaana ŋmei yɛŋ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo tso lɛ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ baafee tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni eshã.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn pale yellow even after I clear the farm land and burn the bushes like my elders taught me?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse eyɛ mli akɛ mijie ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni mishã jwɛi lɛ tamɔ bɔ ni onukpai lɛ tsɔɔ mi lɛ moŋ?

english: Burning bushes destroys the organic matter and friendly living organisms in the soil that crops need to feed on. Yellow leaves usually mean your crops lack nitrogen, which gets burnt away in farm fires, so using compost or manure works much better than burning.
ga: Tsoi bibii ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ naanyobɔɔ nibii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehe hiaa ni tsei aye niyenii lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli, ni abaashã yɛ ŋmɔ mli la mli. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe nɔ ni ashãa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees die during the hot, dry season in my area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be kɛ hulutsoo be yɔɔ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside your young cocoa trees provides a living umbrella that keeps the air cool and soil moist until the cocoa matures.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Dumɔ tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ o-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ajɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baakwɛ̃.

english: Is it true that planting my cassava sticks very close together will give me a bigger harvest from my plot?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ, kɛ́ midu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he lɛ, ebaaha mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná yibii babaoo?

english: No, planting crops too close together makes them fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Leaving adequate space between plants lets the roots spread out fully so the cassava tubers can grow thick and heavy.
ga: Dabi, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ awu yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Shi gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã kwraa. Enɛ ji koni eha ŋmei shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsii.

english: How do I know the exact right time to sow my maize seeds after the long dry period?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmãa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You should wait until the major rains have settled and soaked deep into the ground, rather than planting after the very first light rainfall. Soil needs steady moisture so seeds don't germinate and then dry up under the hot sun.
ga: Esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ wulu lɛ aba shi ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ yɛ shishijee mli lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ni ená ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ ni amɛgbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: Can I just save seeds from my previous maize harvest to plant again next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ ato koni madu ekoŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds harvested from old crops lose their strength and yield potential over time. Buying certified improved seeds ensures your crops grow uniform, withstand local pests better, and yield much more food.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akpaa kɛjɛɔ tsei momo amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔwui ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ hemɔ baaha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ be fɛɛ be. Hewalɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni teɔ shi ewoɔ maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo

english: Why do weeds always grow faster and stronger than the crops I planted on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa be fɛɛ be fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to steal nutrients, water, and sunlight faster than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds early in the crop's life prevents them from choking your plants before they can grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe esa akɛ amɛju niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ yɛ gbekɛbiiashi lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkatswa otso lɛ dani eda waa.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the life out of the leaves. Applying safe treatments like neem oil water helps kill these small pests so the plant can grow healthy leaves and fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni shwieɔ wala kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe tamɔ neem fɔ nu ni akɛtsuɔ nii Eyeɔ ebuaa ni egbeɔ nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ baai kɛ aduawai ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce many flowers, but the flowers drop off without forming tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee tomato?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and feeding the plant helps the flowers turn into full tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni aha tsei lɛ niyenii lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛfɔ̃ ni amɛfee tomato fɔfɔi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why does my land yield less harvest every year even though I plant the exact same crop in the same spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome moŋ?

english: Planting the same crop every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil until it becomes exhausted. Rotating different crops, especially legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas, naturally restores nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛbaafite. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi ni atsakeɔ Titri lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii. Ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly on hot days, and how can I keep it moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ anɔ lɛ? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nu yɛ mihe?

english: Bare soil loses water rapidly to the hot sun through evaporation. Covering the earth around your plants with dry grass, leaves, or palm fronds (mulching) acts like a blanket that traps water in the soil and keeps plant roots cool.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ ehe kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ni egbi, baai, loo ŋmei tsei (mulch) awo tso lɛ he. Enɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu, emɔɔ nu yɛ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why do some crops produce large harvests in one region of Ghana but perform poorly in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana kpokpaa ko nɔ shi amɛwooo yibii babaoo yɛ kpokpaa kroko nɔ lɛ?

english: Crops react differently to rainfall, temperature, and soil types across regions. For instance, cocoa thrives in the humid southern forest zones, while grain crops like millet and sorghum perform much better in the drier northern savanna climate.
ga: Tsei tsuɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔ he nii yɛ hei srɔtoi. Ákɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, kookoo shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ kooi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmaa nibii tamɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kwraa yɛ kooyigbɛ savannah kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni mli egbi lɛ mli.

english: How do I determine which crop is best suited to grow on my specific farm location?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsei ni sa jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ he pɔtɛɛ ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crop behavior depends heavily on local soil type, drainage, and seasonal weather patterns. Testing your soil and observing which local crops naturally grow strong and healthy in nearby fields can help you choose the best crop for your farm.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ subaŋ damɔ shikpɔŋ henɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ nɔ, nu ni hoɔ kɛ be mli kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi. Kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ ni okadi maŋ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua bo ni ohala ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Is it true that groundnuts grow much better in sandy northern soils than in heavy forest zones?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ kooyigbɛ shikpɔji ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ anɔ fe kooi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, groundnuts prefer well-drained, light sandy soils found commonly in northern areas because it is easier for their pods to expand underground. Heavy, wet forest soils can cause groundnut pods to rot before harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ kooyigbɛ hei lɛ Enɛ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi mlɛo. Koo mli shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmei ŋmeii lɛ agboi dani akpa.

english: Why do cash crops like maize generate higher volume harvests on large lands than quick vegetables like tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shika ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ hei wuji fe aduawai ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Maize plants produce heavy grain heads that can be stored for long periods and grown closely on large fields, whereas vegetables are soft, spoil quickly, and require intensive manual care on smaller land plots.
ga: Abɛi woɔ dumɔwui ayitsei ni tsii ni abaanyɛ akɛto be kakadaŋŋ ni adu yɛ ŋmɔji wuji amli ni bɛŋkɛ kpaakpa. Shi aduawai lɛ, amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛgboiɔ oya, ni ehe hiaa ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔji bibii anɔ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers remain very small while another farm nearby gets huge cassava yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ faaa kwraa lolo yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ kroko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ woɔ cassava babaoo lɛ?

english: Cassava tuber size depends on soil looseness, fertility, and variety. Compacted or poor soil prevents tubers from expanding, while loose, fertile soil gives roots the space and nutrients needed to grow large.
ga: Kasava shishifã lɛ dalɛ damɔ bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse ha lɛ nɔ. Fɔmɔ kɛ Srɔtoi Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ loo ni ehiɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baatsi ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni baa nii lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara.

english: Why does my maize farm yield significantly less volume during the minor rainy season compared to the major season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ mli kɛ akɛto be titri lɛ he lɛ?

english: Maize needs steady soil moisture especially when forming silks and grain kernels. The minor rainy season has shorter, less reliable rainfall, which stresses the plants and reduces total grain weight.
ga: Abɛi he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ daa. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ afee siliki kɛ dumɔwui. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ kuku ni anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ baa shi.

english: Why do fast-growing short-season crops yield smaller overall weight than long-term crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni daa oya, ni yeɔ be kukuoo lɛ fɛɛ tsiimɔ waaa kwraa fe tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Short-season crops direct their energy into quick reproduction before dying within a few months, whereas long-term crops build strong root and stem structures over time that support heavier, continuous yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ ni hiɔ shi be kuku lɛ kɛ hewalɛ woɔ fɔmɔ oya mli dani egboɔ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli. Nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ maa shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni mli wa yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ lɛ. ni haa nibii ni tsii ni yaa nɔ babaoo baa

english: Why do grain crops like maize require frequent commercial fertilizer while cowpeas grow well without much added fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa he hiaa jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ lɛ? Shi tsina ŋmeii lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii babaoo wooo mli lɛ, amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Maize extracts nutrients heavily from the soil without replacing them. Cowpeas are legumes, meaning their roots naturally trap nitrogen from the air and enrich the soil themselves, reducing the need for external fertilizer.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ekɛwooo mli ekoŋŋ. Cowpea ji ŋmãa tso. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nɔ ni jara wa. Enɛ haa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jɛɔ kponɔgbɛ atsu nii.

english: Why does growing yams require so much land space compared to leafy green vegetables?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potatoes ni akwɛɔ lɛ biɔ he ko babaoo fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ?

english: Yam plants need deep soil beds and wide spacing so their vines receive plenty of sunlight and their underground tubers have sufficient room to expand without competing with neighboring plants.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ shɔŋŋ koni eha wain tsei lɛ hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa. Ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ yɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛkɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ akaŋ.

english: How does planting tall shade trees near my crops change how those crops grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsei kakadaji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ tsakeɔ bɔ ni amɛdaraa amɛhaa lɛ?

english: Shade trees keep the soil cool and retain moisture, which benefits sun-sensitive crops like young cocoa, but too much shade will starve sun-loving crops like maize or yams of the light they need to grow strong yields.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni hulu lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe tamɔ kookoo bibii lɛ, shi hulutsoo babaoo baatsi tsei ni sumɔɔ hulu tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni ŋɔɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa.

english: Why does maize seem to grow almost anywhere I plant it in Ghana, but yields better in some specific areas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ he fɛɛ he ni miduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ? Shi yibiiwoo lɛ hi fe hei komɛi titri.

english: Maize is a very hardy and adaptable crop that can sprout in most soil types across Ghana. However, it yields its maximum potential in regions with deep, fertile soil and consistent rainfall patterns that match its growth stages.
ga: Abele ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ni nyɛɔ etsakeɔ ehe ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ shikpɔŋ fɛɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ Ghana fɛɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ ni fe fɛɛ haa yɛ hei ni shikpɔji ni mli kwɔ ni baa nii babaoo yɔɔ lɛ. ni eyɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be ni kɛ dalɛ be lɛ kpãa gbee.

english: Is it true that certain crops can grow anywhere, or should I only plant what is suitable for my local area?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ abaanyɛ akwɛ tsei komɛi yɛ he fɛɛ he? Aloo esa akɛ madu tsei ni sa kɛha he ni miyɔɔ lɛ pɛ?

english: While versatile crops like maize can survive across different soil types and districts, every crop performs best where rainfall, temperature, and soil conditions perfectly match its specific needs.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ srɔtoi tamɔ ŋmãa baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔji srɔtoi kɛ hei srɔtoi anɔ moŋ, shi ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, latsaa, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shihilɛi lɛ kɛ ehiamɔ nii pɔtɛɛi lɛ kpãa gbee pɛpɛɛpɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which plants need to stay green and build strong stalks. When nitrogen is scarce, the plant starves its older leaves to keep the young leaves alive at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni tsei ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛma ŋmeii ni wa. Kɛ nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei yeɔ baa momoi lɛ ahe hɔmɔ bɔni afee ni baa bibii lɛ ahi nɔ.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with bushy leaves, but the roots underground stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ? Shi shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi lɛ ji bibii lolo?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen but lacks potassium, the cassava plant spends all its energy building leafy stems above ground instead of storing food in the tubers below.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ shi potassium bɛ mli lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa baai ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ amli.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when they face extreme heat, uneven watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus. Keeping the soil constantly moist and feeding the plants balanced crop food helps flowers turn into big fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei baawo fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni naa wa waa he. Nu ni oooha amɛ be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa, tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ niyenii ni ja ni oooha otsei lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfee kui wuji.

english: Why are my young cocoa trees dropping their leaves and looking scorched during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛshã yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive roots that cannot reach deep groundwater yet. Without shade from bigger plants like plantains or tree canopies, the hot sun dries out the soil and burns the delicate leaves.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu ni mli kwɔ lɛ he lolo. Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be ko bɛ tsei wuji tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ashishifãi ahe lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gĩɔ ni eshãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants make my farm soil richer for the next crop I plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tsei lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛbaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen naturally from the air and store it in small nodules on their roots. When the plant dies and rots, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil as free plant food for your next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ ŋmeii bibii amli yɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo ni egbo. Nakai nitrogen ni amɔmɔ lɛ lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tsei niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are my maize plants staying short and stunted even after I applied fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ kuku ni amɛhe ejɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ lɛ?

english: If your soil is too sour or acidic, the plant roots lock up and cannot swallow the food you give them. Adding agricultural lime to the field balances the soil so the crop can drink up the applied nutrients.
ga: Kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ loo eyɛ acid tsɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baatswa amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmi niyenii ni okɛhaa lɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ okwaayeli mli lime fata ŋmɔji ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ feɔ ekome bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anu niyenii ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up into tight cups and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛfeɔ kɔɔpoi ni mli wa ni amɛkpaa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is often a natural defense reaction when tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips attack, or when the plant is trying to conserve water during dry, windy weather.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tso lɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni haa mɔ he tseɔ kɛji kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu lɛ, tamɔ thrips, tutua lɛ, loo kɛ́ tso lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ nu nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni kɔɔyɔɔ miitswa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam leaves develop brown spots that look like burns during heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ nɔ ni ashã amɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Frequent rains create high moisture that allows leaf spot fungi to spread quickly across yam foliage. Planting certified clean seed tubers and clearing old plant waste reduces this leaf disease.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo be babaoo baa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa leaf spot fungus ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ atomo baai lɛ anɔ. Dumɔwui ayitsei ni he tse ni awo he odase akɛ aaadu kɛ tsei amli jwɛi momo ni ajieɔ lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ foliar hela nɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my vegetable crops grow much faster when I put cow dung around their roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ daa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ tsina ŋmei bɔle amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like a slow-release meal that feeds beneficial soil organisms, softens tough ground, and holds soil moisture so plant roots can easily drink up nourishment over a long period.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo blɛoo ni haa bɔɔ nii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ niyenii. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni eha sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ mlɛo.

english: When is the best time to feed my rice crop so that the heads fill up with heavy grains?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ aha ŋmãa tsei niyenii koni ŋmãa tsei lɛ aná dumɔwui ni tsii?

english: Rice needs food at two main growth moments: once shortly after planting to build strong roots, and again when the stems begin to swell right before the grain heads emerge.
ga: Niyenii he miihia ŋmãa yɛ dalɛ bei titrii enyɔ mli: klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, beni adu lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ, koni shishifãi ni wa aba; Ni agbɛnɛ hu beni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛshwieɔ shi dani dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil is low on nitrogen, which gives the plant its green color and strength. Applying well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer around the stems will help restore healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ewaa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha tso lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: When cowpeas get too much nitrogen from the soil, they put all their energy into leaf growth instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen, so adding extra nitrogen causes leaf overload while reducing pod production.
ga: Kɛji tsina ŋmei nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tsina ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ woɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli moŋ fe fɔfɔi. Cowpeas jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ adebɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen kroko fata he lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ atsu nii fe nine, ni ebaaha pod ni afeɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil when the rains become heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when standing water prevents oxygen from reaching them in the ground. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shi, ni no haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ aya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: What makes my yam tubers grow twisted and misshapen underground?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi sweet potato tubers lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers become misshapen when they push against hard, stony, or compacted soil while growing. Digging deep, loose, rock-free soil mounds gives the yam space to expand smoothly and straight.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashɛ amɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni wa mli. tɛi loo ni akɛwo mli shiŋŋ beni aduɔ lɛ Kɛ́ atsa shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni tɛi bɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha sweet potato lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ ni efee tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my sweet potato vines spread all over the farm while the tubers inside the ground stay tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Excessive foliage growth happens when sweet potatoes receive too much nitrogen, forcing the plant to build stems and leaves rather than store energy in the roots. Pruning excess vine tips encourages the plant to focus on enlarging its tubers.
ga: Baai ni yaa hiɛ fe nine lɛ baa kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ lɛ nine shɛ nitrogen babaoo nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ baato amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Wein tso lɛ yitsei ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa e-bulbs lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ nɔ.

english: Mature cocoa pods change color from green or deep red to a bright yellow or orange-yellow. Harvesting when they turn fully yellow ensures the sweet pulp and beans inside are fully developed for high-quality fermentation.
ga: Kookoo tsei ni eda lɛ tsakeɔ su kɛjɛɔ eŋɔli loo etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo ŋmɔŋ-akutu. Nikpamɔ be mli ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ kwraa lɛ haa loo kɛ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young oil palm seedlings dry up and die shortly after transplanting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni mikɛwo he kroko lɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young oil palms die after transplanting if their root systems dry out in hot weather before establishing in the ground. Planting at the start of the rainy season and placing a layer of dried leaves around the base retains soil moisture.
ga: Mu tsei bibii lɛ baagboi yɛ be mli ni ajie amɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ sɛɛ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli dani adu amɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Dumɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli ni okɛ baai ni egbi awo shishigbɛ lɛ he koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Why do my plantain suckers take a very long time to start growing after planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ be babaoo dani mi dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛdaraa beni midu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers pause growth if weeds compete with them for water and soil nutrients near the surface. Clearing weeds in a wide circle around the base and mulching keeps the soil soft, moist, and ready for fast root growth.
ga: Plantain suckers lɛ baakpa shweremɔ kɛji jwɛi kɛ amɛ ye akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ lɛ. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ kooyigbɛ ni da ni bɔle he lɛ he. Base kɛ mulching baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee bɔdɔɔ, edɔ ni efee klalo kɛha shishifãi ni baa oya.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when extreme sun heat or dry soil stresses the plant, making it drop blossoms to conserve water. Watering regularly at the base and providing slight shade during midday heat keeps the flowers attached.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulu la ni fa babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi miigba tso lɛ naa. Ha egbee shi koni akɛto nu he. Okɛ nu afɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ daa ni oha hulutsoo be fioo yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni fɔfɔi lɛ ahi shi.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves. Spraying the undersides of the leaves with mild soapy water or neem oil clears the insects so new leaves can grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Ni akɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni akɛshwieɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Aloo neem fɔ lɛ baaye abua ni egbe kooloi bibii koni baai heei akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.
