english: Why do some of my oil palm fruits fall off the bunch easily while others stay stuck tight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm yibii lɛ ekomɛi jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ amɛbu lɛ mli oya shi ekrokomɛi hu hiɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ?

english: Oil palm fruits naturally loosen from the bunch as they reach full maturity and oil content. When fruits pull out easily, it means they are fully ripe, while tight fruits are still developing and need more time on the tree.
ga: Mu tso yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ kwraa ni mu yɛ mli. Kɛ́ aduawai lɛ je kpo mlɛo lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ ehoo kwraa yɛ be mli ni aduawai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ lolo ni ebiɔ be babaoo yɛ tso lɛ nɔ.

english: How should I pack my harvested palm fruits into sacks so they do not spoil on the way to the market?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mawo mi-palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ awo kotokui amli koni amɛkafite yɛ gbɛ ni yaa jara nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Pack the fruits tightly in breathable sacks and press them down firmly. This stops them from bouncing around and bruising during transport, which prevents rot and keeps the fruit fresh.
ga: Okɛ aduawai lɛ awo kotoku ko ni mumɔ baanyɛ ashɛ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni onyɛ shi jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaho amɛhe ni amɛkapila yɛ be mli ni akɛ amɛ majeɔ lɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaaa egbo, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ feɔ ehee.

english: Why do some small palm fruits inside the bunch remain small and hard to pull out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei yibii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ ji bibii lolo ni ewa akɛ abaajie kɛjɛ mli lɛ?

english: The small inner fruits often lack enough sunlight and space because the larger outer fruits block them. If the tree does not get enough water or nutrients, these inner fruits fail to swell properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ bɛ hulu la kɛ he ko ni sa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tso yibii lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã ni da lɛ baaha nɔ. Kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ Nɛkɛ mligbɛ yibii nɛɛ shwereŋ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to press down and firmly pack my harvested crops inside the bag before moving them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mamɔ mikpamɔ lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ ni mawo kotoku mli dani matsi kɛya he kroko lɛ?

english: Firmly pressing crops down removes loose air spaces inside the bag. This keeps the load stable on trucks or motorbikes and prevents the crops from rubbing against each other and damaging their skins.
ga: Kɛ́ onyɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ, ejieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotoku fɛɛ kotoku ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni jatsu ni yɔɔ lɔle loo okɔɔkpe nɔ lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ. ni etsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii anaa koni amɛkatswa amɛhe ni amɛkafite hewolo lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my oil palm bunch is ready for harvesting without cutting it down too early?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ ni akpaaa amɛ mra tsɔ?

english: A palm bunch is ready when its color turns deep orange-red and a few loose fruits start falling naturally to the ground around the base of the tree.
ga: Palm tsei lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ-tsuru ni mli kwɔ. Ni aduawai ni egbee shi lɛ ekomɛi baaje shishi amɛgbee shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What causes my harvested palm fruits to turn sour or produce bad oil if I leave them in bags for a few days?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-palm yibii ni mikpa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ejieɔ mu gbonyo kɛji mishi yɛ kotoku lɛ mli gbii fioo komɛi?

english: Once palm fruit is detached from the tree, enzymes quickly start breaking down the oil inside. If left packed in a warm bag for too long, this reaction increases acid levels, making the oil sour and low quality.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ mli yibii lɛ gbala kɛjɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, Enzymes lɛ baabɔi mu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mligbalamɔ oya. Kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ kotoku ni mli edɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Nɛkɛ nifeemɔ nɛɛ haa acid lɛ yaa hiɛ. Enɛ haa fɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiii kwraa.

english: Why do the outer fruits on an oil palm bunch ripen faster than the ones tucked inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ mu tsei akui lɛ asɛɛ lɛ shwereɔ oya fe nɔ ni akɛwo mli lɛ?

english: Outer fruits get direct exposure to sunlight and fresh air, which accelerates their ripening. The inner fruits stay shaded and covered, so they take a little longer to mature.
ga: Yibii lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ naa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni ekwɛ̃ oya. Yibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo mli ni ehaa nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, eheɔ be fioo dani eshɛɔ.

english: Is it better to pick loose palm fruits by hand from the bunch or harvest the whole bunch at once?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ niji baakpa ŋmei yibii kɛjɛ kui amli loo akpa kui muu lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kome mli?

english: It is best to harvest the whole bunch once a few loose fruits drop. Harvesting the entire bunch ensures all fruits are processed at peak freshness before pests or mold can reach them.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookpa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ beni aduawai fioo komɛi egbee shi lɛ. Kɛ́ akpa tso yibii lɛ fɛɛ lɛ, ehaa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ atsuɔ aduawai lɛ fɛɛ ahe nii koni amɛfee ehee jogbaŋŋ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai loo ŋmeii baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my freshly bagged palm fruits seem to lose weight after sitting in storage overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ palm yibii ni akɛwo mli ehee lɛ No hewɔ lɛ etamɔ nɔ ni minɔ lɛ egbɔjɔ beni mita nitoohe nyɔɔŋ kome sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Harvested fruits are alive and continuously lose water vapor into the air. This moisture loss causes them to shrink slightly and drop in weight overnight.
ga: Yibii ni akpa lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni ekɛ nu ni mli edɔ miiho kɛmiiya kɔɔyɔɔ mli be fɛɛ be. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi nɛɛ haa amɛhe shwieɔ shi fioo ni amɛhe shwieɔ shi nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Why do insects attack my harvested palm fruit inside the storage bags so quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miitutua mi-palm yibii ni akpa yɛ nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui amli lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Insects are attracted to the sweet smell of damaged or bruised fruit skin. If fruits are bruised during harvesting or packed loosely, pests can easily creep in and feed on them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai ahe tsɔi ni efite loo ekpɔtɔ lɛ ahe muji lɛ gbalaa kooloi. Kɛji akɛ aduawai lɛ egbo yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli loo akɛ amɛ ebɔ he mlɛo lɛ, ŋmeii baanyɛ abote mli ni amɛye nii oya.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves that act like living umbrellas, providing necessary shade and preserving soil moisture for the cocoa during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni okwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛha kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why is it important to lift and stake my yam vines off the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ ni mikɛma shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam plants need maximum sunlight on their leaves to produce food that swells the underground tubers. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground, preventing soil diseases and allowing better exposure to sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni baa lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Etsiɔ helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Yellowing starting from the tip and moving down the center of lower leaves indicates a nitrogen deficiency. Nitrogen is the essential nutrient that gives plants their green color and fuels leaf growth.
ga: Yellow ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii lɛ ashishigbɛ ni eyaa shi kɛyaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa baa lɛ daa.

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so root systems can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil concentrates the salts, which can scorch and burn the roots rather than feeding the plant.
ga: Ehe miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ koni etsɔ shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha ŋmei lɛ afee ekome. Enɛ baanyɛ ashã ni esha shishifãi lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha tso lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and dig into the dirt after blooming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfoɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts form their pods underground. After pollination, the flower produces a stem called a peg that pushes itself down into the soil so the nut can safely grow beneath the surface.
ga: Peanuts feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii. after pollination Fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni atsɛɔ amɛ pegs ni tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. To protect itself, the plant discards flowers to conserve water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. koni obu ohe he No sɛɛ lɛ Tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi ni yaa nɔ yɛ amɛdalɛ mli lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young maize leaves have ragged holes with caterpillar droppings in the center funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii yɛ amɛteŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. It crawls deep into the growing center of the plant to feed on tender new leaves before they unfold.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Efoɔ kɛboteɔ tso lɛ dalɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni eye baai heei dani amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Curled leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viruses transmitted by these pests as they suck the plant sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa beni amɛnuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my maize seeds rot in the ground when I plant immediately after the first light rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first light rain often does not wet the soil deeply enough. If hot dry weather returns immediately, the seeds get trapped in warm, damp dirt with insufficient water to germinate, leading to rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fioo lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli egbi ni edɔ lɛ, ekuɔ esɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Dumɔwui kpɛtɛɔ muji ni mli edɔ, ni mli ewo fɔ mli ni nu bɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃. kɛ fitemɔ baa

english: How can I tell if my cassava stems are mature enough to harvest underground tubers?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa ŋmeii lɛ?

english: As cassava matures, the lower leaves naturally yellow and drop off, leaving leaves mostly at the very top. You will also notice cracks in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers expand.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei kwɛ̃ lɛ Baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi. Baai lɛ ateŋ babaoo hiɔ shi yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ. Obaana ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli beni bulb lɛ mli lɛɛɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is even ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ po feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to stay green. When the plant doesn't find enough in the soil, it steals nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ tsei enaaa nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ejuɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many big leaves, but give me very small roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ehaa shishifãi bibii waa kɛji akpa?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from the soil or too much shade, the plant puts all its energy into growing leaves and branches above ground instead of sending food down to build heavy tubers underground.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ nine shɛɔ nitrogen babaoo nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ jɛmɛ. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai kɛ niji yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeetsu niyenii kɛba shi koni efee ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants dry up and fall off without producing any peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni pepper ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get too hot or stressed by dry soil. Extreme heat damages the pollen, so the plant drops the unpollinated flower to save its water and energy for survival.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baajie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji edɔ tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa lɛ fiteɔ pollen. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees drop their blossoms instead of forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they lack enough shade, water, or nutrients during hot periods. Tiny insects like mirids sucking on young stems can also cause the tree to drop its blossoms before pods develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛbɛ hulutsoo, nu loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kplukai bibii tamɔ mirids ni nuɔ tso lɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ agbo dani pods lɛ aba.

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects, or by severe heat and uneven watering, which causes the plant to curl its leaves to prevent water loss.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa kɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ shwieɔ baai lɛ anɔ koni nu akafite.

english: Why do I see ragged holes and brown dirt inside the center of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji ni etse kɛ muji ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf funnel of the maize plant during the day, eating the soft young leaves and leaving behind its waste.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ. Ye baai bibii lɛ ni oshi jwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers get soft and rot inside the soil before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Yam tubers rot underground when the soil stays too wet for long periods due to poor drainage. Excessive water starves the tubers of air and allows rotting fungi and bacteria to multiply.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ hewɔ. Nu babaoo baaha kɔɔyɔɔ yitsei lɛ aye hɔmɔ. ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ faa babaoo.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over when I plant many seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo lɛ? Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the young plants compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This makes them stretch upward too quickly, resulting in weak, skinny stalks that bend easily in the wind.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. ni haa ekpãa oya tsɔ Enɛ haa tso lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ tswaa oya.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts alongside my maize makes the soil better for crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ du ŋmãa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that have natural bacteria in their roots. These bacteria take nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil, acting like a natural fertilizer for neighbor crops like maize.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Nɛkɛ muawai nɛɛ heɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Can I mix dry wood ash with my harvested cowpea seeds to keep insects from eating them?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ tso mli sũ ni egbi lɛ afutu tsina ŋmei dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ koni kooloi akaye amɛ?

english: Yes, dry wood ash fills the small gaps between stored seeds and coats them. This prevents seed beetles from moving around, suffocates young insects, and stops adult beetles from laying eggs.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso sũ ni egbi lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ ayi obɔ. Dumɔwui ni ato kɛ nɔ ni awo nɔ lɛ ateŋ Enɛ baatsi dumɔwui ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafã kɛya he fɛɛ he. ni haa kooloi bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ kooloi bibii ni eda lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo wɔji.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants turning yellow and falling off early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi oya lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your plants are missing important soil nutrients like nitrogen, or they are stressed by drought or pests like green mites. Adding well-rotted manure or compost helps restore soil nutrients and keeps the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ bɛ sũ mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, loo hɔmɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ miihao lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba, ni ebaaye ebua ni ebaaha baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why are my pepper blossoms dropping off the stems before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ shishi dani ebatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, too little water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Ensuring steady watering during flowering and avoiding excessive chemical fertilizer helps the plant hold onto its flowers until peppers form.
ga: Fɔfɔi baagbee shi kɛji tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. nu fioo tsɔ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo Kɛ́ akwɛ koni afɔ lɛ nu be fɛɛ be yɛ fɔfɔii ashishijee mli, ni ajie tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli babaoo lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni emɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baafee.

english: What is causing small holes in my maize leaves and making the central stem wither?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai anɔ ni eha ŋmãa ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ agbo?

english: This is typically caused by fall armyworms or stem borer caterpillars that feed inside the young maize leaves and stems. Applying recommended pest controls early when the plants are small prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji cutworms loo stem borers ni egbee shi ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ahe baai kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra Kɛji tsei lɛ ji bibii lɛ enɛ tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why did the maize seeds I sowed last week fail to sprout out of the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu yɛ otsi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if the soil is too dry after planting, if they were buried too deep, or if ants and subterranean insects ate them before they could break through the surface.
ga: Dumɔwui kwɛ̃ŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ dumɔ sɛɛ. loo afu amɛ tsɔ Aloo kɛji ŋmeii kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ye amɛ dani dumɔwui lɛ nyɛ amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: What will happen to my plantain crops if I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi plantains lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: When crops are crowded, their roots and leaves fight over sunlight, water, and soil food. This leaves you with tall, weak stems and small, light bunches instead of heavy, healthy plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tso ni kɛlɛ ni egbɔjɔ kɛ niji bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ plantain ni tsii ni mli wa najiaŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa protects the seedlings from heat and keeps the ground moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛ latsaa he, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my plantain leaves curl up and droop during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ shwane be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing moisture from escaping into the hot air until the temperature cools down.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛha he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ amɛnɔ lɛ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekajo foi kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my planted crops right after the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu beni nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to the local environment, so their roots quickly absorb rainfall and soil nutrients before cultivated crops can establish themselves. Early weeding gives your crops a head start.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ gbalaa nugbɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya dani tso lɛ nyɛɔ edaa. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná sɛɛnamɔ

english: How can I tell if my soil is healthy enough to support a good crop yield without expensive tests?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai ni kaa ni jara wa bɛ mli?

english: Healthy farm soil is dark in color, crumbles easily in your hand, holds moisture well after rain, and contains earthworms or decaying plant matter, which show that the soil is rich in living nutrients.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kpakpa mli lɛ yɛ diŋŋ. Efoɔ yɛ nine mli oya Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsei ni fiteɔ nibii ni eshwɛ yɛ jɛmɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I trim off extra branches and leaves from my tomato bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji kɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tomato tso mli lɛ?

english: Trimming unproductive side shoots allows the plant to direct its energy, water, and nutrients into producing bigger, healthier fruits rather than wasting food on growing extra leaves.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni wooo yibii lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Instead of wasting food by growing excess leaves

english: Why do my crops grow better when I mix dried animal manure into the soil instead of doing nothing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbi futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ fe nɔ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts as natural food for the soil, slowly releasing essential nutrients like nitrogen that plants need to grow strong green leaves and big roots while keeping the soil moist.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni tsei taoɔ koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ shishifãi wuji lɛ fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why does burning dried grass and bush on my farm before planting make the soil weak after a few seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni egbi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ gbɔjɔɔ yɛ bei fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fire burns away the good topsoil and kills tiny living organisms that make the ground fertile. Letting grass rot naturally turns it into compost that keeps your land rich year after year.
ga: La shãa sũ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni efiteɔ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ. ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii Kɛ́ oha ojwɛi lɛ fite yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii afi fɛɛ afi.

english: How can I protect my tomato plants from insects without buying expensive chemical sprays from the store?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ahe ni miheee tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ shwapo mli?

english: You can crush neem leaves or mix mild soapy water to spray on leaves; these natural mixtures repel hungry bugs without destroying the soil or harming beneficial insects.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ neem baai lɛ atswa loo okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ ni mli edɔ afutu mli. Koni akɛshwie baai lɛ anɔ Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii nɛɛ shwieɔ kooloi ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ ni efiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ loo eyeee kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ awui.

english: Why do caterpillars suddenly show up and eat the leaves of my maize crop after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ trukaa lɛ, ŋmeii yeɔ mi-abɛi lɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Warm, rainy weather causes moth eggs hidden in the soil and leaves to hatch quickly into hungry caterpillars like fall armyworms, which feed on soft, growing maize leaves.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii akui ni akɛtee shikpɔŋ kɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ shwieɔ oya ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ, tamɔ fall armyworms. ni yeɔ ŋmãa baai bibii ni miida lɛ

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and dry up when the sun is very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that lose water easily under direct heat. They need temporary shade plants like plantains to act as umbrellas until their stems grow strong.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo la mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo kɛyashi be mli ni tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ baawa.

english: Why is it good to leave large shade trees standing inside my cocoa farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ mashi tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefo tsei lɛ fɛɛ

english: Big trees create a cool forest climate, keep the air humid, and protect soil from drying out, which helps cocoa trees live longer and produce pods for many years.
ga: Tsei wuji lɛ haa koo lɛ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ baa. Kwɛmɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekagbi Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii afii babaoo.

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil because oxygen cannot reach them. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my yam plants with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egboi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground, keeps the soil cool on dry days, and stops weeds from taking over your crop.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ anɔ. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye onibii anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers before any peppers actually grow on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ dani pepper lɛ kwɛ̃ diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, lack of water, or low soil nutrients, preventing fruits from forming.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hao amɛ. Enɛ haaa yibii lɛ afee.

english: Why do my plantain plants easily fall over when strong winds blow through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots and carry heavy stems. If tiny insects burrow into the underground root base, the roots weaken and cannot hold the plant up during heavy winds.
ga: Plantains shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ tsii. Kɛji kooloi bibii tsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishitoo lɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛmɔ tso lɛ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a sign that your crop lacks nitrogen. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed new growth at the top. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea early in the season will stop this from happening.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ onibii amli. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni enɛ akafee.

english: How do I apply fertilizer so that heavy rains do not wash it away from my farm?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afata he koni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akaŋɔ lɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after light rain, rather than during heavy downpours. Dig a small hole or shallow ring around the base of the plant, place the fertilizer inside, and cover it back with soil so rain cannot wash it off.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni okɛbaafata he yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, gbee bu bibioo ko loo ŋwɛi ŋta ni mli ekɔɔɔ he ebɔle tso lɛ shishi, ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ni okɛ sũ aha nɔ koni nugbɔ akafɔ lɛ.

english: Legume crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in their roots. When the plants die, that nitrogen stays in the soil, working like natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ eshishifãi amli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ sũ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa time to establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa kookoo bibii lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛfeɔ shishifãi ni wa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and shady conditions. Pruning excess shade tree branches lets sunlight and air flow through the farm, drying out dampness and preventing the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. dry the moisture and prevent fungus

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves but have tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ miiya hiɛ waa lɛ? Eyɛ baai eŋɔli ni mli tse shi shishifãi bibii yɛ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or leaves are heavily overgrown, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tops instead of tubers. Using balanced nutrients rich in potassium encourages the plant to grow bigger underground roots.
ga: Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo baai babaoo yɔɔ mli. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa tso lɛ yiteŋ moŋ fe ŋmei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ja ni potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tsei hewalɛ ni amɛná shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my tomato fruits split open on the plant just as they start turning red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato yibii lɛ tswaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ kɛ́ amɛje shishi amɛfee tɔrɔmɔɔ lɛ?

english: Fruit splitting happens when plants experience a sudden heavy watering after a long dry spell. The inside of the tomato grows faster than the skin can stretch, causing the outer skin to crack open.
ga: Yibii amli gbalamɔ baa kɛji akɛ aha tso lɛ nu babaoo trukaa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Tomato lɛ mli lɛ daa oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he. This causes the outer layer of skin to open.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids, or by a viral infection they spread. The insects suck juice from young leaves, causing them to twist, crumple, and stunt the plant's growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa. Insects suck juice from young leaves. Ekɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa baa.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops even after I have already applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds are stronger and faster at stealing nutrients, sunlight, and water than your crops are. If weeds are left on the farm, they will absorb the fertilizer first, leaving your crops weak and starved.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, hulu la, kɛ nu oya fe oŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Amɛbaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni hɔmɔ baaye bo.

english: Why are the central leaves of my young maize plants dying and turning brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ gboi ni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: This damage, often called 'deadheart', is usually caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch inside the stem and eat it from the inside out, blocking water and nutrients from reaching the top leaf shoot.
ga: Nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ ‘tsui gbele’ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, stem borers ni fɔɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ nii kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Enɛ haa nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii nyɛɛɛ ashɛ baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I plant my crops in a low-lying area on my farm that gets flooded during the rainy season?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni nu hoɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ mli?

english: Most crops cannot survive in standing water because their roots drown from a lack of oxygen. It is best to avoid flooded spots or build raised beds and drainage channels to carry excess water away.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ateŋ babaoo nyɛɛɛ ahi shi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsi ohe kɛjɛ hei ni nu afua baa lɛ loo ooofee saatsoi ni awo nɔ kɛ nu homɔ gbɛi koni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli.

english: How do I know if my farm soil has too much water for planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu babaoo tsɔ ni abaanyɛ adu?

english: If you squeeze a handful of soil and water freely drips out or forms a muddy lump, the land is too wet. Planting seeds in such soil often leads to seed rot before germination.
ga: Kɛji okɛ sũ fioo ko shwie shi ni nu lɛ hoɔ oya loo etsɔ sũ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tamɔ nɛkɛ nɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: What will happen to my crops if water sits around their stems for several days after heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nu hi tsei lɛ ahe gbii babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Prolonged standing water suffocates crop roots and encourages root rot and fungal diseases, causing leaves to turn yellow and plants to die.
ga: Nu ni ŋmɛɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni ehaa shishifãi ni fiteɔ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tso lɛ gboɔ.

english: Will heavy rain ruin my farm produce if the field takes a long time to drain?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baafite nibii ni anáa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmɔji lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani nu hoɔ?

english: Poor soil drainage forces roots to stay submerged, which stops them from absorbing essential nutrients and leads to stunted growth or total crop loss.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni ehiii lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ abote nu shishi. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ. ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afiteɔ kwraa baa.

english: Is it possible for me to grow crops on rocky ground or land with lots of stones?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei yɛ hei ni tɛi yɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tɛi babaoo yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Crops cannot grow directly on bare rock because roots need deep, soft soil to spread out, anchor the plant, and absorb water and nutrients.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ yɛ tɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ji akɛ, shishifãi taoɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã, amɛma tso lɛ shi, ni amɛgbala nu kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my crops struggle to grow in areas where the soil layer over solid rock is very shallow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tɛsaa ni wa lɛ nɔ lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Shallow soil holds very little moisture and nutrients, and it prevents plant roots from growing deep enough to keep the crop stable during strong winds or dry spells.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ. ni etsĩɔ tso shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ ahi shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa loo hɔmɔ bei amli.

english: How should I select the right piece of land on my farm for a new planting season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mahala shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be hee lɛ?

english: Choose land with deep, loose soil that drains water well, avoiding bare rock patches or low spots where water pools without draining.
ga: Halamɔ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kwɔ, ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tɛi ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Are there specific crop varieties I should buy if my farm soil stays wet for a long time?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mahe tso pɔtɛɛ ko kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ edɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Yes, plant breeders produce specific crop varieties that tolerate wet or swampy soil conditions better than standard varieties, helping prevent root diseases.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni kwɛɔ tsei anɔ lɛ feɔ tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni baanyɛ aŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛi amli jogbaŋŋ fe tsei srɔtoi ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ. ni yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ shishifã helai anaa

english: Why should I consult an extension officer about crop varieties before planting in a marshy area?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ extension officer lɛ agba tsei srɔtoi ahe sane dani madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Different varieties of the same crop react differently to water, and an extension officer can guide you toward specialized varieties that suit high-moisture conditions.
ga: Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome mli lɛ feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ nu he. Ni mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie tsei srɔtoi pɔtɛɛ ni sa kɛha shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ kpo.

english: Should I plant my entire land with a new crop right away or test a small plot first?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu shikpɔŋ muu lɛ fɛɛ ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo maka shikpɔŋ bibioo ko makwɛ klɛŋklɛŋ?

english: Testing a small plot first allows you to observe how the crop behaves in your farm's specific soil and moisture conditions without taking a large financial risk.
ga: Small plot test Klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ haa okwɛɔ bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii amɛhaa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ pɔtɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ shihilɛ mli. ni ekɛ shika he oshara kpele ko wooo mli

english: Why do my crops grow taller at the bottom of my farm's slope than at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miida babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ shishigbɛ ŋshɔkpɔi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes away loose topsoil and fertilizers from the hilltop down to the valley. The lower land collects this nutrient-rich mud and moisture, giving the crops down there extra food to grow faster and taller.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ gɔji lɛ anɔ kɛyaa jɔɔ lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ buaa muji kɛ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ naa. Ha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ niyenii krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara oya ni amɛdara.

english: Does rainwater flowing across my field carry plant food with it?
ga: Ani nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ kɛ tsei aniyenii yaa?

english: Yes, flowing rainwater dissolves and carries away valuable soil nutrients like nitrogen, as well as organic matter. While it deposits these nutrients in lower areas, it deprives the higher parts of your field of essential plant food.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ mli nibii ni jara wa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ yaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nɛkɛ niyenii mli nibii nɛɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ moŋ Shi efiteɔ tso niyenii nine ni he hiaa lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do unwanted weeds grow so thick and fast along the path where rainwater flows through my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ shwereɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ nu gbɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Flowing water carries weed seeds from other areas along with rich soil nutrients. When this water settles in small channels, it provides both the seeds and the food they need to sprout and spread quickly.
ga: Nu ni hoɔ lɛ woɔ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛjɛɔ hei krokomɛi kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii lɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ nu nɛɛ shwie shi yɛ hei bibii lɛ, ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã oya lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Can water flowing from a neighbor's farm bring bad weeds and diseases onto my land?
ga: Ani nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ akutsoŋnyo ko ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ekɛ jwɛi kɛ helai aba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, heavy rain runoff acts like a highway, carrying weed seeds, fungal spores, and plant diseases from upstream farms directly into your soil. Digging drainage trenches helps direct this dirty water away from your crops.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbɛjegbɛ wulu ko. Kɛtsɔ jwɛi dumɔwui ni akɛbaa Fungal spores kɛ tsei ahe helai ni jɛɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ Nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ nu mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsɔɔ nu fɔŋ nɛɛ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: If I apply fertilizer at the top of a hill, will the crops further down get some of it too?
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo gɔŋ lɛ nɔ Ani tsei ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hu baaná ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, heavy rain will dissolve the fertilizer and wash a portion of it downhill to lower crops. However, this means the crops at the top lose the food you gave them, so it is better to build soil mounds or ridges to hold the fertilizer in place.
ga: Hɛɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli ni efɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fã ko he kɛya gɔŋ lɛ shishi koni ekɛba ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ. Shi kɛlɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ baafite niyenii ni okɛha amɛ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ ooofee gɔŋji loo ŋmeii ni baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: Is water flowing from another farm safe to use for watering my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ kroko mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛbaatsu nii kɛha mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ mli nu?

english: While runoff water carries rich organic matter, it can also bring harmful agricultural chemicals, disease spores, and weed seeds from upstream. It is safer to collect the water in a settling pond before using it on delicate vegetables.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli moŋ, shi amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo okwaayeli mli tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ jwɛi dumɔwui kɛjɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ hu. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oookɛ nu lɛ ato nubu ko ni shwieɔ shi mli dani okɛtsu nii yɛ aduawai ni yɔɔ mlɛo nɔ.

english: Why do crops planted right inside a water drainage path fail to grow well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu yɛ nu homɔ gbɛi anɔ lɛ ekwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Even though the water carries rich food, constant strong water flow washes soil away from roots and suffocates them by removing air from the soil. Crops need moist, steady soil rather than direct, moving water currents.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nu lɛ yɛ niyenii babaoo moŋ, Shi nu ni hoɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ hoɔ sũ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaa amɛmli shwieɔ shi kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Tsei sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ, ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ moŋ fe nu ni hoɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: How far away from a stream or water channel should I plant my crops?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛjɛ faa loo nu gbɛ ko he kɛya he ko tɛŋŋ?

english: Planting a short distance away from moving water allows crop roots to spread out and drink underground moisture comfortably without risking root rot or being washed away during heavy rainstorms.
ga: Dumɔ yɛ gbɛ kuku nɔ Kɛjɛ nu jɛɛhei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔ shishifãi ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa ni amɛnuɔ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ jogbaŋŋ. ni oshara ko bɛ he akɛ shishifãi lɛ baafite loo nu baaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crop roots grow sideways toward water channels instead of straight down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa afã kɛyaa nu gbɛ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Roots naturally search for the easiest source of food and moisture. If nutrients and water are moving through a nearby surface channel, the roots will stretch horizontally toward that rich water source.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, shishifãi taoɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ jɛɛhe ni yɔɔ mlɛo fe fɛɛ. Kɛji niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ nu tsɔ ŋwɛi gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ kɛyaa nu jɛɛhei ni fa babaoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do crops turning yellow in low areas where rainwater gathers, even though there is plenty of food in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei ni nugbɔ nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: When water sits still in one spot for too long, it drowns the roots by blocking oxygen. Even if the water is full of nutrients, a plant cannot drink or feed if its roots are suffocating under standing water.
ga: Beni nu lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ he kome be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Nu baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shishi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ tsiɔ naa lɛ hewɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu mli eyi kɛ niyenii kpakpai moŋ, shi Tsei nyɛŋ anu nu loo amɛye nii kɛkɛ kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ shwie shi yɛ nu ni yɔɔ dioo shishi.

english: Why do my yam vines die off completely during the dry season even when the tuber inside the ground is still alive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboiɔ kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ ŋmeii lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo po?

english: Yam plants naturally dry up above the ground when the dry weather arrives to conserve water. The tuber underground stays alive in a sleeping state, using stored nutrients to survive until the next rainy season brings new shoots.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi ba koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛ ko ni mli wa mli, ni amɛkɛ niyenii ni ato lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛhi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli beni tsei heei jeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why do I need to build big soil mounds to plant my yams instead of just digging small holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo ko ni akɛduɔ sweet potatoes yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsa bu bibioo ko?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose, and deep soil to expand easily into large shapes. Big mounds give the underground tuber plenty of room to grow while protecting it from standing water that causes rotting.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ ahe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni mli tse, ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo ni amɛfee agboi. Gɔŋ agbo lɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ náa hegbɛ babaoo ni amɛdaraa. kɛ agbɛnɛ hu, ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni ekã shi ni kɛ fitemɔ baa lɛ he.

english: How can I prevent my harvested yams from growing green shoots while sitting in my storage barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli beni mita mi-shĩa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yams naturally start to sprout after a period of rest. To slow this down, store them off the ground in a cool, dark, well-ventilated shade, and carefully snap off any small buds as soon as they appear.
ga: Sweet potatoes baaje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji amɛjɔɔ amɛhe be fioo sɛɛ. Bɔni afee ni enɛ asɛɛ afo lɛ Ha amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ mli ni ofo ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli blɛoo. Je kpo kɛji ejie ehe kpo pɛ

english: If the early rains start briefly in March, should I plant my crop seeds immediately?
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ be kukuoo ko yɛ march mli Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Early rains can often stop suddenly for weeks, leaving seeds to dry up and die in hot soil. It is safer to wait until the rain becomes regular and moistens the soil deeply over several consecutive days before planting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ kpaɔ trukaa otsii babaoo. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ be fɛɛ be ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa gbii babaoo ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani oduɔ nii.

english: Why are the bottom leaves on my young maize plants turning yellow in a V-shape?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the tip in a V-pattern show that your soil is low on nitrogen. Feeding your crop with nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure restores the green color and helps cobs fill out properly.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi efeɔ V yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmei loo kooloi ŋmei ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha amɛhe afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ŋmei lɛ ahi he ni sa.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts before maize makes my maize yield higher?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ko kɛɛ mi akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei dani miwo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei ni miwoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts belong to the legume family, which takes nitrogen gas from the air and fixes it into the soil. When you plant maize in that same soil afterward, the maize feeds on that leftover plant food and grows stronger.
ga: Peanuts fata legume weku lɛ he, ni ejieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ yɛ ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ŋmãa lɛ baaye tso niyenii ni eshwɛ lɛ ni ebaada waa.

english: What causes small, ragged holes in my young maize leaves that look like they were chewed overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni kɛ buji bibii ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baa lɛ mli ni tamɔ nɔ ni ashɛre amɛ nyɔɔŋ kome lɛ baa?

english: This damage is usually caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms. They hide inside the central funnel of the plant during the day and eat soft leaves before they unroll.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the daytime weather gets too hot, when watering is inconsistent, or when there are no beneficial insects around to shake and pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛji kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ bɛ he ni amɛbaakpokpo ni amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why does my harvested cassava turn dark blue and rot within just a few days of digging it up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava ni mikpa lɛ batsɔ bluu ni mli edɔ ni egbo yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli beni atsa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Unlike yams, cassava roots do not have a protective outer skin to keep air out. Once exposed to oxygen, rapid chemical reactions start inside the root, so cassava must be eaten, sold, or processed right after harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni tamɔɔɔ sweet potato lɛ, cassava shishifãi bɛ kponɔgbɛ hewolo ni buɔ mɔ he koni kɔɔyɔɔ akabote mli. Kɛji akɛ oxygen bote mli lɛ Tsofafeemɔ ko ni yaa oya jeɔ shishi yɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ aye, ahɔ̃ɔ, loo atsu he nii kɛji akpa ŋmei lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantain suckers next to my new cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛkuu nɔkwɛlɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo dumɔwui heei ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under harsh direct sunlight. Plantain plants grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity needed for young cocoa roots to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni he hiaa koni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are extremely sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight, which scorches their leaves and dries out their roots. Planting them near shade crops like plantain or temporary shade trees provides the living canopy they need to survive and build strong roots during their first couple of years.
ga: Kookoo dumɔwui bibii nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Enɛ baashã baai lɛ ni eha shishifãi lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaha ená ŋwɛi ŋta ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi ni ená shishifãi ni wa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves in maize are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is essential for green leaf growth, so when the soil lacks it, the plant moves whatever nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves to feed the growing upper leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he hiaa waa kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ Tsei lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fɛɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ koni ekɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: What is causing small ragged holes in my young maize leaves with powdery dirt inside the leaves?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? yɛ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli ni muji ni tamɔ powder yɛ baai lɛ amli

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm, a destructive caterpillar that hides inside the central shoot (funnel) of the maize plant to feed. Detecting them early allows you to control them using recommended bio-pesticides or approved chemicals before they destroy the crop's center.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa titri ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmãa (cone) mli koni eye niyenii. mra be mli ni anaa Ehaa okɛ tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛnɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋgbɛ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids, thrips, or mites, or a virus transmitted by whiteflies. Applying neem oil spray or appropriate insecticide early helps eliminate these insects and prevents further distortion of plant leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, thrips, loo mites, loo helai ni whiteflies gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Neem fɔ ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra ni sa. Ebaaye ebua ni ajie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ebaatsi tsei ahe baai lɛ ni efite lɛ anaa.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crops very close to each other in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Planting crops too close together forces them to compete intensely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with tall, weak stems and very low yields instead of healthy, food-producing plants.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ waa kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii. Enɛ haa onáa tsei ni kɛlɛ, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni yibiiwoo ni baa shi waa, moŋ fe tso ni woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa.

english: Why do I need to put wooden stakes next to my yam plants after they sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tso ko fɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ tso ko masɛi beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need support so their leaves can spread out properly to catch sunlight and make food. Keeping the vines off the wet ground also protects leaves from fungal diseases, leading to larger tuber growth.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛfee niyenii. Wein tsei ni akɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni da.

english: This condition is called Blossom End Rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the developing fruit, usually triggered by irregular watering. Ensuring steady moisture in the soil helps the plant continuously draw calcium from the soil into the growing tomatoes.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ Blossom End Rot, ni calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛjieɔ calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa tomato ni miida lɛ mli be fɛɛ be.

english: Why should I avoid growing maize on the exact same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be mli lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and causes crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts restores nitrogen to the soil and disrupts pest life cycles.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni efoɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛ mli

english: Weeds are wild, tough native plants adapted to quickly absorb available water and soil nutrients faster than cultivated farm crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get the food and moisture they need to establish strong roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ. Amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛŋɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei lɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa.

english: How can I tell that my cassava roots are fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months after planting, marked by the lower leaves turning yellow and falling off and noticeable cracking in the soil around the plant stem caused by expanding tubers beneath.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛbaagbee shi. ni ŋmeii ni anaa faŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Akɛ yitso ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ mlilɛɛmɔ lɛ feɔ tso lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade trees or plantains around them to block the harsh heat, the leaves get sunburned and dry out.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulutsoo be lɛ bɛ he ni baatsi la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, hulu lɛ baashã baai lɛ ni amɛbaagbi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which is the food plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding manure or the right fertilizer gives the crop back its energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: What is making the leaves of my cassava plants curl up and show light yellow spots?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse?

english: This is caused by cassava mosaic disease, which is spread by tiny flying insects called whiteflies. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela, ni koolooi bibii ni fɔ̃ɔ ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ tsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and thin with small cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa bibii ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving them proper space lets every plant grow strong and produce large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni sa ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso fɛɛ tso ni edaraa waa ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato plants rot and die at the roots when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Too much water sitting around tomato roots chokes them so they cannot breathe, leading to fungal diseases. Planting on raised soil mounds or ridges lets extra water drain away safely.
ga: Nu babaoo ni bɔleɔ tomato shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa amɛmuɔ. kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How do weeds slow down the growth of my pepper crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi haaa mi-pepper tsei lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ?

english: Weeds act like thieves on your farm—they drink the water and steal the soil nutrients intended for your pepper plants, leaving your crops weak and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛhaa o-pepper tsei lɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagbɔjɔ.

english: If I save seeds from my harvested maize to plant next season, why do I get a smaller yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpaa lɛ mli lɛ to koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, Mɛni hewɔ miwooo yibii babaoo lɛ?

english: Many modern seed varieties are bred for one great harvest. The seeds saved from that harvest lose their strength, resulting in weaker plants and smaller yields compared to fresh certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui srɔtoi babaoo kɛha kpamɔ kome ni hi jogbaŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do officers recommend planting cowpeas or beans together with my cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ onukpai lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ adu tsina loo ŋmeii ni akɛ ŋmeii fata he lɛ?

english: Beans and cowpeas feed the soil by taking nitrogen from the air and trapping it in their roots. When grown alongside cassava, they enrich the soil and help both crops yield better.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ tsinabii haa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii kɛtsɔ nitrogen ni amɛjieɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ akɛ ŋmeii fata he lɛ Amɛbaahã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tsei enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: How do small insects get inside my stored dried maize and turn it into powder?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko bote ŋmãa ni egbi ni mikɛto lɛ mli ni etsɔ powda?

english: Weevils lay tiny eggs on maize while it is drying, or enter through gaps in storage bags. Drying your maize thoroughly and using airtight storage bags smothers insects and stops them from multiplying.
ga: Kpɔŋɔ lɛ woɔ wɔji bibii. yɛ ŋmãa lɛ nɔ be mli ni egbiɔ loo kɛyaa he ni yɔɔ kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ vacuum storage bags tsu nii lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ ni ebaatsi amɛnaa koni amɛkafa babaoo.

english: Why do people cover the ground around young crops with dry grass and leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi kɛ baai ni egbi haa he ni tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: This is called mulching. Dry grass acts as a blanket that stops the sun from drying out the soil quickly, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching. Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni tsiɔ hulu lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: How deep into the soil am I supposed to plant my crop seeds so they can grow properly?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu midumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Planting seeds too deep prevents them from reaching the surface before running out of stored energy, while planting them too shallow leaves them dry or vulnerable to birds. A general rule is to plant a seed at a depth equal to two or three times its width.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛto lɛ aba naagbee. yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ baaha amɛgbi loo ebaafee oshara kɛha okpoi. Mla ni afɔɔ namɔ ji ni adu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ ni ekɛ elɛɛmɔ lɛ toi enyɔ loo etɛ yeɔ egbɔ.

english: Why are my seeds struggling to break through the ground after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of moisture, warmth, and loose soil to sprout. If the soil surface is hard and packed down, or if the seed was pushed down too deep, the fragile seedling cannot push through and may rot underground.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ fɛ̃i, dɔlɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wa ni ebɔle ehe loo kɛji akɛ ashɛre dumɔwui lɛ kɛtee shɔŋŋ tsɔ Dumɔwui ni waaa lɛ nyɛŋ atsɔ mli ni ebaanyɛ egbo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Can I successfully grow crops inside fertilizer bags or rice sacks instead of planting directly in the ground?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsei yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmãa kotokui amli moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yes, growing crops in bags works well for many crops like vegetables, especially where land is limited or soil is poor. However, you must poke drainage holes at the bottom of the bags and fill them with rich topsoil so water doesn't collect and rot the roots.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa tsei babaoo, tamɔ aduawai, titri lɛ yɛ hei ni he ko bɛ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii lɛ. Shi kɛlɛ, esa akɛ ogbala nu ni hoɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ shishi lɛ mli ni okɛ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni jara wa afata he koni nu akabua ehe naa ni ekafite shishifãi lɛ.

english: How often do I need to water my crops if I am growing them in sacks or bags?
ga: Shii enyiɛ ehe baahia ni mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nu kɛji akɛ adu yɛ kotokui loo kotokui amli?

english: Crops in bags dry out much faster than crops in the ground because the sun heats the sides of the bag. You should check the soil daily and water early in the morning or late evening whenever the top layer feels dry.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ejaakɛ hulu la lɛ haa kotoku lɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ mli dɔɔ. Esa akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa gbi ni okɛ nu awo mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ be fɛɛ be ni ŋwɛi fã lɛ baanu he akɛ egbi.

english: Is pure sandy soil good for growing my crops?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ hi kɛha mi tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ?

english: Pure sandy soil holds very little water and plant nutrients, causing crops to dry out quickly and grow weakly. Mixing sand with dark topsoil and decomposed manure creates a better mix that holds moisture while staying loose.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni he tse lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛ tsei amli niyenii fioo ko pɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbiɔ oya ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔɔ jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋã futu shikpɔŋ nɔ sũ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmei ni egbo lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa ŋã ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni ehiɔ shi mlɛo lɛ baa.

english: Does black or dark soil automatically mean my land is good for planting without adding anything else?
ga: Ani shikpɔŋ diŋ loo ediŋŋ tsɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛ nɔ kroko fataaa he?

english: Dark soil usually has good organic material, but color alone does not guarantee high yields. Soil can be dark but still lack important nutrients or be too acidic, so adding organic manure or fertilizer is often still necessary for healthy crop growth.
ga: Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ediŋŋ lɛ fɔɔ nibii kpakpai ni wala yɔɔ mli. Shi kɔla pɛ haaa yibii babaoo aba. Shikpɔŋ lɛ baanyɛ afee ediŋŋ shi niyenii ni he hiaa bɛ mli loo eyɛ acid tsɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ he miihia lolo koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Should I loosen hard ground before I put my seeds inside?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli dani mikɛ dumɔwui afata he?

english: Yes, breaking up hard ground makes it easy for young root tips to spread quickly and collect food and water. Loose soil also absorbs rainwater easily instead of letting it run off and wash your seeds away.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akumɔ lɛ haa shishifãi bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛbuaa niyenii kɛ nu naa oya. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ hu shwieɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mlɛo. Mohu ɔ, ha nɛ nu nɛ e ho nɛ e kɛ fɔ duwu ɔmɛ.

english: What causes my young crops to fall over easily in the wind, and how can I help them stand firmly?
ga: Mɛni haa mi dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli? Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ maye mabua lɛ ni eŋmɛ etsui shi?

english: Crops fall over when their roots are shallow or the surrounding soil is too soft. Plant your seeds at the correct depth and heap extra soil gently around the stem base as the plant grows to give the roots a firm anchor.
ga: Tsei shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ejɔ tsɔ. Dumɔ dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ni sa ni okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ato he fioo. Ebɔle tso lɛ shishigbɛ he beni tso lɛ daa lɛ koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: How do I choose the right seed variety to plant when I buy from the agricultural market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala dumɔwui srɔtoi ni sa ni madu kɛji mihe nii yɛ okwaafoi ajarayelihe lɛ?

english: Look for certified seed varieties recommended for your region's weather and soil conditions. Certified seeds are tested to resist local pests and diseases better, giving you higher yields than unverified grain bought from open food markets.
ga: Taomɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni ajieɔ yi yɛ okpokpaa lɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ amli koni ana kɛji amɛbaanyɛ amɛshi maŋ lɛ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai. Enɛ haa anáa yibii babaoo fe ŋmaa ni akwɛɛɛ mli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ niyenii ajarayelihe ni agbele naa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it harmful if I put too many seeds together in one small hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu bibioo kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole causes the seedlings to fight each other for light, water, and soil food. This makes all of them grow thin and weak; spacing them properly ensures each plant grows strong and produces good yield.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ wuɔ yɛ la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii he. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛhe waaa. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso daa waa ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa plants turning yellow and scorching under full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu lɛ tso waa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily in direct sun. They need shade crops like plantains or shade trees above them during their first few years to protect them until they grow strong enough to withstand direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni yɔɔ amɛyiteŋ lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tightly like straws during the hot dry afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ tamɔ jwɛi yɛ shwane ni edɔ ni edɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves to protect themselves from extreme heat. By rolling up, the leaf exposes less surface area to the hot air, which helps the plant reduce water loss and survive dry conditions.
ga: Abele tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. kɛji akɛ abɔle ehe Baai lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ baa shi ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: Why am I getting very bushy cassava plants with huge leaves but tiny tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miyɛ jwɛi agbo ko ni ŋmei baai yɔɔ mli shi ŋmei bibii yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall leaves and branches above ground instead of sending food down to build thick tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai kɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛya shi koni amɛma ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering or dry spells while the fruit is forming.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo egbiɔ yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miikwɛ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines off the ground with stakes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Lifting yam vines on stakes allows all the leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight powers leaf growth, which creates the energy needed to feed and swell the tuber beneath the soil.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ fɛɛ naa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ. Hulu la haa hewalɛ kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni akɛye shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni amɛfuu lɛ baa.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and weak with small cobs when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ egbɔjɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Akɛni midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ hewɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, causing them to stretch tall for light without having enough food to produce strong stems or large cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛná la ni niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii ni wa loo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting groundnuts in my farm make the maize I plant afterwards grow much stronger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ daa waa lɛ?

english: Groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When the plant roots decay in the soil, they leave behind natural fertilizer that feeds the next crop.
ga: Peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ tso shishifãi fite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛha tso ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to turn pale yellow and stop growing so fast?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ oya ni amɛmiikpa shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds have fast-growing root systems that steal water and fertilizers from the soil before your crops can reach them, leaving your plants starving for nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baashɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye otsei lɛ yɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off the plant without turning into peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni etsɔɔɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely hot, pepper plants become stressed and drop their flowers to save water and energy rather than trying to support growing fruit.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oye obua aduawai akwɛ̃mɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after heavy rains and light winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that sit close to the top of the soil. When heavy rain thoroughly soaks the ground, the soil becomes loose, and the roots lose their anchor, causing the heavy plant to fall over.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli fũu lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛma shi. ni haa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi

english: What kind of land or soil do I need if I want to start growing rice?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ loo sũ he hiaa mi kɛji miitao mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Rice grows best in low-lying wet soils or swampy areas that hold water well, though upland varieties can also grow in fertile soils that get regular rainfall.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo hei ni nu yɔɔ ni nu hiɛɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Gɔŋ nɔ tsei srɔtoi po baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni baa nii ni nugbɔ nɛɔ daa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does rice require so much water compared to crops like maize or cassava?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in shallow water or very moist soil because the water helps suppress weeds, keeps the plant cool, and makes soil nutrients easier for the roots to absorb.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe yɛ nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni hulutsoo babaoo yɔɔ nɔ. Ejaakɛ nu yeɔ ebuaa ni ekpaa jwɛi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ mlɛo

english: Why are my rice plants producing empty heads with no seeds inside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ woɔ yitsei ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ mli lɛ?
