english: Empty rice grains usually happen if the plant suffers from lack of water during flowering, poor soil nutrients, extreme heat, or damage from pests and diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko baa kɛji nu bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nibii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai fiteɔ

english: How can I tell if my crops are hungry and need fertilizer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hɔmɔ miiye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni ehe miihia ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: When crops lack nutrients, their leaves often turn light green or yellow instead of dark green, their growth slows down, and their stems stay short and weak.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ, bei pii lɛ, ebaai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ. shweremɔ blɛoo ni tso lɛ baafee kuku ni egbɔjɔ

english: Can I use animal waste like grasscutter droppings as fertilizer for my crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii afolɔ jwɛi. Ani ebaanyɛ efee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yes, dried manure from animals like grasscutters adds valuable organic matter and natural nutrients to the soil, helping it hold water better and feeding crops over time.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni egbi ni jɛɔ kooloi tamɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfoɔ jwɛi lɛ amli lɛ kɛ nibii ni jara wa ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. ni amɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: When is the right time to feed my crops with fertilizer after planting?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha tsei beni adu amɛ sɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is usually applied in two main stages: a small amount when planting to help roots grow, and a second portion when the crops are growing fast or getting ready to produce grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛi titrii enyɔ nɔ: fioo ko yɛ dumɔ mli koni eye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara; ni nɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ ji be mli ni tso lɛ miida oya loo eesaa ehe koni ewo dumɔwui.

english: Why are the leaves on my young crops curling up during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up on hot afternoons to protect themselves and reduce water loss when the hot sun dries the plant faster than the roots can drink water from the soil.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe he ni amɛha nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi beni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa tso lɛ gĩɔ oya tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ anu nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my crop seeds too close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin, weak plants with low harvest yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ, ni amɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my crop harvests keep getting smaller every year on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpaa lɛ faaa daa afi yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ?

english: Growing crops on the exact same land repeatedly drains essential nutrients from the soil; the land needs organic fertilizer, crop rotation, or rest to rebuild its fertility.
ga: Tsei ni akwɛɔ yɛ he kome lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ loo hejɔɔmɔ koni akɛfee babaoo hee

english: Why should I adopt new planting methods instead of sticking to my traditional way of farming?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ gbɛi heei ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ nii lɛ atsu nii moŋ fe blema okwaayeli lɛ?

english: Modern farming methods teach proper spacing, correct fertilizer use, and better field management, which help you produce a much bigger harvest from the same size of land.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ okwaayeli gbɛi tsɔɔ gbɛ ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ okwaayeli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ nɔkwɛmɔ kpakpa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nibii babaoo kɛjɛɔ he ni dalɛ tamɔ nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow while the plant is still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ be mli ni tsei lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant nutrient. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn deep green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni tsuɔ nii waa.

english: How can my cassava plants stay alive during the dry Harmattan season without watering?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni mi-cassava tsei lɛ ahi shi yɛ harmattan be ni mli egbi lɛ mli ni awooo amɛ nu?

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during long dry spells to save water and stores its energy safely in the underground tubers. Once the rains return, it uses that stored energy to grow new leaves quickly.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli shweshweeshwe. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, ekɛ hewalɛ ni eto lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ baai heei oya.

english: What causes small holes and sawdust-like dirt inside the central leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmei ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the leaf funnel of maize plants. Applying recommended biopesticides or neem extract early in the morning targets them before they ruin the harvest.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ahe baai amli lɛ. Tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛtsu nii leebi lɛ baatutua amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do I need to heap soil into mounds or ridges before planting my yam or sweet potatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabua sũ naa yɛ gɔji loo ŋmeii amli dani madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii?

english: Root crops need soft, loose soil so their tubers can expand easily into large sizes. Mounds and ridges also prevent heavy rain from pooling around the roots and causing the young tubers to rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse he miihia tsei ni shishifãi yɔɔ mli lɛ bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛyashɛ agboi amli oya. Gɔji kɛ ŋmeii hu tsiɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekabɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe ni efite ŋmeii bibii lɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning brown and black during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ediŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Pruning excess branches lets sunlight and air into the farm, drying out the moisture and stopping the fungus from spreading.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Gbɔmɔtso ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo shihilɛi amli kɛbaa. Niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni afolɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ mli egbiɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high or when the soil goes from extremely dry to very wet. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps the plants hold onto flowers until tomatoes form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni edɔ waa nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tomatoi lɛ feɔ.

english: How does planting cover crops like leguminous beans help control weeds on my farm?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Cover crops grow fast and spread thick leaves across the ground, blocking sunlight from reaching weed seeds. This smothers weeds naturally while also putting nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tsei ni haa shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ daa oya ni amɛgbɛɔ baai ni mli tse amɛshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsi hulu lɛ naa koni ekashɛ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Enɛ gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be mli ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why will planting my maize seeds too close together reduce my final yield?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he kome tsɔ lɛ haa minaagbee yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: When crops are overcrowded, they compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough food and light to grow sturdy stems and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ ŋmɔshi nibii eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ yɛ amɛteŋ. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ tsei ni wa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking sap from underneath the leaves. Spraying neem leaf water or insecticidal soap controls these pests and lets healthy leaves grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaakudɔ kooloi nɛɛ ni eye ebua baa heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow strong and stay green. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer will help your maize regain its green color.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara waa ni amɛhi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my field produce smaller harvests if I plant maize in the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize pulls specific nutrients out of the dirt every season. Planting it in the same plot repeatedly drains the soil of those nutrients. Rotating your field with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts naturally puts nutrients back into the soil.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be. Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ dumɔwui haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ shii abɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake oŋmɔji lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot in the ground when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rains flood flat soil without good drainage, water fills all the air spaces, causing the tubers to suffocate and decay. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps extra water drain away.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nu kpakpa hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Nu lɛ baayi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui lɛ fɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a hot dry spell that can dry out young seeds before their roots settle. Waiting until the rains become steady ensures the soil stays moist enough for your seeds to grow and survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni mli edɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that support heavy fruit bunches, making them top-heavy. Insects like stem borers can also weaken the base. Supporting your plants with bamboo poles and keeping the base free of pests helps them stand firm.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni fiɔ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo. Kplukai tamɔ trunk borers. Ebaanyɛ eha shishitoo lɛ hu agbɔjɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei tsei fi otso lɛ sɛɛ ni oha shishitoo lɛ akafee nɔ ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni edamɔ shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines off the ground using sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei atsu nii ni mikɛdu sweet potato wain tsei kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking keeps the leaves high in the sun and off the damp ground where diseases can attack them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni eshɛ tsei lɛ ahe koni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni miida lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ shɛɔ hulutsoo be mli ni ejɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni helai baanyɛ aba lɛ. baanyɛ atutua

english: Curling yellow leaves on tomato plants are usually caused by a disease spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. Removing infected plants early and managing whiteflies helps keep the disease from spreading to the rest of your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ mra Ni akwɛɔ ŋmeii yɛji anɔ lɛ baaye abua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli hei krokomɛi.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their flowers before growing cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani adu kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from heat stress, lack of moisture, or insect attacks. Keeping tall shade trees around your cocoa and protecting the farm from dry winds helps the tree hold onto its flowers so pods can develop.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli haomɔ ba amɛnɔ. Fɛ̃i ni bɛ loo kooloi ni shwieɔ amɛ lɛ ni akɛ hulutsoo baaha kɛjɛ tsei kakadaji ni bɔle Cocoa he lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he ni abuɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he lɛ baaye abua tsei lɛ ni amɛmɔmɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ adara.

english: Why do my pepper plants look healthy but keep dropping their blossoms without giving me peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ shi no sɛɛ lɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ekɛ pepper ko kwraa baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper blossoms drop off when temperatures get too high or when the soil gets too dry during hot afternoon weather. Giving your plants light shade and watering them during dry spells helps the flowers turn into peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei lɛ wo hulutsoo be mli ni aha amɛ nu yɛ fɛ̃i be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why should I plant groundnuts or beans in between my main crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans are special plants that take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. Planting them alongside your main crops improves soil quality and acts like a natural fertilizer for the whole farm.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ odu nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaatsu nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle strong sunlight and harsh dry weather directly. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava planted near them to protect them from heat and keep the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa waa lɛ ahe gbɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants stop growing and drop their flowers when the weather gets too hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni ekɛ fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Extreme heat causes pepper plants to conserve water by shedding their flowers and leaves. Providing light shade or mulching around the base keeps the roots cool and helps them retain blossoms.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa pepper tsei lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛtsɔ amɛbaai kɛ fɔfɔi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ. Shading loo mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ akafitemɔ.

english: Why are small green worms chewing holes through the hearts of my young maize stalks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei bibioo ko ni ji eŋɔli lɛ tsɔ mibi lɛ ŋmei tso lɛ tsui mli lɛ?

english: These are fall armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets young maize leaves. Spraying early with recommended organic or chemical pest controls directly into the funnel of the plant protects your harvest.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji fall asraafoi. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa baai bibii anɔ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ mra Kɛtsɔ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ anɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebuɔ onibii ahe.

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn pale yellow and curl up into strange shapes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies that suck plant juices. Planting disease-resistant stem varieties from agriculture officers prevents this disease.
ga: Kasava mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Whiteflies bibii ni nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Okwaayeli nitsulɔi ni duɔ tsei srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are my maize stalks thin and pale yellow even though we get plenty of rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain gives plants water, but plants also need nutrients from the soil like nitrogen to stay dark green and strong. Adding compost, animal manure, or fertilizer gives the soil the nutrients your crop needs.
ga: Nugbɔ haa tsei nu. Shi tsei hu taoɔ niyenii ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting cowpeas or groundnuts makes the land better for next year's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu tsina loo ŋmei lɛ, ehaa afi ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen gas from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. When the plant dies, that nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ niyenii.

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun and keeps them off the hot, wet ground where rot and diseases spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ ni ehaaa jɛmɛ adɔ ni edɔ, he ni ŋmeii kɛ helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã lɛ.

english: Why should I cut down the extra young shoots sprouting around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Too many shoots around one stem steal food and water from the main mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main stem grows large, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Tso lɛ tsei babaoo tsɔ baaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ adara ni etsɔ plantains akuu agbo ko ni tsii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers drop to the ground without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off if the soil gets too dry, if temperatures get too high, or if the soil lacks nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist around the base helps flowers turn into healthy fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ Konu lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Is it better to pour water directly over cabbage leaves or water only the dirt around the roots?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooofɔse nu yɛ kaabii baai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ loo oooshwie shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ pɛ nɔ nu?

english: It is best to water the soil at the base of the plant. Pouring water over cabbage leaves in hot weather can trap moisture between the leaves, encouraging soft rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ nu. Kɛ́ afɔ nu awo kaabe baai anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ emɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai aba.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your soil is low on nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green leaves. Adding manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai eŋɔlii Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my farm producing fewer bags of corn every year even though I plant on the same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa kotokui fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop on the same land every season drains the exact same nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover. Rotating your crops with beans or groundnuts helps put nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe. Nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I clear all the shade trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ beni mijieɔ cacao tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to heat and direct sunlight, which causes their leaves to burn and dry out. They need living shade, such as plantains or leguminous trees, to shelter them during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka, tamɔ dumɔwui loo ŋmãa. Koni akɛ wɔɔhe aha klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ

english: Why do my yam tubers turn out small and rotten when planted in heavy, waterlogged soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛgboɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams need loose, well-draining soil so their underground roots can breathe and expand easily. Soil that holds too much water cuts off oxygen to the roots and causes rot-causing fungi to thrive.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ. Bɔni afee ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anyɛ amu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo. Nu ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ daa.

english: Why does my cassava crop manage to stay alive even when it does not rain for months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛko nyɔji babaoo moŋ?

english: Cassava is built for dry weather; it stores moisture and nutrients in its deep underground roots and can drop its leaves to reduce water loss until the rains return.
ga: Abɔ cassava kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli egbi. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ baai ashwie shi koni nu ni fiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛyashi nugbɔ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upwards during hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in strong heat to expose less surface area to the hot sun, which helps the plant save water and stay cool.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ dɔlɛ koni ekɛba he ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛhaa amɛhe jɔɔ.

english: Why do I get very small cobs when I plant my maize seeds too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mináa ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu ŋmeii dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the young crops compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, leaving no single plant with enough energy to grow big cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei bibii lɛ baatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Tomatoes drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, poor watering, or lack of soil nutrients like phosphorus, as the plant tries to preserve its remaining energy.
ga: Tomatoi baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ he. nu ni ehiii loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, be mli ni tsei bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛbu hewalɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ he.

english: Why is a strange purple-flowered weed causing my sorghum plants to turn yellow and stay stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɛkɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni fɔfɔi yɔɔ mli nɛɛ miiha mi-sorghum tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: That weed is likely Striga, a parasitic weed that attaches its roots directly to your crop's roots under the ground, stealing water and food before the crop can use it.
ga: Ekolɛ jwɛi lɛ ji Striga, ni ji jwɛi ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni kɛ eshishifãi lɛ kpãa otso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛjuɔ nu kɛ niyenii dani tsei baanyɛ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why do fall armyworms destroy my maize leaves while completely ignoring my cassava foliage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fall armyworms fiteɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ ni amɛkuɔ amɛhiɛ amɛshwieɔ mi cassava baai lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Fall armyworms prefer cereal grasses like maize because young leaves are soft and easy to digest, while cassava leaves contain natural bitter chemicals that deter the pest.
ga: Fall armyworms sumɔɔ ŋmãa jwɛi tamɔ ŋmãa ejaakɛ baai bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ oya. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsofai ni mli wa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni eshwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ yɛ cassava baai amli.

english: Why do some farmers put chemical medicine on their crop seeds before planting them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsofa woɔ amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli dani amɛduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Treating seeds with protective chemicals or coatings prevents soil pests and fungal diseases from attacking the seed before it can germinate, giving your crop a much stronger and healthier start.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai loo nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ tsuɔ dumɔwui ahe nii lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ akatutuaa dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛ haa onibii lɛ jeɔ shishi jogbaŋŋ, ni amɛnáa hewalɛ.

english: What is the difference between planting saved seeds from my last harvest and buying packaged seeds from an extension agent?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɔ ko ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ teŋ?

english: Saved traditional seeds are free but can lose their strength and yield less over time, while packaged hybrid seeds are specially bred to resist diseases and produce larger harvests, though they must be bought fresh each season.
ga: Kusum dumɔwui ni akɛto lɛ aheee nɔ ko. Shi ekolɛ amɛhewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, atsɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni yɔɔ paketii amli lɛ anɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni amɛwo yibii babaoo. Eyɛ mli akɛ esa akɛ ahe ehee yɛ be fɛɛ mli moŋ.

english: How do I know the exact measurement of fertilizer to give my crops so I do not burn them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni mikɛbaahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ? Bɔni afee ni mikashã.

english: Fertilizers are calculated in specific weights like kilograms per acre based on what the crop needs; applying too little will not feed the plant properly, while applying too much builds up chemical salts that burn the roots.
ga: Akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ko, tamɔ kilogram ni yɔɔ acre kome mli lɛ buɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe akɔntaa. taakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiamɔ nii yɔɔ lɛ naa Kɛ akɛ nɔ fioo pɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaaa tso lɛ aye nii jogbaŋŋ. yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ buaa tsofai ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi lɛ anaa.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential plant food like nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to build chlorophyll and capture sunlight for healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ehe miihia ni tsei afee klorofil ni amɛkɛ hulu la ato koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my vegetable seedlings droop and wilt during the hottest part of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai amli dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young plants wilt when their leaves lose water into the hot air faster than their short roots can pull water out of the dry soil, which is why providing light shade or watering early in the morning helps them recover.
ga: Tsei bibii lɛ gboɔ kɛ́ baai lɛ fite nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi kukuji lɛ baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo loo nu wo tso lɛ nɔ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ehe lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants keep falling off without turning into hot peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ pepper ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Flowers fall off when the crop experiences shock from extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of soil nutrients, causing the plant to drop its flowers to save energy to survive.
ga: Fɔfɔi shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛkɛhi shi lɛ he.

english: Weeds are wild, hardy plants with aggressive root systems that are naturally better adapted to steal water, fertilizer, and sunlight from the soil faster than domestic crops can.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli. Amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ oya fe shia tsei.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together in the same farm plot without them spoiling each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mifiteee amɛhe?

english: Yes, intercropping cassava and maize works well because maize grows quickly and feeds near the top layer of soil, while cassava grows deeper and takes longer, allowing them to share nutrients without competing directly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa teŋ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya ni eyeɔ nii yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ. Shi ŋmei lɛ, ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa shɔŋŋ ni ekɛ be babaoo tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa amɛjaa niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe etswaaa akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my crop roots struggle to grow deep when the soil turns hard after the rains stop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ais beni nugbɔ lɛ ekpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Hardened soil lacks compost and organic matter, which creates air spaces; without those soft spaces, roots cannot push deep into the earth to find water during dry periods.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ bɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ni no haa kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui baa. Kɛ nakai hei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛyana nu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ bei amli.

english: Why is it important to move seedlings out of the shaded nursery shelter and into the open field at the right time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli kɛya ŋmɔ mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings to the open field allows their stems and roots to toughen up under natural sunlight, but doing it too early or without proper water will cause them to die from heat shock.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ awo ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaawaje tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ kɛ shishifãi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ mli hulu la shishi. Shi kɛ́ afee oya tsɔ loo nu ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ agboi yɛ latsaa mli.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure will help restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and food in the soil. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know when my cassava is mature and ready to harvest under the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni ŋmei ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting when the bottom leaves start turning yellow and dropping off, and small cracks begin to show in the soil around the base of the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ ŋmeii bibii Ebaabɔi kpojiemɔ yɛ sũ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the soil, while groundnuts and cowpeas put good food, especially nitrogen, back into the dirt naturally. Rotating them keeps your land fertile for the next season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ tsina ŋmeii feɔ niyenii kpakpa. titri lɛ nitrogen Ku osɛɛ kɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa Rotation haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes in the leaves of my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni miiye buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi lɛ amli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes in maize leaves are often caused by caterpillars like the fall armyworm. Checking the center of the plant early and applying recommended neem extracts or insecticides can stop them from destroying the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ fall armyworms lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ mli lɛ baa. Nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli kwɛmɔ mra Ni kɛ akɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi ni awieɔ he lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa ŋmɔ mli hiɛkpatamɔ.

english: Yam vines are natural climbers that need to spread their leaves in the air to catch sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground, preventing diseases and helping the plant build bigger yam tubers under the soil.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ji adebɔɔ mli tsei ni kwɔɔ ni ehe hiaa ni amɛgbɛ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwã kɔɔyɔɔ mli koni amɛná hulu la lɛ. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ yɛ. Etsiɔ helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, works like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, holds water in the ground longer during dry days, and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ehaa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbii ni nu bɛ lɛ amli. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa

english: Why is it wrong to apply chemical fertilizer when the soil is very dry and the sun is hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai baawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi waa ni hulu lɛ hu edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve so the plant roots can drink it safely. Applying fertilizer on hot, dry soil can burn the crop's roots and damage the plant instead of helping it grow.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tso shishifãi lɛ anu lɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ ashã tso lɛ shishifãi ni efite tso lɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeye ebua tsei ni amɛdara lɛ

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my food crops when the rain starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miniyenii ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ bɔi nɛmɔ?

english: Weeds are wild plants natively adapted to the soil, so they drink water and take up food faster than planted crops. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks stops them from crowding out your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni kɛ amɛhe ebɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛnuɔ nu ni amɛyeɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ. Kɛ́ ojie jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni okɛtsi otsei bibii lɛ anaa.

english: Pruning removes dead, diseased, or unnecessary branches so air and sunlight can reach the inner parts of the tree. This helps the cocoa tree direct its energy into growing strong and producing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni egboi, ni hela emɔ amɛ, loo ni he ehiaaa lɛ jieɔ tsei lɛ. Bɔni afee ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la anyɛ ayashɛ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ekɛ ŋmeii ni wa baa.

english: Will cutting branches off my cocoa tree hurt its growth?
ga: Ani kookoo tso niji ni aaafo lɛ baaná dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: No, as long as it is done correctly, pruning helps the tree save energy and direct its strength into producing pods instead of wasting resources on extra leaves and unneeded shoots.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Tso lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite nibii yɛ baai ni fa fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni he ehiaaa lɛ anɔ lɛ.

english: When is the best time for me to prune my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mafolɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time to prune cocoa trees is usually right after the main harvest or just before the rainy season starts, before the tree begins flowering heavily.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ afolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ ji yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ sɛɛ loo dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi. Dani tsei lɛ baabɔi fɔmɔ waa

english: Is chicken manure good for my cocoa crop?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmei hi kɛha mi-kokoo tsei lɛ?

english: Yes, chicken manure is very rich in essential nutrients that feed the soil and help cocoa trees grow bigger, stronger leaves and produce more pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa cacao tso lɛ ni edara, ni ewoɔ baai ni wa, ni ewoɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ fa babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmeii amli.

english: How should I apply poultry manure to my cocoa trees so I do not burn them?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ mikɛ kooloi afɔfɔi awo mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛkashã cacao tsei lɛ?

english: You should let the manure dry or compost first, then spread it around the base of the tree under the canopy line, keeping it slightly away from touching the stem directly.
ga: Esa akɛ oha ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ agbi klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛgbɛ ashwã tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shishi lɛ he pɛpɛɛpɛ. Kɛtsɔ ekɛ tsɔne lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo lɛ nɔ.

english: What happens to my soil if I regularly use manure instead of relying only on rain?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii daa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ̃ nugbɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Adding organic manure improves the soil's structure, helps it hold water for longer during dry periods, and steadily feeds your crops with vital nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. ni okɛ niyenii ni he hiaa aha onibii lɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn small or fail to mature properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ daraaa loo amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Small or weak pods usually happen when the tree lacks sufficient nutrients from the soil, receives too little sunlight, or is carrying too many crowded branches.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii loo ni bɛ hewalɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Hulu la fioo pɛ ni enine shɛɔ nɔ loo tsei lɛ aniji lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ

english: What are the key things I need to do to make my cocoa trees bear more fruit?
ga: Mɛni ji nibii titrii ni esa akɛ mafee koni mi-cacao tsei lɛ awo yibii babaoo?

english: To get high yields, your cocoa trees need good soil feeding using manure or fertilizer, regular pruning to allow sunlight in, and protection from pests and diseases.
ga: koni onine ashɛ yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ O-cacao tsei lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpa kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei lɛ daa koni hulu la abote mli. kɛ hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ helai ahe.

english: How can an extension officer help me manage my cocoa farm better?
ga: Te extension nitsulɔ ko baanyɛ aye abua mi tɛŋŋ ni makwɛ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: An extension officer can visit your farm to teach you practical skills like proper pruning techniques, correct fertilizer application, and early detection of crop diseases.
ga: Nitsulɔi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ ayasara oŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛbatsɔɔ bo nibii ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii, tamɔ gbɛi ni sa ni atsɔɔ nɔ afoɔ tsei lɛ. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ tsei ahe helai ni anaa mra

english: Can I learn practical farming techniques like pruning even if an extension officer cannot visit my farm regularly?
ga: Minyɛ mikase okwaayeli he ŋaai ni anyɛɔ atsuɔ he nii tamɔ tsei ni afoɔ. Kɛji akɛ extension nitsulɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ayasara miŋmɔ lɛ daa po?

english: Yes, extension officers can demonstrate techniques during group training sessions or guide you step-by-step through community demonstrations so you can practice on your own field.
ga: Hɛɛ, mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ baanyɛ ajie ŋaai srɔtoi akpo. Yɛ kuu tsɔsemɔ be mli loo etsɔɔ bo gbɛ-kɛ-gbɛ kɛtsɔ akutsoŋ nifeemɔi anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ okɛ ohe awo mli yɛ bo diɛŋtsɛ onitsumɔhe lɛ.

english: Why is it important to plant my maize right after the first major rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Planting immediately after the first major rain ensures the seeds get enough soil moisture to germinate quickly and build strong roots before the topsoil dries out under the hot sun.
ga: Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ aná shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. ni amɛma shishifãi ni wa dani shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and shallow roots that burn easily under direct sunlight, so they require shade from fast-growing plants like plantain to trap moisture and block harsh light during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni kookoo tsei lɛ aná hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛtsi la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to stay green and produce strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why should I wait until the ground is wet before putting fertilizer around my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer requires soil moisture to dissolve into a liquid form that roots can drink, and putting fertilizer on dry ground can scorch and destroy the plant roots.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ koni etsɔ nu ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã ni efite tsei shishifãi.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches indicate cassava mosaic disease, a sick condition spread between plants by tiny insects called whiteflies.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ yucca mosaic hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ateŋ.

english: How does covering the dirt around my pepper plants with dry grass help them grow during hot weeks?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, stops the sun from evaporating soil water and keeps the roots cool during hot periods.
ga: Ale jwɛi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni hulu la lɛ akafee nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ

english: Why do I need to put long wooden stakes next to my yam vines as they grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama emasɛi lɛ? Sweet potato wain tsei beni amɛdaraa lɛ

english: Yam plants are vines that need to lift their leaves off the ground toward the sun to make energy, which feeds the underground tuber so it grows large.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ewo ebaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ kɛya hulu la lɛ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ aba. ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ niyenii koni amɛdara

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my farm make the maize I plant in that same soil next season grow much better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni miduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground through their roots, naturally fertilizing the soil for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans jieɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Koni efee adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants with deep, established root systems that let them consume water and soil food much faster than young crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni haa amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ oya fe dumɔwui bibii lɛ.

english: Why will putting my maize seeds too close together in the same hole give me small ears of corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ŋmãa toi bibii baa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the grown plants fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving less energy to form large cobs.
ga: Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛfeɔ cob dumɔwui wuji lɛ faaa.

english: How long does it usually take for maize to mature and be ready for harvest after I plant it?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa lɛ shwereɔ jogbaŋŋ ni efeɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most common varieties of maize in Ghana take between 3 to 4 months (90 to 120 days) from planting to harvest, depending on whether you plant early-maturing or late-maturing seeds.
ga: Abɛi henɔi ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 (gbii 90 kɛyashi 120) kɛjɛɔ be mli ni aduɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni akpaa. Edamɔ dumɔwui ni shwereɔ mra loo dumɔwui ni shwereɔ sɛɛ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 9 to 12 months after planting when the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem starts to crack as the tubers swell.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Beni baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni bulb lɛ mli fũuɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off due to 'blossom drop,' which happens when temperatures are too high, watering is irregular, or the plant lacks key nutrients like nitrogen and phosphorus.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ ‘Blossom drop’ ni baa kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa Aloo tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛ phosphorus.

english: Why do the leaves on my corn turn yellow even though I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa amɛ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on corn usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to make leaves green and healthy. It can also happen if the soil is waterlogged and the roots cannot breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛbaai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛhe wa. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: When plants are crowded, they compete against each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and food to grow strong and produce good yields.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa hegbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and die shortly after I move them from the nursery to the main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seedlings suffer from transplant shock if moved during hot sun or if their roots are damaged. Transplanting late in the afternoon and watering them immediately helps seedlings settle into the new soil smoothly.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baaná transplant shock kɛji ajie amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo kɛji amɛshishifãi lɛ fite. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes the leaves of my cassava plants to curl up and turn sticky?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-cassava baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe wa?

english: Curled and sticky cassava leaves are usually caused by sap-sucking insects like whiteflies or mealybugs. They suck nutrients from the plant and leave behind a sticky waste that can cause black mold to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo mealybugs kɛ cassava baai ni ebɔle amɛhe ni wa lɛ baa. Amɛmuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛɔ tsei amli ni amɛshiɔ jwɛi ni shwieɔ shi. No baanyɛ aha ŋmɔtɔ diŋ aba.

english: When is the best time to start planting my crops during the major rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ aje tsei akwɛmɔ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ mli?

english: The best time to plant is immediately after the first two or three heavy, steady rains when the soil is thoroughly wet. Planting too early before the rains are established can burn seeds in dry ground.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ adu ji yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa 2-3 lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ dani nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Planting maize repeatedly on the same plot exhausts the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil-borne pests and diseases that target maize to build up. Rotating with beans or groundnuts helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ baafite. ni ehaa sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni ŋmãa kwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii tsake lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does the soil on my farm form hard clay-like clumps when the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ tamɔ shikpɔŋ ni wa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Heavy clay soil holds water when wet, but bakes into hard, solid clumps as it dries out in the heat. Mixing organic matter like compost, dried crop residues, or manure into the soil breaks up these hard clumps, allowing air and water to move freely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni tsii ni ji shikpɔŋ sũ lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli kɛ́ edɔ. Shi ewaa ni etsɔɔ nɔ ko ni wa kɛ́ akɛ la egbi. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, tsei ni egbi ni afolɔ ashwie shi, loo ŋmɔshi nibii futu sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaagbala nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa nɛɛ amli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu nyɛɔ amɛyaa he fɛɛ he.

english: Why do the roots of my crops grow sideways near the surface instead of growing deep into the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ afãgbɛ ni bɛŋkɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaaya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: When the soil underneath is too hard and compacted, plant roots cannot push downwards. Loosening the hard subsoil layer before planting allows roots to grow deep, giving plants better stability and access to underground moisture.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tse lɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ shi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ni wa lɛ ni ajieɔ dani aduɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛnáa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen, or the ground is flooded with too much water. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving drainage restores healthy green foliage.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ abele bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he loo nu lɛ hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, ebaaha baai eŋɔli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Cassava tubers rot when heavy soil holds onto excessive standing water for too long. Excessive moisture blocks oxygen from reaching the roots, allowing soil bacteria and fungi to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni tsii hi nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Fɛ̃i babaoo haaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees scorch and turn brown under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ shãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa creates a canopy shield that protects the leaves from heat and preserves soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata kookoo bibii ahe lɛ, ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he lɛ baa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why does spread dry grass around the stems of my crops help them handle hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni akɛfɔ̃ɔ shi lɛ ji No hewɔ lɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkpeɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, shields the soil from high sun temperatures. This prevents soil water from evaporating quickly and keeps root zones cool.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Enɛ haaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ atsɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers before setting fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed flowers when exposed to heat stress, irregular watering, or extreme drying. Maintaining steady soil moisture through regular watering and mulching helps the plant retain flowers and form peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛbote dɔlɛ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa loo ni egbiɔ waa Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa.

english: Why are my vegetable plants producing small, weak fruits even though they look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Small fruit size often happens when crops do not receive enough nutrients during their flowering stage or when plants are crowded too close together, forcing them to compete for available food in the soil.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai bibii baa kɛji tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. aloo kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, esa akɛ tsei lɛ abɔi niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ he akaŋ.

english: Why are dark spots spreading across my tomato leaves during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa tomato baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High humidity and continuous moisture on crop leaves during rainy periods create favorable conditions for fungal diseases like leaf spot and blight. Pruning lower leaves to improve airflow helps leaves dry faster and reduces disease spread.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni yaa nɔ yɛ tsei ahe baai anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi baa kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baa mli ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa baa lɛ ni egbiɔ oya, ni ehaa helai gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do my maize stems break in half easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ, ŋmãa fãa mlɛo yɛ enyɔ mli lɛ?

english: Easily broken stalks are often caused by stem borer pests that bore inside the stem to feed. The internal tunneling weakens the plant structure, causing the stalk to snap under light wind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛtao niyenii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa oya lɛ baa. Gbɛjegbɛi ni yɔɔ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ tso lɛ fãa ni etswaa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ fioo ko tswa.

english: Maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to stay green and grow. The plant moves the limited nitrogen it has from its older lower leaves up to the younger top leaves to keep growing.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛ́ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa koni ŋmɔ lɛ ahi shi ni ekwɛ̃. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen fioo kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛya nɔ amɛdara.

english: Why do people recommend I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on my farm before planting my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ mi ŋaa akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani madu ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil. When you plant maize afterward, it uses that trapped nitrogen as free fertilizer to grow stronger and produce bigger yields.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛgbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛŋmɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ekɛ nitrogen ni emɔmɔ lɛ lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋmãa ni aheee nɔ ko koni ekwɛ̃ ni ewa ni ewo yibii babaoo.

english: How do I tell which way to push cassava stem cuttings into the soil when planting?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be ni esa akɛ otsi ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ mli kɛ́ oodu?

english: Look closely at the tiny raised bumps (nodes) where leaves used to grow on the stem; these bumps have small buds that point upward toward the sky. Planting with the buds pointing up ensures the roots grow down and the shoots emerge easily.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii ni awó nɔ (nodes). Yɛ he ni tsutsu lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ yɛ fɔfɔi bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Dumɔ ni aduɔ ni ŋmei lɛ kwɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ daa ni ŋmeii lɛ jeɔ kpo mlɛo.

english: Yam plants use their leaves like solar panels to make food that goes down into the soil to grow big tubers. Staking lifts the vines off the ground so the leaves get maximum sunlight and don't rot from touching damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii ni yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛ bulbs agboi akwɛ̃. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. ni egbooo kɛ́ ekɛ ehe wo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop so many flowers on the ground without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni etsɔɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands more flowers than they can support to ensure pollination happens. The tree voluntarily drops excess flowers so it can focus its energy on nourishing the small percentage that successfully turn into full pods.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ, fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua koni amɛkwɛ akɛ fɔfɔi lɛ shwereɔ. Tso lɛ jɛɔ etsui mli ekɛ fɔfɔi ni fa fe nine lɛ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama niyenii ni ekɛhaa lɛ mlijaa oha mlijaa bibioo ko nɔ. koni ebatsɔ pod ni eyi obɔ yɛ omanyeyeli mli

english: Extra suckers act like extra mouths to feed, stealing water and nutrients from the main stem. Leaving only one or two strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough food to produce a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Suckers krokomɛi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ daaŋ krokomɛi kɛha niyenii. Kɛtsɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ ni ejuɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites living under the leaves, or viruses spread by insects. As these insects suck the plant's sap, the leaves buckle and twist as they grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa Beni kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ tsei amli nu lɛ Baai lɛ hu shwieɔ shi ni amɛfiteɔ beni amɛdaraa lɛ.

english: Sudden wilting in moist soil is usually caused by bacterial wilt or root rot, which are soil diseases that block the tubes inside the stem that carry water. Even though water is in the soil, the plant cannot transport it up to its leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ Tsei nyɛŋ ajie amɛ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya baai lɛ amli.

english: How can swamp rice survive standing in flooded water when my other crops rot?
ga: Te ŋmɔ mli ŋmãa baafee tɛŋŋ ahi shi yɛ nu afua mli beni miŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi lɛ miifite lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special hollow tubes inside their stems and roots that act like tiny snorkels, allowing air from above to travel down to the roots underwater, whereas crops like maize suffocate without oxygen in wet soil.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ ŋmeii krɛdɛɛi ni yɔɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi amli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛmuɔ nii. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni jɛɔ ŋwɛi lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu shishi. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my crop seeds right after the major rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe midumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants whose seeds have adapted over thousands of years to stay dormant in the soil and sprout instantly with the very first drops of rain, giving them a head start over domestic farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ko ni edumɔwui etsake amɛhe yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛwɔ, ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ nɛ pɛ. Enɛ haa amɛnáa hegbɛ fe okwaayeli nibii ni aduɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the base of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, or that heavy rains have washed away the nutrients before the roots could reach them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani shishifãi lɛ eshɛ amɛhe.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when planted in heavy, waterlogged soil that holds too much water during the rainy season, allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ waa ni nu babaoo yɔɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my young maize stems have holes in them and start drying up early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ yɛ bu ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ oya lɛ?

english: Holes in young maize stems are caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch from eggs laid by moths, burrowing inside the stem to eat the plant from within.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ abele tsei bibii amli lɛ jɛɔ stem borers ni jɛɔ ŋmeii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli lɛ amli. Amɛfoɔ bu amɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli koni amɛye tso lɛ kɛjɛ emli.

english: Tomato leaves curl when infected by a virus spread by tiny whitefly insects that feed on the sap of the plant.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ emɔ amɛ. ni yeɔ tsei amli nu lɛ

english: Why are small black insects covering the stems and pods of my cowpeas?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii diji miiha mi-cowpea tsei lɛ kɛ mi-pods lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: These tiny black insects are aphids, which attach to the plants to drink their liquid sap, causing the stems to weaken and the pods to shrivel.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii diji nɛɛ ji aphids. ni kpɛtɛɔ tsei ahe koni enu nu ni mli ewo nu Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that get scorched by direct, harsh sunlight; they need partial shade from larger canopy trees or plantains to survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa amɛ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo fã ko kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo dumɔwui amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up toward sunlight, which allows the plant to catch sun energy needed to grow large roots underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo nɔ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛnɔ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la mli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they do not get enough water during hot spells or when there are no tiny pollinating insects like midges around to fertilize the flowers.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛnáaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni haa fɔfɔii lɛ feɔ fɔfɔi tamɔ medium bɛ he ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their blossoms instead of growing peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi yɛ pepper ni amɛduɔ lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop blossoms when the weather gets too hot and dry or when they suffer from uneven watering, which stresses the plant into shedding flowers to save energy.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. Aloo beni nu ni akɛhaa lɛ ni eyaaa nɔ lɛ miipiŋ lɛ? Enɛ haa tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Plantain trees fall easily because their root system is naturally shallow, and microscopic soil worms called nematodes often damage those roots, weakening the plant's anchor in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, sũ mli ŋmeii bibii waa ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes lɛ fiteɔ nakai shishifãi lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso lɛ ŋmei ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to make food. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or animal manure helps the maize turn green again and produce strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji tsei ni he hiaa koni akɛfee niyenii Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni abele lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my young rice plants turning reddish-brown in my swamp field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ miitsɔ tsuru-tsuji yɛ mi-swamp ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Reddish leaves in flooded fields often mean there is too much iron in the wet soil. Draining the field occasionally to let air into the roots and adding potassium fertilizer helps the roots stay healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai tsuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dade babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ajie nu kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ be kɛ bei amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ abote shishifãi lɛ amli, ni akɛ potassium ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ ahiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting inside the soil when heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when left in standing water because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows extra water to drain away easily.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my yam vines grow lots of big leaves but produce very small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi amɛshishifãi lɛ ji bibii waa lɛ?

english: Using too much nitrogen fertilizer makes yam plants put all their energy into leafy growth above ground instead of feeding the root. Balanced soil nutrients with potassium encourage larger tuber growth.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaha sweet potato tso lɛ afite ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaakwɛ baai yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeeha shishifãi lɛ niyenii. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ja ni potassium yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when stressed by hot sun, dry weather, or tiny insects like mirids. Planting shade trees and protecting the farm from pests helps flowers turn into pods.
ga: Kookoo tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulu la ni mli edɔ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo kooloi bibii tamɔ atatui shɛ amɛhe. Tsei ni aduɔ koni akɛha hulutsoo ni abu ŋmɔji ahe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain roots are shallow, making the plant top-heavy when the fruit bunch grows. Supporting the stems with wooden Y-sticks and mounding soil around the base keeps them upright against wind.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, ni no haa tso lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii beni aduawai akui lɛ daraa lɛ. Akɛ tsei ni tamɔ Y kɛ muji ni abua naa ni ebɔle ehe lɛ fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ Shishitoo lɛ haa ehiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Black bottoms on tomatoes, called blossom end rot, happen when plants do not get consistent water or calcium from the soil. Regular watering and adding compost or lime to the soil prevents this.
ga: Atsɛɔ hei diji ni yɔɔ tomato nɔ lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu loo calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nu ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmeii awo mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plant leaves curling up like little cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ ebɔle ehe tamɔ kɔɔpoo bibioo ko lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny sucking insects like whiteflies or thrips feeding on them. Spraying neem oil or organic pest control keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni yeɔ amɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ekpɔtɔ yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni jɛ bɔɔ nii amli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my watermelons split open on the farm before I can harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon lɛ miitswa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Watermelons split when they absorb a sudden, heavy rush of water after a dry spell, expanding faster than the skin can stretch. Watering evenly throughout their growth prevents cracking.
ga: Watermelons fiteɔ kɛji amɛmu nu ni hoɔ trukaa ni tsii waa yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. ni shwereɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ Nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa yɛ dalɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni akagbala.

english: Why do my groundnut plants push their yellow flowers down into the dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miitsi fɔfɔii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛmiiya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants naturally push their fertilized flowers into loose soil so the peanuts can grow safely underground. Keeping the soil loose around the plant base helps them yield better.
ga: Peanut tsei lɛ tsiɔ amɛ fɔfɔi ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ewo muji lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa bɔni afee ni peanut lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle Tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni eha yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and dry up when I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ beni mifolɔ tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense heat and direct sunlight. Large shade trees or food crops like plantains act as natural shields, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa leaves from burning until the trees are mature enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei wuji ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo niyenii tsei tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni obu kookoo baai bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ená hulu la ni fa babaoo.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize plants turning yellow during the hot sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant cannot pull enough nitrogen from the soil, often made worse by heat stress and lack of water. Heat speeds up moisture evaporation, making it harder for roots to absorb necessary nutrients.
ga: Abele baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli lɛ haa enɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Dɔlɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya. Enɛ haa ewaa ahaa shishifãi lɛ akɛ amɛaaŋɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ.

english: Why does my cassava yield get smaller every year when I plant on the same farm plot without taking a break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi daa afi kɛ́ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ ni mikɛ mihe wooo mli lɛ?

english: Cassava absorbs large amounts of nutrients from the ground to grow its roots. Continuous planting on the exact same spot exhausts the soil's natural food supply without giving the soil time to rest or recover.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni eshishifãi lɛ adara. Tsei ni yaa nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ fiteɔ ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛjɔɔ ehe loo ekɛ ehe awo mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops look hungry even after I apply fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo amɛmli dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away dissolved fertilizer from the topsoil before the roots can absorb it. This process, called leaching, leaves nutrients out of reach of your crops deeper in the ground or washed off into streams.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbɛ eshwa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ nɛɛ akɛ leaching. Ejieɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ onibii amli ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ loo ni faai hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my plantain suckers produce thin trunks and small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii lɛ? Be ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight underground for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from each other. Spacing gives each plant enough space to gather resources and produce large fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe lɛ. He ni jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ lɛ haa nitsumɔhe fɛɛ nitsumɔhe náa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbuaa nibii anaa ni ewoɔ aduawai wuji.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster than my pepper seedlings after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants with aggressive root systems naturally adapted to seize water and nutrients quickly, allowing them to outgrow cultivated crops that take longer to establish.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ ji koo mli tso ni wa ni shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei yɔɔ mli. Amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ amɛfɔmɔ su mli koni amɛhiɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ oya. Enɛ haa amɛdaraa oya fe tsei ni aduɔ, ni amɛheɔ be babaoo dani amɛmaa shi lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my pepper plants dropping off instead of forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when stressed by irregular watering, excessive heat, or poor pollination. Dropping flowers allows the plant to conserve energy to survive the stressful conditions.
