ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Fɔfɔi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers under the ground are mature enough to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akpa?

english: Yams signal maturity above ground when the leaves and vines naturally turn yellow and dry up. This shows that the vine has finished sending nutrients down into the tuber.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ amɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ dalɛ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ egbe niyenii mli hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa shi kɛyaa bulb lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do cocoa pods turn black and rot so quickly during the wet, rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in cool, damp, and shady environments. Rain droplets splash fungal spores from the soil onto the pods, spreading the rot across the farm.
ga: Fɔ̃ɔ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, shade yɔɔ lɛ kɛ black pod hela baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Gbalamɔ rot hela mli yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do insect pests swarm my cowpea field as soon as the plants start to bloom?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai shwieɔ mi-cowpea ŋmɔji lɛ amli kɛji tsei lɛ je shishi amɛfɔ̃ɔ pɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers produce rich nectar and soft petals that attract insects like thrips and pod borers looking for high-energy food and suitable places to lay their eggs.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ jieɔ nu ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni gbalaa kooloi tamɔ thrips kɛ pod borers. Amɛmiitao niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ waa kɛ he ko ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛwui lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize plant leaves are turning yellow because of a disease or because of an insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abɛi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hela loo kooloi ni tutuaa mi lɛ hewɔ?

english: Insects usually leave physical signs like chew marks, holes, or visible pests on the leaves, whereas diseases often cause uniform color changes, spots, or powdery coatings across the leaves without direct physical damage from chewing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ he okadii, bu loo kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Yɛ be mli ni helai srɔtoi Bei pii lɛ, ekɛ su tsakeɔ, ŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔ ni tamɔ powder baa baa muu lɛ fɛɛ nɔ ni gbɔmɔtsoŋ nɔ ko nɔ ko fiteee tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔlɔ mli.

english: Can I use the same agrochemical medicine to kill insects and treat leaf rots on my tomato farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ agrochemicals nɛɛ nɔŋŋ agbe kooloi bibii ni mikɛtsa baa ni egbo yɛ mi-tomato ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: No, insecticides are specially designed to target insect bodies, while fungicides treat fungal infections; using an insecticide for a disease will not work and wastes money.
ga: Dabi, afee tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni akɛgbe kooloi lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsaa ŋmeii ahe helai. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛtsaa helai lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ, ni eji shika fitemɔ.

english: Why does the pest spray I bought stop working after a heavy rain falls on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi bibii ni mihe lɛ kpa nitsumɔ beni nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rain washes away chemical treatments sitting on the surface of leaf tissues before the plant or target pests can absorb them, requiring sprays with sticking agents or reapplication after rainfall.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ tsofai ni ekpɛtɛ tso lɛ baa lɛ he lɛ dani tso loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni akɛtaoɔ lɛ lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Esa akɛ okɛ spray ni akɛ nibii ni akɛkpɛtɛɔ nii ahe lɛ atsu nii loo okɛwo nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves droop and wilt during the afternoon sun even when the soil is moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shwane hulu lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Plants droop during intense heat as a natural defense mechanism to reduce their surface area facing the sun and conserve moisture, usually recovering once temperatures cool down in the evening.
ga: Tsei gboiɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ kpeɔ lɛ aba shi ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Extreme heat or nutrient imbalances cause high stress to the crop, making the plant shed its blossoms to save energy for its own survival rather than producing seed and fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni bɛ shiŋŋ lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni mli wa baa ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ. Ha tsei afɔlɔ koni amɛbu hewalɛ kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ wuhi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees produce fewer pods during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry conditions, cocoa trees naturally slow down pod production and shed leaves to save water and keep the main tree trunk alive until the rainy season returns.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cacao tsei lɛ haa pod lɛ feɔ mlɛo yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛha tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ ahi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds around my cassava before applying fertilizer to the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ? Cassava dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Weeds have fast-growing roots that steal fertilizer nutrients faster than crops can, so removing them ensures your cassava gets the full benefit of the plant food.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni daa oya ni juɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya fe bɔ ni tso lɛ baanyɛ afee. No hewɔ lɛ, ejiemɔ lɛ haa ŋmei lɛ náa tsei aniyenii lɛ ahe sɛɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why does planting groundnuts on my farmland make the soil better for planting maize the following season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha afi ni baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts work with friendly soil bacteria to trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground, leaving natural fertilizer behind for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ sũ mli helai ni ji naanyobɔɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛmɔmɔ nitrogen gas ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛto shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ashiɔ ahaa wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nɔ.

english: Can planting specific flowers alongside my vegetables really protect them from pests without using chemicals?
ga: Ani fɔfɔi pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni miduɔ yɛ mi-aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ baanyɛ abu amɛhe kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii?

english: Yes, certain companion plants like marigolds release natural scents or root chemicals that repel harmful pests like root nematodes, acting as a living fence for your vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei komɛi ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ ekome, tamɔ marigolds lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai loo tsofai kɛjɛɔ amɛshishifãi amli ni shwieɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ shishifãi ni ji nematodes lɛ. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni hiɛ ka kɛha o-vegetables lɛ.

english: How do beneficial insects like ladybugs help protect my crop leaves from damage?
ga: Te kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ladybugs lɛ baanyɛ abu mitso lɛ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite lɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Beneficial insects act as natural predators by hunting and eating soft-bodied crop pests like aphids, keeping pest numbers down naturally without harming your plants.
ga: Kplukai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɛi anɔ kɛtsɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ blɛoo, tamɔ aphids lɛ ni amɛgbeɔ ni amɛyeɔ lɛ nɔ, koni amɛha kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ayibɔ aba shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛyeee otsei lɛ awui.

english: Should I start planting my seeds right after the very first rainfall of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mabɔi dumɔwui akwɛmɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is usually better to wait for two or three steady rains so the soil gets deeply soaked. The very first rain often only wets the surface, and hot sun afterwards can dry out and destroy your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ nugbɔ enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni efite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Is it good practice to dig my planting holes in advance and leave them open before planting?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaatsɔ hiɛ atsa bu ni akɛduɔ nii ni ashiɔ lɛ efolo dani aduɔ nii?

english: Yes, digging holes early allows the soil inside to loosen and catch early rain moisture. When you eventually place your crops inside, the soft, moist soil helps roots spread faster.
ga: Hɛɛ, bu ni atsa mra. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. Kɛ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ wo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni mli edɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: Why do experienced farmers prefer planting their seedlings late in the evening instead of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛdu dumɔwui gbɛkɛ moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Planting in the cool evening protects young crops from intense afternoon heat. It gives seedlings the whole night to settle into the soil and absorb water without drying out.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ shwane mli latsaa ni naa wa lɛ he. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni amɛmuɔ nu ni amɛgbiɛɛ.

english: Do I need to water my fresh seedlings immediately after putting them in the ground?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mawo dumɔwui heei lɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yes, pouring water immediately around newly planted seedlings helps settle the loose soil firmly against the roots and provides moisture for quick recovery from planting stress.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni oooshwie dumɔwui heei ni adu lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ ni etse ehe lɛ akpɛtɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe jogbaŋŋ. ni ehaa nu ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ oya kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui ahe haomɔ mli.

english: How can I tell if the ground is moist enough for me to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Scoop a handful of topsoil and squeeze it in your hand; if it forms a soft ball without dripping water or crumbling into dry dust, the soil moisture is ideal for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni okɛwo oniji amli. Kɛji efee bɔɔlu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni nu shwieee shi loo efolɔ etsɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do my newly transplanted crops wither even when the weather feels relatively cool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni midu ehee lɛ shwieɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli ejɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Transplanting disturbs the roots, making it hard for plants to suck up water at first. Without immediate water or proper soil contact, the leaves lose moisture quickly and cause the crop to wither.
ga: Kɛ́ adu lɛ, ebaahao shishifãi lɛ. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei akɛ amɛaaŋɔ nu yɛ shishijee mli. Kɛji nu bɛ loo ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpaa gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ Baai lɛ fiteɔ oya ni ehaa tso lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: What is the best way to organize my helpers during planting so the crops do not dry out?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni matsɔ nɔ mato miyelikɛbualɔi lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ yɛ dumɔ be mli koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Divide the work so that one group digs and places the seedlings while another group follows immediately behind with water. This keeps fresh plant roots from sitting in dry soil for too long.
ga: Jaa nitsumɔ lɛ mli awo kuu kome mli koni atsa ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ awo mli. Kuu kroko lɛ kɛ nu nyiɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ baatsi tsei heei ashishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ sũ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: If I dig holes early and it takes a long time for rain to fall, will the holes become too dry for crops?
ga: Kɛji otsa bu oya ni ehe be babaoo dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ lɛ, Ani bu lɛ baagbi tsɔ ni anyɛɛɛ adu nii?

english: If open holes stay dry for too long under intense heat, the soil inside can harden again. In that case, add water to the holes or wait for another rainfall to soften the soil before planting.
ga: Kɛji akɛ gbɛ ni agbele lɛ mli lɛ gĩ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ekoŋŋ. Kɛ́ nakai eba lɛ, okɛ nu awo bu lɛ mli loo mɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo dani odu.

english: If it rains heavily for just one hour, can I go out and plant straight away?
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ŋmɛlɛtswaa kome pɛ lɛ, ani manyɛ maya ni mayadu nii?

english: It is best to check the ground first. Heavy rain can run off quickly without soaking deep into the earth, so ensure the soil is thoroughly wet below the surface before planting.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajo foi oya ni eboteee shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ kwɛmɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shishigbɛ dani odu.

english: Can I just push my seeds or seedlings straight into unbroken soil after a light rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ matsi dumɔwui loo dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ ni etseee nɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ?

english: No, hard, unbroken soil prevents roots from spreading easily to find nutrients. Preparing soft planting holes gives roots space to breathe and store rainwater efficiently.
ga: Dabi, shikpɔŋ ni wa ni etseee lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã mlɛo koni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ. Dumɔ bu ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni asaa lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛmuɔ ni ehaa nugbɔ nu lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings dry up and die when there are no bigger plants around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni cacao tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and cannot withstand harsh, direct sunlight. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa from sunburn and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cocoa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛkpɛlɛɛɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ tɛ̃ɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Yam leaves need sunlight to manufacture food that feeds the growing tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves into the sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil where diseases can spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii. Staking haa tso lɛ yibii lɛ shɛɔ hulu la nɔ ni ehaaa sũ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni no haa helai baa. baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava stem cuttings upside down in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei niji ni mikɛ mihe woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava stems have small buds that point upward. Planting them upside down forces new shoots to grow downward first before curving up, which weakens the plant and reduces the size and number of tubers.
ga: Kasava tso lɛ shishifãi yɛ ŋmeii bibii ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu amɛ kɛtee shishi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii heei lɛ adara kɛya shi dani amɛba ŋwɛi. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ. ni ajie yitsei lɛ adalɛ kɛ amɛyibɔ ​​shi

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient. Adding compost, animal manure, or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves stay green and produce full maize cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmãa ni eyi obɔ.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots. When the plants harvest or rot, that nitrogen stays in the soil as natural fertilizer for future crops.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Beni akpaa tsei loo amɛfiteɔ Nakai nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha tsei ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my vegetables with cut grass or husks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he? Aduawai ni akɛ jwɛi ni afo loo ŋmãa ŋmɔji ewo mli?

english: Covering the soil with organic matter, called mulching, blocks direct heat from the sun. This keeps the root area cool, slows down water evaporation, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsiɔ la ni jɛɔ hulu lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Enɛ baaha shishifã lɛ he lɛ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo. ni etsĩ jwɛi lɛ anaa koni ekaye nɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl upward and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl is caused by small insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking juices from the plant and spreading plant viruses. Controlling these pests early with neem leaf sprays or mild insecticides prevents leaf distortion.
ga: Kplukai bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. Ni aaaye nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔ mra Kɛ akɛ neem baa mli tsofa loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni waaa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ akafite.

english: What causes holes in my maize leaves with tiny brown dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-abɛi lɛ ahe muji bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ? Bu ko yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing stem of the maize plant to eat soft leaves, which can be treated early using recommended biological control sprays.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii. ni abaanyɛ atsa mra kɛtsɔ tsofa ni akɛbuɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe ŋaa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the flowers on my tomato plants falling off without forming fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they experience high heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insect visits for pollination. Keeping soil water levels steady helps the flowers set fruits successfully.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛwo la ni mli edɔ waa mli. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa Aloo kooloi bibii baaa ni amɛbafee pollination. Kɛ́ nu lɛ hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I prune extra shoots growing around the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi plantains titrii lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Having too many shoots (suckers) creates competition for water, light, and soil nutrients. Leaving only one primary sucker alongside the main stem directs food energy into growing a bigger cluster of plantains.
ga: Suckers (shoots) babaoo kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu, la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi sucker titri kome pɛ yɛ tso titri lɛ masɛi lɛ, ehaa niyenii hewalɛ ni haa plantains lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ kui wuji.

english: Is it profitable for me to start planting coconuts on my land right now?
ga: Ani sɛɛnamɔ baaba he akɛ mabɔi ŋmeii dumɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bianɛ?

english: Yes, planting coconuts is a profitable venture because local market demand in Ghana has risen significantly, and mature trees produce harvests consistently for many years.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii adumɔ ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nɔ ni maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ taoɔ lɛ etee hiɛ waa. Ni tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa nɔ daa afii babaoo.

english: Why are so many people in Ghanaian cities suddenly buying fresh coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ miihe ŋmeii heei trukaa lɛ?

english: More consumers in towns and cities are buying coconuts because of a growing awareness of the health benefits of fresh coconut water and natural coconut products.
ga: Nihɔɔlɔi ni yɔɔ maji srɔtoi anɔ Mɛi babaoo miihe ŋmeii. Nɔ ni ha ebalɛ nakai ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmei nu kpakpa kɛ ŋmei nibii ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ he nilee ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Do I need to look for buyers outside Ghana to make money from my coconuts?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni matao mɛi ni baahe nii yɛ Ghana kponɔgbɛ koni maná shika kɛjɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: No, you do not need to export; the local market within Ghana consumes large quantities of coconuts, making it easy to sell your harvest right in nearby markets.
ga: Dabi, ehe ehiaaa ni okɛmaje maŋsɛɛ. Ghana maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ kɛ ŋmeii babaoo tsuɔ nii. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ ooohɔ̃ɔ onibii yɛ jarayeli hei ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ.

english: Apart from selling the fresh water and meat, what other products can I get from coconuts?
ga: Kɛfata nu kpakpa kɛ loo ni ohɔ̃ɔ lɛ he lɛ, mɛɛ nibii krokomɛi onine shɛɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli?

english: Coconuts yield several useful products: the meat can be processed into coconut oil, the outer husk produces fiber for brushes and soil mulching, and the dry leaves can be used to make brooms.
ga: Akɛ ŋmeii haa nibii babaoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ baa, tamɔ abaanyɛ afee ŋmeii lɛ amli fɔ. Kpojiaŋ ŋmei lɛ feɔ tsɔji ni akɛfeɔ brɔshi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Ni abaanyɛ akɛ baai ni egbi lɛ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why should I consider making coconut oil instead of only selling green coconuts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ masusu ŋmei fɔ feemɔ he moŋ fe ni mahɔ̃ɔ ŋmei ŋmɔŋ pɛ?

english: Processing mature coconut meat into oil adds value, lasts much longer without spoiling, and commands a higher price in cooking and cosmetics markets.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ loo ni egbɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ fɔ lɛ haa ejara walɛ yaa hiɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee, ni ejara wa fe niyenii kɛ tsofai ni akɛsaa gbɔmɔtso lɛ jarayelihei lɛ.

english: How much space should I leave between my coconut seedlings during planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ jɛkɛmɔ ahi ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ enyiɛ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ?

english: Coconut trees require plenty of sunlight and root space, so seedlings should be spaced about 7 to 9 meters apart so their mature fronds do not block light from each other.
ga: Hulu la babaoo kɛ shishifãi ahe miihia ŋmei tsei. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ato he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ ji mitai 7 kɛyashi 9, koni baai ni eda lɛ akafee amɛ shade kɛjɛ amɛhe.

english: Yes, while young coconut trees are small, you can plant crops like maize, beans, or cassava between them to get food and income before the trees grow tall enough to shade the ground.
ga: Hɛɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ daraaa moŋ, shi obaanyɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, ŋmei, loo ŋmei tsei lɛ ateŋ hu koni oná niyenii kɛ shika dani ŋmei tsei lɛ agbɔ bɔ ni sa ni amɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How long will my new coconut trees take before they start bearing fruit?
ga: Be enyiɛ ebaahe dani mi ŋmei tso hee lɛ baawo yibii?

english: Depending on the variety you plant, dwarf coconut varieties start fruiting in 3 to 4 years, while traditional tall varieties usually take about 6 to 7 years.
ga: Dwarf coconuts lɛ baaje yibiiwoo shishi yɛ afii 3 kɛyashi 4 mli, ni enɛ damɔ srɔtoi ni odu lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmeii srɔtoi ni kɛlɛ lɛ fɔɔ aaafee afii 6 kɛyashi 7 heɔ.

english: Why do some of my coconut trees drop their young green fruits before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ekomɛi shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni ji eŋɔli dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Young coconut fruit drop is usually caused by lack of water during dry periods, insufficient soil nutrients like potassium, or damage from pests.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni bɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii baa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa, tamɔ potassium, loo nɔ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Do coconut trees continue producing fruits all year round or only in specific seasons?
ga: Ani ŋmei tsei yaa nɔ amɛwoɔ yibii afi muu lɛ fɛɛ loo yɛ bei komɛi amli pɛ?

english: Once a coconut tree reaches maturity, it produces new flower bunches and fruits continuously throughout the year if it receives sufficient water and nutrients.
ga: Beni ŋmei tso lɛ da ni eshɛɔ ŋmei lɛ he lɛ Ebaaya nɔ ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai heei yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ kɛji enine shɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist while the cocoa trees are young and vulnerable.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ ji gbekɛ lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is essential for green growth. When nitrogen runs out, the plant starves its older bottom leaves to feed the growing top leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ ba naagbee Tsei lɛ yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛha ŋwɛi baai ni miida lɛ niyenii.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in the ground, leading to poorer yields over time.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why is it bad to throw chemical fertilizer directly against the stem of my cassava plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii baawo ŋmei tsei lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Concentrated fertilizer placed directly against a stem can burn the plant's skin and roots. Fertilizer needs to be buried a short distance away from the stem where the roots can safely reach out and absorb it.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ hewolo kɛ eshishifãi lɛ. Esa akɛ afu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ fioo. Shishifãi lɛ baaje kpo ni amɛbaatsɔ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: When plants are crowded, they starve each other by competing for the same sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with smaller roots and fruits.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛyeɔ amɛhe hɔmɔ, ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni shishifãi kɛ aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Trimming extra side branches stops the plant from wasting food on useless leaves, directing its energy instead into producing larger and healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ ni afolɔ haaa tso lɛ akafite niyenii yɛ baai ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ anɔ. ni moŋ okɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni okɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even when there seems to be enough rain for everything?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nɔ fɛɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster and take up fertilizer and water much quicker than your crops can. Even with rain, weeds choke out your crops and steal the essential nutrients meant for them.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nu oya fe otsei lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ po lɛ, jwɛi haa onibii ahe ni amɛjuɔ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper flowers fall off without growing into peppers during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ pepper yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and water stress make pepper plants drop their blossoms as a survival strategy to save energy and water for the rest of the plant.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ nu he haomɔ haa pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ baai akɛ gbɛ ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛhi shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he kɛha tso lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers turn soft and rot in the soil when rain is too heavy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa tsɔ lɛ?

english: Too much water standing in the soil drowns the roots by blocking air, allowing fungi to thrive and rot the tubers before they can be harvested.
ga: Nu babaoo ni shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsiɔ amɛhe lɛ hewɔ. Aŋmɛɔ ŋmei lɛ gbɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ ni egboɔ yɛ bulb lɛ nɔ dani abaanyɛ akpa amɛ.

english: Holes in the funnels of young maize leaves are typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the growing tip of the plant and eat the fresh leaves from the inside out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ ni amɛyeɔ baai heei kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kpo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli lɛ baa.

english: Yam plants are vines that naturally seek sunlight to produce energy for tuber growth. Giving them sticks lifts the leaves off the damp ground, exposing them to more light and preventing fungal diseases caused by wet soil.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni taoɔ hulu la yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛná hewalɛ kɛha tuber dalɛ. Niji ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa la babaoo baa, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shikpɔŋ ni efɔ kɛbaa lɛ baa lɛ naa.

english: Why do farmers in Ghana often plant cassava and maize together on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ Ghana lɛ feɔ ekome kɛduɔ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, while cassava grows slowly and takes up to a year. Planting them together allows you to harvest maize first while giving the cassava room to fill out later, maximizing land use and reducing weeds.
ga: Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo ni ekɛ afi tsuɔ nii lɛ. Hefatalɔi dumɔ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmãa lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa gbɛ kɛhaa ŋmei ni akɛwoɔ mli sɛɛ mli. Eji shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he fe fɛɛ, ni ehaa jwɛi baa shi.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are sitting in waterlogged soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants use to build green leaves and grow strong stalks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ eta sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai eŋɔli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves of my pepper plants curling up and growing very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfee bibii nɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites feeding on the sap under the leaves, or by a virus transmitted by these insects. Treating the insects early stops the leaf damage and restores healthy growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ nu ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ kɛbaa lɛ anɔ Kooloi ahe tsamɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni akafite baai lɛ ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers before producing any fruit during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi dani amɛwoɔ yibii yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get extremely high, tomato plants experience heat stress, which prevents flowers from pollinating properly. The plant sheds unpollinated flowers to save energy until weather conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Tomato tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee pollination jogbaŋŋ. Tsei lɛ baajie fɔfɔi ni shwieee amɛhe lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot directly on the tree before ripening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ dani amɛshwere lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, overly shaded conditions. Pruning excess cocoa branches and removing infected pods improves airflow and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ tsɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ kookoo niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ, ebaaha kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily after they form a heavy bunch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya beni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems that do not anchor deep into the soil. When the fruit bunch grows heavy, the weight shifts the center of gravity, causing the trunk to snap or uproot unless supported with a sturdy wooden prop.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Kɛji akɛ aduawai akuu lɛ tsii lɛ Weight tsakeɔ ŋwɛi hewalɛ ni tsiɔ nii kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ fãa loo ajieɔ lɛ. ja tso ni wa fiɔ sɛɛ

english: Early morning is best because it gives plants moisture before the sun gets hot and allows wet leaves to dry quickly in the sun, which prevents fungal diseases from developing overnight.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa tsei lɛ nuɔ dani hulu lɛ tsoɔ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa baai ni efɔ lɛ ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ eyɛ hulutsoo be mli Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli aba nyɔɔŋ kome mli.

english: Why does my farmland soil become hard and cracked just a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa ni egbɛ eshwa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa lɛ sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Soil becomes hard when it lacks organic matter like decomposed leaves or compost. Adding organic material creates a spongy texture in the soil that retains moisture longer instead of baking hard under the hot sun.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni wa kɛ́ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, tamɔ baai loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ bɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ ni baaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã waa yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so quickly on my field even after I clear the land completely?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miidara oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ moŋ?

english: Weed seeds can remain inactive in the soil for years. When you clear the top vegetation, sunlight hits the bare ground, signaling thousands of dormant weed seeds to sprout all at once.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii babaoo. Kɛ́ ojie tsei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Hulu lɛ kpɛɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Okadi kɛha jwɛi dumɔwui ni ehiɛ edɔ Dumɔwui akpei abɔ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow before they even produce cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmei lɛ po jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your soil is running out of nitrogen (plant food) or the ground has too much water logged in it. Giving the plants fertilizer like urea early in their growth helps them stay green and produce strong, full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. (tso niyenii) loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea ha tsei yɛ amɛdalɛ mli mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are my cassava roots getting smaller every harvest even though I use the same land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ bibii be fɛɛ be ni makpa amɛ lɛ, eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Soil gets exhausted when you plant the same crop year after year without a break or proper fertilizer. Rotating cassava with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps put nutrients back into the dirt so your roots grow large again.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa wooo mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ kuɔ sɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni oha oshishifãi lɛ aku amɛsɛɛ amɛdara ekoŋŋ

english: Why do I need to walk through and inspect my farm every few days instead of just waiting for harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsɔ mli ni makwɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa gbii fioo moŋ fe ni mamɛ nikpamɔ be kɛkɛ lɛ?

english: Pests and crop diseases start small and spread very quickly across a field. Checking your farm regularly helps you catch early signs of trouble like leaf spots or armyworms before they destroy your whole crop yield.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsei ahe helai jeɔ shishi bibioo. ni egbɛ eshwa oya yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ amli fɛɛ Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa lɛ baaye abua bo ni ona naagbai ahe okadii mra, tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ baai amli loo ŋmãa mli ŋmãa. Dani amɛbaakpãtã onibii fɛɛ ahiɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they get stressed by sudden dry spells or excessive heat. Maintaining proper shade trees and keeping soil covered with mulch helps retain moisture so the flowers can turn into cocoa pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi trukaa loo latsaa ni naa wa hao amɛ. Shade ni sa kɛha tsei kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi.

english: How can tiny insects that I can barely see cause my tomato plants to wither and die?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni kooloo bibioo ko ni minaaa lɛ aha mitato tsei lɛ agbo ni amɛgboi?

english: Tiny insects like whiteflies multiply very quickly and feed on plant sap while spreading deadly plant viruses. Small, continuous feeding damage adds up over time and causes the whole plant to weaken and stop fruiting.
ga: Kplukai bibii, tamɔ whiteflies, fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei amli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa. Nɔ ni niyenii bibii ni akɛhaa mɛi daa lɛ baafite lɛ baafata he yɛ be ni sa mli. ni ehaa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ekpaa yibiiwoo

english: When crops are planted too close, they fight each other for sunshine, soil food, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough space and resources to grow thick stalks and large cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ nu he akaŋshii mli. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my young green mangoes fall off the branch long before they are ready to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-mango bibii ni ji eŋɔli lɛ miigbee shi kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruit trees drop young fruit when they don't have enough water and food to support all of them, or when pests attack the fruit stems. Ensuring the tree gets adequate nutrients and pest control during flowering helps it retain its fruit.
ga: Yibii tsei shwieɔ yibii bibii kɛji amɛbɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛ fɛɛ amɛye amɛbua amɛ. aloo be mli ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutuaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ Kɛ́ akwɛ koni tso lɛ aná niyenii ni sa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ eyibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers dry up and die when the heat gets very strong in the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli latsaa waa lɛ?

english: Young plantain suckers have shallow roots and broad leaves that lose water very fast in hot sun. Covering the base of the plant with dry grass or leaves (mulching) keeps the root area cool and holds moisture in the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ baai ni mli kwɔ ni nu lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛji akɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ha tso lɛ shishi (mulching) lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds grow back much faster than my planted crops right after a heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are naturally tougher and adapted to local conditions, so they absorb rainwater and soil nutrients faster than farm crops. Clearing weeds early prevents them from robbing your crops of the food they need to grow.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsuɔ nii waa, ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛmɔɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe ŋmɔ mli tsei. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju oniyenii tsei ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper seedlings droop and look dead right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper dumɔwui lɛ gboɔ trukaa ni amɛfeɔ tamɔ mɛi ni egboi beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings damages their fine roots, causing transplant shock where the plant temporarily loses its ability to soak up water. Planting late in the afternoon and watering immediately helps seedlings recover without dying.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baafite shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe yɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli. Tso lɛ nyɛŋ aŋɔ nu yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ shwane mli ni awo amɛ nu amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛgbooo.

english: When maize leaves turn yellow from the bottom up, it usually means the soil lacks nitrogen. The plant naturally moves its limited food supply from its older bottom leaves up to feed the new leaves growing at the top.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛ shishi kɛtee ŋwɛi Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei tsiɔ niyenii ni fa fioo kɛjɛɔ baai ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛyaye baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why do my maize stalks grow tall and skinny without big cobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii wuji bɛ mli beni miduɔ amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crops planted too close together fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of putting energy into making big corn cobs, the stalks stretch upward competing for sunlight.
ga: Tsei ni adu yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ kɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii ni akɛfee ŋmãa ŋmeii wuji lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hulu la lɛ abɔ he akaŋ.

english: Why do I need to make raised soil mounds before planting my yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, loose earth to expand easily into large tubers. Raising the soil into mounds also stops heavy rainwater from standing around the tubers and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato bulbs lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo ni etsɔ bulbs wuji. Shikpɔŋ ni awoɔ nɔ kɛfeɔ gɔŋ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni nugbɔ nu ni naa wa lɛ akabɔle ŋmeii lɛ ahe ni eha amɛgboi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as extreme heat, drought, or too much water. The plant discards the flowers to save its strength and survive the difficult condition.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo nu babaoo. Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛhiɛ hewalɛ mli ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli.

english: Why shouldn't I put dry fertilizer on my crops when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi woɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the roots can drink it up. When put on bone-dry soil, the strong chemicals stay concentrated in one place and can burn or destroy the plant's roots.
ga: Nu he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Kɛ akɛwo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Tsofai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ baahi he kome. ni ebaanyɛ eshã loo efite tsei shishifãi.

english: How do weeds hurt my cassava plants even if they are not touching the roots?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye mi-cassava tsei lɛ awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛtaaa shishifãi lɛ ahe moŋ?

english: Weeds act like extra mouths to feed in the field. They soak up water, light, and nutrients from the surrounding soil before your cassava roots can reach them, starving your crop.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii tamɔ naabui krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli. Amɛheɔ nu, la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli dani ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die if there are no plantain trees planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji akɛ aduko dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves easily burn under the hot sun. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that create a shade umbrella, keeping the young cocoa cool and moist while it gets established.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo baa. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa be mli ni ekɛ ehe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Extra side shoots waste the plant's food and water to grow useless extra leaves. Removing them forces the plant to send all its energy into growing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Tso lɛ tsei krokomɛi ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ fiteɔ tso lɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni baa ni fa fe nine ni he ehiaaa lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ. Tomatoi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my bean seeds rot underground if I plant them in flooded soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji midu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds need air trapped in the soil to breathe and sprout. When the soil is completely soaked with water, there is no air left, causing the seeds to drown and rot before they can grow.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni emɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu ni amɛkwɛ̃. Beni nu ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kwraa lɛ Kɔɔyɔɔ ko eshwɛɛɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni amɛgboɔ dani amɛdaraa.

english: Why do my elders say planting groundnuts makes the soil better for maize next season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi onukpai lɛ kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei dumɔ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmei yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants have special roots that grab nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the groundnuts are harvested, that extra nitrogen stays behind as free food for the next maize crop.
ga: Peanut tsei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Be ni esa akɛ akpa ŋmei Nakai nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baakã he ahi shi akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmei ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have very delicate leaves that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Without protective shade crops like plantain or nursery shade trees, the hot sun dries out the leaf tissues, causing them to scorch and turn brown.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo waa ni nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni buɔ mɔ he, tamɔ plantains loo nursery tsei bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ agbi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛshãa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize plants showing tiny holes and yellowing early in the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni ŋmɔŋ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli?

english: Tiny holes in young maize leaves are usually caused by early-stage caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm feeding on the growing center of the plant. As the worm eats the leaves, the plant loses its ability to feed itself properly, causing the foliage to turn yellow and weaken.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mra be mli, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii baai amli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ ye baai lɛ Tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ ehe jogbaŋŋ dɔŋŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is typically caused by tiny pests like thrips or mites sucking the sap from the undersides of young leaves. This sap loss damages the leaf tissues, causing them to distort, curl up, and stunt the overall plant growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ nu ni laajeɔ nɛɛ fiteɔ baa lɛ mli fãji. Enɛ haa amɛtsakeɔ, amɛfoɔ amɛhe ni amɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ fɛɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Will spraying weedkiller near my young maize crop damage how the plant grows?
ga: Ani tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni mikɛshwieɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ahe lɛ baafite tso lɛ dalɛ?

english: Yes, non-selective weedkillers absorb through green plant leaves and stems. If the spray drifts onto young maize, it disrupts the crop's internal growth systems, causing leaves to yellow, twist, or completely dry up.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi ni halaaa lɛ tsɔɔ tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baai kɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ Ebaafite tso lɛ mligbɛ dalɛ gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛgbiɔ kwraa.

english: How does spraying chemical medicine on my cocoa trees stop the pods from turning black and rotting?
ga: Te tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baaha tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii lɛ akatsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛkafite?

english: Black pod is caused by tiny fungal germs that spread quickly in wet weather. Chemical fungicides act as a protective barrier on the skin of the pod, killing the fungus before it can penetrate and rot the cocoa beans inside.
ga: Fungi bibii kɛ pods diji baa. ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ mli Tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni buɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo lɛ he. Egbeɔ ŋmei lɛ dani eboteɔ mli ni efiteɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water settles in the field for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing soft-rot bacteria and fungi in the soil to attack and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ ŋmɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ ni amɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves of my crops turn pale yellow when water collects on my farm after rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni nu bua ehe naa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Waterlogged soil pushes out oxygen, preventing roots from absorbing essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Deprived of food and air, the crop's leaves lose their deep green color and turn pale yellow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ tsiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa. Etsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ́ niyenii kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ faaa. Tso lɛ baai lɛ laajeɔ amɛ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow thin and fall over easily when I plant many seeds in one spot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ he kome lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This competition forces the stems to stretch thin and weak to reach the light, making them easy to break in strong winds.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɛkɛ akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tso lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ koni enyɛ eshɛ la lɛ he. Ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why is my crop producing many dark green leaves but very few fruits after adding fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ woɔ baai ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo shi ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Using a fertilizer that is too high in nitrogen encourages the plant to put all its energy into growing leaves and branches instead of producing flowers and fruits. Balanced plant feeding is required to encourage fruiting.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii yɛ baai kɛ eniji ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai lɛ, ehe miihia ni aha tsei lɛ niyenii ni sa koni ekɛwo aduawai ni ato lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Extreme heat stresses tomato plants and damages the pollen inside the flowers. When temperatures get too high, pollination fails, and the plant drops its unfertilized flowers to save energy and survive.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Beni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii. Ni tsei shiɔ fɔfɔi ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ ni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my maize plants turn yellow and dry up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow at the bottom when the plant lacks nitrogen or water. During dry spells or in poor soil, the plant moves nutrients from its older, lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shishigbɛ kɛ́ nitrogen loo nu bɛ tso lɛ mli. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ tsiɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi shweremɔ hee lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the air is too hot or when the plant doesn't get a steady supply of water. High heat disrupts pollination, causing the plant to shed flowers to save its energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ tsiɔ pollination naa. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why do my cassava roots taste bitter after a long dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava produces natural defense chemicals to protect itself. When the plant experiences drought stress, these bitter chemicals increase in the tubers, making them taste bitter.
ga: Cassava feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni buɔ ehe he. Kɛ tsei kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ kpe Tsofai ni mli edɔ nɛɛ yaa hiɛ yɛ bulb lɛ mli, ni ehaa efeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my pepper plants curl up into small cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni efee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids or thrips feeding under the leaves, or by intense heat causing the leaf to curl up to hold onto water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛmɔ nu lɛ mli

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of big leaves but very few pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpeas lɛ baai lɛ dara waa shi ŋmɔtɔi lɛ faaa lɛ?

english: Cowpeas produce excess leaves instead of pods when there is too much nitrogen in the soil. High nitrogen forces the plant to focus on leafy growth rather than flowering and producing food.
ga: Cowpeas woɔ baai ni fa fe nine yɛ pods najiaŋ kɛji nitrogen fa babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ nyɛɔ tsei anɔ koni amɛkɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ ama baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ niyenii ni amɛfeɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my groundnut plants produce empty shells with no seeds inside underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut tso lɛ miiwo ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko ni dumɔwui bɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called pops, happen when the soil lacks calcium during the time the pods are developing underground. Without enough calcium, the kernel inside cannot form.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ pops lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ lɛ Kernel ni yɔɔ mli lɛ nyɛŋ afee.

english: Why do my young plantain suckers fall over easily during rain and wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that stay near the surface. If tiny root pests or rot damage those roots, the plant loses its anchor and topples over when heavy rains soften the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. If small root pests or rotting and destroying those roots Plants lose their anchor and fall over when heavy rains weaken the soil.

english: Why do my cabbage heads split open right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage yitsei lɛ mli gbalaa dani akpaa nii lɛ?

english: Cabbage heads split when they receive a sudden, heavy amount of water after a dry period. The inside of the cabbage absorbs the water and grows faster than the outer leaves can stretch.
ga: Kaaba yitsei lɛ baatswa kɛji akɛ nu babaoo bote mli trukaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ sɛɛ. Kaabeji lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni edaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ baai lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why does my farm soil become as hard as concrete after I clear and harvest my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni mijie mli ni mikpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it is left uncovered under direct sunlight and rain. Without dead leaves, grass, or organic matter to protect and soften it, the soil bakes hard and loses its ability to hold air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa kɛji akɛ ashi lɛ yɛ he ko ni hulu la kɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛji baai, jwɛi, loo nibii ni egboi ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni ehaa efeɔ blɛoo lɛ bɛ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee shiŋŋ ni enyɛŋ emɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my yam vines start dying off early before the yams are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes lɛ miibɔi gbele dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Yam vines die early when fungal diseases attack the stems or when heat bakes the roots near the surface. Planting without mulching or ground cover overheats the roots and cuts the growing season short.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ gboiɔ oya kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai tutua amɛshishifãi lɛ loo kɛ́ dɔlɛ shã amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ adu ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awooo mli lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi lɛ adɔ fe nine, ni ebaaha be ni akɛdaraa lɛ afee kuku.

english: Can I feed the leftover cake from pressing groundnut or soybean oil to my farm animals?
ga: Ani manyɛ maha miŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ ni ji ŋmei loo soybean fɔ keeki ni eshwɛ lɛ?

english: Yes, the seed meal left over after oil extraction is very rich in protein and makes great feed. However, because it is so concentrated, you must mix it in the right proportion with grains like maize so it does not cause digestive problems for your animals.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui niyenii ni ashiɔ yɛ fɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ protein ni ehaa niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa. Shi, yɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ babaoo ha lɛ hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni okɛ ŋmaa tamɔ ŋmãa afutu mli yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ. Enɛ baatsi niyenii ni shwieɔ shi lɛ he naagbai fɛɛ anaa kɛha okooloo lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my soybean seeds are dry enough to store or send for oil pressing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-soybeans lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ akɛto loo matsu koni akɛwo mu mli?

english: You can test your seeds by pressing one with your fingernail or biting it gently. If the seed is hard, makes a sharp cracking sound, and leaves no dent, it is dry enough for processing and long-term storage.
ga: Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onineshi ni ooonyɛ nɔ loo ooomɔ amɛ blɛoo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ amɛhe wa lɛ, amɛfeɔ gbee ni tswaa. and no dents Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ atsu he nii ni akɛto be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they get too stressed by intense heat or dry soil. Giving your plants consistent water and a little shade during the hottest mid-day sun helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji dɔlɛ babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ hao amɛ. Kɛ́ oha tsei lɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are the fruits on my oil palm trees falling off before they get ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ nɔ yibii lɛ miiho dani amɛmiikwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Young oil palm fruits usually drop early due to severe water drought or attacks by bugs on the fruit stem. Mulching around the base of the tree keeps moisture in the ground and prevents fruit drop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mu tso yibii bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa yibii lɛ ahe lɛ hewɔ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my seed pods produce light, empty seeds inside after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui akui lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli ni tsiimɔ waaa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Empty or unfilled seeds happen when the crop does not get enough water while setting seeds, or when there are not enough bees around to pollinate the flowers properly when they bloom.
ga: Dumɔwui ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni eyi mli obɔ lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ beni amɛduɔ dumɔwui lɛ. Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔii lɛ amli fɔfɔii jogbaŋŋ beni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔii lɛ bɛ lɛ.

english: You can save seeds from traditional crops, but if you planted hybrid seeds, the crops grown from their saved seeds will yield much less and grow unevenly. It is best to buy fresh seed for hybrid crops.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua dumɔwui kɛjɛ blema tsei amli. Shi kɛji odu dumɔwui ni ji hybrid Tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni ato mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa ni amɛdaraa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei kɛha tsei ni akɛfee tsofa kroko.

english: Why are my crop seedlings growing very tall and thin instead of strong and bushy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ dumɔwui lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ waa ni amɛmiifee mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Plants stretch tall and skinny when they are planted too close together or grow under thick shade, as they are competing with each other to stretch up and reach sunlight.
ga: Tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ ni amɛbaafee bibioo kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛgbala amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la lɛ mli.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is the main food crop plants need to build healthy green leaves, so applying compost or nitrogen fertilizer will fix this.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my cowpea pods have small round holes in them while growing on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea pods lɛ yɛ buji bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ? beni ekwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Holes in seed pods are caused by insects like pod-boring caterpillars that lay eggs inside the flowers. The tiny worms hatch and eat their way out through the seed pods.
ga: Koolooi, tamɔ pod borer caterpillars, ni woɔ wɔji yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ feɔ bu yɛ dumɔwui lɛ amli. Kplukai bibii fɔɔ ni amɛyeɔ gbɛ kɛjɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ amli.

english: As cassava plants pass their maturity peak, they stop storing soft starch in the roots and begin converting that food into tough fiber to support the plant's top growth, making the roots hard to cook.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ eho e-dalɛ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ Amɛkpaa ŋmei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni amɛje nakai niyenii lɛ tsakemɔ shishi amɛfee tsɔji ni wa koni eye ebua tso lɛ dalɛ ni fa fe fɛɛ Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahoomɔ feɔ nɔ ni wa.

english: What is the benefit of keeping a Prekese tree on my farmland instead of cutting it down?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ Prekese tsei ni mikɛtoɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he moŋ fe ni mafolɔ amɛ?

english: Prekese trees produce valuable medicinal pods that can be sold for extra income, and their falling leaves break down to feed the soil while providing beneficial shade for shade-loving crops.
ga: Prekese tsei lɛ woɔ tsofafeemɔ mli ŋmeii ni jara wa ni abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ koni aná shika kroko. ni amɛbaai ni egbee shi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛye shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsei ni sumɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ náa hulutsoo ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crops need to stay green and grow. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or animal manure will help them regain their deep green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhiɛ amɛhe ni amɛdara. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛná amɛsu ni mli kwɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How do I know which way is the right side up when planting cassava stems in the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole fã ni kwɛɔ ŋwɛi beni oduɔ ŋmei tso yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Look at the small raised nodes or buds where leaves used to grow on the stem; these little bumps should always point upward toward the sky so the leaves can sprout easily.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo hiŋmɛii lɛ. He ni awo nɔ ni be ko ni eho lɛ baai kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ. Esa akɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii bibii nɛɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi be fɛɛ be koni eha baai lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them in a cleared field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot survive strong, direct sunlight because they dry out quickly. They need temporary shade from fast-growing crops like plantain or cassava to protect them during their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛgbiɔ oya. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be kukuoo ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains loo yucca lɛ adɛŋ. Koni abu amɛhe yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli

english: This condition is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, which usually happens when the soil dries out too much between waterings.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tsei amli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ yɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ teŋ.

english: Why do experienced farmers spread dry leaves and grass around the base of their crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi ni yɔɔ niiashikpamɔ lɛ shwieɔ baai ni egboi kɛ jwɛi amɛshwieɔ amɛtsei lɛ ashishi lɛ he lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool, holds water in the soil so it stays moist longer, stops weeds from growing, and turns into natural manure as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ekɛ nu toɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ Ni ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji egbo.

english: What should I do if I see tiny worms eating holes inside the center leaves of my young corn?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji mina ŋmeii bibii? Ni oooye bu ni yɔɔ abifao ŋmãa baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Those worms are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing tips of corn; spraying recommended treatments or applying a mix of ash and botanical neem extract directly into the funnels can suppress them.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsaa hela lɛ shwie nɔ loo akɛ ashwishwɛ kɛ neem tso mli nu ni akɛfutu mli lɛ tsu nii tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ etsi enɛɛmɛi anaa.

english: Raising yam vines on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight needed to grow big tubers underground, while keeping them off the hot, damp soil prevents leaf diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei ni aduɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni he hiaa kɛha bulb agbo ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha ekɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akabɔ he koni foli helai akabote mli.

english: How do I test if the soil is moist enough for planting seeds after the first rains?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ aka shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Dig down a few inches into the dirt, grab a handful of soil, and squeeze it; if it forms a ball that holds together without dripping water or crumbling into dry dust, the soil is ready.
ga: Tsɔɔmɔ inchi fioo komɛi awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Okɛ sũ ni okɛ nine awo mli lɛ atsu nii ni okɛmimɔ mli. Kɛji akɛ ebɔle ehe ni nu ŋmɔtɔ ko bɛ mli loo egbɛ eshwa ni etsɔ sũ ni egbi lɛ, no lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ efee klalo.

english: Can I plant cowpeas together with my maize, or will they steal nutrients from each other?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ adu tsina ŋmãa? Aloo amɛbaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nii kɛjɛ amɛhe?

english: Planting cowpeas with maize is actually beneficial because legumes like cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil, which helps the maize grow better.
ga: Sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he diɛŋtsɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut my cocoa pods carefully instead of twisting or pulling them off the trunk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oootsɔ mli loo oootsi kɛjɛ tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Cocoa pods grow from delicate flower cushions on the tree stem. Twisting or pulling pods rips these cushions off, preventing new flowers and pods from growing in those exact spots during future seasons.
ga: Cocoa pods kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi akushin ni yɔɔ tsei ashishi. Kɛ́ otsi loo ogbala tsɔne lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kushɛŋ lɛ agbo. Tsi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii heei anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃. Ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei komɛi yɛ bei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: How do I cut a ripe cocoa pod off the tree without damaging the trunk?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafolɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni mifiteee tso lɛ shishifã lɛ?

english: You should use a sharp harvesting hook or cutlass to slice cleanly through the stalk of the pod, leaving a small stub attached to the tree without gouging into the main bark.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ hoo loo kakla ni naa wa atsu nii. Kpãa pod lɛ shishifã lɛ he. ni ŋmei bibioo ko ni eshwɛ yɛ tso lɛ he ni efooo tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli.

english: What happens to my cocoa tree if I accidentally slice into the bark while cutting off a pod?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ kɛji mikɛ oshara shwie eshishifãi lɛ anɔ be mli ni mifoɔ eshishifãi lɛ?

english: Wounding the bark creates an open door for fungal diseases like black pod and pests like stem borers to enter, which can weaken or kill that part of the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ afite tso lɛ yibii lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai, tamɔ ŋmeii diji, kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ aha tso lɛ fã nɛɛ agbɔjɔ loo egbe lɛ lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cocoa trees producing fewer pods now compared to how they used to yield years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ woɔ ŋmeii fioo fe bɔ ni ewo afii ni eho lɛ?

english: Over time, soil loses its nutrients, trees grow old, and stem damage from poor harvesting or diseases accumulates. Without pruning, soil feeding, and proper care, older trees naturally produce less fruit.
ga: Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Sũ lɛ mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ baafite. Tso lɛ miigbɔ. kɛ tsei ni kpamɔ ni ehiii loo helai ni ebua amɛhe naa lɛ efite. Kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ niyenii kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei ni edara lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do some of my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani akpa lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, humid conditions. It spreads through rain splashes, overgrown shade, and leaving infected pods on the tree.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔshiimɔi, hulutsoo ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ anɔ.

english: Why is it important to prune excess branches from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ kookoo tso nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy so sunlight and air can reach the main stem, which dries out excess moisture that causes diseases and encourages the tree to grow bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ashɛ tso lɛ shishi. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ hela baa lɛ agbi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Why do cocoa pods grow directly on the main trunk instead of on the thin branches at the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ niji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods are heavy and need the strong support of the main trunk and thick branches so they do not snap off or break the tree while growing.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsii ni ebiɔ yelikɛbuamɔ ni mli wa kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ niji ni mli tse lɛ amli. Enɛ ji koni tso lɛ akafo loo ekafo be mli ni aduɔ nii lɛ.

english: A ripe pod changes color completely—green pods turn bright yellow, and red or purple pods turn orange. Tapping a ripe pod also makes a hollow sound because the beans inside have detached from the outer shell.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su kwraa. Pods eŋɔli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. ni ŋmɔtɔ tsuru loo ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛ́ otswa pod ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu, ehaa gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji baa ejaakɛ kɔfe ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ efo kɛjɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: What happens if I harvest my cocoa pods while they are still partially green?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii lɛ be mli ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔŋ fioo lolo lɛ?

english: Unripe pods have beans that are flat and lack natural sugars, which leads to poor fermentation, lightweight beans, and lower prices at the buying depot.
ga: Pods ni edako lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni sugar bɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni ehiii baa lɛ Beans ji nɔ ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni jara ni yɔɔ he ni aheɔ nii yɛ lɛ ba shi.

english: How long does it take for a cocoa flower to turn into a ripe pod that I can harvest?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: After a flower is pollinated, it takes about five to six months for it to grow into a fully mature, ripe pod ready for cutting.
ga: Beni afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli pollination sɛɛ lɛ Ebaahe aaafee nyɔji 5-6 dani amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni eda kwraa ni asaa he kɛha ŋmɔlɔ.

english: I see numbers like 15-15-15 or 30-30-0 on fertilizer bags at the store. What do these numbers actually mean for my crops?
ga: Minaa yibɔi tamɔ 15-15-15 loo 30-30-0 yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe kotokui anɔ yɛ shwapo lɛ mli. Mɛni yibɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Those numbers show the balance of three main nutrients: Nitrogen for leaf growth, Phosphorus for strong roots, and Potassium for fruit production and disease resistance. A 15-15-15 blend has equal parts of all three, while a 30-30-0 blend has high nitrogen and phosphorus but no potassium.
ga: Yibɔi nɛɛ tsɔɔ bɔ ni niyenii mli nibii titrii etɛ yeɔ egbɔ: nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ; Phosphorus kɛha shishifãi ni wa kɛ potassium kɛha aduawai afeemɔ kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛhe amɛyeɔ. 15-15-15 ni akɛfutuɔ lɛ yɛ fãi etɛ lɛ fɛɛ mli fãi ni yeɔ egbɔ. Yɛ be mli ni 30-30-0 ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ mli lɛ, nitrogen kɛ fɔsfɔs fa babaoo. Shi potasium bɛ

english: Why do different fertilizers come in different colors like white, yellow, or dark grey?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi, tamɔ eyɛŋ, ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: The color comes from the raw minerals used by the manufacturer or dyes added so you can identify the brand. The color itself does not make the fertilizer better or worse—what matters most are the nutrient numbers on the bag.
ga: Su lɛ jɛɔ shika tsuru ni afee lɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mɔ ni fee lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli koni onyɛ oyɔse nɔ ni afee lɛ. Su haaa ŋmɔshi nibii afee nɔ ni hi loo nɔ ni ehiii kwraa. Nɔ ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ji niyenii mli hewalɛ yibɔi ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Is the traditional 15-15-15 fertilizer still good for my farm, or should I switch to the newer fertilizer blends on the market?
ga: Ani blema 15-15-15 ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hi lolo kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ? Aloo esa akɛ matsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ anɔ?

english: 15-15-15 is still a great general fertilizer for balanced growth, but newer blends are designed for specific crops or soils. Switching to a newer formula can be better if your specific crop needs more of one nutrient at a certain growth stage.
ga: 15-15-15 fɔmula lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha dalɛ ni ja. Shi afee ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii heei lɛ aha tsei loo shikpɔji pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oootsake kɛya fɔmla hee nɔ kɛji akɛ oŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ lɛ biɔ niyenii ni fa fe ekome yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ko mli ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: If I buy a fertilizer with higher numbers like 30-30-0 instead of 15-15-15, should I apply less of it to my farm?
ga: Kɛ mihe ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo, tamɔ 30-30-0 yɛ 15-15-15 najiaŋ lɛ, ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Yes, because fertilizers with higher numbers are more concentrated. Since they contain more plant food in every handful, you need smaller amounts to feed your crops compared to lower-strength blends.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo lɛ baafee nɔ ni mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛyɛ tsei niyenii babaoo yɛ nine fɛɛ nine mli. No hewɔ lɛ ehe miihia ni oná fioo ko ni okɛha onibii lɛ niyenii. Kɛ akɛto nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ ahe

english: How do I know which specific fertilizer brand or blend is best for my soil?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfee ekome ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: The best choice depends on what crop you are growing and your soil's health. You can observe your crops for signs like yellowing leaves or ask an extension officer to test your soil so you buy the exact blend your field needs.
ga: Nɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni obaahala lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ kɛ bɔ ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Obaanyɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli koni ona okadii tamɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo obi extension nitsulɔ ko ni eka oshikpɔŋ lɛ ekwɛ. koni ohe nibii ni kɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli hiamɔ nii kpãa gbee lɛ

english: Why are there so many different agricultural companies selling fertilizer in Ghana today?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli nitsumɔhei babaoo ni hɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ Ghana ŋmɛnɛ lɛ?

english: Different companies produce specialized nutrient mixtures suited for different crops like cocoa, maize, or vegetables, giving farmers more choices to match their specific budget and farming conditions.
