ga: Nitsumɔhei feɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, ŋmãa loo aduawai ahe, ni ehaa okwaafoi lɛ naa gbɛi babaoo ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛtsu amɛshika kɛ okwaayeli shihilɛi pɔtɛɛi ahe nii.

english: Can I use the same NPK fertilizer blend for both my cassava and my vegetable garden?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutu mli lɛ nɔŋŋ atsu nii kɛha mi-cassava kɛ mi-vegetables abɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ?

english: You can, but it might not give the best yield. Quick-growing vegetables usually need higher Nitrogen early for big leaves, while root crops like cassava need more Potassium to build large, heavy tubers.
ga: Obaanyɛ, shi ekolɛ ekɛ sɛɛnamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ baaha bo. Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ fɔɔ nitrogen babaoo he miihia amɛ mra kɛha amɛbaai wuji lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei he hiaa potassium babaoo koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: What will happen to my crops if I apply the wrong type of fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii?

english: Using the wrong fertilizer won't kill your plants, but it can cause issues like heavy leaf growth with very little fruit, or you might end up wasting money on nutrients your soil already has enough of.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ejaaa tsu nii lɛ, egbeŋ otso lɛ. Shi ebaanyɛ ekɛ naagbai tamɔ baai ni mli tse kɛ aduawai fioo ko pɛ aba. Aloo ekolɛ obaagbe naa ni ofite shika yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ yɔɔ momo lɛ he.

english: Why does my land need fertilizer today when crops used to grow well without it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa ŋmɔshi nibii ŋmɛnɛ lɛ? Akɛni tsutsu lɛ tsei daa jogbaŋŋ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull natural food out of the ground. Over years of farming, the soil gets tired and loses these nutrients, so fertilizer is needed to restore the soil so crops can grow strong again.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Afii babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ okwaayeli he nii Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tɔ̃ɔ ni niyenii nɛɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii ni akɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ekoŋŋ koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I make sure I am buying genuine, high-quality fertilizer when I go to the agro-dealer?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ miheɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ diɛŋtsɛ kɛ mitee okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ŋɔɔ?

english: Always buy from registered dealers, check that the bag is properly factory-sealed, and make sure the nutrient numbers, brand name, and approval seals are clearly printed on the package.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, hemɔ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni aŋma egbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ dɛŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ atsĩ kotoku lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ ni aŋmala niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ yibɔ, gbɛi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ kɛ nɔ ni tsɔɔ akɛ akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why is it important to clear and prepare my land before the major rain season starts in June?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni asaa he dani nugbɔshiimɔ be wulu lɛ aba yɛ June mli lɛ?

english: Preparing your land early allows the soil to absorb moisture and makes it easier for seeds to sprout. Planting at the onset of the rains ensures young crops receive adequate water during their critical early growth stage.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ he saamɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ mlɛo. Dumɔ ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ haa tsei bibii lɛ náa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and thin with tiny corncobs when I plant them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo kɛ abele bibii lɛ? Beni midu amɛ ni amɛbɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ

english: When seeds are planted too close, crops compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing ensures it gets enough light and nourishment to grow strong stems and large ears of corn.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa la kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa baa koni ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii agboi lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Can I just plant seeds taken from food crops I bought at the local market, or should I get certified seeds?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ niyenii tsei ni ahe yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ mli? Aloo esa akɛ maná dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli?

english: Grains bought at the food market are often not suited for planting and may yield poor harvests or carry diseases. Certified seeds from approved agro-dealers are specially selected and treated to give higher yields and resist common local diseases.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni aheɔ yɛ niyenii ajarayelihei lɛ esaaa akɛ aduɔ ni ebaanyɛ ewo ŋmɔshi nibii ni ehiii loo helai aba amɛnɔ. Ahalaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni jɛ okwaayeli mli jarayelɔi ni akpɛlɛ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ krɛdɛɛ ni atsuɔ he nii koni amɛwo yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi helai ni baa maŋ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wilt and die when planted under direct sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside cocoa provides temporary shade and keeps the soil moist until the cocoa trees grow strong enough to handle direct light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni shwereɔ oya tamɔ plantains yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo yɛ be kukuoo mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tsei lɛ baadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Curled leaves with yellow patches are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Planting stem cuttings from disease-resistant cassava varieties recommended by extension agents helps prevent this issue.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii srɔtoi ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ ni mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmeii anɔ lɛ woɔ he ŋaa lɛ amli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away. Applying balanced fertilizer or organic manure restores nitrogen, turning the leaves green and boosting growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nitrogen lɛ aku sɛɛ aba. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdaraa.

english: Why does my pepper crop wilt in the afternoon heat even when the ground feels wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peppers lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: Wilting in wet soil often points to root rot caused by standing water around the roots. Improving soil drainage allows roots to breathe and absorb water properly without rotting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ tsɔɔ shishifãi ni nu ni damɔ shi yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ kɛbaa. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ ni afeɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ muɔ ni amɛheɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛgbooo.

english: Tomatoes shed flowers when temperatures are too high or when soil moisture changes abruptly. Mulching the soil and watering regularly helps stabilize soil conditions so flowers can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsake trukaa. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔii lɛ atsɔ aduawai.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are fully mature and ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yams are mature when the leaves and vines on top of the soil dry up and turn brown. Harvesting at this point ensures the tubers under the ground have reached full size and will store well without spoiling.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ shɛɔ shweremɔ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nikpamɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ daraa ni amɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛfiteee.

english: How does growing cowpeas or groundnuts in my field help my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts trap nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil. When you plant maize after legumes, the maize feeds on that naturally left-behind nitrogen, growing stronger with less commercial fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts mɔɔ nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛjieɔ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji okɛ ŋmãa fata ŋmãa he lɛ ŋmãa yeɔ nitrogen fɛɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni ebaada waa kɛtsɔ jarayeli mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni faaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do the lower leaves on my young maize crops turn yellow in a V-shape from the tips?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli kɛmiijɛ amɛshishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape mean your maize lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help bring back the green color and restore healthy growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ baa lɛ naagbee ni yɔɔ V su mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree leaves turn yellow and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and dry air without sufficient shade. They shed leaves to save water, so planting shade trees or plantains alongside them keeps the soil moist and protects them from heat.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi lɛ gbɛ kɛji hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ amɛhe. Amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔ tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ loo plantains yɛ amɛmasɛi. Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he.

english: Why do my cowpea plants grow plenty of leafy vines but produce very few flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ woɔ wain tso ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli shi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes cowpeas put all their energy into producing leaves instead of flowers. Cowpeas naturally make their own nitrogen from the air, so switch to phosphorus-rich fertilizers like superphosphate to encourage blooming.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa cowpea kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛfeɔ baa lɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi najiaŋ. Cowpeas lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ otsake kɛya ŋmɔshi nibii ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ superphosphate lɛ anɔ. Koni ekɛwo fɔfɔii lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in cold, wet, and dark conditions. Pruning extra canopy branches lets in sunlight and air flow, which dries out the farm space and stops the fungus from spreading.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ duŋ mli. Afolɔ tsei niji krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ ahe koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔ lɛ mli afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny pests like thrips or aphids sucking the sap from young leaves, or transmitting a virus. Spraying with neem leaf extract or insecticidal soap helps clear the pests and keeps new leaves growing flat.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baa bibii amli nu lɛ loo helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ okɛ neem tso lɛ mli nu loo samla ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi lɛ ni eha baa heei ni eda lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil around them for too long, encouraging fungal rot. Planting your cassava stems on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away from the root zone.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ beni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ. kɛha be kakadaŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmei lɛ baanyɛ afite. Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my maize stems have small holes in them with sawdust-like material coming out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni nɔ ko ni tamɔ ŋmei je kpo?

english: This is caused by maize stem borer caterpillars that hatch on leaves and chew their way into the stem to feed inside. Cleaning up crop residues from previous harvests and intercropping with cowpea helps interrupt their life cycle.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji ŋmãa tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni amɛyeɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli koni amɛye mligbɛ. Nibii ni eshwɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa tsutsu lɛ amli kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tsina ŋmeii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni efoɔ amɛshihilɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa trees act like tender seedlings that easily scorch under full sun. Plantains grow very fast with broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa needs during its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ dumɔwui bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa kɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why is it important for me to stake my yam vines instead of letting them spread flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ mi-sweet potato wain tso lɛ awo tso nɔ moŋ fe ni mahã egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves up toward the sun so the plant can catch light and make more food for large tuber growth. It also keeps leaves off damp ground, preventing soil-borne fungal diseases.
ga: Staking woɔ sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ la babaoo ni efee niyenii kɛha bulbs wuji lɛ adalɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ anaa

english: Plantains have shallow roots and fibrous stems that struggle to hold heavy weight during strong winds. Supporting the main stem with a double bamboo prop or piling extra earth around the base keeps the tree upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛye amɛbua nibii ni tsii yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tso ni ji ŋmei enyɔ loo muji kroko ni akɛfata he ni ebɔle shishi lɛ fi tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is lacking nitrogen, which gives plants their green color and growth energy. Adding compost, animal manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps them regain their green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tsei feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛyɛ hewalɛ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Is it fine if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot of land every single season?
ga: Ani ehi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi?

english: Planting maize on the same land every season drains the specific nutrients maize needs and allows soil pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like beans or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ be fɛɛ be Be lɛ haa abɛi lɛ mli niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ buaa amɛhe naa Rotate corn kɛ legumes tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why does my soil turn hard and dry like a stone just a few days after heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa ni egbi tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Soil hardens when it lacks organic matter to hold moisture and maintain a loose structure. Mixing dry plant leaves, crop residue, or farmyard manure into the soil helps it hold water longer and stay soft for root growth.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waɔ kɛ́ ebɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni baaha ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekwɛ bɔ ni eyɔɔ mlɛo lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni etse, loo ŋmeii futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ehi shi blɛoo koni shishifãi lɛ adara.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, keeping the soil moist and protecting young cocoa plants during their first years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe yɛ shishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are weeds growing much faster than my pepper plants even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miida oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ? Nɔ ni midu yɛ nakai gbi lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to quickly steal water, sunlight, and nutrients from the soil before cultivated crops can. Clearing weeds early gives your pepper plants room and resources to grow faster.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya dani tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baaha pepper tso lɛ aná hegbɛ kɛ nibii ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ oya.

english: Cassava root rot usually happens when water gets trapped around the roots in heavy soil during rainy periods. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps roots healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji nu ŋmɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli, ni ebaaye ebua ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my cut cassava stems fail to sprout after I plant them in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tsei ni mifo lɛ ekomɛi ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stem cuttings fail if they are taken from old or diseased plants, planted upside down, or left to dry out too long before planting. Using fresh cuttings from the middle section of mature, healthy stems ensures strong sprouting.
ga: Yucca tsei ni afo lɛ baafee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni egbɔ loo helai emɔ amɛ lɛ amli, ni adu amɛ ŋwɛi, loo ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ dani adu. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei heei ni afolɔ kɛjɛ tso ni mli wa ni eda lɛ teŋgbɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ waa.

english: How can I tell that my yam tubers are fully grown and ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ edara jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines turn yellow and naturally dry up. This change shows that the vine has stopped growing and has transferred all its stored energy down into the underground tuber.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai lɛ kɛ wain tso lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Tsakemɔ nɛɛ tsɔɔ akɛ wain tso lɛ ekpa dalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ etee shi kɛtee ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants suffer from heat stress or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and applying mulch around the base keeps the root zone cool, helping flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni oooha efee ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni okɛ ŋmɔtɔ awo shishigbɛ lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifã lɛ he lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why does planting my cowpeas too close together give me fewer beans at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii fioo pɛ baa kɛji akpa lɛ?

english: When cowpeas are crowded, their leaves shade each other and compete heavily for root space and water. Proper spacing allows sunlight and air flow through the plants, reducing disease and producing more pods.
ga: Beni tsina ŋmei lɛ mli eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaai lɛ haa amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛyeɔ akaŋ waa koni amɛná shishifãi ahe he kɛ nu. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ tsei lɛ amli. Ha helai ni baa lɛ aba shi ni ofee pods babaoo.

english: Why did the cheap maize seeds I bought from the local market fail to grow, even though the seller promised they were good?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni jara waaa ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ lɛ? Kɛji akɛ nihɔɔlɔ lɛ wo dumɔwui kpakpai shi po.

english: Regular grain sold in open markets is often damaged, old, or improperly stored, which destroys its ability to sprout. Certified seeds from registered agro-dealers are tested to ensure high germination rates and uniform crop growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmaa ni ahɔ̃ɔ daa yɛ jara nɔ lɛ fiteɔ, egbɔ loo akɛtoɔ he jogbaŋŋ. ni fiteɔ nyɛmɔ ni amɛyɔɔ ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ̃ lɛ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔi ni aŋmala amɛgbɛi awo wolo nɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana akɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ babaoo ni tsei lɛ daalɛ yaa hiɛ be fɛɛ be.

english: I sprayed a cheap chemical to kill weeds, but my crops stopped growing instead—what happened to them?
ga: Mikɛ tsofai ni jara waaa shwieɔ shi koni mikɛgbe jwɛi. Shi moŋ, miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kpa shweremɔ. Mɛni ba a nɔ?

english: Adulterated or fake agrochemicals often contain harmful ingredients or incorrect chemical concentrations that shock and stunt crop roots. Using genuine, approved chemicals at the recommended dosage protects your crops while controlling weeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui loo tsofai ni ejaaa yɔɔ mli yɛ okwaayeli tsofai ni akɛfutu mli loo amale mli. Enɛ baanyɛ aha tso shishifãi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tsofai diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni akɛtsu nii yɛ bɔ ni sa mli lɛ baabu onibii ahe, ni ebaakudɔ jwɛi hu.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, won't I get a bigger harvest from my small plot of land?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ manyɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ he bibioo ko. Ani minɔ ni?

english: When crops are planted too close, they compete fiercely for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and tiny ears. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce larger, heavier yields overall.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni da ni tsii.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die after I cut down all the large trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ beni mifo tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to intense direct sunlight and high heat. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees provides the cool shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo ni mli ejɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer bags of yam every year when I plant on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Growing the same heavy-feeding crop repeatedly in the same spot strips specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests to build up. Rotating your crops with legumes like cowpeas restores soil fertility naturally.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ niyenii babaoo lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ajieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii tsake oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and drying up from the tip inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi kɛmiijɛ amɛnajiaŋ kɛmiiya mli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed new top growth, indicating it needs fertilizer application.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Tsei juɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli.

english: Why did my crops burn and dry up shortly after I placed fertilizer directly against their stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated mineral salts that draw moisture directly out of plant tissues when in direct contact, burning the roots and stem. Fertilizer should always be applied in a ring or band a few inches away from the stem.
ga: Mineral salts ni mli eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei ahe fãji amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Enɛ baaha shishifãi kɛ tsei lɛ ashã. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni kɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves droop heavily in the hot afternoon even though I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: Leaves droop temporarily in extreme heat as a natural defense to reduce surface area and prevent water loss. As long as the root zone has water, the plant will recover its upright shape once the afternoon heat cools down.
ga: Shi amɛ ni amɛgbee shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli be kukuoo ko akɛ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ akwɛɔ he nɔ koni akɛba ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ shi ni nu akafite. Shii abɔ ni nu yɔɔ shishifã lɛ he lɛ Tso lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa egbɛhe ni ja lɛ nɔ beni shwane mli latsaa lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper flowers dropping off the plants before turning into pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani ebatsɔ pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Flower drop occurs when plants face stress from insect pests like thrips, extreme heat, or irregular watering. Managing pests early and keeping soil moisture steady encourages the plant to retain its flowers and set fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui tamɔ thrips, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ baawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are my cassava leaves curling up and turning yellow when the farm right behind mine has the same issue?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ? Akɛni ŋmɔ ni yɔɔ misɛɛ lɛ hu yɛ naagba nɛɛ nɔŋŋ hewɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava Mosaic Disease is spread by tiny whiteflies that easily blow from neighboring fields onto your crops. Planting certified, disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings protects your farm even if pests arrive from surrounding land.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela lɛ jɛɔ ŋmeii bibii ni shwieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔji ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ amli oya kɛbaa oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ amli. Kasava tsei ni yɔɔ he odaseyeli ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai jɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ nɔ po.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying from the tips inward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigboi kɛmiijɛ amɛmligbɛ tsitsii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential plant food. When nitrogen is lacking in the soil, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and dry up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do my groundnut pods end up empty with no seeds inside when I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut pods lɛ efee efolo ni dumɔwui bɛ mli beni mikpaa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium while the pods are developing underground. Adding agricultural lime or wood ash to the soil gives the plant the calcium it needs to fill out the seeds.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'pops' lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ miiya hiɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ lime loo tso sũ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná calcium ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛwo amɛdumɔwui lɛ amli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is my plantain tree falling over by itself even when there is no strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbeeɔ shi eyɛ mli akɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ waaa moŋ?

english: Plantain trees fall over when microscopic worms called nematodes or banana weevils eat and destroy the roots underground. Without healthy roots to anchor it into the soil, the heavy plant easily drops to the ground.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo banana moths lɛ ye ni amɛfite shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifãi ni wa bɛ ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ atswa shi lɛ Tsei ni tsii baagbee shikpɔŋ oya.

english: Why do my yam vines dry up and die long before it is time to harvest the tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato lɛ egbi ni egbo be saŋŋ dani be ni akɛkpaa ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines dry up prematurely mostly due to a fungal disease called yam anthracnose or attacks by yam beetles. Using healthy seed yams, planting with proper spacing, and rotating crops every season stops the disease from spreading.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ ŋmei anthracnose loo ŋmei ŋmei lɛ tutuamɔ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei tsei lɛ agbiɔ oya. Sweet potato dumɔwui ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ hewalɛ mli Dumɔ kɛ gbɛ ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ daa be Ebaakpa helai gbɛfaŋnɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling tightly upward and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛtee ŋwɛi ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curl in tomatoes is usually caused by a virus transmitted by tiny whitefly insects, or by stress from extreme heat and dry soil. Controlling whiteflies early with neem oil spray helps keep the plants healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ haomɔ ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli baa lɛ mli. Whitefly Kudɔmɔ Mra Kɛtsɔ neem mu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, awoɔ tsei lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating holes in my cowpea leaves and pod stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-cowpea baai kɛ pod stems lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These caterpillars are pod borer pests that hatch from eggs laid by small moths on the crop. Spraying early with organic solutions like neem leaf extract or approved insecticides stops them before they ruin your harvest.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni ŋmeii bibii fɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ okɛ tsofa ko ni jɛ wala mli tamɔ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ shwie nɔ mra lɛ, ebaaye ebua. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite bɔ ni otsuɔ nii ohaa lɛ.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping all their flowers and small fruits during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai bibii lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers and young fruits when the air is too hot and the soil is too dry. The plant does this to save energy and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔfɔi kɛ amɛyibii bibii lɛ laajeɔ kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi. Tso lɛ feɔ enɛ koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite ni ekɛtsi ehe koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting in the ground before I dig them up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miibɔi fitemɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani mikɛ amɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot underground when the soil stays waterlogged for too long during heavy rains, starving the roots of air. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cocoa trees dropping almost all their flowers without forming cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miiho amɛfɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛjieee cacao ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally drop many flowers, but losing almost all of them happens when the tree lacks water, lacks shade, or is attacked by insect pests like mirids. Keeping shade trees in your farm helps preserve moisture and flowers.
ga: Yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ, cacao tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi babaoo. Shi nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ lɛ fɛɛ baa kɛji tsei lɛ bɛ nu, amɛbɛ hulutsoo, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ pollen tutua amɛ. Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ahiɔ shi.

english: Weed seeds sit hidden in the soil for a long time and sprout immediately when clearing opens up direct sunlight and rain. Planting your crops at the recommended close spacing helps crop leaves shade out weeds quickly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji ajie hulu la kɛ nugbɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ amɛmli. Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ baai lɛ ajie jwɛi lɛ oya.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct heat. Fast-growing plantains provide temporary shade and moisture, protecting cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough to withstand direct sunlight.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya haa be kukuoo mli hɔɔ kɛ fɛ̃i. Ebuɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight to make food for growing big tubers underground. Staking holds the leaves up toward the sun while keeping them away from damp soil pests and diseases.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato wain tsei lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛfee niyenii kɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ kwɛɔ hulu lɛ hiɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ helai baaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or the soil is waterlogged. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer like urea helps restore green healthy leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa. aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after a moderate rain. Applying during dry heat can burn roots, while applying right before heavy downpours washes the food away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ la ni mli egbi tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni akɛbaatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ ni naa wa lɛ baaho niyenii lɛ.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts along with my main crop improve my soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni mikɛduɔ kɛfataa miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ahe lɛ haa mishikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen from the air and store it in their roots. When left in the ground, they naturally feed the soil and fertilize surrounding crops.
ga: Beans kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ŋmɔshi nii.

english: Why does covering the soil around my plants with dried grass or leaves help them grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dried grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the soil cool and moist during hot days, stops weeds from growing, and adds food to the soil as it decays.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ niyenii fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni efiteɔ lɛ

english: What is eating ragged holes in my maize leaves and leaving small dark waste inside the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli buji ni ekumɔ lɛ ni eshiɔ jwɛi diŋŋ fioo ko? nitsumɔhe lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworms, a common caterpillar pest in Ghana. Checking plants early and applying neem extract or approved sprays into the leaf funnels can control them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana lɛ. Tsei lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Kɛ neem mli nu loo tsofai ni akpɛlɛ nɔ ni akɛshwieɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ baanyɛ akudɔ tsei lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in flooded soil without air. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to drain away so roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Shishifãi lɛ wa.

english: Leaf curling is caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips that spread viral infections. Spraying plants with neem oil or mild soapy water helps protect leaves from these pests.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ aphids loo thrips lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni gbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie tsei anɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛ nɛkɛ helai nɛɛ ahe.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping flowers without growing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi shi amɛwooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when weather gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when given too much nitrogen fertilizer, causing the plant to grow leaves instead of setting fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo beni akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo haa lɛ Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ woɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the soil is missing key nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become too waterlogged from heavy rain, which chokes the roots and stops the plant from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmã nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ lɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ kpaɔ tso lɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Curling leaves with yellow spots are a main sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness spread by tiny insects called whiteflies that weakens the leaves and stops the tubers underground from growing big.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii titri. Enɛ ji hela ko ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Those worms are Fall Armyworms, a pest that hides in the soft growing centers of young corn to feed on leaves; catching them early and spraying targeted remedies during the cool morning or late afternoon helps stop them before they ruin the crop.
ga: Nakai ŋmeii lɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmeii bibii ni miida lɛ amli koni amɛye baai lɛ. Mɔ amɛ mra. ni okɛ tsofa ni akɛmamɔ hiɛ lɛ afɔ nɔ yɛ leebi loo shwane ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli. Ebaaye ebua ni akpa amɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers dry up and fall off before any fruit comes out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot and dry, or when the soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet, which stresses the plant and forces it to shed flowers to save water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo beni shikpɔŋ lɛ tsakeɔ trukaa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛyaa ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ ni enyɛɔ enɔ ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he.

english: Why do my pepper bushes grow very tall with lots of leaves but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ miiya hiɛ waa nɛkɛ? Baai babaoo shi ŋmɔtɔ fioo pɛ?

english: When pepper plants get too much nitrogen fertilizer or manure without enough phosphorus, they put all their power into growing big leaves instead of making flowers and fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ pepper tsei lɛ ná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni phosphorus ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ Amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai wuji ni amɛkwɛɔ lɛ he nii moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai.

english: Why do cocoa trees grow better when big shade trees are planted near them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ be mli ni tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily in hot sunlight; tall shade trees act like natural umbrellas that shield cocoa leaves, keep the farm cool, and help the soil hold water during dry months.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ amɛnɔ. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why do some shoots on my plantain tree grow thick while others stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ni yɔɔ midumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ mli edɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu daraaa ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: When too many sucker shoots grow from one plantain stem, they fight each other for water and food; cutting away the extra weak shoots lets the main plant grow strong and bear large, heavy bunches.
ga: Beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli. Amɛbaatswa akaŋ yɛ nu kɛ niyenii he. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ titri lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ ada ni ewo fɔfɔi wuji ni tsii.

english: Staking yam vines spreads out the leaves toward the sun so the plant can catch light to manufacture food, which then flows down to feed and swell the tubers underground.
ga: Staking sweet potato wein tsei lɛ gbɛɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwãa kɛyaa hulu lɛ he bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ la ni ekɛfee niyenii. ni no sɛɛ lɛ ehoɔ kɛbaa shi koni eye niyenii ni ekɛfutu ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ

english: How do I know the right time to start planting my maize after the dry season ends?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mije ŋmãa dumɔ shishi beni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ eho lɛ?

english: It is best to plant maize after two or three strong rains have wet the ground deeply, ensuring the soil stays moist long enough for the seed to sprout and build deep roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooodu ŋmãa beni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa shii 2-3 eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ waa sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛfee shishifãi ni mli kwɔ.

english: Why does my soil get hard and dry quickly even after I put chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbiɔ oya eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ewo mli moŋ?

english: Chemical fertilizer feeds the plant roots but does not feed the soil itself; adding animal manure or decomposed leaves helps soil hold water like a sponge and stay soft for root growth.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei shishifãi niyenii shi amɛhaaa sũ lɛ niyenii. Koolooi ashishi loo baai ni egboi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aŋɔ nu tamɔ sponji. ni ehiɛɔ blɛoofeemɔ mli koni shishifãi lɛ ada

english: Why do the leaves on my maize crops turn yellow before the ears are fully grown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani toi lɛ daraa kwraa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main food crops need to build healthy green leaves. When the soil lacks nitrogen, the plant steals it from older leaves to feed new growth, making the bottom leaves turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ juɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii heei ni eda lɛ niyenii. Ehaa shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantains on the same land with my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ wo mi ŋaa akɛ madu plantains yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mi-cocoa tsei bibii lɛ yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily dry out and burn in direct sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as living canopy umbrellas, providing the shade and soil moisture young cocoa needs to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ oya ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains lɛ daa oya waa ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ha hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni he hiaa kookoo bibii lɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Too much standing water fills up all the small air spaces in the soil, preventing root crops from breathing. Without air, root tissues die and soil fungi quickly invade, turning the tubers soft and rotten.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ, ni ehaaa tsei shishifãi lɛ amu. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ Shishifãi lɛ gboiɔ ni shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii lɛ boteɔ mli oya. Ehaa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my yield go down if I plant maize on the exact same plot of land every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year without giving the earth time to recover. It also allows pests and soil diseases that feed on that specific crop to build up in large numbers.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ baaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afi fɛɛ afi ni ehaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why did the fertilizer I applied make my young crops dry up and burn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa midumɔwui lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛshãa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated mineral salts. If placed too close to delicate stems or applied when the soil is dry, it draws water out of the plant roots instead of feeding them, causing the crop to scorch and wither.
ga: Mineral salts ni mli wa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Kɛ akɛwo tso ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ he tsɔ loo akɛwo nɔ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi lɛ, Ejieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishifãi amli moŋ fe ni eeeha lɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shãa ni egboɔ lɛ baa.

english: How does a disease on just a few crop plants spread to destroy my entire farm so quickly?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni hela ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo komɛi pɛ amli lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite miŋmɔ lɛ oya nɛkɛ?

english: Fungal spores and viruses travel easily through wind, splashing rain, contaminated farm tools, and insects flying from plant to plant. Once a single plant is sick, these pathways rapidly carry the infection across healthy crops.
ga: Fungal kɛ virus spores lɛ fãa gbɛ oya kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kɛ okwaayeli nibii ni mli ewo muji lɛ amli. kɛ kooloi bibii ni foɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ Kɛ tso kome hela mɔ nɛkɛ gbɛjegbɛi nɛɛ yeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hela oya.

english: When crops experience extreme heat, drought, or nutrient stress, they drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism to save energy and stay alive, rather than spending limited resources on producing fruit.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ he haomɔ kpeɔ lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni akɛbuɔ amɛhe koni amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato ni amɛhi wala mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ nibii fioo pɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii

english: Why do crops grown from seeds saved from my previous harvest grow weaker than seeds bought in certified bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ mli lɛ nyɛɔ etswaa oya fe dumɔwui ni ahe yɛ kotokui ni awo he odaseyeli mli lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid crops lose their uniform strength and disease resistance in the second generation. Certified seeds are specially produced under controlled conditions to ensure high vigor, uniformity, and resistance every time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ hewalɛ, nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ helai ni nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ helai yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Afeɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ yɛ shihilɛi ni akudɔɔ mli koni ana hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ, nɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ shitee-kɛ-woo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do weeds cause my main crops to stay small even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ feɔ bibioo yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds have aggressive root systems that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients faster than your main crops can. Even with plenty of rain, the weeds absorb the plant food first, leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni okɛ amɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi jwɛi lɛ baaŋɔ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei amli klɛŋklɛŋ. ni hɔmɔ aye nyɛŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl up during the hot afternoon sun even if the ground was moist in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ leebi po

english: In intense afternoon heat, leaves lose water vapor into the air faster than roots can suck water up from the soil. Curling leaves is the plant's natural way of reducing its surface area to trap moisture and protect itself from drying out.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa mli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ nu lasu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso ko adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ebaa ehiɛ he lɛ shi koni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni ekɛtsi ehe gbɛ koni ekagbi.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food, or the soil is too waterlogged. Adding well-rotted manure or the right fertilizer gives the plants the energy they need to turn green and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele lɛ kɛha nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo nu babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛtsɔ ŋmɔji ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is my land producing smaller harvests every year even though I plant the same crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Growing the exact same crop on the same piece of land every season drains the specific food that crop needs from the soil. Changing crops each season—like planting beans or groundnuts after maize—helps the soil rest and refill its natural nutrients.
ga: Tsei komekomei ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa be lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni he hiaa tsei lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakemɔ daa be mli, tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmei sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ jɔɔ ehe ni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ woɔ mli ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my cassava sticks close together so I can fit more on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ mihe koni ekwɛ̃ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need room under the dirt to expand into large tubers. If you plant them too close, the roots fight underground for space, water, and soil nutrients, leaving you with many small, thin roots instead of big, heavy tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ shishi he ko he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛdara ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Kɛji odu amɛ obɛŋkɛ tsɔ Shishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, oyɛ shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant gets stressed by intense heat, a sudden dry spell, or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist with regular watering and adding dry leaves around the base helps protect the flowers so fruits can form.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa miigba tsei anaa. trukaa ŋmɔlɔ loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be fɛɛ be kɛtsɔ nu ni oooha lɛ daa kɛ baai ni egbi ni okɛbaabɔle he lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ shishi buɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni amɛwo yibii.

english: How can I stop my young plantains from dry season heat damage during the Harmattan?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi dumɔwui bibii anaa koni amɛkafite la yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ Harmattan beaŋ?

english: Plantains lose a lot of water through their wide leaves in hot, dry winds. Covering the soil around the base of the plant with dry grass, cocoa husks, or leaves traps moisture in the ground and acts like a cooling blanket for the roots.
ga: Plantains laajeɔ nu babaoo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai ni mli kwɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi mli. Mulching around Jwɛi ni egbi, kookoo ŋmɔji loo baai shishitoo baamɔmɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni etsu nii tamɔ nɔ ni haa shishifãi lɛ jɔɔ.

english: Weeds are native to the area, so their roots are naturally tougher and faster at drinking up fresh rainwater and soil food than cultivated crops. Clearing weeds while they are still tiny prevents them from stealing food and water from your young crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji jwɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshishifãi lɛ ahe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛnuɔ nugbɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi lɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ, ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: That white powder is a common fungal leaf disease that thrives when plants are crowded together in damp air. Spacing your plants out so breeze can pass through them, and watering only the soil instead of splashing the leaves, keeps the leaves dry and healthy.
ga: White powder ji fungal leaf hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni daa kɛji akɛ abua tsei anaa yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ mli. Shi gbɛ yɛ tsei lɛ ateŋ koni kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. kɛ nu ni oooha shikpɔŋ lɛ pɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni oooshwie baai lɛ anɔ Enɛ baaye abua ni baai lɛ agbi ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant in the dirt never come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are buried too deep in the soil, if the ground is too dry, or if soil insects eat them before they sprout. Planting seeds about two fingers deep in moist, loose soil gives them the best chance to push through.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ye amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ ni mli ewo muji nɔ ni mli kwɔ aaafee inchi enyɔ lɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ready to be dug up from the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo akɛ abaakumɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the green leaves and climbing vines start to turn yellow and dry up naturally. This signals that the plant has finished sending all its energy down into the tuber beneath the ground.
ga: Sweet potato kɛɛ bo akɛ efee klalo beni baai eŋɔli kɛ wain tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛbaa shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why are tiny insects eating holes in my harvested maize inside my storehouse?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miiye bu yɛ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa yɛ mi nitoohe lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Grain insects love damp seeds and lay their eggs inside maize that still holds water. Drying your harvested maize under the sun until the grains are very hard before storing them prevents insects from breeding and destroying your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ sumɔɔ ŋmãa ni mli efɔ ni amɛwoɔ amɛwui yɛ ŋmãa ni nu yɔɔ mli lolo lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ogbala o-abele ni okpa lɛ mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi eshishifãi lɛ mli wa waa dani okɛto lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafɔ ni amɛkafite oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without turning into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally produce thousands of flowers, but many fall off due to lack of nutrients, water stress, or poor pollination by tiny insects like midges.
ga: Cocoa tsei woɔ fɔfɔi akpei abɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shi fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo gbee shi yɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi bibii tamɔ midges ni haaa ŋmeii lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why does my farm flower heavily during certain months of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɔfɔii babaoo yɛ afi lɛ mli nyɔji komɛi amli lɛ?

english: Flowering in crops like cocoa is triggered by seasonal climate changes, especially when rainy seasons begin and humidity levels rise.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni baa yɛ be mli lɛ ji nɔ ni tsirɛɔ tsei tamɔ kookoo fɔfɔi. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi ni hulutsoo be lɛ tee hiɛ.

english: What can I do to prevent my crop flowers from drying up and wasting?
ga: Mɛni manyɛ mafee koni fɔfɔi ni midu lɛ akagbi ni amɛkafite?

english: You can protect your flowers by applying recommended fertilizers, providing adequate shade, and using proper pest control so tiny pollinators can safely visit the flowers.
ga: Obaanyɛ obu ofɔfɔi lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛwo mli lɛ ni okɛbaatsu nii lɛ nɔ. Ha hulutsoo ni sa ni okɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sa atsu nii. kɛha kooloi bibii ni amɛfee pollination Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooyasara fɔfɔi lɛ.

english: How do flowers on my cocoa tree actually turn into pods?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Flowers must be pollinated by tiny insects called midges carrying pollen from flower to flower, which fertilizes the flower so it can swell into a pod.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen. Atsɛɔ lɛ midge ni hiɛɔ pollen kɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko mli. ni kɛ fɔfɔii fɔɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii

english: What is hand-pollination, and how can it help me get more pods on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii? Ni te ebaafee tɛŋŋ eye ebua mi ni maná pods babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hand-pollination means manually moving pollen from one cocoa flower to another using a small brush or tool, ensuring almost every flower successfully turns into a pod.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine ni akɛwoɔ fɔfɔi amli lɛ he ji ni akɛ niji ajie fɔfɔi kɛjɛ kookoo fɔfɔi kome nɔ kɛya ekroko nɔ kɛtsɔ brɔsh loo dɛŋdade bibioo ko nɔ. Enɛ haa nɔ ni miihe ashɛ fɔfɔi fɛɛ fɔfɔi yeɔ omanye ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Can farm pests destroy my flowers before they form fruits?
ga: Ani ŋmɔ mli kooloi baanyɛ afite mifɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛwo yibii?

english: Yes, pests like mirids (capsids) and thrips feed on delicate flower stems, causing the flowers to wither, turn brown, and fall off before pods can form.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ mirids (capsids) kɛ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ. haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ blɔfo ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ.

english: Which fertilizer should I use to help my cocoa trees hold onto their flowers?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii koni eye ebua mi cacao tsei lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ fɔfɔi ahe?

english: Fertilizers high in potassium and phosphorus help trees develop strong flowers and retain young pods, while excessive nitrogen makes the tree grow leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni potassium kɛ phosphorus babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa otsei lɛ ni amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛbuɔ amɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahe. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha tso lɛ aná baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: Does pruning my cocoa trees encourage them to bloom and set more fruit?
ga: Ani mi-cacao tsei lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo?

english: Yes, removing excess leaves and unwanted branches opens up space for air and sunlight, which stimulates healthy flower production along the main trunk and branches.
ga: Hɛɛ, baai ni fa fe nine kɛ tsei niji ni ataooo lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ he lɛ gbɛ kɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ hulu la. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi ni mli wa baa tso lɛ shishi kɛ niji wuji lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my crops lose their flowers as soon as the dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ fɔfɔi fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi pɛ lɛ?

english: When water becomes scarce, the tree sheds its flowers to save energy and protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Kɛ́ nu faaa Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ amɛhe ni amɛgbi kwraa lɛ he.

english: How does shade cover affect the flowers on my cocoa trees?
ga: Te hulutsoo be lɛ náa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Shade trees keep the air around your cocoa cool and humid, which protects delicate flowers from scorching heat and creates a good environment for pollinating insects.
ga: Tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ohe lɛ akabote mli. Kookoo ni mli ejɔ ni edɔ Enɛ buɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. ni efee shihilɛ kpakpa kɛha kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why should I plant plantain trees next to my young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ? Mi kookoo tso bibioo lɛ

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow rapidly and have large, wide leaves that act like natural sunshades, keeping the young cocoa plants cool and conserving moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ amɛnɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo tsɔnei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: How does growing beans together with my maize help the soil stay healthy?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baadu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Beans and similar legumes pull nitrogen gas from the air and fix it into the soil. This naturally enriches the ground with plant food that maize needs to grow strong, reducing the need for expensive chemical fertilizers.
ga: Beans kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ nakai lɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ tsei niyenii ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai ni jara wa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ atsu nii.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, heavily shaded conditions. Pruning extra tree branches and clearing weeds allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm and stop the fungus.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Nibii krokomɛi ni akɛfoɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gĩɔ ni etsiɔ ŋmeii anaa.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over during moderate winds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli wa waa lɛ?

english: Plantain roots are shallow, and microscopic worms called nematodes or weevils often attack the root system underground. Without a strong root anchor, the heavy stem easily tips over when wind blows.
ga: Plantain lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛji shishifã ŋta ni mli wa bɛ lɛ Tso ni tsii lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ tswa.

english: Why are tiny white insects covering the leaves of my cowpea plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yɛŋ No hewɔ lɛ eha mi cowpea baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Those insects are aphids, which suck the nutrient-rich sap out of the leaves and cause them to curl. Spraying the leaves with homemade neem tree extract or mild soapy water can clear them off without harming the crop.
ga: Nɛkɛ koolooi nɛɛ ji aphids, ni amɛmuɔ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli ni amɛhaa amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ni akɛ neem tso mli nu ni afee yɛ shia loo samla ni mli ejɔ baashwie baai lɛ anɔ Abaanyɛ afɔ baai lɛ ahe ni eyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: How do I know the right time to put my cassava cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava stem cuttings should be planted at the onset of the main rainy season when the soil is damp. This allows the cuttings to establish strong root systems before any dry spell occurs.
ga: Esa akɛ adu ŋmeii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be titri lɛ shishijee mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli wa dani hɔmɔ shihilɛi baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my garden pepper plants fall off without forming peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmɔtɔ baaa lɛ?

english: Pepper flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat or prolonged dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist with regular watering or mulching helps the flowers stay attached and form peppers.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ hao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ kɛtsɔ nu loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛfee ŋmeii.

english: Yellowing leaves usually signal that the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. Heavy rains can wash nitrogen deep into the ground where roots cannot reach it, so adding compost or fertilizer is needed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ajie nitrogen kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii afata he.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow small and bent instead of straight and large?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee tɛ̃ɛ ni eyɛ agbo lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deeply tilled earth to expand freely underground. If the mounds are built on hard, rocky, or compacted soil, the growing tuber cannot push through and becomes stunted or misshapen.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli kwɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ shishi amɛha amɛhe. Kɛji akɛ ama gɔŋ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni miida lɛ nyɛŋ abote mli ni amɛbaafee ŋmeii loo amɛhe afee shoo.

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits get dark, rotten spots before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai ashishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egboɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This spot is called blossom-end rot and happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium to the growing fruit. Irregular watering—letting the soil dry out completely and then soaking it—blocks the plant from absorbing calcium properly.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa beni tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛwo yibii lɛ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ be fɛɛ be—ni aaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi kwraa, ni no sɛɛ lɛ atsɔ mli lɛ—baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekaná calcium lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, harsh sunlight. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains nearby provides living shade and holds moisture in the soil so the young cocoa roots can survive their first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Enɛ ji koni kookoo shishifãi bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do I need to put long sticks in the ground for my yam plants to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei niji kakadaji awo shikpɔŋ koni mi-sweet potato tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam is a climbing vine that creates food for itself through sunshine on its leaves. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground into the sunlight, helping the plant build large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni feɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ niyenii kɛtsɔɔ hulu la ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛmaa bulbs agboi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food. This causes all the plants to grow weak and produce small fruits or low yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo loo fioo.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen nutrient. The plant moves whatever nitrogen it has left to its newest upper leaves to survive, showing that your soil needs fertilizer or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni ji nitrogen lɛ faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni ehi shi. Etsɔɔ kɛji oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and roll inward during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a defense trick the plant uses to save water. By curling its leaves, the plant reduces the leaf surface exposed to the hot sun, stopping moisture from evaporating too fast.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji ŋaa ni buɔ mɔ he ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ okɛ baai lɛ shwie shi lɛ, ebaaha baai lɛ anɔ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ aba shi. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ.

english: Why is it helpful for my farm if I plant groundnuts or beans after harvesting maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei loo ŋmei beni mikpa ŋmei lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize uses up a lot of soil nutrients, but crops like groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil, naturally resting and feeding the soil for the next season.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, shi ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛmɔɔ lɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Koni ekɛ ehe ajɔɔ ehe yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛ niyenii aha shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot and smell bad when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the ground for too long, it chokes the roots and creates the right conditions for fungal rot to destroy the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Efoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni efiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes inside the center leaf funnels of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji ni ekpɔtɔ yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Eyɛ mi-baby corn tso lɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This is typically caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central growing point of the maize plant because it is tender and nutritious, eating the leaves before they unroll.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars ji mɛi ni kɛbaa, ni amɛteeɔ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋgbɛ hei ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ blɛoo ni amɛhaa niyenii mli hewalɛ. Amɛyeɔ baai lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, hot dry winds, or a lack of water. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni mli egbi, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ mli. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why should I pinch off extra side branches on my pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji krokomɛi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Removing small extra branches helps the plant focus its water and energy on growing larger, healthier peppers instead of wasting energy on useless leaves and small stems.
ga: Niji bibii ni akɛbaa Baai ni fa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛnu kɛ hewalɛ haa ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ tsei ahe lɛ, sɛɛnamɔ ko bɛ he

english: Why do my harvested mangoes turn soft and rot so quickly after I pick them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni mikpa lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni egboɔ oya beni mikpa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Mangoes are living fruits that continue to breathe and ripen very fast after harvest. In hot weather, this natural ripening process speeds up, causing the fruit to soften and decay within just a few days if it is not kept cool or sold quickly.
ga: Mango ji aduawai ni hiɛ ka ni yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya waa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ baafee oya. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ feɔ bɔdɔɔ ni egboɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli kɛji akɛ akwɛɛɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ oya.

english: What happens to my harvested crops if I leave them sitting under the direct sun while waiting for transport?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikpa lɛ anɔ kɛji miha amɛtara hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni amɛmiimɛ ni akɛmaje amɛ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight heats up the harvested crop, causing it to lose water quickly and wilt or soften. Heat also creates the perfect environment for bacteria and fungi to multiply, causing the fruit to spoil much faster than if kept in the shade.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baaha tsei ni akpa lɛ adɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya ni egbɔjɔɔ loo efeɔ blɛoo. Dɔlɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha muawai kɛ ŋmeii adalɛ baa. Ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya fe bɔ ni akɛtoɔ hulutsoo be mli.

english: Why is it bad to stack harvested fruits tightly in large bags or deep containers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo aduawai ni akpa lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ awo kotokui wuji loo tsɛnsii ni mli kwɔlɔ amli lɛ?

english: When fruits are piled deeply, the ones at the bottom get crushed by the weight. Tightly packed crops also trap heat and moisture produced by the fruits' natural breathing, which creates warm conditions that make the whole pile rot rapidly.
ga: Kɛ́ ato aduawai lɛ anaa shɔŋŋ lɛ, aduawai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ etsiimɔ shishi. Nibii ni aduɔ ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu hiɛɔ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i ni aduawai lɛ adebɔɔ mli mumɔ haa lɛ mli. Enɛ ha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli edɔ ba ni ha ŋtayaa muu lɛ fɛɛ fite oya.

english: Why do my fruits rot much faster when the transport truck travels on a very rough, bumpy road?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya waa kɛ́ tsɔnei ni akɛ nibii yaa lɛ nyiɛ gbɛjegbɛi ni nɔ edɔ ni nɔ edɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Bumping and shaking cause the fruits to hit each other and bruise. Even if the skin does not break, bruised tissue inside the fruit breaks down quickly and creates entry points for rot-causing germs to spread.
ga: Nɔ ni hosoɔ kɛ nɔ ni hosoɔ lɛ haa aduawai lɛ tswaa amɛhe ni amɛshwieɔ shi. Kɛji akɛ hewolo lɛ ekuuu po Shi fãji ni egbo ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ oya ni eji he ni helai ni fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Should I wash my harvested fruits with regular water before sending them to the market?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ nu ni afɔɔ nitsumɔ lɛ afɔ mi-fruit ni mikpa lɛ he dani mikɛmaje jara nɔ?

english: It is usually better not to wash fruits unless you can dry them completely before packing. Wet fruit surfaces encourage mold and bacteria to grow, which shortens how long the crop stays fresh during travel.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooofɔ aduawai lɛ ahe. Ja obaanyɛ ogbi aduawai lɛ kwraa dani okɛwo tsɔne mli. Yibii ni efɔ lɛ woɔ ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Enɛ baaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ yɛ gbɛfaa lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right stage to harvest my mangoes so they last long enough to reach far markets?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male he ni sa ni esa akɛ akpa mi-mango lɛ koni amɛhi shi be kakadaŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛyashɛ jarayeli hei ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Pick mangoes when they are fully grown and mature but still firm and mostly green. If you wait until they turn completely yellow and soft on the tree, they will spoil too fast during travel.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ mango be mli ni edara ni edara shi eyɛ shi shiŋŋ lolo ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ babaoo. Kɛji omɛ kɛyashi tsei lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛfee blɛoo yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ. Ebaafite oya tsɔ yɛ gbɛfaa mli.

english: If one fruit in my harvest basket starts rotting, why does it quickly spoil all the healthy ones around it?
ga: Kɛji aduawai ni yɔɔ mikpamɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ ekome bɔi fitemɔ Mɛni hewɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ ebɔle he lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ, ani efiteɔ oya?

english: A rotting fruit releases mold spores that spread to nearby fruit, and it gives off a natural ripening gas called ethylene that makes surrounding fruits ripen and spoil much faster.
ga: Yibii ni egboi lɛ jieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa yibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli. ni ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. ni haa aduawai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Eshwereɔ ni efiteɔ oya kwraa.

english: Why do fruit flies cause my mangoes to turn watery and rot from the inside out?
