ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai amli ŋmeii miiha mi mangoi lɛ miifee nu ni amɛmiifite kɛmiijɛ mli kɛmiijɛ kpo lɛ?

english: Fruit flies lay tiny eggs under the skin of the fruit. When the eggs hatch into maggots, they feed on the fruit's flesh from the inside, introducing bacteria that turn the inside into soft rot before you even notice on the outside.
ga: Yibii amli ŋmeii fɔɔ wɔji bibii. tso yibii lɛ hewolo shishi Beni ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii Ebaaye tso yibii lɛ loo kɛjɛ mli. Enɛ haa helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ dani oyɔseɔ kponɔgbɛ po.

english: Why do my fruits crack open on the tree just before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ miihoso yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakpa lɛ?

english: Fruit cracking usually happens when there is a long dry spell followed by sudden heavy rain or overwatering. The inside of the fruit takes in water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, aduawai amli fãmɔ baa kɛji hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ eba. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa loo nu babaoo tsɔ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ mligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mligbalamɔ.

english: Why do buyers reject my fruits if they have small scratches or insect marks on the skin?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ kpooɔ mi aduawai lɛ kɛji amɛyɛ ŋmɔlɔ bibii lɛ? Aloo kooloi akadii ni yɔɔ hewolo lɛ nɔ?

english: Even small scratches break the protective outer barrier of the fruit. Buyers know that these small wounds allow rot organisms to enter, meaning those fruits will spoil before they can be sold to final consumers.
ga: Kpoji bibii po baanyɛ afite tso yibii lɛ kponɔgbɛ gbogbo ni buɔ ehe lɛ. Mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ le akɛ pilamɔi bibii Enɛɛmɛi haa nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ boteɔ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nɛkɛ aduawai nɛɛ baafite dani abaahɔɔ aha naagbee mɔ ni yeɔ lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize relies on to grow green and healthy. When nitrogen is low, the plant moves what little it has to the newer upper leaves, causing the older bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa damɔɔ nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ ni efee ŋmɔŋ ni efee hewalɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen lɛ faaa Tso lɛ baajie emli nibii lɛ fioo kɛya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Should I clear the weeds on my farm before or after I apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awo mli loo beni mikɛwo mli sɛɛ?

english: Always clear weeds before applying fertilizer. Weeds grow faster than main crops and will absorb the nutrients from the fertilizer first, leaving your crops hungry and wasting your money.
ga: Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli. Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tso titri lɛ. ni ebaaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii amli klɛŋklɛŋ Hɔmɔ ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛ shika ni efiteɔ

english: What is causing tiny ragged holes in my young maize leaves and small black dirt inside the plant funnel?
ga: Mɛni haa buji bibii baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji diji bibii amli Yɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the central shoot of the maize plant during the day and eat the soft young leaves, leaving behind droppings that look like saw dust.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋmeii lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ baai bibii lɛ Amɛshiɔ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do my tomato flowers keep dropping off without turning into fruit during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry air stress tomato plants, causing their pollen to dry out so flowers cannot be fertilized. When flowers aren't fertilized, the plant drops them to conserve water.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tomato tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa pollen ni egbi lɛ baa. Anyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔmɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ fɔfɔi ko ehiɛɛɛ fɔ Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛto nu.

english: When cassava plants are overcrowded, their root systems compete for the same sunlight, soil water, and nutrients. Giving each cassava stem enough space allows roots room to expand into large tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, shikpɔŋ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome lɛ nɔŋŋ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha cassava tso fɛɛ tso he gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct midday sunlight because their tender leaves scorch easily. Keeping larger shade trees or temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa until their roots fully establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli ejaakɛ amɛbaai bibii lɛ shãa oya. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do crops grown from seeds I saved from last year's hybrid maize produce a smaller harvest than the original seeds I bought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni adu kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli ŋmãa ni akɛfee ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe shishijee dumɔwui ni mihe lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds lose their strong vigor after the first harvest. Planting saved seeds from a hybrid crop results in unpredictable plants that yield much less than the original certified seed.
ga: Hybrid dumɔwui lɛ ahewalɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kpamɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ baa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo kwraa fe shishijee dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ.

english: How do I choose the best suckers from my plantain field to start a new farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mahala tsei ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Look for maiden or sword suckers, which have narrow, spear-shaped leaves and a sturdy base. Avoid broad-leaved suckers because they produce weaker stems and smaller plantain bunches.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii loo klante ŋmeii. Eyɛ baai bibii ni tamɔ lance kɛ shishi ni wa. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsei ni baai lɛ mli lɛɛ he ejaakɛ enɛ baaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee gbɔjɔmɔ kɛ plantain tsei bibii.

english: The very first rain is often followed by a dry spell of hot weather. If you plant too early, seeds will sprout but then scorch and die in the dry soil before the main rains settle in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra fe fɛɛ lɛ nyiɛɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ waa sɛɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi amɛbaashã ni amɛgboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ anɛ.

english: Why is it bad for me to spray water on my vegetable leaves during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ aduawai ahe baai anɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ ehiii kɛha mi lɛ?

english: Watering under hot sun causes rapid evaporation and heat shock to leaves. Wet leaves in hot temperatures also create a humid environment that encourages fungal leaf diseases to spread.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ baaha baai lɛ atsɔ la oya ni ebaaha baai lɛ adɔ fe nine. Baai ni mli efɔ yɛ he ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ lɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa trees turn brown and drop off during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are very sensitive to intense sunlight and dry winds. During the dry season, the trees lose water faster than their small roots can take it up, so they shed leaves to survive. Planting shade crops like plantains or shade trees keeps the soil cool and moist, protecting the young leaves.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ Tsei fiteɔ nu oya fe shishifãi bibii. Akpɛlɛɔ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛshwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛhi shi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ baai bibii ahe

english: Why do my maize plants grow very tall and thin but fail to produce big cobs when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa waa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ shi amɛwooo ŋmeii wuji kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close to each other, the crops end up competing for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. The plants stretch upward to reach light, making them weak and leaving them with very little energy to produce full, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwui baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli kɛ nu fioo Tso lɛ tsɔɔ ehe koni eha la abote mli. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛshiɔ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ koni amɛkɛfee ŋmei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants have huge green leaves but small, thin roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi shishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizers, it spends all its energy growing big foliage above ground instead of storing food in the roots. Loose, well-draining soil and balanced soil nutrients encourage the plant to grow thick tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ebaai wuji lɛ anɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe ni ekɛ niyenii baato eshishifãi lɛ amli. Shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni sa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ bulbs ni mli tse.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences heat stress, dry spells, or a lack of nutrients like calcium. Keeping the soil consistently moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay attached and turn into fruits.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. shihilɛi ni mli egbi loo niyenii mli hewalɛ tamɔ calcium bɛ mli. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ nu wo mli daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛ amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if there is enough soil for everything to grow?
ga: Te jwɛi baaye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji shikpɔŋ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni nɔ fɛɛ nɔ baanyɛ akwɛ̃?

english: Weeds grow faster and are tougher than farmed crops. They aggressively steal water, plant food, and root space from the soil, leaving your main crop hungry and weak even if the farm looks large enough for all plants.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛkɛ ekãa juɔ nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ shishifãi ahe gbɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha onibii titrii lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ. Eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eda bɔ ni sa kɛha tsei srɔtoi fɛɛ moŋ.

english: Black pod is a plant disease caused by a tiny water mold that thrives in dark, damp, and cool conditions. Pruning extra cocoa branches lets sunlight in and helps air dry off the pods, making it harder for the disease to attack.
ga: Black pod ji tso hela ko ni nu mli ŋmeii bibii kɛbaa. Ehiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni jɛmɛ ejɔ. Kɛ́ ofolɔ kookoo niji krokomɛi ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulu la aba mli ni eye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa hela lɛ tutuamɔ waaa.

english: Why should I cut away healthy-looking branches from my pepper bushes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei niji ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛ mi-pepper bush lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-producing side shoots and low branches that suck up energy from the plant. Cutting these off allows the bush to direct all its nutrients and water into growing larger, healthier peppers.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei ni yɔɔ sɛɛ ni wooo yibii kɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni shwieɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afo enɛɛmɛi sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu lɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do seeds saved from my previous maize harvest yield less grain than new certified seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their original vigor and disease resistance over time through cross-pollination. Certified seeds are carefully bred under clean conditions to maintain high yields and strong resistance to local pests.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ laajeɔ amɛ shishijee hewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni be hoɔ yɛ cross-pollination hewɔ. Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli tse mli koni amɛná yibii babaoo ni amɛnyɛ amɛshi he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it a bad idea to plant pepper on the exact same spot on my farm every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ madu ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he kome yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that plant loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the dirt. Rotating pepper with leguminous crops like cowpeas helps replenish nutrients and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Peppers ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ cowpeas tsakeɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ asɛɛkuu lɛ kpaa.

english: Why do my yam vines turn yellow and dry up long before the tubers are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi dani ŋmeii lɛ dara bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Yam vines need healthy green leaves to catch sunlight and make food for the growing tuber below. Vines dry up early when attacked by leaf diseases or when soil lacks moisture; staking vines off the ground keeps leaves healthy so tubers can reach full size.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia baai ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni amɛha niyenii aha ŋmeii ni miida yɛ shishigbɛ lɛ. Wein tso lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji akɛ foliar hela mɔ lɛ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu bɛ. Wein tso lɛ shishifãi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ mli waa bɔni afee ni bulb lɛ anyɛ ada kɛyashɛ egbɔmɔtso lɛ he.

english: Why do my mature maize plants easily fall over whenever strong winds and heavy rain hit my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei ni eda lɛ shwieɔ shi mlɛo be fɛɛ be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa baatswa miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize plants have shallow root systems and become top-heavy when their cobs grow full. High winds can easily push them over if the roots are not firmly supported by heaped soil or if the plants are planted too shallowly.
ga: Abɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni eyɛ tsii kɛji akɛ ŋmei lɛ eda kwraa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ atswa yɛ amɛnɔ oya kɛji akɛ sũ ni abua naa lɛ efiii shishifãi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ loo kɛji akɛ adu tso lɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ.

english: What happens to my cassava tubers if heavy rains cause floodwaters to sit on my farm for several days?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu shwie miŋmɔ lɛ mli gbii babaoo?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water covers the field for too long, oxygen cannot reach the roots, causing the cassava tubers to suffocate, rot, and spoil under the ground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ nu ha ŋmɔji ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Oxygen nyɛɛɛ ashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do the leaves of my young cocoa seedlings turn yellow and dry up during the bright sunny season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct sunlight because their root systems are too small to keep up with water loss. They need shade from taller plants, like plantains, to shield them until they grow stronger.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa ejaakɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ daraaa tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛye nu ni fiteɔ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hɔnɔ ni jɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ plantain lɛ adɛŋ koni ebu amɛhe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight with each other for light, soil nutrients, and water. Instead of building strong stalks and large fruits, they stretch upward as fast as possible just to reach the sunlight.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛbaawuu amɛha la lɛ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ feɔ tsei ni wa kɛ aduawai wuji moŋ. Amɛbaagba amɛhe oya bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need wooden stakes to climb instead of just growing flat on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ he hiaa tso tso ni ekɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu lɛ shikpɔŋ tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to lift their leaves high up toward the sun to make food efficiently, while keeping their leaves off the wet ground where fungal diseases can easily infect them.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kwɔɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu lɛ he koni amɛhoo niyenii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo lɛ

english: Why do my pepper plants drop all their flowers without producing peppers during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ efɔfɔi lɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, pepper plants experience heat stress. To save energy and moisture to survive, the plant naturally sheds its flowers instead of spending resources to grow fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ baaná hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ato koni enyɛ ehi shi. Tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛkɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot when there is too much rain and shade on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ kɛ hulutsoo babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Black pod disease is caused by a tiny fungus that thrives in dark, damp conditions. Too much shade and standing rain keep the pods constantly wet, making it easy for the fungus to multiply and destroy the crop.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛ ŋmei bibioo ko mli. No kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Shade babaoo kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa ŋmeii akɛ amɛaafa ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow in a V-shape while the top leaves stay green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on lower leaves is a sign that your soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send whatever nitrogen is left to the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ amaje ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ.

english: Why does my plantain tree die after producing just one bunch of plantains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tso lɛ gboɔ beni ewo ŋmei kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stem is designed by nature to flower and produce fruit only once. After fruiting, the main stem dies, but it leaves behind smaller shoots (suckers) at the base to grow into new producing stems.
ga: Adebɔɔ ji nɔ ni fee plantain tsei lɛ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ. Kɛ́ ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ yibii titri lɛ gboɔ. Mohu ɔ, a ngmɛɛ tso nyafii (tso ɔmɛ) ngɛ sisi konɛ a wa nɛ a pee tso ehehi.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds fail to come up out of the ground if I bury them deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ ejeee kpo kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mikɛ amɛ fu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ?

english: Seeds carry limited food energy inside them to sprout and reach the surface. If planted too deep, the seed runs out of energy and oxygen before its shoot can break through the soil into the light.
ga: Dumɔwui bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ mli tsɔ lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ hewalɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ fiteɔ dani ŋmei lɛ nyɛɔ eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa la lɛ mli.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wilt and dry up when I plant them in an open field with full sunlight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves and shallow root systems that cannot withstand intense sunlight and heat. Planting temporary shade crops, such as plantains, around young cocoa trees provides them with cool shade and preserves soil moisture until they are mature enough to handle full light.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ gbɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains, yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha hulutsoo be ni mli ejɔ aba ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi kɛyashi tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná la ni fa.

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the crop matures?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani tso lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of a maize plant are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. The plant moves nitrogen from older lower leaves to feed newer growth at the top, which can be fixed by adding compost, manure, or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋmeii heei ni eda yɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ niyenii. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we get heavy rainfall during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in heavy rain because excess water fills the air spaces in flat soil, suffocating the roots and creating a prime environment for soil fungi. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa ejaakɛ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyi kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Planting maize repeatedly in the same soil drains the exact same nutrients every season and allows pests and soil diseases to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts traps nitrogen from the air back into the soil and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ, ebaaná niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ kɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni efo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe sɛɛkuu lɛ mli

english: Why do weeds hurt my young crops so much more than mature plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ mi tsei bibii lɛ awui fe mi tsei ni eda lɛ?

english: Young crops have small roots and few leaves, making them weak competitors for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients against fast-growing weeds. Clearing weeds early gives young plants the uninterrupted resources they need to build strong roots and stems.
ga: Tsei bibii yɛ shishifãi bibii kɛ baai fioo. Enɛ haa efeɔ akaŋshilɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛha hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛha jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa tsei bibii lɛ nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii ni wa.

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the crops to fight one another for light, water, and nutrients, resulting in tall, thin, weak plants with very small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room to spread its roots and produce larger fruits or grains.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye la, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni no haa tsei ni kwɔlɔ, ni yɔɔ mlɛo, ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo fioo pɛ baa lɛ baa. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ teŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛgbɛɔ eshishifãi lɛ eshwaa ni ewoɔ yibii loo dumɔwui wuji.

english: How can I tell if caterpillars are attacking my maize, and what damage do they cause?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji ŋmeii miitutua mi-ŋmei lɛ? Ni mɛɛ fitemɔ amɛfiteɔ?

english: If you see ragged holes in the leaves and powdery, sawdust-like droppings inside the central funnel of the plant, caterpillars like the Fall Armyworm are feeding on it. They eat the growing tip of the plant, which severely stunts growth and reduces overall corn yields.
ga: Kɛji ona buji ni etse ehe yɛ baai lɛ amli kɛ ŋmeii ni tamɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworm lɛ miiye amɛ. Amɛyeɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi, ni no haa amɛdalɛ baa shi waa ni ehaa ŋmãa fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass or leaves on top of the soil around their plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi toɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi amɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ amɛtsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Spreading dry organic materials on the soil surface is called mulching. It acts as a protective blanket that keeps the soil cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly in the heat, and stops weed seeds from receiving sunlight to grow.
ga: Atsɛɔ nibii ni egbi ni akɛshwãa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ latsaa be mli. ni etsĩ jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná hulu la koni amɛdara

english: Black rot on the bottom of tomatoes is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant, often triggered by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently damp helps the roots steadily absorb calcium and prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ akɛ blossom end rot. ni jɛɔ calcium ni bɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ mli baa Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli ni ejaaa lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛya nɔ amɛŋɔ calcium, ni ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: When is the best time for me to apply chemical fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Fertilizer should be applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, typically a few weeks after germination. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn plant roots, while applying it right before heavy rains can wash the nutrients away.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Shi kɛ akɛfata he dani nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaaha niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ baaje mli.

english: Is it safe to use the same chemical spray on my tomatoes that my neighbor uses on his cocoa farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tomato nɔ ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ekoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ baatsu nii?

english: No, different crops require specific chemicals and dosage levels. Agrochemicals made for tree crops like cocoa can burn delicate vegetable crops like tomatoes or leave dangerous chemical residues on food meant for quick consumption.
ga: Dabi, tsei srɔtoi biɔ tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛ bɔ ni esa akɛ akɛtsu nii aha. Agrochemicals ni afee kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ cocoa lɛ baanyɛ ashã aduawai ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ tomato loo amɛshi tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eshwɛ yɛ niyenii mli koni aye oya.

english: Why do some chemical sprays work well on my farm while the same spray damages my brother's crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai komɛi ni akɛshwieɔ mɛi anɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ nɔŋŋ kpata minyɛmi nuu lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Crops react differently based on their variety, soil type, crop age, and application timing. Using the wrong strength or spraying during the heat of the day can burn crops, even if the same chemical works fine under different conditions.
ga: Tsei feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ yɛ srɔtoi, shikpɔŋ henɔ, tso lɛ afii, kɛ be ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Hewalɛ ni esaaa loo tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ ashã. Eyɛ mli akɛ tsofa kome lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi srɔtoi amli moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which plants need to build strong leaves and stalks. Heavy rains can also wash these essential nutrients away from the plant roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni tsei he hiaa koni amɛfee baai kɛ ŋmeii ni mli wa Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu baanyɛ afɔ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ ahe kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli.

english: How can I tell if my soil is tired and needs fertilizer before I plant my yams?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ etse ni ehe miihia ni awo mli ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: If previous crops on the land grew slowly, had pale leaves, or produced very small yields, the soil has lost its nutrients and will need organic manure or fertilizer to support a healthy yam crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tsutsu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dara blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni ebaabi ni akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii koni eye ebua ni sweet potato tso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants have delicate leaves that dry out easily in direct sunlight. Planting shade crops like plantain or shade trees shields young cocoa from harsh heat and keeps moisture in the soil until the cocoa trees mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli lɛ, amɛgbiɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, ni ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛyashi tso lɛ baadara.

english: Why do some of my plantain suckers grow big quickly while others beside them stay weak and small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ ekomɛi miida oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ lolo ni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Suckers grow poorly if they are competing with too many neighboring suckers for light and nutrients, or if the parent plant was infected with soil pests like nematodes that damage the roots.
ga: Suckers lɛ edaŋ jogbaŋŋ kɛji ehe bahia ni amɛkɛ suckers ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ abɔ akaŋ tsɔ koni amɛná la kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ nematodes, ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ emɔ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and humid weather when water stays on the pods for too long without adequate sunlight and airflow.
ga: Enɛ ji black pod hela. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli beni nu ta ŋmɔtɔi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli lɛ.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a destructive pest that hides inside the central growing point of maize plants to feed on tender leaves, which can destroy the crop if not treated early.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji kooloi ni fiteɔ nii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii mra.

english: Why do my cassava leaves curl up, turn pale, and stop growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe, amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni amɛdaraaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, a disease spread by tiny whitefly insects that feed on the sap of the leaves and transfer the virus between plants.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus, ni ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni yeɔ baa mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ amɛshwãa tsei ateŋ

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which forces the plant to focus on growing leaves instead of holding onto flowers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo hao amɛ. Enɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe fɔfɔi.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and drying up in the full sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ hulu la ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to intense direct sunlight and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains around them creates a protective cover that keeps the cocoa leaves cool and moist while the tree is young.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ ehe lɛ haa nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa kookoo baai lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛhe jɔɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei lɛ daraa lolo lɛ baa.

english: Yam vines need direct sunlight on their leaves to generate energy to build big tubers underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground, preventing leaf diseases and allowing the plant to catch maximum sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ hia hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛkɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji. Staking baaye abua ni ajie baai kɛjɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in my young maize leaves and leaving saw-dust like dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ amli lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii tamɔ muji yɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ amli?

english: This is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center whorl of the maize plant during the day and feeds on young leaves. Catching them early with appropriate targeted treatments protects your maize yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ ŋtayaai amli yɛ gbi mli ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Targeted treatments yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ o-corn ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, which happens when the tomato plant cannot get enough calcium or experiences irregular watering while the fruit is growing. Keeping soil moisture consistent and adding compost helps prevent it.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tomato tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo amɛnáaa nu yɛ be fɛɛ mli be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni aaakwɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: How can I tell if my land's soil is too weak to grow healthy crops before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ hewalɛ tsɔ ni enyɛŋ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ dani mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: If previous crops grew slowly, had pale or yellow leaves, or if wild weeds on the plot grow thin and short, your soil is likely low in nutrients and will benefit from animal manure, compost, or fertilizer.
ga: Kɛji tso ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ da blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni tsuɔ loo ŋmɔŋ Aloo kɛji koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni eyɛ kuku Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni obaaná ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe sɛɛ.

english: How does planting groundnuts alongside my maize crop help my farm soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni akɛfataa ŋmãa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which naturally pulls nitrogen gas out of the air and traps it in the soil. Maize uses a lot of nitrogen, so growing groundnuts nearby feeds the soil and helps the maize grow stronger.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi kɛ nitrogen babaoo tsuɔ nii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii ni eye ebua ŋmeii lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Cassava plants drop their leaves naturally when dry weather hits to save water and protect themselves from drought. As long as the stem remains green, the plant is alive and holding its tubers safely underground until the rains return.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ bɛŋkɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hɔmɔ he. Be fɛɛ be ni tso lɛ yitso lɛ baafee eŋɔli lɛ Tso lɛ yɛ wala mli lolo ni akɛ ŋmeii lɛ toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ be mli ni nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Leaving too many small shoots (suckers) forces the mother plantain tree to share its nutrients and water with all of them. Pruning away excess suckers leaves the mother tree strong enough to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii bibii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ dumɔwu nyɛ lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ amɛ fɛɛ aja niyenii kɛ nu. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ aná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii baa.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my planted crops after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ dara oya fe tsei ni midu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds sit dormant in the soil in large numbers and are adapted to sprout and grow immediately when moisture arrives. Clearing weeds early within the crop's first month stops them from stealing sunlight and plant food.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ ehi shi. yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ babaoo Ni ebaatsake ehe koni ekwɛ̃ ni eda kɛji ŋmɔtɔ ba pɛ. Kɛ́ agbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ ni akɛduɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni amɛkaju hulu la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop small insects from destroying my stored maize after I harvest it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi bibii ni fiteɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ naa beni akpa ŋmãa lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Insects like weevils thrive when stored grain still contains moisture. Drying your maize completely in the sun until it is hard, then storing it in airtight containers or hermetic storage bags, cuts off oxygen and stops insects from multiplying.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛji dumɔwui ni ato lɛ tee nɔ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli kɛyashi ebaawa. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛwo tsɛnsi ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo vacuum ni akɛtoɔ nibii ahe lɛ mli. Efoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ mli lɛ mli ni ehaaa kooloi afɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen. Heavy rains can wash this key nutrient out of the soil, so applying a light dose of fertilizer or well-rotted manure gives the plants the nutrients they need to grow green and produce large ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ nɛkɛ niyenii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii agboi.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have tiny nodes on their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and turn it into plant food in the soil. When the crop is harvested, that extra plant food remains in the ground to nourish the next crop, such as maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ nodes bibii. yɛ shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa efeɔ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ Beni akpaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Nakai tsei niyenii ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings cannot survive under direct, harsh sunlight and high heat. They need temporary shade crops like plantains or leftover timber trees to protect their leaves from drying out while their root systems develop.
ga: Cocoa tsei nyɛŋ ahi shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa shishi. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo tsei ni eshwɛ. Enɛ buɔ baai lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Plantain trees do not have deep taproots; their root system spreads out close to the surface. When the soil becomes soaked and soft, the shallow roots struggle to hold up the heavy trunk and heavy fruit bunches during strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ bɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ. Amɛshishifãi lɛ shɛɔ he ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ lɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛmɔ tsei ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii amli yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa be mli.

english: Cassava tubers need air in the soil to stay healthy. When excess rainwater sits on the farm without proper drainage, water fills the air gaps in the soil, suffocating the roots and causing underground fungus to rot the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Beni nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hiɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu ni hoɔ jogbaŋŋ bɛ mli. Nu baawo kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off before any fruits start to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miiho dani aduawai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when tiny pests like thrips feed on the flower stems. Keeping the soil consistently moist and treating pests early helps the plant set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips yeɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ajiemɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwoɔ yibii

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are typically caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or mites, which can also spread plant viruses. Spraying the crop early with neem oil or soapy water keeps these pests from draining the plant's sap.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo mites ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. ni baanyɛ agbɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ashwã tsei amli hu Ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ mra Neem fɔ loo nu ni akɛ samla tsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ akajie nu ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ.

english: How do I know when my cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready for picking?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-kookoo lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ ajie lɛ?

english: Cocoa pods change color clearly when they are ripe: green pods turn bright yellow, while red or purple pods turn orange-yellow. Harvesting pods only when fully ripe ensures the beans inside have developed proper sweet mucilage for successful fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe yɛ gbɛ ni kadiɔ mɔ nɔ beni amɛshwereɔ lɛ. Pods eŋɔli lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse. yɛ be mli ni pods tsuru loo purple lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ-ŋmei. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmeii lɛ beni amɛshwere kwraa pɛ lɛ, no haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ mli ŋmeii ni ŋɔɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ omanye lɛ yɔɔ mli.

english: Why does my harvested maize turn moldy in storage even after I dry it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele ni mikpaa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ, kɛ́ migbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli po lɛ?

english: Maize grains often feel dry on the surface while still holding moisture deep inside the cob or core. Storing grains in airtight bags before they are completely dried allows trapped moisture to create sweat, causing mold and attracting grain borers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa ŋmeii lɛ nuɔ he akɛ amɛgbi yɛ amɛhiɛ yɛ be mli ni amɛhiɛɔ nu mli lolo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli loo amɛmligbɛ. Dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ vacuum kotokui amli dani amɛgbiɔ kwraa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ni emɔ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni egbalaa dumɔwui ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal sunlight, growing space, and soil nutrients before your crop roots can reach them. Clearing weeds within the first few weeks gives your crops full access to the water and nutrients they need.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, he ni amɛdaraa, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shɛɔ amɛhe. Kɛ́ ogbe jwɛi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha otsei lɛ aná nu kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight. Without shade from larger trees like plantain or forest trees, the sun scorches their leaves and dries up the moisture in the soil, causing the seedlings to turn yellow and die.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ tsei wuji tamɔ plantains loo kooi amli hulutsoo bɛ lɛ hulu lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli egbiɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: When maize plants are crowded together, they have to fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves them weak and thin, producing small or empty cobs instead of healthy, large corn.
ga: Beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ eyi amɛhe obɔ lɛ Esa akɛ amɛye akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa amɛgbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe feɔ shoo. ni kɛ ŋmei bibioo loo efolo baa Yɛ ŋmei agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ

english: Leaf curling in cassava is usually caused by the Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny insects called whiteflies. It prevents the plant from making food properly, which reduces the size of the cassava tubers under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mosaic hela lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmei baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whitefly lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafee niyenii jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ ayibɔ aba shi.

english: How do I know if my soil needs fertilizer before I plant my vegetables?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu aduawai?

english: If your previous crops grew slowly, had pale yellow leaves, or produced small harvests, your soil is likely low in nutrients. Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which plants need to grow green and strong.
ga: Kɛji oŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ dara blɛoo Eyɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. loo ewoɔ nibii fioo Ekolɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ hu faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji nɔ ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, usually caused by irregular watering, extreme heat, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the flowers stay on the plant and form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Maize removes a lot of nutrients from the soil. Groundnuts and beans are legumes that put nitrogen back into the soil naturally through their roots, restoring fertility for your next crop without buying expensive fertilizers.
ga: Abɛi gbalaa niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni kɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi anɔ. Ye obua ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aku sɛɛ aba oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli ni ehe ehiaaa ni ohé ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why do the leaves of my yam plants dry up early before the yams are big enough to harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya dani sweet potato lɛ daraa bɔ ni sa ni abaanyɛ akpa lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam leaves is often caused by a fungal disease called anthracnose. It destroys the green leaves that feed the growing yam tubers underground, resulting in very small yams.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ anthracnose lɛ kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Efiteɔ baai eŋɔli ni fiɔ sweet potato ŋmeii ni adu yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ faaa kwraa.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and stronger than my main crops during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants adapted to survive harsh conditions, so they absorb rain and soil nutrients much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing food and water from your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni atsake amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. No hewɔ lɛ, amɛheɔ nugbɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛjiemɔ mra Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ onibii amli.

english: A plantain bunch is ready when the individual fruits become plump and full, the sharp corners on the fingers become rounded, and the top leaves of the plant start turning yellow naturally.
ga: Plantains kuu ko efee klalo kɛ́ aduawai lɛ eko fɛɛ eko etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ niji lɛ anɔ lɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Ni tso lɛ yiteŋ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Those holes and powder are caused by maize weevils, small insects that eat into dry grains. Storing your well-dried maize in airtight hermetic bags suffocates the insects and protects your grain from damage.
ga: Buu kɛ sũ lɛ jɛ ŋmei ŋmeii, ni ji kooloi bibii ni yeɔ dumɔwui ni egbi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ agbɔjɔ, ni ebaabu ŋmãa lɛ he koni ekafite.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow green and strong. The plant moves nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the new top growth, causing the bottom leaves to turn yellow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momoi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi dalɛ hee lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: Why does my groundnut farm produce pods that are completely empty inside when I harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-peanut ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ́ mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Empty groundnut pods, often called 'pops,' happen when the soil lacks calcium during the time the pods are forming underground. Groundnuts need calcium directly from the damp soil around the pods to fill the nuts properly.
ga: Peanut ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ nɔ ko, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ lɛ 'pops' lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ calcium yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Calcium he miihia ŋmeii ni jɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ. pods koni akɛ calcium awo dumɔwui lɛ amli

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, which is a fungus that spreads quickly in damp, shaded conditions during heavy rains. The fungus attacks the pod skin, turning it black and destroying the beans inside if the pods are not removed quickly.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ hela nɛɛ baa ji black pod disease, ni ji ŋmei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni edɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Fungus tutuaa pod lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛji ajieee ŋmeii lɛ oya.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and dry up during the daytime even when the soil has plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ trukaa ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ moŋ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil sickness where microscopic germs block the water-carrying tubes inside the plant's stem. Because water cannot travel up to the leaves, the plant wilts in the heat of the day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. aloo shikpɔŋ nɔ helai ni helai bibii waa tsiɔ paipii ni kɛ nu yaa yɛ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu nyɛɛɛ aya baai lɛ anɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei gboɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat, very dry air, or too much water around their roots. When stressed, the plant saves its energy by dropping blossoms instead of spending energy on growing fruits.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi waa, loo nu babaoo ni bɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ hao amɛ. Tsei kɛ hewalɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite hewalɛ ni amɛkɛduɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow short, crooked, and small instead of long and smooth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ kukuji, amɛhe ejɔ, ni amɛfeɔ bibii moŋ fe ni amɛaafee kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yams become crooked and small when the soil under them is too hard or full of rocks, preventing the tuber from expanding downward easily. Making high, soft mounds or ridges gives the yam soft soil so it can grow straight and large.
ga: Sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ kɛyaa shishi mlɛo. Kɛ́ afee gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aná shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo bɔni afee ni amɛdara tɛ̃ɛ ni amɛdara.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I plant cassava on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ kɛji midu ŋmei yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi lɛ?

english: Cassava heavy feeds on nutrients in the soil over time. Planting it in the same place every year completely drains the soil of food and allows cassava-specific pests and diseases to build up in the field, leading to smaller harvests each year.
ga: Cassava baaye niyenii babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ be ni sa mli. Dumɔ yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be Afi lɛ baajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ kwraa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmei pɔtɛɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits around the roots in flat or heavy clay fields, the roots suffocate and rot, which is why planting on raised mounds or ridges helps water drain away.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baafo ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni dumɔwui yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ kwɔlɔ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why should I keep dry crop leaves on top of my soil instead of burning them off?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe baai ni egbi lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ moŋ fe ni mashã amɛ lɛ?

english: Leaving dry leaves on the soil acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during hot days, prevents weeds from sprouting, and breaks down into natural food for your next crop.
ga: Baai ni egbi ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or soybeans on my farm make the soil better for my next maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo soybeans ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and soybeans have friendly microscopic organisms in their roots that pull nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil. When the legumes finish growing, that trapped nitrogen stays in the soil to feed the next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ soybeans yɛ nibii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe feɔ naanyo yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ legume tsei lɛ egbe naa lɛ Nakai nitrogen ni aŋã lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha tsei ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do crops on one spot of my land keep getting sick while crops on another spot of the same farm stay healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ko lɛ hela mɔ amɛ lɛ? Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni adu yɛ hei krokomɛi yɛ ŋmɔ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ lolo.

english: Soil conditions and water drainage vary across a farm. Damp areas with poor drainage or hidden plant debris allow fungal and bacterial diseases to linger in the ground long after old crops are gone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kɛ nu ni hoɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi. Hei ni nu hoɔ yɛ ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli jogbaŋŋ loo tsei amli ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ baaha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ bacteria helai ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ beni tsei momoi lɛ etee lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why does plant disease stay in my soil even after I cut down and clear all the infected trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai hiɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mifoɔ tsei fɛɛ ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni mijieɔ amɛ kɛjɛɔ mli lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases produce microscopic spores that hide in the dirt or decaying roots for months or years, waiting to infect new healthy roots planted in the same spot.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo haa ŋmeii bibii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ shikpɔŋ loo shishifãi ni egboi amli nyɔji loo afii babaoo lɛ baa. Mɛɛ ni shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni adu yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ aná hela.

english: What simple steps can I take to stop cocoa tree diseases from spreading across my farm?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mafee nibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mɛni mafee koni cacao hela akagbɛ eshwa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ?

english: Regularly clean your cutlasses and pruning tools after treating sick trees, cut away infected pods immediately, and keep weeds low so humidity doesn't build up around the tree trunks.
ga: Tsumɔ ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni akɛfoɔ tsei lɛ ahe daa kɛ́ otsa tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ sɛɛ. Kpɔ̃ɔ pods ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Ni ha jwɛi lɛ ahi shi bɔni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ akabua amɛhe naa. tso shishi

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and rot right on the tree before they mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is typically Black Pod disease, a fast-spreading fungal infection caused by heavy rain, high humidity, and damp shade that traps moisture on the pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, eji black pod hela. ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, kɛ hulutsoo ni mli edɔ ni mɔ̃ɔ hulutsoo yɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: My young cocoa trees started growing very fast, but why are their leaves suddenly turning yellow and dropping?
ga: Mi cacao tso bibioo lɛ bɔi dalɛ oya waa, shi mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ trukaa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ?

english: Young trees burn through energy fast. If direct sun gets too strong, water becomes scarce, or nutrients run out in the soil, the plant sheds leaves to protect itself from dying.
ga: Tsei bibii shãa hewalɛ oya. Kɛji hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, nu baafee nɔ ni faaa loo niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baaho. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ gbele he.

english: Why is shade so important for my young cocoa trees during their first few years in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulutsoo he hiaa mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni amɛyɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa leaves are delicate and their roots are shallow. Temporary shade trees like plantains protect them from harsh sunlight and keep the surrounding air and soil moist.
ga: Kookoo baai bibii lɛ yɛ mlɛo ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tso lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: How can I tell if my tree stopped growing because of a disease or simply because it lacks rain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ ekpa dalɛ yɛ hela hewɔ loo nugbɔ ni enɛɛɛ kɛkɛ hewɔ?

english: Drought makes all leaves wilt evenly and turn brown at the tips, whereas diseases usually cause localized dark spots, swollen stems, distorted leaf patterns, or rotting pods.
ga: Hɔmɔ haa baai lɛ fɛɛ shwieɔ shi pɛpɛɛpɛ ni baai lɛ ashishigbɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ. yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ hela lɛ haa ŋmeii ni tsuɔ diŋ, ŋmeii ni efuu, baai ni etsake, loo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ baa.

english: As a woman starting out in cocoa farming in Ghana, what basic practices will help me get a good yield?
ga: Ákɛ yoo ni jeɔ kookoo ŋmɔ shishi yɛ Ghana lɛ Mɛni ji shishijee nifeemɔi komɛi ni baaye abua mi ni mawo yibii?

english: Focus on good spacing when planting, establish shade using plantains, weed regularly, prune dead branches for better air circulation, and harvest pods promptly when ripe.
ga: Kɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ nɔ kɛ́ oodu nii. Kɛtsɔ plantains nɔ afee hulutsoo. Jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ kɛjɛ ohe daa. Kpɔ̃ɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli jogbaŋŋ. Ni okpa ŋmeii lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to ask community elders about the history of our farmland before planting cocoa?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi woɔ akutsoŋ onukpai lɛ hewalɛ ni abi wɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ahe yinɔsane dani adu kookoo lɛ?

english: Elders often remember past weather patterns, historical pest outbreaks, and which spots on the land have traditionally struggled with disease or flooding.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, onukpai kaiɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni eho lɛ. Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni eho ni eho Ni mɛɛ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ehe ebahia ni ekɛ helai loo nu afua akpe?

english: Can infected cocoa trees recover on their own if I leave them untreated on the farm?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baanyɛ aná hewalɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ? Kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni atsaaa amɛ

english: Major cocoa diseases in Ghana like Swollen Shoot or Black Pod do not heal naturally; leaving infected plants in place allows the disease to spread to nearby healthy trees.
ga: Anyɛɛɛ atsa kookoo helai ni he hiaa yɛ Ghana, tamɔ ŋmeii ni efu loo ŋmeii ni efee diŋ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ́ ashi tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela lɛ agbɛ ashwã tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted manure restores their healthy green color and helps them grow taller.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ akwɛ̃ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔji lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ ni eye ebua amɛ ni amɛdara.

english: What is eating holes in my corn leaves and leaving tiny dark dirt inside the center of the plants?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu yɛ mi ŋmãa baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji fioo ko ni tsuɔ nii? Okɛwo tso lɛ teŋ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest in Ghana that burrows into the center of young corn plants. Applying recommended crop sprays or natural neem oil mixtures early on helps protect your farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ. Nibii ni akɛshwieɔ tsei anɔ loo adebɔɔ mli neem fɔ ni akɛfutuɔ nii lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii mra. Ebaaye ebua ni ebu oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the weather is too hot and dry, or when the plant lacks sufficient water and nutrients. Giving the plants consistent water and applying fertilizer rich in phosphorus helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni edɔ. aloo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nɔ nu daa ni akɛ tsofa ni fɔsfɔs babaoo yɔɔ mli wo mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to full, direct sunlight and lose water quickly. Planting shade crops like plantains nearby creates a cool environment that shields cocoa seedlings until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa, ni nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya. Shade tsei tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ haa shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashiɔ amɛhe waa.

english: Is it bad if I plant my seeds very close together so I can get more crops on my field?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too closely forces crops to compete with each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants and smaller yields. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and grow fully.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni edaa jogbaŋŋ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows plant pests to build up in the field. Swapping maize with beans or groundnuts restores soil richness and breaks pest cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa tsake ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ ni ebaaku tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ amli.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans helps the soil grow other crops better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni aduɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛo koni akɛdu tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a family of plants that naturally take nitrogen from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This acts as a natural fertilizer that feeds future crops planted on that land.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji tsei aweku ko ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛjieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when trapped in waterlogged soil because they need air to breathe. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows excess rainwater to flow away from the roots, keeping them safe.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli ejaakɛ kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia amɛ koni amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe. koni akɛto he shweshweeshwe

english: Why does the soil on my farm dry out and crack so quickly under the sun after it rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni egbɛɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Bare soil loses moisture fast when exposed to direct sunlight and wind. Covering the ground around your plants with dried grass or leaves—a method called mulching—keeps the soil cool and locks in water for longer.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ lɛ fiteɔ nu oya kɛji akɛ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ he lɛ nɔ. Atsɛɔ gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsuɔ he nii lɛ akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow so much faster and stronger than the food crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe niyenii tsei ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants naturally suited to survive harsh soil conditions and steal water and crop food quickly. Clearing weeds early in the season ensures your crops receive the light and nutrients they need to grow strong.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ amɛhi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ ni amɛjuɔ nu kɛ tsei aniyenii oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ be lɛ mli mra lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná la kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds in the exact same planting hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui etɛ loo ejwɛ yɛ ŋmãa dumɔ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When too many maize seeds are planted in one hole, the growing stalks fight each other for water, sunlight, and soil food. Spacing them out allows each stalk to grow strong and produce large, full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa dumɔwui babaoo yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ŋmãa ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ baaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko ada waa ni ewo ŋmeii wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Leaf rolling is a crop's natural way of saving water during intense heat. By rolling up, the leaf reduces its exposed surface area to prevent moisture from evaporating into the hot air.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu toɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ. kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ Baai lɛ haa he ni ajie lɛ kpo lɛ baa shi koni ŋmɔtɔ akatsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava bushes twisting and turning pale yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Twisted and yellowing cassava leaves are usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies sucking on the leaves. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stems prevents this crop damage.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Cassava Mosaic Virus lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ cassava baai ni etsake ni etsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa, ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa. Kasava tsei ni afee amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ baaye abua ni akafite nɛkɛ ŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ.

english: Yams need soft, loose soil to expand easily under the ground. High mounds keep the soil loose, improve water drainage so the tubers do not rot, and give the yams space to grow long and thick.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse bɔni afee ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi oya. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ koni bulbs lɛ akafite. ni oha ŋmɔtɔ lɛ afee kakadaŋŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Tomato blossoms drop off when the plant suffers from sudden dry spells, extreme heat, or lack of soil nutrients. Regular watering at the base and applying balanced fertilizer keep the flowers attached until fruit sets.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi trukaa, latsaa ni naa wa, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ daa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja lɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ kɛ aduawai lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper bushes grow lots of leafy green branches but very few peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper bush lɛ yɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ baai eŋɔli babaoo shi pepper fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them grow leaves instead of fruits. Switching to a fertilizer richer in phosphorus and potassium encourages the plant to form abundant flower buds and pepper pods.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ akwɛ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ. Kɛ́ otsake kɛtee ŋmɔshi nibii ni phosphorus kɛ potassium babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaawo tsei lɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do my rice seeds fail to sprout if I sow them right before a short dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ kwɛɛɛ kɛji midu amɛ dani be kukuoo ko ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Rice seeds need continuous moisture in the topsoil to break open and germinate. If the soil dries out after sowing, the seed goes dormant, dies, or gets eaten by birds before the heavy rains return.
ga: Omɔ dumɔwui he miihia ni nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi yɛ dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baaya wɔɔhe, amɛbaagboi loo okpoi baaye amɛ dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa seedlings turning yellow and dropping to the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves on young cocoa trees usually point to a lack of nitrogen in the soil or insufficient shade cover. Adding organic compost around the plant base helps restore nutrients and keeps the leaves green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ cacao tsei bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ŋmɔlɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Organic compost ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni eye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi ŋmɔŋ.

english: How can I tell underground cassava roots are fully grown and ready to harvest?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole kɛji akɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava is ready when lower leaves naturally turn yellow and drop, leaving a bare stem, and the ground around the root base begins to crack as the expanding tubers push the soil upward.
ga: Yucca efee klalo beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgbee shi lɛ. ni eshiɔ tso ni nɔ ko bɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛgbalaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni mli lɛɛɔ lɛ tsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for leaf growth. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the ground too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-abele tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ho niyenii mli nibii lɛ kɛtee loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot on my farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ he kome yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop over and over drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Switching to crops like groundnuts or beans helps put nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do I need to plant plantain suckers near my young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains yɛ mi-kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under the hot sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity young cocoa needs to survive its early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa kookoo bibii koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they end up fighting each other for sunlight, water, and plant food in the soil. This leads to thin, weak stems and very small or empty cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ tsei niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii waa loo nɔ ko bɛ mli baa.

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves keeps the soil cool under the hot sun, prevents water from evaporating quickly, stops weeds from growing, and adds good plant food to the dirt as it rots.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya Ehaa jwɛi shwereɔ ni ekɛ tsei niyenii kpakpa fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he beni egboɔ lɛ.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy. When heavy rain sits on the farm without draining away, it drowns the roots and encourages soil fungus to attack and rot the tubers.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu lɛ efooo Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu mli ni ewo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ni amɛha ŋmeii lɛ agbo.

english: What causes small worms to hide inside the leaf funnels of my maize plants and eat them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii bibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ baai amli ni amɛyeɔ amɛ?

english: That damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm. The parent moth lays eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl deep inside the plant's funnel where it is moist to feed on the tender young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai anɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nakai fitemɔ lɛ baa. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Amɛshwereɔ kɛboteɔ tsei ni mli efɔ lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, dry soil, or a lack of insects to move pollen around. When stressed, the plant drops its flowers to save energy rather than trying to feed growing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo kooloi ni bɛ ni baanyɛ ajie pollen lɛ kɛya he fɛɛ he lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛji haomɔ ba Tsei baashwie fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooobɔ mɔdɛŋ ni oha tomato ni miida lɛ niyenii

english: Why do weeds cause my crops to stay small and weak even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ bibioo ni egbɔjɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ jogbaŋŋ moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than main crops and aggressively steal sunlight, moisture, and soil nutrients. Even with good rainfall, the weeds end up drinking most of the water and food before your crops can reach it.
ga: Jwɛi daa oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, fɛ̃i kɛ niyenii kpakpai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli waa. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ miinɛ moŋ, shi ehi. Shi jwɛi lɛ hu nuɔ nu kɛ niyenii lɛ babaoo dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yashɛɔ jɛmɛ.

english: Why is it better for me to put fertilizer on my farm when the ground is damp rather than dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? He ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ fe shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ?

english: Crop roots can only drink in fertilizer after it has dissolved in water. Applying fertilizer to dry ground means it will sit unused on top of the dirt or can even burn the roots if the heat is too strong.
ga: Tso shishifãi baanyɛ anu ŋmɔshi nibii kɛji etsɔ nu mli pɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ kɛji latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ.

english: Why do tomatoes grow so naturally well in our Ghanaian soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomatoi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ wɔ Ghana shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ?

english: Tomatoes thrive in warm sunlight, moderate humidity, and well-draining soil rich in organic matter, which are natural environmental conditions found in many parts of Ghana.
