ga: Tomato daa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i ni fa fioo kɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli babaoo yɔɔ mli. Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli shihilɛ ko ni anaa yɛ Ghana hei babaoo.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato leaves curl and turn yellow when the plant gets heat-stressed or lacks enough water, as it tries to reduce moisture loss to protect itself.
ga: Tomato baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ latsaa mli loo nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ ehe. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tomatoi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛha ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe.

english: Flowers drop off when temperatures get too high, water is inconsistent, or the soil lacks nutrients, which prevents proper pollination and fruit set.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Nu lɛ ejaaa. loo shikpɔŋ ni niyenii mli nibii bɛ mli Enɛ tsiɔ pollination kɛ yibiiwoo ni sa naa.

english: Why do the skins of my tomatoes crack open just as they start to turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato hewoloi lɛ tswaa kɛ́ amɛbɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes crack when there is sudden heavy watering or rainfall after a dry period, causing the inside of the fruit to expand faster than the skin can stretch.
ga: Tomato baagbala kɛ nu ni mli wa loo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa tso yibii lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni hewolo lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ he.

english: Why do my tomato plants have big bushy green leaves but very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni ebɔle ehe shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes the plant focus all its energy on growing thick leaves instead of producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai ni mli tse ni miida lɛ he nii. Mohu ɔ, e woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ yiblii.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over onto the ground as they get bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are naturally weak and cannot hold heavy fruits on their own, so they need wooden stakes or sticks for support to stay upright and prevent disease.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛjɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ aduawai ni tsii. by yourself No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ tomatoi aná tsei loo tsei ni baaha amɛhi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛtsi helai anaa.

english: How can I tell if small pests are attacking my tomato plants early on?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji kooloi bibii miitutua mi-tomato tsei lɛ mra?

english: Check under the leaves for tiny insects, fine webs, or small spots on the stems, which are early signs of pests eating the plant before noticeable damage occurs.
ga: Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi kɛji kooloi bibii, ŋmeii bibii, loo ŋmeii yɛ tsei lɛ ashishi. Enɛɛmɛi ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ kooloi emɔ mɔ ko dani nɔ ko ni kadiɔ mɔ lɛ baafite.

english: How do I know if my harvested tomatoes are good enough to sell to a processing factory?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ tomato ni mikpa lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ aha nitsumɔhe ko ni feɔ nibii nɛɛ?

english: Factories look for firm, fully red, uniform tomatoes without bruises, cracks, or rot, because clean fruit produces better paste and lasts longer.
ga: Nitsumɔhei taoɔ tomato ni wa, ni tsuɔ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebɛ ŋmɔlɔ, ni egbɛ eshwaaa loo egbooo, ejaakɛ aduawai ni he tse lɛ woɔ ŋmɔlɔ ni ehiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do so many of my harvested tomatoes rot quickly while being transported to the market?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato ni mikpaa lɛ babaoo fiteɔ oya beni mikɛyaa jara nɔ lɛ?

english: Stacking delicate tomatoes loosely in heavy crates under direct sunlight causes heat buildup and crushing, which speeds up spoiling.
ga: Tomato paste ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ato he gbɛjianɔ yɛ adekai ni tsii amli yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaaha dɔlɛ aba ni ebaakumɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni efite oya.

english: Is tomato farming a good choice for young people who are new to farming?
ga: Ani tomato okwaayeli ji gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha oblahii kɛ oblayei ni jeɔ okwaayeli shishi kɛkɛ?

english: Yes, tomato crops mature quickly in about three months, meaning with basic training and care, young farmers can see quick income returns on their hard work.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tomato tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ kɛtsɔ shishijee tsɔsemɔ kɛ nɔkwɛmɔ nɔ lɛ, okwaafoi oblahii kɛ oblayei baanyɛ ana sɛɛnamɔi ni jɛɔ amɛnitsumɔ ni wa lɛ mli baa oya.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning yellow and pale instead of staying dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, which is essential plant food, or that excessive rain is washing nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ. Aloo, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ miifɔ niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ ahe.

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when temperatures get too high, when water supply is inconsistent, or when the soil lacks phosphorus to help set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Beni nu ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ ejaaa loo be mli ni fɔsfɔs bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni baaye abua ni ewo yibii

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall in one section of my field but staying small and weak in another?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miida babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ fã lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi eji bibioo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ he kroko.

english: Soil fertility varies across a field, meaning parts with poor, rocky, or washed-away topsoil hold fewer nutrients and less water for crop roots.
ga: Esoro bɔ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baa nii jogbaŋŋ ehaa lɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hei ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ ehiii, ni tɛi yɔɔ nɔ, loo ni nu efo mli lɛ baahiɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fioo kɛ nu fioo kɛha tsei shishifãi.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads fast in dark, damp, and overly shaded farm conditions with little air movement.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli ewo duŋ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli, ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni kɔɔyɔɔ hu faaa mli lɛ amli.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly and stop producing new shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ekpaa ŋmeii heei ni ekwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies, which damage the leaves and transmit viruses to the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ekɛ hela lɛ yaa tso lɛ mli

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects in the soil without draining, allowing waterborne fungal diseases to attack and decompose the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni nu kɛbaa lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ ni efiteɔ amɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other for sunlight, soil moisture, and nutrients, leaving none of them strong enough to produce a full yield.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli nibii, ni eshiuuu tsei ni he wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ awo yibii ni fa lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops look sickly even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni hela mɔ amɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ enɛ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster than most crops and aggressively steal the nutrients, water, and sunlight that your crops need to stay healthy.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei babaoo ni amɛjuɔ niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do I get a smaller harvest every year if I keep planting maize on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɛɛ yibiiwoo nɔ daa afi kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving it time to recover, while also allowing pests and soil diseases to build up.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaaa lɛ be ni ekɛbaatsu nii ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekɛ kooloi kɛ helai aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why does fertilizer not help my crops when I spread it right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii eyeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ midu nii dani nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes fertilizer away off the surface of the soil before the crop roots have time to drink it in, wasting the fertilizer.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni afiteɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and keeping the soil moist so the young cocoa can survive its first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha hulutsoo ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ ji koni kookoo bibii lɛ anyɛ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to spread their leaves to the sunlight. Sunlight helps the leaves create energy, which flows down to build bigger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tso lɛ ji wain tso ni esa akɛ ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni eha ebaai lɛ aje kpo yɛ hulu la mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ hewalɛ ni hoɔ kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is running out of nitrogen. Maize needs nitrogen to build strong stalks and large cobs, so adding organic manure or fertilizer early in the season fixes this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ efo. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Always plant cassava cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky. If planted upside down, the stems struggle to grow upright and produce fewer, smaller tubers.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei niji ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji akɛ adu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Tso lɛ tso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ekwɛ shi shiŋŋ ni ekɛ bulbs bibii fioo aba.

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants compete for light, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants and a low harvest.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmaa fioo ko baa.

english: Maize uses up a lot of nutrients from the ground. Crops like beans and groundnuts take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring its fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Eheɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni akɛ adebɔɔ mli fɔmɔ aba ekoŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli

english: Why should I cover the soil around my vegetable beds with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-vegetables tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves, known as mulching, stops the hot sun from evaporating water, keeps the roots cool, and prevents weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛ baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ebaaye ebua ni nu akajɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my seeds fail to grow even though I planted them right after the first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ?

english: The very first rain often moistens only the top layer of soil, which quickly dries out in the heat. If a seed absorbs water once and then completely dries out, the plant embryo inside dies.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni egbiɔ oya kɛji akɛ edɔ lɛ Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ shwie nu shikome pɛ lɛ no lɛ amɛgbi kwraa. Tso lɛ mli fɔmɔ kotoku lɛ baagbo.

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the plant sap, or by a virus. Spraying with neem water can help drive away these small insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso mli nu loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Neem nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ashwie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, irregular watering, or lack of calcium in the soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps flowers set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao. Nu ni akɛhaaa be fɛɛ be loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to grow green and strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure around the plants helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni etsɔ eŋɔli ni ehe wa. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ NPK loo kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ ni akɛbaabɔle Tsei ahe lɛ baaye abua ni atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants bloom with plenty of flowers, but the flowers keep falling off without growing into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛwooo yibii?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the air gets too hot, when watering is uneven, or when insects do not visit to move pollen around. Keeping the soil evenly moist and planting flowers nearby to attract pollinators helps the fruit set.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Kɛji nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ gbɛjianɔtoo mli loo be mli ni kooloi baaa koni amɛbajie pollen kɛjɛ fɔfɔi amli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ koni egbala pollenbii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa aduawai lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he.

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and burn under direct harsh sunlight. Planting plantain trees alongside your young cocoa creates living shade umbrellas that keep the seedlings cool and moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa yɛ hulu la shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Plantains ni akɛ cocoa bibii duɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni haa dumɔwui lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe feɔ fɛ̃i kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛhe waɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does spreading dry grass over the ground around my garden crops help them during hot dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni mikɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ mibɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: Covering the dirt with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, acts like a blanket. It shields the dirt from direct sun, keeps water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the crop roots cool.
ga: Jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli, ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ muji ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ akafo oya. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i

english: Cassava roots rot when rainwater settles around them in flat, heavy soil without draining. Planting cassava stems on top of raised earth mounds or ridges allows excess water to drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ ebɔle amɛhe. Yɛ hei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ hei ni tsii ni nu hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ lɛ Kasava tsei ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji loo ŋshɔkei anɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Groundnuts and cowpeas are special plants that pull natural fertilizer from the air and put it back into the earth, helping restore soil nutrients for your next crop.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa niyenii mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ baa ekoŋŋ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes inside my young corn leaves and leaving brown sawdust-like dirt in the middle of the plant?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ amli ni eshiɔ muji ni tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ.

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, a common pest that hides deep inside the corn leaves. Applying recommended neem leaf extract or approved insecticides early into the top whorl stops them.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii, ni ji ŋmeii ni afɔɔ namɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa baai amli shɔŋŋ lɛ. Akɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ tsu nii mra. Yaa shi kɛya ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ nɔ koni okpa amɛ.

english: How do weeds hurt my main crop even when they are not touching each other?
ga: Te jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔ titri lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛji amɛtaaa amɛhe po?

english: Weeds steal food and water from the dirt beneath the surface where you cannot see, and their roots choke out crop roots. Removing weeds early leaves all the soil nutrients and moisture for your crops to grow.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ muji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi ni onyɛɛɛ ona lɛ mli. Ni amɛshishifãi lɛ fiteɔ tsei ashishifãi. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ebaajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔtɔ fɛɛ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Plantain roots do not grow very deep in the ground, making the tree top-heavy once fruit appears. Propping up the fruiting stem with a strong, bamboo or wooden fork stick supports the weight so wind cannot push it down.
ga: Plantain shishifãi lɛ eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yiteŋ tsiiɔ kɛ́ aduawai lɛ pue. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmei loo tso ni wa ŋmɛ tso yibii lɛ tso lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni efi muji lɛ sɛɛ koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ akatsi lɛ kɛba shi.

english: Why do I need to put long wooden sticks into the ground for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ awo shikpɔŋ koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need plenty of sunlight on their leaves to make big tubers underground. Staking raises the foliage into the air where it gets maximum sun and stays dry, protecting the leaves from rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ bulbs wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli, ni amɛnáa hulu la ni fa fe fɛɛ ni ehaa amɛgbiɔ. Ebuɔ baai ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii ahe.

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves and thin bark that dry out easily under intense heat. Planting temporary shade crops like plantain alongside them provides the necessary humidity and sun protection until the cocoa trees grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ amɛhewolo ni mli tseee ni gbɛ́ɔ oya yɛ latsaa ni naa wa shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains, kɛfata tsei nɛɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulutsoo hebuu aba kɛyashi be mli ni cacao tsei lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do wild animals and rodents keep damaging my cocoa pods before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ ŋa nɔ kɛ ŋmeii fiteɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Animals are naturally attracted to the sweet pulp inside cocoa pods, especially when natural food sources in surrounding bushes become scarce. Keeping the farm cleared of dense thickets, using protective barriers, and harvesting promptly helps reduce animal damage.
ga: Koolooi sumɔɔ loo ni ŋɔɔ ni yɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔji amli lɛ. Titri lɛ, kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni jɛɔ jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli lɛ faaa lɛ, ehe miihia ni jwɛi ni mli tsei akafee ŋmɔ lɛ mli. kɛtsɔ gbɛtsii nibii ni buɔ mɔ he lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ baaye abua ni kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ aba shi.

english: What causes small insects to suck the sap out of my young cocoa shoots?
ga: Mɛni haa kooloi bibii lɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ mi-kookoo bibii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Insects like mirids (akate) feed on tender green shoots and young pods, especially when tree canopies have large sunlit gaps. Maintaining balanced shade and applying recommended pest control treatments prevents these insects from ruining new growth.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mirids (akate) yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ yitso lɛ mli hulu la agbo ko yɛ. Kɛ́ ahiɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli kɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baatsi nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anaa koni amɛkafite nibii heei ni eda lɛ.

english: Cocoa trees drop their flowers when they suffer from environmental stress, such as long dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or insect damage. Giving plants adequate nutrients and controlling pests helps the tree retain flowers so they can turn into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii kɛji amɛna shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ hulutsoo be ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Niyenii ni ehiii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii lɛ fiteɔ Niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni akɛhaa tso lɛ kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why do some cocoa farms yield high amounts of pods every season while others produce very little?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmɔji komɛi woɔ pod yibii babaoo daa afi lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni hei komɛi woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: High yields depend on consistent farm care, including proper tree spacing, regular weeding, pest control, shade management, and feeding the soil. Trees that receive routine care produce abundant pods reliably.
ga: Yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo damɔ ŋmɔ mli kwɛmɔ ni yaa nɔ daa lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni fata he ji tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa. Nibii ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ ahe nitsumɔ daa Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tsei ni akwɛɔ amɛ daa lɛ baaha ŋmeii babaoo aba yɛ gbɛ ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ.

english: Weeds compete with cocoa trees for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, which weakens the main crop. Keeping the base clear reduces competition and eliminates hiding places for harmful pests.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ kookoo tsei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ shishitoo lɛ mli tse lɛ, ebaaha akaŋshii aba shi, ni ebaajie hei ni kooloi ni yɔɔ oshara lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why should I prune dead branches and extra foliage from my cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tso niji ni egboi kɛ baai krokomɛi ni fata he lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to allow sunlight and airflow, which prevents fungal dampness. It also directs the tree's energy away from unwanted branches and into developing bigger, healthier pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Etsɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ hu kɛjɛɔ niji ni ataooo lɛ ahe. ni amɛfee pods ni dara ni yɔɔ hewalɛ hu

english: How can I tell if my farm soil is missing nutrients needed for good crop growth?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks essential nutrients, crop leaves often turn yellow, growth becomes stunted, and the plants produce fewer fruits or pods. Applying organic matter or appropriate fertilizers restores soil balance and plant health.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ bɛ lɛ, bei pii lɛ tso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Dalɛ baafee mlɛo. ni tso lɛ baawo yibii loo ŋmeii fioo pɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome ekoŋŋ ni tsei lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Black pod disease is caused by a fungus that thrives in excessive moisture and dark, unventilated conditions. Pruning excess branches to improve air movement and harvesting ripe pods quickly reduces fungal spread.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ fe nine kɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji ni fa fe nine lɛ amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ, ni akpa tsei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɛfaŋnɔ aba shi oya.

english: Why should I harvest ripe pods right away instead of leaving them on the tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makpa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ moŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree attracts pests, leads to over-ripening, and encourages diseases that can easily spread to nearby healthy green pods.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaagbala ŋmeii kɛba. Enɛ haa ahoɔ nii fe nine. ni ewoɔ helai ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli oya lɛ he hewalɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because full direct sunlight generates too much heat and dries them out. Leaving tall trees or planting temporary shade crops like plantains protects young cocoa until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔŋ ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ haa amɛdɔɔ fe nine ni amɛgbiɔ. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni aaashi loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli, tamɔ plantains ni aadu lɛ baaye abua ni abu kookoo bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: Is it really necessary to tie my yam vines onto wooden poles as they grow?
ga: Ani ehe miihia diɛŋtsɛ ni akɛ sweet potato wain tsei akpɛtɛ tsei ahe beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Yes, lifting yam vines onto stakes raises the leaves off the damp ground so they catch maximum sunlight to grow bigger tubers, while also preventing fungal diseases that spread on wet soil.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, sweet potato wain tsei ni awoɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ he ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ená hulu la babaoo koni ekwɛ̃ bulbs wuji. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ hu naa.

english: Can I plant cassava and maize together on the same piece of farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee ekome kɛdu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: Yes, planting maize and cassava together works very well. Maize grows fast and is harvested within three to four months, giving you an early food crop while leaving the field clear for the slower-growing cassava to spread out later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Abɛi daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ nyɔji etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ mli. Enɛ haa onáa niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii oya yɛ be mli ni oshiɔ ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ faŋŋ hu koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ agbɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my vegetable crop with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko he lɛ? Aduawai ni baai egbi loo jwɛi yɔɔ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil so it doesn't dry out quickly in the hot sun. It also keeps the soil cool and stops weeds from growing.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsei ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ lɛ, egbiɛɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants lack nitrogen, which is a vital food for plant growth, or that excessive rain has flooded the roots. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or improving water drainage can bring the green color back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ enɛ babaoo, ni eha shishifãi lɛ etsɔ nu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ wo mli loo aha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: Growing maize in the same spot every year drains the exact same nutrients from the soil and allows corn-specific pests and diseases to build up. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans restores nitrogen to the soil and starves corn pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni kɔɔ ŋmãa he pɔtɛɛ aba. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni atsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ ŋmei mli lɛ.

english: How can I prevent my cassava roots from rotting in the ground before harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi ŋmei shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa?

english: Cassava roots rot when water sits around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised mounds or soil ridges allows extra water to drain away, keeping the roots healthy until harvest time.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaaha nu babaoo atsɔ mli. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be mli.

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress or lack water during flowering. Regular watering and providing light shade during extremely hot weather helps the plant hold onto its flowers so fruit can grow.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli yɛ fɔfɔi be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ nɔ daa kɛ hulutsoo be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni ewo yibii.

english: What is eating the middle leaves of my corn plants and leaving dark brown dust inside?
ga: Mɛni ji mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni ayeɔ ni ashiɔ sũ ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide inside the growing center of the corn plant to feed, so applying neem oil or approved pest treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning helps control them.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ koni amɛye nii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ akɛ gbeɔ kooloi lɛ wo tsɔne lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akudɔ amɛ.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is caused by tiny pests like mites, aphids, or thrips sucking plant juices and spreading plant viruses. Spraying the leaves with a mild soapy water solution or soapy neem liquid can help eliminate these tiny insects.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ baa ji kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii, ŋmeii, loo thrips ni nuɔ tso nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli ejɔ loo neem samla kɛ nu shwie baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Planting fast-growing nurse crops like plantains provides living umbrellas that shield young cocoa from harsh heat while preserving soil moisture.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Nurse tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni buɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yellowing lower leaves indicate a nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize needs nitrogen to stay green and healthy, so applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or well-composted manure will restore their growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nii jogbaŋŋ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting cassava too close causes the stalks to compete for sunlight, ground water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant proper spacing allows the roots enough room underground to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ abɔi hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ aha gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ tso fɛɛ tso teŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa shishifãi ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can planting cowpeas alongside my main crop help me control weeds?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ cowpea ni mikɛ miŋmɔshi nibii titri lɛ baadu lɛ baaye abua ni akudɔ jwɛi lɛ?

english: Cowpeas spread quickly across the ground and form a thick leafy cover. This green cover blocks sunlight from reaching the soil, preventing weeds from sprouting while also adding nitrogen back into your soil.
ga: Cowpea gbɛɔ eshwaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya ni efeɔ baai ni mli tse ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɛkɛ nɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eŋɔli nɛɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa koni ekashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ ni ekɛ nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants droop and rot at the base during heavy rainy seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess standing water around the base of pepper plants suffocates the roots and encourages destructive water-borne fungi. Planting on raised mounds or ridges allows surplus rain to drain away safely.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi fe nine ni ebɔle Pepper tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nu lɛ hewalɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: What is eating ragged holes into the center whorl of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Ragged holes inside the growing center of corn are typical signs of Fall Armyworm attack. Early detection allows you to apply recommended pest control methods, such as organic sprays or targeted treatments, into the whorl before the crop is ruined.
ga: Buji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa ni miida lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji okadi ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Fall Armyworm tutuamɔ he. Yɔsemɔ lɛ mra. Ehaa okɛ gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsuɔ nii kɛgbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ kooloi anɔ loo tsofai ni akɛtoɔ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii. kɛtee ŋshɔ lɛ mli dani akpata ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahiɛ.

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and lets pests and diseases multiply in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or beans restores soil fertility and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni oha tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai Agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Okɛ ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: Why do I need to build large soil mounds before planting yam setts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ama gɔŋ agbo dani adu ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Yam tubers grow deep beneath the surface and need soft, loose earth to expand fully. High mounds gather nutrient-rich topsoil and ensure the tubers do not hit hard, compacted ground as they stretch downwards.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ ni ehe hiaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa. Gɔŋ ni kɛlɛ lɛ buaa ŋwɛi sũ ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekwɛɔ koni bulb lɛ akatswa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni amɛkpãa shi kɛyaa shishi lɛ.

english: Multiple shoots suck energy, water, and nutrients away from the main mother plant. Removing excess shoots leaves one strong successor, ensuring the main stem gets enough food to produce a heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii babaoo lɛ shwieɔ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ tso titri ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi sɛɛyelɔ kome pɛ ni he wa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ naa niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfeɔ tso ni tsii.

english: Why shouldn't I spread chemical fertilizer on my dry field during a drought?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔji ni egbi lɛ anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fertilizers need water to dissolve so plant roots can safely take them up. Applying fertilizer to hot, dry soil concentrates the chemicals and burns the roots, wasting your investment and damaging your crops.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe. Shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha tsofai lɛ afee ekome ni ebaashã shishifãi lɛ. Eji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fitemɔ ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: How often am I supposed to spray my crops so I don't wait too long or spray too early?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ koni mikamɛ be kakadaŋŋ loo mafɔ oya?

english: Spraying timing depends on the specific crop and pest, but waiting too long—like two months—allows pests to multiply and damage crops, while following the recommended schedule protects plants without causing unnecessary stress.
ga: Be ni akɛshwieɔ tsofa lɛ nɔ lɛ damɔ ŋmɔshi nibii pɔtɛɛ ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ nɔ. Shi kɛ́ omɛ be kakadaŋŋ, tamɔ nyɔji enyɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ aya hiɛ ni amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni gbɛjianɔtoo ni atsɔɔ lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaye abua ni abu tso lɛ he ni ekɛ haomɔ ni he ehiaaa baaa.

english: Will applying chemical sprays make my crops tired and exhaust them?
ga: Ani tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baaha etɔ mi ni egbɔjɔ?

english: Chemical sprays will not exhaust your crops if mixed and applied correctly; proper spraying protects the plant from pests and diseases so it can focus its energy on healthy growth and flowering.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ egbeŋ oŋmɔshi nibii kɛji akɛ akɛfutu ni akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa shwie tsei anɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe. Bɔni afee ni enyɛ ekɛ hewalɛ ama dalɛ kpakpa kɛ fɔfɔi anɔ.

english: What happens to my plants if I use more chemical than what is recommended on the bottle?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ tsofai babaoo tsu nii fe bɔ ni atsɔɔ yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using too much chemical can burn crop leaves, damage roots, waste money, and cause pests to become resistant to the treatment over time.
ga: Tsofai babaoo ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei ahe baai, efite shishifãi, efite shika ni eha tsɛŋemɔ helai nyɛɛɛ atsa amɛ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the hot midday sun can evaporate the spray too quickly or cause the chemical to burn the crop leaves.
ga: Leebi loo shwane mli ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ atsɔ oya tsɔ loo eha tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ashã tsei ahe baai.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow after I finish spraying them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni migbe tsofa lɛ naa lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow after spraying when the chemical mixture is made too strong or applied during extreme heat, causing chemical stress or scorching on the plant.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ashwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ beni tsofa ni akɛfutu lɛ mli eyi obɔ tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ. Enɛ kɛ tsofai ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli loo eshãa tso lɛ.

english: Should I wait until I see insects eating my plants before I start spraying chemical treatments?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ kɛyashi mana kooloi bibii ni miiye mitsei lɛ dani mabɔi tsofai ni akɛtsaa hela lɛ shwiemɔ?

english: No, waiting until pests appear often means damage is already done; following preventative spraying schedules helps stop pest outbreaks before they can ruin your harvest.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ mɔ ko mɛ kɛyashi tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ baaje kpo lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ efite nii lɛ momo. Kɛ́ onyiɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni akpa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa lɛ dani amɛfite onibii.

english: Why are chemical sprays not working on my crops even though I apply them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ nɔ daa moŋ?

english: Sprays may fail if pests have built resistance from overusing the same chemical, or if the mixture is inaccurate or applied at the wrong growth stage of the plant.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni ehiii kɛji akɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ma shi kɛjɛ tsofa kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ mli. aloo kɛji akɛ nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ejaaa loo akɛtsu nii yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ be ni ejaaa mli.

english: Why is it important for me to follow official extension guidelines instead of my own spraying routine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ makwɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ be ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ he lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni makɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ daa?

english: Extension guidelines are tested by agricultural scientists to give you the highest yield safely, whereas unguided routines often lead to chemical overload, crop damage, or wasted effort.
ga: Okwaayeli he nilelɔi eka gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ agbɛɔ ashwãa lɛ ekwɛ koni eha oná yibii babaoo shweshweeshwe. Yɛ be mli ni bei pii lɛ, nifeemɔi ni afeɔ daa ni kɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi tsuuu nii lɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine, ŋmɔshi nibii ni efiteɔ, loo mɔdɛŋbɔɔ ni afiteɔ lɛ baa lɛ,.

english: Can I use my knapsack sprayer for different farming activities like pest control and liquid fertilizing?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ sɛɛgbɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ atsu okwaayeli nitsumɔi tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he nii?

english: Yes, a single sprayer can be used for multiple farm tasks, provided you clean it thoroughly with clean water and soap between different chemical uses to avoid crop contamination.
ga: Hɛɛ, abaanyɛ akɛ tsɔne kome ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ atsu nitsumɔi babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Esa akɛ okɛ nu ni mli tse kɛ samla atsumɔ he jogbaŋŋ yɛ tsofai srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ateŋ koni akafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different chemicals together in my sprayer to save time?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsofai enyɔ baafutu yɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ nii anɔ lɛ mli koni mikɛ be akafite?

english: Mixing chemicals without expert advice can cause dangerous chemical reactions that neutralize the treatments or create a mixture that harms your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni ŋaawolɔi komɛi bɛ he lɛ baanyɛ aha tsofai ni yɔɔ oshara aba ni baaha tsofa lɛ afee nɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ loo ekɛ nibii ni yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui aba.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the plants lack nitrogen in the soil or the roots are waterlogged from heavy rains, which prevents them from taking up nutrients properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Aloo shishifãi lɛ amli eyi kɛ nu yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haaa tsei lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can crop diseases stay hidden in the soil even after I clear my farm after harvest?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛji mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ po?

english: Yes, many fungal and bacterial diseases can live in the soil or on leftover plant roots for months or years, waiting to infect the next set of crops you plant.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo baanyɛ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso shishifãi ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ nyɔji loo afii babaoo. koni omɛ tsei akuu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni odu lɛ ni egbɛ eshwa

english: Why do my coconut trees suddenly start dropping young nuts before they mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso lɛ miibɔi gbee trukaa dani ebaanyɛ eda lɛ?

english: Sudden nut fall in coconut trees usually happens when the tree is stressed by extended dry spells, poor soil nutrients, or the onset of diseases like Cape St. Paul Wilt that affect the tree's water transport.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni fiteɔ trukaa yɛ ŋmeii tsei amli lɛ baa kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ haoɔ. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo helai okadii tamɔ Cape St. Paul’s wilt ni jeɔ shishi. ni saa nu ni akɛyaa tsei amli lɛ he

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers but very few actual tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shi tomato diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ?

english: Tomatoes drop flowers without setting fruit if weather temperatures get too high during pollination, or if too much nitrogen fertilizer is used, causing the plant to put energy into growing leaves instead of fruits.
ga: Tomato baafɔ̃ ni ewooo yibii kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli latsaa lɛ fa tsɔ yɛ be mli ni pollination lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii Enɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛwoɔ baai yɛ aduawai najiaŋ.

english: How can I tell if my cassava is fully mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 to 12 months, and you can tell it is ready when the lower leaves yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the stem begins to crack.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ daa yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 mli, ni obaanyɛ ona akɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ je shishi egbɛ eshwa.

english: Why do my pepper plants curl their leaves up and stop growing during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ ni amɛkpaa shweremɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in dry weather is often caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies that spread viruses, as hot weather helps these insects multiply quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa kooloi nɛɛ ni amɛfɔɔ oya.

english: How do changes between the rainy and dry season affect when my crops catch diseases?
ga: Te tsakemɔ ni baa nugbɔshiimɔ be kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋ lɛ saa miŋmɔshi nibii ahe ehaa tɛŋŋ kɛ́ hela lɛ emɔ mi?

english: Rainy seasons create wet conditions that help fungal diseases spread quickly across wet leaves, while dry seasons weaken plants from water stress, making them easy targets for insect pests.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli edɔ baa ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ kɛjɛɔ nu he haomɔ mli. Enɛ haa amɛfeɔ mɛi ni tsɛŋemɔ helai baanyɛ atswa amɛ oya.

english: Why does planting the same crop on the same piece of land every year reduce my yields?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni miduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baa shi lɛ?

english: Why is it important for me to remove weeds from around my young crops early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ midumɔwui lɛ amli mra lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients, and they also provide a hiding place for insect pests that bring diseases to your farm.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Eji he ko hu ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baanyɛ ekɛ helai aba oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ teeɔ amɛhe yɛ.

english: Why do young cocoa seedlings need taller plants like plantains grown next to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ tamɔ plantains ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he hiaa kookoo tsei lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong, direct sunlight, so temporary shade crops like plantains keep the soil moist and protect the seedlings until they grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebu dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara waa.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die when the hot season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboiɔ beni hulutsoo be lɛ bɛŋkɛɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves and small roots that cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. They require temporary shade plants like plantains or shade trees to protect them from heat stress and keep the soil moist during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi bibii ni hulu la nyɛɛɛ ashɛ amɛhe tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa amɛnáa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo hulutsoo tsei. Bɔni afee ni akafee dɔlɛ he haomɔ ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my maize seeds very close together to get more crops from my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close forces the crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough resources to produce big, healthy ears instead of many weak, barren stalks.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ toi wuji ni mli wa. Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, tsei babaoo ni bɛ hewalɛ ni egbi yɛ.

english: Why should I wait for the main rains to establish before planting my corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa koni madu ŋmãa?

english: If you plant after just one early rain, a dry spell can follow and burn the fresh seedlings. Waiting until the soil has steady moisture ensures seeds germinate properly and survive their critical early growth stage.
ga: Kɛji odu yɛ leebi nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, Hɔmɔ baanyɛ anyiɛ sɛɛ ni eshã dumɔwui heei. Mɛmɔ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Enɛ baaha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni amɛhi shi yɛ mra be mli dalɛ be ni he hiaa waa lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves starting from the bottom of the plant usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, a key nutrient crops need to stay green and grow strong. Adding compost or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ehe miihia ni tsei ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ waa lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so it does not wash away?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli koni ekafo?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is moist and crops are actively growing, but avoid applying right before heavy downpours that wash nutrients away. Placing the fertilizer in the soil near the roots rather than scattering it on top also helps plants absorb it best.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii miida lɛ. Shi tsi ohe kɛjɛ he ni okɛbaatsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ anɛ waa, ni no baajie niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo sũ lɛ mli ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ moŋ fe nɔ ni akɛwoɔ nɔ lɛ, no hu yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow faster than my planted crops, and why must I clear them early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi lɛ mra?

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants naturally adapted to steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients from your crops. Clearing them early prevents them from crowding out young crops while they are small and weak.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ onibii amli lɛ mli. Nibii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Enɛ baatsi ŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkayimɔ obɔbɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛji bibii ni amɛhe waaa lolo lɛ.

english: What is eating small holes in the fresh center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ bu bibioo ni yɔɔ tso lɛ baa hee ni yɔɔ mi-bi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of young corn plants. Catching them early and applying approved insecticides or ash into the leaf funnels can save your crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo sũ ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo baai lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ohere oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ayiwala.

english: Why do my tomato plants wilt and die even when I water them regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ miwoɔ amɛ nu daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Sudden wilting in wet soil is often caused by soil diseases like fungal or bacterial root rot. Too much water or poorly drained soil suffocates the roots, allowing harmful germs to enter and block water flow inside the plant stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ helai, tamɔ fungal loo bacteria shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa. Nu babaoo loo shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mli ni amɛtsiɔ nu ni hoɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Cassava is usually ready between 8 to 12 months after planting, depending on the variety. You can tell it is ready when lower leaves drop off, the plant stem thickens, and small cracks appear in the soil around the base of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 8 kɛyashi 12 mli yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Edamɔ tso lɛ henɔ lɛ nɔ Obaanyɛ ona akɛ tso lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ eshishi baai lɛ shwie shi, eshishifã lɛ mli tsɔ, ni ŋmeii bibii hu yɛ mli. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle tso lɛ shishi lɛ mli.

english: Why do certified maize seeds from agro-dealers yield better than seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni jɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko ŋɔɔ lɛ woɔ yibii ni hi fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mikpamɔ ni tsɔ hiɛ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Certified seeds are specially bred and tested to resist pests, diseases, and drought while producing high yields. Saved seeds from hybrid crops lose these strong qualities in the next generation, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Akwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni aka amɛ akwɛ koni amɛnyɛ amɛshi tsɛŋemɔ helai, helai kɛ hɔmɔ. kɛfata yibiiwoo ni nɔ kwɔ ni akɛhaa lɛ he Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ tsei ni akɛfee ekome lɛ amli lɛ baafite sui ni mli wa nɛɛ yɛ yinɔ ni baa lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni afee lɛ fioo.

english: Flowers drop off when they are not pollinated. Pollination happens when tiny insects or humans transfer pollen within the flower, which fertilizes it so it can grow into a full pod instead of drying up.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ ashɛɛɛ amɛhe. Pollination baa kɛji kooloo bibioo ko loo gbɔmɔ ko kɛ pollen lɛ tee fɔfɔi ko mli. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii bɔni afee ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaagboi.

english: Why are bees and small bugs important for my crops if they don't feed on the plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii No hewɔ lɛ ani ehe hiaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛji amɛjeee jwɛiyelɔi?

english: These insects act as natural pollinators. As they move from flower to flower drinking nectar, they carry pollen on their bodies, which helps your crops produce fruits, pods, and seeds.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii ni haa ŋmeii baa. be mli ni amɛjɛɔ fɔfɔi kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli koni amɛnu nu mli nu lɛ Amɛhiɛɔ pollen yɛ amɛgbɔmɔtsei lɛ anɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwoɔ aduawai, ŋmeii, kɛ dumɔwui.

english: Why do my watermelon vines have many flowers, but only a few grow into actual fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon wain tso lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔii fioo komɛi pɛ tsakeɔ amɛfeɔ aduawai diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Watermelons have separate male and female flowers. Only the female flowers can become fruits, and they will only grow if pollen from a male flower is carried over to them by insects or by hand.
ga: Watermelon yɛ fɔfɔi hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi. Fɔfɔi yei pɛ baanyɛ afee aduawai. Ni amɛdaraa pɛ kɛji akɛ ŋmeii loo niji kɛ pollen ni jɛ fɔfɔi hii amli lɛ ba amɛŋɔɔ.

english: What does hand pollination mean, and why should I do it on my farm?
ga: Mɛni ji nine ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ shishi? Ni mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafee yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Hand pollination is using a small brush or your fingers to move pollen between flowers yourself. Doing this ensures more flowers get fertilized, which can greatly increase your crop yield when natural insects are scarce.
ga: Nɔ ni fata nine nɔ pollination he ji ni akɛ brɔsh bibioo ko atsu nii. loo onine ni okɛ onine tsi pollen lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ. Enɛ baaha fɔfɔi lɛ aná fɔmɔ nii babaoo. Enɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ waa kɛ́ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii faaa.

english: Can manually pollinating my cocoa flowers produce more pods than letting nature do it?
ga: Ani kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛwoɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee ŋmeii babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛhaa adebɔɔ feɔ?

english: Yes, because natural insects like midges only reach a small fraction of cocoa flowers. When you pollinate by hand, you guarantee that many more flowers turn into pods, increasing your harvest.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ adebɔɔ mli kooloi bibii tamɔ midges baanyɛ ashɛ kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ fã bibioo ko pɛ he kɛji okɛ onine wo amɛmli. Akɛ nɔmimaa ha bo akɛ fɔfɔi babaoo baatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ haa nitsumɔ ni otsuɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: What is the best time of day for me to pollinate the flowers on my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli?

english: Early morning is best because flowers are fresh, open, and receptive to pollen, and the morning moisture helps pollen stick properly.
ga: Leebi ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ ehee, amɛgbele amɛhe waa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha pollen. Ni hulutsoo ni baa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni pollen lɛ kpɛtɛɔ he jogbaŋŋ.

english: Will spraying insecticides on my farm reduce the amount of fruit my crops produce?
ga: Ani tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha yibii ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ lɛ aba shi?

english: Yes, if chemicals are sprayed carelessly, they kill beneficial insects like bees and midges that pollinate your flowers. Without these insects, fewer flowers will turn into fruits or pods.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai shwie shi yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ Ebaagbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ teŋgbɛ nibii ni haa ofɔfɔi lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛji kooloi nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ baafee yibii loo ŋmeii fioo.

english: How can I encourage more helpful pollinating insects to stay on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mawo ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ babaoo lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛhi miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You can plant flowering herbs around your farm borders, reduce heavy chemical spraying, and leave moist organic shade where small pollinating insects like midges can live.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu tsofai ni woɔ fɔfɔi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he, ni ebaaha tsofai ni tsii ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ aba shi. ni oha organic shade lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii bibii tamɔ midges baanyɛ ahi.

english: How does heavy rainfall during the flowering stage affect my harvest?
ga: Te nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ saa mikpamɔ lɛ he ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash pollen away from open flowers and prevent insects from flying around, which leads to poor pollination and fewer fruits developing.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ afɔ fɔfɔi amli muji lɛ ahe. ni etsĩɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkafo kɛbɔle amɛhe. Enɛ haa pollination lɛ ehiii ni aduawai lɛ hu eyaaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do all crops rely on insects to turn their flowers into harvestable food?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii anɔ koni amɛtsake fɔfɔi amɛfee niyenii ni abaanyɛ akpa?

english: No, crops behave differently. Some crops like tomatoes can pollinate themselves, maize relies mostly on wind to move pollen, while crops like cocoa and watermelons rely heavily on insects or human hand pollination.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii feɔ amɛnii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ. Tsei komɛi, tamɔ tomato, baanyɛ afee amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ. Abele babaoo kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nɔ koni ekɛ pollen aya. yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo kɛ watermelon Ekɛ ehe fɔ̃ɔ kooloi bibii loo gbɔmɔ nine nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ waa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow while the rest of the plant stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tso lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni tso ni eshwɛ lɛ kã he eji ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil is running low on nitrogen, which is an essential food crops need to stay green and grow strong. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea early in the season helps keep the whole plant healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo tso lɛ mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: How do I know if my farm soil actually needs fertilizer before I spend money to buy it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii diɛŋtsɛ? Dani mafite shika kɛhe?

english: You can watch how your previous crop grew—slow growth and pale green leaves signal poor soil nutrients—or you can take a small soil sample to an extension officer for testing to find out exactly what nutrients are missing.
ga: Obaanyɛ ona bɔ ni onibii ni okɛtsu nii tsutsu lɛ dara ha. Dalɛ blɛoo kɛ baai eŋɔli tsɔɔ akɛ sũ mli niyenii kpakpai bɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ okɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko aya extension nitsulɔ ko ŋɔɔ koni eka lɛ ekwɛ koni ena niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ mli.

english: Tomato leaves curl up during intense heat as a natural defense to trap moisture and stop water from evaporating too quickly. If the leaves bounce back and stand upright in the cool evening, your plant is healthy and just protecting itself.
ga: Tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli akɛ adebɔɔ mli nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛtsi ŋmɔtɔ naa ni ekɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaho oya tsɔ. Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛba ni amɛdamɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ miitso lɛ, Etsɔɔ akɛ otso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni ebuɔ ehe kɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall and leafy but yield only tiny roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi ehaa shishifãi bibii pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted under heavy tree shade or given too much nitrogen fertilizer, the plant puts all its energy into growing tall leafy stems towards the sun instead of sending food down to build big roots.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei yɛ tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ ashishi loo akɛ nitrogen ŋmei babaoo miiwo mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei ni yɔɔ baai kakadaji ni kwɛɔ hulu lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaatsu niyenii kɛba shi koni amɛma shishifãi wuji

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers on the ground without forming any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ewooo yibii ko lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress, such as very high temperatures, dry soil, or a sudden lack of nutrients. Keeping the soil consistently moist during flowering helps the blossoms stay on and turn into fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ trukaa lɛ he. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃i pɛpɛɛpɛ yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛtsɔɔ aduawai.

english: Why is it bad for my land if I keep planting maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the specific soil nutrients that plant loves and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpea or groundnuts puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni yaa nɔ edaa lɛ baaha niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ lɛ pɛ ajɛ mli. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa tsake lɛ, no baaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Removing tiny side shoots—often called suckers—stops the plant from wasting food and water on extra leaves, allowing it to send all its energy into producing larger, healthier tomato fruits.
ga: Ajieɔ ŋmeii bibii, ni bei pii lɛ atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii. Enɛ baatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekafite niyenii kɛ nu ni baai babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa anyɛɔ atsuɔ hewalɛ fɛɛ he nii koni akɛfee tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn dark black and rot before they are ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛfee klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads easily in dark, humid conditions. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and fresh air reach the pods helps keep them dry and safe from the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni duŋ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Kɛ́ afo tsei niji krokomɛi amli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni niji lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛkafiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cabbage crop full of tiny round holes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cabbage baai lɛ eyi kɛ bu bibii ni yɔɔ kokroo lɛ?

english: Tiny holes in cabbage leaves are usually eaten out by young caterpillars like the diamondback moth larvae. Inspecting leaf undersides early and using safe bio-pesticides or neem extracts can protect your crop before the leaves are destroyed.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ diamondback moth larvae lɛ yeɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ cabbage baai lɛ amli lɛ. Kwɛmɔ baai lɛ ashishi mra. Ni kɛ okɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe loo neem mli nibii ni ajieɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ ebu onibii ahe dani baai lɛ afite.

english: Why do some of the maize seeds I plant fail to sprout out of the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ kɛjɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seeds usually fail to germinate if they were planted too deep for light and warmth to reach them, if the soil dried out completely after planting, or if soil insects ate the seeds before they could sprout.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ ni la kɛ dɔlɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa beni adu lɛ sɛɛ Aloo kɛji kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why is it bad for me to burn my land before I plant my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ mashã shikpɔŋ lɛ dani madu nii lɛ?

english: Burning destroys rich organic matter and beneficial organisms in the soil that help feed your crops. It leaves the soil exposed, dry, and poor, which lowers your yield over time.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fa babaoo kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni yeɔ ebuaa onibii lɛ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, egbiɔ, ni ehiii kwraa, ni no baaha onibii ni obaaná lɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: The first rain usually only wets the surface while the deeper soil remains hot and dry. If a hot spell follows, your seeds will germinate and quickly dry up; it is better to wait until you get two or three steady rains so the soil holds enough moisture.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã he edɔ ni egbi. Kɛji nifeemɔ ko ni mli edɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛgbiɔ oya. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ anɛ shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ anyɛ ahi nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mli.

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs to grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain leaves too much standing water around the roots, preventing them from breathing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmãa lɛ adara waa Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ ha nu babaoo ebɔle shishifãi lɛ ahe, ni eha amɛmiigbɔjɔ.

english: Groundnuts and beans take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground through their roots. This naturally enriches your soil and feeds your maize, giving you better crops without spending as much on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Akpɔlɔi kɛ ŋmeii jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni ebaaha ŋmãa lɛ aná niyenii. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni okɛ tsofai babaoo ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuuu nii.

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate direct sunlight because their leaves burn easily. They need shade from plantains or larger trees to keep them cool and preserve soil moisture during their first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya. Ehe miihia ni amɛná hulutsoo kɛjɛ plantains loo tsei wuji amli koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn and leaving holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni ye mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ ni eshi bu yɛ baai lɛ fɛɛ nɔ?

english: This is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide inside the central leaves of the maize plant to feed. Checking your field early allows you to treat the crop before the pests destroy the whole farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ateŋ baai amli koni amɛye nii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ehaa okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii toɔ dani tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to support my plantain trees with wooden poles when they start producing bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei afi dumɔwui lɛ asɛɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ bɔi kpojee pɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems and heavy, water-filled trunks. When a bunch grows large, the top becomes too heavy, and strong winds can easily pull the entire plant down if it is not supported with a prop.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni tsii ni nu eyi mli obɔ. Beni kuu lɛ da lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ fã lɛ baafee nɔ ni tsii tsɔ. Ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa baanyɛ agbala tsei muu fɛɛ kɛba shi yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsei fĩii amɛ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb high wooden stakes to give me big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛná ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam leaves use sunlight to manufacture food that gets stored in the tuber under the ground. Staking lifts the leaves off the soil so they receive maximum sunlight and stay clean from soil-borne diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ niyenii ni akɛtoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Staking woɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ená hulu la babaoo ni eha amɛhe tse kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Cassava is usually mature between 9 and 12 months after planting. You will see the lower leaves turn yellow and drop off, and you can carefully dig up one plant to check if the tubers are thick and firm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei hiɔ shi yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 teŋ yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaana akɛ baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbee shi. Ni obaanyɛ okɛ hiɛdɔɔ atsu tso lɛ he nii koni ona kɛji ŋmeii lɛ amli eyi kɛ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants fall off without turning into fruit during hot dry days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ ni nu bɛ lɛ amli lɛ?

english: High temperatures combined with dry soil cause extreme stress to tomato plants, making the flowers drop before they can form fruit. Keeping the soil cool with mulch and regular watering helps the flowers stay on.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa ni akɛfataa shikpɔŋ ni egbi he lɛ kɛ haomɔ ni naa wa baa tomato tsei anɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ nɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crop leaves turn bright green and grow faster right after I pour water on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛdaraa oya kɛji mikɛ nu wo nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Water dissolves important nutrients hidden in the soil so the plant roots can drink them, which triggers healthy leaf growth and turns the plant lush green.
ga: Nu shwieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli koni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ anu. Enɛ baawo baai lɛ adalɛ kpakpa he hewalɛ ni eha tso lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: How much water do I need to pour on new seeds to get them to sprout without damaging them?
ga: Te ehe baahia ni mafɔ dumɔwui heei anɔ nu abɔ tɛŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee amɛ?

english: Seeds need soil that is moist like a wrung-out sponge; pouring too much water buries them in mud and rots them before they can breathe and sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ tamɔ sponji ni ajie lɛ kpo. Nu babaoo ni oooshwie nɔ lɛ baafu amɛ yɛ muji lɛ mli ni amɛbaagboi dani amɛmu ni amɛdara kɛjɛ mli.

english: How do I know the exact right time to cut my palm nuts for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmei yibii kɛha kpamɔ?

english: Oil palm bunches are ready for harvest when a few loose orange-red palm nuts naturally drop to the ground around the base of the tree.
ga: Mu tsei akui lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni tso lɛ mli tsei ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ji ŋmɔtɔ fioo ko ni jɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔleɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why are the lower branches of my oil palm tree turning yellow while the top remains green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-oil palm tso lɛ niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi niji lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Older lower leaves naturally yellow and die as the palm tree directs its energy and water to the top leaves and growing fruit bunches.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni egbɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu yaa baa ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni ehaa aduawai akui shwereɔ lɛ.

english: How can I safely store my harvested palm nuts so they do not spoil before I process them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-palm nut ni akpa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni nut lɛ akafite dani atsu he nii?

english: Keep harvested palm bunches under shade on a dry surface and process them within two to three days to keep the oil fresh and prevent rotting.
ga: Kɛ tsei ni akpa lɛ ato hulutsoo shishi yɛ he ko ni egbi. ni atsu he nii yɛ gbii enyɔ loo etɛ mli koni fɔ lɛ ahi shi ehee ni ekafite.

english: Why did my farm produce a much bigger harvest this year compared to last year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo kwraa afi nɛɛ fe nyɛsɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: A unusually large harvest happens when your crops get the perfect balance of timely rains, proper sunshine, and healthy soil throughout the growing months.
ga: Nikpamɔ agbo ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baa beni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. hulu la ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ nyɔji ni shwereɔ lɛ amli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my crops grow differently every year even when I plant the exact same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ daraa yɛ gbɛi srɔtoi anɔ daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ?

english: Changes in weather patterns, such as early or late rains and hotter sun, affect how fast plants grow and how much food they produce each year.
ga: Tsakemɔi ni baa kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi amli, tamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra loo sɛɛ mli. ni hulu lɛ mli woɔ la waa Esaa tsei ni daraa oya kɛ tsei aniyenii babaoo ni amɛyeɔ daa afi lɛ he.

english: What naturally happens in the soil after a heavy rain to make plants look so fresh and green?
ga: Mɛni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ ni ehaa tsei feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛfee ehee ni amɛfee ŋmɔŋ?

english: Rainwater carries small amounts of natural nitrogen from the air into the dirt, giving your crops a instant burst of energy to build green leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ woɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen fioo ko kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha onibii lɛ hewalɛ oya koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli.

english: Why do some parts of my farmland stay green during dry periods while other parts dry up quickly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi shikpɔji lɛ ekomɛi feɔ ŋmɔji yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ be mli ni hei krokomɛi hu gbɛ́ɔ oya lɛ?

english: Soil type changes across a field; darker soils with organic matter or clay hold water longer, while sandy areas drain quickly and dry out.
ga: Shikpɔŋ henɔi tsakeɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ. Shikpɔji ni mli edɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo shikpɔŋ sũ babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, hei ni ŋã yɔɔ lɛ hoɔ oya ni amɛgbiɔ.

english: Why do crops grow faster when planted right at the very start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei daa oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: The first rains flush locked-up nutrients out of warm soil, giving early-planted seeds a powerful boost of nourishment right as they germinate.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni emɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni adu mra lɛ naa niyenii ni mli wa kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually show that the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil or that the roots are waterlogged. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK helps the leaves turn dark green again so the plant can grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nu eyi shishifãi lɛ amli obɔ. Kɛ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ koni tsei lɛ adara jogbaŋŋ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing ensures each plant gets enough food and light to develop thick stems and good yields.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa niyenii kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli tse ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Why should I wait until the soil is wet before applying fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ dani mawo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil so the roots can absorb it. Putting fertilizer on dry soil can burn the crop roots and cause the nutrients to waste away into the air.
ga: Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni ekɛbote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ aya kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die even when I give them water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ mihaa amɛ nu moŋ lɛ?
