english: This sudden drying is often caused by bacterial wilt or root fungi living in the soil that block water from moving up the stem. Rotating your crops and avoiding planting tomatoes in the same spot every year helps prevent this disease.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni baa trukaa nɛɛ baa ji helai ni gbeɔ mɔ loo ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni haaa nu aya ŋwɛi tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ amɛhe kɛ tomato ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni atsĩɔ hela nɛɛ naa.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or mites that suck the sap and spread plant viruses. Controlling these insects early prevents the leaves from curling and keeps the plant producing fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni ekafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do I see small holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the central shoots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ muji ni tamɔ powder ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii amli lɛ mli

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that feeds on the growing center of maize plants. Applying targeted treatments early in the morning or late evening kills the caterpillars before they ruin the entire farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni yeɔ ŋmei tsei lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ tsu nii leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Covering the soil with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, keeps the ground cool, traps moisture so you water less often, and stops weeds from taking over your farm.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akɛ mulching. baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i Locks in moisture bɔni afee ni okɛ nu akawo mli fioo. ni otsi jwɛi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil holds too much water during heavy rains. Planting your cassava on raised ridges or mounds helps excess water drain away so the tubers stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ nu babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni yitso lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they suffer from prolonged dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or damage from pests like mirids. Keeping shade trees and protecting the farm from sucking pests helps flowers stay on the tree to become pods.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna amanehulu yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ pollen lɛ efiteɔ Tsei lɛ ni akɛ amɛ woɔ hulutsoo mli ni abuɔ ŋmɔ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni nuɔ amɛ lɛ ahe lɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ kpɛtɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and heavy stems, which makes them top-heavy when bearing fruit. Supporting the main stem with wooden or bamboo stakes helps hold the tree upright against strong winds.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ kɛ shishifãi ni tsii. ni haa efeɔ nɔ ni tsii kɛji ewo yibii Kɛ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tsei fiɔ tso lɛ yitso wulu lɛ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying before the corn ears are mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ dani abele toi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil lacks nitrogen, which maize needs heavily to grow strong. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted poultry manure will help keep the leaves green and support bigger corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ŋmãa he hiaa ni ekwɛ̃ babaoo Kɛ akɛ nitrogen ŋmãa tamɔ urea loo kooloi ŋmãa ni fiteɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ni eye ebua ŋmãa lɛ toi lɛ ni ekwɛ̃.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall with plenty of leaves, but producing tiny roots underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo shi eyɛ shishifãi bibii lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or is overloaded with fresh manure, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing leaves instead of roots. Avoiding heavy nitrogen fertilizer late in growth and pruning excess stems encourages the tubers to swell.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii heei babaoo yɔɔ mli. Cassava tso lɛ kudɔɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa baai ni miida lɛ anɔ moŋ fe shishifãi. Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa blɛoo kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni afoɔ fe nine lɛ baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli alɛɛ.

english: Why do agricultural extension officers recommend covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ jwɛi aha shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering soil with dry grass, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating under the hot sun, keeps the root zone cool, blocks weed growth, and slowly turns into compost that feeds your soil.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. Etsiɔ jwɛi lɛ adalɛ naa, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: This rot is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in dark, cold, and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade branches to let sunlight and air into your farm, along with removing rotted pods, prevents the fungus from spreading.
ga: Blackpod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni shwereɔ yɛ hei ni yɔɔ duŋ, ni mli ejɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo ni oookpa lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Jiemɔ ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ hu. Koni tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like whiteflies or thrips that suck sap and transmit viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil spray or safe insecticides protects young plants from getting damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo thrips ni nuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ni amɛkɛ helai baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Kɛ́ akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite.

english: Why do my cowpea plants look very green and healthy but produce empty pods or no pods at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ ni eyɛ hewalɛ shi eyɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko loo ŋmeii bɛ mli kwraa lɛ?

english: Tiny insects called flower thrips often attack cowpea flowers before pods can form, causing the blossoms to fall off. Spraying recommended plant-safe treatments right when the first flowers open ensures proper pod formation.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ flower thrips lɛ tutuaa cowpea fɔfɔi lɛ dani amɛfeɔ pods. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni akɛhaa akɛ tsofa ni haa tsei lɛ yeɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ shwieɔ nɔ kɛji klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi lɛ fɔ̃ɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa pod lɛ feɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Must I stake my yam vines with sticks, or can I just let them spread on the bare ground?
ga: Ehe bahia ni madu sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ niji loo maha amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ kɛkɛ.

english: Staking lifts yam leaves into the sunlight so the plant can make enough food to build large tubers. Leaving vines on the hot ground burns the leaves and exposes them to soil diseases, which reduces your overall harvest.
ga: Ni akɛ sweet potato baai lɛ baawo hulutsoo be mli koni tso lɛ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee bulbs agboi. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ ashã ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ helai aba. Enɛ baaha onitsumɔ lɛ fɛɛ aba shi.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without producing any fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop off when temperatures get too high or when soil moisture swings quickly between very dry and very wet. Mulching around the base and watering evenly keeps the soil moist so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ oya yɛ nɔ ni egbi waa kɛ nɔ ni mli edɔ waa teŋ. Mulching ni akɛwoɔ shishigbɛ lɛ he kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Why do my fruiting plantain trees fall over during strong winds even when the main stem does not break?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui ni woɔ yibii lɛ gbeeɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ ekuuu lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots, and heavy fruit bunches make the top very heavy, allowing strong winds to pull the roots out of the ground. Supporting fruiting trees with bamboo props or wooden poles keeps them upright until harvest.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ni aduawai akuu ni tsii lɛ haa ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni tsii waa. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswaa shishifãi lɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii loo tsei ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ fiɔ yibii tsei asɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni amɛhiɔ shi jaŋŋ kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why are the bottom tips of my young watermelons turning soft and black while still on the vine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-watermelon bibioo lɛ naji lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo ni eyɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni eyɔɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This soft black tip is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium or irregular watering while the fruit is growing quickly. Consistent watering and adding wood ash or lime to your soil helps prevent the fruit tips from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ ŋmei diŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo nɛɛ akɛ blossom end rot. Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida oya lɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni okɛ tso sũ loo lime fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni aduawai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akafite.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings burn and die when there are no bigger trees planted around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot tolerate full, harsh sunlight during their first couple of years. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a natural canopy that protects the young cocoa leaves from heat stress and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he lɛ baa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why are the flowers falling off my pepper plants before they ever turn into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii shwieɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants often drop their flowers when they suffer from high heat, lack of water, or poor pollination. Keeping the soil consistently damp and allowing bees or wind to move freely through the field helps the flowers stay attached and produce fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo pollination ni ehiii lɛ miipiŋ amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ ji nɔ ni mli edɔ be fɛɛ be. ni oha ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli oya. Enɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ akpɛtɛ he ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking side shoots from my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe ŋmeii ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Removing extra side branches (called suckers) prevents the tomato plant from wasting its energy on excessive leaf growth, allowing it to direct vital nutrients toward growing larger and healthier fruit.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ Baai lɛ adalɛ (ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers) lɛ tsiɔ tomato tso lɛ naa koni ekafite hewalɛ yɛ baai babaoo ni edaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa tomato hiɛɔ niyenii ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ aduawai wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate a lack of nitrogen in the soil or root suffocation from waterlogging. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost helps the plant rebuild its green pigment and continue growing strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli yɛ nu ni eyi obɔ lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen yɔɔ mli tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni etswa e-green pigment lɛ ekoŋŋ ni eya nɔ eda waa.

english: Why is it bad practice for me to plant yam on the exact same plot of land every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ ŋmeii yɛ he kome be fɛɛ be lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani abuɔ enɛ akɛ eji nifeemɔ gbonyo?

english: Planting yam repeatedly on the same land drains specific soil nutrients and lets soil-borne pests, such as nematodes, build up in the ground, leading to weaker yields with each new harvest.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ Yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaajie niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. ni eha shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ nematodes lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmaa hee fɛɛ ŋmaa hee mli.

english: Why do some farmers spread dry grass and leaves around the base of their young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi kɛ baai shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ? Etso bibioo lɛ shishi?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass (mulching) keeps the ground cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly during dry hot days, and stops unwanted weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i. Etsiɔ nu naa koni ekatsɔ oya yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ amli. ni otsi jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my cassava plants yield thin, small roots when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When cassava is planted too close together, the roots compete underground for space, water, and soil food. Giving each plant proper distance ensures the tubers have room to expand into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ gbɛ ni sa ha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa hegbɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwaa kɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do I need to tie my bean plants to wooden stakes instead of letting them spread across the bare dirt?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ ŋmei lɛ fĩɔ tso ko he lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Staking raises the plant stems off the ground, which protects the leaves and pods from soil moisture rot, improves airflow, and gives flowers better exposure to pollinators.
ga: Staking woɔ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Enɛ buɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite kɛjɛ sũ mli ŋmɔtɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ yaa hiɛ. ni eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔii ni amɛkɛ pollinators lɛ yeɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why shouldn't I just save seeds from tomatoes I bought at the local market to plant on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tomato dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ toɔ ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Market tomatoes are often hybrid varieties whose saved seeds will not grow into plants as strong or yield-heavy as the original fruit. Certified seeds bought from trusted extension dealers give reliable yields and disease resistance.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato ni yɔɔ jara nɔ lɛ ji tsofai ni akɛfee tsei ni dumɔwui ni ato lɛ edaaa ni amɛfeɔ tsei ni he wa loo amɛwooo yibii babaoo tamɔ shishijee aduawai lɛ. Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hegbɛ ni aheɔ kɛjɛɔ mɛi ni kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ amɛnɔ lɛ adɛŋ lɛ haa yibiiwoo ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ, ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛnɔ.

english: Why do some vegetable farmers plant onions or strong-smelling herbs along the edges of their crop beds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nitsulɔi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii loo tsofai krokomɛi ni mli wa yɛ amɛŋmɔji lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Strong-smelling crops act as natural pest deterrents because their intense scent confuses and repels insect pests that would normally feed on tender vegetable leaves.
ga: Tsei ni ŋmɔlɔ waa yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛhenumɔ ni naa wa lɛ futuɔ kooloi ni kulɛ amɛyeɔ aduawai ahe baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ni eshwieɔ amɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn yellow from the bottom up while the crop is still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛmiijɛ shishi kɛmiiya ŋwɛi be mli ni tso lɛ miida lolo lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves from the bottom up usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. When nitrogen in the soil is low, the plant moves what little it has to the new top leaves, leaving the bottom leaves to turn yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ Kɛ́ nitrogen ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ tsiɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Ha baai ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ afee ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboi.

english: Why do people advise me to plant beans or groundnuts in the same farm with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni miduɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like beans and groundnuts have special roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and convert it into natural plant food in the soil. Sharing the field with maize feeds the soil naturally and helps your maize produce better yields without relying entirely on expensive artificial fertilizers.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni etsakeɔ lɛ efeɔ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okwaafoi ashikpɔŋ ni okɛ ŋmãa baaja lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni eye ebua oŋmãa lɛ ni ewo yibii kpakpai ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ ŋmãa ni jara wa awo mli.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow huge leafy green bushes but produce very few peppers when I give them lots of manure?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jwɛi wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli shi amɛwoɔ pepper fioo ko pɛ kɛ́ mikɛ amɛ wo mli babaoo lɛ?

english: Animal manure is rich in nitrogen, which encourages plants to build strong stem leaves. However, too much nitrogen tells the plant to focus only on growing foliage instead of flowering and setting fruit, so balancing manure with nutrients like phosphorus helps the plant bloom and produce more peppers.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Enɛ woɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo baai kɛ tsei ni wa. Shi kɛlɛ, nitrogen ni fa fe nine lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai ni miida lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii kɛ niyenii mli nibii tamɔ fɔsfɔs to he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛwo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: Young cocoa plants have thin, sensitive leaves that easily dry out and burn under full heat from the sun. Planting fast-growing crops like plantains creates a living umbrella that shields young cocoa plants from sun exposure and keeps the surrounding air moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshãa oya kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ feɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why do my tomato blossoms drop off without turning into fruit during the extremely hot weeks of the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ otsii ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ yaa nɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When temperatures get too high, the heat damages the delicate pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing them from being fertilized to form fruits. When fertilization fails, the plant naturally drops the unpollinated flower to save energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, hulutsoo be lɛ fiteɔ pollen ŋmeii ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Enɛ haaa amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛwo yibii. Kɛji fɔmɔ nyɛɛɛ aba lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni fɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ kɛjɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do small caterpillars show up and eat the heart of my young maize leaves overnight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii je kpo nyɔɔŋ kome mli koni amɛye mi-abɛi bibii lɛ atsui lɛ?

english: These pests, often known as Fall Armyworms, hide inside the tightly wrapped center leaf funnel during the hot daytime to stay safe and come out at night to eat the soft young growth. Treating the funnel of the plant early protects the growing tip so the corn can continue developing normally.
ga: Nɛkɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui nɛɛ, ni bei pii lɛ ale amɛ akɛ Fall Armyworms lɛ, kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ateŋ gbɛi ni akɛwo mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ amli yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. kɛha shweshweeshwe shihilɛ ni amɛje kpo gbɛkɛ koni amɛye ŋmeii ni miida lɛ. Tso lɛ ŋmeii ahe nitsumɔ mra Ebuɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ahe. Bɔni afee ni ŋmãa lɛ aya nɔ ada bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants curl up tightly and stop growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛfeee agbo lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is typically caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or whiteflies hiding underneath the leaves. As they suck out the plant's juices, they inject toxic saliva that twists the leaves and prevents the plant from absorbing light properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Beni amɛnuɔ nu ni jɛɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ. Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni fiteɔ baai lɛ ni ehaaa tso lɛ aŋɔ la jogbaŋŋ.

english: The very first rain often moistens only the top layer of dirt, while the ground deeper down remains hot and dry. If a long dry spell follows that initial rain, the newly germinated seeds will run out of water and burn up before the main rains begin.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ mra lɛ haa muji ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ kã he edɔ ni egbi. Kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ shishijee nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, nu baaje dumɔwui ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ amli ni amɛbaashã dani nugbɔshiimɔ titri lɛ aje shishi.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become hard, woody, and difficult to boil if I leave them in the ground too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ wa, amɛfeɔ tsei, ni kɛ́ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ, ewa akɛ abaahoo lɛ?

english: Cassava roots store starch for food, but as the plant gets older and reaches maturity, it converts that soft starch into tough wooden fibers to support its stem. Harvesting cassava at the right age ensures the tubers remain high in starch and tender to cook.
ga: Cassava shishifãi kɛ starch toɔ akɛ niyenii. Shi beni tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Ehaa nakai ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ feɔ tso mli tsɔi ni mli wa koni ekɛfi tso lɛ shishi. Kasava ni akpaa yɛ afii ni sa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ŋmeii babaoo yɛ mli lolo ni amɛhe yɛ bɔdɔɔ kɛha nihoomɔ.

english: Why does letting weeds grow close to my young cassava plants cause the tubers to stay small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmei tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii lɛ?

english: Weeds are fast growing and aggressive, so they steal nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight away from your crops. When young cassava plants have to compete with weeds, they cannot produce enough food energy to expand their underground roots into large tubers.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛfeɔ basabasa. No hewɔ lɛ amɛjuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ lɛ yaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Beni esa akɛ cassava tsei bibii lɛ kɛ jwɛi lɛ abɔ akaŋ lɛ. Enyɛŋ ejie niyenii hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: How do I know if a farm medicine I bought for my crops has expired?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni mihe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ efo?

english: Just like medicine for people, crop medicines have an expiry date printed on the bottle. If that date has passed, the chemical loses its power to cure plant sickness and will not protect your crops.
ga: Tamɔ tsofa kɛha gbɔmɛi Tsofai ni aduɔ lɛ yɛ be ni akɛbaatsu nii ni aŋma yɛ tɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji gbi ni awie he lɛ eho lɛ, Chemicals lɛ hu baafee nɔ ni nyɛŋ atsa tsei ahelai ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛbu onibii ahe.

english: What will happen to my crops if I spray them with expired farm medicine?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔ mli tsofa ni efite lɛ wo mli?

english: Expired farm medicine loses its strength, meaning it will fail to stop the pests or diseases damaging your crops. In some cases, old chemicals can even break down and burn your plant leaves.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni be eho lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ, etsĩŋ kooloi bibii loo helai ni baafite onibii lɛ anaa. Yɛ shihilɛi komɛi amli lɛ, tsofai momo baanyɛ akumɔ ni ashã otso lɛ baai.

english: Can old crop chemicals stored from last farming season cause my crops to stop growing well?
ga: Ani tsofai momo ni akɛto kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ho lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, if the chemicals stored from last season have passed their expiration date, they can degrade into harmful compounds that stunt plant growth instead of helping your crops recover.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji tsofai ni ato kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli lɛ eho be ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ he. Nakai tsofai lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ ni amɛfee nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui ni haaa tsei akwɛ̃. Mohu ɔ, e maa ye bua o ngmɔ ní ɔmɛ nɛ a he maa hi.

english: What important details should I check on a chemical container before buying it for my sick crops?
ga: Mɛɛ saji ni he hiaa esa akɛ makwɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma mli dani mahe kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: You should check two main things: the expiry date to ensure the medicine is still active, and the color mark or label at the bottom to confirm it is meant for the specific disease affecting your crops.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ nibii enyɔ ni he hiaa: Be ni tsofa lɛ baagbe naa lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii lolo. kɛ okadi loo niŋmaa ni yɔɔ kɔla ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni baama nɔ mi akɛ eji hela pɔtɛɛ ni miigba onibii lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ.

english: Can I use the same farm medicine to treat any disease I see on my crops?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ tsofai ni jɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ atsa hela fɛɛ hela. Ani manyɛ mana yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ?

english: No, farm medicines are formulated for specific illnesses. The red mark or color code on the bottom of the container indicates which exact crop sickness or pest the medicine is designed to cure.
ga: Dabi, afee ŋmɔ mli tsofai kɛha helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Okadi tsuru loo kɔla ni yɔɔ tsɛnsi lɛ shishi lɛ tsɔɔ tso hela loo tsɛŋemɔ hela ni afee tsofa lɛ koni ekɛtsa.

english: Why are my crop leaves still turning yellow even after I sprayed them with farm medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves may continue to turn yellow if you used an expired medicine that lost its strength, or if you applied a chemical designed for a different sickness than the one affecting your plant.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofa ni efite ni efite nibii ni ekɛtsuɔ nii lɛ tsu nii. aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ tsofai ni afee aha hela kroko ni yɔɔ srɔto fe nɔ ni saa otsei lɛ ahe lɛ tsu nii.

english: Why is my cocoa farm still suffering from black pod disease after I applied chemical spray?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ black pod hela lolo yɛ tsofa ni akɛshwie nɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The spray might not work if the medicine has expired or if it was formulated for insect pests rather than fungal diseases like black pod. Always check the specific disease mark on the label before spraying.
ga: Ekolɛ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuuu nii kɛji tsofa lɛ be eho loo afee aha tsɛŋemɔ helai. Jeee tsɛŋemɔ hela, tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji. Kwɛmɔ hela pɔtɛɛ ko he okadi ni aŋmala nɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be dani okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ nɔ.

english: What do the colored marks at the bottom of farm chemical bottles tell me about my crops?
ga: Mɛni okadii ni yɔɔ kɔla ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsɛnsii lɛ ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ mi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe?

english: The colored marks on chemical containers show the specific crop illness or pest the product treats, as well as safety indicators so you know you are applying the right cure to your field.
ga: Okadii ni yɔɔ kɔla ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi ni tsofa lɛ tsaa. kɛ agbɛnɛ shweshweeshwefeemɔ he okadii Enɛ ji koni ole akɛ okɛ tsofa ni sa kɛha oŋmɔ lɛ miitsu nii.

english: Why did insects keep destroying my maize even after I sprayed the field yesterday?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii yaa nɔ amɛgbeɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ nyɛ moŋ?

english: The insects may persist if the chemical you sprayed was past its expiry date and no longer effective, or if the product was meant to treat plant diseases rather than insect pests.
ga: Kplukai baanyɛ ahi shi kɛji tsofai ni okɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ eho be ni esa akɛ ekɛtsu nii lɛ he ni etsuuu nii dɔŋŋ. Aloo kɛji akɛ afee nɔ ni akɛfee lɛ koni akɛtsa tsei ahe helai moŋ fe tsɛŋemɔ helai.

english: How do I make sure I am buying the right medicine for my damaged vegetable crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mihe tsofa ni sa kɛha aduawai ni efite lɛ?

english: Identify the exact symptom on your vegetables first, then check the color mark at the bottom of the medicine bottle to ensure it matches the disease, and verify that the expiry date has not passed.
ga: Kwɛmɔ okadi pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ o-vegetables lɛ nɔ lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ. No sɛɛ lɛ, kwɛmɔ okadii ni yɔɔ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma lɛ shishi lɛ koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ amɛkɛ hela lɛ kpãa gbee lo. ni okwɛ akɛ gbi ni akɛbaatsu nii lɛ ehoko lolo

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to strong sunlight. Plantain trees grow quickly and provide large leaves that shade the young cocoa plants from harsh sun and keep the soil moist during their first few years.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa he waa. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya ni amɛwoɔ baai agboi ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shaa kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my maize crops turning yellow before they produce corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmãa dani amɛwo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is a vital food for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or Urea early in the season helps keep the leaves green and boosts yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo urea wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni eha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready 9 to 12 months after planting, when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and drop off, and the ground around the base of the plant starts cracking open.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei feɔ klalo akɛ abaadu yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ, beni shishigbɛ baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ. kɛ hei ni ebɔle ehe lɛ Tso lɛ shishi bɔi fãmɔ.

english: This damage is usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the central leaves of young maize plants. Catching them early and spraying recommended insecticides or neem extract stops them from destroying the farm.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Ni okɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi akɛ akɛshwie nɔ lɛ baaye abua ni amɛkafite ŋmɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without turning into tomatoes during the hot season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ tomato yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when they get stressed by extreme heat or irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist and spreading dry leaves around the base helps keep roots cool and saves the flowers.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baafɔ kɛji akɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hao amɛ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ po nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ baai ni egbi lɛ mlijaa yɛ he fɛɛ he Konus lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to spread their leaves to catch maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to make food, which travels down to grow large, healthy tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛbai lɛ amɛshwã koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛfeɔ niyenii. ni tsiɔ ehe kɛyaa shi koni ekwɛ̃ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa

english: Too many shoots steal food and water from the main plant, leading to small bunches. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main plant gets enough nutrients to produce a large, heavy bunch.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ tso titri lɛ mli. ni kɛ tso bibioo ko baa Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yibii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛfee tsei niji wuji ni tsii.

english: Planting maize continuously in the same soil drains specific nutrients and allows crop pests to build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil and cleans out pests.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii pɔtɛɛ komɛi hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai shwereɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa nitrogen kuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni egbeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Is it better to put fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy rain or after?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli ŋmɔshi nibii dani nugbɔ nɛ waa loo beni nugbɔ enɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain, or right before a light drizzle. Heavy downpours wash the fertilizer away into streams before the plant roots can absorb it.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. aloo dani nugbɔ fioo ko aba Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ faai amli dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or aphids under the leaves. Spraying with a soapy water mixture or neem oil solution helps clear these pests so new leaves grow normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni yɔɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ nu ni mli edɔ loo neem fɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie nɛkɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai nɛɛ. koni baai heei anyɛ akwɛ̃ bɔ ni sa

english: Why are my seeds failing to sprout in the nursery bed after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekwɛɛɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds need the right balance of depth, moisture, and care to sprout. If seeds are planted without consistent depth or proper moisture control, many will fail to germinate or rot under the soil.
ga: Ehe miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ aná mlibotemɔ, ŋmɔtɔ, kɛ kwɛmɔ ni sa koni amɛkwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo be ni sa bɛ mli lɛ, Dumɔwui babaoo kwɛŋ loo amɛbaafite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it good practice for me to put two or three seeds in one nursery bag?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ akɛ dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ baawo grow bag kome mli?

english: Putting two or three seeds in a single bag ensures that at least one good plant grows even if some seeds fail. Once they sprout, you can remove the weaker ones so the strongest seedling has space to grow.
ga: Dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ ni akɛwoɔ kotoku kome mli lɛ haa kɛ hoo lɛ, tso kpakpa kome baakwɛ̃ kɛji ekomɛi nyɛɛɛ akwɛ̃ po. Kɛ amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ, obaanyɛ ojie tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni he wa fe fɛɛ lɛ naa gbɛ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do some seeds in my nursery bed germinate quickly while others next to them do not come up at all?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ kwɛɛɛ oya lɛ?

english: Seeds sprout unevenly when they are planted at different depths or receive unequal amounts of water. Consistent planting depth and careful watering help all seeds germinate at the same time.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ hei srɔtoi loo aha amɛ nu babaoo. Dumɔwui lɛ amlibotemɔ ni yaa nɔ daa kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ fɛɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: What care do my planted seeds need in the nursery bed before I start seeing green leaves?
ga: Te mi dumɔwui ni midu lɛ he hiaa ha tɛŋŋ yɛ ŋmɔ mli dani mabɔi baai eŋɔli namɔ?

english: Before seeds sprout, they need light daily watering to keep the soil moist, protection from heavy direct rain, and correct soil coverage so they can push through easily.
ga: Dani dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ Ehe miihia ni afɔ amɛ nu fioo daa gbi koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Ebuɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa tɛ̃ɛ he. ni osaa shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɔne lɛ he bɔni afee ni anyɛ atsɔ mli mlɛo.

english: How deep should I dig the ground when planting a seedling from a nursery bag?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu dumɔwui kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli kotokui amli?

english: The hole should be about one finger's depth so that the top soil of the nursery bag sits perfectly level with the ground when planted. This keeps the roots protected without suffocating the plant.
ga: Esa akɛ bu lɛ mli ashɛ aaafee 1 inch bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ grow bag lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ekome kɛji adu. Enɛ buɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe ni ehaaa tso lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I bury the nursery bag too deep in the soil?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji mifu grow bags lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli tsɔ?

english: Burying a nursery bag too deep covers the tender stem with soil, which traps moisture around the trunk and can cause stem rot or stunt the growth of your crop.
ga: Ni aaafu dumɔ kotoku lɛ mli tsɔ ni ekɛ sũ aha tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ anɔ Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ ebɔleɔ tso lɛ he ni ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo loo etsĩ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: How do I make sure my nursery bag sits correctly in the field when I plant it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ mi-grow bags lɛ yɛ he ni sa beni miduɔ mitsei lɛ?

english: Place the nursery bag in the dug hole so its surface matches the level of the field soil exactly, then fill the sides with loose dirt to hold it firmly in place.
ga: Okɛ grow bag lɛ awo bu ni ofo lɛ mli bɔni afee ni ehiɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ akpã gbee. No sɛɛ lɛ, okɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli tse afata he. yɛ afã lɛ koni emɔmɔ mli shiŋŋ.

english: Can planting my seeds too deep under the dirt prevent them from coming up?
ga: Ani midumɔwui lɛ ni mikɛduɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi shɔŋŋ tsɔ lɛ baanyɛ atsĩ amɛnaa koni amɛkakwɛ̃?

english: Yes, if seeds are buried too deep, they run out of stored energy before their shoots can reach the surface, causing them to die underground.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ afu dumɔwui lɛ amli tsɔ Hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baaho dani ŋmeii lɛ ashɛ nu lɛ hiɛ. Enɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ gboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my young seedlings wilt or die soon after I move them from the nursery into my main farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi loo amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee miŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings often suffer shock if they are planted too shallowly or too deeply, or if their roots dry out during transplanting. Matching the original nursery soil depth helps them settle quickly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ naa shoofeemɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ loo amɛbote mli tsɔ. aloo kɛji shishifãi lɛ gĩ yɛ be mli ni aduɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ mlibotemɔ ni atsakeɔ yɛ shishijee ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa amɛwoɔ shishifãi oya.

english: How long should I wait to see sprouts in my nursery before I know the seeds are dead?
ga: Be enyiɛ esa akɛ mamɛ ni makwɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani male akɛ amɛgboi?

english: Most crop seeds should sprout within one to two weeks depending on the variety. If nothing appears after this time, it usually means the seeds rotted, were buried wrong, or were not viable.
ga: Esa akɛ dumɔwui babaoo akwɛ̃ yɛ otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ mli, ni enɛ damɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nɔ ko ejeee kpo yɛ be nɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ egbo, amɛfu yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ, loo yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are sensitive to harsh, direct sunlight, which burns their young leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Planting fast-growing shade plants like plantains creates a canopy that protects young cocoa trees until they grow strong enough to withstand direct sun.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni naa wa waa he tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ baaha baai bibii lɛ ashã ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ agbi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ haa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ cacao tsei bibii ahe lɛ baa kɛyashiɔ be mli ni tsei lɛ daa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ amɛtsui shi yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food that builds big tubers underground. Using wooden stakes lifts the vines off the ground, giving leaves maximum sunlight and keeping them off damp soil where diseases spread.
ga: Hulu la he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛfee niyenii ni feɔ bulbs wuji lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Tsoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tsei lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ji helai ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ lɛ jɛɛhe lɛ naa

english: Why do farmers put dry grass on top of the soil around their pepper plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo lɛ kɛ jwɛi fɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or straw, known as mulching, stops the sun from drying out the soil too quickly. It keeps the roots cool, conserves water, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi loo jwɛi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha hulu lɛ akaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Ehaa shishifãi lɛ amli jɔɔ, ehiɛɔ nu mli, ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃.

english: Yellow leaves near the base of a corn plant are a classic sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Nitrogen is an essential food for crops, and when the soil lacks it, the plant moves what little it has to the newest growth at the top.
ga: Baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ ji okadi ni ale jogbaŋŋ ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli etse Tso lɛ baajie nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛya shweremɔ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ nɔ.

english: Maize consumes a lot of nitrogen from the soil, leaving it weak. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts naturally pull nitrogen from the air and return it to the soil, refreshing your land for the next planting season.
ga: Abɛi heɔ nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji shikpɔŋ ni bɛ hewalɛ Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ diɛŋtsɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ehee kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii akwɛmɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots and leaves fight with each other for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to feed and produce full yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛyeɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ekpamɔ lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava stems twisting up and turning patchy yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋwɛi ni efee ŋmɔŋ yɛ hei srɔtoi lɛ?

english: This leaf curling is caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried and spread from plant to plant by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting certified disease-resistant cassava varieties prevents this issue.
ga: Cassava mosaic hela ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi nɛɛ baa. Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ amɛ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa kɛjɛɔ tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ. Kasava henɔi ni ana he odaseyeli akɛ helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ adumɔ baanyɛ aye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do the bottoms of my green tomatoes rot and turn black before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ miifite ni etsɔ ediŋŋ dani ekwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Black, sunken bottoms on tomatoes are caused by blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot pull up enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Tomato shishi ni egbo, ni ji diŋ lɛ jɛ fɔfɔi ni egbo lɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite.

english: Weeds grow much faster than crops and aggressively steal nutrients, water, and sunlight meant for your plants. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to thrive.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni ekɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ, nu, kɛ hulu la ni ato he gbɛjianɔ aha otsei lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa oŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do my harvested yam tubers start growing shoots in the barn even when I don't plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato tubers ni mikpa lɛ miibɔi shweremɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ miduuu amɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers naturally go through a resting period after harvest, but after a few months, they wake up and try to grow into new plants using the energy stored in the tuber. Keeping them in a cool, well-ventilated yam barn slows down this sprouting process.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ yɛ be ni amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Shi yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ Ebaate shi ni ebɔ mɔdɛŋ ni etsɔ tso hee kɛtsɔ hewalɛ ni ato yɛ eyitso mli lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ amɛ wo sweet potato ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha amɛkwɛ̃mɔ aya hiɛ fioo.

english: When cocoa pods turn dark or black before ripening, it is usually a sign of Black Pod disease caused by excessive moisture and fungal infection. Healthy pods naturally change from green or red to yellow or orange when they are ready for harvest.
ga: Beni kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ loo ediŋŋ dani amɛshwereɔ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ ji black pod hela ni ŋmɔtɔ babaoo kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ kɛbaa lɛ he okadi. Pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baatsɔ adebɔɔ naa kɛjɛ eŋɔli loo etsuru mli kɛya ŋmɔŋ loo akutu mli kɛji amɛfee klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ.

english: What causes tiny dark spots and dry scars on my young cocoa pods and stems?
ga: Mɛni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii baa? kɛ ŋmeii ni egbi ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: These dark spots are typically caused by mirid bugs, commonly known in Ghana as 'Akate.' These pests pierce the skin of young pods and shoots to suck out sap, leaving dark, dead patches that can stunt pod growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, mirid kooloo ni ale lɛ waa yɛ Ghana akɛ 'Akate' lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ baa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ tsɔɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ahewolo nɔ koni amɛmu nu lɛ mli nu lɛ. Eshiɔ hei ni tsuɔ, ni egboi ni baanyɛ aha pod lɛ adalɛ aba shi.

english: How do I know if a new spray or chemical will actually help my cocoa yield?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofa hee ko ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ loo tsofa ko baaha kookoo yibii lɛ aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: You can confirm if an input is safe and effective by checking if it is approved by the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), asking your local extension officer, and testing it on a small section of your farm before spraying everywhere.
ga: Obaanyɛ oma nɔ mi akɛ saji ni okɛwo mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe ni etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛtsɔ Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) lɛ kpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni no sɛɛ lɛ obi he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli nitsulɔ ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ nɔ. ni oka lɛ okwɛ yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ he bibioo ko dani okɛ tsofa lɛ afɔ he fɛɛ he.

english: Young cocoa trees have sensitive foliage that easily scorches under direct, harsh sunlight. Without shade plants like plantain or permanent shade trees to shield them, the intense sun pulls water out of the leaves faster than the roots can supply it.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni shɛɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Kɛji akɛ tsei ni hiɛdɔɔ yɔɔ mli ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo daa bɛ ni baaha nɔ lɛ, Hulu ni naa wa lɛ gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aha lɛ.

english: Dropping leaves during the dry Harmattan period is a natural survival trick cocoa trees use to reduce water loss. The fallen leaves also form a protective blanket on the soil surface to hold in remaining soil moisture.
ga: Baai ni ashwieɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli wala yiwalaheremɔ gbɛ ni cacao tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Baai ni egbee shi lɛ hu feɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni eshwɛ lɛ ahi shi.

english: Cocoa trees shed flowers when they suffer from stress, such as prolonged dry spells, nutrient deficiency in the soil, or pest damage to the flower stems. Maintaining proper shade and soil fertility helps more flowers set into pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ nɔ ko miigba amɛnaa, tamɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni nu egbi. niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ fiteɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ He ni akwɛɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be ni sa kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɔfɔii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi babaoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Will cutting off extra branches from my cocoa trees reduce how many pods I harvest?
ga: Ani mi cacao tso lɛ niji krokomɛi ni mifoɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii ni mikpaa lɛ ayibɔ aba shi?

english: Pruning unnecessary or diseased branches actually increases your yield. It allows light and air to circulate through the canopy, lowers disease risk, and forces the tree to direct its energy into producing healthy pods.
ga: Niji ni he ehiaaa loo hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ baanyɛ aha yibiiwoo aya hiɛ diɛŋtsɛ. Ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ mli. Ha helai ni baanyɛ aba lɛ aba shi ni enyɛ tso lɛ nɔ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛfee ŋmeii ni mli wa.

english: A cocoa pod is ripe when its outer skin turns completely yellow or orange, depending on the variety, and makes a hollow sound when you tap it gently with your knuckles.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ kwraa. Edamɔ henɔi lɛ anɔ Ni ebaafee gbee ni mli ewo muji kɛ́ okɛ otsitsi tswa lɛ fioo.

english: Why do I need to heap my cocoa beans and cover them with banana leaves after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mibuaa kookoo ŋmeii anaa ni mikɛ banana baai haa nɔ beni mikpa lɛ?

english: Covering the fresh beans with banana leaves creates a warm environment for fermentation to happen. This natural heating process changes the color of the beans and creates the true chocolate flavor buyers look for.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ banana baai ha ŋmeii heei ahe lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ baa koni ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmeii. Nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli latsaa gbɛ nɛɛ tsakeɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ ahe su ni ehaa tsokolate lɛ mli ŋɔɔmɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni mɛi ni heɔ lɛ taoɔ lɛ baa.

english: Why are some of my dried cocoa beans purple inside instead of dark brown?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ mli lɛ ji purple yɛ brown ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Purple beans inside mean the cocoa was not fermented long enough before drying. Proper fermentation breaks down the bitter purple compounds inside the bean, turning them a rich brown color.
ga: Purple beans ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ cocoa lɛ shwieee shi be kakadaŋŋ dani egbi. Kɛ́ afee ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, efiteɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli lɛ. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do some farmers use heated machines to dry maize instead of just leaving it in the sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsɔnei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii kɛgbiɔ amɛŋmãa lɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaashi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Applying controlled heat removes water from maize kernels much faster than the sun, which protects the harvest from unexpected rain, high humidity, and mold growth.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni akudɔɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa mli oya fe hulu la. Enɛ buɔ dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ trukaa, hulutsoo ni naa wa, kɛ ŋmeii ni baa lɛ ahe.

english: Can applying heat to my harvested maize damage the grains?
ga: Ani la ni mikɛwoɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afite ŋmaa lɛ?

english: If the heat is controlled properly, it safely reduces moisture without harming the grain; however, if the heat is too high, it can burn the kernels or ruin maize meant for seed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ akudɔ latsaa lɛ jogbaŋŋ Enɛ baaye abua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aba shi shweshweeshwe ni eyeee dumɔwui lɛ awui. Shi kɛji la lɛ fa tsɔ Ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo efite ŋmãa ni ato akɛ abaadu lɛ.

english: Why does my maize lose weight after it goes through a drying process?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize loses weight during drying because the water trapped inside the kernels evaporates into the air, leaving behind solid, dry grain.
ga: Abele lɛ mli tsiimɔ baa shi yɛ be mli ni egbiɔ lɛ, be mli ni nu ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ. Ashiɔ dumɔwui ni wa ni egbi lɛ yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why is it dangerous to store my freshly harvested maize while it still feels wet or damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ makɛ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa ehee lɛ ato be mli ni enuɔ he akɛ eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo eyɛ ŋmɔtɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Damp maize holds trapped water that creates a warm environment for fungi and dangerous molds to grow, which causes the crop to rot and spoil rapidly.
ga: Abɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ haa nu hiɔ shi, ni no haa shihilɛ ni mli edɔɔ baa kɛha ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ adalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ oya.

english: Does keeping water out of my stored maize help prevent insect attacks?
ga: Ani nu ni akɛtoɔ ŋmãa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ tsiɔ kooloi ni baatutua amɛ lɛ anaa?

english: Yes, pests like weevils thrive in soft, moist grains. Lowering the water level makes the grains hard and dry, making it difficult for insects to feed and reproduce.
ga: Hɛɛ, kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Kɛ́ ajie nu lɛ shi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa koolooi akɛ amɛaaye nii ni amɛfɔ bii.

english: How does removing moisture from my maize help me get a better market price?
ga: Te ŋmɔtɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni maná jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ yɛ jara nɔ lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry maize lasts longer without spoiling, allowing you to store it safely and sell it when market supply drops and prices rise.
ga: Abɛi ni egbi lɛ baahi shi be kakadaŋŋ ni efiteee. Ehaa okɛ nibii toɔ ni ohɔ̃ɔ shweshweeshwe kɛ́ jarayeli nibii lɛ ba shi ni amɛjara hu tee ŋwɛi.

english: Why shouldn't I put freshly harvested maize straight into heavy sacks right after picking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ni akpa ehee lɛ woɔ kotokui ni tsii amli tɛ̃ɛ kɛ́ akpa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Fresh maize continuously releases moisture. Trapping that moisture inside sealed sacks creates heat and sweat, causing the grain to rot in just a few days.
ga: Abele hee jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be. Fɛ̃i ni akɛwoɔ kotoku ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ haa dɔlɛ kɛ latsaa baa. Ehaa omɔ ŋmaa lɛ fiteɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ mli.

english: Why is reducing water in maize necessary before taking it to the mill to grind into flour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ ajie nu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ shi dani akɛya ŋmãa ŋtayaa he koni atsɔ mli ashikiŋsha lɛ?

english: Wet maize turns into a sticky paste that clogs milling machines and spoils quickly, whereas properly dried maize grinds into fine, long-lasting flour.
ga: Abɛi ni efɔ lɛ tsɔɔ oya ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ naa ni efiteɔ. Beni abele lɛ gĩɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, agbɛɔ lɛ ni efeɔ powda kpakpa ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Does removing moisture from maize cobs make them easier to shell?
ga: Ani ŋmɔtɔ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaajie ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Yes, as maize loses moisture, the kernels shrink slightly and loosen from the central cob, making them much easier to remove without damaging the grain.
ga: Hɛɛ, ejaakɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. Kɛkɛ lɛ dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo ni amɛjɛɔ ŋmei lɛ teŋgbɛ amɛshwieɔ shi. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kwraa akɛ abaajie ni efiteee dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my harvested maize has high moisture inside it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele ni akpa lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ mli?

english: High-moisture maize feels soft to bite, leaves dampness on your hands, makes a dull sound when dropped, and easily dents when pressed with a fingernail.
ga: Abɛi ni mli edɔ waa lɛ nuɔ he akɛ eyɛ blɛoo kɛ́ ekɛmiiye. Eshiɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ oniji anɔ Gbee ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa kɛji akɛ ashwie shi. ni efoɔ mlɛo kɛji akɛ akɛ niji nyɛ nɔ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep drying up and dying when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ? He ni tsei wuji komɛi bɛ he lɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Big shade trees act like natural umbrellas that protect cocoa seedlings from burning, keep the soil moist, and shield them from strong winds.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo baa lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni buɔ kookoo dumɔwui ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. ni abuɔ he kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa he

english: What happens if I plant my cocoa trees very close together so I can get more trees on my land?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ midu kookoo tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa koni maná tsei babaoo yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Planting crops too close together forces the trees to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak trees that produce very small yields compared to properly spaced trees.
ga: Tsei ni aduɔ yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he. Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ woɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ kɛ akɛto tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ ahe lɛ baa.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off to the ground without growing into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛdaraaa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Flowers usually drop off when the tree is stressed by dry weather, lacks essential soil nutrients, or gets damaged by small insects before the flowers can fully develop into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii efite Dani fɔfɔi lɛ baanyɛ adara kwraa ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves on my cocoa tree turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that your crop is hungry for nutrients, particularly nitrogen, or that the soil is too dry or waterlogged for the roots to feed properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he miihia onibii. titri lɛ nitrogen Aloo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ ni enyɛŋ eha shishifãi lɛ aná niyenii ni sa.

english: Why should I cut off healthy-looking extra branches from my tree if I want it to produce more fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ niji ni fa fe nine ni tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ kɛjɛ mitso lɛ mli kɛji miisumɔ ni ewo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning removes unnecessary branches so the tree can send all its water and energy directly into growing healthy fruits, while also letting light and air flow through to stop diseases.
ga: Niji ni afoɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ tsei niji ni he ehiaaa lɛ. Enɛ ji bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akudɔ enu kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛya aduawai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni miida lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli koni ekɛtsi helai srɔtoi anaa.

english: What are those small green bushes growing on my cocoa tree branches, and are they harming my crop?
ga: jwɛi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ Mɛni ji mɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi koko tso lɛ niji anɔ lɛ? Ni ani amɛyeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui?

english: Those green bushes are parasitic plants called mistletoes. They grow directly into your tree's branches to steal water and nutrients, which gradually weakens the tree and lowers pod production.
ga: Nakai tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ ji tso ko ni tsɛŋeɔ mɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ mistletoe. Amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tso niji tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛju nu kɛ niyenii, ni no haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ fiofio ni ehaa pod ni ajieɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Can I plant cassava directly next to my young cocoa trees, or will it ruin the farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ kookoo tso bibioo ko masɛi? Aloo ebaafite ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots spread fast and drink a lot of water and nutrients from the earth. Planting it too close to young cocoa starves the cocoa seedlings, so plantain is preferred because it provides good shade without aggressively choking the cocoa roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi gbɛɔ eshwaa oya ni amɛheɔ nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo bibii lɛ tsɔ lɛ, hɔmɔ baaye kookoo dumɔwui lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, mɛi sumɔɔ plantains ejaakɛ ehaa hulutsoo kpakpa baa ni efiteee kookoo shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why should I leave dry fallen leaves under my trees instead of sweeping the ground clean?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi baai ni egboi ni egbee shi lɛ yɛ tso lɛ shishi moŋ fe ni mafo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Fallen leaves form a natural blanket over the soil that holds water during dry seasons, stops weeds from growing, and slowly rots into rich organic fertilizer for your crops.
ga: Baai ni egbee shi lɛ feɔ adebɔɔ mli tsɔne ko ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛhiɛ nu mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads fast in damp, dark, and overly wet conditions. Clearing weeds and pruning excess tree branches lets air in to dry out the moisture that causes the rot.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni edɔ, ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ fe nine. Tso lɛ niji ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni afoɔ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ mli koni ejie ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tso lɛ fiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why do I need to spread my cocoa beans in the sun right after taking them out of the pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-kokoo ŋmeii lɛ agbi yɛ hulutsoo be mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Sun drying removes moisture from the beans after fermentation. This prevents mold from growing on them and ensures the beans develop the right quality and flavor for sale.
ga: Hulu ni akɛgbiɔ lɛ jieɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛjɛɔ kɔfi yibii lɛ amli beni amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haaa ŋmeii aya hiɛ, ni ehaa kɔfi ŋmeii lɛ ahilɛ-kɛhamɔ kɛ amɛhe ŋɔɔ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha jarayeli.

english: Why do my young tomato seedlings look weak and droopy a few days after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui bibii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi yɛ gbii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Seedlings experience transplant shock when moved to a new environment. Their roots need a few days to settle into the main soil, so watering them in the evening and providing temporary shade helps them recover quickly.
ga: Dumɔwui naa transplant shock kɛji ajie amɛ kɛtee he ko hee. Amɛshishifãi lɛ heɔ gbii fioo dani amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ afɔ amɛ nu gbɛkɛ ni aha amɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo ko lɛ, ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛhe awa amɛ oya.

english: How do I prepare my pepper seedlings in the nursery so they do not die when exposed to the strong sun in the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masaa pepper dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔ mli? Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ akagbo kɛ́ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛ enɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: You need to train or 'harden off' the seedlings by gradually exposing them to more direct sun and slightly reducing water for about a week before moving them to the main field.
ga: Ani esa akɛ okɛ ohe awo mli? ‘Okɛwo dumɔwui lɛ amli waa’ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ fiofio ni okɛ nu lɛ baa shi fioo aaafee otsi kome dani okɛ amɛ awo saatso wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa plants need palm fronds shaded over them when I first plant them out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso bibioo lɛ he bahia ni maná shade palm baai beni midu lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ kwraa lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under intense heat. Providing overhead shade creates a comfortable, protected environment for the first few months until their roots grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋwɛi ŋmɔlɔ haa lɛ, ehaa shihilɛ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni abuɔ he yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔji fioo lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ ahe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: If some of my maize seeds fail to germinate after two weeks, should I plant new seeds in those empty spots?
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui komɛi ekwɛɛɛ yɛ otsii enyɔ sɛɛ Ani Esa akɛ madu dumɔwui heei yɛ nakai hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ amli?

english: Yes, this is called gap filling or supply planting. Doing this early ensures every space on your farm produces crops without the older plants growing too tall and shading out the new ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ gap filling loo nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ ni yaa hiɛ. Nifeemɔ kɛjɛ shishijee Enɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ mli he fɛɛ he aná ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsei momo lɛ akakwɛ̃ tsɔ ni amɛtsi eheei lɛ anaa.

english: What happens to my cassava crop if I plant the cuttings too close together?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ?

english: Planting too close forces the crops to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives each plant enough comfort and room to grow large, healthy roots.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa miishɛjemɔ kɛ he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ shishifãi wuji ni wa baakwɛ̃.

english: Should I mix manure into the soil before or after I transplant my vegetable seedlings?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii afutu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu aduawai dumɔwui loo beni midu sɛɛ?

english: It is best to mix manure or compost into the soil a week or two before transplanting so the nutrients integrate into the ground, making food immediately available for the roots.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli otsi kome loo enyɔ dani okɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. koni eha niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ abote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Ehaa niyenii baa shishifãi lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant pepper on the exact same plot of land where I just harvested tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa mi-tomato lɛ nɔ kɛkɛ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ?

english: Tomatoes and peppers belong to the same plant family and share the same soil pests and diseases. Moving them to a different plot breaks the disease cycle and keeps the soil productive.
ga: Tomato kɛ pepper yɛ tso weku kome mli ni amɛ fɛɛ amɛyɔɔ sũ mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai kome. Kɛ́ ajie amɛ kɛtee shikpɔŋ kroko nɔ lɛ, ebaakpa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu lɛ, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ awo yibii babaoo.

english: Can I plant cowpea together with my maize on the same plot at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tsina ŋmei kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen from the air and feed the soil, which helps the maize grow better while covering the ground to prevent weeds.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsina ŋmeii mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jwɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: How can I tell if my newly moved cabbage crops are suffering from heat stress?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ mi-cabbage ni mikɛwo mli ehee lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: If the leaves turn yellow, get crispy along the edges, or remain wilted even after watering in the evening, the crops are stressed by excessive heat and need extra moisture or shade.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛnaagbɛ, loo amɛtee nɔ amɛgboi yɛ be mli ni awo amɛ nu gbɛkɛ po sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hulutsoo ni fe nine lɛ haa tsei lɛ haoɔ. ni ebiɔ ni hulutsoo loo hulutsoo kroko afata he.

english: Why do some vegetable farmers plant their seeds in batches every two weeks instead of planting the whole field at once?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai abɔɔ mli nitsulɔi komɛi duɔ dumɔwui akuu kome daa otsii enyɔ, shi jeee ni amɛduɔ ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ?

english: Staggering your planting spreads out your harvest over time so you always have fresh crops to sell, preventing all your produce from getting ripe at once and spoiling before sale.
ga: Dumɔ ni ooodu yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔtoi nɔ lɛ baagbɛ okpamɔ lɛ eshwa yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, oyɛ nibii heei ni okɛhɔ̃ɔ be fɛɛ be. Tsi onibii fɛɛ ni okɛwoɔ mli lɛ naa koni amɛkakwɛ̃ shikome ni amɛfite dani ohɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains or cassava next to my new cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu plantains loo cassava yɛ mi-cocoa tso hee lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under strong sunlight. Fast-growing plants like plantains provide living shade and keep the soil cool and moist while the young cocoa matures.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains haa hulutsoo ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa yɛ be mli ni kookoo bibii lɛ daa lɛ.

english: When seeds are planted too close, the growing crops fight each other for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil, leading to thin stalks and small or empty ears.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ toi bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli lɛ baa.

english: Yam plants are vines that need to climb high to capture maximum sunlight. Elevating the leaves allows the plant to produce more energy, which builds larger tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni esa akɛ amɛkwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa hewalɛ babaoo. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji baa.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize is lacking nitrogen in the soil or the ground is overly waterlogged, which prevents the roots from taking up nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi sũ lɛ mli tsɔ. ni tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with huge green leaves but give me small roots at harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ewoɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ akpa?

english: Too much nitrogen in the soil makes cassava put all its energy into growing stem and leaves above ground instead of storing starch in the root tubers below.
ga: Nitrogen ni fa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmei kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ starch toɔ tso ɔ sisi fã nɛ ngɛ sisi ɔ mi.

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil, naturally restoring soil nutrients that hungry crops like maize took away.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Koni ekɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: What is eating small holes into the central leaves of my young maize and leaving dark powder?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ buji bibii ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli ni eshiɔ powda ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ sɛɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the central leaf whorl and feeds on the soft growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ ŋmeii ni miida blɛoo lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Tomato blossoms fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks key nutrients required to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii lɛ

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and stunted even when there is enough rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ bɔ ni sa po lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than crops and steal the fertilizer, soil water, and light that your crop needs to develop properly.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: How do I know the soil has enough moisture for me to start planting my seeds after the early rains?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ mabɔi dumɔwui adumɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Seeds need steady moisture to germinate without drying out; wait until the soil is damp a few inches deep for a couple of consecutive rainy days before sowing.
ga: Dumɔwui taoɔ nu ni mli edɔ daa koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛgbiŋ. Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ 2-3 inches mli kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ gbii 2-3 ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ dani odu dumɔwui.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their tender leaves from harsh direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantain plants to shield them, the intense sun burns the seedlings and dries out the moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ biɔ hulutsoo koni amɛbu baai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he. Kɛji tsei ni baaha hulutsoo be loo dumɔwui ni baaha hulu la ni tsoɔ waa bɛ lɛ baashã dumɔwui lɛ ni ebaaha nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ agbi.

english: Yam vines produce leaves that need maximum sunlight to make food for the growing tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the damp ground, preventing rot and giving the leaves full exposure to sunlight.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ baai ni biɔ hulu la babaoo koni ekɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ niyenii. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ fitemɔ naa ni ekwɛɔ koni baai lɛ aná hulu la ni fa.

english: Why do people cover the soil around crops with dry grass during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, keeps the ground cool and prevents soil water from evaporating quickly under the hot sun, keeping moisture available for the crop's roots.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Koni afee ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi tsei ashishifãi lɛ amli

english: Why is it bad for me to apply fertilizer right before heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaawo ŋmɔshi nibii amli dani nugbɔ anɛ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer off the surface of your field before the crop roots have time to absorb it, which wastes your money and can pollute nearby water sources.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani tsei shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii. Enɛ fiteɔ shika, ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ muji aba nu jɛɛhei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does rice require so much water compared to corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants are naturally adapted to grow in saturated soil, which suppresses weeds and keeps the plant cool. Corn roots, on the other hand, need air in the soil and will rot if underwater for long periods.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni eyi obɔ kɛ nu nɔ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ jwɛi lɛ tsiɔ naa ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ he miihia ni kɔɔyɔɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ebaagbo kɛji akɛ akɛto nu shishi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves of my young corn look like someone shot small holes all over them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni mɔ ko etswa amɛ fɛɛ lɛ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, a caterpillar that burrows into the center of the plant to feed on tender growing leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tswaa bu yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ koni eye baa bibii ni miida lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ bu baa.

english: Root rot occurs when water sits in the soil for too long without proper drainage, causing fungal growth. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Shishifãi fitemɔ baa kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ekɛ fungal dalɛ baa. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking the sap from the leaves, or by a viral infection spread by these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ baai lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. loo kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli

english: Yellowing lower leaves on maize usually mean the plant lacks nitrogen, an essential nutrient needed for healthy leaf growth. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps restore healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa koni baa lɛ aya hiɛ waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ baa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences stress from excessive heat or irregular watering. When stressed, the plant drops its blossoms to save energy for survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ dɔlɛ ni fa fe nine loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ mli. Kɛji nɔnyɛɛ ba Tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛhi shi.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade because direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil moisture. Keeping bigger shade trees or planting plantains nearby protects them until they grow strong enough to handle full sun.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ.
