Tsei akwɛmɔ koni amɛfee wuji loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ Ebaaye ebua ni abu tsei nɛɛ ahe kɛyashi amɛbaadara ni amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhe hulu la lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow healthy leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer restores their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi a-nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Crops like beans and groundnuts naturally capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil. Planting them after maize restores nutrients to the land without having to buy extra fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa sɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni niyenii mli hewalɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe ehiaaa ni ahe ŋmãa kroko kɛfata he.

english: If cassava stems are planted too close together, they fight for nutrients and sunlight, putting all their energy into leafy stems instead of roots. Spacing them properly gives the roots enough room and food to swell into large tubers.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmei ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Ebaatswa akaŋ kɛha niyenii kɛ hulu la. Kɛtsɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli kɛ baai ni ekɛwoɔ shishifãi najiaŋ lɛ nɔ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa gbɛ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛshwere ni amɛtsɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Too many extra shoots, or suckers, steal water and food from the main plantain tree. Removing most of them leaves enough energy for the main plant to produce big, heavy bunches of plantain.
ga: Tsobii krokomɛi loo tsei bibii juɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ dumɔwu titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie emli babaoo lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantains akui wuji ni tsii.

english: Yam plants are climbing vines that need maximum sunlight on their leaves to make food. When the vines climb high on sticks away from weeds, the plant can direct more food underground to grow bigger yams.
ga: Sweet potato tsei ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa hulu la babaoo yɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛfee niyenii. Kɛ wain tso lɛ kwɔ kɛtee tso nine ko nɔ ni kɛ jwɛi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ Tsei lɛ baanyɛ atere niyenii babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛkwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell that can dry out the ground and kill fresh seedlings. Waiting until the rains become regular ensures the soil stays wet enough for seeds to grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku ni baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi ni egbe dumɔwui bibii lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔ ni sa koni dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the soil gets too dry or when the daytime heat is too high. Regular watering during hot dry periods keeps the soil moist so flowers can form tomatoes.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo kɛ́ latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ yɛ gbi lɛ mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ anyɛ adara ni amɛtsɔ tomatoi.

english: Why do people cover the soil around their vegetable plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ gbɔmɛi kɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle amɛ aduawai lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground so you do not have to water as often, keeps the soil cool, and prevents weeds from growing.
ga: Ale jwɛi ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ ehe ehiaaa ni okɛ nu afɔ nɔ shii abɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves and powdery dirt inside the leaf funnels?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu kɛ sũ yɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of the young maize plant and eats the tender leaves. Spotting them early allows you to treat the crop before they destroy the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ ni amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛtaomɔ mra Enɛ baaha onyɛ otsu onibii ahe nii dani amɛfite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: If I only have two or three acres of land, can I still get a good crop harvest?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ shikpɔŋ ni dalɛ ji acre enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ Ani manyɛ maná ŋmaa kpakpa lolo?

english: Yes, crop yield depends more on proper care, good spacing, and soil health than on land size. Managing a smaller plot well often yields better harvest than spreading limited resources across a large farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni baa lɛ damɔ kwɛmɔ ni sa nɔ. Gbɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ fe shikpɔŋ lɛ dalɛ kɛkɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔji bibii ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ haa ŋmaa kpakpa baa fe nibii fioo ni yɔɔ lɛ ni agbɛɔ ashwãa ŋmɔji wuji amli.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant them too close together to fit more on my plot?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ bɔni afee ni mikɛ mihe lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, their roots fight each other for water and soil nutrients, while their leaves block sunlight from one another, resulting in thin plants with very small yields.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la lɛ naa kɛjɛɔ amɛhe Enɛ haa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ yibii fioo ko pɛ baa.

english: Why do weeds slow down the growth of my young crops so much?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ miiba shi waa lɛ?

english: Weeds act like aggressive competitors that quickly steal light, soil food, and moisture directly from your crop's root zone, leaving your crops hungry and stunted.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ akaŋshilɔi ni mli wa ni juɔ la, shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, kɛ ŋmɔtɔ oya kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii ni oduɔ lɛ ni egbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my cassava plants look weak and yellowish even though I planted them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ ni eyɛ ŋmɔŋ eyɛ mli akɛ miduɔ amɛ moŋ? Adu yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli?

english: Rainwater alone is not enough; crops need soil nutrients to grow. Yellowish leaves often indicate that the soil lacks essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, which the crop needs to make green leaves and food.
ga: Nugbɔ nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Niyenii nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛdara. Bei pii lɛ, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ tsei ahe nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, ni he hiaa tsei lɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli kɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my yam plants produce small tubers when planted in hard clay soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ náa ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow by pushing outward into the soil. Hard clay soil acts like a solid wall, making it difficult for the tuber to expand freely and form large roots.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛshwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni wa tsuɔ nii tamɔ gbogbo ni wa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akɛ amɛaagbɛ amɛshwã ni amɛfee shishifãi wuji.

english: Leaf curling in intense heat is a natural defense mechanism crops use to reduce the amount of leaf area exposed to the sun, helping the plant conserve water and prevent drying out.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ latsaa ni naa wa mli lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛba baa lɛ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛbuɔ nu he ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: Why are my maize plants growing tall and thin instead of developing strong, thick stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ miida ni amɛmiiya shɔŋŋ ni amɛmiifee mlɛo moŋ fe ni amɛaafee hewalɛ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: When crops do not receive enough direct, unshaded sunlight, they stretch rapidly upwards to reach for light, using up energy that should have gone into making strong stems and large cobs.
ga: Beni tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni ebɛ hulutsoo be ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ. Tso lɛ baatsi ehe oya kɛya ŋwɛi koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Hewalɛ ni esa akɛ akɛma tsei ni wa kɛ tsei wuji ni akɛtsuɔ nii.

english: Why do insect pests seem to attack my vegetable plants more when they are young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai tutuaa mi aduawai lɛ babaoo beni amɛji bibii lɛ?

english: Young crop shoots are tender, full of moisture, and easy for insects to chew, making them much more attractive to pests than older, tougher plant tissues.
ga: Tsobii bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo. ni eyi obɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni kooloi bibii ŋmɔmɔ waaa Enɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ sumɔɔ amɛ fe tsei amli fãji ni etsɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ waa lɛ.

english: Why do my crops produce less yield when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same specific nutrients from the soil and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up permanently in that plot.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ pɔtɛɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni baa tsei anɔ lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli daa.

english: Why do young cocoa trees need shade crops like plantains planted around them when starting out?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he hiaa ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛhe lɛ? Mra beni ojeɔ shishi?

english: Young cocoa trees are delicate and their leaves burn easily under direct sunlight. Plantains grow quickly with large leaves, acting like living umbrellas that shield young cocoa until they mature.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛbaai lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ mli. Plantains daa oya kɛ baai wuji. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ akpɔlɔ ni hiɛ kã ni buɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni edaa.

english: Young crops like cocoa are delicate and burn easily under strong sunlight. They need shade from fast-growing plants like plantains to keep the soil cool and moist while their roots grow strong.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ bibii tamɔ kookoo lɛ he waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛshishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing lets each plant get enough resources to produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛbaatswa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize is beneficial because beans naturally add nitrogen to the soil, which feeds the maize and improves its growth while giving you two harvests from one land.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ ŋmãa kɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii ni ehaa edalɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: Weeds grow much faster than young crops and will quickly steal the food, water, and sunlight your plants need, choking them before they can get established.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii bibii, ni ebaaju niyenii, nu, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa otsei lɛ oya. ni efo amɛ dani amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ shi.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking essential nutrients in the soil like nitrogen, or the ground is flooded with water and preventing the roots from breathing.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni eha shishifãi lɛ miigbɔjɔ.

english: Why do armyworms suddenly appear and eat my maize when the weather gets warm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ cutworms baa trukaa koni amɛbaye mi ŋmãa lɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Warm weather speeds up the hatching of pest eggs, causing sudden outbreaks of armyworms that feed on soft, growing maize leaves when humidity and heat spike.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ haa kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ afɔ̃ɔ oya. Enɛ haa armyworms ni yeɔ ŋmãa bibii ni miida lɛ ahe baai lɛ baa trukaa kɛ́ hulutsoo kɛ latsaa ba.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off without producing any fruit when it gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ amɛgbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: When tomato plants experience heat and dry conditions, they drop their flowers to save energy and water so the main plant can survive until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji akɛ tomato tsei lɛ shɛ latsaa kɛ hulutsoo be he lɛ Ebaashwie efɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ kɛ nu akafite. Enɛ ji koni tomato tsei lɛ anyɛ ahi shi kɛyashi shihilɛi lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed for a single strong harvest; planting seeds saved from that harvest usually results in weak plants and a low yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha kpamɔ kome ni mli wa. Bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ahereɔ kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni aduɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo.

english: Why shouldn't I sow my seeds after the very first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain is often a brief shower followed by weeks of dry heat, which can dry out and kill your newly germinated seeds before the actual rainy season settles in.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji nɔ kuku. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii babaoo ni hulutsoo be ni mli egbi. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui heei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ agbi ni amɛgboi dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ aba.

english: How do I know when my yam tubers are ready to be harvested?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ klalo akɛ abaakpa?

english: Yam tubers are ready when the leaves and vines on top of the ground naturally turn yellow and die back, showing that the plant has stored all its energy underground.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni amɛgboi. Etsɔɔ akɛ tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ eto shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow fast and have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting the young cocoa until it is strong enough to handle direct sunlight.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu cacao tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why should I cover the soil around my young pepper plants with dry leaves or grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei bibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, keeps the hot sun from drying out the ground too quickly. It retains moisture in the soil and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which is an important food in the soil. It can also happen if heavy rains have washed the nutrients away or if the roots are standing in too much water.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛji nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ jie niyenii mli nibii loo shishifãi lɛ damɔ nu babaoo mli.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when the plant lacks proper nutrients. Keeping the soil evenly moist can help the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ niyenii ni sa Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why are there small holes appearing in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ejeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ ateŋ?

english: Holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by caterpillars, such as the Fall Armyworm, eating the plant. Checking the central leaves early allows you to treat or remove the pests before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii, tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii baa ŋmeii bibii amli. Baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra Ehaa onyɛɔ otsaa loo ojieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why should I leave proper space between my crops instead of planting them very close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi gbɛ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: Spacing your crops properly ensures each plant gets enough light, water, and soil nutrients. Planting too close causes the crops to fight each other for food, resulting in weak plants and smaller harvests.
ga: Gbɛ ni sa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ateŋ lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa la, nu kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ awuu yɛ amɛhe koni amɛye niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi fioo.

english: Why should I cut off some of the small plantain shoots growing around my main plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ plantain yitsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ Ajieɔ Mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ.

english: Leaving too many young shoots allows them to steal food and water from the main mother plant. Removing extra suckers ensures the main tree grows strong and produces a large, healthy bunch.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii bibii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ajie tsei bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaawo tso titri lɛ hewalɛ ni edara waa ni efee tso agbo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to put tall wooden sticks next to my yam plants for them to climb?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ tso kakadaŋŋ ama sweet potato tso lɛ masɛi koni amɛkwɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high so their leaves can catch direct sunlight to produce food. Staking keeps the leaves off the hot ground and helps the plant produce larger yam tubers underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni hulu la ashɛ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni amɛná niyenii. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ, ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ewo sweet potato ŋmeii wuji yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why is it important for me to clear weeds from my farm while my crops are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ darako lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and quickly steal their water, sunlight, and fertilizer. Removing weeds early allows your young crops to establish strong roots and grow without competition.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Ye obua onibii bibii lɛ ni amɛná shishifãi ni wa ni amɛdara ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Most cassava varieties mature between 9 to 12 months after planting. You can tell they are mature when the lower leaves start to turn yellow and fall off, or by carefully digging up one stem to check the tuber size.
ga: Cassava henɔi babaoo hiɔ shi aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 yɛ be mli ni adu lɛ sɛɛ. Obaanyɛ ona akɛ amɛdara kɛji shishigbɛ baai lɛ je shishi amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. aloo kɛtsɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ ni ooofo jogbaŋŋ koni okwɛ bɔ ni eyitso lɛ da ha lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn easily under direct sunlight. Retaining shade trees or planting temporary shade crops keeps the soil moist and creates a gentle environment that helps the cocoa roots establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be mli lɛ akwɛmɔ loo tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli jɔ ni haa kookoo shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ lɛ baa.

english: What makes my cocoa pods turn black and dry up during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Black pods are caused by a fungal disease that thrives in wet and humid conditions. Pruning extra shade branches allows sunlight and fresh air to dry out the farm, stopping the fungus from spreading to healthy pods.
ga: Fungal hela ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ black pods baa. Niji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo babaoo lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa haa ŋmɔ lɛ mli gbiɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to stay green. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer gives the plant the energy it needs to form full cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishigbɛ baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni esa akɛ ŋmãa ahi shi eŋɔli. Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts make my soil better for the next crop?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ aya hiɛ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural roots that pull nitrogen food from the air and store it in the soil. When you harvest them, this stored nitrogen stays in the ground to fertilize your next crop.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli shishifãi ni gbalaa nitrogen niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni okpaa nii lɛ Nitrogen ni ato nɛɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛwo oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay healthy and breathe. When land stays flooded, the roots suffocate and rot, which is why planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ he miihia cassava shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛná hewalɛ ni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaagboi. Enɛ hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa lɛ.

english: Why do tomato flowers drop off without turning into fruit when the weather gets hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ?

english: Extreme heat and dry soil cause tomato plants stress, making them drop their flowers to save water. Adding grass mulch around the base keeps the soil cool and holds moisture so the flowers can turn into tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Ha amɛshɛrɛ fɔfɔi amɛshwie koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Mulch ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ tomatoi.

english: Yam leaves act like tiny solar panels that turn sunlight into food for the underground tubers. Staking lifts the vines high into the light and keeps the leaves clean from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii. ni haa hulu la lɛ feɔ niyenii kɛhaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛyaa la lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa tso lɛ yibii lɛ ahe tseɔ kɛjɛɔ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ.

english: What happens if I plant four or five maize seeds together in the same hole?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmeii ejwɛ loo enumɔ wo bu kome mli?

english: When too many seeds grow in one hole, the plants fight each other for food, water, and space. Planting only one or two seeds per hole gives each stalk enough room to grow strong and yield big cobs.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui babaoo kwɛ̃ yɛ bu kome mli Tsei lɛ baawu amɛha niyenii, nu, kɛ he ko. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui kome loo enyɔ pɛ yɛ bu kome mli lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko aná he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛ hewalɛ adara ni ekɛ ŋmei agbo aba.

english: Curled pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects sucking juice from the undersides of leaves. Spraying the leaves with soap water or neem oil destroys these pests so clean leaves can grow back.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii kɛ pepper baa curl baa. Nu ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi Kɛ́ akɛ nu ni akɛ samla loo neem fɔ shwie baa lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaakpata nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ahiɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai ni he tse lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ.

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy bunches during high winds. Supporting the main stalk with sturdy wooden poles prevents the trees from snapping before harvest.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ koni amɛfi ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni wa fiɔ tso titri lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekakumɔ dani akpa.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow and curling up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow and curl to protect themselves from losing moisture when the soil lacks water, or when the soil lacks essential nutrients like nitrogen.
ga: Abele baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ebɔleɔ ehe koni ŋmɔtɔ akafite kɛji nu efo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. aloo be mli ni niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ

english: Extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of insects to pollinate the blossoms can stress the tomato plant, causing it to drop its flowers early.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni akɛhaaa yɛ be fɛɛ mli Aloo kooloi bibii ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni bɛ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji fɔfɔi lɛ ni shwieɔ shi oya.

english: Why do the leaves on my crops look burnt and brown after I spray my farm for weeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eshã ni efeɔ ŋmɔtɔ beni mikɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ eshwie miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using damaged spraying equipment that leaks or spraying on a windy day can cause herbicides to drift onto your main crops, burning their leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ jwɛi ni efite ni hoɔ nu loo ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ gbii anɔ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsofai ni gbeɔ jwɛi lɛ atsɔ ŋshɔ hiɛ yɛ onibii titrii lɛ anɔ. ni eha amɛbaai lɛ ashã.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a clear open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh direct sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains planted alongside them to act as living umbrellas and keep the soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa amɛhe hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains ni adu yɛ amɛmasɛi lɛ he miihia amɛ. Koni etsu nii akɛ hulutsoo ni hiɛ kã ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Why are my maize stalks growing very thin and tall with very small cobs?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ shwilafoi bibii waa lɛ?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces the maize plants to compete aggressively for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, resulting in weak stalks and low yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la he akaŋ. Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waaa ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Seeds fail to germinate if they are planted too deep in the dirt, if the soil dries out completely, or if farm pests eat them before they can sprout.
ga: Dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, loo ŋmɔ mli kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: How can I tell if the holes in my cassava leaves are caused by insects or a disease?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ kooloi loo helai ji nɔ ni kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmei baa mli lɛ baa?

english: Insects usually leave clean, bitten holes in the leaves, whereas diseases cause yellow or brown spots around the edges of the holes or make the leaf wither.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shĩɔ bu ni he tse ni amɛkpãtã yɛ baai lɛ amli. yɛ be mli ni hela lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ baa bu lɛ naa loo ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do my plantain leaves get dark brown spots and dry up starting from the bottom leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbi yɛ amɛshishi lɛ?

english: This is typically caused by a fungal leaf disease that thrives in humid weather, attacking the older lower leaves first before moving up the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, fungal leaf hela ko ni yaa hiɛ yɛ hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Etutuaa shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ dani aduɔ tso lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant roots turn soft and rot when there is too much rain on my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating the roots and creating a wet environment where harmful soil fungi can rot the root system.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ he fɛɛ he ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ.

english: Why are my green mangoes dropping off the tree before they are big enough to ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mangoi ni eŋɔli lɛ miiho kɛmiijɛ tso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Trees drop young fruit prematurely when they experience sudden water stress, heavy pest attacks from fruit flies, or a lack of proper tree nutrients.
ga: Tsei baashwie aduawai bibii oya kɛji amɛna nu he haomɔ trukaa. Yibii amli ŋmeii ni tsii ni tutuaa mɔ loo niyenii ni sa ni jɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ ni bɛ

english: Why are the bottom leaves of my young maize crop turning yellow and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves on maize usually mean the crop is starving for nitrogen nutrient or the soil is waterlogged. The plant takes nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to keep the top growing leaves alive, which causes the bottom ones to yellow and die.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen niyenii bɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei kɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli lɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛkwɛ baai ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why is it bad to apply all my chemical fertilizer at once when planting my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii yɛ be kome mli kɛ́ oodu ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: If you put all fertilizer at once, heavy rains will wash most of it away before the young plant's small roots can soak it up. Splitting the application—giving a little at planting and more as the crop grows bigger—ensures the plant gets food when it needs it most.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo mli shikome Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ babaoo kɛyaa dani eshɛɔ shishifãi bibii lɛ ahe. ni tso bibioo lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ lɛ Nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni agbalaa mli—ni akɛ fioo haa tso lɛ kɛ babaoo be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ—yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛnáa niyenii yɛ be mli ni ehe hiaa amɛ fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or beans together with maize helps the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo ŋmei ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hewalɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which have special bacteria on their roots that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Maize feeds on this natural nitrogen, saving you money on commercial fertilizer.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji legumes ni yɔɔ bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ amɛshishifãi ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi yeɔ nitrogen yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Enɛ haaa oná shika babaoo yɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii ahemɔ mli.

english: What is eating ragged holes in the leaves inside the central whorl of my maize plants?
ga: Te eji tɛŋŋ akɛ aye baai ni ekpɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mi-abele tso lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋwɛi ŋta lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. They hide deep inside the funnel of the plant during the day to feed on the fresh foliage before it expands, leaving visible holes as the leaf grows out.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei agbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye tsei ahe baai heei dani amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Amɛshiɔ bu ni anaa be mli ni baai lɛ daraa kɛjeɔ kpo lɛ.

english: Why are the fresh leaves of my pepper plants twisting and curling upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ baai heei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sucking insects like thrips or mites living underneath the leaves. They feed on the plant juices and transmit viruses, causing the young leaves to distort and stop growing properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni hiɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ni amɛnuɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛtsɛɔ helai. Enɛ haa baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaaa amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the blossom tips of my tomato fruits turning black and rotting before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ ahe fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani akpa lɛ?

english: This condition is known as blossom end rot, which happens when the tomato plant lacks calcium or experiences inconsistent watering. Irregular soil moisture prevents the roots from carrying calcium up to the developing fruit tips.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ calcium bɛ tomato tsei amli loo akɛ nu haa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni bɛ ekome lɛ tsiɔ shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkawo calcium kɛyashɛ aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ ashishigbɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do I need to plant cassava stem cuttings with the leaf buds pointing upwards?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ odu ŋmei ni afo lɛ ni baai lɛ ashishifãi lɛ akwɛ ŋwɛi lɛ?

english: Cassava buds need to grow sprouts towards the sky and light. Planting stems right-side up allows fast leaf growth above ground and strong tuber development underground, whereas upside-down stems waste energy turning foliage upright.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmei tso lɛ ada kɛya ŋwɛi kɛ la he. Tso lɛ tsei ni aduɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ woɔ baai lɛ adalɛ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tuber ni mli wa lɛ he hewalɛ. Yɛ be mli ni tso lɛ shishi lɛ, efiteɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛhaa baai lɛ damɔ shi shiŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yam leaves require maximum sunlight to produce energy that goes into filling the large tuber below ground. Staking lifts the foliage away from damp soil, preventing fungal diseases and allowing every leaf to catch sunlight.
ga: Hulu la babaoo he miihia sweet potato baai lɛ koni amɛná hewalɛ ni yaa koni amɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli ekoŋŋ lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi fungal helai anaa ni oha baa fɛɛ baa aná hulu la

english: Why do weeds harm my crops much more when the plants are still tiny?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miifite miŋmɔshinii lɛ babaoo lɛ? He ni tso lɛ yɔɔ bibioo lolo lɛ?

english: Young crop plants have small, weak root systems and few leaves. Fast-growing weeds easily overpower them by stealing sunlight, ground moisture, and soil nutrients before the main crop can establish itself.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifãi bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ baai fioo pɛ. Jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛnɔ yɛ gbɛ ni waaa nɔ kɛtsɔ hulu la ni amɛjuɔ lɛ nɔ. shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ dani tsei titrii lɛ baanyɛ adara.

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they experience stress, such as dry weather spells, poor soil nutrients like potassium, or damage from mirid insects feeding on flower stalks. Strong trees retain flowers when well-shaded and fed.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji amɛhao, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii, tamɔ potassium, loo nɔ ni jɛɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ miishɛɛ ni yeɔ fɔfɔii ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ fiteɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ baahiɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛji akɛ aha amɛ hulutsoo ni aha amɛ niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I make my farm land fertile again after harvesting from it for several years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔ lɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ yɛ afii babaoo ni mikɛkpa nii lɛ sɛɛ?

english: You can restore exhausted soil by gathering organic farm residues and spreading them directly around the base of your crops. Over time, rain helps these materials break down and soak into the earth, returning essential nutrients to the land.
ga: Obaanyɛ oha shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni eshwɛ ni akɛ tsofai tsuuu nii yɛ mli lɛ ni ooobua naa ni okɛgbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Beni bei hoɔ lɛ Nugbɔ yeɔ ebuaa nibii nɛɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ni amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ aku sɛɛ aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ

english: Is it safe to dump leftover plant waste and fibers underneath my growing crops?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mashi tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi kɛ amɛhe tsɔi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ni mikwɛɔ lɛ ashishi?

english: Yes, pouring organic plant waste around the base of your crops is very beneficial. It acts as a protective cover that retains moisture and gradually decomposes into natural manure that feeds the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tso mli jwɛi ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ he fɛɛ he. O ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ni fiofio lɛ, efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Why is my soil struggling to hold water when it rains heavily?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ehiɛ nu mli kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ?

english: Bare soil often lets water run off or evaporate quickly under the sun. Adding a layer of fibrous plant waste beneath your crops helps trap rainwater so it can slowly soak deep into the root zone.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ haa nu hoɔ loo efoɔ oya yɛ hulu lɛ shishi. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei amli jwɛi ni yɔɔ fibrous fata oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni emɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ koni enyɛ ebote shishifãi lɛ amli fiofio.

english: I cannot afford chemical fertilizers for all my farm plots around Accra, what cheap alternative can I use?
ga: Minyɛɛɛ mahe tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmɔji amli yɛ Accra fɛɛ lɛ. Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi ni jara waaa atsu nii moŋ?

english: You can collect leftover fibrous crop waste or organic by-products and transport them to your fields. Spreading this material underneath your crops enriches the land naturally without needing expensive chemicals.
ga: Obaanyɛ obua tsei ni yɔɔ fibrous ni eshwɛ loo nibii ni jɛɔ mli baa lɛ anaa ni okɛya oŋmɔji amli. Nibii nɛɛ ni ooogbɛ oshwã onibii ashishi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsofai ni jara wa he ehiaaa.

english: Why does putting plant waste at the base of my crops work better than burning it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ mashi tsei ahe jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Burning crop waste destroys valuable nutrients and leaves the ground exposed. Spreading the waste underneath your plants allows it to decay slowly, softening the land and enriching the soil over time.
ga: Nibii ni adu mli lɛ amli jwɛi ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ faŋŋ. Muji ni agbɛɔ ashwãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni efiteɔ fiofio. It softens and fertilizes the soil over time.

english: How does pouring farm waste underneath crops actually turn into soil nutrients?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni ŋmɔ mli jwɛi ni afɔɔ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: When you pile organic waste under plants, rain and soil organisms break down the tough fibers. This allows the nutrient-rich matter to soak straight into the ground where roots can reach it.
ga: Kɛji okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ to tso ko shishi Nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni jɛɔ nugbɔ lɛ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ ŋmeii ni wa lɛ. Enɛ haa niyenii ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ashɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: I have several farm plots in different locations, how can I systematically build up their soil health?
ga: Miyɛ okwaayeli shikpɔji babaoo yɛ hei srɔtoi. Te mafee tɛŋŋ matswa shikpɔŋ hewalɛnamɔ yɛ gbɛjianɔtoo naa?

english: Whenever you gather organic waste or processing residue, transport it to your different plots and pour it directly beneath your plants. Doing this regularly across all your farms keeps each piece of land fertile.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaabua nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo nibii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛ nifeemɔ ko mli lɛ anaa koni okɛya shikpɔji srɔtoi anɔ lɛ, no ji onɔ̃ ni okɛshwie tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ ni ooofee daa yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ baaye abua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ fã fɛɛ fã afee nɔ ni baa nii.

english: How long does it take for plant waste dumped on the farm to start improving the land?
ga: Be enyiɛ eheɔ dani tsei ahe jwɛi ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ ko mli lɛ jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ saamɔ shishi?

english: As soon as moisture hits the waste, it begins to break down and soak into the ground. Within a few months, it decomposes enough to noticeably improve soil softness and water retention.
ga: Kɛji ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shɛ jwɛi lɛ nɔ pɛ kɛkɛ ni ebɔi fitemɔ ni eboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite bɔ ni sa ni baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo kɛ nu ni ahiɔ mli lɛ aya hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Do I need to dig crop waste into the ground, or can I just leave it on top around my plants?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni mafo ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo mashi amɛ yɛ he fɛɛ he? Mi tso lɛ hi?

english: You can simply pour the material on top of the soil underneath your crops. Rainwater will carry the decaying nutrients down into the soil naturally without requiring you to dig it in.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nibii lɛ awo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashishi lɛ nɔ. Nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ niyenii ni fiteɔ lɛ yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ehe ehiaaa ni okɛfo shi.

english: Why does my soil become dry and hard after a long dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi ni ewa yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Direct sunlight bakes bare soil and evaporates moisture. Placing a thick layer of organic waste around your plants shades the ground and helps it hold onto whatever moisture is available.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ebaaha nu ni mli edɔ lɛ aya hiɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebaaye ebua ni ehiɛ ŋmɔlɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do extension officers encourage us to plant plantain trees on the farm before putting in young cocoa seedlings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ mɛi hewalɛ ni adu dumɔwui yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani adu kookoo dumɔwui bibii lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under full sun. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that create shade and keep the soil moist, giving the young cocoa the protection it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa abuɔ kookoo bibioo lɛ he koni ehi shi yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Can I plant cassava directly under my young cocoa trees to make extra cash, or will it hurt the cocoa?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmei yɛ mi-kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ashishi tɛ̃ɛ koni maná shika kroko? Aloo ebaafite kookoo lɛ?

english: Cassava grows aggressively and consumes a lot of soil nutrients and water. Planting it too close to young cocoa will starve the cocoa trees, so it is better to use plantain or cocoyam for shade instead.
ga: Cassava daa oya ni eyeɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli. Kɛ́ adu cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha hɔmɔ aye cacao tsei lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ plantain loo cocoa baatsu nii kɛha hulutsoo moŋ.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close to each other, will I get more bags of maize at harvest time?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa Ani mana ŋmãa kotoku kroko yɛ kpamɔɔ be mli?

english: Planting maize too close causes the plants to fight for sunlight and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin stalks and very small or empty cobs, reducing your overall harvest and profit.
ga: Abele ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli. Enɛ haa okpamɔ fɛɛ kɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow very tall and bushy under big trees but yield very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ waa ni efeɔ ŋmɔji yɛ tsei wuji ashishi shi ewoɔ yibii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Tomatoes need direct sunlight to produce flowers and fruit. When planted under heavy shade, the plant spends all its energy stretching upward to reach the light rather than growing tomatoes.
ga: Tomato he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni ewo fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai. Kɛ adu yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa shishi lɛ Tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ehe koni eha la lɛ abote mli. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu tomato

english: Why is it bad for me to plant yam on the exact same plot of land for three years in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nɔ fɔŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Planting yam repeatedly on the same land drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows yam-specific pests and diseases to build up, resulting in smaller tubers and lower market value.
ga: Sweet potatoes ni aduɔ shii abɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ amɛhelai pɔtɛɛi lɛ buaa amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa yitsei bibii kɛ jarayeli jara baa shi.

english: How do I choose fast-growing vegetables to plant alongside my main cassava crop to get quick income while waiting for harvest?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ahala aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya ni akɛbaakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmei titri lɛ masɛi koni aná shika oya yɛ be mli ni emɛɛɔ kpamɔɔ lɛ?

english: Select short-season crops with shallow roots like garden eggs, pepper, or okra. They mature within three months and can be harvested without disturbing or competing heavily with the slow-growing cassava.
ga: Halamɔ nibii ni aduɔ yɛ be kukuoo mli ni shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ, tamɔ abɔɔ mli wɔji, shitoi, loo okra. Amɛshwereɔ yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli ni abaanyɛ akpa amɛ ni akɛ ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ gbaaa amɛnaa loo amɛyeee akaŋ waa.

english: Pepper leaves curl during hot weather to reduce water loss from the heat. However, if the leaves stay curled or turn yellow, it means the plants need more water or lack nitrogen in the soil.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli koni ekɛba nu ni jɛɔ dɔlɛ mli baa lɛ shi. Shi, kɛji akɛ baai lɛ tee nɔ amɛkpã loo amɛtsɔ ŋmɔŋ, Etsɔɔ akɛ nu babaoo he miihia tsei lɛ loo nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my mango trees drop most of their flowers before any small fruits can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii bibii lɛ?

english: Mango trees drop flowers when they experience sudden water shortage, pest attacks, or fungal diseases like powdery mildew. Keeping the tree watered and treating diseases early helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Mango tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛna nu ni faaa trukaa, kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ, loo tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ powdery mildew. Okɛ nu awo tso lɛ nɔ ni otsa lɛ mra. Ye obua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee aduawai

english: Why do I need to tie my tomato plants to sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fĩɔ tsei aniji ahe moŋ fe ni mahã amɛgbɛ amɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Staking keeps the leaves and fruits off the wet soil, preventing rot and fungal diseases while exposing the plant to sunlight, which results in cleaner, higher-quality tomatoes that sell for better prices.
ga: Staking baaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Tsi ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ naa be mli ni okɛ tsei lɛ woɔ hulu la mli lɛ. Enɛ haa anáa tomato ni he tse, ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni ahɔ̃ɔ kɛ jara ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I put extra chemical fertilizer on my pepper field, will it automatically make the plants produce double the yield?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ tsofa kroko fata pepper ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ Ani ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ aya hiɛ shii enyɔ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Applying too much fertilizer can burn plant roots, cause excess leaf growth with no fruits, and waste your money. Giving the right amount at the right growth stage gives the best economic return.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ shishifãi ashã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ daa fe nine ni yibii bɛ mli. kɛ shika ni afiteɔ Shika ni sa ni akɛaaha yɛ dalɛ be ni sa mli lɛ baaha shika helɛtemɔ mli sɛɛnamɔi ni hi fe fɛɛ aba.

english: Why do some farmers put chemical treatment on rice seeds before planting them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi kɛ tsofai woɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui anɔ dani amɛduɔ lɛ?

english: Treating seeds before planting protects them from soil pests, fungi, and early diseases, helping them germinate healthy and strong instead of rotting in the soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ akwɛmɔ dani aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, ŋmeii, kɛ helai anaa yɛ shishijee mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ waa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaafite yɛ sũ mli.

english: What happens if I plant untreated seeds straight into the field?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji mikɛ dumɔwui ni atsuuu he nii lɛ wo ŋmɔ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Untreated seeds are vulnerable to insects, birds, and soil fungi, which can eat or destroy them before they sprout, leading to poor germination and weak crops.
ga: Dumɔwui ni atsako amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni kooloi, okpoi kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii baanyɛ aye amɛ. ni baanyɛ aye amɛ loo efite amɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃ Enɛ haa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my crop leaves wither and dry up even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ bɔ ni sa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Leaves can wither despite rain if pests attack the roots, or if a fungal disease blocks the plant from absorbing water properly. Spraying the right crop medicine early prevents this.
ga: Baai lɛ baanyɛ agbi yɛ nugbɔ po sɛɛ kɛji kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui tutua shishifãi lɛ. aloo kɛji akɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko tsi tso lɛ naa koni enyɛŋ eŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Tsei ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛ ni sa nɔ mra lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Should I wait until my crops get sick before I spray them with medicine?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mamɛ ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aná hela dani mawo amɛ tsofa?

english: It is usually better to apply preventative treatments early, as protecting crops before diseases strike is easier and cheaper than trying to cure plants after they are already damaged.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ akɛ tsofa ni tsiɔ hela naa lɛ baatsu nii mra. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe ni abuɔ dani hela baa lɛ waaa ni ejara hu waaa fe bɔ ni abɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ahere tsei ayiwala beni amɛfite lɛ sɛɛ.

english: How can I tell if my crops are dying from disease or just lacking water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hela loo nu ni faaa yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ miigboi?

english: Water-stressed plants usually droop during the hottest part of the day and recover slightly at night, whereas diseased plants show yellowing patterns, spots, or rot that remain regardless of watering.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu haa amɛhe feɔ shoo lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛhe waaa fioo gbɛkɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ baajie ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yaa nɔ ehiɔ shi ekɔɔɔ he eko nu ni akɛhaa amɛ.

english: How do I know which exact medicine to buy for my crops when they are sick?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa ni esa akɛ mahe mahã miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛ́ hela mɔ amɛ?

english: You should first identify the specific problem—like insects, yellow leaves, or fungal spots—and ask an extension officer for advice so you don't buy the wrong chemical that could harm your crop.
ga: Esa akɛ oyɔse naagba pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ klɛŋklɛŋ, tamɔ kooloi bibii, baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ, loo ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii amli. ni obi ŋaa kɛjɛ mɛi ni kwɛɔ nibii anɔ lɛ adɛŋ Bɔni afee ni okahe tsofai ni ejaaa ni baanyɛ aye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: Does the time of day I spray medicine on my crops really matter?
ga: Ani gbi lɛ mli be ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ he hia?

english: Yes, spraying early in the morning or late in the afternoon works best because strong sun can dry up the chemical too quickly or burn the leaves, while heavy heat makes the medicine evaporate.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ leebi loo shwane lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ fe fɛɛ. Yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ hewɔ Enɛ baanyɛ aha tsofa lɛ agbi oya tsɔ loo eha baai lɛ ashã. yɛ be mli ni la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baaha tsofa lɛ atsɔ la.

english: Why is it important to follow the correct mixing instructions on crop chemical bottles?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni anyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja ni kɔɔ tsofa ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Using too little chemical will not kill the pests, while using too much can burn your crops, waste your money, and make pests resistant to the medicine over time.
ga: Tsofa fioo ko pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ egbeŋ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ. Yɛ be mli ni kɛ akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ baanyɛ ashã ŋmɔshi nibii, efite shika ni eha kooloi ni yeɔ tsofa lɛ nyɛŋ atsu nii yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my crops still get diseased even after I sprayed them with medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lolo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ tsofa lɛ shwieɔ amɛnɔ moŋ?

english: Medicine may fail if it was washed away by rain immediately after spraying, applied at the wrong dosage, or used against a pest or disease that the specific medicine does not treat.
ga: Tsofa lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni tsuuu nii kɛji nugbɔ shwie nɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni afɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ falɛ ni ejaaa atsu nii loo akɛtsu nii ashi tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni tsofai pɔtɛɛ komɛi tsaaa lɛ.

english: How does spraying under the crop leaves help protect the plant?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ tsei ahe baai ashishi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe?

english: Many pests and fungal spores hide on the undersides of leaves where it is cool and moist, so spraying beneath the leaves ensures the medicine directly hits and protects those hidden areas.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi yɛ he ni hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, shwiemɔ tsofa lɛ yɛ baai lɛ ashishi koni tsofa lɛ atswa nakai hei ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ ni ebu he.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer gives the maize the food it needs to stay green and build large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaha ŋmei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ewo ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting cowpeas on my field make my next maize crop grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina ŋmãa ni mikɛduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaha mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and beans gather nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil through their roots. When you plant maize afterwards, it feeds on this trapped nitrogen, growing much stronger without extra chemical fertilizer.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ beans buaa nitrogen naa kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Kɛji odu ŋmãa sɛɛ mli lɛ Ebaaye nitrogen ni ekpɛtɛ ehe lɛ. Edaraa waa ni ehe ehiaaa ni akɛ tsofai krokomɛi awo mli.

english: Young cocoa plants burn easily under direct sunlight. Tall trees or plantain plants act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the air moist around the delicate cocoa seedlings until they mature.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei kakadaji loo dumɔwui tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ehaa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. Cocoa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baadara.

english: Why do my plantain trees stop bearing big bunches when too many suckers grow around the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji feemɔ beni ŋmeii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Small shoots, or suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. If you cut off extra suckers and leave only one or two strong ones, the main tree keeps all its energy to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: ŋmeii loo ŋmeii bibii Ju nu ni amɛdu niyenii kɛjɛ nyɛ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛji ofolɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni oshi ŋmeii kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baakwɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ nɔ koni ekɛwo ŋmeii wuji ni tsii.

english: Why do my yam vines grow bigger tubers when I stake them with tall sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ daa bulbs wuji beni mikɛ tsei kakadaji shwieɔ amɛnɔ lɛ?

english: Staking lifts yam leaves high up into the sunlight where they can make maximum food for the plant. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground, protecting them from rot and disease so the tuber underground can grow large.
ga: Staking baawó sweet potato baai lɛ anɔ kɛya hulu la lɛ mli he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛha niyenii babaoo aha tso lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebaatsiɔ baai anaa koni ekahi shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Tsi fitemɔ kɛ helai anaa koni ŋmeii lɛ adara.

english: Why do my cassava plants lose all their leaves in the dry season, and are they dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ baai fɛɛ fiteɔ yɛ fɛ̃i be mli ni egboɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava drops its leaves during long dry spells to conserve water and protect itself from heat. The plant is not dead; as soon as the rains return, it will grow fresh leaves and continue growing its tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ ebaa lɛ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu ehe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tso lɛ gboko lolo. Kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ, baai heei baakwɛ̃ ni shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ baaya nɔ akwɛ̃.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop in the hot afternoon sun but stand upright again by morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miiho yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ete shi tɛ̃ɛ ekoŋŋ leebi.

english: On hot days, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink from the soil, causing them to wilt to save moisture. During the cool night, roots catch up on drinking water, making the leaves bounce back by morning.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Gbi gbɛkɛ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baakpɛtɛ nu ni anuɔ lɛ he. Ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi leebi

english: Why do weeds make my crops look weak and thin even when there is plenty of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ nugbɔ babaoo ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds are aggressive plants that steal soil nutrients, root space, and sunlight from your crops. Even with heavy rain, if weeds consume the soil food first, your crops will starve and grow thin.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ waa moŋ Kɛji jwɛi ye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ klɛŋklɛŋ Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ hɔmɔ baaye amɛ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies hiding under the leaves and sucking out plant juices. Controlling these insects early stops them from damaging new leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe tee baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛnuɔ tso lɛ nu lɛ kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔkwɛmɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite baai heei ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: Tomato plants shed flowers when temperatures become too hot, when watering is uneven, or when small insects attack the blooms. Keeping the soil moist with mulch and watering regularly helps the flowers stay on and form fruits.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Kɛ́ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ bɛ daa loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii tutua fɔfɔi lɛ, kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni okɛ nu shwie nɔ daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantain plants grow quickly and produce large leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa trees are mature enough to survive direct heat.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daraa oya ni amɛyɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baadara bɔ ni sa ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ dɔlɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually indicate that the soil is lacking nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted animal manure or a nitrogen-rich fertilizer around the roots helps the plants recover.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kooloo ŋmei ni egbo loo nitrogen ŋmei ni akɛfataa he lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Why is burning my field after clearing it bad for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ ni mikɛshãa beni mijie lɛ sɛɛ lɛ ehiii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic matter and beneficial organisms in the topsoil that hold moisture and plant food. Leaving cut weeds and bush to decompose naturally forms a protective cover that enriches the soil for your crops.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ yiteŋ ni hiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei amli niyenii lɛ. Kɛ́ oshi jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni afolɔ lɛ koni amɛgbo lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni buɔ mɔ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ŋɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil for too long because the roots cannot breathe. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges allows extra rainwater to drain away, keeping the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ejaakɛ shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɛmu. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu babaoo hoɔ kɛyaa. Ha shishifãi lɛ awa

english: Why do I get smaller maize cobs when I put many seeds into one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minine shɛɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmãa babaoo wo bu kome mli lɛ?

english: Putting too many seeds in one hole forces the plants to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Spacing seeds properly ensures each stalk gets enough resources to form large, full ears of corn.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo ni akɛwoɔ bu kome mli lɛ nyɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ abɔ he akaŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ to he jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko náa nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaafee ŋmãa toi agboi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my tomato plants without turning into fruit during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ aduawai yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Extreme hot air and dry soil stress tomato plants, causing their flowers to dry out and drop off before pollination occurs. Mulching the soil with dry grass and watering early in the morning keeps the roots cool and helps set fruit.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ haoɔ tomato tsei. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwie nɔ ni akɛ nu shwie nɔ leebi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaa yibii lɛ woɔ shi.

english: Why are caterpillars hiding in the center funnel of my young corn stalks and eating the fresh leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-baby corn tso lɛ teŋgbɛ funnel lɛ mli ni amɛyeɔ baai heei lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which prefer the soft growth inside the central funnel of young corn. Applying recommended organic or chemical treatments directly into the funnel early in the morning stops them before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni sumɔɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ blɛoo yɛ ŋmãa bibii lɛ ateŋ. Akɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ woɔ ŋmei lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ leebi. Ekpaa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfiteɔ tip ni miida lɛ.

english: How can I tell that my yams are fully grown and ready to harvest under the soil?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam tubers are mature when the leaves and vines on top of the ground naturally turn yellow and begin to dry up, showing that the plant has finished storing food in the root.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ shɛɔ dalɛ he beni baai kɛ wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe ni amɛjeɔ shishi amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ kɛ niyenii eto eshishifãi amli.

english: Why should I not save seeds from this year's hybrid maize harvest to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ afi nɛɛ hybrid ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially crossed to produce a high yield for one season only. Seeds saved from that harvest will lose those special qualities, leading to uneven growth and much lower yields in the next season.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui krɛdɛɛi lɛ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni ejaaa kɛ yibiiwoo ni baa shi kwraa yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli baa.

english: Why is it better for my crops if I water them early in the morning rather than in the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ kɛji mikɛ nu wo mli leebi moŋ fe gbi lɛ?

english: Watering early in the morning lets the plant roots absorb water before the hot sun causes fast evaporation, reducing plant stress and saving water.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛshishifãi lɛ ni amɛmuɔ nu dani hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ haa efoɔ oya. Tsɔɔmɔ tsei ahe haomɔ shi ni okɛ nu ato.

english: How can I tell if my land is good for growing maize before I start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi kɛha ŋmãa dumɔ dani mabɔi ŋmãa dumɔ?

english: Good maize soil should be dark, loose, and drain water well without becoming waterlogged. You can test it by squeezing a handful of moist soil; if it forms a loose ball that crumbles easily when gently pressed, it has a good texture for maize roots to spread.
ga: Esa akɛ ŋmãa shikpɔŋ kpakpa lɛ afee ediŋŋ, ni egbɔjɔ, ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni nu akabote mli. Obaanyɛ oka enɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ fioo ni oootsi lɛ nɔ. Kɛji akɛ etamɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni etse ehe ni fãa oya kɛji akɛ anyɛ nɔ fioo lɛ Ebaaha ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã jogbaŋŋ.

english: If I plant maize on the same piece of land every year, what will happen to my harvest?
ga: Kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi Mɛni baaba mikpamɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Planting maize continuously on the same plot drains specific soil nutrients and causes pests to build up in the soil, leading to smaller harvests each year. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts restores nutrients naturally.
ga: Abɛi ni aduɔ daa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ haa sũ mli nibii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ hoɔ, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, daa afi lɛ, nikpamɔ ni baa lɛ faaa. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under full sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava alongside young cocoa gives them living umbrellas that provide protection and moisture during their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ. Enɛ, kɛ kookoo bibii lɛ baaha amɛná hulutsoo ni hiɛ ka ni baaha amɛbu amɛhe ni amɛná ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall stems but produce very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa shi ŋmeii bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava produces small tubers when planted too close together or given too much nitrogen fertilizer. Close spacing causes the leaves to shade each other, making the plant waste energy growing tall stems to reach light instead of swelling its roots.
ga: Cassava baawo ŋmeii bibii kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ loo aha amɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Gbɛ ni kã amɛteŋ lɛ haa baai lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe naa. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa amɛshishifãi ni kɛlɛ lɛ koni amɛshɛ la he moŋ, ni no haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for growing large tubers underground. Staking lifts the vines off the ground, maximizing leaf exposure to the sun and keeping the foliage away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii kɛha ŋmeii wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking yeɔ ebuaa ni ewoɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ. Ha baai lɛ aná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni abaanyɛ. ni etsĩ baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkaye helai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over so easily whenever there is heavy rain or strong wind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over if too many suckers (shoots) are allowed to grow around the main stem, or if root-damaging pests weaken the base. Removing extra suckers leaves 2-3 strong shoots and keeps the main plant anchored securely.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii (ŋmeii) kwɛ̃ yɛ amɛhe. too main trunk Aloo kɛji akɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ haa shishitoo lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii fioo komɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ni ebaaha tso titri lɛ ahi shi shiŋŋ.

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape down the middle leaf vein mean the plant lacks nitrogen. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like Urea or NPK at the correct growing stage will restore green leaf color and boost crop growth.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ baa lɛ naa yɛ V su mli kɛyaa shishigbɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea loo NPK wo mli yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ baa lɛ afee eŋɔli ekoŋŋ ni eha tso lɛ adalɛ aya hiɛ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures become too hot or when soil moisture fluctuates heavily between dry and wet. Mulching the soil and maintaining consistent watering at the root zone helps flowers stay on and set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wo la tsɔ. aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ waa yɛ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ teŋ. Mulching kɛ nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ aduawai.

english: How do weeds hurt my crops if there is plenty of rain for all plants on the farm?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ fɛɛ ná nugbɔ babaoo?

english: Even with abundant rain, weeds steal essential soil nutrients, space, and sunlight that your main crops need to produce heavy fruits. Weeds also act as breeding sites for insects and plant diseases.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo moŋ, shi Jwɛi lɛ hu juɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni he hiaa, ŋwɛi, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa onibii titri lɛ koni ewo yibii babaoo lɛ. Jwɛi hu tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni kooloi bibii kɛ tsei ahe helai fɔɔ yɛ.

english: Why are there ragged holes in my young maize leaves with tiny droppings in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ yɛ bu ni etse kɛ ŋmeii bibii lɛ? Yɛ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ?

english: This damage is caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars hiding inside the leaf funnel of the young maize. Applying approved treatments or neem extract directly into the funnel early in the morning kills the caterpillars before they destroy the growing tip.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe ewo ŋmãa bibii lɛ baai amli lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ko ni akpɛlɛ nɔ loo neem mli nu ko wo ŋmei lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe ŋmeii lɛ dani amɛfite ŋmeii lɛ ashishifãi ni miida lɛ.

english: What does NPK 15-15 actually do for my crops when I apply it?
ga: Mɛɛ sɛɛnamɔ NPK 15-15 lɛ yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii kɛ mikɛtsu nii?

english: NPK stands for Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium in equal measures. Nitrogen makes leaves grow green and leafy, Phosphorus builds deep and healthy roots, and Potassium helps the crop fight off diseases and produce heavy fruits or grains.
ga: NPK damɔ shi kɛha Nitrogen, Fosforus kɛ Potasium ni falɛ tamɔ amɛhe. Nitrogen haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni amɛfeɔ baai. Fosforo lɛ feɔ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni amɛhe wa. Ni potassium yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛwuɔ amɛshiɔ helai. ni ewoɔ aduawai loo ŋmaa ni tsii

english: Why are there different types of fertilizers on the market instead of just one standard kind?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi babaoo yɔɔ jara nɔ moŋ fe nɔ kome pɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Different crops require different nutrients at specific stages of their life. Some fertilizers boost early leaf growth, while others are mixed specifically to strengthen roots, restore exhausted soil, or help plants produce flowers and seeds.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ srɔtoi biɔ niyenii srɔtoi yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli fãi srɔtoi amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ekomɛi haa baa lɛ daa mra. Yɛ be mli ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii komɛi futuɔ mli tɛ̃ɛ koni ekɛwaje shishifãi lɛ. Shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ ni aku sɛɛ akɛba loo aye abua tsei ni amɛwo fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui

english: How do I know if my crop leaves are turning yellow because of poor soil or because of a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mitso lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo hela hewɔ?

english: Yellowing from poor soil usually spreads evenly across older leaves because the plant lacks basic food like nitrogen. Yellowing from disease usually leaves patchy spots, twisted edges, or strange patterns across both new and old leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ mli lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa baai ni egbɔ lɛ anɔ ejaakɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen. Bei pii lɛ, hela ni haa mɔ he feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔi, loo nibii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ baa baai heei kɛ momoi anɔ.

english: When plants are overcrowded, they fight each other for sunlight. They waste all their energy stretching upward to reach the sun instead of growing thick stems, deep roots, or plenty of fruit.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ eyi obɔ lɛ Amɛbaatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Amɛfiteɔ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ ni amɛshɛɔ Hulu lɛ he lɛ. Mohu ɔ, du tsohi nɛ a mi wa, sisi nɛ mi kuɔ, aloo yiblii fuu.

english: Why do my maize plants roll their leaves and wilt during the afternoon even when the soil isn't completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ miihoso ni amɛmiigboi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbiko kwraa lɛ?

english: This is a natural defense trick. Plants curl their leaves during the hottest hours to shield themselves from the sun and slow down water loss through evaporation, resting until the air cools down in the evening.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋaawoo ni akɛtsiɔ hela naa. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la he kɛ nu ni hoɔ fiofio kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ. Hii shi kɛyashi ebaajɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: What causes my crop flowers to drop off before they can grow into full fruits or vegetables?
ga: Mɛni miiha mitso lɛ fɔfɔii lɛ miiho dani etsɔ aduawai loo aduawai kwraa?

english: Flowers fall off when the plant feels sudden stress, such as extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of essential soil nutrients needed to support the plant while it sets fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ nu haomɔ he trukaa, tamɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ daa. aloo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni he hiaa koni eye ebua tso lɛ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why does my piece of land yield fewer crops every year even though I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Harvesting crops repeatedly pulls food out of the ground without putting it back. Over time, the soil becomes tired and empty, which can be fixed by rotating crops or adding organic manure and fertilizer.
ga: Nibii ni akpaa lɛ gbalaa niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shii abɔ. ni akɛwooo sɛɛ Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite ni ebaafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Abaanyɛ atsake enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ loo humus kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ni akɛbaafata he lɛ nɔ.

english: How does adding animal manure help my soil differently than using factory-made fertilizer?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfataa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mishikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ nitsumɔhe lɛ?

english: Factory fertilizer feeds the crop directly with quick nutrition, but animal manure improves the soil structure itself. Manure acts like a sponge, helping the soil hold onto water and nutrients longer for future seasons.
ga: Nitsumɔhe ŋmɔshi nibii haa ŋmɔshi nii tɛ̃ɛ kɛ niyenii ni tsuɔ nii oya. Shi kooloi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ diɛŋtsɛ shishitoo lɛ yaa hiɛ. Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ be kakadaŋŋ kɛha be ni baa lɛ.

english: Why do some seeds sprout fast and healthy while others from the local market fail to come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya kɛ hewalɛ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ? Kɛjɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ ekwɛɛɛ?

english: Certified seed varieties are clean, well-stored, and bred for strong energy to germinate evenly, whereas uncertified market seeds may be old, damaged by heat, or infected with hidden seed-borne diseases.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi ni awo he odase lɛ he tse. Akwɛɔ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni akwɛɔ koni ekɛ hewalɛ ni nɔ kwɔ aha kɛha shweremɔ po. Yɛ be mli ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ jara nɔ ni bɛ he odaseyeli lɛ baanyɛ afee nɔ ni etsɛ, ni dɔlɛ efite loo helai ni dumɔwui ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ kɛbaa lɛ emɔ amɛ.

english: How can I keep my crops from dying when the dry season comes early in Ghana?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagboi kɛ́ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ ba mra yɛ Ghana?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry grass or leaves, called mulching, traps moisture in the soil, keeps plant roots cool, and protects the ground from baking under intense heat.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ni atsɛɔ lɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he koni ekashã yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi.
