english: Why do seeds remain intact even after farm animals eat all the leaves off my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔ mli kooloi eye mi tsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ fɛɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Many plant seeds have tough outer shells designed to survive being chewed or swallowed by animals. While animals easily digest soft leaves, the hard seed coat protects the inner seed so it can still grow into a new plant.
ga: Dumɔwui babaoo yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni wa ni afee koni kooloi anyɛ amɛye loo amɛmi. Eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ baai bibii lɛ oya moŋ, shi dumɔwui lɛ ahe atade ni wa lɛ buɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe koni enyɛ eya nɔ eda ni etsɔ tso hee.

english: Can I collect and plant seeds from crops that livestock have already grazed on?
ga: Ani manyɛ mabua dumɔwui ni jɛ tsei ni kooloi eye momo lɛ amli lɛ anaa ni makwɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, as long as the seeds themselves are mature and undamaged, you can harvest them to plant or spread on your farm. Animals usually chew the leaves and stems, leaving hard seeds unharmed and ready for planting.
ga: Hɛɛ, be fɛɛ be ni dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko efiteee lɛ. Obaanyɛ okpa amɛ ni okɛdu loo okɛja yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, kooloi yeɔ baai kɛ tsei ashishifãi. Shi dumɔwui ni wa lɛ ni amɛfee klalo kɛha dumɔ.

english: What is the best way to collect and store seeds from my farm to plant next season?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuaa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ anaa ni akɛtoɔ koni akɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Harvest seeds when they are fully mature and dry on the plant. Clean off any leftover plant material, dry the seeds completely in a shaded, well-ventilated area, and store them in sealed containers in a cool, dry place.
ga: Kpaa dumɔwui lɛ beni amɛdara kwraa ni amɛgbi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ. Tsumɔ tso mli nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe. Gbi dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi ko ni aŋã mli yɛ he ko ni mli ejɔ ni egbi.

english: Why do some crop seeds need to be thoroughly dried before I spread them on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni dumɔwui komɛi agbi kwraa dani agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Drying seeds lowers their moisture content, which prevents them from rotting or growing mold. It also stops them from sprouting too early before they are properly planted in moist soil.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ni agbiɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa shi. Enɛ baaye abua ni dumɔwui lɛ akafite loo amɛkafee ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya tsɔ hu dani aduɔ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Will my crops still yield good seeds if animals eat most of their green leaves?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baawo dumɔwui kpakpai lolo kɛji kooloi ye baai eŋɔli lɛ ateŋ babaoo?

english: Many crops can still produce good seeds if leaf damage happens late in the season after the seeds have already formed, or if the plant has enough stored energy in its stem and roots to recover.
ga: Tsei babaoo baanyɛ awo dumɔwui kpakpai lolo kɛji akɛ baai lɛ fite yɛ be lɛ naagbee gbɛ beni dumɔwui lɛ ebɔi sɛɛ. aloo kɛji tso lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato yɛ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi amli koni ekɛtsa ehe

english: Why do plants sprout new leaves after farm animals chew them down to the stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei lɛ woɔ baai heei beni ŋmɔ mli kooloi eye amɛ kɛyashi amɛshishifã lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Plants keep energy reserves in their roots and lower stems. When animals strip the top leaves, the plant uses these hidden energy reserves to quickly push out new shoots and leaves.
ga: Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni ato lɛ toɔ amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛshishigbɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kɛ kooloi jie baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ Tsei kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ nɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsi ŋmeii kɛ baai heei oya.

english: How do weeds and pasture plants keep spreading across my farm even when animals graze on them constantly?
ga: Te efeɔ tɛŋŋ ni jwɛi kɛ kooloi alɛɛhe tsei gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ kooloi miiye amɛ be fɛɛ be moŋ?

english: Grazing animals eat the foliage, but hard seeds drop to the ground or pass through the animal unharmed. When it rains, these seeds germinate in the soil, allowing the plants to spread easily across the farm.
ga: Koolooi ni yeɔ jwɛi lɛ yeɔ baai. Shi dumɔwui ni wa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ he loo amɛtsɔɔ kooloi amli. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, dumɔwui nɛɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ tsei baagbɛ amɛshwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Can I spread harvested seeds directly onto unplowed land and expect them to grow?
ga: Ani manyɛ magbɛ midumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ ni makpa gbɛ akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃?

english: Some hardy pasture crops and cover plants can grow on unplowed land if there is sufficient rain, but clearing weeds and lightly loosening the soil surface helps seeds make better contact with the earth and grow much stronger.
ga: Prairie tsei komɛi ni wa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa nɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni atsuuu nii yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa. Shi jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ajieɔ lɛ fioo lɛ yeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kpaa gbee jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: How can my grazing animals help spread useful plants across my farmland?
ga: Te koolooi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni amɛgbɛ tsei ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ amɛshwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: When animals eat plants with mature seeds, they carry those seeds in their stomach and drop them elsewhere in their manure. The manure acts as natural fertilizer, helping the seeds sprout quickly in new parts of your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ kooloi ye tsei ni dumɔwui yɔɔ mli lɛ, no lɛ amɛdara kwraa. Amɛwoɔ nakai dumɔwui lɛ yɛ amɛmli ni amɛshiɔ yɛ he kroko yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Manure tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ fãi heei amli. ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: How do I protect mature seeds from being ruined or lost before I can harvest them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu midumɔwui ni edara lɛ ahe koni amɛkafite loo amɛkafite dani akpa amɛ?

english: You should harvest seed heads as soon as they turn brown and dry on the stalk. If birds or free-roaming animals are a problem, you can cover individual seed heads with cloth bags or harvest them slightly earlier to finish drying off the field.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ kɛji amɛtsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbi yɛ tso lɛ shishi pɛ. Kɛji okpoi loo kooloi ni nyiɛɔ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ ji naagba Obaanyɛ okɛ mama kotoku aha dumɔwui lɛ ayitso fɛɛ yitso loo okpa mra fioo koni egbi yɛ kpo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Which direction should I plant my cassava stick cuttings in the soil so they sprout properly?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ esa akɛ adu ŋmei niji yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Always plant cassava cuttings with the buds pointing upwards toward the sky. If you plant them upside down, the stems struggle to emerge and you will get very few, weak tubers.
ga: Be fɛɛ be lɛ, dumɔ ŋmei niji ni ŋmeii lɛ tsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛji odu lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ Stems lɛ baafee nɔ ni wa ni obaaná bulbs ni bɛ hewalɛ fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why must I make high mounds of soil before planting my yams?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mawo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani madu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Yams need soft, loose earth to expand into large tubers. High mounds give the roots plenty of space to grow down easily and protect the tubers from rotting in standing water.
ga: Sweet potato he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse koni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii wuji. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ haa shishifãi lɛ hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni amɛdara mlɛo. ni etsĩɔ ŋmeii lɛ anaa koni amɛkafite yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli.

english: Should I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rainfall of the season?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady, usually after two or three good rains. Planting right after the very first rain risks burning your seeds if a long dry spell follows.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ aba. Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ yɛ oshara akɛ ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã kɛji hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ nyiɛ sɛɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is essential food for leaf growth. Applying fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure helps restore their green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ lɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baaye abua ni eha ehiɛ afee ŋmɔŋ kɛ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant suffers from high heat, dry soil, or a lack of nutrients. Regular watering in the morning and putting dried grass around the roots keeps the plant cool enough to set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa leebi kɛ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he Shishifãi lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ mli ajɔ bɔ ni sa ni ewo yibii.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or mites sucking the sap from young leaves. Spraying with neem oil or appropriate remedies helps control them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni sa shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eye okadii nɛɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that act as living umbrellas, shielding young cocoa from excessive heat and conserving soil moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he. ni ekwɛ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Yes, cowpeas trap nitrogen gas from the air and release it into the soil as plant food. This naturally fertilizes your maize while giving you two crops from one field.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsina ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ejieɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha tsei lɛ niyenii. Enɛ baaha o-abele lɛ afɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ agbɛnɛ hu ni ebaawo ŋmɔshi nibii enyɔ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ kome mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees keep falling over when the fruit bunches grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ miigbee shi beni aduawai lɛ daraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow roots that struggle under the heavy weight of a maturing bunch, especially during strong rain or wind. Supporting the stem with a strong wooden or bamboo pole keeps them standing.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ niji ni eda ni tsii lɛ shishi. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔ loo kɔɔyɔɔ be mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso loo ŋmei tso ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni edamɔ shi.

english: How early do I need to clear weeds away from my newly sprouted crops?
ga: Te ehe baahia ni majie jwɛi kɛjɛ tsei ni ekwɛ̃ ehee lɛ amli oya ha tɛŋŋ?

english: You should clear weeds within the first two to three weeks after your crops sprout. Removing weeds early prevents them from stealing water, fertilizer, and sunlight from your young crops.
ga: Esa akɛ ojie jwɛi lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ mli beni onibii lɛ ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: Why do people say planting soybeans is good for my soil before I plant other crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ soybeans dumɔ hi kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ dani midu tsei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soybeans naturally pull nitrogen from the air and store it in the ground. When the crop is harvested, the leaves and roots break down into natural food for the soil, making it richer for heavy-feeding crops like corn.
ga: Soybeans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ. Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ Baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fãa ni amɛfeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii kɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ. Enɛ haa efeɔ fɛo waa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why do my soybean plants produce tiny bumps on their roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi soybean tso lɛ yɛ ŋmeii bibii yɛ eshishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Those small bumps are a great sign. They house friendly natural organisms that capture plant nutrients from the air and turn them into natural fertilizer for your crop.
ga: ŋmeii bibii Nomɛi ji okadii kpakpai. Amɛji adebɔɔ mli nibii ni yɔɔ naanyobɔɔ su ni mɔ̃ɔ tsei amli niyenii kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛfeɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛhaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashia.

english: Can I just take tree seedlings from the bush and plant them directly on my open farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ jwɛi mli ni madu amɛ yɛ miŋmɔ ni agbele naa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Wild tree seedlings taken straight from the shaded bush usually suffer from shock if placed directly into open sunlight on a farm. They usually need to be nurtured in a nursery first to get used to sunlight and proper spacing.
ga: Koo mli dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ jwɛi ni yɔɔ hulutsoo mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ fɔɔ shoofeemɔ mli kɛji akɛ akɛwo hulu la mli tɛ̃ɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli. Bei pii lɛ, ehe miihia ni atsɔse amɛ yɛ gbekɛbii akwɛmɔhe koni amɛle hulu la kɛ he ni sa ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does it take several years for planted trees to bear fruit compared to quick crops like corn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani aduɔ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ? Kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa oya tamɔ ŋmãa he?

english: Trees spend their first few years growing strong, deep root systems and thick trunks to carry heavy weight. Quick crops like corn invest all their energy into fast foliage and seeds right away before dying in a single season.
ga: Tso lɛ heɔ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo dani ewaa. shishifãi ni mli kwɔ kɛ tso ni mli tse ni baaye abua nibii ni tsii ni tsii Nibii ni aduɔ oya tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ baai kɛ dumɔwui ni yaa oya lɛ ahe nii dani amɛgboiɔ yɛ be kome mli.

english: Should I clear away every single tree on my land before I start growing new crops?
ga: Ani esa akɛ majie tso fɛɛ tso ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani mabɔi tsei heei dumɔ?

english: No, leaving selected trees provides natural shade, protects your soil from direct heat and heavy erosion during downpours, and generates fallen leaves that enrich your farm ground naturally.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ ashi tsei ni ahala lɛ ni nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ, ebaaha adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo aba. Buu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ shwiemɔ ni naa wa he yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli. ni ofee fall foliage ni kɛ sɛɛnamɔ baa oŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ.

english: Why do my young corn leaves turn light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young corn usually mean the plant is missing nitrogen food in the soil or standing in waterlogged dirt. Adding soil nutrients or clearing excess rainwater helps restore their green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo edamɔ sũ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ fata shikpɔŋ lɛ he loo nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will heavy shade from big trees stop my corn crop from growing tall and healthy?
ga: Ani hulutsoo ni tsii ni jɛɔ tsei wuji amli lɛ baaha mi-ŋmã lɛ akakwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ akafee hewalɛ?

english: Yes, corn requires full sunlight most of the day to make energy. Under heavy shade, corn plants stretch thin, become weak, and produce small or empty cobs.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia ŋmãa yɛ gbi lɛ mli babaoo koni enyɛ ená hewalɛ. yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli wa lɛ shishi Abele tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, amɛhe waaa ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii. loo dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ mli

english: How deep should I put corn seeds into the ground when planting?
ga: Te esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tɛŋŋ kɛ́ midu?

english: Corn seeds do best when planted about 3 to 5 centimeters deep. If planted too shallow, birds or rain wash them away, and if planted too deep, they exhaust their energy before reaching the surface.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aduɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni mli kwɔ aaafee sɛntimita 3 kɛyashi 5. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ tsɔ lɛ, Okpoi loo nugbɔ baaho amɛ. ni kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ Amɛhewalɛ baaho dani amɛshɛ ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ.

english: Is it possible for me to plant corn and soybeans on the same farm plot at the same time?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ makwɛ ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: Yes, intercropping corn and soybeans works very well. The soybeans help cover and feed the ground while corn grows tall above it, allowing you to harvest two different crops from the same land.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa kɛ soybeans ni akɛfutu mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. Soybeans yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa niyenii. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: How can I tell that my soybeans are completely ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-soybeans lɛ eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Soybeans are ready when the green leaves turn yellow, dry up, and fall off the stems. When you shake the brown dry pods on the plant and hear the seeds rattle inside, it is time to harvest.
ga: Soybean lɛ efee klalo kɛji baai eŋɔli lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ, amɛgbi, ni amɛgbee shi kɛjɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Beni otsiɔ ŋmeii ni egbi ni yɔɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ni onuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ni miihoso yɛ mli lɛ. Nikpamɔ be eshɛ

english: How can I tell the difference between male and female pawpaw trees on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ pawpaw tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ateŋ?

english: Pawpaw trees can be male, female, or hermaphrodite. Male trees produce long, hanging stalks with many small flowers that do not bear fruit, while female trees produce larger flowers close to the trunk that develop into round fruits when pollinated.
ga: Pawpaw tsei baanyɛ afee nuu, yoo, loo nɔ ni kɛ hii feɔ yakayaka nii. Tsei hii yɛ tsei kakadaji ni fĩɔ shi kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. Mɛi babaoo wooo yibii. yɛ be mli ni tsei yei woɔ fɔfɔii wuji ni bɛŋkɛɔ tso lɛ shishi ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ aduawai ni yɔɔ kokroo kɛji akɛ amɛwo amɛhe ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Do cocoa trees have separate male and female trees, or can every tree produce pods?
ga: Ani kookoo tsei hii kɛ yei sɔrɔtoi yɛ? Aloo ani tso fɛɛ tso baanyɛ awo ŋmeii?

english: Cocoa trees do not have separate male and female trees. Each individual cocoa flower contains both male and female parts, but they rely on tiny insects like midges to carry pollen between flowers so pods can form.
ga: Cacao tsei bɛ tsei ni ji hii kɛ yei ni yɔɔ srɔtoi. Kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ eko fɛɛ eko yɛ nuu kɛ yoo fãi fɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, a ngɔɔ a hɛ kɛ fɔɔ koolohi nyafii a nɔ kaa nihi nɛ a kɛ mɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ɔmɛ a kpɛti konɛ a nyɛ nɛ a pee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop without setting fruit due to extreme heat, insufficient water, or poor pollination. When temperatures get too high, pollen loses its viability, preventing the flower from forming a tomato.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa waa lɛ hewɔ. Nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo pollination ni ehiii Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ lɛ, Pollen lɛ nyɛɛɛ akwɛ wala nɔ. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi afee tomato.

english: Why do some of my cassava plants produce flowers while others in the same field do not?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava fɔfɔi lɛ ekomɛi miifɔlɔ shi ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ miifɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Flowering in cassava depends on the specific variety and weather conditions. Flowering does not affect tuber yield—cassava plants continue to grow tubers underground whether they produce flowers on top or not.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cassava mli lɛ damɔ henɔ pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Fɔfɔi ni shwereɔ lɛ enaaa tuber yibiiwoo nɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmei yaa nɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii kɛji amɛfɔ̃ɔ yɛ nɔ loo amɛfɔɔɔ.

english: Why do different fertilizers come in different colors like white, pink, or dark grey, and how do I choose the right one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi, tamɔ yɛŋ, pinki, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ? Ni te abaafee tɛŋŋ ahala ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa lɛ?

english: Fertilizer colors come from the raw minerals used or added dyes. White fertilizers like Urea supply high nitrogen for leafy growth, while multi-colored NPK blends provide balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium for roots and fruit development.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe su lɛ jɛɔ sũ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli yɛŋ tamɔ urea lɛ mli eyi obɔ kɛ nitrogen kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, NPK ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛfutuɔ nii ni yɔɔ sui srɔtoi lɛ haa nitrogen, phosphorus kɛ potassium ni sa kɛha shishifãi kɛ aduawai adalɛ.

english: Why do some commercial maize seeds come coated in bright pink or green powder?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akɛ powda ni mli tse loo eŋɔli ni mli tse woɔ jarayeli ŋmãa ŋmeii komɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Seed companies treat seeds with safe chemical coatings—dyed red, green, or pink—to protect the planted seeds against soil insects, fungi, and birds during germination.
ga: Nitsumɔhei ni feɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛ tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe woɔ dumɔwui ahe—ni akɛ tsofa tsuru, eŋɔli, loo pinki woɔ mli—koni akɛbu dumɔwui ni adu lɛ ahe kɛjɛ kooloi bibii, ŋmeii, kɛ okpoi ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ lɛ.

english: How can I check if the corn seeds I stored from last season are still good before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji ŋmãa dumɔwui ni mikɛto yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ hi lolo dani madu?

english: You can do a simple germination test by placing 10 seeds inside a damp cloth or newspaper for 3 to 5 days. If 8 or more seeds sprout healthy roots, your batch of seeds is good to plant.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shweremɔ he kaa ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Obaanyɛ ofee enɛ kɛtsɔ dumɔwui 10 ni okɛaawo mama loo adafitswaa wolo ni mli efɔ mli gbii 3 kɛyashi 5 lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui 8 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kwɛ̃ shishifãi ni mli wa lɛ, Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ odumɔwui akuu lɛ sa kɛha dumɔ.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up to conserve water and protect themselves from intense sunlight. Yellowing is a sign of water stress or tiny sap-sucking insects like aphids that multiply during hot, dry conditions.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛbu nu he ni ebu he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Yellowing ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nu mli haomɔ loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ aphids, ni faa yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why do yam vines always need to climb and wrap around wooden stakes to yield well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ni amɛbɔle tsei ahe koni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aya nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Yam vines naturally climb to reach maximum sunlight. Staking keeps the leaves off the damp ground to prevent fungal diseases and allows the plant to produce more food for growing large tubers underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ baakwɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Staking baaha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ekɛtsi tsɛŋemɔ helai anaa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa niyenii babaoo kɛha bulbs wuji ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do young plantain suckers lose their lower leaves as they grow taller?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantain tsei bibii lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi beni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: As plantains grow, older outer leaves naturally turn brown and dry up so the plant can direct its energy and nutrients toward growing fresh, strong leaves from the center.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ dara lɛ, kponɔgbɛ baai ni edara lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ tsɔɔ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛyaa baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛteŋgbɛ.

english: How do I know the exact time my maize is ready to be plucked and harvested from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be pɔtɛɛ ni esa akɛ ajie ŋmãa ni akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn dry and brown, and the leaves start yellowing. You can test a grain by pressing it with your fingernail—if it is firm and no milky liquid comes out, the corn is mature and ready for harvest.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ egbi ni efee ŋmɔtɔ. ni baai lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ Obaanyɛ oka dumɔwui lɛ okwɛ kɛtsɔ onineshi ni ooonyɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ wa ni nu ko ni tamɔ atatu ejeee kpo. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni esa akɛ akpa.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and stunt before the plants even produce corn ears?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiigbɔjɔ dani tso lɛ woɔ abele toi po lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen in the soil or the roots are suffering from waterlogged ground. Applying balanced fertilizer like NPK early in the plant's life helps it stay green and grow tall.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo akɛ shishifãi lɛ miipiŋ yɛ ŋshɔkpɔi ni nɔ edɔ waa lɛ anɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni ja tamɔ NPK wo tso lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa lɛ ni ehiɔ shi eŋɔli ni edaa.

english: Why do crops like cassava need to be uprooted while crops like maize are only plucked from the top?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni ajie tsei tamɔ ŋmei yɛ be mli ni ajieɔ tsei tamɔ ŋmãa kɛjɛɔ ŋwɛi pɛ lɛ?

english: Cassava stores its food underground inside its thick roots, so the whole plant must be pulled up to harvest the crop. Maize forms its food above ground on the stem, so you only need to pluck the cob off the stalk.
ga: Cassava kɛ niyenii toɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ eshishifãi ni mli tse lɛ amli. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbala tso muu lɛ fɛɛ kɛya ŋwɛi koni akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Abɛi feɔ niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ yɛ tsei ahe. No hewɔ lɛ, ogbalaa ŋmei lɛ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ shishi kɛkɛ.

english: If I uproot my cassava plants, can I cut the stems and plant them back in the exact same hole immediately?
ga: Kɛji ajie ŋmei tso lɛ Ani manyɛ mafo tso lɛ ni mikɛku sɛɛ mikɛwo shishijee bu lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: While you can grow new cassava from stem cuttings, planting in the exact same spot right away drains the soil of its nutrients and exposes young stems to soil diseases. It is better to clear the land, add compost, or rotate crops before replanting.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ odu ŋmei hee kɛjɛ ŋmeii amli moŋ, shi kɛ́ odu amɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hoɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba tsei bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anɔ. Esa akɛ ajie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, afee lɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo atsake ŋmɔshi nibii dani adu ekoŋŋ.

english: What should I do with the dry maize stalks left in the field after I finish harvesting?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee beni mikpa ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Instead of burning the dried stalks, you can chop them and spread them over the soil as mulch. This covers the ground, retains moisture, prevents weed growth, and gradually turns into natural fertilizer as it decays.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshã tsei ni egbi lɛ Obaanyɛ ofolɔ mli ni okɛshwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi, ehaaa jwɛi akwɛ̃, ni fiofio lɛ, etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni efiteɔ lɛ.

english: Why does my farmland yield fewer crops every year even when I plant at the start of the rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi kɛ́ midu nugbɔ dumɔwui po lɛ?

english: Every time you harvest crops, they pull nutrients out of the earth. If you farm continuously without resting the land, adding organic manure, or growing leguminous crops like beans, the soil becomes weak and produces smaller yields.
ga: Be fɛɛ be ni obaakpa ŋmɔshi nibii Ebaajie niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji otsuɔ okwaayeli he nii be fɛɛ be ni okɛ organic fertilizer loo ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmeii afata he lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni ebaawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my corn leaves curl up into tight tubes during hot sunny afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baa lɛ shwieɔ shi efeɔ tsɔnei ni mli wa yɛ hulutsoo be mli shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaf rolling is a natural survival defense. By curling its leaves, the maize plant reduces the surface area exposed to the sun to prevent water from evaporating too quickly from its leaves during intense heat.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nɔ ko ni buɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ wala he. Abɛi haa ehiɛ ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi kɛtsɔ ebaai lɛ ni efoɔ koni nu akajɛ baai lɛ amli oya tsɔ yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are tiny caterpillars eating the inner leaves of my young maize plants during the dry spells?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii yeɔ mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli baai lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, which attack the growing point or 'funnel' of young maize plants during dry periods. Applying recommended organic or chemical pest control directly into the funnel early in the morning helps protect the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni tutuaa ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ he loo ‘gbɛi’ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni wala yɔɔ mli loo tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tsu nii leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: How do I prevent insects from destroying my corn after I gather and store it in the barn?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi kooloi ni fiteɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ naa beni abua naa ni akɛto ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Make sure the corn is thoroughly dried under the sun before storing it. Storing clean, dry grain in hermetic (airtight) storage bags starves insects of oxygen and keeps your harvest safe from pests without chemical damage.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ hulu la shishi dani okɛto. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui ni he tse ni egbi lɛ wo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli (vacuum) lɛ, ebaaha kooloi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ehaa onibii lɛ hiɔ shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe ni tsofai efiteee.

english: Can I save the corn grains from my harvest to use as seeds for the next planting season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ ŋmãa ni jɛ kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛtsu nii akɛ dumɔwui kɛha ŋmãa be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: If you planted hybrid maize seeds, saving and replanting those grains will lead to weak plants and much lower yields. It is best to purchase fresh certified seeds every season to guarantee a healthy and heavy harvest.
ga: Kɛji odu hybrid corn dumɔwui Okɛto ni okɛto ekoŋŋ lɛ baaha tsei lɛ agbɔjɔ ni amɛwo yibii ni baa shi kwraa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase daa be mli koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ abaakpa nii jogbaŋŋ ni tsii.

english: Why do my crops grow poorly when I leave old tree stumps and hard roots in my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ edaaa jogbaŋŋ beni mishiɔ ŋmeii momoi kɛ shishifãi ni wa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Old tree stumps and living roots continue to steal water and plant food from the soil. Leaving them underground also blocks your new crop roots from spreading easily to find nutrients.
ga: Tsoi akui momo kɛ shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ juɔ nu lolo ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ashi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, no hu haaa tso shishifãi heei agbɛ ashwã mlɛo koni amɛna niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow twisted and small when the soil has a lot of leftover woody roots?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ etsɔ ŋmeii ni efee bibii be mli ni shishifãi babaoo eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, obstacle-free soil to expand deep and straight. When a growing tuber hits hard underground roots or stumps, its growth gets blocked, causing it to bend and stay small.
ga: Sweet potato tubers lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ, ni nɔ ko tsiii amɛ gbɛ koni amɛdara kɛya shɔŋŋ ni amɛfee linear. Beni bulb ni miida lɛ tswa shikpɔŋ shishi shishifã loo tso shishifã ko ni mli wa lɛ. Abaatsi edalɛ naa. Ha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee bibioo.

english: Does burning cleared bushes make my crop soil better than leaving the leaves to rot naturally?
ga: Ani tsei bibii ni he tse ni ashãa lɛ haa mi sũ ni mikɛwoɔ tsɛnsi mli lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi fe ni maha baai lɛ agbo yɛ adebɔɔ naa?

english: Burning gives ash that offers a short burst of nutrients, but it burns away organic material. Leaving cleared leaves and small plants to rot creates rich mulch that holds water and feeds crops for a longer time.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ haa ashwishwɛ ni haa niyenii mli hewalɛ be kukuoo pɛ baa. shi ebaashã nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ Aŋmɛ gbɛ ni baai ni ajie kɛ tsei bibii lɛ fite lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii ni fa babaoo ni hiɛɔ nu mli ni yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cassava plants growing very tall without producing big tubers under shady trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ nɛkɛ ni efeee bulbs agboi yɛ tsei ni haa hulutsoo lɛ shishi lɛ?

english: Cassava needs full sunlight to make food for its roots. In deep shade, the plant uses all its energy to stretch upwards toward the sun, leaving no energy to build thick tubers underground.
ga: Hulu la ni fa babaoo he miihia Yucca koni ekɛfee niyenii aha eshishifãi lɛ. Yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛgbala ehe kɛya ŋwɛi kɛya hulu lɛ he. Hewalɛ ko bɛ ni eshwɛ ni akɛbaafee ŋmeii ni mli tse yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: If I clear all the small trees and bushes off my field, will the sun dry out my crop soil faster?
ga: Kɛji mijie tsei bibii kɛ tsei bibii fɛɛ kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli Ani hulu lɛ baaha midumɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi oya?

english: Yes, clearing all plant cover exposes the bare soil directly to hot sun and wind, causing moisture to evaporate quickly. You can protect the soil by spreading cleared leaves around your crops as mulch.
ga: Hɛɛ, shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii fɛɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ baashɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ shwieɔ shi oya Obaanyɛ obu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛtsɔ baai ni ajie lɛ ni ooogbɛ ashwã he lɛ nɔ. Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ji mulch.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees get scorched and dry up when I remove all the tall trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ kɛ́ mijie tsei kakadaji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ? Nakai tso lɛ je kpo?

english: Young cocoa trees have delicate leaves that burn under direct heat. Tall trees provide necessary shade that cools the leaves and keeps the surrounding air moist while the cocoa grows strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, kookoo yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa.

english: Why do wild shrubs grow back faster than my planted maize after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi lɛ da oya fe ŋmãa ni midu beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild shrubs are naturally hardy and already have deep, established roots that quickly absorb water and fertilizer. They grow fast to steal light and nutrients before young maize seeds can get established.
ga: Koo mli tsei lɛ ahe wa yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni amɛyɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni shwieɔ nu kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii oya. Amɛdaraa oya koni amɛju la kɛ niyenii kpakpai dani ŋmãa dumɔwui bibii aba.

english: If I only cut small shrubs at ground level, why do they keep coming back to choke my crops?
ga: Kɛji mifo tsei bibii pɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Mɛni hewɔ amɛyaa nɔ amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa koni amɛbafite miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Cutting only the top leaves leaves the underground root system alive and full of stored food. The root continuously sends up new sprouts that will compete with your crops until the root itself is destroyed.
ga: Kɛ́ afolɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ pɛ lɛ, ebaaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ahi shi ni niyenii ni ato lɛ eyi mli obɔ. Shishifãi lɛ baatsu dumɔwui heei ni kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baabɔ akaŋ be fɛɛ be kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my tomato plants get leaf rot when planted close together near thick bush growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ baa lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ jwɛi ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ?

english: Thick surrounding bushes block natural airflow, trapping damp air around crowded tomato leaves. Excess moisture on leaves creates the ideal environment for fungal rot to grow and spread.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛi ni mli tse ni ebɔle he fɛɛ lɛ Tsĩɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni hoɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ naa Kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni ebɔleɔ tomato baai ni mli eyi obɔ lɛ he lɛ nɔ Fɛ̃i ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ feɔ shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ koni amɛdara ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã.

english: Why do wild bushes around the edges of my farm cause my pepper plants to get more insect pests?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ koo mli jwɛi ni bɔle miŋmɔ lɛ naa lɛ kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai babaoo miiba mi-pepper tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Overgrown wild bushes act as breeding sites for harmful insects like whiteflies and caterpillars. When the bush growth is close to your crops, these pests easily jump over to feed on your pepper plants.
ga: Tsoi ni yɔɔ shishi ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ ji he ni kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ. Kɛji jwɛi lɛ bɛŋkɛ oŋmɔshi nibii nɛɛ Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ baatsɔ nɔ oya ni amɛye o-pepper tsei lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato seedlings look weak and wilted right after I move them from the nursery to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛgbɔjɔ ni amɛgboi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mijie amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛtee shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: When young plants are moved to a new field, their roots get disrupted and experience 'transplant shock'. They need a few days to settle into the new soil environment and re-establish their root connection before they can absorb water properly and stand strong again.
ga: Kɛ́ ajie tsei bibii kɛtee he ko hee Amɛshishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛnaa amanehulu. Gbii fioo komɛi he miihia amɛ koni amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ hee lɛ nɔ ni amɛfee shishifãi heei ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ ni amɛto amɛhe shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it important to gradually expose my nursery seedlings to full sunlight before planting them outside?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni okɛtsu nii blɛoo lɛ? Ha dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mi-nursery lɛ mli lɛ hulu babaoo dani odu amɛ yɛ kpo nɔ.

english: Seedlings grown under nursery shade are delicate. Slowly exposing them to direct sunlight—a process called hardening off—helps them adjust to harsher field conditions so they do not suffer from sudden sun shock when planted in the open field.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shishi lɛ he waaa. Ni akɛ tso lɛ aaawo hulu la mli fiofio Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ coagulation. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli shihilɛi ni mli wawai amli. Bɔni afee ni hulu la ni tsoɔ trukaa lɛ akapiŋ lɛ beni aduɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ.

english: Can I take maize seeds bought from a dry region like Tamale and plant them directly in Kumasi without any special preparation?
ga: Ani manyɛ maŋɔ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni ahe kɛjɛ hei ni nu bɛ tamɔ Tamale lɛ ni madu yɛ Kumasi tɛ̃ɛ ni mikɛ hesaamɔ krɛdɛɛ ko tsuuu he nii?

english: Seeds adapt over time to the specific climate and soil where they are raised. When moved to a wetter or different area, they may experience stress, so you must carefully monitor their soil moisture and local growing conditions as they adjust.
ga: Dumɔwui baatsake amɛhe yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni adu amɛ yɛ nɔ lɛ. Kɛji amɛmiiya hei ni nu yɔɔ loo hei krokomɛi Amɛbaanyɛ amɛna haomɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ jogbaŋŋ be mli ni amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Watering early in the morning or late in the evening is best because the soil temperature is cooler. This gives the roots enough time to drink the water before the heat of the afternoon sun evaporates it from the soil surface.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu lɛ dani hulu ni tsoɔ yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli dɔlɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do extension officers recommend spraying pesticides on crops late in the evening instead of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni kwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ woɔ ŋaa akɛ afɔse tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ gbɛkɛ mli moŋ fe shwane lɛ?

english: Spraying in the cooler evening prevents strong sunlight from breaking down the chemical too quickly, reduces evaporation, and avoids killing beneficial insects like bees that work on flowers during daytime hours.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai lɛ shwieɔ nɔ yɛ gbɛkɛ ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ fiteɔ tsofai lɛ oya tsɔ, ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi, ni ehaaa egbe kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ tamɔ ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii yɛ fɔfɔi anɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Leaf curling in direct heat is a crop's natural defense mechanism to conserve water. By curling, the leaves reduce the amount of surface area exposed to the hot sun, helping the plant retain moisture.
ga: Baai ni abɔleɔ amɛhe kɛtsɔ dɔlɛ nɔ lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛjianɔtoo koni ekɛbu nu he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why are my garden eggs plants developing mold and leaf spots after rain in the late evening?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplants ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ baai lɛ ahe ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ gbɛkɛ ko sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on leaves overnight without sunlight to dry it, it creates a damp environment where fungal diseases thrive. Spacing plants properly allows air to flow through and dry the leaves quickly.
ga: Beni nu ta baai anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome ni hulu la bɛ mli koni eha baai lɛ agbi. Ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa mɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Tsei ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli ni ehaa baai lɛ gĩɔ oya.

english: Should I apply fertilizer to my maize on the exact day I put the seeds in the soil?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi-ŋmãa lɛ mli yɛ gbi ni mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: No, you should wait until the seeds germinate and the young roots settle in. Applying chemical fertilizer directly to fresh seeds or fragile new sprouts can burn them; waiting a week or two after germination yields much better growth.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ omɛ kɛyashi be mli ni dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ ewo shishifãi. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ dumɔwui heei loo dumɔwui heei ni bɛ hewalɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha amɛshã. Kɛ́ omɛ otsi kome loo enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: Is it better to give my cabbage plants all their fertilizer at once or divide it into multiple feedings?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo kaabe tso lɛ mli shikome loo ojara mli owo mli shii abɔ?

english: Dividing fertilizer into smaller regular doses feeds the plant gradually as it grows. This prevents nutrients from washing away during heavy rainfall and ensures the crop receives a steady supply of food throughout its life.
ga: Kɛ́ ojara ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli bibii bibii daa lɛ, ebaaye ebua tso lɛ ni eda fiofio. Enɛ baaye abua ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ akaho yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. ni ekwɛɔ koni aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii daa yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli.

english: How long should I leave my land to rest after clearing the grass before planting cassava?
ga: Kɛ́ ajie jwɛi lɛ agbe naa lɛ, be enyiɛ esa akɛ ashi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe dani adu ŋmei?

english: Allowing cleared vegetation to settle and break down for about one to two weeks before planting enriches the soil structure and creates a stable, nutrient-rich root bed for your cassava cuttings.
ga: Kɛ́ aŋmɛ tsei ni ajie lɛ gbɛ ni amɛhi shi ni amɛfite otsi kome kɛyashi enyɔ dani adu lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛo. ni ofee shishitoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ, ni niyenii mli hewalɛ babaoo yɔɔ mli kɛha o-cassava ni ofo lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to stay green and grow strong. When nitrogen is low in the soil, the plant moves what little it has from old bottom leaves to feed new upper leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa shishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ. Kɛji nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ faaa Tso lɛ jieɔ nɔ fioo ni eyɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momo lɛ amli koni ekɛye ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers keep falling off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the crop experiences stress, such as extremely hot afternoon temperatures, erratic watering, or lack of nutrients. The plant drops its flowers to save energy so it can survive the heat.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tso lɛ miihao, tamɔ shwane mli latsaa ni mli edɔ lɛ. nu ni bɛ shiŋŋ loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he koni amɛnyɛ amɛdamɔ dɔlɛ naa.

english: Why do my crops look wilted in the hot afternoon sun even when the soil is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni egbo yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo moŋ

english: On very hot days, leaves lose water into the air faster than the roots can pull it up from the soil. The plant wilts temporarily to close its leaf pores and conserve water, usually bouncing back by evening as temperatures cool down.
ga: Yɛ gbi ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ nɔ lɛ Baai lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tso lɛ baagbi be kukuoo ko koni ekɛgbala baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ ni ekɛ nu ahi mli. Bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli ejɔ waa lɛ.

english: How can I tell if the soil is ready for planting after the first rains start?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ eshɛ kɛha dumɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ asɛɛ?

english: Wait until the rain dampens the top soil to about the depth of your hand. Squeeze a handful of the dirt—if it holds together softly without dripping water or crumbling into dust, it has the right moisture balance for seeds to germinate without rotting.
ga: Mɛɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ kɛyashɛ onine mli. Mimɔ muji ni eyi obɔ lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ aŋɔ lɛ blɛoo ni ehaaa nu atsɔ mli loo egbɛ eshwaaa sũ Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛfiteee.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil without giving the ground time to recover. It also allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil, leading to weaker harvests each season.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ be ni ekɛtsake ehe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hu ni amɛbua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, nibii ni afeɔ lɛ baa shi yɛ be fɛɛ mli.

english: How does applying fertilizer actually help my crops produce bigger fruits and grains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo aduawai kɛ ŋmaa wuji?

english: Fertilizers act like concentrated food for crops, putting back essential soil nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that plants feed on to build strong roots, thick stems, and healthy fruit.
ga: Fertilizer tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni mli ewo muji kɛha tsei. Ekɛ niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen, phosphorus, kɛ potassium ni tsei yeɔ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa, amɛshishifãi ni mli tse, kɛ aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ kuɔ sɛɛ amɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still on the branch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ tso lɛ nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Blackening cocoa pods are usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in humid, shady conditions. Trimming excess branches to let sunlight and air flow through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ cocoa ŋmeii ni efee ediŋŋ lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ ni hulutsoo yɔɔ. Niji ni fa fe nine ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot when water stays trapped in waterlogged soil for too long, suffocating the roots and allowing soil-borne fungi to rot the tubers underground.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu hi shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. kɛ ŋmeii ni hiɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ ni amɛŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛfiteɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ

english: Why do the bottoms of my tomato fruits turn dark and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato aduawai shishi feɔ ediŋŋ ni eyɛ bɔdɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, which happens when the plant cannot send enough calcium to the developing fruit. It usually occurs when watering is irregular during dry spells.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ekɛ calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa aha aduawai ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ baa mli kɛ́ nu lɛ efɔɔɔ shi be fɛɛ be yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli.

english: Why do weeds in my field make my main crops stay small and weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ afee bibii ni amɛhe waaa lɛ?

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and soil nutrients. Because weeds grow quickly, they steal these vital resources before your main crops can get enough to feed themselves.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ otsei lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, jwɛi lɛ daa oya. No sɛɛ lɛ, amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ dani oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ náa nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do I lose so much of my grain when I beat it inside sacks after harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mifiteɔ ŋmaa babaoo nɛkɛ kɛ́ mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Beating grain manually in sacks causes seeds to crush, crack, or get left behind inside the husks. It also punctures the sacks, allowing seeds to spill onto the ground and go to waste.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ niji tswa ŋmaa ni yɔɔ kotoku lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaha egbɛ eshwa, efo, loo ebaashi ŋmaa lɛ mli. Amɛfoɔ kotokui lɛ amli hu koni dumɔwui ashwie shikpɔŋ ni amɛshwie jwɛi.

english: How does using a threshing machine save more of my crop than doing it by hand?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baa shi fe oniji ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ?

english: A threshing machine gently and cleanly separates seeds from the husks without crushing them. It processes large amounts quickly, preventing grain from scattering on the floor or remaining stuck in the pods.
ga: Mɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa lɛ gbalaa ŋmãa lɛ kɛjɛɔ ŋmãa lɛ mli blɛoo ni ehaa ehe tseɔ ni ekɛ amɛ shwieee shi. Tsu nii babaoo he nii oya Enɛ haaa dumɔwui lɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ loo amɛkamɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: What happens to my crop if rain falls on it right after I harvest it?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nii lɛ anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ beni mikpa nii lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: When rain wets newly harvested crops, the trapped water causes the seeds to rot, grow mold, or start sprouting again. This spoils the quality and makes the grain unfit for eating or selling.
ga: Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, tsei ni akpa ehee lɛ fɔ̃ɔ. Nu ni emɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ agbo, amɛfee ŋmɔtɔ, loo amɛje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ. Enɛ fiteɔ su lɛ ni ehaa dumɔwui lɛ esaaa akɛ ayeɔ loo ahɔ̃ɔɔ.

english: How can I protect my harvested crops if rain suddenly starts while I am still on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mikpamɔ lɛ he kɛji nugbɔ nɛ trukaa beni miyɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: You should immediately cover the harvested crops with waterproof tarpaulins or move them under a roof. Raising the crops off the bare ground on wooden pallets also stops rainwater from soaking in from below.
ga: Esa akɛ okɛ tarp aha okpamɔ lɛ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ loo okɛjie kɛya ŋwɛitsu ko shishi. Tsei ni akwɛɔ kɛjɛɔ hei ni nɔ ko bɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ hu tsiɔ nugbɔ nu naa koni ekajɛ shishi kɛbote mli.

english: Why do I end up with less grain at home than what I actually harvested from my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ diɛŋtsɛ minine shɛɛɛ ŋmaa nɔ yɛ shia fe nɔ ni mikpaa kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Crop loss happens stage-by-stage during cutting, carrying, manual beating, and drying. Rough handling scatters seeds, and inefficient thrashing leaves good grain behind in the crop stalks.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ laajeɔ baa fiofio yɛ be mli ni afoɔ, akɛtsuɔ nii, akɛ niji tswaa, ni agbiɔ lɛ. Nitsumɔ ni mli wa lɛ gbɛɔ dumɔwui lɛ eshwaa. Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsuuu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ shĩɔ dumɔwui kpakpai yɛ sɛɛ.

english: Why do some of my harvested grains break into small pieces during processing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ akumɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ ekomɛi amli bibii bibii lɛ? yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ

english: Grains break when they are beaten too hard with heavy sticks or when they are processed while too dry and brittle. Using proper threshing tools or machines helps keep the grains whole.
ga: The rice grains break when hit too hard with a heavy stick. aloo kɛ́ atsu he nii yɛ be mli ni egbi tsɔ ni egbɔjɔ Kɛ́ akɛ tsɔne ni akɛshwieɔ ŋmãa loo tsɔne ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ akayi obɔ.

english: Why is it dangerous to put my harvested grain directly into storage bags while it is still damp?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ akɛ dumɔwui ni akpa lɛ baawo kotokui ni akɛtoɔ nii amli tɛ̃ɛ be mli ni amɛmli edɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Damp grain creates warmth inside the storage bag, which causes destructive mold to grow fast and attracts insects. Wet grain will spoil within days and ruin your entire harvest.
ga: Tso mli ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ haa hulutsoo baa kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ mli. Enɛ haa ŋmei lɛ daa oya ni egbalaa koolooi. Dumɔwui ni efɔ lɛ baafite yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli ni ebaafite onibii fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested crop pods refuse to open easily when I try to shell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso ni mikpa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ egbeleee mlɛo kɛ́ mibɔ mɔdɛŋ ni mafolɔ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Crop pods hold tightly to seeds when they still contain too much moisture. Letting your harvested pods dry thoroughly in the sun makes them brittle so they snap open easily without damaging the seeds inside.
ga: Tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ mɔ̃ɔ dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ babaoo yɛ lolo. Kɛ́ oŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni anyɛ akumɔ amɛ mlɛo ni amɛfiteee dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: Why do buyers pay me less money when my harvested grains get wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ mi nyɔmɔ fioo beni mikpamɔ lɛ mli edɔ lɛ?

english: Wet grains spoil quickly, weigh unnaturally heavy with water, and produce poor-quality flour. Buyers pay lower prices because they have to spend extra time drying it or risk losing their investment to mold.
ga: Nibii ni efɔ lɛ fiteɔ oya. Akɛ nu susuɔ he yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni ehaa ashikiŋsha ni hi jogbaŋŋ baa Mɔ ni heɔ lɛ woɔ jara ni baa shi ejaakɛ ebiɔ be kroko kɛha ŋmɔlɔ loo eyɛ oshara akɛ shika ni akɛfee ŋmɔlɔ lɛ baafite.

english: Why do my harvested seeds start germinating and sprouting stems on their own before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikpa lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃ɔ dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ amɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds naturally awaken and sprout whenever they touch water and warmth. If your harvested crop gets wet from rain or damp ground, the seed thinks it is time to grow into a new plant, which ruins it for selling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ baate shi ni amɛbaakwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be ni amɛkɛ nu kɛ hulutsoo baakpe. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okpaa lɛ mli ewo nu kɛjɛ nugbɔ loo hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ Dumɔwu lɛ susuɔ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ eda ni etsɔ tso hee, ni efiteɔ koni ekɛhɔ̃ɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant three or four maize seeds together in one single hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ loo ejwɛ feɔ ekome yɛ bu kome mli lɛ?

english: When you put too many seeds in one hole, the young plants fight each other for water, sunlight, and nutrients in the soil. Spacing them out allows each stalk to grow thick and strong enough to bear large, healthy cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ dumɔwui babaoo wo bu kome mli Tsei bibii lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. He ni akɛtoɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehe wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ aye abua ŋmeii wuji ni he wa lɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow quickly and have broad leaves that create natural shade, keeping the young cocoa seedlings cool and keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo baa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do people tell me that planting groundnuts or beans makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ mi akɛ kɛ́ midu ŋmei loo ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ ahi jogbaŋŋ kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to a crop family that pulls nitrogen from the air and traps it in the ground. When the leaves and roots rot after harvest, they leave natural fertilizer in the soil for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi fite yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ Ebaashi adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: If your crop leaves start turning pale green or yellow instead of deep dark green, or if the plant stays small and weak despite getting rain, the soil does not have enough nutrients to feed the plant.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otso lɛ baai lɛ bɔi ŋmɔŋ loo ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ. Aloo kɛji akɛ tso lɛ ji bibioo lolo ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaye abua tsei lɛ.

english: Why are there small worms hiding in the middle leaves of my young maize plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii komɛi kɛ amɛhe ewo mi-ŋmei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The adult moth lays eggs on the leaves, and the hatched caterpillars crawl into the central leaves (the funnel) to eat the soft growing parts of the maize plant.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei onukpa ko ni woɔ wui yɛ baai anɔ. Ni ŋmeii ni efɔ lɛ shwereɔ kɛboteɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli (cones) koni amɛye ŋmei tsei bibii ni daraa lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly dry up and die even when the soil is still wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ gbɛ́ɔ trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ lɛ? Ani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a disease in the soil that enters the plant's roots and clogs the internal tubes, stopping water from reaching the leaves even if the ground is soaked.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni eboteɔ tsei ashishifãi amli ni etsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa nu nyɛɛɛ abote baai lɛ amli kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ po.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they are under stress, usually caused by extremely high heat, irregular watering, or tiny insect pests like thrips attacking the delicate blossoms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baafɔfɔi ashwie shi kɛji amɛhao. Bei pii lɛ, dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa loo kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips ni tutuaa fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ.

english: Why should I cut off the small shoots growing around my main plantain stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei bibii lɛ? ni miida yɛ Mi plantain tso titri lɛ he lɛ ajie

english: These extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and nutrients from the main mother plant. Pruning them leaves only the strongest shoot and allows the main plant to produce a big, heavy bunch.
ga: Nɛkɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi nɛɛ, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ, juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei ni wa fe fɛɛ lɛ pɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa tso titri lɛ woɔ tsei wuji ni tsii.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant seeds right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The first rain often warms up the dry dirt without soaking deep into the ground, and it is usually followed by a dry hot spell that can dry out and kill young germinating seeds before the real rain starts.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ mli dɔɔ ni ehaaa edɔ waa. Ni bei pii lɛ, latsaa ni mli egbi ni baanyɛ aha dumɔwui bibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ dani nugbɔ lɛ je shishi lɛ nyiɛɔ enɛ sɛɛ.

english: Cassava is usually ready when the bottom leaves turn yellow and drop off, and the soil around the base of the plant begins to crack open as the growing tubers push outward under the surface.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Yucca lɛ efee klalo kɛ́ shishigbɛ baai lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi. Ni shikpɔŋ ni bɔle shishigbɛ lɛ jeɔ shishi egbɛɔ eshwaa be mli ni ŋmeii ni miida lɛ tsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shishi lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow green and healthy. It can also happen when heavy rains flood the field and wash nutrients deep into the soil away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ eyi ŋmɔ mli ni ekɛ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ, ni ekɛ shishifãi lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa tree flowers drop off without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa kwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers often drop when the tree is stressed by excessive sun heat, prolonged dry weather, or attacks from insects like mirids. Keeping adequate shade trees and managing pests helps the flowers stay on and develop into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulu ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo kooloi bibii ni tutuaa mɔ tamɔ atatu ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ hulutsoo be ni sa ha kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiifee tamɔ mɛi ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is frequently caused by viruses transmitted by tiny insects like whiteflies, or by extreme heat and dry soil. Keeping the soil consistently moist and controlling sucking insects prevents this problem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hela ko ni kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ kooloi ni nuɔ nu lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ baaye abua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms before any peppers appear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani pepper lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their blossoms when the weather gets too hot or when watering is irregular. Giving the plants consistent moisture during the flowering stage helps them hold onto blossoms so fruits can form.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ nu lɛ haaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ha tso lɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ ahe koni ewo yibii.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts capture nitrogen from the air and deposit it into the soil. This naturally fertilizes your maize, covers the bare ground to stop weeds, and keeps the soil cool and moist.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha o-corn lɛ afɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Ha hei ni nɔ ko bɛ lɛ nɔ koni jwɛi lɛ akpa. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i ni edɔɔ

english: Why is it useful to cover the soil around my crops with dry grass or leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mikɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi baawo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle miŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry plant material, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket. It stops hot sunlight from drying out the soil, reduces weed growth, and eventually breaks down into rich organic manure.
ga: Atsɛɔ tsei ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni buɔ mɔ he Eyeɔ ebuaa ni hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ haaa shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi. Ha jwɛi lɛ adalɛ aba shi ni naagbee lɛ efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa.

english: Why shouldn't I cut down all the large forest trees on my cocoa farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mifoɔ koo mli tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Large trees provide shade that protects cocoa trees from scorching sun and hot winds, keeping the soil cool and moist. They also shed leaves that decay into natural plant food, helping cocoa trees live much longer.
ga: Tsei ni edara lɛ haa hɔɔŋ ni buɔ kokoo tsei lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ he. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ. Ekɛ baai ni egboi lɛ hu shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔ amɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei aniyenii. Eyeɔ ebuaa kookoo tso lɛ ni ehiɔ shi be babaoo.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava root rot happens when water sits around the roots for too long, suffocating them and encouraging fungal diseases. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fitemɔ baa kɛji nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe ni ewoɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela he hewalɛ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ oya.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily when they start carrying big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji shweremɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall over because microscopic pests called nematodes or root weevils weaken their shallow roots under the soil. Supporting heavy trees with bamboo props and planting clean suckers prevents this.
ga: Plantains lɛ gbee shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo root weevils lɛ haa shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ gbɔjɔɔ. Tsei ni tsii ni akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ fiɔ amɛsɛɛ kɛ ŋmeii ni he tse ni akwɛ̃ɔ lɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ enɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out crooked or split open inside the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miida ni ebɔle amɛhe loo amɛmli eja yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yams split or grow deformed when they hit hard, compacted soil while expanding, or when heavy rains suddenly follow a long dry spell, making the inside of the tuber grow faster than the skin.
ga: Sweet potatoes fiteɔ loo efiteɔ kɛji etswa shikpɔŋ ni wa ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ beni egbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ. aloo be mli ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa trukaa kɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ daa oya fe hewolo lɛ.

english: Why should I grow my vegetables in plastic sacks or bags instead of planting them directly in my open farmland soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu aduawai yɛ kotokui loo plastic kotokui amli moŋ fe ni madu yɛ okwaayeli shikpɔŋ ni agbele nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Growing in sacks allows you to use good, rich soil even if your main farmland has poor soil or pest problems. It conserves water, keeps weeds away, and makes it easier to care for your crops right near your home.
ga: Kɛ́ okwɛɔ yɛ kotokui amli lɛ, ehaa okɛ shikpɔŋ kpakpa ni baa nii tsuɔ nii. Kɛji akɛ he titri ni okwɛɔ nii yɛ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii loo tsɛŋemɔ helai ahe naagbai po. Ehaa nu sɛɛ foɔ, egbeɔ jwɛi, ni ehaa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ aaakwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ shia lɛ anɔ.

english: What is the benefit of growing crops under a nursery shelter compared to planting them directly out in the open field?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he kɛ akɛto ŋmɔ mli ni aduɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he?

english: A nursery shelter acts like a shield for young plants, protecting delicate seedlings from heavy torrential rain, scorching sun, and insect pests so they can build strong roots before facing harsh outdoor weather.
ga: Tso lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gãimlibi kɛha tso bibioo lɛ. Ebuɔ dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he. hulu la ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kooloi bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui Enɛ ji koni dumɔwui lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni mli wa dani amɛyashɛ shihilɛi ni mli wa ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ amli.

english: If I switch from my traditional seeds to improved seed varieties, will my crops grow faster?
ga: Kɛji mitsake kɛjɛ shishijee dumɔwui lɛ amli kɛtee dumɔwui ni atsake amɛ lɛ anɔ Ani miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya?

english: Yes, improved seed varieties are bred to mature faster and withstand tough weather. This means you can harvest early, avoid dry season losses, and sometimes plant twice in one rain season.
ga: Hɛɛ, afɔɔ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya ni amɛdamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ shihilɛi ni mli wawai anaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ obaanyɛ okpa mra. Tsi ohe kɛjɛ nibii ni laajeɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ he. ni bei komɛi lɛ, aduɔ shii enyɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kome mli.

english: Why do my neighbor's crops mature so much faster than mine even though we planted on the exact same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ tso lɛ miida oya fe mi nɔ lɛ? ni wɔdu yɛ gbi kome nɔ lɛ

english: Crop growth speed depends on the seed variety used, how well the soil was prepared, and whether the crops received enough plant food and moisture early on. Improved seeds paired with proper fertilizer grow much faster.
ga: Bɔ ni tso lɛ daa oya lɛ damɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ nɔ. Te asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ ahaa tɛŋŋ? ni kɛji akɛ tsei lɛ ná tsei niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa mra lɛ, dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa fata he lɛ baakwɛ̃ oya kwraa.

english: If I use commercial fertilizer on my food crops, will it change the taste of the food when I cook it?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii yɛ mi niyenii tsei lɛ anɔ Ani niyenii lɛ ŋɔɔ baatsake kɛ́ mihoo?

english: No, commercial fertilizer simply feeds plants the essential minerals they need to grow strong, like nitrogen and potassium. When used correctly, it improves crop size and health without spoiling the natural taste of your food.
ga: Dabi, tsofai ni akɛwoɔ jarayeli mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa nibii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃, tamɔ nitrogen kɛ potassium pɛ. Kɛ akɛtsu nii jogbaŋŋ Ebaaha tso lɛ dalɛ kɛ hewalɛ aya hiɛ ni efiteee oniyenii lɛ mli adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔlɔ.

english: Will vegetables grown inside a protective shelter look or taste different from crops grown in normal open fields?
ga: Ani aduawai ni aduɔ yɛ shia lɛ baafee srɔto loo amɛmli ŋɔɔ fe tsei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni agbele mli daa lɛ?

english: Vegetables grown under shelter often look cleaner, larger, and spot-free because they are safe from rain damage and pests. Their taste remains delicious and natural, but their market appearance is usually much better.
ga: Aduawai ni adu yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe tse, amɛdara ni nɔ ko nɔ ko bɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ amɛhe yɛ shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ nugbɔ kɛ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ ahe. Nɔ ni ŋɔɔ lɛ ŋɔɔ lolo ni eji adebɔɔ nɔ. Shi bei pii lɛ, bɔ ni jara lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ hi fe no kwraa.

english: Why do my outdoor tomato plants rot during heavy rains while crops under protective coverings survive?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei ni yɔɔ kpo nɔ lɛ fiteɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ ni naa wa mli yɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ tsɔi lɛ hiɔ shi lɛ?

english: Heavy rains splash mud onto tomato leaves, spreading hidden fungal diseases, and excess water rots roots. Coverings block direct rain droplets while still allowing light and air through to keep plants dry and safe.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ muji nɔ yɛ tomato baai lɛ anɔ Egbɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ lɛ eshwaa ni shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛjɛɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ mli. Nɔ ni haa nɔ lɛ tsiɔ nugbɔshiimɔi lɛ anaa tɛ̃ɛ. yɛ be mli ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ lolo kɛ la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli lɛ. Koni tso lɛ akagbi ni ehi shi shweshweeshwe

english: How does using a shade net help my crops grow better than leaving them under full outdoor sunlight?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shade netting ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ni mashi amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli?

english: Shade nets reduce extreme sun heat that causes leaves to dry up and wilt. They keep the moisture in the soil longer and physically block insects from coming in to eat your crop leaves.
ga: Shade ŋshɔŋlooi haa dɔlɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa ni haa baai lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛgboɔ lɛ baa shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. ni etsĩɔ kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye otsei lɛ ahe baai

english: How do I know what food or fertilizer my crop needs when I notice the leaves turning yellow?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male niyenii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni he hiaa mitso lɛ beni mina akɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a cry for help showing the crop lacks nutrients, especially nitrogen. Adding the right fertilizer gives the crop the energy it needs to make green leaves and produce heavy yields.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ tso lɛ mli. titri lɛ nitrogen Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo.

english: Why do different crops on my farm need different types of plant food to grow properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ biɔ tsei niyenii srɔtoi koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Different crops use nutrients in different ways. Leafy crops like cabbage need extra nitrogen to build leaves, while fruiting crops like tomatoes need extra phosphorus and potassium to produce firm, heavy fruit.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii yɛ gbɛ sɔrɔto nɔ. Tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ kaabe he miihia nitrogen kroko koni amɛfee baai. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tomato biɔ phosphorus kɛ potassium krokomɛi koni amɛwo yibii ni tsii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Adding nitrogen fertilizer or compost helps the leaves turn green so the crop can properly feed itself and produce big cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji. No hewɔ lɛ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the crop's roots are established—usually 2 to 3 weeks after sprouting—and while the soil is moist, so the plant can easily drink up the nutrients.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ema shi—bei pii lɛ, otsii 2 kɛyashi 3 sɛɛ beni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ—kɛ be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ lolo lɛ. No hewɔ lɛ tsei baanyɛ anu niyenii mli hewalɛ nii mlɛo.

english: Leaving space ensures plants do not fight each other for sunlight, water, and nutrients in the soil. Good spacing also allows air to blow through, which keeps the leaves dry and prevents diseases.
ga: He ko ni ashiɔ lɛ baatsi tsei anaa koni amɛkaye hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. He ni jɛkɛmɔ kpakpa hu haa kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔɔ mli. Enɛ baaha baai lɛ agbi ni helai baatsi enaa.

english: Why do some of the crop seeds I plant fail to sprout from the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu lɛ ekwɛɛɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are buried too deep, if the soil is too dry or flooded, or if the seeds were already old or damaged by insects before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ loo dumɔwui lɛ edara momo loo kooloi bibii efite amɛ dani adu.

english: What is causing holes to appear on the leaves of my crops overnight?
ga: Mɛni haa buji jeɔ kpo yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ anɔ nyɔɔŋ kome mli?

english: Holes are typically caused by pests like caterpillars or beetles feeding on the leaves. Inspecting the undersides of leaves early in the morning helps you catch the pests early before they ruin the entire leaf.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni yeɔ baai lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ buji baa. Kɛ́ okwɛ baai lɛ ashishi leebi lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni omɔ kooloi ni yeɔ amɛ awui lɛ mra. Dani amɛbaafite baai lɛ fɛɛ

english: Pepper flowers often drop off when the plant is stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or when insects fail to pollinate them. Regular watering during hot dry spells helps the plant hold onto its flowers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kɛ́ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ amɛwo amɛmli lɛ miigba tsei lɛ anaa. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu daa yɛ be mli ni latsaa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: How do I know if my cassava crop is suffering from a lack of water during dry weather?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ miihe nu yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Cassava plants show water stress when their lower leaves turn yellow and drop off early, or when young leaves curl up. This is the plant's way of reducing water loss to stay alive.
ga: Cassava tsei jieɔ nu he haomɔ kpo kɛji baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbee shi oya. aloo beni baai bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi Enɛ ji gbɛ ni tso ko tsɔɔ nɔ ehaa nu ni efiteɔ lɛ baa shi koni ehi shi.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool, slows down water evaporation during sunny days, and stops weeds from growing around your crops.
ga: Ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i. Ha nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ aya hiɛ fioo yɛ hulutsoo be mli. ni otsi jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ oŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ naa.

english: Why shouldn't I plant the exact same crop on the same piece of land season after season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every year and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the soil.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa afi. ni ehaa tsei ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai babaoo baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: How can I tell when my yam tubers are ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ eshɛ he koni akpa?

english: Yams are usually ready for harvest when the leaves and vines turn yellow and dry up naturally, signaling that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber under the ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, sweet potatoes lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni baai kɛ wain tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ e-bulbs lɛ amli yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ naa.

english: Why do my harvested tomatoes spoil so quickly when I pick them during the heavy rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato ni akpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛ́ akpa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni naa wa lɛ mli lɛ?
