english: High moisture and humidity create perfect conditions for fungi and bacteria to grow on fruit skins. Excess water trapped inside and outside the fruit during harvest speeds up rotting, especially if they are packed in tight crates without ventilation.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo kɛ fɛ̃i ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛhaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ aduawai ahe tsɔi anɔ. Nu ni fa fe nine ni ŋmɛɔ aduawai lɛ amli kɛ kponɔgbɛ yɛ kpamɔ be mli lɛ baaha amɛfite oya. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛji akɛ akɛwo adeka ko ni mli wa mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli.

english: How can I plan my planting dates so my crops mature when market prices are highest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mato gbi ni mikɛbaadu nii lɛ he gbɛjianɔ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashɛ shweremɔ be mli ni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ?

english: You need to count backward from the peak demand period using the crop's maturity days. Planting early at the very start of the rains helps you harvest before the market becomes oversaturated and prices drop.
ga: Esa akɛ okane kɛya sɛɛ kɛjɛ nibii ni ataoɔ babaoo lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe gbi ni esa akɛ akwɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ odu nii mra yɛ nugbɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ehaa onyɛɔ okpaa nii dani jara lɛ nɔ eyiɔ obɔ kɛ nibii ni jara baa shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers without producing peppers when there is heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ jieɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Excessive rainfall washes away pollen and keeps pollinating insects away. Too much water in the soil also stresses root systems, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ hoɔ pollen lɛ he ni ehaa kooloi ni feɔ pollen lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ. Nu babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hu saa shishifãi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Why do my maize plants grow faster during the early rains compared to the middle of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋma lɛ daa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli fe nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: At the start of the rains, warm soil releases a sudden burst of accumulated nitrogen (known as the nitrate flush), giving young maize rapid growth. Heavy, mid-season rains cool the soil and can waterlog roots, slowing growth.
ga: Yɛ nugbɔ lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ jieɔ nitrogen ni ato lɛ trukaa. (ni atsɛɔ lɛ nitrate flush) lɛ haa ŋmãa bibii lɛ daa oya. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ be lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ, ni ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ atsɔ nu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji dalɛ ni yaa hiɛ blɛoo.

english: Which vegetables can survive constant rainfall and still sell well in the market?
ga: Mɛɛ aduawai baanyɛ adamɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ naa ni amɛhɔ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ lolo yɛ jara nɔ?

english: Water-tolerant leafy greens like gboma, jute mallow (ayoyo), and indigenous spinach handle heavy rain better than delicate fruiting crops like tomatoes. Because delicate crops fail often in heavy rain, growing resilient vegetables ensures a steady harvest when market supply is low.
ga: Nu mli tsei ni yɔɔ baai tamɔ boma, jute (ayoyo) kɛ amaranth ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni waaa tamɔ tomato. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, tsei ni waaa lɛ fɔɔ shweremɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Aduawai akwɛmɔ ni anyɛɔ atsakeɔ lɛ haa ŋmaakpamɔ ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ baa kɛji jara nɔ nibii ni yɔɔ lɛ faaa.

english: Why do my cassava tubers rot underground if I leave them in the soil during prolonged rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots require oxygen in the soil to stay alive. Waterlogged soil cuts off air supply to the roots, allowing harmful soil fungi to infect and decay the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni tsɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ naa. Enɛ yeɔ sũ mli ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ anɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds grow much faster than my crop right after the first rain of the season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Weed seeds are wild and tough, remaining dormant in dry soil ready to sprout at the first sign of moisture. Your cultivated crop seeds take longer to establish roots, giving weeds an early advantage in taking up water and nutrients.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui lɛ wa ni amɛhe wa. Amɛwɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, ni amɛfee klalo akɛ amɛbaakwɛ̃ kɛji amɛna klɛŋklɛŋ okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ eba. Dumɔwui ni odu lɛ baahe be babaoo dani efee shishifãi. Enɛ haa jwɛi lɛ náa sɛɛnamɔ mra. Koni ekɛjie nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves turn yellow after heavy rainfall even though I already applied fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ewo amɛmli moŋ?

english: Heavy rains wash away water-soluble nutrients like nitrogen deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them. Waterlogged roots also lose the ability to absorb nutrients due to a lack of oxygen in the soil.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii mli nibii ni mli tse, tamɔ nitrogen, yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Shishifãi ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ hu nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hewɔ.

english: Why do my cowpea seeds get damaged by insects in storage much faster during humid weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui lɛ yeɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ oya yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: High moisture levels in the air during damp seasons raise the moisture content of stored grains. This warmth and moisture cause grain weevil eggs to hatch faster and feed aggressively.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni fa babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ haa fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ ŋmaa ni ato lɛ mli lɛ yaa hiɛ. Nɛkɛ dɔlɛ kɛ fɛ̃i nɛɛ haa ŋmaa ŋmei wui lɛ fɔɔ oya ni amɛyeɔ nii waa.

english: Will supplying extra water during short dry spells help my crops yield better than relying only on natural rainfall?
ga: Nu kroko ni akɛhaa yɛ hulutsoo be kukuoo mli Ani ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai fe ni mikɛ mihe baafɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ pɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, consistent moisture prevents plant stress during flower and fruit development. Unpredictable breaks in rainfall cause plants to shed flowers or produce small, cracked fruits, reducing your final harvest quality.
ga: Hɛɛ, hulutsoo be fɛɛ be yeɔ ebuaa ni etsĩɔ tsei anaa yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai adalɛ be mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba lɛ haa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi loo amɛwoɔ aduawai bibii ni egbɛ eshwa, ni ehaa onaagbee kpamɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: How far apart should I plant my plantain suckers if I am not using fertilizer?
ga: Te esa akɛ madu plantain tsei lɛ kɛjɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ yɔɔ ha tɛŋŋ kɛji akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii?

english: If you are not applying fertilizer, you should use normal spacing by taking three steps between each plantain sucker to ensure each plant gets enough natural soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ Esa akɛ okɛ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ ni ji 3 steps ahi plantain ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ daa koni ona nɔmimaa akɛ tso fɛɛ tso miiná adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: How can I measure the planting distance for plantains if I do not have a measuring tape?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ masusu mi plantains lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ he kɛji mibɛ tsɔne ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe?

english: You can measure the standard distance by taking three normal strides or steps from one planting hole to where you place the next one.
ga: Obaanyɛ osusu gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ he kɛtsɔ gbɛi etɛ ni afɔɔ nɔ loo gbɛi ni oootsɔ nɔ kɛjɛ dumɔ bu kome mli kɛya he ni okɛ bu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baawo lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do plantains planted without fertilizer need to be spaced further apart?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ atse plantains ni aduɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Unfertilized plantains rely only on natural soil nutrients, so they need more space between them so their roots do not compete for the limited food in the ground.
ga: Plantains ni awooo amɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ pɛ nɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni amɛná gbɛ babaoo yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ ji koni amɛshishifãi lɛ akashi akaŋ yɛ niyenii fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he.

english: Will my plantains grow well if I plant them close together without giving them fertilizer?
ga: Ani mi dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli?

english: No, if you plant them close together without fertilizer, the plants will fight for soil food and light, which results in weak growth and smaller bunches.
ga: Dabi, kɛji akɛ odu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wooo mli. Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa shweremɔ ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ kui bibii baa.

english: How many steps should I take between plantain holes when setting up a regular field?
ga: Nibii enyiɛ esa akɛ mafee yɛ plantain bu lɛ ateŋ beni miitoɔ gbɛ ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ he gbɛjianɔ lɛ?

english: For regular planting without fertilizer, you should take three steps between each planting point to give the plantains enough room to grow.
ga: Kɛha dumɔ ni aduɔ daa ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tsuuu nii. Esa akɛ ofee nibii etɛ yɛ he ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ eko fɛɛ eko teŋ koni eha dumɔwui lɛ aná hegbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛdara.

english: Does applying fertilizer change how close I can plant my plantains?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha mabɛŋkɛ mi plantain lɛ dumɔ he eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Yes, using fertilizer enriches the soil so you can safely plant plantain suckers closer together without them competing for nutrients.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa sũ lɛ feɔ fɛo. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ odu plantain tsei lɛ ahe shweshweeshwe ni okɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa lɛ akaŋ.

english: How does using fertilizer allow me to fit more plantain trees on my farm?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ni makwɛ dumɔwui babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Fertilizer supplies extra food to the soil, meaning plants do not need as much root space to feed, allowing you to reduce the distance between crops and plant more per acre.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa niyenii krokomɛi. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he ehiaaa shishifãi babaoo ni ekɛye nii. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okɛ tsei kɛ tso teŋ jɛkɛmɔ baa shi kɛtsɔ babaoo ni oooha yɛ acre kome mli lɛ nɔ.

english: What determines the right spacing distance to use when planting plantains?
ga: Mɛni tsɔɔ he ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui?

english: Plantain spacing depends directly on your management plan—specifically whether you plan to feed the crop with fertilizer or rely on natural soil fertility.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ damɔ gbɛjianɔtoo ni okɛkwɛɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Pɔtɛɛ, kɛji oto gbɛjianɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii aha otsei lɛ loo okɛ ohe afɔ̃ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ ni ŋmɔshi nii yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: If I plan to fertilize my plantain farm, should I place the suckers closer than three steps apart?
ga: Kɛji mito gbɛjianɔ koni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi plantain ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmeii lɛ abɛŋkɛ he ko ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ fe ŋwɛi ŋtayaai etɛ?

english: Yes, if you are adding fertilizer, you can place your plantain suckers closer together than the standard three-step distance.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ okɛ fɔmɔ nii wo mli. Obaanyɛ okɛ plantain tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ abɛŋkɛ amɛhe fe bɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ ni ji ŋwɛi ŋsɔɔdoi etɛ lɛ.

english: Why does soil food affect how near or far plantains can stand next to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ saa nyɛmɔ ni plantains yɔɔ ni amɛkɛdamɔ shi yɛ he ni bɛŋkɛ kɛ he ni yɔɔ shɔŋŋ fɛɛ lɛ he lɛ?

english: When soil food is abundant from fertilizer, plants can share smaller areas without starving; when soil food is low, plants must be spaced further apart to find food.
ga: Be mli ni niyenii babaoo yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli. Tsei baanyɛ aja he bibioo ko. ni hɔmɔ bɛ mli Beni niyenii fioo pɛ eshwɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Ehe baahia ni ajie tsei lɛ kɛjɛ amɛhe shɔŋŋ koni ana niyenii.

english: Young cocoa trees need shade to survive because harsh sunlight burns their leaves and dries out their roots. Leaving taller shade trees or planting plantains alongside young cocoa acts like an umbrella, providing the cool, moist environment young plants need to grow strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ hia hɔɔŋ koni amɛhi shi ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai lɛ ni ehaa amɛshishifãi lɛ gĩɔ. tsei kakadaji ni ajieɔ lɛ Ha hulutsoo loo dumɔ dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ ahe koni amɛtsu nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ye obua tsei bibii Ha shihilɛ ni mli ejɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ mli aha tsei bibii lɛ koni amɛdara waa.

english: Why is burning dry grass on my farm before planting bad for my soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ni ashãa yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli dani aduɔ lɛ ehiii kɛha mishikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Burning clears the field fast, but the intense heat destroys natural soil nutrients, kills helpful earthworms, and removes organic matter. Over time, burned soil becomes dry and hard, making it difficult for crop roots to find food and water.
ga: La ni ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ tseɔ oya. Shi dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ fiteɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni ojie nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ kɛjɛ mli Beni be hoɔ lɛ Shikpɔŋ ni ashã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaana niyenii kɛ nu.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crops help them during the hot season?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te miŋmɔshi nibii yeɔ ebuaa amɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli tɛŋŋ?

english: Covering the soil around plants with dry grass, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and keeps the soil cool under direct sunlight. This stops water from evaporating quickly and helps crops survive long dry spells.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ oya, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ shihilɛi ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ amli.

english: Yellow leaves at the bottom of maize plants usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient responsible for green leaf growth. Applying compost, manure, or nitrogen fertilizer restores healthy green growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei ashishi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baai eŋɔli lɛ daa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of nutrients like phosphorus and calcium. Consistent watering and feeding help the plant hold onto its blossoms to produce fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ ná dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ tamɔ phosphorus kɛ calcium ni bɛ lɛ Nu kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ amli koni ewo yibii.

english: What is eating the center leaves of my young corn plants and leaving small brown droppings behind?
ga: Mɛni yeɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ ni eshiɔ ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the growing central leaf funnel of maize. Checking crops early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract solutions stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ he ŋaawoo. Ehaa nakai tsei lɛ kpaa nitsumɔ dani amɛfiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground if I leave them in the wet soil for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Excess water staying around cassava roots in heavy soil creates wet conditions where root-rot fungi thrive. Harvesting mature cassava promptly when the rain season slows down keeps the tubers firm and healthy.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni bɔleɔ ŋmei shishifãi ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii nɔ lɛ haa shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ ni shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ mli lɛ baa. Kɛ́ akpa ŋmei ni eda lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ blɛoo lɛ mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmei lɛ hiɔ shi shiŋŋ ni ehiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do I need to use wooden stakes to support my growing yam vines?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe hiaa mi koni mikɛfi mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ shweremɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to catch maximum sunlight so their leaves can produce food for the underground tubers. Leaving vines on the hot ground exposes them to diseases and leads to smaller, weaker yam yields.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Bɔni afee ni ebaa lɛ anyɛ afee niyenii aha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ ashi wain tsei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hela aba amɛnɔ ni ebaaha sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afee bibioo ni egbɔjɔ.

english: Why should I leave recommended distance between my cassava stems instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ ato he ko moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting stems too close together forces crops to fight over water, sunlight, and ground food, resulting in thin stalks and tiny tubers. Giving each plant proper space lets the roots expand fully.
ga: Tsoi ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni atswa, ni no haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kwraa.

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred for a single high-yielding harvest, but seeds saved from that harvest lose those good traits in the next generation. Re-using hybrid seeds leads to uneven growth and lower yields compared to buying fresh certified seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome lɛ krɛdɛɛ kɛha ŋmaakpamɔ kome ni woɔ yibii babaoo. Shi dumɔwui ni hiɔ shi yɛ nikpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ laajeɔ nakai sui kpakpai lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome ni akɛtsuɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ haa amɛdaraa ni ekɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee ni yibiiwoo baa shi kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli he lɛ he.

english: Why are the young cocoa seedlings I planted dying when the rain stops for just a few days?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii ni midu lɛ gboi beni nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛmɔ gbii fioo pɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and thin leaves that cannot handle direct sunshine or dry soil. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains to keep the soil cool and moist until their root systems grow deep enough to survive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo. ni nyɛŋ aná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ fɔmɔ kotoku nɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi amɛshishifãi lɛ baatsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why does it take a few years for my cocoa trees to start giving me cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii fioo komɛi dani mi-cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛhaa mi cacao ŋmeii lɛ?

english: A cocoa tree must first spend its early years building a thick trunk, strong branches, and deep roots to support heavy pods later. Hybrid cocoa varieties usually start producing pods within 2 to 3 years, while older traditional varieties take 4 to 5 years.
ga: Cacao tso lɛ he miihia be yɛ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli. koni ekɛfee tsei ni mli tse niji ni mli wa kɛ shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni baaye abua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ Hybrid cocoa henɔi lɛ fɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ afeemɔ shishi yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni blema cocoa henɔi ni etsɛ lɛ heɔ afii 4 kɛyashi 5.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants curl up into tight tubes during the hot afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abɛi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efeɔ tsɔji ni mli wa yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling is the corn plant's natural way of protecting itself from heat. By rolling its leaves, the plant reduces the surface area exposed to the hot sun, which keeps water from evaporating out of the plant too quickly.
ga: Baai ni ajieɔ lɛ ji gbɛ ni ŋmãa tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ hiɛ ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ baa shi. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli oya tsɔ.

english: Why is my maize growing tall and thin with light green leaves instead of thick and dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele lɛ daa ni ekwɛɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni mli tseee lɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: When soil lacks nitrogen, maize plants stretch upward trying to find light but remain weak and pale. Pale, thin stalks mean the plant does not have enough nutrients to build strong stems or produce large, healthy cobs.
ga: Beni nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Abele lɛ tsɔɔ ehe, ni ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni ena la, shi ehiɔ shi ni egbɔjɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Tso lɛ shishi tsei ni mli tseee ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha tso lɛ shishi tsei ni wa loo ekɛ ŋmeii wuji ni mli wa aba.

english: Why do my okra flowers keep falling off without forming any okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra fɔfɔi lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛfeee okra ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Okra flowers usually drop off when the plant suffers from heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of balanced nutrients in the soil. Keeping soil moisture consistent and feeding the plant helps the flowers turn into pods.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Roselle fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miipiŋ yɛ hulutsoo be mli. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli be fɛɛ be loo niyenii ni sa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be kɛ niyenii ni akɛhaa tso lɛ baaye abua ni fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why are my okra plants growing plenty of big leaves but very few actual okra pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra lɛ baai wuji waa shi okra ŋmɔtɔi diɛŋtsɛ fioo pɛ yɔɔ lɛ?

english: If crops receive too much nitrogen, they put all their energy into growing tall stems and large leaves instead of flowering. Balancing the soil food encourages the plant to stop making leaves and start producing flowers and pods.
ga: Kɛji tsei ná nitrogen babaoo lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii kɛkwɛɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ baai wuji moŋ fe ni amɛaawo fɔfɔi. Nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpaa baai ni amɛjeɔ fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii afeemɔ shishi.

english: How does adding fertilizer actually help my crops produce more food?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ni amɛwo niyenii babaoo?

english: Fertilizer provides essential minerals like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil loses over time. These nutrients act like food for the crops, allowing them to build strong roots, greener leaves, and larger fruits or grains.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa nibii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiam. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ be ni sa mli Nibii nɛɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii kɛhaa tsei. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni etswaa shishifãi ni wa, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ aduawai loo ŋmaa wuji

english: Why do my crops turn pale yellow after many days of continuous heavy rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa gbii babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes water-soluble nutrients deep into the ground where crop roots cannot reach them. It also fills air spaces in the soil with water, which temporarily suffocates the roots and stops them from taking up food.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Ekɛ nu hu fataa kɔɔyɔɔ hei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko, ni ehaaa amɛye nii.

english: Why is it dangerous to place fertilizer directly against the stem of my young plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baawo mi tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ?

english: Fertilizers contain concentrated salts. Placing them directly against tender stems or roots draws moisture out of the plant tissue and burns it. Fertilizer should always be applied a small distance away from the stem.
ga: Fertilizer lɛ yɛ ŋoo babaoo. Kɛ́ okɛwo tsei loo shishifãi ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaajie nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ fãji amli ni eshã. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ fioo.

english: How do I know if my land needs fertilizer before I start planting my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii dani mabɔi ŋmɔshi nitsumɔ?

english: Signs like weak crop growth from the previous season, pale leaves, or sandy, worn-out soil indicate low nutrients. Testing your soil or observing how quickly weeds and past crops grow helps determine if fertilizer is needed.
ga: Okadii tamɔ tsei ni egbɔjɔ kɛjɛ be ni eho lɛ mli, baai ni tsuɔ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ ni efite lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ faaa. Kɛ́ oka oshikpɔŋ lɛ okwɛ loo okwɛ bɔ ni jwɛi kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni eho lɛ ekwɛ̃ oya lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni onaa kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe miihia.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the key food plants need to build healthy green leaves, or that heavy rain has washed nutrients away from the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛwo baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ eŋɔli. Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why do my weeds grow so much faster than the corn I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mijwɛi lɛ miida oya fe ŋmãa ni miduɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds are wild plants that naturally spread fast and steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer from your soil before your corn plants get a chance to drink and feed.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ adebɔɔ mli ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Dani ŋmãa tsei lɛ baaná hegbɛ amɛnu nu ni amɛye nii

english: Why do other farmers plant plantains right next to young cocoa trees when starting a new farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi krokomɛi duɔ plantains yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛ́ amɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get burnt very easily by strong sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants have wide leaves that act like umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture to keep young cocoa alive.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya waa kɛ́ hulu la ni naa wa shɛ amɛnɔ. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ehaa hulutsoo ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni eha kookoo lɛ ahi shi bibioo.

english: Does lifting my yam vines onto tall wooden sticks actually help me get bigger tubers?
ga: Ani sweet potato wain tsei ni miwoɔ yɛ tsei kakadaji anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ni mikwɛɔ bulbs wuji?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves up to catch maximum sunlight, which allows the plant to produce more food and store it deep underground as larger yam tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa tsei woɔ niyenii babaoo. ni ekɛto shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ tamɔ ŋmei ni da fe no.

english: Why are tiny green bugs making the leaves of my pepper plants curl up and twist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli Ni haa mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛshwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: Those bugs, like aphids, suck the sap out of the young leaves and can spread plant sicknesses, causing the leaves to dry out and curl.
ga: Nakai kooloi bibii, tamɔ aphids lɛ, nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai bibii amli lɛ, ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ tsei ahe helai amɛshwã. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛkpãa.

english: What is eating holes into the center leaves of my maize plants before they even open?
ga: Mɛni ji nɔ ni yeɔ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso baa lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ dani egbeleɔ po?

english: That damage is caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the deep center funnel of young corn plants to eat the soft, growing leaves.
ga: Nɔ ni fiteɔ nii ji tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm caterpillars, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi ni mli kwɔ lɛ amli koni amɛye baai bibii ni miida lɛ.

english: How far apart should I space my cassava stick cuttings when planting them?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafo mi-cassava niji lɛ amli kɛ́ midu?

english: Planting cassava cuttings about one meter apart gives each root enough room underground to swell up into big, heavy tubers without fighting neighboring plants for nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmei niji ni kɛ amɛhe jɛkɛmɔ aaafee mita kome lɛ, ehaa shishifã fɛɛ shishifã náa shishifã ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaatsɔ ŋmei agbo ni tsii. ni ehe ehiaaa ni ekɛ tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ awuu kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ

english: Should I cut away the extra small shoots growing at the base of my main plantain stem?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ ŋmeii bibii? Ani nɔ ko krɛdɛɛ ko yɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ plantain wulu lɛ shishi?

english: Yes, removing extra shoots leaves only two or three strong stems, ensuring the plant puts all its energy into growing one large, heavy bunch of plantains instead of small ones.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ baaha ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ aba ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛduɔ plantain tsei wuji ni tsii yɛ niji bibii najiaŋ.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the heat is too high or the soil gets too dry, causing the plant to drop its flowers to conserve energy and water.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛná latsaa babaoo loo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi tsɔ. Enɛ haa tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ kɛ nu he.

english: When is the best time for me to put fertilizer on my farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ nugbɔ be mli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist, but avoid doing it right before a heavy downpour so the rainwater carries nutrients to the roots instead of washing them off the farm.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo lɛ. Shi kaaŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ nɛ waa anɛ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni nugbɔ nu lɛ kɛ niyenii mli nibii aya shishifãi lɛ amli moŋ fe ni eeefɔ amɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why should I leave dry corn stalks on my field after harvesting instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving corn stalks on the field acts as natural mulch. It protects the soil from the hot sun, holds in moisture, and breaks down over time into rich nutrients that feed your next crop.
ga: Abele tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baatsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni efiteɔ ni etsɔɔ niyenii kpakpai babaoo yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Is it better to clear my land completely bare before planting or keep some plant cover on the ground?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaatsumɔ he lɛ dani adu loo aha tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ ahe?

english: Keeping some organic cover on the soil prevents wind and rain from washing away the topsoil, keeps the ground cool, and helps seeds germinate better than on bare, sun-baked soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ akwɛmɔ yeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni eyeɔ ebuaa dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni hulu eshã lɛ nɔ.

english: Planting too close forces the crops to fight for light, water, and soil nutrients. This results in thin, weak stalks and small corn cobs with low overall yield.
ga: Kɛ́ adu tso ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ kɛ ehe woɔ la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmãa tsei ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmãa bibii ni haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ baa shi lɛ baa.

english: How can I tell if my maize crops are suffering from lack of water or just daytime heat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji nu ni faaa yɛ mi-abele lɛ mli loo hulutsoo be mli latsaa kɛkɛ?

english: When maize lacks water, its leaves roll inward like narrow tubes and stay rolled up even in the cool morning. Heat-stressed plants usually unroll their leaves once the sun sets.
ga: Kɛji nu bɛ ŋmãa lɛ Ebaai lɛ shwieɔ mli tamɔ tsɔne bibioo ko. Ni efoɔ lolo yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli po. Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni dɔlɛ haa amɛnaa lɛ jieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli beni hulu lɛ nyɔ shi lɛ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my growing corn plants turning yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing on the lower leaves usually means the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil. Adding animal manure or a nitrogen fertilizer will help the plant regain its healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛhe wa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my corn stalks fall over easily when the wind blows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei komɛi shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ tswa lɛ?

english: Stalks fall over when the root system is weak, planted too shallowly, or damaged by pests. Piling extra soil around the base of the plant during weeding helps anchor the stalks firmly.
ga: Tso lɛ shishifã lɛ gbeeɔ shi kɛ́ shishifã lɛ bɛ hewalɛ. Adu yɛ he ko ni mli ekwɔɔɔ tsɔ loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite Shikpɔŋ kroko ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishi yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ mli lɛ baaye abua ni emɔ tso lɛ shi shiŋŋ yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young corn leaves and inside the main stalk?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Yɛ mi ŋmãa baai bibii lɛ amli kɛ tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ mli

english: Those holes are caused by stem borer caterpillars that hatch on leaves and eat their way into the stalk. Catching them early with appropriate controls prevents them from killing the main growing tip.
ga: Buji nɛɛ jɛɔ tso lɛ mli ŋmeii ni fɔ̃ɔ yɛ baa lɛ nɔ ni amɛyeɔ tso lɛ mli. Amɔmɔ amɛ mra Nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa tsiɔ amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbe ŋmeii titri ni yaa hiɛ lɛ.

english: Can I plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field alongside my maize?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu cowpeas loo peanuts yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ kɛ ŋmãa?

english: Yes, planting legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts with maize is beneficial because legumes draw nitrogen from the air into the soil, which naturally feeds the maize crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa woɔ mli lɛ he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmãa niyenii

english: How do I know that my corn is fully mature and ready to harvest from the field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-ŋmãa lɛ egbɔ ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Corn is fully mature when the outer husks turn dry and papery brown, and the kernels become hard enough that you cannot easily dent them with your fingernail.
ga: Abɛi eda kɛji kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ, egbi ni efee tamɔ wolo. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ atsɔ otsitsii lɛ anɔ atsɔ mlɛo.

english: How can I prevent my harvested corn from spoiling when transporting it over long distances to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ naa koni ekafite kɛji akɛ mikɛtee jara nɔ he ko ni jɛkɛ?

english: Ensure the corn is dried thoroughly before packing it into clean, breathable sacks. Keep the sacks off wet surfaces and protect them from rain during transit so mold does not grow.
ga: Kwɛmɔ akɛ ŋmãa lɛ egbi kwraa dani okɛwo kotokui ni he tse ni mumɔ baanyɛ ashɛ mli lɛ amli. Ha kotoku lɛ akashɛ hei ni efɔ lɛ ahe, ni obu he kɛjɛ nugbɔ be mli ni okɛyaa he kroko lɛ. Koni ŋmeii lɛ akakwɛ̃

english: Why are the crop seeds I planted in my farm failing to sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni midu yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout when they are buried too deep, when the soil lacks enough moisture, or if the seeds were old, damaged, or poorly stored before planting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ kwɛŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Aloo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ, amɛfite, loo akɛtooo jogbaŋŋ dani adu.

english: Why do crop seeds brought from foreign countries often fail to grow well on my field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei pii lɛ dumɔwui ni akɛjɛɔ maŋsɛɛ baa lɛ kwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ miŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Foreign seeds are developed for different weather, soil, and pest conditions; without the exact cooler climate or specialized care they require, they struggle in Ghanaian soil.
ga: Afee dumɔwui ni jɛ maŋsɛɛ kɛha kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi, shikpɔji kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai srɔtoi. Kɛji akɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ko ni mli ejɔ fe nɛkɛ loo kwɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko bɛ. Amɛbɔɔ mɔdɛŋ yɛ Ghana shikpɔŋ nɔ.

english: Is it better for me to buy certified seeds from accredited dealers or save seeds from my last harvest?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ kɛjɛ jarayelɔ ko ni awo he odase lɛ ŋɔɔ loo makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ minaagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato?

english: Certified seeds are tested for high germination rates and disease resistance, whereas saved seeds from previous harvests often produce weaker plants and lower yield.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ akwɛɔ koni ana kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ bɔ ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni yibiiwoo lɛ hu baa shi.

english: How can I tell if the plant seedlings I buy at the local market are healthy before I plant them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ dumɔwui ni miheɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli jarayelihe lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani miduɔ amɛ?

english: Healthy seedlings have dark green leaves, thick stems, and firm roots without brown spots, pest damage, or yellowing leaves.
ga: Dumɔwui ni yɔɔ hewalɛ yɛ baai eŋɔli diŋŋ, tsei ni mli wa, kɛ shishifãi ni wa ni he ko bɛ amɛhe. Akpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai ahiɛ loo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: How many weeks or months does it take for improved maize varieties to mature for harvest?
ga: Otsii loo nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ dani ŋmãa ni asaa lɛ feɔ klalo kɛha kpamɔɔ?

english: Most improved maize varieties in Ghana mature between 90 to 120 days (about 12 to 17 weeks), depending on rainfall, temperature, and variety.
ga: Abele henɔi ni atsake amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ Ghana lɛ ateŋ babaoo daa yɛ gbii 90 kɛyashi 120 teŋ (aaafee otsii 12 kɛyashi 17), ni enɛ damɔ nugbɔshiimɔ, hulutsoo kɛ henɔi lɛ anɔ.

english: How long will my cassava plants stay good in the soil before I must harvest them?
ga: Be enyiɛ mi-cassava tsei lɛ baahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani ehe baahia ni akpa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots generally reach peak yield between 9 and 12 months after planting, after which they can become woody and lose market value.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei shishifãi woɔ yibii ni fa fe fɛɛ yɛ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 sɛɛ beni adu lɛ sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ nɔ ni hiɔ shi daa ni amɛjarayeli jara lɛ sɛɛ foɔ.

english: How many months can I continuously pick fresh peppers from a single pepper plant?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ manyɛ makpa ŋmeii heei kɛjɛ ŋmeii tso kome mli be fɛɛ be?

english: With adequate water, good soil nutrients, and regular picking, a healthy pepper plant can continuously produce fruits for 3 to 6 months after flowering.
ga: Beni nu fa bɔ ni sa Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kpakpai kɛ halamɔ daa Pepper tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 6 yɛ fɔmɔ sɛɛ.

english: What will happen to my crop if I do not give it proper care during its early growth stage?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikwɛɛɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ yɛ amɛ shishijee be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: Crops that lack early weed control, water, and nutrients become stunted, take longer to mature, and produce very small harvests or fail completely.
ga: Tsei ni bɛ jwɛi akudɔmɔ mra, nu kɛ niyenii kpakpai lɛ baafee shoo. Eheɔ be babaoo dani ekwɛɔ ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ loo efiteɔ kwraa.

english: Will applying fertilizer make my crops mature much faster than their normal growing time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni mikɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha mitsei lɛ adara oya fe be ni akɛduɔ nii daa lɛ?

english: Fertilizers give plants the nutrients needed to grow strong and produce maximum yield on time, but they do not drastically shorten the crop's natural life cycle.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be naa. Shi ehaaa tso lɛ adebɔɔ mli wala be lɛ afee kuku kwraa.

english: Why do my vegetable crops drop their flowers before setting any fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani amɛwo yibii lɛ?

english: Flower dropping is usually caused by environmental stress such as extreme sun heat, lack of soil moisture, or a shortage of essential plant nutrients like phosphorus.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shihilɛ mli haomɔi tamɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ fe nine lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi ni laajeɔ baa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni bɛ

english: Young cocoa trees cannot survive direct, intense sunlight and harsh dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a canopy that protects the cocoa leaves and retains moisture in the soil.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa ŋwɛi ŋta ni buɔ kookoo baai lɛ ahe ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: Why do my pepper plants shed all their flowers before any fruits actually grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ fɛɛ miifɔ fɔfɔi dani aduawai lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they suffer heat stress or irregular watering. Providing consistent water at the root level and light shade during midday heat helps the plant retain its flowers to form fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe hulutsoo loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ he daa kɛ hulutsoo yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekwɛɔ efɔfɔi lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ koni ewo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with thick green leaves, but produce small, thin roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ, ni ehiɛ baai eŋɔlii ni mli tse, shi eshishifãi bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen, the cassava plant spends all its energy developing leaves and stems instead of feeding its tubers. Proper spacing and avoiding excessive leaf fertilizers help the plant direct energy into the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ lɛ Cassava tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ baai kɛ ŋmeii moŋ fe ni eeeha ŋmeii lɛ niyenii. He ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tsei lɛ ahe kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ yaa shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my yam vines need to climb tall wooden stakes instead of just trailing on the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need maximum sunlight exposure to produce enough food for the tuber growing beneath the ground. Lifting the leaves onto stakes also protects them from soil-borne fungal diseases that thrive on wet leaves.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Kɛ́ awó baai lɛ anɔ yɛ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ hu buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ baai ni efɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why are tiny holes showing up in the leaves of my young maize, with small worms hidden in the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bu bibii jeɔ kpo yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ? Kɛ ŋmeii bibii ni akɛtee tsɔne lɛ mli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm, which feeds on the growing center of young maize plants. Detecting them early and applying organic neem solutions or recommended treatments protects the growing point so the maize can mature.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni miida lɛ ateŋ lɛ. mra ni anaa Ni kɛ akɛ organic neem solution loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni abu he ni ŋmãa lɛ daa lɛ he koni ŋmãa lɛ anyɛ ada.

english: Maize heavily consumes specific soil nutrients like nitrogen. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts the soil and allows maize-specific pests and diseases to multiply in the ground.
ga: Abɛi kɛ niyenii pɔtɛɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, tamɔ nitrogen tsuɔ nii waa. Kɛ́ adu nii shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa sũ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi, ni ehaa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni yeɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ babaoo yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Legumes like groundnuts have special root nodules that absorb nitrogen from the air and fix it into the ground, naturally enriching the soil with nutrients for whatever crop is planted next.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni shwieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni niyenii yɔɔ mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha tsei fɛɛ ni abaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium reaching the fruit, often due to dry soil or irregular watering. Keeping the soil moisture steady allows the plant to pull calcium from the earth into the fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. ni calcium ni faaa lɛ kɛbaa. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi loo nu ni afɔɔɔ nɔ daa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛgbalaa calcium kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛyaa aduawai lɛ amli.

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy stems and fruit bunches. Propping up the main stem with a sturdy wooden fork supports the weight and prevents wind damage.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛye amɛbua tsei ni tsii kɛ aduawai akui. Kɛ́ akɛ tso ni mli wa fiɔ tso lɛ yitso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ tsiimɔ lɛ ni ehaaa kɔɔyɔɔ afite.

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest produce weaker crops than certified seeds bought from extension officers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ wo yibii ni bɛ hewalɛ fe dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli ni ahe kɛjɛ extension agent lɛ dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds lose their strength, purity, and disease resistance over generations. Certified seeds are specially selected and tested to ensure high germination, disease tolerance, and uniform harvest yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ahere amɛyiwala lɛ ahewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. hetsemɔ kɛ helai ahe shiwoo kɛha yinɔi babaoo Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ ni akaa amɛ akwɛɔ koni amɛkwɛ akɛ amɛshwereɔ jogbaŋŋ, helai nyɛɔ amɛshiɔ amɛhe, ni amɛkpaa nii daa.

english: Why do all my tomato plants produce and ripen their fruits at the exact same time instead of bit by bit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ woɔ yibii ni ekwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be kome mli moŋ fe fiofio lɛ?

english: Certain tomato varieties are 'determinate,' meaning they are programmed to grow to a fixed size, flower, and ripen all their fruit within a short window. If you want a continuous harvest over a longer period, you can plant 'indeterminate' varieties or stagger your planting dates every two weeks.
ga: Tomato henɔi komɛi yɛ "fixed," ni tsɔɔ akɛ ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ dalɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ, amɛwo fɔfɔi, ni amɛshwere amɛyibii lɛ fɛɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli. Kɛji oosumɔ ni okpa nii daa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli Obaanyɛ odu ‘indeterminate’ henɔi loo otsake dumɔ gbii lɛ daa otsii enyɔ.

english: Cassava roots are living plant tissues that rapidly react to oxygen once detached from the main stem. This natural chemical reaction, called post-harvest physiological deterioration, causes the root to discolor and rot within 48 to 72 hours unless preserved or processed quickly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ji tso fãji ni hiɛ ka ni tsuɔ nii oya kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa kɛji ajie kɛjɛ tso lɛ shishifã lɛ mli. Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ adebɔɔ mli tsofafeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni fiteɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ ahe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfiteɔ yɛ ŋmɛlɛtswai 48 kɛyashi 72 mli, ja akɛto loo atsu he nii oya.

english: Why does my harvested maize get warm and damp inside the sacks right after I bag it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli edɔɔ ni edɔ yɛ kotoku lɛ mli beni mikɛwo kotoku mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Freshly harvested maize grains are still 'breathing' and releasing internal moisture. If you bag the maize before drying it to a low moisture level (around 12 to 13%), this trapped moisture creates heat, which rapidly causes mold and spoilage.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa ehee lɛ ‘muɔ’ lolo ni ejieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kpo. Kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa ni baa shi (aaafee 12 kɛyashi 13%) wo ŋmãa kotoku mli dani okɛgbi lɛ, ŋmãa ni emɔ mli nɛɛ baaha hulutsoo aba. Enɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ oya.

english: If I leave my mature yams in the soil after the vines dry up, will they spoil?
ga: Kɛ́ mishi ŋmei ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ beni wain tso lɛ egbi sɛɛ lɛ, Ani ebaagbo?

english: Once the leaves dry up, the yam tuber stops growing and enters a resting state. It can safely remain underground for a short time in dry soil, but if heavy rains begin, the excess water will cause the tuber to sprout or rot.
ga: Kɛ́ baai lɛ egbi lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ kpaɔ dalɛ ni amɛboteɔ shihilɛ ni haa mɔ tsui nyɔɔ emli mli. Ebaanyɛ ehi shikpɔŋ shishi shweshweeshwe be kukuoo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ, shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, Nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baaha bulb lɛ akwɛ̃ loo egbo.

english: Can I plant my pepper seeds a few weeks apart to keep my farm from yielding all its peppers at once?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmeii dumɔwui yɛ otsii fioo komɛi ateŋ koni miŋmɔ lɛ akawo ŋmeii lɛ fɛɛ shikome?

english: Yes, staggered planting works very well. By planting small batches of seeds two to three weeks apart, your crops will mature at different times, allowing you to harvest peppers continuously over several months.
ga: Hɛɛ, dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ waa. dumɔwui bibii ni aduɔ Otsii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee Oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ bei srɔtoi amli. Enɛ haa onáa ŋmeii ni yaa nɔ nyɔji babaoo.

english: Why are my plantain suckers bearing fruit at different times even though I planted them on the same day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ woɔ yibii yɛ bei srɔtoi amli eyɛ mli akɛ midu amɛ yɛ gbi kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Plantain suckers naturally vary in energy reserves, root strength, and size when planted. Because each sucker establishes itself at a slightly different pace, their flowering and fruiting cycles naturally spread out over time.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli plantain tsei lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ amɛ hewalɛ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ mli. shishifãi ahewalɛ kɛ amɛdalɛ kɛji adu Enɛ ji akɛ, sucker henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ srɔto fioo. No hewɔ lɛ, fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo he gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa yɛ be kɛ bei amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when exposed to extreme heat, drought, or poor soil nutrients. Dropping flowers is the plant's natural defense mechanism to conserve water and energy until growing conditions improve.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛji amɛyashɛ hulutsoo be ni naa wa, hɔmɔ, loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii ni ehiii lɛ he. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni etsɔɔ nɔ ekɛ nu kɛ hewalɛ toɔ he kɛyashi be mli ni shihilɛi ni haa edaa lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes my green cocoa pods to turn black and dry up before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ dani amɛdaraa?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid conditions. The fungus attacks green pods, causing them to rot, turn black, and shrivel before the beans inside can mature.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ hei ni mli ewo duŋ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ. Fuji lɛ tutuaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ, ni ehaa amɛgboiɔ, ni ehaa amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ. ni egboɔ dani dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my green plantains ripen and soften so quickly when stored in a hot room together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains eŋɔli lɛ shwereɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo oya kɛji akɛ akɛto he kome yɛ tsu ko ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: As plantains ripen, they release a natural ripening gas called ethylene. When stored together in a closed or warm space, this trapped gas accelerates the ripening process for all the surrounding plantains at once.
ga: Kɛ́ plantain lɛ shwere lɛ, ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli kɔɔyɔɔ ko ni haa eshwereɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ ethylene lɛ kpo. Kɛ akɛto he kome yɛ he ko ni afo he loo he ko ni mli edɔ Gas ni amɔmɔ lɛ nɛɛ haa gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahaa dumɔwui ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ daa lɛ yaa oya. Ehooɔ nii oya yɛ be kome mli.

english: Why do my sweet potato tubers split open in the ground right before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ miigba yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani kpamɔɔ be lɛ?

english: Sweet potatoes crack when heavy rain follows a long dry period. The dry plant suddenly drinks up large amounts of water, causing the inside of the tuber to expand faster than its outer skin can stretch.
ga: Sweet potatoes tswaa kɛji nugbɔ ni naa wa nyiɛ sɛɛ be kakadaŋŋ. Trukaa lɛ, tso ni egbi lɛ nu nu babaoo. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ mligbɛ lɛ mli lɛɛɔ oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Why are my maize leaves rolling up and turning yellow when the sun gets very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ shɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When maize experiences intense heat and lack of rain, its leaves roll up to reduce surface area and trap moisture. Yellowing occurs because dry conditions prevent the plant from absorbing key nutrients like nitrogen from the soil.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli edɔ waa ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛba ŋmãa lɛ nɔ ni ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Yellow baa ejaakɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ tsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkaná niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ nitrogen kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my seeds when the rainy season start dates keep changing?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui? Kɛjɛ gbi ni nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsakeɔ be fɛɛ be.

english: Instead of planting after the very first light shower, wait until the soil is thoroughly soaked by two or three consecutive heavy rains. Planting too early in dry soil causes seeds to scorch or germinate and then die.
ga: Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu nii yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ Mɛɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ. Kɛ́ adu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ mra tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha dumɔwui lɛ ashã loo amɛgboi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their blossoms without producing any peppers during the dry spell?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni ekɛ pepper baaa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers as a survival mechanism during high heat or water stress. The plant drops flowers to save its water and energy until weather conditions become favorable again.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛhiɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be ni naa wa loo nu he haomɔ baa lɛ. Tsei baashɛ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ashwie shi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛyashi be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does cassava grow very well on my upland farm but rots in the soil on my swampy plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ mi-ŋwɛi ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi eefite yɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ mi peatland lɛ nɔ lɛ mli?

english: Cassava roots require loose, well-drained soil to breathe and grow. Swampy or low-lying land retains too much water, which starves the tuber roots of oxygen and leads to fungal rot.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse, ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he hiaa cassava shishifãi koni amɛmu ni amɛdara. Shikpɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ hiɛɔ nu babaoo tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ náaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela aba.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller yam tubers when I plant yam on the exact same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ sweet potato ŋmeii bibii kwraa beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Yams feed heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting them in the same spot repeatedly exhausts those specific nutrients and allows root-damaging pests to accumulate in the soil.
ga: Sweet potatoes yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ shii abɔ lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii pɔtɛɛi lɛ baaje mli, ni ebaaha kooloi ni fiteɔ shishifãi lɛ abua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I leave dried weeds on top of the soil after clearing my land instead of burning them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi jwɛi ni egbi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni mijie shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni mashã lɛ?

english: Leaving cleared weeds as a mulch layer protects the soil from hot sunlight, keeps moisture in the ground for longer, prevents rain from washing away topsoil, and slowly rots into natural fertilizer.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni he tse akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Kwɛmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ Etsiɔ nugbɔ naa koni ekafɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fã ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ ni efiteɔ fiofio ni etsɔɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves and fragile root systems that easily scorch in direct sun. They need tall shade trees to block intense sunlight and create a humid microclimate while they establish.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii kɛ shishifãi ni waaa ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Amɛmiitao tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa ni amɛfee kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ bibioo ko ni mli edɔ beni amɛfeɔ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why are my plantain plants producing very small bunches when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ woɔ ŋmeii bibii waa kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: Planting plantains too closely forces them to compete for sunlight, underground water, and plant food. Spacing them properly allows each plant enough root space and light to build strong stems and large bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ kɛbɛŋkɛɔ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛye akaŋ yɛ hulu la, shikpɔŋ shishi nu, kɛ tsei aniyenii he. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa shishifãi kɛ la ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekɛfee shishifãi ni wa kɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom during hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom end rot. It happens when irregular watering and high heat prevent the plant from absorbing calcium from the soil, causing the bottom of the fruit tissue to break down.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛ́ nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei lɛ amli be fɛɛ be kɛ la ni mli edɔ waa lɛ tsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa koni amɛkaŋɔ calcium ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa fãji ni yɔɔ aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why are the leaves of my cassava plants curling up with tiny white flies under them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni ŋmeii bibii yɛŋ yɔɔ shishi lɛ?

english: The whiteflies suck sap from the underside of the leaves and spread plant viruses. As the plant loses vital juices and contracts the virus, its leaves curl up and stunt overall crop growth.
ga: Whiteflies nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni amɛgbɛɔ tsei ahe helai amɛshwãa. Kɛ tso ko mli nu ni he hiaa lɛ fite ni hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ mɔ lɛ Ebaai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsĩɔ tso lɛ fɛɛ dalɛ naa.

english: Cassava naturally drops its leaves during dry spells to conserve water and survive. Once the rains return, the plant will sprout fresh green leaves and continue growing.
ga: Cassava shwieɔ baai lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli koni ekɛbu nu he ni ehi shi. Kɛ nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba lɛ Tso lɛ baakwɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaaya nɔ eda.

english: Why do my pepper plant flowers drop off before turning into peppers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ pepper lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when temperatures get too high or when there is not enough moisture in the soil, as the plant tries to save energy to keep itself alive.
ga: Pepper tsei jieɔ fɔfɔi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ mli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, pepper tso lɛ miitao ni ekɛ hewalɛ ato koni ehi shi.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin when planted under big trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo waa kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ashishi lɛ?

english: Crops need direct sunlight to produce food. When shaded by big trees, they stretch upward searching for light, which makes them grow tall, weak, and thin.
ga: Tsei taoɔ hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛna niyenii. Kɛ́ eyɛ tso agbo ko shishi lɛ, ebaagbala ehe koni eyatao la. Enɛ haa amɛkwɔɔ, amɛgbɔjɔ, ni amɛhe waaa.

english: Why should I plant my yams on soil mounds instead of flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ gɔŋ nɔ moŋ fe shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the topsoil so yam tubers can expand easily without struggling against hard dirt. It also prevents heavy rains from drowning the roots.
ga: Mounding haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shwieɔ shi bɔni afee ni sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ anyɛ agbɛ ashwã mlɛo ni amɛkɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa akawuu. Ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hu shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees provide broad leaves that shade the young cocoa plants and keep the soil cool and moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni haa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni edɔɔɔ.

english: Why did many of my maize seeds fail to sprout after I planted them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele dumɔwui lɛ babaoo ekwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize seeds may fail to sprout if planted too deep in the soil, if the ground was too dry, or if birds and ants ate the seeds before they could germinate.
ga: Abele dumɔwui nyɛŋ akwɛ̃ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ Aloo kɛji okpoi kɛ ŋmeii ye dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: These are Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that feeds on tender growing leaves inside the plant stem, which can be treated with recommended organic or chemical sprays.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni yeɔ baai ni mli tse ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tsei akutsei amli lɛ. Abaanyɛ akɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nibii anɔ loo tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ atsu enɛ he nii.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wilt and die while their leaves are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa ni amɛgboiɔ be mli ni baai lɛ ji eŋɔli lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by bacterial wilt, a soil-borne disease that blocks the movement of water inside the stem, causing the plant to dry up rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, helai ni baa mɔ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji hela ko ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli ni tsiɔ nu ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Ha tso lɛ agbi oya

english: When is the right time for me to put fertilizer on my maize field?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mi ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: The best time for the first fertilizer application is about two weeks after sprouting when root systems start forming, followed by a second application when the plants reach knee height.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii klɛŋklɛŋ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ ji aaafee otsii enyɔ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ sɛɛ, be mli ni shishifãi lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ. Nyiɛmɔ sɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ji enyɔ lɛ beni tsei lɛ shɛɔ amɛnaji ahe lɛ.

english: Why do my stored maize grains end up full of holes and white powder after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikɛto lɛ eyi kɛ bu kɛ powda yɛŋ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils attack stored maize if the grains were not dried thoroughly before storage or if the storage bags were not properly sealed against insect pests.
ga: Weevils baatutua ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛji ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. aloo kɛji akɛ atsĩko kotoku ni akɛtoɔ nii lɛ naa jogbaŋŋ koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akafee nɔ ko.

english: Swollen stems and yellowing leaves are key signs of cocoa swollen shoot disease, a harmful viral infection that stops nutrients from moving freely through the tree.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni efuu kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadii ni he hiaa ni tsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli efuu hela. Enɛ ji hela ko ni yɔɔ oshara ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli ni tsiɔ niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa koni ekatsɔ tso lɛ mli oya.

english: Why do my young cocoa pods dry up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiitsɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Pods drying up early can be caused by fungal infections like black pod disease or severe stress from lack of water and tree sickness.
ga: Nɔ ni baanyɛ aha ŋmeii lɛ agbi oya ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko, tamɔ black pod hela, loo haomɔ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ nu ni faaa kɛ tso hela mli baa.

english: Why do extension officers ask me to cut down my sick cocoa trees instead of giving me chemical medicine to spray on them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ biɔ ni afolɔ kookoo tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛkɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ baawo amɛmli lɛ?

english: Certain plant viruses live deep inside the sap of the tree where chemical sprays cannot reach, so cutting down infected trees is the only proven way to keep the disease from spreading to healthy crops.
ga: Tsei amli helai komɛi hiɔ tsei amli nu lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Biɛ ji he ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ, no hewɔ lɛ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ ni aaafo lɛ ji gbɛ pɛ ni ana he odaseyeli ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsĩɔ hela lɛ naa koni ekagbɛ eshwa ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli.

english: What am I supposed to do with the branches and trunks of cocoa trees after cutting them down because of disease?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ afee kookoo tso niji kɛ eshishifãi beni afo lɛ yɛ hela hewɔ?

english: Cut branches should be gathered and left to dry away from healthy trees or safely burned so that pests hiding in the wood do not crawl onto healthy plants.
ga: Esa akɛ abua tsei niji ni afo lɛ anaa ni ashi amɛ ni amɛgbi shweshweeshwe yɛ he ko ni kɛ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ loo ashã koni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ amli lɛ akatsɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can I immediately plant new cocoa seedlings in the exact spot where I cut down diseased trees?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu kookoo tso hee yɛ he ni afo tso ni hela emɔ lɛ lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: You can replant, but you must first clear all old infected roots and wait for the area to be completely free of disease-carrying insects before putting new seedlings in the ground.
ga: Obaanyɛ odu ekoŋŋ. Shi klɛŋklɛŋ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ojie shishifãi momo ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Ni mɛ ni ŋmeii ni kɛ helai baa lɛ akafee nɔ ko kwraa yɛ jɛmɛ dani okɛ dumɔwui heei awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Does the disease that killed my cocoa trees stay inside the soil after the trees are removed?
ga: Ani hela ni gbe mi-cacao tsei lɛ baakã he ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni ajie cacao tsei lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Most cocoa viral diseases live in the living plant tissues and insects rather than the dirt itself, but leaving infected root pieces in the soil can keep pests alive.
ga: Cocoa virus helai babaoo hiɔ tsei ni hiɛ ka kɛ kooloi amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ najiaŋ. Shi kɛ́ ashi shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahi shi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings burn easily under strong sunlight; plantains grow fast and provide big leaves that shield young trees from heat while keeping moisture in the soil.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni ewoɔ baai agboi ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ he, yɛ be mli ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli nu lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: How do I know if my newly planted cocoa trees are getting too much sunlight?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cocoa tso ni midu ehee lɛ miiná hulu la babaoo tsɔ?

english: If young cocoa leaves look scorched, pale, or brownish around the edges, the trees are getting too much direct sun and need extra shade crops around them.
ga: Kɛji akɛ kookoo baai lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, amɛhe edɔ, amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, loo amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ amɛnaa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiná hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo tsɔ. ni ehe miihia ni afee shade tsei krokomɛi ni ebɔle ehe lɛ

english: How do small insects spread sickness from one cocoa tree to another?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi bibii gbɛɔ helai kɛjɛɔ cacao tso kome nɔ kɛyaa ekroko nɔ?

english: Insects like mealybugs feed on the sap of diseased trees, picking up the virus and transferring it into healthy trees when they move across branches to feed again.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ mealybugs yeɔ tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ amli nu lɛ. Kɛkɛ lɛ, amɛheɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ ni amɛkɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli beni amɛtsɔɔ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ koni amɛyatao niyenii ekoŋŋ lɛ.

english: Walking through your farm at least once a week allows you to spot early symptoms like yellow leaves or swelling stems before the sickness spreads across your whole farm.
ga: Kɛ hoo lɛ, kɛ́ onyiɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli shikome yɛ otsi mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua bo ni ona mra be mli okadii tamɔ baai ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ loo tsei ni efuu. Dani hela lɛ baagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings wither and die when I plant them on open, cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct, intense sunlight. Planting crops like plantain or cassava alongside them provides living shade and holds moisture in the ground, protecting the young trees until they grow strong enough to endure the heat.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ adu tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná hulutsoo ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi. Buu tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛdamɔ hulutsoo lɛ naa.

english: Does it matter which direction I point the cassava stem stick when I push it into the soil?
ga: Kɛ́ ootsi ŋmei tso lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, mɛɛ gbɛ ebaatsɔɔ?

english: Yes, the small growth buds or 'eyes' on the stem must point upward toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down forces the new shoots to waste energy bending upward, resulting in weak growth and smaller tubers.
ga: Hɛɛ, esa akɛ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘hiŋmɛii’ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ atsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Cassava ni akwɛɔ nɔ kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ baaha ŋmeii heei lɛ ahewalɛ ni amɛkɛaabɔle amɛhe kɛya ŋwɛi lɛ afite. Enɛ haa amɛdalɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii.

english: Yam vines need sunlight to create energy for growing tubers underground. Lifting the leaves off the ground using stakes allows them to catch maximum sunlight while keeping the leaves away from damp soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia hulu la koni amɛná hewalɛ amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo baai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa baa lɛ naa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni eeenyɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo fɔ he ni helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya lɛ he.

english: Which plantain suckers should I dig up from my old farm to start a new field?
ga: Mɛɛ plantain tsei esa akɛ mafo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli koni mikɛje ŋmɔ hee shishi?

english: Choose 'sword suckers'—young shoots that have thin, narrow leaves shaped like blades rather than wide leaves. These suckers have stronger root bases and grow into healthier, heavy-fruiting plantain trees much faster.
ga: Halamɔ ‘sword suckers’, ni ji tsei bibii ni baai bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ najiaŋ. Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ yɛ shishitoo ni mli wa ni amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo oya.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the plant is hungry for nitrogen, which acts as fuel for green leaf growth. Applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure early in the season will restore the green color and protect your yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ he miihia nitrogen, ni tsuɔ nii akɛ fuel kɛha baa eŋɔli lɛ dalɛ. Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo mli yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize in the same field every season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop year after year drains specific nutrients from the soil and lets pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like cowpeas or groundnuts puts natural nitrogen back into the earth and restores soil fertility.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ jieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ feɔ ekome. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii ekoŋŋ.

english: Should I apply my crop fertilizer when the soil is dry or after a good rain?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii atsu nii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ waa sɛɛ?

english: Always apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain. Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the crop roots can drink it in; placing dry fertilizer on dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money.
ga: Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anu. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã shishifãi lɛ ni efite shika.

english: Why are my tomato plants dropping their flowers before any small tomatoes can form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani tomato bibii baanyɛ afee lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant gets stressed by irregular watering or extreme daytime heat. Mulching the soil around the plants with dry grass keeps the roots cool and moist, helping the blossoms turn into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ tso lɛ miihao kɛjɛ nu ni akɛhaa lɛ be fɛɛ be loo hulutsoo ni naa wa waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ mli. Mulching ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ Tsei lɛ ahe lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni amɛshishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my hot pepper plants curling up into small, tight cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi chili baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii ni mli wa lɛ?

english: Curled leaves on pepper plants are caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like thrips or mites hiding under the leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or soapsuds cleans off the insects so the leaves can expand and feed the plant again.
ga: Kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites ni kɛ amɛhe ewo baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. Ni akɛ neem fɔ loo samla baashwie nɔ mra Ebaaye ebua ni etsumɔ ŋmeii lɛ. Bɔni afee ni baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛha tso lɛ niyenii ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are there ragged holes and dark dirt inside the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn lɛ teŋgbɛ baai lɛ amli eyi kɛ muji ni mli edɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center funnel of the maize plant. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem powder directly into the center funnel early in the morning kills the pest before it destroys the growing point.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem powder ni akɛwoɔ ŋshɔ lɛ teŋgbɛ gbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ wo mli leebi maŋkpa lɛ, ebaagbe kooloi lɛ dani efite he ni amɛdaraa yɛ lɛ.

english: Why should I cover my young cocoa seedlings with palm fronds after planting them in the open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmei baai aha kookoo tsei bibii ahe beni midu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that scorch easily under harsh, direct sunlight. Covering them with palm fronds provides temporary shade, keeps the soil cool, and retains moisture so the plants can establish strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shãa oya. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei ahe baai ha nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ená hulutsoo be kukuoo ko. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei lɛ anyɛ afee shishifãi ni wa

english: Why do some of my young seedlings wither and die shortly after I move them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi gboɔ ni amɛgboiɔ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ amɛ wo ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Moving seedlings from a nursery to an open field creates 'transplant shock' due to sudden exposure to heat and full sun. Providing shade cover and plenty of water during the first few weeks helps them survive this transition.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa ŋmɔ ni mli tse lɛ mli lɛ baaha ‘Graft shock’ aba yɛ hulutsoo kɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni baa trukaa lɛ hewɔ Ni akɛ hulutsoo kɛ nu babaoo haa amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii fioo lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ tsakemɔ nɛɛ mli.

english: How does intense heat from the hot sun affect the growth of my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa ni jɛɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli baa lɛ saa midumɔwui lɛ adalɛ he?

english: Extreme heat causes young plants to lose water faster through their leaves than their small root systems can absorb from the soil, leading to wilting, stunted growth, or death.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa haa tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe amɛshishifãi bibii lɛ. Abaanyɛ ajie enibii lɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmɔtɔ Ebaanyɛ eda ni egbɔjɔ loo egbo.

english: Will buying improved crop seeds guarantee a big harvest even if I don't give the farm much extra daily care?
ga: Ani dumɔwui ni asaa amɛhe lɛ ahemɔ baaha maná ŋmaa babaoo kɛji mikwɛɛɛ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ daa gbi po?

english: Good seed varieties give your crops high yield potential, but proper management—like weeding, shade control, and regular monitoring—is what actually determines whether those plants produce well.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi kpakpai baaha otsei lɛ aná yibii babaoo. Shi nɔkwɛmɔ ni sa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Shade nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ daa kwɛmɔ No ji nɔ ni tsɔɔ kɛji nakai tsei lɛ woɔ yibii kpakpai loo amɛwooo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why does my neighbor get a better cocoa harvest than I do when we both planted the exact same crop variety?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ naa kookoo yibiiwoo ni hi fe mi yɛ be mli ni wɔyi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ wɔduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ?

english: Differences in harvest usually come down to management practices, or 'attention activities,' such as regular clearing, proper shading, timely pruning, and protecting young plants from soil dryness.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, srɔtofeemɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli lɛ damɔ bɔ ni akwɛɔ nɔ ahaa loo ‘Atention activities’ tamɔ hulutsoo ni sa ni ajieɔ daa He ni afoɔ yɛ be ni sa mli kɛ tsei bibii ahebuu kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: How often should I inspect my crop field to make sure my plants are growing well?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ nibii ni midu lɛ amli koni mana nɔmimaa akɛ mitsei lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ?

english: Checking your farm regularly—at least once or twice a week—allows you to catch problems like pest damage, dried-out soil, or overcrowding early before they damage your harvest.
