ga: Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa Kɛ hoo lɛ shikome loo shii enyɔ yɛ otsi mli. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oyɔseɔ naagbai tamɔ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ oya dani amɛfiteɔ okpamɔ lɛ.

english: What happens to my soil if I clear my farmland by burning all the bush and plant waste?
ga: Mɛni baaba mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji mijie miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛtsɔ jwɛi kɛ tsei ahe sũi fɛɛ ni mashã lɛ nɔ?

english: Burning land clears it quickly, but the high heat destroys organic matter, dries out topsoil, and kills useful soil organisms that nourish your crops.
ga: Abaajie hei ni shã lɛ oya. Shi la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ baafite nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi. ni efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii.

english: Why is it helpful to leave dry leaves and plant material covering the ground around my plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ mashi baai ni egbi kɛ nibii ni akɛduɔ nii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni bɔle mitsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Leaving plant material on the soil acts like a blanket, keeping the soil moist, stopping weed growth, protecting roots from excessive heat, and slowly turning into natural soil nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi tsei ahe nibii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Ekpaa jwɛi lɛ adalɛ Ebuɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine he ni fiofio lɛ ebafeɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ.

english: Why do weeds appear so quickly on my field right after I clear the land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi jeɔ kpo oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli beni mijie he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Weed seeds lie sleeping in the soil. When you clear the land, sunlight and rain reach these seeds directly, causing them to germinate and grow rapidly.
ga: Jwɛi dumɔwui ni kã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Kɛji otsi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Hulu la kɛ nugbɔ shɛɔ dumɔwui nɛɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛdaraa oya.

english: My cocoa trees are old and stopped producing well; do I have to destroy the whole farm to fix the problem?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ egbɔ ni amɛkpa yibiiwoo jogbaŋŋ. Ani esa akɛ makpãtã ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ koni manyɛ matsu naagba lɛ he nii?

english: Not necessarily. Old farms can often be rehabilitated by pruning away dead branches, replacing dying trees with fresh shaded seedlings, and improving soil care rather than clearing the entire land.
ga: Ehe ehiaaa. Bei pii lɛ, abaanyɛ atswa ŋmɔji momoi lɛ ama shi ekoŋŋ kɛtsɔ tsei niji ni egboi lɛ ni abaafolɔ ashwie shi lɛ nɔ. Kɛ dumɔwui heei ni haa hulutsoo ato tsei ni mii gboi lɛ najiaŋ. ni aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔkwɛmɔ aya hiɛ moŋ fe ni abaajie hei muu fɛɛ.

english: Why should I leave measured space between my maize plants instead of planting them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ abɔle amɛhe moŋ fe ni madu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to thin stalks and small yields. Proper spacing gives each plant room to feed and produce full ears.
ga: Kɛ adu he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ haa tso lɛ tsu fɛɛ tsu yeɔ nii ni efeɔ toi ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do my hands and chest burn after spraying my farm, and is it safe to keep chemical bottles in my home?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miniji kɛ mitsitsi shãa beni mikɛ tsofa shwie ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Ni ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ akɛ tsofa-kɛ-ŋma tsɛnsii baawo shia?

english: Agricultural chemicals are strong poisons that easily pass through skin and lungs, causing severe illness. You must wear protective clothing, wash immediately after spraying, and store all farm chemicals in a locked shed far away from children, food, and drinking water.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ okwaayeli mli lɛ yɛ awui waa ni etsɔɔ hewolo kɛ fɛ̃i mli oya, ni ekɛ helai ni naa wa baa. Esa akɛ owo atadei ni buɔ mɔ he. Kɛji okɛ tsofa lɛ eshwie nɔ lɛ, afɔ he amrɔ nɔŋŋ. ni okɛ tsofai fɛɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ato tsũ ko ni aŋã mli ni gbekɛbii, niyenii, kɛ nu ni anuɔ lɛ bɛ he ko.

english: Yellowing leaves from the bottom up usually mean your soil is short on nitrogen. Adding nitrogen fertilizer like urea or well-rotted animal manure will help the maize regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ shishi kɛyaa ŋwɛi lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni etsɔ hewalɛ.

english: Weeds are wild native plants with strong roots adapted to take immediate advantage of rainwater and soil nutrients. Clearing weeds early within the first three to four weeks stops them from taking light and food away from your young seedlings.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni shishifãi ni mli wa yɔɔ mli ni atsake amɛ koni amɛkɛ nugbɔ nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli mra Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi ejwɛ lɛ mli lɛ ehaaa amɛjie la kɛ niyenii kɛjɛ otsei bibii lɛ amli.

english: What is eating small holes into the center leaves of my maize overnight?
ga: Mɛni ji bu bibioo lɛ yeli? Yɛ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ nyɔɔŋ kome?

english: This damage is usually caused by pests like the Fall Armyworm, which hide inside the plant funnel during the day. Inspecting your farm early and applying recommended control measures early prevents them from destroying the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ Fall Armyworm, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei amli ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kwɛmɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli mra ni okɛ gbɛjianɔtoi ni atsɔɔ akɛ akudɔɔ lɛ atsu nii mra. Ebaatsi ŋmɔji anaa koni amɛkafite ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava roots turn soft and rot in the ground when the heavy rains start?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water in waterlogged soil cuts off air to the cassava roots, allowing fungal rots to grow. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges and harvesting on time prevents the roots from soaking in water.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ mli lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. ni eha ŋmeii ni egbo lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ, ni akpa yɛ be naa lɛ, ebaatsi shishifãi lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsɔ ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Curled, wrinkled leaves on pepper plants are usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with proper sprays keeps the leaves flat and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo whiteflies ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. Ekɛ tso mli nu lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ eshwaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛji akɛ afɔse tsofa lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe awa.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when weather temperatures are too high or when water supply in the soil is uneven. Regular morning watering and proper plant feeding keep flowers healthy so they can turn into fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ ejaaa. Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa leebi kɛ niyenii ni sa ni akɛhaa amɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni fɔfɔi lɛ anáa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa koni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting and shrinking after sitting in my room for a few weeks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikpa lɛ bɔi shweremɔ ni egbɔjɔ beni mita mitsu lɛ mli otsii fioo komɛi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yams start to sprout when kept in warm, poorly ventilated spaces, which consumes the moisture and energy inside the tuber and makes it shrink. Storing them in a cool, shady, and well-ventilated traditional yam barn stops premature sprouting.
ga: Sweet potatoes jeɔ shishi ekwɛ̃ɔ kɛji akɛ akɛto he ko ni mli edɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ yeɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ ni ehaa egbɔjɔɔ. Kɛ amɛ ato he ko ni mli ejɔ, ni hulutsoo yɔɔ, ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa hu boteɔ mli jogbaŋŋ yɛ blema sweet potato ŋmɔ mli. Ekpaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwereɔ oya lɛ.

english: When lower maize leaves turn yellow in a V-shape starting from the tip, it usually means the soil is running low on nitrogen. The plant naturally steals nitrogen from its older, lower leaves to feed the young growth and growing ears at the top.
ga: Beni ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ V su mli ni ejeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ eshishigbɛ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei juɔ adebɔɔ mli nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai ni edara kɛ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha tsei bibii kɛ toi ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do so many of the small young pods on my cocoa tree turn black and shrivel up even when there is no disease?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii bibii lɛ No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigboi eyɛ mli akɛ hela ko bɛ mli moŋ?

english: This natural process is called cherelle wilt. The cocoa tree intentionally thins out its own crop, dropping extra young pods it cannot feed so that it has enough nutrients to grow the remaining pods into healthy, full-sized cocoa.
ga: Atsɛɔ adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ nɛɛ akɛ cherry wilt. Kakao tsei lɛ tsɔ hiɛ amɛha amɛŋmɔshinii lɛ shwie shi. Afeɔ enɛ kɛtsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni fa fe nine ni nyɛŋ aha niyenii lɛ ni ashɛrɛɔ ashwieɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ afee kookoo ni da ni ehi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when we receive heavy rains during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in waterlogged soil for too long without draining, it suffocates the roots, allowing ground fungus and bacteria to break them down and rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni ejɛɛɛ mli. Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fiteɔ ni amɛfiteɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants shed all their flowers without producing any tomatoes during very hot weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: When day or night temperatures get too hot, tomato pollen becomes dry or sterile, preventing insects or wind from pollinating the flowers. Unpollinated flowers cannot form fruit, so the plant drops them to save energy.
ga: Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo be mli loo gbɛkɛ mli latsaa lɛ mli wa tsɔ Tomato pollen lɛ mli egbi loo ebɛ fɔmɔ nii. Etsiɔ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ naa koni ekafee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ. Fɔfɔi ni pollin bɛ mli lɛ nyɛŋ awo yibii. No hewɔ lɛ, tsei shwieɔ shi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: How does putting wooden stakes under my yam vines help the tubers grow bigger under the ground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tso ni midu yɛ mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ shishi lɛ ye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ dara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that convert sunlight into energy to build tubers. Staking lifts the vines so the leaves catch maximum sunlight and stays dry, preventing leaf rot caused by touching damp soil.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulu la, ni etsakeɔ hulu la lɛ ewoɔ hewalɛ mli koni ekɛfee tubers lɛ. Staking woɔ wain tso lɛ nɔ koni eha tso lɛ baai lɛ ashɛ hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ he ni eha egbi. Enɛ ji koni baai lɛ akafite ni shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni akɛkpeɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: What is causing the leaves of my pepper plants to curl up tightly and stop growing?
ga: Mɛni haa pepper tso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛkpaa dalɛ?

english: Leaf curl in peppers is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like thrips, aphids, or mites feeding on the undersides of young leaves. As they suck plant juices, they inject saliva that damages leaf tissue and twists the leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips, aphids, loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ chili baa lɛ baa. be mli ni amɛmuɔ tso mli nu lɛ Amɛwoɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli koni amɛfite baai lɛ amli fãji ni amɛtsiɔ baai lɛ.

english: Why do I harvest smaller plantain bunches when I leave all the young suckers growing around the main stool?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa plantains bibii lɛ? Kɛjɛ be mli ni mishi ŋmeii bibii komɛi yɛ sɛi wulu lɛ he lɛ.

english: The main plantain stem and all its suckers share the same root system. Leaving too many suckers forces them to compete for water and soil nutrients, leaving less energy for the mother plant to produce a big bunch.
ga: Plantain tso lɛ shishifã titri lɛ kɛ eshishifãi lɛ fɛɛ yɛ shishifã kome. Kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ shwere fe nine lɛ, ehaa amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso nyɛ lɛ náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: Why does planting cowpeas or groundnuts in my field make the soil richer for the next season's crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts team up with helpful bacteria in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and deposit it into the soil. When the roots decay, this nitrogen acts as a free natural fertilizer.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts hiɛ helatsɛmɛi ahe nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni shishifãi lɛ miifite Nitrogen nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko.

english: Why do my garden egg plants wilt in the hot afternoon sun but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eggplant ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi etamɔ nɔ ni ehe ejɔ lɛ leebi lɛ?

english: During hot afternoons, leaves lose water into the hot air faster than the roots can pull it from the soil, causing leaves to go limp. Overnight, water loss stops, allowing the roots to drink up water and restore the plant.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. ni haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi Gbi gbɛkɛ ko lɛ, nu ni hoɔ lɛ kpaɔ. Ha shishifãi lɛ anu nu lɛ ni amɛha tso lɛ aná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why are some of my pineapple plants flowering while others planted on the same day are still just leaves?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-anane tsei lɛ ekomɛi miifɔ fɔfɔi shi ekrokomɛi ni adu yɛ gbi kome lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ, baai pɛ yɔɔ amɛmli lolo lɛ?

english: Pineapples only flower when the plant reaches a specific maturity weight and experiences stress like a cold night or dry spell. Plants in slightly poorer soil or shaded spots grow slower and take longer to reach flowering size.
ga: Pineapple baafɔ̃ kɛji tso lɛ eda jogbaŋŋ ni ehao, tamɔ gbɛkɛ ni fɛ̃i yɔɔ mli loo be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ pɛ. Tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii fioo loo hei ni hulutsoo yɔɔ lɛ baakwɛ̃ blɛoo ni amɛhe be babaoo dani amɛwo fɔfɔi.

english: Young cocoa plants cannot handle direct sunlight because their leaves are very tender. They need shade crops like plantain or cassava grown beside them to act as living umbrellas until the cocoa grows strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ ejaakɛ amɛbaai lɛ darako kwraa. Amɛmiisumɔ ni adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo cassava yɛ amɛmasɛi. Koni etsu nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo lɛ baatsɔ hewalɛ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do I see tiny holes in my young maize leaves and caterpillars hiding inside the stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minaa buji bibii lɛ? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ amli

english: That damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm. The parent moths lay eggs on the leaves, and when the caterpillars hatch, they crawl into the central leaves (the whorl) to feed on the tender growing parts of the maize.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ fitemɔ baa ji Fall Armyworm, ni ji ŋmei ko ni woɔ ŋmeii yɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Ni kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ fɔ Ekɛ ehe shwieɔ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ (whorl) koni eye ŋmei lɛ fãi ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant maize on the exact same spot of land three seasons in a row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ bei etɛ ni nyiɛɔ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Maize feeds heavily on specific soil nutrients. Planting it repeatedly in the same spot exhausts those nutrients and allows maize-specific pests to build up in the soil, leading to poor yields over time.
ga: Abɛi yeɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛi babaoo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, ni kɛ́ adu lɛ shii abɔ yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha nakai niyenii lɛ afite. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa pɔtɛɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Enɛ haa ŋmãa lɛ baaa shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When water sits in the field for long periods without draining, it suffocates the tubers and allows rot-causing fungi to multiply rapidly.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ ko mli be kakadaŋŋ ni ajieee kɛjɛɛɛ mli. Nu lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ feɔ babaoo oya.

english: Why produce smaller maize ears when I plant many seeds close together in one hole?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa toi bibii yɔɔ lɛ? Be ni miduɔ dumɔwui babaoo Dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ bu kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too closely, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Proper spacing gives every plant enough room to grow strong and produce big, healthy ears.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ Tsei kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso naa gbɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa koni ekwɛ̃ waa ni ená toi wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why are my tomato plants growing plenty of green leaves and flowers, but the flowers keep dropping off without producing tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ yɛ baai kɛ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shi fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛwooo tomato ko kwraa.

english: Flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. High nitrogen makes the crop spend energy growing thick green leaves instead of developing fruit.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. Nitrogen ni fa babaoo lɛ haa tsei kɛ hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ baai ni mli tse ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo yibii

english: Yam plants use their leaves to catch sunlight to create food that fills the tuber underground. Staking lifts the leaves off the ground so they get maximum sunlight and stay safe from soil disease.
ga: Sweet potato tsei kɛ amɛbaai lɛ tsuɔ nii ni amɛkɛmɔɔ hulu la koni amɛkɛfee niyenii ni haa ŋmeii lɛ eyiɔ shikpɔŋ shishi. Staking baaha baai lɛ akaje shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo ni amɛhi shi shweshweeshwe kɛjɛ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli baa lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curling is usually caused by tiny sucking insects like aphids or thrips feeding on the underside of the leaf, or a virus spread by these insects that slows down the leaf's normal growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. loo helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Enɛ haa baai lɛ adalɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it a mistake to put chemical fertilizer on my crops right before a heavy downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji tɔmɔ akɛ mikɛ tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baawo miŋmɔshi nibii amli amrɔ nɔŋŋ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain washes the fertilizer deep into the soil below the root level or carries it away off the field (leaching) before the plant roots get a chance to drink it in.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ shishifãi lɛ ashishi loo ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli (leaching) dani tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ náa hegbɛ amɛnuɔ lɛ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops turn pale and weak even when there is good rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa midumɔ nii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔɔ yɛ nugbɔ enɛ po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow much faster than most crops and steal the fertilizer, soil water, and sunlight meant for your crops, effectively starving them even when conditions seem good.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni amɛjuɔ ŋmɔshi nibii, sũ mli nu, kɛ hulu la ni yɔɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ yeɔ hɔmɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shihilɛi lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ po.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and burn when there is too much sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa kɛ́ hulu la lɛ fa babaoo lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that cannot handle direct, strong sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or tree cover to protect them from heat stress until their leaves mature and can handle full exposure.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni nyɛɛɛ aná hulu la ni naa wa tɛ̃ɛ. Amɛmiitao tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ tsei bibii loo tsei ahe nɔ. Enɛ ji koni akɛbu tso lɛ he kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi baai lɛ baadara ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛtsu hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he nii.

english: Why do new leaves on my cocoa trees come out soft and reddish-pink before turning green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai heei ni yɔɔ mi cacao tso lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo blɛoo ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ dani amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: New cocoa leaves produce temporary red pigments to shield sensitive young leaf tissue from sun damage. As the leaf thickens and builds chlorophyll for photosynthesis, it gradually turns dark green.
ga: Kookoo baai heei jieɔ su tsuru ko ni tsuɔ nii be kukuoo ko koni ebu baa bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he. Be ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ chlorofil kɛha fotosintɛsis lɛ, baai lɛ tsɔɔ eŋɔli ni tsuɔ fiofio.

english: Why do flowers grow directly on the thick trunk of my cocoa tree instead of on the thin branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ moŋ fe tsei lɛ aniji bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees naturally grow flowers directly on the trunk and thick branches so that the tree can hold and support heavy mature pods without breaking delicate outer stems.
ga: Cacao tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ tsei akutsei kɛ tsei niji ni mli tse lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ amɔmɔ tsei ni eda lɛ ni eye ebua amɛ ni efoŋ tso ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ mli.

english: Why do many small, young cocoa pods shrivel up and turn black before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii babaoo shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ dani amɛdaraa lɛ?

english: This is a natural process called cherelle wilt, where the cocoa tree sheds excess tiny pods it cannot nourish properly so that the remaining pods can grow into full, healthy fruits.
ga: Enɛ ji adebɔɔ mli nifeemɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ Cherelle Wilt, he ni cacao tso lɛ shwieɔ eshishifãi bibii lɛ. Ajieɔ nɔ ni fa fe nine ni anyɛɛɛ aye nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ. Enɛ ji koni ŋmeii ni eshwɛ lɛ adara ni amɛfee aduawai ni eyi obɔ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are my growing cocoa pods turning black and rotting during the heavy rains?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo ni miida lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni egboɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Excess water and high air moisture create ideal conditions for fungal black pod disease. Raindrops bounce off infected soil or nearby diseased pods and spread fungal spores to healthy pods, causing them to turn black and rot.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha fungal black pod hela lɛ baa. Nugbɔshiimɔi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni hela emɔ nɔ loo ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ. ni egbɛ fungal spores lɛ eshwa pods ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛfeɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ.

english: Why does my cocoa tree grow so many weak branches inside the main canopy without producing pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso lɛ niji bibii babaoo kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋwɛitsu wulu lɛ mli ni efeee ŋmeii lɛ?

english: These weak internal shoots, called water shoots or chupons, waste energy from the tree. Removing them lets sunlight and air pass through the tree, encouraging main branches to flower and yield heavy pods.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ mligbɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ akɛ nu ŋmeii loo chupon ŋmeii. Eji hewalɛ ni jɛɔ tsei amli lɛ ni afiteɔ. Kɛ́ ojie lɛ, ebaaha hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Enɛ haa niji titrii lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni tsii.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show that the soil is short on nitrogen. When nitrogen is low, the crop moves available nutrients from older lower leaves up to young growing top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen faaa lɛ Tsei lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: Why do my cassava plants have thick green stems and big leaves but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛ baai wuji shi shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii bibii waa lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium, cassava puts all its energy into growing tall leafy branches above ground instead of storing starch in the tubers underground.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛtoɔ potassium he lɛ. Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ niji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ ashikishaŋ lɛ baato ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ,.

english: Why do multiple small shoots pop up around my main plantain stem on the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei bibii lɛ Tsei babaoo ebɔle he fɛɛ lɛ. Mi plantain tso titri ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ

english: Plantains reproduce by sending out underground root buds that develop into side shoots called suckers. Pruning unnecessary suckers ensures the main stem gets enough food and water to yield big bunches.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ shishi shishifãi ni amɛtsuɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni atsɛɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. Tso lɛ tsei ni he ehiaaa lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ haa tso titri lɛ naa niyenii kɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo tsei niji wuji.

english: How do I know when cocoa pods are fully ripe and ready to be harvested from the tree?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa ni esa akɛ akpa kɛjɛ tso lɛ nɔ?

english: Cocoa pods change color when mature, turning from green to bright yellow, or from dark red to orange-yellow. Harvesting them at full maturity ensures the beans inside have developed proper sugar content for good fermentation.
ga: Cocoa ŋmeii lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe su be mli ni amɛdaraa lɛ. Tsakemɔ kɛjɛ eŋɔli kɛya ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse loo kɛjɛ etsuru ni mli edɔ kɛya ŋmɔŋ-ŋɔli. Kɛ́ akpa amɛ beni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ náa sugar ni sa yɛ mli koni ekɛwo ŋmeii lɛ amli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my young cocoa trees dry up and die after I cut down all the big shade trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ gboi beni mifo cacao tsei wuji ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants cannot withstand direct, strong sunlight. They need shade from bigger trees or plantains to protect their tender leaves from burning and to keep the soil moist until they grow strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii nyɛŋ akpɛlɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ nɔ. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo plantains amli koni ebu baai bibii ahe koni amɛkashã. kɛ koni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashi ebaawa bɔ ni sa.

english: Why does the soil become very hard and dry right after clearing bush and cutting down big trees from my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa ni egbi amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni ajie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni afo tsei wuji kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Big trees act as a natural shelter that shades the ground and drops leaves to keep the soil soft and moist. Removing them exposes the bare earth directly to the hot sun, causing moisture to evaporate quickly.
ga: Tsei ni eda lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shĩai ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ahe ŋmɔlɔ koni shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo ni edɔ. Amɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ naa hulu la ni mli edɔ lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔtɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya.

english: Bottom leaves turning yellow usually means your maize is lacking nitrogen from the soil. The plant moves whatever little nitrogen it has left to the upper leaves to keep growing, leaving the lower leaves starved.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi tsɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen ni jɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen fioo ni eshwɛ lɛ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ anɔ koni baai lɛ aya nɔ ada. kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni eŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ nɔ

english: Why does my cassava plant produce huge stems and leaves above ground but very small roots underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ yɛ shishifãi wuji kɛ baai ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shi shishifãi bibii waa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or leaves are overgrown, the plant spends all its energy producing top foliage instead of food storage. Cassava needs balanced soil nutrients, especially potassium, to expand its tubers below ground.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo eyɛ baai ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni tso lɛ kɛ niyenii baato lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ eŋwɛi baai lɛ anɔ. Nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni sa yɛ sũ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia Cassava. titri lɛ potassium ni akɛgbalaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli

english: Why do my crops grow thin and tall without producing good yields when I plant them close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ mlɛo ni amɛwooo yibii kpakpai kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When planted too close, crops compete intensely for sunlight, water, and soil food. The plants stretch unnaturally tall to beat their neighbors to the light, leaving them with no strength to develop fruits or seeds.
ga: Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ waa. Tsei lɛ baashɛ he ko ni nɔ kwɔ waa koni amɛtswa amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ amɛshwie la lɛ mli. Enɛ ɔ he ɔ, a be he wami nɛ a kɛ maa wo yiblii loo a kɛ du wuhi.

english: Why do the flowers on my pepper plants fall off before producing any pepper pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miiho dani pepper ŋmɔtɔi lɛ jeɔ kpo lɛ?

english: Pepper plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from intense sun, extreme heat, or a lack of water. It is the plant's way of conserving energy to survive dry conditions.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ kɛji hulu la ni naa wa, dɔlɛ, loo nu ni bɛ lɛ hao amɛ. Eji gbɛ ni tsei tsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ hewalɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli.

english: This is known as blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, which is often caused by irregular watering when the ground dries out completely between rains.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji nu ni afɔɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi kwraa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔi ateŋ lɛ.

english: Why do yam vines need to climb up tall wooden stakes to give a good harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni sweet potato wain tsei akwɔ tsei kakadaji anɔ koni amɛwo ŋmaa kpakpa lɛ?

english: Yam leaves need maximum exposure to sunlight to manufacture food. Staking spreads out the leaves so they can catch light, sending energy down to grow a large, healthy tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la babaoo koni amɛná niyenii. Staking gbɛɔ baai lɛ eshwaa koni la abote mli. Etsuɔ hewalɛ kɛyaa shi koni ekɛfee shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji ni he wa.

english: Why does covering the bare soil around my crops with dry grass help them stay alive in dry weather?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mikɛ jwɛi duɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛhi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli lɛ.

english: Dry grass acts as mulch, creating a blanket over the soil that blocks direct sunlight, reduces water evaporation, keeps the plant roots cool, and prevents the soil from drying out fast.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ mulch. Feemɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɔne ko ni baatsi hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Nu ni hoɔ lɛ nɔ baa shi Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i. ni etsĩ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya

english: Weeds grow faster and are stronger than cultivated crops. They aggressively steal the food and fertilizer from the soil before your crops can absorb it, leaving your crops hungry regardless of rainfall.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛhe wa fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ niyenii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, hɔmɔ baaye onibii lɛ ekɔɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ he.

english: Is it good for me to just scatter my seeds across the farm instead of planting them one by one?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ magbɛ dumɔwui lɛ mashwã ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ moŋ fe ni madu amɛ komekomei?

english: Scattering seeds, also called broadcasting, is fast and easy, but seeds might end up too close together. This makes the crops compete for space, water, and nutrients, which can lower your yield compared to planting in neat rows.
ga: Dumɔwui agbɛfaŋnɔ, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ dumɔwui agbɛfaŋnɔ lɛ yaa oya ni ebɛ mlɛo. Shi ekolɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ amɛhe woɔ he ko, nu, kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ, ni baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii ni onáa lɛ aba shi kɛ akɛto ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli ni ato he gbɛjianɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ he.

english: What is 'broadcasting' when planting, and does it work for all crops?
ga: Mɛni ji ‘gbɛjianɔtoo’ kɛ́ adu nii? Ni ani abaanyɛ akɛtsu nii kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii srɔtoi fɛɛ?

english: Broadcasting means throwing seeds loosely over the land by hand. While it works well for small grains like rice or pasture grasses, bigger crops like maize grow better when planted in straight lines with proper spacing.
ga: Gbɛjianɔtoo tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ nine baagbɛ dumɔwui ashwã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Eyɛ mli akɛ etsuɔ ​​nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ ŋmaa bibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmɔshi nibii moŋ. Shi ŋmɔshi nibii wuji tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ adu yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ ni gbɛ ni sa yɔɔ mli.

english: Can I put fertilizer on my farm when the ground is dry and there is no rain?
ga: Ani manyɛ mawo miŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi ni nugbɔ enɛko lɛ?

english: No, you should avoid putting fertilizer on dry ground during a drought. Fertilizer needs moisture to dissolve into the soil; without water, the strong chemicals stay concentrated and can burn your crop roots.
ga: Dabi, esa akɛ okpa shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli. Fɛ̃i he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii koni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ nu bɛ lɛ, tsofai ni yɔɔ mli lɛ hiɔ shi ni ebaanyɛ eshã otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why does fertilizer fail to help my crops when there is no water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yeee ebuaaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be mli ni nu bɛ lɛ?

english: Plants cannot eat dry fertilizer. Crops take up nutrients through their roots in liquid form, so if there is no water in the soil, the fertilizer just sits there unusable and can even harm the crop.
ga: Tsei nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbi. Tsei shwieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ yɛ nu mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛji nu bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baata jɛmɛ kɛkɛ ni ebaafee nɔ ni anyɛɛɛ akɛtsu nii ni ebaanyɛ eye ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ awui.

english: When is the safest time for me to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe fe fɛɛ ni mikɛbaawo miŋmɔshi nii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nii?

english: The best time to apply fertilizer is when the soil is already moist, such as shortly after a rainstorm or after watering your farm, so the nutrients melt into the ground where roots can soak them up safely.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli ji be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo, tamɔ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ loo beni awo ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu sɛɛ. No sɛɛ lɛ, niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ shweshweeshwe lɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if a long drought hits and I cannot irrigate them?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji hɔmɔ ba be kakadaŋŋ ni minyɛɛɛ mawo nɔ nu?

english: During a drought without water, crops wilt, stop growing, and close up their leaves to save moisture. If the dry period lasts too long, the plants dry out completely and die because they cannot move food through their stems.
ga: Yɛ fɛ̃i be lɛ mli lɛ, nu bɛ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi, ekpaa dalɛ ni eŋaa ebaa lɛ koni ekɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Kɛji nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛ tsɔ Tso lɛ gbiɔ kwraa ni egboɔ ejaakɛ enyɛɛɛ ekɛ niyenii atsɔ tso lɛ shishi.

english: How does hot, dry weather change the way my plants grow?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ tsakeɔ tsei adalɛ?

english: In hot and dry conditions, crops slow down their growth to save water. They focus on survival rather than making flowers or fruits, which delays harvest time until moisture returns.
ga: Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ haa amɛdalɛ baa shi koni ekɛbu nu he. Amɛsusuɔ wala ni amɛaahi shi lɛ he moŋ fe fɔfɔii loo aduawai feemɔ. Enɛ haa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ŋmɔtɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it better to plant crops on my empty farm land rather than leaving it clear?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ miŋmɔ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ efee nɔ ko lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni mashi nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ?

english: Planting something on bare ground protects your soil from rain damage and severe sun exposure. Living crop roots hold the soil together, prevent weeds from taking over, and make productive use of your land.
ga: Kɛ́ odu nɔ ko yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu oshikpɔŋ lɛ he koni nugbɔ kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ akafite lɛ. Tso shishifãi ni hiɛ ka lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome. Etsiɔ jwɛi naa koni amɛkaye nɔ. ni okɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ atsu nii jogbaŋŋ

english: Are there official rules or guidelines I should know about before planting crops on my land?
ga: Ani maŋ mlai loo gbɛtsɔɔmɔi komɛi yɛ ni esa akɛ male dani makwɛ tsei yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yes, standard farming guidelines recommend using approved seed varieties, following crop spacing rules, and respecting environmental laws near rivers to keep your land fertile and legally protected.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli gbɛtsɔɔmɔi tsɔɔ akɛ akɛ dumɔwui henɔi ni akpɛlɛ nɔ atsu nii. Nyiɛmɔ tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ he mlai asɛɛ. ni obu shihilɛ mli mlai ni bɛŋkɛ faai lɛ ahe Bɔni afee ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni baa nii ni mla abu he.

english: Why do my crops stop taking up food from the ground when there is no rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be mli ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Roots need moisture as a carrier to absorb nutrients from the soil. When the soil is completely dry, the nutrient flow shuts down, making the plants starve even if the soil itself is rich.
ga: Shishifãi he miihia ŋmɔtɔ akɛ nɔ ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ mli. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa lɛ, niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ hoɔ. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa nii moŋ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize is lacking nitrogen, which is the main food crop plants need to grow leaves. Adding manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ baai lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛhe su ni ji eŋɔli ni mli edɔ lɛ mli ni amɛdara waa.

english: How do I know if my farm plants are being damaged by insects or if they are just sick from a disease?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ efite loo hela emɔ amɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Insect pests usually leave visible signs like chewed holes in leaves, missing stems, or small bugs crawling underneath. Diseases usually cause smooth color changes, wilting, powdery dust, or brown spots without any leaf pieces missing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii shiɔ okadii ni anaa, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, tsei ni elaaje, loo kooloi bibii. Bei pii lɛ, helai ni shwieɔ shishi lɛ haa amɛhe su feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, amɛshwieɔ shi, amɛfeɔ sũ, loo amɛhe feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni baa bibii komɛi bɛ mli.

english: Young cocoa plants are very sensitive to heat and direct sun. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a cooler environment and shields the leaves from burning until the cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ kɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he waa. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantains, ni aduɔ yɛ emasɛi Ehaa shihilɛ mli jɔɔ ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shãa he kɛyashiɔ be mli ni cacao tso lɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ baa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits get black, rotten patches at the bottom before they fully ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ tsɔi diji ni egbo dani eshɛɔ kwraa lɛ?

english: This condition is called blossom-end rot, caused when the plant cannot take up enough calcium or when watering is irregular. Keeping the soil moist continuously during fruit growth prevents the fruit bottoms from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ shihilɛ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Enɛ baa mli kɛ́ tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. aloo be mli ni nu lɛ bɛ be fɛɛ mli Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ewo ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ yaa hiɛ lɛ, ebaatsi aduawai lɛ ashishi lɛ naa koni ekafite.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above the ground but tiny tubers underneath?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi yitso bibioo ko yɛ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen fertilizer, the cassava puts all its energy into growing tall branches and thick leaves, leaving very little energy to build up the tubers under the ground.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ, Yucca kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ tsei niji ni kwɔlɔ kɛ baai ni mli tse. Hewalɛ fioo pɛ eshwɛ ni akɛfeɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Is it bad for my soil if I plant maize on the exact same piece of land every single year?
ga: Ani ebaaye mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa afi?

english: Yes, planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil year after year and allows pests that feed on maize to multiply in the soil.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ lɛ baajie niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi fɛɛ afi. ni eyeɔ ebuaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ ni amɛshwereɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do people say planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for other crops later?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi kɛɔ akɛ kɛ́ adu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special root helpers that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, acts as free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans ji ŋmeii ni yɔɔ nyɛmɔ krɛdɛɛ ko ni amɛkɛmɔɔ nitrogen ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Can I just save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant for next season?
ga: Ani manyɛ makɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ mli lɛ ato koni mikɛdu yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their strong traits in the second generation, resulting in weak plants and a much smaller harvest. It is best to buy fresh certified seeds for high yields.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ laajeɔ amɛsui ni mli wa lɛ yɛ yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ, ni ŋmaa lɛ hu baa shi kwraa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli kɛha yibiiwoo babaoo.

english: Weeds compete directly with your crops for water, sunlight, and plant food in the soil. They steal these essential resources away from your crops, slowing down their growth.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná nu, hulu la, kɛ tsei aniyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛjuɔ nibii ni he hiaa nɛɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. haa dalɛ baa shi

english: Why do my seeds rot in the ground when I plant them right after the very first rain of the year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ beni midu amɛ yɛ afi lɛ mli klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The first rain is often followed by a heat spell that dries out the topsoil. If the seeds germinate and then run out of moisture immediately, they die and rot in the dry ground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, hulutsoo be ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sũ lɛ gĩɔ lɛ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Kɛji dumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ ni nu bɛ amɛhe trukaa lɛ Dumɔwui lɛ baagboi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, direct sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have huge leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and moisture they need to survive their first two years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantain lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii enyɔ lɛ mli.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient crop plants use to build green leaves and produce energy for growth. Adding well-rotted animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the plant recover its dark green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ baai eŋɔli ni amɛhaa hewalɛ kɛha dalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloo ŋmei ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmei fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛná amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts have roots that pull natural nitrogen from the air and store it in the earth. When the plants die, that stored plant food stays in the soil to nourish whatever crop you plant next, such as maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ shishifãi ni kɛ amɛhe gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ tso lɛ gbo lɛ, tso niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni adu lɛ niyenii. nɔ fɛɛ nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa

english: Can I put fresh goat or chicken manure directly around my seedlings when planting?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ too ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei hee awo mli. Ani abaanyɛ adu dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ?

english: Fresh animal manure is too strong and hot, which can burn young plant roots and seeds. It is best to heap the manure and let it dry and break down for a few weeks before putting it around your crops.
ga: Nibii ni afee lɛ ehee lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni edɔ. ni baanyɛ ashã shishifãi kɛ dumɔwui bibii Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmeii lɛ ato he ni oha egbi ni efite otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Why is my cassava growing very tall with many leaves but producing tiny roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ani shishifãi bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When the soil has too much nitrogen or water, cassava sends all its energy upward to grow leaves instead of storing energy underground. Cutting back some top growth and avoiding nitrogen heavy fertilizers encourages the plant to direct its energy into growing larger roots.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei kɛ hewalɛ baato shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ, ŋmei tsuɔ ehewalɛ fɛɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni ekwɛ baai. Kɛ́ afo ŋwɛi shweremɔ lɛ ekomɛi amli ni ajie nitrogen ni tsii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ, ebaawo tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ lɛ aya shishifãi wuji ni yaa hiɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Yam leaves need to spread out in full sunlight to capture energy and make food. Staking lifts the leaves off the wet ground so they can catch sunlight better and stay free from leaf rot, leading to larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni agbɛ sweet potato baai lɛ ashwã koni enine ashɛ hulu la ni fa nɔ koni akɛto hewalɛ ni akɛhoo niyenii. Staking woɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ koni amɛná hulu la jogbaŋŋ. ni baa ni fiteɔ hela bɛ mli lɛ kɛ yitso ni da baa

english: Why should I cover the dry soil around my pepper plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni bɔle mi-pepper tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, shields the soil from the hot sun. It keeps the roots cool, prevents water from evaporating quickly, and keeps the soil moist so the pepper plants stay healthy.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i Ehaa nu shwieɔ oya ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i koni ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops grow weak and produce small fruits when I plant the seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots fight each other underground for food and water, while their leaves block sunshine from each other. Spacing plants properly ensures each crop gets enough light, air, and nutrients to grow strong.
ga: Kɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Eshishifãi lɛ wuɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ haa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe lɛ nɔ. Tsoi lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa yeɔ ebuaa ni tso fɛɛ tso nine shɛɔ la, kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ koni ekwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Black spots on the bottom of tomatoes happen when the plant cannot pull enough calcium from the soil, usually caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist helps the roots transport calcium smoothly to build healthy fruit.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ tomato shishi lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nyɛɛɛ ajie calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛkɛ calcium lɛ yaa jogbaŋŋ koni amɛwo aduawai ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: What causes tiny holes in my young maize leaves and white powder inside the leaf funnel?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai bibii kɛ powda yɛŋ ni yɔɔ mibaa ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ mli

english: Holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by armyworm caterpillars hiding and feeding inside the central leaf whorl. Applying natural neem leaf extract or recommended treatments early in the morning reaches the pests before they ruin the plant's growing point.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii kɛ bu ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai bibii amli lɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ teeɔ amɛhe ni amɛyeɔ nii yɛ baa lɛ teŋgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ adebɔɔ mli neem tso lɛ mli nu loo tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsu he nii lɛ wo mli leebi lɛ, ebaafite tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ dani amɛfite he ni tso lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do some of my bean seeds have smooth skins while others look rough and wrinkled?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ekomɛi hiɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi hu tamɔ nɔ ni ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: The texture of a bean's skin is determined by its genetic variety. Smooth coats help protect seeds from moisture damage during storage, while rough coats can help the seed absorb water faster when planted or prepared for cooking.
ga: Nɔ ni tsɔɔ bɔ ni nut lɛ mli ŋmei lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ ji bɔ ni wala yibii sɔrɔtoi lɛ yɔɔ ha. Nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ he beni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nɔ ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛŋɔ nu oya kɛ́ amɛmiidu loo amɛmiisaa amɛhe koni amɛhoo nii.

english: Is it true that bean seeds brought from neighboring countries like Nigeria will grow better than our local Ghanaian seeds?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmeii ni akɛbaa kɛjɛɔ maji ni bɛŋkɛ wɔ tamɔ Nigeria lɛ amli lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ fe wɔ Ghana dumɔwui ni yɔɔ wɔmaŋ lɛ?

english: Not necessarily. A crop's yield depends on the physical quality of the seed coat, seed health, and how well that variety adapts to local soil and rainfall, rather than simply which country the seed came from.
ga: Dabi, bɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii baawo lɛ damɔ bɔ ni dumɔwui lɛ ahe tsɔne lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ nɔ. Dumɔwui ahewalɛ kɛ bɔ ni srɔtoi lɛ tsakeɔ amɛhe amɛhaa shikpɔji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Jeee maŋ ni dumɔwui lɛ jɛ mli lɛ pɛ he ewieɔ.

english: How can I tell which dark-colored beans are best to keep as seeds for next season versus those I should just cook?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male ŋmeii ni tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ mikɛto akɛ dumɔwui kɛha be ni baa lɛ? Kɛ akɛto dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ, esa akɛ mikome too mahoo.

english: Always select dark beans that have clean, unbroken coats without tiny hole damages from insects. Seeds with undamaged coats protect the baby plant inside from rotting in the soil after you plant them.
ga: Halamɔ ŋmeii ni hiŋmɛi diji yɔɔ mli ni yitsɔi ni he tse ni etseee. Kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii efiteee lɛ, buji bibii. Dumɔwui ni nɔ ko bɛ he lɛ buɔ tso bibioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ he koni ekafite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni odu sɛɛ.

english: Why do my bean plants yield seeds with different coat colors even when planted in the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tso lɛ woɔ dumɔwui ni hiɛ sui srɔtoi eyɛ mli akɛ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ moŋ lɛ?

english: Different coat colors mean you are either growing mixed seed varieties or cross-pollination happened between different bean plants nearby, resulting in natural color variations in the harvested seeds.
ga: Kootu sui srɔtoi tsɔɔ akɛ oodu dumɔwui ni akɛfee ekome loo cross-pollination ni baa yɛ bean tsei srɔtoi ateŋ lɛ. ni bɛŋkɛ Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, dumɔwui ni akpaa lɛ yɛ sui srɔtoi yɛ adebɔɔ naa.

english: Why do my dark-colored harvested beans take much longer to boil soft on the fire than lighter ones?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans ni mikpa ni yɔɔ ediŋ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani efeɔ blɛoo yɛ la mli fe beans ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Darker bean coats contain higher levels of natural plant compounds called tannins. These compounds make the outer seed skin thicker and tougher, which slows down water absorption when cooking.
ga: Adebɔɔ mli tsofai ni atsɛɔ amɛ tannins lɛ fa babaoo yɛ ŋmeii ni awo amɛhe diŋ lɛ amli. Nɛkɛ nibii nɛɛ haa dumɔwu lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ewaa. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi fioo kɛ́ oohoo nii.

english: Why does the skin of some beans peel off easily when boiled while other beans stay whole on the fire?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii komɛi ahe ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ ahoo amɛ lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni nuts henɔi krokomɛi lɛ kanei fɛɛ tsoɔ lolo?

english: The strength of the bond between the coat and the inside seed varies by variety. Beans with loosely attached coats shed their skin quickly when heated, making them suitable for dishes requiring smooth bean paste.
ga: Hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ kɛ mligbɛ dumɔwui lɛ ateŋ lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ srɔtoi amli. Nuts ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Hewolo lɛ baatse oya kɛji akɛ edɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ nɔ ni sa kɛha niyenii ni biɔ ni aŋɔ ŋmeii awo mli lɛ.

english: Why do my beans become much harder to cook soft after I store them in bags for several months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-beans lɛ ahoomɔ wa waa beni mikɛwo kotoku lɛ mli nyɔji babaoo sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Prolonged storage in warm, humid conditions causes chemical changes in the seed coat—known as the 'hard-to-cook' effect—making it very difficult for hot water to penetrate the skin.
ga: Nitoo be kakadaŋŋ yɛ he ni edɔ, fɛ̃i kɛ tsofa tsakemɔi baa dumɔwui lɛ ahe. Ale lɛ hu akɛ ‘hard to cook’ effect, ni ehaa ewaa waa akɛ nu ni mli edɔ lɛ baabote hewolo lɛ mli.

english: Does the roughness or smoothness of a bean's coat affect how quickly it sprouts after I plant it?
ga: Ani bɔ ni ŋmeii lɛ ahe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ saa bɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya beni adu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ he?

english: Yes, bean seeds with rougher coats often absorb soil moisture faster, which can trigger quicker sprouting compared to smooth-coated seeds that resist water entry slightly longer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛŋɔ sũ mli nu lɛ oya. Enɛ baanyɛ aha ekwɛ̃ oya kɛ akɛto dumɔwui ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni nyɛɔ nu boteɔ mli be fioo lɛ ahe.

english: How does the outer coat of a bean seed protect it after I place it under the soil?
ga: Te ŋmei lɛ kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ baabu mihe aha tɛŋŋ beni mifu lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi sɛɛ lɛ?

english: The outer coat acts like protective armor, defending the fragile seed inside against soil pests, fungal rot, and harsh weather until the seedling is strong enough to shoot up.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ kponɔgbɛ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋmei ni buɔ mɔ he. Buu dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛjɛ sũ mli nibii ni fiteɔ nii, fitemɔ, kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni mli wa lɛ ahe kɛyashi dumɔwui lɛ baaná hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛje kpo.

english: Why do market women prefer buying certain seed coat types over others when purchasing beans in bulk?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jarayeli yei sumɔɔ ni amɛhe dumɔwui akui henɔi komɛi fe ekrokomɛi beni amɛheɔ ŋmeii babaoo lɛ?

english: Traders choose specific coat types based on traditional cooking uses; for instance, seeds with rich dark coats are preferred for dishes like Waakye because the skin naturally releases desirable food color during cooking.
ga: Jarayelɔi halaa atadei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ni damɔ blema gbɛi ni atsɔɔ nɔ ahoɔ nii lɛ anɔ. Akɛ nɔkwɛmɔnɔ lɛ, asumɔɔ dumɔwui ni mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ediŋŋ kɛha niyenii tamɔ Waakye ejaakɛ hewolo lɛ jieɔ niyenii lɛ su ni ataoɔ lɛ kpo yɛ adebɔɔ naa beni ahoɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know how many months my maize will take before it is ready for harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male nyɔji enyiɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ baahe dani eshɛ he ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Different crop varieties have fixed growth periods; early-maturing maize varieties take about 3 months (90 days), while medium-maturing varieties take up to 4 months (120 days) from planting to harvest.
ga: Tsei srɔtoi yɛ be pɔtɛɛ ni amɛkɛdaraa. Abɛi henɔi ni shwereɔ mra lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 3 (gbii 90), yɛ be mli ni abele henɔi ni shwereɔ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ heɔ aaafee nyɔji 4 (gbii 120) kɛjɛɔ dumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ ŋmaakpamɔ mli.

english: Why do some crops like cowpea produce food in three months, but cassava takes almost a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei komɛi, tamɔ cowpea lɛ woɔ niyenii yɛ nyɔji etɛ mli lɛ? Shi? Cassava heɔ nɔ ni miihe ashɛ afi?

english: Every plant species has a different biological clock built into its seed; quick-maturing crops grow flowers and seeds rapidly, whereas root crops need many months to store energy underground to form big tubers.
ga: Tso fɛɛ tso yɛ wala yibii ahe ŋmɛlɛtswaa sɔrɔto yɛ edumɔwui amli. Tsei ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya lɛ woɔ fɔfɔi kɛ dumɔwui oya. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ahe miihia nyɔji babaoo dani amɛkɛ hewalɛ ato shikpɔŋ shishi koni amɛfee ŋmeii wuji.

english: How can I tell if my yam tubers are fully mature underground without digging them up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ ekwɛ̃ kwraa yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni mikɛ amɛ efoŋ?

english: When yam tubers reach full maturity, the vines and leaves above ground naturally stop growing, turn yellow, and dry up at the end of the rainy season.
ga: Kɛji akɛ sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ dara kwraa lɛ Wein tso lɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ baai lɛ baakpa amɛdalɛ yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe. etsɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni egbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee.

english: How does my pepper plant change from making leaves to growing actual fruits?
ga: Te fee tɛŋŋ ni mi-pepper tso lɛ je baai ni ewoɔ lɛ nɔ kɛtee aduawai diɛŋtsɛ ni ewoɔ lɛ mli?

english: As a plant reaches a certain age, it uses energy from sunlight and soil nutrients to form flowers, which then get fertilized and swell into peppers.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ shɛ afii pɔtɛɛ ko Ekɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ fɔfɔii. Kɛkɛ lɛ, amɛfeɔ ekome ni amɛfeɔ chili ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Extreme heat, dry air, or lack of soil moisture causes stress to tomato plants, leading them to drop their flowers as a defense mechanism to save energy.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi, loo shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha tomato tsei lɛ aná haomɔ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, esa akɛ tomato tsei lɛ ajie amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ amɛshwie shi akɛ hebuu gbɛ koni amɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry conditions to conserve water and protect the tubers underground, and they will produce fresh leaves once the rains return.
ga: Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be mli ni nu hɔmɔ baa koni amɛhiɛ nu mli ni amɛbu shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ ahe. ni ebaawo baai heei kɛji nugbɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba

english: Young cocoa trees get burned easily by harsh sunlight, so plantains are planted next to them to provide broad leaves that shade and keep the soil moist.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ shãa cacao tsei bibii lɛ oya. No hewɔ lɛ, aduɔ dumɔwui yɛ amɛmasɛi. koni baai ni mli kwɔ lɛ aha hulutsoo ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Young crops have small root systems, so removing weeds early prevents them from stealing sunlight, water, and soil nutrients needed by the young plants.
ga: Tso bibioo lɛ yɛ shishifã bibioo ko. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaye abua ni amɛkaju hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni tsei bibii taoɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing well if I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for food and water in the soil, causing all the plants to stay small and yield less.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ akaŋ. Enɛ haa tso muu lɛ fɛɛ feɔ bibioo ni ewooo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do my pepper plants give smaller fruits during the third harvest compared to the first?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ wooo yibii fioo yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni ji etɛ lɛ mli kɛ akɛto klɛŋklɛŋ nɔ lɛ he lɛ?

english: As crops produce multiple harvests, they exhaust the nutrients in the soil, so applying organic manure or fertilizer helps sustain large fruit production.
ga: Kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii shii abɔ Niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaho aya. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛ wala mli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni akwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow before the maize is ready for harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miifee ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo akɛ abaakpa lɛ?

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is a key nutrient plants need to grow strong. Adding nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or well-rotted animal manure gives them the food they need to stay green and develop large cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa ni tsei lɛ adara waa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ NPK loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaha amɛ niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli ni amɛná ŋmɔshi nibii wuji.

english: Covering the soil with dry leaves or grass, called mulching, keeps the ground cool and traps moisture so the sun doesn't dry out your crop roots quickly. It also stops weeds from taking over and rots over time to feed the soil.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi haa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli. Enɛ baatsi hulu la lɛ naa koni ekaha otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ agbi oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni jwɛi lɛ akaye shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛkafite yɛ be ni sa mli koni amɛkɛha shikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: The first rain of the season can be a false start followed by weeks of hot, dry weather. If you plant too early, your seeds will sprout but then dry up and die from lack of follow-up water, so it is safer to wait until rains become frequent.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ afee amale shishijee. Nɔ ni nyiɛ enɛ sɛɛ ji otsii komɛi ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni edɔ waa lɛ. Kɛji odu mra tsɔ Dumɔwui lɛ baakwɛ̃ shi no sɛɛ lɛ amɛbaagbi ni amɛgboi yɛ nu ni bɛ hewɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ baanɛ shii abɔ. baafee shweshweeshwe fe tsutsu lɛ

english: How do I know which side is up when planting cassava stem cuttings into the ground?
ga: Te ooofee tɛŋŋ ole fã ni esa akɛ ekwɛ ŋwɛi kɛ́ oodu ŋmei niji awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: Look for the small bumps or 'nodes' on the stem where leaves used to grow, and make sure those bumps point upwards toward the sky. Planting cassava stems upside down makes it difficult for the plant to sprout and leads to poor tuber growth.
ga: Taomɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘nodes’ yɛ tso lɛ yiteŋ he ni baai lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ be ko ni eho lɛ. Ni kwɛmɔ akɛ nakai ŋmeii lɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ, ebaaha ewa aha ŋmei lɛ akɛ ebaakwɛ̃, ni ebaaha ŋmei lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ akwɛɛɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant gets stressed by extreme heat, lack of water, or insect attacks. Keeping the soil constantly moist and providing light protection from direct heat helps the flowers stay attached and set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni faaa yɛ amɛmli, loo kooloi bibii tutua tsei lɛ miigba amɛnaa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha afee fɛ̃i ni aha la, hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he tɛ̃ɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yam vines need to climb up so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible, which powers the growth of the big tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off damp ground, protecting them from fungal rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ koni amɛha baai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. ni tsirɛɔ shikpɔŋ shishi bulbs lɛ adalɛ Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ eshwɛɔ yɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ ŋmɔtɔ naa koni ekafite.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny sucking pests like aphids, mites, or whiteflies that feed on leaf sap. Spraying your pepper plants with neem tree leaf extract or recommended pest sprays helps clear these insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ aphids, mites, loo whiteflies ni yeɔ baa lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ neem baa mli nu loo tsofa ni akɛwoɔ kooloi amli ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ shwie pepper tsei anɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi nɛɛ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under intense tropical sunshine. Planting shade crops like plantains alongside young cocoa acts like a canopy, protecting the seedlings from drying out until they are strong enough.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ shishi. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo tamɔ dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ kookoo bibii ahe lɛ baatsu nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta. Ebuɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe koni amɛkagbi kɛyashi amɛhe wa bɔ ni sa.

english: Is it helpful for me to plant cowpeas together on the same field as my maize?
ga: Ani tsina ŋmeii ni mikɛaadu yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ ŋmãa lɛ baaye abua mi?

english: Yes, planting cowpeas with maize is beneficial because cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and fix it into the soil, which feeds the maize. This mixed planting also shades the soil to block weeds and gives you two different crops from one plot.
ga: Hɛɛ, sɛɛnamɔ yɛ tsina ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ he ejaakɛ tsina ŋmãa lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛfiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni no haa ŋmãa lɛ niyenii. Nɛkɛ dumɔwui ni akɛfutuɔ nii nɛɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni jwɛi akaje mli, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii sɔrɔtoi enyɔ baa kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ.

english: If too many small shoots (suckers) grow around one main plantain stem, they steal food and water from each other, resulting in tiny plantain bunches. Pruning away extra suckers leaves only one or two strong stems to produce large, heavy bunches.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii (ŋmei) kwɛ̃ ni ebɔle ehe single main trunk Amɛbaaju niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ amɛhe. ni kɛ niji bibii baa Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni baafee kuu agbo ni tsii baashi.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and have wide leaves that act as natural shade umbrellas, protecting the young cocoa plants and keeping the soil moist until the cocoa grows strong.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya ni eyɛ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hulutsoo. Ebuɔ kookoo tsei bibii ahe, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ mli waa.

english: Yes, planting beans with maize improves soil fertility because beans take nitrogen from the air and put it into the soil, which feeds the maize and saves you money on chemical fertilizer.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa duɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ yaa hiɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ŋmeii lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii kɛha ŋmãa ni ehaa okɛ shika baatsu nii yɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ ahemɔ mli

english: Why do I need to clear the weeds around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafo jwɛi yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii ahe be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds steal water, sunlight, and food from the soil that your crops need to grow, so removing them early ensures your crops get all the nutrients to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii mli nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Enɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Leaf curling on pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like mites or whiteflies sucking the juices out of the leaves, or by a virus spread by those insects.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni nakai kooloi lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ

english: Tomato flowers drop off without setting fruit when the weather becomes too hot, when the plant lacks sufficient water, or when there are not enough insects to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi ni amɛwooo yibii kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei lɛ bɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ

english: Why do the roots of my cassava rot in the ground before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays too wet for long periods, especially in low-lying areas during heavy rains where water cannot drain away easily.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ tsɔ be kakadaŋŋ. Titri lɛ, yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli ni nu nyɛŋ ajɛ mli oya lɛ.

english: Yellowing leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen in the soil, which is the main nutrient it needs to grow green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Amɛji niyenii titrii ni he hiaa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do I need to lift my yam vines onto wooden sticks instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mawo sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbee shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Staking yam vines lifts the leaves toward the sun so they can make more food for the plant, and keeps the leaves away from wet soil where fungal diseases breed.
ga: Staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛyaa hulu la lɛ he koni amɛfee niyenii babaoo amɛha tso lɛ. Ni ha baai lɛ akashɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ, ni ji he ni ŋmeii fɔɔ yɛ lɛ he.

english: It is best to wait until the soil gets two or three heavy rains that soak deep into the ground so that your seeds do not dry out and die after germinating.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni naa wa enyɔ loo etɛ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ bɔni afee ni odumɔwui lɛ akagbi ni amɛgboi beni amɛkwɛ̃ sɛɛ.

english: Why are small insects destroying my harvested maize after I put it in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii fiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ beni mikɛwo nitoohe lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Insects like grain weevils attack stored maize when the cobs were not dried completely before storage or when the storage sacks and rooms are not properly sealed.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmãa ŋmeii tutuaa ŋmãa ni ato lɛ kɛ́ ŋmãa lɛ egbiko kwraa dani akɛto. aloo be mli ni aŋmɛɛɛ kotokui kɛ nitoohei lɛ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my crops turning yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to build strong leaves. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps leaves stay green and produce food for the crop.
ga: Baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛma baai ni wa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔtɔ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua baa lɛ ni ehi shi eŋɔli ni eha niyenii aha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How exactly do leaves help my crops grow and produce food?
ga: Te baai yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Leaves act like small solar panels for the plant. They catch sunlight and combine it with air and water to manufacture sugars and proteins that feed the plant so it can yield fruits or grains.
ga: Baai lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei bibii kɛha tso lɛ. Amɛmɔɔ hulu la ni amɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nu feɔ sugar kɛ protein ni haa tsei niyenii koni amɛfee aduawai loo ŋmaa.

english: Plants naturally lose water through their leaves. During dry weather, the cassava plant drops some leaves on purpose to conserve moisture in its stem and roots so it does not dry out.
ga: Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ ekomɛi koni ŋmɔtɔ ahi amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli koni amɛkagbi.

english: Can decaying leaves and plant waste help my soil feed my crops better?
ga: Ani baai ni fiteɔ kɛ tsei amli jwɛi yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Yes, decaying leaves break down into rich organic matter called compost. As they rot, they release stored proteins and minerals back into the soil while helping the ground hold water longer.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, baai ni fiteɔ lɛ fãa kɛfeɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni atsɛɔ amɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii. Kɛ amɛfite lɛ Amɛjieɔ protein kɛ mineral ni ato lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny insects gathering under the leaves of my vegetable plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ mi-vegetables lɛ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Insects sit under leaves because the tissue there is soft and protected from heat. They suck out the liquid sap and nutrients the plant makes, which weakens the leaf and stunts crop growth.
ga: Kplukai taraa baai ashishi ejaakɛ fãji ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulutsoo he. Amɛmuɔ nu ni mli tse kɛ niyenii ni tsei feɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni etsĩɔ tsei lɛ adalɛ naa.

english: Why is my crop growing huge bushy leaves but not producing any flowers or fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ yɛ baai agboi shi ebɛ fɔfɔi loo aduawai lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes a plant focus only on leaf growth. Crops need a balanced diet that includes phosphorus and potassium to transition from growing leaves to producing flowers and fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baa lɛ pɛ nɔ. Niyenii ni ja ni phosphorus kɛ potassium fata he lɛ he miihia tsei koni amɛtsake kɛjɛ baai ni miida lɛ amli kɛya fɔfɔi kɛ aduawai ni amɛwoɔ lɛ mli.

english: How does spreading dry leaves around the base of my crops help them survive hot days?
ga: Baai ni egbi ni agbɛɔ ashwãa he fɛɛ he Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Dry leaves act as mulch, forming a protective cover over the soil. This blanket shades the ground from the direct sun, stopping water from evaporating so the plant roots stay moist longer.
ga: Baai ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ni amɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kuntu nɛɛ buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Tsi nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ naa Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ahiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ.

english: How do plant roots take in nutrients from the ground to nourish the leaves?
ga: Te tsei shishifãi lɛ feɔ tɛŋŋ amɛjieɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛha baai lɛ hewalɛ?

english: Roots have fine hair-like threads that drink up water from the soil. When soil nutrients dissolve in that water, the plant draws the liquid upward through its stem to feed the leaves.
ga: Shishifãi lɛ yɛ yitsɔi bibii ni tamɔ yitsɔi ni gbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ shwie nu lɛ mli Tso lɛ gbalaa nu lɛ kɛyaa ŋwɛi kɛtsɔɔ tso lɛ shishi koni ekɛha baai lɛ niyenii.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. The plant rolls its leaves inward to reduce the surface area exposed to intense heat, helping it trap moisture and avoid drying out.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo ni naa wa baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi ni ehaaa baai lɛ agbi.

english: How do green leaves that rot in the field turn into plant food for the next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni baai eŋɔli ni miifite yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ afee niyenii kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Tiny organisms in the soil called microbes eat the fallen leaves. As they break the leaf material down, the nutrients inside are transformed into forms that the roots of a new crop can easily soak up.
ga: nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli Yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nibii bibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ yeɔ baai ni egbee shi lɛ. Beni efoɔ baa lɛ mli nibii lɛ mli lɛ, niyenii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ efeɔ nɔ ko ni tso hee lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food, or that the soil is waterlogged, which stops the roots from breathing and absorbing nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji tsei aniyenii ni he hiaa loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ amu ni amɛkaŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce much smaller harvests every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kwraa daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the soil of specific nutrients. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like groundnuts or cowpeas puts natural nitrogen back into the soil and restores its strength.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba shi. Abele ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa sũ lɛ mli ni ehaa ehewalɛ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the small pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiifite dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet, overly shaded farms. Pruning extra tree branches to let sunlight and air circulate through the farm helps keep the pods dry and healthy.
