ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli efɔ ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ amli. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmeii lɛ agbiɔ ni amɛhiɛɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting, curling up, and turning pale green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ebɔle ehe, ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried by tiny whitefly insects and infected planting stems. Using disease-resistant cassava stems for planting prevents this problem.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ji ŋmeii bibii ni hiɛɔ ŋmeii bibii kɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ Kɛ akɛ ŋmei ŋmeii ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ baatsu nii yɛ dumɔ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni atsĩ naagba nɛɛ naa.

english: Why do my yam vines turn brown and dry up long before it is harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato wain tsei lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi be kakadaŋŋ dani kpamɔ be lɛ baashɛ lɛ?

english: Early drying of yam leaves is usually caused by anthracnose, a fungal disease that attacks the leaves in warm, humid weather, cutting off the plant's food supply to the growing tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, anthracnose ji nɔ ni kɛ sweet potato baai lɛ gbiɔ oya. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni tutuaa baai yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, afoɔ tso lɛ niyenii jɛɛhe lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii ni miida lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce a lot of flowers, but the flowers drop off without turning into tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo nɛkɛ lɛ? Shi ani fɔfɔi ko gbeeɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ tomato?

english: Tomato plants drop their flowers when they suffer from extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of insect pollinators. Giving the plants steady water and light shade during severe hot spells stops flower drop.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛ́ amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ hewɔ. Irregular watering or not enough pollinating insects Giving water to trees and providing light shade During hot weather, the flowers will not fall off.

english: Why are the bottom ends of my pepper fruits turning black and soft while still growing on the plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper aduawai lɛ shishigbɛ fã lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo be mli ni edaa yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot. It happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium, usually caused by irregular watering where the soil dries out completely and then gets flooded.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji tsei lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa ni no sɛɛ lɛ nu afua.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow, even before the bunch is fully ripe?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa amɛ dani ŋmeii lɛ shwere kwraa lɛ?

english: Plantain trees fall easily when tiny pests called nematodes or plantain root weevils destroy their roots underground, leaving the heavy plant without strong anchor roots to hold it in the soil.
ga: Ewaaa akɛ ŋmeii bibii shwieɔ dumɔwui anɔ. Nɔ ni atsɛɔ lɛ nematode loo plantain shishifã ŋmei lɛ fiteɔ eshishifãi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Shi tsei ni tsii ni shishifãi ni wa bɛ amɛhe koni amɛmɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and yield very little when I plant the seeds very close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mli tseee ni ewoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ beni miduɔ dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leaving no single plant with enough food to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tsei komɛi bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛdara ni amɛwo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my crop seeds rot in the soil instead of sprouting after I plant them right after the first rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi aduawai dumɔwui lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛakwɛ̃ beni midu amɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: The very first rain after a long dry season often isn't enough to soak the deep soil. Planting too early means seeds sit in hot, damp dirt that bakes them before steady rains start.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ faaa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaahã shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Dumɔwui lɛ adumɔ mra tsɔ tsɔɔ akɛ ehe miihia ni dumɔwui lɛ ahi shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ ni mli edɔ nɔ he ni amɛbaashã dani nugbɔ lɛ aya nɔ anɛ.

english: Where is the best place for me to get reliable cocoa seedlings for my new farm?
ga: Nɛgbɛ ji he ni hi fe fɛɛ ni manyɛ mana kookoo dumɔwui ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ kɛha miŋmɔ hee lɛ?

english: It is best to get seedlings directly from official Seed Production Division stations of COCOBOD. These seedlings are certified, bred to resist common local diseases, and yield faster than seeds picked from random pods.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooŋɔ dumɔwui kɛjɛ COCOBOD dumɔwui afeemɔ he ni yɔɔ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ tɛ̃ɛ. Akɛ odaseyeli haa dumɔwui nɛɛ. Fɔmɔ ni akɛteɔ shi awoɔ helai ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ maŋ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ yibiiwoo oya fe dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii amli

english: How can I check if the young seedlings I brought to my farm are healthy before planting them?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ kɛji dumɔwui ni mikɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ hewalɛ dani madu?

english: Look for bright green leaves, a straight sturdy stem, and a healthy root system. Avoid seedlings with yellowing leaves, dark spots, holes, or swollen stems, as these are early signs of disease or pest damage.
ga: Taomɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni kpɛɔ. tso lɛ shishifãi ni ja ni wa kɛ shishifãi ni wa Tsi ohe kɛjɛ dumɔwui ni baai lɛ efee ŋmɔŋ, he ni edɔ, bu loo amɛshishifãi ni efuu lɛ ahe ejaakɛ enɛɛmɛi ji mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela loo tsɛŋemɔ helai efite.

english: Why are the leaves on my one-year-old cocoa trees turning yellow and showing red veins?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tso ni eye afi kome lɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiitsɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves with clear red veins on young cocoa trees often signal the onset of Cocoa Swollen Shoot Virus Disease (CSSVD). It can also indicate severe nutrient deficiency or stress from too much direct sunlight.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ ŋmeii tsuru ni mli tse jeɔ kpo yɛ cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ. Bei pii lɛ, etsɔɔ akɛ kookoo tso mli hela (CSSVD) lɛ je shishi. Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ ni naa wa loo nɔnyɛɛ ni jɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ babaoo mli baa lɛ hu.

english: What causes the stem of my young cocoa plant to swell up in certain spots?
ga: Mɛni haa mi cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei komɛi?

english: Swelling on the stem or shoots of a young cocoa tree is a primary symptom of Swollen Shoot Disease, which is caused by a virus spread by mealybugs. There is no chemical cure for the virus once a tree is infected.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ ashishifã loo amɛyiteŋ ni efuu lɛ ji Bud Swollen Hela lɛ he okadi titri. Virus ko ni mealybugs gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsofai komɛi bɛ ni akɛtsaa hela nɛɛ kɛji tso lɛ emɔ hela lɛ pɛ.

english: Why is my young cocoa tree dying even though I give it water and clear the weeds around it regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ miigboi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu woɔ hei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli ni mikɛ jwɛi shwieɔ amɛnɔ moŋ? Ton daa?

english: Good cultural practices like weeding and watering help, but they cannot stop viral diseases or underground root pests. Young trees can also die from too much direct sunlight if they lack shade, or from disease spread by insects.
ga: Kusum nifeemɔi kpakpai, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa, shi enyɛŋ ekpa helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ. Tsei bibii hu baanyɛ agboi kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ fe nine mli kɛji amɛbɛ hulutsoo. loo kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi bibii gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ amli

english: Why do my cocoa seedlings wither and dry up a few weeks after transplanting them to the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ otsii fioo komɛi asɛɛ beni mikɛ amɛ ewo shikpɔŋ wulu lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by transplant shock combined with strong heat and lack of shade. Young seedlings need plantains or shade trees around them to keep the soil moist and block harsh direct sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji tsɔne ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli lɛ mli shoofeemɔ ni fata he kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hulutsoo ni bɛ. Esa akɛ tso bibioo lɛ aná tsei bibii loo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ ni ebɔle ehe. Koni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛtsi hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa.

english: What should I do when a sickness on my young cocoa tree gets out of control and spraying does not fix it?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛ́ hela ni yɔɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ anɔ lɛ je kpo ni tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ esaaa lɛ?

english: If normal chemical sprays fail, the tree likely has a viral disease like Swollen Shoot. The infected tree must be safely cut down and uprooted to stop the virus from spreading through insects to surrounding healthy trees.
ga: Kɛji tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ daa lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ hu baanyɛ aná helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa, tamɔ akɔɔblei ni efuu. Esa akɛ afo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe ni ajie amɛ koni hela lɛ akatsɔ kooloi amli kɛya tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: Can diseases spread from an old cocoa farm nearby to my newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Ani helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã kɛjɛ kookoo ŋmɔji momoi ni bɛŋkɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ amli?

english: Yes, insects like mealybugs and airborne fungus spores easily travel from old, diseased farms to fresh young trees. Keeping a clean border or planting temporary barrier crops helps protect your new farm.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, kooloi bibii tamɔ mealybugs kɛ fungal spores ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aya kɛjɛ ŋmɔji momoi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛya tsei bibii amli. easily fresh Husui lɛ ahe tsemɔ loo be kukuoo mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni ooodu lɛ baaye abua ni ebu oŋmɔ hee lɛ he.

english: At what age should I expect my young cocoa trees to start showing flowers and pods?
ga: Mɛɛ afii esa akɛ makpa gbɛ akɛ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ baabɔi fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii feemɔ?

english: Improved hybrid cocoa varieties usually begin flowering and producing pods between 2 to 3 years after planting, provided they receive good shade, weed control, and fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kookoo henɔi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ jeɔ fɔfɔii ashishi ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii yɛ afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli kɛjɛ be mli ni adu lɛ, kɛji akɛ amɛná hulutsoo kpakpa. Jwɛi ahe nitsumɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii

english: Who should I contact for help when I cannot identify a strange sickness spreading across my farm?
ga: Namɔ esa akɛ matswa koni eye ebua mi? Beni minyɛɛɛ mayɔse hela ko ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ

english: You should report the problem immediately to your local Agricultural Extension Officer or the nearest Cocoa Health and Extension Division (CHED) unit. They can visit your farm to diagnose the problem and guide you on proper treatment.
ga: Esa akɛ obɔ naagbai ahe amaniɛ oya oyatsɔɔ okwaayeli he nitsumɔ he nitsulɔ ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ loo Cocoa Hewalɛ kɛ Nitsumɔhe ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ (CHED). Amɛbaanyɛ amɛyasara oŋmɔ lɛ koni amɛyakwɛ naagba lɛ ni amɛwo bo ŋaa yɛ tsofafeemɔ ni sa he.

english: Yellow leaves on maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential nutrient for plant growth. Applying nitrogen-based fertilizer or compost helps the leaves regain their deep green color and energy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha tsei adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛná amɛ su ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads quickly during rainy periods with high humidity. Clearing excess shade branches to let sunlight in and spraying recommended copper fungicides helps protect your pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kɛ hulutsoo be mli. Kɛ́ ojie tsei niji ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ hulutsoo lɛ mli lɛ koni hulu la abote mli, ni okɛ akɔɔble tsofa ni gbeɔ ŋmeii ni akɛwoɔ ŋaa lɛ afɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu o-pods lɛ ahe.

english: Leaf curl in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies sucking the plant juices and spreading viruses. Controlling these insects early with neem oil or targeted spray stops the curling.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ kɛbaa. Nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ neem fɔ loo spray tsu nii yɛ he ni eyɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔlɔ lɛ akpa ŋmɔlɔ.

english: How do I stop small caterpillars from eating the center leaves of my young maize?
ga: Te aaafee tɛŋŋ atsĩ ŋmeii bibii ni yeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anaa?

english: These caterpillars are likely Fall Armyworms that hide in the central whorl of the plant. Inspecting your farm every week and applying approved crop protection products directly into the central funnel kills them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ ŋmeii nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ateŋ ŋmeii amli. Kɛ́ okwɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa otsi ni okɛ tsofa ko ni buɔ tsei ahe ni akpɛlɛ nɔ lɛ awo tsɔne ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaagbe amɛ dani amɛbaafite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: How can I protect my harvested maize from weevils while it is stored in my room?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ he kɛjɛ ŋmeii ahe be mli ni mikɛtoɔ mitsu lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Insects attack stored grain if it is not dried enough or kept exposed. Drying your maize until the grains are very hard and storing them in airtight hermetic bags prevents weevils from surviving and eating your harvest.
ga: Kplukai baatutua dumɔwui ni ato lɛ kɛji amɛgbiko bɔ ni sa loo ashi amɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko kwɛɛɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ ogbala o-corn lɛ mli kɛyashi be mli ni ŋmeii lɛ mli wa waa ni okɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, no haaa ŋmeii lɛ ahi shi ni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and burn easily under strong direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantain plants provide wide leaves that act like living umbrellas, shading the cocoa until it grows strong enough to handle the sun.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains ni daa oya lɛ woɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ ambrela. Ha kookoo lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛyashi ebaada ni ená hulu la.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot in the ground before I harvest them during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani akpaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in waterlogged soil for too long, which suffocates the roots and allows fungal rots to develop. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess water drain away from the roots.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ekɛ fungal rot aba. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my yam tubers grow out small and bent instead of big and straight?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tubers lɛ ji bibii ni ebɔle ehe moŋ fe ni eeefee agbo ni eja lɛ?

english: Yam tubers need soft, deep soil to expand downward easily. If the soil is hard, shallow, or stony, the tubers become bent and small; building high, soft soil mounds gives the yams room to grow large and smooth.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã kɛya shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ mlɛo. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa, ekɔɔɔ he eko, loo eyɛ tɛi lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee bibii. Gɔŋ kakadaŋŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni afee lɛ yeɔ ebuaa sweet potatoes ni amɛdaraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the weather gets too hot or when the plant does not get steady water. Keeping the soil consistently moist and planting at the right time helps flowers turn into fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ afɔɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ nu daa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni adu yɛ be ni sa mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua fɔfɔi ni amɛtsɔ aduawai.

english: Giving cowpeas too much nitrogen fertilizer causes the plant to spend all its energy growing leaves instead of flowers and pods. Cowpeas make their own nitrogen, so they need balanced nutrients focused on phosphorus to bloom well.
ga: Nitrogen babaoo ni akɛhaa tsina ŋmei lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ hewalɛ ni jɛɔ baai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii. Tsinai lɛ diɛŋtsɛ feɔ amɛ nitrogen. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni eye niyenii ni ja ni kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ ama fɔsfɔs nɔ koni enyɛ ewo fɔfɔi kpakpai.

english: How does bringing river water directly onto my dry land help my crops grow better than depending only on rains?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni mikɛbaajɛ faa lɛ mli tɛ̃ɛ kɛba mishikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ fe nugbɔ pɛ ni mikɛ mihe fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Using river water through irrigation gives your crops a steady supply of moisture whenever they need it, allowing you to farm during the dry season when rains fail and sell crops when market prices are highest.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ faa mli nu tsu nii kɛtsɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ daa be fɛɛ be ni ehe baahia amɛ. Ehaa otsuɔ okwaayeli yɛ hulutsoo be mli beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ, ni ohɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔshi nibii beni jara nɔ jara wa fe fɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when I watered them earlier in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu wo amɛmli leebi maŋkpa moŋ?

english: In intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can suck it up from the soil. Watering very early in the morning or late in the evening reduces water evaporation and helps plants stay hydrated.
ga: Yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ waa mli lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ afɔ tso lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ lɛ, ehaa nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa shi, ni eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehaa tso lɛ mli shwieɔ shi.

english: Will watering my farm continuously throughout the dry season allow me to harvest crops twice or thrice a year?
ga: Ani kɛ́ maya nɔ mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ lɛ, ebaaha manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii shii enyɔ loo shii etɛ yɛ afi mli?

english: Yes, reliable irrigation removes reliance on natural rainfall cycles, allowing you to plant and harvest multiple crop cycles each year as long as you maintain soil fertility.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi ni anyɛɔ akɛ he fɔ̃ɔ nɔ lɛ jieɔ hekɛnɔfɔɔ ni yɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ adebɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛyaa. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ oduɔ nii ni okpaa ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo daa afi, kɛji akɛ okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Can I use water directly from a muddy pond to irrigate my vegetables, or will it harm my crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛ muji bu lɛ mli lɛ afɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaaye midumɔ nii lɛ awui?

english: Slightly muddy water is usually safe, but thick mud can coat plant leaves, block sunlight, and seal the topsoil so air cannot reach the roots. Letting heavy mud settle before watering is safer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nu ni mli ewo muji fioo lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe. Shi muji ni mli edɔ baanyɛ aha tsei ahe baai ahe, ni etsĩ hulu la naa ni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ naa, ni eha kɔɔyɔɔ akashɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ oooha muji ni tsii lɛ ahi shi dani okɛ nu awo mli.

english: Why do the leaves of my pepper plants turn yellow when too much water stays on the farm after heavy watering?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ beni nu babaoo yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nu ni awo amɛ waa sɛɛ lɛ?

english: When water sits on the farm without draining, root systems suffocate because they cannot get air in waterlogged soil. Without air, roots fail to feed nutrients to the leaves, causing them to turn yellow.
ga: Kɛ nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ yɛ mli lɛ Shishifãi lɛ baagbɔjɔ ejaakɛ enyɛŋ ejie kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ lɛ Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ahã baai lɛ niyenii. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ.

english: When planted too close, crops compete fiercely for limited sunlight, groundwater, and soil nutrients. This stress forces them to grow tall to fight for light, leaving little energy to grow thick stems or big cobs.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná hulu la ni faaa, shikpɔŋ shishi nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kpakpai. Nɛkɛ haomɔ nɛɛ nyɛɔ amɛnɔ koni amɛdara koni amɛwu amɛha la. Enɛ haaa hewalɛ fioo pɛ aná koni akɛkwɛ tsei ni mli tse loo tsei wuji.

english: Why do my bean plants drop their flowers without forming pods when the soil gets too dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bean tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeee ŋmeii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi tsɔ lɛ?

english: When a plant experiences severe water stress during flowering, it aborts its blossoms as a survival instinct to conserve moisture for its own stems and roots rather than spending energy making seeds.
ga: Kɛ tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ ni naa wa kpe yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ Ebaakpa fɔfɔi fɔmɔ akɛ wala yibiiwoo su ko ni haa ŋmɔtɔ baa eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ hewalɛ baatsu nii kɛfee dumɔwui

english: Why should I cover the bare ground around my tomato plants with dry grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ maha he ni nɔ ko bɛ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ? Tomato tsei ni jwɛi ni egbi yɔɔ mli

english: Covering the ground with dry grass (mulching) acts like a protective blanket that shades the soil, keeping it cool and stopping strong sunlight from evaporating moisture out of the earth.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ (mulching) lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ko ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ fɛ̃i, ni ehaaa hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ akajie ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ.

english: Why is it necessary to water my farm right after applying solid fertilizer near my crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ nu awo miŋmɔ lɛ mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni wa ewo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Crop roots cannot eat solid fertilizer dry. Water dissolves the fertilizer granules into liquid food that root hairs can easily drink up, while also preventing concentrated fertilizer from burning the plant roots.
ga: Tso shishifãi nyɛŋ aye ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa ni egbi. Nu shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ efeɔ niyenii ni ji nu ni shishifãi lɛ ahe yitsɔi lɛ baanyɛ anu mlɛo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, etsĩɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ naa koni ekashã tsei shishifãi.

english: Which crops are most profitable for me to grow if I get access to an irrigation scheme during the dry season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he waa kɛha mi akɛ makwɛ kɛji minine shɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ he gbɛjianɔtoo nɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli?

english: Fast-growing vegetables like tomatoes, onions, peppers, and okro yield high profits under dry-season irrigation because fresh vegetables become scarce and expensive in local markets when the rains stop.
ga: Aduawai ni kwɛ̃ɔ oya tamɔ tomato, ŋmei, ŋmei kɛ okra he yɛ sɛɛnamɔ waa yɛ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi yɛ be mli ni hɔmɔ baa lɛ shishi. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, kɛ́ nugbɔ lɛ kpa lɛ, ewa akɛ aaana aduawai heei, ni amɛjara wa yɛ maŋ lɛ jarayelihe lɛ.

english: Yellow lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need to grow green and strong. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore soil nutrients.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛhe wa. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba.

english: How does planting groundnuts or beans make my soil better for maize next season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ aha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi kɛha be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmãa?

english: Groundnuts and beans belong to the legume family, which has special root bacteria that take nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the leaves and roots decompose, they naturally fertilize the soil for future crops.
ga: Peanuts kɛ beans fata legume weku lɛ he, ni bacteria krɛdɛɛ ko ni gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ yɛ mli. Kɛji baai kɛ shishifãi lɛ fite Ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When rain leaves standing water around the roots, the water drowns the roots and encourages soil fungi to attack, causing the tubers to rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ lɛ, nu buaa ehe naa yɛ shishifãi lɛ ahe. Nu lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛtutua amɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni egbo

english: Why is it bad to water my pepper plants at mid-day when the sun is very hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ aaaha ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ nu yɛ shwane mli beni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ?

english: Watering under a hot sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before the roots can absorb it, and droplets left on leaves can act like tiny magnifiers, scorching the foliage in intense heat.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi lɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛŋɔɔ nu lɛ. Ni nu mli nu ni ashiɔ yɛ baai anɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee tamɔ glase bibii ni haa nɔ ko feɔ bibioo. ni haa baai lɛ shãa kɛ la ni naa wa lɛ

english: Why do my young cocoa trees wither when I clear away all the bigger trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ shi beni mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that easily burn under direct sunshine. Planting fast-growing shade plants, like plantains or shade trees, acts as a protective shield against heat and conserves soil moisture while the cocoa matures.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ dumɔwui loo shade tsei adumɔ. Etsuɔ nii akɛ nɔ ni tsiɔ dɔlɛ naa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Why do my yam plants need sticks to climb on to produce big tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa niji ni ekwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi ni efee ŋmeii wuji lɛ?

english: Yam vines produce food for the underground tubers using sunlight. Lifting the vines off the ground on stakes allows the leaves to catch maximum sunlight and keeps them away from damp soil diseases.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ kɛ hulu la tsuɔ nii kɛfeɔ niyenii amɛhaa amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Wein tsei lɛ ni awóɔ nɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ naa hulu la babaoo, ni ehaaa helai aba shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ nɔ.

english: Why should I cut away some of the extra suckers growing around my plantain tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ ehe lɛ? Mi plantain lɛ baai lɛ

english: Leaving too many suckers forces the mother plant to share its limited food and water. Keeping only two or three strong suckers ensures the main tree gets enough energy to produce large, heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Kɛ́ ajieɔ ŋmeii babaoo tsɔ lɛ, enyɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ nɔ koni ekɛ niyenii kɛ nu fioo pɛ aha. Kɛ́ okɛ tsei enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ to lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaawo plantain jwɛi agbo ni tsii.

english: Why do my maize plants grow tall and skinny with tiny cobs when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmli ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ? Mɛɛ be esa akɛ adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops compete fiercely with each other for light, water, and soil nutrients. Giving each plant enough space allows them to grow thick stalks and full cobs.
ga: Kɛ́ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso he ko ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ, ebaaha tsei lɛ aná ŋmeii ni mli tse kɛ ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Why do flower buds fall off my tomato plants without turning into fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsɔko aduawai lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when plants experience heat stress, irregular watering, or attacks from tiny insect pests. Keeping the soil evenly moist and providing mulch helps protect the blossoms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ mli be fɛɛ be loo tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ atuatsemɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaaha efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaye abua ni abu fɔfɔi lɛ ahe.

english: Why should I avoid planting maize on the exact same farm patch every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ matsi mihe kɛjɛ ŋmãa dumɔ he yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the same nutrients from the soil and allows specific pests and diseases to build up in the earth. Changing crops each season breaks pest life cycles and gives the soil time to recover.
ga: Tsei kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii kɛ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ yɛ be fɛɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela lɛ wala shihilɛ, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa be ni ekɛbaatsa ehe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crop lacks nitrogen, an essential soil nutrient needed for growth. Applying nitrogen fertilizer or well-rotted manure helps the plant build chlorophyll, turning the leaves green and boosting growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli ni he hiaa kɛha dalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ wo tsei lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee chlorophyll. Ehaa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni ehaa amɛdalɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: If your crops grow slowly, have pale leaves, or yield small harvests despite good rain, your soil lacks nutrients. Extension officers can test your soil, or you can watch for leaf discoloration to know which fertilizer to apply.
ga: Kɛji akɛ otsei lɛ daraa blɛoo, amɛyɛ baai ni tsuɔ, loo amɛwoɔ yibii fioo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Extension nitsulɔi baanyɛ aka oshikpɔŋ lɛ amɛkwɛ. Aloo obaanyɛ okwɛ bɔ ni baai lɛ ahe su tsakeɔ ehaa lɛ koni ole ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do small caterpillars chew holes inside the leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii miiye bu yɛ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ baai lɛ amli lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that targets maize leaves. Controlling them early using recommended insecticides or natural methods protects the growing tip of the plant so it can produce full corn ears.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ ŋmãa baai ahe. Amɛ nɔyeli mra Kɛ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo adebɔɔ mli gbɛi ni atsɔɔ akɛ atsuɔ he nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu tsei lɛ ashishifãi ahe koni enyɛ efee ŋmãa toi lɛ fɛɛ.

english: Why do extension officers advise me to plant plantain trees alongside my new cocoa saplings?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ wo ŋaa akɛ madu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ kookoo tsei heei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under intense sunlight. Fast-growing plantain trees have large leaves that provide living shade and keep the soil moist, protecting young cocoa during its fragile first few years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantain ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni haa hulutsoo ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ kookoo bibioo he kɛjɛɔ eklɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my tomato plants grow lots of big leafy branches but produce very few fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ niji kɛ baai wuji waa shi ewoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer makes plants focus on leaf growth instead of flowering. Balancing nitrogen with phosphorus and potassium encourages the crop to stop producing extra foliage and start setting fruit.
ga: Nitrogen ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi. Nitrogen kɛ phosphorus kɛ potassium ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkpaa baai krokomɛi ni amɛwoɔ lɛ ni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi.

english: Cassava roots starve of air and rot when submerged in standing water for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni amɛgboɔ kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni ekã shi be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: How can drip irrigation help my vegetable garden survive through the dry Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nu ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi aduawai abɔɔ lɛ ni ehi shi yɛ Harmattan hɔmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Drip irrigation delivers small amounts of water directly to crop roots through tubes. This saves water from evaporating into the dry air and keeps plants hydrated even when rainfall stops completely.
ga: Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ kɛ nu fioo ko baa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛtsɔɔ paipii anɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi mli. ni ehaa tsei lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa kwraa po.

english: Why should I buy certified hybrid seeds instead of using seeds saved from my previous harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mahe dumɔwui ni ji hybrid ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ moŋ fe ni mikɛ dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ baatsu nii?

english: Certified hybrid seeds are specifically bred to resist local pests, withstand dry periods, and yield more harvest. Saved seeds lose these strength traits over generations, leading to smaller yields.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni akɛwo mli ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui. Ehiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo bei amli ni ewoɔ babaoo Dumɔwui ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ laajeɔ nɛkɛ hewalɛ sui nɛɛ yɛ yinɔi babaoo amli. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nibii ni anáa lɛ fioo.

english: Why is it necessary to cut off extra branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni afo niji krokomɛi kɛjɛ kookoo tso ni eda lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning opens up the tree canopy to let in sunlight and air flow, which stops black pod disease from spreading in humid conditions and directs the tree's energy into growing bigger cocoa pods.
ga: Kpojiemɔ lɛ gbeleɔ tso lɛ shishi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ atsɔ mli. Enɛ baaye abua ni black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã hei ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. ni okɛ tso lɛ hewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo kookoo ŋmeii wuji amli.

english: Weeds compete directly with crops for nutrients, soil moisture, and sunlight. If weeds are left in the field, they steal the food your main crops need to grow big fruits and grains.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei yeɔ akaŋ tɛ̃ɛ kɛha niyenii mli hewalɛ. shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ hulu la kɛji akɛ ashi jwɛi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli Ebaaju niyenii ni he hiaa oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ aduawai wuji kɛ ŋmaa.

english: How can I tell if my crops are suffering from a disease or if they are just thirsty for water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ hela emɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ loo kumai miiye lɛ kɛkɛ?

english: Thirsty crops usually wilt in the hot afternoon sun and bounce back in the cooler evening, whereas diseased crops show spots, yellowing, or rot that remain on the leaves and stalks regardless of watering or time of day.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ gboɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, ni amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa yɛ gbɛkɛ ni mli ejɔ waa lɛ mli. yɛ be mli ni tsei ni hela emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ baajie ŋmɔtɔ kpo. Yellowing loo ŋmɔtɔ ni shwɛɔ yɛ baai kɛ tsei lɛ anɔ ni ekɔɔɔ nu ni akɛwoɔ mli loo gbi lɛ mli be he.

english: What causes small worms to eat holes in the leaves of my young maize plants, and how do I stop them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmei feɔ bibioo nɛkɛ? Mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ amli buji ni ayeɔ Ni te mafee tɛŋŋ makpa amɛ?

english: These are usually Fall Armyworms, which lay eggs on young leaves; checking the central funnel of the plant early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract prevents them from destroying the growing tip.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni woɔ amɛwui yɛ baai bibii anɔ. Tso lɛ teŋgbɛ nu lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni tso lɛ akafite ŋmeii ni miida lɛ.

english: Why does my land produce less corn now compared to when I first started farming on it years ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmãa faaa fe beni mibɔi okwaayeli afii babaoo ni eho nɛ lɛ?

english: Soil loses its natural nutrients over time when crops take up food from the earth season after season without adding compost, manure, or organic matter to rebuild the soil's strength.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ fiteɔ niyenii mli nibii yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli. Kɛji akɛ aha tsei niyenii yɛ be kɛ bei amli kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli fataaa he koni ekɛsaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ.

english: Maize leaves roll up as a natural self-defense mechanism to reduce the surface area exposed to the sun, preventing the plant from losing too much water through evaporation during dry spells.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Koni akɛba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni hulu la lɛ shɛɔ nɔ lɛ shi. Etsiɔ tsei anaa koni amɛkafite nu babaoo kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize plants turning yellow and dying even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgboiɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa moŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually show a lack of nitrogen, an essential plant food that fuels growth; adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps the plant regain its green color and strength.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa. ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa tsei lɛ daraa Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛfee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How can I safely store my harvested corn so insects do not destroy it before I can sell or eat it?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa lɛ ato shweshweeshwe koni kooloi akafite lɛ dani manyɛ mahɔ̃ɔ loo maye?

english: Drying the corn thoroughly until the kernels are hard, followed by storing them in airtight Purdue Improved Crop Storage (PICS) bags, suffocates insects and prevents weevils from damaging the grain.
ga: Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ŋmãa lɛ baafee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Nɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ji akɛ, kɛ́ akɛto Purdue Enhanced Crop Storage (PICS) kotokui ni akɛ ŋwɛi ŋtayaai ewo mli lɛ amli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafite dumɔwui lɛ.

english: How do I decide how much of my harvested crop to keep for my home before taking the rest to the market?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ mikpamɔ lɛ mlijaa enyiɛ ni mikɛbaato shia lɛ he dani mikɛ nɔ ni eshwɛ lɛ aya jara nɔ?

english: Calculate how many bags your household needs to eat each month until the next harvest season, set that amount aside in safe storage first, and only sell the remaining surplus so you do not have to buy food later at high prices.
ga: Buu kotokui enyiɛ ni he baahia oshia lɛ daa nyɔŋ nɔ kɛyashi kpamɔɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ he akɔntaa. Okɛ shika lɛ awo he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe klɛŋklɛŋ. ni ohɔ̃ɔ nɔ ni eshwɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ pɛ Bɔni afee ni ehe akahia ni ohé niyenii yɛ sɛɛ mli kɛ jara ni wa.

english: How do I know the exact right time to plant my seeds when the rains keep coming late?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ madu tsei beni nugbɔ lɛ miinɛ fiofio lɛ?

english: Wait until the soil receives a deep, soaking rain that penetrates well below the surface rather than planting after the very first light shower, which can cause seeds to sprout and dry up quickly if the rain stops.
ga: Mɛɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nugbɔ ni mli kwɔ ni ebote shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooodu yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi oya kɛji nugbɔ lɛ kpa nɛ.

english: Why is it better to buy certified seeds instead of saving seeds from my previous corn harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ? Mohu ɔ, i ngɔ dumɔwu komɛ kɛ je ye ngma kpami nɛ i kpata be ko nɛ be ɔ mi ɔ yi.

english: Certified seeds are specially selected to grow uniformly, resist local diseases, and produce higher yields, whereas seeds saved from previous harvests lose their vigor and produce smaller, unpredictable yields.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odaseyeli lɛ krɛdɛɛ koni amɛdara daa. local disease resistance ni ewoɔ yibii babaoo Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ ŋmaakpamɔi ni eho lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ baa shi ni ewoɔ yibii bibii ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ nɔ ni baaba.

english: Will planting cassava and maize together on the same farm harm the growth of my corn?
ga: Ani ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baaná ŋmãa lɛ dalɛ nɔ hewalɛ ni ehiii?

english: When planted with correct spacing, maize grows quickly and is harvested early, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes over the space later, allowing you to get two harvests from the same piece of land without harming either crop.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu kɛ he ni sa lɛ, Abɛi daa oya ni akpaa mra. yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni sɛɛ mli lɛ eŋɔ jɛmɛ. Enɛ haa onyɛɔ okpaa nii shii enyɔ kɛjɛɔ he kome ni oyeee ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko kwraa awui.

english: Can I just plant the same rice grains that I harvest and eat at home?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmaa ni mikpaa ni miyeɔ yɛ shia lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: While you can eat your harvested rice, planting grains kept specifically as seed ensures higher germination and healthier crops, because seed grains are carefully selected, dried, and stored to remain disease-free.
ga: Eyɛ mli akɛ obaanyɛ oye ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ moŋ Shi dumɔwui ni akɛtoɔ akɛ dumɔwui pɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ baaha ŋmãa lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, ahalaa dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ, agbiɔ amɛ ni akɛtoɔ koni hela akamɔ amɛ.

english: Why do agricultural officers encourage us to try new rice varieties instead of sticking to our traditional seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi miiwo wɔ hewalɛ koni wɔka ŋmãa henɔi heei wɔkwɛ moŋ fe ni wɔkɛ wɔhe aaakpɛtɛ wɔ blema dumɔwui lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: New rice varieties are bred by scientists to resist local pests, withstand dry conditions, mature faster, and yield more sacks of rice per acre compared to older traditional seeds.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi fɔɔ ŋmãa henɔ hee koni ekɛte shi ewo maŋ lɛ mli kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ Eŋmɛɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ anaa, ekwɛɔ oya ni ehaa ŋmãa kotokui babaoo yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto blema dumɔwui ni etsɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Does planting my rice in neat, straight rows really give me more yield than scattering seeds by hand?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo fe dumɔwui ni akɛ niji duɔ lɛ?

english: Planting in straight rows gives each rice plant equal access to sunlight, water, and soil nutrients while making weed control and harvesting much easier, leading to a bigger harvest.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ ŋwɛigbɛ ni ja lɛ haa ŋmãa tso fɛɛ ŋmãa naa hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa jwɛi lɛ anɔkwɛmɔ kɛ amɛkpamɔ feɔ mlɛo kwraa. Enɛ kɛ kpamɔ babaoo baa.

english: Why should I nurse my rice seeds in a small bed before transplanting them into the main field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ madu ŋmãa dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ lɛ? Dani obaafã kɛya ŋmãa ŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli?

english: Raising seedlings in a nursery bed protects young sprouts from pests, birds, and weeds, ensuring that only strong, healthy plants are transferred to your main farm.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akwɛɔ yɛ tsei akwɛmɔhei lɛ buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai, okpoi kɛ jwɛi ahe, ni ehaa tsei ni he wa ni yɔɔ hewalɛ pɛ ji nɔ ni ajieɔ kɛyaa oŋmɔ wulu lɛ mli.

english: What causes my rice stalks to bend and fall over flat on the ground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmãa toi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egbeeɔ shikpɔŋ dani akpaa?

english: Rice stalks fall over—a condition called lodging—when they receive too much nitrogen fertilizer, are planted too closely together, or face strong winds and heavy rains when the seed heads get heavy.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi, ni ji shihilɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ lodging, kɛ́ amɛná nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo. adu ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Aloo okɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kpeɔ beni dumɔwui lɛ ayitsei lɛ tsii.

english: Why are my rice grains falling off the heads onto the ground before I start harvesting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ dani kpamɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi lɛ?

english: Grain shattering happens when rice is harvested too late, gets overly dry in the sun, or if you are using a variety prone to dropping its seeds easily.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa mligbalamɔ baa kɛji kpamɔ lɛ eshɛ sɛɛ tsɔ. Hulu ni tsoɔ babaoo Aloo kɛji akɛ okɛ ŋmãa henɔ ko ni haa dumɔwui lɛ shwieɔ shi oya tsu nii.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer to my rice crop so I don't waste my money?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo ŋmɔji amli? No hewɔ lɛ, ofiteee shika?

english: Fertilizer works best when applied early during planting or transplanting, and again when the rice plant begins forming grain heads inside the stem, which is when it needs nutrients most.
ga: Kɛ akɛwo mli mra lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni aduɔ nii loo atsakeɔ Ni ekoŋŋ beni ŋmãa tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛnáa dumɔwui yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ. Be nɛɛ ji be ni niyenii mli hewalɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my rice field when birds start eating the grains right on the farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe beni okpoi jeɔ ŋmɔ mli ŋmaa lɛ yeli shishi lɛ?

english: Birds attack when rice grains are soft and milky. You can reduce damage by planting at the same time as neighboring farmers, scaring birds during early morning and late afternoon, or using shiny reflective tapes.
ga: Okpoi tutuaa kɛ́ ŋmaa lɛ mli efee blɛoo ni eyɛ su tamɔ mliki. Obaanyɛ oha nɔ ni efiteɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ bo lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ. Okpo gbee yɛ leebi maŋkpa kɛ shwane mli Aloo okɛ reflective tape ni kpɛɔ atsu nii.

english: How should I store my saved rice seeds so they stay good for planting next season?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ makɛ mi-ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ ato koni amɛhi lolo kɛha dumɔ yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli?

english: Store your seed rice in clean, airtight sacks or sealed containers kept on raised wooden pallets off the floor in a cool, dry room to protect them from moisture, mold, and insects.
ga: Kɛ ŋmaa ato kotokui ni he tse ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli loo tsɛnsii ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli ni akɛto tsei ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ yɛ tsu ko ni mli ejɔ ni mli egbi mli. Koni abu he kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ kooloi ahe.

english: Why do some rice varieties cook very soft and sticky while others stay hard and separate?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa henɔi komɛi feɔ bɔdɔɔ waa ni amɛkpɛɔ kɛji ahoo lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mɛi krokomɛi hu wa ni amɛtse amɛhe lɛ?

english: The cooking behavior depends on the type of starch inside the grain. Varieties with low starch stick together when cooked, while high-starch varieties remain firm and loose.
ga: Nihoomɔ su damɔ starch henɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmaa lɛ mli lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni starch faaa yɛ mli lɛ baakpɛtɛ he kɛji ahoo. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, ŋmeii srɔtoi ni starch babaoo yɔɔ mli lɛ baakã he ahi shi shiŋŋ ni amɛbaafee mlɛo.

english: How long can long-term tree crops like cocoa or cashew keep producing fruit on my farm if I care for them well?
ga: Be enyiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yeɔ afii babaoo tamɔ kookoo loo cashew nuts baanyɛ awo yibii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli kɛji mikwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Long-term tree crops are investments that can live and produce continuously for 10 to 14 years or more if you take good care of them and protect them from diseases.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ji shika ni akɛwoɔ mli ni baanyɛ ahi shi ni ewo yibii be fɛɛ be afii 10 kɛyashi 14 loo nɔ ni fe nakai kɛji okwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni otsi helai anaa.

english: Is it true that certain crops can give me continuous harvests for over ten years without needing to replant every season?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ tsei komɛi baanyɛ aya nɔ awo yibii fe afii nyɔŋma ni ehe ehiaaa ni adu amɛ ekoŋŋ daa be mli?

english: Yes, perennial tree crops remain in the soil for over a decade, giving you continuous growth and yields year after year as long as they stay healthy.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ ni fe afii nyɔŋma. Enɛ haa oyaa nɔ okwɛɔ ni owoɔ yibii afi fɛɛ afi, be fɛɛ be ni eyɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: What is the main difference between growing seasonal crops like maize and growing long-term tree crops?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ titri ni yɔɔ be mli nibii ni aduɔ, tamɔ ŋmãa, kɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni aduɔ lɛ teŋ?

english: Seasonal crops finish their life in a few months, while long-term tree crops stay on your land for 10 to 14 years, providing steady, long-term growth and yields if properly managed.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ be mli lɛ baafite yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, tsei ni yeɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ baahi oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afii 10 kɛyashi 14, ni amɛha amɛdalɛ kɛ yibiiwoo ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ baaha kɛji akɛ akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my neighbors' tree crops live and bear fruit for over ten years while mine die early?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikutsoŋnyo tso lɛ hi shi ni ewo yibii fe afii nyɔŋma yɛ be mli ni minɔ lɛ gbo oya lɛ?

english: Tree crops require regular attention and protection from sickness; trees that receive proper care and stay free from disease can live and stay productive for up to 14 years.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei anɔ daa ni abu amɛhe kɛjɛ helai ahe. Tsei ni akwɛ amɛ jogbaŋŋ ni hela bɛ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ ahi shi ni amɛwo yibii kɛyashi afii 14.

english: What happens to the lifespan of my crop trees if I ignore early signs of plant disease?
ga: Mɛni baaba mitsei lɛ awala be nɔ kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie mra be mli okadii ni tsɔɔ akɛ hela emɔ tsei lɛ anɔ?

english: Ignoring disease causes tree crops to weaken and die long before their full lifespan, preventing you from getting the 10 to 14 years of continuous harvests they can naturally produce.
ga: Helai ni akuɔ hiɛ ashwieɔ nɔ lɛ haa tsei kɛ tsei gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛgboiɔ be kakadaŋŋ dani amɛhiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ. Enɛ haaa ona adebɔɔ mli ŋmaa afii 10 kɛyashi 14.

english: How often should I inspect my permanent tree crops for pests and diseases?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ makwɛ mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ amli koni mana kɛji amɛyɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai?

english: You should check your crops regularly throughout the year so you can catch and treat sickness early, keeping the plants healthy enough to grow and produce for up to 14 years.
ga: Esa akɛ okwɛ oŋmɔshi nibii amli daa yɛ afi lɛ mli fɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ omɔ helai mra ni otsa amɛ. Ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ bɔ ni sa ni amɛdaraa ni amɛwoɔ yibii kɛyashiɔ afii 14.

english: How does keeping my farm clean and maintained help my tree crops survive for many years?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli ni mikwɛɔ koni ehe atse ni mikwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi afii babaoo?

english: Regular weeding, pruning, and disease monitoring protect the plants from stress and infection, allowing them to achieve continuous growth and reach a long life of 10 to 14 years.
ga: weeding pruning Ni helai ni akwɛɔ nɔ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei ahe kɛjɛɔ haomɔ kɛ helai ahe. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa be fɛɛ be ni amɛhiɔ shi afii 10 kɛyashi 14.

english: How do I make sure my soil stays fertile enough to support long-term crops for over ten years?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maná nɔmimaa akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ mli tse bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu ŋmɔshi nibii ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe afii nyɔŋma?

english: Applying compost, manure, or suitable fertilizers regularly replenishes soil nutrients, feeding long-term crops so they remain healthy and fruitful throughout their 10-to-14-year lifespan.
ga: Kɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ aba ekoŋŋ daa. Ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii niyenii ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ Koni tsei lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ ni ji afii 10 kɛyashi 14 lɛ mli.

english: If a long-term crop tree starts looking weak after a few years, can good care restore its growth?
ga: Kɛji tso ko ni ehi shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ bɔi tamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ yɛ afii fioo komɛi asɛɛ Ani kwɛmɔ kpakpa baanyɛ aha eda ekoŋŋ?

english: Yes, if the tree is not fatally diseased, providing good soil nutrition, clearing weeds, and treating sickness can revive it and keep it growing continuously for up to 14 years.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ bɛ hela ni naa wa. Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ niyenii kpakpai ni akɛhaa, jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli, kɛ helai ni atsaa lɛ baanyɛ aku sɛɛ aba shi ni ekwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be kɛyashi afii 14.

english: Why do extension officers compare taking care of tree crops to taking care of domestic animals?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi kɛ tsei akwɛmɔ toɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shia lɛ akwɛmɔ he lɛ?

english: Both require daily monitoring, proper nutrition, and protection from sickness over many years; with consistent care, both remain healthy and provide long-term benefits to your family.
ga: Enɛɛmɛi enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ biɔ ni akwɛ amɛ daa gbi. niyenii kpakpa kɛ helai atsimɔ afii babaoo. Kɛ́ okwɛ ohe be fɛɛ be lɛ, obaanyɛ oná hewalɛ kpakpa ni okɛ sɛɛnamɔi ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ aha oweku lɛ.

english: If I leave a few ripe cocoa pods on my trees after harvesting, will it affect my next crop?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ mishi kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ beni akpa kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ hu? Ani ebaana miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ hewalɛ?

english: Yes, leaving unharvested cocoa pods on the tree encourages pests like capsids and fungal diseases like Black Pod to grow. Cleaning the trees completely during harvest prevents these diseases from spreading to your next crop.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ashi kookoo ŋmeii ni akpako yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ewoɔ ŋmeii tamɔ capsids kɛ ŋmeii helai tamɔ black pods lɛ adalɛ he hewalɛ. Kɛ́ otsumɔ tsei lɛ ahe kwraa yɛ ŋmaakpamɔi lɛ ateŋ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai nɛɛ akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ amli.

english: This is usually caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives in wet and dark conditions. Regularly clearing weeds, pruning branches, and removing infected pods keeps the farm dry and protects your harvest.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ kɛ duŋ mli. weeding tree pruning Ni ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ daa lɛ baaha oŋmɔ lɛ agbi ni ebu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: My cocoa trees produced a huge harvest last season, but why are they producing very few pods this year?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ wo yibii babaoo yɛ afi ni ho lɛ mli. Shi mɛni hewɔ pods fioo ko pɛ je kpo yɛ afi nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Fruit trees go through cycles where a heavy harvest drains their stored energy. The tree needs time and nutrients to rest and recover; applying organic fertilizer and giving it adequate water helps it rebuild energy for the next big yield.
ga: Yibii tsei tsɔɔ sɛɛkuu mli he ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii ni akɛkpaa nii lɛ kɛ hewalɛ toɔ lɛ. Tsei he miihia be kɛ niyenii koni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe ni amɛhe awa amɛ. Organic fertilizer ni akɛaatsu nii kɛ nu ni fa ni sa ni akɛaaha lɛ baaye abua ni afee hewalɛ hee kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii wulu ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Does my farm land need to rest empty for a season after growing maize and vegetables?
ga: Ani esa akɛ miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ afee efolo kɛyashi be kome beni midu ŋmãa kɛ aduawai sɛɛ?

english: Yes, continuous farming removes essential nutrients from the soil. Letting the land rest (fallowing) or rotating crops with legumes like groundnuts allows the soil to naturally regain its nutrients and organic health.
ga: Hɛɛ, okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe (etsuɔ ​​nii) loo etsakeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni enáa ebɔɔ nii amli niyenii kɛ bɔɔ nii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ ahewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants droop and curl during the hot afternoon hours?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Cassava plants temporarily droop their leaves during peak heat to conserve water and protect themselves from harsh sunlight. It is a natural behavior that reduces moisture loss, and they usually recover by evening.
ga: Yucca tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he. Eji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ni haa ŋmɔtɔ ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi. ni bei pii lɛ, ehiɛ baa shi gbɛkɛ

english: Why should I use hybrid cocoa seeds instead of taking seeds directly from my best harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ hybrid cocoa beans atsu nii moŋ fe ni mana dumɔwui tɛ̃ɛ kɛjɛ mikpamɔ ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ mli?

english: Hybrid cocoa seeds are bred in research centers to produce pods much faster—usually in two to three years—and are designed to resist common diseases much better than traditional farm seeds.
ga: Akwɛɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni akɛfee ekome lɛ yɛ niiamlitaomɔ hei koni ekɛ ŋmeii aba oya kwraa. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ afii enyɔ kɛyashi etɛ. Ni afee amɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ jogbaŋŋ kwraa fe blema ŋmɔ mli dumɔwui.

english: Why are extension officers telling me to cut off green branches from my healthy cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɔ ni kwɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ kɛɛ mi akɛ mafolɔ mikoo tso ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ niji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Pruning removes non-fruitful branches so the tree doesn't waste energy maintaining extra leaves. It opens up the tree canopy to sunlight and fresh air, which encourages more flowering directly on the main trunk.
ga: Tso lɛ niji ni afoɔ lɛ jieɔ tsei niji ni wooo yibii lɛ koni tso lɛ akafite hewalɛ ni ekɛkwɛɔ baai ni fa fe nine lɛ nɔ. Ehaa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ gbeleɔ amɛhe kɛhaa hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa. Enɛ woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo hewalɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ yitso titri lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers dry up and drop off before they can grow into pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo fɔfɔi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi dani amɛdaraa amɛfeɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop off when the tree is under stress from dry weather, lack of soil nutrients, or insect damage. Ensuring adequate shade and applying proper fertilizer helps flowers turn into full pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ miigba tso lɛ naa. Niyenii ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi ni fiteɔ nii Kɛji akɛ hulutsoo ni sa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: How do I know if my cocoa trees are getting too much shade on my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ kookoo tsei lɛ miiná hulutsoo babaoo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: If your cocoa trees are tall with very few lower branches, or if you notice moss growing on the trunks and frequent Black Pod rot, your farm has too much shade and needs tall tree branches trimmed.
ga: Kɛji akɛ o-cocoa tso lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ niji ni baa shi fioo pɛ, Aloo kɛji akɛ bei pii lɛ onaa ŋmeii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tso lɛ shishi kɛ ŋmeii diji ni miifite lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli hulutsoo be babaoo ni ehe miihia ni afo tsei ni kwɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the ground when the heavy rainy season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot in waterlogged soil because standing water starves the roots of oxygen. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ ejaakɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ haaa kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni haa wala yibii lɛ anáa lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ atsɔ mli ni eye ebua ni ewaje shishifãi lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize turning yellow instead of staying green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which the crop needs to build strong green leaves, or the soil has too much water, suffocating the roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Biɛ ji he ni ehe hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii awo baai ni wa, ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji. loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu babaoo Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: What is causing small, ragged holes in the middle of my young corn leaves?
ga: Mɛni kɛ bu bibii ni etse ehe ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ baa?

english: Ragged holes in young corn leaves are usually caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars, which hide inside the leaf funnel and chew on tender leaves before the cob forms.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baa lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ baa bibii lɛ amli dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ŋmeii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni fãa yɛ ŋmei baai bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Tomato flowers often fall off when the plant experiences extreme heat, dry soil, or sudden changes in watering, which prevents the flower from successfully forming a fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nu ni akɛhaa lɛ tsake trukaa. Enɛ haaa fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in thin plants with small tubers instead of large roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei komɛi yɛ shishifãi bibii moŋ fe shishifãi wuji.

english: Why do farmers plant cowpea or beans together with maize on the same field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi duɔ tsina loo ŋmeii kɛfataa ŋmãa he yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Beans take nitrogen from the air and add it to the soil to nourish the maize, while maize provides a tall stalk that helps support the bean vines.
ga: Beans jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmãa lɛ aya hiɛ. Abele yɛ tsei kakadaji ni fiɔ bean wain tso lɛ sɛɛ.

english: Planting pepper in the same soil every season drains specific nutrients and allows pepper-specific pests and soil diseases to multiply, reducing your yields over time.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa be lɛ, ebaaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi ajɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ pepper pɔtɛɛ kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ helai babaoo. Enɛ haa nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do I need to clear weeds when my crops are still very small?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mafolɔ jwɛi lɛ be mli ni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ faaa lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young crops and will steal the water, sunlight, and nutrients your small plants need to establish strong root systems.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛbaaju nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa otsei bibii lɛ koni amɛma shishifãi ni wa.

english: Fertilizer works best when the soil is moist after a light rain, and during periods when crops are actively growing, such as two to three weeks after planting.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔ fioo ko sɛɛ. kɛ be mli ni tso lɛ miida lɛ, tamɔ otsii enyɔ loo etɛ sɛɛ beni adu lɛ

english: Why should I cut off the extra side branches growing on my tomato stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo tsei niji ni yɔɔ sɛɛgbɛ ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ tomato tsei anɔ lɛ?

english: Removing small side shoots helps the plant direct its energy and nutrients into growing bigger, healthier tomatoes rather than unnecessary stems and leaves.
ga: Afã tsei bibii ni afoɔ Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ hewalɛ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛkwɛ tomatoi wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsei kɛ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii lɛ

english: Why do the seeds I saved from my last harvest produce smaller yields than fresh seeds bought from the agro-dealer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni mikɛto kɛjɛ naagbee kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ woɔ yibii fioo fe dumɔwui heei ni ahe kɛjɛ okwaayeli jarayelɔ ko dɛŋ lɛ?

english: Saved seeds from modern crop varieties lose their vigor and disease resistance in the next generation, leading to weaker plants compared to fresh, certified seeds.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ato kɛjɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsei srɔtoi amli lɛ ahewalɛ kɛ helai ahe hewalɛ baa shi yɛ yinɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ akɛto dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my crops dry up and die so quickly even after a few days of heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gĩɔ ni amɛgboiɔ oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛ waa gbii babaoo po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops need steady moisture at their roots, not just occasional rain. If the soil cannot store water, heavy rain quickly runs off or evaporates, leaving plant roots dry again within a short time.
ga: Tsei lɛ hia nu ni mli edɔ daa yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli. Jeee nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ bei komɛi amli lɛ pɛ. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ahiɛ nu Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ oya loo etsɔɔ la. Enɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ be kukuoo mli.

english: How can I keep my crops alive during the dry season if there is no river or dam near my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli? Kɛji faa loo faa ko bɛ miŋmɔ lɛ masɛi?

english: You can harvest rainwater during the wet season using storage tanks, dig simple shallow farm ponds, or use dry grass as mulch to trap moisture in the soil around your plants.
ga: Obaanyɛ okɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ atsu nii ni okɛ nu ni akɛtoɔ nu mli lɛ atsu nii. Tsɔɔmɔ nubu ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ. Aloo okɛ jwɛi ni egbi atsu nii akɛ mulch koni ekɛha sũ ni bɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi.

english: Is it true that watering my crops in the middle of a hot day can hurt them?
ga: Ani eji anɔkwale akɛ nu ni ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ baanyɛ aye amɛ awui?

english: Yes, watering under intense midday sun causes water to evaporate rapidly before roots can drink it, and heat stress can harm the leaves. It is best to water early in the morning or late in the evening.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ afɔ nu yɛ hulutsoo be mli yɛ shwane mli lɛ, ebaaha nu lɛ atsɔ oya dani shishifãi lɛ anu. Ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ baanyɛ aye baai lɛ awui. Esa akɛ afɔ lɛ nu leebi loo gbɛkɛ.

english: Can giving my crops too much water actually damage them?
ga: Ani nu ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli fe nine lɛ baanyɛ akpata amɛhiɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Yes, excessive water drowns plant roots by removing air from the soil. This causes root rot, turns the leaves yellow, and can eventually kill the plant.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, nu babaoo shwieɔ tsei shishifãi anɔ kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ejieɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbo. baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɛ naagbee lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha tso lɛ agbo.

english: Why are my traditional planting months no longer giving me the good yields I used to get?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi kusum nyɔŋ ni mikɛduɔ nii lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai tamɔ tsutsu lɛ dɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Weather patterns are shifting, causing rains to start later or end earlier. To get good yields, farmers must adapt by changing planting dates and choosing crop varieties that mature quickly.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi haa nugbɔ nɛɔ sɛɛ mli loo egbeɔ naa mra fe bɔ ni eji daa lɛ. bɔni afee ni amɛná yibiiwoo kpakpa Ehe ebahia ni okwaafoi lɛ atsake amɛhe kɛtsɔ gbii ni amɛduɔ nii lɛ tsakemɔ kɛ tsei srɔtoi ni daa oya lɛ ni amɛhalaa lɛ nɔ.

english: What simple change can I make on my land to help the soil stay wet for longer periods?
ga: Mibaanyɛ matsake nibii mlɛo. yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni eye ebua ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ?

english: Covering the ground around your crops with dry leaves, straw, or grass—known as mulching—shades the soil from the hot sun and stops water from evaporating quickly.
ga: Mulching around Kɛ baai ni egbi, jwɛi loo jwɛi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ aha oŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Enɛ baaye abua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee shade kɛjɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni ebaatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekaho oya.

english: Why are agricultural officers telling us to stop burning our crop bushes after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he onukpai lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔkpa jwɛi ni ashãa kɛji akpa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ?

english: Burning crop leftovers destroys organic matter that acts like a sponge to hold water in the soil. Leaving crop residues to rot naturally enriches the soil and improves moisture retention.
ga: Nibii ni eshwɛ ni ashãa lɛ fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji ni haa nu hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni amɛgboi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ fɛo ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which crops are best for me to plant if my area receives very little rainfall?
ga: Mɛɛ tsei hi jogbaŋŋ akɛ makwɛ kɛji nugbɔ fioo pɛ nɛɔ yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ?

english: Crops like cassava, millet, sorghum, and specially bred drought-tolerant maize require much less water to grow and can survive extended dry spells better than leafy vegetables.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa ni nyɛɔ eŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ nɔ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ. Eheɔ nu fioo kwraa dani enyɛɔ ekwɛ̃ɔ. Ni ebaanyɛ ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli be kakadaŋŋ fe aduawai ni baai yɔɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I fetch water for my farm without getting into conflicts with neighboring farmers who share the same stream?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mafo nu kɛha miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛ okwaafoi ni bɛŋkɛ mi ni kɛ faa kome lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii lɛ bɛ béi?

english: Farmers can form a water-sharing schedule and adopt water-saving tools like drip kits or watering cans, ensuring everyone gets a fair share without drying up the stream.
ga: Okwaafoi baanyɛ afee nu mlijaa he gbɛjianɔtoo ni amɛkɛ nibii ni akɛbuɔ nu he tamɔ drip irrigation kits loo nu ni akɛshwieɔ nu nɔ lɛ atsu nii. Enɛ haa mɔ fɛɛ mɔ nine shɛɔ egbɛfaŋnɔ ni sa nɔ ni faa lɛ gĩii.

english: Can I tap into underground water for my crops if government dams cannot be built in my area?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu atsu nii kɛdu ŋmɔshi nibii? Kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ ama nɔyeli dam yɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ

english: Yes, where big dams are not possible, digging small hand-dug wells or shallow tube wells lets you tap underground water safely to irrigate your fields.
ga: Hɛɛ, yɛ shihilɛi ni anyɛɛɛ ama faa agbo mli lɛ amli. Kɛ́ otsa nubu bibioo ko ni akɛ niji tsu loo nu bu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ, ebaaha okɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ atsu nii shweshweeshwe ni okɛshwie oŋmɔji lɛ anɔ nu.

english: Why does my rice crop take almost a whole year to mature while my neighbor harvests twice in a year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa lɛ heɔ afi lɛ mli be babaoo ni ekɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋbii lɛ kpaa lɛ shii enyɔ yɛ afi mli lɛ?

english: Different rice varieties have different growth cycles; some are long-duration varieties that take up to a year and rely on natural rainy seasons, while short-duration varieties mature in a few months if you have good irrigation.
ga: Omɔ henɔ fɛɛ henɔ yɛ bɔ ni edaraa ehaa. Ekomɛi ji kooloi ni hiɔ shi be kukuoo ni hiɔ shi kɛyashiɔ afi, ni amɛdamɔ adebɔɔ mli nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ nɔ. Yɛ be mli ni be kukuoo mli henɔi lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi amli kɛji oyɛ nu kpakpa.

english: Why do my maize plants die when water sits on the field, but my rice thrives in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ gboiɔ be mli ni nu yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ? Shi ani mi-ŋmãa lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃ yɛ nu ni yɔɔ kpoo mli?

english: Rice plants have special air channels in their stems that allow their roots to breathe underwater, whereas maize roots drown and rot if they sit in flooded soil for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ baagbee nu mli ni amɛbaafite kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: How does using droppings from my chicken farm help my maize grow bigger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni jɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ ni mikɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ?

english: Chicken manure is rich in nitrogen and essential nutrients that feed the soil, helping crops build strong stems and healthy green leaves naturally.
ga: Nitrogen kɛ niyenii ni he hiaa ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛ babaoo yɛ tsina ŋmɔ mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants roll up tight during the middle of the day?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize plants curl their leaves during hot afternoon sun to protect themselves from losing moisture, helping the plant stay hydrated until the weather cools down.
ga: Abɛi tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni baa shi lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ.

english: Can I grow rice and maize on the exact same plot of land at the same time?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ yɛ be kome mli?

english: It is better to separate them because rice prefers wet, low-lying land that holds water, while maize needs well-drained sloping soil where excess water can run off.
ga: Esa akɛ ajie amɛ kɛjɛ mli ejaakɛ ŋmãa sumɔɔ hei ni nu yɔɔ ni nu ŋmɛɔ shi. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa he miihia shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ, ni etse ehe banee, he ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ baanyɛ atsɔ mli.

english: Why do armyworms attack my young maize leaves so aggressively compared to other wild grass nearby?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii lɛ tutuaa mi-baby corn baai lɛ waa fe koo mli jwɛi krokomɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ?

english: Young maize leaves are soft, juicy, and full of nutrients, making them a preferred food source for pests compared to tough wild grass.
ga: Baby corn baa lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ, eyɛ nu ni niyenii mli hewalɛ eyi mli obɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ niyenii ni tsɛŋemɔ helai sumɔɔ waa kɛ akɛto koo mli jwɛi ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahe.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields if I plant maize on the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛji midu ŋmãa yɛ he kome daa afi lɛ?

english: Maize heavy-feeds on specific soil nutrients, so planting it continuously drains the soil; rotating with crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores those missing nutrients.
ga: Akɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ komɛi ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ haa ŋmãa waa. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmãa ni aya nɔ adu lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu atsɔ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni atsakeɔ lɛ baaye abua ni aku sɛɛ aha nakai niyenii ni elaaje lɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my young rice plants grow thin and yellow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiha mi ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ miifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛmiifee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow faster than young rice and steal the sunlight, water, and soil food that your crop needs to develop strong stems and green leaves.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei bibii ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he hiaa otsei lɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: If I plant seeds saved from my last maize harvest, why is the yield lower than when I buy fresh certified seeds?
ga: Kɛji midu dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ naagbee ŋmãa kpamɔ lɛ mli Mɛni hewɔ yibiiwoo lɛ baa shi beni miheɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ?

english: Seeds saved from hybrid harvests lose their vigor and disease resistance over time, while fresh certified seeds are specially bred to produce high yields every time.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpaa lɛ amli lɛ hewalɛ kɛ helai ahewalɛ baa shi yɛ be ni sa mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, akwɛɔ dumɔwui heei ni awo he odase lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ ko nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo be fɛɛ be.

english: Why do my maize plants need the flowers at the top to produce corn cobs on the side?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ he hiaa fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ koni amɛwo ŋmãa yɛ amɛsɛɛgbɛ lɛ?

english: The top flower releases pollen that must drop onto the sticky silks of the cob below; without this pollen transfer, the corn cob will not form full kernels.
ga: Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ jieɔ pollen ni esa akɛ efo kɛya siliki ni wa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji nɛkɛ pollen transfer nɛɛ bɛ lɛ, Abɛi ŋmeii lɛ wooo ŋmeii ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yes, you can plant them together because maize grows quickly and is harvested in about three months, while cassava grows slowly at first and takes longer to mature. By the time cassava needs the full space, your maize will already be harvested.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ okɛ amɛ afee ekome ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa yɛ aaafee nyɔji etɛ mli. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei daa blɛoo yɛ shishijee mli ni ekɛ be babaoo tsuɔ nii dani edaa lɛ. Be mli ni ŋmãa lɛ he hiaa he ko ni eyi obɔ lɛ Agbɛnɛ akpa Oŋmãa lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen is the plant food that gives leaves their deep green color and helps the stalk grow tall and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn tsei lɛ kɛha nitrogen ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Nitrogen ji tso niyenii ni haa baai lɛ feɔ eŋɔli ni eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa ni amɛhe wa.

english: Fertilizer is like dry powder that crops can only drink through water. If you put fertilizer on dry soil, the heat can burn the plant roots, or the fertilizer will sit on top without helping the crop until moisture melts it into the ground.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ tamɔ powda ni egbi ni tsei baanyɛ anu kɛtsɔ nu pɛ nɔ. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi. Aloo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baata nɔ ni eyeee ebuaaa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛyashi ŋmɔtɔ lɛ baatsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli.

english: Curling pepper leaves usually happen when tiny insects like aphids or mites are sucking the sap from under the leaves. When these pests drink the plant's juice, the leaves shrink and curl up.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, pepper leaf curl lɛ baa kɛji kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites lɛ nu nu ni jɛɔ baa lɛ shishi lɛ mli. Kɛji nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ nu nu kɛjɛ tsei amli lɛ, Baai lɛ baagbɔjɔ ni amɛbaakpãtã.

english: Why do white spots appear on my cassava leaves, and why are the leaves shrinking?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ yɛ ŋmeii yɛŋ lɛ? Ni mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ?

english: This is a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. The disease stops the leaves from catching sunlight properly, which means the plant cannot make enough food to grow big cassava roots.
ga: Enɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa Hela nɛɛ haaa baai lɛ aná hulu la ni sa. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaakwɛ ŋmeii wuji.

english: If yam seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight over the same water and soil nutrients. This results in many small, light tubers instead of large, heavy yams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ baatswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni fa tamɔ nu kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔŋŋ. Enɛ haa anáa ŋmeii bibii ni tsiimɔ waaa yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii lɛ najiaŋ.

english: Why is it bad if weeds grow close to the stem of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji jwɛi kwɛ̃ yɛ mi tomato tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ ahe lɛ?
