english: Weeds act like thief neighbors that steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients meant for your tomatoes. They also shelter insects and sicknesses that can easily jump onto your tomato plants.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ julɔi kɛjɛɔ okutsoŋbii lɛ adɛŋ, ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha o-tomato lɛ mli. Ehaa kooloi bibii kɛ helai ni baanyɛ atsɔ o-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ oya lɛ hu aná he ko amɛhi.

english: When the weather gets too hot and dry, the tomato plant gets stressed and drops its flowers to save its own water and energy, preventing it from producing fruits until conditions improve.
ga: Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni egbi Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ ni amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu nu kɛ hewalɛ he yɛ amɛhe. Tsi yibiiwoo naa kɛyashi shihilɛ lɛ baafee jogbaŋŋ.

english: How can I tell that my groundnuts are fully grown underground and ready to harvest?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-ŋmeii lɛ edara yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Groundnuts are usually ready when the green leaves start turning yellow and dry up. You can also dig up one plant as a test; if the inside of the shells has dark brown markings instead of white, they are ready.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ efee klalo beni baai eŋɔli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ. Obaanyɛ otsa tso kome ni okɛka lɛ okwɛ. Kɛji akɛ ŋshɔŋloo lɛ mli lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni tsuɔ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ najiaŋ. Tsɔɔmɔ akɛ ofee klalo.

english: Why does it take several years for cocoa trees to start producing good pods after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ afii babaoo dani cacao tsei lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛwoɔ ŋmeii kpakpai beni midu amɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees need time to build a strong root network and sturdy branches before they can support heavy pods. In the first few years, all their energy goes into growing strong roots and leaves so they can sustain high yields for decades later.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ he miihia be ni amɛkɛma shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ niji ni mli wa dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛye amɛbua ŋmeii ni tsii lɛ. Yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli lɛ, akɛ hewalɛ nɛɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni akɛwo shishifãi kɛ baai ni wa. koni enyɛ ekwɛ yibiiwoo ni fa babaoo nɔ afii nyɔŋmai abɔ ni baa lɛ

english: Why do my cassava leaves turn yellow during the rainy season even when there is plenty of water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli eyɛ mli akɛ nu babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ moŋ?

english: Yellow leaves often mean the plant is lacking key nutrients like nitrogen, or the soil has become waterlogged. When water covers the roots for too long without air, the plant cannot absorb food properly despite the abundance of moisture.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ bɛ niyenii kpakpai, tamɔ nitrogen, loo akɛ nu eyi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Beni nu ha shishifãi lɛ anɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ mli. Tsei nyɛŋ aŋɔ niyenii jogbaŋŋ kɛji ŋmɔtɔ babaoo po yɛ mli.

english: Why do my food crops grow very tall with thin stems when I plant them under big shade trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miniyenii tsei lɛ daraa babaoo ni amɛyɛ ŋmeii bibii beni midu amɛ yɛ tsei wuji ni haa hulutsoo lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: When crops do not get direct sun, they stretch upward quickly to search for light. Because they use all their energy just to grow tall, their stems stay thin and weak, and they produce very little fruit.
ga: Kɛ tso lɛ enine shɛɛɛ hulu la nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ tso lɛ shwieɔ ehe oya kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni eyatao la. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ amɛtso lɛ mli tsei ni amɛhe waaa. ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo ko pɛ.

english: Why do caterpillars attack my maize leaves as soon as the young plants come up after the rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tutuaa mi-abele baa lɛ kɛji dumɔwui lɛ je kpo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ pɛ?

english: Pest eggs live through the dry season in weeds and soil. As soon as the rainy season starts and young, tender maize leaves emerge, the eggs hatch quickly because the fresh leaves provide easy food for the growing caterpillars.
ga: Pest ŋmeii hiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ mli. Kɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ je shishi ni ŋmãa baai bibii je kpo pɛ kɛkɛ, Akpɔlɔi lɛ baafɔ oya ejaakɛ baa heei lɛ haa ŋmeii ni miida lɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo.

english: Why do the flowers on my tomato plants dry up and drop off without forming any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni amɛfeee tomato ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the plant experiences stress from high heat or dry soil. When the crop gets too stressed by heat, it drops its flowers to save water and keep itself alive instead of making fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo shikpɔŋ ni egbi. Kɛ́ tsei miihao kɛjɛ latsaa ni fa fe nine mli Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛaawo yibii lɛ, fɔfɔii shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu nu he ni amɛha amɛhe ahi wala mli.

english: Why are my yam tubers coming out small and bent even though the vines on top look healthy?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni amɛbɔle amɛhe eyɛ mli akɛ wain tso ni yɔɔ nɔ lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ lɛ?

english: Yam tubers grow deformed or small when the soil underground is too hard and compact for the root to expand downward freely. Healthy leaves show the plant is feeding, but hard ground stops the tuber from swelling properly.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni ehiii loo amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ amɛshishi lɛ mli wa tsɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ amɛhe kɛya shi. Baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ miiye nii. Shi shikpɔŋ ni wa baaha bulb lɛ akafu jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why is it risky for me to plant my seeds after the very first rain in April?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ mihe baawo oshara mli akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛ yɛ April mli lɛ sɛɛ?

english: The very first rain of the season is often followed by a short dry spell. If your seeds sprout after that first shower and then face weeks without rain, the young seedlings will dry up and die in the hot sun.
ga: Nugbɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ be kuku sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ odumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ ni nugbɔ enɛɛɛ otsii babaoo. Tsei bibii baagbi ni amɛbaagboi yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli.

english: Why does planting cassava on the exact same plot three times in a row make the ground weak?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ shii etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbɔjɔɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots draw heavy amounts of nutrients out of the earth to grow large tubers. Planting it continuously on the same land drains those nutrients away without giving the soil time or manure to rebuild its strength.
ga: Cassava shishifãi jieɔ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛfeɔ ŋmeii wuji. Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ lɛ haa nakai niyenii mli nibii lɛ hoɔ ni ehaaa sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ be ni ekɛtswa ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds grow back so much faster than my pepper plants after I clear my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe mi-pepper tsei lɛ beni mijie ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Wild weeds are native plants that are naturally tough and adapted to quickly grab water and sun from the soil. Cultivated crops like pepper need extra care because they grow more slowly than wild bush plants.
ga: Koo mli jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni amɛhe wa ni amɛtsake amɛhe koni amɛgbala nu kɛ hulu la kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ oya. Tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmeii biɔ hiɛdɔɔ krɛdɛɛ ejaakɛ amɛdaraa blɛoo fe ŋmɔ mli tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why do I harvest fewer cocoa pods when I plant my trees very close together to fit more on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpaa kookoo ŋmeii fioo pɛ kɛ́ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe koni ekɛ he ni miyɔɔ lɛ akpã gbee jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: When cocoa trees are overcrowded, their leaves block sunlight from each other and their roots fight for food in the soil. Overcrowding also traps humidity, which encourages fungal diseases like black pod to destroy your yield.
ga: Kɛji kookoo tso lɛ mli eyi tsɔ lɛ Baai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la ni jɛɔ kookoo tso lɛ nɔ lɛ naa. ni shishifãi lɛ baatswa niyenii he akaŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Nibii ni eyi obɔ lɛ hu mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Enɛ woɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai tamɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai diji lɛ hewalɛ koni amɛfite onibii.

english: Why are the leaves on my newly planted cocoa trees turning brown and drying up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-cocoa tso ni midu ehee lɛ nɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛmiigbi lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot withstand harsh direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains next to them protects the tender leaves from sunburn and keeps the surrounding soil moist.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa waa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains ni yɔɔ Emasɛi lɛ adumɔ baabu baai bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulutsoo he, ni ebaaye ebua ni shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop most of their flowers before any pods form?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ miifɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ateŋ babaoo shi dani ŋmeii lɛ feɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they are stressed by long dry spells, excessive shade, or a lack of nutrients in the soil. Proper pruning and soil feeding help the tree hold onto its flowers.
ga: Cocoa tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛkpe yɛ hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ lɛ mli. hulu la ni fa fe nine loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Tso lɛ ni afoɔ jogbaŋŋ kɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛhaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the key nutrient plants need to grow healthy green leaves and big corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why does my land produce smaller crop yields every year even when I use the same seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii fioo daa afi eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ tsuɔ nii moŋ?

english: Farming the same piece of land continuously removes natural nutrients from the soil over time. Allowing the land to rest or rotating crops helps replenish soil fertility.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ nitsumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ jieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni akɛhaa hejɔɔmɔ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ shweremɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I put fertilizer right at the base of my plant's stem?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mitso lɛ shishigbɛ lɛ?

english: Placing concentrated fertilizer directly against the stem can burn the plant's tissue and roots. Spreading it a few inches away allows the roots to safely draw in the nutrients.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni mli wa wo tso lɛ shishi tɛ̃ɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tso lɛ fãji kɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ agbɛ ashwã inchi fioo ko lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbalaa niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why are my cassava tubers rotting under the ground before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays in the soil around them for too long. Planting cassava on raised soil ridges helps rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa ni ehi shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmeii ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: How can I keep my vegetable crops from drying out during short dry spells?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ matsi mi-vegetables lɛ anaa koni amɛkagbi yɛ be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ be mli?

english: Covering the soil around your plants with dry leaves or straw, known as mulching, traps moisture in the ground and prevents the sun from drying out the root zone.
ga: Ale shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle otsei lɛ ahe lɛ ni okɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni ehaa hulu la lɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ agbi.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm, a pest caterpillar that hides inside the central funnel of maize plants and feeds on new leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ gbɛjegbɛi lɛ amli ni eyeɔ baai heei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: How do weeds actually harm my crops if I leave them in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baanyɛ aye miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui eha tɛŋŋ kɛji mishi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds steal vital sunlight, water, and soil nutrients away from your crops, which starves your main plants and leads to low crop yields.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni he hiaa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why is it harmful to plant my seeds very close to each other in the row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji oshara akɛ aaadu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ sɛɛkuu mli lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too closely together, the growing plants compete with each other for food and light, resulting in thin, weak stalks and small harvests.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii kɛ la he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ feɔ mlɛo, ni amɛhe waaa, ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo.

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential food for plant growth, or that heavy rains have washed nutrients away from the root area.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-corn lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Aloo nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ efo niyenii mli nibii ni haa tsei lɛ shishifãi lɛ yɔɔ lɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and gives pests that feed on maize a permanent place to live and multiply.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be. ni ehaa kooloi ni yeɔ ŋmãa lɛ feɔ shihilɛhei ni hiɔ shi daa ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: What is the difference between manure from my animals and the bag fertilizer from the shop?
ga: Mɛni ji srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ mi kooloo ŋmei kɛ kotoku mli ŋmei ni jɛ shwapo lɛ mli lɛ teŋ?

english: Animal manure feeds your plants slowly while improving the soil's ability to hold water, whereas bag fertilizer gives plants a fast, powerful boost of nutrients but does not build up the soil long-term.
ga: Manure haa otsei lɛ niyenii fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ehiɛɔ nu mli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ kotoku mli lɛ haa tsei lɛ náa niyenii mli hewalɛ oya lɛ, amɛtswaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my yam seeds very close together in the mound?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa yɛ gɔŋ ko mli lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close together, their roots fight over water, food, and sunlight, which leaves you with many tiny tubers instead of large, healthy yams.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la he akaŋ, ni no haa onáa ŋmeii bibii babaoo yɛ ŋmeii wuji ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ.

english: You should plant your cassava cuttings after the first two or three steady rains have deeply soaked the ground, ensuring the soil stays moist enough for roots to sprout without drying out.
ga: Esa akɛ odu ŋmei ni afo lɛ beni klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔi fioo ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ eha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli edɔ waa lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ ji koni shikpɔŋ lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ adara ni amɛgbiŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wither and drop their leaves during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ miiho ni amɛmiigbee shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: In extreme afternoon heat, pepper leaves lose water faster than the roots can suck it up from the dry ground, causing the plant to wilt to protect itself from drying out completely.
ga: Yɛ shwane ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, Pepper baai lɛ laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ. Ha tso lɛ agbo koni ekɛtsi ehe gbɛ koni ekagbi kwraa.

english: Very high temperatures or lack of water cause stress to the plant, making it drop its blossoms to save energy rather than spending resources on producing tomatoes.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Ha tsei afee fɔfɔi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite moŋ fe ni okɛ nibii ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ baatsu nii kɛfee tomato.

english: Curled, yellow-patterned leaves are a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, a sickness carried from plant to plant by tiny whiteflies that suck the plant's juices.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji cassava mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. Enɛ ji hela ko ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies ni nuɔ tsei amli nu kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa tso kroko nɔ lɛ kɛbaa.

english: What causes tiny holes in my cabbage leaves and how does it hurt my crop?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ kaabeji baai anɔ Ni te eyeɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ awui ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Caterpillars and beetles eat through the leaves to feed themselves, which weakens the plant because it needs whole leaves to catch sunlight and grow a solid cabbage head.
ga: Kplukai kɛ ŋmeii yeɔ baai koni amɛkɛye amɛhe niyenii. Enɛ haa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ejaakɛ ehe miihia ni tso lɛ baa muu lɛ fɛɛ aná hulu la ni ekwɛ̃ ni etsɔ kaabe yitso ni hi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow slower even if I water the farm regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwereɔ blɛoo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ nu haa miŋmɔ lɛ mli daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds act like thief plants that aggressively steal soil food, root space, and water away from your crops, leaving your actual farm plants weak and malnourished.
ga: Jwɛi feɔ amɛnii tamɔ tsei ni juɔ, ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ shikpɔŋ niyenii, shishifãi ahe gbɛ, kɛ nu kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Nɔ ni jɛ mli ba ji akɛ, tsei ni yɔɔ oŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛnáaa niyenii kpakpa.

english: Why do my maize leaves roll up tight during the dry hot afternoons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ miitso waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize leaves curl up as a natural defense mechanism to reduce water loss through evaporation when it is hot. Covering the soil around the plants with dry leaves or straw helps trap moisture in the soil so the crop stays hydrated.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ shwieɔ shi akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni baaha nu ni laajeɔ lɛ aba shi kɛtsɔ la ni hoɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ baai ni egbi loo jwɛi shwie tso lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli bɔni afee ni tso lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Is it better for me to water my tomato crop early in the morning or late in the afternoon?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ mawo mi-tomato tsei lɛ anɔ nu leebi loo shwane mli?

english: Watering early in the morning is best because it gives the roots time to absorb water before the heat of the day causes evaporation. It also gives wet leaves time to dry, which prevents fungal diseases from growing.
ga: Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli leebi lɛ hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ ehaa shishifãi lɛ náa be ni amɛkɛnuɔ nu lɛ dani gbi lɛ mli latsaa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Ehaa baai ni efɔ lɛ hu be ni amɛgbi. Enɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli lɛ akaya hiɛ.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that burn under full sun and dry winds. Planting fast-growing shade crops like plantain beside them protects the soil water and keeps the young trees cool.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa yɛ hulu kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ lateral plantains lɛ adumɔ Ebaaye ebua ni ebu nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he ni eha tsei bibii lɛ afee fɛ̃i.

english: Why should I wait for the major rains to fully start before planting my cassava stems?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ akpa dani madu ŋmei tsei?

english: Cassava stem cuttings need constant soil moisture to grow roots and fresh shoots. If planted in dry soil, the heat will dry out the stem cut before it can establish itself.
ga: Kasava tso ni afo lɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ejɔ daa koni shishifãi kɛ ŋmeii heei akwɛ̃. Kɛji akɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ Dɔlɛ lɛ baaha tsei ni afo lɛ agbi dani amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi.

english: How does making ridges across my sloped farm help my crops get enough water?
ga: Te ŋshɔkei ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ ni etse ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa lɛ aha tɛŋŋ?

english: Building mounds or ridges across a slope traps rainwater so it sinks slowly into the soil near the roots instead of running off down the hill and carrying away topsoil.
ga: Gɔji loo ŋshɔkei ni afee yɛ ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ bɔni afee ni eho blɛoo. Okɛ ohe awo shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Mohu ɔ, e hoɔ kɛ jeɔ yoku ɔ mi nɛ e ngɔɔ zugba nɛ ngɛ yi mi ɔ kɛ yaa.

english: Why do my pepper plants yield smaller fruits when I plant them too close to each other?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ woɔ yibii bibii beni mikɛ amɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too close, their roots compete heavily for the limited water and nutrients in the soil, leaving each plant with less energy to develop big, healthy fruits.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ akaŋshii mli waa koni amɛná nu kɛ niyenii ni fa fioo ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náaa hewalɛ babaoo ni ekɛbaawo yibii wuji ni mli wa.

english: Why does rice grow well in flooded fields while my maize rots and dies in standing water?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ ŋmãa ŋmɔji ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ be mli ni mi-abele lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ yɛ nu ni ekã shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Rice plants have special internal air channels that allow air to reach their roots underwater, whereas maize roots suffocate and rot when water stays pooled around them for too long.
ga: Omɔ tsei yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui krɛdɛɛi ni haa kɔɔyɔɔ shɛɔ nu shishi shishifãi lɛ ahe. Shi yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, ŋmãa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛ́ nu bua amɛhe naa be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ.

english: Why do my garden egg plants drop their flowers during a hot dry stretch?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii tsei ni yɔɔ mibɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔii yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ?

english: When plants do not get enough water, they enter survival mode and drop their flowers to save moisture, which prevents them from making fruits until water is available again.
ga: Kɛ tsei lɛ enine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ lɛ Amɛyaa wala shihilɛ mli ni amɛjieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Enɛ haaa etsu nii kɛyashi nu baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil between my vegetable rows with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni yɔɔ aduawai akutsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Mulching bare soil with dry grass acts like a blanket that blocks the direct sun, keeping the soil cool and stopping soil water from evaporating quickly into the air.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni tsiɔ hulu la ni baa tɛ̃ɛ lɛ naa. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Can I use water from a stream running near a sprayed field to water my vegetables?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ nu ni jɛɔ faa ko ni hoɔ yɛ mi-spray ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii kɛfɔ mi-aduawai lɛ anɔ nu?

english: No, stream water that contains runoff from chemical sprays can harm delicate vegetable roots, destroy beneficial soil life, and make your harvested food unsafe to eat.
ga: Dabi, nu ni jɛɔ faa mli ni tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shi lɛ mli hoɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye aduawai shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ awui. efiteɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ wala ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ ni ehaa niyenii ni okpa lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade to protect their soft leaves from direct, hot sunlight. Leaving some tall trees or planting fast-growing shade crops like plantains protects the young cocoa until it becomes strong enough to withstand full sun.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ hia hulutsoo koni amɛbu amɛbaai bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ hulu la ni mli edɔ ni shɛɔ amɛ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. tsei ni kwɔlɔ ni ashiɔ Aloo tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya, tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni ebu kookoo tsei bibii ahe kɛyashi amɛhe baawa bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ naa.

english: Why do the leaves on my maize plants turn pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abɛi tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is running out of nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to build strong stems and healthy green leaves. Adding animal manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps restore their deep green color and vigor.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛná tsei ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha amɛhe su ni mli kwɔ kɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ.

english: What causes my cassava roots to rot in the ground before I get the chance to harvest them?
ga: Mɛni haa ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani amɛnáa hegbɛ ni amɛkpaa amɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays waterlogged for too long, allowing fungal diseases to attack the tubers. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away and keeps the roots healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu ehi shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii helai tutuaa ŋmeii lɛ. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ waa.

english: Why do my tomato plants drop their flowers without forming any fruit during the hot, dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miifɔlɔ ni amɛwooo yibii yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms when they suffer from intense heat and drought stress. Watering them regularly at the base and covering the surrounding soil with dried grass keeps the roots cool enough for the flowers to set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji amɛmiipiŋ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa kɛ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mli. Nu ni afɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ nɔ daa ni akɛ jwɛi ni egbi shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔ ni sa koni fɔfɔii lɛ anyɛ akwɛ.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds very close to one another in the same row?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii akɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe yɛ ŋmãa kome mli lɛ?

english: When maize seeds are planted too close together, their roots fight each other for soil nutrients and water, while their leaves block sunshine from reaching neighbors. Giving them proper space allows each stalk to grow thick and yield bigger cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Amɛshishifãi lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ kɛ nu mli lɛ. yɛ be mli ni amɛbaai lɛ tsiɔ hulu la naa koni ekashɛ amɛkutsoŋbii lɛ ahe. Kɛ́ aha he ko ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tso lɛ eko fɛɛ eko afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ekɛ ŋmeii wuji aba.

english: Why should I prune or cut off extra small branches from my mature cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafolɔ loo mafolɔ tsei niji bibii lɛ? Ani oooshi kookoo tso ni eda kwraa?

english: Cutting away extra or dead branches opens up the canopy so sunlight and fresh air can flow through the tree. This airflow stops fungal diseases like black pod from spreading and encourages the tree to grow more pods.
ga: Niji ni fa fe nine loo ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ gbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ naa koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa atsɔ tso lɛ mli. Nɛkɛ kɔɔyɔɔ nɛɛ haa ŋmeii helai tamɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛfaŋnɔ kpaa, ni ewoɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ ni ewo ŋmeii babaoo.

english: How do I know the right time to sow my crop seeds when the major rainy season begins?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be ni sa ni esa akɛ adu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be ni fe fɛɛ lɛ shishijee mli?

english: You should sow your seeds after the soil has received two or three heavy, steady rains so that the ground is deep wet. Planting too early into dry soil after just one light shower can burn seeds before they sprout.
ga: Esa akɛ odu dumɔwui lɛ beni shikpɔŋ lɛ ená nugbɔ ni naa wa shii enyɔ loo etɛ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ sɛɛ bɔni afee ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔtɔ waa. Kɛ́ adu mra tsɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã dumɔwui lɛ dani amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do some extension officers advise covering the soil around crops with dried grass?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi komɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ akɛ jwɛi ni egbi awo shikpɔŋ ni bɔle ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Covering the ground with dry leaves or grass—known as mulching—acts like a blanket. It stops moisture from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the soil cool, and prevents stubborn weeds from popping up.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egbi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ nɔ ni akɛwoɔ tsɔne mli. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛ́ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa jwɛi ni yitsoŋ wa lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why shouldn't I save seeds from my harvested hybrid maize to plant again next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ mi-hybrid corn ni mikpaa lɛ mli lɛ toɔ koni mikɛdu ekoŋŋ afi ni baa lɛ?

english: Hybrid seeds are specially bred to produce a high yield for only one season. If you save and replant those seeds, the second generation will grow unevenly and yield much smaller cobs than the original crop.
ga: Akwɛɔ dumɔwui ni ji hybrid lɛ yɛ gbɛ krɛdɛɛ nɔ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ be kome pɛ mli. Kɛji okɛto ni okɛdu ekoŋŋ Yinɔ ni ji enyɔ lɛ mli dumɔwui lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ bibioo kwraa fe shishijee tsei lɛ.

english: Why is it helpful to plant groundnuts or cowpeas between rows of tall crops like maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sɛɛnamɔ yɔɔ he akɛ aaadu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ tsei kakadaji tamɔ ŋmei ni ato amɛhe gbɛjianɔ lɛ ateŋ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas take nitrogen from the air and feed it into the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil for nearby crops while covering the ground to choke out unwanted weeds.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli amɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ yɛ be mli ni ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ mli koni jwɛi ni ataooo lɛ akabote mli.

english: Yellowing leaves are usually a sign that your maize is missing nitrogen in the soil or getting flooded with too much water. Adding well-rotted manure or nitrogen fertilizer helps the leaves regain their deep green color so the plant can grow strong cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli loo nu babaoo yɛ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why is it good practice to plant beans on the same land where I harvested my maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ madu ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mikpa ŋmeii yɛ nɔ yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil, but leguminous crops like beans put nitrogen naturally back into the earth through their root nodules. Rotating maize with beans refreshes your soil so future crops grow better without needing as much commercial fertilizer.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shi ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii lɛ kuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛhaa nitrogen kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Abɛi ni okɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ baaha oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. No hewɔ lɛ wɔsɛɛ tsei lɛ baakwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ ni jarayeli ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo he ehiaaa amɛ.

english: Young cocoa trees have tender leaves that burn easily under the hot sun. Fast-growing plantains produce large broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings the shade and soil moisture they need during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui ni daraa oya lɛ woɔ baai agboi ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ shade. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do weeds hurt my crops even when they are not physically touching them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi yeɔ miŋmɔshi nibii awui eyɛ mli akɛ amɛkɛ amɛhe kpaaa gbee moŋ lɛ?

english: Weeds have roots underneath the ground that secretly drink the water and eat the fertilizer meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops receive full sunlight, moisture, and nutrients without competition.
ga: Jwɛi yɛ shishifãi yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi ni nuɔ nu yɛ teemɔŋ ni eyeɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ato he gbɛjianɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa hulu la, ŋmɔtɔ kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ fɛɛ ni akaŋshii bɛ mli.

english: Curled and patchy leaves are symptoms of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is carried from plant to plant by small insects called whiteflies. Planting improved, disease-resistant cassava stem cuttings will stop the disease from spreading and protect your yields.
ga: Baai ni ebɔle ehe ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadii. ni kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ whiteflies lɛ woɔ kɛjɛɔ tso kome mli kɛyaa ekroko nɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ odu ŋmei ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni helai nyɛŋ emɔ lɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã ni ebu onibii ahe.

english: Pepper plants drop their blossoms when they experience heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Consistent watering at the roots and mulching the base keeps the soil damp and helps the plant retain its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he. Nu ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli daa loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli daa kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eye ebua tso lɛ ni ehiɛ efɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashi ebaawo yibii.

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick beneath the surface, which requires soft and loosened soil. High mounds keep the earth loose for root expansion while preventing heavy rains from waterlogging the roots and causing them to rot.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi. Enɛ biɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni mli tse. Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ shishifãi lɛ anɔ ni ehaaa amɛgboi.

english: The first rain of the season is often followed by a long dry spell that can dry out and kill tiny newly sprouted roots. Waiting until the rainy season fully settles ensures continuous moisture so your seeds germinate and establish properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ nugbɔshiimɔ klɛŋklɛŋ ni nɛɔ yɛ nakai be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ. Enɛ baanyɛ aha shishifãi lɛ agbi ni efite shishifãi bibii. ni baanyɛ akwɛ̃ ekoŋŋ Kɛ́ omɛ kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ baaho lɛ, ebaaha odumɔwui lɛ aya nɔ aná ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛma shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why should I cut off the low-hanging leaves and extra shoots at the base of my tomato plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mafo baai ni shwieɔ shi kɛ ŋmeii krokomɛi ni yɔɔ tomato tsei lɛ ashishi lɛ?

english: Pruning lower branches directs the plant's energy toward making bigger fruits instead of unnecessary leafy stems. It also keeps leaves off the wet ground, stopping soil-borne fungal diseases from splashing onto the plant during rains.
ga: Niji ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni afoɔ lɛ kudɔɔ tso lɛ hewalɛ koni ewo yibii wuji. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ tsei ni yɔɔ baai ni he ehiaaa baatsu nii lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hei ni nu yɔɔ lɛ. Tsi tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie tsei anɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli.

english: Why do my stored dried maize grains get full of small holes and insects after a few months?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni egbi lɛ mli eyi kɛ bu bibii lɛ? Ni kooloi bibii yɛ nyɔji fioo komɛi asɛɛ?

english: Grains attract weevils if they are stored with too much moisture inside or kept in open bags. Sun-drying your maize until it is completely hard and storing it in sealed, airtight bags prevents insects from eating your harvest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baagbala ŋmeii kɛji akɛ akɛto mli ni hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli loo awo kotokui ni agbele mli. Kɛ́ ogbi ŋmãa kɛyashi ewa kwraa ni okɛwo kotoku ko ni akɛ vacuum ewo mli lɛ, ebaatsi kooloi bibii anaa koni amɛkaye oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, a key nutrient it needs to grow green and healthy. Adding well-rotted manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer early in the crop's growth helps fix this.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye ŋmãa tso lɛ kɛha nitrogen. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he mra yɛ tso lɛ dalɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: Why does my lowland rice grow much better when there is shallow water standing in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa yɛ be mli ni nu ni mli ekwɔɔɔ ni damɔ shi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Standing water drowns out weeds that compete with rice for sunlight and nutrients. Rice plants are unique because their roots can survive in wet soil, making water a natural shield against unwanted plants.
ga: Nu ni damɔ shi lɛ shwieɔ jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe miitswa hulu la kɛ niyenii ni jɛɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ he akaŋ lɛ. Omɔ tsei yɛ srɔto ejaakɛ amɛ shishifãi baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu feɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛtsii nii ni tsiɔ tsei ni ataooo lɛ anaa.

english: Look closely at the small buds or 'eyes' on the cassava stick where old leaves used to grow. Make sure these buds point upwards toward the sky before pushing the stick into the soil so the branches sprout properly.
ga: Kwɛmɔ ŋmeii bibii loo ‘ŋmeii’ ni yɔɔ ŋmei tso lɛ nɔ he ni baai momoi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ be ko ni eho lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Kwɛmɔ akɛ nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ miitsɔɔ ŋwɛi dani okɛ niji lɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ewo niji lɛ adalɛ ni sa he hewalɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb so their leaves can spread out and catch as much sunlight as possible. Sunlight gives the plant energy to build large, heavy yam tubers underground instead of resting on the damp soil where leaves can rot.
ga: Ehe miihia ni akwɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛbaai lɛ agbɛ ashwã ni amɛná hulu la babaoo. Hulu la haa tso lɛ hewalɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii wuji ni tsii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Mohu ɔ, a jɔɔ a he ngɛ zu nɛ e mi ngɛ he nɛ baai ɔmɛ ma nyɛ maa puɛ ɔ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa plants have tender leaves that burn easily under direct, harsh sunlight. They need shade from bigger trees or temporary plants like plantains to keep them cool and hold moisture in the soil while they are young.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ shishi. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo kɛjɛ tsei wuji loo tsei ni yeɔ be kukuoo tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ koni amɛhe afee fɛ̃i ni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ.

english: When too many young shoots grow around one plantain tree, they steal water and food from the mother plant. Leaving only one or two strong shoots ensures the main tree has enough energy to produce a big, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Beni ŋmeii bibii babaoo ni miida yɛ dumɔwu kome he lɛ Ejuɔ nu kɛ niyenii kɛjɛɔ tso nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛwo tso wuji ni tsii babaoo.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when the weather gets too hot, when the soil dries out completely, or if insects are not visiting to pollinate them. Regular watering during hot weeks helps the flowers stay on and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo kooloi bibii baaa koni amɛbawo fɔfɔi lɛ Nu ni afɔɔ amɛ daa yɛ otsii ni mli edɔ lɛ amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny pests like aphids or whiteflies feeding on the undersides of leaves, or by viruses spread by these insects. Controlling these pests early keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii tamɔ ŋmeii loo ŋmeii yɛŋ ni yeɔ baai lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ ŋmeii amli. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ mli Kooloi nɛɛ anɔyeli mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baa lɛ mli waa.

english: Why do my groundnut flowers bend down and push themselves into the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmei fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ?

english: Groundnut plants form their seeds underground. After the flower is fertilized above ground, it grows a stem-like peg that pushes down into the soil where the groundnut pod can safely grow and ripen.
ga: Peanut tsei woɔ dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Beni afɔ fɔfɔi lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ sɛɛ lɛ Ebaaná ŋmei tamɔ ŋmei ni tsiɔ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bean ŋmɔtɔi lɛ baanyɛ adara ni amɛkwɛ̃ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do small holes keep appearing in my cowpea pods right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Ani ejieɔ ehe kpo yɛ mi-cowpea pods lɛ amli dani akpaa?

english: Small holes are caused by pod borer caterpillars that eat their way inside to feed on the developing beans. Spraying safe, recommended pest controls or neem extracts when flowering starts protects the pods.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ bu bibii lɛ baa ji pod borers ni yeɔ ŋmeii ni miiya hiɛ lɛ. Tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ lɛ kpo yɛ fɔfɔii lɛ ashishijee mli ni ajieɔ yi akɛ ashwie nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen, which acts as essential food for leaf growth. Adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer or well-rotted animal manure helps the leaves turn green and healthy again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele tsei lɛ amli. ni tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ loo kooloo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops wilt during the hot afternoon even when it rained two days ago?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Ni nugbɔ nɛ gbii enyɔ ni eho nɛ?

english: In intense sun, crops lose moisture through their leaves faster than their roots can pull it from the ground. Covering the soil around your crops with dry grass or leaves (mulching) helps trap soil moisture so roots stay hydrated longer.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii fiteɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ ajie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi ŋmɔɔ (mulching) yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: When is the best time to apply fertilizer so that my crop gets the full benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mawo ŋmɔshi nii koni maná miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ahe sɛɛ fɛɛ?

english: Fertilizer is best applied when the soil is moist and the crop is actively growing, usually a few weeks after sprouting and just before flowering. Applying during a dry spell wastes the fertilizer, while applying before heavy rain washes it away.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ hi jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida jogbaŋŋ. Bei pii lɛ, enɛ heɔ otsii fioo komɛi beni ekwɛ̃ sɛɛ, kɛ dani ewoɔ fɔfɔi. Kɛ́ akɛwo mli yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite. Yɛ be mli ni akɛwoɔ mli dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ, ebaafɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe.

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that hide in the growing tip of the plant. Inspecting your farm early and using recommended treatments or neem leaf solutions can protect your crops before the damage spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ tsei ni miida lɛ ashishigbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni tsofa ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii loo neem baa mli tsofa lɛ kɛ nitsumɔ baanyɛ abu oŋmɔshi nibii ahe dani nɔ ni efite lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking the sap out of young leaves, or by a virus spread by these insects. Controlling these sap-sucking pests early prevents the foliage from twisting.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii lɛ amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ nɔ Kudɔ kooloi ni nuɔ nu nɛɛ mra. Enɛ baatsi baai lɛ anaa koni amɛkatsake.

english: Cassava root rot happens when the soil stays overly soaked for a long time during heavy rains, starving the roots of air. Planting your cassava on raised mounds or ridges helps excess rainwater drain away safely.
ga: Cassava shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ baa kɛji akɛ nu babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Enɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ shishifãi lɛ amli. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die when I plant them in a wide open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo tso bibioo lɛ gbo beni midu yɛ ŋmɔ ko ni mli kwɔ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate leaves that easily burn under strong direct sunlight. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains alongside them creates a living shelter that protects the seedlings while they establish roots.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ be kukuoo ko, tamɔ plantains lɛ yɛ he kome lɛ, ehaa anáa he ko ni buɔ dumɔwui lɛ ahe yɛ be mli ni amɛwoɔ shishifãi lɛ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off due to extreme heat, irregular watering, or a lack of beneficial insects to pollinate them. Keeping the soil consistently damp and avoiding over-use of chemical sprays helps the flowers set fruit successfully.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa hewɔ. Nu ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ ni bɛ Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ kɛ tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ fɔfɔi lɛ anɔ fe nine ni akɛtsuɔ nii fe nine lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii jogbaŋŋ.

english: When plants are crowded, their roots and leaves compete against each other for space, sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Following proper spacing guidelines gives every plant enough resources to grow sturdy and produce well.
ga: Kɛ́ tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo lɛ Amɛshishifãi kɛ amɛbaai lɛ kɛ amɛhe miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná he ko, hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni sa ni kɔɔ sɛɛjɛkɛmɔ he lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ baaha tso fɛɛ tso aná nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha eda be fɛɛ be ni ekɛ yibii kpakpai aba.

english: Is it better to buy fresh certified seeds or save seeds from my last harvest to plant?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ ooohe dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli loo oookɛ dumɔwui ni jɛ naagbee kpamɔɔ lɛ mli lɛ ato koni okɛdu?

english: Certified seeds are specifically selected to resist common diseases and yield more food. Seeds saved from past harvests naturally lose their strength and vigor over generations, resulting in smaller harvests.
ga: Ahalaa dumɔwui ni awo he odase lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛte shi amɛwo helai ni afɔɔ namɔ ni amɛha niyenii babaoo aba. Dumɔwui ni ajie kɛjɛ kpamɔ ni eho lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ hewalɛ kɛ hewalɛ yɛ yinɔi amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji nikpamɔ bibioo.

english: Why do I need to plant plantains next to my young cocoa seedlings in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees get scorched easily under the harsh midday sun. Plantains grow rapidly with big leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing the temporary shade and moisture cocoa seedlings need to survive their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya kɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha kookoo dumɔwui lɛ aná be kukuoo mli hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato plants fall over and rot on the ground once they start producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ miigbee shi ni amɛmiifite beni amɛjeɔ yibiiwoo shishi lɛ?

english: Tomato stems are often too weak to hold the weight of heavy fruit. Tying the plants to wooden stakes keeps the leaves and fruits off the damp ground, preventing fungal diseases and rot.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato tsei lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ tsɔ ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛkwɛ aduawai ni tsii lɛ amli. Kɛ́ akɛ tso lɛ fĩ tso ko he lɛ, ebaaha baai kɛ aduawai lɛ akashwɛ yɛ he ni edɔ lɛ nɔ. Etsiɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela kɛ tsɛŋemɔ hela naa.

english: If I plant my maize seeds very close together, will I get a larger harvest from my farm?
ga: Kɛ midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ Ani maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Planting seeds too close together forces crops to fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leaves you with thin, weak stalks and small ears of corn, yielding less overall harvest than properly spaced plants.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ nyɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ koni amɛye hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ baaha oná ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni bɛ hewalɛ kɛ ŋmeii bibii. Enɛ haa yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ baa shi fe tsei ni akɛ amɛ ebɔ he jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil. Maize needs plenty of food to build green leaves, so applying manure or nitrogen fertilizer early on helps keep leaves green and productive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Niyenii babaoo he miihia ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii afata he mra. Ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ ahi eŋɔli ni ebaawo yibii kpakpai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop during the hot afternoon sun but look fresh again early in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli, shi amɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛbaa kɛ hejɔɔmɔ leebi lɛ?

english: Under intense heat, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up. Drooping is a temporary defense mechanism to expose less leaf surface to the sun, and the plant recovers overnight as temperatures drop.
ga: yɛ la ni mli edɔ waa shishi Tsei lɛ shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu. Defoliation ji be kukuoo mli hebuu gbɛ ni akɛbaa hulu la ni tsoɔ baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Ni tsei lɛ baaná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ nyɔɔŋ kome mli kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ ba shi.

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets crop-specific pests build up. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts natural nitrogen back into the soil.
ga: Tsei komekomei lɛ akwɛmɔ be fɛɛ be lɛ haa niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be mli, ni ehaa tsei pɔtɛɛ komɛi ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai baa shi. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ haa adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ kuɔ esɛɛ kɛbaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: My cocoa trees are getting old and producing fewer pods every season, so do I need to cut them all down?
ga: Mi cacao tsei lɛ miida ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii fioo ko pɛ daa afi. No hewɔ lɛ, ani esa akɛ mafo fɛɛ mli?

english: As cocoa trees pass 25 to 30 years of age, their natural productivity drops. You can temporarily boost yields through heavy pruning and fertilizer, but gradually replanting sections of your farm with improved hybrid seedlings is necessary for long-term production.
ga: Kɛ́ kookoo tso ye afii 25 kɛyashi 30 lɛ, nɔ ni ejɛɔ ebɔɔ su mli lɛ baa shi. Obaanyɛ oha yibiiwoo lɛ aya hiɛ yɛ be kukuoo mli kɛtsɔ tsei ni afolɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ, shi fiofio lɛ, okɛ fãi komɛi adu ekoŋŋ. Dumɔwui ni afee lɛ srɔtoi ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni oooha oŋmɔ lɛ he miihia waa kɛha be kakadaŋŋ mli nibii ni anáa lɛ.

english: Why are the flowers on my cowpea plants dropping off without forming any bean pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mi-cowpea tso lɛ nɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛjieee pea ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa lɛ?

english: Cowpea flowers drop when the plant suffers from severe heat stress, lack of soil moisture, or damage from tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips. Managing moisture and spraying early against pests helps the flowers stay on to form pods.
ga: Cowpea fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tso lɛ na hulutsoo ni naa wa waa. ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips lɛ efite. Fɛ̃i nɔkwɛmɔ kɛ mra be mli tsɛŋemɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ Yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛhiɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants curling up, turning pale, and looking stunted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ ebɔle ehe, eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ?

english: Curled, pale cassava leaves are a clear sign of Cassava Mosaic Virus, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. Using virus-free stem cuttings for planting stops the disease from spreading across your field.
ga: Kasava baai ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ cassava mosaic hela lɛ yɛ. ni ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji lɛ tsu nii beni oduɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hela lɛ akagbɛ eshwa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why do my harvested yams start sprouting green shoots in the barn even when I haven't planted them in soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ shweremɔ lɛ? Eyɛ mli akɛ miduuu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli moŋ.

english: Yams are living tubers that enter a natural sleeping period after harvest. Once this resting phase ends, the warmth and humidity in your barn signal to the yam that it is time to grow a new vine.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni amɛboteɔ shihilɛ ni bɛ shihilɛ mli yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛji akɛ hejɔɔmɔ be lɛ ba naagbee lɛ Dɔlɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ otsu lɛ mli lɛ baatsɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ akɛ be eshɛ ni esa akɛ adu wain tsei heei.

english: Why does my land produce less maize every year even though I plant the same seeds and work just as hard?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmãa fioo daa afi lɛ? He ni miduɔ dumɔwui kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni mitsuɔ nii waa nakai nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops take nutrients out of the ground as they grow. If you plant the same crop year after year without adding organic matter, manure, or fertilizers, or without resting the land, the soil loses its food and cannot support healthy, high-yielding crops.
ga: Tsei jieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli beni amɛdaraa lɛ. Kɛji akɛ odu ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi ni okɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii fataaa he, loo okɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔɔ lɛ, Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ he jɔɔ lɛ baa shi ni enyɛŋ ekwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni woɔ yibii babaoo lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do farmers say that planting groundnuts or cowpeas makes the soil better for my next crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafonyo ko kɛɔ akɛ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei dumɔ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni hi kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have special roots that trap nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. Nitrogen is like strong food for crops, so planting legumes leaves behind natural fertilizer for the next crop you plant, like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ shishifãi krɛdɛɛi ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen tamɔ niyenii ni mli wa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii. No hewɔ lɛ, ŋmeii ni ooodu lɛ shĩɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni oduɔ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why should I wait until my maize sprouts before applying my first fertilizer instead of putting it all in the ground before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mamɛ ni mi-ŋmã lɛ akwɛ̃ dani mikɛ mi-klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ awo mli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani odu.

english: Young seeds cannot absorb large amounts of fertilizer before their roots develop. If you put all the fertilizer in the ground too early, heavy rains will wash it away into the soil where the plant roots cannot reach it.
ga: Dumɔwui bibii nyɛŋ aŋɔ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo dani shishifãi lɛ akwɛ̃. Kɛji okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya tsɔ Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii yaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall with many leaves, but give me very small tubers under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ kɛlɛ ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Shi ha shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ afee bibii waa?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or when plants are crowded too closely together, the cassava puts all its energy into growing big leaves to catch sunlight instead of storing food below the ground in the roots.
ga: Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ loo be mli ni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛwo baai wuji amli koni enine ashɛ hulu la nɔ. Mohu ɔ, a toɔ niye ní ngɛ tso sisifãhi nɛ a ngɛ zugba a sisi ɔ a mi.

english: Why do I need to clear the grass around my crops while they are still young?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni majie jwɛi ni ebɔle mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii be mli ni amɛji bibii lolo lɛ?

english: Weeds and grass are very aggressive and steal sunlight, water, and soil food from your crop. Clearing weeds early ensures your young crop gets all the nutrients it needs to grow strong roots and stem.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ jwɛi feɔ basabasa waa ni amɛjuɔ hulu la, nu kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni odumɔwui lɛ aná niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni shishifãi kɛ shishifãi ni wa akwɛ̃.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with tall sticks instead of letting them trail on the bare ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni madu mi-sweet potato tso lɛ niji ni kwɔlɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeha enyiɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ lɛ nɔ?

english: Lifting yam vines off the ground lets the leaves catch direct sunlight from all sides, which makes the plant produce bigger tubers. It also keeps leaves off the damp soil, preventing fungal diseases.
ga: Kɛ́ awó sweet potato wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni jɛɔ he fɛɛ he lɛ shɛɔ tsei lɛ ahe tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ naa yitso ni da. Eyeɔ ebuaa hu ni ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ he. Tsi fungal helai anaa

english: Why do the bottom leaves of my cocoa trees turn yellow and drop off during the dry harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ harmattan be ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry weather, plants lose water quickly through their leaves. Cocoa trees shed lower leaves to conserve water and protect their stems from drying out completely until the rainy season returns.
ga: yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ enyɔ shi lɛ Tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu oya kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ. Cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛshishigbɛ baai lɛ koni nu ahi mli ni amɛtsi amɛshishifã lɛ naa koni ekagbi kwraa kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do my tomato fruits turn black and soft at the bottom before they turn red?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni efeɔ blɛoo yɛ shishigbɛ dani etsɔɔ etsuru lɛ?

english: This is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the growing fruit, often due to uneven watering. When water supply goes up and down drastically, the fruit cannot get the steady calcium it needs to form healthy skin.
ga: Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ blossom end rot, ni nɔ ni kɛbaa ji calcium ni bɛ aduawai ni miida lɛ mli lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ nu ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsakeɔ waa lɛ, Yibii lɛ nyɛŋ ana calcium ni he hiaa be fɛɛ be koni ekɛfee hewolo ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rains even when the stem is strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi wa moŋ?

english: Plantains have shallow root systems that are often damaged by microscopic worms called nematodes or root rot. Damaged roots lose their grip on the soil, causing the heavy plant to tip over under wind and rain.
ga: Plantains yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ nematodes loo shishifãi ni fiteɔ lɛ fiteɔ amɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dɔŋŋ. ni haa tsei ni tsii shwieɔ shi yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ hewɔ

english: Why do small holes appear on my young maize leaves with tiny dark droppings inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ buji bibii yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ? Yɛ mi-baby corn lɛ baai lɛ anɔ ni ŋmeii bibii ni tsuɔ diŋ yɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli?

english: This damage is caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which feeds inside the growing center of young maize plants. Catching and treating them early prevents them from destroying the leaf growth center.
ga: Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii yɛ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ adalɛ hei lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Nibii ni anaa mra kɛ tsamɔ Enɛ baatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkafite he ni baa lɛ daa lɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves are a clear sign of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Maize plants need nitrogen to grow healthy green leaves, and when the soil lacks enough of it, the plant pulls nitrogen from its older bottom leaves to feed the newer top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ faŋŋ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia ŋmãa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ, ni ji eŋɔli. ni kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa Tsei lɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni etsɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛha ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ niyenii.

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop many of their young flowers before any pods develop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi bibii babaoo dani ŋmeii lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees drop flowers when they face environmental stress, such as dry weather, low soil nutrients, or a lack of tiny insects called midges that are needed to pollinate the blossoms.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ shihilɛ mli haomɔi, tamɔ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi lɛ kpe. Niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo kooloi bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ midge, ni he hiaa kɛha fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔmɔ nii.

english: Why do my mango trees produce a huge harvest one year, but almost no fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango tsei woɔ yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko kwraa baajɛ mli aba?

english: This behavior is called alternate bearing. Using energy to produce a large crop leaves the mango tree exhausted and low on nutrient reserves, so it spends the following year recovering rather than making flowers and fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ subaŋ nɛɛ akɛ sɛɛkuu-kɛsaramɔ. Hewalɛ ni akɛtsuɔ nii koni akɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo lɛ haa mango tsei lɛ ahe jɔ̃ɔ amɛhe ni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mli lɛ faaa. No hewɔ lɛ, afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni akɛtsaa he moŋ fe ni eeewo fɔfɔi ni ewo yibii.

english: Why do small caterpillars hide and eat inside the central leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii teɔ shi amɛwoɔ mi-abɛi bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ amli ni amɛyeɔ nii lɛ?

english: These pests are likely Fall Armyworms, which target the soft, tender inner leaves (the whorl) of young corn plants because those leaves are easiest to chew and provide shelter from predators and heat.
ga: Ekolɛ nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ ji Fall Armyworms, ni kwɛɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii amli baai ni yɔɔ blɛoo (rings) lɛ anɔ. Ejaakɛ nakai baai lɛ ji nɔ ni ŋmɔmɔ waaa fe fɛɛ, ni ehaa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe kɛjɛɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ hulutsoo be lɛ he.

english: Why do my cassava tubers start rotting underground if I leave them in the farm during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmei shishifãi jeɔ shishi egboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Excess water from rain fills the air pockets in the soil, suffocating the roots and creating a damp environment where harmful fungal and bacterial rot diseases thrive.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine ni jɛɔ nugbɔ mli lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ amli obɔ. ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ehaa shihilɛ ni mli edɔ baa Biɛ ji he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui kɛ bacteria rot baanyɛ aya hiɛ yɛ.

english: Yam vines need to climb high on stakes to expose their leaves to maximum sunlight. Sunlight allows the leaves to produce energy, which is sent down to nourish and expand the yam tuber underground.
ga: Esa akɛ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ tsei ni kwɔlɔ koni amɛbai lɛ ajie amɛhe kpo yɛ hulu la ni fa babaoo mli. Hulu la yeɔ ebuaa baai lɛ ni amɛjieɔ hewalɛ ni akɛbaa shi koni ekɛha sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ niyenii ni amɛkwɛ̃ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: How does planting cowpeas or groundnuts on my farmland help my next crop of maize grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni eda jogbaŋŋ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil through their roots, leaving behind natural fertilizer that helps the next crop grow stronger.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛmɔɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Amɛshiɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii koni eye ebua ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ ni amɛdara waa.

english: Why should I cover the bare soil around my tomato plants with dry leaves or straw?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ baai ni egboi loo jwɛi awo shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ ni bɔle mi-tomato tsei lɛ ahe lɛ nɔ?

english: Covering soil with organic material, known as mulching, stops water from evaporating quickly in the sun, keeps the root zone cool, and prevents heavy rain from splashing soil-borne fungal diseases onto the tomato leaves.
ga: Atsɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni akɛhaa lɛ akɛ mulching. Enɛ baatsi nu lɛ naa koni ekatsɔ la oya kɛji akɛ hulu la shɛ enɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifã lɛ he lɛ mli jɔɔ. ni etsĩ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ naa koni ekaha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli baa lɛ agbɛ ashwã tomato baai lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plant leaves curl up tightly during the dry afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi shiŋŋ yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl inward during hot, dry periods as a natural survival technique to reduce leaf surface exposure to the sun, which helps the plant conserve moisture.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe kɛyaa mli yɛ be mli ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ, ni egbiɔ akɛ adebɔɔ mli wala gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ ajieɔ hulu la ni baa lɛ nɔ lɛ shi. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees fall over easily during heavy rainstorms even when the stem looks strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa mli eyɛ mli akɛ tso lɛ shishi lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ moŋ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow root systems that do not go deep into the earth. When soil gets soft and wet from heavy rain, the roots cannot hold the heavy weight of the plant and fruit bunch against strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni eyaaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee blɛoo ni edɔ kɛjɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ nyɛŋ akwɛ tso lɛ kɛ aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ anɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why are the leaves of my maize turning yellow instead of healthy green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves usually turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen in the soil, when weeds are stealing its food, or when too much standing water is suffocating the plant's roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmãa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛ́ tso lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Beni jwɛi juɔ niyenii Aloo be mli ni nu ni ekã shi babaoo lɛ haa tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as very hot daytime temperatures, lack of water in the soil, or a sudden change in weather during flowering.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ shi kɛji amɛkɛ haomɔi tamɔ hulutsoo be mli latsaa, shikpɔŋ nɔ nu ni faaa, loo kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi trukaa yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli kpe.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism tomato plants use to hide from strong sunlight and reduce water loss; however, if leaves stay curled all day, it may indicate a lack of water or a plant virus.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ni tomato tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ he ni amɛha nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Shi kɛji akɛ baai lɛ ebɔle ehe gbi muu lɛ fɛɛ Ebaanyɛ etsɔɔ akɛ nu bɛ loo hela ko yɛ tso lɛ mli.

english: Planting cassava too close together forces the plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, which results in thin, small tubers instead of big, thick roots.
ga: Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo baa yɛ shishifãi wuji ni mli tse najiaŋ.

english: How do I know if my farmland needs manure or fertilizer before I plant?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii dani madu?

english: If crops from your previous harvest had yellowish leaves, stayed small, or yielded poorly, your soil has lost its nutrients and needs organic manure or fertilizer to feed the new crops.
ga: Kɛji tsei ni jɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ko ni eho mli lɛ yɛ baai ni tsuɔ, amɛji bibii, loo amɛwooo yibii kpakpai Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ efo oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni ehe miihia humus loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛhaa tsei heei niyenii.

english: Why do some farmers plant beans in the same farm as their maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi duɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli ni amɛduɔ ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Beans are special crops that pull nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil, which naturally fertilizes the soil and helps neighboring maize plants grow stronger.
ga: Beans ji tsei krɛdɛɛi ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa.

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads rapidly in cool, wet, and overly shady conditions during the rainy season.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛbaa ji black pod hela. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni mli ejɔ, ni efɔ, ni hulutsoo be lɛ yɔɔ fe nine yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do small insects attack and destroy my harvested maize so quickly in storage?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa ni amɛfiteɔ mi-ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ?

english: Insects like weevils lay eggs inside the grain before or during harvest, and if the maize is not dried properly before storage, the warm, moist environment helps them hatch and multiply rapidly.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ ŋmeii woɔ ŋmeii yɛ ŋmãa mli dani akpaa loo yɛ be mli ni akpaa ŋmãa lɛ. Ni kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋmãa lɛ jogbaŋŋ dani akɛto Shihilɛ ni mli edɔ ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baaye abua amɛ ni amɛfɔ ni amɛfɔ oya.

english: Why is it best for me to plant my seeds right at the start of the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ?

english: Planting at the onset of the rains ensures seeds get consistent moisture to germinate quickly and develop deep, strong roots before any temporary dry spells occur.
ga: Dumɔwui ni aduɔ beni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ haa dumɔwui lɛ náa ŋmɔtɔ ni yaa nɔ be fɛɛ be koni amɛkwɛ̃ oya. ni amɛnáa shishifãi ni mli kwɔ ni mli wa dani be kukuoo mli hɔmɔ baa.

english: Weeds are wild, tough plants that are naturally adapted to your soil, allowing them to absorb available water, sunlight, and nutrients much faster than cultivated crop seeds.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni wa ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛtsake amɛhe amɛwo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa amɛmɔɔ nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ lɛ oya fe dumɔwui ni adu lɛ.

english: This is usually caused by Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny white insects called whiteflies. It prevents the cassava plant from making energy, leading to smaller tubers underground.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmei mosaic hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Kplukai bibii yɛŋ ji nɔ ni gbɛɔ eshwaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Etsiɔ ŋmei tso lɛ naa koni ekafee hewalɛ. Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ feɔ bibii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a pest common in Ghana that hides inside the tender funnel of the maize plant during the day and feeds on the leaves.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ naa yɛ Ghana ni kɛ ehe woɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ amli ŋmeii amli yɛ gbi mli ni eyeɔ baai lɛ.

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly during rainy weather when there is too much shade and moisture trapping air around the pods.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ jɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ mli. Beni hulutsoo be babaoo yɛ ni kɔɔyɔɔ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni bɔleɔ ŋmɔtɔi lɛ ahe lɛ.

english: Does it matter which way up I push my cassava stems into the dirt?
ga: Ani gbɛ ni mitsɔɔ nɔ mikɛ ŋmei tso lɛ woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he hiaa?

english: Yes, cassava stem cuttings must be planted with the tiny leaf buds pointing upward toward the sky; planting them upside down makes it hard for shoots to grow and reduces tuber yield.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, esa akɛ adu ŋmei ni afo lɛ kɛ fɔfɔi bibii. ni tsɔɔ ŋwɛi Kɛ́ adu kɛtee ŋwɛi lɛ, ehaa ewaa kɛhaa ŋmeii lɛ akwɛmɔ ni ehaa ŋmeii ni anáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my tomato stems fall over and rot when the heavy fruits start growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shwieɔ shi ni egboɔ kɛ́ aduawai ni tsii lɛ je shishi amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ?

english: Tomato plants have weak stems that cannot support heavy fruit on their own, so they need wooden stakes driven into the ground to tie them upright and keep fruits off wet soil.
ga: Tomato tsei yɛ ŋmeii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛhiɛ aduawai ni tsii. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni tomatoi kɛ tsei ni atsɔ mli awo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ atsu nii ni amɛkɛfi amɛ shi shiŋŋ ni amɛtsi yibii lɛ anaa koni amɛkamɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under direct sunlight. Fast-growing plantains have large leaves that act as living umbrellas, giving cocoa seedlings necessary shade and moisture during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Tso bibioo ni daa oya lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Enɛ haa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ fɛ̃i yɛ amɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crop leaves dry up and drop off so quickly during the Harmattan season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi oya yɛ harmattan be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: The dusty Harmattan winds carry very low humidity, which rapidly pulls water out of leaves; plants naturally drop leaves to conserve internal water and survive the dry spell.
ga: Harmattan kɔɔyɔɔ ni sũ yɔɔ mli lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be ni baa shi waa. ni jieɔ nu kɛjɛɔ baai lɛ amli oya Tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ adebɔɔ naa koni amɛkɛ nu ato amɛmli ni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Why do the flowers on my cocoa trees fall to the ground without turning into small pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ cacao tsei anɔ lɛ gbeeɔ shikpɔŋ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers drop if they are not pollinated by tiny biting midges, or if the tree experiences stress from dry weather and drops flowers to save its own energy.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji akɛ kooloi bibii ni shwieɔ mɔ lɛ etswaaa amɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Aloo kɛji tso lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ he haomɔ kpe ni ekɛ efɔfɔi lɛ shwie shi koni ekɛbu lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ehewalɛ he.

english: How does planting beans or groundnuts help my soil grow better maize next season?
ga: Te ŋmeii loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mishikpɔŋ lɛ ni ekwɛ ŋmãa kpakpa yɛ be ni baa lɛ mli lɛ eha tɛŋŋ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and beans gather nitrogen gas from the air and store it in their roots, naturally adding free nutrients into the soil for future crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii Buaa nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa ni ekɛtoɔ shishifãi lɛ amli. Enɛ kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni aheee nɔ ko fataa shikpɔŋ lɛ he yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: Why are my yam seed pieces rotting in the ground before they even sprout?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ miifite yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ dani amɛkwɛ̃ po lɛ?

english: Yam seed pieces rot if the soil is soaked with standing water or if the cut edges were not dried in the shade or coated with wood ash before planting to block soft-rot bacteria.
ga: Sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ amli fãi lɛ baagboi kɛji akɛ akɛ nu ni damɔ shi ewo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo kɛji akɛ agbiko ŋwɛigbɛi ni afo lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo akɛ tso sũ ewo mli dani adu koni ebu he kɛjɛ helai ni fiteɔ lɛ ahe.

english: Sandy soil has large particles with wide spaces between them, causing water to drain away fast instead of staying near the roots. Mixing organic manure or compost into sandy soil acts like a sponge, helping the ground hold water much longer for your crops.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ ŋmeii wuji kɛ gbɛ ni da yɛ amɛteŋ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ hoɔ oya moŋ fe ni eeebɛŋkɛ shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ ŋã mli lɛ futu mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛɔ nu kɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii be babaoo.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize turning yellow even after heavy rains and applying fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baa ni yɔɔ mi-ŋmã lɛ nɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ sɛɛ po lɛ?

english: Heavy rains in sandy or loose soil can quickly wash fertilizer nutrients deep into the ground below the reach of roots before the plant can use them. Applying smaller amounts of fertilizer more frequently, rather than all at once, prevents nutrients from washing away.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ŋã loo ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ afɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa ŋmɔshi nibii yɔɔ mli lɛ amli oya aahu akɛ shishifãi nyɛŋ ashɛ he dani tsei lɛ kɛtsu nii. Ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii bibii baafata he shii abɔ Yɛ no najiaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ fɛɛ fata he shikome lɛ, ebaatsi niyenii mli nibii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ anaa koni ekaho.

english: Why does covering the soil around my crops with dry palm leaves or straw help them grow better during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mulching around I duɔ mi ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ ŋmei baai loo jwɛi ni egbi ni no yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa jogbaŋŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Covering the ground with dry grass or leaves, known as mulching, shields the soil from direct sunlight. This keeps the ground cooler and stops moisture from evaporating quickly into the air, keeping water available for your crops.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egboi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ jɔɔ, ni ehaa nu ni mli edɔ lɛ shwieɔ oya kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Enɛ haa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow much bigger tubers when I plant them on soil mounds rather than flat ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tsei lɛ yɛ bulbs wuji babaoo beni midu amɛ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ moŋ fe he ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Mounding loosens the soil and creates good drainage around the plant. Loose soil allows cassava roots to expand easily without pushing against hard ground, leading to larger and healthier tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni aaabɔle he lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shwieɔ shi ni ehaa nu kpakpa hoɔ kɛbɔleɔ tso lɛ he. Shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo ni amɛtsiii shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa yitso lɛ feɔ agbo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.
