english: How does planting cowpeas alongside my maize help my maize crops grow stronger?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ tsina ŋmei ni aduɔ yɛ ŋmãa masɛi lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mi ŋmãa lɛ ni ená hewalɛ?

english: Cowpeas are legumes that naturally capture nitrogen gas from the air and deposit it into the soil through their roots. The nearby maize uses this extra nitrogen as free food to build strong stalks and green leaves.
ga: Cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ amɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Abɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ kɛ nitrogen ni fa fe nine nɛɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai eŋɔli.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full, hot sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and produce broad leaves that act like natural umbrellas, providing the shade and humidity cocoa seedlings need during their early years.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Dumɔwui lɛ daa oya waa ni amɛwoɔ baai ni mli kwɔlɔ ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋwɛi ŋtayaai. Ehaa kookoo dumɔwui lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ hulutsoo ni he hiaa amɛ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Leaf curling is a natural defense mechanism. By curling its leaves inward, the pepper plant reduces the surface area exposed to intense heat, helping it retain water and survive excessive sunlight.
ga: Baai lɛ ni ebɔleɔ amɛhe lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ. Pepper tsei lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli kɛyaa mli koni ekɛba he ni hulutsoo ni naa wa baa amɛnɔ lɛ shi. Eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nu mli ni eŋmɛɔ hulu la ni fe nine lɛ gbɛ.

english: Why do my yam seeds need to be planted with the skin side positioned correctly in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ adu sweet potato dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni hewolo lɛ fã lɛ aba shi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Yam sprouts emerge from specific buds near the skin. Placing the seed properly ensures the young shoot grows straight up toward light instead of wasting energy struggling upward from an inverted position.
ga: Sweet potatoes kwɛ̃ɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni bɛŋkɛ hewolo lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni akɛwoɔ mli jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha ŋmeii bibii lɛ adara tɛ̃ɛ kɛya la lɛ he. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofite hewalɛ ni okɛmiibɔ mɔdɛŋ kɛya ŋwɛi kɛjɛ shihilɛ ni tsɔɔ shishi lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I burn all the weeds and farm clearing waste on my field before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mishãa jwɛi kɛ jwɛi fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ dani miduɔ nii?

english: Burning destroys valuable organic matter and useful soil organisms that keep your land fertile. Leaving plant residue to rot naturally feeds the soil and improves its ability to hold nutrients and water.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni jara wa kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni haa oshikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii lɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni tsei ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ, ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ yeɔ niyenii ni ehaa nyɛmɔ ni eyɔɔ ni ekɛhiɛɔ niyenii kɛ nu mli lɛ yaa hiɛ.

english: Why are my tomato fruits turning black and rotting at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ miitsɔ ediŋŋ ni efiteɔ yɛ shishigbɛ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This rot, called blossom-end rot, happens when soil moisture fluctuates wildly, preventing the roots from absorbing calcium. Regular, consistent watering keeps the fruit healthy and prevents the bottoms from turning black.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔi naagbee fitemɔ. Ebaa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ tsakeɔ waa. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ calcium. Nu ni akɛwoɔ aduawai lɛ amli daa kɛ daa lɛ haa aduawai lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ, ni ehaaa amɛshishi lɛ afee ediŋŋ.

english: Why do my crops start turning yellow and rotting when we get continuous heavy rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi ŋmɔŋ ni amɛmiifite beni wɔnáa nugbɔ ni naa wa ni yaa nɔ lɛ?

english: Excess rain fills up all the air spaces in the soil, suffocating crop roots so they cannot breathe or absorb food. The extra dampness also creates an ideal environment for fungal diseases to grow quickly on stems and leaves.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ babaoo lɛ eyiɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ mli obɔ. Enɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛmu loo amɛŋɔ niyenii. Fɛ̃i ni yaa hiɛ lɛ hu haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha tsɛŋemɔ helai ni baa oya yɛ tsei kɛ baai anɔ lɛ baa.

english: How does too much rainfall cause damage to crop roots underground?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ fe nine lɛ fiteɔ tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ ashishifãi?

english: When rainwater stays on the field without draining, crop roots drown due to a lack of oxygen. Drowned roots turn soft and rot, causing the plant to wilt and die even though there is plenty of water around it.
ga: Kɛji nugbɔ nu lɛ tee nɔ ehi ŋmɔ lɛ mli ni nu hoɔ Tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baagbo yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ bɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shishifãi ni yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ baafee blɛoo ni amɛbaafite. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji nu babaoo yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ po.

english: Why do fungal diseases spread so fast across my farm right after a long period of rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsɛŋemɔ hela ko gbɛɔ eshwaa miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Fungal spores thrive in cool, humid weather. Rain droplets physically splash disease spores from the soil or infected plants onto healthy leaves, spreading the infection across the whole field very fast.
ga: Fungal spores lɛ yeɔ omanye yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ, ni mli edɔ mli. Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ shwieɔ helai ahe tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ loo tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ anɔ kɛyaa baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa hela lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ oya.

english: Why do my crops produce fewer fruits or grains during a very rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔ nii lɛ wooo yibii loo ŋmaa babaoo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Heavy rain knocks delicate flowers off plants and washes away pollen before bees or wind can pollinate them. Without pollination, flowers drop off instead of developing into fruits, pods, or grain heads.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwieɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ tsei lɛ anɔ ni efoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli fɔfɔi lɛ dani ŋmeii loo kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ afee fɔfɔi lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ. Kɛji akɛ pollination bɛ lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafee aduawai, ŋmeii, loo dumɔwui ayitsei.

english: Why does heavy rain wash away the strength of my farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ miifite shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hewalɛ lɛ?

english: Heavy rain causes a process called leaching, where rainwater pushes vital nutrients deep into the ground beyond the reach of crop roots, leaving the topsoil poor and starving your plants.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ kɛ nɔ ko ni atsɛɔ lɛ leaching baa. he ni nugbɔ nu lɛ tsiɔ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ fe bɔ ni tsei shishifãi baanyɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Efiteɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ otsei lɛ.

english: Is it a good idea for me to apply fertilizer on my crops during heavy rain periods?
ga: Ani eji jwɛŋmɔ kpakpa akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: No, applying fertilizer during heavy rain is wasteful because runoff water washes the nutrients away before crop roots can absorb them. It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist but heavy rain is not falling.
ga: Dabi, ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ ji shikafitemɔ ejaakɛ nu ni hoɔ lɛ hoɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ aŋɔ amɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ shi nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa enɛɛɛ.

english: How can I protect my field from accumulating too much water when the rains become heavy?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu miŋmɔji lɛ ahe koni nu akabua amɛhe naa fe nine yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli?

english: You can construct raised soil beds for your crops and dig shallow drainage channels around and through your field to collect and direct excess rainwater away from crop roots.
ga: Obaanyɛ ofee shikpɔŋ nɔ saatsoi ni awó nɔ kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii ni otsa nu ni hoɔ yɛ jɛmɛ ni mli ekwɔɔɔ. Yɛ oŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛtsɔ oŋmɔji lɛ amli koni obua nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine kɛjɛ tsei shishifãi amli lɛ naa ni okɛjie.

english: Why do my crops grow plenty of green leaves during heavy rain but give a small harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tsei lɛ naa baai eŋɔli babaoo yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa be mli shi amɛwoɔ yibii fioo lɛ?

english: Excess water and soft conditions encourage plants to spend all their energy growing tall stems and leafy foliage rather than directing nutrients into expanding fruits, seeds, or root tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine kɛ shihilɛi ni mli jɔ lɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii kakadaji kɛ baai kakadaji. Mohu ɔ, a kɛ níhi nɛ haa nɔ he wami ɔ tsuɔ ní konɛ a kɛ bli tso yiblii, dumɔwuhi, aloo sisi fã ɔmɛ a mi.

english: Why do crops harvested during heavy rainy periods spoil very quickly after harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ oya yɛ ŋmaa lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Crops harvested in wet weather absorb excess moisture and have softer skins, which makes them easily damaged and allows rot-causing bacteria and mold to multiply rapidly in storage.
ga: Tsei ni akpaa yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ mli lɛ shwieɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ, ni amɛhewolo lɛ yɔɔ blɛoo. ni fiteɔ tsei oya ni ehaa helatsɛmɛi kɛ ŋmeii ni fiteɔ nii lɛ feɔ babaoo oya yɛ he ni akɛtoɔ lɛ.

english: How can I tell the difference between a crop suffering from too much water and one suffering from pest damage?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ tso ni awo mli nu fe nine kɛ nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai efite lɛ teŋ?

english: Waterlogged crops usually turn uniformly yellow, droop, and have soft, smelly roots, whereas pest damage shows up as bitten leaves, holes, rolled foliage, or visible insects on the stems.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni tamɔ amɛhe, amɛgbee shi, ni amɛshishifãi lɛ yɛ blɛoo ni shãa. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, nɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai fiteɔ lɛ jeɔ kpo akɛ baai ni emɔ, bu, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo kooloi bibii ni anaa yɛ tso lɛ shishi.

english: Why shouldn't I leave ripe cocoa pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashiɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes them to become overripe, which makes the seeds inside start germinating. This ruins the quality of the cocoa beans and attracts pests and diseases to your farm.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha amɛshwere fe nine. Enɛ haa dumɔwui ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛkwɛ̃ɔ. Enɛ fiteɔ kookoo yibii lɛ ahe ni egbalaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. Ba oŋmɔ lɛ mli

english: What happens to the quality of my crop if I harvest overripe cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji mikpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Overripe pods often contain sprouted beans, which have lower oil content and poorer flavor after fermentation. Buyers often pay less or reject cocoa batches that have too many sprouted or damaged beans.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii yɛ pods ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine lɛ amli. Fɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli, ni ehiɛ ŋɔɔ waa kɛji afee lɛ fɛ̃i. Bei pii lɛ, mɛi ni heɔ nii lɛ woɔ nyɔmɔ fioo loo amɛkpooɔ kookoo ni ŋmeii babaoo yɔɔ mli loo efite lɛ.

english: A ripe pod changes color completely—usually from green to bright yellow, or from dark red/purple to orange. Tapping the pod also produces a hollow sound because the beans inside have detached from the outer shell.
ga: Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ tsakeɔ ehiɛ su kwraa—bei pii lɛ, ejɛɔ eŋɔli mli kɛyaa ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse mli. loo kɛjɛ tsuru/purple ni mli edɔ kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Kɛ́ otswa pod lɛ hu, ehaa gbɛɛmɔ ko ni mli ewo muji baa ejaakɛ kɔfi ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ jeɔ kpo kɛjɛɔ kponɔgbɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli.

english: Is it harmful to harvest cocoa pods while they are still green?
ga: Ani eyɛ oshara akɛ ooobua kookoo ŋmeii anaa yɛ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lolo lɛ?

english: Yes, harvesting green or underripe pods produces beans that do not ferment properly, leading to a bitter taste and small bean size. It is best to wait until the pod completely turns color before cutting it down.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmeii ni ji eŋɔli loo ŋmeii ni eshɛko lɛ to lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ akafɔ jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa ŋmɔlɔ ni mli wa kɛ dumɔwui bibii baa. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi ŋmeii lɛ atsake su kwraa dani ofolɔ amɛ.

english: Should I cut off old or spoiled cocoa pods before starting my main harvest?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tsei ni egbɔ loo ni efite lɛ dani mabɔi ŋmaakpamɔ titri lɛ?

english: Yes, going through your farm to remove diseased or overripe pods before the main harvest stops fungi like black pod disease from spreading to healthy pods. It keeps your farm clean and protects your remaining yield.
ga: Hɛɛ, feemɔ nɔ ko yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli ni ojie ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ loo ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ dani kpamɔ titri lɛ aba koni ŋmeii, tamɔ black pod hela lɛ akagbɛ ashwã ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli. Ye obua ni oŋmɔ lɛ mli atse ni obu onibii ni eshwɛ lɛ ahe.

english: Why do some cocoa pods turn black and dry up while still hanging on my tree?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii komɛi feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgbiɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ mitsei lɛ anɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is usually caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that spreads in damp, shaded conditions. Removing these infected pods quickly prevents spores from spreading to neighboring trees.
ga: ni bei pii lɛ, black pod hela kɛbaa Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ, ni hulutsoo be yɔɔ. Kɛ́ ajie nɛkɛ ŋmeii ni hela emɔ amɛ nɛɛ oya lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii lɛ akagbɛ ashwã tsei ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why should I use a sharp harvesting hook instead of pulling cocoa pods off with my hands?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mikɛ ŋtayaa ni mli wa atsu nii moŋ fe ni mikɛ minine baagbala kookoo ŋmeii lɛ?

english: Pulling pods by hand damages the flower cushion on the tree trunk, which is the spot where future flowers and pods grow. A sharp tool cuts the pod stalk cleanly without hurting next season's yield.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ onine gbala ŋmeii lɛ, ebaafite fɔfɔii akushin ni yɔɔ tso lɛ shishi lɛ, he ni fɔfɔi kɛ ŋmeii ni baaba wɔsɛɛ lɛ baakwɛ̃ yɛ lɛ. Dɛŋdade ko ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔ shwieɔ pod lɛ shishifã lɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ ni enaaa be ni baa lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ hewalɛ.

english: What should I do with rotten or damaged pods after I cut them off the tree?
ga: Kɛ́ mifo tso lɛ mli ŋmeii lɛ, mɛni esa akɛ mafee ŋmeii ni egbo loo efite lɛ?

english: You should gather rotten pods and bury them or dispose of them away from the farm area. Leaving them on the soil allows fungal spores to stay alive and infect healthy trees when it rains.
ga: Esa akɛ obua ŋmeii ni egboi lɛ anaa ni okɛfu loo okɛshwie he ko ni kɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ. Kɛ́ ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ ahiɔ shi ni amɛyeɔ tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ hela kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ.

english: How often should I go through my farm to harvest ripe cocoa pods during peak season?
ga: Shii enyiɛ esa akɛ maya ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni mayakpa kookoo ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ yɛ be mli ni mɛi fa babaoo lɛ?

english: You should harvest every two to three weeks during the main season. Regular harvesting prevents pods from becoming overripe on the tree and keeps diseases from multiplying.
ga: Esa akɛ okpa daa otsii enyɔ loo etɛ yɛ be titri lɛ mli. Kɛ́ akpaa tso lɛ daa lɛ, ehaa ŋmeii lɛ shwereɔ fe nine yɛ tso lɛ nɔ, ni ehaaa helai agbɛ ashwã.

english: Can I mix beans from overripe pods with fresh beans during fermentation?
ga: Ani manyɛ mikɛ ŋmeii ni egbɔ fe nine lɛ afutu ŋmeii heei yɛ be mli ni amɛhooɔ lɛ?

english: It is best not to mix them. Overripe or sprouted beans ferment differently and can introduce mould or off-flavors to the entire batch, lowering the grade of your cocoa.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ okɛ amɛ akafutu. Cocoa ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ fe nine loo ekwɛ̃ lɛ baaho yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ. ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ ni bɛ ŋmɔtɔ aba batch lɛ mli fɛɛ. Nɔ ni baajɛ mli aba ji akɛ, o-cocoa grade lɛ baa shi.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning pale yellow while the top ones are still green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ shi ŋwɛi baa lɛ yaa nɔ efeɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your soil has run out of nitrogen, which is the main nutrient plants need for green growth. The plant moves nitrogen from older leaves to feed the new leaves at the top, showing you that it needs extra fertilizer.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara. Tso lɛ tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo lɛ amli koni baai heei lɛ ahi nɔ. Etsɔɔ bo akɛ ehe miihia ni akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii krokomɛi afata he.

english: What does chemical fertilizer actually do to my crops that makes them yield more than unfertilized crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sɛɛnamɔi ni yɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ ahe kɛhaa miŋmɔshi nibii? Mɛni haa ewoɔ yibii fe tsei ni awooo amɛ fɔ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer provides essential plant foods like nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium that soil naturally loses over time. Adding fertilizer makes roots grow deeper, stems grow stronger, and plants produce larger grains or fruits.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsei amli niyenii ni he hiaa tamɔ naitrɔjin, fɔsfɔs, kɛ potasiɔm. ni shikpɔŋ lɛ baafite yɛ adebɔɔ naa yɛ be ni eho lɛ mli Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ adara kɛya shɔŋŋ. Tso lɛ mli wa fe tsutsu lɛ. ni tsei woɔ dumɔwui loo aduawai wuji

english: Is it better for me to put fertilizer on my farm when the ground is dry or after rain falls?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ aaawo ŋmɔ lɛ mli ŋmɔshi nibii beni shikpɔŋ lɛ egbi loo beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ?

english: It is best to apply fertilizer when the soil is moist after rain because water dissolves the fertilizer so plant roots can absorb it. Applying fertilizer to bone-dry soil can burn your crop roots and waste the fertilizer.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu baajie ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni tso shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi ni fãji yɔɔ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eshã tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni eha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afite.

english: Cassava plants shed their leaves during dry months to conserve water and protect themselves from heat. The plant goes quiet above ground while keeping energy stored safely in its tubers under the soil until the rain comes back.
ga: Cassava tsei shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ yɛ nyɔji ni nu bɛ lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu nu he ni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Tsei lɛ feɔ dioo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ be mli ni amɛkɛ amɛhewalɛ lɛ toɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli shweshweeshwe kɛyashiɔ nugbɔ baa ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do my tomato plants produce plenty of yellow flowers but end up dropping them without producing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ babaoo shi eegbee shi ni ewooo yibii lɛ?

english: Tomato blossoms drop when the weather gets too hot, when the plant lacks water, or when the soil lacks nutrients like phosphorus that help turn flowers into fruits.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Be mli ni tsei bɛ nu Aloo be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii tamɔ fɔsfɔs ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa fɔfɔi feɔ aduawai.

english: Why do my pepper leaves curl up into small cups instead of spreading out broad and flat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe kɛfee kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee nɔ ni mli kwɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ?

english: Curling pepper leaves are usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking the sap from under the leaf, or by a virus, which stunts the leaf growth and weakens the plant.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ pepper baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ baa. loo hela ko ni gbeɔ mɔ kɛbaa Enɛ tsiɔ baai lɛ adalɛ naa ni ehaa tso lɛ gbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why is it good for me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field with my maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miduɔ tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli kɛ mi-ŋmei lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas capture nitrogen from the air and put it back into the soil through their roots. This naturally enriches the soil and helps neighbor plants like maize grow stronger without exhausting the land.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛkuɔ esɛɛ kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ jɛmɛ lɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa, ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛfiteee shikpɔŋ lɛ.

english: Yam tubers grow bent and short when the soil is too hard or full of stones, making it difficult for the tuber to push downward smoothly as it expands.
ga: Sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baatsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛbaafee kuku kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo eyɛ tɛi. Enɛ haa ewaa kɛhaa yitso lɛ akɛ ebaatsi kɛya shi mlɛo kɛ́ eegbɛ eshwa.

english: Ragged holes in young maize leaves are typically caused by caterpillars like fall armyworm eating the fresh leaves while they are still rolled up inside the stem.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii tamɔ ŋmeii ni egbee shi ni amɛye baai heei lɛ be mli ni amɛbɔle amɛhe lolo yɛ tso lɛ mli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ ŋmei baai bibii amli lɛ baa.

english: Why are my cocoa pods turning dark brown and rotting directly on the trees during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni egboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by black pod disease, a fungal infection that thrives in dark, humid weather and wet conditions, spreading quickly through rain splashes from pod to pod.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ni shwereɔ yɛ duŋ, fɛ̃i, kɛ fɛ̃i shihilɛi amli. Egbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛtsɔɔ nu mli nu ni jɛɔ pod kome mli kɛyaa ekroko mli lɛ nɔ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen or water. Applying NPK fertilizer or well-rotted manure around the base gives the crop the essential nutrients it needs to regain its green color and grow strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen loo nu bɛ o-abele lɛ mli, ni okɛ NPK ŋmɔshi nibii, loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo ni ebɔle he lɛ miitsu nii. Shishitoo lɛ baaha tsei lɛ aná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi jogbaŋŋ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop off when the plant experiences heat stress or uneven watering. Mulching around the roots keeps the soil cool and moist, which helps the plant hold onto its flowers until fruit forms.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be. Mulching around Shishifãi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ baa. Enɛ haa tso lɛ nyɛɔ emɔɔ fɔfɔii amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: I noticed tiny holes and dirt inside the center leaves of my maize. What is causing this?
ga: Miyɔse bu bibioo ko. kɛ muji ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli Mɛni kɛ enɛ ba?

english: Tiny holes with small greenish droppings inside the central shoot are clear signs of Fall Armyworm. Catching them early allows you to apply recommended pest control before they destroy the growing tip of the plant.
ga: Bu bibioo ko ni mli eyi kɛ ŋmɔtɔ bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ ateŋ lɛ mli ji Fall Armyworm he okadi ni yɔɔ faŋŋ. Amɛ ni ooomɔ amɛ mra Enɛ baaha okɛ tsofai ni akɛbuɔ kooloi ni yeɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahe ŋaa lɛ atsu nii dani amɛfite tso lɛ shishigbɛ ni miida lɛ.

english: When cassava reaches full maturity (around 9 to 12 months), the lower leaves will turn yellow and shed, and small cracks will appear in the soil around the base of the stem as the tubers swell underneath.
ga: Beni ŋmei lɛ daa (aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12) lɛ, shishigbɛ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi. ni ŋmeii bibii baaje kpo yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli. Tso lɛ shishigbɛ beni bulb lɛ daa yɛ shishi.

english: The first rain usually only wets the surface, and hot sun right after will dry out the topsoil quickly. It is safer to wait until two or three good rains have soaked deep into the soil before planting your seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋshɔ lɛ hiɛ pɛ. Ni hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ agbi oya. Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ kɛyashi nugbɔ anɛ. Nibii fioo komɛi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ dani adu dumɔwui lɛ.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings get dry and scorched when I clear all the big shade trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ egbi ni amɛshã beni mijie tsei wuji ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants have sensitive leaves that burn easily under direct midday sun. Keeping taller shade trees or planting plantains beside them shields the tender cocoa from excessive heat and keeps the soil moist.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shwane mli lɛ shishi. Tsei ni kɛlɛ ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ loo dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ amɛmasɛi Ebuɔ kookoo ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ he kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni fe nine lɛ he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: If I plant my crops very close together, will I get a bigger harvest from my small piece of land?
ga: Kɛ midu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe waa lɛ maná yibii babaoo kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ bibioo ko nɔ. Mi nɔ loo daabi?

english: No, planting too close forces crops to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, resulting in weak plants with tiny yields. Giving each plant proper space helps them produce bigger, healthier crops.
ga: Dabi, kɛ́ adu tso lɛ ni ebɛŋkɛ tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ abɔi hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni amɛwoɔ yibii babaoo. Kɛ́ aha tso fɛɛ tso gbɛ ni sa lɛ, ebaaye ebua lɛ ni ewo ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to make food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground on wooden stakes exposes more leaves to sunlight, which makes the underground yam tubers grow larger.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ he miihia hulu la tɛ̃ɛ koni efee niyenii eha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ owó wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ yɛ tso nɔ lɛ, ebaaha hulu la babaoo ashɛ tsei lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ feɔ wuji.

english: Is it best to apply my fertilizer right before a heavy rainstorm starts?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa aba?

english: No, heavy rainfall will wash the fertilizer away into streams before your crop roots can absorb it. It is better to apply fertilizer when the soil is already moist after rain, or right before a light drizzle.
ga: Dabi, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baajie ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛ faa lɛ mli dani otsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Esa akɛ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ momo yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ sɛɛ loo dani hulutsoo be fioo ko baa.

english: When is the most important time for me to weed my farm so my crops do not suffer?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni he hiaa fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ majie jwɛi kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akafite?

english: Weeding is most critical during the first three to six weeks after planting. Young crops are weak at this stage, so removing weeds early prevents them from stealing water, light, and nutrients from your plants.
ga: Jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ he hiaa fe fɛɛ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ otsii etɛ kɛyashi enumɔ ni adu sɛɛ lɛ mli. Dumɔwui lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ nɛkɛ be nɛɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ, jiemɔ jwɛi lɛ mra. Ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkaju nu, la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli.

english: How can I stop my harvested maize from getting moldy and spoiled in my storehouse during the rainy season?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ akpa ŋmãa ni akpa lɛ koni ekafee ŋmɔtɔ ni efite yɛ nitoohe lɛ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Moisture in the air promotes mold growth on harvested grains. Store your maize on raised wooden platforms (cribs) off the bare ground, keep the room well-ventilated, and ensure the grains are thoroughly dried in the sun before bagging.
ga: Fɛ̃i ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmeii daa yɛ ŋmaa ni akpa lɛ nɔ. Too abele yɛ tso kpoku ni awo nɔ (cradle) nɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ. Ha kɔɔyɔɔ abote tsu lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. ni okɛ dumɔwui lɛ agbi jogbaŋŋ dani okɛwo kotokui amli

english: What is the best way to keep mice and rats from destroying my stored bags of rice?
ga: Mɛni ji gbɛ ni hi fe fɛɛ ni aaatsɔ nɔ atsĩ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkafite mi-ŋmãa kotokui ni mikɛto lɛ?

english: Rodents enter storage areas looking for easy food. Keep your storehouse clean of spilt grain, seal cracks in walls and doors, elevate storage bags on wooden pallets away from walls, and install metal rodent guards on building supports.
ga: Rodents boteɔ hei ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ koni amɛtao niyenii ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Ha onitoohe lɛ he atse ni ŋmaa ni eshwie shi akafee nɔ ko. Okɛ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ gbogboi kɛ shinaai amli lɛ awo mli. Wo nibii ni akɛtoɔ kotokui ni yɔɔ tsei ahe lɛ anɔ lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ gbogbo lɛ he. ni okɛ dade ni ŋmeii nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ awo tsu lɛ shishi.

english: Why do insects start eating my stored cowpea seeds just a few weeks after I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii bɔi mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yeli yɛ otsii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ beni mikpa amɛ lɛ?

english: Weevils often lay invisible eggs on crop pods while they are still in the field. These eggs hatch after harvest, so you must dry seeds properly and store them in airtight containers or treated storage bags to stop them from multiplying.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii lɛ woɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa amɛ yɛ tsei ahe ŋmeii anɔ be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ. Nɛkɛ wɔji nɛɛ fɔɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe miihia ni ogbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Ni okɛto tsɛnsi loo kotoku ko ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli mli koni amɛkafee babaoo.

english: How can I protect my dried cocoa beans from pests while waiting for buyers to arrive?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mabu mi-kookoo ni egbi lɛ he kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe be mli ni mimɛɔ ni mɛi ni baahe lɛ aba lɛ?

english: Store your dried cocoa beans in clean jute bags placed on raised wooden slats away from walls. Keep the storage space swept clean of trash and food scraps so pests are not attracted to the area.
ga: Okɛ kookoo ŋmeii ni egbi lɛ awo jute kotoku ni mli tse mli. Okɛwo tso ni awó nɔ ni kɛ gbogbo lɛ teŋ jɛkɛ lɛ nɔ. Ha he ni akɛ nibii toɔ lɛ he atse ni jwɛi kɛ niyenii ni efite akafee nɔ ko koni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote jɛmɛ.

english: Why does leaving rotting crop leaves and old stalks in my field cause diseases in my next planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni kɛ́ mishi ŋmɔshi nibii ni egboi kɛ tsei momo yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ekɛ hela baa ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: Old crop residues and rotting plant material act as breeding grounds for insect pests and fungal spores, allowing diseases to survive in the field and attack your new seedlings as soon as they grow.
ga: Tsei amli sũi momo kɛ tsei amli nibii ni fiteɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai fɔɔ yɛ. Ekɛ helai srɔtoi ni baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ aba ni etutua odumɔwui heei lɛ kɛji amɛdara pɛ.

english: Why do weeds growing around my vegetables attract so many destructive insects?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mihe lɛ? No hewɔ lɛ ani mi-vegetables lɛ miigbala kooloi ni fiteɔ nii babaoo nɛkɛ?

english: Weeds serve as alternate host plants where insect pests feed, hide, and reproduce. Clearing weeds regularly deprives insects of shelter and prevents them from spreading to your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi tsuɔ nii akɛ tsei ni ji enyɔ ni tsɛŋemɔ helai yeɔ, amɛteeɔ amɛhe ni amɛfɔɔ bii. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi shwieɔ shi daa lɛ, ebaaha kooloi akabote oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli, ni ebaatsi amɛ gbɛ koni amɛkagbɛ amɛshwã oŋmɔshi nibii titrii lɛ amli.

english: How do pests get into my yam barn even when I close the main door?
ga: Te afeɔ tɛŋŋ ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ boteɔ mi sweet potato ŋmɔ lɛ mli? Eyɛ mli akɛ miŋa shinaa wulu lɛ moŋ

english: Pests like beetles and rodents can enter through tiny gaps in walls, thatched roofs, or directly from infested yams brought into the barn. Inspecting tubers before storage and keeping the barn surrounding clean prevents pest entry.
ga: Nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui tamɔ ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ atsɔ ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ gbogboi amli, jwɛi ni akɛwo tsũi amli, loo kɛjɛ ŋmeii ni akɛbaa ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ okwɛ ŋmeii lɛ amli dani okɛto, ni oha ŋmɔ ni ebɔle he lɛ mli atse lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmeii akabote mli.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot under the soil when heavy rains flood my farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa ni eha ŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ?

english: Flooded soil leaves no air space for roots to breathe, causing the plant tissues to suffocate and decay. Planting cassava on raised ridges or mounds allows excess rainwater to drain away safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ haaa gbɛ ko kwraa aha shishifãi lɛ ni amɛmu. Enɛ haa tso mli fãji lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ ko nɔ loo gɔŋ ko ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black rotten spots at the bottom when heavy rain comes after a long dry period?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato yibii lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔtɔ diŋ baa beni nugbɔ nɛɔ waa yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Sudden shifts between dry weather and heavy rain disrupt how the plant takes up water and calcium, causing blossom end rot. Mulching your soil helps keep moisture levels steady throughout changing weather.
ga: Tsakemɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli egbi kɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ teŋ lɛ gbalaa bɔ ni tsei tsɔɔ nu kɛ calcium mli lɛ mli. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ fiteɔ. Mulching yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulutsoo be lɛ yaa hiɛ daa kɛtsɔ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ.

english: Why do my young vegetable seedlings die after a heavy rainfall even though crops need water to grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-vegetable dumɔwui bibii lɛ gboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa sɛɛ eyɛ mli akɛ nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ moŋ?

english: Heavy rain can wash away topsoil, expose tender seedling roots, or break fragile stems. Using shade nets or nursery beds protects young plants from the physical impact of heavy downpours.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ baanyɛ ahoo sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ. Ha dumɔwui lɛ ashishifãi lɛ afee blɛoo Aloo tso lɛ shishifã ni waaa lɛ baanyɛ akumɔ. Shade netting loo nursery beds ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebuɔ tsei bibii ahe kɛjɛɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ he nibii ni baa amɛnɔ lɛ ahe.

english: No, planting maize too close together causes plants to compete for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This leads to thin, weak stalks that produce very small ears or no grain at all.
ga: Dabi, ŋmãa ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei bibii ni bɛ hewalɛ ni woɔ toi bibii waa loo dumɔwui ko kwraa baa.

english: Young cocoa seedlings have delicate roots and sensitive leaves that cannot tolerate harsh sunlight. They need shade crops like plantains or bananas to shield them and keep the surrounding air humid.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni yɔɔ mlɛo kɛ baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni nyɛɛɛ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo, tamɔ plantain loo banana he miihia amɛ. Koni ebu kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ he ni eha edɔ

english: Tomato plants drop flowers when exposed to extreme heat or irregular watering. When heat or drought stresses the plant, it sheds flowers to save energy and protect its own survival.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛhe wo la ni mli edɔ waa loo nu ni akɛhaa amɛ be fɛɛ be mli. Beni latsaa loo hɔmɔ haoɔ tsei lɛ Fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he ni amɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: Why are my yam tubers growing small and twisted even though the vines are very bushy and green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tsei lɛ bibii ni etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ wain tsei lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔji ni eyɛ ŋmɔji moŋ lɛ?

english: Bushy green vines with small tubers happen when the soil has too much nitrogen relative to potassium. Nitrogen encourages leaf and stem growth, while potassium is what actually feeds and expands the underground tuber.
ga: Wein tsei ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli ni ŋmeii bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa fe nine kɛ akɛto potassium he. Nitrogen haa baa kɛ tso lɛ dalɛ yaa hiɛ. Yɛ be mli ni potassium yeɔ nii diɛŋtsɛ ni ehaa ŋmeii kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why do my pepper plants wilt in the afternoon sun even when the ground around them is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane hulutsoo be mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle ehe lɛ mli egbi moŋ? Ani ebaafee ŋmɔtɔ?

english: Afternoon wilting in wet soil usually means the roots are damaged by fungal rot from too much standing water. Damaged roots cannot absorb water properly, causing the plant to dehydrate under hot sun.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shwane mli ŋmeii ni shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmeii ni jɛɔ nu ni damɔ shi babaoo mli lɛ efite shishifãi lɛ. Shishifãi ni efite lɛ nyɛɛɛ aŋɔ nu jogbaŋŋ. Enɛ haa nu shwieɔ tsei amli yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi.

english: How can I tell if my cassava crops are suffering from drought before they completely dry up?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji mi-cassava tsei lɛ miiye hɔmɔ dani amɛgbi kwraa?

english: Cassava shows early drought stress by dropping its lower leaves and curling its upper leaves inward. This helps the plant reduce water loss through its foliage.
ga: Cassava tsɔɔ hɔmɔ he haomɔ mra kɛtsɔ shishigbɛ baai lɛ ni ekɛshwieɔ shi kɛ ŋwɛi baai lɛ ni ekɛwoɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni nu ni amɛlaajeɔ kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my cassava plants have sticky white spots and start curling up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebɔi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: Sticky white spots and curling leaves indicate a whitefly or mealybug infestation. These tiny insects suck sap from the underside of leaves and secrete a sugary substance that attracts mold.
ga: Hei yɛŋ ni kpɛtɛɔ he kɛ baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ whitefly loo mealybug hela eba. Nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ mli ni amɛjieɔ nɔ ko ni ŋɔɔ ni gbalaa ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do black spots spread so fast across my cocoa pods during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii diji lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ anɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Black spots on cocoa pods during wet weather are caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that thrives and spreads easily through rainwater splashes, high humidity, and poor air movement between trees.
ga: Black pod hela ji nɔ ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ cocoa ŋmɔtɔ nɔ yɛ be mli ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni daa oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, hulutsoo ni fa babaoo, kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni ehiii ni tsɔɔ tsei ateŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do my crops yield less every year when I plant maize on the exact same plot of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific soil nutrients and allows pests and diseases tailored to that crop to build up in the soil. Rotating maize with legumes helps restore soil health.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni etsɔ tso lɛ he lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Abɛi ni akɛ ŋmeii tsakeɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Will cutting off the bottom leaves of my tomato plants hurt them or help them produce more?
ga: Ani mi-tomato tsei lɛ ashishi baai lɛ ni mifoɔ lɛ baaye tomato lɛ awui loo ebaaye ebua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii babaoo?

english: Pruning the lower leaves that touch the soil actually helps the plant. It improves airflow, prevents ground-dwelling fungal spores from splashing onto leaves, and directs food towards fruit development.
ga: Kɛ́ afo shishigbɛ baai ni taa shikpɔŋ lɛ he lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ waa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ hoɔ jogbaŋŋ Etsiɔ ŋmeii ni hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ anaa koni amɛkashwie baai lɛ anɔ. ni amɛkɛ niyenii amaje aduawai akwɛmɔ

english: Why do my maize plants produce very small ears when I plant the seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ woɔ toi bibii waa kɛ́ midu dumɔwui lɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the crops fight each other for sunlight, soil nutrients, and water. Proper spacing gives each plant enough room and resources to grow strong and produce large, full ears of corn.
ga: Kɛji adu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Tsei lɛ baatswa hulu la he akaŋ. Shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛ nu Gbɛ ni sa ni akɛtoɔ tso fɛɛ tso he lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso náa hegbɛ kɛ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ekɛbaakwɛ̃ ni ewo ŋmãa toi wuji ni eyi obɔ.

english: Yam vines need to lift their leaves up to catch maximum sunlight to build food for the tubers underground. Staking also keeps the leaves off the wet soil, which prevents rot and leaf diseases.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ awo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo koni amɛkɛfee niyenii amɛha amɛ shikpɔŋ shishi tsei lɛ. Staking hu yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa baai lɛ shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaye abua ni atsĩ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ tsei ahe helai anaa.

english: Why are the lower leaves on my young maize crops turning pale yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ ashishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves are usually a sign that the soil is running low on nitrogen, which is the nutrient plants need to grow green and leafy. Adding animal manure, compost, or nitrogen fertilizer will help bring back the healthy green color.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛná baai. Kɛ́ akɛ kooloi aŋmei, ŋmɔshi nibii, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ŋmɔji lɛ ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: How does planting groundnuts or cowpeas help make my soil richer for my next crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii loo tsina ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aye abua ni eha mishikpɔŋ lɛ afee nii babaoo kɛha miŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legumes like groundnuts and cowpeas have natural helpers on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the ground. When you harvest them, that stored nutrient stays in the soil to feed the next crop you plant.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmei kɛ tsina ŋmei yɛ adebɔɔ mli yelikɛbuamɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. ni mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Beni okpaa nii lɛ Niyenii ni ato lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ ni obaadu lɛ niyenii.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are tender and easily burn under direct sunshine. Plantains grow very fast and produce large leaves that act as natural umbrellas, providing shade and trapping moisture for the cocoa trees in their first few years.
ga: Cocoa tsei lɛ yɛ mlɛo waa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ha kookoo tso lɛ hulutsoo kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, steal water and plant food from the main mother tree. By removing most of them and leaving just one or two strong ones, the main tree gets all the power it needs to produce a large bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso krɛdɛɛi ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ juɔ nu ni amɛduɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ fɔlɔ tso titri lɛ mli. Kɛtsɔ emli babaoo ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ mli ni ashiɔ tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ nɔ lɛ, tso titri lɛ baaná hewalɛ fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ koni ekɛwo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: What is causing tiny holes in my corn leaves and sawdust-like dirt in the center of the plant?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? yɛ ŋmãa baai kɛ muji ni tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ tso lɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ mli

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which eats through the tender leaves and hides inside the funnel of the plant. Checking your field early and using appropriate treatments protects the crop before they destroy the yield.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ nii kɛtsɔɔ baai bibii amli ni amɛteɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ tsei ashishifãi amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He ni aduɔ nii yɛ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra Ni akɛ tsofa ni sa baatsu nii lɛ baaye abua ni abu ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe dani efite ŋmɔshi nii lɛ.

english: Why are the bottoms of my green tomato fruits turning dark brown and soft before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato eŋɔli lɛ shishi feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efeɔ blɛoo dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This problem is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot get enough calcium while the fruit is growing, often due to dry soil. Watering your plants regularly helps them take up calcium and prevents the fruit from rotting.
ga: Atsɛɔ naagba nɛɛ akɛ fɔmɔ naagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa lɛ kɛ́ tso lɛ náaa calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ be mli ni aduawai lɛ miida lɛ. Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ ni egbi ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ okɛ nu wo otsei lɛ amli daa lɛ, ehaa amɛnáa calcium, ni ehaa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Why do the leaves on my cassava plants drop off when the long dry season starts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmei tsei anɔ lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Dropping leaves is the cassava plant's way of protecting itself during dry weather. By shedding its leaves, the plant saves water inside its stems and roots so it can survive until the next rains come.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ kome ni ŋmei tso lɛ tsɔɔ nɔ ebuɔ ehe yɛ be mli ni nugbɔ nɛɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ ajieɔ baai lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ nu toɔ eshishifãi kɛ eshishifãi lɛ amli bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehi shi kɛyashi nugbɔshiimɔ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli.

english: Why do my pepper leaves roll up tightly during the hottest hours of the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi waa yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ amli lɛ?

english: Pepper leaves curl up in strong sunshine to hide from the heat and stop water from evaporating out of the plant. Once the weather cools down in the evening, the leaves usually open back up.
ga: Pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ mli. Koni ekɛtee ehe kɛjɛ latsaa lɛ he ni ekɛtsi nu ni hoɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ naa. Kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ gbeleɔ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why does my soil need to be plowed with a tractor or hoe before I put seeds in the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ akɛ trakta loo ŋmei atsu shikpɔŋ lɛ he nii dani adu dumɔwui lɛ?

english: Plowing breaks up hard, packed soil so plant roots can spread easily to find water and nutrients. It also buries weeds and creates soft dirt where delicate young roots won't struggle to grow.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ gbálaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ mli koni efee mlɛo aha tsei shishifãi lɛ ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã koni amɛyatao nu kɛ niyenii. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni shishifãi bibii lɛ bɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ lɛ.

english: If I clear weeds from my farm, is it better to burn them or leave them on top of the soil before planting?
ga: Ani ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ aaajie jwɛi kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ashã, loo ashi yɛ shikpɔŋ dani adu?

english: Leaving cleared weeds on the ground acts like a blanket that keeps the soil cool and traps moisture during hot days. Burning clears the field fast but burns away valuable nutrients that could feed your soil.
ga: Kɛ́ ashi jwɛi ni ajie lɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ tsɔne ni yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi yɛ gbii ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ amli. Shãa oya haa he ni oyɔɔ lɛ mli tseɔ shi eshãa niyenii ni he hiaa ni baanyɛ aha oshikpɔŋ lɛ niyenii.

english: Will plowing my field every season make the soil lose its strength over time?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ daa be lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ aba shi yɛ be ni sa mli?

english: Frequent deep plowing can wear out the soil structure and cause rich topsoil to wash away in heavy rains. To keep your land strong, alternate plowing with minimal tilling and leave crop residues on the field.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii shii abɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii lɛ afite. ni ehaa sũ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi ni baa nii lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli. Bɔni afee ni oshikpɔŋ lɛ afee nɔ ni hi Tsɔɔmɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo pɛ atsu nii ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ashi yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Should I plant my seeds immediately after the very first rain of the season, or wait longer?
ga: Ani esa akɛ madu dumɔwui yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ yɛ be lɛ mli lɛ sɛɛ nɔŋŋ loo esa akɛ mamɛ be babaoo?

english: It is safer to wait until the rains become steady. The first rain is often a 'false rain' that quickly dries up; if hot weather returns right after planting, your seeds will dry out and die under the dirt.
ga: Eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ ooomɛ ni nugbɔ lɛ aba shi. Bei pii lɛ, klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔ lɛ ji ‘nugbɔ amale’ ni gbɛ́ɔ oya kɛji kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ ku esɛɛ eba amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni adu nii lɛ sɛɛ. Dumɔwui lɛ gbiɔ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: What time of the day is best for me to sow my crop seeds into the soil?
ga: Mɛɛ gbi mli be hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha mi akɛ madu aduawai dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ?

english: Early morning or late afternoon is best because the soil is cooler. Sowing during intense midday heat can stress and scorch tender sprouts as soon as they try to break open.
ga: Leebi loo shwane ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ejaakɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ejɔ. Dumɔ yɛ shwane mli ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ lɛ mli lɛ baanyɛ aha tsei bibii lɛ aná nɔnyɛɛ ni amɛshã amɛ kɛji amɛbɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: How do I test if my field has enough moisture after plowing to start planting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maka kɛji miŋmɔ lɛ mli nu lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli nitsumɔ sɛɛ koni mabɔi dumɔwui?

english: Grab a handful of soil from a few inches deep and squeeze it into a ball. If it holds together without dripping water and easily crumbles when poked, the soil moisture is just right for planting.
ga: Kpɔ̃ɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni ji inchi fioo ko ni okɛmimɔ mli ni okɛfee bɔɔlu. Kɛji akɛ ekɛ ehe kpɛtɛɔ he ni nu shwieee shi ni efoɔ oya kɛji akɛ atswa lɛ. Etsɔɔ akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ sa kɛha dumɔwui.

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. Instead of producing big cobs, the plants spend all their energy stretching upward to reach the light.
ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni Tsei lɛ baafee cob blɔkii wuji lɛ kɛ amɛhewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii koni amɛshɛ ŋwɛi koni amɛná la.

english: Why do my crop leaves droop and curl during hot afternoons even when the soil was prepared well?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbee shi ni amɛkpãa shi yɛ shwane ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ? Kɛji akɛ asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jogbaŋŋ po.

english: In strong afternoon sun, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink from the soil. Curling or drooping is a defense mechanism to conserve water, and they usually bounce back by evening.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli kɛ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nu ni shwieɔ shi loo ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji gbɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ abuɔ he koni akɛbu nu he. ni bei pii lɛ, efoɔ esɛɛ gbɛkɛ

english: Why do cassava plants stay alive during dry spells when my other crops die?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava tso lɛ hiɔ shi yɛ fɛ̃i be mli beni mitsei krokomɛi lɛ gboi lɛ?

english: Cassava stores water and food in its thick underground roots. During long dry periods, it drops its leaves to save moisture and rests until the rains return to wake it back up.
ga: Cassava kɛ nu kɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ toɔ eshishifãi ni mli tse ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ amli. Yɛ be kakadaŋŋ mli lɛ, baai lɛ shwieɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he ni amɛjɔɔ amɛhe kɛyashi nugbɔ lɛ baaku esɛɛ eba ni ebate amɛ shi ekoŋŋ.

english: Why do some of my seeds sprout within a few days while others in the same field never come up?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ ekomɛi kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ gbii fioo komɛi amli yɛ be mli ni ekrokomɛi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ kwɛɛɛ kwraa lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to sprout if they are planted too deep, eaten by underground pests, or if the seeds were old or damaged. Planting good quality seed at the correct shallow depth ensures uniform sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ adu amɛ shɔŋŋ tsɔ. Shikpɔŋ shishi kooloi yeɔ loo kɛji dumɔwui lɛ egbɔ loo efite Dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni adu yɛ he ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni sa lɛ baaha amɛkwɛ̃ be fɛɛ be.

english: Why are the leaves on my young maize plants turning pale yellow from the tips downward?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛ amɛshishigbɛ kɛbashi shi lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves in maize usually signal a lack of nitrogen in the soil, which is an essential nutrient for leafy growth. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizers like Urea or well-decomposed animal manure will help restore the leaves to a healthy green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ sũ lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa kɛha baai lɛ adalɛ Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni shwieɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baa lɛ aku sɛɛ afee eŋɔli kwraa.

english: Why do people advise me to plant groundnuts or cowpeas alongside my maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mɛi woɔ ŋaa akɛ madu ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ mi ŋmei lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Groundnuts and cowpeas are legumes that pull nitrogen gas from the air and trap it in the soil through their roots. This naturally fertilizes the soil, helping nearby crops like maize grow bigger and healthier without relying solely on chemical fertilizers.
ga: Peanuts kɛ cowpeas ji ŋmeii ni gbalaa nitrogen gas kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔshi nii yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ, tamɔ ŋmãa lɛ, ni amɛdaraa ni amɛnáa hewalɛ ni amɛkɛ amɛhe fɔ̃ɔɔ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ pɛ nɔ.

english: Why are my young cocoa seedlings drying up and dropping leaves during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo tsei bibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ ni amɛbaai lɛ fiteɔ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are extremely sensitive to direct intense sunlight and dry winds. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains or cassava around young cocoa provides a protective canopy that reduces heat stress and retains soil moisture.
ga: Kokoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Be kukuoo mli hulutsoo tsei tamɔ plantains loo cassava ni aduɔ yɛ jɛmɛ he fɛɛ he. Kookoo bibioo haa ŋwɛi ŋtayaa hebuu ni haa dɔlɛ he haomɔ baa shi ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi.

english: Upward leaf curling on pepper plants is commonly caused by tiny sap-sucking pests like thrips or mites, or viral infections spread by them. Spraying with organic neem extracts or recommended insecticides helps clear the pests so new, healthy leaves can grow.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ thrips loo mites lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei anɔ lɛ baa. loo helai ni jɛɔ helai amli ni amɛgbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Kɛ́ akɛ organic neem extract loo tsofa ko ni akɛwoɔ he ŋaa ni akɛgbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie kooloi ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ koni baai heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: What causes small holes and chewed edges on the leaves at the center of my maize plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Ni ŋmeii ni ashɛreɔ yɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ ateŋ lɛ anɔ lɛ?

english: This damage is typically caused by Fall Armyworm caterpillars that feed inside the central leaf whorl of young maize plants. Inspecting fields early and applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem solutions stops them before they destroy the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni yeɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ashishifãi ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. He lɛ mlikwɛmɔ mra kɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi loo neem tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii ni atsɔɔ akɛ akɛtsu nii lɛ. Kpa nibii nɛɛ dani amɛfite ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot under the soil before I harvest them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani akpaa lɛ?

english: Cassava roots rot when they sit in overly wet or waterlogged soil for too long, which deprives roots of oxygen and invites fungal infections. Planting cassava on raised mounds or ridges improves water drainage and protects the tubers.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji amɛtara shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ loo nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ. Enɛ haa shishifãi lɛ bɛ kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa ni ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai baa. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ehaa nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ ni ebuɔ ŋmeii lɛ ahe.

english: Lowland rice varieties thrive in wet conditions because controlled flooding smothers weeds that compete for nutrients, while keeping the soil roots moist and continuously nourished.
ga: Omɔ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, nu afua lɛ baaye abua ni ejie jwɛi ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ he akaŋ lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ehaa amɛnáa niyenii be fɛɛ be.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the plant experiences extreme heat stress, irregular watering, or insect attack. Keeping the soil consistently moist and shielding plants during intense midday heat encourages flowers to set fruit.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa. Nu ni akɛhaa be fɛɛ be loo kooloi ni tutuaa amɛ Enɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ ni ebuɔ tsei ahe yɛ hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ waa lɛ mli. Tswaa fɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛwo yibii

english: Why do I need to clear weeds and stake my yam vines with tall wooden sticks?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tsei kakadaji ajie jwɛi ni mikɛdu mi-sweet potato tsei lɛ?

english: Yam vines need to climb high to capture enough sunlight to make food, which is then stored in the underground tubers. Staking lifts leaves off the damp ground, preventing leaf diseases and leading to much larger tubers.
ga: Ehe miihia ni sweet potato wain tsei lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi shɔɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha nihoomɔ. ni abaato shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii lɛ amli Staking haa baai lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ. Etsiɔ tsei ahe helai anaa ni ekɛ tsei ni dara babaoo baa.

english: Why do my plantain trees easily fall over when they start producing big bunches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ ebɔi ŋmeii wuji feemɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain trees have shallow root systems and become very top-heavy when carrying full fruit bunches. Propping the stems with sturdy bamboo poles supports the weight and protects the roots from snapping in strong winds.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ yɛ shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ, ni amɛhe wa kɛji amɛwo yibii ni ebɔle amɛhe jogbaŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmei tsei ni wa fiɔ tso lɛ sɛɛ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛfiɔ muji lɛ sɛɛ, ni ehaaa shishifãi lɛ akumɔ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli.

english: Why do my crops grow faster when I mix animal manure into the soil before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa oya kɛ́ mikɛ ŋmɔtɔ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani midu lɛ?

english: Animal manure acts like rich food for the soil. It slowly releases nutrients that crops need to grow strong, while also helping the soil hold onto rainwater longer so the roots do not dry out.
ga: Manure tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni fa babaoo kɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ, ni ejieɔ niyenii ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ lɛ kpo fiofio. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. No hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ egbiɛɛ.

english: Can I put fresh goat manure directly around my young plants, or will it harm them?
ga: Mibaanyɛ mikɛ too ŋmɔtɔ hee abɔle he. Ani abaanyɛ adu mi dumɔwui lɛ tɛ̃ɛ? Aloo ebaaye amɛ awui?

english: Fresh animal manure produces heat and strong chemicals as it breaks down, which can burn and damage tender crop roots. It is best to let the manure dry and rot in a pile for a few weeks before putting it on your farm.
ga: Manɔ hee jieɔ dɔlɛ kɛ tsofai ni mli wa kpo beni efiteɔ lɛ. ni baanyɛ ashã ni efite tsei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ ashishifãi Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oooha ŋmeii lɛ agbi ni egbo yɛ ŋmei mli otsii fioo komɛi dani okɛfata oŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Dry grass acts like a blanket over the soil. It shades the earth from the harsh sun so water does not evaporate quickly, prevents weeds from growing, and turns into rich plant food as it breaks down.
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Ebuɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni naa wa lɛ he bɔni afee ni nu lɛ akasha oya. Etsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ ni ebafeɔ tsei niyenii ni jara wa kɛji egbo

english: Why are the leaves of my maize crop turning light yellow instead of dark green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your crops are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant nutrient found in healthy soil or organic manure. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot make the green color it needs to feed itself.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia onibii. ni ji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni anaa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni hi jogbaŋŋ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee su ni ji eŋɔli ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkɛkwɛ amɛhe lɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable crops droop down in the afternoon heat even when I water them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ mibɛ eko moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: During the hottest part of the day, plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it up from the ground. They droop to conserve moisture, but they usually bounce back once the afternoon cools down.
ga: yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni mli edɔ fe fɛɛ lɛ mli Tsei shwieɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ oya fe bɔ ni amɛshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Amɛkotoɔ shi koni amɛbu ŋmɔtɔ he. Shi amɛfɔɔ sɛɛkuu be mli ni shwane lɛ mli jɔɔ lɛ.

english: Pepper plants drop their flowers when they experience stress, such as severe heat, lack of water, or poor soil fertility. The plant sheds the flowers because it feels it does not have enough energy to support growing fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ baashwie amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ kɛji akɛ amɛkpe haomɔi tamɔ latsaa ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo shikpɔŋ ni ehiii lɛ nɔ. Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ ejaakɛ amɛnuɔ he akɛ amɛbɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛye amɛbua aduawai ni miida lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots stay thin and small when I plant them in hard ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni amɛfeɔ bibii kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa nɔ lɛ?

english: Root crops like cassava and yams need soft, loose earth to expand outward easily. When planted in hard, packed soil, the roots struggle to push through the dirt, resulting in small, thin, or twisted tubers.
ga: Shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei kɛ ŋmei Ehe miihia shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ koni egbɛ eshwa kponɔgbɛ mlɛo. Kɛ adu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ nɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛtsi shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛya ŋwɛi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, yitso lɛ feɔ bibioo, eyɛ mlɛo, loo egbɛ eshwaa.

english: What happens to my crops if I plant seeds too close to each other in the same field?
ga: Mɛni baaba miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli?

english: When seeds are planted too close together, the growing plants fight each other for sunlight above ground and for food and water below ground. This competition makes all the plants grow tall, thin, and weak.
ga: Beni dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei ni miida lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, kɛ niyenii kɛ nu ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi lɛ. Akaŋshii nɛɛ haa tsei lɛ fɛɛ daraa kɛkwɔlɛɔ, amɛgbɔjɔɔ, ni amɛgbɔjɔɔ.

english: Why do my crops produce smaller harvests when I plant the exact same crop on the same plot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop every season drains the soil of the specific nutrients that particular crop loves, while allowing pests that prefer that plant to build up in the soil. Changing your crop each year gives the soil time to rebuild.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa be lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ naa niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni tso lɛ sumɔɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni sumɔɔ nakai tso lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ daa afi lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ náa be ni ekɛsaa ehe.

english: The rain causes crops to sprout tender new leaves, which naturally attract hungry insects looking for soft food and moisture. Wet conditions also make it easier for many farm pests to hatch and multiply quickly.
ga: Nugbɔ lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ baai heei blɛoo. Enɛ gbalaa kooloi bibii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitao niyenii ni mli jɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Shihilɛi ni mli ewo fɔ lɛ hu yeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔ mli kooloi babaoo ni amɛfɔɔ ni amɛshwereɔ oya.

english: If the stream water near my farm is muddy and polluted from upstream washing, will it harm my cabbage and pepper crops if I use it to water them?
ga: Ni kɛji akɛ nu ni yɔɔ faa ni bɛŋkɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli ewo muji ni ejɛ faa lɛ ŋwɛigbɛ nu ni afɔɔ he lɛ mli ewo muji hu? Ani ebaaye mi-cabbage kɛ pepper tsei lɛ awui kɛji mikɛtsu nii kɛha amɛ nu?

english: Yes, water contaminated with chemicals, heavy metals, or excessive sediment can poison the soil, damage root tips so they cannot absorb nutrients, and leave harmful substances on fruits and vegetables.
ga: Hɛɛ, nu ni akɛ tsofai ni fa fe nine, dade ni tsii, loo sũ ewo mli lɛ baanyɛ afite sũ lɛ. Efiteɔ shishifãi lɛ ashishifãi lɛ aahu akɛ amɛnyɛŋ amɛŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ. ni eshiɔ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ aduawai kɛ aduawai anɔ.

english: Why does my land produce fewer crops each year after the top layer of black soil was washed away by rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ ŋmɔshi nibii fioo daa afi beni nugbɔ efo shikpɔŋ diŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Topsoil contains almost all the natural manure and beneficial micro-organisms crops need to feed; once topsoil is lost, the hard subsoil underneath cannot hold water or feed plant roots properly.
ga: Nɔ ni miihe ashɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛɛ ji adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni he hiaa ni ŋmɔshi nibii aye lɛ. Kɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ laaje lɛ Shikpɔŋ shishi ni wa ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ nyɛŋ ahiɛ nu loo eye ebua tsei shishifãi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant suffers from extreme heat, lack of water, or too much nitrogen fertilizer, which makes the plant focus on growing big green leaves instead of setting fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na piŋmɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo nitrogen ni fa babaoo ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ hewɔ. Enɛ haa tso lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ moŋ fe ni eeewo yibii.

english: Why do I need to stake my yam vines with wood instead of leaving them to spread across the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso awo mi-sweet potato wain tsei lɛ amli lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeeŋmɛ gbɛ ni egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Lifting yam leaves onto stakes helps them catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the underground tuber, while keeping the leaves off the damp ground prevents rot and fungal diseases.
ga: Sweet potato baai ni aaawo nɔ yɛ tsei anɔ lɛ haa amɛnáa hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ hei ni ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ koni ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ akafee nɔ ko.

english: Why are my cassava roots growing small, thin, and woody instead of big and soft?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ ji bibii, ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni tamɔ tsei yɛ agboi ni yɔɔ blɛoo najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots become woody when the soil is packed too tightly for the roots to expand, or when the plant lacks potassium and water during the critical months when tubers are filling out.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ bafeɔ tso kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ebɔle ehe aahu akɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã. Aloo beni tso lɛ bɛ potassium kɛ nu yɛ nyɔji ni he hiaa waa ni bulb lɛ eyi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: Why are my green cocoa pods turning brown and black while still hanging on the tree branches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cocoa ŋmɔtɔi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji lɛ amli lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ediŋŋ be mli ni amɛkã tso nine lɛ nɔ lolo lɛ?

english: This is Black Pod disease, caused by a fungus that spreads rapidly in wet, humid conditions when trees are pruned too little or shaded too heavily, trapping moisture inside the farm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ black pod hela lɛ baa ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ shihilɛi ni mli edɔ mli beni afolɔ tsei fioo tsɔ loo hulutsoo be babaoo yɔɔ mli, ni emɔɔ fɛ̃i yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Yellowing starting at the leaf tip usually means your maize is starving for nitrogen, an essential food crop roots need to build healthy green leaves and large corn ears.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shishijee ŋmɔŋ ni baa yɛ baai lɛ anaa lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Enɛɛmɛi ji niyenii tso shishifãi ni he hiaa koni aná baai eŋɔli ni mli wa kɛ ŋmãa toi wuji.

english: Why does my field become hard like concrete after I burn all the weeds and farm bush before planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli wa tamɔ kɔnkrit beni mishã ŋmɔ mli jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii lɛ fɛɛ dani midu lɛ sɛɛ?

english: Burning destroys the organic material and leaf litter that act like a sponge to keep soil loose and moist; without it, rain bakes the bare ground into a dry, hard crust.
ga: Shãa fiteɔ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ baai amli jwɛi ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ sponji koni eha sũ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ lɛ, ebaashã shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ lɛ. Etsɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni wa ni egbi.

english: Why do my okra leaves turn pale yellow and dry up early even when I weed regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi okra baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ oya kɛ́ mikɛ jwɛi shwie shi daa po lɛ?

english: Pale, dry leaves despite weeding often point to root-knot nematodes—tiny worms in the soil that attack roots and block water from moving up the plant—or severe nutrient deficiencies in poor soil.
ga: Baai ni mli tse, ni egbi yɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ lɛ fɔɔ shishifã-knot nematodes tsɔɔ. Enɛɛmɛi ji ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni tutuaa shishifãi lɛ ni amɛtsiɔ nu naa koni ekaya tso lɛ nɔ. loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa waa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni ehiii nɔ

english: Why does my harvested maize spoil so quickly if I leave it sitting in my storage shed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpa lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji mishi yɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Harvested maize naturally holds moisture inside the grains. If left unprocessed or undried, this moisture traps heat, attracting insects and causing mold and rot to destroy the crop.
ga: Abɛi ni akpa lɛ haa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ eshishifãi lɛ amli yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛji akɛ ashi ni atsuuu he nii loo egbi lɛ, nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ mɔ̃ɔ dɔlɛ, egbalaa kooloi, ni ehaa ŋmɔtɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa ni efiteɔ ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why is it necessary to dry my freshly harvested paddy rice before milling it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa ni akpa ehee dani ashɛre lɛ?

english: Wet rice grains are soft and fragile, causing them to crack and crush into small broken pieces when milled. Proper drying hardens the rice grains so they come out whole and store well.
ga: Omɔ ŋmaa ni efɔ lɛ yɛ bɔdɔɔ ni egbɛɔ eshwaa, kɛ́ atsɔ mli lɛ, egbɛɔ eshwaa bibii bibii. Kɛ́ egbi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmaa lɛ mli awa. No hewɔ lɛ, dumɔwui lɛ jeɔ kpo muu ni amɛtoɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my stored yams start sprouting green shoots even when they are kept inside a cool barn?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-sweet potatoes ni mikɛto lɛ miije shishi amɛmiikwɛ̃ eyɛ mli akɛ akɛto ŋmɔ ko ni mli ejɔ mli moŋ?

english: Yams are live tubers that naturally enter a short resting period after harvest. Once that rest period ends, warmer temperatures signal the yam to use its stored food energy to grow new vines.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji ŋmeii ni hiɛ ka ni amɛboteɔ be kukuoo mli ni amɛhiɛɔ shi yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ sɛɛ. Kɛ nakai hejɔɔmɔ lɛ ba naagbee lɛ, hulutsoo be ni mli edɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ sweet potatoes kɛ niyenii hewalɛ ni ato lɛ baatsu nii ni ekɛdu wain tsei heei.

english: How do I know when my maize stalks are mature and ready for harvesting?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-abele tsei lɛ edara ni esa akɛ akpa?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the leaves turn dry and brown, and the silks on top of the cob turn dark. Pressing a grain with your fingernail should feel firm without releasing milky liquid.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ kɛji baai lɛ egbi ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Ni siliki ni yɔɔ ŋmei lɛ yiteŋ lɛ baatsɔ ediŋŋ. Esa akɛ kɛ́ okɛ onineshi tsɔne mii dumɔwui lɛ anɔ lɛ, onu he akɛ eyɛ shiŋŋ ni ejieee nu ko ni tamɔ mliki kpo.

english: Why do my crops produce a huge harvest in some years but very little in other years?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ afii komɛi amli shi fioo pɛ yɛ afii krokomɛi amli lɛ?

english: Crop yields naturally change based on weather conditions. When rains fall at the exact right times during flowering and fruiting without long droughts or heavy flooding, crops produce abundant yields.
ga: Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ tsakeɔ yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ be ni sa mli yɛ fɔfɔi kɛ yibiiwoo teŋ ni hɔmɔ ni sɛɛ tsɛɔ loo nu afua ni naa wa bɛ mli. Nibii ni adu lɛ baawo yibii babaoo.

english: Why do the leaves on my growing maize plants turn yellow before the cobs are formed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei ni miida lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmɔŋ lɛ baa lɛ?

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the maize plant is lacking essential nutrients like nitrogen from the soil. Without enough nitrogen, the plant cannot feed its leaves properly, which hurts crop growth.
ga: Baai ŋmɔŋ tsɔɔ akɛ ŋmã tso lɛ bɛ niyenii ni he hiaa, tamɔ nitrogen, kɛjɛ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛji nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa bɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ aha foliar niyenii ni sa. ni yɔɔ hewalɛ gbonyo yɛ tsei adalɛ nɔ

english: Why does rice require so much wet mud or standing water to grow compared to maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa biɔ muji ni mli efɔ loo nu ni damɔ shi babaoo dani ekwɛ̃ kɛ akɛto ŋmãa he lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally thrive in waterlogged soil because their root system is built to absorb oxygen underwater, while the standing water also prevents weeds from growing around the crop.
ga: Omɔ tsei daa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ nɔ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, afee shishifãi lɛ koni amɛŋɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yɔɔ nu shishi lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hu tsiɔ jwɛi anaa koni ekakwɛ̃ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe.

english: Yam tubers grow long and thick underground. Raised soil mounds create soft, loose earth that allows the root to expand easily while protecting it from standing water that rots tubers.
ga: Sweet potato tsei lɛ daraa kakadaŋŋ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi. Gɔŋ ni nɔ kwɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni etse ehe ni haa shishifãi lɛ shwereɔ mlɛo yɛ be mli ni ebuɔ he kɛjɛɔ nu ni ekã shi ni haa ŋmeii lɛ fiteɔ lɛ he.

english: Why does a plantain tree die after producing just one big bunch of fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ plantains gboɔ beni ewo aduawai agbo kome pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: A plantain stalk is programmed by nature to flower and bear fruit only once in its life. After producing fruit, the stalk dies back so it can pass its energy down to the young sucker shoots at its base.
ga: Adebɔɔ eto plantain tsei lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ koni amɛwo fɔfɔi ni amɛwo yibii shikome pɛ yɛ amɛshihilɛ mli. Beni ewo yibii sɛɛ lɛ, tso lɛ gboɔ bɔni afee ni anyɛ atsu hewalɛ kɛya tso bibioo lɛ nɔ yɛ eshishi.

english: Allowing too many shoot suckers to grow creates competition for water, sunlight, and soil food. Pruning away extra suckers leaves enough strength for the main stem to yield a large, heavy bundle.
ga: Ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ŋmeii babaoo shwereɔ lɛ kɛ akaŋshii baa kɛha nu, hulu la kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Kɛ́ afolɔ tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ aná hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha efee agbo ni etsii.

english: Why is my new cocoa farm not producing any pods even though the trees are already tall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔ hee lɛ ewooo pods eyɛ mli akɛ tsei lɛ ekwɛ̃ momo moŋ?

english: Cocoa trees focus their early energy on growing a strong root system and frame before producing fruit. It usually takes 3 to 5 years for cocoa trees to fully mature and start bearing pods.
ga: Cacao tsei lɛ kɛ amɛjwɛŋmɔ maa shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ bɔ ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ nɔ dani amɛwo yibii. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ afii 3 kɛyashi 5 dani cacao tso ko daa ni ebɔi ŋmeii feemɔ.

english: Why can't I harvest my cassava after 4 months like my neighbor harvests his maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ minyɛɛɛ makpa ŋmãa yɛ nyɔji 4 sɛɛ tamɔ bɔ ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ kpaɔ eŋmãa lɛ?

english: Maize is a fast-growing cereal crop, whereas cassava is a root crop that needs 9 to 12 months to build up and store starch underground in its tubers.
ga: Abɛi ji ŋmaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni daa oya. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmei ji ŋmei lɛ, eheɔ nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani ekɛ ŋmei lɛ feɔ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ shishi yɛ ŋmei lɛ mli.

english: I applied fertilizer to my maize field yesterday, so why haven't the leaves turned green yet?
ga: Nyɛsɛɛ nɛɛ mikɛ ŋmãa wo ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ mli, shi mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ etsɔko ŋmãa lolo lɛ?

english: Fertilizer takes time to dissolve in soil water before the roots can absorb it. It usually takes a few days to a week to see visible improvements in the plants.
ga: Be he miihia ni ŋmɔshi nibii atsɔ shikpɔŋ nu mli dani shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ. Bei pii lɛ, eheɔ gbii fioo komɛi kɛyashi otsi kome dani anaa hiɛyaa ni kadiɔ mɔ yɛ tsei lɛ amli.

english: Why does poultry manure take longer to show results on my vegetables compared to chemical fertilizer?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi ashishifãi heɔ be babaoo dani etsɔɔ nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa yɛ mi aduawai lɛ anɔ kɛ akɛto tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Poultry manure is an organic material that soil microbes must slowly break down before plants can feed on it, whereas chemical fertilizers dissolve and act almost immediately.
ga: Kooloi ashishifã ji nɔ ko ni wala yɔɔ mli ni esa akɛ sũ mli helai bibii ajie fiofio. Efiteɔ dani tsei baanyɛ aye lɛ. Shi tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ, shwieɔ shi ni etsuɔ ​​nii aaafee amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are tiny green oranges falling off my tree before they grow big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tangerine bibii miiho kɛmiijɛ mitso lɛ nɔ dani amɛdara lɛ?

english: Citrus trees naturally drop excess young fruits if they do not have enough stored energy, water, or soil nutrients to support all of them to maturity.
ga: Citrus tsei lɛ shwieɔ aduawai bibii ni fa fe nine lɛ yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛji amɛbɛ hewalɛ, nu, loo niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni ato yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni baaye abua amɛ kɛyashi amɛdara.

english: My tomato plants have plenty of yellow flowers, so why are there no tomatoes forming yet?
ga: Mi tomato tsei lɛ yɛ fɔfɔi ŋmɔŋ babaoo. No hewɔ lɛ mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ efɔɔɔ lolo lɛ?

english: Flowers must first be pollinated by insects or wind and complete fertilization before the petals wither away and the green fruit begins to grow.
ga: Esa akɛ kooloi bibii loo kɔɔyɔɔ afee fɔfɔi lɛ pollen klɛŋklɛŋ. Ni ebaawo mli kwraa dani tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ agbi ni tso yibii eŋɔli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃.

english: Why do grafted mango trees produce fruit much faster than mango trees planted from seeds?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mango ni akɛwo tso mli lɛ woɔ yibii oya fe mango tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Grafted branches are taken from mature trees that are already capable of fruiting, while trees grown directly from seed must spend several years maturing first.
ga: Tsei niji ni akɛwo tsei wuji ni baanyɛ awo yibii momo lɛ amli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei ni jɛ dumɔwui amli tɛ̃ɛ lɛ heɔ afii babaoo dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ klɛŋklɛŋ.

english: I pruned my cocoa trees last week, but why do they look bare instead of bushy now?
ga: Mifolɔ kookoo tsei lɛ otsi ni eho lɛ. Shi mɛni hewɔ amrɔ nɛɛ etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeefee ŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: Pruning briefly removes foliage to let sunlight reach the inner branches. It takes a few weeks for the tree to respond by pushing out fresh, healthy shoots.
