ga: Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi lɛ jieɔ tsei ahe tsei yɛ be kukuoo mli. koni hulu la lɛ ashɛ tsei niji ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahe Tso lɛ baahe otsii fioo komɛi ni ekɛha hetoo kɛtsɔ ŋmeii heei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ekɛbaa lɛ nɔ.

english: Why should I leave my farm land unfarmed for a season when I need to plant every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi miŋmɔshi shikpɔŋ lɛ ni mɔ ko mɔ ko bɛ nɔ kɛyashi be kome lɛ? Ni esa akɛ madu daa afi?

english: Continuous planting drains the soil of essential nutrients. Resting the land gives time for natural organic matter and soil life to restore fertility for future crops.
ga: Dumɔ ni yaa nɔ lɛ haa niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Shikpɔŋ lɛ hejɔɔmɔ haa be kɛhaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ wala koni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: I planted oil palm seeds two weeks ago, so why haven't any sprouts come out of the soil yet?
ga: Midu mu tso dumɔwui otsii enyɔ ni eho nɛ. Mɛni hewɔ ekwɛko kɛjɛko shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lolo lɛ?

english: Oil palm seeds have thick, hard outer shells and natural dormancy periods, meaning they often take several weeks or even months to break open and germinate.
ga: Mu tso dumɔwui yɛ kponɔgbɛ ŋmei ni mli wa, kɛ adebɔɔ mli wɔɔhe be. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ bei pii lɛ amɛheɔ otsii loo nyɔji dani amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ.

english: Why do extension officers tell us to plant two or three maize seeds together in one hole instead of just one?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔdu ŋmãa dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ ekome yɛ bu kome mli moŋ fe ekome pɛ lɛ?

english: Planting two or three seeds together ensures that if one seed fails to sprout, another will take its place. Young seedlings growing close together can also help each other push through tough soil before you thin them out.
ga: Dumɔwui enyɔ loo etɛ ni aduɔ yɛ he kome lɛ haa anáa nɔmimaa akɛ kɛji dumɔwu kome kwɛɛɛ lɛ, Dumɔwu kroko baaye esɛɛ. Dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛhe ni amɛtsɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani okɛ dumɔwui lɛ afee bibioo.

english: Why do my crops grow very tall and thin with poor yield when I plant them too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kɛlɛ ni amɛhe yɔɔ mlɛo ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When crops are planted too closely, they compete with each other like siblings fighting over food. They stretch upward to reach sunlight, spending all their energy growing tall instead of producing heavy fruits or grains.
ga: Kɛ adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ tsɔ Ebaatswa akaŋ tamɔ nyɛmimɛi ni miiwu yɛ niyenii he. Amɛkpã amɛhe koni amɛmɔ hulu la lɛ. Ekɛ hewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii moŋ fe ni eeewo aduawai loo ŋmaa ni tsii.

english: Young cocoa trees burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow very fast and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving young cocoa plants the shade and cool air they need to survive.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains daa oya waa ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Ehaa kookoo tsei bibii lɛ naa hulutsoo kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛhi shi.

english: If I save seeds from my best maize crop this year, will the next harvest be just as good?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ afi nɛɛ ŋmãa dumɔwui ni hi fe fɛɛ lɛ to Ani ŋmãa ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ baafee nɔ ni hi nakai nɔŋŋ?

english: Seeds taken from parent plants share similar traits with their parent crop, but hybrid seeds lose their strength over generations. Using fresh certified seeds ensures every plant stays uniform and yields well.
ga: Dumɔwui ni ajieɔ kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ tso lɛ mli lɛ. Shi dumɔwui ni akɛfee hybrid lɛ hewalɛ baa shi yɛ amɛwala be fɛɛ mli. Dumɔwui heei ni awo he odaseyeli ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ haa tso fɛɛ tso feɔ ekome ni ewoɔ yibii kpakpai.

english: Is it good to grow cassava and maize together on the same plot of land?
ga: Ani ehi akɛ abaadu ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ?

english: Yes, planting them together works well because maize grows quickly and is harvested early, leaving the field open for the slower-growing cassava to expand its roots later.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmãa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmãa mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ ejaakɛ ŋmãa daa oya, ni akpaa lɛ mra. Shi ŋmɔ lɛ mli koni ŋmei ni kwɛ̃ɔ blɛoo lɛ anyɛ agbɛ eshishifãi lɛ ashwã sɛɛ mli.

english: Leaf curling is a natural behavior pepper plants use to protect themselves. By rolling up their leaves, they reduce the amount of leaf surface exposed to direct sun to keep water from escaping.
ga: Baai lɛ ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji adebɔɔ mli subaŋ ko ni pepper tsei kɛtsuɔ nii kɛbuɔ amɛhe he. Kɛ́ atsɔ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ, ehaa hulu la ni shɛɔ baa lɛ nɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baa shi koni nu akaje mli.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my yellow corn plants turning yellow while the top stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmei tso ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ shishigbɛ baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ be mli ni ŋwɛi baai lɛ kã he amɛfee ŋmɔŋ lɛ?

english: Yellowing lower leaves mean the soil is running out of nitrogen. The plant naturally shifts its remaining food from the older bottom leaves up to feed the young, growing top leaves.
ga: Baai ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tsei jieɔ niyenii ni eshwɛ kɛjɛɔ baai ni egbɔ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa ŋwɛi koni amɛkɛye baai bibii ni miida yɛ ŋwɛi lɛ.

english: Why are my tomato plants producing plenty of flowers but dropping them before any tomatoes grow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tso lɛ miiwo fɔfɔi babaoo shi efoɔ dani tomato lɛ daa lɛ?

english: Tomato plants shed their flowers when they experience stress from extreme heat or lack of water. Without enough moisture, the plant saves energy by dropping flowers instead of trying to make fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ hulutsoo loo nu ni bɛ lɛ kpe. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ faaa lɛ Tsei buɔ hewalɛ he kɛtsɔ fɔfɔi ni amɛjieɔ lɛ nɔ moŋ fe ni amɛaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do we need to make high soil mounds when we are planting yam tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni wɔma gɔji ni kwɔlɔ koni wɔkɛdu ŋmeii lɛ?

english: High soil mounds create soft, loose earth so yam tubers can expand easily underground without hitting hard soil that distorts their shape and slows down growth.
ga: Gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ lɛ feɔ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni etse ehe. No hewɔ lɛ, sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã shikpɔŋ shishi oya ni enaaa shikpɔŋ ni wa lɛ nɔ hewalɛ. Enɛ fiteɔ bɔ ni eyɔɔ lɛ ni ehaa edalɛ baa shi.

english: Why do weeds grow faster and choke my cassava crop if I delay weeding in the first month?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni efiteɔ mi-cassava tsei lɛ? Ni kɛji akɛ mikɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ lɛ shwieɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nyɔŋ lɛ nɔ hu?

english: Weeds are aggressive wild plants that absorb water, fertilizer, and sunlight much faster than cultivated crops. Clearing them early prevents them from stealing vital nutrients away from young cassava roots.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni yɔɔ gbeyei ni amɛheɔ nu, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la oya fe tsei ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ. Ehe saamɔ mra Enɛ baatsi enaa koni ekaju niyenii ni he hiaa ni yɔɔ ŋmei bibii lɛ ashishifãi lɛ amli lɛ.

english: What is a soil bund, and how does building one help my crops?
ga: Mɛni ji sũ ni abua naa? Ni te gɔŋ ni mitswaa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ehaa tɛŋŋ?

english: A bund is a low wall or ridge made of soil built around or across your field. It acts as a barrier that slows down rainwater so it doesn't rush off your land, giving the water time to sink into the soil where your crop roots can drink it.
ga: Bund ji gbogbo loo ŋshɔ ni yɔɔ shishi. Akɛ shikpɔŋ ni ama kɛbɔle ehe lɛ fee. loo kɛtsɔ ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ anɔ Etsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni haa nugbɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, ehooo kɛjɛɛɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ haa nu lɛ naa be ni ekɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli he ni otso lɛ shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu lɛ yɛ lɛ.

english: Why does rainwater wash away from my farm so quickly after a downpour?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli oya nɛkɛ beni nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Rainwater washes away fast when land is sloped or bare, because there is no obstacle to block its path. Creating small ridges across the slope and keeping cover crops stops the water from rushing off, keeping moisture right where your crops grow.
ga: Nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ loo ejie ehe kpo. Ejaakɛ gbɛtsii nii ko bɛ ni tsiɔ gbɛ lɛ naa. ŋshɔkei bibii ni afeɔ Ofo ŋshɔkei lɛ amli ni okwɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nɔ koni nu akajo foi kɛya. ni okwɛ koni hulutsoo be ahi he ni otsei lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ lɛ.

english: How can I stop heavy rains from breaking the soil walls I built around my field?
ga: Mahã nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ akafite sũ gbogbo ni mitswa kɛbɔle lɛ lɛ. Te aaafee tɛŋŋ ni ŋmãa ŋmɔji lɛ

english: Soil walls break when they are made of loose earth or are not high enough. Compact the soil tightly when building them, plant grass along the tops so roots hold the earth together, and leave a small controlled channel for excess water to spill out safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ gbogboi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ sũ ni mli ejɔ fee loo amɛhe ejɔɔɔ bɔ ni sa. Kpɛtɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ he jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ooma tsu. Dumɔ jwɛi yɛ ŋwɛitsu lɛ nɔ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ amɔmɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ. ni oshi he ko bibioo Ha ehi shi jogbaŋŋ bɔni afee ni nu ni fa fe nine lɛ ajɛ mli shweshweeshwe.

english: How do I make my sandy soil hold onto water longer so my crops don't dry out?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ maha shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ ahiɛ nu mli be kakadaŋŋ koni miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akagbi?

english: Sandy soil has large spaces that let water slip right through. Mixing compost, animal manure, or decomposed plant waste into the soil acts like a sponge, helping the earth hold onto moisture much longer after it rains.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni ŋã yɔɔ nɔ lɛ yɛ he ko ni da ni nu baanyɛ atsɔ mli. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii, kooloi ashishifãi, loo tsei ni egboi ni efite lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ, etsuɔ ​​nii tamɔ sponji. Eyeɔ ebuaa shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ehiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nugbɔ sɛɛ.

english: What happens to my crops if rainwater stays trapped around their roots for too many days?
ga: Mɛni baa miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛji nugbɔ nu hi shishifãi lɛ ahe be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Plant roots need oxygen from the air just like humans do. When water sits on a field for too long, it starves roots of air, causing them to rot and turning the leaves yellow unless the crop is specially adapted to wet conditions, like swamp rice.
ga: Taakɛ adesai ji lɛ, tsei shishifãi hu hia kɔɔyɔŋ kpakpa ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli. Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ Ebaaha shishifãi lɛ aná kɔɔyɔɔ. Enɛ haa egboɔ ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Ja tso lɛ etsɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ waa, tamɔ ŋmãa ni yɔɔ ŋshɔ mli lɛ mli jogbaŋŋ.

english: Which food crops in Ghana actually enjoy standing water on the farm?
ga: Mɛɛ niyenii ni aduɔ yɛ Ghana lɛ sumɔɔ waa ni amɛnu ŋmɔ mli nu ni yɔɔ shiŋŋ?

english: Paddy rice is the main crop that thrives in standing water because its roots can breathe even in flooded soil. Crops like maize, cassava, and vegetables prefer moist soil but will rot if left submerged in standing water.
ga: Paddy ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli ejaakɛ eshishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi nɔ obɔ lɛ po mli. Nibii ni aduɔ tamɔ ŋmãa, ŋmãa kɛ aduawai sumɔɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ. Shi ebaagbo kɛji akɛ ashi yɛ nu ni damɔ shi shishi.

english: How can I make sure rainwater spreads evenly across my whole farm instead of gathering in just one low spot?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni nugbɔ nu lɛ aja miŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oookɛ ojwɛŋmɔ ama he kome ni baa shi lɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Water gathers in low spots because the land surface is uneven. Levelling your land before planting and creating small connected channels helps water distribute smoothly across all your crop rows instead of flooding just one side.
ga: Nu buaa ehe naa yɛ hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni bɛ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ hewɔ. Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni afee lɛ pɛpɛɛpɛ dani adu nii kɛ gbɛi bibii ni kɛ amɛhe kpaa gbee lɛ afeemɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ŋmɔshi nibii amli jogbaŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni nu afua lɛ baaho yɛ fa kome pɛ nɔ lɛ

english: Why do my crop leaves wilt just a few days after a big rainstorm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ni mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ nugbɔ wulu ko sɛɛ gbii fioo komɛi pɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Strong sun quickly evaporates surface soil moisture if the land is left uncovered. Spreading dried grass or leaves around the bases of your plants—a practice called mulching—shades the soil and keeps the moisture from disappearing into the air.
ga: Hulu la ni naa wa lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ atsɔ oya kɛji akɛ ashi ni ahaaa nɔ ko nɔ. Kɛ́ okɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwie tso lɛ shishi (ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching) lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni ebaatsi ŋmɔtɔ ni hoɔ kɛyaa kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ naa.

english: How do I catch and save rainwater on sloped land so my cassava roots stay hydrated?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mamɔ nugbɔ nu ni yɔɔ ŋshɔkpɔ ko nɔ lɛ ni mikɛto? Bɔni afee ni mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ aná nu ni fa bɔ ni sa

english: Digging small trenches or mounds across the slope—following the curve of the hill—creates natural pockets that catch rain as it flows downward, forcing it deep into the soil right next to your cassava roots.
ga: Gbɛjegbɛ bibioo ko loo gɔŋ ko ni atsaa. Yɛ ŋshɔ lɛ naa—ni enyiɛɔ gɔŋ lɛ ŋshɔ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ—efeɔ adebɔɔ mli gbɛ ko ni mɔɔ nugbɔ be mli ni ehoɔ kɛyaa shi lɛ. Nyɛɛ nɔ kɛbote shikpɔŋ ni bɛŋkɛ o-cassava shishifãi lɛ amli shɔŋŋ.

english: Is standing water good or bad for my maize farm?
ga: Ani nu ni damɔ shi lɛ hi loo ehiii kɛha mi ŋmãa ŋmɔ lɛ?

english: Standing water is bad for maize because maize roots rot easily in logged soil. Maize needs well-drained soil where water soaks in and drains away quickly while leaving the ground moist.
ga: Nu ni ekã shi lɛ ehiii kɛha ŋmãa ejaakɛ ŋmãa shishifãi fiteɔ oya yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsei yɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nu hoɔ yɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ he miihia ŋmãa. he ni nu boteɔ mli oya ni ehoɔ kɛyaa, ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ.

english: Why do my maize leaves turn yellow and the stalks stay short even when I water them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni ŋmãa lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ kuku kɛji awo amɛ nu po sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing and stunted growth are usually signs of nitrogen deficiency in the soil. Plants need nitrogen to build healthy green leaves and grow tall, so adding a nitrogen-rich fertilizer can help restore their health.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ ni egbɔjɔ lɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen he miihia tsei koni amɛwo baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni amɛdara. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ lɛ fata he lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni amɛná hewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why shouldn't I apply my granular fertilizer on the farm right before a heavy rain storm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ akɛ granular fertilizer tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli dani nugbɔ ni naa wa baa lɛ?

english: Heavy rainfall washes away surface fertilizer before the roots of your crops have time to absorb it. This wastes your money and can wash the fertilizer into nearby water sources.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani tsei shishifãi lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛŋɔ. Enɛ baaha ofite shika ni ebaanyɛ ekɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ afɔ nu gbɛi ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ amli.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I plant maize on the exact same plot every single year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ woɔ yibii fioo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly exhausts specific soil nutrients and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to build up in the soil. Rotating with crops like groundnuts or beans helps restore soil fertility.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ lɛ baaha niyenii pɔtɛɛ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ afite ni ebaaha tsɛŋemɔ helai pɔtɛɛi kɛ tsei ahe helai abua amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ amli tsakemɔ, tamɔ ŋmei loo ŋmei Yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ekoŋŋ.

english: What is eating small ragged holes inside the funnels of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni ji buji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni yɔɔ mi-baby corn tsei lɛ a-cone lɛ mli lɛ yeli?

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides deep inside the growing funnel of the maize plant to feed on tender young leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei ni miida lɛ amli shɔŋŋ koni amɛye baai bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa.

english: Excess water staying in the soil starves root tubers of air and encourages fungal rot. Planting on raised mounds or ridges helps drain excess water away from the tubers.
ga: Nu ni fa fe nine yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ baaha shishifãi lɛ agbɔjɔ ni ewo ŋmeii ni fiteɔ lɛ hewalɛ. Kɛ́ adu yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni nu ni fa fe nine ni yɔɔ bulb lɛ mli lɛ ajie.

english: Why do my crops grow thin and produce smaller fruit when I plant seeds close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ mlɛo ni ewoɔ yibii bibii kɛ́ midu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe lɛ?

english: When plants are overcrowded, their roots and leaves fight each other for limited sunlight, soil nutrients, and water, leaving less energy for fruit production.
ga: Beni tsei lɛ ebɔle amɛhe tsɔ lɛ Shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ wuɔ koni amɛná hulu la. niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛ nu ni faaa Enɛ haa hewalɛ ni akɛwoɔ yibii lɛ faaa.

english: Why do weeds make my crops produce less yield even if I add fertilizer to the farm?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi haa miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ ŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ?

english: Weeds grow fast and steal the water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients meant for your crops. Clearing weeds early ensures your crops get all the food they need to produce a good harvest.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni haa onibii lɛ yeɔ niyenii. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Eyeɔ ebuaa ni okwɛɔ koni oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ana niyenii fɛɛ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛwo ŋmɔshi nibii kpakpai.

english: Seeds stored in warm or moist conditions can rot, get attacked by insects, or lose their vitality. Storing seeds in a cool, dry, and sealed container keeps the living embryo inside healthy until planting.
ga: Dumɔwui ni akɛto hei ni mli edɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ yɔɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbo, koolooi baanyɛ atutua amɛ, loo amɛhewalɛ baaje amɛdɛŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ wo tsɛnsi ko ni mli ejɔ, ni egbi, ni atsĩ mli lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni fɔmɔ nii ni hiɛ ka ni yɔɔ mli lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ kɛyashi be mli ni aduɔ.

english: Why do young cocoa tree leaves burn and drop off when planted in an open field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei bibii lɛ shãa ni amɛgbeeɔ shi kɛ́ adu amɛ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to intense, direct heat and dry winds. They require partial shade from nurse crops like plantains during their first few years to protect their leaves and retain moisture.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ dɔlɛ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli egbi he waa. Amɛmiitao hulutsoo be ko kɛjɛ tsei ni kwɛɔ helatsɛmɛi anɔ tamɔ plantains lɛ adɛŋ yɛ amɛshishijee afii lɛ amli. Koni ebu baai lɛ ahe ni eha ŋmɔtɔ ahi mli.

english: Why are my tomato flowers falling off the plant without growing into any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛjɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ ni amɛdaraaa ni amɛfeɔ tomato lɛ?

english: Tomato plants drop their blossoms under high heat or water stress as a defense mechanism to conserve energy. Regular watering and shielding plants from extreme heat helps them hold flowers and set fruit.
ga: Tomato tsei fɔ̃ɔ yɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa loo nu mli haomɔ shishi akɛ gbɛ ni buɔ mɔ he koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite. Nu ni afɔɔ tsei anɔ daa ni abuɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen nutrients in the soil or the ground is too waterlogged, which stops the roots from feeding properly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-abele lɛ bɛ nitrogen yɛ sũ lɛ mli loo sũ lɛ mli eyi kɛ nu tsɔ. Enɛ haaa shishifãi lɛ ana niyenii jogbaŋŋ.

english: Tomato flowers often drop off when the weather gets too hot, when plants don't get enough water, or when there are no insects around to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ fɔɔ gbee kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ. Beni tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii bɛ amɛhe ni amɛbaawo fɔfɔi lɛ amli ŋmɔtɔ

english: Why do I need to put wooden sticks next to my growing yam plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mikɛ tso ama sweet potato tso ko ni miida lɛ masɛi lɛ?

english: Yams are climbing vines that need support to lift their leaves off the ground so they can catch direct sunlight, which helps the crop produce larger tubers.
ga: Sweet potatoes ji wain tsei ni kwɔɔ ni he hiaa yelikɛbuamɔ koni amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ koni amɛná hulu la tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ewoɔ ŋmeii wuji.

english: When is the right time to apply fertilizer to my crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: Apply fertilizer when the soil is damp and your plants are growing quickly, but avoid applying it right before heavy rain so it doesn't wash away.
ga: Okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ ni tso lɛ miida oya. Shi kaawo dani nugbɔ nɛ waa koni ekafo.

english: What causes my cocoa pods to turn black and dry up on the tree branch?
ga: Mɛni miiha mi-kookoo ŋmɔji lɛ miifee ediŋŋ ni amɛmiigbi yɛ tsei lɛ aniji lɛ anɔ?

english: Black pod is a fungal disease that spreads rapidly in dark, overly shaded, and humid farms during rainy seasons when air cannot circulate well.
ga: Black pod ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ ŋmɔji ni mli ewo duŋ lɛ amli. Shade babaoo yɛ jɛmɛ tsɔ. kɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli beni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ eyaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why are tiny worms eating the inner leaves of my young maize crop?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii bibii Koni amɛye mibi lɛ ŋmãa lɛ mli baai lɛ?

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest that burrows into the growing central leaf tube of young maize plants to feed.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ ni shwieɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni eye niyenii.

english: Cassava roots rot when the soil stays soaked with too much water for long periods or when soil fungal diseases attack the tubers in poorly drained land.
ga: Kasava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji akɛ akɛ nu babaoo wo shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ. aloo kɛ́ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni jɛɔ shikpɔŋ mli baa lɛ tutua ŋmeii yɛ hei ni nu hoɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ lɛ.

english: Planting maize in the same spot continuously drains the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and allows maize pests and diseases to build up in the ground.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ŋmãa yɛ he kome lɛ, ebaaha niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ajɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa be fɛɛ be. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmãa mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I plant my crops too close together in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ miduɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil food, and tight leaves trap moisture that causes fungal diseases to spread.
ga: Beni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe lɛ Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Ni baai ni mli wa lɛ mɔ̃ɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni haa tsɛŋemɔ helai ni haa mɔ he jɔ̃ɔ ehe lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa.

english: Why do wild weeds always seem to grow faster than the crops I planted?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ etamɔ nɔ ni koo mli jwɛi lɛ daa oya fe tsei ni miduɔ lɛ be fɛɛ be lɛ?

english: Weeds are native wild plants that adapt quickly to the soil and weather, allowing them to steal soil nutrients and water faster than your cultivated crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni tsakeɔ amɛhe oya kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa amɛjuɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ nu lɛ mli oya fe tsei ni oduɔ lɛ.

english: Why are my crops getting sick with leaves turning yellow more often now that the weather patterns have changed?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yeɔ hela ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ shii abɔ be mli ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsakeɔ lɛ?

english: Unpredictable weather and sudden temperature shifts stress plants, making them weaker and more vulnerable to viral infections that spread quickly in changing climates.
ga: Kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni anyɛɛɛ akɛɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni baa trukaa lɛ tsakeɔ tsei ni haoɔ mɔ lɛ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni amɛhe waaa kɛha helai ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ mli lɛ.

english: How can I tell if my maize crop has a virus disease instead of just needing more water?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mi-abele lɛ yɛ hela ko ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ehe baahia nu babaoo?

english: A thirsty crop usually wilts uniformly and recovers when it rains, while a plant virus causes strange leaf colors, twisted growth, or spots that do not go away even after watering.
ga: Tsei ni kumai yeɔ amɛ lɛ sumɔɔ ni amɛgboi daa ni amɛhe baajɔ amɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni yɔɔ tsei amli lɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ sui ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ. distorted growth Loo ŋmeii ni sɛɛ efooo kɛji awo nu po sɛɛ.

english: Why do new diseases attack my farm even though I am planting the same traditional seeds my father used?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ helai heei Amɛtutua miŋmɔ lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ midu dumɔwui ni mitsɛ kɛtsu nii lɛ nɔŋŋ moŋ.

english: As weather patterns shift, new pests and viruses move into areas where they were not found before, and older seed varieties often lack natural protection against these new threats.
ga: Kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi tsake lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai heei baafã kɛya hei ni anako amɛ dã. Ni bei pii lɛ, dumɔwui ni egbɔ lɛ bɛ adebɔɔ mli nibii ni buɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ nɛkɛ gbeyeishemɔi heei nɛɛ ahe.

english: Can small insects like whiteflies carry diseases into my crop fields, or do they only bite the leaves?
ga: Ani kooloi bibii tamɔ whiteflies baanyɛ amɛkɛ hela aba miŋmɔji amli? Aloo amɛyeɔ baai pɛ?

english: Tiny insects act like dirty needles; when they feed on an infected plant, they pick up viruses and inject them into healthy crops on your farm.
ga: Kplukai bibii feɔ amɛnii tamɔ ŋmeii ni he tseee. kɛ amɛye tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ Amɛheɔ hela lɛ ni amɛkɛwoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ amli yɛ oŋmɔ lɛ mli.

english: Why do agricultural officers tell us to clear bush and weeds around our farm borders to prevent diseases?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔjie jwɛi kɛ jwɛi ni bɛŋkɛ ŋmɔji husui lɛ koni helai akashɛ wɔhe lɛ?

english: Weeds and tall bushes act as living hiding spots for rodents and insects that carry crop diseases, allowing them to easily jump onto your main crops.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ tsei bibii ni kwɔlɔ lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ he ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii ni kɛ tsei ahelai baa lɛ teeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ amɛhe. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa amɛ akɛ amɛbaatu kɛya onibii titrii lɛ anɔ.

english: How do researchers and extension officers find ways to protect our farms from insect-spread diseases?
ga: Te niiamlitaolɔi kɛ mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ baafee tɛŋŋ ana gbɛi ni amɛaatsɔ nɔ amɛbu wɔŋmɔji lɛ ahe kɛjɛ helai ni kooloi kɛbaa lɛ ahe?

english: Scientists study the behavior of pests in laboratories to see which insects carry specific plant viruses, helping them develop disease-resistant seeds and safe control methods for farmers.
ga: Jeŋ nilelɔi kaseɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ asubaŋ yɛ laboratori lɛ mli koni amɛna kooloi ni hiɛ tsei amli helai pɔtɛɛ komɛi. Ye obua amɛ ni amɛfee dumɔwui ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ kɛ gbɛi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni atsɔɔ nɔ akudɔɔ okwaafoi.

english: Why do grasscutters and field mice attack my cassava tubers more during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi ŋmɔji kɛ ŋmɔ mli ŋmeii tutuaa mi-cassava ŋmɔji lɛ babaoo yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: During dry spells, small wild animals run low on food and water in the bush, so they invade farms to feed on juicy tubers to survive.
ga: yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ, koo mli kooloi bibii lɛ aniyenii kɛ nu baaho yɛ koo lɛ mli. No hewɔ lɛ amɛtutuaa ŋmɔji koni amɛyatao ŋmeii ni mli ewo muji koni amɛhi shi.

english: What simple things can I do to stop rats from destroying my harvested crops inside my storage barn?
ga: Mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo. Mibaanyɛ mafee ekomɛi koni ŋmeii akafite ŋmɔshi nibii ni akpa yɛ mi shĩa lɛ mli lɛ.

english: Raising your storage structures off the ground, keeping the surrounding area clean, and sealing entry holes prevents rats from reaching and ruining your harvested food.
ga: Onibii ni okɛtoɔ lɛ ni ooowo nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ Oha he ni ebɔle ohe lɛ he atse Ni oootsi bu ni akɛboteɔ mli lɛ naa lɛ baatsi ŋmeii anaa koni amɛkabote niyenii ni akpa lɛ mli ni amɛfite.

english: How should I handle and store my freshly harvested produce so it stays safe and clean for my family to eat?
ga: Te esa akɛ mafee tɛŋŋ matsu aduawai kɛ aduawai ni akpa ehee lɛ ahe nii ni mikɛto koni miweku lɛ aye amɛ shweshweeshwe ni amɛhe tse?

english: Harvested food should be dried properly, stored in cool, well-ventilated spaces, and kept separate from damaged crops to prevent mold and germs from spreading.
ga: Esa akɛ agbi niyenii ni akpa lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Okɛto he ko ni mli ejɔ ni kɔɔyɔɔ kpakpa yɔɔ. ni oha amɛtsi amɛhe kɛjɛ tsei ni efite lɛ ahe koni ŋmeii kɛ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ akagbɛ ashwã.

english: Is it safe for my family to cook and eat crops that have been partially nibbled by rodents or insects?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ miweku lɛ baahoo nibii ni ŋmeii loo kooloi bibii eye fã ko lɛ ni amɛye?

english: It is risky because small animals carry dangerous bacteria and viruses in their saliva and droppings that can contaminate the rest of the crop and cause illness.
ga: Oshara ko yɛ ejaakɛ kooloi bibii hiɛɔ helai kɛ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui yɛ amɛmli kɛ amɛmli ŋmeii ni baanyɛ afite ŋmɔshi nibii ni eshwɛ lɛ amli ni ekɛ hela aba.

english: Why do my crops grow smaller and produce less every year when I plant on the exact same piece of land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ feɔ bibii ni amɛwoɔ yibii fioo daa afi beni miduɔ amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ lɛ?

english: Farming the same plot every year continually drains all the essential nutrients from the soil without giving nature time to rebuild them, leading to weaker crops over time.
ga: Shikpɔŋ kome nɔ okwaayeli afi fɛɛ afi lɛ haa niyenii mli nibii fɛɛ ni he hiaa lɛ hoɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ be fɛɛ be. ni ehaaa adebɔɔ be ni ekɛtswa ehe ekoŋŋ Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ baagbɔjɔ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do some farmers leave their land untouched for a year or two before planting on it again?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi komɛi shiɔ amɛshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afi loo afii enyɔ dani amɛduɔ nii ekoŋŋ lɛ?

english: Leaving land to rest allows the soil to naturally regain missing nutrients, restore organic matter, and recover its strength so future crops grow much better.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ niyenii ni efite lɛ baa ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. Kɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli lɛ aku sɛɛ aba ni okɛ hewalɛ aba ekoŋŋ koni wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ kwraa.

english: How does moving my farm to a new spot help my crops grow better than staying on my old field?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ miŋmɔ lɛ ni mikɛyaa he kroko lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe kɛji amɛyɛ miŋmɔ momo lɛ mli?

english: Moving to a new plot gives your crops access to fresh, nutrient-rich soil while breaking the cycle of pests and soil diseases that build up in continuously farmed soil.
ga: Shikpɔŋ hee nɔ ni oooya lɛ haa onibii lɛ naa shikpɔŋ hee ni niyenii mli hewalɛ yɔɔ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, efoɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni buaa amɛhe naa be fɛɛ be yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akwɛɔ nɔ lɛ mli lɛ mli.

english: How can I tell if my resting land has recovered enough strength for me to plant on it again?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji he ni mijɔɔ mihe yɛ lɛ yɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ madu nii ekoŋŋ?

english: Land has usually recovered when natural vegetation grows back thick and green, and the soil underneath turns darker, holds moisture better, and feels crumbly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ baa shi kɛji akɛ adebɔɔ mli tsei lɛ ku amɛsɛɛ amɛfee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfee eŋɔli. ni shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ yɛ su ni tsuɔ waa Ehaa ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ ni enuɔ he akɛ egbɔjɔ

english: Is it bad if I just scatter my fertilizer everywhere across the field instead of placing it near each plant?
ga: Ani ehiii kɛji mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ shwie he fɛɛ he yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni mikɛaawo tso fɛɛ tso he?

english: Scattering fertilizer randomly wastes expensive nutrients on weeds and empty ground, whereas targeted application near crop roots ensures the plants get maximum feeding.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ fiteɔ niyenii ni jara wa yɛ jwɛi kɛ shikpɔŋ ni efite lɛ nɔ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ tsu nii jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ aná niyenii babaoo.

english: What is the proper systematic way to apply fertilizer so my crops benefit the most?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni maná sɛɛnamɔ babaoo kɛjɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli?

english: A systematic method involves measuring precise amounts of fertilizer and placing them in small holes or rings near the root zone of each plant so roots absorb it quickly.
ga: Gbɛ ni ato he gbɛjianɔ lɛ biɔ ni asusu ŋmɔshi nibii ayibɔ pɔtɛɛ ni akɛwoɔ bu bibii loo ŋmeii amli. ni bɛŋkɛ tso fɛɛ tso shishifã he lɛ bɔni afee ni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ lɛ oya.

english: Will applying fertilizer fix my land if the soil is tired from farming it every single year?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baatsake mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛji akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ etɔ kɛjɛ daa afi dumɔwui amli?

english: Fertilizer provides a quick food boost for crops, but it cannot fully repair the long-term loss of soil health and structure caused by continuous farming without rest.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ kɛ niyenii fataa ŋmɔshi nibii ahe oya. Shi enyɛŋ esaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hewalɛnamɔ kɛ egbɛjianɔtoo ni fiteɔ be kakadaŋŋ ni okwaayeli ni yaa nɔ ni hejɔɔmɔ bɛ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ kwraa.

english: Why would a farmer choose to harvest all their crops at once instead of picking them gradually?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okwaafoi halaa akɛ amɛbaakpa amɛnibii lɛ fɛɛ shikome moŋ fe ni amɛbaakpa fiofio lɛ?

english: Harvesting all at once clears the entire field together, making it easier to prepare the land for the next planting cycle or to give the soil a complete break to rest.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa fɛɛ shikome lɛ, ebaaha jɛmɛ fɛɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ abaasaa shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛha dumɔwui ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ loo aŋmɛ gbɛ ni shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe kwraa.

english: Does clearing and harvesting my entire crop at the same time harm or help my soil?
ga: Ani miŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ ni mikpaa shikome lɛ yeɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ awui loo eyeɔ ebuaa mi?

english: Harvesting all at once helps clear pest habitats and allows you to properly manage leftover plant matter, allowing the land to start its recovery process undisturbed.
ga: Kɛ́ okpa lɛ fɛɛ shikome lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ejieɔ ŋmeii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ashihilɛhei, ni ehaa onyɛɔ okwɛɔ tsei ni eshwɛ lɛ anɔ jogbaŋŋ. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ jeɔ sɛɛkuu nitsumɔ lɛ shishi ni mɔ ko mɔ ko gbaaa enaa.

english: How does giving my land a break after a full harvest help my crop yields in future years?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɛ́ mishikpɔŋ lɛ ha hejɔɔmɔ yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eye emuu sɛɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ yɛ wɔsɛɛ afii amli?

english: Giving the soil a break after a full harvest allows beneficial soil microorganisms to rebuild natural soil fertility, leading to stronger plants and bigger yields in coming years.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aŋmɛɔ gbɛ ni ejɔɔ ehe yɛ ŋmaakpamɔ ni eye emuu sɛɛ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ saa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe ekoŋŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni he wa ni woɔ yibii babaoo baa yɛ afii ni baa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my crops dry up so fast even when it rains a little bit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya nɛkɛ kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ fioo po lɛ?

english: When the soil is bare, the sun evaporates moisture very quickly. Covering the soil around your crops with dried grass or leaves keeps the soil cool and holds water in the ground longer for the roots to drink.
ga: Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Hulu la lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ oya. Mulching around Nibii ni akɛ jwɛi loo baai ni egbi shwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha shikpɔŋ lɛ mli afee fɛ̃i ni ebaaha nu ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ koni shishifãi lɛ anu nu.

english: Fertilizer needs water to dissolve so the plant roots can swallow it. Applying fertilizer to dry soil can burn the roots and waste your money because the crop cannot use it.
ga: Nu he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anyɛ ami amɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii wo shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha shishifãi lɛ ashã ni efite shika ejaakɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ nyɛŋ amɛkɛtsu nii.

english: Why is it bad if I plant my maize seeds too close together?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehiii kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ?

english: When seeds are planted too close, the crops fight each other for sunlight, water, and food in the soil. This leads to weak stalks and small or empty cob heads.
ga: Kɛ dumɔwui lɛ bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Tsei lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ashishifãi lɛ bɛ hewalɛ kɛ tsei lɛ ayitsei bibii loo nɔ ko bɛ mli.

english: Yam leaves need direct sunlight to produce food for the plant. Lifting the vines off the ground with stakes allows the leaves to catch full sunshine, which makes the yam tubers grow much larger under the ground.
ga: Sweet potato baai lɛ biɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha tso lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsei wo wain tso lɛ nɔ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsei lɛ ahe tsei lɛ náa hulu la ni fa babaoo. Enɛ haa sweet potato ŋmeii lɛ daraa babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ shishi.

english: Young cocoa seedlings are fragile and burn easily under the strong sun. Plantains grow quickly and have large leaves that act like natural umbrellas, giving the young cocoa the shade it needs to survive its first few years.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ waaa ni amɛshãa oya yɛ hulu la ni naa wa shishi. Plantains lɛ daa oya ni eyɛ baai wuji ni tsuɔ nii tamɔ adebɔɔ mli ŋmeii. Enɛ haa kookoo bibioo lɛ naa hulutsoo ni he hiaa lɛ koni enyɛ ehi shi yɛ eshishijee afii lɛ amli.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning yellow down the center?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing down the middle of a maize leaf usually means the crop is hungry for nitrogen, which is a key plant food needed to keep leaves green and healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa baai lɛ ateŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia tso lɛ. Eji tso niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni baai lɛ ahi shi eŋɔli ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Pepper flowers drop off when the plant is stressed by severe heat, lack of water, or a lack of specific soil food like phosphorus needed to convert flowers into fruits.
ga: Pepper fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo niyenii pɔtɛɛ ko ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, tamɔ fɔsfɔs, ni he hiaa koni fɔfɔi lɛ atsɔ aduawai lɛ ha tsei lɛ miihao.

english: This damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which hides inside the center of young maize plants, chewing the leaves and leaving sawdust-like waste behind.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ ŋmãa tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ lɛ ji mɛi ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Ekɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni eshiɔ jwɛi ni tamɔ ŋmei.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects and stays around the roots for too long without draining away, which drowns the tubers and causes soil fungi to attack them.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua amɛhe naa ni ebɔle amɛhe. shishifãi lɛ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ ni nu bɛ mli Enɛ haa ŋmeii lɛ shwieɔ nu mli ni ehaa ŋmeii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ tutuaa amɛ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly steals the same nutrients from the soil every season and allows crop-specific pests and diseases to live and multiply in that soil permanently.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ Ejuɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa be ni ehaa tso pɔtɛɛ ko mli tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai hiɔ nakai shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa ni amɛfɔɔ bii.

english: Yellow leaves on young maize usually mean the crop is lacking nitrogen, an essential plant food, or the roots are suffocating in waterlogged soil. Applying nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or improving soil drainage helps the leaves turn deep green again.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmãa bibii anɔ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. tso niyenii ni he hiaa Aloo shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofa ni nitrogen eyi mli obɔ tamɔ urea tsu nii loo shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni baai lɛ atsɔ ŋmɔŋ ekoŋŋ.

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with legumes like groundnuts or cowpeas puts nitrogen back into the soil naturally and breaks insect pest cycles.
ga: Tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni akwɛɔ shii abɔ Ejieɔ niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ bua amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmãa ni akɛ ŋmãa tamɔ ŋmãa loo tsina ŋmãa tsake lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ekoŋŋ yɛ adebɔɔ naa. ni efoɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ amli

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle harsh, direct sunlight and high heat. Fast-growing shade crops like plantains act as living umbrellas, protecting young cocoa from sun damage and keeping the soil moist while the cocoa roots grow strong.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni naa wa kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Shade tsei ni daa oya tamɔ plantains tsuɔ nii akɛ ŋwɛi ŋta ni hiɛ ka. Buu kookoo bibii ahe kɛjɛ hulu la he. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo shishifãi lɛ daraa waa lɛ.

english: How does spreading dry grass around the base of my crop plants help them survive the heat?
ga: Jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛwoɔ he lɛ Te mi tsei lɛ ashishitoo yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli amɛhaa tɛŋŋ?

english: Spreading dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a protective blanket over the soil. It prevents sunlight from evaporating soil moisture quickly, keeps the roots cool, and stops weeds from taking over.
ga: Hay ni agbɛɔ ashwãa, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ mulching lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ nɔ ni buɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ he. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa hulu la lɛ shwieɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ oya. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i ni ehaaa jwɛi akaye nɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets extremely hot, when the soil dries out completely, or when there are no beneficial insects around to pollinate them. Watering regularly at the root level helps the flowers stay attached and form fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ waa. Beni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa loo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni baaha fɔfɔi lɛ afee ŋmɔtɔ lɛ bɛ Nu ni afɔɔ nɔ daa yɛ shishifã lɛ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛwoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my pepper leaves droop in the afternoon heat even when the soil is wet?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli eyɛ mli akɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ moŋ?

english: In intense sunlight, pepper plants lose water through their leaves faster than their roots can drink it from the ground. The leaves wilt temporarily to protect themselves from heat, but they usually perk back up once the sun cools down in the evening.
ga: Yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ, ŋmɔtɔ tsei lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Baai lɛ shwieɔ shi be kukuoo ko koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Shi bei pii lɛ, ekɛ ehe woɔ mli ekoŋŋ kɛ́ hulu lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ.

english: Why does my cassava produce huge green leaves above ground but very small tubers underground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca lɛ hiɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ? Shi ani yitso bibioo ko yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi?

english: When soil has too much nitrogen or water, the cassava plant puts all its energy into growing tall stems and lush leaves instead of storing energy in the roots. Balanced soil allows the energy to go down into swelling the tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ yɛ nitrogen loo nu babaoo Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ŋmei tso lɛ kɛ hewalɛ baato shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ kɛ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni ja lɛ haa hewalɛ baa shi kɛyashiɔ be mli ni bulb lɛ shwieɔ shi.

english: Why do the leaves of my corn plants look like holes have been eaten through them with small dirt inside the funnel?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-corn tso lɛ baai lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛyɛ bu ni aye kɛ muji bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmeii lɛ amli lɛ?

english: This leaf damage is usually caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar. The caterpillar hides inside the central growing leaves during the heat of the day and feeds on the soft leaf tissues before they unfurl.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii lɛ kɛ baa lɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kplukai lɛ kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli yɛ gbi lɛ mli be ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ mli. ni amɛyeɔ baai lɛ amli fãji ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ dani amɛjieɔ amɛhe kpo.

english: Why do tiny insects destroy my harvested corn even after I tie the grains tightly in bags?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii miifite mi ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ eyɛ mli akɛ mikɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo kotokui amli shiŋŋ moŋ?

english: Insects like grain weevils hatch from invisible eggs laid inside the grain while it was still in the field or if the grain was stored wet. Thoroughly drying the corn until hard and using airtight storage bags suffocates these insects.
ga: Kplukai tamɔ dumɔwui amli ŋmeii lɛ fɔɔ kɛjɛɔ ŋmeii ni anaaa ni akɛwoɔ dumɔwui amli be mli ni amɛyɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lolo lɛ amli. aloo kɛji akɛ akɛ dumɔwui lɛ ewo nu mli Gbimɔ ŋmãa lɛ kɛyashi ebaawa ni okɛ vacuum storage bags atsu nii ni okɛshwie nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ.

english: Why do my freshly harvested leafy vegetables rot so quickly before I can sell them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-aduawai ni yɔɔ baai ni akpa ehee lɛ fiteɔ oya dani abaanyɛ ahɔ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Harvested vegetables continue to breathe and generate heat, which causes them to spoil fast if trapped in tight plastic bags or left under direct heat. Harvesting early in the cool morning and storing produce in shaded, ventilated crates keeps them fresh longer.
ga: Aduawai ni akpa lɛ yaa nɔ amɛmuɔ ni amɛfeɔ dɔlɛ. Enɛ haa aduawai lɛ fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akɛwo plastic kotokui ni mli wa mli loo ashi yɛ la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ shishi. Nikpamɔ yɛ leebi ni hulutsoo be mli kɛ nibii ni adu lɛ ni akɛtoɔ adekai ni yɔɔ hulutsoo ni kɔɔyɔɔ yɔɔ mli lɛ amli lɛ baaye abua ni aduawai lɛ ahi shi ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my young cocoa trees turning yellow and burning up during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshãa yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees cannot handle direct sunlight and high heat. Without shade trees or nurse crops like plantains to shelter them, the harsh sun burns the tender leaves and dries out the moisture in the soil, causing the leaves to yellow and drop.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ nyɛŋ aŋmɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa lɛ gbɛ. Kɛji tsei ni haa hulutsoo loo tsei ni aduɔ tamɔ dumɔwui kɛha wɔɔhe bɛ lɛ, Hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shãa baai bibii ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ gĩɔ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛshwieɔ shi.

english: Why are my maize leaves turning pale yellow starting from the tips during early growth?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ kɛjɛɔ amɛyitseiaŋ yɛ be mli ni amɛdaraa mra lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves starting from the tip in a V-shape indicate that your maize lacks nitrogen in the soil. Nitrogen gives maize its rich green color and strength, so applying a nitrogen-rich fertilizer like NPK or urea early will fix this issue.
ga: Baai ni ji ŋmɔŋ ni jeɔ shishi kɛjɛɔ naagbee ni feɔ V lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nitrogen haa ŋmãa feɔ eŋɔli ni ewaa. No hewɔ lɛ, okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ NPK loo urea atsu nii mra. lɛ baaye abua ni asaa naagba nɛɛ.

english: This damage is typically caused by the Fall Armyworm caterpillar, which burrows into the center of young maize plants during the day to feed on soft leaves. Applying recommended bio-pesticides or neem extract into the leaf center early in the morning can stop them.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, Fall Armyworm ŋmeii ni shwieɔ ŋmeii bibii lɛ ateŋ yɛ gbi lɛ mli koni amɛye ŋmeii bibii lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa. Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli lɛ loo neem mli nu ni ajieɔ yi lɛ wo tsei lɛ ateŋ leebi lɛ, ebaanyɛ ekpa amɛ.

english: Cassava roots rot underground when water collects and stays stagnant in the soil, suffocating the roots. Planting cassava on high mounds or ridges helps rainwater drain away quickly and prevents root rot.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi be mli ni nu lɛ buaa ehe naa ni ehiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu. Kɛ́ adu ŋmei yɛ gɔji ni nɔ kwɔlɔ loo ŋshɔkei lɛ anɔ lɛ, nugbɔ nu lɛ hoɔ oya, ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ.

english: Is it necessary to put wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb?
ga: Mi sweet potato wain tso lɛ miikwɔ. Ani ehe miihia ni mikɛ tso ama shi?

english: Yes, staking yam vines lifts the leaves off the ground so they can capture maximum sunlight to feed the growing tuber underneath. Unstaked vines stay on the ground, catch fungal diseases easily, and yield much smaller tubers.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, staking sweet potato wain tsei lɛ woɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni amɛnyɛ amɛmɔmɔ hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛkɛha bulbs ni kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ amɛshishi lɛ niyenii. Wein tsei ni atswako amɛhe shi lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eyɛ mlɛo akɛ ooona tsɛŋemɔ hela. ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, caused by a lack of calcium in the plant or irregular watering. Keeping the soil consistently moist and adding agricultural lime or organic compost improves calcium uptake and prevents fruit damage.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa ji calcium ni bɛ tsei amli loo nu ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli be fɛɛ be. Kɛ́ oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa ni okɛ lime loo organic compost fata he lɛ, ebaaha calcium lɛ aná mli jogbaŋŋ ni ebaatsi aduawai lɛ afitemɔ naa.

english: Why are my pepper plants dropping their flowers instead of producing pepper fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni eeewo pepper yibii lɛ?

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they experience extreme heat, dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer. Regular watering during hot periods and balancing fertilizer helps the plant hold onto flowers until they set fruit.
ga: Pepper tsei fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛji akɛ amɛyashɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa, shikpɔŋ ni egbi, loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo nɔ. Nu ni akɛhaa tso lɛ daa yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ, kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ mli yɛ gbɛ ni ja nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tso lɛ ni ehiɛɔ fɔfɔi lɛ amli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni ewoɔ yibii.

english: Why do my mature plantain trees easily fall over when strong winds blow?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain ni eda lɛ gbeeɔ shi oya kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa tswa lɛ?

english: Plantain plants have shallow roots and can become top-heavy, especially when growing too many side shoots (suckers) or when root pests attack. Pruning excess suckers and supporting heavy bunches with strong wooden props prevents trees from falling.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛfee tsiimɔ. Enɛ ji anɔkwale titri lɛ kɛ́ akwɛ̃ sɛɛ ŋmeii (ŋmeii) babaoo tsɔ loo kɛ́ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ tutua shishifãi lɛ. Kɛ́ afo tsei ni fa fe nine lɛ amli ni akɛ tsei ni wa fiɔ tsei ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ lɛ, ebaatsi tso lɛ naa koni ekagbee shi.

english: Why do weeds make my crops grow weak and yield very little harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi lɛ miiha miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miigbɔjɔ ni amɛmiiwo ŋmɔshi nibii fioo ko pɛ lɛ?

english: Weeds grow fast and aggressively steal water, sunlight, and fertilizer nutrients from your crops. Clearing weeds early gives your crops full access to the nutrients they need to grow strong and yield well.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛkɛ yiwalɛ juɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ niyenii ni haa mɔ he waa kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli. Jwɛi ni ajieɔ mra Ehaa otsei lɛ naa niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ ni amɛwo yibii.

english: How does planting cowpeas or beans make my farm soil better for my next crop?
ga: Te tsina loo ŋmeii ni aduɔ lɛ baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha tɛŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Legume crops like cowpeas have tiny root nodules that capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil. When the cowpea plants die, that natural nitrogen remains in the ground to feed the next crop like maize or cassava.
ga: Legumes tamɔ cowpeas yɛ shishifãi bibii. ni mɔɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Kɛ́ tsina tso lɛ gbo Nakai adebɔɔ mli nitrogen lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni ekɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli ŋmɔshi nibii, tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa.

english: Why should I leave some big trees standing on my farm instead of cutting them all down?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ mashi tsei wuji yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli moŋ fe ni mafo amɛ fɛɛ?

english: Standing trees help pull water into the soil and keep moisture in the air, which creates a healthy environment for crops like cocoa, plantain, and cassava to thrive.
ga: Tsei ni yeɔ afii babaoo lɛ gbalaa nu kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli fɛ̃i hiɔ shi. Enɛ haa shihilɛ kpakpa baa kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ kookoo, plantain, kɛ cassava ni amɛduɔ.

english: Is it bad practice for me to clear all the trees on my farmland before the rainy season begins?
ga: Ani eji nifeemɔ gbonyo akɛ majie tsei fɛɛ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ aba?

english: Yes, clearing all trees before the rain falls strips the land of its natural protection and moisture, which causes major trouble for your crops when the weather gets hot.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ́ ajie tsei fɛɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ dani nugbɔ anɛ lɛ, ebaajie adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ kɛjɛ jɛmɛ. Enɛ kɛ naagba wulu baa oŋmɔshi nibii anɔ kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ.

english: How do shade trees help protect my crops during hot weather?
ga: Te tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ lɛ baanyɛ abu miŋmɔshi nibii ahe yɛ be mli ni hulu tsoɔ waa lɛ?

english: Trees absorb sunlight and help draw water into the soil while keeping the surrounding air moist, protecting your crops from drying out under intense heat.
ga: Tsei lɛ ŋmɛɔ hulu la ni amɛyeɔ amɛbuaa ni amɛgbalaa nu kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli, ni amɛhaa kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ hu feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ. Buu onibii ahe koni amɛkagbi yɛ la ni naa wa waa shishi.

english: Do big trees on my farm steal water from my crops or help them get more water?
ga: Ani tsei wuji ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli loo eyeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛnáa nu babaoo?

english: Big trees actually help by drawing water into the soil and holding moisture in the air, which makes more water available for your crops.
ga: Tsei wuji yeɔ amɛbuaa diɛŋtsɛ kɛtsɔ nu ni amɛgbalaa kɛyaa sũ lɛ mli ni amɛmɔɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ nɔ. Enɛ baaha nu ni fa bɔ ni sa aha onibii.

english: How does moisture in the air help my crops grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ?

english: Moist air prevents plants from losing too much water through their leaves, helping crops like cassava, cocoa, and plantain grow strong and thrive.
ga: Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ haaa tsei akaje nu babaoo kɛtsɔɔ amɛbaai lɛ anɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei, kookoo, kɛ plantains ni amɛdaraa waa ni amɛshwereɔ.

english: How can I make sure the soil on my farm retains enough water for my plants?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mana nɔmimaa akɛ shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha mitsei lɛ lolo?

english: Keeping trees on your land helps pull and store water in the ground, preventing the soil from drying out quickly.
ga: Tsei ni yɔɔ oshikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ akwɛmɔ baaye abua ni ajie nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ni akɛto. Etsiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ naa koni ekagbi oya.

english: What kind of conditions do my cocoa plants need to yield well?
ga: Mɛɛ shihilɛ esa akɛ mi-kokoo tsei lɛ ahi mli koni amɛwo yibii kpakpai?

english: Cocoa thrives best when there is plenty of moisture in both the soil and the air, which is naturally provided when trees are left to protect the farm.
ga: Cocoa daa jogbaŋŋ kɛ́ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ fɛɛ mli. Enɛ baa mli yɛ adebɔɔ naa kɛ́ ashi tsei koni amɛbu ŋmɔ lɛ he.

english: Why do my plantains and cassava grow so much better when the surrounding air is cool and moist?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantains kɛ cassava lɛ daa jogbaŋŋ waa beni kɔɔyɔɔ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ mli ejɔ ni edɔ lɛ?

english: Plantain and cassava are sensitive to dry conditions; moist air supported by nearby trees helps them absorb nutrients and grow without heat stress.
ga: Plantains kɛ cassava nuɔ shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ ahe waa. Kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛ lɛ fiɔ sɛɛ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛheɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛdaraa ni dɔlɛ he haomɔ ko bɛ amɛhe.

english: Can I grow cocoa, plantain, and cassava together on land that has tree cover?
ga: Aduɔ kookoo, plantain kɛ ŋmei. Ani wɔbaanyɛ wɔfee ekome yɛ he ko ni tsei ehà nɔ?

english: Yes, all three crops thrive together in environments where surrounding trees maintain good soil water and air moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, nɛkɛ tsei etɛ nɛɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ he ko ni tsei ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ feɔ ekome kɛkwɛ̃ɔ yɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ kɛ hulutsoo ni yɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ nubu lɛ mli lɛ hiɔ shi.

english: What will happen to my young cassava plants if I remove all the trees and exposure them to full sun before rains come?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-cassava tsei lɛ anɔ kɛji mijie tso muu lɛ fɛɛ ni mikɛwo hulutsoo be mli dani nugbɔ lɛ nɛ?

english: Without trees to hold water in the soil and air, the sudden exposure to dry heat will stress the crops and put your yield in trouble before the rains arrive.
ga: Kɛji tsei bɛ ni akɛ nu baato shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ, Dɔlɛ ni mli egbi ni baa trukaa lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii haoɔ. Ni oha onibii lɛ apiŋ dani nugbɔ lɛ aba.

english: Which type of maize can I plant if I know there will be very little rain this season?
ga: Mɛɛ ŋmãa manyɛ madu kɛji mile akɛ nugbɔ fioo pɛ baanɛ yɛ be nɛɛ mli?

english: Drought-tolerant maize varieties are specifically developed to grow and produce grains even when rainfall is low or irregular during the dry season.
ga: Afee ŋmãa henɔi ni nyɛɔ ehiɔ shi yɛ hɔmɔ mli lɛ pɔtɛɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ ni amɛwo dumɔwui kɛ́ nugbɔ enɛɛɛ fioo loo enɛɛɛ be fɛɛ be yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli po.

english: Why do some seed varieties grow better than others when the weather is extremely hot and dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ fe ekrokomɛi yɛ hei ni kɔɔyɔɔ mli edɔ waa ni jɛmɛ egbi lɛ?

english: Certain seed varieties have stronger root systems and special traits that help them hold onto moisture and withstand high temperatures without dying.
ga: Dumɔwui srɔtoi komɛi yɛ shishifãi ni mli wa kɛ sui krɛdɛɛi ni yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛhiɛɔ ŋmɔtɔ mli ni amɛdamɔɔ hulutsoo be ni mli wa naa ni amɛgbooo.

english: How do I choose between different varieties of maize seeds when buying from a vendor?
ga: Mibaahala ŋmãa dumɔwui srɔtoi. Beni oheɔ nii kɛjɛɔ nihɔɔlɔ ko dɛŋ?

english: You should select seeds based on your local weather patterns; drought-resistant seeds are best if rain is unreliable, while traditional seeds may require constant heavy rainfall.
ga: Esa akɛ ohala dumɔwui yɛ bɔ ni kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ he ni oyɔɔ lɛ yɔɔ ha lɛ naa. Dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ hi fe fɛɛ kɛji akɛ anyɛɛɛ akɛ he afɔ̃ nugbɔ nɔ. yɛ be mli ni blema ŋmaa baanyɛ abi ni nugbɔ nɛ waa be fɛɛ be.

english: Does maize need heavy rainfall every day to give me a good harvest?
ga: Ani nugbɔ ni naa wa he miihia ŋmãa daa gbi koni ená ŋmãa kpakpa?

english: Not all maize needs heavy rain; improved resilient varieties can produce a decent harvest even with small, occasional amounts of water.
ga: Abɛi henɔi komɛi biɔ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa. Henɔi ni nyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ lɛ baanyɛ awo yibii ni sa kɛji akɛ akɛ nu fioo ko po wo mli yɛ bei komɛi amli.

english: What happens if I plant my maize seeds and the rain stops shortly after?
ga: Mɛni baa kɛji midu ŋmãa dumɔwui ni nugbɔ lɛ kpa no sɛɛ etsɛɛɛ?

english: Standard seeds may dry up and fail, but improved drought-tolerant seeds can withstand short dry spells and keep growing when a little water becomes available.
ga: Dumɔwui ni afɔɔ namɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbi ni amɛfite. Shi dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa lɛ baanyɛ adamɔ hɔmɔ be kukuoo naa ni amɛya nɔ amɛkwɛ̃ kɛ nu fioo pɛ.

english: Can I still get a crop harvest if I only have a small amount of water to give my fields?
ga: Ani manyɛ makpa ŋmɔshi nibii lolo kɛji akɛ miyɛ nu fioo pɛ kɛha ŋmɔji lɛ?

english: Yes, if you plant water-efficient seed varieties, the crops can make maximum use of small amounts of moisture to mature and yield food.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛji akɛ odu dumɔwui ni kɛ nu tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ. Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɔ amɛkɛ nu fioo ni yɔɔ mli lɛ tsuɔ nii jogbaŋŋ koni amɛshwere ni amɛwo niyenii.

english: Why do my crops wither quickly during a dry spell while my neighbor's farm stays green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ gboɔ oya yɛ hɔmɔ be mli yɛ be mli ni mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli tseɔ lɛ?

english: Your neighbor may be using improved seed varieties engineered to survive dry weather conditions and conserve water better than traditional seeds.
ga: Ekolɛ okutsoŋnyo lɛ kɛ dumɔwui srɔtoi ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni afee koni ehi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni mli egbi mli ni ekwɛ nu nɔ jogbaŋŋ fe blema dumɔwui lɛ miitsu nii.

english: How can I ensure my family has food to eat even if the dry season lasts longer than expected?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makwɛ koni miweku lɛ aná niyenii ni amɛye kɛji akɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ sɛɛ tsɛɔ fe bɔ ni mikpaa gbɛ po?

english: Planting drought-tolerant and resilient crop varieties ensures you get at least a partial harvest to feed your household, even in bad weather.
ga: Tsei ni nyɛɔ amɛŋmɛɔ hɔmɔ naa ni amɛnyɛɔ amɛhiɔ shi lɛ ni oookwɛ lɛ haa kɛ hoo lɛ, onine shɛɔ onibii lɛ eko nɔ ni okɛhaa oshiabii lɛ niyenii. Yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔ ni ehiii po mli

english: Is there a way to harvest my crop faster before the severe dry season sets in?
ga: Ani gbɛ ko yɛ ni matsɔ nɔ makpa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ mra dani hɔmɔ ni naa wa lɛ aba?

english: Yes, using early-maturing seed varieties allows your crops to grow and produce food quickly before the soil completely loses its moisture.
ga: Hɛɛ, kɛ okɛ dumɔwui ni kwɛ̃ɔ mra lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ daa ni amɛwoɔ niyenii oya dani shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nu lɛ sɛɛ foɔ kwraa.

english: Will improved maize seeds still give me something to harvest if weather conditions turn bad?
ga: Ani ŋmãa hee ni afee lɛ jogbaŋŋ lɛ baaha mi nɔ ko lolo ni makpa? Kɛji kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ ehiii

english: Yes, these seeds are designed as a safeguard so that even in tough dry conditions, you still yield enough crops to take home for your family.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, afee dumɔwui nɛɛ koni amɛbu he yɛ shihilɛi ni mli ejɔ po mli. Owoɔ nibii ni fa bɔ ni sa lolo ni okɛbaa shia kɛhaa oweku lɛ.

english: Is starting a cocoa farm difficult, and how long will it take before I harvest my first pods?
ga: Ani ewa akɛ aaaje kookoo ŋmɔ shishi? Ni be enyiɛ eheɔ dani akpaa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ?

english: Cocoa farming requires consistent care, especially in the early stages. With modern hybrid varieties, your trees can start bearing fruit in about 2 to 3 years, whereas older varieties take around 4 to 5 years. The main work early on is providing shade, clearing weeds, and protecting young saplings from harsh sun and pests.
ga: Cocoa ŋmɔshi nibii biɔ ni akwɛ nɔ jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be, titri lɛ yɛ shishijee mli. kɛ ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ tsofai ni akɛfee ekome lɛ Otso lɛ baaje yibii womɔ shishi yɛ aaafee afii 2 kɛyashi 3 mli, yɛ be mli ni tsofai ni etsɛ lɛ baahe aaafee afii 4 kɛyashi 5. Nitsumɔi titrii ni atsuɔ yɛ shishijee fãi lɛ amli ji ni aha tso lɛ hulutsoo, ajie jwɛi lɛ, ni abu tso bibioo lɛ he kɛjɛ hulu kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings die if I clear away all the big trees on my land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikoo tsei bibii lɛ gboiɔ kɛji mijie tsei wuji fɛɛ ni yɔɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants are sensitive to direct sunlight and high heat. Leaving mature shade trees or planting plantains keeps the soil moist and protects tender cocoa leaves from burning until the crop matures and builds its own canopy.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ kɛ dɔlɛ ni naa wa he waa. Kɛ́ ashi tso lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli loo adu plantains lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ, ni ehaaa kookoo baai bibii lɛ ashã kɛyashi tso lɛ baakwɛ ni efee lɛ diɛŋtsɛ e-canopy.

english: Why do many flowers fall off my cocoa tree without turning into cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ anɔ ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi lɛ?

english: It is normal for cocoa trees to produce thousands of flowers but only turn a small percentage into pods. Heavy flower drop happens when the tree lacks water or nutrients, or when tiny beneficial insects fail to pollinate the flowers properly.
ga: Eji nɔ ni afɔɔ feemɔ akɛ cacao tso baawo fɔfɔi akpei abɔ. Shi ebaakwɛ̃ ni etsɔ ŋmeii fioo komɛi pɛ. Fɔfɔi ni shwieɔ shi waa lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ bɛ nu loo niyenii mli hewalɛ. Aloo be mli ni kooloi bibii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ jogbaŋŋ

english: Why do extension officers tell us to cut off extra small branches and suckers from cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ wɔ akɛ wɔfolɔ tsei aniji bibii kɛ tsei ashishifãi lɛ? Kɛjɛ kookoo tso lɛ mli?

english: Removing extra shoots (chupons) allows the tree to direct its energy, water, and food straight into developing healthy pods. It also opens up the canopy so air can flow, which reduces the dampness that causes black pod disease.
ga: Kɛ́ afo tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine (chupon) lɛ, ehaa tso lɛ nyɛɔ ekɛ hewalɛ, nu, kɛ niyenii tsuɔ nii tɛ̃ɛ ni ekɛwoɔ ŋmeii ni mli wa. Egbeleɔ ŋwɛitsu lɛ hu koni kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ atsɔ mli. Enɛ haa hulutsoo ni kɛ black pod hela baa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does planting beans or cowpeas next to my maize help the maize grow better?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduɔ ŋmei loo tsina ŋmei yɛ No hewɔ lɛ mi ŋmei lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmei lɛ ni ekwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ.

english: Legumes like beans act as natural soil builders. Their roots capture nitrogen from the air and store it in the soil, which acts as natural fertilizer for nearby crops like maize.
ga: Legumes tamɔ ŋmeii tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ tsumalɔi. Amɛ shishifãi lɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Etsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni bɛŋkɛ tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: How does tilling the soil before planting help my seed grow into a healthy crop?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitsumɔ dani adu lɛ baanyɛ aye abua midumɔwui lɛ ni amɛdara ni amɛfee ŋmɔshi nibii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Loosening the soil makes it easier for tender new roots to push deep into the ground to find water and nutrients. It also buries weeds and lets air enter the soil so seeds can breathe and germinate smoothly.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo akɛ shishifãi heei ni yɔɔ blɛoo lɛ baabote shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ koni amɛna nu kɛ niyenii. Efuɔ jwɛi hu ni ehaa kɔɔyɔɔ boteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni dumɔwui lɛ amu ni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ.

english: No, planting seeds too close together usually lowers your total yield. When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients, leading to weak plants with smaller leaves and fruits.
ga: Dabi, bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ odu dumɔwui ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ lɛ, ebaaha onibii fɛɛ ni obaawo lɛ aba shi. Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni baai kɛ aduawai bibii yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Leaf rolling is a survival trick crops use to protect themselves from heat. By curling up, the leaf exposes less surface to the hot sun and dry wind, conserving internal water until temperatures drop.
ga: Baai ni atsiɔ lɛ ji wala yiwalaheremɔ ŋaa ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, hulu ni tsoɔ waa kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa egbiɔ lɛ shɛɛɛ baai lɛ ahe tsɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni nu hiɔ mli kɛyashiɔ be mli ni hulutsoo be lɛ baa shi.

english: Yellow, twisted leaves on cassava are usually a sign of Cassava Mosaic Disease, which is spread by tiny whiteflies. You can prevent this by planting disease-free stems provided by agricultural officers.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ yucca nɔ lɛ ji yucca mosaic hela lɛ he okadi. ni ŋmeii bibii ni ji whiteflies lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa lɛ Obaanyɛ otsĩ enɛ naa kɛtsɔ tsei ni hela bɛ mli ni okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ kɛhaa lɛ ni ooodu lɛ nɔ.

english: Why shouldn't I leave yellow, ripe cocoa pods hanging on the tree for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ kookoo ŋmɔtɔ ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ shwieɔ shi lɛ? Ani ashi yɛ tso lɛ nɔ be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ?

english: Leaving ripe pods on the tree causes the beans inside to start sprouting or rotting. Overripe pods also attract animals and pests, and can spread fungal diseases to remaining green pods on the tree.
ga: Kɛ́ oshi ŋmeii ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii ni yɔɔ mli lɛ aje shishi amɛkwɛ̃ loo amɛgboi. Pods ni ekwɛ̃ lɛ hu gbalaa kooloi kɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai. ni ebaanyɛ egbɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ashwã tso lɛ nɔ ŋmɔji ni eshwɛ lɛ amli.

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because strong, direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the soil before their roots grow deep enough to reach groundwater.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni naa wa ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ agbi dani shishifãi lɛ atsɔ shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛshɛ shikpɔŋ shishi nu lɛ he.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the soil lacks nitrogen, which is an essential nutrient crops need to build strong green leaves and grow healthy cobs.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji tso mli niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa koni eha baai eŋɔli ni yɔɔ hewalɛ aba ni ekwɛ̃ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why does my land produce smaller harvests when I grow maize on the same field every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa be lɛ?

english: Growing the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests and diseases that prefer that crop to build up in the ground.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ni sumɔɔ tsei ni miida lɛ buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: When crops are planted too close together, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and plant food, which results in weak, thin plants with very small cobs.
ga: Kɛji adu tsei ni bɛŋkɛ amɛhe tsɔ Amɛyeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni jɛ tsei amli. Enɛ haa tsei ni bɛ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ mlɛo ni ŋmeii bibii waa yɔɔ mli lɛ baa.

english: Why is it bad to apply chemical fertilizer on my field when the ground is completely dry?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ woɔ miŋmɔji amli lɛ? Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ egbi kwraa, no hewɔ lɛ ehiii?

english: Fertilizer needs soil moisture to dissolve so plant roots can drink it; on dry ground, fertilizer can burn plant roots and evaporate into the air.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ he miihia ni ŋmɔtɔ ahi shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni etsɔ mli bɔni afee ni tsei shishifãi lɛ anu. Yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi nɔ lɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii baanyɛ ashã tsei shishifãi ni efo kɛya kɔɔyɔɔ mli.

english: Leaf curling in peppers is usually caused by tiny insects like aphids or thrips sucking plant sap, or by viruses spread by these insects that distort leaf growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo thrips ni nuɔ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tso lɛ mli nu lɛ baa. aloo kɛtsɔ helai ni gbeɔ mɔ ni nɛkɛ kooloi bibii nɛɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa ni fiteɔ baai lɛ adalɛ nɔ

english: Weeds steal valuable soil food, fertilizer, and sunlight from your crops, and they also hide pests that jump over to attack your plants.
ga: Jwɛi juɔ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii, ŋmɔshi nibii, kɛ hulu la ni he hiaa waa kɛjɛɔ onibii amli. Ekɛ tsɛŋemɔ helai ni shwieɔ shi ni amɛtutuaa otsei lɛ hu teeɔ.

english: Tomato flowers drop when temperatures get too high, when the soil lacks steady moisture, or when bees and insects fail to pollinate the flowers.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ. Be mli ni shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ bɛ ŋmɔtɔ be fɛɛ be Aloo be mli ni ŋmeii kɛ kooloi bibii nyɛɛɛ afee fɔfɔii amli ŋmɔtɔ.

english: Why do I need to use tall wooden stakes for my yam vines to climb on?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi koni sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ lɛ?

english: Staking holds yam leaves up toward sunlight where they manufacture food for the tubers underground, while keeping leaves away from wet soil diseases.
ga: Staking lɛ hiɛɔ sweet potato baai lɛ ni kwɛɔ hulu la lɛ hiɛ koni ekɛ niyenii aha ŋmeii lɛ. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ha baai lɛ akashɛ helai ahe yɛ shikpɔŋ ni efɔ nɔ.

english: Waterlogged soil cuts off oxygen to cassava roots, creating damp conditions where harmful fungi and bacteria multiply and decay the tubers.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ ŋmɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ ni haa wala yibii lɛ yaa ŋmei shishifãi lɛ amli. cause humidity Biɛ ji he ni ŋmeii kɛ helatsɛmɛi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ faa yɛ ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii lɛ.

english: Why do my crops stop growing and turn yellow during dry periods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ kpaɔ shweremɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Crops need water to carry nutrients from the soil up into their roots and leaves. Without regular water, the crop cannot 'feed' itself, causing growth to stop and leaves to turn yellow from starvation.
ga: Tsei hia nu koni amɛkɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛya amɛ shishifãi kɛ baai lɛ anɔ. Kɛji nu ni sa bɛ lɛ, Nibii ni aduɔ lɛ nyɛɛɛ ‘aye’ amɛhe, ni no haa amɛdalɛ kpaa ni baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hɔmɔ hewɔ.

english: Is it possible for me to plant and harvest crops three times in one year instead of waiting for the rain?
ga: Ani ebaanyɛ eba akɛ madu ni makpa ŋmɔshi nibii etɛ yɛ afi kome mli moŋ fe ni mamɛ nugbɔ?

english: Yes, crops can grow year-round regardless of rainfall if they have a constant water source like irrigation or dams, allowing you to start a new planting cycle as soon as one harvest finishes.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei baanyɛ akwɛ̃ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ ni nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ kɔɔɔ he eko. Kɛji nu jɛɛhe ko yɛ daa, tamɔ nu ni akɛshwieɔ shi loo nu ŋshɔnaa Enɛ haa onyɛɔ ojeɔ dumɔwui hee shishi kɛji ogbe ŋmaakpamɔ kome naa pɛ.

english: Why do my vegetable plants grow much faster when I water them regularly from a well compared to waiting for rainfall?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitsei lɛ daraa oya waa kɛ́ mikɛ nu shwie amɛnɔ kɛjɛ nubu mli daa lɛ fe nugbɔ ni mimɛɔ lɛ?

english: Regular watering prevents crop stress and keeps the soil wet enough for roots to continuously absorb food, whereas waiting for rain subjects plants to dry spells that slow down their natural growth cycle.
ga: Nu ni akɛhaa tsei lɛ daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛtsiɔ tsei lɛ anaa, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli fũuɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ anyɛ aŋɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ be fɛɛ be. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ lɛ mɛmɔ baaha tsei lɛ agbi. Enɛ haa bɔ ni adebɔɔ mli dalɛ yaa nɔ ehaa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why does rice need so much more water to grow compared to crops like cassava or maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nu babaoo he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekwɛ̃ fe ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmãa loo ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice plants naturally adapted to marshy, wet conditions and have internal air tubes that let their roots breathe underwater, whereas cassava and maize roots will rot if left in standing water.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsakeɔ amɛhe amɛwoɔ shihilɛi ni mli efɔ lɛ amli, ni amɛyɛ kɔɔyɔɔ tsɔnei ni haa amɛshishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛmuɔ yɛ nu shishi. yɛ be mli ni ŋmãa kɛ ŋmãa shishifãi baagboi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ nu ni damɔ shi mli.

english: Why are the grains on my rice plant small and empty this season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmaa ni yɔɔ mi ŋmãa tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ ji bibii ni nɔ ko bɛ mli yɛ be nɛɛ mli lɛ?

english: Empty or light rice grains usually happen when the plant doesn't get enough water during its flowering stage, preventing it from transferring sugars into the developing seeds.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ŋmeii ni bɛ nɔ ko loo ni yɔɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ baa kɛji tso lɛ nine shɛɛɛ nu ni fa bɔ ni sa nɔ yɛ be mli ni ewoɔ fɔfɔi lɛ. Etsiɔ sugar ni yaa dumɔwui ni miiya hiɛ lɛ anaa.

english: What kind of soil conditions does rice prefer to produce heavy heads of grain?
ga: Mɛɛ shikpɔŋ shihilɛi amli ŋmãa sumɔɔ ni ekɛ dumɔwui ni tsii aha?

english: Rice grows best in clay-rich or lowland soils that hold water for long periods, giving the plant's roots continuous moisture to develop heavy, full grain heads.
ga: Omɔ kwɛ̃ɔ jogbaŋŋ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni shikpɔŋ yɔɔ nɔ loo shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu hiɔ mli be kakadaŋŋ lɛ nɔ. Ha tso shishifãi lɛ afee fɛ̃i be fɛɛ be koni amɛ wo dumɔwui ni tsii, ni eyi obɔ.

english: Can I plant rice on the exact same plot of land right after I harvest the first crop?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu ŋmãa yɛ shikpɔŋ kome nɔ nɔŋŋ beni akpa klɛŋklɛŋ ŋmãa lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ?

english: Yes, you can replant immediately if you have continuous water and replenish the soil nutrients with manure or fertilizer, as repeated farming drains the soil's natural strength quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, obaanyɛ odu ekoŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji oyɛ nu ni yaa nɔ ni okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli nibii amli ekoŋŋ. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, okwaayeli ni afɔɔ feemɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli hewalɛ ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ baa shi oya.

english: Why do my crops produce a smaller yield per acre compared to larger farms in other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ woɔ yibii fioo yɛ acre kome mli kɛ akɛto ŋmɔji wuji ni yɔɔ kpokpai krokomɛi anɔ lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Lower yields usually happen when crops face water stress, lack essential soil nutrients, or are planted using low-quality seeds that naturally produce fewer fruits or grains.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, yibiiwoo ni baa shi lɛ baa kɛji tsei kɛ nu he haomɔ kpe. Niyenii ni he hiaa ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ loo ni akɛ dumɔwui ni hi jogbaŋŋ ni jɛɔ adebɔɔ mli woɔ yibii loo ŋmaa fioo pɛ tsuɔ nii kɛduɔ.

english: How does deep tilling and breaking up hard soil help my crop roots grow better?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ ni akɛtsuɔ nii kɛ shikpɔŋ ni wa ni akuɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ aye abua mitso lɛ shishifãi lɛ ni amɛdara jogbaŋŋ?

english: Loosening hard soil allows crop roots to easily push deep into the earth to find buried moisture and food, resulting in stronger stems and larger harvests.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni shwieɔ shi lɛ haa tsei shishifãi lɛ nyɛɔ amɛtsiɔ amɛhe kɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ oya koni amɛyatao ŋmɔtɔ ni afu kɛ niyenii. Enɛ haa tsei lɛ ahe waa ni amɛkpaa nii babaoo.

english: Why do hot, dry sun rays cause my crop leaves to curl up during the afternoon?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ hulu ni mli edɔ ni egbi lɛ haa mitso lɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Leaves curl up to protect themselves from heat and reduce water loss through their surface, acting as a natural defense mechanism when the plant loses water faster than its roots can drink.
ga: Baai lɛ shwieɔ amɛhe koni amɛbu amɛhe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he ni amɛha nu ni hoɔ kɛtsɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ nɔ lɛ aba shi. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli hebuu gbɛ ejaakɛ tsei laajeɔ nu oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ anu.

english: What happens to my maize if I plant too many seeds close together because my land is small?
ga: Mɛni baaba mi-abele lɛ nɔ kɛji midu dumɔwui babaoo yɛ amɛhe ejaakɛ mihegbɛ lɛ faaa?

english: When crops are crowded, they fight each other for sunlight, water, and soil nutrients. This causes them to grow tall, thin, and weak, resulting in tiny cobs or no yield at all.
