ga: Kɛji akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ebɔle amɛhe babaoo Amɛyeɔ hulu la, nu kɛ niyenii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he akaŋ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, amɛkwɔ, amɛhe waaa, ni amɛhe waaa, ni nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji ŋmei bibioo ko. loo afeee nɔ ko kwraa

english: How do I decide how many crops to plant when my farm land is very small?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ makpɛ miyiŋ yɛ ŋmɔshi nibii enyiɛ ni esa akɛ madu lɛ he be mli ni mishikpɔŋ lɛ faaa kwraa lɛ?

english: You should follow recommended spacing guidelines for each crop rather than trying to fit as many as possible. Planting fewer, properly spaced crops produces a higher total harvest than overcrowding a small field.
ga: Esa akɛ onyiɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni akɛha akɛ esa akɛ ato he kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ eko fɛɛ eko lɛ sɛɛ. Mohu ɔ, bɔɔ mɔde nɛ o to he blɔ nya bɔ nɛ o ma nyɛ. Kɛ́ adu tsei fioo ni akɛto amɛhe jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha yibiiwoo fɛɛ ni anáa lɛ aya hiɛ fe tsei babaoo ni adu yɛ he ko bibioo.

english: If I notice one of my cassava plants is sick, should I spray it with medicine or pull it out of the ground?
ga: Kɛji ona akɛ hela mɔ ŋmei tso kome Ani esa akɛ mawo lɛ tsofa loo majie kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli?

english: If only one plant shows signs of a severe disease, it is best to pull it out and destroy it away from the farm. This creates a safe space and stops the sickness from spreading to your healthy crops.
ga: Kɛji tso kome pɛ jie hela ni naa wa he okadi kpo Esa akɛ ajie amɛ ni akpata amɛhiɛ kɛjɛ ŋmɔ lɛ he. Enɛ haa he ko ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe baa ni ehaaa hela agbɛ ashwã onibii ni yɔɔ hewalɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: How can I tell if a sick crop can still be saved with medicine or if it is going to die?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji akɛ abaanyɛ akɛ tsofa atsa ŋmɔshi nibii ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ lolo loo ebaagbo?

english: If only the leaves have light spots or yellowing, medicine can usually revive the crop. However, if the main stem or roots are rotten and the plant is completely wilted, medicine will not work and the plant will die.
ga: Kɛji akɛ baai lɛ yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ loo ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ Tsofai baanyɛ aha ŋmɔshi nibii aya hiɛ ekoŋŋ, shi kɛlɛ, kɛji akɛ tso lɛ shishifã loo shishifãi titri lɛ fite ni tso lɛ fite kwraa. Tsofa lɛ tsuuu nii ni tso lɛ baagbo.

english: Can a disease on just one tree spread and kill my entire cocoa farm?
ga: Ani hela ko ni yɔɔ tso kome pɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã ni efite mi-kookoo ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ?

english: Yes, crop diseases like Black Pod or Swollen Shoot spread easily through rain splashes, insects, or dirty tools from an infected tree to surrounding healthy ones if not handled quickly.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmɔshi nibii ahe helai tamɔ ŋmeii ni edɔ loo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa mlɛo kɛtsɔɔ ŋmeii, kooloi bibii, loo nibii ni he tseee ni jɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ amli kɛyaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ anɔ. Kɛji akɛ atsuuu he nii oya

english: What are the early signs I should look for to know my crops are starting to get sick?
ga: Mɛni ji mra be mli okadii ni esa akɛ matao koni male kɛji miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ miibɔi hela?

english: Watch out for unusual leaf color changes like yellowing or browing, spots on stems, stunted growth, leaf curling, or sudden wilting during the cool morning hours.
ga: Kwɛmɔ tsakemɔi ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ ni baa baa lɛ su mli, tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ loo ŋmɔtɔ, ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ anɔ, dalɛ ni eyaaa hiɛ, baai ni ebɔle ehe, loo ŋmɔtɔ ni baa trukaa yɛ leebi ŋmɛlɛtswai ni hulutsoo be mli lɛ.

english: Why do my tomato plants suddenly wither and die just when they start bearing fruit?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgboiɔ kɛji amɛbɔi yibiiwoo pɛ?

english: This is often caused by soil-borne fungal or bacterial wilt diseases. The sickness blocks the tubes inside the stem that carry water, causing the plant to starve and collapse rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, wilt hela ni fungi loo bacteria ni yɔɔ sũ mli lɛ kɛbaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. Hela nɛɛ tsiɔ paipii ni yɔɔ tsɔne lɛ mli ni kɛ nu yaa lɛ anaa. Enɛ haa hɔmɔ yeɔ tsei oya ni amɛkuɔ shi.

english: Why are my pepper leaves curling up and turning pale even when there is enough rain?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ pepper baai lɛ ebɔle amɛhe ni amɛhe efee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ? Nɛgbɛ ji he ni nugbɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa yɔɔ?

english: Leaf curling is usually not caused by lack of water, but by tiny insects like whiteflies or mites that suck the plant's sap and spread viral sicknesses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, jeee nu ni bɛ lɛ kɛ baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. Moŋ lɛ, koolooi bibii tamɔ whiteflies loo mites ni nuɔ tsei amli nu ni amɛgbɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ helatsɛmɛi amli baa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa.

english: If I only have a small stock of chemical medicine left, should I share it among all my crops or focus on a few?
ga: Kɛji miyɛ tsofa fioo ko ni akɛ tsofa tsuɔ nii yɛ mli lɛ ni eshwɛ Ani Esa akɛ mikɛha ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ loo mikɛ mijwɛŋmɔ ama fioo komɛi anɔ?

english: It is better to treat a specific section properly with the full required dose. Giving a weak, diluted dose to all crops will not cure any of them and wastes the little medicine you have.
ga: Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ shika ni he hiaa lɛ fɛɛ atsu he lɛ he nii jogbaŋŋ. Niyenii ni akɛhaa ŋmɔshi nibii bibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ haŋ ŋmɔshi nibii ko kwraa yiwala. ni ofite tsofa fioo ni oyɔɔ lɛ

english: How do I know the right amount of chemical medicine or fertilizer to keep in stock for my field?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsofa loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni sa ni esa akɛ mikɛto miŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: You calculate your stock based on the exact size of your field and the crop type. Keeping a little extra allows you to respond immediately when sickness first appears before it destroys the whole field.
ga: Obuɔ onibii lɛ ahe akɔntaa yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ dalɛ pɔtɛɛ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe. Kwɛmɔ fioo ko ni fata he lɛ haa onyɛɔ otsuɔ he nii oya kɛ́ hela ko je kpo klɛŋklɛŋ dani ekpata ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ hiɛ.

english: If I put fresh animal manure straight onto my crops, why do the leaves turn yellow and dry up?
ga: Kɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii hee wo miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ anɔ tɛ̃ɛ Mɛni hewɔ baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ lɛ?

english: Fresh manure from animal pens is too hot and strong for plant roots, which causes them to burn and yellow the leaves. When manure is left in a designated spot to cure and break down over time, it turns into a gentle fertilizer that feeds your crops safely without burning them.
ga: Nuŋtsɔ hee ni jɛ tsinai atsu lɛ mli lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ tsɔ kɛha tsei shishifãi. Enɛ haa amɛshãa ni ehaa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ. Enɛ ji be mli ni ashiɔ ŋmɔshi nibii yɛ he ko ni ato he gbɛjianɔ koni etsa ni efite yɛ be ni sa mli. Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ bafeɔ tsofa ni yɔɔ blɛoo ni haa onibii lɛ niyenii shweshweeshwe ni eshãaa amɛ.

english: Why do my maize plants grow taller and greener when I add cured animal waste to the farm soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ daraa ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔji beni mikɛ kooloi amli jwɛi ni atsa lɛ fataa shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ he lɛ?

english: Cured animal waste acts like food for the soil, releasing natural nutrients slowly over time. These nutrients help maize plants build strong stems and healthy green leaves, which trap sunlight to help the plant produce bigger ears of corn.
ga: Koolooi ahe jwɛi ni atsu he nii lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ mli. Ejieɔ adebɔɔ mli niyenii mli hewalɛi fiofio. Beni be hoɔ lɛ Nɛkɛ niyenii nɛɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa tsei ni amɛnáa ŋmeii ni wa kɛ baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. ni mɔ̃ɔ hulu la lɛ koni eye ebua tsei ni amɛwo ŋmãa toi wuji

english: Is it safe to grow food crops like cassava and vegetables in soil mixed with animal manure?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ abaadu niyenii ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ ŋmei kɛ aduawai yɛ shikpɔŋ ni akɛ kooloi aŋɔli efutu mli?

english: Yes, cured animal manure is completely safe for both your crops and the environment. Letting the manure rest and cure neutralizes bad smells and harmful organisms while preserving the good nutrients that help food crops grow naturally.
ga: Hɛɛ, ŋmeii ni atsa lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa kɛha onibii kɛ shihilɛ ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ fɛɛ. Kɛ́ aŋmɛ gbɛ ni ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ jɔɔ amɛhe ni etsa lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ejie ŋmeii kɛ nibii ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ kɛjɛ mli. Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ekwɛɔ niyenii kpakpai ni yeɔ ebuaa niyenii tsei ni amɛdaraa yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe lɛ anɔ.

english: How does cured animal manure behave differently in my soil compared to store-bought chemical fertilizers?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ feɔ enii yɛ gbɛ ni yɔɔ srɔto nɔ yɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eha tɛŋŋ kɛ akɛto tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli ni aheɔ yɛ shwapo mli lɛ he?

english: Chemical fertilizers give plants a quick boost but can wash away easily when heavy rain falls. Cured animal manure stays in the soil longer, improving the soil structure year after year while steadily feeding your crops.
ga: Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ tsei amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa oya shi kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, ebaanyɛ efo amɛhe oya. Nuŋtsɔ ni atsa lɛ hiɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli be babaoo. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii feɔ jogbaŋŋ afi fɛɛ afi Yɛ nakai beaŋ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ehaa onibii lɛ niyenii be fɛɛ be.

english: How does using animal manure on my farm help my crops survive during dry spells?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ ŋmeii ni mikɛtsuɔ nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa miŋmɔshi nii lɛ ni amɛhiɔ shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli?

english: Cured manure improves the soil so it can hold onto moisture like a sponge. Soil enriched with cured organic waste stays moist much longer after rain, keeping your crops hydrated even when water is scarce.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni atsa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ fɛo bɔni afee ni enyɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ mli tamɔ ŋmɔtɔ. Shikpɔŋ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni asaa he lɛ eyi mli obɔ lɛ baahi shi be babaoo yɛ nugbɔ enɛ sɛɛ. Ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ amli nu shwieɔ shi kɛ́ nu faaa po.

english: Why do the roots of my crops grow thicker and spread wider when I clear space to add organic compost?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso lɛ shishifãi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa babaoo kɛ́ mijie he ko ni mikɛ organic compost afata he lɛ?

english: Organic fertilizer made from cured waste softens heavy soil, making it easier for plant roots to breathe and spread out. A wider root system allows the crop to pull up more water and plant food from deep in the ground.
ga: Organic fertilizer ni akɛ jwɛi ni atsu he nii lɛ feɔ lɛ haa shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ feɔ blɛoo. Enɛ haa efeɔ mlɛo kɛhaa tsei shishifãi akɛ amɛaamu ni amɛgbɛ amɛshwã. Shishifãi ni mli kwɔ lɛ haa tsei lɛ gbalaa nu kɛ niyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ.

english: Why do my pepper plants drop their flowers before producing fruit, and can organic manure fix this?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ miiho fɔfɔi dani ewo yibii lɛ? Ni ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ baanyɛ atsu naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Pepper plants drop flowers when they lack nutrients or face soil stress. Adding cured manure gives the soil a steady supply of nutrients, helping the plant grow strong enough to hold onto its flowers and produce lots of peppers.
ga: Pepper tsei lɛ fɔɔ fɔfɔi kɛ́ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ amɛmli loo amɛna shikpɔŋ nɔ haomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ aná niyenii kpakpai daa. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei lɛ ni amɛdaraa waa bɔ ni sa ni amɛhiɛɔ fɔfɔii ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii babaoo.

english: When is the best time to apply cured animal waste to my land so my crops get the full benefit?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni hi fe fɛɛ ni esa akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni atsa lɛ awo mishikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ koni maná miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ahe sɛɛ fɛɛ?

english: The best time is during early land preparation before you plant your seeds. Mixing cured manure into the soil ahead of time gives the nutrients time to settle so your young crops can feed on them as soon as they sprout.
ga: Be ni hi fe fɛɛ ji be mli ni asaa shikpɔŋ lɛ dani aduɔ dumɔwui. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwo mli lɛ futu shikpɔŋ lɛ mli dani be shɛ lɛ, ehaa niyenii mli nibii lɛ naa be ni amɛkɛbaa shi. Enɛ ji koni onyɛ oye oŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ kɛji amɛkwɛ̃ pɛ.

english: Why do weeds seem to grow so fast around my crops after I put cured animal fertilizer in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ mihe lɛ? Miŋmɔshi nibii beni mikɛ kooloi aŋmɔshi nibii efata ŋmɔji lɛ ahe sɛɛ?

english: Cured manure enriches the entire soil bed with nutrients, making it easy for all plants—including weeds—to grow rapidly. You will need to weed your farm regularly so your crops do not have to share that rich plant food.
ga: Nuŋtsɔ ni atsa lɛ haa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli eyiɔ kɛ niyenii kpakpai. Ehaa tsei fɛɛ, ni jwɛi fata he lɛ, baakwɛ̃ oya. Ebaabi ni okɛ jwɛi awo oŋmɔ lɛ mli daa bɔni afee ni ehe ehiaaa ni onibii lɛ kɛ nakai tsei niyenii ni jara wa lɛ aha.

english: How does keeping livestock like farm animals directly help me grow better food crops?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ kooloi ni mikɛ amɛ yeɔ tamɔ ŋmɔ mli kooloi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mi tɛ̃ɛ koni makwɛ niyenii ni hi jogbaŋŋ?

english: Farm animals produce waste that can be collected from their pens and left to cure into valuable natural fertilizer. Feeding this cured waste back into your crop field creates a continuous cycle where your animals help nourish your land and crops naturally.
ga: Koolooi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ jieɔ jwɛi ni abaanyɛ abua naa kɛjɛ amɛ ŋtayaai amli ni ashi koni akɛtsu nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni jara wa. Shwɛi ni atsa lɛ ni oookɛku sɛɛ kɛya oŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ haa sɛɛkuu ni yaa nɔ yɛ he ni okooloi lɛ haa oshikpɔŋ kɛ oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ baa.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, an essential plant food. As the crop grows, it pulls nitrogen from older bottom leaves to feed fresh upper leaves. Adding organic manure or nitrogen-rich fertilizer helps keep the whole plant green and strong.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen, ni ji tso niyenii ni he hiaa waa lɛ bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Kɛ tsei lɛ dara Ejieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai momoi amli koni ŋwɛi baai lɛ ahi shi ehee. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii fata he lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni tsei lɛ afee ŋmɔji ni amɛná hewalɛ.

english: Why does my soil turn hard like a rock in the dry season, and how can I keep it soft for planting?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wa tamɔ tɛsaa yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be mli lɛ? Ni te aaafee tɛŋŋ aha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee blɛoo kɛha dumɔ?

english: Bare soil loses all its water under direct sunlight, causing it to bake hard and kill helpful earthworms. Covering your field with dead leaves or straw—called mulching—shades the soil, keeps moisture trapped inside, and keeps the ground loose.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni bɛ nɔ ko nɔ ko lɛ laajeɔ emli nu fɛɛ kɛji hulu la shɛ enɔ tɛ̃ɛ. Enɛ haa amɛshãa waa ni amɛgbeɔ shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ lɛ. Akɛ baai loo jwɛi ni egboi haa ŋmɔji anɔ (Atsɛɔ enɛ akɛ mulching.) Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ, ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmɔtɔ hiɔ mli. ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ

english: Weeds are wild native plants that have adapted to your local soil over hundreds of years. Their seeds wake up instantly with rain and their aggressive root systems steal water and nutrients before your cultivated crops can get established.
ga: Jwɛi ji tsei ni yɔɔ koo lɛ mli ni etsake amɛhe kɛtee shikpɔŋ ni oyɔɔ nɔ lɛ nɔ yɛ afii ohai abɔ ni eho lɛ amli. Dumɔwui lɛ teɔ shi kɛji nugbɔ nɛ pɛ. Ni amɛshishifãi ni boteɔ mli lɛ juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii dani ŋmɔshi nibii ni oduɔ lɛ baanyɛ akwɛ̃.

english: Why is it good practice to plant plantain trees alongside my newly planted young cocoa trees?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji nifeemɔ kpakpa akɛ aaadu dumɔwui yɛ kookoo tsei ni adu ehee lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Young cocoa seedlings have tender leaves that burn easily under full sunlight. Plantains grow fast and produce broad leaves that act as living umbrellas, providing essential shade and keeping the soil cool while cocoa gets established.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii yɛ baai bibii ni shãa oya yɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. Plantains daa oya ni ewoɔ baai ni mli kwɔ ni tsuɔ nii akɛ hulutsoo. Ha hulutsoo ni he hiaa ni oha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ be mli ni kookoo lɛ jeɔ shishi etswaa lɛ.

english: When temperatures get too high or heavy rains flood the root area, tomato plants get stressed and cannot complete pollination. When pollination fails, the plant sheds the flower to conserve energy.
ga: Kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo nugbɔ nɛ waa lɛ, nu hoɔ yɛ shishifã lɛ he. Tomato tsei lɛ haoɔ amɛhe ni amɛnyɛŋ amɛwo ŋmɔtɔ. Kɛji pollination lɛ nyɛɛɛ atsu nii lɛ Tsei lɛ baaja amɛfɔfɔi lɛ amli koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he.

english: Yams tell you they are ready when the vines above ground start turning yellow and drying up at the end of the rainy season. This signals that the plant has finished storing energy in the tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potatoes tsɔɔ bo akɛ amɛfee klalo beni wain tsei ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ jeɔ shishi amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛgbiɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ naagbee lɛ. Enɛ ji okadi ni tsɔɔ akɛ tso lɛ egbe hewalɛ ni ekɛtoɔ e-bulb ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ mli lɛ naa.

english: Why do my cocoa pods turn black and rot right on the tree during the wet season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo ŋmɔji lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboɔ yɛ tso lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly in damp, dark conditions. Pruning extra tree branches lets sunlight and dry air into the farm, which stops the fungus from thriving.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya yɛ hei ni efɔ kɛ duŋ. Niji krokomɛi ni afolɔ ashwie shi koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni egbi abote ŋmɔ lɛ mli Enɛ baaye abua ni ŋmeii akakwɛ̃.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or whiteflies that hide under leaves and suck out the sap. As they feed, they cause the leaves to distort and can also spread crop viruses.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo whiteflies ni kɛ amɛhe woɔ baai lɛ ashishi ni amɛmuɔ nu lɛ mli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. be mli ni amɛyeɔ niyenii Amɛfiteɔ baai ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛgbɛ helai hu amɛshwã tsei amli.

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to breathe. When excess rain sits in the soil without draining away, the roots suffocate and fungi take over, causing the tubers to rot. Planting on raised soil mounds solves this problem.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛmu. Beni nugbɔ nɛɔ babaoo yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ni nu bɛ mli. Shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni ŋmeii haa amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji yitso ni egbo Dumɔ yɛ gɔji ni awó nɔ lɛ anɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni etsuɔ ​​naagba nɛɛ he nii.

english: Why should I clear away old stems and diseased plants after harvest instead of leaving them in the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esa akɛ majie tsei ni egbɔ kɛ tsei ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ kɛjɛ kpamɔ lɛ sɛɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooshi yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ?

english: Leaving old crop remains in the field gives pests and plant diseases a safe home to survive the dry season. Clearing or burning diseased debris cleans the field so new crops start fresh without immediate infection.
ga: Nibii ni etsɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔji amli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ tsei ahe helai náa shihilɛhe ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe koni amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ be lɛ mli. Nibii ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ loo ashãa lɛ haa jɛmɛ he tseɔ bɔni afee ni ŋmɔshi nibii heei aje shishi ekoŋŋ ni hela ko akabote mli amrɔ nɔŋŋ.

english: Why are the leaves on my maize plants turning light yellow instead of staying deep green?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miitsɔ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ lɛ?

english: Maize leaves turn yellow when the plant lacks nitrogen, which is its main food for leafy growth. This usually happens when the soil nutrients are exhausted or when heavy rains wash the plant food deep into the ground where roots cannot reach.
ga: Abɛi baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛji nitrogen bɛ tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii titri ni haa baa lɛ daa lɛ Bei pii lɛ Enɛ baa kɛji shikpɔŋ mli niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ lɛ faaa loo kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ haa tsei aniyenii hoɔ kɛboteɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do my corn leaves roll up tightly into straws during the afternoon heat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-abele baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ jwɛi ni mli wa yɛ shwane mli lɛ?

english: Corn leaves roll up to protect themselves from losing water during intense heat. It is the plant's natural defense to save moisture when the roots cannot find enough water in the soil.
ga: Akɛ ŋmãa baai shwieɔ shi koni nu akaje mli yɛ be mli ni hulu lɛ tsoɔ waa lɛ. Eji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu nii akɛ ehiɛ ŋmɔtɔ be mli ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ ana nu ni fa yɛ sũ lɛ mli.

english: Why are birds and small animals digging up my corn seeds right after I plant them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ okpoi kɛ kooloi bibii Koni amɛfolɔ mi ŋmãa dumɔwui lɛ amrɔ nɔŋŋ beni midu amɛ lɛ?

english: Animals smell the soft starch and moisture in planted seeds near the soil surface. Planting seeds at the recommended depth and firming the soil over them makes it difficult for animals to find and dig them up.
ga: Koolooi baanyɛ anu ashikishaŋ ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni yɔɔ dumɔwui ni adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɛ lɛ he. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ni atsɔɔ akɛ adu lɛ mli lɛ, kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ ni aaawo mli lɛ baaha ewa aha kooloi akɛ amɛaana dumɔwui lɛ ni amɛfo mli.

english: Why are the flowers falling off my fruit plants before any fruit actually grows?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔii miiho kɛmiijɛ mi tso lɛ yibii lɛ nɔ dani tso lɛ yibii lɛ daa diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Flowers drop off when the plant experiences stress from high temperatures, lack of water, or poor pollination by insects. The plant drops its flowers to conserve energy for its own survival.
ga: Fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ tsei lɛ na haomɔ kɛjɛ hulutsoo ni naa wa, nu ni bɛ, loo kooloi bibii ni haaa fɔfɔi lɛ afee nɔ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ mli. Tsei shwieɔ fɔfɔi koni amɛkɛbu hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do my fruit trees give a huge harvest one year but almost no fruit the next year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tso ni woɔ yibii lɛ wo yibii babaoo nɛkɛ yɛ afi kome mli lɛ? Shi afi ni baa lɛ mli lɛ, eshwɛ fioo ni nɔ ko kwraa baajɛ mli aba?

english: This pattern is called alternate bearing. Producing a massive crop exhausts all the tree's stored food energy, so it spends the following year recovering and rebuilding its strength instead of making new fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ style nɛɛ akɛ bearing ni akɛtoɔ najiaŋ. Nibii babaoo ni aduɔ lɛ baaha tso lɛ niyenii hewalɛ fɛɛ ni ekɛto lɛ afite. No hewɔ lɛ, ehe afi ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ dani ehiɛ ba shi ni etswa ehewalɛ ema shi ekoŋŋ. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooofee hetooi heei

english: Why are my fruits splitting open on the tree while they are still growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yibii lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ yɛ mitso lɛ nɔ be mli ni amɛdaraa lolo lɛ?

english: Fruits split when a long dry spell is suddenly followed by heavy rain or heavy watering. The inside of the fruit absorbs water quickly and expands faster than the outer skin can stretch, causing the skin to burst.
ga: Yibii lɛ tswaa kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa loo nu babaoo nɛ yɛ hɔmɔ be kakadaŋŋ sɛɛ. Yibii lɛ amligbɛ lɛ shwieɔ nu oya ni egbɛɔ eshwaa oya fe bɔ ni kponɔgbɛ hewolo lɛ baanyɛ agbɛ eshwa. Enɛ haa hewolo lɛ fãa.

english: Why does my farm give smaller crop yields when I plant the same crop in the same spot every year?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo kɛ́ midu tso kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ yɛ he kome afi fɛɛ afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop repeatedly steals the exact same nutrients from the soil every season and lets specific pests build up in the dirt. Rotating different types of crops keeps the soil balanced and starves out pests.
ga: Tse kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ shii abɔ lɛ juɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ kɛjɛɔ sũ lɛ mli daa be, ni ehaa tsɛŋemɔ helai komɛi buaa amɛhe naa yɛ sũ lɛ mli. Nibii sɔrɔtoi ni aduɔ lɛ ni atsakeɔ Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ ekome ni ejieɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ.

english: Why do insects attack my crop leaves more aggressively during the rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kooloi bibii tutuaa mitsei lɛ baai lɛ waa yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: Rainy weather produces tender, fresh leaves that insects love to eat, while the high air moisture provides the perfect environment for insect eggs to hatch and survive.
ga: Nugbɔshiimɔ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni amɛfeɔ blɛoo, ni kooloi sumɔɔ ni amɛye. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ waa lɛ haa shihilɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ kɛha kooloi bibii lɛ afɔ̃ɔ ni amɛhiɔ shi.

english: Why do my crop seeds sprout fast in some areas of my farm but fail completely in other parts?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ midumɔwui lɛ kwɛ̃ɔ oya yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ hei komɛi shi amɛkwɛɛɛ kwraa yɛ hei krokomɛi lɛ?

english: Soil texture and moisture vary across a farm. Hard, packed soil or low spots where water collects prevent seeds from getting the oxygen and warm air they need to sprout successfully.
ga: Shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ su kɛ latsaa lɛ yɛ srɔtoi yɛ ŋmɔ fɛɛ ŋmɔ mli. Shikpɔŋ ni wa ni mli edɔ loo hei ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni nu buaa ehe naa yɛ lɛ tsiɔ dumɔwui lɛ anaa koni amɛkaná kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛkwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ.

english: Why do root crops like cassava turn soft and rot underground before harvest time?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ shishifãi tamɔ ŋmei feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi dani kpamɔɔ be baashɛ lɛ?

english: Root crops rot when water stays trapped in heavy soil for too long without draining away properly. Too much water starves the roots of air and encourages soil fungi to attack the crop.
ga: Tsei shishifãi fiteɔ kɛji nu lɛ ŋmɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii mli be kakadaŋŋ ni enyɛɛɛ ejɛ mli jogbaŋŋ. Nu babaoo baaha shishifãi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ aye hɔmɔ ni ewo shikpɔŋ nɔ ŋmeii hewalɛ koni amɛtutua ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: What is fertilizer, and why do my crops need it to grow well?
ga: Mɛni ji ŋmɔshi nibii ni mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mitsei lɛ akwɛ̃ jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Fertilizer is like nutritious food for plants. Soil often loses its natural nutrients over time, so adding fertilizer gives crops the essential food they need to build strong roots, grow healthy green leaves, and produce heavy yields.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ tamɔ niyenii ni hewalɛ yɔɔ mli kɛha tsei. Shikpɔŋ lɛ fɔɔ niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni eyɔɔ lɛ sɛɛ foɔ yɛ be ni sa mli. No hewɔ lɛ, kɛ́ akɛ tsofa wo tsei amli lɛ, ebaaha amɛná niyenii ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná shishifãi ni wa. Kwɛmɔ baai eŋɔli ni mli wa ni ofee nibii babaoo ni anáa

english: How do I know if the soil on my farm lacks enough food for my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ?

english: When soil lacks nutrients, crops will grow very slowly, appear pale yellow instead of deep green, have thin stems, or drop their leaves early even when there is enough rainfall.
ga: Beni niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ Tso lɛ daa blɛoo waa. Ejeɔ kpo yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli tse yɛ ŋmɔŋ ni mli edɔ najiaŋ, eyɛ tsei bibii, loo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi oya kɛji nugbɔ nɛ bɔ ni sa po.

english: When is the right time to start applying fertilizer to my young crops?
ga: Mɛɛ be ji be ni sa ni esa akɛ maje miŋmɔshi nibii bibii lɛ amli ŋmɔshi nibii awo mli?

english: It is usually best to apply plant food early in the crop's life—either during planting or shortly after root establishment—especially at the start of the rainy season when plants are growing rapidly.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ oookɛ tso niyenii aba mra yɛ tso lɛ wala mli. Ekolɛ yɛ dumɔ be mli loo beni shishifãi ewo mli etsɛɛɛ lɛ. Titri lɛ, yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli beni tsei miida oya lɛ.

english: Why is my one-year-old mango tree still very small and not growing properly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi mango ni eye afi kome lɛ ji bibioo kwraa lolo ni edaaa jogbaŋŋ lɛ?

english: Young fruit trees often get stunted if they lack proper plant food (fertilizer) or are choked by surrounding weeds that steal water and nutrients from their roots.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei bibii ni woɔ yibii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji amɛbɛ tsei niyenii ni sa (ŋmei) loo jwɛi ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ saa amɛhe. obstruction, ni juɔ nu kɛ niyenii mli nibii kɛjɛɔ shishifãi lɛ amli lɛ

english: Why do my young crops look weak and yellowish even though it rains regularly?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui lɛ tamɔ nɔ ni amɛhe waaa ni amɛhe yɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ eyɛ mli akɛ nugbɔ nɛɔ daa moŋ lɛ?

english: Rainwater supplies water, but water alone is not enough. If the soil lacks nutrients, the plant cannot make food, causing leaves to turn yellow and growth to stall despite plenty of rain.
ga: Nugbɔ nu haa nu, shi nu pɛ kɛkɛ faaa. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ niyenii mli hewalɛ Tsei lɛ nyɛŋ afee niyenii. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ ni amɛdalɛ sɛɛ foɔ kɛji nugbɔ nɛ waa po.

english: How can I tell if my plant is hungry for food rather than suffering from an insect attack?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji hɔmɔ miiye mitsei lɛ moŋ fe ni ŋmeii baatutua amɛ?

english: A hungry plant generally turns pale yellow all over and stays small, whereas an insect attack leaves visible holes, bitten leaves, or pests crawling on the crop.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsei ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ he fɛɛ he ni amɛfeɔ bibii. Beni kooloo lɛ tutuaa lɛ, abaana buji. baai ni akɔmɔ loo kooloi ni shwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ

english: Can I just plant a fruit tree seedling in the ground and leave it to grow on its own?
ga: Ani manyɛ madu tso yibii dumɔwui yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mahã amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛkwɛ̃?

english: If you leave a young tree without care, weeds will steal its nutrients and it will struggle to grow. Fruit trees need active attention, including weeding and fertilizer application, during their first few years.
ga: Kɛji oshi tsei bibii ni atsaaa amɛ lɛ, Jwɛi lɛ baaju niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ. Ni ebaabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eda. Ehe miihia ni akwɛ tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ jogbaŋŋ. Nɔ ni fata enɛ he ji jwɛi ni ajieɔ kɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni akɛwoɔ mli yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ afii fioo lɛ amli.

english: Do I still need to care for my fruit trees after they have been growing for a whole year?
ga: Ani ehe miihia ni makwɛ mi tsei ni woɔ yibii lɛ anɔ lolo beni midu amɛ afi muu lɛ fɛɛ sɛɛ?

english: Yes, young trees still need regular feeding, protection from pests, and weed clearance after a year to ensure they build strong trunks and start bearing fruit early.
ga: Hɛɛ, tsei bibii lɛ ahe miihia niyenii daa lolo. Hebuu kɛjɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui ahe kɛ jwɛi ni ajieɔ yɛ afi kome sɛɛ koni tsei lɛ afee ŋmeii ni wa ni amɛje yibiiwoo shishi oya.

english: What happens if I ignore my young tree farm and stop paying attention to it?
ga: Mɛni baaba kɛji miku mihiɛ mishwie mitso bibioo lɛ ŋmɔ lɛ nɔ ni mikpa nɔ mijwɛŋmɔ?

english: Neglecting young trees allows weeds and diseases to take over, which can permanently stunt the trees or kill them before they ever yield any fruit.
ga: Kɛ́ aku hiɛ ashwie tsei bibii anɔ lɛ, ebaaha jwɛi kɛ helai aye nɔ, ni baanyɛ aha tsei lɛ afee shoo daa loo egbe amɛ dani amɛwo yibii.

english: How does feeding my young fruit trees help them produce fruit faster?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ niyenii ni mikɛhaa midumɔwui lɛ baanyɛ aye abua amɛ ni amɛwo yibii oya?

english: Giving plants fertilizer speeds up their early growth by building strong branches and healthy leaves, allowing the tree to mature faster and bear good fruit sooner.
ga: Nibii ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ daa mra kɛtsɔ niji ni he wa kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni efeɔ lɛ nɔ. Eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛdaraa oya ni amɛwoɔ yibii kpakpai oya.

english: Why are the lower leaves of my maize turning yellow from the tips down the middle?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ kɛjɛɔ enaagbee kɛyaa teŋgbɛ lɛ?

english: Yellowing leaves usually mean your maize is hungry for nitrogen, which is the main nutrient it needs to stay green and grow tall. Adding fertilizer or well-rotted manure early in the season supplies this nitrogen so the plant can make healthy green leaves.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ hɔmɔ miiye o-corn lɛ kɛha nitrogen. Eji niyenii mli hewalɛ titri ko ni he hiaa koni ehi shi eŋɔli ni ekwɛ̃. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni egbo jogbaŋŋ fata he yɛ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ, ebaaha nitrogen kroko aba. Bɔni afee ni tso lɛ anyɛ awo baai eŋɔli ni mli wa.

english: Why do my tomato fruits develop black, sunken spots on the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmɔlɔi diji yɔɔ dani eshɛɔ lɛ?

english: This black spot is called blossom-end rot, and it happens when the plant cannot take up enough calcium from the soil, often caused by irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant pull calcium all the way into the growing fruit.
ga: Atsɛɔ nɛkɛ he diŋ nɛɛ akɛ fɔfɔii anaagbee fitemɔ. Ni ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni akɛwoɔ mɔ mli ni ejaaa lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ pɛpɛɛpɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua tsei lɛ ni amɛŋɔ calcium lɛ amɛwo aduawai ni miida lɛ amli kwraa.

english: Leaf curl is usually caused by tiny insects like thrips or aphids sucking sap from the young leaves, or by viruses they spread. Spraying with safe organic or chemical pest controls early keeps the leaves flat so they can catch sunlight.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo aphids ni nuɔ baai bibii amli nu lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ baa. aloo kɛjɛ helai ni amɛgbɛɔ amɛshwãa lɛ amli Mra ni akɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ wala mli loo tsofai ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni akɛshwieɔ nɔ lɛ baaha baai lɛ afee ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ bɔni afee ni hulu la lɛ ashɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow tall with lots of leaves but only produce small, thin roots under the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi yucca tso lɛ daa ni eyɛ baai babaoo lɛ? Mohu ɔ, e ngɛ sisi nyafii nɛ a ngɛ tsɔwi pɛ ngɛ zugba a sisi.

english: When soil has too much nitrogen and not enough potassium, or when plants are crowded together, the cassava spends all its energy making stems and leaves instead of storing starch in the root tubers.
ga: Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nitrogen fa tsɔ ni potassium ni fa bɔ ni sa loo beni tsei ebua amɛhe naa babaoo lɛ, Cassava kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛfeɔ ŋmeii kɛ baai. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni akɛ starch baato shishifã lɛ mli lɛ

english: Why do my cocoa trees drop their small green pods before they fully mature?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ miiho ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli lɛ? Dani amɛbaadara kwraa?

english: Young cocoa pods drop off—a process called cherelle wilt—when the tree is stressed by dry weather, shade competition, or a lack of soil nutrients, causing the tree to naturally reduce the number of pods it has to feed.
ga: Kookoo ŋmɔji bibii lɛ baagbee shi. Enɛ ji gbɛ ko ni ale lɛ akɛ cherelle wilt, beni shihilɛi ni mli egbi lɛ haa tsei haoɔ lɛ. Ni ehaa hulutsoo fioo loo niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Enɛ haa tso lɛ baa shi yɛ ŋmeii ni esa akɛ eye niyenii yɛ adebɔɔ naa lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do yam vines need tall wooden stakes to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he hiaa tsei kakadaji koni amɛkwɔ lɛ? Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ooonyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ?

english: Yam vines need stakes to lift their leaves up to catch as much sunlight as possible, which allows the leaves to make plenty of food that travels down to build a large tuber underground.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ he miihia shishitoo ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛwo amɛbaai lɛ anɔ koni amɛná hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ. Enɛ haa baai lɛ feɔ niyenii babaoo ni fãa kɛyaa shi ni efeɔ shikpɔŋ shishi ŋmeii wuji.

english: Extra suckers act like hungry children competing for the mother plant's food and water. Leaving only one or two strong suckers allows the main plant to produce a bigger, heavier bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii krokomɛi lɛ feɔ amɛnii tamɔ gbekɛbii ni hɔmɔ yeɔ amɛ ni miitswa akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii kɛ nu kɛjɛ tso lɛ nyɛ lɛ mli. Kɛ́ ashi tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ, ebaaha tso titri lɛ awo tso wuji ni tsii.

english: How does covering the soil around my crops with dry grass help them grow during hot weather?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛdaraa yɛ kɔɔyɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ mli?

english: Covering the ground with dry grass, known as mulching, acts like a blanket that traps moisture in the dirt, keeps the plant roots cool under the hot sun, and stops weeds from popping up.
ga: Atsɛɔ jwɛi ni egbi ni akɛhaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ hu akɛ mulching. Etsuɔ nii tamɔ kuntu ni ŋmɛɔ nu ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli lɛ. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni tso shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi. ni etsĩ jwɛi ni kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ anaa.

english: Why do extension officers tell me to plant cowpeas or groundnuts in the same field where I planted maize?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ extension nitsulɔi lɛ kɛɔ mi akɛ madu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ ni miduɔ ŋmã yɛ nɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ nɔ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts are legumes that pull nitrogen gas out of the air and fix it into the soil through their roots, naturally fertilizing the ground for future heavy-feeding crops like maize.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts ji ŋmeii ni jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli kɛtsɔɔ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ haa adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ kɛha wɔsɛɛ be mli kooloi aniyenii ni tsii, tamɔ ŋmãa.

english: The first rain is often followed by a long dry spell before the real rainy season sets in, which can cause seeds to sprout and then wither away in the dry soil before the next rain falls.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, nugbɔshiimɔ be kakadaŋŋ nyiɛɔ klɛŋklɛŋ nugbɔshiimɔ lɛ sɛɛ dani nugbɔshiimɔ be diɛŋtsɛ lɛ baa. Enɛ baanyɛ aha dumɔwui lɛ akwɛ̃ ni amɛgbi yɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi lɛ nɔ dani nugbɔ ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ anɛ.

english: Yellowing lower leaves usually mean your maize lacks nitrogen, which is the main food plants use to grow strong. When there isn't enough nitrogen in the soil, the plant pulls it from its older bottom leaves to keep the young top leaves growing.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni ji ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ o-abele lɛ mli. Eji niyenii titri ni tsei kɛtsuɔ nii koni amɛdara waa. Kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ bɛ nitrogen ni fa bɔ ni sa Tso lɛ gbalaa lɛ kɛjɛɔ shishigbɛ baai ni edara lɛ anɔ koni ŋwɛi baai bibii lɛ aya nɔ ada.

english: How do crops like cowpea and groundnuts help improve my farm's soil for future crops?
ga: Te ŋmɔshi nibii tamɔ tsina ŋmeii kɛ ŋmeii baanyɛ aha shikpɔŋ ni yɔɔ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ aya hiɛ aha wɔsɛɛ ŋmɔshi nibii?

english: Legume crops have natural bacteria living in their roots that pull nitrogen out of the air and put it into the soil. When the crop finishes growing, that nitrogen stays behind in the soil as free plant food for whatever you plant next.
ga: Legumes yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni hiɔ amɛshishifãi amli. Enɛ gbalaa nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni ekɛwoɔ sũ lɛ mli. Kɛ tso lɛ gbe ekwɛ̃ naa Nakai nitrogen lɛ baakã shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ tso niyenii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha nɔ ni obaadu yɛ sɛɛ mli lɛ.

english: Why shouldn't I spread fertilizer right before a heavy rain falls?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ ashwieɔ ŋmɔshi nibii anɔ dani nugbɔ nɛɔ waa lɛ?

english: Heavy rain quickly washes fertilizer off the top of the soil and carries it away into streams or deep underground where plant roots cannot reach it, wasting your money and leaving your crops hungry.
ga: Nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ hoɔ ŋmɔshi nibii kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli oya ni ekɛwoɔ faai amli loo shikpɔŋ shishi shɔŋŋ yɛ he ni tsei shishifãi nyɛɛɛ ashɛ he lɛ. Efiteɔ shika ni ehaa hɔmɔ yeɔ onibii.

english: Why do many of the flowers on my cocoa trees drop off without forming any cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi babaoo ni yɔɔ mi cacao tsei lɛ anɔ lɛ miigbee shi ni cacao ŋmɔtɔ ko kwraa efeee lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees produce far more flowers than they can support. Many flowers drop because they were not pollinated by tiny insects, or because hot weather and drought stress cause the tree to shed flowers to protect itself.
ga: Cacao tsei woɔ fɔfɔi babaoo fe bɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛkwɛ nɔ. Fɔfɔi babaoo shwieɔ shi ejaakɛ kooloi bibii kɛ amɛhe wooo mli. Aloo akɛni kɔɔyɔŋ mli dɔlɛ kɛ hɔmɔ haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ anɔ koni amɛkɛbu amɛhe hewɔ.

english: Extra shoots, called suckers, compete with the main plantain tree for soil nutrients, water, and light. Removing all but one or two strong suckers allows the mother plant to focus its energy on growing a large, heavy bunch of plantains.
ga: Tso lɛ yibii ni fa fe nine, ni atsɛɔ amɛ suckers lɛ kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii ni yɔɔ sũ lɛ mli, nu, kɛ la mli. Kɛ́ ajieɔ tsei ni hi jogbaŋŋ lɛ fɛɛ, ja tso kome loo enyɔ pɛ lɛ, ehaa tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ kɛ ejwɛŋmɔ maa plantains tsei wuji ni tsii lɛ anɔ.

english: Why do my pepper plants lose their flowers when the afternoon sun gets extremely hot?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ fɔfɔi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji shwane hulu lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ lɛ?

english: When heat becomes severe, pepper plants experience temperature stress. They drop their blossoms as a defense mechanism to conserve water and prevent themselves from drying out.
ga: Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa waa lɛ, Pepper tsei lɛ naa hulutsoo be mli haomɔ. Amɛshwieɔ fɔfɔii amɛshwieɔ shi akɛ gbɛ ni amɛtsɔɔ nɔ amɛbuɔ nu he ni amɛtsiɔ enaa koni ekagbi.

english: Why do my yam plants need stakes to climb on instead of just trailing along the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi sweet potato tso lɛ he hiaa tso ni ekɛkwɔ nɔ moŋ fe ni eeenyiɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam leaves act like solar panels that need maximum sunlight to make food for growing big tubers under the ground. Staking holds the leaves high into the light and keeps them off damp soil where diseases easily spread.
ga: Sweet potato baai tsuɔ nii tamɔ hulutsoo be mli tsɔnei, ni ehe miihia ni hulu la babaoo aná niyenii koni ekɛ niyenii aha bulbs ni miida yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ. Staking haa baai lɛ yaa ŋwɛi yɛ la mli, ni ehaa sũ lɛ mli ewoɔ ŋmɔtɔ, he ni helai baanyɛ agbɛ ashwã oya lɛ.

english: Why do my cassava roots rot underground when water sits on the field for too long?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi kɛ́ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ lɛ?

english: Cassava roots need air in the soil to stay alive. When water covers the ground for days, oxygen is trapped out, causing the roots to suffocate, die, and get eaten by rot-causing organisms in the wet soil.
ga: Cassava shishifãi taoɔ kɔɔyɔɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli koni amɛhi shi. beni nu ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ gbii babaoo lɛ Oxygen lɛ baatsi. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, shishifãi lɛ shwieɔ shi, amɛgboiɔ ni nibii ni wala yɔɔ amɛmli ni kɛ fitemɔ baa shikpɔŋ ni efɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ yeɔ amɛ.

english: Why are the leaves of my tomato plants curling upwards and stopping from growing bigger?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi tomato baai lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiikpa dalɛ lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is a sign of stress, usually caused by lack of water, severe heat, or viruses carried by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies. The plant curls its leaves to reduce water loss.
ga: Tomato baai ni ebɔle ehe lɛ ji haomɔ he okadi. Bei pii lɛ, nu ni faaa yɛ gbɔmɔtso lɛ mli, dɔlɛ ni naa wa, loo helai ni kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu tamɔ whiteflies lɛ hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ enɛ baa. Tsei lɛ baafolɔ amɛbaai lɛ amli koni nu ni amɛfiteɔ lɛ aba shi.

english: Weeds are wild plants that have adapted over thousands of years to survive tough local soils and weather with very little water or care. Because of this, they are much faster at grabbing nutrients and sunlight than cultivated farm crops.
ga: Jwɛi ji koo mli tsei ni etsake amɛhe yɛ afii akpei abɔ ni eho lɛ amli koni amɛhi shi yɛ he ni amɛyɔɔ lɛ shikpɔji ni wa kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi ni nu loo kwɛmɔ fioo pɛ yɔɔ mli lɛ anɔ. Enɛ hewɔ lɛ, amɛjieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ kɛ hulu la oya kwraa fe ŋmɔshi nibii ni aduɔ lɛ.

english: How do I know if my soil is good enough to support heavy crops like plantain?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ mishikpɔŋ lɛ hi bɔ ni sa ni baanyɛ akwɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii tamɔ plantain nɔ?

english: Good soil for plantains is dark, rich in decayed organic matter, retains moisture without getting waterlogged, and is deep enough for roots to spread safely.
ga: Shikpɔŋ ni hi kɛha plantains ji shikpɔŋ ni tsuɔ. Eyɛ nibii ni wala yɔɔ mli ni fiteɔ babaoo. Kwɛmɔ ni hulutsoo be lɛ ahi shi ni nu akabote mli ni mli kwɔ bɔ ni sa koni shishifãi lɛ agbɛ ashwã shweshweeshwe.

english: Why do crops yield better in some parts of Ghana compared to other regions?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmɔshi nibii woɔ yibii babaoo yɛ Ghana hei komɛi kɛ akɛto kpokpai krokomɛi ahe lɛ?

english: Ghana has distinct ecological zones with varying rainfall patterns, temperatures, and soil types, making the southern forest belt ideal for plantains and cocoa, while northern regions suit grains.
ga: Ghana yɛ shihilɛhei srɔtoi ni nugbɔ nɛɔ yɛ srɔtoi, latsaa kɛ shikpɔŋ henɔi. Enɛ haa kooi lɛ anaigbɛ hei lɛ feɔ hei ni sa kɛha dumɔwui kɛ kookoo dumɔ. yɛ be mli ni kooyigbɛ hei lɛ hi kɛha ŋmaa.

english: Why does my plantain tree fall over when the fruit bunch starts getting big?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ ŋmeii lɛ je shishi amɛdara lɛ?

english: Plantains have shallow roots that struggle to support heavy fruit bunches against strong winds, so you must prop the stem with sturdy wooden bamboo poles.
ga: Plantains lɛ shishifãi lɛ mli ekɔɔɔ. Ebɔɔ mɔdɛŋ ni efi aduawai akui ni tsii lɛ asɛɛ yɛ kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa mli, no hewɔ lɛ esa akɛ okɛ tsei ni akɛfee ŋmeii ni wa afi tso lɛ shishi.

english: How many months does it take from planting a plantain sucker to harvesting the fruit?
ga: Nyɔji enyiɛ eheɔ kɛjɛɔ plantain tsei lɛ adumɔ mli kɛyashiɔ aduawai ni akpaa lɛ nɔ?

english: A plantain sucker usually takes about 9 to 12 months to flower, and another 3 to 4 months for the fruit bunch to grow full and mature.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, plantain tsei lɛ aheɔ aaafee nyɔji 9 kɛyashi 12 dani amɛwoɔ fɔfɔi, ni amɛheɔ nyɔji 3 kɛyashi 4 krokomɛi hu dani aduawai akui lɛ shwereɔ ni amɛdaraa.

english: Why do the flowers at the end of my plantain bunch fall off without turning into fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ tso bibioo lɛ naagbee lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛtsakeee amɛfeɔ aduawai lɛ?

english: Only the first set of flowers at the top are female flowers that develop into fruit fingers; the remaining lower flowers are male and drop off naturally.
ga: Klɛŋklɛŋ fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ ŋwɛigbɛ lɛ pɛ ji fɔfɔi yei ni daa ni amɛfeɔ aduawai. Fɔfɔi ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ ni eshwɛ lɛ ji hii ni amɛgbeeɔ shi yɛ amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛhe.

english: Why do my crops slow down in growth and look weak around January?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ miŋmɔshi nii lɛ daa blɛoo ni etamɔ nɔ ni ebɛ hewalɛ yɛ January mli lɛ?

english: January is the height of the dry Harmattan season, when cold dry winds and lack of rain force plants to conserve water by dropping leaves and slowing growth.
ga: January ji be ni harmattan ni mli egbi lɛ fa fe fɛɛ. Enɛ ji be ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli ejɔ kɛ tsei ni nugbɔ nɛɔ ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛbu nu he kɛtsɔ amɛbaai ni amɛshwieɔ shi ni amɛhaa amɛdalɛ baa shi lɛ nɔ lɛ bɛ.

english: Can I plant new crops during the dry season if I water them by hand?
ga: Ani manyɛ makwɛ tsei heei yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli kɛji mikɛ minine wo amɛnɔ nu?

english: It is much safer to plant at the start of the rainy season so roots grow deep enough to survive severe dry periods later without dying.
ga: Dumɔ ni aduɔ yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ shishijee mli lɛ yɛ shweshweeshwe kwraa. No hewɔ lɛ shishifãi lɛ daa kɛyaa shɔŋŋ bɔ ni sa ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛhi shi yɛ hɔmɔ ni naa wa mli ni amɛgbooo sɛɛ mli.

english: Why do trees grown from seeds take so much longer to produce fruit than those grown from suckers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ni akɛ dumɔwui kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ heɔ be babaoo dani amɛwoɔ yibii fe tsei ni akɛ suckers kwɛ̃ɔ lɛ?

english: Seedlings go through a long juvenile phase building wood and roots before fruiting, whereas suckers are mature plant tissue that fruits much faster.
ga: Dumɔwui tsɔɔ gbekɛbiiashi be mli ni amɛdaraa tso kɛ shishifãi dani amɛwoɔ yibii. Yɛ be mli ni ŋmeii ji tso lɛ mli fãji ni eda ni woɔ yibii oya kwraa lɛ.

english: Why is my plant growing huge dark green leaves but producing very small fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mitso lɛ baai agboi ni tsuɔ waa shi ewoɔ yibii bibii waa lɛ?

english: Too much nitrogen fertilizer creates excess leaves, while plants need extra potassium and phosphorus nutrients to build large, heavy fruits.
ga: Nitrogen ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo baaha baai babaoo aba. Yɛ nakai beaŋ lɛ, tsei biɔ potassium kɛ phosphorus niyenii krokomɛi koni amɛwo yibii wuji ni tsii.

english: Where can I go in Accra or my local district to register my farm for government support?
ga: Nɛgbɛ manyɛ maya Accra loo mimaŋ kpokpaa lɛ nɔ koni miyaŋmala miŋmɔ lɛ he wolo koni nɔyeli lɛ aye abua mi?

english: You can visit the nearest Ministry of Food and Agriculture (MoFA) district office or headquarters in Accra to register your farm and get extension support.
ga: Obaanyɛ oyasara Niyenii kɛ Okwaafoi anitsumɔhe (MoFA) kpokpaa nɔ nitsumɔhe loo nitsumɔhe yitso ni bɛŋkɛ bo fe fɛɛ yɛ Accra lɛ. Koni okɛ oŋmɔ lɛ awo wolo nɔ ni onine ashɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni yaa hiɛ nɔ

english: Young cocoa seedlings have shallow roots and tender leaves that dry out easily under direct sunlight. Planting them under plantain trees provides temporary shade and keeps the soil cool and moist until the cocoa plants grow strong roots.
ga: Kakao tsei bibii lɛ shishifãi ni mli ekɔɔɔ kɛ baai bibii ni hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ gbɛ́ɔ oya. Kɛ́ adu lɛ yɛ dumɔwui lɛ ashishi lɛ, ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ aná ŋmɔlɔ be kukuoo ko, ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ afee fɛ̃i ni edɔ kɛyashi be mli ni kookoo tso lɛ baaná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Why are the leaves at the bottom of my maize plants turning yellow before the corn is ready?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmãa tso lɛ shishi lɛ feɔ ŋmɔŋ dani ŋmãa lɛ feɔ klalo lɛ?

english: Yellowing of bottom leaves usually means the soil lacks nitrogen, which is the main food maize needs to build green leaves. The plant moves nitrogen from old lower leaves to feed the new growth at the top.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai lɛ ashishigbɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Enɛ ji niyenii titri ni he hiaa ŋmãa koni ekɛ baai eŋɔli aba. Tsei tsiɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ baai momo ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ amli koni ekɛha ŋwɛi tsei heei ni eda lɛ niyenii.

english: Tomato flowers drop when the weather gets too hot or when the plants do not get enough water. Extreme heat stresses the plant, causing it to drop flowers to save energy.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli edɔ tsɔ loo kɛ́ tsei lɛ náaa nu ni fa bɔ ni sa. Dɔlɛ ni naa wa waa kɛ haomɔ baa tsei anɔ. Enɛ haa fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi koni ekɛ hewalɛ akafite.

english: Why are my cassava roots rotting in the soil when heavy rains come?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmeii shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: When water sits in the field for too long, the soil gets waterlogged and leaves no air for the roots to breathe. This causes fungi to grow and rot the cassava tubers underground.
ga: Kɛ nu hi ŋmɔ lɛ mli be kakadaŋŋ tsɔ Shikpɔŋ lɛ baafee nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ bɛ ni shishifãi lɛ baanyɛ amu. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, ŋmeii daa ni amɛfiteɔ ŋmeii shishifãi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ shishi lɛ.

english: Why is it bad to throw fertilizer right against the stem of my maize plant?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ mikɛ ŋmɔshi nibii baabɛŋkɛ mi-abele tsei lɛ ahe lɛ?

english: Fertilizer contains concentrated salts that can burn the soft stem and roots if touched directly. Applying it a few inches away from the stem allows the roots to safely drink the nutrients without damaging the plant.
ga: Nɔ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ ji ŋmeii ni mli eyi obɔ ni baanyɛ ashã tsei bibii kɛ shishifãi kɛji akɛ amɛshɛ he tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ akɛtsu nii yɛ he ko ni kɛ tso lɛ teŋ jɛkɛmɔ ji inchi fioo ko pɛ lɛ, ebaaye ebua shishifãi lɛ ni amɛnu niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ ni amɛfiteee tso lɛ shweshweeshwe.

english: Why shouldn't I spray pest chemicals on my vegetables during the hot afternoon sun?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ esaaa akɛ mikɛ tsofai ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ mi-vegetables lɛ anɔ yɛ shwane hulu ni tsoɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Spraying in hot sun causes the liquid chemical to evaporate into the air before it can destroy the pests. Strong heat combined with the chemical can also scorch and burn your crop leaves.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ tsofai ni mli edɔ lɛ shwie nɔ lɛ, ehaa tsofai ni ji nu lɛ shwieɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli dani enyɛɔ ekpãtãa tsɛŋemɔ helai lɛ ahiɛ. Dɔlɛ ni akɛ tsofai fataa he lɛ baanyɛ ashã ni eshã tsei ahe baai.

english: How do weeds actually reduce the size of my cassava yield if I leave them in the field?
ga: Te jwɛi baafee tɛŋŋ aha mi-cassava ŋmɔshi nibii lɛ aba shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ yɛ ŋmɔ mli?

english: Weeds compete with your cassava for water, plant food, and sunlight in the soil. When weeds take those resources, the cassava plant doesn't have enough energy to develop big tubers.
ga: Jwɛi kɛ ŋmei yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná nu, tsei aniyenii, kɛ hulu la yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛ jwɛi ye nakai nibii lɛ, Cassava tsei lɛ bɛ hewalɛ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni amɛkɛbaafee ŋmeii wuji kɛkɛ.

english: If too many small shoots grow around one main plantain tree, they all steal nutrients from each other, resulting in small plantain bunches. Pruning extra shoots ensures the main stem gets enough food to produce big fruit.
ga: Kɛji ŋmeii bibii kwɛ̃ yɛ dumɔwu titri kome he lɛ, Amɛbaaju niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii kɛjɛ amɛhe. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji niji bibii Nibii ni afolɔ ashwie shi krokomɛi ni akɛfataa he lɛ baaha tso titri lɛ aná niyenii ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha ewo yibii wuji.

english: What causes tiny holes and green dirt in the center leaves of my young corn plants?
ga: Mɛni kɛ buji bibii lɛ baa? Kɛ muji eŋɔli ni yɔɔ mi-abele tsei bibii lɛ ateŋ baai lɛ anɔ lɛ

english: This damage is caused by caterpillars like Fall Armyworms that crawl into the central leaves of the corn to feed on tender growth. The green dirt is the waste left behind by the worm.
ga: Nɔ ni kɛ nɛkɛ fitemɔ nɛɛ baa ji ŋmeii tamɔ Fall Armyworms ni shwieɔ ŋmeii ni yɔɔ teŋgbɛ lɛ amli koni amɛye ŋmeii ni shwereɔ lɛ. Muji eŋɔli ji jwɛi ni ŋmeii shĩɔ yɛ amɛsɛɛ.

english: How do I know when my maize is dry enough on the field to harvest safely?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male be mli ni mi-ŋma lɛ egbi bɔ ni sa ni manyɛ makpa shweshweeshwe?

english: Maize is ready for harvest when the outer husks turn completely brown and dry, and the grains become hard enough that your thumbnail cannot make an indentation in them.
ga: Abele lɛ efee klalo kɛha kpamɔ beni kponɔgbɛ ŋmɔtɔ lɛ batsɔ ŋmɔtɔ kwraa ni egbi lɛ. Ni dumɔwui lɛ mli wa bɔ ni sa akɛ otsitsii bibii lɛ nyɛŋ afee ŋmeii.

english: Why does my harvested rice end up with so many small stones and dirt mixed in it?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mikpamɔ lɛ hiɛ tɛi bibii lɛ? Ni muji babaoo efutu mli?

english: When rice is dried directly on the bare ground or threshed on soil, small rocks and dirt mix with the grains. Using clean tarpaulins for drying and processing the rice through de-stoning machines helps separate these hard objects, making the rice clean and easy to cook.
ga: Beni agbiɔ ŋmãa lɛ tɛ̃ɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ bɛ nɔ loo ashwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Tɛi bibii kɛ muji baafutu ŋmaa lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ tarpaulin ni he tse tsu nii ni akɛgbala ŋmãa lɛ ni akɛ tɛ ni akɛgbalaa ŋmãa lɛ tsu nii lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni agbala nibii ni wa nɛɛ amli. Ehaa ŋmãa he tseɔ ni ehoomɔ waaa

english: What causes my rice grains to break into small pieces when they are processed?
ga: Mɛni haa mi-rice ŋmeii lɛ fãa bibii bibii kɛ́ atsu he nii?

english: Rice grains break easily if they are harvested too late when they are overly dry, or if they are dried too fast under scorching heat. Harvesting at the right moisture level and drying the paddy gradually in the shade keeps the grains whole and strong during processing.
ga: Omɔ ŋmeii lɛ fãa oya kɛji akɛ akpa amɛ sɛɛ tsɔ beni amɛgbi tsɔ lɛ. aloo kɛji egbi oya tsɔ yɛ la ni tsoɔ waa lɛ shishi Kpamɔ yɛ hulutsoo be ni sa mli kɛ fiofio. Kɛ́ agbi ŋmãa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ŋmãa lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ ni ehe awa yɛ be mli ni atsuɔ he nii lɛ.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are hungry for nitrogen, which is a key nutrient they need to grow strong green leaves. Applying the right amount of NPK or urea fertilizer around the roots gives the plants the food they need to stay green.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen he miihia o-corn tsei lɛ. Enɛ ji niyenii ni he hiaa ni he hiaa amɛ koni amɛná baai ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ. NPK ŋmɔshi nibii loo urea ni sa ni akɛwoɔ tso lɛ he Shishifãi lɛ haa tso lɛ niyenii ni he hiaa lɛ koni ehi shi eŋɔli.

english: Why do my tomato leaves curl up and turn yellow during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔŋ yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in tomatoes is often caused by tiny sap-sucking insects like whiteflies that spread plant viruses, or by severe water stress. Protecting young plants with nursery netting and maintaining steady soil moisture keeps the leaves healthy.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii ni nuɔ nu, tamɔ whiteflies, ni gbɛɔ helai ni baa tsei amli lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ tomato baai lɛ shwieɔ shi. aloo kɛjɛ nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa mli Tsei bibii ahe ni akɛ ŋshɔŋlooi ni akɛwoɔ ŋshɔŋ lɛ buɔ he kɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni ahiɔ shi daa lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ebaa lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ.

english: Why do my sweet pepper fruits get black rotten spots at the bottom before they ripen?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-bell peppers lɛ shishigbɛ ŋmeii diji ni fiteɔ dani amɛshwereɔ lɛ?

english: Black spots at the bottom of pepper fruits, called blossom-end rot, happen when the plant cannot take up enough calcium due to irregular watering. Keeping the soil evenly moist helps the plant carry calcium to developing fruits.
ga: Nibii ni yɔɔ diŋ yɛ pepper aduawai lɛ shishi Atsɛɔ lɛ blossom end rot. Ebaa kɛji tsei nyɛɛɛ ana calcium ni fa bɔ ni sa yɛ nu ni akɛhaa amɛ daa lɛ hewɔ. Kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkɛ calcium tsuɔ nii koni amɛwo yibii.

english: Why do my cassava plants grow very tall stems with big leaves but give me thin, small tubers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava lɛ yɛ ŋmeii ni kɛlɛ waa kɛ baai wuji shi ŋmeii bibii ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ?

english: When cassava gets too much nitrogen from soil or heavy fertilizers, it spends all its energy building tall stems and leafy foliage instead of storing food in its roots. Balancing the soil nutrients helps the plant feed the underground tubers.
ga: Beni ŋmei náa nitrogen babaoo kɛjɛɔ sũ loo ŋmɔshi nibii ni tsii mli. Ekɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ tsuɔ nii ni ekɛmaa tsei ashishifãi kakadaji kɛ tsei ahe tsei ni yɔɔ baai yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni ekɛ niyenii baato shishifãi lɛ amli. Niyenii mli nibii ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ ni akɛtoɔ he lɛ yeɔ ebuaa tsei ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ ŋmeii yɛ shikpɔŋ shishi.

english: Why do my rice stalks fall over and lay flat on the muddy ground right before harvest?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ŋmãa tsei shwieɔ shikpɔŋ ni mli ewo muji nɔ dani akpaa ŋmãa lɛ?

english: Rice stalks bend and fall over, known as lodging, when they are planted too close together, receive too much nitrogen, or face strong winds. Spacing your plants properly and using sturdy varieties keeps the rice standing tall until harvest.
ga: Omɔ tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi ni amɛgbeeɔ shi, ni ale lɛ hu akɛ lodging. Kɛji adu yɛ he ko ni bɛŋkɛ he tsɔ Nitrogen babaoo ni anáa loo kɔɔyɔɔ ni naa wa ni akɛkpeɔ Tsei lɛ ateŋ jɛkɛmɔ ni sa kɛ henɔi ni wa ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ŋmãa ni edamɔ shi kɛyashiɔ kpamɔ.

english: Why do my cocoa flowers drop off without turning into actual cocoa pods?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kokoo fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi ni etsɔɔɔ kookoo ŋmɔtɔi diɛŋtsɛ lɛ?

english: Cocoa flowers fall off when there are not enough beneficial insects like tiny midges to pollinate them, or when the tree is stressed by excessive shade or drought. Managing farm shade and avoiding harsh sprays during flowering helps flowers set pods.
ga: Cocoa fɔfɔii lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛ́ kooloi ni he yɔɔ sɛɛnamɔ ni fa bɔ ni sa ni baaha amɛwo fɔfɔi lɛ bɛ. aloo be mli ni hulu la loo hɔmɔ babaoo shɛɔ tso lɛ nɔ. Kɛ́ akwɛɔ hulutsoo nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ lɛ mli, ni ajieɔ tsofa ni akɛshwieɔ shi waa yɛ fɔfɔii akwɛmɔ be mli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛtoɔ amɛ ŋmeii lɛ ahe gbɛjianɔ.

english: Why do my stored cowpea bean seeds develop small holes and turn into powder inside the sack?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cowpea dumɔwui ni mikɛto lɛ yɛ bu bibii lɛ? ni etsɔ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ kotoku mli

english: Tiny insects called grain weevils lay eggs inside the seeds before or during harvest, and their young eat the grain from the inside out while in storage. Thoroughly drying seeds and storing them in airtight hermetic bags suffocates these pests without using dangerous chemicals.
ga: Kplukai bibii ni atsɛɔ amɛ seed moths lɛ woɔ amɛwui yɛ dumɔwui amli dani akpaa loo yɛ kpamɔ be lɛ mli. Ni amɛbii lɛ yeɔ dumɔwui lɛ kɛjɛɔ mli kɛyaa kponɔgbɛ yɛ be mli ni akɛtoɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ agbi dumɔwui lɛ jogbaŋŋ ni akɛto kotokui ni kɔɔyɔɔ nyɛŋ abote mli lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa nɛkɛ kooloi nɛɛ shwieɔ shi ni akɛ tsofai ni yeɔ mɔ awui tsuuu nii.

english: Why does seed saved from my previous maize harvest yield much less grain than certified seed from the store?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ mi ŋmãa ni mikpa tsutsu lɛ mli lɛ woɔ dumɔwui fioo kwraa fe dumɔwui ni shwapoi lɛ kpɛlɛɔ nɔ lɛ?

english: Many modern certified seeds are hybrid varieties designed to give high yields only in their first generation. Seeds saved from that harvest lose their special vigor in the next season, resulting in smaller cobs and uneven plant growth.
ga: Ŋmɛnɛŋmɛnɛ beaŋ dumɔwui babaoo ni awo he odase lɛ ji dumɔwui ni afee amɛ koni amɛwo yibii babaoo yɛ klɛŋklɛŋ yinɔ lɛ pɛ mli. Dumɔwui ni abua naa kɛjɛɔ nakai kpamɔ lɛ mli lɛ fiteɔ amɛhewalɛ kroko yɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ mli. Enɛ haa dumɔwui bibii kɛ tsei adalɛ ni ejaaa baa.

english: How do I know if the chemicals I spray on my crops will make the food unsafe to eat?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male kɛji tsofai ni mikɛshwieɔ miŋmɔshi nibii anɔ lɛ baaha niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni esaaa akɛ ayeɔ?

english: Every farm chemical has a pre-harvest interval, which is the required number of days you must wait between spraying and harvesting. Waiting for this safety period allows the chemical to break down completely so the food is safe for consumption.
ga: Tsofa fɛɛ tsofa ni akɛtsuɔ nii yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ yɛ be ni akɛkpaa nii. Enɛ ji gbii abɔ ni esa akɛ omɛ yɛ shwiemɔ kɛ ŋmaakpamɔ teŋ. Be ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe nɛɛ ni mɛɔ lɛ haa tsofai lɛ fiteɔ kɛyashiɔ niyenii lɛ feɔ nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ.

english: Why does my harvested maize develop mold in storage, and is it dangerous to eat?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-ŋmãa ni mikpaa lɛ yɛ ŋmɔtɔ yɛ nitoohe lɛ? Ni ani eyɛ oshara kɛji akɛ aye?

english: Mold grows when grain is bagged while still holding moisture. This mold creates hidden poisons called toxins that make the food unsafe to eat, so maize must be dried thoroughly under the sun until it is hard before storage.
ga: Mold daa kɛji akɛ akɛ ŋmaa wo kotoku mli be mli ni edɔ lolo. Nɛkɛ ŋmɔtɔ nɛɛ feɔ tsofai fɔji ni yɔɔ teemɔŋ ni atsɛɔ amɛ tsofai fɔji. Enɛ haaa niyenii lɛ afee nɔ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni ayeɔ. No hewɔ lɛ, esa akɛ agbi ŋmãa yɛ hulu mli kɛyashi ebaawa dani akɛto.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean your maize plants are lacking nitrogen nutrients in the soil or are sitting in waterlogged ground. Adding balanced fertilizer or improving drainage helps the leaves regain their green color and support strong growth.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ o-corn tsei lɛ bɛ nitrogen niyenii yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli loo amɛta hei ni nu eyi mli obɔ lɛ. Kɛ́ akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni ja fata he loo aha nu ni hoɔ lɛ aya hiɛ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua baai lɛ ni amɛku amɛsɛɛ amɛba amɛsu ni ji eŋɔli lɛ mli ekoŋŋ, ni eha amɛdara jogbaŋŋ.

english: Leaf curling is often caused by tiny insects like aphids or mites sucking sap from the underside of leaves. Spraying early with neem oil or recommended insecticides stops the insects and allows new leaves to expand normally.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi bibii tamɔ aphids loo mites ni nuɔ nu ni jɛɔ baai lɛ ashishi lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛ baa lɛ shwieɔ shi. Akɛ neem fɔ loo tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi lɛ shwieɔ nɔ mra. Ehaa kooloi bibii lɛ kpaa gbee ni ehaa baai heei lɛ shwereɔ bɔ ni sa.

english: Why do my cocoa leaves droop and dry up during the hot dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Cocoa plants droop in severe sun to reduce water loss from hot winds. Planting fast-growing shade trees like plantains alongside cocoa provides canopy shelter and retains soil moisture during dry spells.
ga: Cocoa tsei tsiɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu ni mli edɔ lɛ he koni nu ni kɔɔyɔɔ ni mli edɔ lɛ fiteɔ lɛ aba shi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ oya tamɔ tsei bibii yɛ kookoo masɛi lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni hulutsoo be lɛ aya hiɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ ŋmɔtɔ ahi shi yɛ nugbɔshiimɔ be lɛ mli.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures are too high or when plants experience water stress. Keeping the soil evenly moist with mulch helps cool the root zone so flowers can set fruit.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ tso lɛ na nu he haomɔ. Kɛ́ akɛ mulch ha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ edɔ daa lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shishifãi lɛ feɔ fɛ̃i bɔni afee ni fɔfɔi lɛ awo yibii.

english: Cassava roots rot when water collects around them in heavy soils, allowing soil diseases to attack. Planting cassava on raised soil mounds or ridges lets extra rainwater drain away so the roots stay healthy.
ga: Cassava shishifãi lɛ fiteɔ kɛji nu bua ehe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ ni tsii lɛ nɔ. Ebaanyɛ ekɛ hela aba shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kasava ni aduɔ yɛ gɔŋ loo ŋshɔkpɔ ni nɔ kwɔ nɔ lɛ haa nugbɔ nu ni fa fe nine lɛ hoɔ kɛyaa. Koni shishifãi lɛ ahi shi jogbaŋŋ

english: Can putting too much fertilizer on my crops actually burn or kill them?
ga: Ani ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo ni mikɛwoɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ baanyɛ ashã loo egbe amɛ?

english: Yes, excessive chemical fertilizer acts like salt and draws water out of plant roots, causing the leaves to scorch and dry up. Always measure fertilizers carefully and keep them a short distance away from plant stems.
ga: No ji anɔkwale, tsofa ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli babaoo lɛ tsuɔ nii tamɔ ŋoo ni egbalaa nu kɛjɛɔ tsei shishifãi amli. Ehaa baai lɛ shãa ni amɛgbiɔ. Susumɔ ŋmɔshi nibii jogbaŋŋ be fɛɛ be ni okɛto tsei ashishifãi ahe.

english: How does clearing weeds away from my crops actually help them produce a better harvest?
ga: Mɛɛ gbɛ nɔ jwɛi ni mijieɔ kɛjɛɔ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mitsei lɛ diɛŋtsɛ ni amɛkpaa nii jogbaŋŋ?

english: Weeds steal sunlight, water, and soil nutrients directly from your crops. Removing them gives your crops full access to food and light, which makes the farm look healthy and significantly improves crop yields.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ juɔ hulu la, nu, kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ niyenii kɛjɛɔ onibii amli tɛ̃ɛ. Kɛ́ ojie amɛ lɛ, ehaa oŋmɔshi nibii lɛ náa niyenii kɛ la kwraa. Enɛ haa ŋmɔ lɛ feɔ tamɔ nɔ ni eyɛ hewalɛ, ni ehaa ŋmɔshi nibii ni anáa lɛ yaa hiɛ waa.

english: Why do some seeds fail to sprout after I plant them in the soil?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ dumɔwui komɛi kwɛɛɛ beni midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Seeds fail to germinate if buried too deeply, if the soil dries out completely, or if soil insects attack them. Planting seeds at a shallow depth equal to twice their size in moist soil ensures quick sprouting.
ga: Dumɔwui lɛ ekwɛ̃ŋ kɛji akɛ afu amɛ tsɔ, shikpɔŋ lɛ mli egbi kwraa, loo shikpɔŋ nɔ kooloi tutua dumɔwui lɛ. Dumɔwui ni aduɔ yɛ he ko ni mli ekɔɔɔ ni kɛ amɛdalɛ toi enyɔ yeɔ egbɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli efɔ nɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa amɛ ni amɛkwɛ̃ɔ oya.

english: Yellow leaves usually mean the soil is low in nitrogen, which is the main food plants need to stay green and grow strong. It can also happen when heavy rain washes nutrients away or leaves the ground too waterlogged for roots to breathe.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen faaa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Eji niyenii titri ni he hiaa tsei koni amɛhi shi eŋɔli ni amɛdara hewalɛ. Ebaanyɛ eba hu kɛ́ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ shwie niyenii ni haa mɔ hewalɛ loo eha shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ eyi kɛ nu tsɔ ni shishifãi lɛ nyɛɛɛ amu.

english: Why do my pepper plants grow large green leaves but fail to produce fruits?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ yɛ baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji shi ebɛ yibii lɛ?

english: Giving plants too much nitrogen fertilizer makes them spend all their energy growing tall and leaf-rich. To get fruits, plants need less nitrogen and more phosphorus and potassium, which encourage flowers and fruit to form.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen babaoo ha tsei lɛ, ebaaha tso lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekwɛ̃ ni ehiɛ baai babaoo. koni ená aduawai Tsei he miihia nitrogen fioo kɛ fɔsfɔs kɛ potasium babaoo. ni kanyaa fɔfɔii kɛ aduawai

english: Rolling leaves is a plant's natural defense against heat. By curling up, the leaves hide from direct sunlight so they do not lose too much water through evaporation during the hottest part of the afternoon.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi lɛ ji tso adebɔɔ mli hebuu kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he. Kɛtsɔ ŋmɔlɔ nɔ lɛ, baai lɛ teɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ he. Enɛ ji koni nu babaoo akafite kɛtsɔ la ni shwieɔ shi lɛ nɔ yɛ shwane ŋmɛlɛtswai ni mli edɔ waa lɛ amli.

english: Why do my tomato flowers fall off before turning into fruits when the heat gets very strong?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi dani amɛfeɔ aduawai kɛ́ hulutsoo be ni naa wa ba lɛ?

english: Extremely high temperatures kill the pollen inside tomato flowers, preventing pollination. When a flower isn't pollinated, the plant drops it to save water and energy for its own survival.
ga: Dɔlɛ ni mli wa waa lɛ gbeɔ pollen ni yɔɔ tomato fɔfɔi lɛ amli lɛ. Bɔni afee ni akafee pollination Beni pollination bɛ fɔfɔii amli lɛ Tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛto nu kɛ hewalɛ he kɛha amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala.

english: Why do the pods on my cocoa trees turn black and rot during the wet rainy season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo ŋmeii lɛ feɔ ediŋŋ ni amɛgboiɔ yɛ nugbɔ be mli lɛ?

english: This is caused by Black Pod disease, a fungus that spreads rapidly when rain wetness stays on pods and high humidity keeps the air cool and damp. Pruning branches to let sun and air in helps prevent it.
ga: Black pod hela lɛ kɛ enɛ baa. Enɛ ji ŋmei ko ni gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛ́ nugbɔ nɛ ni ekɛ ŋmeii lɛ shwie ŋmeii lɛ anɔ. ni hulutsoo ni fa babaoo lɛ haa kɔɔyɔɔ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa hulutsoo baa. Kɛ́ afolɔ tso lɛ mli koni hulu la kɛ kɔɔyɔɔ abote mli lɛ, ebaanyɛ eye ebua ni ebu he.

english: Why are the leaves on my cassava plants twisting up and showing yellowish patches?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi yucca tso lɛ nɔ lɛ etsɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ ni eyɛ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ lɛ?

english: This is Cassava Mosaic Disease, caused by a virus carried by tiny insects called whiteflies. Planting healthy, disease-free stems and pulling up infected young plants stops the disease from spreading across your farm.
ga: Hela nɛɛ ji ŋmei mosaic hela. Virus ko ni kooloi bibii hiɛɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni kɛbaa. ni atsɛɔ lɛ whitefly Aduɔ tsei ni he wa ni hela bɛ mli ni ajieɔ dumɔwui ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Enɛ baaye abua ni helai akagbɛ ashwã oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why is it recommended that I plant cowpeas or groundnuts on the farm where I grew maize last season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ atsɔɔ akɛ midu tsina loo ŋmeii yɛ ŋmɔ ni midu ŋmã yɛ mli yɛ afi ni eho lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Maize takes a lot of food out of the soil. Legumes like cowpeas and groundnuts pull nitrogen from the air and put it back into the ground, naturally restoring soil fertility for the next planting season.
ga: Abele heɔ eniyenii babaoo kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. Legumes tamɔ cowpeas kɛ peanuts lɛ jieɔ nitrogen kɛjɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli ni amɛkɛkuɔ amɛsɛɛ amɛyaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Koni ekɛ adebɔɔ mli shikpɔŋ lɛ aba ekoŋŋ kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni yaa hiɛ lɛ be ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ

english: Yams need loose, soft soil to expand easily. If the ground is hard, clay-heavy, or filled with rocks, the tubers struggle to push downward, resulting in stunted and misshapen yams.
ga: Sweet potatoes he miihia shikpɔŋ ni mli tse, ni yɔɔ bɔdɔɔ koni egbɛ eshwa mlɛo. Kɛji shikpɔŋ lɛ ji shikpɔŋ ni wa ni tsii loo tɛi eyi mli obɔ lɛ Yitso lɛ baabɔ mɔdɛŋ ni eshɛ shi. Enɛ haa sweet potatoes lɛ shwieɔ shi ni efiteɔ.

english: Why do weeds harm my crops so much even when there is plenty of rain for all plants?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ jwɛi miiye miŋmɔshi nibii awui waa eyɛ mli akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii fɛɛ naa nugbɔ babaoo moŋ?

english: Weeds grow faster and have stronger roots than crops. They steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients directly from your plants, leaving your crops weak and reducing your total yield.
ga: Jwɛi lɛ daa oya ni amɛshishifãi lɛ wa fe ŋmɔshi nibii. Amɛjuɔ nu, hulu la, kɛ shikpɔŋ mli niyenii kɛjɛɔ otsei lɛ amli tɛ̃ɛ. Ehaa onibii lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa onibii fɛɛ ni onáa lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do my harvested onions start rotting so quickly after I bring them home from the field?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-onions ni mikpaa lɛ jeɔ shishi egboɔ oya nɛkɛ beni mikɛ amɛ jɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛba lɛ?

english: Onions rot easily if they are harvested while damp or stored before their outer skins dry completely. Leaving harvested onions under a shady, airy shelter to cure for a few days hardens their skin and preserves them longer.
ga: Sabalai fiteɔ oya kɛji akɛ akpa be mli ni edɔ loo akɛto dani kponɔgbɛ fã lɛ egbi kwraa. Kɛ́ ashi ŋmeii ni akpa lɛ yɛ hulutsoo kɛ la shishi koni etsa gbii fioo komɛi lɛ, ebaaha ŋmeii lɛ ahewolo lɛ mli awa ni ebaahi shi be kakadaŋŋ.

english: Why do government agriculture officers take leaf and soil samples from my farm to test in a laboratory?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ nɔyeli okwaayeli he nitsulɔi lɛ miihe baai kɛ shikpɔŋ nɔ nibii kɛjɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli koni amɛka amɛ akwɛ yɛ laboratori lɛ?

english: Testing samples in a laboratory helps officers identify the exact pest, disease, or nutrient shortage affecting your crops using special equipment so they can recommend the precise treatment instead of guessing.
ga: Nɔkwɛmɔnii ni aka amɛ akwɛ yɛ Lab mli lɛ yeɔ ebuaa mɛi ni tsuɔ he nii lɛ ni amɛyooɔ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui, helai, loo niyenii mli hewalɛ ni faaa ni saa onibii ahe kɛtsɔ nibii krɛdɛɛi anɔ. Bɔni afee ni amɛtsɔɔ gbɛi pɔtɛɛ ni atsɔɔ nɔ atsaa mɔ lɛ moŋ fe ni amɛaasusu he.

english: What should I do if my crops show strange symptoms like yellow leaves or swollen stems that I have never seen before?
ga: Mɛni esa akɛ mafee kɛji akɛ mitso lɛ miitsɔɔ okadii ni yɔɔ naakpɛɛ, tamɔ baai ni miifee ŋmɔŋ loo eshishifãi ni efuu ni minako dã?

english: When you notice unfamiliar crop symptoms, avoid applying random chemicals immediately; report it to an extension officer so they can inspect the plants, take samples, and run tests to diagnose the actual disease.
ga: Kɛji ona tso he okadii ni oleee lɛ Tsi ohe kɛjɛ tsofai ni akɛtsuɔ nii trukaa lɛ ahe amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Abɔ amaniɛ aha extension officers lɛ koni amɛkwɛ tsei lɛ amli, amɛbua nɔkwɛmɔnii anaa, ni amɛfee kaai koni amɛna hela diɛŋtsɛ.

english: How can I tell if the crop medicine or chemical I bought for my farm is real and safe to use?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male akɛ ŋmɔshi nibii loo tsofai ni miheɔ kɛhaa miŋmɔ lɛ ji nɔ ni yɔɔ diɛŋtsɛ ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe?

english: Genuine crop medicines have verified chemical formulas and proper labeling; agricultural officers can inspect or test chemical samples to help you confirm whether a product is authentic and safe for your crops.
ga: Akwɛ ŋmɔshi tsofai diɛŋtsɛ amli kɛha tsofa fɔmulai ni ja kɛ okadii. Okwaafoi anitsumɔ he nitsulɔi baanyɛ akwɛ loo amɛka tsofai ni akɛwoɔ mli lɛ amɛkwɛ koni eye ebua bo ni ona nɔmimaa akɛ nɔ ko ji anɔkwale ni ehi kɛha oŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Is it safe for me to mix two different crop medicines together when spraying my farm?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ mikɛ tsei ahe tsofai enyɔ baafutu beni mikɛ tsofai shwieɔ miŋmɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Combining different crop medicines without scientific advice can damage your plants or reduce the chemicals' power; you should consult an extension officer to learn which treatments work safely together.
ga: Kɛ́ okɛ ŋmɔshi nibii babaoo tsu nii yɛ he kome ni jeŋ nilee ŋaawoo bɛ he lɛ, ebaanyɛ efite otsei lɛ loo eha tsofai lɛ ahe nitsumɔ aba shi. Esa akɛ okɛ extension nitsulɔ ko agba sane koni ole tsofafeemɔi ni yɔɔ shweshweeshwe ni okɛbaatsu nii.

english: Why do my crops sometimes look weak or wilted right after I apply chemical medicine to them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ bei komɛi lɛ, kɛ́ mikɛ tsofai etsu nii yɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ, etamɔ nɔ ni egbɔjɔ loo egbo amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ?

english: Crops can suffer temporary shock or stress if the medicine dose is too high or applied incorrectly, which is why following exact scientific measurement guidance is necessary to protect plant health.
ga: Tsei baanyɛ ana be kukuoo mli shoofeemɔ loo haomɔ kɛji akɛ tsofa lɛ fa tsɔ loo akɛtsu nii yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ. Enɛ hewɔ ni gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni ja, ni kɔɔ jeŋ nilee he ni akɛsusuɔ nii ahe lɛ sɛɛnyiɛmɔ he hiaa koni abu tsei ahewalɛ he lɛ.

english: Why do some crop diseases require long-term solutions instead of disappearing immediately after spraying chemical medicine?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai komɛi biɔ ni atsa amɛ be kakadaŋŋ yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni amɛbaafite amrɔ nɔŋŋ kɛji akɛ akɛ tsofai eshwie nɔ lɛ?

english: Chemical sprays usually kill surface pests quickly, but deep plant diseases or viruses stay inside the crop's system and require long-term strategies like breeding disease-resistant plant varieties to fully solve.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, tsofai ni akɛshwieɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ gbeɔ kooloi ni yɔɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ oya. Shi tsei ahe helai loo helai ni mli kwɔ lɛ kã ŋmɔshi nibii ahe gbɛjianɔtoo lɛ mli. Ni esa akɛ akɛ gbɛi ni heɔ be kakadaŋŋ atsu nii, tamɔ tsei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ amɛhe lɛ afɔmɔ. Koni akɛtsu naagba lɛ he nii kwraa

english: Why does it take several years for researchers to bring us new disease-resistant crop varieties?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eheɔ niiamlitaolɔi afii babaoo dani amɛkɛ tsei srɔtoi heei ni helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ lɛ aba wɔŋɔɔ lɛ?

english: Developing resistant crop seeds or seedlings requires continuous research, field trials, and laboratory verification over multiple seasons to ensure the new plants can survive local conditions and yield well before release.
ga: Dumɔwui loo dumɔwui ni nyɛɔ hela lɛ afeemɔ biɔ niiamlitaomɔ ni yaa nɔ. ŋmɔ mli kaa kɛ laboratori mlikwɛmɔ yɛ bei babaoo mli koni ana nɔmimaa akɛ tsei heei baanyɛ ahi shi yɛ shihilɛi ni yɔɔ jɛmɛ lɛ amli ni amɛwo yibii jogbaŋŋ dani ajie amɛ kpo.

english: Why is it important for me to report early signs of crop sickness before my whole farm gets infected?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ ehe hiaa ni mabɔ ŋmɔshi nibii amli hela he okadii lɛ ahe amaniɛ mra dani ŋmɔ muu lɛ fɛɛ aná hela lɛ?

english: Catching plant sickness early allows extension officers to run tests and isolate the problem quickly, saving you money and preventing the infection from spreading across your entire farm.
ga: Ni aaamɔ tsei ahe helai mra Enɛ haa mɛi ni tsuɔ nii yɛ sɛɛgbɛ lɛ kaa naagbai lɛ amɛkwɛɔ oya ni amɛjieɔ amɛhe kɛjɛɔ he. Ehaa okɛ shika baa shi ni ehaa helai ni gbeɔ mɔ lɛ gbɛɔ eshwaa oŋmɔ lɛ mli fɛɛ.

english: Why does crop sickness spread so quickly from my neighbor's field to my own crops?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tsei ahe helai gbɛɔ eshwaa oya kɛjɛɔ mikutsoŋnyo lɛ ŋmɔ mli kɛyaa mi diɛŋtsɛ miŋmɔshi nibii amli lɛ?

english: Many crop diseases spread through wind, rain splash, insects, or shared farm tools, meaning unmanaged sickness on one farm can easily travel to surrounding fields if not tested and treated early.
ga: Tsei ahe helai babaoo gbɛɔ eshwaa kɛtsɔɔ kɔɔyɔɔ, nugbɔ ni nɛɔ, kooloi bibii, loo okwaayeli nibii ni akɛhaa lɛ nɔ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ helai ni akwɛɛɛ nɔ yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli lɛ baanyɛ aya ŋmɔji ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ amli mlɛo kɛji akɛ aka amɛ akwɛ ni atsaaa amɛ mra.

english: How do government agricultural research officers help smallholder farmers protect their harvest?
ga: Te nɔyeli lɛ okwaayeli he niiamlitaolɔi yeɔ amɛbuaa okwaafoi bibii lɛ koni amɛbu amɛŋmɔshi nibii ahe amɛha tɛŋŋ?

english: Research officers study plant behaviors, test farm inputs for authenticity, and create scientifically proven pest and disease solutions that guide extension workers in helping farmers maintain high yields.
ga: Nibii amlipɛimɔ nitsulɔi kaseɔ tsei subaŋ Kaa ŋmɔ mli nibii ni afeɔ lɛ okwɛɔ kɛji eja. ni amɛfee tsabaai ni jeŋ nilee etsɔɔ mli kɛha helai kɛ kooloi ni yeɔ mɔ awui lɛ ahe naagbai. Koni ekɛ gbɛtsɔɔmɔ aha extension nitsulɔi lɛ yɛ yelikɛbuamɔ ni akɛhaa okwaafoi lɛ koni amɛhiɛ ŋmɔshi nibii ni amɛwoɔ lɛ amli babaoo lɛ mli.
