english: Why are some of my cocoa trees drying up and dying?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei lɛ ekomɛi miiho ni amɛmiigboi lɛ?

english: Cocoa trees usually dry up due to severe diseases like swollen shoot virus or black pod, as well as extreme water stress or root pests. Inspecting the roots and stems helps identify the exact cause so infected trees can be managed before the problem spreads.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei lɛ shwieɔ shi yɛ helai ni mli wa tamɔ bud swelling virus loo ŋmeii ni efee diŋ lɛ ahewɔ. Nu mli haomɔ ni naa wa loo shishifãi amli tsɛŋemɔ helai fata he. Kɛ́ akwɛ tsei lɛ ashishifãi kɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ amli lɛ, eyeɔ ebuaa ni anaa nɔ ni kɛ hela lɛ baa koni anyɛ atsa tsei ni hela lɛ emɔmɔ amɛ lɛ dani naagba lɛ agbɛ ashwã.

english: Sick cocoa trees often show early warning signs such as yellowing leaves, swollen branches, unusual spots on pods, or sudden leaf drop. Checking your farm regularly helps you spot these symptoms early so you can take action.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, cacao tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ lɛ jieɔ kɔkɔbɔɔ okadii mra, tamɔ baai ni yɔɔ ŋmɔŋ, niji ni efuu, kɛ hei ni ejaaa ni yɔɔ tsei lɛ ahe lɛ akpo. loo baai lɛ shwieɔ shi trukaa Oŋmɔ lɛ mlikwɛmɔ daa baanyɛ aye abua bo ni ona okadii nɛɛ mra. no hewɔ lɛ obaanyɛ ofee he nɔ ko

english: Should I cut down a cocoa tree if it looks diseased, or will it recover on its own?
ga: Ani esa akɛ mafolɔ kookoo tso ko kɛji hela ko emɔ lɛ? Aloo ebaalaaje lɛ diɛŋtsɛ?

english: Certain serious diseases, such as cocoa swollen shoot disease, have no cure, so removing affected trees is essential to protect the rest of your farm. Leaving incurable sick trees in the field allows pests to spread the disease to healthy neighboring plants.
ga: Helai komɛi ni naa wa, tamɔ kookoo ŋmeii ni efuu lɛ, anyɛɛɛ atsa No hewɔ lɛ, tsei ni hela lɛ emɔ amɛ lɛ ni ajieɔ lɛ he hiaa koni abu oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ he. Tsei ni hela mɔ amɛ ni anyɛɛɛ atsa lɛ ni ashiɔ yɛ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa tsɛŋemɔ helai gbɛɔ eshwaa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ.

english: Can a disease spread from a dead cocoa tree to healthy ones nearby?
ga: Ani hela baanyɛ ajɛ cacao tsei ni egboi lɛ amli kɛya cacao tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni bɛŋkɛ lɛ anɔ?

english: Yes, dead or dying trees often harbor fungal spores or insects like mealybugs that can carry infection to surrounding healthy trees. Safely removing and clearing out dead plant material prevents pests from invading the rest of your farm.
ga: Hɛɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsɛŋemɔ helai loo kooloi bibii, tamɔ mealybugs, ni baanyɛ atswa tsei ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ yɛ tsei ni egboi loo ni miigboi lɛ amli. Tsoi ni egboi lɛ ni ajieɔ kɛshwieɔ shi shweshweeshwe lɛ baaye abua ni tsɛŋemɔ helai akabote oŋmɔ lɛ fã ni eshwɛ lɛ mli.

english: Is it safe to plant new cocoa seedlings in the same spot where old trees died of disease?
ga: Ani eyɛ shweshweeshwe akɛ aaadu cacao tso hee yɛ he ni cacao tso lɛ gbo yɛ hela hewɔ lɛ nɔŋŋ?

english: Replanting immediately in the exact same spot can expose new seedlings to lingering soil pests or pathogens. It is best to clear out infected roots, let the soil rest, and plant disease-resistant cocoa varieties.
ga: Kɛ́ adu ekoŋŋ yɛ he kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ amrɔ nɔŋŋ lɛ, ebaanyɛ eha dumɔwui heei lɛ aná tsɛŋemɔ helai loo helai ni baa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ. Ehi jogbaŋŋ akɛ abaajie shishifãi ni hela emɔ amɛ lɛ. Ha shikpɔŋ lɛ ajɔɔ ehe. kɛ kookoo henɔi ni tsei helai nyɛɔ amɛyeɔ.

english: What simple daily steps can I take to stop diseases from entering my cocoa farm?
ga: Ani manyɛ mafee nɔ ko ni yɔɔ mlɛo daa gbi koni helai akabote mi-kookoo ŋmɔ lɛ mli?

english: Good farm hygiene—such as clearing weeds, removing rotten pods, pruning dead wood, and cleaning your farm tools regularly—drastically reduces the chances of diseases taking root.
ga: Okwaafoi amli hetsemɔ kpakpa, tamɔ jwɛi ni ajieɔ ŋmɔ mli tsei ni egboi lɛ ajiemɔ Niji ni egboi lɛ akwɛmɔ kɛ ŋmɔ mli nibii ni akɛtsuɔ nii lɛ ahe saamɔ daa Enɛ baaha hegbɛ ni helai baanyɛ atswa shishifãi lɛ aba shi waa.

english: How can I distinguish between damage caused by insects and damage caused by a disease on my crops?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ mayɔse srɔtofeemɔ ni yɔɔ kooloi ni fiteɔ nii kɛ helai ni fiteɔ miŋmɔshi nibii lɛ ateŋ?

english: Insect damage usually leaves physical signs like chewed leaves, holes, or sticky residue, whereas plant diseases typically cause leaf discoloration, swollen stems, wilting, or rotting without clear bite marks.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kooloi ni fiteɔ nii lɛ haa gbɔmɔtsoŋ okadii, tamɔ baai ni ashɛre, bu, loo nibii ni shwieɔ shi ni shwieɔ shi lɛ shiɔ. Yɛ gbɛ kroko nɔ lɛ, bei pii lɛ, tsei ahe helai kɛ baai lɛ tsakeɔ su, amɛshishifãi lɛ efuu, amɛgboiɔ, loo amɛfiteɔ ni nɔ ko bɛ ni tsɔɔ akɛ amɛye amɛhe.

english: Why do the leaves on my young cocoa plants turn brown and drop during the dry season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ ahe baai lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshwieɔ shi yɛ hulutsoo be lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants drop leaves during dry periods to save water because their shallow roots cannot reach deep soil moisture. Planting temporary shade crops like plantains helps keep the soil cool and reduces water loss.
ga: Cacao tsei bibii lɛ shwieɔ amɛbaai lɛ shi yɛ be mli ni hulu enyɔ shi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu nu he. Nɔ hewɔ ji akɛ, shishifãi ni mli ekwɔɔɔ lɛ nyɛŋ ashɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli kwɔ lɛ he. Tsei ni haa hulutsoo be kukuoo mli tamɔ plantains ni aduɔ lɛ yeɔ ebuaa ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli jɔɔ ni ehaa nu ni fiteɔ lɛ baa shi.

english: Why do cocoa trees in very sunny parts of my farm seem to get sick faster than those under shade?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ kookoo tsei ni yɔɔ hei ni hulu tsoɔ waa yɛ yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ hela mɔ amɛ oya fe tsei ni yɔɔ hulutsoo be mli lɛ?

english: Direct, heavy sunlight puts stress on cocoa trees, weakening their natural defenses against pests and diseases. Moderate shade acts as a protective shield, maintaining soil moisture and keeping the trees healthier.
ga: Hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ kɛ haomɔ baa kookoo tsei anɔ. Ehaa adebɔɔ mli nibii ni tsiɔ mɔ he kɛjɛɔ tsɛŋemɔ helai kɛ helai ahe lɛ baa shi. Shade ni mli tse lɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ gbɛtsii nii ni buɔ mɔ he. Ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ fɛ̃ɔ ni ehaa tsei lɛ náa hewalɛ.

english: How do I know which training advice or extension teachings I should apply to my farm?
ga: Te mafee tɛŋŋ male tsɔsemɔ loo tsɔɔmɔ he ŋaawoi krokomɛi ni esa akɛ mikɛtsu nii yɛ miŋmɔ lɛ mli lɛ?

english: Agricultural extension teachings are based on proven scientific methods tested for local soil and weather conditions. Following guided recommendations on pruning, shade control, and disease management helps avoid costly trial-and-error mistakes.
ga: Okwaayeli mlilɛɛmɔ tsɔɔmɔ damɔ jeŋ nilee gbɛi ni ana he odaseyeli ni aka amɛ akwɛ kɛha maŋ lɛ mli shikpɔŋ kɛ kɔɔyɔŋ tsakemɔi anɔ. Gbɛtsɔɔmɔi ni kɔɔ ŋmɔshi nibii ahe lɛ asɛɛnyiɛmɔ Shade control Kɛ helai ahe nitsumɔ tsiɔ tɔmɔi ni jara wa ni ji kaa-kɛ-tɔmɔi lɛ anaa.

english: Why do my young cocoa leaves turn brown and burn when there are no big trees around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-kookoo baai bibii lɛ feɔ ŋmɔtɔ ni amɛshãa yɛ be mli ni tsei ni eda bɛ he lɛ?

english: Young cocoa trees are very sensitive to direct sunlight and heat. Without shade trees or plantains nearby to block the harsh sun, the delicate leaves dry out and burn before the plant can establish strong roots.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ nuɔ hulu la kɛ dɔlɛ he waa. Kɛji tsei loo tsei bibii ni haa hulu la ni naa wa lɛ bɛ jɛmɛ ni baatsi hulu la ni naa wa lɛ naa lɛ, Baai ni yɔɔ mlɛo lɛ baagbi ni amɛbaashã dani tso lɛ aná shishifãi ni wa.

english: Yellowing bottom leaves usually mean the maize plant is starving for nitrogen, an essential nutrient for growth. The plant starves its older bottom leaves to send remaining nitrogen up to the newer top leaves to survive.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, kɛ́ baai lɛ ashishi feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ, no tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ ŋmei tso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha dalɛ Tsei yeɔ shishigbɛ baai ni egbɔ lɛ hɔmɔ koni amɛkɛ nitrogen ni eshwɛ lɛ aya ŋwɛi baai heei lɛ anɔ koni amɛhi shi.

english: If I plant my cassava stick upside down by mistake, will it still produce tubers for me?
ga: Kɛji okɛ ŋmei du ŋmei yɛ oshara mli Ani ebaaha mi yitso lolo?

english: If planted upside down, cassava stems spend too much energy twisting themselves around to grow upward toward the light. This weakens the plant severely and leads to tiny roots or no usable cassava harvest at all.
ga: Kɛji akɛ adu Yucca tsei lɛ ahiɛ shi lɛ kɛ hewalɛ babaoo tsuɔ nii ni ekɛtsakeɔ ni edaa kɛyaa la mli. Enɛ baaha tso lɛ agbɔjɔ waa ni ebaaha shishifãi bibii aba loo enyɛŋ ekpa ŋmei lɛ kwraa.

english: Tomato flowers fall off when temperatures get too high or when soil goes from very dry to suddenly wet. Heat stress and water shock cause the plant to drop flowers to protect its own survival.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ baagbee shi kɛ́ hulutsoo be lɛ mli wa tsɔ loo kɛ́ shikpɔŋ lɛ tsake trukaa kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ ni egbi waa kɛtee ŋmɔtɔ mli. Dɔlɛ mli haomɔ kɛ nu tsakemɔi haa tsei shwieɔ amɛfɔfɔi lɛ koni amɛkɛbu amɛ diɛŋtsɛ amɛwala he.

english: Why do I need to put a tall wooden stick for my yam vines to climb on instead of letting them spread on the ground?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ tso kakadaŋŋ he hiaa mi lɛ? Ha sweet potato wain tso lɛ akwɔ kɛya ŋwɛi. Yɛ nɔ najiaŋ ni oooha egbɛ eshwa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ lɛ?

english: Yam vines need tall sticks so their leaves can capture maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the underground tubers. Vines left lying on the hot ground are exposed to heat diseases and produce much smaller yams.
ga: Sweet potato wain tsei lɛ ahe miihia ni amɛná niji ni kɛlɛ bɔni afee ni amɛbaai lɛ anyɛ ana hulu la babaoo bɔ ni amɛaanyɛ koni amɛná niyenii amɛha ŋmeii lɛ. Wein tsei ni ashiɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni mli edɔ lɛ nɔ lɛ baanyɛ aná dɔlɛ hela waa, ni amɛwoɔ ŋmeii bibii kwraa.

english: Why does my main plantain tree stop producing big bunches if I allow all the shoots around it to keep growing?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi dumɔwui titrii lɛ kpaɔ ŋmeii wuji kɛji miha ŋmeii ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ kwɛ̃ lɛ? Tso lɛ yaa nɔ edaa.

english: The young shoots around the base suck water, nutrients, and sunlight away from the main mother plant. Cutting away extra shoots leaves only one strong follower stem, allowing the main plant to produce heavy plantain bunches.
ga: Tso bibii ni bɔleɔ shishi lɛ shwieɔ nu, niyenii, kɛ hulu la kɛjɛɔ tso ni ji fɔlɔ lɛ he. Kɛ́ ofolɔ tsei lɛ ashishifãi ni fa fe nine lɛ, ebaashi tso kome pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ. Nɔ ni jɛɔ mli baa ji akɛ, tso titri lɛ baanyɛ awo dumɔwui babaoo.

english: How do cowpeas or groundnuts make the soil richer for the maize crop I plant after them?
ga: Te cowpeas loo peanuts feɔ tɛŋŋ ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ feɔ nɔ ni baa shi jogbaŋŋ kɛha ŋmãa ni miduɔ yɛ no sɛɛ lɛ?

english: Cowpeas and groundnuts have natural bacteria on their roots that trap nitrogen gas from the air and store it in the soil as food, which acts as a free natural fertilizer for the next crop.
ga: Cowpeas kɛ peanuts yɛ adebɔɔ mli helai ni gbeɔ mɔ yɛ amɛshishifãi lɛ anɔ. Enɛ mɔ̃ɔ nitrogen gas ni jɛɔ kɔɔyɔɔ mli lɛ ni ekɛtoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli akɛ niyenii. Enɛ tsuɔ nii akɛ adebɔɔ mli ŋmɔshi nibii ni aheee nɔ ko kɛha ŋmɔshi nibii ni nyiɛ sɛɛ lɛ.

english: Why are the leaves on my pepper plants curling upward and twisting like tiny cups?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ baai ni yɔɔ mi-pepper tso lɛ nɔ lɛ miibɔle amɛhe ni amɛmiibɔle amɛhe tamɔ kɔɔpoi bibii lɛ?

english: Leaf curling in pepper plants is a physical reaction to tiny insects like thrips or mites feeding on the underside of young leaves, causing the leaf tissue to grow unevenly and wrinkle.
ga: Baai ni shwieɔ shi yɛ pepper tsei amli lɛ ji gbɔmɔtsoŋ nifeemɔ ko ni kɔɔ kooloi bibii tamɔ thrips loo mites ni yeɔ baai bibii lɛ ashishi lɛ ahe. Enɛ haa baa lɛ mli fãji lɛ daaa yɛ gbɛ ni ejaaa nɔ ni amɛfeɔ ŋmɔlɔŋmɔlɔ.

english: Why do my vegetable leaves wilt during the hot afternoon sun even when I watered them in the morning?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ aduawai gboɔ yɛ hulu ni tsoɔ waa yɛ shwane mli lɛ mli eyɛ mli akɛ amɛgbi moŋ? Higbɛ esa akɛ awo nu yɛ leebi?

english: In intense midday heat, leaves lose water through evaporation faster than roots can pull moisture from the ground. As temperatures cool down in the evening, the plant recovers its firm structure.
ga: Yɛ shwane mli latsaa be lɛ mli lɛ, latsaa ni naa wa waa ba. Baai lɛ laajeɔ nu kɛtsɔɔ la ni hoɔ oya fe bɔ ni shishifãi baanyɛ agbala nu kɛjɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Kɛji hulutsoo be lɛ mli jɔ gbɛkɛ lɛ Tso lɛ baaná ehewalɛ ekoŋŋ.

english: Why is it bad to give my crops heavy chemical fertilizer right when they start showing flowers?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ eji jwɛŋmɔ gbonyo akɛ maha miŋmɔshi nii lɛ tsofai ni tsii kɛji amɛbɔi fɔfɔi kpojiemɔ pɛ?

english: High nitrogen fertilizer applied during flowering tricks the crop into spending its energy producing big green leaves instead of developing heavy fruits, pods, or grains.
ga: Kɛ́ akɛ nitrogen ni fa babaoo tsu nii yɛ fɔfɔii afeemɔ be mli lɛ, ebaalaka tso lɛ ni ekɛ ehewalɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo baai agboi ni yɔɔ ŋmɔji amli. Mohu ɔ, a peeɔ yiblii nɛ tsii, tso yiblii, aloo dumɔwuhi.

english: Why do my young cocoa seedlings keep dying when I plant them on fully cleared land?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cacao tsei bibii lɛ yaa nɔ amɛgboɔ kɛ́ midu amɛ yɛ shikpɔŋ ni nɔ tse kwraa nɔ lɛ?

english: Young cocoa plants need shade because intense direct sunlight burns their delicate leaves and dries out the surrounding soil. Planting shade crops like plantains or leaving canopy trees protects young cocoa from heat stress until their roots grow deeper.
ga: Kookoo tsei bibii lɛ he miihia amɛ ni amɛná hulutsoo ejaakɛ hulu la ni tsoɔ tɛ̃ɛ lɛ baashã amɛbaai bibii lɛ ni ebaaha shikpɔŋ ni ebɔle amɛhe lɛ agbi. Kɛ́ adu tsei ni haa hulu tsoɔ tamɔ plantains loo ashiɔ ŋshɔ lɛ mli lɛ, ebaaye ebua ni ebu kookoo bibii lɛ ahe kɛjɛ dɔlɛ he haomɔ he kɛyashi shishifãi lɛ baashɛ shi.

english: These are likely Fall Armyworms, a common pest in Ghana that targets the growing center (funnel) of maize plants. They feed on young leaves, which weakens the plant and reduces harvest if left untreated with appropriate pesticides or natural controls early.
ga: Ekolɛ enɛɛmɛi ji Fall Armyworms, ni ji tsɛŋemɔ hela ko ni afɔɔ namɔ yɛ Ghana ni ekɛ ehiɛ fɔ̃ɔ ŋmãa tsei lɛ adalɛ hei (gbɛi) lɛ anɔ. Amɛyeɔ baai bibii, ni no haa tsei lɛ gbɔjɔɔ ni ehaa ŋmaa lɛ baa shi kɛji akɛ ashi amɛ ni tsofa ni gbeɔ kooloi bibii ni sa loo adebɔɔ mli nibii ni akudɔɔ amɛ mra lɛ bɛ mli.

english: Yellowing of lower leaves usually means your crop lacks nitrogen, a vital nutrient for plant growth. Maize moves available nitrogen from older leaves to support new growth at the top, indicating your soil needs nitrogen-rich fertilizer like urea or compost.
ga: Bei pii lɛ, baa ni yɔɔ shishigbɛ lɛ ni feɔ ŋmɔŋ lɛ tsɔɔ akɛ nitrogen bɛ otso lɛ mli. ni ji niyenii ni he hiaa waa kɛha tsei adalɛ Abele tsiɔ nitrogen ni yɔɔ lɛ kɛjɛɔ baai momoi amli koni eye ebua dalɛ hee ni yɔɔ ŋwɛi lɛ. Enɛ tsɔɔ akɛ oshikpɔŋ lɛ he miihia ŋmɔshi nibii ni nitrogen babaoo yɔɔ mli, tamɔ urea loo ŋmɔshi nibii.

english: Why does my land produce smaller yields when I plant maize on the exact same farm every single season?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mishikpɔŋ lɛ wooo yibii babaoo beni miduɔ ŋmãa yɛ ŋmɔ kome mli daa afi lɛ?

english: Planting the same crop continuously drains specific nutrients from the soil and allows pests to build up in the ground. Rotating maize with leguminous crops like cowpeas or groundnuts restores soil nitrogen and breaks disease cycles.
ga: Nibii kome too lɛ nɔŋŋ ni aduɔ daa lɛ haa niyenii pɔtɛɛ komɛi jeɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli. ni eyeɔ ebuaa ni ŋmeii buaa amɛhe naa yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ. Okɛ ŋmãa tamɔ tsina ŋmãa loo ŋmãa atsake ŋmãa. Eyeɔ ebuaa ni ekɛ nitrogen baa shikpɔŋ lɛ mli ekoŋŋ ni ekpaa hela lɛ sɛɛkuu.

english: How do I know if my soil needs chemical fertilizer or if dried cow dung is enough?
ga: Te abaafee tɛŋŋ ale kɛji akɛ tsofai ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli lɛ he miihia loo tsina ŋmei ni egbi lɛ faaa?

english: Animal manure improves long-term soil structure and water retention, but releases nutrients slowly. Chemical fertilizers provide immediate nutrients to growing crops. Combining both gives crops quick nourishment while keeping the soil healthy over time.
ga: Koolooi ashishifãi haa shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ nibii kɛ nu ni hiɔ shi be kakadaŋŋ lɛ yaa hiɛ. Shi ejieɔ niyenii mli hewalɛ nibii fiofio. Tsofai ni akɛwoɔ ŋmɔ mli lɛ haa ŋmɔshi nibii amrɔ nɔŋŋ. Kɛ́ akɛ enyɔ lɛ fɛɛ fata he lɛ, tsei lɛ náa niyenii oya, yɛ be mli ni ehaa shikpɔŋ lɛ hiɔ shi jogbaŋŋ yɛ be ni sa mli.

english: Why do my plantain trees produce very small bunches when I leave all the new shoots growing around them?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi plantain tsei lɛ daraa bibii waa beni mishiɔ ŋmeii heei yɛ he fɛɛ he lɛ? Nɛkɛ tsei nɛɛ

english: Multiple shoots (suckers) compete with the main plantain tree for nutrients, sunlight, and water. Cutting away extra suckers and keeping only two or three strong ones allows the main tree to put its full energy into growing larger fruit bunches.
ga: Tso lɛ mli tsei babaoo (tsei lɛ) kɛ plantain titri lɛ yeɔ akaŋ koni amɛná niyenii, hulu la, kɛ nu. Kpɔ̃ɔ ŋmeii ni fa fe nine lɛ ni okɛ ŋmeii enyɔ loo etɛ pɛ ni yɔɔ hewalɛ ahi shi. Enɛ baaha tso titri lɛ kɛ ehewalɛ fɛɛ atsu nii ni ekɛwo yibii wuji.

english: Staking gets yam leaves up off the ground where they can catch maximum sunlight to manufacture food for the tuber below. It also protects leaves from soil-borne diseases and excess moisture that causes rot.
ga: Staking haa sweet potato baai lɛ teɔ shi kɛjɛɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ he ni amɛbaanyɛ amɛná hulu la ni fe fɛɛ lɛ koni amɛfee niyenii amɛha bulbs ni yɔɔ shishi lɛ. Ebuɔ baai lɛ ahe kɛjɛɔ helai ni jɛɔ sũ mli kɛ ŋmɔtɔ ni fa fe nine ni kɛ ŋmɔtɔ baa lɛ hu he.

english: Why do the blossoms on my tomato plants dry up and fall off without producing any tomatoes?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-tomato fɔfɔi lɛ miigbi ni amɛmiigbee shi ni tomato ko kwraa ekwɛɛɛ lɛ?

english: Tomato flowers drop when the plant experiences heat stress, irregular watering, or a lack of calcium in the soil. Consistent watering early in the morning helps the flowers stay attached and form healthy tomatoes.
ga: Tomato fɔfɔi lɛ shwieɔ shi kɛji tsei lɛ na dɔlɛ he haomɔ. Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ daa loo calcium ni bɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli Nu ni akɛwoɔ shikpɔŋ lɛ mli daa leebi lɛ yeɔ ebuaa fɔfɔi lɛ ni amɛkpɛtɛɔ he ni amɛfeɔ tomato ni yɔɔ hewalɛ.

english: Why do my cassava tubers become soft and rot inside the soil during heavy rain seasons?
ga: Mɛni hewɔ mi-cassava shishifãi lɛ feɔ blɛoo ni amɛgboɔ yɛ shikpɔŋ lɛ nɔ yɛ nugbɔ ni nɛɔ waa lɛ mli lɛ?
